As Yu Wan walked past, she happened to see a cook washing dishes and pots.

Sun Qianran was frail and sickly, so she needed a separate kitchen for her meals.

Because of this, Yu Wan thought of another advantage of living here.

Zhao Xuanyou wasn't particular about food. All three meals were delivered from the Travel Palace's kitchen. But other families would definitely bring their own chefs. With three families sharing one kitchen, it would be busy from morning to night, and there would be no peace.

In August, the capital was so hot that one would sweat every day. In comparison, the climate of the Lichuan Travel Palace, warm like spring, was really comfortable.

Yu Wan wanted to go out and take a look, but since she was new here, she was afraid of causing trouble by wandering around, so she gave up.

Back in the room, she wrote a letter to Chen Da Niu, explaining that she was traveling with the heir. If anything urgent came up, he could go to the Marquis's mansion to find Yingxue. Or if there was any change in her mother's condition, he could write to inform her.

After writing the letter, she entrusted Yuan Yi to send it to the capital, then lay down on the bed to rest.

Perhaps it was because Sun Qianran was in good condition during the day, or perhaps the walls of the Travel Palace's side courtyard were thick. Yu Wan didn't hear a single cough and quickly fell asleep.

chapters.title: Friend or Foe
chapters.content:
When Zhao Xuanyou dared to look back at him, the Crown Prince could not conceal his burning rage.

He was the esteemed heir to the throne; even his younger brothers had to bow and scrape before him. Prince Ping, though harboring ill intentions, did not dare to act openly against him. How could Zhao Xuanyou, a mere heir of a marquisate, dare to do so?

No, his seventh brother, Zhao Qi, was just as reckless.

What was Father thinking, putting these two detestable men together?

Facing the Crown Prince’s unbridled hostility, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression remained completely calm.

He had already made up his mind; he would not let Zhao Zun and Cui Yichu, that wretched pair, stir even the slightest ripple in his heart.

That time in the Listening to Rain Pavilion, when he had lost his temper and cursed at Cui Yichu, had already been enough to make him regret it.

He glanced indifferently at the Crown Prince, his demeanor unyielding. This haughty and self-assured attitude only infuriated the Crown Prince further.

"Old Seven," the Emperor, oblivious to their silent confrontation, addressed his son.

Standing at the end of the line of imperial princes, Zhao Qi stepped forward reluctantly and called out, "Father Emperor."

"I intend to have you study martial arts under Xuanyou. Are you willing?" The Emperor did not mind Zhao Qi’s attitude and asked kindly.

Zhao Qi glanced at Zhao Xuanyou, his gaze filled with scrutiny.

Zhao Xuanyou stood at the end of the line of officials, and Zhao Qi at the end of the line of princes. The earlier exchange of glances between the Crown Prince and Zhao Xuanyou had all been observed by Zhao Qi.

He did not know Zhao Xuanyou, nor did he have any interest in him.

But seeing that Zhao Xuanyou dared to defy the Crown Prince, he figured the man must have some courage.

"I am willing," Zhao Qi replied.

Before his words had even settled, the Crown Prince blurted out urgently, "Father Emperor, Seventh Brother hasn’t even mastered the Four Books and Five Classics. He doesn’t understand loyalty, filial piety, or propriety. If you let him follow Zhao Xuanyou to study martial arts, he will only become even more hopeless. Zhao Xuanyou is a military man, unlearned in literature…"

Hearing the Crown Prince’s disparagement of himself, Zhao Qi did not get angry, nor did he retort. He stood there indifferently, as if none of it concerned him.

The Emperor glanced at the Crown Prince. "Who told you Xuanyou is unlearned in literature?"

The Crown Prince had not expected the Emperor to speak up for Zhao Xuanyou. He hesitated for a moment before forcing out, "Isn’t he a military man?"

"Many military men are both literary and martial talents. Let Old Seven study martial arts under Xuanyou first. If there are any issues with his studies, he can ask Xuanyou or go to Pei Tao. It’s no big deal. That’s settled then."

"Your subject obeys."

With the Emperor’s final word, the audience was dismissed.

As they left the Hall of Bright Virtue, the Crown Prince shot a furious glance at Zhao Xuanyou before storming off.

Zhao Xuanyou acted as if he noticed nothing and walked down the steps. Zhao Qi, however, had somehow slipped to his side and said with ill intent, "He bears a strong grudge. You’re in trouble."

Meeting Zhao Qi’s gaze, Zhao Xuanyou gave a faint smile. "Your Highness must have offended him long before I did. Yet you don’t seem to be in trouble, so perhaps I need not worry either."

Zhao Qi had not expected such a response. He coldly scoffed and left in a huff.

After exiting the palace, a eunuch led them to their respective residences.

As the other officials left one by one, Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Pei Tao beside him. Pei Tao happened to be looking at him as well.

"It seems, Lord Zhao and I will be staying here for two months. Please forgive any inconvenience," Pei Tao said.

"We are colleagues. Lord Pei need not be so polite."

Pei Tao said softly, "My wife has been unwell, often coughing. I suppose Lord Zhao is already aware."

Zhao Xuanyou certainly was. The violent coughing last night had been impossible to ignore.

It had woken him up in the middle of the night; no one would be pleased by that.

Even Yu Wan, usually so obedient and gentle, had been restless in his arms for a long time before falling back asleep.

"If Lady Pei is unwell, how could others blame her?"

"Thank you for your understanding, Lord Zhao," Pei Tao said, then added, "Were you aware of today’s arrangement in the Hall of Bright Virtue?"

"You mean teaching the Seventh Prince martial arts? No."

Pei Tao smiled slightly. "Before we were in the palace, His Majesty mentioned this to me. I recommended you."

The Emperor had arranged for him to teach Zhao Qi on Pei Tao’s recommendation?

Zhao Xuanyou had no personal connection with Pei Tao; they had only become vaguely familiar during the journey. Why would Pei Tao recommend him? As the son-in-law of Prime Minister Sun, a man of deep scheming, Pei Tao should not be taking sides among the princes.

So was he trying to get closer to him?

Facing this famous beauty of the capital, Zhao Xuanyou had originally felt nothing. But then he recalled what had happened at the post station last night.

At that time, Yu Wan had been standing in the corridor, staring blankly; seemingly at Pei Tao’s retreating figure.

If they were to stay in the same courtyard for the next two months, she might keep looking at him.

Zhao Xuanyou felt an inexplicable irritation. He gave a perfunctory "Thank you" in response to Pei Tao’s attempt at conversation, then averted his gaze.

Soon, the eunuch led them to the end of the guest courtyard, where they indeed found themselves assigned to the same residence. Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered.

As they entered the courtyard, Yu Wan happened to step out of the side room. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou, she sweetly called out, "Master is back."

Zhao Xuanyou had entered with Pei Tao at his side. Seeing that Yu Wan’s gaze had fallen on him first, the irritation he had felt earlier instantly vanished.

But in the next moment, as Yu Wan approached, she greeted Pei Tao with a curtsy.

"Lord Pei."

"Miss Yu Wan." Pei Tao responded warmly.

This exchange made them seem quite familiar.

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression darkened again. He gave Pei Tao a perfunctory cupped-hand salute, then took Yu Wan’s sleeve and went back inside.

"Master," Yu Wan, puzzled, couldn’t help but mutter after being pulled into the room, "This servant was in the kitchen making plum tea to relieve the heat. It should be ready now; time to bottle it."

Noticing his bad mood, Yu Wan hummed in acknowledgment, studied him for a moment, then asked softly, "Has this servant done something wrong again?"

"You are my maid. Why be so warm to others?"

Warm? To whom?

Was he talking about Pei Tao?

Yu Wan truly didn’t think she had been warm. Lord Pei Tao was a high-ranking official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. If she encountered him directly, shouldn’t she greet him properly?

"Are you very familiar with him?"

"Master has misunderstood this servant," Yu Wan said, shaking her head upon realizing "him" referred to Pei Tao. "This servant is not familiar with Lord Pei at all. We only spoke a few words yesterday. However, Lady Pei has been very kind to me; unlike other ladies, she doesn’t put on airs. The ingredients for the plum tea I made were given to me by her."

"I don’t want to drink it." Zhao Xuanyou had no interest in such sweet and sour things.

"Then would Master like some tea? This servant will prepare it."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou remain silent, Yu Wan hurried to pour tea from the side.

"This is the good tea His Majesty bestowed upon the officials earlier. It smells very fragrant. Please try it, Master."

Faced with Yu Wan’s smile, and recalling how she had looked at him first earlier, Zhao Xuanyou finally accepted the tea cup.

The tea was indeed excellent.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yu Wan, then remembered what Pei Tao had said to him earlier. His sword-like brows knitted slightly.

He didn’t know whether Pei Tao was a friend or a foe. From now on, in Lichuan, every step would have to be taken carefully.

---

chapters.title: Playing in the Water
chapters.content:
Thinking of this, Zhao Xuanyou slowly set down his tea cup and looked at Yu Wan.

"The imperial retreat is not like the marquis’s residence. Every word and action must be carefully considered. If something goes wrong, no one will be able to protect you."

This was not just a reminder to Yu Wan, but also to himself.

In the marquis’s residence, he was the unquestioned young master. But in the imperial retreat, the young master was just a low-ranking official.

If he made even the slightest mistake, it would be a disaster.

"This servant only speaks with Lady Pei about food and medicinal cuisine. Nothing else."

Zhao Xuanyou knew Yu Wan was clever. He stopped there, saying no more.

After sitting quietly for a while, Zhao Xuanyou said, "Accompany me for a walk."

Yu Wan had been cooped up in the courtyard all day and was, of course, eager to go out.

Hearing this, she immediately smiled. "Yes."

Seeing her joy, Zhao Xuanyou quickly curved the corner of his lips and stood up to leave.

The courtyard where Zhao Xuanyou was staying was the farthest one, but it also had the best view. Stepping out, one could see the mountains and water.

The guest courtyards where the officials stayed were separated from the palace complex where the nobles resided by a small stream.

Zhao Xuanyou led Yu Wan around the small courtyard and down the stone path for a dozen steps, arriving at the stream.

On the opposite bank, many Feathered Forest Guards could be seen patrolling. Behind the golden and jade-like palaces were towering, overlapping peaks, covered in various trees. Though the view was a sea of green, the varying shades and depths of green intertwined to create a natural masterpiece that even the most skilled painter would struggle to replicate.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan stood quietly by the stream, listening to the babbling water and gazing at the natural painting before them, both deeply entranced.

"With such beautiful scenery, it’s no wonder His Majesty enjoys coming to Lichuan," Zhao Xuanyou said softly after a long while.

Yu Wan’s previous village had also been scenic, but it lacked such steep peaks and cliffs.

"Master, have you never been to Lichuan before?"

Zhao Xuanyou shook his head.

When he was a child in the capital, the Lichuan Imperial Retreat had not yet been built. Later, he went to Yuzhou to lead troops and rarely returned to the capital, let alone the retreat.

"Let’s walk further ahead."

"Yes."

As the sky gradually darkened, Zhao Xuanyou led Yu Wan deeper into the mountain valley.

Seeing that they were getting farther and farther from the guest courtyard, a strange beast’s cry suddenly echoed from the mountain.

Yu Wan instinctively let out an "ah" and looked around.

The dense foliage on the mountain blocked the view; nothing could be seen but trees.

"Scared?"

Yu Wan replied, "This servant is just curious about what wild beast is on the mountain. Following Master, what is there to fear?"

Zhao Xuanyou turned to look at her.

The night wind stirred the loose strands of hair by Yu Wan’s ears. Her beautiful face was slightly upturned as she looked at him, her brows and eyes like a painting, her gaze filled with a mix of joy and anticipation, stirring something in his heart.

"Are you not afraid of me?"

"Why would this servant fear Master?"

Zhao Xuanyou lowered his voice. "What if we encounter a fierce beast? To save myself, I might just throw you to it."

Yu Wan looked at him askance. The wind grew stronger, making their clothes flutter.

With no one around, she too became bold.

"That would be fine. After all, being eaten is being eaten. Does it matter who does the eating?"

Hearing her bold words, Zhao Xuanyou let out a light hum and glared at her.

Come to think of it, at the mention of eating, he did feel a bit hungry.

Meeting Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, Yu Wan quickly took two steps back.

"Can you run?"

"Not necessarily unable to."

Before Yu Wan could finish, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly reached for her.

This time, she reacted quickly, hopping to the side. But she didn’t notice her foot stepping on a slippery stone by the stream.

She let out a soft "ah," and seeing Zhao Xuanyou approach, she bent down and splashed water at him without hesitation.

Zhao Xuanyou had originally reached out to steady her, not expecting her to be so wild. Before he could regain his balance, she had already splashed water at him. Though he turned his face away, his neck and chest still got wet.

"Have you lost your mind!" Zhao Xuanyou said, half angry and half teasing, grabbing her arm and pulling her up.

Yu Wan knew when to stop. She quickly said in a coquettish voice, "Young Master, spare me!"

"Too late." Zhao Xuanyou coldly replied.

"Master, don’t be so petty. It’s just a wet robe. Can’t this servant make amends?"

"What do you think?"

"This servant thinks it’s possible."

"Hmph..."

As they bantered back and forth, Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze suddenly shifted warily to the side.

Yu Wan, noticing this, instinctively followed his gaze and saw Pei Tao and Sun Qianran standing not far away, smiling as they watched them.

Sun Qianran wore a thin silk cloak and, to guard against the wind, a hood. She held Pei Tao’s arm, nearly leaning her entire body against him.

Seeing them look over, Pei Tao smiled warmly. "We’ve disturbed Lord Zhao’s peace."

Yu Wan’s face flushed slightly.

She had thought no one was around, which was why she had dared to play with Zhao Xuanyou. She hadn’t expected to be seen by others.

At that moment, she was still encircled in Zhao Xuanyou’s arms, which was rather embarrassing.

"Lord Pei, Lady Pei." Zhao Xuanyou said coolly, loosening his hold on Yu Wan slightly.

Yu Wan said nothing, standing obediently behind Zhao Xuanyou.

The others were all masters; it wasn’t her place as a servant to speak.

Pei Tao said, "If you walk further ahead, there is a waterwheel and a pond filled with fish that Lord Zhao can go see. Beyond that is the boundary wall of the guest courtyard. There are guards at the gate who won’t allow anyone to go out, saying the mountains are dangerous."

"Thank you for the information, Lord Pei. I was just strolling around. Please, you and Lady Pei continue on."

Pei Tao gave a slight nod, supporting Sun Qianran as they passed by.

But after walking a short distance, Sun Qianran couldn’t help but look back, seeing Zhao Xuanyou holding Yu Wan’s hand as they continued forward.

She withdrew her gaze and looked at the handsome man beside her.

"Has my lord offended Lord Zhao? I noticed he seems quite cold toward you."

Pei Tao wore a crab-shell green long robe, and under his jade crown, his features were strikingly handsome, perfectly complementing the surrounding green mountains and clear waters.

He looked at Sun Qianran, sighed slightly, and gave a bitter smile. "Lord Zhao is very guarded. I was too hasty, eager to show goodwill, and instead made him wary of me."

"I see." Sun Qianran seemed thoughtful.

"Madame has sharp eyes; nothing can be hidden from you."

Sun Qianran said, "My lord need not worry. We still have two months in this retreat. This is only the first day; there will be plenty of opportunities to make amends. It’s a pity... he currently has no wife, only Yu Wan as a maid. If his wife were here, I could lend a hand."

It was true that the other ladies had been unwilling to stay with her, but having Zhao Xuanyou stay in the same courtyard as them was the result of her bribing the eunuchs heavily.

Pei Tao, hearing this, recalled the scene of Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan flirting by the stream just now.

This was the first time he had seen the two of them interacting privately.

Under the golden sunset, Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had been playing by the water, their faces filled with bright, poetic joy, as if isolated from the world’s troubles. Even he had been moved.

Previously, he had assumed Yu Wan was just a concubine, but that scene had clearly shown affection between them.

Pei Tao’s heart jolted. He looked at Sun Qianran and said firmly, "Miss Yu Wan should be able to help me."

chapters.title: Ingratiating Overtures
chapters.content:
Yu Wan had offended Zhao Xuanyou by the stream, and since he was a vengeful man, he retaliated fiercely that very night, leaving her unable to even straighten her back.

The next morning, Zhao Xuanyou dressed and went to the imperial palace to attend to his duties, while Yu Wan stayed in bed until the sun was high in the sky.

She was not someone who slept a lot; her eyes had been open for a long time, but her body was too exhausted to move.

Only when hunger became unbearable did she force herself to sit up and eat the now-cold breakfast.

"Miss Yu Wan." A knock came from outside the door, accompanied by Sun Qianran's voice.

Yu Wan was in a disheveled state, having not yet dressed or done her hair, so she couldn’t open the door in such a condition. She could only speak through the door: "Does Madame Pei need something?"

Sun Qianran’s voice was gentle: "Nothing much. I just wanted to chat with you for a while. My cook made extra yam cakes this morning. We could eat while we talk."

"Thank you, Madame Pei. I have something to attend to right now. I’ll come pay my respects later."

"Very well."

After hearing Madame Pei’s footsteps fade away, Yu Wan let out a small sigh. She couldn’t help but recall what Zhao Xuanyou had said the day before.

At the time, she hadn’t thought much of Madame Pei, but now she realized there was something off.

Madame Pei was the wife of a high-ranking official. Even if she was open-minded and treated servants kindly, it was unusual for her to personally deliver yam cakes and show such warmth toward a mere concubine like herself.

Yu Wan had heard a saying: "Unsolicited kindness is either a trick or a trap."

A mere maidservant like her had no real value to exploit. Madame Pei’s kindness toward her was likely still tied to Zhao Xuanyou.

Could Madame Pei be hoping she would whisper in Zhao Xuanyou’s ear on her behalf?

Yu Wan didn’t know whether to call Madame Pei foolish or simply too optimistic.

Still, living in the same courtyard, Yu Wan couldn’t afford to openly offend such a prominent lady.

She quickly pinned her hair into a bun with a jade hairpin, washed her face, and stepped out barefaced.

The door to the main house was open, with only a peach-colored gauze curtain to keep out mosquitoes.

As Yu Wan approached, the maidservant guarding the door lifted the curtain to let her in.

The main house was not much larger than the side rooms, but its windows faced the stream, offering a view of the palace across the water. The scenery outside was far superior.

Perhaps due to poor health and a sallow complexion, Sun Qianran’s attire was always vibrant. Today, her skirt and blouse were embroidered with colorful gold thread, exceptionally luxurious, and the pearl hairpins in her hair swayed gently, drawing the eye.

Seeing Yu Wan arrive, a faint smile appeared on her sickly face: "Miss Yu Wan, you’ve come."

"Greetings to Madame Pei."

Sun Qianran quietly studied Yu Wan, a faint envy rising in her heart.

Yu Wan did not have the slender, frail figure favored by noblewomen in the capital. Instead, she had a graceful, voluptuous figure, exuding a natural charm.

Moreover, her skin was fair and smooth. Even without any makeup, her cheeks had a natural flush, and her lips were moist, making her look radiant.

Recalling how she had seen Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou playing in the stream the previous evening, with Yu Wan’s feet in the icy water, Sun Qianran thought that if it had been her, she would have coughed up blood.

Such vitality was truly enviable.

Sun Qianran suppressed the sadness in her heart and looked at Yu Wan warmly: "Sit down and keep me company for a while."

Yu Wan respectfully smiled: "Madame, if you have something to say, please go ahead. This servant is fine standing."

"Here in the palace, neither of us is a master. There’s no need for such formality. Please, sit."

Perhaps sensing Yu Wan’s insistence, Sun Qianran signaled a maidservant, who quickly brought a stool for Yu Wan.

"Thank you for the seat, Madame." Only then did Yu Wan sit down.

Sun Qianran ordered the yam cakes to be served. Yu Wan took one and found the taste pleasant, but noticing Sun Qianran’s constant gaze, her heart sank.

It seemed Zhao Xuanyou had been right; Madame Pei did have ulterior motives toward her.

Yu Wan felt a wave of annoyance.

She had to avenge her family against the Cui clan and cure her mother’s illness. She already had enough on her plate without getting entangled in more troubles.

She didn’t want to sit, but if she refused, she might end up in a longer conversation. Zhao Xuanyou had explicitly told her to keep her distance from Madame Pei. No matter what Madame Pei said, Zhao Xuanyou would likely blame her for it.

But living in the same courtyard, they were bound to cross paths often. Yu Wan couldn’t avoid her forever.

"The yam cakes made by Madame Pei’s cook are truly delicious. This servant has never tasted such good yam cakes before." Yu Wan forced a smile, hoping Madame Pei would take the hint and stop scheming.

Sun Qianran smiled faintly: "I’m glad you like them. My cook is best at making all kinds of pastries. From now on, I’ll have her make more."

"That’s too much trouble, Madame. This servant is just a maidservant." Yu Wan quickly declined.

"Why must you belittle yourself, Miss Yu Wan? I can see that Lord Zhao cares for you deeply."

Cares? About what...

As expected, the conversation turned to Zhao Xuanyou. Yu Wan silently cried for help. She wished she could grab Sun Qianran’s hand and earnestly tell her that Zhao Xuanyou was a deep and calculating man. His affection for her was limited to the bed, once he put his pants back on, he would turn his back on her.

She was only carefully trying to please Zhao Xuanyou now. If she ever provoked him, she would end up like Mama Zhou and Baozhu.

"You’re mistaken, Madame. Lord Zhao is a noble heir. How could he care for a mere maidservant?"

Sun Qianran could hear the evasion in Yu Wan’s words. To be honest, she thought the same.

Yu Wan was just a concubine. Zhao Xuanyou had brought her to the palace because he had no one else to keep him company and to seek pleasure.

But her husband said Yu Wan could be useful, and she trusted her husband’s words completely. She was willing to try.

Recalling what her husband had said last night, Sun Qianran looked at Yu Wan with a gentle gaze.

"To be honest, the reason I invited you today is to ask for your help in passing a message to Lord Zhao." Seeing Yu Wan’s lips part slightly, Sun Qianran quickly added, "Don’t rush to refuse. At least hear me out first. If you think what I say is unreasonable, then treat it as the ravings of a sick woman. You won’t have to say a word to Lord Zhao."

What did she mean by that?

Yu Wan wanted to refuse, but Sun Qianran had already anticipated her refusal, leaving her speechless.

As expected of the daughter of a prime minister; her persuasive skills were impressive.

"Miss Yu Wan, are you willing to hear out my ‘ravings’?" Sun Qianran’s frail body made her look pitiful, and with her humble posture and pleading tone, Yu Wan felt helpless.

If she left now, she might still be cornered by Sun Qianran later. It was better to hear her out today.

Besides, she had only asked her to pass a message. At worst, she could just not deliver it.

With that thought, Yu Wan gave an awkward smile, neither accepting nor refusing. She took another yam cake and ate it silently.

Seeing that she wasn’t in a hurry to leave, Sun Qianran felt a slight relief.

"Actually, my husband wants to befriend Lord Zhao because of the Xingguo Duke’s estate."

---

chapters.title: Conspiracy
chapters.content:
The Xingguo Duke’s estate?

Yu Wan truly hadn’t expected Pei Tao and Sun Qianran to have any connection to the Xingguo Duke’s estate.

Originally, passing a message was none of her concern, but now it seemed to involve her as well.

Were they enemies or allies with the Xingguo Duke’s estate?

Yu Wan steadied her mind and said gently, "Lord Zhao has already divorced the Cui family of the Xingguo Duke’s estate. There are no entanglements between the two families. To be honest with you, Madame, Lord Zhao has even forbidden us servants from mentioning the Cui family. I wouldn’t dare pass on such a message."

"We have a feud with the Xingguo Duke’s estate. It’s precisely because we know about Lord Zhao’s history with the Cui family that we wish to speak with him."

Yu Wan was slightly taken aback, finding it hard to believe.

Sun Qianran was the daughter of a prime minister. Prime Minister Sun had served in the court for decades without a noble title, but he had always been at the center of power. The Xingguo Duke’s estate, no matter how arrogant, wouldn’t dare provoke Prime Minister Sun.

As for Cui Yichu, her atrocities were only directed at maidservants and servants. Given her previously good reputation, she must have put on a good show in social situations. It was unlikely she had conflicts with someone of Sun Qianran’s status.

However, from Sun Qianran’s words, it seemed she wouldn’t reveal the details to her.

What Sun Qianran wanted her to pass on was that they, too, had a feud with the Xingguo Duke’s estate and wanted to join forces with Zhao Xuanyou against them.

This was, of course, good news for Yu Wan.

But the decision lay with Zhao Xuanyou.

To be honest, Yu Wan wasn’t sure what Zhao Xuanyou thought.

Cui Yichu had cuckolded him, so naturally, he resented her.

If it were someone ruthless, they might have already killed Cui Yichu. But Zhao Xuanyou, a general who had killed countless on the battlefield, had not laid a hand on her.

Although he had humiliated the Xingguo Duke’s estate by not only keeping Cui Yichu’s dowry but also taking double the betrothal gifts when he visited, he had ultimately agreed to the divorce.

This was partly because the Xingguo Duke had paid a heavy price, but Yu Wan knew that the Jingyuan Marquis’s estate was not short of money, and Zhao Xuanyou didn’t care much for wealth.

He had let go because Cui Yichu’s lover had powerful backing.

As long as Cui Yichu’s lover remained in power, Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t act recklessly.

Of course, these were just Yu Wan’s speculations.

If Pei Tao and his wife could come up with a good plan, perhaps the situation would be different.

"I understand your meaning, Madame. When Lord Zhao returns this evening, I will relay your message to him. However, whether he agrees or not is beyond my control."

Hearing Yu Wan’s agreement, Sun Qianran was overjoyed. She was about to speak when she started coughing again.

Yu Wan immediately stood up and walked over, gently patting her back to help her breathe. Seeing a maidservant approach, she quickly had the maidservant bring a cup of warm water to soothe her throat.

After Sun Qianran recovered, she looked at Yu Wan with gratitude.

"Thank you."

"You’re welcome, Madame."

Sun Qianran signaled the maidservant, who quickly brought over a small pouch.

"Miss Yu Wan, this is a token of my gratitude."

Yu Wan glanced at it. The pouch was plump, seemingly filled with a considerable amount of silver.

She was in need of money, so there was no reason to refuse.

Out of courtesy, she still had to decline once.

"This servant is only passing a message. I can’t do much else for you, Madame. You really don’t have to give me this."

Sun Qianran said, "You serve Lord Zhao. Asking you to pass a message is already an imposition. If it angers Lord Zhao, it might bring you trouble. Please accept it, or I won’t feel at ease."

Her ability to say such words showed that she was indeed different from Cui Yichu.

Yu Wan accepted the pouch, stayed and chatted with Madame Pei for a while longer, then took her leave.

Zhao Xuanyou returned just before sunset.

Yu Wan was setting the table in the room when she turned and saw Zhao Xuanyou standing behind her.

"You’re back, my lord." Yu Wan’s voice was sweet and soft, her demeanor full of youthful charm.

The coldness in Zhao Xuanyou’s brows unconsciously softened.

He gave a light "mm," and Yu Wan stepped forward to greet him, leading him into the inner room to change into a stone-blue brocade robe.

"The food tonight smells quite good."

Yu Wan smiled: "Yuan Qi said he bought a wild pheasant from a nearby hunter. This servant stewed it into a soup and added some wild mushrooms. It really does smell good."

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression was calm as he washed his hands and sat at the table.

The brocade robe he wore looked unassuming, but the fabric was of the finest quality; a tribute bestowed by the emperor during his last palace visit. It made him look refined and dignified.

Feeling Yu Wan’s gaze, Zhao Xuanyou looked at her.

"What are you scheming?"

Yu Wan quickly averted her eyes, served him half a bowl of pheasant soup, a chicken leg, and three slices of wild mushrooms, and respectfully placed them before him.

She hoped Zhao Xuanyou would cooperate with Pei Tao and his wife against the Xingguo Duke’s estate, but she couldn’t show any trace of this in front of Zhao Xuanyou. She was anxious.

"My lord, this servant did encounter something today, but let’s talk about it after you’ve eaten."

The setting sun’s last rays slanted into the room, casting a soft golden glow over Yu Wan’s delicate skin.

Her lips curved slightly, her lashes fluttered, and her almond-shaped eyes sparkled with unhidden affection.

Zhao Xuanyou saw through her intentions but, facing those eyes, ultimately said nothing.

After dinner, Yu Wan cleared the dishes and served fresh tea.

Before Zhao Xuanyou could ask, she placed the pouch Sun Qianran had given her on the table.

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow at the pouch, waiting for her to explain.

"This is the pouch Madame Pei rewarded this servant with. There’s ten taels of silver inside."

"Seems like you didn’t take a single word I said yesterday to heart."

Yu Wan pitifully said, "This morning, as soon as this servant woke up, Madame Pei came knocking, inviting me to her room for pastries. As the wife of an official, she personally invited me. This servant couldn’t refuse without being rude. After just a few bites of the cakes, she gave me this pouch."

"What did she ask you to do?" Yu Wan had been direct, and Zhao Xuanyou was equally blunt.

Yu Wan replied, "She wanted this servant to pass a message for her."

"What if I don’t want to hear it?"

Yu Wan took the opportunity: "If my lord doesn’t want to hear it, this servant won’t say it."

"Taking someone’s money means you have to do their bidding. You took her silver but won’t do the job?" Zhao Xuanyou asked with interest.

"This servant did take the pouch, but this servant didn’t agree to anything." Yu Wan’s eyes curved with a pleased smile. "It’s best if my lord doesn’t want to hear it. She might give this servant more silver later."

So she was planning to use him to hoard favors, was she? She deserved punishment.

Zhao Xuanyou reached out and pulled her into his lap, casually slipping a hand into her thin summer shirt.

His palm was broad and rough, while her skin was smooth and tender. The contrast created a unique sensation.

Yu Wan let out a soft "mm," her beautiful eyebrows slightly furrowing; partly from the physical teasing, partly from her inner frustration.

Did he really not want to hear it?

It was rare to find someone willing to join forces against the Xingguo Duke’s estate, but Yu Wan couldn’t push him.

She wrapped her arms around his shoulders. Only after Zhao Xuanyou had his fun did he finally ask:

"Alright, what was the message she wanted you to pass?"

chapters.title: Coming to Pick a Fight
chapters.content:
Yu Ying did her best to suppress the joy in her heart and said calmly, "Madame Pei said that she and her husband have a feud with the Duke of Xingguo's mansion."

"So what?"

"So they want to talk to the Heir. That's all they said, nothing else."

Yu Ying gazed quietly at Zhao Xuanyou, whose eyes gradually darkened as if lost in thought.

Was he still wary of Madame Pei’s lover?

Yu Ying nervously clenched her fingers but did not dare to urge him.

Seeing his hand slide out from his own clothes, knowing he was not in the mood, Yu Ying obediently stepped out of his embrace and replaced the cold tea on the table with hot tea.

After a moment of thought, Zhao Xuanyou had already made up his mind.

Seeing Yu Ying stand up, he asked again, "Aren't you going to take your reward?"

Hearing the teasing tone in his voice, Yu Ying smiled and forced down her unease, putting away the purse.

Regardless of whether Zhao Xuanyou was willing to cooperate with the Pei couple, she had earned ten taels of silver, enough for two acupuncture sessions for her mother. That wasn’t a bad thing.

---

The next few days passed peacefully.

Zhao Xuanyou still left early and returned late, having no extra words with the Pei couple. Madame Pei did not ask Yu Ying about the message either, still speaking to her kindly.

It was as if the message had never been delivered.

One day, while Yu Ying was steaming pastries in the kitchen, someone suddenly barged into the courtyard, loudly asking, "Where is Zhao Xuanyou?"

The maid standing in the courtyard was from the Pei mansion. Hearing the question, she shook her head blankly and said she didn’t know.

"Useless! Didn’t I say he lives in this courtyard? Why are you acting like an idiot?"

Yu Ying quickly wiped her hands and went to the courtyard.

"My young master hasn’t returned yet, I don’t know..." Standing in the courtyard was a boy of fifteen or sixteen. Meeting his arrogant gaze, and seeing the expensive clothes he wore, Yu Ying guessed he was of noble status.

But she didn’t know his exact identity and didn’t dare address him presumptuously.

She could only bow to him and truthfully say, "At noon, the young master came back to change clothes and said he was going hunting with a noble. He probably won’t return until nightfall."

The boy had an extremely graceful demeanor and a handsome face, but his eyes were exceptionally arrogant and cold, with no restraint in his sharp gaze.

"So he went hunting, no wonder he’s not here."

Seeing the boy gnashing his teeth, Yu Ying didn’t dare speak.

A boy who could act so boldly in the imperial palace was likely a noble. She didn’t dare provoke him.

"Are you Zhao Xuanyou’s maid?"

As soon as he spoke, Yu Ying knew it was trouble. She could only respectfully say, "Yes."

The boy’s gaze swept over Yu Ying without restraint, a hint of mockery appearing on his fair, jade-like face.

"Looking at his cold and serious appearance, it seems he’s just pretending. To think he keeps a maid like you; he must have spent many nights in brothels."

He didn’t explicitly say what kind of maid Yu Ying was, but it was clearly not a compliment.

If it weren’t for his young age, Yu Ying would have thought he was Madame Pei’s lover. Otherwise, why would he have such hostility toward Zhao Xuanyou and herself?

Having been a maid for years and having died once, Yu Ying had long since lost her temper.

Hearing him say this, Yu Ying still maintained a respectful posture, standing there with a smile as he mocked her.

The boy, after saying those humiliating words, saw that Yu Ying had no reaction, as if his fist had landed on cotton.

Unwilling to give up, he said, "I’ve been here so long and you haven’t even offered tea. Is this the rule Zhao Xuanyou taught you?"

Offer tea?

Serving tea wasn’t difficult, but Yu Ying didn’t want to lead him into the house. If he sat down, who knew how long she’d have to entertain him.

Just then, the door of the main house suddenly opened, and Sun Qianran, supported by a maid, walked out. Seeing the boy, she steadied herself and bowed to him.

"Ah, so it’s the Seventh Prince. Please forgive me for not welcoming you."

Seventh Prince?

No wonder he was so bold; he was a prince.

Yu Ying carefully observed the Seventh Prince’s expression and saw his gaze slightly soften when Sun Qianran appeared. She secretly sighed in relief.

He knew Sun Qianran, so he should give her some face and not cause more trouble.

"Dispense with the formalities." Zhao Qi did recognize Sun Qianran, but he didn’t even respect the Crown Prince, so naturally, he didn’t respect others either.

Sun Qianran softly said, "I have some fine white tea from Wuyi here. Would Your Highness like to try some?"

"It’s just white tea. I use it to rinse my mouth." Zhao Qi said indifferently.

At this moment, Yu Ying understood; he wouldn’t give face to anyone.

He dared to come here and curse Zhao Xuanyou, and he dared to slight Sun Qianran.

Sun Qianran had come out to help her, but since he was so rude, Yu Ying couldn’t let the person who came to help her be embarrassed.

So Yu Ying said, "Since the Seventh Prince wishes to wait for the young master, why not sit in the house for a while? This servant will prepare tea for Your Highness."

Zhao Qi glanced at her and coldly said, "This place is just a few shabby rooms. I don’t care to go in."

Not going in?

Yu Ying quickly came up with a solution: "Your Highness, please wait a moment. This servant will move the table and chairs outside."

"Move them outside? You want me to drink tea in the courtyard?"

Zhao Qi was purely looking for trouble. As he spoke, he only thought of refuting her, not considering whether she could do it. He just hoped she would be at a loss and make a fool of herself.

"Yes." Yu Ying respectfully said, "Sitting in this courtyard, you can see the distant mountains and hear the stream. It should be much more comfortable than sitting inside."

Zhao Qi humphed and didn’t speak.

The surrounding mountains were clear, and the water was beautiful; indeed, a pleasant sight.

Seeing that he didn’t refute her anymore, Yu Ying quickly went into the house and first carried out a chair.

The other party had come to pick a fight. If they were of equal status, when he made a move, Yu Ying would have to return it double.

But their statuses were worlds apart. He was a prince, superior even to Zhao Xuanyou. When he made a move, Yu Ying could only endure it, responding to each move as it came, ensuring he couldn’t find the slightest flaw.

Seeing Yu Ying bring out the chair, and knowing the table was heavy and she, a weak woman, couldn’t move it alone, Sun Qianran ordered a maid to go help.

But before the maid could take two steps, Zhao Qi scolded, "I came to find Zhao Xuanyou. What does it have to do with you Pei family people? All you idle onlookers, get lost and stop watching the show."

The maid didn’t dare move further, and Sun Qianran was also helpless against this unruly Seventh Prince.

If he couldn’t find Zhao Xuanyou, he might take his anger out on the maid.

Sun Qianran was worried about Yu Ying, so she took the maid and sat under the corridor of the main house. If it was just drinking tea, that would be fine. If this troublemaker caused too much of a scene, she would find a way to mediate.

The table was made of high-quality rosewood, and the wood was very heavy. Even though Yu Ying was used to farm work and had considerable strength, she had to rest three times before she barely managed to drag and pull the table past the threshold.

Once past the threshold, it was easier. Yu Ying crouched under the table, grabbed one of the table legs with each hand, and lifted the table onto her shoulders.

When the table landed with a heavy thud in the courtyard, everyone in the courtyard stared in shock.

---

chapters.title: Too Strong
chapters.content:
Yu Ying didn’t realize everyone was staring at her.

The force she had used to lift the table just now had been too strong, and her waist seemed to have twinged.

She quickly supported her waist and rubbed it, feeling a bit better. Then she turned to Zhao Qi: "Your Highness, please wait a moment. This servant will go prepare tea."

The boy’s eyes were bright with astonishment.

He stared blankly at Yu Ying, momentarily forgetting to mock her. He truly hadn’t expected that this fair and delicate girl would have such strength; she had actually lifted the table.

Seeing he didn’t speak, Yu Ying, still holding her waist, went into the house to get the tea leaves.

Zhao Xuanyou always traveled light when he went out, bringing few servants. He didn’t bring much food or supplies, only seven or eight sets of clothes to change into. Naturally, the tea he used was provided by the imperial palace.

She carried the teapot and cups out, and by this time, Zhao Qi had recovered. He gave a disdainful glance and naturally didn’t use them.

"Just drinking tea is boring. Don’t you have any pastries?"

Zhao Xuanyou disliked sweet and greasy things the most, so there really were no pastries in the house.

Yu Ying respectfully asked, "What would Your Highness like to eat?"

"Do you have whatever I want?"

"Since the young master doesn’t like pastries, nothing is prepared in the house. If Your Highness wants something, this servant will prepare it later."

Yu Ying’s tone was always gentle, showing neither panic from the reprimand nor the slightest disrespect.

On the contrary, she kept her eyes on Zhao Qi, her gaze full of humility.

Sun Qianran, sitting under the corridor, lightly played with her fan.

She knew Yu Ying didn’t need her help.

Her husband was indeed better at judging people. Whether it was Zhao Xuanyou or Zhao Qi, no matter how overwhelming their power was, Yu Ying could handle them with ease.

"What? Nothing at all? Not even eight-treasure cakes? How boring." As soon as Zhao Qi finished speaking, a commotion suddenly came from outside the courtyard.

Everyone in the courtyard looked toward the sound and saw a group of palace attendants surrounding two beautiful and charming girls who had arrived at the courtyard gate.

The two girls were dressed in magnificent clothes made of brocade silk, their robes embroidered with intricate patterns. Gold hairpins adorned their high, elaborate hairstyles, and every movement they made exuded nobility.

"Oh, this courtyard is so remote, yet it’s so lively." One of the girls in red glanced indifferently at the courtyard, her lips curling into a slight smile.

"Isn’t it? Who lives here? How come Seventh Brother is here?"

Yu Ying didn’t recognize them, but hearing the address "Seventh Brother," she knew they were the two princesses favored by the Emperor.

"Your Highnesses, Princess Yi’an and Princess Yi’ning." Sun Qianran greeted them.

Zhao Qi, seeing the two princesses, still had an indifferent attitude and coldly said, "What does it matter to you where I am?"

Princess Yi’ning and Princess Yi’an were not close to this unruly younger brother. Knowing his temper, they didn’t get angry at his attitude.

After all, Zhao Qi didn’t even give face to the Empress. Apart from the Emperor, he feared no one.

Of course, they didn’t want to pay attention to Zhao Qi either.

Princess Yi’an walked into the courtyard, her gaze passing over Zhao Qi and falling on Sun Qianran. "No need for formalities."

"Thank you, Your Highness."

"How do the palace servants do their work? How could they place Sister Qianran in such a remote place?" Sun Qianran was the pearl of the Prime Minister’s mansion. Every time she entered the palace, the Empress treated her very kindly. Naturally, the princesses were also very polite to her.

"I’ve always preferred quiet places. Living here is just fine."

Princess Yi’ning had just been snapped at by Zhao Qi. After entering the courtyard, she looked around, and her gaze fell on Yu Ying.

What a striking maid... She looked somewhat familiar.

She was indeed curious why Zhao Qi was staying in this courtyard. Seeing Yu Ying standing behind Zhao Qi, she couldn’t help but wonder. Had Zhao Qi come because of that beautiful maid?

That couldn’t be. Zhao Qi was still so young, just a bratty kid. Had he already developed such desires?

Feeling the princess’s gaze on her, Yu Ying bowed her head even lower, but she was also curious; she wondered which princess Cui Yichu was a companion reader for.

Princess Yi’an said, "Seventh Brother, this courtyard is full of women, and Sister Qianran is still recovering from illness. You really shouldn’t be making a racket here."

"Hmph," Zhao Qi sneered upon hearing this, "It’s none of her business. I didn’t come to find her."

"Then who are you looking for?" Princess Yi’ning’s gaze fell on Yu Ying again, carefully sizing her up. The more she looked, the more familiar she seemed.

"Father Emperor ordered Zhao Xuanyou to teach me martial arts. I’m looking for Zhao Xuanyou. It’s by imperial decree. Understand? Don’t block my way."

Looking for Zhao Xuanyou?

Princess Yi’ning’s eyes flickered, and she glanced at Princess Yi’an beside her. Seeing that Princess Yi’an didn’t speak, she leisurely said, "Don’t you know that Lord Zhao has accompanied Father Emperor to the hunting grounds? I just heard from Mother Empress that Father Emperor will have dinner at the hunting grounds before returning to the palace. Don’t waste your time here."

Zhao Qi indeed didn’t know where Zhao Xuanyou had gone.

He had come here only to vent his frustration on Zhao Xuanyou. Confirming that Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t be back for a while, even bullying a maid seemed pointless.

"Showing off stinks!" With that, Zhao Qi left without looking back.

Watching this troublemaker leave, Yu Ying sighed in relief.

"Seventh Brother is unruly. He’s made Sister Qianran laugh."

"How could that be?" The princesses were Zhao Qi’s own family. No matter how they argued among themselves, no one else dared to criticize them. Sun Qianran respectfully said, "The Seventh Prince is just being true to his nature as a young man."

After a pause, Sun Qianran said, "I brought a lot of tea from the mansion. Would the two princesses be willing to try some?"

"There’s no need for tea," Princess Yi’an said with a slight smile. "We two just came out for a casual stroll. We only came here because we saw Seventh Brother causing trouble."

As she spoke, Princess Yi’an took Princess Yi’ning’s arm and walked out of the courtyard.

"Respectfully seeing off the two princesses." Sun Qianran stood up and bowed. Yu Ying, along with the other maids in the courtyard, knelt down.

The two princesses had walked a good distance when Princess Yi’ning pulled her hand out of Princess Yi’an’s arm, her expression cooling slightly.

"Sister deliberately brought me here because you knew Zhao Xuanyou lives there."

Princess Yi’an’s thoughts had been seen through by her sister. Her gaze flickered, and she acted as if nothing was wrong. "So what if I did? What if I didn’t? It doesn’t harm you. Besides, you’d be bored staying in the palace anyway."

"If Sister had told me the truth earlier, I would have saved Sister the trouble of this trip."

Hearing the sarcasm in Princess Yi’ning’s voice, Princess Yi’an didn’t refute her. She walked forward with light steps.

Princess Yi’ning pondered for a moment. Seeing that Princess Yi’an had walked far ahead, she quickly caught up, her face breaking into a smile. "Sister has always been very particular. Mother Empress has looked through all the noble families and new officials in the capital for you, but none have caught your eye. How come you’ve taken a fancy to someone discarded by Cui Yichu?"

Seeing the discord between the two princesses, the surrounding palace attendants tactfully stepped back a bit.

"Hmph," Princess Yi’an said, as if she had heard something amusing. She turned her head to look at her sister. "You don’t know the full story of Cui Yichu’s scandal, but you’ve always been clever. You should be able to guess most of it."

"She wanted to be the Crown Princess, so she seduced the Crown Prince and angered Mother Empress."

Princess Yi’an slightly raised her chin, neither confirming nor denying.

"Could there be more to it?"

"In any case, Zhao Xuanyou is not the one discarded by Cui Yichu. On the contrary, it was he who discarded Cui Yichu."

chapters.title: Righteous Fury for a Beauty
chapters.content:
Cui Yichu was Princess Yi’an’s study companion, so naturally, Princess Yi’an knew better than anyone else why her mother had banished her from the palace.

But since Cui Yichu’s disgrace was a palace secret, those outside knew nothing of it.

"So what?" Princess Yining slightly raised her eyebrows. "Whether Cui Yichu looks down on Zhao Xuanyou or Zhao Xuanyou looks down on Cui Yichu, in others’ eyes, they are merely separated by mutual consent. Sister, you are so noble. Do you really intend to marry a man who has already been married?"

"And what of it?" Princess Yi’an was unimpressed. "Emperors of past dynasties have even married widows as empresses. What’s wrong with me marrying a man who has been married before? I’d rather choose a capable minister like Zhao Xuanyou than marry some useless man who has never been married."

Princess Yining fell silent for a moment, then looked at her elder sister.

The emperor had only two daughters, and rarity lent them value. The respect they received in the palace was no less than that given to the princes.

Neither of them was born of the empress, but Princess Yi’an had always been favored by the empress and could outshine her in everything.

Seeing Princess Yi’an’s resolute expression, Princess Yining couldn’t help but frown.

"I may not know Zhao Xuanyou well, but he has led troops outside for many years and must have some real ability. But have you considered, Sister? Mother has spent a great deal of effort on your marriage. If you end up choosing Zhao Xuanyou, won’t that displease her?"

Princess Yi’an turned her head and gave a light laugh. "It seems, little sister, you don’t understand Mother’s intentions at all."

She reached out and took Princess Yining’s hand. The two sisters walked forward slowly, their voices dropping to a whisper.

"You must know, when I truly take Zhao Xuanyou as my husband, Mother will be very pleased."

Pleased?

Princess Yining frowned slightly, then gradually understood.

Though she was a woman, she had grown up in the imperial family and had some knowledge of court affairs.

In recent years, Father Emperor had repeatedly reprimanded the Crown Prince, and many officials had submitted memorials impeaching him. Mother had been greatly troubled by this and had secretly been recruiting officials to rally around the Crown Prince.

The Marquis of Jingyuan’s mansion was part of the imperial clan and held hereditary military power.

Zhao Xuanyou was the commander of the Mingchuan Guard. Recently, he had also gained Father Emperor’s favor, not only serving in the Secretariat but also accompanying the emperor to the summer palace, where he was teaching the Seventh Prince martial arts.

If Princess Yi’an married Zhao Xuanyou, given her close relationship with the empress, Zhao Xuanyou would surely become a powerful sword in the Crown Prince’s hands.

When the Crown Prince ascended the throne, Zhao Xuanyou would be rewarded for his merits, and Princess Yi’an’s honor would not be any less than it was now.

Princess Yining looked up at her sister beside her; her skin was as delicate as fine porcelain, her face as radiant as spring blossoms, and her mind as sharp as a jewel. Listening to the faint sound of the flowing stream, Princess Yining sighed softly in her heart.

Over the years, she had always been overshadowed by her sister, and it was not without reason.

---

The moon hung high in the sky when Zhao Xuanyou finally returned, stepping in the moonlight.

As soon as he entered the courtyard and saw the table and chairs placed at the entrance, he couldn’t help but frown, wondering what kind of trick Yu Wan was playing this time.

He tossed his bow and arrows to Yuan Qing and headed straight into the house.

A lamp was lit inside. Yu Wan lay motionless on the couch.

Zhao Xuanyou thought something was wrong with her and quickly stepped forward. Before he could check, Yu Wan turned her head and saw him.

"You’re back, my lord."

Hearing her usual sweet and soft voice, the worry in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes vanished instantly. He walked to the edge of the couch and sat down.

"You don’t even come to greet me when I return? Why are you lying here?"

His tone was displeased. Yu Wan explained softly, "This servant didn’t mean to neglect you. You left too quickly. By the time I wanted to get up, it was already too late."

Zhao Xuanyou detected a hint of grievance in her voice. Narrowing his eyes, he asked, "What’s wrong with you?"

"Nothing much… just my back hurts."

Back pain?

Zhao Xuanyou’s mind flashed back to what he had made Yu Wan do last night. It had been strenuous, but he hadn’t lost control; it shouldn’t have been so bad that she couldn’t move.

Thinking he was the one who had started it, Zhao Xuanyou didn’t want to dig deeper.

"Here?" He reached out and pressed on Yu Wan’s back.

Yu Wan let out a loud "wah" and cried, "There! That’s the spot that hurts!"

Zhao Xuanyou hummed, his expression showing a hint of disdain, but he gently pressed on the nearby acupoints for her.

He wasn’t a doctor, but years in the military had given him considerable knowledge of injuries from falls and bruises.

What they had done last night shouldn’t have caused such severe pain.

"Exactly how did you get injured?" he finally asked.

"After I moved the table outside, I felt my back give out. I endured it for a while during the day, but by evening, I couldn’t straighten up at all. At first, it just hurt, but later, it stopped hurting; I just couldn’t feel my waist anymore."

Zhao Xuanyou was surprised. "You moved that table in the courtyard by yourself?"

"Mm."

"Alone?"

"Mm."

Zhao Xuanyou listened to this nonsensical explanation, then got up and took a jar of ointment for external injuries from the cabinet.

He lifted Yu Wan’s top and applied the ointment to her smooth, fair back, pressing on the nearby acupoints again.

Yu Wan’s skin was as white as snow, her flesh as soft as congealed fat. As Zhao Xuanyou slowly pressed, the masculine aura around him subtly grew stronger.

Feeling certain muscles in his body tense, Zhao Xuanyou coughed lightly and did his best to suppress his reactions, focusing on pressing her acupoints.

Yu Wan, while enduring the pain, also felt it improving; her previously numb waist finally regained some sensation.

"Thank you, my lord." Yu Wan’s eyes welled up with tears from the pain.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her lying there, crying. Her usually charming and graceful features now looked like a pear blossom in the rain, pitiful and helpless.

He had been feeling sorry for her, but then he remembered she had inexplicably moved the table and hurt her back, which made him a little angry.

"What possessed you to move that table? Even if you had to, couldn’t you have called for help?"

Wasn’t she supposed to be clever and quick-witted?

"Madame Pei originally wanted to have the maids help, but the Seventh Prince wouldn’t allow it. I had no choice but to move it myself."

The Seventh Prince?

Zhao Xuanyou’s sword-like eyebrows suddenly knitted together. The hand pressing on the acupoints abruptly increased its force, causing Yu Wan to yelp in pain.

He came back to his senses and restrained his strength, slowly rubbing in the ointment.

"Did the Seventh Prince come by today?"

"He barged into the courtyard shouting your name. I told him you had gone hunting, and he said he would wait for you. Madame Pei heard him shouting and came out to help me, but she was mocked by the Seventh Prince."

"Was he looking for me?"

"He probably wanted to find you, but since I was the only one from the marquis’s mansion in the courtyard, the misfortune fell on me."

Zhao Xuanyou had witnessed Zhao Qi’s venomous tongue firsthand.

But...

"What does this have to do with the table?"

"The Seventh Prince said he wanted tea. I invited him inside, but he complained the room was too small. So I thought of moving the table outside. But he wouldn’t let Madame Pei’s maids help, so I had to move it myself."

As soon as Yu Wan finished speaking, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression darkened abruptly.

So it was Zhao Qi who had done this to her.

---

chapters.title: Slightly Tipsy
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou didn’t speak for a long time, and Yu Wan grew uneasy.

She secretly turned her head to look at him, only to find his eyes dark and terrifying.

Was he angry with her?

Yu Wan had injured her back, so naturally, she couldn’t attend to him tonight.

After some thought, Yu Wan said, "It was my fault for acting too rashly. Now that I think about it, the Seventh Prince only speaks harshly. If I hadn’t moved that table, I would have just endured more scolding; nothing as bad as hurting my back."

"Who’s blaming you?" Zhao Xuanyou put down the ointment, picked up Yu Wan, and flipped her over. "Lying on your stomach isn’t good for recovery. Lie down and don’t move."

With that, he went to wash up.

Today, the emperor had been in high spirits at the hunting ground. Zhao Xuanyou had accompanied him the entire time, killing two deer and a rabbit, working up a sweat.

When he returned to the inner room, he was still drying his hair with a towel.

He hadn’t put on his sleeping robe yet. The muscles of his chest and abdomen were distinctly defined. Yu Wan stared without blinking.

"You’ve seen it before." Zhao Xuanyou said, then put on his sleeping robe.

Yu Wan replied, "I have seen it, but I’ve never looked closely."

At night, it was always Zhao Xuanyou taking the lead. Sometimes he wanted to look at Yu Wan carefully, but Yu Wan never got the chance to look at him carefully.

Hearing her words, Zhao Xuanyou seemed to consider something. He lay down beside Yu Wan, facing her, as if intentionally letting her look her fill.

Yu Wan pursed her lips and pressed her hand firmly against his chest.

His muscles were firm and taut. Yu Wan felt as if she had touched a warm wall.

For a moment, she grew playful and lightly scraped her hand across his chest.

The candlelight in the room was dim. Yu Wan lay beside Zhao Xuanyou like a well-behaved, coquettish kitten, stretching out her claws to gently scratch her master.

Zhao Xuanyou was close to her, his gaze fixed intently on her.

From the corners of her eyes and eyebrows, to her delicate nose and red lips, and then to her fair, tender collarbones.

"My lord, did you have a good hunt today?"

"Of course."

"Did you catch the most?"

Facing her misty gaze, Zhao Xuanyou’s heartbeat suddenly quickened.

Tonight, at the hunting ground, he had drunk a lot of fine wine with the emperor and eaten roasted deer and rabbit meat. Looking at Yu Wan before him, he felt his blood gradually heat up, and the hunting instincts aroused on the field became clearer and clearer.

He could clearly feel his breath scorching.

"That’s enough. Go to sleep." Zhao Xuanyou’s Adam’s apple rolled, and he suddenly swatted away Yu Wan’s hand.

His voice was unusually hoarse, clearly restraining something.

Yu Wan naturally noticed his change.

Tonight, with her back injured, she didn’t dare to act boldly, so she stopped teasing him.

"Alright, this servant is indeed sleepy."

"Where’s your nightgown?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"It’s in the cabinet. Actually, I can just sleep like this."

Zhao Xuanyou muttered a low "No," got up, and fetched her nightgown from the cabinet. Facing her snow-white, translucent skin, he restrained his desires and helped her change.

After laying Yu Wan down, he looked at her neat bun, then removed the jade hairpin, letting her long black hair loose. Finally, he took off her earrings before reaching out to extinguish the candle.

This was probably the first time he had done these things, and to his surprise, he did them quite skillfully.

Yu Wan curved the corners of her lips and obediently closed her eyes to sleep.

That night, though they shared the same bed, they maintained a rare distance.

The next morning, Zhao Xuanyou got up first and went out.

He went to the kitchen to fetch water but encountered Pei Tao in the courtyard.

"Worldly Son," Pei Tao saw him carrying water and, recalling what his wife Sun Biyan had said last night, suddenly understood something. "I heard from my wife that Miss Yu Wan moved something heavy yesterday. Did she get injured?"

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t really want to deal with Pei Tao, but besides Yu Wan, he only had Yuan Qing and Yuan Zuan around.

During the day, when Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t there, someone had to take care of Yu Wan’s meals, water, and trips to the outhouse.

Yuan Qing and Yuan Zuan were reliable, but they were men. He didn’t want to leave Yu Wan in their care.

"She strained her back, but fortunately, it’s not serious. Lying in bed for a couple of days should take care of it."

"Oh." Pei Tao was a zhuangyuan (top scholar), the cream of the literary world, and immediately understood why Zhao Xuanyou had softened his attitude. "My wife and Miss Yu Wan have always gotten along well. During the day, she will arrange for a maid to take care of her. You need not worry, Worldly Son."

"Thank you." Zhao Xuanyou was brief, then carried the water into the house.

Yu Wan had also woken up but found that even the slightest movement of her waist caused severe pain, so she could only lie still on the couch.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou enter with water, she thought he would wash his own face, but instead, he wrung out a towel and began wiping her face.

Yu Wan suddenly felt a little disoriented.

When she was young, her mother had taken care of her, wiping her face every day. She hadn’t expected that Zhao Xuanyou would be the second person, after her mother, to do this for her.

Thinking of her mother, Yu Wan’s eyes couldn’t help but moisten.

Even though she said she could wait three or five years, how she longed for her mother to wake up immediately.

"Why are you crying just from having your face wiped?" Zhao Xuanyou’s voice pulled Yu Wan back from her thoughts. She rearranged her smile and softly said, "Thank you, Worldly Son."

Facing Yu Wan’s grateful gaze, Zhao Xuanyou casually said, "During the day when I’m not here, Madame Pei will arrange for a maid to take care of you. You need to rest now. Don’t move around recklessly."

"This servant understands."

Zhao Xuanyou personally brought breakfast over. He didn’t feed Yu Wan but placed a steamed bun and a mantou within her reach.

Yu Wan picked them up and ate by herself. He helped Yu Wan wipe her hands, then gave her a cup of water before changing into his official robes and leaving.

The room hadn’t been quiet for long when a knock sounded at the door.

"Miss Yu Wan, may I come in now?"

"Madame Pei, please enter."

Sun Biyan led a maid into the room. Seeing Yu Wan lying on the couch, unable to move, she immediately felt guilty. "The Seventh Prince is so mischievous. It was my fault yesterday. I should have stopped him from causing trouble earlier."

"Madame Pei already helped this servant a lot yesterday. It was my own fault for being too rash and trying to show off by carrying the table."

Recalling the scene of Yu Wan carrying the table out yesterday, Sun Biyan still felt a lingering fear.

"That table is so heavy, even eunuchs need two or three people to carry it. You actually carried it out by yourself."

"It was just a moment of recklessness."

Yu Wan felt a little embarrassed.

Over the past two years, she had been doing light chores in the marquis’s mansion, and her strength had diminished a lot.

Back in the village, carrying a table would have been nothing.

"This is my maid, Xiang Xu. Today, she will stay here to take care of you. Feel free to give her any orders."

"Sister Xiang Xu, thank you for your trouble."

"You’re welcome, Miss Yu Wan." Xiang Xu had been by Sun Biyan’s side and had become familiar with Yu Wan over the past two days.

Sun Biyan said, "You should rest well. I’ve already ordered the cook to make a pot of bone broth for you today to help you recover."

Whether she was acting out of ulterior motives or genuine kindness, at this moment, her willingness to take care of Yu Wan was indeed a great help.

"Thank you, Madame Pei."

---

While Yu Wan quietly rested, tension was rising between Zhao Xuanyou and the Seventh Prince, Zhao Qi, at the training grounds.

chapters.title: Taking Personal Revenge
chapters.content:
Looking at Zhao Xuanyou’s dark, gloomy eyes, Zhao Qi felt quite pleased with himself.

He knew Zhao Xuanyou had already found out about yesterday’s incident.

To be honest, that beautiful maid from the Marquis’s mansion, soft on the outside but sharp within, had made him very unhappy. He had been so angry when he returned to the palace yesterday that he barely ate a bite.

Now that Zhao Xuanyou looked unhappy, Zhao Qi felt delighted again.

Zhao Qi lifted his chin, looking at Zhao Xuanyou in his dark brocade robe, his tone filled with disdain. "Zhao Xuanyou, Father Emperor ordered you to teach me martial arts. You stand there like a wooden stake, not saying a word for half a day. Are you going to teach me or not?"

Zhao Xuanyou said in a deep voice, "Once Your Highness has held the horse stance for a full hour, this subject will begin teaching martial arts."

"A full hour of horse stance?" Zhao Qi sneered. "Are you trying to exhaust me to death?"

At first, when Zhao Qi started learning martial arts from Zhao Xuanyou, he didn’t feel much resistance.

After all, Zhao Xuanyou was a thorn in Crown Prince Zhao Zun’s eye. Following the principle that the enemy of my enemy is my friend, Zhao Qi even found Zhao Xuanyou quite interesting.

But Zhao Xuanyou refused to teach him any real martial arts. He only made him stand in postures or hold the horse stance.

Zhao Qi had protested repeatedly, but Zhao Xuanyou ignored him every time, which infuriated him.

Zhao Xuanyou said, "This subject has been ordered by His Majesty to teach Your Highness martial arts. How to teach is this subject’s business. Your Highness only needs to follow instructions without question."

"If you’re going to teach, then teach! Why must you make me hold the horse stance? I already knew how to do that when I was five. Do I need you to teach me?"

The reason Zhao Qi acted so arrogantly was not only because, as the youngest son, he was especially doted on by the Emperor, but also for another important reason.

His late mother, the Benevolent Noble Consort, was a fierce tigeress from a military family. His maternal grandfather and uncle guarded the southern borders, holding military power just like the Marquis of Jingyuan.

It was rumored that Zhao Qi had several shadow guards by his side whose skills were not inferior to the imperial guards. They had been personally trained by his maternal grandfather, the Duke of Ning, to protect him.

"Previously, this subject had heard that the Duke of Ning personally taught Your Highness martial arts. It seems the rumors were false."

"What did you say?" Zhao Qi coldly laughed. "Compared to my grandfather, who do you think you are? Do you think your kung fu is that good?"

"This subject has indeed never crossed hands with the Duke of Ning, but this subject’s martial arts are more than enough to teach Your Highness."

"I don’t need to kill with my own hands."

Zhao Qi’s eyes suddenly sharpened. Of course, he knew he couldn’t defeat Zhao Xuanyou in a fight.

But he was confident that the people around him could deal with Zhao Xuanyou.

Damn Zhao Xuanyou. The Emperor had only casually mentioned teaching martial arts; it was just for show.

As a royal prince, did he need to train as hard as a guard?

As a master, it was enough to have capable subordinates. Why bother doing things himself?

If Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t take a hint, he couldn’t blame him for being ruthless.

"Yin Ping, Mu Di, take him down for me!"

As soon as Zhao Qi spoke, two guards in tight-fitting clothes leaped out from behind him.

He looked at Zhao Xuanyou smugly. "Don’t kill him. Father Emperor would be angry. Just make him kneel and admit his mistake."

"Yes."

The two guards, upon hearing the order, stood on either side of Zhao Xuanyou.

The Duke of Ning was a renowned war hero with extraordinary martial arts. The assassins he personally trained were not to be underestimated.

Yin Ping and Mu Di, having received their orders, instantly attacked Zhao Xuanyou. The wind whistled past his ears as he swiftly moved, gliding more than a dozen steps away.

Zhao Xuanyou would not underestimate his opponents, nor did he need to.

In the blink of an eye, Zhao Qi, who had been smug just moments ago, found himself under Zhao Xuanyou’s control, stunned into silence.

"Master!" Yin Ping and Mu Di abruptly stopped, their faces instantly draining of color.

Their original mission was to protect Zhao Qi. Now that Zhao Qi’s life was in danger, it was their failure.

Who could have imagined that someone would dare to attack a prince directly in the imperial training grounds?

"Zhao Xuanyou, let go of His Highness immediately!" Yin Ping shouted angrily.

Zhao Xuanyou’s hand was around Zhao Qi’s neck. He raised an eyebrow at Yin Ping and Mu Di.

"I have been ordered by His Majesty to teach His Highness self-defense. Unrelated personnel should step back immediately, or I will certainly report to His Majesty who is obstructing His Highness’s training."

He spoke lightly, but his index finger tightened slightly, pressing down on Zhao Qi’s neck.

Zhao Qi’s throat was constricted, unable to utter a single word.

Yin Ping and Mu Di were both experts. They knew Zhao Qi’s life was hanging by a thread in Zhao Xuanyou’s grip.

They didn’t dare move again, only standing silently to the side, watching Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Qi closely, waiting for another chance to rescue him.

Zhao Xuanyou said indifferently, "Didn’t Your Highness say he learned the horse stance at five? Try it."

Zhao Qi, with his neck nearly choked, was in no mood to hold the horse stance.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t mind. He lifted his foot and kicked Zhao Qi a few times, each kick landing on his knees.

Having been pampered and raised in luxury since childhood, when had he ever endured such hardship?

But with Zhao Xuanyou’s hand around his neck, he couldn’t even cry out in pain. His face just turned red.

"Zhao Xuanyou, have you lost your mind? How dare you treat His Highness like this!" Yin Ping angrily shouted. "Aren’t you afraid of His Majesty’s wrath?"

"I am only making His Highness hold a horse stance. Why would His Majesty be furious?" Zhao Xuanyou coldly laughed. "Looking at you two, you seem to have been by His Highness’s side since you were young. The Duke of Ning originally wanted to pass on all his martial arts to His Highness, but unfortunately, he doted on his grandson too much; he couldn’t bear to make him stand in postures or hold the horse stance, so he ended up teaching you two instead."

Although he hadn’t truly exchanged blows with them, he could see that Yin Ping and Mu Di had impressive martial arts. If he were to truly face them both, he wouldn’t easily win.

That was why he had captured the king first; directly taking Zhao Qi.

Yin Ping and Mu Di were about the same age as Zhao Qi. Originally, the Duke of Ning had selected them to be Zhao Qi’s sparring partners. Unfortunately, Zhao Qi couldn’t endure hardship. As a child, he would cry and throw tantrums, and the Duke of Ning, thinking of his late daughter, ultimately couldn’t bring himself to be strict. Thus, Zhao Qi’s martial arts had no solid foundation; he had only learned some flashy moves.

Yin Ping and Mu Di listened to Zhao Xuanyou’s words and naturally understood that he was right.

"Understood? Then get out of here. Don’t obstruct me from teaching His Highness self-defense."

With the Emperor’s decree above all, and Zhao Qi in Zhao Xuanyou’s hands, Yin Ping and Mu Di had no choice but to silently retreat to a distance.

Zhao Qi had originally hoped that the two guards would save him, but to his surprise, they were dismissed with just a few words from Zhao Xuanyou. He was so angry his eyes nearly popped out.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes were stormy as he stood to the side, his figure as steady as a mountain.

He slightly loosened his grip on Zhao Qi’s neck, allowing him to catch his breath.

"Zhao Xuanyou!" Zhao Qi was furious. "You’re being insolent! Just you wait. I will have you flayed alive!"

"Is that so?" Zhao Xuanyou said coldly, lifting his foot to kick him a few more times. "Your horse stance isn’t quite right."

"You bastard!" Zhao Qi cursed angrily as he was forced to hold the horse stance. "Do you think I’ll let you off?"

He truly hadn’t expected Zhao Xuanyou to treat the Emperor’s casual order like a sacred decree and actually dare to lay hands on him.

"What’s the rush? After you hold this horse stance for a full hour, you’ll have a chance to get your revenge."

Zhao Xuanyou slightly bent his elbow, pressing Zhao Qi’s neck to keep his upper body straight.

At that moment, he also gave Zhao Qi’s waist a not-too-light, not-too-heavy strike with his other hand.

Yu Yuan had been bedridden for two days because of her waist injury. Zhao Qi should at least be bedridden for a few days as well.

---

chapters.title: The Provocation
chapters.content:
The commotion in the training grounds quickly attracted onlookers.

The first to arrive was the Sixth Prince, Zhao Yu, who had been practicing archery on the other side of the training grounds.

Watching his usually rebellious youngest brother being choked by Zhao Xuanyou and forced to hold the horse stance, Zhao Yu’s eyes gleamed with schadenfreude as he commented from the side.

"Lord Zhao, the Seventh Prince’s palms aren’t facing downward."

Zhao Xuanyou said, "Seventh Highness, the palms must face downward."

"I don’t want to face them down…" Zhao Xuanyou’s fingers slightly moved, and Zhao Qi let out half a scream before falling silent.

The Sixth Prince watched excitedly, then pretended to seriously circle around Zhao Qi. "His feet aren’t spread wide enough. No matter what, they should be at least shoulder-width apart to train leg strength."

This time, Zhao Xuanyou didn’t give Zhao Qi a chance to protest. He lifted his foot and kicked left and right, forcing Zhao Qi’s legs apart.

Zhao Qi winced in pain, and his legs instinctively softened, but Zhao Xuanyou forcibly held him up.

His expression was calm, his voice low. "The Sixth Highness came to laugh at the Seventh Highness. Soon, there will be more onlookers. The Duke of Ning is a renowned war hero with unparalleled martial arts, so naturally, no one doubts him. It is said that the Benevolent Noble Consort was also extraordinarily skilled, having once subdued an assassin who attempted to kill His Majesty. If others see that His Highness can’t even hold a proper horse stance, I’m afraid the joke today won’t be limited to His Highness alone."

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou mention the Benevolent Noble Consort, Zhao Qi’s gaze suddenly trembled.

Zhao Xuanyou had led troops for many years. In the military, there were plenty of young, hot-blooded rebels who refused to obey orders. He knew exactly how to handle them.

With just a few words, Zhao Qi’s expression changed.

Zhao Xuanyou knew the provocation had worked. He loosened his grip on Zhao Qi’s neck.

As expected, even after he let go, Zhao Qi maintained the horse stance.

The Sixth Prince had originally thought that, given Zhao Qi’s usual temper, the moment Zhao Xuanyou released him, he would call his two highly skilled guards over to teach Zhao Xuanyou a lesson.

Even if he didn’t dare to kill Zhao Xuanyou out of respect for the Emperor’s authority, he would at least curse him out.

Unexpectedly, Zhao Qi remained obediently in the horse stance even after being choked.

Looking at his eyes, he seemed quite serious.

"Sixth Brother, what’s going on?" Life in the imperial palace was idle and boring. When Princess Yining heard the palace servants talk about the excitement at the training grounds, she immediately came over. Walking up to the Sixth Prince, she asked casually.

The Sixth Prince said, "Lord Zhao made the Seventh Brother hold the horse stance. The Seventh Brother refused to obey, so Lord Zhao choked his neck to make him stand properly. Look how obedient the Seventh Brother is now."

Earlier, when Princess Yining heard that Zhao Xuanyou had choked Zhao Qi to force him to train, she found it hard to believe. Now, hearing the Sixth Prince say this, she couldn’t help but ask, "You saw it with your own eyes?"

"Of course. You arrived too late and missed the biggest spectacle."

Princess Yining looked at Zhao Xuanyou in surprise.

She had seen Zhao Xuanyou a few times from a distance. At those times, Zhao Xuanyou had been wearing official robes, exuding a dignified and imposing manner.

Now, Zhao Xuanyou was dressed in a simple raven-black robe. Because the fabric was thin and tailored to fit his body, it outlined his tall and straight figure.

In terms of appearance alone, Zhao Xuanyou could truly be called a dragon among men.

"Sixth Brother and Sister, what are you watching?" Princess Yian’s voice came from behind.

Princess Yining withdrew her gaze, glancing at Yian. Seeing the meaningful smile on her face, she knew Yian had misunderstood, but she only smiled and said, "Sister, you arrived too late. You missed the scene where the Seventh Brother was choked by Lord Zhao."

"It’s not too late to miss it." Princess Yian said with a faint smile, her gaze steadily on Zhao Xuanyou.

She had taken a fancy to Zhao Xuanyou. As long as Zhao Xuanyou was still standing here, it wasn’t too late for her.

The Sixth Prince didn’t understand what the two sisters were getting at. He smiled and agreed, "That’s true. In the past, the Seventh Brother couldn’t succeed in scholarship or martial arts. It’s rare to see him seriously holding the horse stance. Speaking of which, his martial arts were taught by the Duke of Ning. I don’t know if the Duke of Ning’s reputation is just empty fame."

His words were harsh. Zhao Xuanyou watched as Zhao Qi’s expression tensed, then suddenly tapped the flat of his sword lightly on Zhao Qi’s shoulder.
