"Even if Your Highness curses him back now, it won’t change the Sixth Highness’s and others’ opinions. Only when your kung fu surpasses his will he shut his mouth."

Zhao Xuanyou had tested Zhao Qi’s skills a couple of days ago.

All show, a complete mess.

But the Duke of Ning had trained him for five or six years. Although he couldn’t bring himself to make Zhao Qi build a solid foundation, he had indeed passed down all his family’s spear techniques to him.

Zhao Qi refused to train seriously, but he had a good memory and remembered every move clearly.

If he were willing to start training properly from the beginning, he would surely achieve twice the result with half the effort.

Princess Yian suddenly stepped forward at this moment. Her eyes were fixed on Zhao Xuanyou, but she had a look of wanting to speak yet hesitating.

Although she was a proud princess, this was the first time in her life she had shown affection for a man, and she couldn’t help but feel a little shy.

"Lord Zhao." Princess Yining stepped forward from behind, smiling at Zhao Xuanyou. "No wonder Father Emperor ordered you to teach the Seventh Brother martial arts. You truly have a way. No matter how unruly the Seventh Brother is, you can train him to be obedient."

Hearing Princess Yining say what she herself had wanted to say, Princess Yian was naturally displeased and shot her a cold glance.

Princess Yining didn’t mind and continued to smile sweetly.

"Your Highnesses," Zhao Xuanyou cupped his fists in greeting before saying slowly, "The princesses overpraise me. The Seventh Highness has always seriously followed my teachings in martial arts. I have no special methods."

"Seriously followed?" The Sixth Prince was surprised and walked up to Zhao Xuanyou, pointing at Zhao Qi, who was seriously holding the horse stance. "You were just choking his neck!"

"Your Highness," Zhao Xuanyou greeted the Sixth Prince before calmly saying, "This subject was just teaching the Seventh Highness some self-defense techniques, showing him how to escape if he is ever held hostage. I suppose Your Highness misunderstood."

Self-defense techniques?

At these words, Princess Yining and the Sixth Prince were both stunned.

Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Qi had clearly had a huge conflict, publicly choking Zhao Qi in the training grounds. Such a major incident, once it spread to Princesses Yian and Yining’s ears, would naturally spread to the ears of all the masters in the imperial palace.

It was just that, due to their status, they couldn’t come to the training grounds to watch the commotion.

Assaulting a prince was a serious crime. Zhao Xuanyou would certainly have to give everyone an explanation.

The Sixth Prince and the others had come to watch the excitement, not just to see Zhao Qi’s predicament, but also Zhao Xuanyou’s.

Clearly, "teaching self-defense techniques" was a flawless excuse.

Princess Yian, who had been silent all along, looked at Zhao Xuanyou with even greater admiration.

The man before her had an outstanding demeanor, a noble status, and at a young age, he already held great military power.

Although the Marquis of Jingyuan was a hereditary title, Zhao Xuanyou’s rise to his current position was not solely due to his family background.

There were many noble families in the capital, and many useless young masters.

The reason Zhao Xuanyou had won the Emperor’s favor was because of his exceptional martial arts and clever mind.

Her husband should indeed be a man like this.

chapters.title: Strike First
chapters.content:
"Ah, I see. Since Seventh Brother often goes out, he does indeed have more opportunities to encounter villains than others. It’s true that self-defense should be taught before martial arts."

Princess Yi’an smiled sweetly.

Compared to their last meeting at the Imperial Household Department in the palace, her demeanor was much gentler now, without a trace of princessly arrogance.

She had always been the Emperor’s favorite, and aside from the Crown Prince, her other siblings all thought she was spoiled by her favored status.

Yet now, her attitude toward Zhao Xuanyou was so different that even Princess Yi’ning, who knew the situation, was taken aback. Even the Sixth Prince noticed something amiss.

Princess Yi’ning remarked, "Master Zhao is truly impressive. Not only did he get Seventh Brother to obediently practice martial arts, but even my sister, who never praises anyone, can’t stop singing his praises."

The Sixth Prince narrowed his eyes, glancing at Zhao Xuanyou, then at Princess Yi’an.

To be honest, Zhao Xuanyou himself was flawless, but he had been married before. Could Princess Yi’an really take a fancy to him?

Zhao Xuanyou also caught the implication in Princess Yi’ning’s words. Surprised, he showed no reaction, merely cupping his hands in a bow to Princess Yi’an.

"Your Highness flatters me."

Princess Yi’an knew her sister was deliberately stirring trouble, so she reached out and pulled her along.

"Master Zhao is here under the Emperor’s orders to teach Seventh Brother martial arts. We shouldn’t linger here and delay his duties." Then, turning to the Sixth Prince, she added, "Sixth Brother, aren’t you supposed to be practicing archery? Stop crowding around. Otherwise, next time you accompany the Emperor on a hunt, you’ll come back empty-handed again."

The Sixth Prince winced at the jab but had no way to retort against his favored elder sister. Now that Zhao Qi had stopped making a scene and was seriously practicing his horse stance, there was indeed nothing interesting left to watch. He huffed and turned toward the archery range.

Princess Yi’an smiled at Zhao Xuanyou before pulling Princess Yi’ning away from the training grounds.

Zhao Xuanyou turned back and saw Zhao Qi, drenched in sweat, sneering at him.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you’re really something today. Everyone knows you’ve got me under your thumb."

"Your Highness is a noble prince. How could this subject possibly control you?" Zhao Xuanyou replied calmly, his expression indifferent.

"Hmph."

Though Zhao Qi was displeased, he maintained his perfect horse stance, not moving an inch.

Having been pampered since childhood, he had never suffered hardship; whether in the palace or outside, the Emperor doted on his youngest son, and the Duke of Ningguo adored his motherless grandson.

Even in Liu Chuan, where it was cooler than elsewhere, standing in a horse stance under the sun was no easy task.

Normally, Zhao Xuanyou should have let him progress gradually, slowly increasing the duration of the stance. But then he recalled Yu Wan, who had been bedridden the day before, unable to straighten her back.

His expression darkened. "The hour isn’t up yet, Your Highness. Don’t waste your breath talking."

"But Princess Yi’an has taken a liking to you," Zhao Qi refused to stay silent.

He had always been talkative, and even now, while holding the stance, having someone to chat with was better than suffering in silence.

Zhao Xuanyou took a sip of tea, then fed a cup to Zhao Qi.

"Princess Yi’an is the Emperor’s beloved treasure. How could she possibly take a fancy to this humble subject?"

"Who knows? Maybe her eyes are blind." Zhao Qi still spoke harshly, but his tone softened slightly. "But even if you’re nothing special, if you become her consort, I’d still pity you more."

"This subject reassures Your Highness; there’s no need to worry about the princess’s eyesight, nor about this subject’s well-being."

"I’d rather die than marry a woman like her."

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Zhao Qi. "Your Highness is young. For now, focusing on martial arts is what you should be concerned with."

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t engaging, Zhao Qi didn’t mind. He continued on his own, "Anyway, you’d better be careful. Once she sets her sights on something, she’ll do whatever it takes to get it. If she really has taken a fancy to you, she might go straight to the Emperor and request a marriage decree. By then, you won’t even have the chance to refuse."

A marriage decree?

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered.

Princess Yi’an’s attitude toward him today had indeed been unusually warm. If that were simply her nature, it would be fine, but when they had met in the palace before, she hadn’t been this gentle and refined.

It was obvious; her attitude toward him had changed.

Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t certain she had feelings for him, but Zhao Qi’s words had struck a chord.

Princess Yi’an was indeed the type to stop at nothing to get what she wanted.

Just like when they had both wanted that bolt of silk at the Imperial Household Department, once she had set her mind on it, even if Zhao Xuanyou had taken it first, she would still find a way to claim it.

If she truly had feelings for him, she might very well request a marriage decree from the Emperor.

Zhao Qi… had indeed warned him.

---

"Younger sister, what are you doing?" Princess Yi’ning, her wrist aching from being dragged by Princess Yi’an, wrenched her hand free as they left the training grounds.

Princess Yi’an stared coldly at her. "I should be the one asking you. What are you doing?"

"Elder sister admires Master Zhao, so I was helping you express your feelings."

"Do you think I need your help?"

Princess Yi’ning said, "Master Zhao is so outstanding. There must be no shortage of women around him. That maid in his courtyard last time was even more beautiful than the new concubines in the palace."

That maid?

Princess Yi’an couldn’t help but recall the maid Zhao Qi had bullied that day; delicate, soft, and movingly beautiful.

Seeing her elder sister lost in thought, Princess Yi’ning added, "I’ve always felt that maid looked familiar. Yesterday, it suddenly hit me; she looks a lot like Cui Yichu. Master Zhao keeps her by his side; perhaps he still hasn’t forgotten Cui Yichu."

Princess Yi’an frowned.

Zhao Xuanyou had decided to divorce Cui Yichu, so their marital affection was over. But that maid did indeed resemble Cui Yichu...

"So I think we should let Master Zhao know of elder sister’s feelings soon. Elder sister’s beauty and status far surpass Cui Yichu’s. Once Master Zhao understands elder sister’s intentions, he’ll naturally forget about Cui Yichu."

"Shut up!"

Princess Yi’an was proud, but both Cui Yichu and that maid were more beautiful than her.

Princess Yi’ning’s words were clearly mocking her.

"I’m warning you; stop meddling in my affairs. Otherwise, don’t blame me for disregarding our sisterly bond."

Hearing the threat in Princess Yi’an’s words, Princess Yi’ning snapped, "We’re both the Emperor’s daughters. What can you do to me? Just wait and see!"

With that, she stormed off in a huff.

Princess Yi’an watched her retreating figure, her own expression darkening.

Her younger sister had always loved competing with her for everything, yet she had never been able to win.

She knew exactly what Princess Yi’ning was thinking.

Earlier, Princess Yi’ning had mocked her for wanting to marry a man who had already been married. Now that she realized Zhao Xuanyou was no ordinary man, she couldn’t bear the thought of her elder sister securing such an outstanding man as her consort and was resorting to petty tricks to stir trouble.

Princess Yi’an didn’t take her seriously.

However, Princess Yi’ning had said one thing right; she should settle this matter soon.

Zhao Xuanyou might still have feelings for Cui Yichu. He was currently in high favor with the Emperor, and countless noble families were taking notice of him. If she delayed, his grandmother might arrange another marriage for him, and then she would have no recourse.

With the Emperor and Empress both in the imperial villa, she needed to strike first.

Princess Yi’an made up her mind and immediately headed toward the Crystal Palace.

---

chapters.title: He Doesn’t Want To
chapters.content:
When Zhao Xuanyou returned to the small courtyard, the sky had already darkened.

Seeing the warm orange candlelight spilling from the house, he paused, standing at the gate and quietly gazing at that glow.

As a child, whenever he returned from martial arts training, Zhao Xuanyou would always run to his mother’s courtyard first.

From afar, the light in the house would fill him with a sense of security.

That glow meant he would find his gentle mother inside, along with a delicious meal.

And now, that same glow still waited for him inside.

Thinking of Yu Wan, Zhao Xuanyou’s exhaustion and irritation faded by half.

"Master Zhao, you must be tired. It’s already this late, and you’ve only just returned."

Pei Tao, dressed in a blue robe, pushed open the door and stepped out, spotting Zhao Xuanyou standing at the courtyard gate.

"Minister Pei." Zhao Xuanyou gave him a polite nod.

Ever since Zhao Xuanyou had asked Yu Wan to pass along a message, his attitude toward Pei Tao had softened from its previous resistance, though he still remained distant and polite, giving Pei Tao no opening to speak.

Well, cooperation required mutual willingness.

Pei Tao simply smiled at him before heading toward the kitchen.

Zhao Xuanyou strolled into the house, stepping past the screen at the entrance and into the inner room.

Yu Wan heard the footsteps and looked over, sweetly calling out, "Master, you’re back."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her. After lying in bed all day with a strained back, she still managed to smile so sweetly.

"Have you eaten?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"Yes, but has Master eaten? It’s so late. You haven’t had dinner yet, have you?"

The eunuchs delivered meals on time every day. Yu Wan, of course, hadn’t touched Zhao Xuanyou’s portion, but by now, it would have gone cold.

"I ate at the training grounds."

His reverse psychology had worked on Zhao Qi, who had practiced with unusual vigor that day.

The Emperor must have heard about the conflict between him and Zhao Qi, but since Zhao Qi had taken his training seriously afterward, the Emperor was likely pleased and had ordered a meal to be sent to the training grounds.

Though Zhao Qi had decided to train seriously, he still refused to eat with Zhao Xuanyou and left with his guards in a huff.

As a subject, Zhao Xuanyou naturally couldn’t refuse imperial generosity, so after enjoying the Emperor’s bestowed dinner alone at the training grounds, he had finally returned.

Though the imperial meal was exquisite, he would have preferred to come back and eat with Yu Wan.

"So it is."

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t say more and went straight to the side room.

Spending the whole day under the sun supervising Zhao Qi’s training had exhausted Zhao Qi, but Zhao Xuanyou had also sweated through his clothes.

After washing up, Zhao Xuanyou dried his hair as he walked back to the bed.

He hadn’t yet changed into his nightclothes, wearing only a silk trousers, revealing his lean, muscular frame.

His dark hair hung loosely around his shoulders, still damp.

Yu Wan couldn’t help but quietly admire him.

After drying his hair, Zhao Xuanyou lifted the thin blanket and sat down beside her. Without a word, he placed his hand on the warmest, softest part of her body and let out a satisfied "mm."

Yu Wan, with her strained back, couldn’t move, so she simply closed her eyes.

She could sense he had something on his mind.

Normally, when they were intimate, he would ignite her passion like wildfire.

But tonight, he seemed patient, only gently caressing her, torturing her with slow, deliberate movements.

"Master..." Yu Wan whispered.

"Don’t speak."

He interrupted her in a low voice, but his movements grew even gentler.

Yu Wan’s ears burned.

Did he even realize what he was doing?

Though they had been physically close for some time, he had always been the one to take the initiative, while she had always resisted; never needing to ask for more.

But now, he had kindled a flame in her heart, only to stoke it slowly, leaving her with an unbearable itch she couldn’t scratch.

How could she bring it up? Yu Wan’s face flushed crimson.

If she took the initiative, Zhao Xuanyou might not like it. If she urged him to be rougher, she might end up annoying him instead.

After much deliberation, Yu Wan decided to grit her teeth and endure.

"Are you this shy?"

Since they were so close, Zhao Xuanyou could feel the heat radiating from Yu Wan’s face. He couldn’t help but frown.

"When have I ever not been shy?" Yu Wan replied in a voice as soft as a mosquito’s buzz.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her awkward expression and assumed she was displeased. Instead, he withdrew his hand from under the blanket.

The two of them lay side by side once more, as separate as the night before.

Yu Wan let out a silent sigh of relief.

Being apart was better than the slow torture of his teasing.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t extinguish the candle. Yu Wan turned her head to look at him and saw him staring fixedly at the top of the canopy, lost in thought.

Recalling what Sun Qianran had mentioned at dinnertime, Yu Wan finally spoke up.

"This servant heard from Madame Pei that Master encountered some trouble today."

Zhao Xuanyou neither confirmed nor denied.

Yu Wan sighed. "That Seventh Prince is indeed difficult to deal with. Yesterday, when he barged in here in a rage, it was clear from his tone that he was dissatisfied with Master. Today’s training must not have gone smoothly."

Indeed, bad news traveled fast.

In just one day, the story of him grabbing Zhao Qi by the throat at the training grounds had spread throughout the imperial villa, even reaching Yu Wan, who was confined to her room.

He couldn’t help but let out a soft snort.

Yu Wan watched his relaxed expression. "It seems Master has already resolved the problem."

"That brat may be reckless, but he’s not much of a problem. Even if he were, it’s the Emperor’s problem, not mine."

Zhao Xuanyou was indeed troubled, but not by Zhao Qi; it was Princess Yi’an who weighed on his mind.

Yu Wan knew nothing about what had happened at the training grounds. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s indifference, she assumed there was nothing to worry about.

The room was bathed in warm candlelight.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the woman beside him, unable to look away.

He loved quietly watching Yu Wan in the candlelight.

Compared to her graceful and dazzling beauty during the day, the flickering light cast a hazy, dreamlike glow over her face, softening her already gentle features. When she spoke, her lashes trembled slightly, impossibly enchanting.

Noticing Zhao Xuanyou studying her, Yu Wan pressed her lips into a smile and nuzzled against his shoulder in a coquettish manner.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened slightly. He reached out and pulled her into his arms, letting her rest her head on his arm.

"Master, let’s go to sleep early."

Zhao Xuanyou responded with a soft "mm," then raised his hand and extinguished the candle with a flick of his palm.

The room fell silent. Soon, Yu Wan’s breathing became steady and even, but Zhao Xuanyou remained wide awake, his mind restless.

Before Yu Wan had entered Honghui Hall, Zhao Xuanyou had never imagined he would care so deeply for a maid.

Even when he had learned he and Yu Wan had been intimate, he had dismissed it as a twist of fate.

In his heart, he had believed he would only ever be devoted to one woman; his lawfully wedded wife.

They would be like his parents, deeply in love and harmonious, living in perfect marital bliss.

But Yu Wan’s appearance had shattered all his plans.

Though, at the root of it all, it was Cui Yichu’s fault; Yu Wan had been forced into the situation. But after divorcing Cui Yichu, he had a chance to start over.

If he wanted, he could, as his grandmother had suggested, seek to marry another noblewoman in the capital and live a proper life.

But... he didn’t want to.

chapters.title: Imperial Bestowal of Marriage
chapters.content:
When Zhao Qiji mentioned that Princess Yi'an had taken a liking to him, Zhao Xuanyou felt a strong resistance in his heart.

In that very moment, Zhao Xuanyou realized that his resistance was not just toward Princess Yi'an, but toward the very idea of taking a wife.

At present, he had no intention of marrying.

With Yu Ying by his side, he lived a comfortable life, and it would be fine to continue like this forever.

What his grandmother hoped for was nothing more than the continuation of the family line, and Yu Ying could bear children for her as well.

As for other duties that a wife would need to fulfill, since he would remain in the capital, there was no need to worry about them.

This would be fine.

Having made up his mind, Zhao Xuanyou turned to his side, kissed the forehead of the woman beside him, and finally fell asleep.

---

Deep into the night, in the Crystal Palace, three imperial concubines were still accompanying the Empress in a game of leaf cards.

"Hey, did I win this round?" the Empress said proudly.

"Congratulations, Mother Empress," Princess Yi'an stifled a yawn and smiled flatteringly, "Mother Empress's card skills are superb. This win is significant; all previous losses have been recovered."

"Congratulations, Your Majesty. Your Majesty's card skills are superb; this concubine is ashamed of her inferiority."

After dinner, the Empress had intended to play a few casual rounds of leaf cards with the three concubines to pass the time. However, her card skills were poor, and her luck tonight was bad, causing her to lose repeatedly.

She was naturally competitive and would not allow anyone to leave until she won. The three concubines, yawning repeatedly, finally let her win a round after deliberately losing.

"Tonight, with the three sisters' company, I have enjoyed myself greatly."

"It is this concubine's honor to accompany Your Majesty."

"It's getting late; all of you should go and rest."

Finally, when the Empress dismissed them, the three concubines felt as if they had been granted amnesty and hastily took their leave.

After they left, the Empress narrowed her phoenix-like eyes, revealing a suspicious expression, and coldly said, "Look at those cheap women, how distracted they were while playing leaf cards with me."

Princess Yi'an stood beside her, massaging her shoulders, and softly said, "It's because they have shallow eyes. It is their fortune to serve Mother Empress, yet they would rather serve Father Emperor, but Father Emperor does not summon them to attend his bed either."

The Empress let out a soft, amused snort and, supported by Princess Yi'an's hand, stood up and led her toward the bedroom.

"You are a clever child. It's a good thing you are a princess. If you were a concubine, I don't know how much trouble you would cause me."

Princess Yi'an's birth mother held a low rank, but as the Emperor's eldest daughter, she had been taken in and raised by the Empress shortly after her birth, who claimed to enjoy having both sons and daughters.

Although they were not biological mother and daughter, Princess Yi'an had received much guidance from the Empress, and their ways of doing things were very similar, making their relationship no different from that of a biological mother and daughter.

Entering the inner hall, the palace maids quickly brought calming tea.

After slowly drinking it, the Empress leaned against the soft pillow on the couch and slowly turned her gaze to Princess Yi'an.

"You rushed to the Crystal Palace and served me diligently all day. What is it that you truly want?"

Princess Yi'an smiled and sat down beside the Empress. "This child indeed has a request to make of Mother Empress."

The Empress's eyes flickered slightly.

Neither of the two princesses was her biological daughter, but relatively speaking, she did favor Princess Yi'an, whom she had raised herself.

Looking at Princess Yi'an, adorned in colorful clothes and jewelry, radiating brilliance, the Empress said indifferently, "You speak so cautiously; it seems like a difficult matter. I may not be able to help you."

Princess Yi'an took a small jade hammer and gently tapped the Empress's legs, speaking softly and respectfully, "It may be difficult for this child, but for Mother Empress, it is as easy as lifting a finger."

"You are of marriageable age. I have looked through all the noble families in the capital for you, and none have caught your eye. Could it be that you still want to delay your marriage?" The Empress had indeed spent a lot of effort on Princess Yi'an's marriage. Guessing what she wanted to say, the Empress's expression changed, and her tone turned cold and hard. "Because you have not settled on a marriage partner, your father even scolded me, thinking I was being harsh on my daughter."

"It is this child's fault," Princess Yi'an quickly admitted her mistake. "It is this child who has been unable to settle on a partner, causing Mother Empress to suffer grievances. This child will go to Father Emperor to admit her wrongdoing another day."

The Empress's expression remained poor, and she still did not speak.

Princess Yi'an pulled on the Empress's sleeve and looked up. "This child indeed came tonight to discuss marriage, but not to delay it. Rather, this child wishes to ask Mother Empress to bestow a marriage upon her."

"Bestow a marriage?" The Empress was quite surprised by this and was intrigued. "Who have you taken a liking to?"

Princess Yi'an had been spoiled and had always looked down on everyone, yet now she was proactively asking for an imperial bestowal of marriage?

"You have taken a liking to whom?" After speaking, the Empress seemed to think of something. After picking for so long in the capital without success, she suddenly wanted to marry as soon as they arrived at the traveling palace. "The person you have taken a liking to is not one of the officials who accompanied your father to the traveling palace, is it?"

Facing the Empress's interrogative gaze, Princess Yi'an smiled. "Mother Empress sets an example for the world; this child's thoughts cannot be hidden from Mother Empress."

"Nonsense!" the Empress angrily said, her kind and gentle demeanor completely gone, her voice filled with authority. "Which of the officials who came to the traveling palace are not already married with families? Are you, a princess, willing to marry someone else as a concubine?"

Before Princess Yi'an could speak, the Empress frowned. "Earlier, I asked you about Pei Ta, and it was you who was vague and did not respond, allowing Minister Sun to take the opportunity. You can only blame yourself."

Princess Yi'an had not expected the Empress to suddenly bring up Pei Ta, and her face flushed red for a moment.

Pei Ta was indeed a good match, but when he was selected as the top scholar by her father, Princess Yi'an was only fifteen years old, not yet emotionally mature, and she did not want to marry early and leave the palace. While she was hesitating, Pei Ta became engaged to Sun Qianran.

Princess Yi'an did not have deep feelings for Pei Ta, but she had always been competitive and secretly decided to find a man better than Pei Ta.

Later, when selecting a husband, she would compare the candidates to Pei Ta.

Unfortunately, Pei Ta was exceptionally handsome, had an extraordinary demeanor, was a top scholar, and was highly learned. How could ordinary people compare to him?

It was unreasonable that Sun Qianran, a sickly person, could marry Pei Ta, while she, a princess, had to settle for an ordinary man.

The image of Zhao Xuanyou appeared in Princess Yi'an's mind.

There was a kind of person in this world whose appearance alone could attract attention like a whirlpool. Pei Ta was such a person, and Zhao Xuanyou was as well.

Moreover, compared to Pei Ta's scholarly and refined demeanor, she preferred Zhao Xuanyou's heroic and spirited appearance.

She had never been to the battlefield and did not know what Zhao Xuanyou looked like leading troops in battle, but just watching him reprimand the Seventh Prince on the training grounds was impressive enough.

As the saying went, "A man of letters can govern the court, a man of arms can pacify the nation." Although Pei Ta was unparalleled in literary talent, Zhao Xuanyou held military power, led troops in battle, and had unmatched prestige.

Furthermore, Zhao Xuanyou was not just a military man; he was both literate and martial, highly favored by the Emperor, and his future prospects were certainly better than Pei Ta's.

Thinking about this, Princess Yi'an felt as if she had finally let out a long-held breath of resentment.

She looked at the Empress, her posture respectful.

"In response to Mother Empress, the person this child has taken a liking to is not Pei Ta, but Zhao Xuanyou."

---

chapters.title: The Beauty's Scheme
chapters.content:
"Zhao Xuanyou?" The Empress's expression became even more incredulous upon hearing this name. "Zhao Xuanyou of the Jingyuan Marquis's mansion?"

"Yes, him." Princess Yi'an respectfully replied.

"Absurd!" The Empress did not know why Princess Yi'an had suddenly decided to marry Zhao Xuanyou. Her tone was already filled with anger. "You have always been willful, but at least you have followed proper procedures in the past. Today, you are talking nonsense!"

"Mother Empress..."

Princess Yi'an was about to defend herself when the Empress raised her hand, signaling her to be silent. "It's late. I will consider this as you talking in your sleep. Dismissed!"

Princess Yi'an and the Empress had always been close, but after all, they were not biological mother and daughter.

She did not dare to speak further and could only kneel down before the Empress.

"Mother Empress, please calm your anger. This child is not being willful on a whim but has thought it through carefully. Please allow this child to speak further."

The Empress's previous reprimand had been a definitive command. Now, seeing Princess Yi'an kneeling on the ground, she felt impatient but refrained from losing her temper due to their past relationship.

Seeing that the Empress did not speak again, Princess Yi'an softly said, "Zhao Xuanyou and Cui Yichu have already divorced, and they have no children. Even if this child marries him, it would be almost the same as a first marriage."

The Empress revealed a cold smile, clearly unmoved by this reasoning.

Princess Yi'an continued, "This child has taken a liking to Zhao Xuanyou not because of his outstanding appearance but because, after several interactions, she believes he is a capable official and wishes to entrust her life to him."

"You are a princess. From the moment you were born, you have been honored and cherished all your life. You do not need to rely on a husband like other women do."

"This child naturally understands. However, since childhood, this child has been under the care of Mother Empress and the Crown Prince. As a woman, there are many things this child cannot help with, but if this child marries Zhao Xuanyou, she will certainly be of benefit in the future."

In the eyes of outsiders, the Empress had lived a life of having whatever she desired: holding the position of Empress, setting an example for the nation, with the Emperor as her husband and the Crown Prince as her son, enjoying the highest honors in the land.

Few people knew the difficulty she faced in maintaining this honor.

On the surface, the Emperor and Empress appeared harmonious, but the Empress knew that since her father's passing, the Emperor's dissatisfaction with her and the Crown Prince had been growing.

More and more officials dared to submit memorials impeaching the Crown Prince, which was ironclad proof.

The Crown Prince had not committed any major errors, so the Emperor would not take action against him for now, but what about the future?

In fact, over the past year or two, the Empress had also been working hard to win over officials. The two Prime Ministers had been promoted by her father and now held great power, but they were old and cunning, remaining vague and unwilling to show loyalty in this matter.

Zhao Xuanyou held military power, was a member of the imperial clan, and was favored by the Emperor. If they could win him over, it would indeed be very useful.

Seeing the Empress deep in thought, Princess Yi'an finally let out a sigh of relief and softly said, "This child truly admires Zhao Xuanyou. If she marries into the Jingyuan Marquis's mansion, she will naturally treat him with all her heart."

The Empress's eyes remained dark. "He suddenly divorced Cui Yichu, certainly because he found out about her and the Crown Prince. With such a history between them, how can he be loyal to me and the Crown Prince?"

"Currently, he may have some resentment toward the Crown Prince, but Cui Yichu was this child's study companion. When this child marries him, she will naturally find an opportunity to reveal Cui Yichu's true nature to him. At that time, as long as the Crown Prince makes a little effort to win him over, it will surely eliminate the resentment in his heart." Princess Yi'an spoke gently. "Even if this child cannot persuade him, he is still a subject and would not dare to be disrespectful to the Crown Prince. The fact that he has gained the Emperor's favor shows that he is a person who understands the situation."

After hearing this, the Empress's expression softened slightly.

The imperial court and the harem were always interconnected. Since the Empress had the intention of winning over officials, she was naturally aware of the dynamics in the imperial court.

Zhao Xuanyou was young and promising. As soon as he returned to the capital, he entered the Secretariat and accompanied the Emperor to Lichuan, showing that the Emperor highly valued him.

It was said that Prince Ping was also trying to win him over. If not for the incident with Cui Yichu, the Empress would have had the Crown Prince make a move long ago.

Since Princess Yi'an had taken a liking to Zhao Xuanyou and had such filial piety and insight, she could indeed be useful.

The Empress examined Princess Yi'an, who was kneeling before her.

A precious daughter of heaven, raised in the imperial palace with a noble and delicate appearance, though not as stunning as Cui Yichu, still had her own charming qualities.

With her graceful and tender appearance, noble birth, and insight and cunning not inferior to that of a prince, if she set her heart on Zhao Xuanyou, she would surely be able to control him.

As she pondered, the Empress's anger silently dissolved.

"You have been kneeling for so long; aren't your knees hurting? I am worried about you. Get up."

Princess Yi'an knew that the Empress had agreed to her request and did not rush to stand up. Instead, she solemnly kowtowed to the Empress. "This child thanks Mother Empress for her help."

"You are my daughter. Planning your marriage is my duty. Get up and talk."

"Thank you, Mother Empress, for your great kindness." Princess Yi'an stood up and sat next to the Empress. The mother and daughter each had their own thoughts, but on the surface, they appeared as affectionate as usual.

The Empress held her hand and slowly said, "Do not be in such a hurry to thank me. Your marriage must be approved by the Emperor. Although I have agreed, the Emperor may not. Tonight, you have shared these personal words with me, and I have listened, but these words cannot be repeated to the Emperor. After all, Zhao Xuanyou has been married before."

"This child understands." This was indeed a difficulty. Princess Yi'an thought for a moment and looked at the Empress. "Mother Empress, do you think this child should go to Father Emperor and express her feelings?"

The Empress narrowed her eyes and thought for a moment. "If you go directly to him, he may not be happy. Recently, Zhao Xuanyou has been frequently accompanying the Emperor. You should also go to your father's side more often. Let him see you and Zhao Xuanyou standing together like a couple. After some time, when I bring it up, it will be easier to push the matter forward."

"After some time, when will that be?"

The Empress glanced at her. "You were never in a hurry before, but now you are impatient?"

"In the past, this child was young and ignorant, which is why someone else took the opportunity. This child does not want to repeat the same mistake."

The Empress, of course, also remembered the matter with Pei Ta. She lightly smiled. "It can only be said that Pei Ta was unlucky. He missed a great opportunity and married a sickly person who can't even withstand the wind. Perhaps in a few years, he will be a widower."

Princess Yi'an did not care about Pei Ta at all and did not respond. She only looked at the Empress expectantly.

"Do not be in a hurry. Before the Emperor returns to the traveling palace, I will naturally bring it up."

---

Zhao Xuanyou did not sleep deeply that night and woke up before dawn.

The woman beside him was still fast asleep. He lay on his side next to her, quietly admiring her sleeping face.

Yu Ying seemed to be dreaming. She frowned, her nose making small humming sounds, and her red lips moved slightly, as if she were saying something.

Zhao Xuanyou reached out to help her close her mouth. He gently poked her, and just as Yu Ying turned her head, his finger touched her cheek.

Her skin was tender, and the poke must have hurt. "Ah," she cried out softly and groggily opened her eyes.

"Master, why are you awake so..."

Before Yu Ying could finish her sentence, the man leaned forward, sealing the rest of her words with a kiss.

chapters.title: Washing the Bedsheets
chapters.content:
The morning breeze gently blew through the window lattice.

The curtains on the bed swayed rhythmically with the breeze before finally coming to rest.

"Master, it's already bright outside," Yu Yuan couldn't help but urge.

In the Marquis's residence, his word was law, and Yu Yuan never reminded him of what to do.

But this was the imperial summer palace, and the courtyard also housed the Pei couple and other servants. If he acted too excessively, it would inevitably spread unfavorable rumors.

Zhao Xuanyou was naturally unwilling.

However, it was indeed getting late, and with her waist injury not yet healed, he had to exercise some restraint.

After hastily finishing, he finally got up to change his clothes.

Yu Yuan looked at the mess on the bed and couldn't help but roll her eyes.

"What's with that expression?" Zhao Xuanyou reached out and pinched her chin, his eyes slightly narrowed, revealing a hint of ferocity.

"Master still dares to ask? This servant is truly being driven to the point of not being able to live!" Yu Yuan complained, something she had never done before.

Zhao Xuanyou cleared his throat lightly, "Does your waist hurt? Didn't I avoid touching your waist?"

Yu Yuan rolled her eyes at him in her mind.

He had indeed been careful, keeping one hand protecting her waist the entire time. But that wasn't what she was talking about.

"My waist is fine."

"Then what's wrong?" Zhao Xuanyou asked, his patience wearing thin, his face stern.

Yu Yuan pointed at the mess on the bed, almost on the verge of tears.

"Normally, it's this servant who washes the bedding and sheets. Now that I'm bedridden and can't move, who will do it? When the Pei madam's maids come over later and see this scene, how can I face them for the next two months in the summer palace?"

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yu Yuan's shy and worried expression, finding it somewhat amusing. He slowly and deliberately took a jade crown to tie up his hair.

"It's just a small matter of washing the sheets. Later, I'll have Yuan Qian come in to clean up."

Yuan Qian?

Yu Yuan glared at him, then deflated.

Fine, Yuan Qian was a man, but at least he was from their own Marquis's residence and wouldn't dare to gossip about Zhao Xuanyou's private affairs.

Zhao Xuanyou watched her resigned expression and then glanced at the messy bedsheets.

He took a thin blanket from the nearby cabinet, wrapped Yu Yuan in it, and carried her to the beauty's couch by the window to lie down.

"Later, have Yuan Qian come in to clean up."

Being able to get away from that bed would at least allow her to maintain a facade of dignity.

Seeing that he had rarely tried to coax her, Yu Yuan smiled slightly, reached out to pull his arm, and gently tugged him towards her.

Zhao Xuanyou followed her pull and leaned down. Yu Yuan propped herself up halfway and kissed his face.

He sniffed disdainfully, "It's just a small matter. What are you making a fuss about?"

With that, Zhao Xuanyou went straight out the door, but at the moment he closed it, the corners of his mouth curled up.

In the courtyard, he encountered Xiang Xu, who was with Sun Qianran. He said, "Yu Yuan is still asleep. Come back later."

"Yes, Lord Zhao."

Considering the time, he should indeed go to the training grounds. Zhao Xuanyou quickly ate breakfast and waited for Yuan Qian to arrive before instructing him to go in and tidy up the bed.

Thinking of Yu Yuan's shy and flushed face, he added another reminder.

"Say less nonsense when you go inside."

Yuan Qian was not like Yuan Qing, who was a naive young man. Having grown up in the Marquis's residence and being a few years older, he understood matters between men and women.

When Zhao Xuanyou ordered him to clean up the bed early in the morning, he knew what had happened.

At this moment, he maintained a serious expression and respectfully said, "Master, rest assured. This servant will clean up and come out immediately."

After a moment's thought, Zhao Xuanyou added, "She hasn't eaten yet. Bring her some food."

Since he had told Xiang Xu to come back later, if Yuan Qian didn't bring her food, wouldn't she go hungry?

Thinking of how she had bared her teeth at him earlier over the bedsheets, Zhao Xuanyou seemed to find it amusing and even more pleased.

Yuan Qian watched as his master couldn't suppress the smile on his lips and secretly admired Yu Yuan.

Even after leaving, he was still savoring it early in the morning... Yu Yuan was truly impressive, having completely captivated the young master in the room...

Of course, he would never dare to express such thoughts. He maintained a blank expression and said, "This servant understands."

After handling the matters in the courtyard, Zhao Xuanyou let out a slight sigh.

The women around him indeed couldn't be treated as lightly as before.

Taking Yu Yuan out required bringing along Yingxue at the very least, otherwise, there would be troubles like today.

He walked out leisurely and headed straight for the training grounds.

From afar, he saw the slender figure practicing the horse stance at the edge of the field, his eyes narrowing slightly.

Yesterday, when he was guiding Zhao Qi, he had secretly added extra force, and given Zhao Qi's delicate constitution, he should not have been able to get out of bed today. Yet, here he was, already practicing at the training grounds so early in the morning?

Hmph, it seemed he had underestimated him.

Zhao Xuanyou entered the training grounds. Zhao Qi glanced at him and then looked straight ahead without turning his gaze.

As he got closer, Zhao Xuanyou finally smelled the strong scent of medicinal ointment on him.

"Your Highness, how much ointment did you apply?"

Although the imperial medicinal ointment was precious, the commonly used ingredients were limited, and they all smelled similar.

"What does it have to do with you? You only care about my martial arts training, not acting as an imperial physician," Zhao Qi retorted, his words sharp even though he admired Zhao Xuanyou's martial skills.

Zhao Xuanyou smiled lightly, "Your Highness is of noble status. Even if I am not an imperial physician, I would not disregard your safety."

"Stop pretending," Zhao Qi said coldly. "Don't think I don't know. If it weren't for you, how could I be so severely injured?"

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow slightly, his gaze flicking to Yin Ping and Mu Di, who were standing at attention nearby.

These two guards were top martial artists trained since childhood. They had probably already guessed last night when applying medicine to Zhao Qi that practicing the horse stance wouldn't cause such bruising.

"Then why did Your Highness still come to train with me today?"

"Training with you is the Emperor's decree, so I naturally have to obey. Since I can't beat you and got injured by you, there's nothing I can say. But, Zhao Xuanyou, mark my words, there will come a day when you'll need to apply ointment."

Zhao Xuanyou listened to Zhao Qi's threat, nodding thoughtfully.

This young prince was indeed not beyond hope. He had set his mind on martial arts, and though he was young, with the best warriors around him, it was hard to say what he might achieve in the future.

Zhao Xuanyou was a proud man, but he had never been blindly confident.

"If Your Highness considers me as your opponent, you cannot rely on a few days of effort. It will take at least two or three years to see results."

"Who said I'm only doing this for a few days?" Zhao Qi retorted, unwilling to back down. "You just wait!"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded slightly, "I will be waiting for Your Highness."

"Hmph." Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou's eyes held no mockery, Zhao Qi slightly restrained the discontent in his gaze. After a moment, he added, "There's something I want to discuss with you."

"Please speak, Your Highness."

"I can practice the horse stance every day, but can we not practice here? That bastard Zhao Yu doesn't practice his archery and keeps coming over to bother me. I really don't want to see him."

Not at the training grounds?

The summer palace was not as spacious as the imperial palace. If they practiced in the palace halls, it might disturb the Emperor and Empress.

"Do you have any ideas, Your Highness?"

"You and Pei Ta aren't living together? The Emperor ordered him to instruct me in literature. If I go to your place, wouldn't that be perfect?"

---

chapters.title: Joining the Fun
chapters.content:
Go to the other courtyard?

Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows twitched as he looked at Zhao Qi.

The young man had started practicing the horse stance early in the morning. Although he was standing in the shade, fine beads of sweat had already formed on his forehead.

There was no trace of his usual arrogance in his eyes; instead, he was intently watching Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou understood.

Zhao Qi wanted to change the training location not just because the Sixth Prince, Zhao Yu, was also there. The training grounds were large and open, with many guards coming and going, and concubines and princesses passing by outside.

He had always been strong-willed and concerned about his reputation. Having so many people watching him made him feel uncomfortable.

Seeing that he could endure the bruises and continue training today, Zhao Xuanyou's opinion of him improved slightly.

The Emperor had indeed ordered Pei Ta to instruct Zhao Qi in his studies. Training at the other courtyard would make it easier to report to the Emperor.

"Then we shall do as Your Highness says. However, if you change the location and still refuse to work hard, then you'll have to return to the training grounds."

"Hmph, no need for you to worry."

Zhao Qi, as if he had truly changed his nature, practiced the horse stance for an hour, then the bow stance for another hour. After a short rest following lunch, he asked Zhao Xuanyou to arrange something else.

Thinking that they had already practiced basic skills for most of the day, Zhao Xuanyou accompanied him in practicing combat techniques.

The Ningguo Duke's family martial arts involved the use of the long spear. Zhao Qi had learned it before but only mastered the superficial form, not the essence.

Although Zhao Xuanyou was not skilled with the long spear, he was still more than a match for Zhao Qi.

By the time the sun was setting, an inner attendant from the Emperor's side arrived at the training grounds, conveying the Emperor's order for them to dine at the Mingde Hall.

Zhao Xuanyou returned to the other courtyard to wash up and change clothes, then quickly rushed back to wait outside Mingde Hall. Before long, Zhao Qi arrived, and the two entered the hall together.

Originally, he thought it was just to accompany the Emperor for a meal, but it turned out that Princess Yian was also present.

Zhao Qi shot Zhao Xuanyou a malicious smile. Zhao Xuanyou became even more convinced of Zhao Qi's suspicions and merely responded respectfully.

The Emperor smiled and granted them seats, unaware of the undercurrents. He ordered the meal to be served immediately. After the meal, the inner attendants served a cooling soup, and only then did the Emperor ask about Zhao Qi's training.

In front of the Emperor, Zhao Qi was much more respectful and simply stated that Zhao Xuanyou had him practice basic skills.

The Emperor nodded slightly. "You were a clever child, and everyone used to say you were a good candidate for martial arts. Unfortunately, both I and the Duke of Ningguo couldn't bear to be strict with you, which delayed you by a few years. Fortunately, now you have Xuanyou. Since you've decided to work hard, you must not be willful anymore."

"When have I ever been willful?" Zhao Qi asked. "Practicing the horse stance is indeed tedious, but as a child, I couldn't persist. Now that I can, I naturally will."

"Regardless of what you say, since I have entrusted you to Xuanyou, he is your teacher. If I hear anything about you not respecting your teacher, I will punish you severely."

"Disrespecting my teacher?" Zhao Qi couldn't help but glare at Zhao Xuanyou. "He is better than me in martial arts. What can I do to him? Father Emperor should see how he treats me."

Before the Emperor could speak, Princess Yian opened her mouth with a smile. "Yesterday, I happened to pass by the training grounds and saw Lord Zhao sparring with my seventh brother. The sages say to teach according to the student's abilities. For a stubborn and unruly child like my seventh brother, he indeed needs Lord Zhao to be stricter."

"Correct," the Emperor nodded. "I have also heard about yesterday's events. Xuanyou did well. The reason I called you here is to reward you handsomely."

Zhao Xuanyou stood up and cupped his hands. "Following the Emperor's orders is the duty of a subject. Your Majesty's praise is undeserved."

"I have always believed in clear rewards and punishments. If you do well, you shall be rewarded. I heard that you traveled lightly to the summer palace this time. I will reward you with some daily expenses. Later, I will have the inner attendants deliver them to you."

"Your subject thanks Your Majesty for the generous reward."

Zhao Qi, seeing that Zhao Xuanyou could choke him and still receive a reward, snorted disdainfully.

Princess Yian had seen Zhao Xuanyou receive rewards from the Ministry of Internal Affairs the first time she met him. Now, seeing the Emperor reward him again, she knew that the Emperor held him in high regard and was secretly pleased with her own choice.

"Father Emperor, I previously discussed with Lord Zhao that I will no longer train at the training grounds."

"Not training at the training grounds, then where?"

Zhao Qi said, "Lord Zhao and Lord Pei happen to live in the same courtyard. If I go there, I can both train in martial arts and ask Lord Pei to instruct me in literature. It would also save them the trouble of running back and forth."

The Emperor narrowed his eyes and thought for a moment. "The other courtyard is not very spacious, and there are women there. Would it be too crowded?"

"Lord Zhao has no family, and Lord Pei's family is only Miss Sun. I have known her since I was a child, so there's nothing to avoid."

Princess Yian's eyes flashed upon hearing this.

Sun Qianran had been in and out of the palace since she was a child and was indeed familiar with the princes and princesses.

Initially, the Emperor had not considered betrothing her to his son only because Sun Qianran's health was too frail.

Given their childhood friendship, it would not be out of place for Princess Yian to visit and chat with her.

"A few days ago, my younger sister Yining and I visited that courtyard. Although it's not big, it only houses Lord Pei and Lord Zhao's families, which is quieter than other residences with large families. There are also empty rooms in the courtyard, which can be cleaned up for my seventh brother to use as a study."

Zhao Qi didn't know what Princess Yian was planning but was happy to have her support and nodded repeatedly to the Emperor.

"Xuanyou, what do you think?" the Emperor asked.

Zhao Xuanyou had already agreed to Zhao Qi's request earlier, so naturally, he said it was good.

The Emperor nodded slowly. "Then, let's try it there for now. If it's too cramped and you can't practice properly, we'll return to the training grounds."

"Thank you, Father Emperor, for your kindness."

After the three of them left Mingde Hall, Zhao Qi glanced at Zhao Xuanyou and then at Princess Yian.

"Why did Royal Sister suddenly speak up for me today?"

With Zhao Xuanyou present, Princess Yian maintained a calm and gentle demeanor. "Since I am your royal sister, it's only natural for me to help my younger brother."

"Is that so? I'm afraid Royal Sister has ulterior motives."

Princess Yian saw that Zhao Qi was intentionally provoking her and didn't mind. She glanced at Zhao Xuanyou out of the corner of her eye and saw that his gaze was calm. She smiled, "I'm just helping you. Why are you overcomplicating things? Fine, I won't meddle in your affairs anymore."

With that, she turned and left gracefully.

Zhao Qi leaned toward Zhao Xuanyou and whispered, "See? She's acting guilty. Don't blame me for not considering our teacher-student relationship by not warning you. If you marry her, your life will be ruined."

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou remained silent, Zhao Qi left smugly.

Zhao Xuanyou was indeed somewhat annoyed.

Princess Yian was the Emperor's beloved daughter. If she were to speak to the Emperor, even if he were already married, the Emperor might still agree.

But he couldn't rashly go to the Emperor to clarify his stance.

If he rejected Princess Yian, would the Emperor be happy? No matter how much the Emperor valued him, it was only the appreciation of a subject, which could not surpass the Emperor's love for his daughter.

Zhao Xuanyou walked back to the small courtyard, looking up at the lantern hanging at the entrance. Just as he was about to enter, Yuan Qing, who was guarding the door, came forward and handed him a secret letter.

"Master, there's news from the capital."

chapters.title: Eyes Lighting Up
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou read the secret letter at a glance and handed it to Yuan Qing.

"Burn it."

"Yes."

Zhao Xuanyou went straight back to the small courtyard. Seeing the warm orange light spilling from the house, he unconsciously pursed his lips and walked in.

That morning, he had moved Yu Wan to the beauty couch by the window. Now, when he returned, Yu Wan was still lying there.

Zhao Xuanyou walked over, picked up Yu Wan, and returned to the couch. Looking at the clean and tidy bed, he proudly asked, "Yuan Xuan tidied it quite well."

Yu Wan knew he was still holding a grudge about her complaints that morning. She couldn't do anything about him, so she just smiled.

He was the heir, and he could order Yuan Xuan around, but she couldn’t.

Zhao Xuanyou had her lie on the couch and, as before, pressed the acupuncture points on her waist.

"Still hurts?"

Yu Wan couldn’t help but hiss a few times, pitifully saying, "It still hurts, but..."

"Not as much as before?"

"Mmm, not as much as before."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded twice. "Your injury isn’t serious. Lie down for another night, and you should be able to get up tomorrow. But you must not lift anything heavy for the next month."

"I won’t," Yu Wan stuck out her tongue, "I’d rather die than lift anything heavy again."

Seeing her regretful expression, Zhao Xuanyou chuckled softly. He helped her roll over again and pulled the blanket over her.

"There’s news from the capital."

"Is it a letter for me?" She had written to Chen Da Niu before but hadn’t received a reply yet.

Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes and asked, "Who wrote to you?"

"Just my mother’s side. Before, I wrote to the innkeeper of Taoran Inn, asking him to keep an eye on my mother. If there’s any change in her condition, I asked him to write and let me know."

Zhao Xuanyou had once been extremely displeased about Chen Da Niu taking care of her mother, so Yu Wan naturally wouldn’t mention Chen Da Niu in front of him.

Of course, Zhao Xuanyou could guess that she was waiting for a letter from Chen Da Niu. Seeing her acting cute, he was pleased.

"Master, what news did you receive? Does it concern me?"

Zhao Xuanyou had always kept public and private matters separate and wouldn’t likely tell her about official business.

"Master, someone from Mingde Hall has arrived." Before Zhao Xuanyou could speak, Yuan Qing knocked on the door from outside.

"Lie down."

Zhao Xuanyou dropped those two words and went out. He returned shortly after. Yu Wan curiously asked, "It’s so late, does His Majesty still have a decree?"

"His Majesty thinks I’ve taught the Seventh Prince well and specially bestowed some gifts."

The Emperor had sent quite a lot of things that evening: a bolt each of silk, brocade, makeup silk, and floral silk, as well as Pu'er tea, Liu'an tea, Wuyi tea, porcelain teapots, teacups, a tea canister, and a small incense burner. Indeed, everything for daily use was covered.

"Congratulations, Master. It seems His Majesty truly likes you."

"If the task is done well, the master will naturally be pleased."

Yu Wan blinked, her red lips slightly pouting as she coquettishly said, "It seems I haven’t done my tasks well enough."

There was a hidden meaning in her words.

Zhao Xuanyou reached out and pinched her chin, leaning close to her face. With a stern expression, he asked, "Are you complaining that I’ve given you too few rewards?"

Yu Wan just smiled at him but didn’t speak.

It wasn’t that he had given too few; he had given her hairpins and clothes, which were valuable. But Yu Wan couldn’t exactly pawn them all for daily use.

She had served him for so long, but his gifts couldn’t compare to the gold melon seeds from Lady Ye or even Cui Yichu’s.

Cui Yichu had given her silver, which she could use directly.

"Being able to serve you is already my fortune. How dare I covet rewards?"

Zhao Xuanyou listened to her insincere sweet words, remembering how she had been raising money to treat her mother. He didn’t feel the slightest annoyance.

However, he had always enjoyed teasing Yu Wan, and seeing her ask for rewards, he naturally wouldn’t give in so easily.

"If you want a reward, you have to do something that makes me happy."

Yu Wan widened her eyes.

Something that made him happy? The only thing that made him happy was... that kind of thing. Normally, it would be fine, but with her waist injured, how could she satisfy him?

Yu Wan knew he was stingy and pouted.

"I understand."

As soon as she finished speaking, Zhao Xuanyou saw her pretty little face turn away, no longer looking at him.

He leaned down next to her and forcibly turned her shoulder back.

"So delicate?"

"I’m useless. I can’t make you happy."

Zhao Xuanyou reached out and traced her lips with his finger, trying hard to make her smile, but she still wore a worried frown.

"Forget it. I really can’t do anything with you. I’ll reward you with a hundred taels of silver. Will that make you happy?"

A hundred taels?

Yu Wan’s large almond eyes suddenly sparkled as her mind quickly calculated.

Physician Feng charged five taels per consultation. If her mother could wake up after ten acupuncture sessions, then fifty taels would remain.

By the time Zhao Xuanyou married, she could take this silver with her when she left the mansion. It would be enough to buy a few houses and some land, ensuring she had a secure future.

Yu Wan was overjoyed, but when she met Zhao Xuanyou’s unpredictable gaze, she quickly composed herself, returning to her usual submissive demeanor.

"Master is teasing me?"

Zhao Xuanyou had indeed felt a little deflated when he saw how delighted she was at the mention of a hundred taels of silver.

He was the heir of a marquisate, yet she remained so calm around him, only to light up at the mention of a hundred taels. It wasn’t that he was angry; just a little displeased.

"When have I ever taken back my word?"

"Thank you, Master." Yu Wan couldn’t suppress her smile. Looking at Zhao Xuanyou, it was as if a hundred taels of gleaming silver were right in front of her.

She couldn’t help but cup Zhao Xuanyou’s face, wanting to kiss him as she had that morning to show her gratitude.

But before her lips could touch his cheek, he raised his hand to cover her mouth.

Yu Wan, muffled, was confused for a moment, not understanding his meaning.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered slightly as he coldly pressed Yu Wan back onto the pillow.

Of course, he liked her kissing him, but not because he had given her a hundred taels of silver.

If he let her kiss him now, wouldn’t the heir of a marquisate seem too cheap?

Yu Wan had no idea about his convoluted thoughts and could only lie obediently on the pillow, lightly tugging at his sleeve.

"Master is tired today. You should rest early."

That sounded reasonable.

Zhao Xuanyou changed into his nightclothes and lifted the blanket to lie beside her.

The faint fragrance from her body wafted over, and the slight displeasure he had felt earlier because of her request for a reward gradually dissipated. He returned to thinking about serious matters.

"I haven’t told you about the news from the capital yet."

"Oh." Yu Wan turned her head to look at him.

"Last time you said that the people from Xingguo Duke’s mansion might target your mother, so I deliberately left some people near Yunshui Nunnery to wait."

Related to the Xingguo Duke’s mansion?

Yu Wan’s heart suddenly tightened. As she listened to Zhao Xuanyou, she didn’t dare breathe loudly.

"What... what did they do?"

"Two days ago, someone went to Yunshui Nunnery to inquire about your mother’s whereabouts. It was someone sent by the Xingguo Duke’s mansion."

---

chapters.title: Asking for His Help
chapters.content:
"Then... then what?" Yu Wan was both worried and relieved.

Fortunately, her mother had already been moved to Taoran Inn, which was Zhao Xuanyou’s property. The people from the Xingguo Duke’s mansion certainly wouldn’t dare cause trouble there.

Yu Wan’s mind once again flashed with Cui Yichu’s face.

Clearly, everything that had happened to her was her own fault. If she had to blame anyone, it should be herself, or at most the adulterer. Yet, she had directed all her hatred toward Yu Wan.

Unable to take revenge on Yu Wan, she wanted to take it out on Yu Wan’s mother.

Zhao Xuanyou heard the worry in her voice and said in a deep voice, "It’s fine. Taoran Inn is safe."

His words were concise.

Taoran Inn was a long-standing property of the marquisate. From the innkeeper to the waiters, they were all servants of the marquisate. Yu Wan’s mother was very safe staying there.

"I understand. It’s just that I feel..." Yu Wan sighed deeply, "a little tired."

The Xingguo Duke’s mansion had chosen to act after Zhao Xuanyou left the capital, clearly showing restraint out of fear of him. They would never dare harm Yu Wan’s mother at Taoran Inn.

But as long as Cui Yichu was alive and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion still held power, the lives of Yu Wan and her mother would always be under threat.

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou remained silent, Yu Wan couldn’t help but feel resentful.

In front of him, she had always been cautious and never overstepped her bounds.

But the Xingguo Duke’s mansion was a behemoth she couldn’t deal with. If he didn’t take action, they would forever remain Yu Wan’s nightmare.

"Master, you and the Cui family have separated. The Xingguo Duke’s mansion and the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion will henceforth be at peace with each other, with no further entanglements. My mother is safe at Taoran Inn, but she can’t stay there forever."

As Yu Wan spoke, tears welled in the corners of her eyes and quickly slid down her cheeks onto the bedsheet.

Zhao Xuanyou watched the silent tears fall and gently wiped away the tear marks on her face with his finger.

"It won’t go on forever."

Yu Wan’s heart stirred. Her lively eyes suddenly lit up as she looked at Zhao Xuanyou, pondering the meaning behind his words.

To eliminate the crisis, Cui Yichu had to die, and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion had to fall.

Did he mean he had decided to join forces with Pei Ta to deal with the Xingguo Duke’s mansion?

Yu Wan felt a hidden joy, but she knew Zhao Xuanyou’s temperament. Asking directly would only displease him.

She simply snuggled closer to Zhao Xuanyou, her cheek resting against his arm.

"With Master here, I’m not afraid."

Zhao Xuanyou embraced her, and the softness of her body finally stirred his interest.

He considered his words carefully before speaking, "Tonight..."

After just two words, Yu Wan understood his meaning.

"Tomorrow night."

In the past, Zhao Xuanyou would do as he pleased without asking, but after spending so much time together, some affection had indeed grown between them.

Hearing Yu Wan interrupt him, he let out a soft laugh, extinguished the candle, and held her as they went to sleep.

---

Leaning in his arms, Yu Wan always slept especially soundly.

However, her deep sleep was interrupted by a loud knocking at the door.

"Zhao Xuanyou! Lord Zhao!"

At the sound of this voice, Yu Wan knew that the troublemaker had arrived again.

She had thought he would behave after being disciplined by Zhao Xuanyou, but he was still the same.

The man beside her had always been a light sleeper and naturally opened his eyes.

"Master, the Seventh Prince is here."

"It’s not time for martial arts practice. Why pay attention to him?" Zhao Xuanyou said, closing his eyes again.

Really, no need to acknowledge him?

Yu Wan felt uneasy, but her waist was still sore and numb. Without help, she couldn’t get up.

However, there were other people living in the courtyard. Soon, someone went to answer the door. After saying something to Zhao Qi, the courtyard fell silent again.

Anyway, Zhao Xuanyou was here today. If there was anything, Zhao Qi would go directly to Zhao Xuanyou. Yu Wan didn’t need to worry.

Seeing that he remained calmly asleep, Yu Wan closed her eyes and soon fell back asleep.

When she woke up again, the space beside her was empty.

"Sister Yu Wan, you’re awake." Xiang Xu approached with a smile.

"Where is the young master?"

"The young master and my husband are both in the courtyard, teaching the Seventh Prince horse stances." Xiang Xu said with a look of helplessness, "This morning, the Seventh Prince knocked so hard on the door that even the madam was startled awake. My husband went to open the door and scolded the Seventh Prince."

So it was Pei Ta who had answered the door in the morning.

He was just like Zhao Xuanyou and didn’t fear Zhao Qi at all. He even dared to reprimand him.

Xiang Xu sighed. "I heard that from now on, the Seventh Prince will come every day."

"Every day? To our courtyard?"

Xiang Xu nodded. "His Majesty ordered the young master and my husband to instruct the Seventh Prince in his studies. I heard that the Seventh Prince finds it convenient to come here, so he requested a decree from His Majesty."

Thinking of Zhao Xuanyou’s calm demeanor earlier, he must have known about this already.

Yu Wan also felt a little disheartened.

Life in this courtyard had been peaceful, and the Pei couple had been easy to get along with. Now that Zhao Qi was here, who knew how much chaos would follow.

Xiang Xu complained for a while, then noticed Yu Wan’s expression and quickly changed the subject. "The young master instructed me earlier to help you get up and walk around the room today. Sister, how are you feeling now? Can you walk?"

Her waist wasn’t very comfortable, but since Zhao Xuanyou said she should walk, Yu Wan naturally listened to him.

After all, he had been pressing her acupuncture points and applying medicine every night. Yu Wan clearly felt her waist improving, so she trusted his judgment.

"Thank you."

Xiang Xu stepped forward to help Yu Wan up and had her sit on the edge of the couch first.

"How do you feel, Sister?"

Yu Wan nodded. "It’s okay. It seems more comfortable than lying down."

"Then try walking a few steps."

Yu Wan, holding Xiang Xu’s hand, stood up and first walked slowly a few steps. Then she sped up and found that she was almost as good as before.

It seemed Zhao Xuanyou was right. Her waist injury wasn’t serious, and it was already almost healed.

"Earlier, the young master also reminded me that you must not lift heavy objects or bend over easily. You must be careful."

"Thank you. It looks like I can go eat by myself today."

"Your breakfast is being kept warm in the kitchen." Xiang Xu said.

The morning light was soft as Yu Wan and Xiang Xu pushed open the door and went out. At a glance, they saw Zhao Qi practicing horse stances in the middle of the courtyard.

The courtyard wasn’t large, so Zhao Qi naturally saw Yu Wan as well.

That day, Yu Wan had moved the table to the courtyard by herself. Such an action was naturally hard to forget.

"Seventh Prince." Yu Wan respectfully greeted him with a curtsy.

Zhao Qi let out a cold snort and arrogantly said, "You still know how to show respect. You’re more sensible than your master."

Was he insulting Zhao Xuanyou for not getting up to greet him this morning?

Yu Wan’s gaze subconsciously shifted to Zhao Xuanyou. Their eyes met, and both had a hint of amusement in their expressions.

Today, they weren’t at the training grounds, so he was much more relaxed. Instead of accompanying Zhao Qi in the courtyard under the sun, he had moved two chairs and was sitting with Pei Ta, sipping tea and chatting idly.

No wonder Zhao Qi was displeased.

After Yu Wan greeted the two men under the veranda, she headed toward the kitchen.

Today’s breakfast was more abundant than usual. In addition to yam porridge and steamed buns, there was a plate of flaky pastries and a plate of pickled mustard greens; all Yu Wan’s favorites.

She pulled up a small stool by the courtyard wall, basking in the sunlight as she ate. Out of the corner of her eye, she glanced at Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta talking under the veranda, and a slight joy rose in her heart.

It seemed that what Zhao Xuanyou had said to her last night wasn’t just a brush-off.

He really was going to join forces with Pei Ta to deal with the Xingguo Duke’s mansion.

chapters.title: Learning in Secret
chapters.content:
In the corridor, Zhao Xuanyou slowly sipped his tea, set down the cup, and said to Pei Tao, "Thank you for answering the door this morning, Minister Pei."

"It was the Emperor's order for me to guide the Seventh Prince in his studies. Whether it was me or Director Zhao who answered the door, it would have been the same."

"The Seventh Prince acts on impulse and never considers others. It seems Minister Pei has a heavy task ahead; you’ll probably have to start from the very beginning with the Book of Rites."

Earlier, Yu Yuan had been startled by the knocking at the door. Sun Qianran was frail and likely frightened by the noise. Pei Tao must have rushed to open the door in a foul mood.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou’s teasing words, Pei Tao gave a faint smile. "The princes in the palace begin their education early. The Four Books and Five Classics are already at the Seventh Prince’s fingertips. I am merely offering some guidance. Unlike Director Zhao, who has the arduous task of training the Prince in martial arts from the basics."

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at him, his expression unreadable. "Martial arts are not like scholarship. Success depends on natural talent. If the Prince does not work hard, there is little I can do."

Pei Tao nodded meaningfully. "Perhaps mastering martial arts is something one can achieve alone, but many things in this world require collective effort."

Zhao Xuanyou only responded with a smirk.

Pei Tao saw that he still refused to engage, sighed inwardly, and did not press further. Instead, he picked up his own teacup.

The sun gradually climbed higher, and the courtyard grew warmer.

"The Seventh Prince has been practicing for an hour. Come, have some water and rest a while."

Zhao Qi walked over, saw the clear tea on the table, and immediately frowned. "I don’t drink tea. Is there any cooling soup?"

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent.

He had called Zhao Qi over simply to prevent him from overheating under the sun. If Zhao Qi wanted to be picky, that was none of his concern.

Pei Tao spoke gently, "There is cool water in the pot. Your Highness has worked up a sweat; plain water will quench your thirst better."

Zhao Qi had never liked tea. Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou ignored him, he had no choice but to pour himself some water to drink.

After Zhao Qi had rested for a while, an inner attendant from the Hall of Virtuous Governance arrived, saying that His Majesty wanted to go hunting again today and ordered Zhao Xuanyou to accompany and protect him.

Pei Tao said, "The Prince has been practicing all morning. I’ll give him a lesson first."

"Very well. The Prince can study first, then practice another hour of horseback archery in the afternoon."

After giving his instructions, Zhao Xuanyou did not delay. He changed his clothes and hurried off with the inner attendant.

Watching his retreating figure, Zhao Qi scoffed, "The Emperor only thinks highly of him because of his martial skills."

"Does Your Highness think Director Zhao’s martial skills are lacking?"

Zhao Qi raised an eyebrow, unimpressed. "He’s stronger than me, but that’s not saying much. Compared to the real masters in the palace, he’s nothing special."

Pei Tao did not agree.

The martial arts of the palace masters were indeed formidable, but Zhao Xuanyou had honed his skills on the battlefield, where every move carried the risk of life and death. That kind of combat experience could not be compared to mere drills in a training ground.

Moreover, warfare required more than just martial prowess.

That was why he had chosen Zhao Xuanyou.

"If Your Highness has rested enough, I shall begin the lesson."

"Go ahead."

Zhao Qi had been determined to improve his martial skills due to Zhao Xuanyou’s provocation, but he still had no interest in the Four Books and Five Classics.

Now that Zhao Xuanyou was gone, he seemed listless.

The empty room in the courtyard had been tidied up. A desk was set up for Pei Tao, and another for Zhao Qi.

Pei Tao had originally selected some strategy essays written by scholars to discuss with Zhao Qi, but seeing his lack of enthusiasm, he switched to the Book of Songs and chose Constant Sibling Affection from the Lesser Odes of the Kingdom.

"The flowers of the constant plant, how bright and fair! Of all men now living, none compare with brothers."

Listening to Pei Tao’s recitation, Zhao Qi curled his lip, looking as if he wanted to laugh.

Thinking of his troublesome royal siblings, he wondered: in the face of power and self-interest, did such brotherly affection truly exist?

"When brothers quarrel at home, they unitedly resist external foes..."

Pei Tao had a pleasant voice. When Yu Yuan first heard it on the way to the imperial villa, she had been captivated even before seeing him.

The kitchen was right next to the study. As Yu Yuan cleaned the pots and pans, she couldn’t help but be distracted by Pei Tao’s voice reciting poetry in the room.

"Is it indeed so? Is it truly so?"

Yu Yuan stepped out of the kitchen and saw that the window of the study was open. Through the thin gauze, she could see Pei Tao holding a book, lecturing earnestly, while Zhao Qi yawned repeatedly, paying no attention at all.

"Your Highness, what do you think of this poem?"

"Not much. I suspect the poet never had any brothers."

"Brothers living under the same roof inevitably have conflicts, but no matter how fiercely they fight among themselves, they will stand together against an external enemy."

"Are you sure? Do you have brothers?"

Pei Tao replied calmly, "I am an only child. I have no brothers."

"Hmph." Zhao Qi sneered. "Then what do you know? You, who have no brothers, are lecturing me about brotherly affection. It’s all just empty talk. Whoever wants to listen can listen."

Pei Tao remained unmoved and still spoke gently, "Everyone’s perspective is limited. That is why the ancients said, 'Reading history can enlighten the mind.' If one cannot see the whole picture from their own experience, they can learn from the experiences of others through history."

Zhao Qi stuck out his tongue, clearly not taking it in.

Pei Tao continued, "This poem begins with both narrative and commentary, discussing the constancy of brotherhood and expressing its profound meaning. Your Highness may not grasp it now, but perhaps you will understand it when you reflect on it alone someday."

"Indeed." Zhao Qi, surprisingly, did not argue. "This poem may be nonsense, but reading some poetry occasionally isn’t so bad. Anyway, there’s nothing else to do here. Not only do I have you here lecturing by the book, but there’s also someone outside eavesdropping on your lesson."

Eavesdropping?

Pei Tao’s gaze shifted toward the window.

Through the gauze, he saw a graceful and beautiful young girl standing outside, her eyes calm as she gazed in their direction.

Her skin was as fine as porcelain, flawless even under the bright summer sun, making her all the more radiant.

"Miss Yu Yuan," Pei Tao called out.

Yu Yuan had just been passing by when she heard Pei Tao reciting poetry. She couldn’t help but stop and listen intently. When she suddenly met Pei Tao’s gaze, she felt a pang of embarrassment.

Hearing him call her name, she gave him an awkward smile. "Minister Pei."

"His Highness doesn’t drink tea. See if there’s any sweet soup in the kitchen and bring a bowl for him."

"Yes."

Minister Pei was truly kind and considerate; he had even found an excuse for her.

Grateful, she bowed to Pei Tao and hurried toward the kitchen.

Sun Qianran loved sweets, and the cook made desserts and sweet soups every day. Earlier, the cook had given Yu Yuan the ingredients to make hawthorn tea.

As expected, when Yu Yuan entered the kitchen, she found a pot of rose dew already prepared.

She ladled two bowls and, after cooling them with a fan, brought them into the study.

Pei Tao was still lecturing on the same poem, explaining its rhythmic cadence. When he saw Yu Yuan enter, he paused.

Zhao Qi, who loved sweets, quickly took a bowl and drank it in one gulp.

"You’ve gone to a lot of trouble." Pei Tao, recalling how Yu Yuan had been standing outside listening attentively, said gently, "If you have nothing else to do, stay here and attend to the tea."

Yu Yuan looked at Pei Tao in surprise.

She knew, of course, that Pei Tao wasn’t assigning her a task out of necessity; the Pei residence had brought four maids, and he didn’t lack servants.

He was allowing her to stay and serve tea so that she could listen to his lecture without drawing attention to herself. Was that it?

Yu Yuan’s cheeks flushed slightly, a mix of embarrassment and gratitude.

Before she could speak, Zhao Qi, sitting beside her, wore a look of disdain. "Can she even read? To her, this lousy poem is no different from heavenly script."

---

chapters.title: Appreciation
chapters.content:
Pei Tao frowned slightly at this.

He was naturally handsome and refined, and the sudden tightening of his brows gave him an unexpectedly imposing presence, as if angering him was a grave offense.
