Zhao Qi, under his gaze, lowered his head awkwardly and picked up the other bowl of rose dew.

Yu Yuan, noticing Pei Tao’s expression, cautiously said, "This servant hasn’t had much schooling, but I can read."

She had grown up in a village as a girl and had never set foot in a school. But when she was little, her mother would teach her characters while working.

She had never thought much about it before, but now, hearing Zhao Qi’s mockery, a doubt arose in her mind: Why did her mother know how to read?

Even in noble families, many clans upheld the belief that "a woman’s virtue lies in ignorance," and even the mistress of the household might be illiterate.

How could her mother, a mere village woman, be literate?

But this doubt flashed through Yu Yuan’s mind only briefly. She would have to wait until her mother woke up to find out.

"Did Your Highness hear that?" Pei Tao’s tone was clearly less amiable than before.

"I did," Zhao Qi replied, then muttered under his breath, "The Emperor ordered you to teach me, not this stinking girl."

"Miss Yu Yuan is only here to help. She isn’t studying."

Yu Yuan seized the moment. "Yes, this servant is here to serve tea to Your Highness. There’s also eight-treasure cake steaming in the kitchen. I’ll bring some over later."

Pei Tao was a zhuangyuan (top scholar). Few in the world could match his learning.

Yu Yuan couldn’t take the imperial examinations, nor did she seek great scholarship. But she understood that there might not be many more leisurely days like this in the imperial villa.

Rather than spending her days confined to the kitchen or lying idle in her room, she would prefer to serve in the study and listen to Pei Tao’s lectures.

She could see that Pei Tao was speaking up for her, so she did her best to please Zhao Qi to avoid being driven away.

Sure enough, when Zhao Qi heard "eight-treasure cake," his eyes flickered slightly.

He had mentioned wanting to eat it when he came here to pester Zhao Xuanyou. He hadn’t expected Yu Yuan to remember.

She was indeed a cunning maid.

Cunning or not, for a boy of his age, it was still rather flattering.

Zhao Qi’s youthful face was full of arrogance. He lightly tapped his empty bowl, and Yu Yuan understood. She stepped forward, placed the empty bowl back on the tray, and went to the kitchen to bring him another bowl of rose dew.

Although Pei Tao had allowed her to listen in, the most honored person in the room was still Zhao Qi. Yu Yuan didn’t dare to be careless. She kept a close eye on Zhao Qi’s movements.

When Zhao Qi needed to write, she would prepare his brush and ink. When there was no breeze in the room, she would fan him.

Her attentiveness was so thorough that even Zhao Qi, as difficult as he was, couldn’t find fault.

Pei Tao’s lectures were not pedantic. He spoke in simple, easy-to-understand terms, yet his explanations were layered, like peeling an onion. Just when Yu Yuan thought she had grasped the meaning, a new understanding would emerge.

The lecture on Constant Sibling Affection lasted nearly half an hour. After Yu Yuan brought the steamed eight-treasure cake from the kitchen, and they had a short tea break, Pei Tao asked Zhao Qi to try writing a poem during his free time, one that, like Constant Sibling Affection, combined both narrative and commentary.

Zhao Qi disliked composing poetry the most. He responded with a noncommittal "mm," clearly having no intention of writing.

At this moment, Zhao Qi’s subordinate arrived to deliver his meal. Yu Yuan helped clear the table before withdrawing.

Pei Tao stood in the corridor and, seeing Yu Yuan come out, said gently, "You’ve worked hard today, Miss Yu Yuan."

"This servant is just a maid. The tasks in the study are light and easy. It’s no trouble at all." Yu Yuan lowered her voice, grateful. "It is this servant who should thank Minister Pei for allowing me to serve here."

Pei Tao smiled. "Lecturing is always easier when there’s someone listening attentively."

Zhao Qi indeed...

Yu Yuan didn’t dare to laugh. She simply nodded at Pei Tao, then bowed and left for the kitchen, not wanting to delay his meal.

Back in the room, the table was already set with a lavish lunch.

After being woken up early and busy all morning, Pei Tao was indeed hungry. He sat beside Sun Qianran and began to eat heartily.

After setting down his chopsticks, Sun Qianran smiled and asked, "My lord, you must be very hungry. It seems the Seventh Prince has given you quite a hard time."

Pei Tao laughed helplessly. "The only good news is that Zhao Xuanyou is also his teacher. How are you?"

When Zhao Qi had come knocking at dawn, Sun Qianran had been startled awake. Frightened, she hadn’t been able to fall back asleep and had spent the morning listlessly in her room.

"It was nothing serious. But my lord, you shouldn’t have lost your temper with the Seventh Prince."

"If I hadn’t, and he kept this up every day, you might have been able to endure it, but I certainly couldn’t."

Sun Qianran poured him a cup of digestive tea and added, "I heard Xiang Xu say that you had Yu Yuan attend in the study?"

Pei Tao nodded. "I noticed she was interested in the Book of Songs, so I let her come in and help. I didn’t expect her to be literate."

"Oh? It seems Director Zhao thinks highly of her."

In noble families, some capable servants, usually men, were taught to read. But it was rare for women.

Pei Tao didn’t think much of it. He slowly sipped his tea, recalling the day’s events with interest. "Yu Yuan has a good aptitude. When I was lecturing the Prince today, I started with the basics and then delved deeper. She was able to follow along."

Sun Qianran watched Pei Tao as he spoke with such enthusiasm, recalling Yu Yuan’s strikingly beautiful face. A faint emotion stirred in her heart.

"That day, the Seventh Prince barged into the courtyard and went out of his way to pick a fight with her. It ended with her straining her back, yet today he allowed her to serve in the room."

Pei Tao smiled faintly. "The Seventh Prince naturally refused at first. Even when I spoke up for her, it didn’t work. But she was quick-witted and managed to smooth things over with a few words. After that, he didn’t cause any more trouble for her."

"I see." Sun Qianran’s gaze flickered. "No wonder she was able to stay by Director Zhao’s side. However, my lord, I think it’s inappropriate to keep Yu Yuan in the study all the time."

"Why?" Pei Tao asked, puzzled.

Sun Qianran lowered her eyes, looking at the dishes on the table. "Director Zhao seems to care about Yu Yuan. If you keep her in the study, he may not be pleased."

Pei Tao was an intelligent man. Hearing his wife’s words, he immediately understood her meaning.

"You mean Director Zhao would be jealous? I was only…"

Sun Qianran raised her slender hand and placed it on Pei Tao’s. "My lord, both you and Yu Yuan are exceptionally good-looking. You stand out separately, but together... you would draw far too much attention."

Pei Tao looked at Sun Qianran in astonishment, feeling both helpless and amused.

"Madam, you... Yu Yuan is Director Zhao’s maid. How could I possibly have any improper thoughts about her?"

"I know you don’t have improper thoughts about her," Sun Qianran leaned against Pei Tao’s arm, greedily inhaling his scent, a strange melancholy rising in her heart. "I’m only telling you how others might feel. When I heard Xiang Xu say you had kept Yu Yuan in the study to listen to your poetry lectures, I felt a pang of jealousy. If Director Zhao finds out, I fear he would feel the same."

chapters.title: Winning Him Over
chapters.content:
Pei Tao gently held his wife, feeling a mix of helplessness and heartache.

Sun Qianran, though born of noble status, had a naturally frail constitution, which made her prone to self-pity deep down.

"Thank you for the reminder, my lady. I should indeed be more cautious about collaborating with Minister Zhao."

"Does my lord think I am being petty?"

"How could I?" Pei Tao lightly kissed her hair. "I will consider carefully the matter of Yu Wan in the study."

After finishing her meal in the kitchen, Yu Wan returned to the courtyard to find Zhao Qi already seated in a chair under the eaves of Zhao Xuanyou’s veranda, resting.

When Zhao Qi saw Yu Wan approaching, he directly ordered, "I want sour plum soup this afternoon."

Yu Wan curtsied to him. "Your Highness has already had three bowls of rose dew this morning. It’s not good to have too much sweet soup."

Zhao Qi flew into a rage. "Is it any of your business?"

Yu Wan smiled respectfully, her clear black-and-white eyes shimmering with vitality, her manner polite and restrained. "This servant will prepare perilla water for Your Highness and ask the cook to steam a basket of pine pollen cakes. They are both refreshing and delicious."

That did sound good. Zhao Qi couldn’t find fault with Yu Wan’s attentive service and cheerful demeanor.

He gave a cold "Hmph." "Then let’s try it. If it’s not good, don’t blame me for throwing it in your face."

Yu Wan only smiled without speaking.

In her heart, however, she grumbled that compared to Zhao Qi, Zhao Xuanyou was much better. At least Zhao Xuanyou’s emotions were stable; whether he was angry or sad, he never smashed things or hit servants.

Seeing Zhao Qi closing his eyes to rest, Yu Wan bowed and retreated.

But as soon as she bent her waist, a sharp pain shot through her.

She let out a soft "Ah," one hand supporting her waist, the other leaning against the wall.

Zhao Qi, disturbed by her noise, opened his eyes and saw her like this. He frowned. "What are you doing? I haven’t even thrown anything at you yet."

"This servant… sprained her waist a few days ago. Just now, when I bent over carelessly, it hurt a little. It’s already fine, please forgive me, Your Highness."

Sprained her waist?

Zhao Qi was initially confused, but as he watched Yu Wan straighten up while holding her waist, the scene of her carrying a table out of the room a few days ago suddenly flashed in his mind.

"Hahaha," he burst into laughter. "Did you sprain your waist that day when you moved the table?"

"Yes." Yu Wan admitted reluctantly.

"Serves you right!" Zhao Qi cursed viciously. "Who told you to talk back to me?"

"It was this servant’s fault. I won’t disturb Your Highness’s rest anymore."

Zhao Qi closed his eyes and continued resting. After a moment, he opened them a slit, watching Yu Wan move slowly toward the house like a turtle. He gave a soft scoff and went back to sleep.

As long as she didn’t bend over, Yu Wan didn’t feel the pain.

Once inside, she quickly found a chair and sat down, pressing her back against it. She indeed felt much more comfortable.

After resting for a while, she went to the couch and lay down. Her whole body relaxed, and she fell into a deep sleep. When she woke up, she sat up with the help of the couch and let out a long sigh.

Zhao Xuanyou was right; her injury wasn’t serious and was healing quickly.

That morning, she had needed Xiang Xu’s help to get up, but now she could do it slowly by herself.

She changed her clothes and went to the courtyard. Zhao Qi was already practicing his horse stance in the shade of a tree.

When he saw Yu Wan come out, Zhao Qi glanced at her and scolded, "Lazy girl, you sleep longer than your master."

Yu Wan accepted the scolding with a smile, then went to the kitchen to prepare perilla water and asked the cook to steam pine pollen cakes.

By the time Zhao Qi finished an hour of horse stance practice, she immediately served the snacks and drink.

The perilla water was excellent for relieving summer heat. Zhao Qi drank a large bowl and felt all his fatigue disappear. Then he took a bite of the pine pollen cake and found it delicious.

As he ate the cake, his gaze lingered on Yu Wan.

Though she was a lazy girl who liked to talk back, she was indeed clever and capable.

He wiped his hands with a handkerchief and cleared his throat. "For now, I’ll let you serve in the study."

Yu Wan was overjoyed that the troublesome prince had actually agreed to let her listen in and learn. Her beautiful eyes sparkled even brighter.

Zhao Qi looked at her smiling, self-satisfied expression and instinctively wanted to mock her. But when he met her clear gaze, he ended up swallowing his words.

He stopped looking at her and ordered his guards to invite Pei Tao to the study.

When Pei Tao arrived, he saw a rare harmonious scene.

Zhao Qi was lazily writing poetry on paper, while Yu Wan stood beside him, grinding ink. Zhao Qi would write a line, discard the paper, and Yu Wan would still praise him before quickly replacing it with a fresh sheet.

"Prince Zhao."

Zhao Qi saw him and threw his brush onto the table.

"I don’t know what’s wrong with the people in this courtyard. Every single one of them makes me wait."

Pei Tao stepped forward, picked up a discarded sheet of paper from the floor, and read it.

To be honest, Zhao Qi’s poetry wasn’t bad; it just completely ignored the rules of prosody.

"Does Your Highness still want to listen to the Book of Songs?" Pei Tao asked.

"As you wish."

Pei Tao nodded slightly.

Since Zhao Qi was no longer young, the Book of Songs was a bit too simple for him. So Pei Tao took out a prepared policy essay and lectured on the current Ministry of Works’ river channel repairs.

The study was bright and clean. Pei Tao spoke eloquently.

Zhao Qi was clearly more attentive than in the morning. He didn’t let Pei Tao do all the talking and occasionally interjected with a few comments.

Some of his questions were off the mark, but others hit the nail on the head.

However, what surprised Pei Tao even more was Yu Wan.

Anyone, even a peddler or a soldier, could appreciate poetry and songs, so it wasn’t strange that Yu Wan was drawn to it in the morning.

But the topic of river engineering; Yu Wan was listening intently to that as well.

As Pei Tao and Zhao Qi discussed, Yu Wan’s expression gradually became serious.

By the time the hour-long lecture ended, she still seemed immersed in the policy essay.

Pei Tao’s gaze fell on her. She felt his scrutiny and quickly composed herself, then respectfully stepped forward to tidy up Zhao Qi’s desk.

"Prince Zhao, in the future, should Yu Wan be allowed to serve here during the lectures?" Pei Tao asked in a deep voice.

Zhao Qi frowned. "Wasn’t it you who called her in?"

"If Your Highness feels that Yu Wan’s presence here distracts you from your studies, then of course I cannot keep her here."

Hypocritical.

Zhao Qi curled his lip and glanced at Yu Wan.

Yu Wan’s expression dimmed slightly. She was nervously watching him.

Recalling how she had dared to talk back to him before, and now she was meekly seeking his approval, the corners of his mouth couldn’t help but lift, and his heart wavered slightly.

To be honest, Yu Wan was quick-witted. She prepared snacks, made perilla water, fanned him when he was hot, and wiped his sweat when he perspired. Even the little eunuchs in the palace weren’t this attentive.

Moreover, Yu Wan was beautiful. Having her around was indeed pleasing to the eye.

Especially since Yu Wan listened to the lectures so seriously. With her standing there, even the dry Four Books and Five Classics, and the tedious policy essays, seemed to become more interesting.

"Let her stay for now. I’ll drive her out when I’m unhappy."

Yu Wan’s heart had been in her throat, but hearing Zhao Qi’s words, she finally relaxed.

Before she could express her gratitude, she saw a familiar tall figure appear at the doorway.

---

chapters.title: The Beauty's Trap
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou wore a light blue thin robe, his hair tied with a jade crown, tall and straight.

It was clear he had changed and tidied himself up after returning.

Yu Wan was no fool. Meeting his deep, contemplative gaze, she knew he was displeased that she wasn’t there to serve him when he returned, yet he found her in the study.

Fortunately, she had already obtained Zhao Qi’s permission. No matter how displeased Zhao Xuanyou was, he had to give Zhao Qi some face.

She lowered her head and stood behind Zhao Qi, not daring to speak.

"Minister Zhao, you’re back. Any gains from the hunting ground today?"

"In reply to Your Highness, I hunted two deer." Zhao Qi was quick-witted. The moment Zhao Xuanyou appeared, he noticed his gaze was on Yu Wan.

Originally, keeping Yu Wan in the study was a trivial matter, but seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s displeasure, Zhao Qi was overjoyed.

He stood up and walked to Zhao Xuanyou’s side. "This maid of yours is quite capable. Coincidentally, I didn’t bring any palace maids this time, so let her serve in the study."

"I only brought one maid with me this time."

"Don’t be so stingy," Zhao Qi patted his shoulder. "It’s fine. Besides, during the day, you’re either teaching me or accompanying His Majesty. You won’t need her, so I’ll go to the Emperor and have your contribution recorded."

With that, Zhao Qi turned to Yu Wan. "Tomorrow, I want eight treasure cakes."

"Yes."

After Zhao Qi left, Yu Wan glanced at Zhao Xuanyou and found his face dark as thunder.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded to Pei Tao, who smiled in acknowledgment. After a brief exchange of pleasantries, Zhao Xuanyou turned and left.

Yu Wan curtsied to Pei Tao and whispered, "Thank you, Minister Pei."

Earlier, when Pei Tao suddenly asked Zhao Qi, Yu Wan had thought he changed his mind and no longer wanted her to learn secretly. Now that Zhao Xuanyou had appeared, she finally understood Pei Tao’s intention.

Pei Tao keeping her in the study was neither proper nor reasonable.

The study was a place for Zhao Qi, her master, to study, and she was Zhao Xuanyou’s maid; it wasn’t Pei Tao’s place to order her around.

Now that Zhao Qi had agreed, it forced Zhao Xuanyou to accept it as well, making her presence in the study legitimate.

Pei Tao gave a faint smile. "I didn’t really do much to help. You should thank yourself."

Earlier, when Pei Tao had invited her to help, it was on a whim. At lunch, after Sun Qianran’s reminder, he realized this might anger Zhao Xuanyou and was rather inappropriate.

Zhao Qi had been resistant to the idea of Yu Wan staying in the study. When he asked, Pei Tao wasn’t sure how Zhao Qi would respond.

It was Yu Wan’s own ability that changed Zhao Qi’s opinion, allowing her to stay in the study.

Yu Wan was slightly taken aback, then smiled at Pei Tao before hurriedly chasing after Zhao Xuanyou.

Inside the room, Zhao Xuanyou sat in a chair, his expression shifting between gloom and calm.

Yu Wan knew he was displeased. She stepped forward to pour him a cup of tea, and without waiting for his word, respectfully began massaging his shoulders.

Zhao Xuanyou, with a fire burning in his heart, reached out and grabbed Yu Wan’s wrist, pulling her toward him.

Yu Wan was no match for his strength. She spun halfway and fell into his embrace.

"Master, the door is still open."

It was still daylight. Anyone passing by the door could see her sitting on his lap. Wouldn’t that be a laughingstock?

Zhao Xuanyou clearly didn’t care. He just stared at her darkly.

"Who told you to go work there?"

Yu Wan replied, "When this servant passed by the study, Minister Pei asked me to help prepare drinks and snacks for Prince Zhao. I suppose Prince Zhao enjoyed them, which is why he wanted to keep me there."

Zhao Qi had ordered Yu Wan to prepare eight treasure cakes for tomorrow before leaving, so this explanation held up.

Zhao Xuanyou stared intently into Yu Wan’s eyes. "You seemed very willing."

Yu Wan’s eyes did sparkle with joy, and she couldn’t hide it. "The work in the study is light. Preparing tea, water, and snacks isn’t troublesome."

"Isn’t lying in the room more comfortable?"

At this point, Yu Wan realized that lying wouldn’t work. She admitted honestly, "Today, Minister Pei lectured Prince Zhao on the Book of Songs. This servant found it very interesting. Being able to work in the study allows me to learn more, so I was happy."

In truth, it wasn’t just the Book of Songs that interested her. That afternoon, when Pei Tao lectured on river management, she found it even more fascinating.

She would never have the chance to attend school in this life. Now, by borrowing Zhao Qi’s influence, she could listen to lectures from the top scholar; an opportunity that even scholars everywhere would envy. Of course she was happy.

"You want to study?" Zhao Xuanyou was somewhat surprised.

"Master didn’t know, but this servant can read and write a little."

Zhao Xuanyou was indeed surprised.

He remembered that Yu Wan came from a farming family. Later, when her mother got into trouble, they sold their fields and house, and she sold herself to become a maid.

How could someone with such a background be literate?

"It was my mother who taught me. This servant doesn’t know why my mother could read and write. I hope she wakes up soon so this servant’s doubts can be resolved."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yu Wan’s delicate and graceful appearance, recalling the brief glimpse he had of her mother at Yun Shui An.

Although she was now thin and worn, her facial features were still delicate and beautiful. He could imagine how striking she must have been in her youth.

It was strange for such a mother and daughter to live in a village, especially since they were literate.

But he didn’t have the idle interest to dig into their past. He could tell Yu Wan was being truthful. He simply said, "I’m hungry. Go to the kitchen and see what there is to eat."

Yu Wan saw that he wasn’t going to pursue the matter further and knew he had consented. For some reason, her eyes suddenly welled up.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at her and asked strangely, "Are you that happy?"

"No, Master. This servant will go to the kitchen." With that, she placed her hand on Zhao Xuanyou’s shoulder and used it to support her waist as she stood up.

"Your waist is better?"

"It doesn’t hurt as long as I don’t bend."

Yu Wan smiled and went to the kitchen. She soon returned with dinner.

The Pei family, eager to befriend Zhao Xuanyou, had the cook prepare two extra dishes for him every evening, and today was no exception.

Zhao Xuanyou accepted their kindness and had Yu Wan deliver a block of Wuyi tea cake to the Pei couple.

When Yu Wan entered, Pei Tao and Sun Qianran were also having dinner.

"Minister Pei, Madam Pei, the Young Master sent this servant to deliver a tea cake."

This tea cake was a gift from the Emperor, an imperial tribute tea.

After they accepted the tea, Yu Wan curtsied to them and respectfully took her leave.

Sun Qianran, thinking of Yu Wan’s charming smile when she entered, looked at Pei Tao. "It seems that Minister Zhao is not angry about Yu Wan serving in the study."

Pei Tao gave a faint smile.

When Zhao Xuanyou first appeared in the study, his expression was extremely unhappy. It seemed that after returning, Yu Wan had said something to turn the situation around.

"What are you smiling about, my lord?" Sun Qianran asked curiously.

"Nothing. I just admire Yu Wan’s ability to turn the tide."

Sun Qianran said, "Since ancient times, heroes have found it hard to resist the allure of beauty. It seems Minister Zhao has been completely won over by Yu Wan."

Was Yu Wan relying on her beauty?

Perhaps, but Pei Tao felt it wasn’t just that.

Recalling how Yu Wan had listened intently to the lecture in the study that afternoon, Pei Tao had a vague feeling that one day, Yu Wan would make everyone sit up and take notice.

chapters.title: Keep Me Company
chapters.content:
The next morning was quiet and peaceful.

Unlike the previous day, Zhao Qi did not come to cause trouble early in the morning but arrived at the third quarter of the Chen hour (around 8:15 AM).

Zhao Xuanyou had not bothered Yu Wan that morning. After an early meal, he went to the courtyard to practice his swordsmanship.

The hereditary martial art of the Jingyuan Hou (Marquis of Jingyuan) residence was swordplay. Even though Zhao Xuanyou was proficient in all eighteen martial arts, he still practiced swordplay every day without fail.

Zhao Qi entered the courtyard and silently stood to the side, watching Zhao Xuanyou’s robes flutter as he wielded his sword with fluid movements, his body darting swiftly. For a moment, Zhao Qi was mesmerized.

Previously, Zhao Xuanyou had fought Zhao Qi in the training grounds, but the disparity in their skills was so great that Zhao Xuanyou had subdued Zhao Qi without even using any advanced techniques.

Zhao Qi’s own martial arts were poor, but the people around him were all highly skilled, so his understanding of martial arts was not shallow.

He glanced at Yin Ping and Mu Di beside him, his expression also solemn.

Zhao Xuanyou’s martial arts were unfathomable. Even if he hadn’t taken Zhao Qi hostage that day, Yin Ping and Mu Di working together still wouldn’t have been able to defeat him.

What was even more terrifying was that Zhao Xuanyou was in his prime, and even the current Duke of Ningguo would struggle to match him.

"Your Highness."

Zhao Xuanyou finished his sword routine at a steady pace, sheathed his sword, and then cupped his hands in a bow to Zhao Qi.

"Lord Zhao, no need for courtesy," Zhao Qi said in a foul mood. Given the current situation, not only could he not defeat Zhao Xuanyou, but he didn’t even know how long it would take to last ten moves against him.

He could only say weakly, "That sword routine looks pretty good. Is it your marquis family’s hereditary swordplay?"

"Your Highness has a good eye."

"No wonder your Jingyuan Hou residence has stood in the northwest for so many years. You have some real skill."

"If Your Highness likes it, this subject can teach it to you."

In front of the imperial family, a subject had no reason to keep secrets.

"There’s no need," Zhao Qi knew his own limits. Though he was arrogant, he was not foolish. "For now, I should practice my horse stance first."

It seemed his previous scolding had not been in vain. Hearing Zhao Qi’s response, Zhao Xuanyou subtly curved the corners of his lips.

"If Your Highness can persist in practicing the horse stance for a year, your foundation will be solid. When you wield that spear of yours, its power will be at least ten times what it is now."

Ten times?

"Really? Can it really be ten times?" Zhao Qi’s eyes lit up, looking at Zhao Xuanyou in disbelief.

Zhao Xuanyou calmly replied, "If Your Highness does not believe this subject, you can ask the guards beside you."

"No need to ask. Of course I believe you. You are the commander of the Mingchan Guards. Who could be more skilled than you?"

Zhao Qi took a deep breath, smoothed his clothes, and seriously assumed the horse stance position.

"Your Highness practiced for one hour each of the past two days. Would you like to try practicing for two full hours today?"

Two hours didn’t sound like much.

"Sure."

Zhao Qi casually agreed without a second thought.

Zhao Xuanyou added, "But you must not stop to rest in the middle. If you do, all your previous efforts will be wasted."

"Easy. If I don’t rest, I won’t rest."

Yu Wan, seeing Zhao Qi’s arrival, busied herself in the kitchen.

The pastries from the day before had been made by the cook of the Pei residence, but since Zhao Qi had ordered them through her, she, as a servant from another household, couldn’t keep troubling the other family’s cook.

That morning, she had specially asked the cook for guidance and personally steamed some eight-treasure cakes. Once the pastries were cooking, she also fried some bohe leaf tea for Zhao Qi.

She was not skilled in cooking, and by the time she finished all this, an hour had already passed.

Yu Wan left the kitchen and saw that Zhao Xuanyou was no longer in the corridor. She had no idea where he had gone.

She turned her head and saw Zhao Qi looking unwell and drenched in sweat. Concerned, she asked, "This servant has made eight-treasure cakes. Would Your Highness like to take a break and have some pastries before continuing?"

"Eat what? I can’t rest today. Go away, don’t disturb me."

Originally, he had thought that practicing for one hour in the morning and one in the afternoon would be the same as practicing for two hours straight.

But who knew that after completing one hour, every subsequent moment would feel excruciatingly long.

His legs felt as if they were about to break, and he could collapse at any moment.

"Can’t I rest?" Yu Wan hadn’t heard his conversation with Zhao Xuanyou. Seeing his condition, she nodded but was still worried as his complexion looked terrible. "Can I at least give you some water?"

Water?

Zhao Qi didn’t know if he was allowed to drink water, but Yu Wan’s words made him realize how parched he was. He hurriedly nodded at her.

Yu Wan quickly went to the kitchen and brought a bowl of cooled bohe leaf tea, which was a refreshing drink perfect for quenching thirst in the summer.

She carried the bowl to Zhao Qi’s side and saw that his youthful face was contorted in pain, as if he could no longer endure. She quickly scooped a spoonful of tea and brought it to Zhao Qi’s lips.

After her mother fell ill, Yu Wan had grown accustomed to attending to her, including feeding her medicine. Now, feeding water to Zhao Qi came naturally to her.

Without needing Zhao Qi to move, she slightly lifted the spoon, and the tea smoothly flowed into his mouth.

Zhao Qi’s thirst was temporarily relieved, and his expression gradually returned to normal, but only for a moment.

When Yu Wan put down the tea bowl and returned to the courtyard, Zhao Qi’s complexion was even worse than before.

"Your Highness, are you alright?" Yu Wan asked with concern.

Zhao Qi felt he could no longer endure. Looking at Yu Wan, he impatiently cursed, "Get lost."

Yu Wan was not afraid of being scolded, but seeing him in such a state, she was worried something might happen to him.

He was a prince, after all. If he died here, even if it had nothing to do with her, she feared she would be blamed and punished.

Seeing that Zhao Qi ignored her, she turned to Yin Ping and Mu Di, who were standing outside the courtyard, and asked worriedly, "Can His Highness really not continue practicing? I’m worried about him..."

"Miss, rest assured. His Highness will be fine."

Yin Ping and Mu Di were both trained to the standards of elite guards. Practicing the horse stance for two hours was as ordinary to them as eating or drinking. They didn’t think it would be life-threatening.

Zhao Qi had been pampered since childhood, so it was natural that he couldn’t endure hardship for a while.

In their hearts, they all hoped that Zhao Qi would truly improve. It was rare for him to make up his mind, and if he couldn’t get through this hurdle, it would be even harder for him to muster the resolve again in the future.

"Stop worrying about nothing! Don’t stand there cursing me!" Zhao Qi shouted angrily.

"It was this servant’s unnecessary concern."

Seeing that he still had the energy to scold her, it seemed he was indeed fine.

Yu Wan decided to keep her distance to avoid being scolded again.

She lowered her head and walked to the side. Before she could slip into the house, Zhao Qi shouted from the courtyard, "Come back here!"

Was he calling her?

Yu Wan decided to play dumb.

"Lazy girl! Come back!" Zhao Qi shouted, "I’m talking to you, Yu Wan! Come back!"

Since he had called her by name, Yu Wan had no choice but to turn back into the courtyard.

"Does Your Highness want more water?"

He had just drunk a bowl of bohe leaf tea, so Zhao Qi wasn’t thirsty.

He had called Yu Wan back only because he had suddenly realized that while he was busy scolding her earlier, he hadn’t noticed the pain in his legs as much.

Seeing that he didn’t speak, Yu Wan asked again, "Does Your Highness have any other orders?"

Yu Wan asked earnestly, her beautiful eyes filled with clarity, as clear as a spring.

Faced with such eyes, Zhao Qi faltered for a moment.

"You..." he said dryly, "Don’t leave. Stay here... keep me company."

---

chapters.title: A Beauty’s Invitation
chapters.content:
"Keep... keep you company?" Yu Wan stared at him, her gaze filled with disbelief. This young prince had been calling her "lazy girl" just moments ago, and now he was asking her to keep him company.

But since he was a prince and had given the order, Yu Wan had no choice but to obey. She respectfully replied, "Yes," and stood to the side.

Zhao Qi was still not satisfied.

"Didn’t I tell you to stay? I meant for you to talk, not just stand there like a post!"

Talk?

Yu Wan understood. He found it hard to endure standing there alone and wanted her to stay and chat to pass the time.

With no other choice, Yu Wan asked about the interesting places around the imperial palace.

Zhao Qi followed the emperor to Lichuan every year to escape the summer heat, so he was naturally familiar with the surroundings. He knew which villages had beautiful scenery, which towns were lively, and which mountains had rare and exotic creatures.

The sun climbed higher, and even though Zhao Qi was standing in the shade, sweat still beaded on his face.

Yu Wan brought warm water to wipe his face. Seeing that he was parched, she once again fed him water with a spoon, just as she had before.

He had only drunk half when the two princesses she had encountered before, Yi’an and Yi’ning, entered together, followed closely by Zhao Xuanyou.

So that was where he had disappeared to for so long; he had been accompanying the princesses.

As Yi’an and Yi’ning, dressed in colorful and embroidered clothes, entered, all the servants in the courtyard bowed.

"Greetings, Your Highnesses."

"You may rise," Yi’an said, looking in high spirits, her expression even brighter than the last time they had met.

In contrast, Princess Yi’ning seemed lost in thought, her gaze wandering, as if deep in contemplation.

Zhao Xuanyou, walking at the rear, maintained his usual composed expression. But as he entered the courtyard, he glanced at Zhao Qi before his gaze firmly settled on Yu Wan.

Yu Wan felt a sense of foreboding and looked at him innocently.

Zhao Xuanyou seemed to snort through his nose and ordered the servant behind him, Yuan Qing, "Go inside and bring out chairs for the two princesses."

"Yes." Yuan Qing quickly brought out chairs.

Princess Yi’an, holding Yi’ning’s hand, took a seat. Looking at Zhao Qi practicing nearby, she smiled and said, "Since receiving Lord Zhao’s guidance, Seventh Brother has become even more diligent. If Father finds out, he will surely be very pleased."

Princess Yi’ning knew she was praising Zhao Xuanyou, but her words were not false. Zhao Xuanyou indeed had some skill; with just a little effort, he had tamed this wild horse.

"Practicing for one day is easy, practicing for two days is easy, but practicing for a year or two is difficult. Seventh Brother must not give up halfway."

"It’s rare for Seventh Brother to make up his mind. As his elder sister, you shouldn’t discourage him." Yi’an smiled warmly at Zhao Qi, exuding the demeanor of an elder sister. "Just now, as we approached, I heard you talking. What were you discussing so animatedly?"

Zhao Qi didn’t want to pay her any mind, but he had to admit that with someone talking beside him, he didn’t focus as much on the agony of holding the horse stance.

"I was telling Yu Wan about the interesting places around Lichuan."

Hearing Zhao Qi mention Yu Wan, Princess Yi’an’s gaze shifted to the maidservant beside him. She immediately recognized her as Zhao Xuanyou’s concubine.

The green summer dress outlined her slender shoulders and tiny waist. The hem of her skirt was embroidered with exquisite grape and vine patterns. As Yu Wan lowered her head, a hint of her delicate, fair collarbone was revealed.

She was indeed beautiful, but unfortunately, she looked too much like Cui Yichu. Yi’an felt annoyed just looking at her.

Fortunately, she was just a maidservant, much easier to deal with than Cui Yichu, and not worth her attention.

"Lichuan does have many interesting places," Princess Yi’an said with a smile.

The imperial palace was magnificent, quiet, and spacious, but staying there for too long was bound to become tedious.

The princes and princesses were not as restricted as the imperial concubines when it came to going out. Rarely away from the imperial palace, they naturally didn’t want to stay cooped up all day. Every few days, they would slip out to play; sometimes to nearby mountains and streams, sometimes to hunting grounds for riding and archery, and sometimes to nearby towns to stroll around.

"Elder Sister, do you really find this place interesting?" Princess Yi’ning immediately understood what Yi’an was thinking and, instead of agreeing, she countered, "You can’t hunt, so the hunting grounds are out of the question. You don’t like walking, so you never go hiking. As for that town, last year when we went, you said it was boring and even scolded Third Royal Brother for kindly taking us out."

Princess Yi’an hummed softly in her heart but kept her smile on her face.

"Last time we went to the small town, it was too hot, and I was very irritable. Now that I think about it, the braised chicken that Third Royal Brother bought for us was quite delicious. The weather has been clear and pleasant these past few days. Why don’t we go again?"

Princess Yi’ning did not like this elder sister of hers. They spent every day together simply because being alone was too boring.

Knowing that Yi’an’s suggestion was not her true intention, but since Yi’an was favored by the empress, as long as she went to the empress and said she wanted to leave the palace to play, the empress would surely agree.

Going out was certainly better than being cooped up in the palace.

Seeing this, Princess Yi’ning decided to go along with it. She looked at Zhao Xuanyou and said, "If the two of us leave the palace, Mother might not feel at ease. Lord Zhao is highly skilled in martial arts and familiar with the common people. How about he escorts us to Cangxi Town?"

Seeing that Yi’ning was finally cooperating, Yi’an was secretly pleased. Fearing that Zhao Xuanyou would refuse, she quickly added, "Lord Zhao has to teach Seventh Brother martial arts and also serve Father. He probably doesn’t have the time."

"If Seventh Brother practices his horse stance every day, he doesn’t need Lord Zhao to watch over him. Why doesn’t Elder Sister ask Father? As long as Father agrees, it’s settled."

Yi’an nodded in agreement. "Alright, I’ll ask Father when I accompany him for tea today."

The two sisters, in perfect harmony, had invoked the emperor, leaving Zhao Xuanyou with no chance to speak, and thus the matter was settled.

Yu Wan had been standing to the side with her head lowered the entire time. After hearing all this, she finally understood that Princess Yi’an had taken a liking to Zhao Xuanyou.

Otherwise, why would they want to go out in disguise, and instead of bringing any of the many Imperial Guards from the palace, they specifically wanted Zhao Xuanyou to accompany them?

She actually liked Zhao Xuanyou?

It wasn’t that Zhao Xuanyou was unworthy, but he was Cui Yichu’s ex-husband, and Cui Yichu had once been her study companion. This princess seemed to have no reservations at all.

Yu Wan’s gaze subtly shifted to Princess Yi’an.

She had only met Princess Yi’an twice and had never spoken directly to her, but she could tell that this princess was a formidable person.

Even though Princess Yi’ning seemed displeased with her, whenever the two sisters were together, Princess Yi’ning was the one being led by the nose.

Would Zhao Xuanyou become a prince consort...

In her idle moments, Yu Wan had thought about her future.

Zhao Xuanyou cared for her, and treated her well. If things continued this way, perhaps she could try to win his favor and secure a position as a concubine in the marquis’s residence, bearing him children. That might be a viable path for survival.

But if the future mistress of the household were to be a noble princess like Yi’an, she would certainly clean house first. Not to mention Yu Wan, even Fen Jirou and Feng Chai would be swept out the door.

Before Zhao Xuanyou and Princess Yi’an’s relationship was finalized, she needed to quickly gather some money. That way, when the time came to leave the marquis’s residence, she would have the means to support herself.

chapters.title: Is She Jealous?
chapters.content:
"Daydreaming again?"

Zhao Xuanyou's deep voice interrupted Yu Wan's thoughts.

"Master," Yu Wan suddenly came to her senses, only to find that Zhao Xuanyou was already standing in front of her. The two princesses who had been sitting on the chairs a moment ago were gone.

They left?

"Quite bold, daring to not pay respects even as the princesses depart."

It was a grave offense to be distracted while serving one's master. Yu Wan hastily replied, "This servant knows her mistake."

Zhao Xuanyou gave her an inscrutable look before turning to Zhao Qi.

"Two hours have passed. Your Highness may rest for today."

"Has it been two hours?" Zhao Qi still maintained his horse-riding stance, looking at Zhao Xuanyou with disbelief.

Compared to his usual vigor, Zhao Qi now looked like a frost-bitten eggplant, too exhausted to even mock the playful exchange between Yi'an and Yi'ning.

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement and praised, "Your Highness did well today. It has earned my admiration."

Honestly, Zhao Qi had only been training with him for three days. It was reasonable if he couldn't last two hours today, yet he had managed to endure.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou's praise, Zhao Qi was too tired to boast or act tough. He merely nodded.

"The beginning is always the hardest. Tomorrow, Your Highness will train for another two hours, and it will feel as easy as training for one hour today."

Zhao Qi tried to stand straight, but his legs gave out, and he stumbled to the side. Fortunately, Yu Wan and Yuan Qing were quick, each supporting him from one side.

"Be careful, Your Highness."

Seeing him fall, his two guards, Yin Ping and Mu Di, rushed in from the courtyard and helped steady him.

"Take His Highness back first. Have a eunuch massage his legs. I'll inform Minister Pei to delay this afternoon's lesson by an hour."

"Understood."

Zhao Xuanyou spoke concisely. After all, Yin Ping and Mu Di were martial artists and knew how to handle such situations.

After the master and servants left the small courtyard, Zhao Xuanyou turned to Yu Wan.

Having stood in the courtyard with Zhao Qi for a long time, the summer heat had already made her forehead glisten with a thin layer of sweat. Strangely, sweating was usually an embarrassing affair, but it didn't look unseemly on Yu Wan. Her face seemed to have been moistened by water, making her skin appear even more tender.

"Master," Yu Wan looked at him ingratiatingly.

Zhao Xuanyou walked straight into the room. Once the door was closed, he coldly said, "You follow him around all day. Aren't you tired?"

Going to the study was indeed something Yu Wan had fought for, but today she was wronged.

Yu Wan made a bitter face. "It wasn't that this servant wanted to follow His Highness. It was His Highness who couldn't hold on much longer and asked this servant to stay by his side and talk to distract him."

"Why you? He has attendants."

How would she know? She could only speak cautiously, "Perhaps His Highness's attendants seem too quiet."

Zhao Xuanyou was well aware of how likable Yu Wan was.

He had made many exceptions for her sake.

As for Zhao Qi, that young lad, Zhao Xuanyou didn't have any particular thoughts about him. It was just that Yu Wan had injured her waist a few days ago. From morning to night, she had been keeping Zhao Qi company, and he didn't know when she would fully recover.

Zhao Xuanyou said irritably, "Lie down and rest for a while. Don't wander around so much in the future."

"Thank you, Young Master. This servant is fortunate to have such a good master." Yu Wan was indeed tired. She followed his words, took off her outer garment, and lay down on the couch.

Her waist and back finally relaxed completely, making her unable to help but let out a comfortable "mm."

The sound was soft and tender, instantly igniting Zhao Xuanyou's desire. He lay down on the couch beside her.

Feeling his intense gaze on her, as if flames were flickering in his eyes, Yu Wan avoided his gaze and softly said, "It's almost time for the meal. I wonder what dishes we're having today."

Zhao Xuanyou did want to do it.

But he wasn't so lust-driven to lose his mind. This small courtyard housed two families. Apart from the Pei couple, there were many attendants, maids, and cooks in the courtyard.

No matter how urgent his desires were, he couldn't pull Yu Wan into that act in broad daylight.

Ah, Honghui Hall was better.

Zhao Xuanyou rarely felt such a longing to return home.

Seeing that he didn't make any further moves, Yu Wan slightly relaxed. She racked her brains for something to say to distract him.

"Where did Master go earlier? How did you end up returning with the two princesses?"

After finishing her tasks in the kitchen, Yu Wan had not seen Zhao Xuanyou anywhere.

Hearing her ask about this, Zhao Xuanyou's eyes flickered, a hint of a smile appearing in his gaze.

"Do you find it strange that I was with the princesses?"

Strange?

Yu Wan didn't find it strange at all. She was just making conversation.

"This servant is just curious. If Master doesn't want to say, then forget it."

"Earlier, the two princesses came to speak with Madame Pei. It seems Madame Pei mentioned a very secluded place upstream. The princesses wanted to go, but they were worried about snakes, so they asked me to accompany them."

Again, they asked him to escort them...

The imperial family had been coming to Lichuan for summer retreats for years. Even the young Zhao Qi knew the area like the back of his hand. How could there still be places in the summer palace that the two princesses hadn't visited? And they needed Madame Pei to point the way?

Yu Wan found the excuse somewhat laughable, but since they were princesses, they could say whatever they pleased.

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze remained fixed on Yu Wan's face. He found her current expression quite amusing.

He narrowed his eyes and suddenly asked, "What are you thinking about?"

"Nothing." Having spent a lot of time with Zhao Xuanyou day and night, she had become much bolder when speaking to him. "This servant just thinks that the Lichuan Summer Palace has been built for so many years, and His Majesty comes every year. The two princesses should have been here many times as well. How could there still be places in the palace they haven't been to?"

Hearing Yu Wan's analysis of the princesses' behavior, Zhao Xuanyou didn't find it inappropriate at all. On the contrary, after hearing her reasoning, a sense of pleasure welled up in his heart.

"Do you mean the two princesses deliberately found an excuse to talk to Madame Pei?"

"This servant didn't say that."

"Then do you mean the two princesses were making something out of nothing?"

Yu Wan didn't continue. She just smiled at Zhao Xuanyou.

Having stayed in the Marquis's residence for a long time, she knew how to gauge her words.

Princesses Yi'an and Yi'ning were noble and precious. A few vague, light-hearted jokes were fine, but if she really said something substantial, it would plant the seeds of disaster. Who knew when old scores would be settled?

After all, she had noticed Princess Yi'an's affection for Zhao Xuanyou. Could Zhao Xuanyou not see it?

All along, she knew Zhao Xuanyou was as sharp as dust.

Back then, he had felt that he had been greatly wronged by the Xingguo Duke's family. Who knew if he didn't want to regain face in the next marriage alliance?

Cui Yichu was Princess Yi'an's study companion. If he married Princess Yi'an, the Xingguo Duke's family would become a laughingstock.

Thinking of this, Yu Wan couldn't say another word.

Zhao Xuanyou didn't wait for her answer. He reached out and pinched her chin, leaning close to her and whispering, "Or, are you jealous seeing me with the two princesses?"

---

chapters.title: Under the Moon
chapters.content:
Yu Wan hadn't expected Zhao Xuanyou to ask that.

Jealous...

She just wanted to find out Zhao Xuanyou's plans so she could make her own arrangements accordingly.

Of course, she couldn't tell Zhao Xuanyou about her little schemes.

If he thought she was jealous, that wasn't so bad.

Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou without flinching, her dark eyes clear and innocent.

"This servant isn't jealous. I was just... just curious. It's all this servant's fault for talking nonsense and upsetting Master."

Zhao Xuanyou's brows knitted slightly. Since they were too close, Yu Wan silently moved back a bit.

He reached out and circled her slender waist, leaving her with no retreat.

Yu Wan was a natural beauty. The closer he got, the more he felt her skin was flawless and delicate.

She timidly said, "This servant knows her mistake. Master, please let this matter go."

After spending so much time together, she understood what kind of demeanor Zhao Xuanyou preferred.

"Hmm?"

Zhao Xuanyou had originally intended to tease her about being jealous. But now, with them so close they could feel each other's breath, other thoughts ignited in him.

He gently pulled Yu Wan a little closer, and their lips touched.

Yu Wan let out a soft "mm," but before she could say anything else, she had no chance.

The man held her while undoing her hair. The jade hairpin fell to the ground with a "clink."

He paid no mind to it, lifting her entirely and placing her on the couch.

Yu Wan supported herself with both hands, sitting at the edge of the couch with her hair scattered, looking up at him and softly saying, "This servant hasn't even washed up today."

"Does it matter if I don't mind?"

This... it's broad daylight...

Seeing her frowning, Zhao Xuanyou chuckled inwardly. Of course, this courtyard wasn't a place where they could do as they pleased. He went to the desk.

In the afternoon, when Zhao Qi came for his lesson, he was still listless. Yu Wan stood by to attend to him without much effort.

After the lesson, Yu Wan saw Zhao Qi off and then went to prepare Zhao Xuanyou's dinner. As soon as she entered the room, Zhao Xuanyou pulled her into his arms and pushed her toward the couch. Before he could speak, there was a knock at the door.

"Master."

It was Yuan Qing.

Zhao Xuanyou's eyes darkened. He suddenly felt that attendants should be as clever as Yuan Mai. At least, Yuan Mai would never come knocking if he saw him and Yu Wan entering the room and closing the door.

Yu Wan saw his expression and couldn't help but smile. She asked playfully, "Master is about to have dinner. What's the matter?"

"Minister Pei said he has prepared a table of food and wine by the stream and would like to invite Master to drink under the moonlight."

Zhao Xuanyou almost shot a fierce glance.

He had a beautiful woman as soft as jade sitting at the edge of the couch in front of him. What was this about drinking under the moon?

Yu Wan's lips curled slightly. She stood up and straightened his collar.

"Today is a clear day. The moonlight should be beautiful at night. Master, you should go."

Seeing her smug expression, Zhao Xuanyou ultimately couldn't let her off. He reached out and pinched her waist.

He knew her weak spot well. With this move, Yu Wan couldn't help but cry out.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled her back into his arms, using his chin to press her head against his shoulder.

"Wait obediently."

"I know." Yu Wan replied in a soft, coquettish voice.

Knowing she had just been in pain, he reached out to rub the spot for her.

Yu Wan quickly pushed his hand away, her face reddening. "This servant isn't in pain."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her embarrassed appearance, his gaze darkening again. Thinking about what Pei Tao might want to discuss, he finally suppressed his amorous thoughts.

He merely glanced at the silver hairpin in Yu Wan's hair and asked, "Where is the jade hairpin?"

Yu Wan replied, "Has Master forgotten? The one that broke at noon was chipped. This servant prefers to wear the silver hairpin."

"It's just a hairpin."

"This servant only has four or five hairpins. Can they withstand Master breaking them repeatedly?"

Listening to her coquettish complaint, Zhao Xuanyou lightly hummed, "I'll give you ten more another day."

Ten?

Please, no more jade hairpins. Pawnshops undervalued jade. It would be better to give gold hairpins. Gold was the most liquid asset in the market.

Though she was pleased inside, Yu Wan maintained a calm exterior.

"It was Master who offered. This servant didn't ask for it."

If she didn't ask for it, why was she so reluctant to part with a hairpin?

Zhao Xuanyou could see through her little schemes but didn't mind at all. He hummed and walked straight out.

Outside, the sky wasn't dark yet. Looking up, it was a light gray-blue, with a golden outline in the middle.

It was indeed a clear night.

Zhao Xuanyou followed Yuan Qing out of the courtyard and along the path to the stream. He saw Pei Tao and Sun Qianran already seated at a table by the stream, with two maids setting out bowls and chopsticks.

Pei Tao was wearing a dark long robe tonight, almost blending into the twilight. Sun Qianran, on the other hand, was dressed brightly, though she had a cape draped over her shoulders, which was uncommon in summer. Clearly, sitting here for a meal wasn't suitable for her.

Both of them were present?

Zhao Xuanyou approached without showing any emotion. Pei Tao saw him and stood up, cupping his hands in greeting.

"Minister Zhao."

"Minister Pei, Madame Pei." Zhao Xuanyou responded coolly.

Sun Qianran smiled, "I'm not feeling well, so I won't stand. Please forgive me, Minister Zhao."

Her voice sounded weak and floaty. Zhao Xuanyou, of course, wouldn't take offense.

"Minister Zhao, please have a seat."

Zhao Xuanyou sat across from Pei Tao. Pei Tao poured him a cup of wine. Zhao Xuanyou smelled it and detected a faint bamboo leaf fragrance.

"This wine is new to me."

Pei Tao said, "It's homemade bamboo leaf wine from my family. Please try it, Minister Zhao."

"Don't let Minister Zhao start drinking as soon as he sits down. The wind is strong here. Let's eat first, or the food will get cold." Sun Qianran gently reminded.

"It was my oversight. Please forgive me, Minister Zhao. Please, eat."

As the guest, Zhao Xuanyou didn't stand on ceremony. After nodding, he picked up his chopsticks and first tasted the main dish.

The Pei family's cook had excellent skills. Today, to entertain a guest, Pei Tao had brought out his best dishes. The steamed Jiaji fish Zhao Xuanyou ate was exquisitely prepared; perfectly seasoned, tender, and delicious.

He gave Pei Tao a slight nod.

Pei Tao smiled slightly, picked up his chopsticks, first served Sun Qianran, and then began to eat.

The three of them didn't talk much during the meal, only occasionally commenting on the scenery of Lichuan. By the time the sky was completely dark, the orange-yellow moonlight spilled onto the stream, making it even brighter than before dusk.

"Xiang Xu, the wind is strong here. You and Minister Zhao continue enjoying yourselves. I'll return to the room first."

"Hongxu, help Madame back to the room."

Hongxu quickly stepped forward, helping Sun Qianran up and putting the hood of her cape on.

After the mistress and maid had walked far away, Pei Tao turned back, looked at Zhao Xuanyou's empty wine cup, and refilled it for him.

"It seems our family's homemade wine suits Minister Zhao's taste."

There was a hidden meaning in his words. Now that Sun Qianran had left with her maid, the real banquet of the evening could begin.

"It is indeed memorable." Zhao Xuanyou answered truthfully. After clinking glasses with Pei Tao, he paused and then got straight to the point. "Since Madame Pei has returned to her room, if Minister Pei has something to say, you might as well speak directly."

"Minister Zhao is straightforward. I admire that."

Straightforward?

Zhao Xuanyou gave a faint smile but didn't speak. However, the image of Yu Wan sitting at the edge of the couch, supporting herself with both hands and smiling at him, appeared in his mind.

He indeed disliked beating around the bush, but at this moment, he only wanted to end tonight's banquet quickly and return to his room as soon as possible.

chapters.title: Family Vendetta
chapters.content:
Seeing Pei Tao still hesitating, Zhao Xuanyou let his gaze linger on Pei’s refined face for a moment before turning to the babbling stream.

"I am well aware of the grudge between me and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion, but I do not know the grudge between you, Minister Pei, and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion."

His implication was that Pei Tao should first show sincerity by revealing his own grievances with the Xingguo Duke’s mansion before Zhao Xuanyou would continue the conversation.

This request was not unreasonable.

Pei Tao poured himself a cup of wine, lifted it, and drank it in one go. In an instant, his eyes sharpened, and a killing intent radiated from him.

He was originally a very gentle and scholarly man, but with such a look, he suddenly exuded an aura of murder.

Zhao Xuanyou frowned slightly.

"Has the Young Master ever heard of Qingsha Town?"

It sounded familiar, but as for the specifics... Zhao Xuanyou asked, "Is it the place that produces pearls?"

"That’s right. Qingsha Town is by the East Sea. Almost all the common folk there make a living by fishing and pearl diving. The pearls there are rounder and more lustrous than those from other places, so every year, they tribute many pearls to the imperial court."

"Is Minister Pei not from an official family?"

Zhao Xuanyou was not one to judge based on family background, but Pei Tao carried himself with a natural scholarly elegance. How could a pearl diver’s household raise such a refined and distinguished young man?

Pei Tao gave a bitter laugh. "An official family... probably not in the eyes of Minister Zhao."

"Please continue, Minister Pei."

"My father was the magistrate of Qingsha Town. Because the place was too remote, and seeing that I was intelligent, he couldn’t bear to let me be buried there, so he sent me to a academy in Jiangnan to study."

"I see."

"The local Governor Tao was the elder brother of the Xingguo Duke’s wife, the Duke’s brother-in-law. He abused his position to embezzle the pearls that the pearl divers were supposed to tribute to the court, then falsely accused them of not paying enough. The required tribute of pearls kept increasing, driving many pearl diver families to ruin. My father, being of low rank and little influence, initially endured it to protect our family. But seeing so many common folk being oppressed, he could no longer tolerate it. He secretly gathered evidence and submitted a memorial to the court."

"Was his memorial intercepted?"

"It must have been. I learned from a family letter that my father had submitted a memorial, and I was very worried. But at that time, I had no official position and couldn’t help him. By the time I received more news from home, my father had been accused of embezzling pearls and thrown into prison."

Zhao Xuanyou remained calm. "And then?"

If Pei Tao’s father had been convicted of corruption, Pei Tao wouldn’t have been able to enter the capital for the imperial examination, let alone become the top scholar.

Pei Tao took a deep breath, his fair face flushing slightly with anger.

"I was in a hurry to go to Qingsha Town, but my teacher stopped me. He had a private connection with Prime Minister Sun; my current father-in-law. After learning the truth, he wrote a letter to the capital to inquire. My father-in-law had the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Rites investigate. They found that the only evidence against my father was testimonial, with no physical evidence. After the Ministry of Justice questioned the witnesses again, they changed their statements, saying they had made a mistake. Only then was my father released without charge. Unfortunately, my father had suffered greatly in prison for speaking up for the people. After his release, he was broken in spirit and body. He could no longer serve as magistrate and soon fell seriously ill and passed away. Not long after, my mother also died from grief."

Zhao Xuanyou listened and roughly understood the situation.

Pei Tao gave a bitter laugh. "After this, I also studied diligently and was later favored by His Majesty, who selected me as the top scholar. I became a prominent figure in the capital and married my current wife."

"Did Lady Pei tell you this?"

Pei Tao nodded, his eyes growing complex.

"My wife is a woman of the inner chambers; how would she know these things? Five years ago, my father-in-law had already uncovered the truth. My father was an honest official. That corrupt Governor Tao had spent a long time fabricating evidence but only managed to find a few false witnesses. Their testimonies were poorly constructed and inconsistent. The officials of the Ministry of Justice saw through the flaws in the case as soon as they reviewed the files."

Zhao Xuanyou said slowly, "After all, the Xingguo Duke is a first-rank duke. Everyone in the capital gives him some face. When his brother-in-law got into trouble, he intervened, not only smoothing things over with the Ministry of Justice to avoid pursuing the false accusations but also persuading Prime Minister Sun to let the matter drop lightly."

Pei Tao remained silent.

Zhao Xuanyou took a sip of wine and continued the story that Pei Tao had left unfinished.

"At that time, you didn’t know this matter involved the Xingguo Duke’s mansion. You only knew that Prime Minister Sun had saved your father, but you didn’t know that Prime Minister Sun had also covered for that corrupt official. After you became the top scholar, you were deeply grateful to Prime Minister Sun for his help in your time of need. Among the many noble families in the capital who wanted you as a son-in-law, you chose without hesitation to marry the frail Miss Sun."

"Most of the Young Master’s guesses are correct. However, I have never resented my father-in-law, nor do I regret marrying my wife."

Although Sun Qianran was frail and often ill, she was gentle and intelligent, always standing by his side. Pei Tao was grateful and fortunate to have her as his wife.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

At that time, Pei Tao was just a scholar. Prime Minister Sun had never met him but had acted on a letter from an old friend. Without gaining any benefit, he had intervened in the matter and had Pei Tao’s father released from prison.

Regardless of any dealings between Prime Minister Sun and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion, Prime Minister Sun had indeed done Pei Tao’s family a great favor.

"How did you find out about these things, Minister Pei?"

Pei Tao said indifferently, "After entering the Hanlin Academy, His Majesty often summoned me to the imperial study for questioning and allowed me to visit various ministries. I read some old files and naturally found out."

Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes and lightly tapped the table with his fingertips.

He had personally witnessed the Xingguo Duke’s way of protecting his family.

It was likely that when his brother-in-law was accused, the Duke had intercepted the memorial and then had his brother-in-law frame the unfortunate magistrate with the charge of embezzling pearls.

Fortunately, Pei Tao was highly intelligent and had studied under a famous scholar in Jiangnan. His teacher, appreciating his talent, had sought help from his old friend, the Prime Minister.

It was also fortunate that Governor Tao was greedy but incompetent. His framing was full of loopholes, allowing Prime Minister Sun to see through the flaws immediately and profit from the Xingguo Duke’s mansion.

The Xingguo Duke had gone to such lengths, likely because Governor Tao had embezzled many pearls that ended up in his own pockets.

No wonder Pei Tao had been so resolute, returning all the betrothal gifts without hesitation.

The silver that the Cui family had squandered was exchanged from pearls that the pearl divers had risked their lives to collect from the depths of the sea.

Originally, they only needed to pay a certain amount of pearls to the court, but the amount kept increasing; doubling, tripling... How many common people had been driven to ruin by them!

Zhao Xuanyou’s hand suddenly clenched into a fist.

Pei Tao watched the change in Zhao Xuanyou’s expression, his brows furrowing with worry.

The corrupt official who had made the false accusations was still in office, and the Xingguo Duke’s mansion remained influential. He wanted revenge, and he had to have it.

But his father-in-law was involved in this.

If it weren’t for his wife, he would have acted without hesitation.

But Sun Qianran was frail. If he exposed this matter to His Majesty, his father-in-law’s past abuse of power for personal gain would inevitably be revealed. If his father-in-law were implicated and punished, she might not be able to bear the emotional strain.

The stream pattered against the rocks, producing a clear, crisp sound.

Zhao Xuanyou lifted his head, returning to his usual calm demeanor. "You came to me because there is no other leverage to bring down the Xingguo Duke’s mansion?"

"Yes. I want to bring down the Xingguo Duke’s mansion, but I cannot implicate my father-in-law. My wife..."

"Minister Pei carries a blood feud and doesn’t want to suffer any losses. Asking me to charge ahead seems inappropriate."

---

chapters.title: A Slap
chapters.content:
"It’s not that I’m asking Minister Zhao to charge ahead." Pei Tao caught the flash of anger in Zhao Xuanyou’s expression and regained his composure. "Embezzling tribute and exploiting the people are serious crimes. The evidence my father left behind still exists."

"But you cannot use that evidence." Zhao Xuanyou said coldly.

Pei Tao replied, "I have already thought of a strategy. I wonder if Minister Zhao would be willing to hear it?"

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent.

Since he had come to sit by the stream, he might as well listen a little more.

"You are right, Minister Zhao. The evidence my father gathered cannot be used. If I bring it out, it will inevitably drag up the old case and expose the past. My father was already cleared of the charges back then; there’s no benefit in reopening the case."

"You want to investigate again?"

"That’s right." Pei Tao glanced around. Seeing the flowing stream, the bright moonlight, and no one else in sight, he lowered his voice. "Witnesses can be found again, and evidence can be gathered. I have a close friend in the Censorate who is upright and outspoken. As long as we have solid evidence, he will come forward to impeach them. There’s no need for Minister Zhao to charge ahead."

The Censorate was responsible for supervision and impeachment of negligent officials.

"Minister Pei has thought this through so thoroughly. Why must I be involved?"

Pei Tao lowered his head slightly and gave a bitter laugh. "To my shame, my family has fallen on hard times. When I first came to the capital for the examinations, I had nothing, not even a servant boy. After entering office, although I have a few attendants, none of them know martial arts, and I haven’t known them long enough to entrust them with such an important task as gathering evidence in Qingsha."

At this, Zhao Xuanyou understood.

After Pei Tao’s parents passed away, he likely dismissed his servants and lived in the academy, eating and residing there. After becoming the top scholar, although he was prominent, his daily expenses were probably managed by his wife, Sun Qianran, who had a rich dowry. The number of people he could personally command was limited.

Bringing down a duke’s mansion and a fourth-rank official was no small matter. Ordinary servants simply didn’t have the ability to gather such crucial evidence.

But Zhao Xuanyou was different.

He was the commander of the Minglian Guard. Under his command were many elite soldiers. Those military households had followed the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion for generations and were loyal to both the Marquis and his heir.

"Do you want me to send people to investigate?"

"There are many victims in Qingsha County. As long as we are determined to investigate, we will find evidence." Pei Tao looked at the calm Zhao Xuanyou, though in truth, he wasn’t very confident.

He and Zhao Xuanyou had known each other for less than ten days and didn’t know each other well.

Everything he knew about Zhao Xuanyou came from rumors.

Rumors said he was highly skilled in martial arts, well-versed in military strategies, and thus his troops were invincible. Other rumors said he governed his troops strictly, with clear rewards and punishments, and the Minglian Guard never disturbed the common people wherever they went.

But they were just rumors.

The only thing Pei Tao was certain of was Zhao Xuanyou’s feud with the Xingguo Duke’s mansion.

Zhao Xuanyou’s deep eyes concealed his emotions. His long fingers rested on the table as he slightly lifted his chin.

"If my people find evidence, I cannot order them to hand it over to you."

Pei Tao was slightly taken aback.

Zhao Xuanyou still didn’t trust him.

He was worried that if he handed over the evidence, it would become leverage in Pei Tao’s hands.

"Is Minister Zhao willing to investigate?" Pei Tao asked.

Zhao Xuanyou’s character was cold and hard to read, and Pei Tao truly couldn’t fathom his thoughts.

"I’ll think about it." Zhao Xuanyou answered vaguely. He picked up the bamboo leaf wine on the table and drank it in one go, then stood up and cupped his hands to Pei Tao. "Thank you, Minister Pei, for the fine wine tonight. When I return to the capital, I will host a banquet in return."

Pei Tao’s gaze darkened as he stood up and cupped his hands in return, watching Zhao Xuanyou leave.

The room was lit, and Zhao Xuanyou pushed the door open to find Yu Wan asleep.

She had spent the morning steaming cakes for Zhao Qi, then accompanied Zhao Qi in his martial arts practice and lessons, busy all day long. It was no wonder she had fallen asleep so early.

Zhao Xuanyou felt a little stifled.

Even though she was his maid, Zhao Qi had taken a liking to her.

Looking at the sleeping Yu Wan, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but lean forward and plant a kiss on her rosy cheek.

Her skin was as smooth as snow, and once his lips touched it, he couldn’t pull away.

Zhao Xuanyou embraced her, his large hands also lifting, slowly and gently caressing her.

She was naturally alluring, always tempting him beyond his control.

Zhao Xuanyou was immersed in the moment when he instinctively sensed danger.

He suddenly turned his head to dodge, and the hand that suddenly swung at him missed his face, the fingertips grazing his chin, which stung quite a bit.

Zhao Xuanyou rubbed his chin, frowning slightly. The woman beside him, still fast asleep, indifferently withdrew her hand back under the covers and turned over to continue sleeping.

So that innocent little white rabbit act was all a pretense. Even in her sleep, she hit people so fiercely.

Zhao Xuanyou’s last bit of drowsiness was dispelled by this sudden attack. He got up and went to the outer room, calling Yuan Can in.

"Master, do you have any orders?" Yuan Can asked respectfully.

"Call Lu Ming and Lu Jun back."

Lu Ming and Lu Jun were two brothers who had accompanied Zhao Xuanyou in martial arts training since childhood. They were highly skilled, loyal, and both brave and resourceful.

Before leaving Yuzhou this time, Zhao Xuanyou had left them there to assist with military affairs.

Now that the Fifth Prince was temporarily in charge of the Minglian Guard and Zhao Xuanyou was staying in the capital, it was time to call them back.

Upon hearing this, Yuan Can looked at Zhao Xuanyou, a little nervously. "Master, has something happened?"

"A minor matter."

"Yes," Yuan Can thought for a moment, then asked, "Should they come directly to the capital or to Liaochuan?"

The matter of investigating Qingsha Town couldn’t be explained clearly in a letter.

"To Liaochuan."

"Understood. This servant will send a message immediately." With that, Yuan Can retreated.

Zhao Xuanyou sat quietly at the table for a while, pondering the night’s events. After washing up, he returned to the inner room.

The candle hadn’t been extinguished yet. The woman on the bed rubbed her eyes and sat up.

"Master is back?" Yu Wan’s voice was thick with sleep. "This servant actually fell asleep."

Really asleep?

That slap had almost landed.

Facing Zhao Xuanyou’s inscrutable gaze, Yu Wan suddenly felt a little nervous. Her sleepiness lessened, and she subconsciously tightened her grip on the blanket.

"Is Master angry?"

Was it worth getting angry over just a nap?

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t answer her. He changed into his nightclothes and lay down beside her.

Yu Wan didn’t know what had happened earlier. Seeing his expression, she thought something unpleasant must have occurred during his dinner with Pei Tao.

"What did Minister Pei say to make Master so angry?"

What did Pei Tao matter to him?

Zhao Xuanyou shot Yu Wan a cold glance. Yu Wan forced a smile, leaning forward from the bed to extinguish the candle.

Just as she was about to retreat back under the covers, the man beneath her suddenly reached out and pulled her down.

"Ah…"

Yu Wan cried out in surprise, landing solidly on his chest.

chapters.title: Wild Chicken
chapters.content:
Yuan had not yet reacted when the man's warm breath swept over her.

The candle had already gone out, but she still closed her eyes.

When the scorching breath in the canopy gradually dissipated, Yuan, resting her head on his sturdy arm, softly asked, "Are you still angry, Master?"

The slight frown that had initially creased Zhao Xuanyou's brow had long since relaxed.

"Don't guess wildly."

Yuan was stumped by his answer.

If he wasn't on bad terms with Pei Ta, why had he been wearing such a bitter face earlier?

It was just as well that Zhao Xuanyou refused to admit it. That way, she could still go to class tomorrow.

If they really had a falling out, he would definitely force Yuan to sever ties with the Pei couple.

"He poured his heart out to me by the stream, telling me about many tragic experiences."

"Huh? Master Pei?" Yuan was somewhat surprised. She wouldn't have thought that Pei Ta had such tragic experiences.

Zhao Xuanyou gave a soft "mm" in response.

"Master Pei seems refined and elegant, with impeccable manners. He doesn't look like someone with a bitter past at all."

Pei Ta had a delicate bone structure and exquisite features. His face was flawless, and despite his outstanding appearance, he was not arrogant or aloof. Whenever he met anyone, there was always a hint of gentleness in his eyes and the corners of his mouth.

Yuan hadn't read many books, but she had heard her mother recite some poems.

"On the road, a man like jade, a peerless nobleman" , that must be describing Pei Ta.

In the darkness, Zhao Xuanyou's eyes flickered slightly when he heard the words "refined and elegant, with impeccable manners."

"How do I look like someone with a bitter past?"

Yuan was usually quick-witted and sensed his displeasure. She quickly changed her words, "Naturally, Master sees clearly. This servant just thought that Master Pei and Madame Pei both have a scholarly air. Since Madame Pei is the daughter of the Prime Minister's residence, I assumed Master Pei's family background was on par with hers."

"His father was only a county magistrate before he passed away. If Pei Ta hadn't passed the imperial examination as the top scholar, he wouldn't even have been able to enter the Prime Minister's residence, let alone marry Sun Qianran."

"Then," Yuan pretended to have a sudden realization, curiously asking, "What kind of tragic past does Master Pei have?"

She was particularly concerned about what had happened by the stream that evening, but not because of Pei Ta.

Pei Ta wanted to deal with the Xingguo Duke's residence. Since he had sought out Zhao Xuanyou tonight, he must want to discuss joining forces.

Zhao Xuanyou gave an extremely brief answer: "Pei Ta's father was once framed by someone. Later, he was released after being proven innocent, but the shock was too great. Not long after, his parents passed away one after another."

Pei Ta had such a heartbreaking past?

But then again, he was the top scholar who had seen all the beauty of Chang'an in a single day. What right did a mere servant like her have to sympathize with him?

"Master, does the Pei family's matter have anything to do with the Xingguo Duke's residence?"

Zhao Xuanyou was not surprised by Yuan's question.

After all, Sun Qianran had once sent Yuan to deliver a message, explicitly mentioning that Pei Ta had a feud with the Xingguo Duke's residence.

Zhao Xuanyou never discussed matters outside the boudoir with Yuan, but tonight he made an exception.

"Mm."

"No wonder he came to find you, Master."

"Why is it no wonder?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Yuan softly replied, "Everyone in the capital knows that you and Madame Cui have separated, and that the two families have since become enemies. And you are so capable. If he wants to deal with the Xingguo Duke's residence, the best choice is naturally to ask for your help."

Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes slightly.

Yuan was deliberately flattering him, but her words were not mindless praise; on the contrary, they made sense.

He suddenly had a different feeling about Yuan's desire to attend classes in the study.

She genuinely wanted to listen to the lectures.

After Yuan finished speaking, she waited for a long time without a response from Zhao Xuanyou. She thought she had said too much and touched a nerve.

She didn't dare to ask about Pei Ta anymore and simply said, "It's late. Let's rest early."

Just as she had been sleeping at a distance to avoid disturbing him, his hand pulled at her thin gauze clothing.

"Are you not sleepy?" Yuan asked.

Sleepy? Of course not.

Zhao Xuanyou muttered, "Again."

---

After their drink by the stream, Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta acted as if nothing had happened. They continued to exchange pleasantries in the courtyard and sat under the veranda drinking tea as usual.

One taught Zhao Qi martial arts, while the other instructed him in literature. The two got along harmoniously and minded their own business.

Yuan hoped that they would join forces against the Xingguo Duke's residence, but she couldn't do anything to facilitate this. She could only wait and see.

Pei Ta's lectures were profound yet easy to understand. Even though Yuan had not read the Four Books and Five Classics, she could still grasp four or five layers of meaning.

Life in Lichuan was peaceful and interesting.

One early morning, Zhao Xuanyou was ordered to escort two princesses to a nearby town for an outing. Yuan was in the courtyard embroidering while accompanying Zhao Qi in practicing his horse stance.

Zhao Qi glanced at her embroidery of mandarin ducks and couldn't help but frown.

"What are you embroidering?"

"This servant is embroidering mandarin ducks playing in the water," Yuan said seriously.

Zhao Qi looked disgusted. "What mandarin ducks? They clearly look like wild chickens."

Even if they were wild chickens, they were the most bizarre-looking kind.

Yuan didn't think her embroidery was bad. She had only been learning needlework for a little over a month. Being able to embroider wild chickens was already quite impressive.
