"Anyway, it's a handkerchief for my own use. If it's ugly, then it's ugly."

Seeing her satisfied expression, Zhao Qi couldn't help but ask, "Zhao Xuanyou went out without taking you. Aren't you upset at all?"

What was there to be upset about?

Princess Yi'an and Princess Yi'ning were born in a magnificent palace. They were the ones who would be interested in the small towns where commoners lived.

Yuan herself was a commoner. If she had a choice, she would want to live in the imperial palace for the rest of her life, enjoying fine clothes and food, rather than going to some town for a fair.

"This servant grew up in a village and is very familiar with villages and towns. There's no need to go see them." Yuan said as she continued to embroider her "wild chickens playing in the water."

Zhao Qi felt that he and Yuan were never on the same page when talking, but he had no choice here and could only talk to her.

Yuan carefully embroidered the eyes of the "wild chicken" and looked up at Zhao Qi. Seeing his gloomy face, she smiled and asked, "Your Highness, do you want to go play like before?"

"I just want to leave the palace. Anywhere is fine as long as I can leave the palace."

"Your Highness has been studying and practicing so diligently these days. If you had asked Master this morning before he left, he would definitely have excused you from today's lessons."

Zhao Qi sneered, "I want to leave the palace, but yesterday, Father Emperor asked me. However, I would rather stay here than go out with Yi'an and the others. That's not playing; that's torture."

Although Yuan could sense that Princess Yi'an was not very kind to the servants, Zhao Qi was her brother. Were their sibling relations so tense?

"Does Your Highness want to go out and play by yourself?"

"Mm." Zhao Qi said listlessly, "Father Emperor said I have to finish my classes before I can go out."

Yuan didn't know how to comfort him. Just at that moment, Pei Ta, supporting Sun Qianran, walked out of the house. Hearing this, he said, "Your Highness has attended classes for ten consecutive days. Take a half-day break."

"Are today's classes canceled?"

Pei Ta nodded.

Calculating the time, Zhao Qi's horse stance practice was almost done. For the past ten days, he had been confined to this small courtyard, spending half the day practicing martial arts and the other half studying. It wasn't forced, but he did want to go out and relax.

Hearing Pei Ta's words, he suddenly stood up straight and, quite rarely, cupped his hands in a bow to Pei Ta, "Thank you, Teacher Pei."

"You're welcome, Your Highness."

Watching Zhao Qi leave with a smile, Yuan continued to work on her embroidery. But before she could even prick the needle down, Zhao Qi returned and grabbed her hand.

---

chapters.title: Graceful
chapters.content:
"Your Highness?" Yuan was suddenly held by his hand. The embroidery in her hand fell to the ground. She looked at him in surprise, "Did you forget something?"

Zhao Qi hesitated for a moment, seemingly conflicted. After a while, he dryly said, "They all go out in groups. It's no fun for me to go alone. You come too."

"This servant... can I just come and go as I please?"

"You're not part of the palace staff. Your master is out, so of course you can go out."

Yuan was not a palace maid and thus not bound by palace rules.

The separate courtyard and the imperial palace were separated by a stream, but the difference between them was like heaven and earth.

On the other side of the stream, the Feathered Forest Guards patrolled day and night, and the checks to enter were as strict as those for the imperial palace.

Although the separate courtyard was managed by eunuchs, officials and their families could come and go freely.

"Let's go!"

Seeing that Yuan had nothing to say, Zhao Qi pulled her hand forward.

Before Yuan could hesitate, she was pulled out of the courtyard by him.

Pei Ta and Sun Qianran stood in the courtyard, watching with some amusement.

"Seventh Prince usually speaks very rudely, but I didn't expect him to be so close to Yuan," Sun Qianran said.

"Time reveals a person's heart. Miss Yuan is graceful and considerate, meticulous and careful. Seventh Prince understands this well."

As Pei Ta spoke, he walked forward and picked up Yuan's embroidery that had fallen in the courtyard, examining it in his hand.

Seeing him looking at it seriously, Sun Qianran walked to his side and softly said, "The beak of the mandarin duck is too pointed. No wonder Seventh Prince called it a wild chicken."

Zhao Qi had a loud voice, and they had heard him from inside the house.

"The stitches are also a bit loose."

"Does my husband understand needlework?"

Pei Ta smiled without saying a word.

When he was studying alone at the academy, although he was often cared for by his teachers, he didn't want to trouble others for everything. Simple mending was done by himself. His stitches were as rough as Yuan's, just barely usable.

He handed the embroidery to Xiang Xu and instructed her to return it to Yuan. Supporting Sun Qianran, he walked out.

The two of them followed the small path next to the courtyard to the stream.

It was another sunny day. The sun felt warm on their bodies. The path along the stream was winding, and the breeze from the river valley made it feel not hot at all, even though it was almost noon.

Sun Qianran looked at the distant scenery with a touch of melancholy. She didn't know why, but she always felt that Pei Ta treated Yuan differently.

Seeing her in a daze, Pei Ta opened a silk parasol to shield her from the sun and, with his arm around her, slowly walked forward.

"If I weren't like this, you would have gone out to play today," Sun Qianran said.

Pei Ta knew she was feeling sentimental and gently said, "I grew up in an academy, so I'm used to staying in. Compared to going shopping, I prefer standing among green mountains and clear waters, quietly appreciating the scenery."

"Then let's find a place to sit?"

"Okay." Pei Ta quickly found a gentle slope by the stream and ordered Xiang Xu to bring two bamboo cool chairs from the courtyard.

The two of them lay side by side by the stream, listening to the sound of the water, feeling the breeze, and basking in the sun. It was indeed enjoyable.

"Husband, these past few days, has Lord Zhao not responded to you?"

"No."

"He was willing to come to the stream for a banquet, so he must have intended to cooperate. Why hasn't he responded to you? Could it be that he thinks your strategy is not good?"

Pei Ta said, "We have not known each other for long. He probably thinks cooperating with me is too risky."

"Shall I go talk to him?"

"No need."

Hearing Pei Ta's response, Sun Qianran curiously asked, "From your tone, it seems you already have a grasp on the situation."

"That day, I was as confused as you. Over the past few days, I've slowly come to realize. As you said, since he was willing to come, he naturally intended to cooperate. I pointed out the direction and provided the strategy. If he doesn't want to cooperate, he must plan to do it himself."

"I see." Sun Qianran's heart stirred slightly.

Zhao Xuanyou not cooperating with Pei Ta was good news for her. Back then, her father had intervened in the case of her father-in-law. Although her father-in-law was released, the corrupt official still escaped punishment. Her father must have accepted some benefits.

If Pei Ta were involved, her father would inevitably find out afterward, and the father-in-law and son-in-law relationship would suffer.

Zhao Xuanyou was willing to handle the case independently, which completely absolved Pei Ta.

Sun Qianran chose to stand on Pei Ta's side and help him avenge his family. Ultimately, she did not want him to fall out with the Sun family.

---

While the Pei couple was leisurely enjoying themselves by the stream, Yuan was helpless.

"You can't ride a horse?" Zhao Qi sat on a tall horse, looking at Yuan in shock.

"This servant cannot ride a horse."

"You're a maid from the Jingyuan Marquis's residence!" Zhao Qi said in confusion.

So what? The military background was for the masters of the marquis's residence, not the servants.

"Forgive this servant for disturbing Your Highness's elegance. This servant knows her mistake and will return to the courtyard now."

Yuan wasn't particularly interested in the small town. Going was fine, and not going was also fine.

Since Zhao Qi wanted to ride a horse there, and she couldn't ride, she had a good reason to return.

But Zhao Qi didn't intend to let her leave just like that.

"Yin Ping."

"At your service."

"Go harness a carriage to take her there. We'll go to the town first."

"This..." Yin Ping was Zhao Qi's personal guard. Normally, he should stay close to Zhao Qi at all times.

However, Zhao Qi still had Mu Di and more than a dozen palace guards with him, so there wouldn't be any problems.

"Understood."

Zhao Qi made up his mind, flicked his whip, and led a team of guards away.

Yuan hadn't expected this arrangement and helplessly followed Yin Ping.

The closest town to the Lichuan imperial palace was Cangxi Town, which was not large, with only one north and one south street.

Zhao Qi could reach it on a fast horse in the time it took to burn a stick of incense. Yin Ping drove the carriage for half an hour before reaching the outskirts of the town.

A guard who had come with Zhao Qi earlier was alone under a big tree, watching over a dozen horses.

Yin Ping brought the carriage to the guard and then returned to Yuan, saying, "The roads in Cangxi Town are very narrow. To avoid disturbing the common people, the horses and carriage will stay here. I will escort Miss Yuan inside."

Yuan had no objections.

Because it was near the imperial palace, and knowing that the nobles from the palace would occasionally visit, Cangxi Town was neater and cleaner than ordinary small towns.

After entering the town, they walked along the street but did not see Zhao Qi.

"How come we can't find him even though the horses are here?" Yuan asked in confusion.

"Don't let the small size fool you. There's a theater and several restaurants in the town. Let's go to the theater first to look for him."

The local troupe performed acrobatics and wrestling, which were quite interesting.

Zhao Qi had come to watch last year.

Yuan noticed a pastry shop nearby. Thinking that she had been well taken care of by Xiang Xu and the cook recently, she wanted to buy some pastries to take back for them to try. So she said, "You go find His Highness first. I'll buy some pastries and then catch up to take a look."

"The theater is just ahead. If anything happens, just call out loudly. I'll hear you."

Yuan entered the pastry shop. Although business was good, the pastries were much coarser than those in the capital. Taking them back as gifts might not be appropriate.

The shop owner enthusiastically let Yuan try some. Only the honey date pastry was decent. Yuan bought a pack of honey date pastries and a jin of roasted melon seeds.

When she arrived at the theater, she saw Yin Ping standing at the entrance. She went up and asked, "Is His Highness inside?"

"Yes." Yin Ping's expression was somewhat unnatural.

Only then did Yuan notice that there were a few guards standing at the theater entrance, dressed similarly to Yin Ping. They all looked tall and strong, with extraordinary skills.

"Are the two princesses inside?"

Yin Ping shook his head. Before he could answer, Yuan felt a heavy gaze fall upon her.

chapters.title: Nobleman
chapters.content:
Yu Ying instinctively looked around, her gaze colliding with a young man walking out of the theater.

The man was about the same age as Zhao Xuanyou, with delicate features, not as refined as Pei Tao, but his entire demeanor exuded an indescribable nobility.

The black brocade robe he wore seemed unremarkable at first glance, but upon closer inspection, it was extraordinarily precious. The intricate dark patterns at the collar and cuffs were so complex they were hard to decipher, making him appear much older than his actual age.

A deep look of surprise flickered in his eyes, as if he was very surprised to see Yu Ying here.

Yu Ying had never seen him before, and being stared at so intently left her somewhat confused.

He walked slowly towards Yu Ying, his gaze fixed firmly on her as he looked down at her from above.

Yu Ying guessed that he was no ordinary person, and not daring to meet his eyes, she took half a step back and lowered her gaze, standing beside Yin Ping.

"New palace maid?" he asked indifferently, but not to Yu Ying; he was asking Yin Ping.

Yin Ping did not bow, but her expression was respectful: "Yu Ying is not a palace maid; she is a maidservant from the Jingyuan Marquis's residence."

At the mention of "Jingyuan Marquis's residence," the man's eyebrows twitched slightly, and his gaze shifted back to Yu Ying.

Seeing Yin Ping's attitude, Yu Ying could well imagine the man's status. She dared not meet his eyes again, lowering her head even further until all she could see were the man's shoes, embroidered with gold and silver thread patterns.

Only when those expensive shoes left her line of sight did Yu Ying slightly lift her head, watching as the man and his entourage rode away on horseback.

"Who was that?" she asked.

The man was traveling in disguise, so Yin Ping did not dare to speak directly. She pointed at the theater and whispered, "Second Brother."

Zhao Qi's second brother... So the man just now was the current Crown Prince?

From the day she learned she would accompany Zhao Xuanyou to the imperial summer palace, Yu Ying knew she might encounter nobles from the palace, but she had never thought that a palace noble would fix his gaze on her.

Why would His Highness the Crown Prince look at her like that?

Yu Ying knew she was strikingly beautiful, but the palace was filled with beauties. How could the Crown Prince, who had seen so much, be captivated by her appearance? Thinking about this, Yu Ying suddenly realized why he had looked at her that way.

She resembled Cui Yichu...

But some things still didn't add up.

Princess Yi'an, Princess Yi'ning, Zhao Qi, and Sun Qianran all knew Cui Yichu. When they first saw her, some paid attention, others didn't. But none of them had stared at her so intently, as if their gaze was glued to her.

If two unrelated people looked alike, it was nothing to be concerned about.

So why was the Crown Prince so concerned... Yu Ying's heart suddenly began to race.

The Crown Prince and Cui Yichu?

Was the Crown Prince the man who had ruined Cui Yichu's chastity?

Zhao Xuanyou had never mentioned anything about Cui Yichu's lover.

That was his greatest shame, a pain he was unwilling to speak of.

Now, thinking back, perhaps it wasn't just that he was unwilling; it was that he couldn't mention it at all.

No wonder... No wonder he had so quickly divorced Cui Yichu and agreed to the Duke of Xingguo's request to keep Cui Yichu's loss of chastity a secret.

Zhao Xuanyou was not a greedy man; the Jingyuan Marquis's residence lacked for nothing. In his rage, the conditions offered by the Duke of Xingguo would not have been enough to make him spare the Duke's residence.

The only explanation was that Cui Yichu's lover was the Crown Prince himself. Zhao Xuanyou, fearing the consequences, had no choice but to back down and accept the Duke's conditions.

"What are you daydreaming about?" Zhao Qi came out of the theater and, seeing Yu Ying's dazed expression, waved his hand in front of her face a few times.

Yu Ying suddenly came back to her senses and instinctively bowed to Zhao Qi: "This servant greets Your Highness."

"Your Highness what!" Zhao Qi scolded in a low voice, grabbing Yu Ying's arm and quickly pulling her aside. "You foolish girl, we are traveling incognito. Do you understand what incognito means?"

Seeing that Yu Ying was still in a state of shock, Zhao Qi looked at Yin Ping, suspicious: "Did she encounter something unnatural?"

Yin Ping whispered, "She ran into that person."

Zhao Qi knew Yin Ping was referring to the Crown Prince. His enjoyment of the play had just been interrupted by the Crown Prince.

He hadn't expected to encounter that guy in Cangxi Town. He was rude, pretentious, and just looking at him was an eyesore.

"Did he make things difficult for Yu Ying? Unlikely."

The Empress had never liked him since he was young, so Zhao Zun enjoyed picking on him. Even if they weren't on good terms, Zhao Zun, in order to please the Emperor, always liked to put on an act of being courteous and approachable. It was unlikely he would make things difficult for a maidservant on the street.

"He didn't make things difficult," Yin Ping whispered. "He just stared at Yu Ying for a while and didn't say anything."

"Oh? So he's also a lecher." Zhao Qi said with a hint of disdain. "Ignore him. Let's go eat the braised chicken noodles. After we finish, we'll go back."

Braised chicken noodles were a specialty of Cangxi Town. Zhao Qi led Yu Ying to a noodle shop in the center of the town. Before they even entered, they saw several familiar faces inside.

Princess Yi'an had been smiling and talking to Zhao Xuanyou about something. When she saw Zhao Qi and Yu Ying, her eyes darkened slightly.

"What a coincidence," Princess Yi'ning, who had been bored out of her mind waiting for food, greeted them warmly upon seeing them.

They had been out for half a day, but they hadn't done much sightseeing or playing. Princess Yi'an had been too busy talking to Zhao Xuanyou, leaving her to stand aside.

Zhao Qi didn't pay any attention to them. Leading Yu Ying, he sat at a table by the window and knocked on the table: "Shopkeeper, two bowls of braised chicken noodles."

"Coming right up," the shopkeeper responded warmly. "There are three bowls ahead of you. Once this pot is ready, yours will be up."

The shopkeeper worked quickly, soon fishing out noodles from the hot broth into the pre-arranged soup bowls, then chopping some braised chicken with a cleaver and placing a few pieces on top of each bowl. He served them to Zhao Xuanyou's table.

The atmosphere in the noodle shop was somewhat awkward. Princesses Yi'an and Yi'ning stopped talking, merely picking at their noodles with their chopsticks without eating.

Both of them were of noble birth; they had come to this noodle shop just to pass the time.

At their table, only Zhao Xuanyou was eating.

Soon, the shopkeeper cooked two bowls of noodles and served them to Yu Ying's table.

Yu Ying first tried a piece of braised chicken. The skin was crispy, and the meat was tender and delicious.

The noodles were hand-rolled by the shop, chewy and firm, and the broth was seasoned with chicken, making it incredibly fresh and flavorful.

Yu Ying hadn't eaten lunch and was already starving. Both she and Zhao Qi ate with great relish.

After finishing a bowl, Yu Ying still felt unsatisfied. After some thought, she asked the shopkeeper to pack a whole braised chicken for her.

Seeing Yu Ying with so many packages in her hands, Zhao Qi asked in surprise, "You're still not full?"

"It's rare to find such delicious braised chicken. I packed one to bring back for the people in the courtyard to try."

"It's not that rare. We can come again another day."

"Are you not going to practice your martial arts anymore?" Yu Ying teased.

"After I finish practicing, we can come out again."

As they spoke, they left the noodle shop and saw Zhao Xuanyou standing tall, clearly waiting for them.

Zhao Qi was impolite to the two princesses but still felt a bit intimidated in front of Zhao Xuanyou.

"I practiced horse stance for two full hours before coming out."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded and then turned his gaze to Yu Ying.

Sensing his displeasure, Yu Ying thought something was wrong and, hardening her resolve, stepped forward and smiled at him.

"My lord, what a coincidence."

---

chapters.title: On Horseback
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow and asked in return, "A coincidence?"

"Your Highness ordered this servant to follow you out of the palace. I didn't expect to meet the Young Master here." Hearing the displeasure in his tone, Yu Ying softly explained the reason for her presence.

She had indeed been dragged out by Zhao Qi against her will.

If given a choice, she would rather stay in and sleep.

"Do you know how to ride a horse?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"This servant does not know how to ride. I came here by carriage."

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou questioning Yu Ying, Zhao Qi stepped forward to help: "The princesses have already mounted their horses. They probably want to return to the summer palace immediately. Lord Zhao, don't delay any longer. I'll take Yu Ying back after a bit more sightseeing."

Zhao Xuanyou wouldn't get angry over such a small matter; he was just teasing Yu Ying: "Yu Ying has already troubled Your Highness greatly. I will take her back myself."

He would take her?

Yu Ying was surprised. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou mount his horse with a cold and stern expression, he only extended his hand to her.

What did he mean?

Ride together?

Under the gaze of the crowd, Yu Ying hesitated, but how could she refuse Zhao Xuanyou?

As soon as she placed her hand on his, Zhao Xuanyou turned his hand to grasp her wrist and pulled her up.

Yu Ying's feet left the ground, and in the next moment, she was seated on the horse.

The two of them were already striking figures; one tall and elegant with a graceful demeanor, the other fair and delicate with a charming bearing.

Standing at the intersection, they had already attracted many onlookers. Now, with the two of them riding together, almost everyone looked their way.

Yu Ying, unaccustomed to so many eyes on her, lowered her head slightly. Zhao Xuanyou, holding the reins, leaned down a bit, his cheek brushing against Yu Ying's ear. Feeling her ear grow hot, he couldn't help but curve his lips into a smile.

They had done far more intimate things, yet a simple shared ride made her so shy.

Not far away, Princesses Yi'an and Yi'ning sat on their horses, watching Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying with indifferent expressions.

"Lord Zhao seems quite fond of that maidservant," Princess Yi'ning said blandly, her words laced with provocation. "He even shares a horse with her."

Princess Yi'an's expression was unreadable. Hearing her sister's words, she casually replied, "He only has one maidservant by his side. It's natural for him to be close to her."

Seeing her sister's indifference, Princess Yi'ning realized she didn't consider a mere maidservant worth her attention.

Princess Yi'ning didn't know Yu Ying, but upon first seeing her, she felt Yu Ying resembled Cui Yichu.

Zhao Xuanyou keeping Yu Ying by his side must be because he couldn't forget Cui Yichu. Even if he married again in the future, he wouldn't send Yu Ying away.

She even thought that Zhao Xuanyou taking Yu Ying to ride with him now was a deliberate act for Princess Yi'an to see.

Yu Ying had originally come with the Seventh Prince. It would have been fine for her to return with him, so why did Zhao Xuanyou have to take her himself?

Of course, Princess Yi'ning knew her elder sister was ambitious and had set her sights on Zhao Xuanyou. She wouldn't listen to her advice, but she would enjoy watching the potential drama unfold.

"Let's go." Princess Yi'an flicked her whip forcefully and led the way out of the town on her horse.

Zhao Xuanyou had escorted the two princesses out, so when they left, he naturally urged his horse to follow with Yu Ying.

As dust flew up, Yu Ying suddenly had a slight change of opinion about Zhao Qi.

Everyone said Zhao Qi was domineering, arrogant, and cynical, but he had left his horses outside Cangxi Town to avoid disturbing the common people.

The much-praised Crown Prince and the two princesses, however, had brought their attendants and ridden their horses through the town.

Watching the commoners carefully stepping aside, Yu Ying felt a pang of emotion.

Zhao Qi truly bore his bad reputation unfairly.

The fast horse soon left the town behind. Surrounded by flowing water, houses, and crisscrossing farmlands, Yu Ying had no time to appreciate the scenery.

The wind howled in her ears, and her cheeks stung from the cold.

She closed her eyes and then turned her body, burying her face in Zhao Xuanyou's shoulder.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her pitiful, curled-up form, like a little kitten, and couldn't help but hold her a little tighter.

"First time riding a horse?" he asked softly.

"Mmm." Yu Ying replied, not forgetting to say obediently, "Thank you, Young Master, for broadening this servant's horizons."

Zhao Xuanyou's eyes darkened slightly.

Speaking of first times, this was also his first time.

The first time he had shared a horse with a woman.

The weather was clear, but Zhao Xuanyou inexplicably thought of a picture he had seen in the "Avoiding Fire Diagram"; a man and a woman riding a horse together, making love on horseback.

When he had flipped through it before, he thought it was the artist's wild imagination. Making love on horseback. Weren't they risking their lives?

But now, with a soft, warm body in his arms, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly thought, maybe it was possible.

At least, with his skills, he could manage it.

Yu Ying, nestled in his arms, felt Zhao Xuanyou's breathing grow heavier.

Sensing something was off with him, she should have moved away, but it was so cold on horseback. Yu Ying couldn't bear to let go, so she clung to his shoulder, pretending to know nothing.

The return trip to the summer palace was much faster than the journey there. Yu Ying followed Zhao Xuanyou and watched as the two princesses entered the summer palace before returning to the separate courtyard on the outskirts.

Seeing Yu Ying carrying so many packages, Zhao Xuanyou asked, "What did you buy?"

"Some pastries, and a braised chicken."

"Can you eat all that?"

"It's for Yuan Qing, Xiang Xu, and the others to try."

Yuan Qing did love chicken. Zhao Xuanyou led Yu Ying forward slowly and asked, "Isn't Master Pei giving a lesson today?"

Yu Ying recounted, "Master Pei heard the Seventh Prince say he wanted to go out and play. Thinking that he had been studying diligently for more than ten days, Master Pei gave him half a day off. When we left, we saw Master Pei and his wife heading towards the stream. They probably wanted to enjoy themselves as well."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded and said nothing more.

Yu Ying thought for a moment and added, "Cangxi Town doesn't seem very big, and there aren't many places to visit. Did you, Young Master, go there early in the morning?"

The town was quite lively, with many shops.

But judging by the way the two princesses couldn't even eat a single noodle in the shop, they naturally wouldn't be interested in the goods sold in the town. It was strange they could spend half a day there.

Hearing her inquiry, Zhao Xuanyou thought she might be jealous and said leisurely, "The two princesses first went to the hunting ground to ride and shoot arrows, then went to the town. They only arrived about half an hour before you."

No wonder...

Zhao Xuanyou saw the strange look on Yu Ying's face and frowned. "What are you thinking about?"

"The weather is nice today. The clouds in the sky are so white, one after another. No wonder the nobles from the summer palace all want to go out."

Zhao Xuanyou was a perceptive man. Hearing her say "nobles from the summer palace," he realized she wasn't just referring to Zhao Qi and the two princesses. So he asked, "Who else did you meet?"

Thinking of the Crown Prince staring at her intently at the theater entrance, Yu Ying felt a bit uneasy.

Facing Cui Yichu, her former mistress, she might have been able to find a way to deal with her. But how could she handle the Crown Prince?

In Lichuan, the only person she could trust and rely on was Zhao Xuanyou.

"Today, at the entrance of the theater in the town, this servant encountered His Highness, the Crown Prince."

"He went to the town as well?" Zhao Xuanyou was somewhat surprised. Looking at Yu Ying's delicate, flawless face, he suddenly thought of something. "He saw you?"

Yu Ying nodded.

After a moment's thought, she added, "His Highness the Crown Prince not only saw this servant but also inquired with Yin Ping. From Yin Ping, he learned that this servant is a maidservant from the Jingyuan Marquis's residence."

chapters.title: Betrothal by Imperial Decree
chapters.content:
"He asked about Yin Ping?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

It wasn’t strange that the Crown Prince would take a second look at Yu Yuan. She was exceptionally beautiful, graceful and elegant; anyone who wasn’t blind would glance at her on the street.

And to the Crown Prince, Yu Yuan bore a five-part resemblance to Cui Yichu. Given the Crown Prince’s relationship with Cui Yichu, it was only natural he would notice her.

But when the Crown Prince actually inquired about Yu Yuan’s identity, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but take it seriously.

Yu Yuan watched his sword-like brows furrow and felt a sense of relief herself.

The Crown Prince was far above her in status; he was someone only Zhao Xuanyou could handle. Since Zhao Xuanyou was aware, she didn’t need to worry about it.

After all, worrying would do no good.

"From now on, this servant will stay in the courtyard and not step outside, to avoid causing trouble for you, my lord."

Hearing her words, Zhao Xuanyou withdrew his thoughts and glanced at her. "No need."

"But…"

"If he wants to look, let him look a few times. It’s no big deal."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s indifference, Yu Yuan nodded. "Understood."

Soon, they entered the courtyard. Zhao Xuanyou went inside to rest, while Yu Yuan took the pastries and braised chicken to the kitchen, calling Yuan Qing and Xiang Xu over to try some. They chatted and laughed, gradually forgetting the matter.

---

Princess Yi’an and Princess Yi’ning returned to the imperial residence and each went to their rooms to rest.

This year, many people from the imperial capital had come to Lichuan. Apart from the Emperor, Empress, and Crown Prince, who each had their own palaces, everyone else had to share accommodations.

After a short nap, calculating that it was about time, the two sisters changed clothes and went to the Liu Li Palace to accompany the Empress for tea.

The Liu Li Palace was second only to the Ming De Palace, where the Emperor resided. Its upturned eaves and soaring roofs exuded grandeur.

After the eunuch announced them, the two entered the tea room of Liu Li Palace and found the Crown Prince already there.

"Greetings to Mother Empress and Royal Brother."

"Take your seats."

At the Empress’s words, Yi’an and Yi’ning respectfully sat at the lower end of the tea table.

Noticing the Empress’s teacup was empty, Yi’an picked up the teapot to pour for her.

Watching Yi’an’s obedient and filial behavior, the Empress nodded in approval. "Did you have fun today?"

Unlike Yi’an, who had taken the initiative with the tea, Yi’ning spoke first. "Thanks to Mother Empress’s concern, the hunting grounds were clear, and many animals came out. This child even saw two spotted deer."

"Did you go to town?"

"Yes, and we even ate braised chicken noodles in town."

The Empress glanced at her and chuckled. "Those commoner foods make me lose my appetite just hearing about them. You take after your father; every time he comes to Lichuan, he orders someone to buy things from town, like that... what was it called?"

"Braised chicken," the Crown Prince indifferently supplied.

Princess Yi’ning had flattered the wrong person and forced a smile, saying no more.

The Empress sipped her tea and looked at the Crown Prince. "Today, you specially went to town to buy something for your father. What did he say?"

"He was very pleased."

The Empress nodded.

Princess Yi’an said, "So Royal Brother also went to Cangxi Town today. We didn’t run into each other."

The Crown Prince’s eyes flickered thoughtfully but he didn’t respond.

Yi’an and Yi’ning weren’t surprised. Zhao Zun was the legitimate son of the Empress, enthroned as Crown Prince from a young age, and had always been cold and aloof. Although he often displayed a fraternal and loving demeanor in front of the Emperor, in reality, he was deeply indifferent, treating others as inferior subjects rather than kin.

After all, their statuses were different. No one else dared to say anything, except for Zhao Qi, who dared to confront him openly, exposing his hypocrisy in front of the Emperor several times, much to the Crown Prince’s irritation.

In the silence, the Empress glanced at Yi’ning. "Speak of the devil, you’re here just in time. I have something to tell you."

"What does Mother Empress command?" Yi’ning felt a sudden tension under the Empress’s gaze.

Her birth mother had told her so much about the Empress that every encounter left her uneasy.

Seeing her tense expression, the Empress smiled. "Don’t be nervous. I have good news for you."

Good news?

At these words, Yi’ning froze.

She had just turned sixteen, the age for marriage discussions. For her, the only "good news" worth mentioning was a betrothal.

Was the Empress arranging a marriage for her?

Though she dared not ask directly.

The Crown Prince, indifferent, continued sipping his tea. Princess Yi’an, seeing Yi’ning’s stunned expression, helped by asking, "What good news is it? Mother Empress, please tell us."

"I mentioned your marriages to His Majesty today."

Both of their marriages?

Unlike Yi’ning’s shock, Princess Yi’an was overjoyed.

The Empress had already spoken to Father Emperor?

Today, just as Zhao Xuanyou had escorted her out of the palace for an outing; it all fell into place perfectly.

But Princess Yi’an knew the Empress wouldn’t discuss her own affairs here, so she feigned shyness. "What did Father Emperor say?"

"Your princess estates have been built for a long time. It’s indeed time for you to marry. After all, imperial daughters are not like commoners who can’t return home after marriage. Even after marrying, you can return to the palace whenever you wish. It’s better to marry early."

"Mother Empress speaks wisely," Yi’an nodded. "But Mother Empress mentioned my sister’s good news. Could it be that Father Emperor has already decided on a match for my sister?"

"Yes."

Yi’ning’s lips moved, but no sound came out.

Yi’an asked again, "Father Emperor’s choice for my sister must be excellent."

Seeing Yi’ning was already too shocked to speak, the Empress stopped beating around the bush and smiled. "Indeed, it is excellent. He has chosen the fourth son of the Anning Marquis’s household, Ye Mo Han."

"Ah, so it’s him," Yi’an said. "The Ye family’s daughter is my sister’s study companion. To betroth my sister to the Ye family’s young master; knowing the family well, their marriage will surely be stable and harmonious."

Ye Mo Han?

Princess Yi’ning’s study companion was a Ye family girl, so she had more opportunities to see Ye Mo Han than other young masters in the capital.

To be honest, in terms of appearance, family background, or talent, Ye Mo Han was decent, but nothing extraordinary.

In literature, he couldn’t compare to Pei Tao; in martial arts, he couldn’t compare to Zhao Xuanyou; in appearance, he couldn’t compare to either of them.

Princess Yi’ning had not hoped for an ordinary man like Ye Mo Han as her consort.

Seeing the disappointment on Yi’ning’s face, Yi’an gently nudged her arm and reminded her, "Sister should thank Mother Empress."

Thank her?

Princess Yi’ning stood up and bowed to the Empress. Before she could speak, the Empress said, "Your marriage was chosen by your father. There’s no need to thank me. Go find your father yourself."

The Empress was clearly annoyed and dismissed her outright.

Yi’ning managed to compose herself somewhat and still said to the Empress, "This child thanks Mother Empress for her grace."

After bowing, she retreated.

Once she left, the Empress couldn’t help but say, "Back then, I wanted to take her in to keep you company, but her birth mother refused no matter what. She can’t even handle a little thing; she’s not as composed as the noble ladies of the capital."

"Mother Empress, please calm down."

"Forget it. All of you, leave. Let me have some peace."

"Yes." The Crown Prince indifferently stood first, followed by Princess Yi’an.

After leaving the Liu Li Palace, the Crown Prince, who was walking ahead, suddenly stopped and turned to look at Princess Yi’an.

"Does Royal Brother have any orders?"

The Crown Prince examined Yi’an and said in a deep voice, "I heard you’ve taken a fancy to Zhao Xuanyou?"

---

chapters.title: Nostalgia for the Past
chapters.content:
Princess Yi’ning wasn’t close to the Crown Prince, so this matter must have been told to him by the Empress.

Judging by the Crown Prince’s current expression, Princess Yi’an guessed he might not approve. She chose her words carefully. "I do have such intentions, and Mother Empress also approves."

The Crown Prince’s expression was grave, his voice cold as frost. "If you marry him, you’re asking for trouble."

Princess Yi’an was displeased by his words but didn’t dare to refute them. She lowered her eyes and softly replied, "He holds military power and is favored by Father Emperor. If he becomes my consort, even if he can’t be of use to Royal Brother, he won’t oppose Royal Brother either."

The Crown Prince gave a cold, disdainful laugh. "A mere fourth-rank official. Even with a hereditary title, what does he amount to in my eyes?"

Princess Yi’an fell silent, lowering her head. After a moment, she said softly, "Royal Brother saw Yi’ning’s reaction today. If she had to choose between Ye Mo Han and Zhao Xuanyou, she would choose the same as me."

The Crown Prince casually remarked, "Don’t blame me for not warning you. Father Emperor values propriety most. Zhao Xuanyou shares the same surname as the imperial clan. Mother Empress may be pleased by you and overlook this, but Father Emperor may not."

Princess Yi’an felt aggrieved and argued, "The Jingyuan Marquis’s household is not descended from Emperor Taizong. They have long been beyond the fifth degree of mourning. What propriety is there to speak of?"

The Crown Prince shot her a cold glance.

"Although the Jingyuan Marquis’s household is not descended from Emperor Taizong, the Ministry of the Imperial Clan has not registered them in the imperial family records. However, their military merits are illustrious, and their rewards during festivals are all bestowed as if they were imperial kin. In Father Emperor’s heart, he and I are the same; both your elder brothers."

Princess Yi’an felt unconvinced and replied dryly, "That’s not the case..."

The Crown Prince gave her a detached glance, his tone tinged with sarcasm. "If you don’t believe me, you can go ask Father Emperor yourself."

"I will go ask."

Seeing she still looked defiant, a long-buried memory suddenly surfaced in the Crown Prince’s mind. His voice grew colder and sharper. "I think you’ve gone mad out of jealousy over Yichu, which is why you’re doing this."

Princess Yi’an’s eyes flickered. She hadn’t expected the Crown Prince to bring this up and quickly said, "Cui Yichu was expelled from the palace by Mother Empress. What does that have to do with me? Why must Royal Brother say such things?"

The Crown Prince wasn’t about to believe her words.

"How did Mother Empress find out about my affair with Yichu? You know in your heart, and I know in mine."

Two years ago, after the Crown Prince’s secret affair with Cui Yichu was exposed, Cui Yichu was expelled from the palace by the Empress. At the time, the Crown Prince had seemed completely indifferent, never mentioning it to Princess Yi’an, as if it had never happened.

Now, after two years, he suddenly brought it up.

Princess Yi’an was flustered. "It was Mother Empress’s decree to expel Cui Yichu from the palace."

The Crown Prince dropped a final warning, "You’d better know what’s good for you," and left with a flick of his sleeve.

Princess Yi’an stood frozen, biting her lip hard until it bled before she came back to her senses.

A palace maid, seeing this, rushed forward to support her. "Your Highness, shall I call the imperial physician to see you?"

"No need."

Seeing her displeasure, the maid softly consoled her, "The Crown Prince was in a bad mood today and took it out on you for no reason. Once he’s vented, it’ll be over tomorrow."

This maid was Princess Yi’an’s confidante and knew about the past. Seeing no one around, she spoke softly to comfort her.

Princess Yi’an felt even more indignant. "Back then, when Mother Empress wanted to expel Cui Yichu, he didn’t say a single word. Now he has the nerve to question me?"

The maid was at a loss for words.

Princess Yi’an coldly scoffed and continued, "Tell me, if he truly cared about Cui Yichu, why didn’t he argue with Mother Empress back then? If he didn’t care then, why is he acting like she’s precious now?"

The maid replied softly, "Back then, he didn’t care because the Crown Prince had already gotten what he wanted and grown tired of her."

Princess Yi’an didn’t doubt the Crown Prince’s fickleness for a moment.

"And now? Cui Yichu is already a discarded woman. If he truly cares, he could bring her into the Eastern Palace. Why take it out on me?"

The maid looked around cautiously before whispering, "The Crown Prince and the Crown Princess have always been distant. It’s been over a year since their marriage, and there’s still no sign of a child. Perhaps he’s started missing the good times with her."

The Crown Princess was the Empress’s niece from her maternal family. Though her background was comparable to Cui Yichu’s, her talent and beauty were far inferior.

The Empress was determined to uphold her family’s honor and wanted her niece to bear the heir, so she had forbidden the Crown Prince from taking concubines.

All the women who had served the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace had been given contraceptive medicine.

Seeing Princess Yi’an’s expression soften slightly, the maid advised further, "It’s just bad luck that you encountered the Crown Prince in a foul mood today. He’s just randomly taking out his anger. Don’t take it to heart, Your Highness."

Princess Yi’an still felt wronged. She thought to herself: Why did the Crown Prince suddenly lash out today after more than two years of peace? Could it be because Mother Empress told him that I’ve taken a fancy to Zhao Xuanyou? But I told the Empress about this long ago, and the Crown Prince comes to pay his respects to the Empress every day. Why did he only react today?

The Crown Prince went to Cangxi Town today. He didn’t meet Zhao Xuanyou and me there... So he...

A thought suddenly struck Princess Yi’an. She recalled Yu Yuan’s delicate and graceful face. It all made sense now.

Yes, the town was so small. The Crown Prince must have seen Yu Yuan in Cangxi Town, which reminded him of Cui Yichu and made him nostalgic. That’s why he took it out on me.

Princess Yi’an felt a surge of anger and cursed silently: It’s all that dead girl’s fault!

---

The Crown Prince entered Chonghua Palace with a dark expression. The palace was filled with precious artifacts and luxurious decorations, all dazzling to the eye.

The palace attendants, seeing his foul mood, knelt to pay their respects.

The Crown Princess, seeing him enter, quickly stood up to greet him, bowing respectfully. "Your Highness."

The Crown Prince shot her a disdainful glance and, without a word, walked straight into the inner palace.

He had never felt much for this cousin of his.

The Empress had long intended for her to be his wife, but the Emperor had not approved. After a long stalemate, the Emperor allowed him to decide for himself.

If he had to choose from the noble ladies of the capital, the Crown Prince’s heart had always been set on Cui Yichu.

He had always loved beautiful women, and in the entire capital, no one could compare to Cui Yichu’s beauty.

Once, while traveling outside the capital with his sisters, he had, in a drunken stupor, taken Cui Yichu into his tent, where they had shared a night of passion.

He had made her no promises, and she had asked for none. It was this very cool detachment that made him want to possess her all the more.

How could the palace maids from the Bureau of Service compare to Cui Yichu?

Zhao Zun had tasted the finest and could not forget it. Whenever he had the chance, he would seek her out.

He had wanted to make Cui Yichu his Crown Princess, but the appointment of a Crown Princess was a major affair, not something he could decide alone.

Zhao Zun had grown up under the Empress’s dominance and was used to obeying her. He didn’t dare to defy her wishes. So, against his own heart, he had named his cousin before the Emperor.

The Empress had been overjoyed, but the Emperor’s expression had been solemn.

Nevertheless, the Emperor’s word was law, and he immediately decreed the marriage between Zhao Zun and his cousin.

He had wanted to make Cui Yichu a concubine, but the Empress had said that Cui Yichu had already lost her chastity and was unfit to marry into the imperial family.

Seeing his disappointment, the Empress had given him a task to leave the capital and travel, hoping it would distract him.

But when the Crown Prince returned to the capital three months later, Cui Yichu had already been expelled from the palace by the Empress and sent back to the Xingguo Duke’s residence.

The Empress had said, "You are the Crown Prince. When you ascend the throne, you can have as many beauties as you want. Why cling to just one?"

Though displeased, the Crown Prince hadn’t dared to defy the Empress and suppressed his feelings.

But today, upon seeing the maid named Yu Yuan, the sweet memories with Cui Yichu came flooding back.

If he had married Cui Yichu back then, would his life now be so bland and tasteless?

chapters.title: Teaching Her to Write
chapters.content:
Yu Wan had been so busy these days that she barely had time to rest, working tirelessly day and night.

Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta took turns teaching, while Yu Wan spent half her day accompanying Zhao Qi in his training and the other half attending lectures. At night, she still had to handle Zhao Xuanyou’s various orders; truly working from dawn till dusk without a moment’s respite.

One day, as Yu Wan was busy sorting through the clean clothes sent by the eunuchs, she couldn’t help but let out a long yawn.

Zhao Xuanyou was seated in the study, pen in hand, writing a letter. Hearing the sound, he looked up at her.

Yu Wan’s face flushed. She lowered her head and continued sorting the clothes, pretending nothing had happened.

“Not awake yet?” Zhao Xuanyou’s lips curled slightly, his tone tinged with amusement.

Yu Wan felt a flicker of annoyance in her heart. Did he not know whether she had slept well or not?

She didn’t bother to argue. After all, he was the master. If she kept disputing, she would only end up at a disadvantage.

Seeing the aggrieved look on her face, Zhao Xuanyou let out a soft laugh, as if murmuring to himself or comforting her: “Next time we go out, bring more people along.”

Hearing this, Yu Wan couldn’t help but look up. “Master, you know that this servant has to do the work of several people alone?”

“I know.” Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

“Then shouldn’t Master give this servant a little more pay?” Yu Wan took the opportunity to bargain.

This girl really had her mind set on money.

Zhao Xuanyou paused briefly before replying in a gentle tone, “When we return to the capital, I’ll pay you double for these two months.”

Yu Wan’s face lit up at once, and her earlier fatigue vanished. Seeing her like this, Zhao Xuanyou chuckled inwardly and continued writing.

After folding the clothes, Yu Wan picked up the teapot to refill his tea.

Zhao Xuanyou held the brush, but his gaze involuntarily fell on her graceful figure. A thought suddenly struck him.

“Last time you said your mother taught you to recognize characters.”

“She did, but not many.” Yu Wan had once thought she knew quite a few characters, but after attending half a month of Pei Ta’s lessons, she realized that she didn’t recognize a small portion of the characters in the texts.

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow. “Can you write?”

“I suppose so.” Yu Wan lowered her head in embarrassment.

“Write something for me to see.” Zhao Xuanyou handed her the brush in his hand.

Yu Wan quickly waved her hands. “This servant has only written with sticks on the ground before. I don’t know how to use a brush.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered at her words, then slowly said, “I’ll teach you.”

Yu Wan looked at him in disbelief. “Master means…?”

Zhao Xuanyou said no more. He directly placed the brush in her hand and laid out a fresh sheet of paper on the table.

Yu Wan held the brush like a pair of chopsticks, her fingers stiff and movements awkward.

Seeing how nervous she was, Zhao Xuanyou found it amusing. He reached out and took her hand, adjusting her grip on the brush bit by bit.

“Don’t grip it too tightly. Hold it with your thumb, index, and middle fingers…” Zhao Xuanyou instructed softly.

Yu Wan let him adjust her hand, feeling as if her fingers no longer belonged to her.

She couldn’t help but ask, “Master, why must we hold the brush in such a strange way?”

Zhao Xuanyou saw her asking like a child just learning to write. He suppressed a laugh and said with a straight face, “You’ve only just started practicing. Once you write more, you’ll realize this is the only way to hold it properly.”

“Then how long must I practice before I get used to it?” Yu Wan asked again.

“Depends on your talent.” Zhao Xuanyou said indifferently.

Yu Wan humphed inwardly, thinking he was mocking her lack of talent.

However, though Zhao Xuanyou’s words were sharp, he was extremely serious about teaching her.

He stood behind her, one hand resting on her shoulder, the other guiding her hand holding the brush, teaching her to write stroke by stroke.

He started with the characters “Yu Wan.” Just as a schoolteacher would first teach students to write their own names, Yu Wan, with his guidance, quickly wrote out her name.

“Look at your characters. Though you’ve barely managed to form the shapes, there’s no sense of stroke technique at all.” Zhao Xuanyou commented.

“I’m already happy I didn’t write them wrong. How can I compare to Master’s handwriting?” Yu Wan said self-deprecatingly.

“Everyone’s handwriting has its own characteristics. You don’t need to compare yourself to me, but you should at least write with proper form.” Zhao Xuanyou’s tone was gentle, yet carried an unyielding firmness.

Yu Wan looked at the crooked characters on the paper, feeling a mix of frustration and determination. She silently vowed to practice her writing well.

Zhao Xuanyou saw her expression and, still holding her hand, wrote a few more characters.

Just then, Princess Yi’an, dressed in brocade and finery, entered the small courtyard.

Through the window’s gauze, she saw Zhao Xuanyou holding Yu Wan’s hand, the two of them intimately writing together. A flood of emotions surged within her. Relying on her status, she didn’t stop but walked straight toward the main room.

“Princess Yi’an.” Sun Qianran, seeing Princess Yi’an’s arrival, quickly stood up to greet her.

Princess Yi’an forced a smile. “Sister Sun, there’s no need for such formalities.”

Sun Qianran led her to a seat and ordered the maid Xiang Xu to serve tea.

Princess Yi’an took a light sip. The tea’s fragrance lingered, and its aftertaste was sweet; truly fine quality.

“Sister Sun, have you been feeling better since coming to the Liuchuan Imperial Palace?” Princess Yi’an asked.

“The air in Liuchuan is fresh, and the climate is pleasant. It’s indeed more comfortable than in the capital.” Sun Qianran replied.

Princess Yi’an gave a slight nod.

“Mother knows you’ve been unwell, so she excused you from paying respects at the Crystal Palace. But she has been thinking of you constantly. Yesterday, the Imperial Household Department sent several fine ginseng roots, and she specially set one aside for you.”

The Empress had recently been working to win over court officials for the Crown Prince. As a prominent minister, Sun Xiang was naturally among them.

However, Sun Xiang was cunning and cautious. The Empress had tried to probe him multiple times but had never succeeded, so she turned her attention to Sun Qianran instead.

Though Sun Qianran was a woman of the inner chambers, she was well-read and deeply understood court affairs.

She didn’t want Pei Ta involved in the struggle for the throne and hoped he could remain untainted. Therefore, she had declined all the palace banquets in the imperial residence, citing illness.

Today, Princess Yi’an had personally delivered the ginseng, so Sun Qianran naturally couldn’t refuse.

“The Empress’s kindness toward me is something I will always remember and can never repay. However, my poor appearance is unfit for a palace audience. I must trouble Princess Yi’an to convey my gratitude on my behalf.”

As she spoke, Sun Qianran, supported by a maid, knelt down in front of the palace maid holding the ginseng.

Princess Yi’an reached out to help her up. “Mother bestowed the ginseng upon you in hopes that you would take good care of yourself and recover your health. She doesn’t care for these empty formalities.”

Sun Qianran understood the deeper meaning in her words. The Empress’s intention was to gain the Sun family’s support.

She gave a noncommittal response and said no more.

Though Princess Yi’an had come today at the Empress’s behest, her mind was not on this matter. After the Crown Prince had reminded her that Zhao Xuanyou was of the same generation as her, she hadn’t dared to rashly bring up the matter to the Emperor.

The Crown Prince’s words were true; the Emperor valued propriety.

Even though Zhao Xuanyou’s lineage was not of the imperial family, the Emperor had always treated him as a member of the royal clan.

Troubled, she had come to the separate residence, intending to sound out Zhao Xuanyou. Unexpectedly, she had caught him in an intimate moment with Yu Wan, even teaching the maid to write…

“Princess Yi’an, try this osmanthus cake.” Sun Qianran noticed Princess Yi’an’s distraction and subtly pushed a plate of pastries toward her.

Princess Yi’an’s expression was complex. She didn’t even touch the plate, staring straight at Sun Qianran as she asked, “Sister Sun, are you still familiar with that maid from the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence?”

---

chapters.title: Jealousy
chapters.content:
The Jingyuan Marquis’s residence had only brought one maid to the Liuchuan Imperial Palace. At Princess Yi’an’s first words, Sun Qianran knew exactly whom she was referring to.

“Is the Princess speaking of Miss Yu Wan, who attends to Lord Zhao?” Sun Qianran smiled slightly, her tone gentle.

Princess Yi’an slightly restrained the darkness in her eyes and feigned indifference. “Is her name Yu Wan? I wasn’t aware.”

Not aware?

If she truly wasn’t, why bring it up?

Sun Qianran knew she was pretending but didn’t expose her, merely giving a faint smile.

“Lord Zhao only brought two attendants and one maid. If the Princess has seen a maid from the Marquis’s residence, it must be Yu Wan. May I ask why the Princess is inquiring about her?”

Princess Yi’an hadn’t stated it outright, but Sun Qianran had long noticed the signs; her frequent visits to the small courtyard.

At first, she had thought the two princesses were coming for Pei Ta, but then realized how absurd that was.

How could a princess covet another woman’s husband?

It wasn’t until the two princesses had personally invited Zhao Xuanyou out of the palace for an outing that Sun Qianran had confirmed Princess Yi’an’s interest was in Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou had already ended his marriage with Cui Yichu. Given his martial arts, appearance, and status at court, it wasn’t surprising that a princess would take a fancy to him.

Sun Qianran had initially thought the only obstacle was that Zhao Xuanyou shared the same surname as the imperial family.

However, the current dynasty had an open-minded culture that didn’t prohibit marriages between people of the same surname. With Princess Yi’an being a favorite of the Emperor and Empress, perhaps the Emperor would consent to this marriage.

She dared to act so boldly, so the Emperor and Empress must have heard something.

Seeing Princess Yi’an’s troubled expression now, Sun Qianran understood; regardless of whether the Empress knew, the Emperor certainly did not.

If the Son of Heaven had already given his decree, why would she be troubled by a mere maid?

The current problem was: Princess Yi’an wanted to marry Zhao Xuanyou, but Zhao Xuanyou had no such intention.

“Is she Lord Zhao’s concubine?” Princess Yi’an asked casually.

“Presumably.” Sun Qianran was a light sleeper. Since they lived in the same courtyard, she had faintly heard some noises at night.

Lord Zhao was in his prime, strong and healthy, and Yu Wan also had a rosy complexion and was efficient in her work. The way they got along seemed like a perfect match.

Of course, Sun Qianran wouldn’t say these things to Princess Yi’an, nor would she mention them to Pei Ta.

Yu Wan and Pei Ta had never overstepped their bounds, but for some reason, Sun Qianran didn’t like seeing Yu Wan close to Pei Ta. Even if it was just standing a little closer, she felt a pang of loss. For this reason, she could understand Princess Yi’an’s feelings.

What puzzled her was that she was jealous of Pei Ta because he was her husband. But Zhao Xuanyou and Princess Yi’an had no connection. Why didn’t Princess Yi’an go to the Emperor to find a solution? Why take it out on Yu Wan?

“Though she’s just a concubine, I see that Lord Zhao values her greatly.” Princess Yi’an’s tone carried a hint of probing.

“How so?” Sun Qianran pretended not to understand.

Princess Yi’an smiled. “You live in the same courtyard as Lord Zhao. How can you not know? Mother often praises Sister Sun for your wisdom, saying you’re a paragon among the noble ladies of the capital. Why pretend to be ignorant in front of me?”

Sun Qianran replied coolly, “The Princess jokes. I only recognize a few characters. How can that be called wisdom? My health is poor, and I rarely go out. I truly don’t know much about Lord Zhao’s affairs.”

“Is that so?” Princess Yi’an’s tone carried a hint of displeasure.

Sun Qianran saw this and softly said, “Yu Wan is Lord Zhao’s concubine. Since he brought only her to Liuchuan, he must care for her deeply. If the Princess is curious about Yu Wan, you must have noticed that she bears some resemblance to Yichu. I think that’s why Lord Zhao dotes on her so much.”

“Perhaps.” Princess Yi’an’s smile was meaningful. “That day in Cangxi Town, Lord Zhao rode back to the imperial palace with Yu Wan on the same horse in full view of everyone, completely unashamed. It was quite a spectacle.”

“Indeed.” Sun Qianran softly agreed.

“Just now, when I entered, I saw Lord Zhao teaching Yu Wan to write.”

“Yu Wan is quite a diligent learner.” Sun Qianran’s tone carried a hint of approval.

Princess Yi’an detected that her previous words had been perfunctory, but this statement seemed genuine. She couldn’t help but sneer. “Isn’t she a good learner? A mere maid, getting daily poetry lessons from Lord Pei and now writing lessons from Lord Zhao; what good fortune.”

Hearing her drag Pei Ta into this, Sun Qianran calmly defended, “My husband is teaching the Seventh Prince by imperial decree. Coincidentally, Miss Yu Wan gets along well with the Seventh Prince. Whether it’s training or studying, the Seventh Prince insists on having her attend him.”

“She’s just using some vulgar tricks.” Princess Yi’an shot Sun Qianran a cold glance, her words laced with sarcasm. “Of the three men in this courtyard, setting aside Lord Zhao, my seventh brother is completely besotted with her. As for Lord Pei, Sister Sun, you’d better be careful.”

Sun Qianran didn’t like seeing Yu Wan close to Pei Ta, but hearing Princess Yi’an speak this way, she found it amusing.

A princess actually resorting to sowing discord over a maid.

However, she knew Princess Yi’an had a narrow mind and didn’t want to openly offend her. So she went along with her words. “The Princess speaks truly. Unfortunately, I am in poor health. Managing myself is already difficult enough; how can I manage others?”

With that, Sun Qianran let out a few light coughs, appearing even more frail.

Princess Yi’an saw she was impervious to her words and silently called her useless. She stood up and said, “Sister Sun, since you’re unwell, I won’t disturb you further. Rest well.”

“Your Highness, safe travels.”

Sun Qianran watched her departing figure and ordered Xiang Xu to put away the ginseng.

Earlier, when Princess Yi’an had been speaking with Sun Qianran, she hadn’t dismissed her attendants. Xiang Xu had heard everything clearly. Returning to Sun Qianran’s side, she gently massaged her legs and whispered, “Madam, Yu Wan wouldn’t…”

Xiang Xu often moved about the courtyard. During Zhao Qi’s lessons, the doors and windows of the room were wide open. Yu Wan stood respectfully to the side, never interrupting. How could she be seducing Pei Ta?

Sun Qianran replied indifferently, “Of course I know it’s all nonsense. I was just going along with her words.”

“I truly didn’t expect that a princess like Her Highness would be so concerned about a maid.” Xiang Xu, also a maid herself, couldn’t help but feel a sense of shared sympathy.

“Do you like Yu Wan?” Sun Qianran asked in return.

Xiang Xu felt a little embarrassed and whispered, “I just think she’s not that kind of person.”

Sun Qianran gave a faint smile. Setting aside Zhao Xuanyou, people like Zhao Qi and Xiang Xu liked Yu Wan not because she used any vulgar tricks.

Yu Wan was charming and alluring, with a pair of eyes that sparkled like a spring; captivating and full of life.

Her appearance was already extraordinary, but her personality was even more rare.

She was gentle and witty, cheerful and generous. Both men and women enjoyed her company.

Sun Qianran’s concern about Yu Wan wasn’t because she was a vixen who seduced men. Rather, Yu Wan was the healthy version of herself that Sun Qianran imagined.

Sun Qianran let out a sigh.

Unfortunately, Princess Yi’an wouldn’t think that way. Since she had set her sights on Yu Wan despite her status, she likely wouldn’t give up easily.

Whether Yu Wan could survive this ordeal remained to be seen.

chapters.title: Persistent Effort
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou had guided Yuhan in writing more than a dozen characters.

Although Yuhan’s calligraphy still lacked any sense of brushwork, her grip on the brush was now proper and standard; her fingers no longer wrestled with the brush handle.

"How is it? Still think the way of holding the brush is too strange?" Zhao Xuanyou teased.

Yuhan replied, "It is this servant’s ignorance. I beg the Young Master not to mock me anymore."

Zhao Xuanyou had never intended to mock her.

At first, he thought Yuhan was clever in her actions, but later, seeing her single-minded desire to follow Zhao Qi in his studies, he thought her a bit ambitious.

After personally teaching her to write, Zhao Xuanyou realized she was indeed highly gifted.

Whenever she made a mistake, a single correction was enough; she would never repeat it.

If Yuhan had not been born into a peasant family but instead into a noble household in the capital, her talent would surely rival that of Cui Yichu and Sun Qianran; perhaps even surpassing them.

Compared to those pampered noble ladies, Yuhan seemed to possess an inexhaustible persistence.

Most beginners found it uncomfortable to write with a suspended wrist, and their wrists would ache after a short while, but she was full of enthusiasm and did not feel tired at all.

Zhao Xuanyou, with a stern face, said, "Write well, and naturally, I won’t mock you anymore."

Seeing his cold expression, Yuhan, of course, did not mind.

On the contrary, she was quite grateful that he had taken the time to teach her calligraphy today.

Previously, Zhao Xuanyou had been displeased with her going to Zhao Qi’s study to attend to him, but she had insisted on going despite the risk of displeasing him.

Now that he was willing to teach her calligraphy, it meant he had fully accepted her presence in the study. She no longer had to worry about being punished upon returning to the Marquis’s residence.

Noticing that his teacup was empty, Yuhan put down the brush, went outside to fetch hot water, and re-steeped the tea.

As Zhao Xuanyou leisurely sat to the side drinking tea, Yuhan laid out a fresh sheet of paper, picked up the brush, dipped it in ink, and began writing.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered.

She truly had an inexhaustible persistence.

"Master, why does my horizontal stroke never look like yours no matter how I write it?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s horizontal strokes were very elegant. Although they were horizontal, they slanted slightly, thin on the left and thick on the right, with a beautiful arc at the end of the stroke.

Yuhan tried to copy them, but her attempts turned out even uglier than her usual writing.

After filling an entire sheet, it still looked terrible.

"Practicing calligraphy is like training in martial arts. Without three to five years of effort, you won’t see results. What’s the rush?" Zhao Xuanyou looked at the more than ten sheets of paper she had filled with scribbles and suddenly had an idea. Remembering how Yuhan’s eyes lit up whenever money was mentioned, he slowly said, "My paper is made by Chengxin Hall. A stack costs one gold. You’ve written so much. Shouldn’t the cost be deducted from your monthly allowance?"

Yuhan had never heard of Chengxin Hall, but upon hearing that a stack of paper cost one gold, she was shocked. That was as expensive as gold itself!

No, it was even more expensive than gold. Gold could still be used as money after being written or drawn on, but paper became worthless once used.

"Then... the ones before were written by you, Master, not me. If you must deduct, you can only deduct for this one sheet!"

Although Yuhan was making excuses, her heart still ached.

Even one sheet might cost her a string of cash.

"I won’t delay Master’s writing anymore." Yuhan took back her scribbled sheet, wanting to leave quickly.

"I was just joking with you!" Zhao Xuanyou saw that she had actually believed him and reached out to grab her sleeve.

"I really won’t write anymore." Yuhan said firmly.

Zhao Xuanyou was unpredictable. If she wrote now, who knew if he might bring out the stack of paper later and demand she pay for it.

"Write when I tell you to." Zhao Xuanyou was a little annoyed by her stubbornness. He had only been teasing, but she had actually taken him for a miser.

"I really won’t write anymore."

"Do you really think I can’t afford a few sheets of paper?"

Yuhan replied, "It’s not that Master can’t afford it, but that I can’t. This paper is so fine, it feels like silk. It would be a waste for me to practice on it. The Seventh Prince will be here soon, and I still need to tidy up the study."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s displeased expression, Yuhan was confused.

Wasn’t it he who had brought up the high cost of paper? Why was he angry now?

Not daring to provoke him further, Yuhan brought him a plate of pastries before leaving.

In the afternoon, when Zhao Qi had his lesson, she wiped down the desk and chairs, then arranged the four treasures of the study.

Just as she finished, Pei Ta entered with a book.

"Minister Pei." Yuhan greeted him, and right after, Zhao Qi walked in. "Seventh Prince."

Zhao Qi only responded with an "mm," exchanged a few pleasantries with Pei Ta, and then took his seat.

Today, Pei Ta’s lecture was on the imperial household registration system. Compared to previous lessons, Yuhan understood much more.

She and her mother had originally been registered as farmers. After selling their land and coming to the capital, her mother became a drifter, while she entered servitude.

If she wanted to leave in the future, she would have to figure out the household registration matter carefully.

Thus, Yuhan listened with particular attention, memorizing how the court settled drifters and how one could free themselves from servitude.

By the time Pei Ta finished his hour-long lecture, Yuhan had a general direction in mind.

"The lesson is over. Where are my pastries?" Zhao Qi, seeing Yuhan listening intently, could not help but knock on the table.

Only then did Yuhan realize she had forgotten to serve Zhao Qi refreshments. She hurried to the kitchen to fetch some.

She brought back Zhao Qi’s favorite snow pear soup and eight-treasure cake. After taking a bite, Zhao Qi’s anger slightly subsided, but he could not help scolding her: "I don’t know if it’s you having the lesson or me. You’re listening more carefully than I am."

Yuhan, fearing she had offended Zhao Qi and might be thrown out of the study, lowered her head and smiled apologetically: "Your Highness, forgive me. It was my negligence."

Her attitude in admitting mistakes was always good, and with such a low posture, Zhao Qi could not find fault.

Pei Ta finished organizing his lecture notes and asked gently, "Miss Yuhan, I heard from my wife that you’ve been practicing calligraphy?"

"I’m just learning to write my name, but I write so poorly. The Young Master said it would take three to five years to see any improvement."

"Calligraphy is about conveying meaning through paper. The primary purpose is to make it legible. Whether it looks good or not is secondary. Miss Yuhan, you need not worry too much about it."

Zhao Qi’s own calligraphy was not great. Hearing this, he suddenly had a newfound respect for Pei Ta.

"You’re right. As long as it’s legible, what’s the point of writing so well?"

Yuhan found this perspective novel, though she thought Pei Ta was just being kind to console her.

She had seen Pei Ta’s writings while tidying the study. Even though she knew nothing about calligraphy, she found them pleasing to the eye.

"Yes, I understand." Yuhan, of course, would not refuse his kindness. Remembering Zhao Xuanyou’s earlier words, she smiled helplessly. "I never thought I could write well. Xuan paper is so expensive, how could I afford it?"

Although she had always known that only wealthy noble families could afford to educate their children for the imperial examinations, today’s experience with the Xuan paper gave her a deeper understanding of this reality.

How could a poor family, unable to even afford the basic brush, ink, paper, and inkstone, talk about studying?

Among the three people in the study, Zhao Qi was completely unaware of the hardships of common people. As he ate the eight-treasure cake, he heard Yuhan’s words and could not help but look up.

Because his mouth was still full of sweet and glutinous food, his speech was muffled.

"Paper? Expensive?"

---

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.content:
Zhao Qi’s words plunged the study into silence.

Yuhan truly did not know how to explain to this imperial prince how prohibitively expensive practice paper was for her.

Pei Ta, noticing her embarrassment, spoke gently: "Yuhan works in the Marquis’s residence with a limited monthly allowance. Buying paper and brushes would indeed be a significant expense for her."

"I see." Zhao Qi glanced at Yuhan, who stood with her head lowered, and said casually, "I have some scrap paper I don’t care for. I’ll throw some your way another day."

"Thank you for your grace, Your Highness."

After spending so many days together, Yuhan had a rough understanding of Zhao Qi’s temperament. Though he was sharp-tongued and enjoyed arguing, he was quite lenient with his subordinates.

Moreover, he was a prince; his so-called "scrap paper" was certainly not truly worthless.

As they were talking, Sun Qianran, supported by Xiang Xu, walked in slowly with a smile. "Class is over. Why are you all still chatting so lively?"

Upon seeing her, Pei Ta stepped forward to help her in, and after she was seated, he said slowly, "Yuhan wants to practice calligraphy but is worried about the cost of paper."

"You are truly diligent and eager to improve, Yuhan." Sun Qianran praised.

Yuhan bowed to Sun Qianran. "You flatter me, Madam. I am just a servant; there’s nothing for me to improve. I only thought that if I could write a few characters, I might be able to handle more important tasks in the future."

"Speaking of practicing calligraphy, I just remembered something my husband once mentioned." Sun Qianran smiled slightly.

Pei Ta understood her meaning and looked at her with a smile.

He was already handsome, and with a slight smile, his eyebrows and eyes exuded an even more refined charm, like a gentle spring breeze and fine rain, which made Sun Qianran’s heart flutter, and she blushed slightly.

She turned her head slightly, shifting her gaze to Yuhan, and said softly, "In the past, when my husband was a student and short on money, he bought coarse paper to practice calligraphy."

"Coarse paper?" Yuhan looked at Pei Ta in shock. How could the son of a county magistrate be so destitute?

How could one write on such rough paper?

As she was surprised, Zhao Qi on the side frowned and asked, "What is coarse paper?"

Sure enough, he was an imperial prince who did not even know what coarse paper was.

Yuhan did not know how to explain it to him, so she vaguely said, "It’s a very cheap and rough kind of paper. It’s so coarse that it pricks your hand when you hold it."

"Oh." Zhao Qi nodded as if he understood, though he clearly did not.

Sun Qianran continued, "To save ink, my husband dipped his brush in water and practiced on the coarse paper. After writing, he would dry the paper in the sun and reuse it."

"Ah, I see!" Yuhan suddenly realized and looked at the Pei couple with gratitude. "This method is perfect for me. It saves both money and paper. Thank you, Minister Pei and Madam Pei, for your guidance."

Seeing the three of them chatting animatedly, Zhao Qi was completely confused. The next day, when he arrived, he saw several sheets of brownish paper on the desk.

Was this what Yuhan used for practice?

Recalling her words from the previous day, he could not help but reach out and touch it.

Hmm... It really did prick his hand.

That day, after finishing his lesson, Zhao Qi did not have time to finish his snacks and hurried to the Mingde Hall.

The Emperor had specifically ordered a family banquet that evening. Zhao Qi, who feared neither heaven nor earth, did not dare to disobey the Emperor’s command.

Even if the only relative present in the hall was the Emperor himself, he had to attend.

Upon entering Mingde Hall, a eunuch led him to his seat.

The Sixth Prince, Zhao Yu, had arrived before him. The two had a poor relationship and, although seated next to each other, ignored one another.

Soon after, Princess Yi’an and Princess Yi’ning arrived.

The two sisters did not look pleased either. They only forced out a greeting, "Sixth Brother, Seventh Brother," before falling silent.

Amid the awkward silence, the two Consorts Li and Consort Wen, who had accompanied the Emperor to Liaochuan, arrived. According to custom, the Empress and the Crown Prince should have arrived by now, but unexpectedly, the Emperor emerged from his bedchamber with the young and beautiful Noble Consort Qin.

The Emperor seemed to be in high spirits. After taking his seat, he inquired about Zhao Yu and Zhao Qi’s studies.

Zhao Yu and Zhao Qi answered one by one. As they were speaking, the Empress and the Crown Prince finally arrived.

"Your Majesty, please forgive my tardiness." The Empress was clearly surprised. The Emperor had come out earlier than expected, and before she had arrived, how had the eunuch already invited the Emperor out?

Crown Prince Zhao Zhen followed behind the Empress, apologizing.

"It’s just a family meal. There’s no such thing as being late. Everyone, please be seated." The Emperor said slowly.

"Thank you, Your Majesty." The Empress led the Crown Prince to their seats. With everyone present, the family banquet officially began.

Even for a family banquet, the imperial feast was filled with rare delicacies. However, the attendees were each lost in their own thoughts and had no appetite.

Halfway through the banquet, the Emperor set down his chopsticks and once again asked about Zhao Yu and Zhao Qi’s studies.

"You two have not neglected your studies since coming to Liaochuan. This pleases me greatly."

The Empress smiled gently. "Yu has always been clever and obedient. Whether in the capital or Liaochuan, he has been equally diligent. As for Qi, he has truly impressed me. Who would have thought he could settle down and study both literature and martial arts? However, I must remind you; mastering a skill requires precision. Don’t just put on a show of studying to please His Majesty, only to end up achieving nothing."

Zhao Qi was no fool. He could tell the Empress was mocking him. Unable to restrain himself, he retorted, "If it’s about pleasing Father Emperor, I learned that from the Crown Prince."

As soon as the words left his mouth, the Crown Prince’s eyes darkened.

The Empress let out a cold laugh in her heart and signaled the Crown Prince with her eyes, indicating he should not speak.

She had deliberately provoked Zhao Qi to let the Emperor see that he was useless. Sure enough, Zhao Qi took the bait.

The Emperor said indifferently, "Qi, is that how you speak to your mother?"

Zhao Qi was not one to back down, but under the Emperor’s gaze, he eventually lowered his head. "This son knows his mistake."

"I sent you to stay by Xuanyou’s side not only to train in martial arts but also to learn from his character."

At the mention of Zhao Xuanyou, the expressions of half the people in the hall subtly changed, their faces growing serious.

"I understand, Father Emperor." Zhao Qi said quietly.

The Empress spoke warmly, "Zhao Xuanyou has only been back in the capital for two months. Your Majesty’s trust in him suggests he is exceptionally capable."

The Emperor listened with interest and asked, "Does the Empress think I favor him too much?"

"I would not dare say that." The Empress said as if casually, "It’s just that Your Majesty has always been cautious in promoting officials. When you appointed Pei Ta, it was only after several senior officials recommended him. Zhao Xuanyou, however, seems to be an exception."

"The Marquis of Jingyuan has guarded the northwest for generations. Xuanyou led armies in his teens. I am well aware of his abilities. As for his character... he is of the Zhao clan, our own kin. Naturally, I trust him."

As soon as the words were spoken, Princess Yi’an’s chopsticks suddenly clattered to the ground.

The Empress, the Crown Prince, and Princess Yi’ning all turned to look at her, their expressions varying; some schadenfreude, some detached, some meaningful.

Princess Yi’an quickly composed herself, took a clean pair of chopsticks from a palace servant, and forced a smile as she looked at the Emperor.

"Father Emperor, although the Marquis of Jingyuan bears the surname Zhao, they are not descendants of Emperor Taizong. How can they be considered part of the imperial clan?"

"The Marquis of Jingyuan fought alongside Emperor Taizong to establish the dynasty, expanding and defending our borders. Their loyalty has spanned generations. How can they not be considered our own?
