"Old Lady." Yu Wan curtsied in greeting.

Old Lady Ye saw the empty street outside the gate and looked at Yu Wan. "Has the Seventh Prince already left?"

"Yes, His Highness’s carriage just departed."

"I see."

Old Lady Ye had also received word from the gatekeeper and had hurriedly changed clothes, bringing Fengchang to greet Zhao Qi.

Zhao Qi had left in a hurry, which saved them the trouble.

"How come you returned to the capital with the Seventh Prince when Xuanyou is still in Lichuan?"

Yu Wan’s sudden return caught Old Lady Ye off guard. Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t had time to send someone back to the capital with news, so Old Lady Ye was quite surprised.

"In response to Old Lady, when the Young Master left the capital last time, he didn’t bring enough things. He ordered this servant and Yuan Qing to return to the capital to fetch them. Coincidentally, the Seventh Prince was returning to the capital to celebrate the Duke of Ningguo’s heir’s birthday, so this servant and Yuan Qing traveled with the Seventh Prince."

The excuse had been prepared in advance. Even if Old Lady Ye noticed some inconsistencies, she wouldn’t question her in front of so many servants at the gate.

She nodded and said no more, then, holding Fengchang’s hand, walked into the residence.

As she turned, Fengchang cast a resentful glance at Yu Wan.

Initially, when she heard that Yu Wan had returned to the capital early, she had been quite pleased.

Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t returned, but he had sent her back. It was obvious he was tired of her and had sent her back early.

Who would have thought that Yu Wan had returned with the Seventh Prince?

Fengchang had spent two years in the Prince of Ping’s residence and knew that the Emperor doted on his youngest son, allowing him to be wild and unrestrained. His older royal brothers often suffered at his hands.

But the Seventh Prince, who was rumored to be reckless and extravagant, had actually brought Yu Wan back?

Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t order the Seventh Prince around. If he had sent Yu Wan to the marquis’s residence, it must have been his own choice.

This woman was truly not to be underestimated.

Yu Wan, of course, felt Fengchang’s dark gaze, but she didn’t take it to heart.

After Old Lady Ye entered the residence, Yu Wan went in as well.

Returning to Honghui Hall, the courtyard was clean, and everything was as it had been.

Yu Wan was still in the courtyard when Yingxue, who was sitting under the veranda, came forward with a face full of joy.

"Sister, you’re back!"

"Yingxue!" After not seeing her for so long, Yu Wan happily took her hand.

During that month in Lichuan, Yu Wan had handled every detail for Zhao Xuanyou, and only then did she realize how hard Yingxue worked.

When she was at Honghui Hall, Yingxue had helped with everything, making her life much easier.

"Is the scenery in Lichuan very beautiful?"

"It truly is."

Yingxue sighed lightly and couldn’t help but exclaim, "I’m so envious of you, Sister. I wish I could leave the capital one day too."

Having grown up, Yingxue had never left the capital, let alone gone to a place like Lichuan.

"The Emperor goes to Lichuan every year, so there will be opportunities. Although you didn’t see the scenery this year, I brought you specialties from Lichuan. Try them."

Yu Wan and Yingxue went to the veranda and were dividing the food they had brought back when Yuan Qing entered the courtyard from outside and called out, "Yu Wan."

"Is something the matter?"

"There’s something. Come over here." Yuan Qing said vaguely.

Earlier, Yuan Qing had led the people carrying the box into the marquis’s residence. Now he had come to call for her. Could it be related to that box?

Thinking of Zhao Qi’s instruction before leaving to whip it hard to vent her anger, Yu Wan became even more certain.

She stood up and said to Yingxue, "The Young Master has ordered other things. I’ll go take a look."

Yingxue had no objections and went into the house to prepare a bed for Yu Wan.

Yu Wan followed Yuan Qing out of the courtyard. Following the wall of Honghui Hall, they soon arrived at a row of side rooms behind Honghui Hall.

Yu Wan’s confusion deepened. If Yuan Qing hadn’t led the way, she would have turned and run at this moment.

Entering the side room, the interior was no different from the other side rooms in the marquis’s residence; a narrow bed, a cabinet, and a small table.

Yuan Qing opened the cabinet door. Inside was pitch black; nothing could be seen.

He lit a lamp on the table, and only then did Yu Wan realize that the cabinet actually concealed a tunnel.

Yu Wan felt inexplicably tense. "What is this place?"

Yuan Qing grinned. "The marquis’s residence dungeon. Let’s go."

He held the lamp and walked ahead. Yu Wan suppressed her accelerating heartbeat and carefully followed him down a dozen steps, quickly descending one level.

The space below wasn’t spacious, about the size of two side rooms. An iron-barred cell had been partitioned off.

Yu Wan saw someone sitting against the wall inside and felt a stir in her heart.

"Is that the person in the box?"

Yuan Qing responded with an "mm" and, taking a key, opened the iron bars. He pulled the person sitting on the ground to their feet.

Hearing the sound of chains dragging, Yu Wan looked closely and saw that the person’s hands and feet were tightly bound with iron chains.

Yuan Qing said, "There’s a whip outside. Pick it up and give him a good lashing."

A whip?

After her initial shock, Yu Wan noticed a wall beside her covered with various torture instruments. Besides whips, there were daggers and other devices that looked painful and whose names she didn’t know.

So the marquis’s residence actually had such a dungeon, and it seemed to be right beneath Honghui Hall.

"If you don’t want to use the whip, pick something else you find handy," Yuan Qing urged from inside the cell.

"Why do you and His Highness insist that I do this?" Yu Wan was truly puzzled. "I’m just a servant. I can’t do this kind of task."

Yuan Qing heard this and suddenly paused, then laughed. "You don’t know who this person is?"

chapters.title: Cannot Die
chapters.content:
Yu Yuan looked at the person in the cell, her eyes filled with unfamiliarity.

It wasn't until Yuan Qing reached out and removed the mask from his face that Yu Yuan suddenly realized.

"Is this the person who kidnapped me?"

"Mm, Silver Bottle and the others chased him for a full day and night before catching him. The Seventh Prince said to leave him to you for punishment." Yuan Qing threw the mask onto the ground. The man seemed to react strongly, desperately trying to pick up the mask. Yuan Qing saw through his intention and kicked the mask away with his foot.

Yu Yuan listened to the heavy sound of chains scraping against the floor and glanced at the mask on the ground.

That night, to escape quickly, she had chatted with the kidnapper, and when she mentioned the mask, he had reacted as well.

After some thought, Yu Yuan bent down, picked up the gray mask, and placed it back inside the cell.

Yuan Qing watched her actions and knew she couldn't bring herself to harm him. He smiled and asked, "No whipping then?"

Yu Yuan shook her head.

Previously, Zhao Xuanyou had told her to deal with Bao Chan, but Bao Chan was still working in the Marquis's mansion, scrubbing chamber pots every day, yet living well.

That was someone who had a deep grudge against her, and she still couldn't bring herself to kill them personally. How could she do it to this shadow guard in front of her?

Yu Yuan could kill a chicken, but she truly couldn't kill a person.

The chains in the cell dragged as the shadow guard struggled to crawl to the cell door, picked up the mask, and placed it over his face.

It was at the moment he put on the mask that Yu Yuan saw half of his face covered by a bright red birthmark.

He was also a pitiful person.

Yu Yuan said, "Let's wait for the Heir to return and deal with him."

"Understood." As he spoke, Yuan Qing carried a bowl of water from outside the cell and placed it on the ground. He looked up at Yu Yuan, "In a couple of days, I have to return to Lichuan. Only you know he is locked here. If you don't kill him, remember to send him food every day."

"Send food?" Although Yu Yuan couldn't bring herself to whip him, every time she saw him, she recalled the terrifying day and night she was kidnapped by him. How could she bring herself to send him food?

"You can let him starve to death if you want," Yuan Qing scratched his head indifferently, "Anyway, both the Seventh Prince and the Master said to leave it to you. Life or death is not considered."

Starve to death?

Seeing Yu Yuan's troubled expression, Yuan Qing burst out laughing, "It's not that complicated. You can just bring him a bowl of water and throw a steamed bun in every day like this."

"That simple?"

"Cannot die." Yuan Qing turned back and pressed a few acupoints on the man's body. He relocked the cell door and led Yu Yuan out.

Yu Yuan felt the dungeon was quite eerie and quickly followed Yuan Qing, curiously asking, "Were you just pressing his acupoints?"

"Mm."

"What happens when his acupoints are pressed?"

"I pressed his mute acupoint and sleep acupoint."

Yu Yuan listened with partial understanding, "So he will keep sleeping and cannot speak? When I come to deliver food, I don't have to worry about anything."

"More or less. Anyway, you don't have to open the cell door. Just put the things down."

"Understood."

Yu Yuan sighed in her heart and secretly envied Yuan Qing.

Both were servants of the Marquis's mansion, but while she only knew how to plant flowers and cook porridge, Yuan Qing had learned a set of excellent martial arts.

If she also knew such skills and could control a person by pressing a few acupoints, how good would that be?

After leaving the dungeon, Yuan Qing locked the door of the side room.

"The key will be placed under the large vase in the main house. I estimate I'll stay in the mansion for another two days. You don't need to worry about him for now. We'll deal with it when I leave."

"Only one meal a day?"

"Of course," Yuan Qing laughed, "Don't be so nervous. He's just a prisoner. Do you expect him to have three meals a day with fish and meat? You can send food when you remember, and starve him for a day when you forget. Cannot die."

"Alright."

When she returned to Honghui Hall, Yingxue had already tidied up the side room where Yu Yuan lived and even helped her boil a large pot of water.

Yu Yuan had traveled a long way by boat and carriage and indeed needed a thorough wash.

After thanking Yingxue, Yu Yuan took care of herself and went to bed early.

The next morning, not long after she got up, Xing Mama from Leshou Hall came to deliver a message, saying that the Old Lady had something to ask her.

The Old Lady certainly didn't believe the explanation given at the mansion gate yesterday and would definitely seek clarification from her.

When she arrived at Leshou Hall, there were already several people inside.

Apart from Fengchang, the cousin Feng Jirou was also sitting in the room, chatting with Old Lady Ye about the crape myrtles in the garden.

She was at the prime age of sixteen, as pretty as a peach in spring, and her smile was extremely charming.

Before coming to the capital, her parents had repeatedly told her to ingratiate herself with the main wife, Cui Yichu, and to get close to Zhao Xuanyou.

Unexpectedly, not long after arriving at the Marquis's mansion, Cui Yichu had divorced Zhao Xuanyou, and Zhao Xuanyou had soon left the capital on a long journey.

The things her parents had repeatedly instructed her to do were now impossible. The Old Lady was kind and easygoing, so in the past month, Feng Jirou had lived more comfortably here than at her maiden home.

When she saw Yu Yuan enter, Old Lady Ye looked up, and Feng Jirou also stopped speaking.

"Has Miss Yu Yuan returned to the capital?"

"Slave greets Old Lady, Cousin, and Concubine Feng." After paying her respects to each of them, Yu Yuan said to Feng Jirou, "Slave returned to the capital last night."

"Has my cousin also returned?" Feng Jirou immediately became tense.

"The Heir is still at the Lichuan Traveling Palace." After saying this, Yu Yuan shifted her gaze to Old Lady Ye, "Yuan Qing has retrieved the item. He will return to Lichuan in a couple of days to serve."

Old Lady Ye's eyes flickered, and her gaze settled steadily on Yu Yuan.

Yuan Qing and Yu Yuan had returned together, claiming they needed to help Zhao Xuanyou retrieve something, but Yu Yuan stayed in the Marquis's mansion while Yuan Qing still had to go back.

It seemed that retrieving the item was just an excuse, and the real purpose was for Yuan Qing to send Yu Yuan back.

"Is Xuanyou doing well in Lichuan?"

Yu Yuan respectfully replied, "His Majesty often summons the Heir to accompany him, going to the hunting grounds together, and even has the Heir instruct the Seventh Prince in martial arts."

"Why would His Majesty have Xuanyou teach when there are so many experts in the palace?"

"Slave is not very clear about the matters at the Traveling Palace," Yu Yuan dared not presume the Emperor's intentions, "Perhaps the Heir and the Seventh Prince have a good rapport."

Old Lady Ye did not say more. She still didn't understand why Zhao Xuanyou had sent Yu Yuan back.

After he returned to the capital, it had always been Yu Yuan attending to him in his room, and he seemed quite at ease, showing no interest in Fengchang at all.

This time, he had only taken Yu Yuan, a single maid, to Lichuan, which was quite telling.

If nothing had happened, how could he suddenly send Yu Yuan back to the capital?

After some thought, Old Lady Ye stood up, "Come with me."

"Yes."

Yu Yuan stepped forward to support Old Lady Ye, and together they went to the inner room.

Feng Jirou and Fengchang sat outside, silently sipping their tea.

"It seems Old Lady has something to discuss with Yu Yuan. I'll take my leave first so as not to delay their important matters." Feng Jirou saw the situation and didn't know how long they would talk. She felt bored and restless.

Fengchang smiled faintly, "Cousin, you may leave first. I will inform Old Lady later."

"Thank you, Concubine Feng."

After Feng Jirou left the main hall, Fengchang, who was sitting to the side, had a slight darkening in her gaze.

Feng Jirou was the Heir's cousin. Once she entered the Marquis's mansion, she would undoubtedly become a honored concubine. Fengchang had no choice but to be polite to her.

But as for Yu Yuan... it was fine if the Heir favored her, but Old Lady also seemed to trust her a lot. She had even been invited into the inner room to talk, leaving her, Fengchang, cooling her heels out here.

She, a concubine, was being suppressed by a mere through-room maid... She had to think of a way to change this.

---

chapters.title: Excuse
chapters.content:
"What exactly happened? Why did Xuanyou suddenly send you back to the capital?"

After entering the inner room, Old Lady Ye ordered Xing Mama to close the door and asked directly.

"Old Lady is wise. There is indeed a reason." Yu Yuan finished speaking and, seeing that Old Lady Ye remained silent, continued respectfully, "This slave's face somewhat resembles that of Madame Cui. While at the separate residence, I encountered His Highness the Crown Prince and Princess Yi'an. The Heir saw them speaking to me and, fearing unnecessary complications, sent me back to the capital."

The room was filled with the scent of burning sandalwood incense, which was calming.

Old Lady Ye looked at Yu Yuan in surprise, "You encountered the Crown Prince?"

After a pause, she added, "And Princess Yi'an?"

"Yes."

"Both Their Highnesses were idly strolling around the separate residence of a minister when they encountered this slave."

"What did they say?"

Yu Yuan replied, "Not much. Princess Yi'an asked for my name and which mansion I served. I answered both."

"And the Crown Prince?"

"The Crown Prince did not speak to this slave."

These explanations had been thought out by Zhao Xuanyou in advance.

Her grandmother was intelligent; outright concealment would not work on her, but revealing everything was also not an option, as it might worry the elderly lady. So, it was better to tell only half the truth.

Sure enough, Old Lady Ye sighed deeply, "Xuanyou is used to staying outside. With Yuan Qing and Yuan Zhi attending to him, it's almost the same. It's good that you've returned to avoid unnecessary complications."

"Yes." After Yu Yuan respectfully finished speaking, she followed Zhao Xuanyou's prior instructions and brought up another matter to change the subject, "The Heir also asked this slave to relay a message to Old Lady."

"Is it about His Majesty including the Marquis's mansion in the Imperial Clan's records under the Ministry of Clan Affairs?"

The Emperor had issued a decree at the Lichuan Traveling Palace, and after Zhao Xuanyou received it, the Ministry of Clan Affairs had also sent an oral edict to the Marquis's mansion. Thus, Old Lady Ye was already aware.

"It's not that matter."

"What else could it be?"

Yu Yuan said, "The Heir said that His Majesty intends to bestow Princess Yinning in marriage to Young Master Ye Mojin of the Anning Marquis's family."

"Oh?" Old Lady Ye was somewhat surprised but not entirely taken aback.

After the Anning Marquis's family had produced a favored concubine, they had gained even more of the Emperor's favor. The young masters and ladies of the family often attended palace banquets.

Ye Mojin was a handsome young man, articulate and charming. It was not surprising that the Emperor would choose him as a son-in-law.

"Mo Han has always been carefree. After becoming an imperial son-in-law, he will have to restrain himself."

"The Heir thinks the same, which is why he asked this slave to inform Old Lady."

"I see."

Ye Mojin was a relative from Old Lady Ye's maiden family. He was a decent person but enjoyed socializing. Since the Emperor had taken a fancy to him, he must not cause any trouble before the marriage decree was issued. Giving him a heads-up to be more cautious would be wise.

Old Lady Ye nodded slightly, "This trip to Lichuan, you were the only one attending to him. It must have been hard. Now that you're back, rest well."

"Thank you, Old Lady." Hearing Old Lady Ye's words, even if they were just polite praise, they were still commendation. Yu Yuan struck while the iron was hot, "This slave has one matter to ask for a favor from Old Lady."

"What is it?"

"This slave has been in Lichuan for a month without a day off. Now that the Heir has not yet returned to the capital, this slave was wondering if I could take all the leave days together."

"You want to rest for two days?"

"Yes."

Old Lady Ye was not very familiar with Yu Yuan's background. Hearing her words, she asked, "Do you still have family in the capital?"

"My mother is still alive, but she is unwell. This slave wishes to visit her."

Yu Yuan knew that ever since Zhao Xuanyou had divorced Cui Yichu, Old Lady Ye's attitude toward her had changed.

She had gone from being a cherished pet to a flirtatious maid who would eventually be dismissed.

If she revealed that her mother was being treated at the Taoran Inn, it would only displease Old Lady Ye.

Old Lady Ye thought for a moment, "With Xuanyou not in the capital, there isn't much to do in Honghui Hall. Since you have filial piety and need rest, take two days off."

"Thank you, Old Lady."

"Do you understand the rules of the Marquis's mansion?"

"This slave understands. I will return before dinner."

In the Marquis's mansion, even if maids returned home, they could not stay overnight outside.

Previously, Yu Yuan had been with Zhao Xuanyou, so naturally, that didn't count. Now that Zhao Xuanyou was not around, breaking the rules would result in punishment.

Old Lady Ye knew Yu Yuan was clever and did not say more, waving her hand in dismissal.

Yu Yuan left the inner room and saw that Feng Jirou had already left, leaving only Fengchang sitting outside.

"Concubine Feng."

Fengchang nodded slightly, her gaze lingering on Yu Yuan.

Seeing Yu Yuan's face flushed with a rosy glow and full of joy, she assumed Yu Yuan had received a reward from Old Lady Ye and felt a pang of jealousy in her heart.

"Do you know when the Heir will return to the capital?"

"The Heir is traveling with His Majesty. He is expected to return in October."

"The Heir is not at home, and you don't have much to do in Honghui Hall. I have been managing the miscellaneous affairs of the mansion and am quite busy. From now on, you can come and help me."

She actually wanted her to help?

Yu Yuan had been busy from morning till night at the Lichuan Traveling Palace. Now that she had finally escaped Zhao Xuanyou, she naturally wanted to rest in the capital.

Moreover, Yu Yuan was not foolish.

She could sense Fengchang's hostility toward her. Knowing there was a tiger in the mountain, why would she willingly go and do hard labor, giving Fengchang a chance to nitpick?

Yu Yuan smiled and curtsied to Fengchang.

"Thank you for your kindness, Concubine Feng. However, before returning to the capital, the Heir specifically entrusted this slave with some tasks. This slave must first complete the Heir's assignments and truly cannot help you share the burden."

Fengchang heard this and her delicate eyebrows slightly rose.

What a silver-tongued, foul-mouthed girl! She actually dared to use Zhao Xuanyou's authority to pressure her.

Yu Yuan was indeed cunning. As long as she stayed in Honghui Hall, even if Fengchang managed the inner mansion's affairs, it would be difficult for her to touch Yu Yuan.

"You are, after all, a person by the Heir's side. I cannot command you."

Yu Yuan remained polite, "Madam is the mistress, and this slave is a maid. If Madam has any orders, this slave dare not disobey. It's just that the Heir has given commands, and this slave is foolish. I fear delaying the Heir's tasks and thus have to decline Madam's kind offer."

Fengchang was about to reprimand her when she saw Xing Mama carrying a bowl of medicine approaching. The anger in her heart instantly turned into schadenfreude.

"Xing Mama, what is this?"

Xing Mama walked up to Yu Yuan and said expressionlessly, "This is the tonic that Old Lady has bestowed upon Yu Yuan."

A thick bowl of medicinal soup, still steaming, had apparently been prepared early in the morning, timed for when Yu Yuan would come to give her report.

Old Lady was indeed meticulous.

Before leaving, there was a bowl of medicine, and upon returning, there was another.

"Thank you for Old Lady's bestowment." Yu Yuan was genuinely grateful. With Old Lady providing the medicine, she didn't have to buy contraceptive medicine herself, saving both trouble and money.

Under the watchful eyes of Fengchang and Xing Mama, she picked up the bowl and drank the medicine in one go.

Seeing that the two of them were still staring at her, Yu Yuan curved her lips into a smile, curtsied to Fengchang, turned around, and left Leshou Hall.

She had more important matters to attend to and didn't have time to chat with them.

chapters.title: Not Mentioning Him
chapters.content:
Back at Honghui Hall, Yu Wan changed into a fresh set of clothes, took the 100 taels of silver notes that Zhao Xuanyou had given her at the imperial palace, and left.

At the money shop outside, she exchanged the notes, bought a few things along the way, and only arrived at Taoran Inn close to noon.

The young waiter at the entrance rushed forward as soon as he saw her, asking what she wanted to eat. The manager, who was counting on the abacus nearby, recognized her and personally led her to the upper room on the third floor.

"Miss Yu Wan, didn't you go to Lichuan with the Heir? Why are you back in the capital so soon?"

Yu Wan replied, "The Heir ordered me to return to the capital to handle some matters."

"I see." The manager was a discreet man; upon hearing this, he merely nodded. When they reached the door, he added, "Brother Chen went out early this morning."

The manager pushed open the door. Inside, a woman in her thirties was sweeping the floor; likely the person hired to care for her mother.

Seeing the manager leading someone in, the woman quickly put down the broom and came over.

"Manager Lin, do you have any instructions?"

"This is Miss Yu Wan. She's here to visit her mother."

"Oh, so you're Miss Yu Wan. I was just about to feed the madam some congee."

The manager noticed Yu Wan staring fixedly at the person lying on the bed. Sensing the moment, he said, "I still have accounts to settle. Miss Yu Wan, please make yourself at home."

With that, he left, taking the cleaning woman with him.

Once the room was quiet, Yu Wan quickly approached the bed.

Her mother was still unconscious, but her complexion was much better than before; no longer alarmingly thin.

"Mother, I'm back in the capital."

If there was any good thing about returning from Lichuan to the capital, it was that she could see her mother.

In the past, whenever Yu Wan visited her mother at Yunshui Nunnery, she had to wash her mother’s hair and body for her. This time, that wasn’t necessary.

Her mother was clean, and even her hair carried the fresh scent of soapberries. It seemed her mother had indeed been well cared for at Taoran Inn.

Yu Wan helped her mother turn over, carefully combed her hair, then tested the congee on the table; it was just the right temperature. She sat by the bed and fed her mother the congee, one small spoonful at a time.

"Daughter went to the Lichuan imperial palace this time, traveling with the imperial procession. It was quite an eye-opening experience."

She spoke softly to her mother, just as she had in the past when she kept her company.

"At first, I thought the Marquis's mansion was the height of luxury, but when I arrived at the imperial palace, I realized the royal family had an entirely different kind of grandeur."

Speaking of which, Yu Wan’s chance to witness the royal splendor was all thanks to Crown Prince Zhao Zun.

She had been staying in a separate courtyard at the imperial palace. If Zhao Zun hadn’t sent someone to "kidnap" her into his palace, she wouldn’t have seen such a grand sight.

But compared to the golden and jade-filled Chonghua Hall, what Yu Wan missed most were the days in the separate courtyard.

"Mother, do you still remember teaching me to read when I was little? This time in Lichuan, I attended lessons with the prince. Though I stood to listen, the teacher was none other than a top scholar."

"Master Pei is exceptionally handsome. I heard that before the imperial examinations, many noble families wanted to marry him."

"He and his wife treated me very kindly. It’s lucky I stayed in the same courtyard as them. If it had been another family, I wouldn’t have had such a good opportunity."

"Mother, I’m learning calligraphy now. When you recover, I’ll write something for you to see; maybe the first poem you taught me. How does that sound?"

As she spoke of many things, Zhao Xuanyou’s face appeared in Yu Wan’s mind.

The person she had spent the most time with was Zhao Xuanyou. But how could she explain her relationship with him to her mother?

"The Heir and I... are still about the same as before."

Actually, it wasn’t quite the same.

Apart from the intimacy at night, he had also started to care about other things.

He taught her calligraphy and even took her back from the Crown Prince.

That night when he appeared in the forest, a feeling she had never experienced before surged in Yu Wan’s heart. At that moment, she only wanted to throw herself into his arms, hold him tightly, and never let go.

But that was only that one night.

Yu Wan didn’t mention Zhao Xuanyou again. She just chattered on about her time in Lichuan; the Pei couple, Zhao Qi, the two proud princesses, and Xiang Xu. Before long, she had finished feeding her mother a bowl of congee.

She took a handkerchief to wipe her mother’s mouth, but before she could touch her, the person on the bed suddenly jerked her head.

"Mother... you..." Yu Wan was shocked, watching as her mother’s lips moved slightly.

"Mother! Mother! Can you hear me?"

Ever since her mother had been injured and fallen into a coma, she had been like a living corpse, unable to move. This was the first time Yu Wan had seen any reaction from her.

She tightly held her mother’s hand, shaking it continuously. But no matter how much she called or shook, her mother on the bed gave no response and slipped back into deep sleep.

Yu Wan’s eyes gradually welled up with tears.

"Yu Wan, are you in the room?"

Chen Da Niu’s voice came from outside the door.

"I’m here. Come in."

Chen Da Niu entered, carrying several packets of medicine. Seeing Yu Wan at the bedside with reddened eyes, he assumed she was emotional from not having seen her mother for so long.

When Yu Wan saw him, she quickly said, "Just now, my mother moved."

"Moved?" Chen Da Niu put down the medicine packets and went to the bedside. Seeing that Yu Wan’s mother looked the same as usual, he turned to Yu Wan. "How did she move?"

"She shook her head a little and moved her lips. Brother Da Niu, has she done this before?"

"No." Chen Da Niu thought for a moment, then added, "I haven’t seen it, but Old Lady Liu said that once, when she was cleaning your mother, your mother’s fingers moved twice."

"Really?" Yu Wan had been afraid that she had imagined it. Hearing Chen Da Niu say this, a surge of joy filled her heart.

Chen Da Niu was still hesitant. "That’s what she said. I’ve never seen it myself."

"Have you told Physician Feng about this?" By now, her mother had already undergone four or five acupuncture sessions. According to Physician Feng’s earlier words, she might improve after three sessions. Her mother’s movement should be good news.

Chen Da Niu shook his head.

Old Lady Liu was efficient in her work, but she seemed a bit scattered. He didn’t even believe Old Lady Liu, so naturally, he hadn’t mentioned it to Physician Feng.

"Then remember this: next time Physician Feng comes, you must tell him about this. Old Lady Liu saw it once, and I saw it once. Understood?"

"I understand." Chen Da Niu nodded, then looked at Yu Wan with some difficulty.

Before he could speak, Yu Wan directly took out a 20-tael silver note and a bag of loose silver from her sleeve.

Previously, she had been worried that Chen Da Niu might be tempted by money, but he had taken such good care of her mother for so long, proving that she hadn’t misjudged him. He was still the honest and kind neighbor from before. So she decided to give him more.

"So much?" Previously, Yu Wan had only given him things to pawn, but this time she directly gave him a silver note.

Yu Wan said, "Use that silver note to pay Physician Feng directly next time. The rest you can keep for your own use."

"I understand."

Not long after, Old Lady Liu came in with tea. When Yu Wan asked her about the previous incident, it turned out to be similar to what she had seen today.

Thinking that her mother was gradually improving, Yu Wan’s mood lifted greatly. She stayed at Taoran Inn until dusk before hiring a sedan chair to return to the Marquis’s mansion.

She was a maidservant, so the sedan chair couldn’t stop at the main gate of the Marquis’s mansion. It had to drop her off about a hundred steps away.

As Yu Wan was about to enter the mansion, she caught a glimpse of a tall and grand carriage parked in front of the Marquis’s gate.

---

chapters.title: Coming to Take Her Away
chapters.content:
Was there a guest visiting the Marquis’s mansion?

Yu Wan withdrew her gaze and entered the alley beside the mansion, going in through the side gate.

Back at Honghui Hall, Yingxue was in the garden helping Ziyan water the flowers. Seeing Yu Wan enter, she came forward and said, "Sister, you’re back."

Yu Wan’s eyebrows twitched slightly. "Is something going on in the mansion?"

"The Second Madam of Ningguo Duke’s mansion has come."

At the mention of Ningguo Duke, Yu Wan knew it must be related to Zhao Qi.

"Is she here to visit the Old Dowager?"

"Of course," Yingxue continued. "There’s only the Old Dowager as the master in the mansion now. She seems to want to see you. Someone from Leshou Hall has come to ask about you twice."

It was already so late, yet the visitor was still at the Marquis’s mansion. It was likely that Zhao Qi had forced her to come urgently to find Yu Wan.

Yu Wan couldn’t delay. She went inside to change her clothes and then headed to Leshou Hall.

The servant at the door let Yu Wan into the courtyard. Soon, Madam Xing came out and led Yu Wan into the house.

In Leshou Hall, Old Dowager Ye and the Second Madam of Ningguo Duke’s mansion were having dinner.

Hearing Madam Xing say that Yu Wan had returned, both women put down their chopsticks. At that moment, the Second Madam let out a long sigh of relief.

Earlier that day, she had been pressured by Zhao Qi into coming to the Marquis’s mansion after lunch.

Who would have thought that Yu Wan was on leave and had left the mansion? Afraid of returning and being harassed by Zhao Qi, she had no choice but to stay at the Marquis’s mansion.

She had drunk several pots of tea, and now she was even having dinner with Old Dowager Ye.

"Are you Yu Wan?" the Second Madam asked.

"This servant greets the Old Dowager and the Madam." Yu Wan stepped forward and bowed.

The Second Madam nodded while examining Yu Wan.

Though she was just a maidservant, her appearance was too striking. If she were dressed up properly, she would be no different from the noble ladies of the capital.

She couldn’t help but think of how Zhao Qi had pestered everyone at the Duke’s mansion to come to the Marquis’s mansion to fetch her. Could that bratty boy have developed a crush so young?

This was not good news, but unfortunately, there was nothing she could do about it.

Zhao Qi was a prince and the only bloodline of the late beloved daughter of the Duke of Ningguo. The entire mansion had to revolve around Zhao Qi.

For now, she would first take Yu Wan back.

So the Second Madam smiled and said, "Before you came, I already told the Old Dowager. Our eldest young lady is getting married in three months and is currently busy embroidering her dowry. However, the most skilled seamstress in our mansion has fallen ill, so we would like to ask you to come and help."

This was complete nonsense.

However, in the capital, it was common for noble families to lend each other a hand, so borrowing a skilled maidservant wasn’t unusual.

"My embroidery?" Yu Wan hesitated. "I’m afraid..."

The Second Madam looked at Old Dowager Ye for help.

Earlier, while drinking tea, she had already conveyed Zhao Qi’s intention to take Yu Wan to Old Dowager Ye, who had agreed. So Old Dowager Ye spoke up, "I was supposed to prepare a dowry for the young lady. Since the Duke’s mansion needs your help, you should go and assist."

"But this servant is still..."

Seeing that Yu Wan was reluctant, the Second Madam quickly said, "You can take leave as needed. The day after tomorrow, I’ll send a carriage to pick you up."

Yu Wan had witnessed Zhao Qi’s unreasonable behavior before, so she wasn’t surprised by the Second Madam’s enthusiasm toward her.

Since Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t at the Marquis’s mansion, Yu Wan had nothing to do all day. Of course, she didn’t want to go work for Zhao Qi.

But then, a thought struck her.

The Marquis’s mansion had strict rules about servants going out. After her leave ended in two days, it would be difficult for Yu Wan to go out again.

If she accepted the job of "embroidering the dowry" at the Ningguo Duke’s mansion, wouldn’t she be able to go out every day?

Thinking of how her mother had moved her lips at Taoran Inn, Yu Wan’s heart raced.

Her mother’s condition was improving. She wanted to visit her every day.

"This servant wouldn’t dare trouble the Madam. I can go to the Duke’s mansion to help on my own."

The Second Madam let out a long sigh of relief upon seeing that Yu Wan was no longer refusing. "If we’re asking you to help at the Duke’s mansion, it’s only natural that the Duke’s mansion sends a carriage to fetch you. Don’t worry, I’ll have a place prepared for you when you return."

"Madam, the Marquis’s mansion has rules that maidservants cannot stay overnight outside. It would be better for this servant to return to the Marquis’s mansion every day." Yu Wan gathered her courage and said, glancing at Old Dowager Ye as she spoke.

After all, Yu Wan was Zhao Xuanyou’s concubine. Old Dowager Ye also knew that Zhao Xuanyou was currently very fond of her. By returning to the Marquis’s mansion every night to rest, she was showing that she was being cautious.

"The mansion does indeed have such rules." Old Dowager Ye said.

"In that case, we shall follow the Marquis’s mansion’s rules."

Yu Wan’s agreement to go to the Ningguo Duke’s mansion meant the Second Madam had accomplished her mission.

She expressed her gratitude to Old Dowager Ye repeatedly and left the Marquis’s mansion with a face full of joy.

Old Dowager Ye looked at Yu Wan with a hint of suspicion and asked, "How did the Seventh Prince let you go to serve him?"

Yu Wan replied truthfully, "The Seventh Prince has to follow the Heir to practice every day. This servant would prepare some pastries and soup for him. Later, when he attended classes with Master Pei, this servant would also serve by the side. Perhaps he found me useful, so he called for me."

Old Dowager Ye’s question was direct, and Yu Wan answered honestly.

"If he likes your service, why didn’t he just take you directly?"

For a prince to go through such trouble for a maidservant was truly unreasonable.

Yu Wan remained silent.

Zhao Qi hadn’t spoken up because he was afraid of Zhao Xuanyou.

But if she were to say that, Old Dowager Ye would only think she was arrogant, believing that Zhao Xuanyou was very fond of her. So she pretended to know nothing.

"Go now. Later, go to the steward to get some silver. Hire a sedan chair for your daily commute."

After all, she was a maidservant. Whether the Duke’s mansion sent a carriage to pick her up or the Marquis’s mansion sent one to drop her off, it would be too extravagant. Hiring a sedan chair was more appropriate.

"Yes."

Yu Wan responded and respectfully withdrew.

---

Lichuan Imperial Palace, Chonghua Hall.

Crown Princess Jiang Ru Shang was stopped at the door by a eunuch.

"Your Highness, His Highness the Crown Prince has a slight headache today and wishes to rest early. He is not available to see you."

Ever since the Empress had severely reprimanded the Crown Prince, he had been avoiding the Crown Princess; either claiming to be too tired or having a headache.

Even if she waited at the palace door every day, the Crown Prince’s attendants would keep them apart.

She wanted to follow her aunt the Empress’s advice and apologize to the Crown Prince, but he wouldn’t even give her a chance to speak.

Looking at the eunuch who was smiling insincerely in front of her, Crown Princess Jiang suddenly turned around and smashed all the dishes of food that the palace maids were carrying behind her onto the ground.

"Oh dear, Your Highness..." The eunuch quickly ordered someone to clean up and forced a smile as he advised, "His Highness is unwell and needs rest. Your Highness must not make such a commotion."

The Crown Prince’s attendants naturally followed his orders alone.

However, with the Empress’s support, even the Crown Prince would be reprimanded if the Crown Princess complained. As a servant, how dare he look down on her?

Even if she made a scene and smashed things at the Crown Prince’s door, he didn’t dare to drag her away. He could only repeatedly advise, "Your Highness, please calm down. If you do this, His Highness will feel even worse."

"Cousin! Cousin!" Crown Princess Jiang shouted at the door, disregarding everything. "I know you’re angry with me. I already know I was wrong! From now on, I’ll do everything according to your wishes. If you like that maidservant, I won’t stop you. I can even help you!"

chapters.title: Sharing a Bed, Different Dreams
chapters.content:
"Your Highness, oh dear, Your Highness..." The eunuch, seeing the Crown Princess shouting loudly, could only plead desperately, "Lower your voice. Whatever you need to say, we servants can relay it for you. Why must you say it yourself? Don’t strain your voice!"

"Cousin, Cousin, "

"Come in."

A deep voice came from inside the palace.

The chief eunuch let out a sigh of relief. Fortunately, His Highness had relented. Otherwise, if this commotion continued, it would disturb Her Majesty the Empress again.

"Your Highness, please."

The eunuch opened the door and bowed, ushing the Crown Princess inside.

Jiang Rushuang had only shouted like that because she was driven to desperation. Now that she had a moment to breathe, she straightened her sleeves slightly and walked calmly toward the inner chamber.

The Crown Prince had changed into a bright yellow night robe and was sitting at the edge of the couch with a dark expression.

Ever since that night when Yu Wan was taken away by Zhao Xuanyou, he had been unable to swallow that insult.

Zhao Xuanyou... actually dared to defy him?

"Your humble servant greets Your Highness." Jiang Rushuang stepped forward and bowed gracefully to the Crown Prince.

"What were you shouting about at the door? As the Crown Princess, you behave like a shrew from the village. Aren’t you afraid of losing face in front of the servants?"

Jiang Rushuang remembered her aunt’s instructions, to learn to appear weak in front of the Crown Prince.

She lowered her head and gently wiped the tears from the corners of her eyes. "Cousin doesn’t pay attention to me anymore. What face do I have left? Cousin, I truly know I was wrong."

The Crown Prince turned his face away.

Jiang Rushuang had no choice but to take a few steps forward and kneel before the Crown Prince, pleading, "From now on, no matter what happens, I will report to you first, Cousin. Whatever you tell me not to say, I will never mention it to Her Majesty."

The Crown Prince didn’t like Jiang Rushuang, but after all, she was his cousin, and he had never been completely estranged from her.

It was just that Jiang Rushuang always relied on her maternal family’s connection to the Empress to pressure him, which he found utterly detestable.

Seeing Jiang Rushuang bowing her head now, the Crown Prince narrowed his eyes slightly.

"Really?"

"Of course. How would I dare deceive you, Cousin?" Jiang Rushuang gently tugged at the Crown Prince’s sleeve and said softly, "That day, I heard a woman’s voice in your room, Cousin. I was so heartbroken that I went to Her Majesty and said those things. Although Her Majesty scolded you, she also reprimanded me."

The Crown Prince gave a cold laugh but said nothing.

Jiang Rushuang continued, "Her Majesty was right. You are the heir to the throne. In the future, the harem will have thousands of beauties. If I get jealous over each one, I’ll drive myself to an early grave."

"You understand now, which is good."

Seeing that the Crown Prince had finally deigned to acknowledge her, Jiang Rushuang let out a sigh of relief and added, "Cousin, you said you liked the maid from the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence. I wonder which one she is? When we return to the capital, I’ll send someone to bring her into the Eastern Palace."

Her Majesty was right.

What she needed to guard against were high-born noblewomen like Cui Yichu who could threaten her position as Crown Princess. As for those lowly maids, if the Crown Prince wanted as many as he liked, she would provide them. Once he grew tired of them, she could deal with them then.

At the mention of Yu Wan, the Crown Prince’s eyes darkened.

"She is Zhao Xuanyou’s concubine. He won’t hand her over."

Jiang Rushuang was slightly taken aback.

Not only was she a maid, but a defiled concubine maid at that? And the Crown Prince actually missed her?

She suppressed the disgust in her heart, afraid of revealing her true feelings and ruining all her efforts. She softened her voice and said, "In the capital, exchanging concubines as gifts is not uncommon. If Your Highness likes her, how would Zhao Xuanyou dare refuse? Besides, I am the Crown Princess. As long as I send someone to fetch her, the Marquis’s residence has no reason to refuse."

The Crown Prince stretched out his hand and pulled it back.

"I am not in the mood tonight."

Jiang Rushuang looked at his cold expression, her heart filled with silent resentment. He had no mood for her, but he had mood for those lowly women?

Could a maid who had warmed Zhao Xuanyou’s bed really be that enchanting?

When they returned to the capital, she would have to see for herself what kind of celestial beauty that wretch was, to have the Crown Prince so infatuated for so long.

But Jiang Rushuang dared not voice her anger.

Right now, being at odds with the Crown Prince would do her no good.

No matter how much her aunt favored her, she was still just an aunt. If she couldn’t give birth to a legitimate son soon, when her younger sisters grew up, her aunt might have other plans.

No matter how heartless or unreasonable the Crown Prince was, she had to endure it, had to coax him.

Jiang Rushuang looked at the Crown Prince, all her resentment turning into grievance.

"My cousin, I didn’t mean it that way. I was just thinking that if we rest here tonight, and Her Majesty asks tomorrow, it would be easier for you to explain, Cousin. What if I have my maid bring my quilt over?"

Thinking of the Empress’s daily pressure, the Crown Prince had no choice but to let out an "mm" and lifted the blanket to lie down, turning his back to Jiang Rushuang.

---

chapters.title: Inviting You
chapters.content:
Yu Wan arrived at the Duke of Ningguo’s residence just after a quarter past the si hour.

The gatekeeper saw a beautiful young lady step out of the sedan chair and quickly approached.

"Are you Miss Yu Wan from the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence?"

"Yes." Yu Wan hastily presented the token left by the Duke’s second madam a few days ago.

The gatekeeper glanced at it, did not take it, and invited Yu Wan inside.

Like the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, the Duke of Ningguo’s family was a prestigious clan that had followed Emperor Taizong to conquer the world over a hundred years ago during the turbulent times.

Although they were not of the same surname or lineage as the imperial family like the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, the first Duke of Ningguo had achieved remarkable military exploits, his valor shaking the southeast. Thus, among the five dukes enfeoffed after Emperor Taizong’s ascension, he secured a place.

Unlike the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, which stayed away from the political struggles of the court, the Duke of Ningguo’s family had intermarried with the imperial family for generations. Zhao Qi’s birth mother, the Kind Consort, was the youngest daughter of the Duke of Ningguo.

Yu Wan entered the main gate of the Duke of Ningguo’s residence. A maid waiting at the gate stepped forward and led her inside.

"Miss, you’ve finally arrived. His Highness has been waiting for you for two days."

Yu Wan let out a soft sigh.

She was just a maid. Zhao Qi had made such a grand arrangement, and now the entire Duke of Ningguo’s household would take notice of her.

She didn’t know what to say, so she simply smiled and nodded.

The Duke of Ningguo’s residence was vast, with overlapping verandas and corridors. After walking for a while, the maid stopped and pointed to a small courtyard with its door half-open. "His Highness is practicing martial arts right now. Please go in, Miss."

Who greets someone from outside the courtyard like that?

Yu Wan looked at the maid doubtfully. The maid now wore an embarrassed smile.

"Just go straight in?"

The maid nodded.

Before Yu Wan could speak, she heard a crisp sound of a teacup shattering from inside the courtyard, followed by Zhao Qi’s angry shout: "What is this? I’ve already said I don’t drink tea! Why are you still pouring tea for me? Do you want me dead?"

In Luichuan, with Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta working together to restrain him, Zhao Qi had been well-behaved for a long time. Yu Wan had almost forgotten the willful and violent demeanor he had shown when they first met.

She also understood why the maid didn’t dare enter and had stopped outside the gate.

Before she could step inside, she heard Zhao Qi shout again: "Didn’t you say Yu Wan was coming today? Why isn’t she here yet? Can’t you go and fetch her? Are your legs broken?"

Hearing Zhao Qi’s growing anger inside, Yu Wan quickly spoke up: "Your Highness, this servant has arrived."

The courtyard fell silent. Soon, someone opened the door; it was Yin Ping, whom she hadn’t seen in days.

Seeing Yu Wan, Yin Ping looked greatly relieved.

"Miss Yu Wan, please come in quickly."

Yu Wan thanked the maid beside her and then walked into the courtyard.

Zhao Qi was in the middle of practicing his horse stance in the courtyard. The teacup he had smashed earlier had already been cleaned up by Mu Di, leaving only water stains on the ground.

Seeing Yu Wan enter, Zhao Qi said with a stern face, "You’ve arrived, yet you don’t come in. Are you eavesdropping outside?"

Yu Wan smiled and replied, "Your Highness is in such a temper. How would this servant dare to come in?"

Zhao Qi scoffed, "What do you have to be afraid of? I’ve invited you to the Duke of Ningguo’s residence multiple times."

Yu Wan noticed a table set up in the courtyard with brush, ink, paper, and inkstone neatly arranged.

She walked to the table and then turned to Zhao Qi. "Is this prepared for me?"

"Would you be able to stay at the Duke of Ningguo’s residence if I didn’t give you something to do?"

Originally, if there hadn’t been the matter of coming to the Duke of Ningguo’s residence, Yu Wan had indeed planned to practice her calligraphy properly at Honghui Hall.

Zhao Xuanyou had agreed to let her practice on xuan paper, and she wanted to take the opportunity while he was away to make good use of his expensive xuan paper.

Thinking of Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Wan’s heart stirred.

Both she and Zhao Qi were not in Luichuan. She wondered what that guy was doing now.

"What are you spacing out for? I’ve already practiced my horse stance for half an hour. You better start writing."

"If the Young Master knew that Your Highness had been practicing diligently every day since returning to the capital, he would be very pleased."

Zhao Qi rolled his eyes. "I’m practicing to beat him up. How could he be pleased?"

Yu Wan couldn’t help but smile at his words.

After a moment’s thought, Zhao Qi instructed, "When he returns to the capital, if he doesn’t ask, then don’t mention that you came to the Duke of Ningguo’s residence."

"How can I hide it?"

"I’m not telling you to hide it. Just don’t bring it up if he doesn’t ask."

Zhao Qi wasn’t stupid.

Back at the villa, he could tell that Zhao Xuanyou really disliked him ordering Yu Wan around. Whether it was Yu Wan accompanying him in his horse stance or studying with him, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression would always be particularly unpleasant.

Of course, Zhao Qi insisted on having Yu Wan by his side precisely to annoy him.

Yu Wan had a very interesting personality. She was thorough in her work and knew how to argue with him, which suited his taste.

With Yu Wan by his side, whether it was practicing martial arts or studying, it didn’t seem so tedious.

For example, this horse stance; back at the villa, he could practice for two hours a day.

The day before yesterday, he had prepared to practice as usual, but after only one incense stick’s time, he couldn’t hold the stance anymore.

After a long time of frustration, he realized what was different; Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t there.

Without Zhao Xuanyou in front of him, the motivation to practice hard to beat him up disappeared.

The relatives at the Duke of Ningguo’s residence thought he didn’t want to practice and tried to persuade him to stop. But how could that be the case? He simply lacked the drive.

Zhao Qi understood that his maternal grandfather doted on him too much and couldn’t bear to push him to practice like Zhao Xuanyou did.

He also understood that if he didn’t push himself, he really wouldn’t amount to anything.

Back at the villa, Zhao Xuanyou often accompanied the Emperor, and with Yu Wan by his side practicing calligraphy, the horse stance didn’t seem so boring.

So Zhao Qi pressured his second aunt to go to the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence and bring Yu Wan over.

He watched as Yu Wan picked up the brush, lightly dipped it in ink, and made an ugly horizontal stroke on the paper. He burst out laughing.

"Yu Wan, if you didn’t say you were writing, I would have thought you were drawing a caterpillar."

Yu Wan felt a little embarrassed.

Writing with water and writing with ink were different, after all.

"Madame Pei said that everything is difficult at the beginning. I’ve only just started practicing."

"What do you mean, just started? You’ve been practicing for over twenty days."

"Your Highness, can you stop teasing me? Can you give me some guidance like Lord Pei and Madame Pei?"

Hearing Yu Wan mention the Pei couple, Zhao Qi narrowed his eyes, feeling as if he had forgotten something important. Just as he was about to recall it, someone suddenly pushed open the courtyard door and peeked inside.

"Oh, Your Highness is practicing."

"Second Aunt, if you’re coming in, just come in. What are you lurking around out there for?" Zhao Qi shouted discontentedly.

"We were worried about disturbing Your Highness’s practice." The second madam who had gone to the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence to fetch Yu Wan entered, followed by two elegantly dressed women and two young ladies.

Yu Wan guessed they were the female relatives of the Duke of Ningguo’s family. She quickly put down the brush and curtsied to them.

As they entered the courtyard, they all stopped in front of Yu Wan, their eyes revealing a hint of concealed amusement.

chapters.title: There’s Another One
chapters.content:
Yu Ying could feel the meaning behind those gazes.

Zhao Qi had caused such a commotion in the Ningguo Duke’s mansion that others naturally had many speculations, thinking he had some intentions toward her.

She glanced at Zhao Qi and saw that he was completely unaware of his aunts and cousins examining him. She decided to feign ignorance as well.

“What is your name?” another noblewoman beside the Second Madam asked.

“This servant is Yu Ying,” Yu Ying replied respectfully.

The Second Madam said, “Yu Ying serves the Heir of the Jingyuan Marquis. She went to Lichuan this time and returned to the capital with His Highness!”

“Yes, this servant was ordered by the Heir to return to the capital to handle some matters and happened to travel back with His Highness.”

Yu Ying had a fuller figure, and the thin summer dress she wore could not conceal her curves at all.

Her slender waist made her chest appear even more prominent and eye-catching.

In the eyes of high-ranking noblewomen, such an appearance was somewhat improper.

But Yu Ying carried herself with decorum, spoke elegantly, and kept her eyes lowered, making her seem quite obedient.

“Do you know how to write?” the Second Madam asked curiously, noticing the brush and ink on the table.

Yu Ying picked up the paper she had just written on and held it up to them, self-deprecatingly, “This servant only recognizes a few characters and cannot write.”

The horizontal stroke she had written was indeed ugly. The Second Madam laughed, “If you can read, you are already outstanding among women. There’s no need to rush; you can practice slowly.”

“Thank you, Madam.”

Seeing that Yu Ying kept her head down, and with so many people in the courtyard, Zhao Qi curled his lip in disdain. “I’m still practicing my martial arts. With so many of you making noise, it’s annoying.”

“Alright, alright, alright, we’ll leave now.” The Second Madam sighed helplessly. Seeing the sweat on Zhao Qi’s forehead, she took a handkerchief to wipe it for him.

Another noblewoman said, “Your eldest sister is making sweet soup for you. It will be sent over soon.”

At the mention of sweet soup, Zhao Qi’s eyes lit up. He turned to Yu Ying and said, “My eldest sister’s cooking is excellent. You should try her cooking later.”

“Thank you for His Highness’s generosity. This servant is fortunate.”

Hearing Yu Ying speak so politely, Zhao Qi knew she was uncomfortable and repeatedly urged them to leave quickly.

After they left, Yu Ying stepped forward and gently closed the courtyard door. She turned back to ask Zhao Qi, “Were those two madams just now Your Highness’s aunts?”

“Mmm, the one who went to the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion is my second aunt. The other is my eldest aunt.”

Zhao Qi’s eldest aunt should be the wife of the heir of the Ningguo Duke’s mansion.

Seeing Yu Ying deep in thought, Zhao Qi said, “They were just curious about you. They are actually very kind people, similar to Madame Pei.”

Hearing Zhao Qi mention Madame Pei, Yu Ying couldn’t help but smile.

Normally, this kid spoke to Sun Qianran quite rudely, but in reality, he knew she was refined and well-mannered.

“If Your Highness thinks Madame Pei is good, why are you so rude to her?”

Zhao Qi scoffed and asked indifferently, “As long as her husband is good to her, what does it have to do with me?”

That made sense.

Yu Ying couldn’t argue with him. She returned to the table to practice writing. As soon as she picked up the brush, Zhao Qi beside her let out an “Ah.”

Before she could ask what was wrong, he started shouting.

“Yin Ping, go to my room and bring out the things Pei Ta gave me.”

Yin Ping quickly brought out a small wooden box and placed it in front of Zhao Qi.

“Why are you giving it to me? Give it to Yu Ying.”

Yu Ying saw that the box was full of books and took the initiative to step forward.

“Are these books from Lord Pei?” The box contained more than ten neatly stacked books and a thick stack of manuscripts.

“Mmm, he gave them to me before we left Lichuan and told me to finish reading them all while in the capital.” If Zhao Qi had a strong interest in martial arts, he had no interest in reading or writing.

She picked up the one on top, which was an annotated version of The Book of Rites. It was not annotated by any famous scholar but was Pei Ta’s own insights from reading. Whenever he had an epiphany, he would write a few words in the margin.

Yu Ying asked curiously, “Does Your Highness want to practice martial arts and read at the same time?”

That would be too difficult.

Zhao Qi rolled his eyes. “Who said I want to read? There’s one in there for you. Take it yourself.”

For her?

Yu Ying was somewhat surprised. Lord Pei had even left something for her.

“Which one is it?”

“The one with no characters on the cover.”

Yu Ying put the book in her hand back and carefully flipped through them. She indeed found a book with a blank cover, which looked newly bound with thread.

“Is this book from Lord Pei for me?”

Zhao Qi responded with an “Mmm,” “Just that one.”

Yin Ping closed the box and put it back in the room.

Yu Ying sat down with the book and opened it. It turned out to be a copybook.

Pei Ta had personally written one hundred characters, and beside each, he had written a line of small notes explaining the points to pay special attention to.

The ink on the copybook was dark, so Pei Ta must have written it while in Lichuan.

His handwriting, like the man himself, was upright and elegant. Although the strokes were slender, they were strong and forceful, without losing their spirit.

Yu Ying didn’t understand calligraphy, but she instinctively felt his handwriting was better-looking than Zhao Mengfu’s.

Holding the copybook, she once again saw Pei Ta’s elegant and refined appearance in her mind.

Although the sun was shining brightly, Yu Ying’s eyes stung a little.

She and Lord Pei were merely chance acquaintances. It was already very kind of him to allow her to listen to lectures in his study.

She hadn’t expected that after leaving Lichuan, he would prepare such a gift for her.

In his heart, did he consider her, like Zhao Qi, as his student?

Zhao Qi stood beside her, watching Yu Ying’s eyes turn red, and said disdainfully, “It’s just a lousy copybook. Is it worth crying over? If you like it so much, I’ll give you ten or a hundred.”

“Thank you, Your Highness. This servant doesn’t need that many copybooks for now. Please don’t laugh at me, Your Highness.”

Yu Ying knew she had lost her composure and quickly raised her hand to wipe her tears.

“Does Zhao Xuanyou usually treat you poorly?” Zhao Qi narrowed his eyes, recalling that Yu Ying had always written on scrap paper in Lichuan, and suddenly had a guess.

“Of course not. The Heir has always been very generous to his servants.”

It was different.

Copybooks were not rare. Zhao Qi could give her ten, and Zhao Xuanyou could also give her ten.

In their eyes, it was because she was a good servant, clever and gentle enough to please them. When the masters were in a good mood, they would be generous and reward her with ten or a hundred.

No matter how many they gave, it was a master’s reward to a servant.

But Pei Ta’s copybook was different.

He did not give it to Yu Ying as a fourth-ranking official of the court to a servant.

The box of books Yin Ping had carried out were not things that could be bought in the market. Each one had his personal annotations and was something he wanted to pass on to his students.

Such a box of books, which embodied Pei Ta’s hard work, actually contained one for her.

Yu Ying’s tears fell again despite herself.

She had originally thought that only her mother would treat her so well in this world. She hadn’t expected there to be another person; Pei Ta.

---

chapters.title: Sister and Brother
chapters.content:
“Your Highness.”

A crisp and pleasant female voice came from outside the courtyard. Zhao Qi responded with an “Mmm,” recognizing who it was. He quickly said, “Sister Yun, come in.”

As soon as he finished speaking, Zhao Qi glanced at Yu Ying beside him.

Yu Ying lowered her head and wiped the tears from her face.

The person who pushed the door and entered was a girl of about seventeen or eighteen, wearing a water-green brocade dress. She had an oval face, willow-leaf eyebrows, and a gentle and elegant beauty.

She first smiled at Zhao Qi and called him “Your Highness,” then turned her gaze to Yu Ying.

Seeing Yu Ying’s red-rimmed eyes, she was somewhat surprised and quickly walked up to Yu Ying, asking with concern, “Miss, what’s wrong?”

“This servant is fine. Something just accidentally got into my eyes.”

The other person could tell this was an excuse and turned to glare at Zhao Qi.

“As soon as Your Highness returned to the capital, you caused a commotion in the mansion and insisted that Second Aunt bring someone from the Marquis’s mansion to keep you company. Now that someone is finally here to play with you, why are you bullying her?”

Zhao Qi was scolded out of the blue and didn’t understand. He was not one to back down verbally and immediately retorted, “Who bullied anyone? She cries if she wants to. What does it have to do with me?”

“When have you not bullied someone? Which maid in this mansion isn’t afraid of you?”

“Afraid of me?” Zhao Qi said hatefully, “That’s because they’re cowardly. What does it have to do with me?”

Seeing the girl arguing with Zhao Qi, Yu Ying quickly said, “Miss, it has nothing to do with His Highness. His Highness has been very kind to me. Just now, I thought of some things at home and couldn’t help but cry.”

“It really wasn’t him bullying you?”

“He didn’t bully me,” Yu Ying shook her head repeatedly. “This servant wanted to write, and His Highness even prepared brush, ink, paper, and inkstone for me. How could he make things difficult for me?”

“That’s good.”

Zhao Qi, standing beside them, shouted, “What’s good about it? I got scolded for no reason!”

“Whether it’s a false accusation or not is still unknown. Besides, even if this time it’s a false accusation, how many times have you bullied maids before? In any case, if you do it again, I won’t make sweet soup for you anymore.”

“Sister Yun, you’re really something! I said it wasn’t me! What kind of sweet soup is it today?”

Zhao Qi loved the eldest cousin’s cooking. In the Ningguo Duke’s mansion, he wasn’t afraid of anyone except this eldest cousin, who could control him with her culinary skills.

“What should I call you, Miss?” She ignored Zhao Qi and instead looked at Yu Ying kindly.

Yu Ying quickly bowed, “This servant, Yu Ying, greets…”

“Her name is Shen Tongyun,” Zhao Qi interrupted.

“This servant, Yu Ying, greets Miss Tongyun.”

Shen Tongyun was the eldest daughter of the eldest branch of the Ningguo Duke’s mansion and the only daughter of the heir of the Ningguo Duke. She was gentle, graceful, and of noble character.

She helped Yu Ying up and said with a smile, “Since you’ve come to the Ningguo Duke’s mansion, you are a guest, not a servant. Besides, you are a guest invited by His Highness, so you are an honored guest.”

“Miss, please don’t say that. This servant really cannot accept such a title.”

“Today, I made a bayberry soup with a little something else added. Try it.”

Shen Tongyun pulled Yu Ying to sit beside her. A maid brought a tray over, and she personally ladled half a bowl and handed it to Yu Ying. “Honored guest, drink first.”

Yu Ying was taken aback by her warmth and accepted it, taking a sip.

It was sweet and sour, with a hint of other fruit fragrances.

“Did you add lychee, Miss?”

When Cui Yichu was at the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion, he didn’t like eating lychee but liked using it to make wine. When Yu Ying served in the Liu Fang Pavilion, she had smelled the fragrance of lychee wine.

The sweet fragrance of lychee was unique; once smelled, it was unforgettable.

“I like eating lychee. Sister Yun, quickly pour me a bowl too,” Zhao Qi urged from the side.

Shen Tongyun said, “You’re still practicing your martial arts. Wait until you’re done.”

Zhao Qi loved sweet soup, and seeing the two of them drinking it, he couldn’t resist.

“Yu Ying, I’m thirsty!”

Yu Ying had no choice but to pour him a bowl and feed it to him.

Shen Tongyun sat beside them, watching Yu Ying feed Zhao Qi with practiced ease, and couldn’t help but find it amusing.

A few days ago, her mother and second aunt had said that Zhao Qi, despite his young age, had already developed an interest in pretty maids from other mansions. They excitedly talked about how they should remind the Bureau of Attendants to arrange a bedchamber maid for him.

But from the looks of it, was that really the case?

Yu Ying seemed very proper, and Zhao Qi was full of childishness. Clearly, he didn’t have those kinds of thoughts.

Whether in actions or expressions, both of them were pure, and their interaction was more like... siblings.

Yes, exactly like siblings. The way Zhao Qi spoke to Yu Ying was more like pouting than giving orders.

Soon, Yu Ying finished feeding Zhao Qi the bowl of sweet soup and returned to her side.

“Sister Yun, your cooking is really too good. I want to drink another bowl.”

Before Shen Tongyun could respond, Yu Ying said, “Your Highness, you shouldn’t have too much sweet soup. Wait until after lunch to drink more.”

Zhao Qi was clearly a little impatient and mumbled a couple of times before falling silent.

“Miss Yu Ying, are you practicing calligraphy?” Shen Tongyun asked curiously.

Yu Ying put away the copybook Pei Ta had given her and said with some embarrassment, “I just started practicing. My writing is ugly.”

Shen Tongyun looked at the horizontal stroke that resembled a caterpillar and softly said, “You write very neatly. It’s just that you dipped too much ink, which is why it blurred like that.”

“Is that so?” Yu Ying picked up the brush again. Shen Tongyun guided her from the side, and Yu Ying quickly understood the difference between using ink and water. The characters she wrote were indeed similar to the ones she had practiced on scrap paper before.

Zhao Qi watched the two of them getting along well and suddenly asked, “Sister Yun, when is your wedding date?”

At the mention of the wedding date, Shen Tongyun’s cheeks turned slightly red, and her voice softened. “The fortune teller said that the 28th of the eleventh month is a good day. That’s about three months from now.”

Zhao Qi slightly furrowed his brows, a hint of reluctance appearing between his eyebrows.

“Then, by the time I come to the mansion next time, won’t I be unable to see you?”

“Your Highness, please don’t say that. How could you not see me?” Shen Tongyun was also reluctant to leave home, but a woman couldn’t stay at home forever; she would eventually get married. “I’m not marrying far away. Even after I get married, it’s only three streets away from the Ningguo Duke’s mansion. When Your Highness returns, I can quickly bring sweet soup over.”

These words were both to comfort Zhao Qi and herself.

Since the husband’s family and her natal family were so close, and both were noble families, they wouldn’t lose contact.

Zhao Qi still couldn’t cheer up. He puffed out his cheeks and said, “Sister Yun, can your marriage still be changed?”

“Your Highness, don’t joke. Both families have already exchanged marriage contracts. It can’t be changed.”

Zhao Qi looked gloomy and said, “I’ve heard that there isn’t a single good person in the Xingguo Duke’s mansion. How about I go and talk to Grandfather, and you don’t marry into their family?”

Yu Ying’s brush heavily poked a blot of ink onto the paper.

What?

Shen Tongyun was going to marry into the Xingguo Duke’s mansion?

Yu Ying’s mind flashed back to the day when Cui Yichu’s three elder brothers had desperately pleaded for her. She wondered which of them Shen Tongyun was going to marry.

chapters.title: Sincerity
chapters.content:
Shen Tongyun listened to Zhao Qi’s words with suspicion. “Who else is talking about these things in front of you?”

“Well… I asked around.”

“You went to ask about Xingguo Duke’s Mansion?” Shen Tongyun looked at him doubtfully. Although Zhao Qi was her cousin, he had a stubborn temper, and the two of them were not particularly close. Why would Zhao Qi go out of his way to inquire about Xingguo Duke’s Mansion for her sake?

Of course, Zhao Qi hadn’t done it for Shen Tongyun’s sake.

When the emperor assigned Zhao Xuanyou to teach him martial arts, Zhao Qi had sent someone to investigate Zhao Xuanyou. He learned that Zhao Xuanyou had divorced Cui Yichu, and it was said that Cui Yichu had been disrespectful to her elders while in the Marquis’s Mansion.

The old Lady Ye of the Marquis’s Mansion was a kind and pious elderly woman. If even such a devout Buddhist was not respected by Cui Yichu, then the family’s morals must be corrupt.

“It’s just…” Zhao Qi pointed at Yuhuan. “I heard it from her.”

Shen Tongyun looked at Yuhuan in surprise. Remembering that she came from Jingyuan Marquis’s Mansion, she suddenly understood.

The news of Zhao Xuanyou’s divorce from Cui Yichu was well-known in the capital. Naturally, the people of Jingyuan Marquis’s Mansion would look down on Xingguo Duke’s Mansion.

Yuhuan, who had been unexpectedly dragged into this by Zhao Qi, didn’t know what to say for a moment.

After thinking for a while, she could only say, “This servant congratulates Miss Yun on her good fortune.”

“Thank you.” Seeing the situation, Shen Tongyun didn’t say more. She accompanied Yuhuan in writing a few more characters before rising to leave.

Yuhuan looked at Zhao Qi helplessly, her long, dark eyebrows slightly furrowed.

“Your Highness, why are you talking nonsense?”

Zhao Qi said, “Anyway, your Marquis’s Mansion and Xingguo Duke’s Mansion are enemies. It’s normal for you to curse them a few times.”

What a load of nonsense.

Yuhuan had no way to deal with him, so she asked again, “Does Your Highness know which young master of Xingguo Duke’s Mansion Miss Yun is going to marry?”

Given Shen Tongyun’s status as the eldest legitimate daughter of Ningguo Duke’s Mansion, she would be most suited to marry Cui Zaizhou, the heir of Xingguo Duke’s Mansion. However, his younger sister, Cui Yichu, had already been married for a year. His elder brother, Cui Zaizhou, should have been married long ago.

But Cui Yichu had been married in a hurry due to an incident, so it was possible that she had gotten married before her elder brother.

“I don’t know.” Zhao Qi answered straightforwardly.

You don’t know?

Yuhuan looked at Zhao Qi in astonishment.

Zhao Qi, uncomfortable under her gaze, frowned and said, “I have to handle countless affairs every day. How can I care about these trivial matters?”

“Your Highness speaks the truth.”

Yuhuan looked at his stubborn expression and, of course, did not expose him.

Although the Ningguo Duke’s Mansion seemed to dote on Zhao Qi, he was a prince and still young. Naturally, he wouldn’t be as attentive to the Shen family relatives as they were to him.

“If you’re curious, I can ask around later.”

“No need, this servant was just asking casually.”

In Yuhuan’s eyes, Xingguo Duke’s Mansion was certainly not a good place. But Shen Tongyun was a respected young lady from a noble family. It wasn’t Yuhuan’s place to worry for her.

People like Shen Tongyun were born under fortunate stars. Even if someone like Cui Yichu committed a huge scandal, her family would have the means to cover it up.

Yuhuan didn’t have the time to meddle in others’ business. She took out the calligraphy book that Pei Ta had given her and carefully flipped through it.

After reading for a while, she picked up a brush to copy the characters.

Pei Ta’s annotations were not detailed, but each word was concise and to the point.

Yuhuan wrote while referring to the annotations in the book, as if Pei Ta were by her side guiding her.

Zhao Qi watched Yuhuan’s focused expression and didn’t say anything else. When Yin Ping came forward to report that two hours had passed, he finally walked over to Yuhuan.

He had to admit that Pei Ta’s calligraphy style seemed more suitable for Yuhuan than Zhao Mengfu’s.

Before, her writing had been like blindly copying, but today, although it wasn’t perfect, it had a discernible structure.

“It seems Pei Ta’s calligraphy book is quite useful.”

“Does Your Highness think this servant writes well?”

Zhao Qi narrowed his eyes, seemingly seriously appraising her work.

“Before, it was just scribbling. Now, at least it looks like characters.”

“Thank you, Your Highness. This servant has a request to make of Your Highness.”

“What is it?”

“When Your Highness returns to Luochuan, could you convey this servant’s thanks to Minister Pei?”

“Hmm,” Zhao Qi said nonchalantly, “If I remember, I’ll say a word for you. But I can’t guarantee it.”

“Thank you, Your Highness.”

Yuhuan was grateful to Pei Ta, but since she and Pei Ta were separated by gender and status, she probably wouldn’t have the chance to thank him in person in the future.

Zhao Qi had practiced all morning and was sweating all over. After saying a few words, he went inside to bathe.

Yuhuan practiced her calligraphy for a while before a maid from the Duke’s Mansion came in and said that the Duke of Ningguo had invited Zhao Qi to lunch. Yuhuan didn’t dare decide on her own, so she waited until Zhao Qi had finished washing up before reporting the matter.

Zhao Qi naturally agreed to go.

Yuhuan’s heart stirred, and she said that since Zhao Qi had already practiced for the required time today, and he had to go accompany the Duke of Ningguo, she would take her leave early and come back the next morning.

After Zhao Qi agreed, Yuhuan left happily.

After leaving the Ningguo Duke’s Mansion, she hired a sedan chair and went straight to the Taoran Inn. She spent most of the day at the inn taking care of her mother and only returned to the Marquis’s Mansion after dinner.

When she entered Honghui Hall, Yuan Qing and Yingxue were both in the room cleaning. Seeing her return so late, they were curious about what she had been doing at the Ningguo Duke’s Mansion.

“It’s the same as when I was in Luochuan; just accompanying His Highness in his practice. But I didn’t come back this late before. I went to sit with my mother for a while after leaving.”

Yuan Qing and Yingxue knew that Yuhuan’s mother was seriously ill. Since the Marquis’s Mansion was currently at leisure, they didn’t see any problem with her taking a detour to visit her mother.

“Yuhuan, I’m returning to Luochuan tomorrow. Do you want me to take anything to the master?” Yuan Qing asked.

Yuhuan was slightly taken aback and looked at Yuan Qing curiously. “Does the master lack anything in Luochuan?”

When they left the capital, Zhao Xuanyou had indeed traveled lightly, but he didn’t live extravagantly in his daily life. He didn’t need many things, and what he had brought was enough.

Moreover, he was highly favored by the emperor, who had bestowed many gifts upon him. He had more than enough.

Seeing Yuhuan’s confused expression, Yuan Qing pointed to the things on the table and said, “Look, Concubine Feng sent over a pair of shoes she made herself, and Cousin sent a bottle of her homemade insect-repellent ointment. Aren’t you going to send something?”

Yuhuan only then noticed the items on the table.

Although she didn’t know how good Feng Jiyuan’s ointment was, the pair of shoes made by Feng Tang looked very thoughtful. They had black sheepskin soles and black silk uppers, with exquisite lotus and green patterns embroidered on them.

“They’re really beautiful.” Yuhuan praised sincerely.

“Sister, don’t just look. You should also send something to the master.” Yingxue, seeing that Yuhuan was unmoved, hurriedly persuaded her. “The master cares so much for you, and even after returning to the capital, you still remember to send him gifts. He’ll definitely be happy when he sees them.”

Yuhuan couldn’t help but smile. She gently poked Yingxue’s shoulder. “I was wondering why Yuan Qing would think of this and ask me to prepare something. So it was you!”

“What about me? Why can’t I think of it?” Yuan Qing was displeased. “If you’re not sending anything, then forget it. I won’t bother.” With that, he stomped out angrily.

After laughing, Yingxue asked, “Sister, are you really not sending anything to the master?”

It wasn’t that she couldn’t.

Zhao Xuanyou was her master. To gain her master’s favor, Yuhuan’s life would be more comfortable.

But she wasn’t good at needlework. She could make some food, but it wouldn’t keep for the journey.

“I really don’t have anything decent to send.”

“Aren’t you making sachets, sister? What about that?”

“No, they’re too ugly.” So ugly that even Yuhuan herself didn’t want to use them.

Yingxue frowned beside her, trying to think of something. Her peripheral vision caught sight of the calligraphy book in Yuhuan’s hand. “What’s that?”

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.content:
“This is…” Yuhuan picked up the calligraphy book. “A calligraphy book bestowed by His Highness.”

After a slight hesitation, she didn’t mention that it was Pei Ta’s work.

“Sister, you can write too?”

Since returning to the capital, Yuhuan hadn’t had a proper chat with Yingxue, so Yingxue didn’t know about her calligraphy practice.

“I only started writing in Luochuan.”

“Were you literate before, sister?” Yingxue asked curiously.

Yuhuan nodded.

Yingxue was stunned, finding it hard to believe.
