“Didn’t you grow up in a village as a child, sister? How do you know how to read? You didn’t go to school, did you?”

“Of course I didn’t go to school.”

The village where Yuhuan lived was very small. There wasn’t even a teacher in the village. The sons of wealthy families had to take ox carts to the private schools in the town to study.

“I don’t know why either. My mother was literate. When I was little, she would teach me to recognize characters while we worked, and sometimes she would read me a few poems.”

“Your mother is so amazing!” Yingxue sighed. “No wonder you seem…”

She stopped abruptly.

Yuhuan’s expression shifted slightly, and she smiled. “Seem what?”

After a moment’s hesitation, Yingxue finished the rest of her sentence. “No wonder you seem so refined and well-educated.”

The Marquis’s Mansion had purchased many country maids. They all seemed coarse and ignorant. It would take a year or two just to teach them the rules, and they still couldn’t serve close to the master. They could only do odd jobs.

But Yuhuan was different. She carried herself with calm and composure, and her speech was elegant. If others didn’t mention it, one would never guess that she came from the countryside.

Yingxue was too embarrassed to say these things aloud. After a pause, she changed the subject. “Have you decided what to send to the master, sister?”

Not yet.

As Yuhuan shook her head, her gaze fell on the calligraphy book in her hand.

In Luochuan, Zhao Xuanyou often taught her to write, but he always teased her about her ugly handwriting.

After practicing calligraphy at the Ningguo Duke’s Mansion today, she had gained some confidence. Even Zhao Qi said it was good, so it must be decent.

Why not write a piece of calligraphy for him to appreciate?

Yuhuan made up her mind and entered Zhao Xuanyou’s study. She took over the space, grinding ink and laying out paper. Just as she was about to start writing, she hesitated.

After thinking for a moment, she took a book of poetry from the shelf and flipped through it. She saw a poem that looked familiar. Picking up Pei Ta’s calligraphy book, she realized that Pei Ta’s calligraphy book actually contained several poems.

This poem was short, and with the existing calligraphy book to copy from, it would naturally be better than writing freely.

Yuhuan placed the poetry book and the calligraphy book in front of her. In one go, she quickly copied a poem, Dream of the Southern River.

She used a fan to dry the ink, then folded it carefully and placed it inside the ugly sachet she had embroidered; one that looked neither like a chicken, a mandarin duck, nor a magpie.

When Zhao Xuanyou received the sachet, he would definitely be displeased by the embroidery on it. But when he took out the copied poem inside, he would surely think it was decent.

Yuhuan handed the sachet to Yuan Qing and instructed him that there was something inside the sachet and to remind the heir to check it.

Under Yuan Qing’s shocked gaze, Yuhuan returned to her room, satisfied.

After Yuan Qing left, Zhao Qi departed for Luochuan ten days later.

Yuhuan’s days of rushing between the two mansions came to an end, but she felt a sense of loss.

Not being able to go to the Ningguo Duke’s Mansion also meant she couldn’t visit her mother every day.

Fortunately, while Yuhuan was at the Taoran Inn, she finally managed to meet Dr. Feng once.

Dr. Feng said that her mother had shown a reaction, which meant the acupuncture points were correct. The stagnant blood was slowly dispersing, and she would likely wake up in another two or three months.

Dr. Feng also said that although her mother couldn’t move now, she could see and hear. The family could talk to her more often.

Yuhuan couldn’t freely enter and leave the Marquis’s Mansion, so she could only try to ask Chen Da Niu and Liu Daniang to talk to her mother more often.

One day, while Yuhuan was writing in the study, Yingxue suddenly ran in and said, “Sister, Concubine Feng is here.”

Concubine Feng was here?

Yuhuan knew that the other woman harbored hostility toward her. Assuming she wouldn’t dare to cause trouble in Honghui Hall, Yuhuan followed Yingxue out.

As soon as she stepped outside, she saw Feng Tang, dressed in a sea-tang red brocade robe, standing proudly at the gate of the courtyard.

“Concubine Feng.” Yuhuan and Yingxue both curtsied to Feng Tang.

Feng Tang swept her gaze across the courtyard and said slowly, “Now that there is no master in Honghui Hall, and only you servants are here, have you been negligent in your duties?”

“Concubine, rest assured. Honghui Hall is the heir’s study. We servants do not dare to be negligent. Although the heir is not at home, the rules of the courtyard remain unchanged. Both the rooms and the courtyard are cleaned morning and evening.”

“Is that so?” Feng Tang suddenly raised her voice and pointed to a cluster of crape myrtle flowers in the corner of the wall. “Then why are those flowers wilted?”

Yuhuan and Yingxue turned to look and saw that the crape myrtle flowers were not withered, just not as vibrant as when they were in full bloom. They realized that Feng Tang had come to nitpick.

Even when Zhao Xuanyou was at home, flowers at this stage wouldn’t be immediately replaced.

But Feng Tang paid no heed to this and questioned sharply, “Yuhuan, you are the head maid of Honghui Hall. The old lady and the heir trust you. How can you make such mistakes in your work?”

“I will order someone to go to the greenhouse and pick a new pot immediately.”

Yuhuan spoke, and Ziyan, who had hurried over upon hearing the commotion, bowed her head and left the courtyard, rushing toward the greenhouse.

Feng Tang let out a cold humph. “Just standing at the door and looking around reveals such a big oversight. Who knows what the inside of the house looks like?”

The maid beside her said, “The heir is not here. We cannot allow these maids to take charge of Honghui Hall.”

They wanted to enter Honghui Hall?

Yingxue also knew this was improper, so she spoke up. “Concubine, you should know the rules of the Marquis’s Mansion. Without the heir’s permission, no one is allowed to enter or leave Honghui Hall.”

“Where do you get the authority to give orders, given that I am the one managing the Marquis’s Mansion now?”

“I wouldn’t dare.” Yingxue curtsied again to Feng Tang. “The rules were set by the heir. Please forgive me, Concubine.”

Feng Tang said, “I know the rules of the Marquis’s Mansion better than you. However, since you can’t even take care of the flowers at the door, who knows about the rest? I need to go inside and see for myself whether you’ve been slacking off!”

Yuhuan and Yingxue remained silent. Feng Tang took a step into the courtyard, but the guard at the door stopped her.

“Concubine, without the heir’s command, I dare not let anyone enter Honghui Hall.”

These guards were all personally trained by Zhao Xuanyou and were loyal to him alone.

Even if it were the old lady herself, they wouldn’t let her in, let alone Feng Tang.

“Please forgive me, Concubine.” Yuhuan said respectfully.

Looking at Yuhuan’s obedient appearance, Feng Tang clenched her fists tightly.

“Forget it. Let you continue to slack off for a few more days.”

She turned around and left quickly with her maid.

The maid looked at Feng Tang’s flushed face and didn’t know what to say.

Before coming, she had advised Feng Tang against it. Honghui Hall was the heir’s study, and the rules were set by the heir. Coming here wouldn’t end well, but the concubine had refused to listen.

As she pondered what to say, Feng Tang restrained her anger and said in a low voice, “Go bring Baochuan here!”

chapters.title: Threat
chapters.content:
Call for Baochuan?

The maid was surprised upon hearing this and whispered, "Bring Baochuan to the concubine's courtyard? What if someone sees her..."

Madame Ye was kind and generous. After Feng Tang took over the household management, she moved from the initially remote attic to a spacious courtyard.

The location was quite good, right next to the Liu Fang Pavilion where Cui Yi initially lived.

Feng Tang remained silent.

Indeed, if something happened to Yu Ying, Zhao Xuanyou would certainly investigate, and it must not be linked to her.

After a moment of thought, Feng Tang said, "I will go inspect each room. You quietly take Baochuan to the firewood shed. Be careful, don't let anyone see you. Otherwise, if something goes wrong in the future, I won't be able to protect you."

"Yes." The maid was frightened but didn't dare to openly disobey Feng Tang. After hesitating repeatedly, she still advised, "Yu Ying is just a maid. Soon, the young lady will enter the household, and the heir won't necessarily favor her. She won't be a threat to you, Concubine."

"Originally, I didn't intend to accept Cui Yi's proposal, but you saw her attitude just now. She, along with that Yingxue, kept talking about rules and didn't put me in her eyes at all."

The maid said, "This is indeed the rule of the Marquis's mansion. Even the old madam wouldn't step into the heir's study."

"Hmph, if the old madam came, would she dare to stop her?" Thinking of the scene where she was stopped by the guards earlier, Feng Tang seemed to relive the moment when she first met Yu Ying.

She had brought personally made cakes to Honghui Hall but was stopped by the guards outside. At that time, Yu Ying was right there, watching her embarrassment clearly.

Today, when the guards stopped her, if Yu Ying had said a word, the guards would have definitely let her into the courtyard.

But Yu Ying didn't.

Yu Ying must have remembered that scene as well. Back then, it was Zhao Xuanyou who stopped her, but now it was Yu Ying.

A concubine who was once a maid was publicly humiliated. If Yu Ying became a concubine in the future, it would be even more unbearable.

"Go quickly!"

Feng Tang and Yu Ying indeed hadn't reached the point of life and death, but Cui Yi was right. With Zhao Xuanyou not in the capital, Yu Ying had lost her greatest support and protection. This was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

"Yes." The maid, unable to persuade Feng Tang, had no choice but to leave hastily.

Feng Tang calculated the time and made a round of inspections in each room. As she was about to reach the firewood shed, she pretended to be tired and rested in a nearby pavilion. When there was no one around, she quickly slipped into the firewood shed.

"Concubine is here." The maid sighed in relief and turned to Baochuan, saying, "Why don't you greet Concubine when you see her?"

"Slave Baochuan pays respects to Concubine Feng Tang."

Feng Tang looked at the woman standing in front of her, almost unrecognizable.

She had not been in the mansion for long, and whether it was Cui Yi, Baozhu, or Baochuan, they had not interacted much with her. But from her impression, they all looked quite delicate.

In just two months, Baochuan seemed to have aged ten years. Her complexion was sallow, and her hair was like withered grass.

What was even more unbearable for Feng Tang was that as soon as she entered the firewood shed, she could smell the stench of a chamber pot.

The closer she got to Baochuan, the stronger the smell became.

Feng Tang almost vomited and gestured to her maid. The maid, also suffocated by the smell, walked to the door of the firewood shed and opened it a crack. Feeling the fresh air outside, she finally felt a bit revived.

"Do you have something to ask of me, Concubine?" Baochuan spoke weakly, looking like a walking corpse, with only her eyeballs still moving.

Feng Tang raised her hand to cover her mouth and nose, "I do have something to ask of you. It's not a small matter."

She hadn't paid much attention to Baochuan's situation before. She only knew that Baochuan had not been sent to the estate and was left in the Marquis's mansion to do hard labor.

After receiving the news from the Xingguo Duke's mansion, Feng Tang inquired and learned that the servants in the mansion had long held a grudge against Baochuan. They assigned her the hardest and most tiring tasks. Every day, Baochuan had to clean chamber pots equivalent to the amount for two guards.

The servants were all snobs. Not only did they give her a lot of work, but they also gave her the least food.

There was even a young servant who secretly carried Baochuan out of her room at night... The cleaning old woman found Baochuan naked in the grass early in the morning.

Although the Marquis's mansion had a clean reputation, the old woman, despite her dislike for Baochuan, sent her back to her room and reported the matter.

When the matter was reported to Feng Tang, she decided to cover it up, saying that family scandals should not be made public. Moreover, Madame Cui, who had been divorced, was evil, and there was no need to care about the life or death of her maids.

"With me in this state, how can I still help you, Concubine? You should find someone else."

Feng Tang said, "I heard that you and Yu Ying didn't get along well in the past."

"So what?" Baochuan countered.

For Baochuan, poisoning Yu Ying seemed like it happened just three months ago, but it felt like a lifetime ago.

Seeing that Baochuan was still indifferent, Feng Tang said, "Madame was expelled from the Marquis's mansion, Baozhu died tragically, and you have fallen to this state. All of this has a lot to do with Yu Ying. Now she is still just a maid, but in the Marquis's mansion, she gets whatever she wants. Aren't you resentful?"

"Not being resentful doesn't change anything. Can I kill her?"

Feng Tang's eyes gleamed, and she glanced at her maid, who looked out the crack in the door to confirm no one was there, then nodded to Feng Tang.

"Now that the heir is not in the mansion, it's the best time to kill Yu Ying."

There was a fierce look in Feng Tang's eyes, but Baochuan still listened indifferently.

"Since Concubine wants to kill Yu Ying and has found the opportunity, you should indeed act. I wish you success."

Even ants struggle to survive. Although she had fallen to this state, Baochuan still wanted to live.

Feng Tang narrowed her eyes.

As expected of a senior maid from the Xingguo Duke's mansion, she was not easy to deceive.

"I am an outsider, so of course I can't order you around. The reason I came to you is that I want you to kill Yu Ying, not on my orders, but on Cui Yi's orders."

"What did you say?" Baochuan looked at Feng Tang suspiciously.

Feng Tang raised her chin, and the smile on her lips deepened.

"I didn't expect that even though all the maids had been sent to the estate by the heir, there would still be someone loyal to Cui Yi in the mansion. You are Cui Yi's personal maid, so you should be very clear about her character. After suffering such a great loss at Yu Ying's hands, how could she be willing?"

"That's right. With Madame's character, Yu Ying must die."

Feng Tang said, "Whether to kill Yu Ying or not doesn't matter to me. I am just passing a message for you. Cui Yi also said that you can go ahead and do it, and she will take care of your family."

At these words, Baochuan's eyes, which had been like a pool of dead water, finally showed some emotion.

"I heard that your father died early, and your mother is in poor health and no longer works in the Duke's mansion. You have two younger sisters at home, and your whole family relies on your monthly salary to live. If you continue to be a senior maid, there would be no problem, but in your current state, your two younger sisters will eventually have to be sold."

Baochuan was originally a native servant of the Xingguo Duke's mansion, but her father died early, and her mother's health deteriorated after giving birth to three children, unable to work. Fortunately, Baochuan was clever and could stay by the young lady's side to serve. Her monthly salary plus rewards were enough to support her family.

Baochuan understood that asking her to kill Yu Ying was indeed Cui Yi's intention.

Only people from the Xingguo Duke's mansion knew about her family.

Feng Tang was right. She knew her mistress well. Her mistress was the cruelest person in the world.

When Cui Yi said those words, she didn't mean to support Baochuan's family but to use her family as a threat.

Baochuan knew she was doomed, and her worthless life could not be saved. She said sadly, "Concubine, please tell me, how do you want me to kill her?"

---

chapters.title: Taking Action
chapters.content:
Hearing that Baochuan had finally agreed, Feng Tang was overjoyed. She could almost see Yu Ying lying dead in front of her.

This woman had monopolized the heir, which was truly infuriating.

It was great that Baochuan was willing to act...

There were servants in the mansion who passed messages to Cui Yi, and now Baochuan herself would kill Yu Ying. Once Yu Ying was dead, she would immediately expose the two of them, sentence them to death, and no one would suspect her.

It was effortless.

Feng Tang suppressed her inner joy and tried to make her expression look calm.

"It's simple. There is a rusty axe in the firewood shed. You just need to wait for the right moment and swing it at Yu Ying's neck."

She had thought carefully.

The axe was already in the firewood shed. Baochuan picked up the axe and, in a moment of impulse, killed Yu Ying.

Baochuan listened to her words and sneered, "She lives in Honghui Hall, with highly skilled guards at the door. Not to mention me carrying an axe over, even if I want to approach Honghui Hall, I would be dragged away halfway."

"Of course, I don't expect you to act inside Honghui Hall."

"I am only fit to wash chamber pots now. I can't go anywhere."

Feng Tang's eyes moved.

Cui Yi must have come to her because she knew that with Baochuan's current situation, she couldn't do anything to Yu Ying.

With her, the managing concubine, helping, they could find an opportunity.

"Don't forget, I am in charge of the household." Feng Tang said slowly, "It's impossible inside Honghui Hall, and it's not feasible during the day with so many servants around."

"Then, am I supposed to wait until late at night and call Yu Ying out to kill her?"

Yu Ying was cunning by nature. If she called her out, she certainly wouldn't come.

Moreover, if Feng Tang sent someone to call Yu Ying out, when Zhao Xuanyou asked about it later, he would surely suspect Feng Tang.

Feng Tang could orchestrate this, but the needle and thread must not be connected to her.

"A few days ago, my maid accidentally discovered that Yu Ying goes to a side room behind Honghui Hall every night. That row of houses is unoccupied. I don't know what she sneaks over there to do."

Baochuan also remembered the side rooms outside the wall of the back courtyard of Honghui Hall.

It was said to be where the guards lived when the Marquis was in the mansion. Now that the Marquis was not there, no one else had moved in.

"What is Yu Ying doing there?" Baochuan muttered. Thinking of Yu Ying's flirtatious appearance, a long-lost hatred surfaced in her heart. "She wouldn't be having an affair, would she?"

"She probably wouldn't be that bold, considering the side room is close to Honghui Hall." Feng Tang said, "Don't think too much. Strike while the iron is hot. You will act tonight."

"So soon?" Although Baochuan knew she was doomed, she didn't expect it to come so quickly.

Feng Tang impatiently said, "The heir is currently staying in Licuan accompanying the emperor. Without an imperial decree, he won't return to the capital. Therefore, the sooner we act, the better. This will give me more time to clean up the mess."

Seeing that Baochuan still seemed hesitant, Feng Tang continued, "I'll tell you the truth. The incident where you were violated at night was reported to me by the servants. Do you know why I didn't investigate?"

Baochuan indifferently said, "The people in the Marquis's mansion would be happy if I died. If Concubine investigates my matter, others would only resent Concubine for meddling in other people's business."

"The Marquis's mansion has a clean and upright reputation and will not harbor filth. When the matter was reported to me, I investigated it. However, it turned out that the person who violated you was a relative of Yingxue from Honghui Hall. I wanted to catch the person, but Yu Ying stopped me and even used the heir's name to pressure me!"

"Really? Was it Yu Ying's doing?"

Feng Tang sighed, "I originally didn't know about your feud with her. After this incident, I realized how much she resents you."

"If she wanted to kill me, the heir wouldn't spare my life."

Baochuan was well aware of Cui Yi's scandals and Zhao Xuanyou's hatred for the Xingguo Duke's mansion.

With a little instigation from Yu Ying, Zhao Xuanyou would certainly not be merciful.

Feng Tang bitterly smiled, "This is where Yu Ying's cunning lies. On the surface, she pretends to be generous in front of the heir, not minding the grudges with you. In reality, she can't wait to get rid of you. If you act sooner, you can take her with you to the underworld. Now that the heir is not in the mansion, if she acts against you first, not only will your life be in danger, but your family will also not survive."

Under the double threat, the color drained from Baochuan's face.

"I understand. I will act tonight."

Feng Tang, seeing this, finally nodded in satisfaction.

"Don't worry. I have thought of a foolproof plan for you. After dinner tonight, my maid will cover for you to hide in the bushes behind Honghui Hall. I will place the axe there in advance. When Yu Ying arrives, you rush into the side room and..."

---

After dinner, Yu Ying sat on the veranda with Yingxue for a while.

With Zhao Xuanyou away, Yingxue didn't need to stay up on duty. After finishing a plate of peanuts, Yingxue could go back to her room to rest early.

After Yingxue left, Yu Ying put all the leftover dinner into a bowl.

In the mansion, the servants' meals were regulated. Normally, when Zhao Xuanyou was present, they could share some of his dishes. Now that he was away, they could only follow the rules and get their meals.

Others didn't know that there was someone locked in the underground cell, so they wouldn't send extra food. Fortunately, Yu Ying and Yingxue didn't eat much, and there were always leftovers from dinner, which were just enough to feed the guard.

Anyway, he wasn't a good person. Having leftovers to eat was already good enough.

With both meat and vegetables, it was better than steamed buns.

Yu Ying placed the bowl into a food box and left Honghui Hall, walking along the courtyard wall towards the back. She soon arrived in front of the row of side rooms.

Tonight was a clear night, with the moon like a jade plate, casting a soft yellow light over the earth.

Yu Ying, familiar with the path, entered the side room and went through the cabinet entrance into the tunnel, carrying the food box as she walked down.

The lamp oil in the underground cell was almost burned out. The remaining small flame was very weak and flickered frighteningly.

She put down the food box, first refilled the lamp oil, and felt the cell brighten up before placing the food box outside the cell door.

"Time to eat." The person in the cell was still squatting in the corner, dark and only a blurred figure visible.

Yu Ying didn't want to talk to him, but being in the cell made her feel uneasy. She felt she had to say something to make it less scary.

"Today's dishes are good. There's stir-fried bamboo shoots with meat, smashed cucumbers, and braised tofu." Yu Ying loved meat, and although there were only a few strands of meat left, there was still plenty of cucumber and tofu.

As she spoke, there was suddenly a sound of chains moving in the cell.

Yu Ying looked up and saw the shadow in the corner moving.

Was he coming over to eat now?

Yuan Qing had instructed her not to open the cell door, so she only placed the bowl and chopsticks outside. To eat, he would have to use the chopsticks to pick up the food from outside the cell.

It was troublesome, but who asked him to kidnap Yu Ying?

In the previous days when she delivered food, he would wait until she left before eating.

Yu Ying nervously watched him. Seeing him sway without approaching, she finally felt at ease.

She was just about to put the empty bowl and chopsticks from the previous day into the food box when she suddenly heard a noise behind her.

Had someone come in?

She was startled and quickly turned her head, only to see a thin figure slowly walking down the stairs.

chapters.title: A Desperate Struggle
chapters.content:
The dungeon was brightly lit after the lamp oil had just been refilled. The moment that person walked down, Yu Wan recognized her; it was Baochuan, whom she had not seen in a long time.

Baochuan looked vastly different from before; gaunt and emaciated, with only a pair of dark, sunken eyes fixed intently on Yu Wan.

Noticing that Baochuan seemed to be hiding something behind her back, Yu Wan’s expression subtly shifted, and she immediately became alert.

"Baochuan, what are you doing here?"

She struggled to maintain her composure.

In the dungeon, she was isolated and helpless. Even if she shouted for help, no one outside would hear her.

She could only try to stall Baochuan and find a way to leave the dungeon as soon as possible.

Baochuan glanced around the dungeon and, upon seeing the dark figure in the cell, muttered, "I didn’t expect the Marquis’s residence to have a place like this."

"Baochuan, if you have something to say, let’s talk outside."

Baochuan seemed not to hear Yu Wan’s words. Her gaze shifted back to Yu Wan, and a coldness crept into her eyes. "The Young Master truly dotes on you, to the point of letting you in on the Marquis’s secrets."

Cui Yichu had been the Young Master’s wife for a year and didn’t even know there was a dungeon in the Marquis’s residence.

"I am a servant of Honghui Hall. Naturally, I know more when assisting the Young Master."

"Hmph, you’re nothing but a vixen! If not for you, the Madam wouldn’t have been driven out of the Marquis’s residence! If not for you, Baozhu wouldn’t be dead! If not for you, I wouldn’t have ended up like this!"

At this point, Yu Wan naturally couldn’t say anything to provoke her further. She could only persuade her, "Baozhu’s death has nothing to do with me. It was the household slaves of the Marquis’s residence who had long-held grudges against her and took the opportunity to retaliate!"

"Are you trying to shift the blame? Are you going to say that those people forcing themselves on me also has nothing to do with you?"

Yu Wan was suddenly jolted.

Those people... Which people had forced themselves on Baochuan?

"This... When did this happen? I stayed at the Lichuan Travel Palace for over a month and only returned a dozen days ago. How could this have anything to do with me?"

Baochuan froze.

When she had been assaulted, Yu Wan had indeed not been in the Marquis’s residence. Could it truly have nothing to do with her?

No, it couldn’t have nothing to do with her.

A surge of intense hatred suddenly erupted in Baochuan’s eyes. She raised the axe and shouted at Yu Wan, "If not you, then it’s that Yingxue by your side! Everyone has already investigated. It’s you two!"

This was bad. Baochuan looked far too unstable.

Baochuan had always disliked her, and after so many incidents, her hatred for Yu Wan was understandable.

How had she managed to follow her to the dungeon?

If she had only followed her... why was she holding an axe?

Yu Wan’s heart pounded violently. Baochuan looked like she was losing control. She needed to find something to defend herself.

There were many torture devices hanging on the wall, but they were some distance away from Yu Wan.

Yu Wan’s mind stirred slightly, and she slowly inched toward that wall.

"Yu Wan, don’t you want to know why I’m here?" After her outburst of rage, a sinister smile appeared on Baochuan’s face.

She knew she was doomed, but if she could drag Yu Wan down with her to the underworld, it would be a consolation.

Seeing her playing with the axe in her hand, Yu Wan’s forehead immediately broke out in a fine sweat.

She dared not hesitate any longer and quickly ran toward the wall covered in torture devices.

But... she was fast, and the axe was faster.

Baochuan swung the axe toward Yu Wan.

Having chopped a lot of firewood while cleaning chamber pots these days, Baochuan wielded the axe with considerable ease.

Yu Wan was terrified and quickly dodged backward. The axe struck the ground with a loud "bang," producing a sharp, resonant sound.

If that axe had landed on her, she would probably have been split in two.

In that instant, Yu Wan realized that the torture devices on the wall might be useful against prisoners, but they were no match for this axe.

She couldn’t fight back; she could only run.

Taking advantage of the moment Baochuan retrieved the axe, Yu Wan immediately dashed past her toward the dungeon exit.

Seeing her attempt to escape, Baochuan grabbed the hem of her clothing.

Yu Wan reacted swiftly. Noticing that Baochuan was holding the axe with only one hand, she reached out to snatch it.

She was strong, and if she could take the axe, she could certainly subdue Baochuan.

But Yu Wan had underestimated Baochuan’s resolve; the resolve of a person determined to do one last thing before dying.

Seeing her try to seize the weapon, Baochuan used her own head as a weapon, viciously ramming it into Yu Wan’s forehead.

Thud…

A dull sound echoed. Caught off guard, Yu Wan’s head buzzed loudly. Suddenly, she couldn’t think or move. Unconsciously, she loosened her grip on the axe, staggered backward a few steps, and collapsed onto the ground.

If not for the cell door supporting her back, she would have already been lying on the floor.

Baochuan, of course, was also in pain from the collision. However, she had been prepared and had used her forehead to strike Yu Wan’s temple, so she was naturally in better condition than Yu Wan.

She swayed for a moment before steadying herself, then picked up the axe again and slowly walked toward Yu Wan.

This time, she would not let Yu Wan escape. She would split Yu Wan’s head open with one swing of the axe!

Yu Wan watched as Baochuan approached step by step, struggling with all her might to stand up, but her mind was still not clear.

As the axe swung toward her, she suddenly took a deep breath and threw herself to the side.

A loud metallic clash echoed through the dungeon…

Yu Wan abruptly lifted her head and saw an astonishing sight.

The person locked in the cell had somehow moved to the front of the cell door. At the moment Baochuan brought the axe down, he had stretched out his hand, and the axe, with perfect precision, had severed the iron chain on his wrist.

The iron chain slipped from his hand, and his masked face seemed to turn toward Yu Wan.

But in the next instant, he reached up, removed the wooden hairpin from his head, snapped it in half, and took out a silver needle. Bending down, he used the needle to pick the lock on his leg irons.

Was he about to escape?

In the blink of an eye, there was now another person in the dungeon who could kill Yu Wan.

She might be able to hold her own against Baochuan, but the man in the cell was far beyond her ability to handle.

She had to quickly deal with Baochuan and then escape back to Honghui Hall!

Yu Wan’s heart raced wildly. Noticing that Baochuan was distracted by the sudden turn of events, she took a deep breath and lunged at Baochuan, knocking her to the ground.

This was a life-and-death struggle.

Yu Wan sat on Baochuan’s axe-wielding arm, her hands tightly throttling Baochuan’s neck.

She saw the intense hatred in Baochuan’s eyes and heard the muffled, incoherent sounds from her throat.

She bit her lip tightly, focusing all her strength into her hands. One thought filled her mind:

She had to live!

She must live!

The hatred in Baochuan’s eyes gradually faded, and her struggling, convulsing body slowly stilled.

But Yu Wan dared not let go.

The reason she had encountered such danger tonight was because she had been too careless.

The hard-won chance to turn her life around had almost been wasted by her.

From now on, she would never be careless again, nor would she ever hesitate!

Yu Wan’s eyebrows knitted tightly, and tears welled in her eyes. Her consciousness grew fuzzy, and she didn’t even notice when someone behind her opened the cell door.

"She’s already dead. Let go."

---

chapters.title: Disappearance
chapters.content:
What was that sound?

Yu Wan turned her head in surprise.

The eerie gray mask was only a step away from her, a pair of deep eyes gazing at her through the mask.

"You... weren’t you sealed by Yuan Qing at your mute acupoint and…"

"He sealed my mute acupoint and my sleep acupoint." He calmly finished the sentence she hadn’t.

"And you?"

A sudden despair washed over Yu Wan. She had exhausted all her strength to deal with Baochuan, but the man before her was someone she could never hope to defeat.

The Gray Mask said indifferently, "I broke the seals myself the day I was locked up. It’s just that these iron chains were too troublesome; I couldn’t remove them by myself."

He reached out, grabbed Yu Wan’s shoulder, and pulled her up from Baochuan’s body.

"She’s already dead."

"Then am I next?" Yu Wan glanced at the still-warm corpse on the ground, feeling she wasn’t much better off.

The Gray Mask said nothing.

Seeing that he hadn’t made a move, the despair in Yu Wan’s heart reignited with a flicker of hope.

"Actually... you don’t have to kill me. You can leave first. I won’t call for help to catch you." Yu Wan looked at him pleadingly, hoping he would spare her. "The dungeon was so noisy just now, but no one outside heard. Hurry and go. Zhao Xuanyou and the others aren’t in the capital. You should quickly return to the Eastern Palace."

The Gray Mask said, "That night, you advised me that as long as the green mountains remain, there will be no shortage of firewood."

Had she?

Yu Wan opened her mouth, somewhat stunned.

She remembered advising the Gray Mask to spare her, but as for how she had phrased it, she truly couldn’t recall.

"Yes, you see, if you hadn’t spared me, you might have died that night. Now, even though you’ve been locked up for half a month, you have a chance to escape and survive. Isn’t that ‘as long as the green mountains remain, there will be no shortage of firewood’?"

The eyes behind the mask seemed to bore deeply into Yu Wan, making her heart race.

"What do you want? As long as you don’t kill me, anything else is negotiable."

"Do you want to live that badly?" he suddenly asked.

"Of course. My mother is seriously ill. I rely on working in the Marquis’s residence to earn money to pay for her treatment. If I die, my mother won’t survive either."

Thinking of her mother, who would soon recover and wake up, Yu Wan truly couldn’t bear to die.

Every word she spoke came from the heart, and in that moment, tears welled in her eyes.

The Gray Mask turned away, no longer looking at her.

"The Crown Prince ordered me to take you to Yongzhou to await him. I must take you there to fulfill my mission."

The low voice seemed to drift from afar, and it struck Yu Wan’s ears like a clap of thunder.

So he only wanted to take her to see the Crown Prince?

As long as he wasn’t going to kill her, that was fine.

If he didn’t kill her, she could still maneuver, still find a way out, still... see her mother again.

Yu Wan secretly sighed in relief. Just as she was thinking of what else to say, she suddenly felt her body lighten. She was lifted into the air as if flying, and in an instant, she was out of the dungeon.

---

The first to notice Yu Wan’s disappearance was Yingxue.

Early in the morning, she went to the kitchen to fetch breakfast, intending to eat with Yu Wan at Honghui Hall. But there was no sign of Yu Wan inside or outside Honghui Hall.

"How strange. Where could Sister have gone so early in the morning?"

Yingxue knew that Yu Wan liked to sleep in and would never get up early to go out unless there was a reason.

But Yu Wan was no longer an ordinary maid.

She had accompanied the Young Master to the Lichuan Travel Palace and had served the Seventh Prince at the Ningguo Duke’s residence. Even Old Lady Ye usually didn’t question her whereabouts, let alone Yingxue.

Perhaps the master had some errand for Yu Wan to run.

Yingxue ate breakfast by herself and went about her usual tasks. By nightfall, there was still no sign of Yu Wan.

A sense of unease grew in her heart. As she reached the gate of the courtyard, she asked the guard standing there, "Did Yu Wan jiejie go out very early?"

"No," the guard replied. "I’ve been here since before dawn and haven’t seen Yu Wan leave."

Just then, the guard coming to relieve the shift was the one who had been on duty the previous night. Seeing the situation, he said, "Yu Wan jiejie went out last night and hadn’t returned by the time I went off duty at midnight."

"Didn’t return? You mean she didn’t come back all night?" Yingxue’s heart pounded wildly.

Yu Wan, though free to come and go during the day, always adhered to the rules and returned to the Marquis’s residence before dark. She would never stay out overnight.

One of the guards pondered for a moment before slowly saying, "Yu Wan jiejie has been taking a food box out every night for the past few days. She would always return within the time it takes to burn an incense stick. Last night, she took a food box with her too. If she hasn’t returned..."

With Yu Wan’s current status, she could enter and exit Honghui Hall without being questioned.

The guards had no idea what she was doing with the food box.

"Something must have happened to her!" Yingxue cried in alarm.

But the Young Master wasn’t in the residence, and neither were Yuan Shen nor Yuan Qing. Whom could she turn to?

The concubine in charge of the household, Lady Feng? No, she resented Yu Wan’s favor with the Young Master. After some thought, Yingxue hurried off to find Manager Song.

At the same time, Feng Tang was also pacing anxiously in her room.

"Still no sign of Baochuan?"

The maid shook her head helplessly.

"Did you search thoroughly?" Feng Tang asked again, unwilling to give up.

"We did. Baochuan didn’t return to sleep last night, and she didn’t show up for work this morning. The matron reported it early, and the steward even arranged for people to search the inner quarters. There’s no trace of her."

According to the original plan, Baochuan was supposed to kill Yu Wan and then turn herself in to take the blame.

Baochuan’s disappearance... did that mean she had failed?

"Did you check Honghui Hall?"

"I went there at noon. Honghui Hall was quiet, as if nothing had happened."

Honghui Hall was different from other places. Feng Tang had no excuse to go there for an inspection, and even her maids weren’t allowed to linger nearby.

"Madam, could it be that Baochuan changed her mind, didn’t dare to kill Yu Wan, and fled the residence in the middle of the night?"

Feng Tang snapped, "If she could flee, would she have waited until now?"

After scolding, Feng Tang felt a wave of exhaustion.

Having Baochuan kill Yu Wan had been a natural course of action.

The best outcome would have been for Baochuan to successfully kill Yu Wan and then sacrifice herself to take the blame.

The second-best outcome would have been for Baochuan to fail to kill Yu Wan but die in the attempt, leaving Yu Wan severely injured.

As long as Yu Wan was crippled, she would never be allowed to stay in the Marquis’s residence.

The worst outcome would have been for Baochuan to be killed by Yu Wan in self-defense.

In Feng Tang’s previous calculations, even in the worst-case scenario, she would only have a busy time dealing with the aftermath and would suffer no real loss.

But now, Baochuan had disappeared, her fate unknown. Feng Tang suddenly thought of an even worse possibility.

What if Baochuan had failed to kill Yu Wan, and Yu Wan had failed to kill Baochuan, but instead, Baochuan had been captured... If Baochuan was captured, she might implicate Feng Tang...

Feng Tang was as restless as an ant on a hot pan. Suddenly, there was a knock at the door.

"Lady Feng, the Old Madam requests your presence."

Feng Tang’s body went limp, and she collapsed onto the floor.

It was over. Everything was over.

chapters.title: Soaring to Success
chapters.content:
"Auntie." The maid helped her up and whispered, "Perhaps the Old Madam has other matters to attend to. Besides, without evidence, Yujuan cannot falsely accuse you."

The maid had initially disapproved of Feng Tang’s actions against Yujuan, but since it was already done, she and Feng Tang were in the same boat. Naturally, she hoped Feng Tang would pull herself together and overcome the current crisis.

That was true.

Even if Baochuan were alive and came forward to accuse her, she could simply deny it.

After all, she was from the Prince Ping’s residence. The Old Madam would have to give her some face.

Feng Tang slightly calmed her emotions, stood up, adjusted her clothes, and led the maid toward Leshou Hall.

Inside Leshou Hall, Old Madam Ye was unusually dressed in formal attire, her expression grave, as if something major had happened.

Feng Tang’s heart pounded as she forced herself to appear calm and greeted Old Madam Ye.

"Concubine greets the Old Madam." She cautiously glanced at Old Madam Ye’s expression and asked with a smile, "Is the Old Madam going out so late?"

Old Madam Ye had been worshipping Buddha for a long time, usually wearing casual clothes. She only wore formal attire during New Year or when entering the palace to pay respects.

"Not going out... someone has come to the door."

Come to the door?

So it really wasn’t about Yujuan.

Feng Tang didn’t know why Old Madam Ye had called her, but as long as it wasn’t about Yujuan, it had nothing to do with her.

Her mood instantly relaxed, and she resumed her usual respectful demeanor.

"At this hour, there are still distinguished guests visiting?"

Old Madam Ye nodded solemnly. "Someone from the Eastern Palace has arrived."

The Eastern Palace?

"A eunuch from the Eastern Palace came. He said that the Crown Princess Consort took a liking to Yujuan while at the traveling palace and specially issued an order to take Yujuan into the Eastern Palace to serve. He is currently having tea in the main hall, waiting to take her away."

Earlier, when Old Madam Ye heard that a eunuch from the Eastern Palace had arrived, she immediately changed clothes to greet him. Upon hearing that the visitor wanted to take away Xuanyou’s personal maid, she forced herself to stay calm, invited him for tea and refreshments, and said she would go to the inner quarters to bring Yujuan out. Only then did she return to Leshou Hall.

"Take her into the Eastern Palace to serve?" Feng Tang’s heart twisted.

The Crown Princess Consort had taken a liking to her?

Yujuan was born with a seductive charm. While beautiful, she didn’t have the appearance of a virtuous woman. How could the Crown Princess Consort have taken a liking to her?

Only men would like that kind of vixen.

That’s right, Yujuan must have caught the Crown Prince’s eye, but it was under the name of the Crown Princess Consort that she was being taken into the Eastern Palace.

Feng Tang gritted her teeth in secret. That girl was so lucky to have caught the Crown Prince’s attention.

"Yujuan actually has such good fortune? But does the Eastern Palace know that Yujuan is the Young Master’s personal maid and has long since lost her innocence?"

Old Madam Ye’s expression darkened. "They know. That eunuch directly said he was here to take Xuanyou’s personal maid to the Eastern Palace."

So they knew... The Crown Prince really wasn’t picky.

Feng Tang had a change of heart and thought it might be a good thing.

No matter how successful Yujuan became, as long as she left the Marquis’s residence, she would no longer be in her way.

Once Yujuan was taken into the Eastern Palace, the matter of Baochuan could be easily covered up, and she would have no more worries.

"This decree has come very suddenly. I wonder if the Young Master knows about it," Feng Tang added.

Old Madam Ye’s face turned slightly pale. Naturally, she was worried about Zhao Xuanyou.

Yujuan and Yuan Qing had returned to the capital without saying anything, but now the Eastern Palace had sent someone to take her away. The experienced Old Madam understood that something bigger must have happened in Lichuan, prompting Xuanyou to urgently send her back.

Both the Crown Prince and Xuanyou were still in Lichuan. The Eastern Palace had chosen this time to come and take her away, clearly intending to make a done deal. By the time Xuanyou returned, he would have to accept the situation.

The relationship between the Crown Prince and Zhao Xuanyou had actually reached this point of confrontation...

The Marquis Jingyuan’s family had always stayed away from the struggle for the succession, but if things continued like this, if the Eastern Palace didn’t change, would the Marquis Jingyuan’s family have a next generation?

Seeing that Old Madam Ye remained silent, Feng Tang softly said, "Old Madam, the Crown Princess Consort’s decree cannot be disobeyed. No matter what, the Marquis’s residence can only send Yujuan to the Eastern Palace as soon as possible."

Old Madam Ye knew this reason all too well.

The other party had come with great momentum and would definitely take Yujuan away today.

"Old Madam," Mama Xing hurriedly ran in from outside.

She had followed Old Madam Ye for many years, usually accompanying her in vegetarian meals and prayers. It was rare to see her in such a panic.

"What happened?" Seeing that Mama Xing was followed by someone else, Old Madam Ye asked, "Since the person has been brought over, let her go and dress up first."

"Old Madam," Yingxue stepped out from behind Mama Xing, tears on her face. "Yujuan is missing."

Feng Tang’s eyebrows shot up suddenly, then quickly lowered her head.

If she had heard this news half an hour ago, she would have been overjoyed. But now, she, more than anyone else, hoped that Yujuan was safe.

She knew very well that Old Madam Ye, though old and lacking energy, was by no means stupid.

The comfortable life they usually led was because Old Madam Ye truly didn’t want to manage affairs.

Now that the Eastern Palace had come to take someone, if something happened to Yujuan, Old Madam Ye, who usually didn’t interfere in household matters, would definitely turn the Marquis’s residence upside down herself.

It was just today... Why hadn’t the Eastern Palace come yesterday?

As Feng Tang was feeling a mix of emotions, Yingxue wiped her tears and recounted how Yujuan had disappeared after leaving Honghui Hall with a food box the day before.

"Yujuan did not leave the Marquis’s residence yesterday, as confirmed by the gatekeepers. She must still be in the residence, but we really don’t know where."

Old Madam Ye knew there was a dungeon in the Marquis’s residence.

Hearing Yingxue say that Yujuan went to the back of Honghui Hall with a food box every evening, she had an idea.

But Yujuan had only gone to deliver food. Disappearing for a day and night was definitely a problem.

"Mama Xing," Old Madam Ye waved her hand, calling Mama Xing to her side, gave her some instructions, and then sighed deeply.

No one else in Leshou Hall dared to speak.

After a while, Mama Xing ran in again.

If she had been in a hurry before, this time she was utterly flustered.

Yingxue, who had grown up in the Marquis’s residence, had never seen Mama Xing in such a state.

"What happened?" Old Madam Ye’s expression darkened.

Upon seeing the Old Madam, Mama Xing calmed down slightly, approached, and whispered something in Old Madam Ye’s ear.

Old Madam Ye’s expression trembled, and before she could speak, Steward Song ran in from outside.

"Old Madam!"

"What now?"

Steward Song said, "That Eunuch Liang from the Eastern Palace has grown impatient. Just now, when a maid served him tea, he smashed the cup and asked if the Marquis’s residence intended to defy the imperial decree."

This kind of situation was beyond what the servants could handle.

Old Madam Ye’s face was filled with worry, her hands tightly clenched.

Yujuan was missing, and now she couldn’t comply with the decree even if she wanted to. She would be accused of defying the imperial order.

What could she do?

In the midst of the dead silence, someone suddenly walked into the center of Leshou Hall.

"Old Madam, I can go to the Eastern Palace in Yujuan’s place."

---

chapters.title: Volunteering
chapters.content:
"You?" Old Madam Ye looked at Zhuang Huaiyue in shock, her fingertips trembling. "But the Eastern Palace wants Yujuan, not you!"

Zhuang Huaiyue was originally a delicate beauty, but at this moment, her usually downcast eyes revealed a rare sharpness.

"I know, but Yujuan is missing now. Eunuch Liang won’t let this go if he doesn’t get someone."

"He came under the Crown Princess Consort’s decree, but both the Crown Prince and Crown Princess Consort are not in the capital. He is just a eunuch and can’t do much to the Marquis’s residence. Moreover, he wants Yujuan. If you go, it won’t help and might even make him take his anger out on you."

Old Madam Ye was a first-rank noble lady. Although defying an imperial decree was a serious crime, to punish her would require the involvement of the Emperor and Empress.

Given their magnanimity, they wouldn’t punish her over a maid.

Zhuang Huaiyue anticipated that the Old Madam wouldn’t easily agree. She continued, "When the Old Madam met Eunuch Liang earlier, I was there too. He made it very clear that the Crown Princess Consort wants the Young Master’s personal maid. I am the same as Yujuan; we are both the Young Master’s personal maids. Sending me to the Eastern Palace doesn’t violate the decree."

"This..."

Old Madam Ye thought carefully. Eunuch Liang had indeed said that.

Although Zhao Xuanyou had only taken Yujuan with him to Lichuan, and only Yujuan had the chance to be noticed by the Crown Princess Consort, Eunuch Liang wanted Zhao Xuanyou’s personal maid. Handing over Zhuang Huaiyue could indeed be justified.

"Huaiyue." Zhuang Huaiyue was, after all, the daughter of an old friend. Back then, the Marquis Jingyuan’s family had taken her from the Ministry of Rites to secure a livelihood for her. Now that the Marquis’s residence was in trouble, handing her over was truly not the act of a noble person. Old Madam Ye pondered again and again but still couldn’t make a decision. "Today’s matter, the Marquis’s residence can endure it. There’s really no need to sacrifice you."

The Crown Prince had taken a liking to Yujuan. If Zhuang Huaiyue went to the Eastern Palace, although it could resolve tonight’s crisis, the Crown Prince wouldn’t favor her. Her future in the Eastern Palace would be dire.

But Zhuang Huaiyue wouldn’t listen to Old Madam Ye’s advice.

"The Old Madam need not worry about Huaiyue. Ever since my father was imprisoned, I have had no way out."

After her family was confiscated, Zhuang Huaiyue had constantly thought of clearing her father’s name and saving herself and her family from the abyss.

While at the Ministry of Rites, she had desperately wanted to enter the palace, but without money to bribe the eunuchs, she was instead framed by those jealous of her beauty and failed even the initial selection for palace maids.

In her moment of despair, she was sent to the Marquis Jingyuan’s residence, where she met Zhao Xuanyou, the man she had secretly admired since childhood.

But because she acted hastily, she had annoyed Zhao Xuanyou.

When she heard Eunuch Liang say in the main hall that he was taking Yujuan to the Eastern Palace, Zhuang Huaiyue’s heart was filled with unwillingness and envy.

Clearly, she was just as beautiful as Yujuan, each with their own charms. Why had Yujuan been favored by both Zhao Xuanyou and the Crown Prince, while she could only copy sutras in the Buddhist hall?

Her parents had been exiled to a distant land. What they needed wasn’t prayers, but an imperial pardon.

If only she were the one going to the Eastern Palace.

The Crown Prince already had a Crown Princess Consort, yet he still took a liking to Yujuan. He must be a romantic man. If she entered the Eastern Palace, she would surely have a chance to gain his favor. As long as she could secure his affection, she would have a chance to save her parents.

The moment she learned that Yujuan was missing, Zhuang Huaiyue made up her mind. No matter what, she had to seize this opportunity.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t like her. Staying in the Marquis’s residence, the best she could hope for was to be freed from servitude in the future.

She wanted to rise in status, she wanted to clear her family’s name, she wanted to save her parents. Entering the Eastern Palace was the right path.

"Have you thought it through?" Old Madam Ye knew that Zhuang Huaiyue, who spent her days by her side, resented being a maid.

The Crown Prince was the heir apparent. If Zhuang Huaiyue could gain his favor, securing a pardon for the Zhuang family would be a small matter.

But gaining favor was not that simple.

The current Crown Princess Consort was from the Empress’s family. Her methods would certainly be the same as the Empress’s. Even outside the palace, Old Madam Ye had heard many rumors. The Crown Princess Consort was ruthless. How could a delicate woman like Zhuang Huaiyue compete with her?

"Huaiyue has made up her mind. I beg the Old Madam to grant my wish."

Seeing the determination in Zhuang Huaiyue’s eyes, Old Madam Ye understood that Zhuang Huaiyue had long wanted to leave the Marquis’s residence. After a moment of hesitation, she still nodded.

---

"Have something to eat."

Outside, the sun was warm and the sky was clear. Yujuan was daydreaming when a deep voice spoke beside her.

After the Gray Mask had taken her from the dungeon that day, he had used the cover of night to move swiftly across the rooftops of the capital for a long time before bringing her to this small courtyard.

This was a vacant small courtyard, with only three rooms in total.

Yujuan confirmed that she was still in the capital but didn’t know where exactly.

Looking at the bowl of simple rice and vegetables he brought over, Yujuan said, "Martial artists need to eat more meat to have strength. Do you always eat such plain food?"

Gray Mask said, "You are not a martial artist."

"I... I am indeed not a martial artist, but I don’t want to eat this bland food. You work for the Crown Prince. Doesn’t he give you money? Do you have to skimp even on food?"

"You eat this meal first. The next one will have meat."

Yujuan lightly huffed, picked up the bowl, and ate a few mouthfuls before saying, "Didn’t you say you were going to take me to Yongzhou? Why are we still in the capital?"

Gray Mask remained silent.

Originally, the Crown Prince had ordered him to take Yujuan to Yongzhou, intending to use the pretext of an inspection tour to distance her from Lichuan, avoiding trouble with Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Qi.

Now that he had been missing for over half a month, the Crown Prince knew that Yujuan had returned to the capital and certainly hadn’t gone to Yongzhou.

After leaving the Marquis’s residence, he had brought Yujuan to this small courtyard where he had stayed hidden in the capital. At the same time, he had sent a message through secret guards to the Crown Prince in Lichuan and was now waiting for the Crown Prince’s instructions.

Seeing that he wasn’t speaking, Yujuan finished her bowl of rice.

She wasn’t a picky eater. She had said those things just to get closer to him.

After finishing the meal, Yujuan saw him take the bowl out, thought for a moment, and followed him outside.

When she had first arrived, Yujuan had tried to run out quickly while he was in the kitchen, but she couldn’t even take five steps before being caught and thrown back into the room, locked up.

Yujuan had begged and pleaded, finally earning the freedom to move around the small courtyard.

Watching him squat in the courtyard washing the bowl, Yujuan also squatted beside him.

"What is your name?"

The other person didn’t answer.

Yujuan refused to give up. She racked her brain and said, "I remember... the Crown Prince called you... called you... Wen something."

"Wen Luo."

"Oh, right, that’s what His Highness the Crown Prince called you, Wen Luo." Seeing that he had finally spoken again, Yujuan was overjoyed. "Can I ask you for a favor?"

The other person answered firmly, "No."

"It’s not about letting me go," Yujuan pleaded. "I told you before, my mother is very ill. She needs to see a doctor twice a month, and each consultation costs five taels of silver. Every month, I send money to the inn. Now that you’ve captured me, there’s no one to send money to the inn. It will be a big problem."

Wen Luo didn’t speak, but he didn’t immediately refuse as before.

Yujuan felt there was hope and continued, "My mother is currently staying at the Taoran Inn to recover from her illness. Could you please, for my sake, send some money to the inn to help her get through this month? I beg you!"

chapters.title: A Treasured Gift
chapters.content:
Taoran Inn was Zhao Xuanyou’s property.

After frequenting the inn for some time, Yu Ying realized it was more than just a business.

The shrewd manager was one thing, but even the waiters seemed well-trained.

Rather than a mere business, Taoran Inn felt more like one of Zhao Xuanyou’s strongholds.

The people there were far from ordinary. If Wen Shu sent silver to his mother at Taoran Inn, they would certainly notice something amiss.

“Your mother lives at the inn?” Wen Shu asked.

“Yes. After she fell ill, I sold our house and land and came to the capital. At first, we stayed at Yunshui Nunnery, but later, when I became a senior maid in the Marquis’s residence, I had enough money to pay for her treatment.”

Yu Ying didn’t deliberately lament her past hardships; these were simply the facts.

Even as she spoke lightly, her eyes unconsciously betrayed a hint of worry.

Wen Shu remained silent for a moment before softly saying, “It won’t take many days before His Highness receives a reply. We can find an opportunity then.”

“My mother can’t wait that long.” Yu Ying sighed. “Please, do me a kindness. Have ten taels of silver delivered for me. You don’t even need to give it to my mother; just leave it with the inn’s manager and say it’s for Chen Da Niu.”

“Chen Da Niu?”

“He’s my fellow villager. I hired him to look after my mother.”

The masked man fell silent.

After their few interactions, they weren’t exactly adversaries. Yu Ying assumed his heart had softened somewhat.

After a moment’s thought, she gently pleaded again, “You don’t need to go yourself. Just hire someone on the street to deliver the silver to the inn. With your skills, how could anyone notice you in a crowd? I truly have no ulterior motives. If you’re worried I’ll escape, you can tie me up before we go out.”

Wen Shu hesitated, then asked, “Taoran Inn?”

Yu Ying’s heart leapt to her throat. Could he possibly know that Taoran Inn belonged to Zhao Xuanyou? Surely she wasn’t that unlucky.

Just as she was fretting, Wen Shu suddenly reached out and poked her.

The next moment, Yu Ying felt as if she had turned to stone; unable to speak or move.

---

Lichuan.

Zhao Qi was practicing martial arts in the courtyard. After more than a month of horse stance training, his foundation had stabilized somewhat.

Though his basics still needed work, Zhao Xuanyou allowed him to practice forms for half an hour.

Zhao Xuanyou stood on the veranda, casually watching Zhao Qi go through his movements.

Dressed in a dark robe, he exuded an elegant and refined demeanor, his deep, unfathomable eyes hidden beneath his sword-like brows.

“The force in your punches is insufficient.” Zhao Xuanyou, seeing Zhao Qi’s listless manner, stepped down from the veranda. “If Your Highness insists on practicing so lazily, you’d be better off not practicing at all and just sitting down for tea.”

“I don’t want to be lazy, but how am I supposed to exert force when I’m just punching the air? It’s boring,” Zhao Qi said, justified.

Faced with Zhao Qi’s unapologetic gaze, Zhao Xuanyou was rather helpless.

“I’ll spar with Your Highness.”

Zhao Qi grinned at the words and immediately assumed his stance, ready to fight Zhao Xuanyou.

It wasn’t that he lacked sparring partners, but he had suffered a crushing defeat at Zhao Xuanyou’s hands before. To reclaim his dignity, didn’t he have to face Zhao Xuanyou again?

Zhao Qi summoned all his energy, each strike aimed straight for Zhao Xuanyou’s vital points.

Faced with his fierce attacks, Zhao Xuanyou remained calm, dodging expressionlessly.

Suddenly, the courtyard gate was pushed open. Zhao Xuanyou glanced toward the entrance, and Zhao Qi seized the opportunity to swing a powerful punch.

As the gust of wind rushed forward, Zhao Xuanyou dodged a little too late. Though he wasn’t hit, the jade pendant and sachet hanging from his waist were knocked loose, landing right in front of Pei Ta.

Pei Ta was refined and otherworldly, yet not effeminate.

Seeing the fallen sachet and jade pendant, he bent down, picked them up, dusted them off, and with a smile, handed them back to Zhao Xuanyou.

“Your Highness, your things fell.”

“Thank you, Minister Pei.”

As Zhao Xuanyou reached out to take them, Zhao Qi curiously glanced over. The jade pendant was made of fine Hetian jade, lustrous and flawless. But the sachet… he suddenly snatched it from Zhao Xuanyou’s hand.

The sachet was made of fine material, but the embroidered mandarin ducks on it were hideously stitched; looking more like chickens or ducks, truly ugly.

Zhao Qi found the embroidery oddly familiar.

“This… did Yu Ying embroider it?”

Zhao Xuanyou’s face darkened terrifyingly. “Give it back.”

Zhao Qi was of course afraid of him, but he was even more eager for gossip.

He clutched the sachet tightly and retreated to Yin Ping and Mu Di’s side, grinning. “Looks like the sachet was a gift from Yu Ying. And you actually wear it close to your heart. Tsk, tsk.”

Pei Ta, hearing this, lightly coughed and helped Zhao Xuanyou persuade him. “That sachet belongs to Lord Zhao. Your Highness, please return it promptly.”

Under Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, Zhao Qi instinctively flinched. In the end, he didn’t dare push too far. Pouting, he threw the sachet back.

Zhao Xuanyou caught it, his face cold. “That’s enough practice for today.” With that, he went inside.

Zhao Qi made a face at his retreating back, then said to Pei Ta, “That’s such an ugly thing. How can he bear to wear it so close to him?”

“Even a thousand gold cannot buy a treasured gift of the heart. It’s not about the object’s quality, but who gave it,” Pei Ta said indifferently.

One only wears something so close if it’s cherished.

Zhao Qi scoffed. “But Yu Ying is just a maid. Can he really have feelings for her?”

Pei Ta’s brows furrowed slightly. He glanced at Zhao Qi, who turned his face away. “I’m going back to change. I’ll come again in the afternoon.”

Watching his swaggering departure, Pei Ta lightly shook his head.

“Husband, you’re back.” Sun Tianran came out of the house. Seeing that Pei Ta had broken a sweat, she took out a handkerchief to wipe his face.

Pei Ta took the handkerchief from her and wiped his own forehead.

“What were you all talking about earlier? It sounded lively.”

“His Highness the Seventh Prince accidentally saw that Lord Zhao was carrying a sachet embroidered by Yu Ying and was teasing him about it.”

“There’s nothing strange about that.”

Sun Tianran was naturally perceptive and had long since noticed that Zhao Xuanyou’s feelings for Yu Ying were far from ordinary lust.

“Didn’t you notice before, husband?”

Pei Ta supported her as they walked inside. Glancing at Zhao Xuanyou’s tightly closed door, he lowered his voice. “Lord Zhao’s feelings for Yu Ying are not hard to see. It’s just that, in the past, His Highness the Seventh Prince seemed quite fond of Yu Ying. What he said earlier… took me by surprise.”

“What did he say?”

“Some belittling remarks.”

Sun Tianran said coolly, “When has His Highness the Seventh Prince ever said anything pleasant? That’s just his temperament. He has treated Yu Ying better than others. Oh, by the way, the Emperor summoned you earlier. What was it about?”

“It was…”

Pei Ta was just about to speak when the courtyard gate was suddenly thrown open with force.

He and Sun Tianran instinctively turned to see Yuan Zhe rushing in from outside, looking flustered.

“What happened?” Yuan Qing, who had been standing on the veranda, stepped forward to ask.

“Big trouble.” Yuan Zhe lowered his voice. “Is the master in his room?”

Yuan Qing nodded.

Without waiting for an announcement, Yuan Zhe pushed open the door and barged in.

---

chapters.title: The Rescue
chapters.content:
“Yuan Zhe, who serves Lord Zhao, has always been calm and collected. For him to rush in like this, something must have happened,” Sun Tianran said softly.

Pei Ta said nothing.

But he knew Sun Tianran was right. Yuan Zhe barging in like this meant not only had something happened, but it was serious. Yet Pei Ta had thought even further.

Ever since Yu Ying left the Lichuan Imperial Palace, life here had been uneventful.

There had been no movement from the Crown Prince’s side. In fact, when he met Zhao Xuanyou, he could still smile and converse as if the abduction of Yu Ying had never happened.

He had taken a fancy to Zhao Xuanyou’s maid, and not only had Zhao Xuanyou refused to hand her over, he had even taken her back by force.

From what Pei Ta knew of the Crown Prince, he certainly did not have such a magnanimous heart.

This incident must be related to Yu Ying.

“Madam, please return to your room.”

Seeing that Pei Ta intended to seek out Zhao Xuanyou, Sun Tianran reached out to stop him, gently advising, “Lord Zhao isn’t even willing to cooperate openly with his own family. Why must you get involved in this murky business, husband? Matters concerning the Eastern Palace are different from others.”

“I have my own considerations. Madam need not worry. It’s windy outside; go in quickly.” Pei Ta removed Sun Tianran’s hand, smiled at her, and walked straight toward Zhao Xuanyou’s room.

As soon as he reached the door, the voices inside abruptly fell silent.

“Who is it?” came Zhao Xuanyou’s deep voice from within.

“Lord Zhao, it’s me, Pei Ta.”

Soon, the door opened a crack, and Yuan Qing said quietly, “Minister Pei, our young master is currently handling family matters.”

“I know.”

Zhao Xuanyou inside, of course, had also heard the reply. After a moment’s hesitation, he finally said, “Please come in.”

Pei Ta entered the room, and Yuan Qing closed the door behind him.

Inside, Zhao Xuanyou sat with a furrowed brow, his expression even uglier than when Zhao Qi had snatched his sachet earlier.

And that very sachet was now clenched in his hand.

“Lord Zhao, has something happened in the capital?” Pei Ta asked directly, given the urgency.

Zhao Xuanyou suppressed his anger and nodded at Pei Ta.

Seeing this, Yuan Zhe realized that Pei Ta was aware of the previous abduction of Yu Ying, so he repeated to Pei Ta what he had just reported to Zhao Xuanyou.

“Yu Ying has disappeared?” Pei Ta was somewhat surprised. “She disappeared inside the Marquis’s residence?”

“Minister Pei may not be aware, but the Marquis’s residence is currently holding a dark guard from the Crown Prince’s side.”

Pei Ta could guess that the dark guard was the one who had abducted Yu Ying. He just hadn’t expected that Zhao Xuanyou had not only rescued her but also captured the Eastern Palace’s dark guard.

“From what I’ve heard, the palace dark guards are highly skilled. Could it be that this guard escaped from captivity and abducted Yu Ying again?”

“Exactly.” Yuan Zhe sighed. “The Eastern Palace has gone too far. Abducting someone while also coming to the door to demand her!”

“Demand her?” Pei Ta was somewhat astonished. “Do they want Yu Ying to enter the Eastern Palace?”

“Yes.” Zhao Xuanyou exhaled heavily. “An inner attendant from the Eastern Palace, acting on the Crown Princess’s orders, came to summon Yu Ying to serve in the Eastern Palace.”

Using the Crown Princess’s name… what a clever scheme.

Pei Ta said, “It seems the dark guard’s escape is still unknown to the Crown Prince, otherwise they wouldn’t act simultaneously.”

Zhao Xuanyou gave a slight nod, agreeing with Pei Ta’s reasoning.

“The Crown Prince’s intention in seizing Yu Ying is not to take her life. Since he is currently in Lichuan, it’s likely that Yu Ying is still safe. For now, the priority is to quickly determine her whereabouts.”

Naturally, Zhao Xuanyou had already considered all of this.

“Lichuan is too small. He wanted to send someone to take Yu Ying away immediately; he would never bring her back to Lichuan. She must still be in the hands of that dark guard.”

“Is it possible that Miss Yu Ying has already entered the Eastern Palace?”

Once inside the Eastern Palace, which was as secure as a fortress, no one in the world, except the Emperor and Empress, could take Yu Ying out.

Zhao Xuanyou stated firmly, “She’s still in the capital.”

The manager of Taoran Inn had also sent word: someone had left a ten-tael silver note at the counter, addressed to Chen Da Niu.

The only person who would send money to Chen Da Niu was Yu Ying.

She was sending a message to Zhao Xuanyou. She was alive. She had not entered the Eastern Palace.

“Without the Crown Prince’s orders, the dark guard would not recklessly bring a living person into the Eastern Palace. Yu Ying is still hidden somewhere in the capital.”

Now that Zhao Xuanyou had received the message, the Crown Prince must have also learned of Yu Ying’s re-capture.

“We must find that dark guard before his orders reach the capital. But I’m here accompanying the Emperor. I can’t return to the capital!” Zhao Xuanyou slammed his fist on the table, shattering the teacup. If he could go back personally, he would definitely find Yu Ying, but with the Emperor’s command binding him, he was truly stretched thin.

Pei Ta was taken aback. Watching Zhao Xuanyou’s solemn expression, he knew he must have evidence.

He said calmly, “If Lord Zhao is worried about how to leave the palace, I do have an idea.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes snapped up. “Please enlighten me, Minister Pei.”

“Earlier, His Majesty summoned me and said that a county yamen a hundred li away had been raided by mountain bandits. He wants me to take His Highness the Seventh Prince to eliminate the bandits and pacify the locals. I’ve already accepted the task. Since Lord Zhao is also His Highness’s teacher, if I request an imperial decree for you to join us, His Majesty will likely consent. This trip will take at least one or two months. Lord Zhao can first return to the capital to rescue Yu Ying, and once that’s done, meet up with us later. Your movements will then be completely untraceable.”

Mountain bandits were nothing to fear; there was no need for a general of Zhao Xuanyou’s caliber.

The Emperor wanted Pei Ta to take Zhao Qi there to learn how to govern as a local official. But since Zhao Qi was also training under Zhao Xuanyou, having Zhao Xuanyou accompany them would be justified.

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly stood up and bowed to Pei Ta. “Thank you, Minister Pei.”

Pei Ta nodded with a smile.

Sun Tianran didn’t want him meddling in others’ affairs, didn’t want him entangled in the Eastern Palace’s conflicts; he understood all of this.

But since he relied on Zhao Xuanyou’s help, he naturally had to return the favor.

Zhao Xuanyou was no ordinary man; he was the heir to the Marquis of Jingyuan and the commander of the Mingjiao Guard. Such a small favor would never be enough to bind him.

One good turn deserves another.

Now, by offering crucial help at a critical moment, Pei Ta had placed Zhao Xuanyou in his debt. In the future, when he made a request, Zhao Xuanyou would find it difficult to refuse.

After settling the matter, they immediately went to the imperial palace.

As favored officials, they didn’t have to wait long before being granted an audience. The Emperor, delighted by Zhao Xuanyou’s voluntary request to accompany Zhao Qi for training, immediately approved and even bestowed fragrant tea upon them.

Things progressed smoothly. As they left the Hall of Virtuous Light, Zhao Xuanyou felt somewhat lighter.

However, after only a few steps, they ran into Crown Prince Zhao Zun.

The Crown Prince wore a crimson silk robe embroidered with the nine-chapter pattern, his crown and attire exuding the dignity of his high rank. His entire demeanor was that of someone long accustomed to power.

Seeing the two of them walking side by side out of the Hall of Virtuous Light, the Crown Prince’s eyes unconsciously flickered with a sharp glint.

To be honest, he found both of these men rather displeasing to look at.

chapters.title: Undercurrents
chapters.content:
As for Zhao Xuanyou, Pei Ta, who had risen through the ranks by clinging to his father-in-law's coattails, had repeatedly ignored his attempts to recruit him.

And now these two were walking together... One was majestic and dignified, with the bearing of a dragon and the grace of a phoenix, while the other had a jade-like face and an elegant demeanor, exuding the fragrance of orchids. Though they were merely subjects, they drew more attention than he, the Crown Prince.

"Your Highness, the Crown Prince." Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta cupped their hands in salute to the Crown Prince.

The Crown Prince replied indifferently, "No need for such formalities."

"Thank you, Your Highness."

"Did the Emperor summon you both for tea again?" the Crown Prince asked casually.

Among the officials accompanying the Emperor, these two had the lowest ranks, yet they were the ones the Emperor summoned most often. Even if the Crown Prince disapproved of them, he understood that their promotions were only a matter of time.

Pei Ta replied, "There has been a rebellion in Heishui County, a hundred miles away. His Majesty has ordered us to accompany the Seventh Prince to handle the matter."

The Crown Prince had long been assisting in court affairs, and he had seen the memorial about the Heishui County rebellion before the Emperor had.

Previously, he had drafted a list of people to send to suppress the rebellion, but the Emperor had neither approved nor rejected it, saying he needed to think it over. Unexpectedly, he had appointed Zhao Qi instead.

The Crown Prince's eyes darkened. The number of people he disliked had increased from two to three, and now they had even banded together.

A wave of inexplicable irritation surged within him.

"These wretched commoners dare to storm the county yamen with weapons. You must not show them any mercy."

Hearing the Crown Prince's icy words, Pei Ta furrowed his brows, recalling past events.

Years ago, when his father had been the magistrate of Qingsha Town, he had witnessed innocent pearl-diving households being driven to ruin by corrupt officials, with no one to turn to for help.

He knew full well that if the people were not driven to desperation, how could they dare to storm the county yamen?

"Your Highness, rest assured. When we arrive in Heishui County, we will enforce the law impartially and punish all the evildoers."

The Crown Prince detected the subtle rebuttal hidden in Pei Ta's seemingly compliant words, and his gaze sharpened.

Pei Ta was exceptionally handsome, but he was not weak or effeminate. Facing the Crown Prince's domineering stare, his demeanor remained calm, as if he didn't take the heir's intimidation to heart at all.

"Hmph," the Crown Prince coldly said, "It's good that you enforce the law impartially. Just don't abuse the Emperor's trust to seek personal gain or bully others under his authority."

Pei Ta listened, his cool gaze sweeping over the Crown Prince before settling on Zhao Xuanyou. They exchanged a knowing look.

Having been an official for two years, Pei Ta had spent most of his time in the capital and had frequent interactions with the Crown Prince.

To be fair, the Crown Prince was not mediocre. Born to the Empress, he had been taught by renowned scholars since childhood and had entered the Secretariat at a young age, possessing both talent and grace.

But unfortunately, everything had come too easily to him under the Empress's protection. Unlike Zhao Xuanyou, who had endured years of hardship on the frontier, or Pei Ta, who had experienced the hardships of the common people early in life, all his knowledge and demeanor were like castles in the air, lacking depth in scheming and strategy.

Pei Ta had only made a perfunctory remark, yet the Crown Prince had lost his composure in the Mingde Hall.

Zhao Xuanyou said, "Your Highness speaks too harshly. We are merely following the Emperor's orders. How could we be scheming or bullying others under his authority?"

His tone was calm, as if he were casually asking a question, but the phrase "following the Emperor's orders" caused the Crown Prince's expression to subtly change.

They were standing at the entrance of Mingde Hall. Every word he said to them could reach the Emperor's ears.

If he accused them of bullying others under the Emperor's authority, wasn't he also mocking the Emperor himself?

The Crown Prince forced a smile. "I am only reminding you to act cautiously and not to disappoint the Emperor's expectations. Go and attend to your duties."

"We take our leave, Your Highness."

After they left, the Crown Prince stood quietly outside Mingde Hall, waiting for the Emperor's summons. His hand, hidden in his sleeve, tightened with force.

Good for you, Zhao Xuanyou. Go and handle the affairs in Heishui County.

Originally, the Crown Prince had planned to place Yu Wan outside the Eastern Palace, but now he had changed his mind.

He would formally bring Yu Wan into the Eastern Palace and bestow a title upon her. Then, let's see if Zhao Xuanyou could still smile!

---

After leaving the traveling palace, Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Pei Ta. "He and I are already at odds. Why did you, Lord Pei, have to provoke him with your words?"

Pei Ta replied, "I did not provoke him, and this matter has nothing to do with you, Lord Zhao. I have already read the memorial about Heishui County. The magistrate there imposed heavy taxes and ignored the Emperor's decree to reduce them, exacerbating the situation during the famine and inciting the rebellion. He has seen the memorial, yet he calls them wretched commoners who deserve to die."

It was absurd that such a person could maintain a reputation for benevolence.

Zhao Xuanyou pondered.

People said that Pei Ta had married the daughter of a powerful minister to climb the social ladder, but Pei Ta's actions were completely different from his cunning and scheming father-in-law.

The matter in Heishui County could not be resolved by simple suppression, of course. But given Pei Ta's compassion for the people, he would likely handle it appropriately. As for Zhao Xuanyou, he had more urgent matters to attend to.

"When do you plan to depart?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Pei Ta took a deep breath, suppressing all his emotions.

"Rescuing the person is the priority. You go and arrange the manpower first. I will inform the Seventh Prince. If all goes well, we will set out from the traveling palace in two hours."
