The empress closed her eyes briefly, steadying her mind, and slowly said, "Initially, your uncle saw that Heishui County was remote and had no special products, so he secretly supported a man to become the county magistrate there. The extra taxes collected were not sent to the Duke of Zhen Guo's vault."

"Then where did it go?" the crown prince asked coldly. "It couldn't have been taken by Mother for me, could it?"

"I did indeed make other arrangements for you. That county magistrate used the money to cast many weapons, which are now hidden in Heishui County."

"Mother, what are you saying?" The crown prince's face suddenly turned pale. "Privately casting weapons is a serious crime of rebellion! How could you... How dare Uncle... I am already the crown prince. Why must you do this?"

At this point, the empress had calmed down considerably. Her gaze was steady and sharp: "Your father and I have long been separated in spirit. Over these years, he has not stopped training your younger brothers, and I am very clear about what intentions he harbors. For your future, I had to make additional arrangements."

"How could Mother not discuss such a big matter with me?" The crown prince's face was pale as he looked at the empress in disbelief.

The empress did not answer the crown prince's question. She only frowned and said, "That county magistrate has received great favors from your uncle and was willing to risk his life to cast weapons. Originally, we thought that he would take the blame for the corruption charges and that would be the end of it. But Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou have been staying in Heishui County for too long, and your uncle is worried that something will go wrong."

The crown prince gave a powerless cold laugh.

"If Uncle wasn't afraid of casting weapons, what else is there to worry about?"

The empress completely ignored the crown prince's emotions and only ordered, "You must go to your father immediately, obtain an imperial decree, and find a way to go to Heishui County. Either expedite the conclusion of the case or deal with that county magistrate."

chapters.title: Blood Ties
chapters.content:
The Crown Prince stared blankly at the Empress, his eyes filled with confusion.

"Mother, I am your son!"

Seeing that the Crown Prince had not taken her words to heart at all, the Empress's gaze suddenly sharpened.

"Precisely because you are my son, I have been scheming for you in every way! Do you think that, as the Crown Prince, you find the things your uncle does beneath you? But have you ever considered how you became the Crown Prince in the first place?"

"I am the Emperor's firstborn son by the principal wife..."

The Empress listened to the Crown Prince's words and sneered, "Zun'er, don't forget, your late elder brother was born to the original Empress. He was the true firstborn son. When you were born, I was a Noble Consort, and ranked second. If that elder brother had not died, how could it have been your turn to be the firstborn son?"

The Crown Prince's chest heaved violently.

Of course, he knew that his birth mother had entered the palace as a Noble Consort, and when he was born, the previous Empress was still alive, and the palace had a son under her care.

By the time he could remember, both the previous Empress and the elder brother had passed away.

There had been rumors in the palace that they had been killed by the Empress. The palace servants who spread the rumors were quickly dealt with, and from then on, no one dared to discuss it.

Hearing the Empress admit to killing the previous Empress and his elder brother, the Crown Prince felt as if he had been struck by a thunderbolt, his eyes filled with pain and struggle.

"Mother, are you saying that my maternal grandfather also..."

The Empress let out a light laugh, "I and your uncle were both personally taught by your maternal grandfather. What do you think? It's just that your uncle's wisdom and schemes are not as good as your grandfather's. He is not thorough enough in his actions, so he needs his nephew to step in and suppress the situation."

After a pause, the Empress continued, "Moreover, think about it. How many sons does your father have? How many sons do I have? Prince Ping has always been eyeing the position of Crown Prince, and your younger brothers are also growing up. I have no choice but to take precautions!"

Seeing the Crown Prince standing there in a daze, the Empress went on, "If you like listening to these things, in the future, I can slowly tell you. But now, we must first handle the matter in Heishui County."

"Mother..."

"Do it immediately!" The Empress raised her voice, her eyes burning as she stared at the Crown Prince.

The Empress had always taken good care of her appearance. Although she was approaching forty, her looks were still as striking as ever. However, her gaze was exceptionally sharp, with eyes that had seen countless storms.

The Crown Prince met her gaze for a moment before lowering his head in defeat.

"I understand."

The Empress nodded, and the Crown Prince added, "Your son takes his leave."

When he left the Liu Li Palace, it was still noon. The Crown Prince looked up, and the autumn sun stung his eyes. Even standing in the sunlight, he felt cold from head to toe.

Just before entering the Liu Li Palace, he had been the Crown Prince who could command the wind and rain. In a moment, he had become a rebellious minister and traitor.

His mother and uncle had privately cast weapons. Even if they had done it without his knowledge, in the eyes of others, it was as if he had done it.

"Your Highness, please take care of your health." A eunuch approached with an umbrella to shield the Crown Prince from the sun.

Seeing his pale complexion and unsteady stance, the eunuch quickly said with concern, "This servant will immediately call the imperial physician for Your Highness..."

"No need." The Crown Prince said weakly, "Help me return to Chonghua Palace."

"Yes." The eunuch supported the Crown Prince back to Chonghua Palace. The Crown Princess Consort, Jiang Rushuang, came out from the palace to greet him. Seeing the Crown Prince's poor complexion, she ordered someone to bring calming soup.

After the Crown Prince was seated, Jiang Rushuang personally fed him the soup.

After drinking a few sips, the Crown Prince felt slightly calmer.

Jiang Rushuang glanced at the people around them. After the palace servants silently retreated, she softly persuaded, "Your Highness need not worry too much. The weapons in Heishui County have already been secretly transported away by my father. As long as Your Highness goes to Heishui County and silences that magistrate, this matter can be resolved."

"You knew about this all along?" The Crown Prince suddenly looked up and grabbed Jiang Rushuang's wrist.

The porcelain cup in her hand fell to the ground, spilling its contents everywhere.

Jiang Rushuang had not expected such a strong reaction from him. She lowered her voice, "When Mother ordered my father to handle this matter, I knew... Mother ordered me not to tell you, cousin. She was afraid you would worry."

"Get out!" The Crown Prince roared.

Jiang Rushuang hastily pulled her wrist from his grip and quickly ran back to the bedroom.

The Crown Prince sat alone in the palace for a long time. When his emotions finally calmed down, he stood up and walked out.

In the Mingde Hall, the Emperor was listening to Consort Qin play the guqin.

Consort Qin was only nineteen years old this year. She had bright eyes, white teeth, and a graceful, otherworldly demeanor. Coming from a prominent family in Jiangnan, she was well-versed in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. Her beauty and talents had earned her the Emperor's favor.

A eunuch entered the hall. After Consort Qin finished playing a piece, he approached the Emperor and said, "Your Majesty, the Crown Prince seeks an audience."

The Emperor's gaze gradually sharpened. Consort Qin, noticing this, stood up and said, "This concubine will go check on the silver thread pastries." With that, she respectfully withdrew.

"Let him in."

The eunuch quickly led the Crown Prince in. The Emperor sat behind his desk, frowning as he looked at him. "Why have you come at this time?"

"Father Emperor," the Crown Prince respectfully said, "Earlier, when you asked if there were any unresolved court matters, I said everything was fine. After returning to Chonghua Palace, I realized there was one matter that was not properly handled and wished to seek your decision."

"What matter?" The Emperor asked softly.

The Crown Prince always felt that the Emperor's gaze was somewhat complex, but he had no way out. Hardening his heart, he continued, "The Seventh Prince has been in Heishui County for over a month. The mountain bandits have long been pacified, yet he has not returned. I am somewhat worried."

"It has indeed been over a month. Do you want me to issue a decree to summon him back?"

"This is the Seventh Prince's first time handling such a task. The delay suggests there might be some difficult matters. As his elder brother, I should naturally show concern for my younger sibling."

The Emperor narrowed his eyes. After a long moment, he said, "You wish to go to Heishui County?"

The Crown Prince replied, "Yes. Recently, you mentioned sending me to Weizhou to inspect the army. Weizhou is not far from Heishui County, so I can handle both matters at once."

"That is true." The Emperor slightly nodded. "When do you plan to leave?"

"I wish to depart tomorrow."

In the Mingde Hall, the dragon's saliva incense was thick. The Emperor looked at the Crown Prince before him, his expression showing a rare sense of fatigue and powerlessness. "So soon?"

Feeling the Emperor's scrutiny, the Crown Prince did not dare to look up. He only stared at the golden lion incense burner slowly emitting smoke in the hall. "I fear Your Majesty's laughter, but having stayed in the imperial palace for nearly three months, I truly wish to go out and travel. I hope Your Majesty will grant this request."

"As you said, the matters in Weizhou and Heishui will be entrusted to you. Once the Heishui case is resolved, there is no need to return to Lichuan. Bring Qi'er back to the capital."

"I obey your decree." The Crown Prince finally received the Emperor's verbal order. The huge stone in his heart finally fell to the ground. He respectfully retreated from Mingde Hall.

The Emperor sat silently behind his desk, his gaze falling on the gilded paperweight, his expression unusually dejected.

The close attendant, Liu Quan, saw that the Emperor had been alone for a long time. He approached respectfully and said, "Your Majesty, Consort Qin has sent over silver thread pastries made by her own hands. Shall this servant present them?"

"He has finally spoken." The Emperor said heavily.

Half a month ago, Zhao Xuanyou had sent a secret letter via express horse to the Lichuan imperial palace, reporting the discovery of privately cast weapons in the Heishui County government office. He also mentioned that there were several chests with the insignia of the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion in the county office.

Although the Heishui County Magistrate had no apparent connection with the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion, once the direction of the investigation was known, the Brocade Guard quickly found clues.

At that time, Liu Quan had advised the Emperor to rest assured, as the Empress and the Zhen Guo Duke were reckless, but the Crown Prince might not have known.

However, at this moment, the Crown Prince had come to request an audience to go to Heishui County. Whether he had known before or not, he had now chosen to side with the Empress and the Zhen Guo Duke.

Liu Quan knew the Emperor's disappointment well and could only forcefully advise, "Your Majesty, please take care of your health."

---

chapters.title: Understanding Him
chapters.content:
"What? The Crown Prince has arrived?"

Yu Ying was practicing calligraphy in the study when she heard Yuan Qing deliver this terrible news.

"Yes, Lord Pei has ordered everyone in the county government to go out of the city to greet him."

"But I... I should still hide." Yu Ying recalled the terrifying night she was trapped in Chonghua Palace and felt a chill. "I'll pack my things immediately."

Fortunately, she had learned to ride a horse and could run fast.

Yuan Qing said, "The master said there's no need to hide. We can go out together to greet him."

"No need to hide?" Yu Ying looked at Yuan Qing in disbelief.

The Crown Prince had caused them so much trouble, and now they were hiding in Heishui County because of him.

She never expected that he would actually chase them to Heishui County.

This... this was unlikely. Although Yu Ying knew she was beautiful, she also understood that the Crown Prince would not chase her all the way to Heishui County just to get her.

Yuan Qing looked at her confused expression and scratched his head. "The master means that the Crown Prince has come for other matters this time. We need not worry."

"Oh."

Yu Ying pouted.

That made sense. Her beauty was far from the kind that could topple cities and countries. How could the Crown Prince chase her all the way here...

"Then I'll change my clothes and go with you."

"Okay."

By the time Yuan Qing and Yu Ying arrived at the county government gate, Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou were already standing there.

"Worldly Son, Lord Pei." Yu Ying stepped forward to pay her respects.

Pei Tao was also aware of the Crown Prince's two attempts on Yu Ying. Seeing her arrival, he could not help but look at Zhao Xuanyou, who seemed composed, and felt somewhat puzzled.

Zhao Xuanyou was very possessive of Yu Ying. He would scowl if other men occasionally spoke to her.

The Crown Prince had long harbored feelings for Yu Ying. Now that he had arrived in person, Zhao Xuanyou had no reaction at all and even boldly called Yu Ying to greet him together. It was indeed suspicious.

"Prince Qi has arrived." Yuan Man saw Zhao Qi leading his guards out of the county government and hurriedly said.

Everyone at the county government gate bowed to Zhao Qi.

"No need for formalities."

Zhao Qi glanced at Yu Ying, with whom he had not spoken in many days, then quickly averted his gaze. He mounted his horse and headed straight for the city gate, with everyone else following.

Yu Ying rode her horse behind Zhao Xuanyou.

After practicing for more than a month, her riding skills had improved greatly. Zhao Xuanyou had picked a new white horse for her.

This horse was only four years old, slightly taller than the previous mare, and had a livelier temperament.

Because of its all-white coat, which was truly beautiful, Yu Ying had tied a pretty ornament to its mane with silk ribbons and named it Snowball.

Every day, she personally fed Snowball and often took it to the river to drink water and bathe.

Everyone rode to the city gate and waited for about half an hour before the Crown Prince's carriage finally arrived.

The carriage approached slowly, the wind stirring the brocade curtains, and the sight was filled with splendor.

Everyone knelt to pay their respects. The Crown Prince, sitting in the carriage, did not come down. A eunuch spoke for him, saying "Rise," and the carriage proceeded into the city.

Yu Ying let out a soft sigh.

It seemed Zhao Xuanyou had guessed correctly. The Crown Prince had come to Heishui County not for personal matters.

Otherwise, given his relationship with the three of them, he would certainly have come out to exchange barbs.

Zhao Qi looked at the luxurious carriage of the Crown Prince, his fists tightly clenched.

"Why has he come at this time?"

Pei Tao also understood that the visitor came with ill intentions and softly said, "It must be because of those chests."

"What dirty deeds has that corrupt official done for the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion to attract the attention of Zhao Zun himself?"

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Zhao Qi with a calm expression.

This young man was reckless, but he still had some brains.

If he had not acted first, they might have discovered something.

"Your Highness, please remain calm."

"How can I be calm? The evidence we finally found. Are we just supposed to hand it over to him?" Zhao Qi shouted.

Angry as he was, he knew in his heart that the Crown Prince was the heir apparent and had always assisted the Emperor in managing court affairs. Since the Crown Prince could come to Heishui County in such a high-profile manner, he must have received the Emperor's approval and would handle the matter entirely.

If he wanted the chests, they had to give them. If he wanted people, they had to hand them over.

"As I have reminded Your Highness before, those few chests alone are not enough to convict the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion. Handing them over is not a problem."

Looking at Zhao Xuanyou's calm expression, Pei Tao's suspicions about him grew even more, but he had no evidence.

Feeling Pei Tao's scrutiny, Zhao Xuanyou lightly coughed, pretending not to notice.

After all, his mood was indeed good.

The secret letter had been sent to the imperial palace half a month ago. The Emperor had long known about the privately cast weapons.

The Crown Prince's appearance in Heishui County now... clearly indicated that he had chosen to side with the Empress and the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion to cover up the matter of the privately cast weapons.

Killing a country's Crown Prince was originally as difficult as ascending to heaven, but what could he do... if he courted death himself.

Seeing Zhao Qi's agitated expression, Pei Tao advised, "Lord Zhao speaks reason. We have interrogated that magistrate for over a month, trying both soft and hard approaches. He only admitted to extorting the common people and refused to acknowledge any connection with the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion. This case has dragged on for so long. If it is not concluded, according to the rules, it should be transferred to the Ministry of Justice."

"And that's it? We just give up?"

"Your Highness, rest assured. The testimonies and evidence have all been recorded. Whether they are handed over to the Crown Prince or kept with us makes no difference."

Seeing that Zhao Qi was still reluctant, Zhao Xuanyou also said, "That man, although corrupt, is a tough bone. His wives, concubines, and children are all dead. He has no ties left and is no different from a dead man. Handing him over is no different from handing over a corpse."

Yu Ying listened to the three of them from the side, watching Zhao Qi's pained expression, and felt a deep emotional stir.

Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao, although wanting to solve the case, were ultimately onlookers and could maintain their rationality.

The Empress had killed Zhao Qi's birth mother. Zhao Qi had lost his mother at a young age and shared a blood feud with the Empress and her son. After finally finding some evidence, he had to hand it over to his enemy. How could he willingly let it go?

Yu Ying felt a pang of sorrow and looked at Zhao Qi with some melancholy. Zhao Qi happened to look her way, and their gazes met unintentionally.

It had been more than half a month since they last spoke.

The last time they spoke was when Yu Ying had made an eight-treasure cake and sent it to him.

Zhao Qi's heart stirred slightly.

Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou had always said they would help deal with the Crown Prince, but at this moment, Pei Tao was calm and gentle, and Zhao Xuanyou was composed, clearly not concerned with his thoughts.

But Yu Ying... she understood his feelings.

"Your Highness." In such a situation, it was not Yu Ying's place to speak, but seeing Zhao Qi looking at her with such a pitiful expression, she overstepped her bounds and said, "Since they have done so much evil, they will surely reveal their flaws again. Missing this opportunity does not mean there won't be another."

Zhao Qi listened to her words, his expression stiffened, and a complex emotion surged in his heart.

"I understand." The young man bit his lip, mounted his horse, and left without further delay.

Pei Tao and the guards followed closely behind.

Zhao Xuanyou, however, turned back to look at Yu Ying, deep in thought.

chapters.title: A Young Man's Troubles
chapters.content:
Yu Wan met his gaze and looked back, confused. "Master, what's wrong?"

"Nothing." Zhao Xuanyou raised his hand and tucked a loose strand of hair behind her ear, blown by the wind. "Let's go."

"Once we return to the county office, should I go back to the courtyard immediately?"

Zhao Zun had arrived suddenly. Only half an hour ago, Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou had received the news. Hechuan County was remote and not prosperous; the posthouse was dilapidated. They feared Zhao Zun might stay at the county office.

Though the county office was better than the posthouse, it was far from the standards of a marquis's residence. The rear courtyard had only three small courtyards in total.

The most spacious one was currently occupied by Zhao Qi. With Zhao Zun's arrival, it would likely be vacated for him.

But once Zhao Qi moved out... Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes in thought. Maybe it would be better for him to give up his courtyard and take Yu Wan to stay at the posthouse instead.

After all, he didn’t care much about these things.

"Let's talk about it when we get back." Zhao Xuanyou didn’t share his thoughts. Seeing that the people ahead had already disappeared from sight, he quickly led Yu Wan and the others to the county office, arriving just before the carriage stopped at the gate. They stood behind Zhao Qi, waiting for the Crown Prince to alight.

"Your subjects welcome Your Highness, the Crown Prince."

The Crown Prince stepped out of the carriage and indifferently ordered everyone to rise.

His gaze passed over Zhao Qi, Zhao Xuanyou, and the others, landing directly on Yu Wan.

But only for a moment. His gaze then shifted to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou calmly raised his eyebrows. When their eyes met, it was as if silent blades clashed between them.

Around them, aside from Zhao Qi and Pei Tao, all the others were minor officials from Hechuan County. The Crown Prince paid them no mind, making no effort to conceal his anger. His gaze toward Zhao Xuanyou was filled with sharpness.

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression remained completely calm, simply staring back at him.

Zhao Qi watched as their eyes locked and coldly scoffed, "The wind is strong outside. Royal brother, standing in the wind to talk might make your tongue go numb."

At these words, the surroundings instantly fell into a deathly silence. The local minor officials had never witnessed such a scene before. Each one lowered their heads in fear, terrified that the nobles might lose their tempers and they would suffer the consequences.

"Insolent!" The Crown Prince was enraged by Zhao Qi’s words. "Just the other day, Father Emperor said you had improved. But I see you not only haven’t improved at all, you’ve become even more outrageous!"

Seeing that Zhao Qi showed no fear and was about to retort, Pei Tao quickly spoke first, "The climate of Hechuan is not as comfortable as that of Lichuan. The Seventh Prince is also concerned for Your Highness’s well-being. This is indeed not the place to talk. Please, Your Highness, enter and rest. Allow me to report the matters here one by one."

The Crown Prince had come to Hechuan to investigate the matter of Marquis Zhen Guo’s private minting of weapons. Currently, the county magistrate was still under Zhao Qi’s control. If they completely broke ties, with Zhao Qi’s madman-like temperament, who knew what he might do.

To avoid unnecessary trouble, the Crown Prince finally swallowed his anger and walked toward the county office with a darkened face.

This time, Pei Tao followed closely behind the Crown Prince. Zhao Qi watched the Crown Prince’s retreating figure, his gaze sharp like a sword tempered in flames.

He had long known that the disgraced county magistrate had an unspeakable connection with the Marquis Zhen Guo’s residence. Now that Zhao Zun had come in person, it was clear that the secrets hidden here were enough to affect the Empress and Zhao Zun.

Yet, he was useless; he couldn’t uncover anything at all.

Zhao Xuanyou observed his expression and knew he couldn’t calm down. He turned to Yu Wan. "The Seventh Prince is not feeling well. Take him back to the courtyard to rest and have some calming tea."

Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou still had to deal with the Crown Prince. Even though Zhao Xuanyou wanted to hide Yu Wan, in the entire Hechuan County, the only person who could soothe Zhao Qi’s emotions was Yu Wan.

"Yes."

After Yu Wan respectfully agreed, Zhao Xuanyou turned and walked into the county office.

Because of the Crown Prince’s arrival, a large crowd had gathered outside the county office. Seeing Zhao Qi’s dejected appearance, Yu Wan softly advised, "Your Highness, return to the courtyard first. Leave the court matters to Master Zhao and Lord Pei. They are both reliable."

Reliable?

Perhaps Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao were not tigers or wolves and bore no ill will toward him. But they were outsiders. No one would care about his personal feud with the Crown Prince.

"As for Lord Pei’s thoughts, this servant does not know. But this servant understands Master Zhao’s intentions to some extent. Your Highness, please trust him this once."

Zhao Qi looked up at Yu Wan and saw her smile gently at him. The hardness in his brows softened slightly, and he silently walked toward the county office.

Yu Wan quickly followed, entering Zhao Qi’s small courtyard with him.

Seeing his dispirited look, Yu Wan opened the menu and had Yin Ping send someone to the restaurant to buy food.

When she turned back, Zhao Qi was sitting blankly at the stone table, looking deeply troubled.

Yu Wan went to the corridor, fetched a kettle, and poured a cup of water for Zhao Qi.

"Some things truly cannot be rushed. Your Highness, please be patient."

"Mother has been gone for eleven years. Is it considered rushing to avenge her now?"

Yu Wan looked at Zhao Qi’s self-defeated expression and thought of her own mother. Suddenly, her nose tingled.

Zhao Qi didn’t hear her speak and looked at her blankly. "Why are you crying?"

"Hearing Your Highness speak of Consort Hui, I was reminded of my mother. When I returned to the capital last time, the physician said her condition had improved. I wonder how she is now?"

"Your mother is ill?" Zhao Qi asked.

Yu Wan nodded. "My mother fell while picking herbs in the mountains. She has been in a coma for more than two years. If it weren’t for her accident, I wouldn’t have left my hometown to come to the capital, let alone entered the marquis’s residence."

This was the first time Zhao Qi had heard Yu Wan speak of her own affairs in all the time he had known her.

"So your mother has never woken up?"

"No. But now we’ve found a skilled physician who treats her with acupuncture every month. Who knows, she might wake up at any time?"

Zhao Qi’s hands trembled slightly. Speaking to Yu Wan, yet also to himself, he said, "Yes, as long as she is alive, there will come a day she wakes up. Unlike me, I can’t even remember Mother’s face clearly anymore."

"All this servant means is that neither when my mother will wake up nor when Your Highness’s great vengeance will be achieved is entirely within our control. We can only do our best and leave the rest to fate."

Zhao Qi listened to Yu Wan’s sincere advice, his emotions surging, but he remained silent.

"Your Highness, there are many people around you who care deeply for you. If you continue to torment yourself like this, they will also feel guilty and blame themselves."

"Do you mean..."

"When this servant was at the Duke Ning’s residence, it was clear that everyone there, from top to bottom, cared deeply for Your Highness. This servant believes they also care deeply for Consort Hui and are always thinking of avenging her."

Apart from others, Zhao Qi naturally knew that his maternal grandfather, Duke Ning, lived every moment in self-reproach, regretting sending his beloved daughter into the palace.

Zhao Qi gave a bitter smile. "In truth, I have never spoken of these things to them."

All his troubles he had always buried deep in his heart. He would not speak of them to the Emperor, nor to his maternal grandfather. Perhaps his close attendants like Yin Ping and Mu Di could guess a thing or two, but the only one before whom he had ever been so unguarded with his feelings was Yu Wan.

---

chapters.title: Out of Reach
chapters.content:
The main hall of the county office was now filled with the aroma of tea. Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou stood respectfully before the Crown Prince, waiting until he had finished a warming cup of tea before stepping forward. "Your subjects have organized all the case files of Hechuan County. They are ready for Your Highness’s review."

As soon as Pei Tao finished speaking, the attendants behind him quickly presented the neatly organized case files.

The Crown Prince coldly glanced at the two of them, then turned to his inner attendant. After the attendant took the documents, the Crown Prince asked in a deep voice, "Has the case been concluded?"

Pei Tao replied, "After my investigation, it was confirmed that County Magistrate Liu Zhixiao of Hechuan had imposed exorbitant taxes, driving the common people to ruin and sparking a rebellion. The mob broke into the county office and killed Liu Zhixiao’s family and several yamen runners. All the involved parties are currently imprisoned. I have submitted the case details to the Ministry of Justice. Once they respond, the case can be closed."

"Have you found out where the silver Liu Zhixiao embezzled has gone?"

The Crown Prince asked calmly, but his heart was slightly uneasy.

Though his talents and strategies were not on par with Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou, he had been educated by distinguished officials and scholars since childhood and was by no means mediocre. Hearing Pei Tao’s words, he immediately realized the crux of the matter.

So much money had been extorted in taxes, yet none of it had been submitted to the court. That silver had to have gone somewhere.

Gold and silver utensils, antiques, and calligraphy; these would have to be produced to convince others.

Pei Tao’s eyebrows twitched slightly at the Crown Prince’s question.

The reason he had been delayed in Hechuan for so long, unable to close the case, was precisely because the county magistrate had admitted to embezzling silver but could not account for where it had gone.

They had searched the entire county office but found nothing of value.

But he also understood that the Crown Prince did not genuinely want to investigate. He only wanted to plug the loophole and close the case seamlessly.

Thus, Pei Tao calmly replied, "According to Liu Zhixiao’s confession, his eldest son was a compulsive gambler who had amassed enormous gambling debts. All the silver he embezzled went to covering his son’s losses."

"And this son?"

"He was hacked to death by the mob during the rebellion at the county office."

The Crown Prince finally let out a sigh of relief.

"A disloyal and unfilial gambler like that deserves to die." As he spoke, the huge weight in his heart finally settled, and his voice became much steadier. "Lord Pei, you have worked hard on this case. Once it is concluded, I will request a reward for you from Father Emperor."

Pei Tao quickly cupped his hands. "Your Highness overpraises me. Since arriving in Hechuan, all matters have been directed by the Seventh Prince. Lord Zhao and I have merely followed his instructions."

"You need not be modest. I am well aware of Zhao Qi’s capabilities, as is Father Emperor. Since you have handled the matter well, I will naturally reward you accordingly." At this point, the Crown Prince changed the subject. "However, you two have been delayed in Hechuan for too long. Father Emperor has entrusted this case to me, so hand over all the prisoners and documents immediately."

"Yes." Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao had already agreed on this. Hearing the Crown Prince’s words, they had no objections.

The Crown Prince glanced at them. "Since the matter is settled, you will return to the capital with me tomorrow."

Tomorrow?

It was sudden, but since all the evidence and prisoners had been handed over to the Crown Prince, staying in Hechuan served no purpose.

Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao both cupped their hands. "Yes."

"Dismissed."

"Your subjects take their leave."

Watching their retreating figures, the Crown Prince finally felt at ease.

He hadn’t expected this trip to go so smoothly. It seemed he had worried too much earlier.

Though his uncle had not informed him in advance, he had at least removed all the privately minted weapons.

Without the weapons, even if Pei Tao and Zhao Xuanyou wanted to oppose him, they would be like a skilled cook with no rice; helpless. They could only obediently hand over the county magistrate.

"Your Highness, how should the county magistrate be dealt with?" Seeing the Crown Prince’s furrowed brows, the inner attendant quietly approached and asked.

The Crown Prince pondered for a moment before slowly replying, "Keep him for now. It seems this Liu fellow is quite tough. He didn’t reveal any flaws even under Zhao Qi and Zhao Xuanyou’s watch. He likely won’t cause any trouble on the way back to the capital. Keep him under strict guard, don’t let anyone near him. Once we return to the capital, we can... give him something. If he dies in the Ministry of Justice’s prison, it will have nothing to do with me."

He had requested the Emperor’s permission to investigate the case. If the prisoner died as soon as he took custody, it would easily arouse the Emperor’s suspicion. It was better to keep him alive for a while longer.

"Your Highness is wise." The inner attendant respectfully replied, then added, "This servant has already inspected the place. The posthouse in Hechuan is in disrepair. Your Highness is noble and precious; it would be unfit for you to rest there. Earlier, Lord Pei informed this servant that a courtyard in the county office has been vacated for Your Highness to rest in tonight. This servant has already ordered it to be cleaned. Your Highness, please enjoy some tea and refreshments here in the main hall before moving over."

With the major matter resolved, the Crown Prince suddenly remembered the graceful figure he had seen at the county office gate.

Zhao Xuanyou had taken Yu Wan from the capital and actually brought her to Hechuan.

"Do they all live in the county office?" the Crown Prince suddenly asked.

"Yes." The inner attendant, seeing the Crown Prince’s interest in the living arrangements, quickly relayed the information he had gathered from the servants. "The Seventh Prince, Lord Pei, and Lord Zhao have all been staying in the county office. Tonight, Your Highness will be staying in the place where Lord Pei resides. He has few personal belongings and has already moved them to the posthouse."

The Crown Prince’s expression was rather amused. He narrowed his eyes. "So, Yu Wan is still here?"

The inner attendant, of course, knew who Yu Wan was.

His master had acted twice for this girl, nearly losing the top-tier lightness skill master Wen Ji in the process.

Seeing the Crown Prince’s gaze, the inner attendant couldn’t help but feel a little helpless.

Though Yu Wan was exceptionally beautiful and charming, the palace was not without such beauties.

The Crown Prince’s fixation on her was partly due to her appearance, partly because she resembled Cui Yichu, but mostly because the Crown Prince had tried twice and failed to obtain her.

She was just a servant girl. Was it really necessary?

"She should be," the inner attendant briefly replied, quickly changing the subject and earnestly advising, "Your Highness has traveled a long way, exhausting both body and mind. Now that the troubles are resolved, why not retire early to rest and regain your strength? You still have to set off for the capital tomorrow."

The Crown Prince frowned at these words and suddenly stood up, striding out.

The inner attendant had no choice but to quickly follow.

The rear residence of the county office was not large. The Crown Prince exited the main hall and walked forward casually. Before long, he saw Yin Ping and Mu Di standing guard in front of a courtyard gate.

It seemed that was where that jinx Zhao Qi lived. The Crown Prince’s eyes darkened, and he was about to quicken his pace when he suddenly heard a woman’s laughter from inside the courtyard.

The laughter was light and unrestrained. Though he hadn’t seen the person, just hearing that laughter was like being bathed in the warmth of a bright spring day.

The Crown Prince had never heard Yu Wan’s laughter before, but he instinctively felt it was her.

His heart stirred, and he walked straight toward that courtyard.

Yin Ping and Mu Di at the gate saw him approaching. As they bowed in greeting, they also loudly announced, "His Highness, the Crown Prince, has arrived."

Inside the courtyard, Yu Wan instinctively fell silent. Beside her, Zhao Qi clenched his fists and slammed them hard on the stone table.

chapters.title: A Direct Confrontation
chapters.content:
"Greetings to His Highness, the Crown Prince." Everyone in the courtyard stood up and knelt in salute to the Crown Prince.

Zhao Qi remained seated on the stone bench, unmoving, still playing with the black chess piece in his hand.

Just now, he had shared many personal thoughts with Yu Wan, and the atmosphere had been quite heavy. So, he had someone bring out a chessboard to teach Yu Wan how to play Go.

It was Yu Wan's first time playing chess, and naturally, she didn't understand the rules. She placed her pieces haphazardly, and even after being teased by him, she didn't get angry. Instead, she just laughed and defended herself.

A good game of chess was ruined by Zhao Zun.

Only when the Crown Prince entered the courtyard did Zhao Qi reluctantly say, "Elder Brother Crown Prince, you've been entrusted by the Emperor to investigate the case. Why aren't you interrogating the suspects? Why come to my shabby courtyard?"

"You and Zhao Xuanyou, Pei Ta have been investigating here for over a month. If you can't even clarify this much about the case, there's no need for you to work for the court in the future."

Zhao Qi laughed without a care, saying nothing.

The Crown Prince had come to the courtyard for Yu Wan, and he hadn't intended to speak with Zhao Qi at all.

Seeing this, he shifted his gaze to Yu Wan, who was standing to the side, and said indifferently, "Rise."

"Thank you, Your Highness," Yu Wan said. She could clearly feel that his tone was completely different from when they had met in his bedchamber that night, and her heart settled slightly.

Seeing that Zhao Qi's emotions had stabilized somewhat, Yu Wan was thinking about how to slip away when she heard the Crown Prince ask, "Do you know how to play chess?"

"I do not, Your Highness. Just now, I learned a little from Seventh Highness, but I only know the basics. I fear I embarrassed myself in front of Seventh Highness."

"Didn't Zhao Xuanyou teach you?"

"I am but a maidservant..."

Yu Wan was carefully choosing her words when Zhao Qi, seeing the Crown Prince persistently harassing Yu Wan, could no longer tolerate it. He shouted angrily at him, "Zhao Zun, will you ever stop?! The Eastern Palace has so many women for you to favor, yet you must pester her? Yu Wan doesn't want anything to do with you. If you know what's good for you, leave at once!"

These words were too blunt. The Crown Prince's eyes suddenly narrowed, and he stared fixedly at Zhao Qi, his expression changing rapidly.

Yu Wan, hearing Zhao Qi's words, was momentarily stunned in place.

"Zhao Qi, you are insolent!" The Crown Prince's face was as cold as ice, and his body radiated anger. "Do you think that just because the Emperor usually dotes on you, I have no way to deal with you? Insolence to a superior is a crime punishable by death!"

Zhao Qi tilted his head indifferently. "Of course you have a way to deal with me. After all, my mother, the Concubine Hui, was silently killed in the palace back then. You can use the same method again!"

He didn't explicitly say who had killed Concubine Hui, but his outburst was clearly directed at the Crown Prince.

"Nonsense! You must be mad."

If this had happened before the incident in Heishui County, the Crown Prince would have been furious upon hearing Zhao Qi's words.

But now he knew that the former Empress and the late Crown Prince had died at the hands of the current Empress. So, what about Zhao Qi's mother, Concubine Hui? Zhao Qi had always been disrespectful to the Empress and had always spoken harshly to him. Could it be that Concubine Hui's death was truly related to the Empress?

Logically speaking, when Concubine Hui gave birth to Zhao Qi, the Empress was already the Empress with the legitimate eldest son by her side, so her position was secure. But now he knew that the Empress was ambitious and would stop at nothing for the position of Empress and the throne.

Could it be that Concubine Hui had truly...

For the first time, the Crown Prince lost his composure in front of Zhao Qi.

Yu Wan hadn't expected Zhao Qi to lose control again so suddenly, but she couldn't step forward to stop him.

One was the Crown Prince of the Eastern Palace, and the other was the Emperor's youngest son. Both were at the pinnacle of power, like dragons and phoenixes among men. How could she, a mere maidservant, interfere?

Moreover, the conflict between them was not about her.

Zhao Qi had sworn to avenge his mother's death and shared a blood feud with the Empress and the Crown Prince.

His anger now was for Concubine Hui, so how could she easily calm him down?

After much thought, Yu Wan decided not to get involved in the brothers' dispute. She silently hoped that Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta would hear the commotion and come quickly to defuse the situation.

Zhao Qi spoke sarcastically, "The fact that my mother died suddenly in the palace is undeniable. Why does Elder Brother Crown Prince say I'm talking nonsense?"

The Crown Prince was, after all, the Crown Prince. Although he had become the heir apparent with the Empress and the old Duke's full support, he had been trained since childhood and possessed the demeanor and dignity of a Crown Prince.

After a moment of distraction, he regained his usual haughty demeanor. "You were only three years old at the time. You must be misremembering. Concubine Hui did not die suddenly; she was afflicted with a serious illness. I remember clearly that after Concubine Hui fell ill, the Emperor ordered the chief physician of the Imperial Physicians' Office to treat her and even moved her into the Zichen Hall to care for her personally. You say there was something suspicious about Concubine Hui's death. Are you suspecting the Emperor?"

Hearing the Crown Prince's sophistry, Zhao Qi's anger grew even more. "You know very well who I suspect!"

The Crown Prince's eyes flashed with a cold smile, and he looked at Zhao Qi with a chilling gaze. However, he didn't say anything to Zhao Qi. Instead, he turned his gaze to Yu Wan.

"You've been treated to quite a show."

Yu Wan, seeing that the Crown Prince was looking at her, cautiously spoke, "This servant is foolish and does not understand what Your Highness and Seventh Highness are talking about."

The Crown Prince had long known that Yu Wan was careful with her words, so he was not surprised by her answer.

"Is there any good tea here?" the Crown Prince asked.

Yu Wan respectfully replied, "Heishui County does not produce tea. Lord Pei brought some tea cakes from the Lichuan Imperial Palace. They are fragrant and soothing. This servant will fetch some for Your Highness now."

She understood that Zhao Qi had worked hard with his people in Heishui County for over a month, and the evidence and witnesses they had painstakingly gathered had all been taken away by the Crown Prince. Zhao Qi was naturally unwilling and couldn't get over this hurdle for the time being.

Zhao Xuanyou had other arrangements but couldn't inform Zhao Qi, so his frustration was understandable.

All she could do was temporarily mediate.

Noticing that the Crown Prince was a person who prided himself on his status and demeanor in front of others, and could repeatedly tolerate Zhao Qi's insults, she thought he wouldn't do anything to her. So, she tried to persuade him to go elsewhere.

"There is a waterside pavilion in the county office with decent scenery. Your Highness might as well go there to drink tea," Yu Wan suggested respectfully.

The Crown Prince, seeing Yu Wan's suggestion to go to the pavilion, readily agreed to step down.

"Very well, let's go sit for a while."

"Let him go by himself. The Eastern Palace isn't short of servants to order around. Could it be that there isn't even one who can pour tea?" Zhao Qi, without further ado, pulled Yu Wan back. "This game of chess isn't finished yet. You're not allowed to leave."

"Are you, as the heir apparent, in a position to be questioned by me?" The Crown Prince's face showed a smile that was almost sinister. "Let go of Yu Wan. She is not your servant."

Hearing these words, Zhao Qi's mind was filled with the scene he had witnessed by the lake: Yu Wan being held in Zhao Xuanyou's arms, taken at will.

It was as if a thorn had pierced his heart, causing him pain.

"Your Highness, this servant is only going to Lord Pei's place to fetch tea cakes. I am clumsy and naturally cannot serve Your Highness properly," Yu Wan said carefully and cautiously, saving face for both of them.

Perhaps seeing Yu Wan's caution, Zhao Qi finally let go of her.

Yu Wan met the Crown Prince's gaze and said frankly, "This servant will first take Your Highness to the pavilion. Your Highness, please follow me."

The Crown Prince nodded and followed Yu Wan out.

Having stayed in Heishui for over a month, Zhao Xuanyou had bought Yu Wan several sets of clothes. Although the fabric was not as fine as those from the Marquis's mansion, the styles were more beautiful and eye-catching than a maidservant's usual attire.

The thin gauze dress she wore swayed gently with the autumn wind, rippling like water.

The Crown Prince glanced over and saw a half-yellow, half-green leaf stuck to her gauze skirt. Without thinking, he reached out to pick off the leaf.

But as soon as his fingertips touched the gauze, a dark shadow suddenly appeared before his eyes, accompanied by an angry shout.

"If you dare touch her again, I'll kill you!"

---

chapters.title: At the End of One's Patience
chapters.content:
"Zhao Qi..." The Crown Prince, seeing the person blocking him and Yu Wan, was filled with rage. "How dare you!"

However, Zhao Qi showed no intention of backing down. Instead, he lifted his head and looked at the Crown Prince without fear.

Yu Wan was terrified and tried her best to control her emotions, but her expression still paled slightly.

Zhao Qi was so impulsive, and Yu Wan worried that he would be punished. But she was just a maidservant; even if she spoke up, her words would carry no weight.

She wondered where Zhao Xuanyou had gone. How could he not have heard the commotion by now?

Although his status was not as high as the Crown Prince's or Zhao Qi's, if he were here, the situation would not have spiraled out of control.

Zhao Qi showed no sign of restraint and continued to curse, "Even if you are the Crown Prince of a nation, don't use those despicable tactics on Yu Wan. It's embarrassing!"

The Crown Prince's chest heaved violently, and in a great rage, he waved his hand and ordered, "Seize Zhao Qi!"

At his command, the guards drew their swords and approached Zhao Qi, pointing their blades at his chest.

Seeing the situation turn dire, Yin Ping and Mu Di immediately stepped forward to block in front of Zhao Qi.

The Crown Prince sneered, "Arrest all three of them, master and servants. If they resist, kill them on the spot!"

The Eastern Palace guards were of high rank. In addition to the sword-wielding guards who followed the Crown Prince closely, there were also archers at a distance.

This time, Zhao Zun was on an imperial tour by decree. Although he had few personal attendants with him, his guards were fully equipped.

Earlier, before the Crown Prince entered the county office, the guard captain had already driven most of Zhao Qi's men out of the county office. Following Eastern Palace regulations, they had set up a guard every ten steps within the county office.

At this moment, the surrounding walls and rooftops were manned by Eastern Palace archers. At the Crown Prince's command, they would not hesitate to loose their arrows.

Hearing the words "kill them on the spot," Yu Wan's face turned pale instantly.

Partly out of concern for Zhao Qi, and partly for herself.

Although the Crown Prince hadn't said he would kill her, swords and arrows had no eyes. She was standing next to Zhao Qi; if the archers behind them trembled, wouldn't she be pierced through the heart?

Seeing that the Crown Prince's guards were not pointing their swords at her, Yu Wan quickly stepped around them and approached the Crown Prince. She pleaded on Zhao Qi's behalf, "Your Highness, please calm your anger. Seventh Highness has been unwell since arriving in Heishui County, so his emotions are unstable, which is why he spoke out of turn."

"Are you saying he did nothing wrong?"

"Of course he was wrong, but Your Highness, considering that Seventh Highness is young and ignorant, please spare him this once."

The Crown Prince, of course, would not order Zhao Qi to be killed.

This was something both the Crown Prince and Zhao Qi knew well.

But Zhao Qi had repeatedly insulted him today, not to mention involving past grievances. It was truly hard for the Crown Prince to endure.

In front of others, the Crown Prince had always been filial to the Emperor and Empress, and fraternal to his siblings. He especially knew that the Emperor doted on Zhao Qi, so no matter how disrespectful Zhao Qi was to him, he had always tolerated it.

After all, in the palace, even the slightest movement would immediately be reported to the Emperor.

The more Zhao Qi acted out, the more the Emperor would think highly of the Crown Prince's tolerance.

But in Heishui County, far from the capital and Lichuan, there was no one who could report to the Emperor over his head.

"His death may be spared, but his punishment cannot be avoided. Seize all three of them, master and servants!"

Yu Wan finally breathed a sigh of relief upon hearing this.

She turned to look at Zhao Qi, hoping he wouldn't say anything more insolent.

To her surprise, Zhao Qi appeared calm and had no intention of fighting with the guards. He reached out and grabbed the tip of the sword closest to him.

"Do you really need such a big show just to arrest me?"

Seeing that he had no intention of resisting, the guards made way, "Seventh Highness, please."

Zhao Qi let out a cold snort, released the sword, and walked forward.

Watching him leave, Yu Wan secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

Zhao Qi's words today had been completely without regard for the Crown Prince's face. The Crown Prince would naturally have to take him down to save his own dignity.

But the Crown Prince wouldn't really do anything to Zhao Qi.

As long as they stopped arguing, the storm would naturally pass.

After Zhao Qi was taken away, Yu Wan felt the Crown Prince's gaze on her. She bowed and said, "This servant will fetch tea for Your Highness now."

Just now, in front of Yu Wan, Zhao Qi had pointed at his nose and cursed so many unpleasant things that the Crown Prince had lost all interest in drinking tea.

"No need."

With that, the Crown Prince turned and left with a dark expression.

"This servant sees Your Highness off."

Yu Wan knelt and bowed. After the Crown Prince had walked far away, she turned around, and Zhao Qi had already been taken away.

Where would the Crown Prince take him?

Surely not to the main jail... But the county office was not that big. Apart from the main jail, there didn't seem to be any other place to detain someone.

"Yu Wan."

Just as she was lost in thought, she suddenly heard Pei Ta's voice.

Yu Wan composed herself and looked at Pei Ta, greeting him with a curtsy.

"Lord Pei."

"What about His Highness the Crown Prince and Seventh Highness?" Pei Ta had a thin layer of sweat on his forehead, looking as if he had rushed over from somewhere.

Yu Wan said, "Seventh Highness spoke out of turn and offended His Highness the Crown Prince. His Highness ordered his guards to take them all away, master and servants. This servant doesn't know where they were taken. His Highness the Crown Prince also left in anger."

Pei Ta looked at Yu Wan with some surprise upon hearing this.

"After seeing His Highness the Crown Prince settled, I went to the post station. Wasn't Lord Zhao in the county office?"

No wonder Pei Ta hadn't appeared despite the big commotion; he had gone to the post station.

That's right, where was Zhao Xuanyou?

Logically, he should have been in the county office. The county office wasn't even half the size of the Marquis's mansion. With such a loud commotion, Zhao Xuanyou couldn't have missed it.

Where had he gone?

Recalling the previous conversation Zhao Xuanyou had with Yuan Xi and Yuan Qing, Yu Wan looked at Pei Ta. "This servant has been with Seventh Highness the whole time, playing chess. I haven't seen our Young Master."

Pei Ta was no fool. If Yu Wan said Zhao Xuanyou was in the county office, he wouldn't believe it. So, she could only plead ignorance.

"It must have been difficult for you, being the only one present during the dispute between the two Highnesses."

Yu Wan gave a bitter smile, recalling the earlier scene, feeling like crying.

"You should go back to your room and rest. I'll go check on His Highness the Crown Prince."

"The Crown Prince was in a terrible mood earlier. He even said he would order the guards to shoot Seventh Highness. Lord Pei, please be careful with your words."

"It got that bad?"

Pei Ta had already known about Concubine Hui, so Yu Wan told him the truth. "Today, Seventh Highness was a bit impulsive and brought up the matter of Concubine Hui."

"I understand. Thank you." Pei Ta gave Yu Wan a slight nod and turned to leave in a hurry.

Yu Wan returned to the small courtyard alone. Zhao Xuanyou was indeed not there, and neither were Yuan Xi and Yuan Qing.

Had he left the residence on business?

Yu Wan let out a soft sigh in her heart.

Today, the Crown Prince had just arrived in Heishui and caused such a big commotion. Tomorrow, they were supposed to set off together to return to the capital. Who knew how many more problems would arise along the way.

And she still didn't know where Zhao Xuanyou had gone.

Yu Wan sat restlessly in the room, trying to practice calligraphy but unable to concentrate. After about an hour, she finally heard the sound of someone pushing open the courtyard gate.

She quickly pushed the door open and went out, seeing Zhao Xuanyou standing upright in the courtyard. The suppressed emotions she had been holding back suddenly surged up.

Her clear, almond-shaped eyes quickly filled with tears, and the corners of her eyes and eyebrows were full of grievance.

Zhao Xuanyou had just returned to the county office when he heard about today's farce. Seeing Yu Wan standing under the corridor with a grievous look, the corners of his lips twitched, and he couldn't help but smile. "I was only gone for a little while. Are you so aggrieved that you can't bear to be without me for even a moment?"

chapters.title: Starving
chapters.content:
"Of course I cannot leave you, my lord." Yu Yuan pouted coyly, then sighed with lingering fear, "Without you, I nearly lost my life."

Zhao Xuanyou took a few steps to the corridor, pulled Yu Yuan’s hand, and led her into the room. Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing tactfully retreated to the courtyard.

After closing the door, Zhao Xuanyou pulled Yu Yuan to sit on the edge of the couch and asked calmly, "Did they hurt you?"

Yu Yuan leaned against his shoulder and sighed deeply. "No, I wasn’t hurt, and no one else was either. But, His Highness the Crown Prince ordered the guards to arrest the Seventh Prince. Did you know about this, my lord?"

"I heard." Zhao Xuanyou’s tone was very calm. Compared to the conflict between the Crown Prince and Zhao Qi, he was more concerned about the delicate beauty beside him. He let her lie in his arms and took the opportunity to lightly inhale the fragrance from her hair. "They said it was because the Crown Prince harassed you, and that’s why the Seventh Prince quarreled with him?"

"More or less."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyebrows twitched slightly, and his expression stiffened. "Did he really harass you?"

"Not today. It’s not so much because of me that they argued. It’s more that it stirred up the Seventh Prince’s memories of Concubine Hui, which is why he lost control in a rage."

Yu Yuan recalled what had happened that day and still felt a lingering fear.

A crown prince and a prince; both were of noble blood. She was caught in the middle. If she accidentally offended someone, even several lives wouldn’t be enough to atone.

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in acknowledgment but said no more.

Seeing his thoughtful expression, Yu Yuan continued, "There’s something I don’t understand."

"What don’t you understand?"

"The Seventh Prince seems unrestrained and arrogant in speech, but after knowing him for so many days, I feel he’s actually quite sensible. His loss of control today was indeed too surprising."

Normally, when Zhao Qi and the Crown Prince were at odds, they would at most exchange veiled sarcasm, maintaining a facade of respect for the heir apparent. They had never openly cursed at each other.

Today’s impulsiveness was truly unlike Zhao Qi’s usual style.

Zhao Xuanyou said, "You needn’t feel guilty. He deliberately provoked the Crown Prince to force his hand."

"Why?" Yu Yuan asked in confusion. "I know His Majesty dotes on the Seventh Prince, but he did speak disrespectfully to the Crown Prince. Even if His Majesty finds out about today’s events, he can’t blame the Crown Prince, can he?"

"He can’t blame him, but the Crown Prince also can’t truly punish the Seventh Prince. At most, he’ll make things difficult for him on the way back to the capital."

"Then the Seventh Prince just wanted to vent his anger?"

Zhao Xuanyou held Yu Yuan and said casually, "This time in Heishui, he found clues related to the Zhen Guo Duke’s estate. Before he could gather evidence, both witnesses and physical evidence were taken away by the Crown Prince. He feels useless, unable to avenge Concubine Hui. He intentionally insulted the Crown Prince to vent his emotions and to punish himself."

Punish himself?

Because he couldn’t avenge her, he let the Crown Prince lock him up to punish himself?

Yu Yuan didn’t quite understand this emotion, but hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this, the previous grievances surged back into her heart.

He was sharp-eared and quick-eyed, and eloquent. If he had been there today, would she have been so nervous?

"My lord, where did you go today? Such a big incident happened, yet you only returned so late."

When the Crown Prince arrived at the county office, Zhao Xuanyou had also received a secret report from his subordinates, saying that a warehouse suspected of storing weapons had been discovered in a village outside the city.

He immediately took Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing to investigate.

Although the warehouse was empty, Zhao Xuanyou still found some clues.

Moreover, after carefully questioning the local villagers, he learned that the warehouse had been rented by a wealthy merchant from Jiangnan. Previously, he had hired villagers to move heavy boxes, which, based on the timeline, was about half a month before Pei Ta and his party arrived in Heishui County.

The Zhen Guo Duke wasn’t stupid. After the Heishui commoners rebelled, he immediately moved the evidence away.

If it weren’t for the fact that the dog magistrate had hidden another batch in the county office, which was coincidentally discovered by the people who stormed the office, even Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t have noticed anything amiss.

No wonder the Crown Prince hadn’t objected when the Emperor sent them there.

The Zhen Guo Duke thought he had handled everything cleanly, with no problems.

But Zhao Qi and Pei Ta had stayed in Heishui County for over a month without leaving, which the Zhen Guo Duke found unusual. So he invited the Crown Prince to Heishui County to clean up the mess and cover the loopholes in the records.

Fortunately, Zhao Xuanyou had discovered the illegal casting of weapons and reported it to the Emperor in advance.

The Empress and the Crown Prince thought they had successfully closed the case without anyone discovering their secrets. Little did they know, in the Emperor’s eyes, they were already traitors.

In any case, seeing the Crown Prince appear in Heishui County today was, for Zhao Xuanyou, a huge piece of good news.

Yu Yuan hadn’t heard Zhao Xuanyou speak for a long time. She tilted her head to look at him and caught his thoughtful expression, knowing he definitely wouldn’t tell her where he had been.

After a moment’s thought, Yu Yuan said, "Earlier, after His Highness the Crown Prince arrested the Seventh Prince, Lord Pei rushed to the county office from the posthouse. He asked about your whereabouts, my lord."

"Oh." Zhao Xuanyou didn’t have any special reaction. "How did you respond?"

The Crown Prince had ordered them to return to the capital with him tomorrow. No matter how much Pei Ta suspected that he was hiding something, he couldn’t investigate further.

Moreover, Zhao Xuanyou had already secretly reported this matter to the Emperor. The Crown Prince had also fallen into the trap, so he didn’t care about anything else.

"I told the truth. I had been serving the Seventh Prince and didn’t know where you were, my lord."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded slightly. "It’s fine."

Pei Ta was smarter than others, but he was just a fourth-rank official. They were equals, so Zhao Xuanyou didn’t need to explain his whereabouts to him.

"Go see what there is to eat in the kitchen. I’m hungry."

"Are you not worried about the Seventh Prince, my lord?" Yu Yuan asked curiously.

Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes slightly and looked down at her, his cheek brushing against Yu Yuan’s ear. "Are you worried?"

Yu Yuan said, "It’s not that I’m worried. It’s just that His Highness the Crown Prince said we would leave Heishui County early tomorrow morning. Now that he has the Seventh Prince locked up, will he release him tomorrow morning?"

"If he’s arrested, he won’t be released easily."

"According to Lord Pei, the Seventh Prince was thrown into the dungeon. Does that mean he will be taken back to the capital in a prisoner’s cart tomorrow?"

Zhao Xuanyou thought about Zhao Qi’s usual demeanor as a troublemaker. Locking him in a prisoner’s cart wasn’t a bad idea, but it was unlikely.

"Using a prisoner’s cart to transport a prince would be too ostentatious. The Crown Prince won’t do that."

Zhao Zhan hadn’t ascended the throne yet. He still had to maintain the image of a filial and benevolent crown prince in front of the world.

Even if he was publicly insulted by his own brother, he couldn’t openly transport this troublesome brother in a prisoner’s cart, exposing the royal family’s disgrace.

"I see." Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was patiently explaining royal matters to her, Yu Yuan turned her head and said, "After saying so much, my lord must be starving."

Zhao Xuanyou covered Yu Yuan’s lips with his, feeling the heat on her cheeks. Unable to resist, he gently bit her ear and whispered, "I am indeed starving."

Before Yu Yuan could respond, he pulled her down onto the couch and raised his hand to drop the brocade canopy.

---

chapters.title: Seeing the World
chapters.content:
As Zhao Xuanyou had predicted, although the Crown Prince had locked Zhao Qi in the county jail for a day, he didn’t make him sit in a prisoner’s cart. Instead, he ordered that his hands and feet be bound with iron chains, but he still rode in a spacious carriage.

The only ones who suffered were Yin Ping and Mu Di, who were locked in the prisoner’s cart along with the other convicts involved in the Heishui County uprising.

Yu Yuan had originally planned to ride a horse, but considering she was the only woman in the group, it would be somewhat inconvenient. Additionally, since Zhao Qi was bound, someone needed to take care of him, so she decided to ride in the carriage with him.

"Your Highness, this servant has prepared two food boxes, all fresh pastries bought from the market stalls early this morning. They’re still warm. Your Highness, see if there’s anything you’d like to eat."

Yu Yuan’s eyes were gently lowered, and as she spoke, she opened the food boxes one by one and placed them on the low table.

Zhao Qi glanced at the dazzling array of food boxes, all of which were his favorites.

"I can’t eat."

Having known Zhao Qi for a while, Yu Yuan was already used to his temper. She closed the food boxes again and smiled. "Then Your Highness can tell this servant when you’re hungry."

"I’m just a prisoner."

"Even prisoners need to eat and drink, don’t they?"

Yu Yuan’s words left Zhao Qi unable to refute. "Then take care of Yin Ping and Mu Di for me."

So he was worried about his subordinates. Yu Yuan said, "Your Highness, rest assured. When this servant went out earlier, I already sent them some things."

"Really?"

Yu Yuan nodded. "But not much, just a steamer of buns and a pot of water."

"They didn’t give you trouble?"

Yu Yuan smiled slyly. "The Young Master was there too."

The guards had originally refused to let her send food, but because Zhao Xuanyou had given the order, they relented.

Zhao Qi lowered his head and remained silent for a long while before muttering, "I want to eat buns too."

"There are some." Yu Yuan picked up a bun with her chopsticks. Since Zhao Qi’s hands were bound, she had to feed him.

Before long, someone outside shouted, "The Crown Prince is departing!" The large procession set off to return to the capital.

On the way back to the capital, Zhao Qi was kept in the carriage the entire time and didn’t meet the Crown Prince at all. Fortunately, no further incidents occurred along the way.

After traveling for more than twenty days, the Crown Prince’s chariot finally arrived in the capital.

The Emperor and Empress were still at the traveling palace, so the Crown Prince’s return to the capital after his inspection tour was naturally the top news in the city. The city gates had long been cleared by the soldiers, and Prince Ping, along with the two prime ministers who had been left in charge of the capital, led a grand assembly of officials to kneel in welcome at the city gates. The scene was no less impressive than when the Emperor and Empress had left the capital.

The last time Yu Yuan had come to the city gates, she had been in the role of a servant from the Marquis’s mansion. She had been too far away to see the situation at the main gate clearly.

This time, she was riding with Zhao Qi, and their carriage followed closely behind the Crown Prince’s chariot. She lifted a corner of the carriage curtain and curiously looked outside.

She saw civil and military officials dressed in the attire of their respective ranks, lined up on both sides of the road.

Those usually arrogant or indifferent old officials now all bowed their heads, looking extremely respectful.

Looking down at them from her high vantage point, Yu Yuan suddenly felt a strange sensation in her heart.

It was no wonder the Crown Prince, Yi’an, and Zhao Qi had developed such temperaments.

If she had been born to be looked up to by others, perhaps she would be even more difficult to get along with than they were.

"What’s so interesting to look at?" Zhao Qi saw Yu Yuan staring fixedly outside and frowned in puzzlement.

"This servant hasn’t seen much of the world." Yu Yuan answered truthfully.

Zhao Qi glanced at her and followed her gaze outside.

"Look, the one at the very front is my good Third Brother, Prince Ping."

Good Third Brother?

That didn’t sound like a compliment.

Yu Yuan hadn’t expected Zhao Qi to introduce the people outside to her. She smiled lightly. "Prince Ping and the Young Master have quite a good relationship. He’s a truly good brother, isn’t he?"

It wasn’t that good, nor was it that bad.

Zhao Qi didn’t want to discuss these matters. He continued, "Next to Prince Ping is the father of Madame Pei."

"Prime Minister Sun?" Upon hearing Zhao Qi’s words, Yu Yuan took a closer look and indeed saw a resemblance in the features to Sun Qianran.

"A cunning old fox. My grandfather told me to be extremely wary of him."

So that was why Zhao Qi had never shown Sun Qianran a good face.

However, Sun Qianran didn’t seem to have any cunning about her. After all, she was just a woman from the inner quarters. Prime Minister Sun probably wouldn’t teach her political schemes.

Soon, the carriage passed through the city gates and entered the capital, continuing all the way to the main gate of the imperial palace before stopping.

Yu Yuan waited with Zhao Qi in the carriage for a while before a eunuch finally arrived.

She didn’t recognize him, but Zhao Qi knew he was from the Eastern Palace.

"Is Zhao Zhan planning to lock me up somewhere else?"

The eunuch respectfully replied, "His Highness the Crown Prince, out of brotherly affection, has ordered this servant to remove the Seventh Prince’s bonds. However, His Highness the Crown Prince also said that since the Seventh Prince has not yet reflected on his mistakes, upon returning to the Western Garden, he should not go out and should reflect on his errors behind closed doors."

With the Emperor and Empress not in the capital, everything was naturally under the Crown Prince’s command.

Zhao Qi rolled his eyes.

Yu Yuan, however, said, "Please trouble the honorable eunuch to remove the Seventh Prince’s bonds."

The eunuch, seeing that Yu Yuan was reasonable, smiled and nodded. He came over and removed the iron chains from Zhao Qi’s hands and feet.

After being bound for over twenty days, even though Zhao Qi had been in the carriage the whole time and hadn’t suffered much, his wrists and ankles were bruised black and blue.

"Your Highness, once you return to the palace, you should summon an imperial physician immediately." Yu Yuan said, glancing at the eunuch. "His Highness the Crown Prince only ordered house arrest, not that medical treatment was forbidden, right?"

Zhao Qi, however, smiled and said, "No need for treatment. I think His Majesty will return to the capital soon. It’s better to let him see this."

The eunuch coughed dryly twice.

The Crown Prince already knew that the Emperor and Empress would be returning to the capital soon, which was why he had ordered Zhao Qi’s chains removed, to prevent the Emperor from seeing his injuries.

Hearing Zhao Qi see through the Crown Prince’s intentions, the eunuch forced a smile. "Your Highness’s noble body must not be neglected. This servant will go to the Imperial Physician’s Office to summon a physician immediately."

Yu Yuan also softly advised, "This honorable eunuch is right. Your Highness is of noble birth. There’s no need to endanger your health out of spite. If your hands and feet are left untreated for too long, what if it affects your future martial arts training?"

Since it was Yu Yuan speaking, Zhao Qi was naturally willing to listen, and her words made sense.

"I understand."

The eunuch said happily, "This servant will help Your Highness out of the carriage. A sedan chair has already been prepared, and we will send Your Highness back to the Western Garden to rest immediately."

"Isn’t this supposed to be a reflection on my mistakes?"

"Both for cultivating the body and the mind."

This eunuch really knew how to speak. No wonder he could serve in the Eastern Palace.

Yu Yuan silently admired his words. After getting out of the carriage, she realized she was standing in front of the main gate of the imperial palace.

The area in front of the palace gate was spacious, and the gate tower was majestic and grand, far surpassing any traveling palace.

Yu Yuan was so dazzled that she forgot herself. She heard someone beside her laugh and say, "Seeing more of the world?"

She hastily withdrew her gaze and saw that it was Zhao Qi teasing her. She smiled and said, "Yes, thanks to Your Highness’s good fortune, this servant has been able to see so much of the world."

Zhao Qi’s expression became slightly strange upon hearing this, and he averted his gaze.

Yu Yuan didn’t know what she had said wrong. Seeing the eunuch urging them to enter the palace, she stepped aside.

After Zhao Qi’s sedan chair entered the palace, Yu Yuan stood there at a loss, looking around, not knowing where she should go.

chapters.title: The Trump Card
chapters.content:
"Miss Yu Wan."

Lost in thought, she was suddenly approached by a eunuch.

"Your Grace," Yu Wan quickly responded.

"Lord Zhao has already prepared a carriage. This servant will take you there now."

The Crown Prince had not summoned Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta into the palace, as they were not officials of the Eastern Palace and thus were not permitted to approach the palace gates.

The eunuch led Yu Wan around to the other side of the palace city, where she finally saw the carriage of the Marquis's residence, driven by Yuan Qing.

"Thank you for your trouble, Your Grace."

"You need not be polite, Miss."

Yu Wan hurried to the carriage, lifted the curtain, and boarded. Just as she was about to speak to Zhao Xuanyou, she saw Pei Ta inside as well.

"Young Master, Lord Pei."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded slightly, gesturing for Yu Wan to sit beside him.

"Yuan Qing, take us to the Pei residence first."

"Yes."

So, they were to take Pei Ta home first. It was unexpected; Zhao Xuanyou had such a kind heart.

"It is too much for Young Master to take me home. I am truly unworthy."

"It is on the way. Lord Pei is a man of great learning and talent. To have a moment to converse with you is my honor."

Listening to their polite exchange, Yu Wan silently opened the carriage curtain and looked out at the street.

Having stayed in Heishui County for over a month, she wondered how her mother's illness was faring. Previously, her mother had opened her eyes. Could she have woken up by now?

The Taoran Inn was filled with Zhao Xuanyou's subordinates. If her mother had woken up, they would have sent word. Perhaps she still hadn't.

"This trip to Heishui County has been quite eventful. I didn't expect His Highness the Crown Prince to arrive suddenly."

"Lord Pei truly didn't expect it?"

After finding several chests bearing the emblem of the Prince of Zhen Guo's residence, it should have been clear that the Prince of Zhen Guo's residence, and even the Empress and the Crown Prince, were connected to Heishui County.

Zhao Xuanyou didn't believe Pei Ta hadn't considered this.

"It was just a few chests. I truly didn't expect His Highness to come in person. Could it be that Young Master anticipated this?"

Seeing Pei Ta's probing intent, Zhao Xuanyou smiled slightly. "Indeed."

Pei Ta hadn't expected Zhao Xuanyou to admit it and couldn't help but ask, "Young Master seems so certain. It appears you've gained a lot in Heishui County."

Zhao Xuanyou didn't deny it but merely said softly, "Rest assured, my gains have nothing to do with Lord Pei. Chancellor Sun has always preferred to stay out of trouble. I believe Lord Pei doesn't want to get involved in palace affairs."

Pei Ta took a deep breath.

With his family vengeance not yet avenged, he naturally wouldn't blindly make enemies.

But as a court official, he didn't want the cases he handled to be unclear, with right and wrong reversed.

"What is the truth? I beg Young Master to enlighten me."

"The Emperor has entrusted this case to His Highness the Crown Prince. Does the truth still matter?"

Zhao Xuanyou's voice was light, but Pei Ta's eyes were filled with deep thought.

Mentioning the Emperor. Could it be that the Emperor already knew the inside story?

But why would the Emperor not trust the Crown Prince and instead trust Zhao Xuanyou?

"I have some good news related to Lord Pei. Would you like to hear it?"

Pei Ta raised his eyebrows and, after a moment of eye contact with Zhao Xuanyou, his heart stirred. "Does Young Master refer to Qingsha Town?"

Zhao Xuanyou smiled without answering.

Regarding family vengeance, Pei Ta solemnly said, "If there is anything I can do, Young Master, just give the order."

"My subordinates have already found relevant witnesses and evidence. When they return to the capital in a few days, I will trouble Lord Pei's friend in the Censorate to present a memorial to the court."

Zhao Xuanyou had already confronted the Crown Prince, so the matter of the Prince of Xingguo's residence was no longer as urgent.

Initially, he had been unwilling to cooperate with Pei Ta because they were not acquainted, and he didn't know Pei Ta's depth or intentions, fearing ill will or deception.

After two months of interaction, Zhao Xuanyou realized that Pei Ta's desire for revenge was genuine, his character was decent, his abilities were competent, and he was willing to join forces.

By having Pei Ta contribute more to this matter, he could conserve his strength to deal with the Crown Prince.

"Very well, I will handle the memorial." Pei Ta, hearing that Zhao Xuanyou had already gathered witnesses and evidence, felt a surge of excitement at the thought of finally bringing down his enemy.

Yu Wan, listening from the side, felt a tremor in her heart.

Had Zhao Xuanyou already gathered enough evidence against the Prince of Xingguo's residence?

If the Prince of Xingguo's residence fell, Cui Yichu would lose his protection and no longer pose a threat to her and her mother.

Then, Yu Wan could truly fulfill the revenge of her past life.

Zhao Xuanyou noticed Yu Wan's slight change in expression and knew she harbored deep hatred for Cui Yichu. He gently placed his hand over hers.

Yu Wan paused for a moment, then smiled at him.

"Then it's settled. When my subordinates are about to reach the capital, I will invite Lord Pei for another discussion."

As they spoke, the carriage arrived at the Pei residence. Pei Ta once again thanked Zhao Xuanyou and then turned to Yu Wan. "Miss Yu Wan, take care."

"Lord Pei, take care." Yu Wan curtsied to him and watched as he alighted from the carriage, sitting down somewhat absentmindedly.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at the worry that lingered on her face and pulled her into his embrace.

"Previously, I spared them out of consideration for certain people. Now, I have no more reservations and will not be lenient with them again."

These words were as much for himself as they were for Yu Wan.

Initially, he had accepted the conditions of the Prince of Xingguo's residence and agreed to cover up Cui Yichu's scandals, pretending that the divorce was amicable. It wasn't because he was magnanimous, but because her adulterous lover was the Crown Prince of the Eastern Palace.

Cui Yichu frequently entered the palace. If people found out about her pre-marital loss of chastity, rumors would inevitably involve the palace.
