"That is Lord Pei Ta; he is a Zhuangyuan (top scholar)."

"How does sister know Lord Pei?" Yingxue asked curiously.

"Last time at the Lichuan Imperial Palace, Lord Pei and Lady Pei stayed in the same courtyard as the young master. We saw them every day, so we got to know each other."

Yingxue stared deeply at Pei Ta's retreating figure until he turned the corner before looking away.

"Lord Pei is as handsome as Pan An; Lady Pei must be a beauty of celestial charm as well."

Yu Wan thought for a moment and said softly, "Lady Pei is a bit frail and her complexion isn't very good. But she is the smartest woman I've ever met; graceful, knowledgeable, and well-mannered. She and Lord Pei are very much in love."

"They truly are a match made in heaven."

Seeing Yingxue's emotional expression, Yu Wan couldn't help but tease, "What? Do you want to get married?"

"Of course not!" Yingxue blushed and retorted, "You're the one! The master dotes on you so much; I think it won't be long before you become a concubine in the mansion."

Really?

Zhao Xuanyou hadn't even married a successor wife yet. Even if he did, he would have to marry Feng Jiyou first.

She was Zhao Xuanyou's cousin; the mansion would certainly give her face and not let her share a title with a servant like herself.

Why was she thinking so much? Anyway, she wouldn't be staying much longer.

"Don't say that; others will laugh at me."

"Laugh at what?" Yingxue saw Yu Wan's indifferent expression and asked in confusion, "Everyone in the mansion knows the master dotes on you the most. Becoming a concubine is only a matter of time."

"He hasn't said anything, so it's not settled yet. Don't mention it again."

Yingxue frowned and hesitated for a moment before saying, "Understood."

---

"Master, Lord Pei has arrived."

Yuan Qing led Pei Ta to the pavilion. Since there were sheer curtains on all four sides and a small heater in the corner, sitting in the pavilion did not feel cold.

"Lord Pei, please."

"Young Master."

Pei Ta entered the pavilion, and Yuan Qing lowered the sheer curtains and exited.

On the table were six dishes of snacks. After Pei Ta took his seat, Zhao Xuanyou raised his hand and personally poured a cup of wine for Pei Ta.

"Thank you for coming at this late hour, Lord Pei. I am truly grateful."

Pei Ta looked around and found that although the residence appeared small, it was actually luxurious. Even the small pavilion's ceiling was painted with colorful designs, depicting the story of Jing Wei filling the sea.

"I didn't expect the young master to have such a secluded place in the bustling capital. Living here with Yu Wan must be quite pleasant."

Hearing Pei Ta mention Yu Wan, Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows slightly furrowed.

How did he know Yu Wan was here?

Yuan Qing wouldn't gossip, so it must be that when he came in just now, he had encountered Yu Wan.

No wonder it had taken so long for him to be announced; Pei Ta must have stopped to talk to Yu Wan.

What did they have to talk about?

Zhao Xuanyou's expression remained calm, but his tone became more formal.

"It's getting late; let's talk business."

Pei Ta nodded and cupped his hands to Zhao Xuanyou: "This time, the young master sent someone to collect evidence in Qingsha Town. I am truly grateful. For the rest, there's no need for the young master to worry; leave everything to me."

"In that case, I won't stand on ceremony."

Pei Ta nodded and took a sip of wine.

The wine was chrysanthemum wine brewed by Lady Ye herself, with a strong chrysanthemum fragrance and a lingering aftertaste.

After putting down the wine cup, Pei Ta laid out his plan in full.

"The emperor and empress will arrive in the capital in ten days. At the next grand court session, I will have my friend, the censor, come forward to impeach the Xingguo Duke and Tao Cheng for embezzling tribute pearls and committing corruption."

Zhao Xuanyou narrowed his eyes and looked at Pei Ta: "Tao Cheng is just a fourth-rank official, but the Xingguo Duke is a first-rank duke. With only one censor coming forward, isn't that a bit insufficient?"

"The censor is responsible for supervision and can impeach any official. Even if it's a first-rank duke, there is no difference."

"I just think that since you and I cannot come forward, during the grand court session, besides your censor friend, it would be best if someone else could support the accusation."

On the battlefield, Zhao Xuanyou always struck the vital point in one move when killing the enemy, never giving the opponent a chance to breathe.

Although he had just returned to the capital, he understood that the treacherous intrigues among the civil officials were even more dangerous than the battlefield.

If they couldn't persuade the emperor at the grand court session and take down the Xingguo Duke and Tao Cheng in one fell swoop, they would give the opponent a chance to breathe.

"Rest assured, young master. I have already seen the list of evidence you sent. With such matters, His Majesty will certainly not show leniency."

"Since Lord Pei is confident, I won't say more. Currently, the witnesses and evidence are hidden in the outskirts of the capital, ready for Lord Pei's disposal at any time." Seeing his confidence, Zhao Xuanyou also stopped talking and glanced at him before slowly adding, "My collaboration with Lord Pei is something your wife is fully aware of. Lord Pei must be cautious."

Pei Ta heard the implication in Zhao Xuanyou's words. Across the stone table, their eyes met.

"Are you worried that my father-in-law will interfere in this matter?"

Zhao Xuanyou let out a light laugh: "Years ago, Minister Sun helped the Xingguo Duke and Tao Cheng cover up their crimes. This is something only you know. Although this case does not involve old matters, you and I do not know if there are more dealings between Minister Sun and the Xingguo Duke."

After experiencing the matter with Cui Yichu, Zhao Xuanyou was already clear that the Xingguo Duke was not a good person.

He also knew that the Xingguo Duke's mansion had embezzled tribute pearls for many years, amassing a huge fortune.

A noble duke already lived a life of luxury; with so much money, it was impossible that he just kept it in the storeroom to admire. He must have other uses for it.

Minister Sun had helped him cover up matters before; there could be more, and their interests might be deeply entangled.

"He would interfere if he knew."

"But he won't know." After understanding Zhao Xuanyou's meaning, Pei Ta's face showed a trace of thin anger, and he said firmly, "Since I started planning my revenge, my wife has been assisting me from the side. How could she leak this to her father? You worry too much, young master."

chapters.title: Gambling with the Heart
chapters.content:
Seeing Pei Ta speak so solemnly, Zhao Xuanyou neither agreed nor disagreed, lifting his wine cup to take a light sip.

"The heir need not worry. My wife is frail in health, so naturally, such matters won’t be brought up to trouble her mind."

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent, his gaze gradually turning cold and sharp.

Seeing his displeasure with the answer, Pei Ta deepened his voice: "This matter may be of little consequence to the heir, but to me, it is a blood feud that cannot be allowed to fail."

Though his voice was not loud, his tone carried extreme gravity.

"Tao Cheng was transferred from his previous position several years ago. The human evidence and material evidence collected in Qingsha Town are all laid out before Director Pei," Zhao Xuanyou paused slightly, then emphasized, "If we cannot succeed in one stroke, there truly will not be a next time."

Tao Cheng was insatiably greedy and not particularly capable, so he had exposed many flaws. The evidence collected was enough to convict him.

But Zhao Xuanyou was not after Tao Cheng; he was after Duke Xingguo, Cui Lingyuan.

Unlike Tao Cheng, Cui Lingyuan had been operating in the capital for many years, enjoying high prestige. Secretly, he was also connected to powerful ministers like Premier Sun. If he were to catch wind of this in advance, the old fox would surely find a way to escape.

"I understand the heir’s concerns. Before submitting the memorial to the Imperial Censor, I will not leak a single word to anyone."

At this point, further words were unnecessary.

Since Zhao Xuanyou had agreed to cooperate with Pei Ta, he naturally had to provide the corresponding trust.

"Tomorrow, if there is time, Yuan Qing can take Director Pei to the outskirts of the capital to receive the evidence. After that, I will no longer interfere."

"Good."

After exchanging toasts, the two men had no more words for each other.

Once Pei Ta left, Zhao Xuanyou strolled back to the main courtyard.

By this time, Yu Ying had finished her toiletries and was sitting by the couch, sorting through Zhao Xuanyou’s clothes. She shook his pouch, and a sachet fell out; it was the one she had previously asked Yuan Qing to deliver to the Lichuan Imperial Palace.

Seeing her staring blankly, Zhao Xuanyou teased, "Disgusted by your own ugly handiwork?"

Hearing his voice, Yu Ying quickly collected her thoughts and looked up at him with a smile. "This sachet is embroidered so poorly. I thought you had already thrown it away."

Indeed, it was rather ugly. If he were to flaunt such an unsightly thing in public, he would become a laughingstock.

But Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t bear to throw it away, so he had kept it in another pouch.

Yu Ying held the poorly stitched mandarin duck sachet and took it aside. "Let’s not use this one. Coincidentally, Yingxue is also at the separate courtyard. I’ll ask her to guide me in making a new one."

"Do as you please," Zhao Xuanyou said, but he picked up the ugly sachet and put it back into his pouch. "The fabric is precious; there’s no need to throw it away."

With him saying so, Yu Ying naturally did not insist.

"Did you meet Pei Ta today?" Zhao Xuanyou sat down by the couch and asked casually.

Yu Ying, while helping him change clothes, lightly responded with an "mm."

"What could you two have talked about?"

Pei Ta had an exceptionally handsome appearance, a rare beauty. It was said that before his marriage, many noble ladies had been infatuated with him, and he had been the talk of the capital.

That time at the Heishui County Yamen, Zhao Xuanyou had seen him standing in the kitchen talking to Yu Ying. Yu Ying had looked up at Pei Ta, her eyes filled with admiration.

Recalling that scene, Zhao Xuanyou always felt uncomfortable.

It wasn’t quite rage born of jealousy, but his chest felt stuffed with cotton, making it hard to breathe.

"We just exchanged greetings. We didn’t talk about much."

Yu Ying answered casually, which only made Zhao Xuanyou feel more stifled.

This residence was small. It shouldn’t have taken Yuan Qing and Pei Ta so long to walk from the gate to the pavilion.

How could it have been just a greeting?

But Yu Ying’s tone was indifferent, clearly not taking his words to heart at all.

If he were to dig deeper, it would make him seem petty.

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was sitting on the couch with no intention of bathing, Yu Ying called for Yingxue to bring hot water and attend to him.

---

That night, Pei Ta walked back to his residence under the moonlight.

The corridors on both sides were already lit with lanterns. As he entered the study, he saw Xiang Xu standing under the veranda.

"Has the madam come?"

"Yes," Xiang Xu replied respectfully.

Pei Ta nodded and went straight into the room.

The study was lit with candles. Sun Qianran was sitting at the desk, pen in hand.

"Madam," Pei Ta called gently. "It’s already this late. Why haven’t you rested yet?"

"These past few days, my husband has been resting in the study. I assume official duties are busy. Today, the kitchen prepared a pot of Tianma pigeon soup. I specially had a portion saved for you to nourish your body."

Though it was still autumn, Sun Qianran had already changed into winter clothes and was holding a hand warmer.

Pei Ta stepped forward and took her hand. "The night is cold. You need not come yourself. You could have had Xiang Xu send a message, and I would have come to you."

"How come the Ministry of Ceremonies is suddenly so busy when the Emperor and Empress have not yet returned to the capital?"

Sun Qianran came from the Premier’s family. Although she was a woman, she was more intelligent than her several brothers. From a young age, she had been personally tutored by Premier Sun, accustomed to the intrigues of the court and familiar with the responsibilities of each ministry and department.

Hearing her words, Pei Ta suddenly recalled what Zhao Xuanyou had said at the separate courtyard that day.

Zhao Xuanyou had repeatedly told him to keep it from his father-in-law, yet he had also mentioned his wife.

Clearly, he did not trust her.

So what about Pei Ta himself? Should he not trust his own pillow partner?

Was she asking this because she had noticed something amiss and was testing him?

No, probably not. She was just concerned about him because he had been leaving early and returning late.

If she really was testing him...

As his thoughts raced, Pei Ta took a deep breath and made up his mind.

"Husband?" Not receiving an answer from Pei Ta, Sun Qianran softly called out.

Pei Ta picked up the bowl of soup on the table and took a few sips. After setting down the spoon, he said, "It’s not the Ministry of Ceremonies’ business."

"Then what is it?" Sun Qianran asked curiously.

Pei Ta gave a faint smile. "The matter I’ve been investigating for a long time will soon come to a conclusion."

"Seeking vengeance for your father?" Sun Qianran opened her mouth in surprise, stunned for a moment before joyfully asking, "Husband, have you gathered all the evidence?"

"Mm. There is both human and material evidence. Not only Tao Cheng, but Duke Xingguo won’t be able to escape either."

"It’s been years of hard work for you to investigate. Finally, your efforts have paid off."

Pei Ta reached out and gently touched Sun Qianran’s hair. "It’s all thanks to Madam’s constant support that we’ve achieved this."

"Did Zhao Xuanyou help this time for things to go so smoothly?"

Pei Ta neither confirmed nor denied.

"In a few days, the Emperor will return to the capital, and the truth will come to light. It’s late. Let me escort you back to the room."

"Alright."

---

Five days later, the Emperor and Empress returned to the capital.

Crown Prince Zhao Zun led the civil and military officials to welcome them at the city gate.

Pei Ta, dressed in his official robes, stood among the ranks of civil officials. Thinking about the grand court session to be held the next day, his heart was not at ease.

Since that night when he had mentioned the matter of revenge to Sun Qianran, the couple had not discussed it again.

That night, he could have kept silent, but he had spoken up.

He was gambling; gambling on her sincerity toward him.

He knew he was acting on impulse, but he still hoped to win this bet.

For now, everything seemed calm, but the calm was too perfect, making him uneasy.

The imperial carriage slowly entered the city gate.

Pei Ta lifted his gaze and, through the crowd of officials, saw Zhao Xuanyou.

The autumn wind howled, and on Zhao Xuanyou’s stern face, his eyes were as deep as an abyss.

---

chapters.title: Oath
chapters.content:
Something had gone wrong?

Pei Ta’s heart suddenly tightened.

He pushed through the crowd toward Zhao Xuanyou, but Zhao Xuanyou turned his face away and walked quickly forward.

"Prince Heir," Pei Ta called out.

Zhao Xuanyou acted as if he had not heard.

"Director Zhao."

Pei Ta caught up and stood in front of Zhao Xuanyou.

"Does Director Pei have some business?" Zhao Xuanyou’s expression was calm, as if nothing had happened between them, as if they had no acquaintance at all.

Pei Ta forcibly suppressed his unease, cupped his hands toward Zhao Xuanyou, and silently stepped back to keep a distance.

The Emperor had just returned to the capital, exhausted from travel, so the grand court session was to be held in two days.

But shortly after Pei Ta returned to the Ministry of Ceremonies, he learned from his friend, the Imperial Censor, the reason for Zhao Xuanyou’s anger.

It turned out that early that morning, Censor Zhang had transferred all the human and material evidence obtained from Pei Ta to the Court of Judicial Review, impeaching Tao Cheng for extorting the people and embezzling tribute pearls during his tenure as prefect.

Every piece of evidence was irrefutable. The Court of Judicial Review immediately set out to arrest the culprit.

But only Tao Cheng.

Censor Zhang had not impeached Duke Xingguo, Cui Lingyuan. All evidence related to the Duke Xingguo’s residence had disappeared.

Censor Zhang also said that this was done under duress from Premier Sun.

He had wanted to help Pei Ta, but he came from a humble background. After passing the imperial examination, he had toiled for four years in the regions before being retained in the capital. He simply did not dare to risk his life and family to oppose a powerful minister.

At this point, what more did Pei Ta not understand?

Premier Sun and Duke Xingguo must have received prior warning.

Who had leaked the information?

The answer was obvious, but Pei Ta still refused to admit that he had lost the gamble, lost utterly.

He spent the day in a daze at the Ministry of Ceremonies. Only when his colleagues urged him did he finally leave at the end of his shift.

He wandered aimlessly through the streets. The market was lit with lanterns, but none of them seemed to shine for him.

"Husband."

A carriage stopped beside him, and a familiar voice called out. He looked up and met a pair of concerned eyes.

Sun Qianran had always looked at him with the softest gaze, filled with affection.

But now, as her gaze fell on Pei Ta, it felt like a needle sharply pricking him.

"Get in the carriage first. Let me explain."

"Explain why you betrayed me?"

Sun Qianran’s eyes welled with tears. Just as she was about to speak, she began coughing violently.

Xiang Xu persuaded from the side, "Sir, please get in the carriage. Madam is frail and cannot stand the cold wind like this."

Pei Ta took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. Slowly, he said, "Fine. Let’s clarify things."

He jumped into the carriage and sat apart from Sun Qianran.

"Husband, I went to find my father not to betray you, but to help you."

"Help me?" Pei Ta asked coldly. "How?"

"Duke Xingguo is a first-rank duke. To bring him down, a single censor’s effort is far from enough. My father is the Premier, with disciples all over the court. If he can come forward to support you, the other officials will surely follow, and the matter will be resolved with half the effort."

Pei Ta gave a slight nod. "That does sound reasonable. But why did Premier Sun not only fail to lead his disciples to bring down Cui Lingyuan, but instead pressured Censor Zhang to destroy all evidence unfavorable to Cui Lingyuan?"

He referred to him as "Premier Sun" rather than "father-in-law," clearly no longer considering himself part of the Sun family.

Sun Qianran was highly intelligent and naturally perceived his change in attitude from his words. She only lowered her head and wiped her tears. "I only found out after seeing my father that he was deeply involved in that matter years ago and that Duke Xingguo had left a handle on him."

"What handle? How many tribute pearls did Premier Sun take from Duke Xingguo?"

"Husband..."

"Isn’t that the case?"

Sun Qianran tightly clenched her fingers, her lips pressed pale.

"My father has always valued his reputation the most. If Duke Xingguo falls, he will surely drag my father down with him... I knew he would intervene, so I argued with him forcefully. He agreed to bring Tao Cheng to justice." Seeing that Pei Ta remained silent, Sun Qianran softly added, "The one who framed your father back then was actually Tao Cheng. Duke Xingguo only helped Tao Cheng clear his name in the background. Now that Tao Cheng is doomed, your father’s spirit in heaven can finally be at peace."

"Admirable how you’ve thought of everything. You can preserve Premier Sun’s reputation and offer up Tao Cheng to quell my anger. Truly a perfect solution."

"Husband, Tao Cheng was indeed the main culprit back then."

The carriage swayed gently. With only a single lantern lit inside, the interior was dim.

Pei Ta said indifferently, "Do you know? That day when I met Zhao Xuanyou in secret, he said you couldn’t be trusted."

"He... why would he say that?"

Pei Ta curled his lips slightly. "At that time, when I heard him speculate about you like that, I was very angry and almost lost my temper with him. But he wouldn’t let it go, so in the end, I had to promise him that I would not reveal a single word to you."

"Then why did you tell me?" Sun Qianran’s voice trembled slightly.

"Because I believed your words. I believed that although your father plays political games, he is not a corrupt official. I believed that since you married me, we would be of one heart as husband and wife. I gambled that you would never betray me."

"I did not betray you!" Sun Qianran read something in Pei Ta’s eyes that she had never seen before. She rushed to his side, grabbed his sleeve, and tears streamed down her face. "Pei Ta, I have been sincere to you. I would never let anyone harm you, including my father!"

"Do you think I haven’t been harmed today?" Pei Ta’s usually clear eyes were now clouded with darkness, his ink-black pupils fixed on Sun Qianran, almost bloodshot. "I can accept failure, but I cannot accept you manipulating me like this."

Sun Qianran dared not meet his gaze, only tightly clutching his sleeve.

"I didn’t manipulate you. I just..."

"You just wanted to protect your father’s reputation and position, and have him sacrifice a pawn to hand Tao Cheng over to me for revenge."

"I truly didn’t know..."

Pei Ta took her hand and pried open her tightly clenched fingers. A grim smile appeared on his lips. "Madam, you are so intelligent. How could you not have known what kind of person your father is before today? Before we were married, did you already know about my family’s affairs?"

Sun Qianran’s lips trembled, her face pale as a sheet.

Of course she had known.

Back then, Pei Ta was a spirited and promising top scholar. When she first saw him, like many other noble ladies in the capital, she had been captivated by him.

But her status was not as noble as a princess’s, her appearance was not outstanding, and she was frail and often ill. Pei Ta would not have paid any attention to her.

Premier Sun had mentioned the matter of Tao Cheng and Pei Ta’s father, originally intending to dissuade her.

But when she learned that her father was Pei Ta’s "benefactor," she had made up her mind to use this "favor" to marry Pei Ta.

Pei Ta smiled bitterly.

"Hard for you, having to act by my side all this time, offering advice and patiently humoring me."

"Husband, my feelings for you are genuine. I swear it on my life."

"There’s no need." Pei Ta gently shook his head. "Save your oath for someone else, Miss Sun."

chapters.title: Drunken Sentiments
chapters.content:
Sun Qianran suddenly lifted her head, staring blankly at Pei Ta, her eyes filled with disbelief.

How could this be?

How had things come to this?

Clearly… clearly she had calculated everything perfectly.

The case involving her father-in-law had been handled meticulously by her father back then. Not a single flaw could be found in the records.

Yet, Pei Ta had spent years poring over the archives of the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Officials, the Ministry of Rites, and the Court of Judicial Review. He had even examined the local chronicles of Qingsha Town, and somehow, he had uncovered every detail of what had happened back then.

At first, that hadn’t been a problem.

After all, the witnesses and evidence had long been destroyed. Even if Pei Ta had uncovered the truth himself, there was no way to reopen the case.

But then, he had seen an opportunity in Zhao Xuanyou’s divorce and sought to collaborate with him.

Initially, Zhao Xuanyou had been unwilling to cooperate. So why had he agreed in the end?

In the end, she had underestimated Pei Ta’s determination for revenge, and she had also underestimated Zhao Xuanyou’s capabilities.

Even so, she had done her best to mediate between her father and Pei Ta, coming up with a solution that would satisfy both sides; handing over Tao Cheng to appease Pei Ta’s anger while ensuring the Duke of Xingguo emerged unscathed.

Who could have known that the trap Pei Ta had set wasn’t aimed at the Duke of Xingguo, but at her?

That night, he had deliberately leaked the information to her…

Sun Qianran closed her eyes tightly, tears sliding down her cheeks.

“My husband still cannot move past the tragedy of his parents’ deaths. They were also my father’s parents. I cannot stand by and watch him fall into a trap.”

“As a child, being filial to one’s parents is not wrong.”

As she looked into Pei Ta’s dim gaze, all the emotions suppressed in Sun Qianran’s heart surged to the surface.

“Husband, tell me. What should I do? Am I supposed to stand by and watch you bring down the Duke of Xingguo, dragging my father into it as well?”

Pei Ta watched her weeping, helpless expression, and said heavily, “You could have told me that your father is deeply connected to the Duke of Xingguo. If the Duke falls, he will surely implicate your father, and by extension, the Prime Minister’s residence.”

“I hid it from you because I hoped things could work out for the best.”

Pei Ta let out a quiet sigh in his heart.

Of course, things could have worked out for the best.

But that night, when he spoke up, it wasn’t for the sake of avenging his family; it was for her.

“When I married, my heart was filled with unease. I had no idea what kind of person my future wife would be. Then you entered my life, and I thought the heavens had favored me, bestowing upon me such a wonderful wife. But it seems… it was all just my wishful thinking.”

If only your heart were like mine, and we would never betray our love.

How poetic it sounded. Who would have thought it would turn out to be a joke?

“That’s not true.”

Pei Ta grabbed Sun Qianran’s wrist, forcing her to let go of his sleeve.

“Take care.”

With that, he lifted the curtain and leapt out of the carriage.

“Husband!” Seeing him leave so resolutely, Sun Qianran chased after him.

But she was weak and frail. The moment she stepped out of the carriage, the sharp autumn wind struck her, causing her to cough violently. The sound of her coughing was particularly harsh in the wind.

Pei Ta heard the sound behind him and, instead of slowing down, quickened his pace.

Though she was frail and often ill, she was clever; far tougher than he had imagined.

Without him, she would still live well.

Pei Ta wandered aimlessly through the streets.

The night sky held a crescent moon, yet the capital’s streets were bustling with carriages and horses, the flow of people and lights dazzling and lively.

He walked down one street, then another, before randomly entering a restaurant and ordering wine from the waiter.

One cup, then another.

Not enough.

Then a pot, then another pot…

When Yu Wan and Chen Da Niu came down the stairs together, they saw Pei Ta arguing with the restaurant owner.

“Lord Pei?”

In Yu Wan’s mind, Pei Ta had always been as refined as the moon after rain, a scholar of elegance. Even when drinking, he was graceful, sipping lightly.

But now, his eyes were blurred with drunkenness, his expression despondent. Despite the numerous empty wine pots on the table, he continued to urge the waiter to bring more.

This reckless drinking, as if his life depended on it, left the owner and the waiter in a difficult position. They dared not serve him more wine and instead tried to persuade him to leave.

“Bring more wine! I’m telling you to bring more! Do you think I can’t afford it?”

Pei Ta untied his money pouch from his waist and slammed it heavily onto the table.

“Honored guest, we’ve sold out of wine for today. If you want to drink, please go elsewhere,” Manager Li signaled to the waiter, and they immediately stepped forward to escort Pei Ta out.

Yu Wan, seeing this, quickly stepped forward to stop them. “Don’t trick him into leaving.”

“Miss Yu Wan, do you know him?”

“I do.”

Manager Li had already noticed that Pei Ta’s clothing was extraordinary, suggesting he was either wealthy or noble. Now, seeing that Yu Wan knew him, he said, “He’s had too much to drink and looks like he’s about to be sick. Since he’s your friend, I’ll have someone take him to the restroom first, then prepare a bowl of sobering soup.”

“Thank you for your trouble.”

Pei Ta seemed to recognize Yu Wan as well. This time, he did not resist and allowed the waiter to help him to the backyard of the restaurant.

Watching Pei Ta in his drunken state, Yu Wan felt a sense of confusion.

Today, the Emperor and Empress were returning to the capital. Soon, they would be able to bring down the Duke of Xingguo’s residence. Shouldn’t Pei Ta be actively preparing? Why was he drunk like this? Had something gone wrong?

It must have.

Yu Wan had not known Pei Ta for long, but they had spent considerable time together at the Lichuan Imperial Palace and the Heishui County Yamen.

She had never seen Pei Ta lose his composure, let alone appear so disheveled.

A moment later, the waiter helped Pei Ta back. His face was pale, but his eyes were no longer as clouded as before, suggesting he had drunk the sobering soup.

He looked at Yu Wan, a forced smile appearing on his ashen face.

“Forgive me for making a fool of myself in front of you, Miss Yu Wan.”

Yu Wan was still thinking about the matter of bringing down the Duke of Xingguo’s residence. Hearing Pei Ta’s words, she only asked, “Lord Pei, why are you drinking alone here? Would you like me to hire a carriage to take you home?”

Pei Ta slowly shook his head. “I can’t go back. I have nowhere to go.”

Nowhere to go?

Yu Wan recalled how harmonious Pei Ta and Sun Qianran usually were. There was something odd in his words.

However, as a married couple’s affair, Yu Wan did not feel it was her place to interfere. But…

“Lord Pei, has something gone wrong with that matter?”

Facing Yu Wan’s gaze, Pei Ta remembered how she had previously congratulated him. Suddenly, he realized that her concern for this matter stemmed from her and Zhao Xuanyou’s shared hatred for the Duke of Xingguo’s residence.

“I’m sorry. I acted impulsively and ruined everything.”

Yu Wan had her suspicions, but hearing Pei Ta confirm it himself left her with a mix of emotions.

With such conclusive evidence, it should have been a sure success. How could it have failed?

Pei Ta watched as the light in Yu Wan’s eyes dimmed, and his guilt deepened. “Miss Yu Wan…”

“Lord Pei,” Yu Wan interrupted him, “I asked the manager earlier. The inn still has rooms available tonight. Would you like to rest here for the night?”

“There’s no need for you to arrange that. I have my own place to go.”

“Then I’ll take my leave.”

Yu Wan bowed to him and turned toward the inn.

How could this be…

She had thought that before leaving the capital, she would see the fall of the Duke of Xingguo’s residence. Yet, something had gone wrong.

What to do?

Her mother’s identity meant she couldn’t stay in the capital for long. At most, by next spring, she would have to leave with her mother.

But in such a short time, she had no way of dealing with the Duke of Xingguo’s residence.

“Yu Wan.”

Pei Ta quickly caught up to her from behind.

---

chapters.title: Personal Revenge
chapters.content:
“Does Lord Pei have more business with me?” Yu Wan turned around at the sound of his voice.

Pei Ta walked up to Yu Wan, his gaze falling on her. After quietly observing her for a moment, he lowered his eyes, apologetic. “This is all my fault. I used such an important matter to test someone’s heart, and I lost the gamble, wasting all of the Worldly Prince’s efforts.”

Yu Wan was indeed disappointed, but Pei Ta had helped her many times before. Seeing him so lost, she couldn’t bring herself to turn against him.

Moreover, Pei Ta was too good-looking.

Even after drinking, with his face worn and tired, he exuded a kind of broken beauty, like the fragments of ice on the rocks by the stream in early spring, melting under the sunlight, more dazzling and radiant than in the depths of winter.

Beautiful people and beautiful scenery always made it hard for one to refuse.

After a moment of hesitation, Yu Wan still asked, “Whose heart did Lord Pei test?”

“My pillow partner.”

Sun Qianran?

He tested Sun Qianran’s heart?

Yu Wan looked at Pei Ta in confusion. Pei Ta nodded at her, and they began walking side by side.

What on earth happened?

Pei Ta said this matter had failed because he had impulsively tested Sun Qianran’s heart?

Did that mean Sun Qianran had sabotaged this impeachment?

“How could that be?” Yu Wan recalled the events at the Lichuan Imperial Palace and still didn’t understand. “Back then, Lady Pei went to great lengths to get our Worldly Prince to cooperate with Lord Pei. How could she betray you?”

“It might not be considered a betrayal.” Pei Ta exhaled heavily. “She has always been like this. It’s just that I couldn’t see it clearly.”

Yu Wan found it hard to believe, but hearing Pei Ta say it himself, she understood that no matter how unbelievable it seemed, it was the truth.

She finally understood why Pei Ta had lost control and gotten drunk at the restaurant.

Why did their marriage have to fall apart now, of all times?

Pei Ta noticed Yu Wan’s troubled expression and asked softly, “Is that Cui in the Marquis’s residence treating you poorly?”

Poorly? That was an understatement.

Yu Wan smiled bitterly. “She hates me to the bone and has tried several times to have me killed.”

Pei Ta’s eyes sharpened suddenly, and he looked at Yu Wan in shock. “Is that true? Does the Worldly Prince know?”

Yu Wan thought of the past events and said helplessly, “If the Worldly Prince didn’t know, my mother and I would probably already be dead at Cui Yichu’s hands.”

“Yu Wan, I…”

Seeing Pei Ta’s guilty expression, Yu Wan smiled slightly to comfort him. “Lord Pei, there’s no need for you to feel guilty. While I did hope you could bring down the Duke of Xingguo’s residence, this is my feud with Cui Yichu. I should handle it myself. I believe I can avenge myself.”

Hearing Yu Wan’s words, Pei Ta suddenly felt a surge of respect for her.

He had always known that Yu Wan was beautiful and intelligent, eager to learn and quick to grasp knowledge. So even though she was just a maid from another residence, he had been willing to write calligraphy for her to copy and give her some guidance.

And that was all.

He had gambled with the matter of revenge, knowing that Sun Qianran might betray him. When he lost, he was so devastated that his heart felt torn apart.

But Yu Wan could face it calmly, without complaining or losing heart.

Compared to her, he felt ashamed.

“But now, all the evidence against the Duke of Xingguo has been destroyed by Sun Congdao. I no longer have a chance to turn the tables.”

Hearing him address the Prime Minister by his given name, Yu Wan was slightly surprised.

Pei Ta’s attitude suggested he wanted to distance himself from Prime Minister Sun and Sun Qianran.

But their marital affairs were none of her business, so Yu Wan didn’t say more.

After a moment’s thought, Yu Wan said, “Prime Minister Sun must have done many favors for the Duke of Xingguo for their relationship to be so deep. The dirty deeds they’ve done together are certainly not limited to the embezzlement of tribute pearls.”

“You’re right.” Pei Ta recalled what Sun Qianran had said and nodded slowly. “They’ve been associated for many years. They must have many secrets on each other, not just this one.”

“Is there still a way?”

Facing Yu Wan’s eyes, which shimmered like a spring, Pei Ta hesitated. “My family was deeply involved in the tribute pearl case, so I know many inside details. I can help the Worldly Prince identify the direction of the investigation. But even that took me several years. To investigate other matters, I truly don’t know where to start.”

“Several years?” Yu Wan shook her head slightly. “That’s too long.”

Her mother couldn’t wait. She didn’t have that much time to spare.

“They hold high positions and great power. Bringing them down is no easy task.”

Yes, high positions and great power; those four words alone were like a mountain pressing down, making it impossible for ordinary people to resist.

In their eyes, Yu Wan was nothing but a blade of grass.

A surge of grief and indignation welled up in her heart. Gritting her teeth, Yu Wan said, “If we can’t bring them down, then so be it. At most, I’ll just set a fire…”

Yu Wan was speaking in frustration, but Pei Ta looked at her in surprise upon hearing this.

“You want to set fire to the Duke of Xingguo’s residence?”

“I do want to, but it’s just a pipe dream. The Duke of Xingguo’s residence is so large, and there are surely water vats placed everywhere. Even if I throw torches into the residence with all my might, they would be extinguished in no time.”

Previously, when Cui Yichu had almost driven her to death, Yu Wan had set a fire in the Marquis’s residence. But as soon as a side room was burned down, the flames were extinguished by the Marquis’s guards who had rushed over upon hearing the news.

It was also because of that incident that Yu Wan knew these noble residences had many places where vats of water were stored to prepare for fires.

The Jingyuan Marquis’s residence was like that, so the Duke of Xingguo’s residence must be the same.

She hadn’t even been able to burn a single hair on Cui Yichu’s head with that fire in the Marquis’s residence. How could she possibly burn anyone in the Duke of Xingguo’s residence?

“Setting a fire isn’t something you can do casually. If you have the architectural plans of the Duke of Xingguo’s residence and study them carefully, you should be able to find suitable places to start the fire.”

This chapter is not yet complete. Please click on the next page to continue reading the rest of the exciting content!

“Really?” Yu Wan looked at Pei Ta in astonishment.

Pei Ta, realizing he was seriously discussing arson with her, chuckled. “I was just playing along with your joke. Forgive me for the nonsense.”

“It was just a joke.”

As Yu Wan spoke, a thought lingered in her mind.

She looked around and found that although the streets were bustling with people, no one was paying attention to them.

But for some reason, Pei Ta’s earlier words were like a small stone dropped into her calm heart, creating ripples that refused to settle for a long time.

Could she really burn down the Cui family with a single fire?

After walking a bit further, Yu Wan couldn’t help but ask, “Lord Pei, what is an architectural plan? Is it a map? I’ve never heard of such a thing.”

Yu Wan had always been eager to learn, so Pei Ta wasn’t surprised by her question. He patiently explained, “An architectural plan is not a map. Simply put, it’s a blueprint drawn before constructing palaces, temples, or houses. It can be viewed horizontally or vertically. Once the craftsmen have the blueprint, they can follow it to build the structures.”

“That’s amazing.” Yu Wan had indeed never heard of such a thing before. “Lord Pei, how do you know so much?”

Pei Ta replied gently, “I spent some time in the Hanlin Academy before moving to the Ministry of Works, where I learned a few basics from the officials there.”

“Who would have the architectural plans for the Duke of Xingguo’s residence? Only they themselves?”

“The Duke of Xingguo was one of the four great dukes personally bestowed by Emperor Taizong after his ascension to the throne. The residence was constructed by the Ministry of Works under imperial decree. The architectural plans for the four great dukes’ residences are all archived in the Ministry of Works.”

“Then… only the officials in the Ministry of Works can obtain them?” As soon as the words left her mouth, Yu Wan laughed. “Am I asking too many questions? Lord Pei, you don’t have to answer me.”

chapters.title: Apology
chapters.content:
Pei Ta heard this and looked slightly surprised.

He had originally thought that Zhao Xuanyou and the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion were enemies only because of their divorce, and that there was no deep-seated grudge between them.

Now, hearing Yu Wan say that the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion had tried to kill her multiple times, he suddenly realized that the feud between them was far from simple.

The reason Zhao Xuanyou had refused to cooperate before was not because he didn’t need it, as he had claimed, but because he didn’t trust Pei Ta.

Now it seemed that Pei Ta was indeed unworthy of trust.

Earlier, Pei Ta had been heartbroken by Sun Qianran’s betrayal, and now he felt too ashamed to face Yu Wan.

"Lord Pei, I was only joking."

Pei Ta withdrew his thoughts, cupped his hands, and bowed deeply to Yu Wan. "Miss Yu Wan, this time it is entirely my fault. I have wronged you, and I hope you can forgive me. If there is anything you need in the future, please do not hesitate to ask. Allow me to make amends for my mistake."

Yu Wan did indeed hope that Pei Ta and Zhao Xuanyou could bring down the Cui family. At this moment, she was indeed disappointed, but seeing Pei Ta suddenly performing such a grand gesture, she felt it was unnecessary.

After all, Pei Ta had never made any promises to her, so there was no question of letting her down.

Noticing passersby looking their way, Yu Wan quickly reached out and pulled Pei Ta into a nearby alley.

"Lord Pei, there’s no need to be so polite. I don’t feel that you have wronged me. However..."

"However, what?"

"My young master will probably be very angry." Yu Wan said honestly.

Pei Ta recalled the scene when he had encountered Zhao Xuanyou outside the city gate earlier that day.

They were not friends to begin with. Given Zhao Xuanyou’s status, he would not care about any apologies.

From now on, they would probably be like strangers to each other.

Seeing Pei Ta lost in thought, Yu Wan’s heart stirred, and she carefully spoke up, "Lord Pei, is a construction diagram more powerful than a map?"

Pei Ta snapped out of his thoughts and nodded.

"Of course. A construction diagram includes the map, as well as the interior of the buildings; how the beams are placed, where the windows are, all drawn clearly. In addition to what we can see, things buried underground, such as foundations, secret rooms, and water channels, are also marked."

"So, if you have a construction diagram, you would understand the mansion better than someone who lives there?"

Pei Ta nodded. "Take our earlier joke as an example. With a construction diagram, you would know where the water storage is in the mansion, which building is closest to here, and which is the farthest. Or, for instance, how many gates the mansion has, and in case of a fire that cannot be controlled, how the people inside should escape."

He was indeed a good teacher. With just a few words, he made Yu Wan truly understand what a construction diagram was.

"Lord Pei."

"Hmm?"

"The young master has held a deep grudge against the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion for a long time and will not let it go easily. Since the construction diagram is such a useful thing, why don’t you give the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion’s construction diagram to him? Maybe it will help him calm down."

"Would he want it? It probably wouldn’t be of much use to him."

Pei Ta, of course, knew that Zhao Xuanyou was unmatched in martial arts and had many capable people under him. If he wanted to burn down the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion, he could certainly do it.

But starting a fire was easy; the trouble that followed would be enormous.

The Xingguo Duke’s Mansion was an imperial first-class ducal mansion. Even routine repairs required approval from the Ministry of Works. If it were really burned down, the court would be furious and would definitely investigate thoroughly.

Zhao Xuanyou, as the young master of a marquis’ mansion, would never take such a risk.

As the saying went, "A barefoot man has nothing to fear from one who wears shoes." Zhao Xuanyou’s family background and future prospects far surpassed those of the Xingguo Duke. How could he do such a thing?

"Of course it’s not for the earlier joke," Yu Wan said with a smile. "It’s just that since the evidence for the Gongzhu case has already been destroyed, we can only start from other matters. If we need to investigate inside the mansion, having a construction diagram would make things twice as easy."

"But evidence obtained by sneaking in..."

"They are corrupt officials, using countless dirty and underhanded methods behind the scenes. How can good people, who always follow the rules and the law, compete with them?"

Hearing Yu Wan’s words, Pei Ta couldn’t help but be slightly startled.

"Miss, your insight is refreshing."

Yu Wan smiled embarrassedly. "I just say whatever comes to mind. Anyway, since the construction diagram is useful, the young master should be able to make good use of it."

Seeing Pei Ta seemingly lost in thought, Yu Wan said, "Lord Pei, you are no longer working at the Ministry of Works, which must be troublesome. I always think of things as they come, so Lord Pei need not worry about this."

Pei Ta looked up at her, and Yu Wan slightly averted her gaze.

"Do you really want it?"

He was not asking Zhao Xuanyou, but Yu Wan.

Yu Wan knew he was smart and had already seen through her intentions. Though she didn’t admit it, she didn’t deny it either.

Seeing her tacit consent, Pei Ta said, "Were the things we said earlier just a joke?"

"Of course they were a joke. How could the young master do such a thing? As for me, I’m just a maid. It’s even more impossible. I was just a little curious."

Pei Ta pondered for a moment and slowly said, "These construction diagrams are all sealed in the Ministry of Works. It’s impossible to take them out. If they go missing, it will attract the court’s investigation."

"It was just a wild idea of mine."

Looking at Yu Wan’s disappointed expression, Pei Ta said, "I said it’s impossible to take them out, but if you want to see them, I have a way."

"What way?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, Yu Wan felt she had been a bit too eager and quickly forced a dry laugh to cover it up.

Facing Yu Wan’s eager gaze, Pei Ta raised his hand and pointed to his head.

"Memorize? Could it be that Lord Pei is the kind of person who can read a book and remember it all?"

"Not to the extent of photographic memory, but my memory is decent."

The Ministry of Rites often needed to visit various departments to review records. He had seen the construction diagram of the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion before, and looking at it again wouldn’t attract attention.

"Then I will wait for Lord Pei’s good news."

Seeing Yu Wan’s eyes burning with anticipation, Pei Ta’s guilt lessened slightly, though he felt a strange sensation in his heart.

Although Yu Wan was indeed just a maid and couldn’t possibly burn down the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion, he knew she was very clever. She wouldn’t do anything pointless.

Wanting the construction diagram must have its reasons.

"Yu Wan."

Pei Ta hesitated for a moment before voicing his concern: "With the young master looking after you, the people of the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion cannot harm you. You must not take any risks."

"Lord Pei, rest assured. I won’t do anything that harms the enemy but also hurts myself. I just think that the construction diagram is so useful. Maybe studying it carefully will really lead to some discoveries."

Pei Ta looked at her face, as gentle as a spring breeze, and felt slightly more at ease.

No matter what, the revenge plan had been ruined because of him, and Yu Wan and her mother had once again fallen into difficulty. Being able to do a small thing to make Yu Wan smile was good.

"Yu Wan, why are you out so late tonight?"

"I originally wanted to accompany my mother to see the doctor, but the doctor was too busy at the clinic. It was already dark by the time he came to the Taoran Inn. It’s getting late, so I should hurry back."

"I’ll take you back."

It was already dark, and it wouldn’t be safe for Yu Wan to go back alone.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t like Pei Ta to begin with. Now, with this incident, it would be better if Pei Ta didn’t appear near him.

Yu Wan declined, "It’s fine. I can just hire a carriage. What about you, Lord Pei?"

Pei Ta had been heavily drunk and had vomited. His complexion was extremely poor at the moment.

"Didn’t that inn have empty rooms earlier? I’ll stay there tonight."

He was already thin, and now, feeling dizzy, he walked with a heavy head and light feet.

Yu Wan quickly stepped forward to support him. "Let me take you back to the inn first."

Pei Ta felt even more ashamed and lowered his head in silence, but Yu Wan just smiled.

However, after taking a few steps forward, a tall figure came into view.

---

chapters.title: Indignation
chapters.content:
It was Zhao Xuanyou.

Why was he here?

Yu Wan didn’t know why Zhao Xuanyou had appeared here, but she could clearly sense the anger radiating from him.

And that anger was clearly directed at Pei Ta beside her.

"Young Master." Yu Wan let go of Pei Ta’s arm and quickly walked toward Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou also took a few steps forward, extending his arm to pull Yu Wan into his embrace, and looked coldly at Pei Ta.

"Yu Wan is my woman. You’d better remember that."

Huh?

Did he think she had some private affair with Pei Ta? That was a misunderstanding.

Yu Wan understood that no matter what she said now, it would only add fuel to the fire. Since Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t angry at her, keeping quiet was the best course of action.

She desperately signaled to Pei Ta with her eyes, telling him not to speak, but Pei Ta misunderstood and said gently, "Young Master, you’ve misunderstood. Miss Yu Wan and I have no..."

"I have nothing to say to a useless man like you. In the future, when you see me, remember to take a detour."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes burned with anger. After saying this coldly, he took Yu Wan and quickly left without lingering.

As they exited the alley, they saw Yuan Zhen waiting with the carriage by the roadside.

Yu Wan nervously twisted her fingers, allowing Zhao Xuanyou to hold her as they entered the carriage.

"Go."

Yuan Zhen, hearing Zhao Xuanyou’s order, fiercely whipped the reins and drove the carriage toward the courtyard.

The wheels rumbled as Yu Wan sat beside Zhao Xuanyou, pondering for a long time without knowing how to speak.

Even though there were only the two of them in the carriage, Yu Wan could still feel the cold anger emanating from Zhao Xuanyou had not dissipated.

The atmosphere in the carriage was stiff. After a long while, Yu Wan tried calling out to him.

"Master."

The man beside her showed no change in expression, his dark eyes beneath his sword-like brows as deep as an abyss.

Yu Wan lifted the corner of her lips, unsure whether to speak again. After a moment of hesitation, as she turned her face away, she finally heard him respond with an "mm."

Although it was just a simple sound, Yu Wan’s suspended heart settled slightly.

She looked back at him, her beautiful eyes slightly raised, and softly said, "After seeing the doctor off, I stayed with my mother for a while. It was only when I went downstairs that I saw Lord Pei drinking himself into a stupor at the restaurant. Seeing that he was very drunk, I asked about it."

Clearly, these few words were not enough to explain why they had been in the alley.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s dark and unclear gaze, Yu Wan reached out and shook his arm.

Zhao Xuanyou was already very annoyed, but he still wouldn’t push her hand away, allowing her to play with his arm.

"You have something to say."

Yu Wan said, "Later, we chatted for a bit. He said that the matter with the Xingguo Duke’s Mansion had been ruined by him. I felt very sad. By then, it was already late, and I was in a hurry to return to the mansion. But Lord Pei followed me."

"He followed you?"

Yu Wan clearly felt Zhao Xuanyou’s anger rising again and quickly said, "He was very drunk, probably frustrated. He told me about his situation with Lady Pei. From what he said, it seems he plans to cut ties with Lady Pei in the future."

A cold smile appeared on Zhao Xuanyou’s face, clearly not caring about the Pei family’s affairs.

"He was talking and then seemed dizzy, as if he was about to fall. So I went up to support him. That’s when you arrived, Master. You don’t think I was doing something I shouldn’t, do you?"

Zhao Xuanyou, of course, did not think Yu Wan was being unfaithful.

He just disliked Pei Ta and disliked Pei Ta standing next to Yu Wan.

"Remember what I said to him earlier."

"Remember what?" Yu Wan blinked her eyes, feigning ignorance. "In the future, when seeing the young master, remember to take a detour?"

Zhao Xuanyou, already annoyed, heard her deliberately being clever and felt his teeth itch, but there was nothing he could do to her.

"You say it again?"

Yu Wan pretended not to understand. "Then what does Master want me to remember?"

"In the future, you are not allowed to speak to anyone with the surname Pei. If you see him on the road, remember to take a detour."

"Why?"

Hearing Yu Wan’s retort, Zhao Xuanyou’s eyebrows tightened, thinking she insisted on talking to Pei Ta. Before he could get angry, Yu Wan said, "Why is it that when you see him, he has to take a detour, but when I see him, I have to take a detour?"

"Are you, a woman, supposed to be so glib?"

"I am being reasonable, not glib." Seeing the frost on his face finally melt a little, Yu Wan secretly felt relieved. She hugged his arm and leaned against him, obediently saying, "I remember. In the future, if I see Lord Pei, I will try to avoid him and try not to talk to him."

"What do you have to say to him that is so necessary?" Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze suddenly tightened.

"There’s nothing that necessary, but he and Lady Pei have been kind to me. I’m not as imposing as you, Master. If they greet me, how can a maid like me turn my face away?"

"Pei Ta is a useless man, which is fine, but as for that Lady Pei, you should stay far away from her in the future, lest she bite me."

Yu Wan’s face held a faint smile as she said softly, "Master makes her sound like a venomous snake."

"If she can even scheme against her own husband, what isn’t she?"

Sun Qianran, though not as despicable as Cui Yichu, also enjoyed manipulating people’s hearts.

Yu Wan was now confused. "What exactly did Lady Pei do? She seemed so concerned about Lord Pei. Back then, she went to such lengths to get close to you, Master. Why would she ruin Lord Pei’s revenge plan just as it was about to succeed?"

Pei Ta had only verbally distanced himself from the Sun family in his words and had not clearly explained what Sun Qianran had done.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at her sideways. "After chatting in the alley for so long, didn’t he tell you?"

"As I said, he was drunk and didn’t say much." Yu Wan, of course, would not mention the construction diagram, but she really hadn’t done anything improper with Pei Ta. Therefore, she was particularly justified. "He’s not like you, Master, with a high alcohol tolerance. Today he was drunk, and he kept cursing Prime Minister Sun. I only understood that the plan had failed. I don’t know anything else."

The Gongzhu case was already over, so there was no need to hide anything anymore.

Zhao Xuanyou then recounted the whole story: first, he had warned Pei Ta, then Pei Ta had leaked the information to Sun Qianran, and Sun Qianran had passed the information to her father, the Prime Minister.

Thus, Prime Minister Sun and the Duke of Xingguo joined forces to suppress Censor Zhang, making him change his impeachment from both the Duke of Xingguo and Tao Cheng to just Tao Cheng.

Tao Cheng was arrested, and all evidence related to the Duke of Xingguo in the Gongzhu case disappeared. Everything ended there.

"So that’s how it was." As Yu Wan listened to Zhao Xuanyou’s account, she detected a different undertone. "Master, did you warn Lord Pei to be wary of Lady Pei?"

"Mm." Zhao Xuanyou’s face was full of mockery. "A useless man with soft ears, incapable of great things."

He had solemnly warned him, yet he still let the secret out.

Useless?

Yu Wan’s ears echoed with Pei Ta’s words.

He had said that this time it was his own fault, that it was his impulsiveness that had brought about the disaster.

"What are you thinking about?" Zhao Xuanyou reached out and rubbed her head.

Yu Wan looked up at him, her eyes clear. "He didn’t accidentally leak it to Lady Pei. He did it on purpose."

chapters.title: Sincerity
chapters.content:
"What difference does it make?" Zhao Xuanyou spoke in an ordinary tone, naturally dismissive.

If it was ruined, it was ruined. Did the reason matter?

Yu Ying curved her lips into a smile and said no more.

Zhao Xuanyou studied her expression, suppressing the irritation in his heart, and asked calmly, "Then what difference do you think it makes?"

"To you, Lord Zhao, there is no difference. To me, there is also no difference," Yu Ying said softly, "But to Madam Pei, the difference is huge."

If it was just revenge being obstructed, Pei Tao would not be so heartbroken even if he suffered a setback.

He chose to believe Sun Qianran, but reality slapped him hard in the face.

No wonder he addressed Sun Xiang by his full name, speaking of the Sun family's affairs as if he were an outsider.

Madam Pei... might soon no longer be Madam Pei.

"Pei Tao is a timid man by nature. Tomorrow, if Sun Qianran pretends to be ill and weeps to him, Pei Tao will surely obediently return and put on the facade of a loving husband and wife again."

No, he won't.

Yu Ying silently thought to herself.

That day, Pei Tao had revealed the news to Sun Qianran not to sabotage the impeachment.

On the contrary, he was certain that Sun Qianran would not leak it, which was why he told her.

He was a man of deep emotion and integrity; it was just that this emotion had been betrayed by Sun Qianran.

Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao were completely different kinds of people. They could never be friends, nor could they understand each other's actions.

Pei Tao would never scheme against his beloved, whereas Zhao Xuanyou... would never have a beloved.

In Zhao Xuanyou's heart, everything and everyone required consideration and trade-offs.

Grand Dowager Ye repeatedly urged her to drink the contraceptive soup, fearing that Zhao Xuanyou doted on her too much. If she had a child, it might lead to the tragedy of a favored concubine overshadowing the wife in the future.

But she knew he would never do that. Such a thing would never happen with Zhao Xuanyou.

Feeling someone playing with her hair, Yu Ying gathered her thoughts and looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, her cheeks filling with a smile again.

"I haven't asked yet, why are you out so late, my lord?"

"What do you think?" Zhao Xuanyou's gaze slightly focused.

Facing his deep, profound eyes, Yu Ying quickly came to her senses: "Did you come specifically to pick me up, my lord?"

Inside the carriage, the candlelight was dim. His face was very close to Yu Ying's, and the light outlined the distinct contours of his eyebrows, the corners of his eyes, his nose, and his chin.

Although Zhao Xuanyou was not as renowned for his looks as Pei Tao in the capital, his appearance was undeniably handsome.

Unlike Pei Tao's fair and elegant bone structure, Zhao Xuanyou had sharp, prominent cheekbones and a straight, noble nose. His demeanor was colder and harder, like a tall mountain shrouded in mist, making it impossible for anyone to approach or see his true face.

"Physician Feng has many patients and is very busy. Today, he was busy at the Huichun Hall until dark before coming over. I kept my mother company in the room, so I was delayed."

"How did the physician say?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"The physician said that the blood stasis has been mostly cleared, but my mother has been in a coma for too long, and her body is very weak. It will take at least a few more years of care for her to recover."

Previously, when her mother was living in the charity hall of Yun Shui Temple, although the nuns did their best to care for her, there were too many patients and their energy was limited. They could only feed her some porridge to keep her alive.

When Yu Ying was reborn, her mother was already on the verge of death.

"That Physician Feng specializes in acupuncture. If we want to regulate her condition, we need to find another physician."

"I was also thinking of finding a new physician."

"There is a Physician Mou in the capital who is skilled in tonic treatment. The ladies of the high-ranking families in the capital often invite him to their homes for consultations. He has also come to the Marquis's mansion to see Grandmother before."

"Physician Mou? I'll remember that."

"You go and invite him, but he might not pay attention. Let Manager Li handle it."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yu Ying, who was close at hand, and slowly reached out to hold her in his arms.

"Thank you, Young Master."

It was late at night, and Yu Ying was also feeling a bit cold. She couldn't help but shrink into his embrace.

At this time, there were already few people on the streets. Sitting in the carriage, they couldn't hear much noise. The two didn't speak, and the sound of the carriage wheels rolling over the road was clear.

Yu Ying had spent the entire day taking care of Ding Wenxi at the Taoran Inn, and now she was feeling a bit tired.

As she dozed off in his arms, she suddenly heard him ask, "Do you think Pei Tao did the right thing?"

Yu Ying didn't really want to answer this question.

There was no right or wrong in this matter.

Pei Tao did not intentionally ruin his own revenge plan. It was because he valued sincerity and believed in it that he ended up with such consequences.

Of course, Yu Ying hoped to bring down the Xingguo Duke's mansion in one fell swoop.

But she didn't think Pei Tao was wrong.

Perhaps, she also hoped that one day someone would treat her with such sincerity.

But saying such things to Zhao Xuanyou would be ridiculous. He would probably think she was a foolish girl with delusions.

She closed her eyes and drowsily replied, "What are you talking about, my lord?"

Her voice was soft, like a mosquito's buzz.

Seeing that she was drowsy, Zhao Xuanyou finally didn't say anything more, and Yu Ying indeed fell asleep.

When the carriage stopped, he carried Yu Ying into the courtyard.

---

Life in the courtyard was much more relaxed than in the Marquis's mansion.

The courtyard was not large, and there wasn't as much work as in the Marquis's mansion.

Every morning, after Zhao Xuanyou left, Yu Ying, along with Yingxue and Ziyan, would finish tidying up the house and then go to the Taoran Inn to visit Ding Wenxi, staying there for most of the day.

Zhao Xuanyou had never said anything about this, which was tacit approval.

Originally, he had brought Yu Ying to the courtyard to discuss the Gongzhu case with Pei Tao. Now that the Gongzhu case was settled, Pei Tao would no longer visit, and Zhao Xuanyou would return to the mansion every few days to pay his respects to Grand Dowager Ye. He hadn't mentioned returning to the mansion.

One day, after court, before he could leave the palace, Zhao Xuanyou was stopped by a eunuch, who led him all the way to the imperial study.

Inside the hall, the curtains were long and hanging, and the aroma of dragon's saliva incense was strong.

After Zhao Xuanyou knelt and paid his respects, the emperor on the throne slowly spoke, "Rise and speak."

"Thank you, Your Majesty."

The last time he had sent a secret letter from Heishui to the emperor, the two had not yet had a private audience.

Seeing that the emperor's expression was not good, Zhao Xuanyou could roughly guess why he had been summoned.

The emperor put down the brush in his hand and gave a signal to the inner attendants. After everyone in the hall had withdrawn, his expression turned cold and he said slowly, "Xuanyou, discovering the illegal casting of weapons in Heishui is a great achievement. I never expected that the Empress and the Crown Prince would be involved in such a big matter."

Illegally casting weapons was a crime of treason. The involvement of the Empress and the Crown Prince was no small matter, and the emperor could not help but feel chilled.

When the emperor received Zhao Xuanyou's secret report, he had only replied with "I know," and did not order Zhao Xuanyou to continue investigating.

Clearly, he had sent someone else to investigate.

He had called Zhao Xuanyou to possibly warn him.

Therefore, Zhao Xuanyou took a step back and spoke on behalf of the Crown Prince: "Your Majesty, according to what I found in Heishui, His Highness the Crown Prince was unaware of this before the incident."

"And the Empress?"

"Only the boxes from the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion were found in the magistrate's residence. There was no evidence linking to Her Majesty the Empress."

The emperor heard this and looked at Zhao Xuanyou with a smile: "The Duke of Zhen Guo is just a subject. He is both my brother-in-law and the Crown Prince's father-in-law. Unless he is tired of living and wants to rebel, he would not give up being the Emperor's father-in-law to start a rebellion."

The emperor had spoken to this extent, and Zhao Xuanyou could no longer feign ignorance.

Seeing this, he cupped his hands to the emperor and said, "I am willing to share Your Majesty's burdens."

chapters.title: Heart Chill
chapters.content:
The emperor's fingers slowly tapped on the imperial desk, pondering: "Zhao Zun is no longer suitable to be in the position of Crown Prince."

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze flickered slightly.

These days, the Lichuan Imperial Palace had been calm, and no major events had occurred in the court.

But the emperor had already made his decision.

Soon after returning to the capital, Zhao Xuanyou realized that the emperor had long intended to eliminate the power of the Empress and the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion to prevent them from influencing the Crown Prince and affecting the imperial power of the Zhao family.

But the Crown Prince could not see the situation clearly and relied on the Empress and the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion as his backing. How could the emperor tolerate the Jiang family overshadowing the Zhao family?

Regarding matters of the heir, Zhao Xuanyou, as a subject, did not dare to interfere and respectfully said, "Your Majesty is wise."

"I truly did not expect Zhao Zun to go this far." The emperor sighed.

The emperor and the empress had once had a loving and harmonious relationship.

When she was welcomed into the palace as a noble consort, although it was a reward to the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion, he had also loved her for her beauty and charm.

When the original empress and the eldest son died in succession, the emperor had suspicions but no evidence.

Later, after the death of Concubine Hui, the mother of Zhao Qi, the emperor and the empress completely grew apart.

But regardless of the empress's actions, Zhao Zun was the emperor's own son.

From the moment Zhao Zun was born, the emperor had placed great importance on him, even transferring the guilt and love he felt for his deceased eldest son onto Zhao Zun.

But fate was cruel, and this carefully cultivated heir still step by step sided with the empress, disappointing the emperor time and time again.

When the Crown Princess was to be established, the empress insisted that Zhao Zun marry Jiang Ru Frost from the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion. The emperor saw that Zhao Zun did not like Jiang Ru Frost and intended to support him.

But in the end, Zhao Zun followed the empress's orders and married his cousin.

If the matter of marriage only disappointed the emperor, then Zhao Zun's covering up of the Zhen Guo Duke's illegal casting of weapons made the emperor completely determined to depose him.

The Crown Prince, personally appointed by the emperor after sacrificing to the heavens and the ancestors, actually turned a blind eye to others' usurpation of power.

If Zhao Zun were to inherit the throne, how could the emperor face his ancestors in the future?

"The empress has made many connections with court officials over the years, and the Zhen Guo Duke still controls the Feiyun Guard. Now that they have illegally cast weapons, they might also have private soldiers. If I directly depose the Crown Prince, they will go all out and start a rebellion."

Zhao Xuanyou understood and said, "After the death of Emperor Hongjing, the Rebellion of the Three Princes broke out, leading to continuous wars and suffering for the people. After Your Majesty ascended the throne, you worked diligently to bring peace and prosperity to the land. Although their rebellion is not a concern, Your Majesty loves the people like your own children and certainly does not want to see them suffer."

"That's right. The world has only been at peace for twenty years. I truly cannot bear to start another war. The empress's faction must be dealt with gradually. First, we need to bring down the Zhen Guo Duke."

"Your Majesty, just give the order."

The emperor rose from the dragon throne and slowly walked to Zhao Xuanyou's side, saying softly, "Nowadays, the old officials in the court are all cunning foxes, lacking in integrity and ambition, and are not worthy of trust. I originally thought that you and Pei Tao, one civil and one military, could assist me in planning. Alas, who knew about Pei Tao... Alas..."

Hearing the emperor's regretful tone, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly realized that the outside world said Pei Tao was able to rise rapidly and have smooth official fortune because of his Prime Minister father-in-law.

It turned out that Pei Tao had long been favored by the emperor.

It made sense. Pei Tao had been named the top scholar in the Golden Hall before Prime Minister Sun had recruited him as a son-in-law.

Zhao Xuanyou asked knowingly, "I saw Director Pei just a few days ago, and he was still full of vigor. Did something happen to him?"

"You don't know? Pei Tao insists on divorcing Sun Qianran. Sun Congdao flew into a rage, and recently I have received several memorials accusing him of favoritism and perverting the law."

It was no surprise. Prime Minister Sun was the kind of person who would retaliate for the slightest offense.

Pei Tao did not want his precious daughter, so of course, they would seek revenge.

This should have been a moment for Zhao Xuanyou to gloat, but given the emperor's tone, it was clear that he could not kick Pei Tao while he was down and had to say a few good words for him.

"When I was in Lichuan, Director Pei was my neighbor. He is a man of great learning and integrity, and should not do anything like favoritism or perverting the law."

"That is natural. Those are all false accusations." The emperor already knew about Pei Tao's father's old case but did not mention it further since he did not know Zhao Xuanyou was also involved. "He is a smart man, but he has spent too much time in the study and, after becoming an official, has always stayed in the capital, which has made him a bit bookish. Sun Congdao is determined to bring him down, and I plan to go with the flow and send him out of the capital to gain some experience. Maybe he can achieve something."

Send Pei Tao out of the capital?

That would be letting him off easy.

But for Zhao Xuanyou, it was good to be out of sight, out of mind.

"I hope Director Pei will not disappoint Your Majesty's efforts."

The emperor reached out and patted Zhao Xuanyou's shoulder: "I have also thought of a place for you."

Zhao Xuanyou heard this and cupped his hands, looking at the emperor with a calm expression.

"You are highly skilled in martial arts. Staying in the Secretariat as a military advisor is indeed a waste of your talents. Last year, the commander of the Jin Yi Wei was severely injured and has been resting at home. After so much treatment, he has not recovered and may not be able to return to duty. You will take over the Jin Yi Wei for me."

Zhao Xuanyou was somewhat surprised. He had thought the emperor would let him command the capital's army, but instead, he was to take over the Jin Yi Wei.

"I only know how to lead troops and fight. I fear I am not up to the task."

The emperor looked at him for a moment, his experienced gaze scanning Zhao Xuanyou.

"Xuanyou, do not underestimate yourself. You and Zhao Qi arrived in Heishui before me, but you were the one who discovered the illegal casting of weapons and handled the matter well. Apart from you, I cannot think of anyone else who could be the commander of the Jin Yi Wei."

Did the emperor know that he had secretly left?

Then he must also know about the conflicts between him and Zhao Zun over Yu Ying.

Zhao Xuanyou was about to apologize, but the emperor said, "Zhao Zun forcibly took a commoner's daughter and did as he pleased. You did nothing wrong. From now on, you will keep a close eye on the Zhen Guo Duke's mansion for me and must find their private soldiers."

"I accept Your Majesty's decree and thank you for your grace."

His expression was firm and resolute.

The emperor looked at his cold and determined face and nodded slightly: "You may leave."

Zhao Xuanyou left the imperial study and immediately ran into Zhao Qi.

"Prince Qi." Zhao Xuanyou cupped his hands in greeting.

"What are you doing here?" Zhao Qi asked.

Zhao Qi had learned martial arts from Zhao Xuanyou for a few months, but the two had never established a formal master-disciple relationship.

Previously, in the imperial palace and Heishui, Zhao Qi had been more restrained, but now that they were back in the imperial palace, Zhao Qi had returned to his old way of speaking with barbed remarks.

"The emperor summoned me." Zhao Xuanyou answered concisely.

"Oh."

Zhao Qi stared at him silently.

Today, Zhao Xuanyou was wearing official robes, his tall and straight figure making him a full half a head taller than Zhao Qi.

Zhao Qi's mind flashed back to the scene he had witnessed by the lake.

Taller, it did seem to match Yu Ying better.

Although Zhao Qi was not yet fifteen, Zhao Xuanyou was too tall. Even when Zhao Qi turned twenty, he might not be as tall.

It was no wonder Yu Ying only saw him as a child.

Zhao Qi felt an inexplicable irritation and, without saying more, walked past Zhao Xuanyou with a dark face towards the imperial study.

chapters.title: Hasty Departure
chapters.content:
After the eunuch announced his arrival, Zhao Qi entered the imperial study.

He walked so quickly that upon entering the hall, his shoulder bumped into the gold-painted plum, orchid, bamboo, and pine folding screen. Had the nearby eunuch not reacted swiftly, the screen would have been knocked over.

The emperor glanced at him, his affectionate gaze tinged with a hint of helplessness.

"At your age, why are you still so reckless?"

Zhao Qi lowered his head and approached the imperial desk. Seeing him so listless, the emperor said, "Look at you, still like a child, unable to take even a single word of criticism."

"Father Emperor, I am not a child anymore," Zhao Qi protested.

"After the New Year, you and Zhao Yu will be fifteen. By the palace's rules, you are indeed no longer a child. But you still act on impulse. How can I treat you as an adult?"

Zhao Qi understood. In the emperor's eyes, being tied up and brought back from Heishui by Zhao Zun was a foolish act.

"I, your son, admit my mistake. I will not do such stupid things again."

"It is good that you understand." The emperor nodded slightly. "I cannot protect you forever. You must learn to stand on your own."

Zhao Qi looked at the single white hair at the emperor's temple and felt a slight jolt in his heart.

Had Father Emperor grown old without him noticing?

He quickly said, "Father Emperor is in the prime of life. You can still protect me for a long time."

The emperor only smiled and changed the subject. "These days, you have been able to settle down and focus on martial arts. That is good. But you are a prince. Merely practicing martial arts is not enough. You must also work hard on your studies."

"I understand. I will listen to Father Emperor and humbly seek teachings from Minister Pei."

"Pei Tao will soon leave the capital for an official post. He will no longer be able to teach you. I will arrange for a new tutor from the Hanlin Academy."

"Ah? He is leaving the capital for an official position?"

Zhao Qi did not particularly like Pei Tao, but Pei Tao's lectures were far more engaging than those of the old scholars. Moreover, after working together on the Heishui case, day and night, Zhao Qi knew Pei Tao's character well.

"I have heard that he is divorcing Sun Tianran, and Sun Congdao had his disciples impeach him. Father Emperor, you do not believe those accusations, do you? Pei Tao would never accept bribes or bend the law."

"You do understand right from wrong." The emperor smiled. "Pei Tao is indeed a reliable man. However, though he is well-read, his understanding of worldly affairs is not as keen as Zhao Xuanyou's."

Zhao Qi had not expected the emperor to suddenly praise Zhao Xuanyou. A sense of unwillingness surged in his heart, and he blurted out, "What is so great about Zhao Xuanyou?"

"What? You think he is incompetent?"

The emperor was somewhat surprised. He had always thought Zhao Qi was closer to Zhao Xuanyou and more distant from Pei Tao. But seeing Zhao Qi's attitude now, it seemed he held Pei Tao in higher regard.

"It is not that he is incompetent, but he is not as good as Father Emperor makes him out to be. He may be skilled in martial arts, but nothing else is extraordinary."

The emperor said, "The Jingyuan Marquis's residence is plagued with illness, and he has only one son, Xuanyou. Xuanyou has been in the military since he was a teenager, wielding his sword in battle. His experience and tactics are beyond what you can compare to."

Moreover, Zhao Xuanyou was not just a military man; he was also well-versed in literature. Among the young officials at court, no one had his level of talent.

If he were the emperor's son, the emperor would not be so troubled now.

"That is because Father Emperor has not given me the chance. If I had been in the military instead of studying in the palace, I might not be worse than him."

Looking at Zhao Qi's youthful vigor, the emperor smiled with satisfaction. "It is good that you have such ambition."

"Father Emperor, your son has more than just ambition." At this point, Zhao Qi suddenly knelt before the emperor and solemnly cupped his hands. "Your son has a request. Please grant it, Father Emperor."

The emperor could not fathom his intentions and narrowed his eyes. "Speak."

"Previously, you sent Fifth Brother to the Mingchui Guard for training. I was very envious. Can Father Emperor allow me to go to my maternal uncle's command? I can start as a lowly soldier. I will not disappoint Father Emperor."

"You want to go to your maternal uncle's army?"

"Yes."

The Duke of Ningguo was old, and he was concerned about Zhao Qi, so he had been staying in the capital. Currently, the one commanding the southeast was the Duke of Ningguo's heir, Zhao Qi's maternal uncle.
