Wen Bo looked at Yu Wan's noblewoman attire and nodded. He carried Bingyun and disappeared into the night.

Yu Wan entered the firewood room with the axe.

Cui Yichu lay on the ground, motionless, her entire body already surrounded by raging flames, yet she was still alive.

Her eyeballs moved slightly, staring straight at Yu Wan.

At the moment their eyes met, a hundred emotions surged into Yu Wan's heart. She swung the axe fiercely at the fireball, returning everything Cui Yichu had given her!

In her past life, Yu Wan had died in the bone-chilling winter. In this life, the murderer who had harmed her finally met the same fate and could no longer harm anyone!

Two clear tears silently slid down Yu Wan's cheeks.

All the hatred, anger, deception, betrayal, humiliation, and trampling ended at this moment. Everything would be burned to ashes by the raging fire, returning to dust and earth like all things in the world.

Suddenly, firecrackers rang out, and the night sky bloomed with countless fireworks, like flowing pearls and jade, like a hundred flowers competing in beauty.

The new year had arrived.

---

chapters.title: A Different Way to Live
chapters.content:
The fire inside the room grew fiercer, and Yu Wan threw down the axe and ran out quickly.

A cold wind slapped her face, cooling her burning cheeks slightly.

She wiped away the tears from her face with her sleeve, smoothed her hair a little, and walked slowly through the manor.

Soon, two servant women came towards her.

Yu Wan appeared composed, slightly lifting her head and raising her face, pretending to be engrossed in watching the fireworks.

Although the servant women found it strange that "Cui Yichu" would appear near the firewood room at this time, they simply bowed to her and quickly left.

After Cui Yichu and Li returned to the manor, her temperament had changed greatly, and the servants all avoided her.

Once the servant women were far away, Yu Wan continued walking forward. It was at this moment that a commotion finally arose behind her.

"Disaster! The firewood room is on fire!"

The fire in the firewood room had finally spread to the roof, and the people outside the courtyard saw the blazing flames and immediately cried out in alarm.

"Someone is lying in the courtyard, quick, save them!"

"Are they drunk?"

"Carry them out first!"

"Quick! Quick, go get water!"

The firewood room was filled with flammable dry wood, so when the manor was built, a large water vat was specifically left beside the firewood room.

However, when people rushed over with buckets and basins to fetch water, they found that the water vats had already been overturned, leaving no water to use.

Chaos erupted around the firewood room, but Yu Wan's steps quickened.

There were still two people guarding the side gate. She was thinking about how to leave in the guise of Cui Yichu when a hand suddenly reached out from the side and pulled her over.

"Shh! It's me."

Yu Wan looked at the person in surprise, "Yangquan, why are you here?"

"Madame was worried about you and sent me to the outskirts of Duke Xingguo's manor to meet up with you. I just encountered Bingyun, who said you were still in the manor, so I came in."

First it was Wen Bo, then her mother and Yangquan. Yu Wan's heart was slightly moved.

Having help was truly good. She was no longer alone in the dark.

She turned her head and saw in the distance the fire rising into the sky. Once the dry wood in the firewood room ignited, it would be difficult to control.

"Let's go."

The two of them silently climbed over the wall and quickly made their way through the alleys, returning to where the carriage was parked.

Lifting the carriage curtain, Bingyun and Wen Bo were indeed inside.

Yu Wan let out a deep breath and sat down next to Bingyun.

Yangquan drove the carriage a long distance before stopping at a place where many other carriages were gathered outside an inn. He then re-entered the carriage.

Bingyun had not lost consciousness, but his complexion looked very poor, and his reactions were extremely slow.

Wen Bo indifferently said, "He inhaled a lot of smoke. Even if he doesn't die, he won't be well for a while and needs to rest quietly."

The original plan was for Bingyun to escort Yu Wan out of the capital and wait for Ding Wenxi and Yangquan at a small courtyard outside the city.

"Bingyun can't leave the capital with me. He needs to see a doctor urgently."

Yangquan and Bingyun were close brothers, so naturally, he didn't want anything to happen to Bingyun.

"But you must leave the capital as soon as possible."

"Bingyun is in no condition to travel. You should take him back to the Ningguo Duke's manor. Once someone is there to take care of him, go to the other courtyard to protect my mother."

"And you?"

"I will drive the carriage. I have my own way to leave the capital."

"That place will be hard for you to find." Yangquan was indeed very worried about Bingyun's safety. Knowing that Yu Wan was not a reckless person, he pondered for a moment and said in a low voice, "There is no curfew in the capital tonight, but the city gates have already been closed. Go to the west city gate and wait there. Before the city gates open tomorrow, I will arrive and take you out of the capital."

"Alright."

After settling this, Yangquan carried Bingyun and left the carriage.

Yu Wan silently prayed in her heart for Bingyun's safety. A moment later, she felt Wen Bo's heavy gaze on her.

"Are you leaving the capital?"

At this point, Yu Wan didn't want to lie to Wen Bo anymore. "I want to take my mother away from the capital."

"So you've been lying to me all along?"

"I needed your help, so I resorted to that."

"That was a poor strategy?" Wen Bo's voice sounded somewhat mocking. After a moment of silence, he suddenly asked, "Where are you going?"

"I haven't decided yet."

Wen Bo frowned slightly, looking at her with some disbelief. "You're leaving Zhao Xuanyou?"

Looking at his expression, Yu Wan smiled lightly. "Is that not allowed?"

"But what about his feelings for you?"

"He's been good to me, but I just want to leave the capital and live differently."

Live differently...

These four words were like a stone thrown into a lake, creating ripple after ripple in Wen Bo's heart.

As far as he could remember, he had only one way to live: desperately practicing his skills and loyally serving his master.

He was like a bat, active at night and silent during the day. No one noticed him, and he forever lived in the dark corners.

He was born with an ugly appearance, perhaps destined to stay in the shadows. It was already fortunate that he could barely survive under the Prince's wing.

But now, hearing Yu Wan say she wanted to live differently, seeing her relaxed demeanor, he felt she was somewhat naive, somewhat foolish, and somewhat enviable.

"How do you want to live?" Wen Bo unconsciously asked.

Yu Wan hadn't expected him to ask so seriously. She thought for a moment and said haltingly, "I should take my mother to a place with beautiful scenery. She's not well, and we can't live in the village anymore. At least we should live in a town where she can see a doctor often. I have some money now and can buy a house. I'll plant trees in the front courtyard and grow flowers in the back. I'll do some small business. Living off savings isn't good; money should generate more money for a sense of security."

Wen Bo liked staying in his small courtyard, but apart from a tree planted by his predecessors, there were no flowers or plants in his yard.

Seeing Wen Bo lost in thought as he listened to her, Yu Wan looked at him and softly asked, "Do you not want to serve the Prince anymore?"

The Prince was actually a decent master; at least he had never mistreated Wen Bo.

Wen Bo didn't want to stop serving the Prince; he just... didn't want to serve anyone anymore.

He lightly hummed in agreement and looked up at Yu Wan. "Can I go with you?"

"You? Go with me?" Yu Wan asked in astonishment.

Wen Bo nodded. "Leaving the Eastern Palace, I can't stay in the capital either. But I have no hometown, no family. I don't know where to go."

He was telling the truth, but not the whole truth.

Perhaps it was when Yu Wan asked Zhao Xuanyou to spare him, or when she brought that plate of dumplings, that he had this idea.

"Do you really want to?" Yu Wan still found it hard to believe.

"Obviously." After saying so much, seeing that she still didn't believe him, Wen Bo became somewhat impatient.

"Really?" Yu Wan suddenly laughed loudly. "That's wonderful! That's wonderful! The new year really brings good fortune! Heaven truly favors me!"

Wen Bo hadn't expected her to be so happy and was momentarily at a loss.

"Is it that exciting?"

"Of course! You're the Prince's secret guard. With you by my side, who in the world would dare to provoke me?" The biggest concern Yu Wan had about escaping the capital with her mother was their safety. She had originally thought about hiring someone after they escaped, but who could be more capable than Wen Bo?

"I'm not going to be your servant." Seeing how delighted Yu Wan was and how highly she thought of him, Wen Bo was ultimately pleased. "Don't think about ordering me around."

"I know. But if I'm in trouble, you can't just stand by and watch, right?"

"It depends on the situation."

Inside the carriage, Yu Wan and Wen Bo argued lively, but outside the side gate of the Marquis Jingyuan's manor, Chen Da Niu was as anxious as an ant on a hot pan, pacing back and forth.

chapters.title: Hard to Enter a Noble's Residence
chapters.content:
Today, Yu Wan said she would stay at Yunshui Nunnery to help prepare vegetarian meals. Chen Da Niu was not comfortable staying long in a nunnery, so he waited for her at a teahouse outside.

He waited and waited, the tea was refilled five or six times, and as the sky darkened, the shopkeeper and the waiters wanted to go home for New Year's Eve dinner and drove him out. Only then did he head to Yunshui Nunnery.

Chen Da Niu searched the nunnery twice, checking the kitchen, the charity hall, and every corner, but there was no sign of Yu Wan.

The nuns all said Yu Wan had left two hours ago, but Chen Da Niu had been sitting at the teahouse outside the whole time. If Yu Wan had come out, he would have seen her.

When Yu Wan disappeared, the nuns were anxious and helped search the nunnery thoroughly again, but still found nothing.

The only certainty was that the nun guarding the gate had not seen Yu Wan leave the nunnery.

The abbess, seeing the situation, had the nuns carefully question others in the nunnery. Finally, a woman who had been helping in the kitchen said that in the afternoon, she had been washing vegetables with Yu Wan. When she turned around, Yu Wan had vanished as if swept away by a gust of black wind.

She thought she had been squatting too long and her head was dizzy, so she didn't make a fuss.

Yunshui Nunnery enshrined Guanyin, and evil spirits would not dare to enter this sacred Buddhist place.

After much thought, Chen Da Niu felt that Yu Wan must have met with an accident.

The abbess advised him not to panic, perhaps Yu Wan had already gone home. If she wasn't found at home, then they could report to the authorities.

Chen Da Niu hurried back to the courtyard in a panic, but Yu Wan had indeed not returned.

By now, it was already dark. Ding Wenxi thought Yu Wan and Chen Da Niu were out enjoying the night market, so she had already eaten dumplings with the maids and guards and retired to her room early.

She only instructed the maids to keep the embers in the stove so they could cook dumplings when they returned.

Chen Da Niu couldn't eat dumplings; he was so worried that he paced around, wanting to wake Ding Wenxi.

The guard advised that Ding Wenxi was not in good health, so she couldn't go out to report to the authorities or search around. Waking her up would only frighten her and worsen her condition.

It would be better for them to search the city themselves first. If something serious had happened, they could report to the authorities early the next morning.

This made sense, so Chen Da Niu immediately went out with Yangquan to search separately.

However, as soon as Yangquan left the courtyard, he went to investigate and assist around the Xingguo Duke's residence. Chen Da Niu honestly searched the streets. As he watched the entire capital city being searched, and it was almost midnight with still no results, he became even more certain that Yu Wan was in trouble.

Yu Wan valued family. It was rare for her to come out of the marquis's residence for the New Year. She would never prioritize her own enjoyment and not return to spend the holiday with Ding Wenxi.

It was too late now. The government offices were already closed, so reporting to the authorities would have to wait.

Chen Da Niu thought and thought, then went to Jingyuan Marquis's residence.

He often came to look for Yu Wan, so the guards at the side gate recognized him.

Yu Wan was a person close to the heir. The heir had helped Ding Wenxi with her illness and even given them a separate courtyard. If Yu Wan was in trouble, the heir should help find her.

However, Chen Da Niu had never had direct contact with the heir and didn't dare to openly say he wanted to see him. He could only go to the side gate and ask the servant to help find Yu Xue, a maid familiar with Yu Wan.

After a while, the side gate opened, and the servant inside said to Chen Da Niu, "Yu Xue left with her mother to go home for New Year's Eve after dinner. She's not in the residence."

Chen Da Niu hadn't expected that after waiting for so long, he would hear this.

Yu Xue wasn't there... then...

Chen Da Niu then thought of Yuan Qing.

Although they weren't very familiar, Yuan Qing had picked up and dropped off Yu Wan at the inn a few times, so he at least knew him.

"Please trouble you to find Yuan Qing. Tell him that there's an urgent matter at Yu Wan's home, and ask him to come out immediately."

It was New Year's Eve, and the guard at the gate was busy gambling with others. He didn't want to run around delivering messages and looked at Chen Da Niu with annoyance.

But thinking that he was an acquaintance of Yu Wan, directly closing the gate might offend Yu Wan, so he said, "At this time, the heir is leading people to set off firecrackers at the main gate. Yuan Qing and Yuan Zhen are definitely there. If Yu Wan has an urgent matter, you should go there quickly. Maybe you can even report it directly to the heir."

With that, he closed the side gate.

Chen Da Niu had no choice but to hurry to the main gate of the marquis's residence.

The guard at the gate hadn't lied to Chen Da Niu.

Before the New Year, Zhao Xuanyou had settled his marriage. Old Lady Ye was very happy and instructed Manager Song to prepare plenty of firecrackers. When the hour of Zi arrived, Zhao Xuanyou personally lit the firecrackers, and they had been going off for a quarter of an hour without stopping.

When Chen Da Niu arrived at the main gate of the marquis's residence, he didn't see Yuan Zhen, only Yuan Qing setting off firecrackers. The servants of the marquis's residence surrounded him, watching. In front of the gate stood a young lady in brocade clothes, around seventeen or eighteen years old, also watching with a smile.

"Yuan Qing! Yuan Qing!" Chen Da Niu couldn't care about anything else and shouted.

Unfortunately, Yuan Qing had been setting off firecrackers for a long time. The constant popping sounds had dulled his hearing, and he didn't hear Chen Da Niu's voice at all. Instead, he enthusiastically lit another string.

Chen Da Niu had no choice but to rush towards him, but he was stopped by a servant beside him.

"Stay back if you're here to join the fun. Do you know where this is? How dare you barge in!"

"I'm here to find Yuan Qing!" Chen Da Niu thought of Yu Wan's life hanging by a thread and changed his words, "I'm here to find the heir. I have an urgent matter to report to the heir."

"Is the heir someone you can just see whenever you want? Don't come to the marquis's residence causing trouble on New Year's Eve." The gatekeeper said, pushing Chen Da Niu aside. Chen Da Niu stumbled and fell to the ground.

Chen Da Niu endured the pain and got up, not bothering to brush off the dust on his clothes. He continued to plead, "I am a member of Yu Wan's family. I really have an urgent matter to report to the heir. Please trouble this brother to announce it."

The gatekeeper heard him mention Yu Wan and gave Chen Da Niu another glance.

Although Chen Da Niu's skin was dark, his cotton-padded jacket was brand new and didn't look cheap. Hearing him mention Yu Wan, the gatekeeper believed him a little and scolded, "Wait here, don't move around."

"Okay."

The gatekeeper quickly ran up the steps and saw Feng Jichou standing there alone. With a smile, he asked, "Cousin, where did the heir go?"

Earlier, Old Lady Ye, the heir, and Cousin had been standing at the gate.

" The heir went to send Old Lady Ye back. He'll be back later," Feng Jichou stood there, looking down. She had also seen the small commotion caused by Chen Da Niu earlier, so she asked, "What happened?"

"That person over there is from Yu Wan's family. He says he has an urgent matter and wants to see the heir."

Yu Wan's family?

Feng Jichou gently pinched her fingers.

She naturally knew that Yu Wan had gone home early in the morning and said she would return to the marquis's residence after the New Year.

Having stayed in the marquis's residence for so long, Feng Jichou didn't have any conflicts with Yu Wan. But this time, when she returned, her mother reminded her that a maid who could tie her cousin's heart so tightly must have some tricks up her sleeve.

At that time, she didn't think much of it, but now she truly saw it.

She had only been gone for half a day and already sent someone to look for him. On New Year's Eve, she couldn't even have a moment of peace. What was she trying to do? Did she want her cousin to abandon his grandmother and fiancée to spend the New Year's Eve with her?

No matter how she thought about it, such tricks were a bit despicable.

"The heir has already retired to rest. If there's something, come back tomorrow. Don't cause trouble at the marquis's residence gate."

---

chapters.title: Leaving the City
chapters.content:
Feng Jichou had already calculated everything in her mind.

Early the next morning, Zhao Xuanyou and Old Lady Ye would enter the palace to pay respects to the emperor and empress. After leaving the palace, they would go to Baima Temple to burn incense and have vegetarian meals, then in the afternoon, they would go watch the Hua Gu drum performance. By the time they returned to the marquis's residence, it would probably be dark.

The gatekeepers were all clever people and immediately understood Feng Jichou's meaning.

"Cousin, rest assured. I won't let him come any closer."

Although Yu Wan was favored, at most she would only be a concubine. The young lady in front of her was the future mistress of the marquis's residence. It was clear who was more important.

Chen Da Niu watched anxiously as the gatekeeper went to report and then returned.

"Brother, can I see the heir now?"

"What is there to see?" The gatekeeper impatiently waved his hand. "The heir has already retired. Don't wait at the gate. Come back tomorrow."

He gave a signal, and a few more servants came over, pushing and shoving Chen Da Niu to the side.

Chen Da Niu hadn't expected this treatment. He could only shout with all his might.

"Yuan Qing! Yuan Qing!"

Yuan Qing was just lighting firecrackers and vaguely thought he heard someone calling him.

He looked up and seemed to see Chen Da Niu.

He knew Chen Da Niu had been helping Yu Wan, so he wanted to go over and ask, but the people beside him kept urging him to light more firecrackers. By the time Yuan Qing had lit all the firecrackers, Chen Da Niu had disappeared.

Yuan Qing clapped the dust off his hands and walked to the gatekeeper, asking, "Xu Er, where is the person who was talking to you earlier?"

The gatekeeper had heard Chen Da Niu mention Yuan Qing, so he assumed they were acquainted. He said, "He said there was a problem at Yu Wan's place. I said the heir was busy at the moment, so he said he would come back tomorrow."

Hearing that there was a problem with Yu Wan, Yuan Qing frowned slightly. But since Chen Da Niu was coming back tomorrow, it probably wasn't a big problem. He would deal with it tomorrow.

Chen Da Niu was driven far away from the marquis's residence by the servants. He also understood that he wouldn't be able to see the heir tonight.

Worried about Yu Wan but helpless, he could only walk back and wait for dawn to report to the authorities.

That night in the capital was filled with colorful lanterns and shimmering lights, a prosperous scene that captivated everyone.

Yu Wan and Wen Qi took turns dozing off in the carriage. As dawn approached, someone lightly knocked on the carriage door.

Wen Qi woke up alertly, lifted the curtain, and saw Yangquan, letting him in.

"How is Bingyun?" Yu Wan asked anxiously.

"You don't need to worry, Miss. He has two or three burns, but they are not serious. There is no danger to his life. However, he inhaled thick smoke, and there is no medicine that can help. He can only recover slowly."

Although Bingyun and Yangquan were Zhao Qi's guards, they were personally trained by the Duke of Ningguo.

After Bingyun was injured last night, Yangquan took him to the Duke of Ningguo's residence. Someone helped check Bingyun's injuries, and after confirming he was fine, Yangquan brought Bingyun back to the courtyard.

Bingyun currently had difficulty breathing and couldn't move much, but dealing with thieves was no problem.

"I will immediately report this matter to His Highness. I expect a reply in six or seven days. His Highness will certainly arrange someone to replace Bingyun."

The matter at the Xingguo Duke's residence was settled. With Wen Qi now helping Yu Wan, she didn't need Zhao Qi to send more people.

"The most dangerous thing is already done. With you in the capital taking care of my mother, there is no need to send more people," Yu Wan said softly. "After all, we are leaving soon."

"Miss's safety is important. You cannot be without a guard."

Yu Wan pointed at Wen Qi and smiled, "With him by my side, there won't be any problems."

Wen Qi had a special identity, and Zhao Qi had conflicts with the crown prince. Yu Wan did not intend to reveal his true identity to Yangquan and Bingyun.

Yangquan didn't know Wen Qi's background, but he had heard from Bingyun that Wen Qi had rushed into the firewood room to save his life, so he didn't suspect him.

As dawn broke, at the hour of Mao, the city gate guards opened the gates.

The commoners entering and exiting the city quickly formed a long line. Yangquan drove the carriage straight towards the city gate.

The guards were about to question them, but Yangquan showed Zhao Qi's token and instructed, "This is a secret mission from His Highness. Even if someone asks, you must not reveal it."

Since it involved the palace, the guards naturally did not dare to be negligent.

"I understand. I will not leak a single word."

With that, he didn't check who was in the carriage and waved them through.

After worrying for so long and fearing for so long, they passed through so easily.

Yu Wan felt a mix of emotions and relief.

Looking at Wen Qi, his tightly knit brows also relaxed slightly.

Their eyes met, sharing a tacit understanding of having survived a disaster.

Once they passed through this city gate, the world would be vast and open.

The carriage quickly passed through the city gate. Yu Wan had successfully escaped. Now, it was up to her mother.

That night, Ding Wenxi had gone to bed early, but she barely slept, sitting restlessly in the dark room.

It wasn't until Yangquan returned and said that Yu Wan had successfully completed the task at the Xingguo Duke's residence that she felt at ease.

Just as she breathed a sigh of relief, Chen Da Niu had disappeared somewhere.

Chen Da Niu might not be very clever, but he had always cared about Yu Wan. Who knew what he would do.

There were plenty of medicinal herbs in the courtyard. After Yangquan left, Ding Wenxi picked some platycodon, apricot kernels, poria, and angelica to make a lung-clearing soup for Bingyun. Just as she was about to send it over, she heard Chen Da Niu arguing with a maid outside.

Before going to bed last night, Ding Wenxi had specifically instructed that she had been tired from making dumplings all day and wanted to rest early, so the maids shouldn't disturb her.

Hearing Chen Da Niu's urgent voice, Ding Wenxi sighed and ordered the maid to let him in.

"Da Niu, it's New Year's Day. We should all say auspicious words. Don't be so irritable."

Facing Ding Wenxi's smiling face, Chen Da Niu couldn't say a single auspicious word.

"You... You don't know yet, but Yu Wan hasn't come back all night!"

"Didn't she go to Yunshui Nunnery with you? I thought you two were out enjoying the festivities last night."

"We did go to Yunshui Nunnery, but I couldn't wait for Yu Wan. The nuns and I searched inside and out, but we still couldn't find her."

"So you came back alone?"

"Mmm." Chen Da Niu nodded, looking distressed. "I thought Yu Wan might have come back first, but she wasn't here either. I searched the city for half the night and still couldn't find her. She wasn't at the marquis's residence either."

Hearing Chen Da Niu mention the "marquis's residence," Ding Wenxi's heart skipped a beat. "You went to the marquis's residence to look for her?"

"I did. Yu Wan wasn't there."

"Did you ask for help from the people at the marquis's residence?"

"I did. Yu Xue wasn't there, Yuan Qing ignored me, and the servants even drove me away."

As long as the marquis's residence wasn't involved, Ding Wenxi breathed a long sigh of relief. She was thinking about how to comfort Chen Da Niu when he suddenly knelt heavily in front of her and slapped himself hard on the face.

"It's all my fault. I should have stayed with Yu Wan."

Ding Wenxi was startled. Looking at his reddened face, she couldn't bear it and quickly helped Chen Da Niu up. "Da Niu, don't blame yourself. The most important thing now is to find her. Hurry and go to the marquis's residence again. Say that Yu Wan is missing and ask the heir for help in finding her."

"Shouldn't we report to the authorities?"

If they could avoid involving the authorities, that would be for the best.

"The heir is a high-ranking official. If he helps, he will definitely find Yu Wan. If he doesn't care..."

He was about to get married, with a beloved fiancée. He wouldn't care too much about Yu Wan.

If the marquis's residence knew that Yu Wan was missing, they would pretend to search for a while, and the matter would gradually die down.

Ding Wenxi was about to speak when a maid suddenly ran in. "Madam, someone from the marquis's residence has arrived."

chapters.title: Who Did It?
chapters.content:
When Ding Wenxi heard that someone from the Marquis's residence had arrived, his expression trembled.

Chen Da Niu said he hadn't seen the heir, and neither had Yuan Qing or Yingxue. The person sent by the Marquis's residence probably wasn't here because of Yu Ying's disappearance.

Ding Wenxi calmed himself slightly, his hand hidden under his sleeve clenched into a fist as he looked at the little maid. "Who from the Marquis's residence has come?"

"It's Young Master Yuan Qing."

"Invite him in."

According to the plan, at the hour of Mao, as soon as the city gates opened, Yu Ying would leave the city. Now it was a quarter past the hour of Chen, even if the Marquis's residence knew about Yu Ying's disappearance, it would be too late to find her.

Yuan Qing soon entered, and saw that the two people in the room were both acting strangely.

Ding Wenxi looked exhausted and haggard, while Chen Da Niu had half of his face swollen.

It was clear that something had happened in the residence. Yuan Qing cupped his hands in greeting to Ding Wenxi. "Madam, happy new year. Today is the first day of the new year, and the heir has sent me to deliver some New Year's gifts."

As he spoke, he handed the brocade box he had brought to the maid.

Ding Wenxi had now changed his expression, looking sorrowful, speaking in a stuttering manner as if sobbing.

"Thank the heir for me, but... but right now, I need the heir to save my life."

Yuan Qing hurriedly asked, "Yesterday, Brother Da Niu came to the Marquis's residence looking for me, but I was setting off firecrackers at that time and didn't get to talk to him. I heard there was an urgent matter at the courtyard residence. Is there anything I can help with?"

That morning, Yuan Qing had attended to Zhao Xuanyou and mentioned Chen Da Niu's visit. Zhao Xuanyou then instructed Yuan Qing to bring some gifts to the courtyard residence to see what was going on.

Ding Wenxi opened his mouth, then took out a handkerchief and turned his face away, as if wiping tears.

Yuan Qing was not Chen Da Niu. If he didn't sound sad enough, it would be easy to expose the act.

"Something has happened," Chen Da Niu stepped forward, grabbing Yuan Qing's hand. "Something really has happened. Yu Ying is missing. Please go back and ask the heir for help. Ask the heir to send someone to find her quickly."

Yuan Qing was stunned, not quite understanding Chen Da Niu's words. He looked at Ding Wenxi, but saw her continuously lowering her head and wiping tears, so he had to ask Chen Da Niu again.

"What do you mean by missing? Didn't Yu Ying come back early yesterday morning? Could it be that she never made it home?"

Chen Da Niu, with a bitter face, said, "She did come back. At noon, we even ate dumplings together lively. In the afternoon, Yu Ying and I went to Yunshui Nunnery to deliver cotton clothes. She saw that the nuns were busy preparing the New Year's Eve dinner, so she stayed to help and told me to wait at a tea house outside. After that, I never saw Yu Ying again."

"You mean, Yu Ying entered Yunshui Nunnery and never came out? She's missing?"

"Yes."

"She didn't come back all night?"

Chen Da Niu shook his head sorrowfully.

"Ah, Brother Da Niu! You! You even went to the Marquis's residence, why didn't you tell me!"

Yuan Qing knew that both the Duke of Xingguo's residence and the Eastern Palace had targeted Yu Ying before, and immediately realized the seriousness of the situation.

A whole night had passed; the worst-case scenario might have already happened.

In Chen Da Niu's mind, Yuan Qing was someone who worked closely with the heir and had been in the Marquis's residence longer than Yu Ying. He was someone who had seen the world.

Seeing that Yuan Qing was now anxious, Chen Da Niu panicked.

Ding Wenxi had been pretending to cry on the side, but seeing Chen Da Niu's change in expression, he became somewhat worried.

He had intentionally hidden the truth from Chen Da Niu to make his act more convincing.

But Da Niu was an honest man and cared deeply for Yu Ying. Ding Wenxi was afraid that if he felt too guilty, he might hurt himself. So Ding Wenxi quickly stepped forward, grabbed Yuan Qing's hand, and tearfully begged, "I don't know what happened to Yu Ying. Please ask the heir to help find her. I'm just a country woman, and in a situation like this, I'm completely at a loss. If something happens to Yu Ying, I... I don't want to live anymore."

After saying this, she seemed unable to support herself and fell backward.

"Madam!" The nearby maid and Chen Da Niu quickly held her up.

Yuan Qing, of course, was also anxious. "Madam, rest assured. I will report this to the heir immediately. We will definitely find Yu Ying."

He took a few steps forward, then seemed to remember something. He turned back, grabbed Chen Da Niu, and pulled him out.

Chen Da Niu was the last person to see Yu Ying and could certainly provide useful clues.

After the two of them ran out, Ding Wenxi slightly composed himself. He said he had a terrible headache and told the maid to help him make a bowl of calming soup.

After sending the maid away, he delivered the lung-clearing soup to Bingyun, closed the door, and continued to feign illness.

Yuan Qing and Chen Da Niu were worried about Yu Ying's safety and soon arrived at the palace gates.

By this time, the emperor had already read the New Year's congratulatory edict in the Golden Hall, bestowed a New Year's banquet to the officials, and distributed blessed meat.

Normally, Zhao Xuanyou should have come out by now, but seeing the officials coming out of the palace in twos and threes, there was still no sign of Zhao Xuanyou.

It turned out that as soon as the New Year's banquet ended, the emperor had called Zhao Xuanyou into the imperial study.

Seeing that the emperor's expression was not good, Zhao Xuanyou stood silently in front of the imperial desk, waiting for the emperor's orders.

"Do you know about the fire at the Duke of Xingguo's residence last night?" the emperor asked.

As he spoke, his voice was low, continuously looking into Zhao Xuanyou's eyes, his fingers lightly tapping the imperial desk.

The Brocade Guards monitored the officials, so Zhao Xuanyou had learned about the incident at the Duke of Xingguo's residence early in the morning from his subordinates.

Feeling the emperor's scrutiny, Zhao Xuanyou felt a sense of inexplicable confusion.

However, he calmly replied, "Last night, near the hour of Zi, a fire broke out in the firewood room of the Duke of Xingguo's residence. Two people died, and four were injured. According to the Duke of Xingguo, it was caused by servants setting off firecrackers, and the firewood room and two adjacent rooms were completely burned down."

The emperor still looked at Zhao Xuanyou meaningfully and slowly said, "Do you know who died in that fire?"

"I do not, Your Majesty."

Since the Duke of Xingguo's residence had not reported to the authorities, the Brocade Guards naturally had not sent anyone to investigate. Before entering the palace, Zhao Xuanyou's subordinates only knew this much.

The emperor slowly said, "Among the two people who died, one was your former wife, Cui Yichu."

Cui Yichu?

The person who died in the firewood room of the Duke's residence last night was Cui Yichu?

Zhao Xuanyou stood before the emperor, his face showing a slight confusion.

Not to mention that last night was New Year's Eve, and the masters of the Duke's residence would have gathered to celebrate, but Cui Yichu was a young lady of the residence. How could the fire in the firewood room have reached her?

The emperor narrowed his eyes and stared for a moment before confirming that last night's incident had nothing to do with him.

Zhao Xuanyou indeed did not know that the dead person was Cui Yichu.

"Forget it," the emperor rubbed the dragon-headed paperweight on the table, and a smile reappeared in his eyes. "Since the Duke of Xingguo said it was an accident, we will treat it as an accident. There is no need to investigate further. Today is the first day of the new year, so I won't keep you here discussing official business. You may leave."

Cui Yichu was just a woman from the inner residence, insignificant to the emperor. Whether it was an accident or a conspiracy didn't matter.

"Your servant takes his leave."

Zhao Xuanyou now understood why the emperor had specifically kept him to ask questions; he suspected that he was the one who set the fire at the Duke of Xingguo's residence last night.

However, the emperor should now know the answer and understand that this matter had nothing to do with him.

The question was, who did it?

Zhao Xuanyou turned around, frowning as he walked out of the imperial study.

A fire that could kill Cui Yichu could not possibly have been an accidental fire.

Who hated Cui Yichu that much?

And who had the ability to set a fire in the Duke of Xingguo's residence to kill her?

There were many people who fit the first criterion. As for those who fit both... it seemed only he did.

No wonder the emperor suspected him first.

As he pondered, Zhao Xuanyou walked down the steps and, lifting his head, saw Crown Prince Zhao Zun in his dignified official attire.

---

chapters.title: The Culprit
chapters.content:
After several confrontations, the two had long been at loggerheads.

Although Zhao Zun was the respected crown prince, Zhao Xuanyou, as the commander of the Brocade Guards, was summoned by the emperor daily and was the most trusted person by the emperor. Clearly, even the crown prince could not do anything to him and could only glare at him with a dark expression.

Seeing Zhao Zun's expression, Zhao Xuanyou knew that he had already learned about Cui Yichu's death and, like the emperor, had assumed it was his doing.

In fact, it was not just the two of them; everyone in the Duke of Xingguo's residence and anyone in the capital who knew about his relationship with Cui Yichu would think that he was the one who set the fire.

Zhao Xuanyou did despise Cui Yichu, and hearing of her death did feel like a release of pent-up anger.

But if he could have set fire to the Duke of Xingguo's residence directly, how could Cui Yichu have lived until now?

Looking at the crown prince's angry gaze, Zhao Xuanyou calmly cupped his hands in greeting.

"This official, Zhao Xuanyou, greets His Highness, the Crown Prince."

Zhao Zun's eyes were as cold as frost. He stepped forward and stood in front of Zhao Xuanyou, speaking in a voice only the two of them could hear. "You had already divorced her and driven her out. Did you have to go so far as to kill her?"

Zhao Xuanyou found the accusatory tone utterly ridiculous.

However, outside the imperial study, Zhao Xuanyou had to maintain the boundaries between a monarch and his subject.

"I do not understand what Your Highness is referring to."

The crown prince glared angrily. "Zhao Xuanyou, don't think that just because you are currently favored by the emperor, you can do whatever you want in the capital! The Brocade Guards are not your private army!"

"Your Highness's words confuse me. The Brocade Guards are the emperor's personal guards. Any case we handle or any arrest we make is by imperial decree."

Zhao Xuanyou did not engage with the crown prince's accusations. His voice was calm, his expression composed, and every word he spoke was reasonable.

"Are you playing dumb?" The crown prince found Zhao Xuanyou's hypocrisy infuriating. "Was the fire at the Duke of Xingguo's residence set by you? What's the matter? Are you too cowardly to admit it?"

"The crown prince speaks out of turn. The matters of the Duke of Xingguo's residence have nothing to do with me." Zhao Xuanyou sneered.

Since Zhao Zun had torn off the pretense, Zhao Xuanyou saw no need to save face for him.

He took two steps forward, getting closer to Zhao Zun.

"Compared to me, Your Highness should want her dead even more, right? After all, with her dead, no one will know about the little affair between Your Highness and her."

Zhao Xuanyou's voice was already deep, and now he deliberately lowered it further. Only Zhao Zun could hear his words.

"You are insolent!" The crown prince flew into a rage, his face turning pale from Zhao Xuanyou's words.

He and Cui Yichu had known each other since they were young and were not without affection.

He had not forced himself on Cui Yichu; their crossing of boundaries had been driven by love.

In his eyes, even if he couldn't make Cui Yichu the crown princess, bringing her into the Eastern Palace was not a difficult matter.

Who would have thought that his mother and uncle would pressure him so much, not only making him accept Jiang Ruoshuang but also refusing to give Cui Yichu the position of a concubine.

After Cui Yichu's divorce from Zhao Xuanyou, the crown prince had secretly made up his mind that when he ascended the throne in the future, free from any restraints, he would bring Cui Yichu into the palace and make amends to her.

Who could have known that at the beginning of the new year, such terrible news would come from the Duke of Xingguo's residence!

Zhao Xuanyou, the murderer, refused to admit his crime and even turned around to bite him.

In his fury, the crown prince grabbed Zhao Xuanyou's robe.

"Your Highness, the emperor has summoned you inside." The close attendant Liu Quan reminded them in a calm voice from the steps.

Liu Quan's voice was not loud, but the crown prince suddenly calmed down.

This was the imperial study; even the slightest noise would reach the emperor's ears.

No one had heard Zhao Xuanyou's insolent words, but everyone had seen the crown prince lay hands on him.

"Fine."

The crown prince had no choice but to suppress his anger and quickly walk towards the imperial study.

Zhao Xuanyou turned and continued walking out, his eyes filled with a thousand raging fires.

No one had the right to question him, let alone Zhao Zun!

Even if Cui Yichu had done many evil things and had malicious intentions, the only person she had been loyal to was Zhao Zun.

If he could have brought both Cui Yichu and Jiang Ruoshuang into the Eastern Palace back then, how could the Marquis of Jingyuan's residence have been involved in so many troubles?

The instigator was now putting on an act in front of him.

Zhao Xuanyou left the palace with a dark expression. From afar, he saw Yuan Qing leading an unfamiliar man, looking anxiously in his direction.

That morning, he had ordered Yuan Qing to go to the courtyard residence to deliver New Year's gifts to Yu Ying and her mother. Now Yuan Qing had come to the palace, looking very anxious. It seemed he had indeed encountered trouble.

"What happened?" Zhao Xuanyou quickly stepped forward, his gaze sweeping over Chen Da Niu as he asked in a deep voice.

Yuan Qing said, "Master, Yu Ying is missing."

Hearing the word "missing," Zhao Xuanyou's brows furrowed.

"Don't talk nonsense."

"Master, please save her!" Although Chen Da Niu had seen Zhao Xuanyou from a distance before, he had never spoken to him. Now, thinking that he was the only hope to find Yu Ying, he quickly knelt before him. "Please, Master, save Yu Ying. She has been missing for a whole night. Please send someone to find her quickly."

"This is not the place to talk."

There must be no noise at the palace gates, and Chen Da Niu's pleading would surely attract the attention of the palace guards.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled Chen Da Niu forward by the collar, and once they were behind the Marquis's carriage, his expression was extremely ugly.

"What exactly happened?"

Chen Da Niu immediately recounted all the events from Yu Ying's return to the courtyard residence yesterday until now.

"She just disappeared like that at Yunshui Nunnery? No one saw her?"

"Yes, it was my fault. I was sitting at the tea house outside the whole time. I don't know what happened to Yu Ying inside the nunnery."

At present, the only clue was Yunshui Nunnery. If they wanted to investigate, they had to start from there.

"Master." Yuan Ben hurried over, and seeing the situation here, he was at a loss for a moment.

Zhao Xuanyou's eyes were cold, Yuan Qing looked anxious, and Chen Da Niu next to them looked dejected. He didn't know what had happened.

He could only harden his head and say, "Uncle and his family have arrived at the palace gates by carriage. The old madam told me to come over and see. She said that since you have left the palace, you should quickly go to Baima Temple to offer incense, so as not to delay the time."

Old Lady Ye had entered the palace early with the external commanding women to pay respects to the empress and had come out half an hour earlier.

Since Zhao Xuanyou had been delayed, she had someone bring the Feng family over to save time.

Zhao Xuanyou answered irrelevant to the question. "Prepare the horses. Have Pan Xun bring ten men with me."

To find someone in the capital, no one was more convenient than those wearing the Feiyu uniform.

Pan Xun was a thousand-household commander of the Brocade Guards' Zhenfu Division, a new man promoted by Zhao Xuanyou after he became the commander. Although he was young, he was capable and reliable in handling matters.

"Yes." Yuan Qing responded and left.

Yuan Ben saw the situation and thought that something major must have happened. But he recognized Chen Da Niu.

Major cases of the court had nothing to do with Chen Da Niu.

He could only cautiously ask, "Master, you have official business to attend to here, so I suppose you can't go to Baima Temple to offer incense. I'll go back and inform the old madam."

Zhao Xuanyou responded with a hum.

Before Yuan Ben could leave, Zhao Xuanyou frowned and said, "Have someone from the Brocade Guards go and ask about the fire at the Duke of Xingguo's residence last night. Find out exactly who died in that fire."

chapters.title: It Can’t Be Her
chapters.content:
"Wasn’t the person who died last night... Madame Cui?"

Yuan Zhen hesitated, looking at Zhao Xuanyou in confusion.

Last night, when a great fire broke out at Xingguo Duke’s mansion, it was the turn of the old and new year. Firecrackers echoed across the capital, and fireworks bloomed in the sky, so no one noticed the flames at Xingguo Duke’s residence.

But early this morning, news had already spread through the capital that the fire at Xingguo Duke’s mansion had claimed the life of Cui Yichu.

Cui Yichu had been famous even before her marriage, renowned for her beauty and talent; a true paragon of both grace and intellect.

Such a celebrated beauty of the capital, after marrying into the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion, had divorced and returned home within a year. Though rumors said she had disrespected her elders, her separation from Zhao Xuanyou had long been a hot topic among the capital’s common folk.

Now, with her perishing in the mansion fire, it only added another tragic tale to the gossip mill, sparking endless speculation.

Yuan Zhen had spent the past two hours waiting for Zhao Xuanyou at the palace gates and had already heard four different theories from the idle bystanders; some said she was a doomed beauty murdered by someone, others claimed she was a discarded wife who took her own life. Each story was told with such vivid detail that it seemed plausible.

"I didn’t ask you to investigate her," Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes burned with fury, his face dark. "Find out who the other dead person is."

Yesterday, Yu Wan had gone missing at Yunshui Nunnery, and last night, Cui Yichu had died in the fire. The two incidents happening simultaneously were no coincidence.

At Yunshui Nunnery, someone had seen Yu Wan being swept away by a black gust of wind. Zhao Xuanyou didn’t believe in supernatural forces; clearly, a highly skilled martial artist with exceptional qinggong had abducted Yu Wan from the nunnery.

Last night, two people had died in the firewood shed at Xingguo Duke’s mansion. One was Cui Yichu. Who was the other, the one no one mentioned?

A terrible premonition surged through Zhao Xuanyou, and in an instant, his blood boiled.

It can’t be her.

She was so clever, so cunning. How could she possibly be dead?

"Go now!"

Hearing the rage in Zhao Xuanyou’s voice, bordering on a roar, Yuan Zhen didn’t dare delay. He hurriedly acknowledged the order and left.

By now, Yuan Qing and Pan Xun had already arrived with their men. Without a word, Zhao Xuanyou mounted his horse and led them galloping toward Yunshui Nunnery.

At that moment, Old Madam Ye and Feng Jirou were just stepping out of a jewelry shop at the street corner.

Old Madam Ye spent her days in the marquis’s mansion, vegetarian and devout, rarely setting foot outside.

Today was a rare outing. Since Zhao Xuanyou had been delayed, she had taken Feng Jirou to a nearby shop to pick out some jewelry.

Just as they finished their purchases and stepped out of the shop, a procession of Brocade Guards came galloping down the main street.

Old Madam Ye was too old to see clearly, so she only frowned slightly. "It’s the New Year, yet the Brocade Guards are still on duty. I wonder if Xuanyou is being held up by this case."

Feng Jirou had sharp eyes and had immediately recognized the man leading the procession as Zhao Xuanyou. She softly replied, "Old Madam, the man who just rode past on horseback was Cousin."

"Ah? Then he won’t be able to go to Baima Temple?"

Before the words had even settled, Yuan Zhen came rushing over.

Before Yuan Zhen could speak, Old Madam Ye sighed. "Alright, I understand."

Yuan Zhen saw the disappointment on Old Madam Ye’s face and didn’t dare say more. He simply lowered his head and delivered his message: "The Young Master has urgent matters to attend to and has ordered me to inform Old Madam that he will not be able to go to Baima Temple today."

Feng Jirou also felt a pang of disappointment, but she didn’t show it in front of Old Madam Ye. Instead, she smiled and consoled her, "Cousin is an important official of the court. His responsibilities are heavy, so even on New Year’s Day, he cannot rest."

Old Madam Ye nodded in agreement.

"He used to be at the border, only returning once a year." As she spoke, she patted Feng Jirou’s hand. "Military officers are not like civil officials; they must travel constantly. Xuanyou is able to stay in the capital now, so at least he can be seen from time to time. You, my dear, are more fortunate than your aunt."

Feng Jirou understood Old Madam Ye’s comforting intentions and lowered her head shyly.

Though Zhao Xuanyou treated Yu Wan with more affection, Old Madam Ye’s care for her meant that her future would not be bad.

She then supported Old Madam Ye toward the carriage, accompanying her to Baima Temple to offer incense.

After they left, Yuan Zhen immediately hurried to the Brocade Guards’ headquarters.

Though he didn’t know why Zhao Xuanyou was concerned about the fire at Xingguo Duke’s mansion, he had served Zhao Xuanyou for many years. From Zhao Xuanyou’s expression earlier, it was clear that something serious had happened; something very serious.

On New Year’s Day, the capital was filled with undercurrents, yet Yu Wan had already escaped the whirlpool.

She sat in the carriage, resting her chin on her hand as she admired the scenery outside.

Yangquan drove the carriage out of the west city gate, then traveled southwest for three hours before finally reaching a place with clear waters and lush mountains.

Yu Wan hadn’t asked where they were going. After all, it was just a temporary stop; she only needed to quietly wait for her mother to arrive.

Before long, Yangquan reined in the horse and stopped the carriage in front of a small farmhouse.

"Let’s go." Yu Wan called out to Wen Sun.

Wen Sun had barely slept the night before and had only dozed off briefly after leaving the city.

Yu Wan didn’t want to disturb him, so she hadn’t spoken the entire way. Only when the carriage came to a stop did she finally speak up to remind him.

Wen Sun opened his eyes and silently followed Yu Wan out of the carriage.

The farmhouse before them looked small, with only five rooms, but its location was excellent. The surrounding terrain was flat and open, and nearby, a small stream flowed. Across the stream was an orchard, though it looked somewhat barren in the depths of winter.

The area was surrounded by rolling hills; clearly a fine place nestled between mountains and water.

"Yangquan, what is this village called?"

"It’s called Jiao Ye Village. It was a tenth birthday gift from His Majesty to the Seventh Prince."

Yu Wan was slightly surprised. "This is an imperial estate?"

Yangquan nodded. "Yes, it’s an imperial estate, so no one would dare come here to search. The head of Jiao Ye Village is very reliable. I’ve already arranged everything with him. The house has food and oil, and every morning, he will deliver vegetables and meat to the doorstep, then leave without disturbing you."

After a pause, Yangquan added, "This courtyard is in a good location, with two paths in and out. If any unwelcome guests enter the village, the head will immediately come to inform you, and you can leave by the other path."

This was indeed a very thorough arrangement.

Yu Wan understood that this was Bingyun and Yangquan’s careful planning and naturally appreciated it. She cupped her hands in gratitude toward Yangquan.

"Then I’ll stay here. I’ll trouble you to take care of my mother and Bingyun."

"You’re too kind, Miss. I’m only following orders. I still need to deal with this carriage."

"Deal with it?" Yu Wan asked, confused.

Yangquan explained, "All the things you used last night were transported with this carriage. Though the items were burned in the fire, there are still traces left on the carriage. Naturally, we need to take care of that."

That made sense. This carriage had also transported a corpse.

Bingyun was injured, and Yu Wan was hiding in this village. Yangquan had too much to handle alone; it was truly exhausting. She quickly said, "Leave the carriage here. I’ll clean it."

Yangquan waved his hand. "No need to wash it. I’ll go ask the village head to help dismantle it later. We can use it for firewood and burn it. You should rest early, Miss."

With that, Yangquan jumped back onto the carriage and drove away.

After watching Yangquan leave, Yu Wan turned around and met Wen Sun’s strange gaze.

"Are they Zhao Qi’s people?"

---

chapters.title: Lying to Oneself
chapters.content:
Since she had decided to escape together, Yu Wan had no intention of lying to Wen Sun any longer.

"Bingyun and Yangquan are the guards that the Seventh Prince left in the capital at my request."

"You and Zhao Qi are that close?"

Yu Wan didn’t know how to answer.

Were they?

She had hidden everything from Zhao Qi, only hoping that he would lend her his guards. If that was considered close, then perhaps not.

But Yu Wan knew that Zhao Qi had a vague, lingering attachment to her. He had indeed been very good to her.

"He is a prince, and I am a maidservant."

This answer was incomplete. If it were someone else, they would never understand what Yu Wan meant, but Wen Sun did.

He lowered his head and smiled. "That’s true. When the Crown Prince is alone, he sometimes pulls us aside to talk about things he wouldn’t discuss with others, as if we were old friends."

But how could he, a mere guard, be friends with the Crown Prince?

"In any case, I owe the Seventh Prince a great debt, but I don’t intend to repay it." Yu Wan said with a helpless smile.

A person with nothing, whose life was as insignificant as a blade of grass, had no right to repay a prince’s favor.

All the silver she had painstakingly saved over the years probably wouldn’t even cover the cost of one meal for the masters in the palace.

"The wind is strong here. Let’s go inside to talk."

Wen Sun didn’t respond but silently followed Yu Wan into the house.

The house looked simple, but it was clearly well-maintained.

Yu Wan went into the kitchen first, tossing a few pieces of firewood into the stove, then lifting the pot to pour in water, preparing to boil some hot water for tea.

Wen Sun followed her into the kitchen and watched as she busied herself at the stove. Then he asked, "So what are you really planning? Leaving the marquis’s mansion, then coming here?"

He had agreed to follow Yu Wan because he was drawn to the kind of life she had described, not because he wanted to betray Zhao Zhen and defect to Zhao Qi.

"I’m only staying here temporarily until my mother leaves the capital."

Wen Sun’s eyes flickered, and he frowned slightly.

"And Zhao Qi?"

"Of course, I won’t let him know." Yu Wan curved her lips into a smile. "I don’t want to get involved in the affairs of the powerful anymore. I just want to live a peaceful life with my mother."

Her smile was bright, but there was a hint of helplessness in her heart.

Though she didn’t yet know what Zhao Zhen had done, she knew that his position as Crown Prince was precarious.

Zhao Qi, despite his often unfiltered words, acted with integrity and honor.

Given time, he would shed his immaturity and become a prince of both literary and martial prowess, with a balanced approach of leniency and strictness. His future was limitless.

Given Yu Wan’s status and circumstances, staying far away from Zhao Qi was the truest form of repayment.

Wen Sun had been worried that Yu Wan would take him to pledge allegiance to Zhao Qi. Hearing her say this, he finally felt at ease and stopped pressing further, instead helping to tidy up the kitchen.

Yu Wan sat on a small wooden stool, using a fire poker to stoke the wood in the stove. The flickering flames were reflected in her eyes.

She had successfully escaped the capital. She wondered how things were in the capital now.

A fire had broken out at Xingguo Duke’s mansion on New Year’s Eve, and it had claimed the life of Cui Lingyuan’s beloved daughter, Cui Yichu. Their family had always been so harmonious; everyone, from top to bottom, must be heartbroken.

As for the marquis’s mansion... Zhao Xuanyou must have heard about her disappearance by now. He wasn’t completely heartless toward her and would likely inquire about it. But with his wedding approaching, he probably didn’t have the time to investigate thoroughly. She only hoped the matter would settle quickly so her mother could leave the capital and reunite with her soon.

The ways of the world were truly mysterious.

Two days ago, she had been fast asleep in Zhao Xuanyou’s arms. Two days later, they were already parted, never to meet again.

But Yu Wan didn’t feel sad.

She had never truly possessed Zhao Xuanyou, so she couldn’t say she had lost him.

Zhao Xuanyou would soon marry, and she, perhaps, would one day meet a reliable man to marry as well.

If not, it didn’t matter. She already had her mother by her side. She wouldn’t demand anything else.

---

At Yunshui Nunnery, Pan Xun, a Brocade Guard captain, stood before Zhao Xuanyou and reported, "Sir, we have carefully inspected the perimeter walls of Yunshui Nunnery. There are traces of someone climbing over in the southeast corner."

Zhao Xuanyou had long known there was no such thing as black shadows or supernatural winds. Now, hearing that Pan Xun had found traces, his fingers instantly tightened.

"Where does the other side of the wall lead?"

Pan Xun replied, "It’s a quiet alley with only three households."

"Have you questioned them?"

"Yes, we have. Someone saw a carriage parked in the alley yesterday afternoon." Pan Xun was indeed skilled in investigations. Before Zhao Xuanyou could ask, he had already handled the matter thoroughly.

However, Zhao Xuanyou was in no mood to praise his abilities. Hearing that a carriage had been parked in the alley, he almost understood how the abduction had been carried out.

First, they entered Yunshui Nunnery to kidnap someone, then climbed over the wall, took Yu Wan into the carriage, and fled.

It was now certain that Yu Wan had been kidnapped.

But thinking of the two deaths at Xingguo Duke’s mansion last night, Zhao Xuanyou didn’t want to believe that it was someone from Xingguo Duke’s mansion who had taken Yu Wan.

Even if it was the Crown Prince, as long as she was alive, it would be fine!

Zhao Xuanyou pinched the joint of his finger, forcing himself to calm down. He only asked in a deep voice, "What kind of carriage?"

Pan Xun, hearing this question, finally showed a hint of uncertainty in his otherwise confident expression.

"We’ve had someone sketch it. It was just an ordinary carriage with green curtains; common in the capital. After leaving the alley, we asked the shopkeepers on the street, and they all said they had seen such carriages. But when we asked which direction the carriage went, everyone gave different answers."

It was clear that the shopkeepers weren’t lying. Such green-curtained carriages were too common, and every day, many of them traveled the capital’s bustling roads.

Hearing this, Zhao Xuanyou naturally understood that someone had meticulously planned Yu Wan’s abduction.

And at this moment, Zhao Xuanyou was almost certain it wasn’t the Crown Prince’s doing.

The Crown Prince was arrogant and self-important. If he wanted Yu Wan, he wouldn’t need such elaborate planning. He could simply send someone to snatch her into the Eastern Palace, and no one would dare to retrieve her from there.

Moreover, the Crown Prince had some lingering feelings for Cui Yichu. As for Yu Wan, it had only been a fleeting attraction, once it passed, he wouldn’t bother with her again.

But Zhao Xuanyou still held onto a sliver of hope.

Perhaps, aside from the Crown Prince, there was someone else who had taken an interest in Yu Wan and had been planning this for a long time, waiting for the moment she left the mansion...

Zhao Xuanyou desperately tried to convince himself, but the more he thought about it, the harder it was to justify.

"Master." Yuan Zhen rushed in from outside, approaching him with a bow.

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression jolted; he knew that Yuan Zhen had results from his investigation at Xingguo Duke’s mansion.

Who was it?

Who was the other person who died besides Cui Yichu?

Zhao Xuanyou’s mind flashed with a delicate and enchanting face, one that always wore a bright, unrestrained smile, radiant and dazzling.

It had nothing to do with her!

Zhao Xuanyou desperately tried to push Yu Wan’s face from his mind.

But as Yuan Zhen drew closer, a quiet fear crept into his heart; he didn’t want to, nor did he dare, hear what had happened at Xingguo Duke’s mansion.

chapters.title: Barging In
chapters.content:
Yuan Cui walked swiftly, and in a moment, he had reached Zhao Xuanyou’s side.

"My lord, the men sent to the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion have sent word. The mansion’s people insist that last night’s fire in the firewood shed was an accident and refuse to let the Brocade Guards enter to investigate. They are still waiting outside the mansion for your orders."

"Didn’t they find anything?" Zhao Xuanyou stared intently at Yuan Cui.

Even if they couldn’t enter the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion, with the Brocade Guards’ skills, they should have been able to uncover some information.

Yuan Cui, still unaware of the connection to Yu Wan, saw Zhao Xuanyou’s fury and quickly relayed everything the messenger had said.

"They questioned a few servants at the side gate. They all know the other corpse was a woman, but no one knows who she was."

All clues pointed back to Yu Wan.

But it couldn’t be Yu Wan.

Zhao Xuanyou’s hand under his wide robe suddenly clenched into a fist.

That morning when he left, Yu Wan had still been fast asleep on the bed.

She had wrapped herself tightly in the cotton quilt, only her head peeking out. Her fair cheeks had a hint of pink, and she looked so warm.

How could such a warm, living person become a corpse?

"My lord," Chen Da Niu, seeing Zhao Xuanyou ask about the Prince of Xingguo’s case, thought he no longer wanted to help find Yu Wan. Though intimidated by Zhao Xuanyou’s imposing presence, he mustered his courage and stepped forward. "Please, show some mercy and investigate Yu Wan’s disappearance first. She’s been missing for a whole night. If we don’t find her soon..."

Hearing this, Zhao Xuanyou’s anger flared, and his gaze fell on Chen Da Niu like a blade.

"You knew she’s been missing this long! Why didn’t you report it last night?"

"I. I did come to the marquis’s mansion to report it! But; but I was driven away." Chen Da Niu had returned to the separate courtyard last night, but he hadn’t slept all night. This morning, he had planned to go to the yamen as soon as it opened.

"Who drove you away?"

"The; the guards at the marquis’s gate."

Seeing Chen Da Niu cower under Zhao Xuanyou’s glare, Yuan Qing felt even more guilty.

The others in Yunshui Nunnery might not have understood Zhao Xuanyou’s conversation with Yuan Cui, but Yuan Qing did.

Last night, two people had died in the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion; one was Cui Yichu, and the other was an unidentified woman.

"My lord, it’s not Da Niu’s fault. It’s all my fault! Last night, I saw Da Niu being driven away, but I didn’t realize it was such a serious matter. I only reported it to you this morning. It’s all my fault! If I had reported it last night, Yu Wan wouldn’t have died!"

Died?

Chen Da Niu and Yuan Cui were both stunned.

Yu Wan was dead?

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression shifted rapidly, his eyes darkening with a terrifying chill.

The leads at Yunshui Nunnery had already run dry. No useful information would come from further investigation there.

To find out if the other female corpse was Yu Wan, he had to go to the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion.

Without a word, Zhao Xuanyou strode out, his Brocade Guards following closely behind.

Yuan Cui patted Yuan Qing’s shoulder and whispered, "It might not be Yu Wan. Don’t jump to guilt. We need to see the body to be sure; alive or dead, we’ll know for certain."

Yuan Qing wiped her tears and glanced at the dumbfounded Chen Da Niu. "Da Niu, go back to the separate courtyard and wait for news. If... if there’s any news, I’ll let you know."

With that, Yuan Qing followed Yuan Cui and the others.

It was the first day of the New Year, and the streets of the capital were bustling with activity, crowds surging like waves.

Even though Zhao Xuanyou was in a hurry, it still took half an hour of riding at full speed to reach the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion.

The gatekeeper, seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s official robes, immediately tensed and hurried inside to report.

Since Cui Yichu had died last night, and she had been divorced and separated, yet her parents were still alive, she was to be buried according to the rites for an unmarried woman; no inscribed banner, only a simple funeral.

Thus, the mansion’s front gate only had its red lanterns and couplets removed, with no other changes.

"Commander," the Brocade Guards who had been sent earlier to inquire saw Zhao Xuanyou’s arrival and quickly stepped forward, bowing respectfully. "They insist it was an accident caused by a servant in the firewood shed who got drunk and started the fire. They refuse to let us in."

The Brocade Guards answered directly to the emperor, and their investigations were usually unrestricted.

But since they had not heard of the emperor ordering a thorough investigation into the fire at the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion, and Zhao Xuanyou had only mentioned coming to identify the other female corpse, they had not forced their way in.

After all, the other party was a first-rank duke; one could not afford to offend him lightly.

After listening to his subordinates’ report, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression darkened, and he silently walked forward.

Having been a military commander for years, he carried an overpowering presence. With more than a dozen men in flying fish uniforms and embroidered spring knives following behind him, the gatekeepers did not dare to block his path.

"Sir, please stop." The mansion’s steward, having rushed over upon hearing the news, cupped his hands toward Zhao Xuanyou. "May I ask if you have a warrant from the Ministry of Justice or the Court of Judicial Review?"

The thousand-household commander Pan Xun, who stood nearby, had already noticed Zhao Xuanyou’s unusual focus on this case.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s unstable emotions, Pan Xun feared he might act recklessly and cause trouble. He stepped forward, pushing the steward aside, and reprimanded, "Are your eyes so blind that you can’t tell who we are? Since when do the Brocade Guards need warrants from the Ministry of Justice or the Court of Judicial Review to conduct an investigation?"

"If it is the Brocade Guards who have come, does that mean you are here by the emperor’s order?"

Pan Xun could see that although this steward was a servant, he was not easy to deal with.

At present, they were not acting on imperial orders. If they carelessly agreed, it would surely cause trouble later.

Just as he was thinking of how to deflect, Zhao Xuanyou grabbed the steward by the collar and coldly asked, "Where is the body?"

"Without the emperor’s decree, we cannot allow a search of the mansion."

Yu Wan’s fate was still unknown, yet this man dared to obstruct his investigation.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened, and his fingers suddenly tightened.

In an instant, the steward could not make a sound. Pan Xun and Yuan Cui, standing nearby, could almost hear the sound of the bones in the steward’s neck grinding together.

Pan Xun had only been working under Zhao Xuanyou for a little over three months, but they had been together almost daily. He deeply admired this superior of his.

He didn’t understand why Zhao Xuanyou, who was usually so composed, was acting so ruthlessly today.

Not only the servants of the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion but even his own subordinates were somewhat intimidated.

The Brocade Guards often employed extreme measures in their investigations, but those were usually done in private.

If the steward were to be strangled to death in broad daylight, it would be a serious matter.

"Daring to block the Brocade Guards. Do you have a death wish?" As a subordinate, Pan Xun could not openly advise his superior in front of others. After shouting this, he quickly grabbed another servant-like figure and threatened, "If you don’t want to die, take us to see the body now."

"Yes! Yes!"

The servants in the front courtyard of the mansion were all experienced. The Cui family’s status was high, and they could handle any official who came with ease. But they had never seen someone who would resort to lethal force so immediately.

Seeing the usually imposing steward nearly strangled to death in moments, they were so frightened that they didn’t dare to try any tricks.

"It’s in the back courtyard, in the back courtyard. This lowly one will take you there at once."

The servant led them forward, trembling.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze turned icy. He understood that Pan Xun and his subordinates thought he was acting impulsively, but how could they understand that he was already at the limit of his patience and restraint?

---

chapters.title: Blocking the Way
chapters.content:
No matter what, as long as he saw the body, he would get his answer.

Zhao Xuanyou waved his hand, tossing the steward, whose fate was unknown, to the side, and strode forward.

On the mansion’s path, the young master Cui Zaizhou, accompanied by his wife Shen Tongyun, hurried over upon hearing the news, only to collide head-on with Zhao Xuanyou.

"Commander Zhao!" Cui Zaizhou saw Zhao Xuanyou’s furious expression and knew he was not here with good intentions. He immediately stepped in front of him, cupping his hands. "Coming uninvited. Is this official business or personal?"

"What if it’s official? What if it’s personal?"

"If it’s official, please present the emperor’s warrant. If it’s personal... the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion has no relationship with Commander Zhao, so we must decline your visit."

As soon as Cui Zaizhou and Shen Tongyun appeared, the servant who had been leading them suddenly found support and quickly ran behind them. "Young Master, Madam, those Brocade Guards are unreasonable! They have no warrant but insist on forcing their way in. Manager Liu almost lost his life!"

Hearing that Zhao Xuanyou dared to harm someone in the mansion, Cui Zaizhou flew into a rage and raised his voice. "Zhao Xuanyou! Don’t think that just because you’re the commander of the Brocade Guards, you can do whatever you want in the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion. If you dare to harm someone here, we won’t fear you even if we report it to the emperor!"

Zhao Xuanyou responded with a cold laugh. "When your Cui family was causing trouble in the Marquis of Jingyuan’s mansion, you weren’t so righteous."

Cui Zaizhou, hearing the mention of Cui Yichu’s past, remembered how he had once knelt before Zhao Xuanyou. He clenched his fists tightly.

"You and our family’s grudges were settled long ago. You should know that Yichu passed away last night. The principle of divorce is that we are no longer related. Don’t you understand that?"

Shen Tongyun, standing beside him, also assumed Zhao Xuanyou had come because of Cui Yichu’s death.

She had previously learned from Yu Wan that Zhao Xuanyou’s divorce from Cui Yichu was due to her moral failings. Now, hearing her husband admit it himself...

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou and Cui Zaizhou at each other’s throats, Shen Tongyun quickly interjected, "Young Master, the deceased is gone. Past grudges should be let go with the wind. Why must you come here to humiliate us?"

Zhao Xuanyou ignored Shen Tongyun’s words, his cold gaze fixed solely on Cui Zaizhou.

"If I were you, I wouldn’t stand in the way right now... unless you have a death wish."

His arrogant demeanor showed he had no regard for Cui Zaizhou’s status as the young master.

"Zhao Xuanyou! How dare you!"

Pan Xun, listening to their exchange, realized the deep-seated grudge between the two families, and his heart grew even more uneasy.

Normally, the Brocade Guards were known for their harsh words during investigations, and Pan Xun himself was no exception; he could be even more ruthless than Zhao Xuanyou.

But Pan Xun knew in his heart that his harsh words were just for show, whereas Zhao Xuanyou...

He would actually follow through.

Beating up a steward was one thing, but if he really laid a hand on Cui Zaizhou, it would surely alarm the emperor.

Pan Xun had been promoted by Zhao Xuanyou himself and naturally did not want to see him make a mistake.

To catch the thief, first catch the king. Acting decisively, Pan Xun rushed in front of Cui Zaizhou, grabbed him by the collar, and growled, "Last night, two people died in the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion; one was Cui Yichu. Who was the other?"

"I don’t know! You hounds of the court, shamelessly humiliating imperial officials. I will make sure you are punished for this!" Though Pan Xun’s grip was tight, he had not, like Zhao Xuanyou, intended to kill. Thus, Cui Zaizhou, though restrained, could still lift his head and retort.

Hearing this, Pan Xun had his answer. Coldly, he said, "Now, a woman from another family has gone missing in the capital. The Brocade Guards suspect she died in your mansion. Since you, Young Master, admit you don’t know who the other body is, then regardless of whether the mansion reports it or not, the Brocade Guards must investigate."

Zhao Xuanyou understood Pan Xun was trying to justify their forced entry, but at this moment, he couldn’t be bothered with such formalities. What were rules and procedures compared to this?

He just wanted to find Yu Wan.

Alive, he needed to see her alive. She couldn’t be dead!

Seeing Pan Xun had restrained Cui Zaizhou, Zhao Xuanyou grabbed the servant who had been leading them earlier. Without a word, he fixed him with a stare. The servant immediately cried out, "Spare me, my lord! Spare me!"

Zhao Xuanyou was not like the pampered nobles of the capital, nor was he like Pan Xun and the other Brocade Guards.

The Brocade Guards often dealt with high-ranking officials, full of official air, bound by rules, and cautious in their actions.

But Zhao Xuanyou had spent years bathing in blood on the battlefield. His heart was as hard as stone, and countless souls had fallen beneath his sword. He had long since cultivated an aura of invincibility.

Those who caught his gaze could, in an instant, feel that murderous intent and understand that he was truly capable of killing.

"I’ll take you there at once."

Zhao Xuanyou finally released his grip and followed the servant inward.

"Stop!" Cui Zaizhou shouted, but Pan Xun, though unwilling to harm him, had no intention of letting him interfere with Zhao Xuanyou. He held him firmly in place.

Only after Zhao Xuanyou and his men had walked far ahead did Pan Xun loosen his hold.

"Bastard!" Cui Zaizhou, furious, swung a punch at Pan Xun.

Pan Xun knew he was enraged and took the blow without flinching. In a calm voice, he said, "What I said earlier was the truth. Commander Zhao did not come here for personal grudges. He is only here to investigate the identity of the other body. Once it’s confirmed, he will leave."

As he said this, Pan Xun didn’t have much confidence.

If the other body wasn’t the person Zhao Xuanyou was looking for, then there would be no issue.

But if it was...

Pan Xun didn’t dare to imagine the consequences.

He truly hoped the person who died in the mansion wasn’t the one the commander was looking for.

Fearful of what might happen, Pan Xun quickly hurried after them.

"Husband, are you alright? Were you hurt?" Shen Tongyun asked with concern.

"I’m fine."

Seeing Cui Zaizhou about to chase after Zhao Xuanyou, Shen Tongyun quickly grabbed his sleeve.

"The other person who died in the mansion last night is indeed of unknown identity. If it’s true that another family reported her missing, then the Brocade Guards coming to investigate is not unreasonable. What that man said makes sense. Let them investigate. Once it’s clear that the mansion has nothing to do with it, we can avoid giving others a chance to talk."

"No! We can’t let them go and disturb Qingyun Courtyard!" Cui Zaizhou gritted his teeth.

Qingyun Courtyard was in an excellent location. After Cui Yichu married and then divorced, the Prince of Xingguo had ostensibly left it vacant for her to stay in when she returned home. In reality, however, he had turned Qingyun Courtyard into his own treasure vault.

Uncle Tao Cheng had embezzled tribute pearls for years, selling most of the ordinary ones, but the rare treasures were mostly sent to the Prince of Xingguo’s mansion.

The Prince of Xingguo, Cui Lingyuan, had no interest in collecting antiques or calligraphy. He only enjoyed playing with jewels. In his spare time, he had used these finest pearls to make many ornaments, which he kept by his side to admire and play with.

After Cui Yichu returned to the mansion, although she still lived in the main house of Qingyun Courtyard, the side rooms were filled with the Prince of Xingguo’s collections.

Last night, Cui Yichu’s sudden death meant her coffin was temporarily placed in Qingyun Courtyard, but the treasures in the side rooms had not yet been moved.

The tribute pearl case had taken his father a great deal of effort to resolve. Now, if Zhao Xuanyou led a group of fierce Brocade Guards into Qingyun Courtyard, wouldn’t that be handing him a huge leverage?

Given the feud between the two families, Zhao Xuanyou would certainly not let this go.

"Madam, quickly send someone to find Father. I’ll go and stall for time."

chapters.title: Rampage
chapters.content:
Delay?

Shen Tongyun was confused.

Last night’s fire at the Duke’s mansion was an accident. Although no one knew why Cui Yichu and the unnamed corpse were in the firewood shed, Shen Tongyun was certain the Duke’s family had nothing to hide.

The Duke and her husband didn’t want the authorities to come because they couldn’t bear for others to see Cui Yichu’s tragic state and wanted her buried quickly.

When the Brocade Guards said they wanted to investigate the other corpse, Shen Tongyun saw no problem.

A life was at stake. What if there was more to it?

Hearing the word "delay," she didn’t understand what her husband meant to delay.

Could it be that the other person’s death was truly suspicious, and they couldn’t let the Brocade Guards investigate?

Thinking of how the Duke, Cui Lingyuan, had firmly refused to let the servants report to the authorities last night, Shen Tongyun’s heart sank further.

"Husband, is there something wrong with the fire?"
