Cui Zaizhou realized he had misspoken and quickly took Shen Tongyun’s hand, suppressing his emotions as he reassured her, "Nothing is wrong. It’s just that Zhao Xuanyou is arrogant and domineering; I fear I can’t control him. Hurry and send someone to fetch Father back."

"I understand." Shen Tongyun still trusted him.

Cui Zaizhou gently rubbed her swollen belly. "After arranging these matters, go back to your room and rest. Don’t let those rough men scare our child."

Cui Yichu had done disgraceful things at the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, and Zhao Xuanyou hated her to the bone. Soon, he would surely humiliate and curse her in front of her spirit.

The other servants were one thing, but Cui Zaizhou didn’t want Shen Tongyun to know of these ugly matters.

"Then I’ll return to my room. Husband, be careful too. They are highly skilled and the Emperor’s personal guards; don’t suffer a loss right in front of you."

The earlier scene had been terrifying. Although Shen Tongyun herself wasn’t afraid, for the sake of her unborn child, she couldn’t take risks.

"I understand. For you and the child, I will be careful." Cui Zaizhou squeezed her hand before turning and leaving in a hurry.

Shen Tongyun watched his retreating figure, but a vague unease lingered.

Since marrying into the Duke’s family, her days had been smooth and comfortable. Her parents-in-law were kind, her husband was gentle, and she had conceived soon after marriage; there wasn’t the slightest dissatisfaction.

But last night’s New Year’s Eve fire, Cui Yichu’s death, followed by the Brocade Guards’ arrival; troubles came one after another, leaving her overwhelmed.

She forced herself to stay strong and ordered the gatekeeper to find Cui Lingyuan, informing him of the Brocade Guards’ intrusion and urging him to return quickly.

Before she could even return to her courtyard, she saw her second brother-in-law, Cui Zaiting, rushing into the mansion.

"Sister-in-law, I heard something happened at home?"

Shen Tongyun nodded.

"Didn’t Father already tell the authorities it was an accidental fire?"

" The Brocade Guards said they want to investigate the other dead person. I don’t know who they are, but they’ve even alarmed the Brocade Guards to come."

Cui Zaiting’s eyes flickered, his gaze somewhat evasive.

"Where are they now?"

"They went to Qingyun Courtyard. Your elder brother said he wouldn’t let them run wild in the Duke’s mansion. I advised him not to conflict with the Brocade Guards, but I fear he won’t listen. Second brother, go quickly and stop your elder brother. Tell him a true hero doesn’t suffer immediate losses."

Cui Zaiting’s mind was elsewhere, and he didn’t take Shen Tongyun’s words to heart at all. He absentmindedly nodded before hurrying toward Qingyun Courtyard.

Inside Qingyun Courtyard, the atmosphere was indeed tense.

Madame Tao glared, standing in front of Cui Yichu’s coffin, pointing at Zhao Xuanyou as she cursed, "My daughter is already dead! While she was alive, she suffered endless humiliation at your hands. What more do you want from her?"

Cui Yichu was Madame Tao’s precious daughter, raised by her own hand. Cui Yichu’s cruelty was inherited from Madame Tao, so naturally, Zhao Xuanyou had no kind expression for such a vicious woman.

"Get out of my way."

Madame Tao, still immersed in grief from losing her beloved daughter last night, met Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze without flinching. Instead, she sneered.

"This is the Duke’s mansion. Do you think you can run wild here? Someone, throw this man out!"

The Duke’s mansion had no shortage of guards. Earlier, the Brocade Guards had barged in too quickly for the guards to gather, but now, upon hearing the news, they had rushed over from all parts of the mansion.

At Madame Tao’s command, they swarmed into Qingyun Courtyard, positioning themselves between her and Zhao Xuanyou.

Pan Xun followed into Qingyun Courtyard and, seeing the situation, loudly declared, "Madame, we are not here to inspect your daughter’s matter. Where is the other corpse that died in last night’s fire? Hand over that body, and we will leave immediately."

Madame Tao’s expression darkened as she looked at them, coldly laughing. "This is where my daughter lived. Only her coffin is here. I know nothing of some stray dog’s corpse. You’ve come to the wrong place. Get out at once!"

The body wasn’t here?

Pan Xun looked at Zhao Xuanyou, who showed no intention of leaving. After scanning the surroundings, he whispered, "Sir, it does seem like only Miss Cui’s body is here."

"Did you see the coffin?" Zhao Xuanyou asked indifferently.

"Yes."

"Five men open the coffin for inspection. Five men search the mansion. Find the other body."

The fire last night at the Duke’s mansion was definitely not an accident; it must have been deliberately set.

On the same day, Yu Wan had been kidnapped; also deliberately.

Even if Zhao Xuanyou didn’t want to admit it, he knew in his heart that these two incidents must be connected.

Although they hadn’t found the other body yet, Cui Yichu’s body was right in front of them.

As long as they opened the coffin for inspection, they would surely learn more about the fire last night.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you dare!"

Cui Zaizhou quickly rushed in from outside. Upon hearing Zhao Xuanyou’s order to open the coffin, a surge of rage shot to the top of his head, and he could no longer heed Shen Tongyun’s earlier advice to act cautiously.

He rushed up to Zhao Xuanyou and swung a fist at him.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t dodge. Instead, he caught Cui Zaizhou’s fist head-on and, with a twist of his hand, pushed him away.

He didn’t hold back, with just one push, he sent Cui Zaizhou flying far away.

"Zaizhou!" Madame Tao shrieked in panic. "Someone! Quickly, seize them! Seize all of them!"

Although the guards feared the power of the Brocade Guards, seeing their master being struck, they naturally couldn’t stand idly by. In an instant, they surrounded Zhao Xuanyou.

"Do I need to say it a second time?" Zhao Xuanyou said coldly.

Not to the people of the Duke’s mansion, but to the Brocade Guards.

"Yes!"

As the commander of the Brocade Guards, his orders were absolute.

Immediately, including Pan Xun, everyone split up to carry out their tasks. Five men lunged for the central coffin, while five others rushed out of the courtyard to search the entire mansion.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t stay idle either. Watching the swarming guards, he leapt into the air and kicked away the first one who swung a sword at him, then punched another who charged forward.

Although the guards were skilled, they were no match for Zhao Xuanyou.

Without even using a weapon, Zhao Xuanyou effortlessly defeated them, sending them flying and scattering their teeth across the ground.

Madame Tao, restrained by two Brocade Guards, saw them about to pry open the coffin and finally lost her composure, screaming madly, "The body you’re looking for isn’t in the mansion! I had it thrown to the mass grave hill at dawn. Hurry and look there. Maybe the wild dogs will have left you a bone!"

---

chapters.title: Broken Jade
chapters.content:
Madame Tao’s curses and insults did not shake Zhao Xuanyou’s resolve.

After dealing with the guards in the courtyard, he leapt up and landed directly beside Cui Yichu’s coffin.

Since it was a funeral for an untimely death, there was no outer coffin, but Cui Yichu was still the beloved daughter of Cui Lingyuan and Madame Tao. Even with just a single coffin, it was made of heavy camphor wood.

At this moment, the coffin lid had been nailed shut, and the five Brocade Guards had to exert considerable effort to open it.

Zhao Xuanyou leaned in to inspect, frowning slightly.

The corpse had clearly been drenched in oil or alcohol. In the raging fire of the firewood shed, little flesh remained; it had been burned beyond recognition.

If not for the green dress Cui Yichu loved so much, Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t have been able to associate this charred skeleton with her.

For it to be burned like this, last night’s fire could not have been an accident.

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart suddenly twisted.

All the clues pointed to the unfavorable side.

Even as he struggled to maintain his composure, his fingers suddenly went numb.

He took a deep breath and, taking a sword from one of his subordinates, used the blade to lift the clothes on the skeleton.

He wasn’t a coroner, but he couldn’t wait for one. He had to investigate as much as possible before Duke Cui could report this to the authorities.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you beast!" Madame Tao roared when she saw him touch Cui Yichu’s corpse. "Even if Yichu did something wrong in her life, she already suffered enough humiliation in your household. Now you won’t even let her rest in peace! You beast! May you die a terrible death! May your entire Jingyuan Marquis family die horribly!"

Zhao Xuanyou lifted the clothes and saw the state of the corpse; his eyebrows shot up.

The coffin contained a broken skeleton.

Not only were several ribs severed by a sharp blade, but even the spine, which supported the body, was barely connected, indicating that Cui Yichu had been fiercely hacked before her death.

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly recalled Yu Wan and Baochuan’s struggle in the dungeon. Looking at the broken ribs, it was clear; such fractures were most likely caused by an axe.

She’s still alive?!

After so long, every piece of news had been bad, but at this moment, Zhao Xuanyou’s nearly dead heart suddenly revived.

Yu Wan had always fought hard to survive. Even if she was captured, she would resist to the end!

Cui Zaizhou, who had been knocked aside by Zhao Xuanyou earlier, was now helped up by the rushing servants.

His chest had taken a punch from Zhao Xuanyou, and now his internal organs felt as if they had been shattered. Enduring the pain, he said to Zhao Xuanyou, "My mother didn’t lie to you. The body you’re looking for hasn’t been in the mansion for a long time. I’m telling the truth. Do yourself a favor. Stop tormenting Yichu and leave the Duke’s mansion at once!"

With those few words, Cui Zaizhou effortlessly shattered the faint hope that had just risen in Zhao Xuanyou’s heart.

Yu Wan was in the Duke’s mansion. Even if she had killed Cui Yichu, she couldn’t have escaped.

"Where is the other body?" Pan Xun grabbed the steward who had led them earlier.

The steward, seeing the guards scattered on the ground, was already so frightened his legs had gone weak. He shook his head and pleaded, "The mansion only has this body. I truly know nothing else!"

Pan Xun frowned. It seemed the Cui family had quietly disposed of the other body to avoid trouble.

At first, no one knew who had died in the fire. Many servants had seen two bodies carried out from the fire, which was how the news had leaked.

If not for the Brocade Guards’ arrival, the Duke’s mansion would have denied that two people had died.

Pan Xun turned to Cui Zaizhou. "Was the other body really thrown to the mass grave hill?"

"I don’t know." Cui Zaizhou said coldly. "It’s not my family’s person. Why would I care?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s long-suppressed anger finally erupted. He lunged at Cui Zaizhou. The servants beside Cui Zaizhou couldn’t stop him in time and watched as Zhao Xuanyou rained blows on Cui Zaizhou.

Cui Zaizhou staggered under the punches, instinctively raising his hands to fight back, but he was no match for Zhao Xuanyou.

Pan Xun was stunned, watching helplessly as Zhao Xuanyou pummeled Cui Zaizhou until he was covered in blood.

This was a disaster; there was no way to resolve this now.

Cui Zaiting rushed in from outside and saw his elder brother being brutally beaten by Zhao Xuanyou. For a moment, he stood frozen.

Unlike the others in the Cui family, Cui Zaiting didn’t think Zhao Xuanyou was being unreasonable or seeking personal vengeance.

A pained look flashed in his eyes as he spoke weakly, "Commander Zhao! Stop! I have the answer you want."

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at him out of the corner of his eye and temporarily stopped his fists, his bloodshot eyes locking onto Cui Zaiting.

Cui Zaiting said nothing more. He took out a handkerchief from his sleeve, unfolded it, and held up the item inside for Zhao Xuanyou to see.

It was a jade hairpin, scorched by fierce flames.

As the saying went, fine jade feared fire. The original hairpin was a fine piece of green jade, but after being burned, it had turned bone-white, its surface cracked.

Zhao Xuanyou paused slightly, staring fixedly at the hairpin.

It was one of the jade hairpins he had given Yu Wan shortly after she moved into Honghui Hall.

This particular hairpin was a vibrant spinach green, with the end carved into the shape of a leaf. It was Yu Wan’s favorite, and she often wore it in her hair, as it complemented her delicate and lively beauty.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t even need to check for the Marquis’s insignia on the hairpin; he knew it was hers.

"Where did you pick this up?"

Cui Zaiting said sorrowfully, "On the other body you’re looking for."

Last night, he had followed the crowd to help put out the fire. Before anyone had confirmed the identity of the body, he had seen this hairpin.

He had once eavesdropped on his stepmother, Madame Tao, and Cui Yichu secretly plotting to kill Yu Wan and her mother. Seeing Yu Wan’s body, he had assumed that his stepmother and sister had captured Yu Wan, brought her to the mansion, and killed her. So he had quietly taken the hairpin.

But he hadn’t expected that, apart from Yu Wan, his sister Cui Yichu had also died.

He didn’t know what had happened last night, but no matter what, Yu Wan’s death in the mansion was the mansion’s fault.

Even seeing Zhao Xuanyou injuring people in the mansion, he still felt guilty.

"You... you mean..." Zhao Xuanyou’s heart pounded violently. He stared fiercely at Cui Zaiting, shaking his head, unable to believe his words. "You picked it up."

Cui Zaiting understood his feelings. His eyes were filled with sorrow. "Commander, the person who died last night was her."

He had no real connection with Yu Wan.

Perhaps his stepmother and Cui Yichu felt the same.

But the fact that they had repeatedly tried to kill a maid they had no connection with left Cui Zaiting feeling a chill in his heart.

He couldn’t help but recall the rumors in the mansion, that his own birth mother had also fallen victim to Madame Tao’s schemes.

He had never believed it before, but after witnessing how they had dealt with Yu Wan, he couldn’t help but believe it.

"Commander, I will immediately send someone to the mass grave hill outside the city to investigate." Pan Xun, observing Zhao Xuanyou’s expression, stepped forward cautiously.

Madame Tao was wailing like a madwoman in the courtyard. Cui Zaizhou was beaten to the brink of death. The servants seemed to truly know nothing about the whereabouts of the other body. It was likely they wouldn’t find anything more in the mansion.

Zhao Xuanyou said nothing, reaching out to take the hairpin. But his fingers trembled uncontrollably.

Snap.

The jade hairpin, brittle from the fire, broke into two pieces.

chapters.title: The Handle
chapters.content:
"They're inside! In Qingyun Courtyard!"

The household guards of the Duke's mansion led the soldiers from the Military Police Office in a hurry. The captain at the front, upon seeing the dozen or so Brocade Guards standing in the courtyard, was instantly stunned.

"You... didn't you say there were thieves breaking into the mansion and injuring people?"

The Military Police Office of Wucheng was in charge of the capital's security and had always maintained a clear separation from the Brocade Guards.

Moreover, the Brocade Guards were the Emperor's personal guards. The Military Police Office was not their superior, so how could they interfere with their investigations?

The steward, who had been dragged along by Pan Xun earlier, hurried forward and begged tearfully, "My lord, please save our madam and the young master! These Brocade Guards didn't present any warrants, they barged into the Duke's mansion, and beat the young master to the point of death!"

The captain glanced at Zhao Xuanyou, who stood woodenly in the courtyard, then at Cui Zaizhou, whose face was covered in blood, and for a moment, he didn't know what to do.

Technically, if there was a disturbance in the Duke's mansion, the Military Police Office should intervene. But they were dealing with the Brocade Guards. What if they were acting on a secret order from His Majesty?

The man standing over there was the Commander of the Brocade Guards. How could a mere captain dare to intervene?

Although Pan Xun didn't recognize Yu Wan, seeing Zhao Xuanyou's expression, he understood that the person he was looking for had indeed died in the Xingguo Duke's mansion.

The longer they stayed in the mansion, the bigger the trouble would be.

At this moment, he cupped his fists towards the Military Police captain and said, "We have finished our investigation. There's no need to trouble you, brother."

"That's good, that's good." The captain didn't want to conflict with the Brocade Guards either. Hearing that they were leaving, he nodded repeatedly.

Pan Xun walked over to Zhao Xuanyou and, looking at the broken hairpin in his hand, whispered, "Sir, let's leave the mansion first. I will immediately go to the mass grave to search."

Zhao Xuanyou didn't seem to be listening, as he didn't respond to Pan Xun's words.

Pan Xun could sense that Zhao Xuanyou, like the burnt jade hairpin in his hand, had lost his vitality.

"Sir." Helpless, Pan Xun called out again.

Zhao Xuanyou slightly lifted his head and stared at him blankly.

"Let's go. To the mass grave."

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou's response, Pan Xun immediately let out a sigh of relief. He turned back to look at the devastated Qingyun Courtyard, then led the Brocade Guards to quickly retreat.

But before they could take a few steps, Cui Lingyuan, the Duke of Xingguo, arrived with a large contingent from the Military Police Office, blocking their path.

Unlike the steward who had invited a mere captain earlier, this time Cui Lingyuan was accompanied by the Commander of the Military Police Office.

Inside Qingyun Courtyard, Madame Tao was holding the dying Cui Zaizhou and weeping loudly. Cui Lingyuan, listening to the servants' reports, had a dark and cold expression.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you are lawless! How dare you bring people to barge into the Xingguo Duke's mansion and injure my son! Commander Yuan, I trouble you to arrest him!"

Although the Military Police Office's rank was not as high as the Brocade Guards, they were responsible for the capital's security. Not only were they equipped with fine crossbows, but they also had the authority to act in emergencies.

The Commander Yuan, who had come with Cui Lingyuan, seeing the situation, signaled his men to aim their crossbows at Zhao Xuanyou. "Commander Zhao, it is a fact that you barged into the mansion without cause and seriously injured a court official. It is my duty to arrest you. I hope you will surrender without resistance."

Zhao Xuanyou's expression was as dark as ink, but it wasn't because of the crossbows in front of him.

He lowered his head to look at the broken hairpin in his hand, carefully put it away, then raised his eyes and casually looked at Cui Lingyuan and Commander Yuan.

"You want me to surrender? You're not worthy."

With that, he walked straight towards the crossbows.

Zhao Xuanyou appeared composed, and although Pan Xun behind him was somewhat alarmed, he still firmly followed his commander forward.

"Where is the other body that was burned last night?"

The servants didn't know the whereabouts of that body, but Cui Lingyuan certainly did.

"Last night, there was a fire in the mansion, and only one person died; my daughter, Yichu."

As expected, he denied it.

"Cui Lingyuan, this is your only chance."

The Duke of Xingguo was furious. "Zhao Xuanyou, you seriously injured my son and committed such an outrageous act. Do you think I will let you off?"

"Step aside." Zhao Xuanyou said coldly.

The nearest crossbowman, meeting his gaze, hesitated for a moment, then carefully looked towards Commander Yuan, only to see that Commander Yuan had averted his eyes. Naturally, he didn't dare to fire.

Zhao Xuanyou raised his hand and pushed aside the crossbow aimed at his chest, then took a step forward and pushed aside the second crossbow.

"Commander Yuan, quickly order your men to shoot him!"

Although Commander Yuan had received many favors from Cui Lingyuan and had brought elite troops to suppress the situation as soon as he heard about the incident at the Xingguo Duke's mansion, killing Zhao Xuanyou was no small matter.

Zhao Xuanyou came from a noble background, was highly favored by His Majesty, and held a high position. If a sixth-rank Military Police Commander like him dared to kill the Commander of the Brocade Guards, not only would the Emperor hold him accountable, but the other Brocade Guards would dare to wipe out his entire family that very night.

"Your Grace, since they are no longer causing trouble, I cannot order my men to fire. This matter will likely require His Majesty's personal judgment. I believe His Majesty will certainly bring justice to Your Grace."

Cui Lingyuan wished he could personally shoot Zhao Xuanyou with a crossbow, but for now, he could only swallow his anger and quickly enter Qingyun Courtyard to check on Cui Zaizhou's injuries.

Hearing Commander Yuan's words, the crossbowmen lowered their weapons and made way for the Brocade Guards.

Zhao Xuanyou did not linger and strode out.

---

In the Eastern Palace, Crown Prince Zhao Zun sat at his desk but had no mood to read.

Zhuang Huaiyue sat beside him, seeing his restless appearance, and gently massaged his shoulders.

"Your Highness, it's not auspicious to frown on New Year's Day." Zhuang Huaiyue said softly.

"Even on New Year's Day..." The Crown Prince gave a cold laugh. "There's not a single good thing happening, but bad things keep coming one after another."

First, Cui Yichu was burned to death last night. Then, early in the morning, the dark guards reported that Wen Luo had suddenly disappeared. After that, he encountered Zhao Xuanyou in the palace, who had the audacity to threaten him right in front of the Imperial Study.

This bastard!

"Your Highness, don't say that," Zhuang Huaiyue tilted her face and kissed his chin. "This year, the Eastern Palace will have one more person. That is a good thing, isn't it? One good thing in the Eastern Palace will surely lead to a second and a third."

Thinking of the child in Zhuang Huaiyue's womb, the Crown Prince forced a smile, but he had no mood to speak.

"Your Highness." A eunuch hurried in.

The Crown Prince frowned. "Has Wen Luo returned?"

The eunuch shook his head.

The Crown Prince slammed the table hard. Wen Luo had been by his side for many years, always dutiful, and he had grown fond of having him attend to him. How could he suddenly disappear?

"Could it be that Zhao Xuanyou has made a move against both Yichu and Wen Luo?"

The more he thought about it, the more possible it seemed.

If Zhao Xuanyou could kill Cui Yichu, it showed that he was a vengeful man, and it was very possible that he had also taken revenge on Wen Luo.

The eunuch whispered, "Zhao Xuanyou has indeed done another deed."

"What?"

"He broke into the Xingguo Duke's mansion, pried open Cui Yichu's coffin, and severely injured the young master, Cui Xingzhou."

"This beast!" The Crown Prince cursed angrily.

But a moment later, a smile appeared on the Crown Prince's face.

"Zhao Xuanyou, Zhao Xuanyou, you have finally given me a handle to use against you!"

---

chapters.title: Reporting to the Emperor
chapters.content:
Zhuang Huaiyue was naturally surprised by the eunuch's report.

From what she had seen in the Jingyuan Marquis's mansion, Zhao Xuanyou had been very calm after his divorce from Cui Yichu and had shown great affection for Yu Wan, without revealing the slightest bit of feeling for Cui Yichu.

How could he go to the Xingguo Duke's mansion to pry open a coffin?

This kind of hatred could be described as bone-deep.

"Yue'er, you were right. Good things will keep coming to the Eastern Palace." The Crown Prince said, then hugged Zhuang Huaiyue and kissed her.

Zhuang Huaiyue quickly composed herself and smiled at the Crown Prince. "Your Highness is blessed by the heavens and has boundless fortune."

"You rest in the room. I will go to the palace. Tell the kitchen to prepare more dishes for tonight."

"Yes." Zhuang Huaiyue replied obediently.

Since she became pregnant, she could no longer serve him at night and had been worried that the Crown Prince might favor another woman.

Although the Crown Prince had summoned other women to his bed, he often called her to keep him company in the study during the day.

Gradually, she had also figured out his temperament. He liked women who were skilled in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting, and were gentle and obedient. Therefore, in front of him, she never disobeyed and always did things according to his wishes.

"This concubine bids Your Highness farewell."

The Crown Prince hurried out of the Eastern Palace and went straight to the Imperial Study.

As the heir apparent, he was announced by the eunuchs as soon as he arrived at the Imperial Study and was quickly ushered in.

As soon as he entered the Imperial Study, he saw Prime Minister Sun also present, having just finished discussing state affairs with the Emperor.

"Why have you come again?" The Emperor looked at the Crown Prince's enthusiastic appearance, let out a slight sigh, and asked with a sinking face.

The Crown Prince, oblivious to the Emperor's mood, solemnly bowed to the Emperor and recounted Zhao Xuanyou's atrocities of breaking into the Xingguo Duke's mansion, prying open Cui Yichu's coffin, and assaulting the Duke's heir.

These were all facts, but he slightly altered the cause and effect, saying that Princess Yi'an and Cui Yichu had always been close. It was said that their divorce was because Zhao Xuanyou had favored a concubine and neglected his wife, and Cui Yichu couldn't bear it anymore, so she initiated the divorce. Who would have thought that Zhao Xuanyou held a grudge and couldn't let it go even after her death.

"Father Emperor, I think last night's fire at the Xingguo Duke's mansion was suspicious. It's very possible that Zhao Xuanyou sent someone to start the fire."

Although the Emperor was past his prime, he was not yet senile.

He had heard about Zhao Xuanyou and Cui Yichu's divorce, though he wasn't particularly interested. But he knew it was due to Cui Yichu's disrespect to her elders, something the Cui family couldn't deny.

If Zhao Xuanyou was in the wrong, how could the Cui family have tolerated it until now?

"Prime Minister, according to the law, how should an act like Zhao Xuanyou's; randomly breaking into a minister's mansion to assault and humiliate an official. Be handled?"

The Brocade Guards acted as the Emperor's personal investigators, and in the past, they had often done such things, but those were always done covertly, in the dark of night. It was rare to see such a blatant act in broad daylight.

However, Prime Minister Sun was an old fox after all. Knowing that the Emperor favored Zhao Xuanyou, he said, "This matter does sound suspicious. Perhaps the Brocade Guards were acting on a royal decree to investigate a major case and had to enter the mansion to search. However, the Xingguo Duke's mansion is the descendant of a founding meritorious official. To barge in and injure someone in broad daylight is indeed inappropriate."

The Emperor's eyebrows twitched slightly.

Compared to the Crown Prince's shallow schemes, Prime Minister Sun's words were much more tactful.

If it was indeed by royal decree, then it was justified. If the Xingguo Duke's mansion resisted the decree, then they deserved the beating.

But if there was no royal decree, then it was the Brocade Guards abusing their power and acting lawlessly.

Come to think of it, the Emperor had not expected Zhao Xuanyou to barge into the Xingguo Duke's mansion, assault someone, and pry open a coffin.

Earlier that morning, when asked about the fire at the Xingguo Duke's mansion in the Imperial Study, Zhao Xuanyou had been composed, with measured actions, as if he were completely uninvolved.

How could he, as soon as he left the palace, act so recklessly?

Everyone knew that the Brocade Guards were his personal guards. The court officials had long been dissatisfied with the Brocade Guards' excessive power.

For the Commander of the Brocade Guards to barge into the home of a high-ranking official, desecrate his deceased daughter, and injure his eldest son, who knew how furious the civil and military officials would be.

It was fortunate that it was the spring holiday; otherwise, tomorrow his desk would be piled high with memorials impeaching Zhao Xuanyou and demanding restrictions on the Brocade Guards.

"I did not order the Brocade Guards to search the Xingguo Duke's mansion." The Emperor stated.

Prime Minister Sun's eyes flickered slightly, and he said gently, "Commander Zhao has always been steady in his actions. Perhaps he has uncovered a new case involving the Xingguo Duke's mansion, and due to the urgency, he had to go there to verify."

"Regardless of the reason, rashly acting and causing serious injury is wrong. Since the Brocade Guards are my personal guards, I will thoroughly investigate. If it is indeed due to personal grudges that he barged in and injured someone, I will severely punish him."

Hearing the Emperor's words, the Crown Prince was taken aback and quickly stepped forward. "I am willing to share Father Emperor's burdens and assist in investigating this matter."

Ever since Zhao Xuanyou returned to the capital, he had repeatedly opposed the Crown Prince.

Although the Crown Prince had tried his best to find a handle on Zhao Xuanyou, he had never succeeded.

This was because Zhao Xuanyou was meticulous in his actions and skilled in managing his subordinates, leaving no room for error.

Now, Zhao Xuanyou had handed him such a big handle by barging into the mansion and injuring someone. His guilt was as certain as a nail in a coffin. The Crown Prince naturally did not want to miss this opportunity and wanted to personally arrest him and see him become his prisoner.

The Emperor raised an eyebrow and looked at the Crown Prince, feeling a surge of disappointment once again.

If the Crown Prince had not known about the Empress and the Duke of Zhen Guo's schemes before, and had been forced onto their ship of illegally minting weapons, he might have had some hesitation and struggle between his loyalty to the Emperor and the Empress.

But now, his mind was solely focused on dealing with Zhao Xuanyou, without a thought for father-son bonds or national duty. The Emperor was truly disheartened.

There's no saving him. He's beyond saving.

He let out a heavy sigh. "The court officials have always had objections to the Brocade Guards' investigations. Since Zhao Xuanyou has committed a serious error, let the Ministry of Justice, the Court of Judicial Review, and the Censorate jointly investigate. Sun Congdao, you will oversee this."

"Your servant accepts the decree." Prime Minister Sun respectfully replied.

The Crown Prince felt a deep sense of disappointment, but then he thought that Prime Minister Sun was not close to Zhao Xuanyou. Especially since Zhao Xuanyou was close to Pei Ta, and Pei Ta had recently offended Prime Minister Sun, it was unlikely that Sun would go easy on him.

With this thought, he felt a bit better.

At this moment, the Chief Eunuch Liu Quan stepped forward. "Your Majesty, the Duke of Xingguo has arrived at the palace gates and requests an urgent audience."

Noticing that the Emperor did not wish to see the Duke of Xingguo, Prime Minister Sun timely interjected, "Your Majesty has countless duties and should rest early. I will go to the palace gates now and inform the Duke of Xingguo about Your Majesty's decree for the three judicial offices to investigate Zhao Xuanyou. I will tell him to return home and await news."

Prime Minister Sun had stood firm in the court for many years, and naturally, he had his reasons for doing so.

The Emperor nodded. "Tell him that I already know of his grievances. Send an imperial physician with him to check on his son."

"Your Majesty's benevolence is a blessing to the officials and the people."

After the Crown Prince and the Duke of Xingguo had left, Liu Quan looked at the Emperor, who was deeply frowning, and stepped forward. "Commander Zhao doesn't seem like the type to act impulsively. Perhaps there is more to this matter?"

"What more could there be? He shouldn't have acted like this!" The Emperor angrily retorted.

The court officials had long been dissatisfied with the Emperor's use of the Brocade Guards to monitor them. Now, Zhao Xuanyou had handed them such a big handle, even making the Emperor lose face.

Originally, he had high hopes for Zhao Xuanyou, but in the end, he turned out just like Pei Ta; brilliant but lacking in experience.

After a pause, the Emperor added, "Later, you personally go to the prison and ask him what happened."

chapters.title: Losing Composure
chapters.content:
"Eunuch Liu, please."

The imperial prison of the Ministry of Justice was a place specifically for detaining high-ranking officials. Since most of the prisoners here held prominent positions, the cells were not shabby. Each had a table, chairs, and a wooden bed. A small window was even carved into the thick stone walls, ensuring it wasn’t pitch black during the day.

After attending to the Emperor’s bedtime routine, Liu Quan changed into plain clothes and left the palace under the cover of night, making his way to the imperial prison.

The guard officer, holding a lantern, personally led Liu Quan deep into the corridor until they finally saw Zhao Xuanyou, who was imprisoned alone.

"Minister Zhao, Eunuch Liu is here to see you," the Ministry of Justice official reminded.

Zhao Xuanyou was a special case. Even though he had been imprisoned today, the Ministry had not neglected him, placing him in the cleanest and most secluded cell.

Upon seeing Liu Quan, the Emperor’s most trusted eunuch, visiting the prison late at night, Zhao Xuanyou understood that his position was not in jeopardy. His tone became even more amiable.

Zhao Xuanyou had been sitting with his back to the wall. At the sound of voices, he seemed to tuck something into his sleeve before turning around. Upon recognizing Liu Quan, he lowered his gaze again.

"You’ve gone to great trouble." Liu Quan waved his hand dismissively.

The Ministry official understood and had the guards bring a chair for Liu Quan to place in front of the cell door. He lit a few nearby wall lamps before respectfully withdrawing.

The dim cell brightened instantly. Liu Quan said softly, "Minister Zhao, His Majesty is very disappointed in you."

"It is this subject who has failed His Majesty’s trust."

Though he spoke these words, Liu Quan could see that Zhao Xuanyou remained calm, seated in the cell without a trace of panic. His eyes held a strange emptiness, as if he were spacing out rather than regretting his impulsive actions.

Earlier that day, Zhao Xuanyou had been stopped by the Ministry of Justice officials at the city gate.

He was not surprised.

The crossbowmen of the Military Command had been deployed, so it was only natural that the news reached the palace.

He followed the Ministry officials into the prison, secretly arranging for Pan Xun to leave.

"Eunuch Liu, I have matters to attend to. I cannot stay here indefinitely."

Upon hearing this, a faint smile appeared on Liu Quan’s face.

So he still wanted to leave; he hadn’t completely lost his mind.

"What for? To beat up the rest of the Xingguo Duke’s household?"

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent.

He had to find out what happened to Yu Wan. If the Xingguo Duke’s household had indeed harmed Yu Wan, he would not let this matter rest.

Liu Quan observed Zhao Xuanyou’s expression and asked, "What exactly happened? If you don’t explain clearly, I cannot help you."

A faint smile tugged at Zhao Xuanyou’s thin lips.

How could he explain clearly when he didn’t even know where Yu Wan’s remains were or what had happened to her before her death?

Regardless, he had to get out of prison as soon as possible.

Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath, stood up, and walked to the cell door. He took something from his sleeve and passed it through the bars to Liu Quan.

It was a pearl hairpin. A large pearl was surrounded by five slightly smaller ones, resembling a lustrous white flower.

Liu Quan took the hairpin and squinted to examine it.

Having spent years in the palace, his eye was sharp. Not only was the central pearl rare, but the five surrounding ones were also treasures seldom seen in the world.

"Pearls of this size and roundness should all be in the palace. Where did Minister Zhao find this?"

"In Cui Yichu’s coffin."

Liu Quan pondered for a moment before smiling. "It seems the tribute pearl case needs to be reinvestigated."

"After we entered the Xingguo Duke’s residence today, Cui Zaizhou did everything to obstruct us. There must be many such pearls in the duke’s residence. My forced entry today has already alerted them. Cui Lingyuan will surely try to move them."

Liu Quan remained silent but nodded.

Zhao Xuanyou said, "If His Majesty allows a search of the Xingguo Duke’s residence, I can recommend Pan Xun to lead the investigation."

"Pan Xun is indeed capable," Liu Quan said, waving the hairpin in front of Zhao Xuanyou. "I will relay Minister Zhao’s words to His Majesty. Before leaving the palace, His Majesty specifically mentioned that Minister Zhao acted too impulsively today. Stay here and calm your mind."

Calm his mind?

Zhao Xuanyou’s brows suddenly furrowed.

"Eunuch Liu..."

Liu Quan waved his hand again, his words heavy with meaning. "His Majesty is doing this for your own good."

The Jin Yi Wei held a special status. Zhao Xuanyou’s forced entry into the duke’s residence as the commander of the Jin Yi Wei, resulting in injuries, had already sparked outrage among the civil and military officials.

Even if the tribute pearl case was used as justification for the intrusion, the officials would never accept it.

To them, the Jin Yi Wei already held too much power and was a department that should not exist.

Of course, the Emperor would not truly suppress the Jin Yi Wei and reduce his own power.

Keeping Zhao Xuanyou imprisoned for a few more days served both as punishment for his impulsive actions and to appease the officials.

Zhao Xuanyou said nothing more. He merely clenched his fists and turned back to face the wall.

Liu Quan sighed softly, tucked away the hairpin, and left the prison.

---

"What? Zhao Xuanyou was arrested?"

Ding Wenxi looked at Yangquan in astonishment after hearing his words, unable to believe it.

Yangquan nodded. "It’s true. He was already locked up in the Ministry of Justice prison yesterday."

"What did he do wrong?"

"After he went to Yunshui Nunnery to look for Yu Wan, he went straight to the Xingguo Duke’s residence. When the duke’s household refused to let him in, he forced his way inside."

So it was because of Yu Wan.

Ding Wenxi thought for a moment and said, "He’s the commander of the Jin Yi Wei. Even if he forced his way in, they wouldn’t arrest him, would they?"

"Apparently, there was a conflict inside the residence with the Xingguo Duchess and the young master, Cui Zaizhou. I heard he ordered people to pry open Cui Yichu’s coffin and search the body. He even severely injured the young master."

"He beat someone up?"

Yangquan nodded. "Now the Xingguo Duke’s household is in chaos. I heard the duchess has gone mad, and Cui Zaizhou is on the verge of death."

Ding Wenxi had met Tao Shi before.

At the Xingguo Duke’s estate, Tao Shi had put on the full airs of a duchess, saying she wanted to take Ding Wenxi back to live with them. Though her words were polite, Ding Wenxi knew she was not someone to be trifled with.

"And where was the Xingguo Duke?" Ding Wenxi asked.

"He wasn’t at the residence when Zhao Xuanyou forced his way in."

Ding Wenxi gave a bitter smile and asked, "Did they find Yu Wan’s ‘body’ in the end at the duke’s residence?"

"No," Yangquan said in a low voice. "Now the Xingguo Duke’s household claims that only Cui Yichu died in the fire that night. They don’t know where the other body is."

"They neither admit to the arson nor to the death of an outsider in the fire, as if they’re afraid of officials coming to investigate."

Yangquan listened to Ding Wenxi’s words and, after a moment of thought, found them reasonable.

These mother and daughter were incredibly clever.

"That’s true. Who knows what they’re hiding in the duke’s residence."

Ding Wenxi didn’t know either.

Cui Lingyuan and Tao Shi’s daughter had tried to kill Yu Wan multiple times. Ding Wenxi felt that Yu Wan’s retaliation had been too light and naturally had no sympathy for them.

But Zhao Xuanyou had been arrested and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice for trying to find Yu Wan, awaiting trial by the Three Courts. This was truly beyond Ding Wenxi’s expectations.

Yu Wan had always said that Zhao Xuanyou treated her no differently, that he only kept her around because his wife was unworthy and he had no other women to serve him.

But now it seemed that Yu Wan held a far more significant place in Zhao Xuanyou’s heart.

For Yu Wan’s sake, Zhao Xuanyou had forgotten his status and lost his composure.

---

chapters.title: Hiding It from Her
chapters.content:
"Madam, now that Zhao Xuanyou is in prison and the officials are in an uproar, it might be some time before he can get out. Should we take action sooner?" Yangquan asked.

Ding Wenxi withdrew her thoughts and said calmly, "We still can’t rush. After all, Yu Wan only met with trouble a couple of days ago, and her body hasn’t been found. Others may accept that she’s dead, but as her mother, I can’t. We’ll have to wait a little longer."

"I understand."

"There’s one more thing I need to trouble you with," Ding Wenxi said.

"Madam need not be polite. Just give your orders."

"Da Niu doesn’t know that Yu Wan faked her death. He’s wracked with guilt. Since I’m pretending to be ill, I can’t comfort him. Please help reassure him so he doesn’t blame himself too much."

Chen Da Niu was indeed a straightforward man. When the people from the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence came to deliver the news last night, his face had lost all color.

If Ding Wenxi hadn’t pretended to faint, and if he had tried to comfort her while barely holding himself together, he might have slapped himself again.

Yangquan naturally knew of Chen Da Niu’s guilt and nodded. "Madam, rest assured. I’ll find a way to comfort him."

"I’ve finished making the lung-clearing soup for Bingyun. Take it to him."

The side courtyard had no floor heating, so they usually relied on charcoal braziers for warmth, making it convenient to cook soups and congee.

"Thank Madam on Bingyun’s behalf."

Ding Wenxi sighed. "He got smoke inhalation while trying to help Yu Wan. As her mother, it’s only natural I should make amends."

Yangquan took the bowl of soup and then remembered something else. "Madam, tomorrow I will go to the Jiao Ye Manor to see how Yu Wan is settling in. Is there anything you’d like me to take to her?"

Living at the Imperial Manor, she would want for nothing in terms of food and drink. Now that Bingyun was injured, all the tasks had fallen to Yangquan. Ding Wenxi didn’t want to trouble him too much.

After a moment’s thought, Ding Wenxi opened the trunk Yu Wan had brought back. Inside were all of Yu Wan’s books.

She flipped through a few pages and saw the neat, forceful annotations, clearly written by Pei Tao.

"I’ll have to stay at least ten days or half a month before I can leave. Take her a few books so she won’t be bored."

"Got it." Yangquan took the books in one hand and the bowl of soup in the other.

Just as he was about to leave, Ding Wenxi remembered something else.

"One more thing."

"Madam, please give your orders."

"Don’t tell Yu Wan about Zhao Xuanyou’s imprisonment."

Although Ding Wenxi believed Zhao Xuanyou had feelings for Yu Wan, Yu Wan had already left. Telling her this would only add to her worries.

Yangquan was slightly taken aback but quickly understood. "Understood. But what if Yu Wan asks about him?"

Yu Wan was intelligent and not easily fooled.

Ding Wenxi smiled helplessly. "If she really asks about Zhao Xuanyou, then tell her the truth."

"I understand." Yangquan respectfully took his leave.

At that moment, in the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, Old Madam Ye had just learned of Zhao Xuanyou’s imprisonment in the Ministry of Justice prison.

"Does the young madam know about this?" Leaf Mo Cong, the fourth young master of the Anning Marquis’s residence, saw the sudden change in Old Madam Ye’s expression and immediately sensed something was wrong.

Old Madam Ye slammed her armrest and stamped her foot in agitation.

"How dare they hide such a big matter from me! Quickly, call those two good-for-nothing brats, Yuan Qian and Yuan Qing!"

When she flew into a rage, Madam Xing immediately rushed to Honghui Hall to bring Yuan Qian and Yuan Qing over.

Old Madam Ye’s face was ashen. "You’ve all grown bold, thinking this old woman’s eyes are too dim to see, huh? How dare you hide such a big matter from me!"

Yuan Qian quickly cupped his hands. "It’s not that this lowly one dared to deceive Madam. It’s just that yesterday, the young master specifically ordered us not to disturb Old Madam with this matter. We dared not disobey the young master’s command."

Feng Jirou was also shocked to hear that Zhao Xuanyou had been imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice. She had intended to say something comforting, but her nervousness made her words stumble.

"How could he be arrested? What crime did Cousin commit?"

Old Madam Ye also looked at Ye Mo Cong.

Ye Mo Cong, hearing that Zhao Xuanyou had ordered them not to tell Old Madam Ye, didn’t know where to begin. He could only offer empty reassurances. "Since Big Brother said so, he must have a plan. It’s probably not a big problem."

Though he offered comfort, Ye Mo Cong himself didn’t believe it.

If it had escalated to a trial by the Three Courts, how could he be released after just a couple of days?

"I’m fine. For now, he’s only in prison. Since there hasn’t been a trial, there’s still room to maneuver." Old Madam Ye was no ordinary old woman. Though surprised, she tried to maintain her composure. She looked at Yuan Qian and Yuan Qing. "When did this happen?"

"Yesterday."

Old Madam Ye was taken aback. "Why wasn’t I informed yesterday?"

Yuan Qian lowered his head. "After the young master was taken away by the Ministry of Justice officials, they initially said it was just for questioning. It wasn’t until nightfall that we heard he had been detained."

Since the matter had already reached Old Madam Ye, there was no point in hiding it any longer.

Old Madam Ye was not an ignorant woman. Perhaps she could still find a way to help the young master. Yuan Qian then recounted the entire sequence of events.

"Yu Wan went missing?" Old Madam Ye looked at Yuan Qian in disbelief. "On New Year’s Eve?"

Yuan Qian nodded. "On New Year’s Eve afternoon, Yu Wan disappeared at Yunshui Nunnery. That night, a fire broke out at the Xingguo Duke’s residence. The young master found it suspicious and went to the duke’s residence to inquire."

"Did Yu Wan really die in the fire like Cui Yichu?"

"Yes."

Old Madam Ye’s emotions were complex as she furrowed her brows in deep thought.

Zhao Xuanyou had lost his composure over Yu Wan’s disappearance, forcing his way into the Xingguo Duke’s residence, prying open coffins, and assaulting people. This was undeniable guilt, which infuriated her.

But now was not the time for anger.

If the Xingguo Duke’s household had indeed killed someone in the capital, even if Yu Wan was just a servant of the marquis’s household, the fault lay with the Xingguo Duke’s household first.

As long as this could be proven, Zhao Xuanyou should be able to escape punishment.

"Currently, is there any evidence related to Yu Wan in the duke’s household?"

"It’s not that there’s none. On New Year’s Eve night, almost all the servants in the duke’s household were busy fighting the fire. Many saw two bodies carried out from the fire scene. Although the Xingguo Duke is trying to cover it up, if we question more people, there must be someone who saw Yu Wan’s body."

At this point, Yuan Qing wiped his tears.

"The servants of the duke’s household initially said there were two bodies, but after the Xingguo Duke arrived, they stopped admitting it. The young master found Yu Wan’s hairpin at the fire scene, but it had already been burned brittle. It’s all my fault! On New Year’s Eve night, when Chen Da Niu came to the marquis’s residence looking for someone, I saw him, but I still let him be driven away. If it weren’t for me, the young master could have saved Yu Wan on New Year’s Eve."

Old Madam Ye was confused by Yuan Qing’s words and didn’t think deeply about them. However, Feng Jirou’s expression suddenly changed.

So... that person who came to the marquis’s residence on New Year’s Eve looking for Cousin was because Yu Wan had gone missing?

The gatekeeper drove him away not because of Yuan Qing, but because of her.

Feng Jirou’s heart pounded violently.

Cousin cared deeply about Yu Wan; far more than she had ever imagined.

He had even gone to the duke’s residence to assault people and ended up in prison, all for the sake of finding Yu Wan.

If Cousin found out that she had prevented Yu Wan’s friend from delivering the message, leading to Yu Wan’s death at the Xingguo Duke’s residence, would he spare her?

chapters.title: Taking Responsibility
chapters.content:
Feng Jiyou never expected to be entangled in Yu Wan’s life-and-death situation.

Beyond the shock, what she felt more was fear.

As she stood beside Lady Ye, the elder noticed her body trembling violently and immediately frowned.

The Jingyuan Marquis’s household was not the kind of family that clung to power. When arranging marriages for their children, they did not only consider status.

Otherwise, Lady Ye would not have chosen a wife from a scholarly family for the Marquis back then.

But the mistress of the Marquis’s household must have a resolute character.

Zhao Xuanyou was in the imperial court; who knew how many storms he would face in this lifetime? Yet, after he was thrown into prison for just one day, Feng Jiyou was so frightened that she was shaking.

If she couldn’t handle such a small matter, how could she bear the responsibilities of the mistress of the Marquis’s household in the future?

Originally, Lady Ye had quite liked her obedience and gentleness, but at this moment, that bit of goodwill vanished in an instant.

However, now was not the time to dwell on such matters. After a moment of thought, Lady Ye had already made a decision.

"Yuan Cui."

"At your service."

"Take stock of the people in the Marquis’s household. Don’t let them idle around; have them go out immediately to search for Yu Wan’s whereabouts."

Yuan Cui replied in distress, "Yesterday, the young master sent people to the charity cemetery and the mass grave to look for Yu Wan’s remains, but they found nothing. I really don’t know how to search."

The day before Zhao Xuanyou was arrested, he had specifically instructed Pan Xun to act separately. Thus, Pan Xun had not only checked the mass grave but also the charity cemetery. However, no matching body was found.

"Since the person disappeared in the Xingguo Duke’s mansion, we should naturally search around there. Check the shops and residents around the front courtyard and back gate, one by one."

"Wouldn’t it be better to have the Brocade Guards investigate?"

Lady Ye narrowed her eyes, thought for a moment, then shook her head. "Xuanyou wore the Feiyu uniform to barge in and beat someone up, which greatly offended His Majesty. We cannot use the Brocade Guards to investigate anymore; we have to handle this ourselves."

"But we are not officials; how can we investigate?"

"Money can make the devil turn the millstone. If you take silver to their door and ask, won’t they tell you? If you’re short on money, ask Manager Song for it." As Lady Ye spoke, she glanced at the weeping Yuan Qing and scolded, "Stop sniveling! Hurry up and do as I say."

"Yes." Yuan Cui and Yuan Qing retreated from the Leshou Hall together.

Listening to Lady Ye’s arrangements, Ye Mo Fan immediately felt deep respect for her. "Aunt, you truly are a heroine among women. With you in command, Big Brother will surely return safely."

"You little..." Even during the New Year, encountering such a matter, Lady Ye felt bitter inside. "Don’t flatter me at a time like this."

She was old; all she wanted was to eat vegetarian meals, chant sutras, and seek peace.

Who would have thought that her usually steady grandson would cause such a disaster, and her future granddaughter-in-law would be as timid as a mouse? It truly gave her a headache.

"I’m not flattering you; I genuinely admire you."

"I’m old and useless. I need to quickly write a letter to Xuanyou’s father and have him return."

The Jingyuan Marquis was plagued by injuries and illnesses, which were especially painful in the winter, so he rarely returned to the capital.

But now that Zhao Xuanyou had become a prisoner, they had no choice but to call him back.

If he returned, perhaps His Majesty would show some leniency toward Zhao Xuanyou out of respect for his military achievements.

---

Yu Wan had spent three days at the Shuoye Village, counting on her fingers.

Although she swept the courtyard, cooked, and took walks every day; there were plenty of things to do, and it had a certain rural charm; she still found it incredibly boring.

Glancing up, she saw Wen Ji lying on the dry trunk of a jujube tree in the courtyard, basking in the sun, and couldn’t help but sigh softly.

Unlike Yu Wan, Wen Ji enjoyed daydreaming and was perfectly content living here.

Just as she was watching him, he suddenly looked back at her.

"Someone’s coming," Wen Ji said.

"Didn’t the village head just deliver vegetables this morning?"

"It’s Zhao Qi’s subordinate."

After saying that, Wen Ji turned his face away again, closed his eyes, and continued sunbathing.

Soon after, someone knocked on the courtyard gate. Yu Wan opened it and indeed saw Yangquan standing there.

"Please, come in."

"Miss Yu Wan." Yangquan entered the courtyard carrying two large packages.

Yu Wan took them and placed them on the table. Opening them, she found one package contained snacks from the capital, and the other held the books Pei Tao had given her.

"You brought my books!" Yu Wan exclaimed joyfully, holding the books.

Having books was wonderful; she could spend the whole day reading without feeling the time drag.

"It was the madam who ordered me to bring them over."

Mother really understood her.

Yu Wan set the books down and looked at Yangquan. "How has my mother been these past few days?"

"Madam is doing well. However, Big Brother Niú has been feeling guilty about what happened to you, so Madam has had to keep up the act, staying in her room all day and eating very little."

"It’s been hard on my mother. If only we could leave the capital sooner."

"And what about Bingyun? Is he better?"

Bingyun had inhaled thick smoke while saving Yu Wan, so these past few days, aside from worrying about Ding Wenxi’s safety, Yu Wan had also been concerned about Bingyun’s injuries.

"He’s much better now."

In the first couple of days, Bingyun had difficulty breathing. Although his mind was clear, his movements were sluggish.

After drinking lung-clearing soup for several days and resting in his room, he had recovered a great deal.

"That’s good."

As Yu Wan spoke, she took a bag of chestnut cakes from the package and called out to Wen Ji on the tree, "Catch!" before throwing it to him.

Wen Ji caught it with one hand, didn’t thank her, and started eating while sitting on the tree.

"Yangquan, you have some too."

Yangquan waved his hand. "Miss, there’s no need to be polite. I don’t care for these. Besides, I can eat them anytime in the capital."

"Then I’ll have them myself." Yu Wan said, eating a piece of ten-color candy.

Yangquan was about to breathe a sigh of relief when he suddenly heard Yu Wan speak again.

"How is the Marquis’s household?"

Sure enough, she had asked.

Yangquan took a deep breath and tried his best to appear calm. "Nothing major has happened. It’s just that when the heir went to the Xingguo Duke’s mansion to inquire about your whereabouts, a conflict arose with the people there."

Yu Wan had always known Zhao Xuanyou was extremely intelligent and meticulous.

Even though she had made thorough preparations at the Yunshui Nunnery, Zhao Xuanyou would inevitably connect the fire at the Xingguo Duke’s mansion to her.

"How did the conflict happen?"

"The Brocade Guards found that two people died in the fire at the Duke’s mansion, but the Xingguo Duke’s household refuses to acknowledge the two deaths, only admitting that Cui Yichu died. They claim the fire was an accident."

"So, Zhao Xuanyou hasn’t found my body yet?"

"No."

So that was the case.

Yu Wan found it puzzling. She had knocked out the people in the firewood room, poured wine there, and even overturned a large water vat. It was clearly arson, so why did the Xingguo Duke’s household call it an accident? Could it be that they had something to hide and were afraid of an official investigation?

But none of that concerned Yu Wan anymore.

She smiled slightly. "It’s better that they didn’t find it. That way, they won’t discover any flaws from the body."

"Exactly. Without getting past the Xingguo Duke’s household, the Brocade Guards can’t investigate further. You’ve finally escaped safely."

"Thanks to you and Bingyun."

Seeing that she didn’t suspect anything, Yangquan secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

Although Ding Wenxi had said that if Yu Wan asked, he should tell her about Zhao Xuanyou’s imprisonment, after receiving the secret order from the Seventh Prince last night, Yangquan had changed his mind.

The Seventh Prince had ordered them to ensure Yu Wan left the capital. If Yu Wan found out about Zhao Xuanyou’s predicament, she might hesitate out of soft-heartedness, and that would be disastrous.

"Miss Yu Wan, the Seventh Prince has written you a letter."

---

chapters.title: Reply
chapters.content:
Zhao Qi had actually written her a letter.

Yu Wan was slightly surprised. Seeing Yangquan hand it over, she smiled and accepted it, not opening it immediately but tucking it into her sleeve.

"If you want to reply, just give it to me."

Although the prince was young, Yangquan understood how much the prince valued Yu Wan.

The fact that he had sent a letter from so far away suggested he was eagerly awaiting a reply.

"I know." Yu Wan said lightly, neither confirming nor denying.

"Bingyun is injured, so I was worried you might not have anyone to order around. I specially arranged for another brother to come to Shuoye Village to protect you."

Even though Wen Ji was there to protect Yu Wan, Yangquan didn’t fully trust him due to his unclear background.

Since the prince had given strict orders to protect Yu Wan at all costs, he couldn’t feel at ease without one of his own men stationed at Shuoye Village.

"Has he arrived?"

Yu Wan didn’t want too many people around her.

Yangquan nodded. "He’s already at the village, but he has some other matters to attend to right now. He’ll come over later."

Yu Wan looked troubled. "Having an extra guard is good, but there are only three rooms here. My mother will be coming over in a few days. Even if it’s temporary, having four people stay here might be inconvenient."

When they had been looking for a place to stay, they had prioritized secrecy. Three rooms were just enough for Yu Wan, her mother, and Bingyun.

Now that Wen Ji occupied one room, adding another person, a grown man, would indeed be inconvenient.

Yangquan naturally understood her concerns and quickly reassured her. "Don’t worry, Miss. For now, the village head has arranged for him to stay elsewhere in Shuoye Village. In the future, if everything is peaceful here, he won’t disturb you. He’ll just patrol the surroundings occasionally. To be honest, I don’t think there will be any trouble. No one can trace us here."

Zhao Xuanyou had been arrested, so who could possibly track them down to Shuoye Village?

As soon as the words left his mouth, Yangquan realized he had almost slipped up and quickly added, "After all, this is an imperial farm."

"That’s true." Yu Wan didn’t think much of it.

They still had to wait for her mother at Shuoye Village. Having an extra guard would be more reassuring; better safe than sorry.

"Almost forgot, last time you mentioned wanting the Jiangnan Customs and Landscapes. I included it in that pile of books."

"Let me see."

Yu Wan moved aside a few copies of the Four Books and Five Classics and indeed found the book Yangquan had mentioned.

This time, when leaving the capital, Yu Wan had told Zhao Qi they were heading to Jiangnan, so she had asked Bingyun and Yangquan to find some books about the customs and landscapes of Jiangnan. Previously, they had been too busy planning for New Year’s Eve to find the time, but now that the situation was settled, Yangquan had bought two copies of Jiangnan Customs and Landscapes from the market the day before.

"Thank you."

As they were talking, someone knocked on the courtyard gate again. Yangquan went to open it, and the other guard was standing outside.

After exchanging greetings, Yangquan and the guard left the small courtyard.

Wen Ji sat up from the tree trunk, watching Yu Wan as she flipped through the Jiangnan Customs and Landscapes with a thoughtful expression. He couldn’t help but ask, "Are you really going to Jiangnan?"

"Let’s go there first." Yu Wan looked at the ink-wash drawings of the water town landscapes in the book and praised, "Jiangnan is indeed a wonderful place. I’ve never seen such beautiful scenery."

Hearing her say that, Wen Ji jumped down and stood beside her, looking at the book with her.

"You’ve never been to Jiangnan either?"

Wen Ji shook his head.

Two years ago, the Crown Prince had toured Jiangnan but hadn’t taken him along.

The two of them silently flipped through the book for a while before exchanging a glance.

"Then... should we go and have a good look around?" Wen Ji asked.

"Anyway, we’ve left the capital. We can go wherever we want." Yu Wan pointed to the Grand Canal in the book and smiled slyly. "The book says Jiangnan’s waterways are interconnected. Once we’re in Jiangnan, after we’ve had our fill of sightseeing, it’ll be convenient to go to other places as well."

"Can we take a boat there?"

"Sure, I’ve never been on a boat before."

In the past, when Yu Wan had lived in the village with her mother, life had been simple, facing the yellow earth and turning her back to the sky.

In the capital, although life had been better, due to her mother’s status and illness, she had never had the chance to explore the city.

Now that they had left the capital, her mother no longer had to live so cautiously and could go out more.

"Exactly. We can hire a boat and travel south all the way, then enjoy ourselves in Jiangnan."

"And after we’re done sightseeing?" Wen Ji looked at the drawing of a tavern in the book, as if an idea had struck him. "You mentioned before that we could do some business. A tavern doesn’t seem bad."

Yu Wan couldn’t hold her liquor and didn’t like drinking, so naturally, she didn’t want to open a tavern.

"Not a tavern. I don’t want a bunch of drunks swaying in front of me."

Wen Ji glanced at the pastries on the table. "Then you must want to open a pastry shop?"

"That’s not impossible, but I don’t know how to make pastries."

"This won’t work, that won’t work."

Yu Wan teased, "You’re so capable. Why don’t you do it yourself?"

She had meant it as a jab, but he took it seriously and pondered for a moment. "I could just sell wine. Whoever wants to buy it can take it away directly."

"Do you know how to brew wine?"

Wen Ji nodded.

So he actually knew how to brew wine.

He was clearly a secret guard, yet he enjoyed daydreaming and brewing wine. No wonder he wanted to leave the Eastern Palace.

"You’d be suited to selling wine. After all, with your martial arts skills, no one would dare cause a drunken scene in your shop."

"And what about you? Have you even thought about doing business?" Wen Ji suddenly asked. "Are you just thinking about how to shake them off once we get to Jiangnan?"

By "them," he naturally meant Yangquan and Bingyun.

Yu Wan blinked and unconsciously smiled. "I wouldn’t say I’ve figured it out yet. I haven’t been to Jiangnan, so I don’t know the best way to act. We’ll see when we get there. Besides, I have you."

These past few days, although Yu Wan had nothing to do, she had thought about many things.

"I can’t take on two people by myself." Wen Ji pouted.

"Then there’s also me."

"True, you’re more troublesome than I am."

Now that they were more familiar with each other, their conversations had become even more casual.

Hearing this, Yu Wan immediately glared at him. "How dare you insult me? You’re not allowed to eat my pastries anymore."

Wen Ji let out a soft "Oh" and, with lightning speed, snatched a copy of the Jiangnan Customs and Landscapes from the table, along with a bag of chestnut cakes, before quickly retreating back to the tree.

Lying on the tree, reading and eating at the same time, was much more enjoyable than just daydreaming.

A cold wind suddenly blew, and Yu Wan shrank her neck. After eating some pastries and flipping through the book for a while, she finally took Zhao Qi’s letter out from her sleeve.

She stared at it for a moment before finally opening it.

The letter had been written by Zhao Qi half a month ago. Life in the military camp was much harder than he had imagined, especially when they went out to sea. The huge waves would crash over the ship, making it sway so much that it felt like the world was spinning.

Fortunately, after going out a few more times, he had gradually gotten used to the rocking and no longer got seasick.

At the end of the letter, he told Yu Wan that even if the plan failed, it wouldn’t matter; he still had a way to take her away.

As she read the letter, Yu Wan could almost imagine the expression on Zhao Qi’s face as he wrote those words, and she unconsciously curved her lips into a smile.

She folded the letter and put it back into the envelope.

She would write a reply to Zhao Qi when it was time to leave.

chapters.title: Breaking Off the Engagement
chapters.content:
"Lord Zhao, people from the Marquis's mansion have come to see you."

The prison guard of the Ministry of Justice led Lady Ye and Ye Moquan to Zhao Xuanyou's cell door and politely called out.

Zhao Xuanyou, who had been sitting cross-legged on the wooden bed, opened his eyes upon hearing the voice.

"Grandmother." Seeing the elderly Lady Ye had come to the prison, Zhao Xuanyou quickly walked to the cell door, feeling somewhat guilty. "How could you, at your age, come to a place like this?"

"In the capital, only you and I, grandmother and grandson, rely on each other. Now that you're in prison, how could I sit still?"

Lady Ye's face was filled with worry as she carefully examined Zhao Xuanyou.

He had been stripped of his imposing commander's uniform and was wearing only a coarse brown robe, looking truly down and out.

"Today, it was also Mo Han who arranged for us to get in to see you."

Ye Moquan said, "Big brother, my aunt and I have brought you some clothes and food."

As he spoke, he pushed the prepared bundle through the iron bars.

The items had been carefully inspected by the prison guards, and only after extra silver was given were they allowed to bring them in.

Zhao Xuanyou took the bundle and placed it on the table, then cupped his hands to Ye Moquan. "Mo Han, thank you for taking care of Grandmother."

" We are brothers, no need to say such things." Ye Moquan knew that the two of them had words to exchange, so after delivering the items, he tactfully said he would wait outside for Lady Ye.

After Ye Moquan had walked away, Lady Ye, with reddened eyes, said earnestly, "Xuanyou, you are the child I raised myself. Storming into a mansion and injuring someone is not something you would do."

Zhao Xuanyou gave a bitter smile.

Indeed, it was not something he would do.

If someone had told him before New Year's Eve that he would do such a thing, even he himself would not have believed it.

But he had done it.

"All for Yuxuan?" Lady Ye sighed heavily.

Yuxuan...

During his days in prison, Zhao Xuanyou had tried his best not to think about this name.

He desperately tried to figure out how to help Pan Xun establish himself in the Jin Yi Wei, how to get out of prison as soon as possible, and how to bring down the Xingguo Duke's mansion. He tried not to think about Yuxuan.

He didn't dare to.

Just thinking about this name felt like a thorn piercing his heart, making it impossible for him to think or breathe.

Only by desperately ignoring this thorn could he barely maintain his composure.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou's dark expression and silence, Lady Ye felt a mix of emotions.

She had seen this expression on Zhao Xuanyou's father's face before.

When her daughter-in-law had died, the Marquis of Jingyuan had looked just like this.

She had wanted to arrange a good marriage for Zhao Xuanyou, but unexpectedly, Zhao Xuanyou had followed in his father's footsteps.

Forget it, the most urgent matter now was to get Zhao Xuanyou acquitted as soon as possible.

"If Yuxuan really died in the Xingguo Duke's mansion, you going there to investigate the case was not wrong, but you went too far with your actions. I have already sent Yuan Qu and Yuan Qing with people to inquire around the Xingguo Duke's mansion to see if anyone saw them disposing of the body."

Although several days had passed, Zhao Xuanyou still found it hard to associate Yuxuan with a corpse.

Clearly, on the night before New Year's Eve, when he had returned late at night, he had held her, fast asleep, and whispered to her for a while.

She had been so delicate, so warm. How could she have become a corpse?!

No.

Lady Ye watched as a fierce look appeared in Zhao Xuanyou's eyes.

She had long noticed his feelings for Yuxuan. She had repeatedly hinted and warned him, hoping he would clarify the positions of wife and concubine to avoid future disasters in the family.

Who would have thought that Yuxuan would die so tragically... As the saying goes, the dead cannot be brought back to life. Her death had only made it harder for Xuanyou to let go.

He couldn't even bring himself to say her name.

"I will have them continue investigating," Lady Ye had to change the subject. "But since you dared to have Yuan Qu and Yuan Qing hide things from me, you must have a backup plan, right?"

Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath. "Grandmother, rest assured. I have made arrangements with the Jin Yi Wei."

"You've only been in the Jin Yi Wei for a few months. It's good that you have useful people there."

Indeed, the Jin Yi Wei was full of talented individuals, especially Pan Xun, who was very capable.

"Once this matter is settled, I can no longer stay in the Jin Yi Wei."

Perhaps, even before the matter was settled, the emperor would dismiss him from his post.

Lady Ye was well aware of the twists and turns in the court. The officials had long been wary of the Jin Yi Wei. This time, Zhao Xuanyou, wearing the Feiyu uniform, had given them a handle, and they would not let him off easily.

It was not just about staying in the Jin Yi Wei; Zhao Xuanyou would find it difficult to stay in the capital at all.

"It doesn't matter. At worst, we can return to the Mingzhu Guard."

Listening to Lady Ye's words, Zhao Xuanyou lowered his eyes. "It is your unfilial grandson's fault."

"You have a backup plan, so I am at ease. On the second day of the New Year, I have already sent someone to deliver a letter to your father by fast horse. I suppose he is already on his way back to the capital by now. Once he returns, you and he can handle the troubles of the court yourselves."

She was old, a woman, and truly did not have the energy or the convenience to run around for Zhao Xuanyou.

After a pause, Lady Ye said, "You need not worry about the affairs at home."

Mentioning this, Zhao Xuanyou spoke, "About my marriage to my cousin..."

Before he could finish, Lady Ye frowned. "Mo Han said your case is to be tried by the three courts. The Ministry of Justice will keep you imprisoned for at least one or two months. Your wedding to Jichou was originally set for March. There is no reason to get married right after getting out of prison. Go back and discuss with the in-laws to postpone the wedding date."

"There is no need to postpone."

Lady Ye looked at Zhao Xuanyou's expression and already understood his intentions.

When she learned that Zhao Xuanyou had lost his composure and stormed into the mansion to injure someone because of Yuxuan, Lady Ye had already suspected this.

Tonight's prison visit only confirmed her earlier suspicions.

This chapter is not yet finished. Please click on the next page to continue reading the following exciting content!

There was not the slightest tone of consultation in his voice; it was clear that he had made up his mind.

If she were ten years younger, she would have given him a good scolding, asking him if he had considered the reputation of the Marquis's mansion when he acted impulsively for a woman.

As the heir of the Marquis's mansion, defending the territory was his duty, and continuing the family line was also his duty.

To cause so much trouble for a woman. Was this worthy of his ancestors?

But she was old, too old to discipline or control him.

"Marrying Jichou was your idea. Now that you don't want to marry her, it is also your own decision. I will convey your wishes to your uncle and aunt. When you get out of prison, you can go apologize to them yourself."

After standing in the cell for so long, Lady Ye was also tired.

Seeing that Lady Ye was about to leave, Zhao Xuanyou said, "Grandmother, your grandson has one more request."

" I've even helped you break off the engagement. What more do you want?"

Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath.

The Ministry of Justice prison was heavily guarded, and it was not convenient for him to send messages out. Some things had to trouble Lady Ye.

"Yuxuan..."

Yuxuan again.

Lady Ye glanced at him and waited helplessly for him to continue.

"Yuxuan and her mother relied on each other. Now that something has happened to her, I should take care of her widowed mother on her behalf."

"How do you plan to take care of her? Are you going to bring her to the Marquis's mansion to show filial piety?"

"Yuan Qu and Yuan Qing know where she lives. Grandmother, after you return to the mansion, instruct them to visit her and see if there is anything she lacks."

Yuxuan was the most filial to her mother.

Presumably, what she would worry about the most was her mother.

At the moment, the only thing he could do was to take good care of her only relative.

Lady Ye looked at Zhao Xuanyou's expression and sighed again.

"I understand."

---

chapters.title: Arranging Posthumous Affairs
chapters.content:
"Madam." A maid knocked on the door. "People from the Marquis's mansion have come."

Ding Wenxi was in the room organizing things. Upon hearing this, she stopped and sat on the bed, asking hoarsely, "Who has come?"

"It is Yuan Qu, who serves the Young Master."

"If it's to deliver things, there's no need to accept them. Just thank them on my behalf."

"The servant has already told him that Madam is too grief-stricken to receive guests. He did bring many things, but he said he wants to see Madam and has some words to say in person."

Ding Wenxi had been feigning illness for more than ten days and had planned to leave the capital after the New Year.

Originally, she did not want to have any more contact with the Marquis's mansion, but upon hearing that Yuan Qu insisted on seeing her, she feared there might be changes on their side. After much consideration, she said, "Please ask him to come in and speak."

"Yes."

The maid complied, and Ding Wenxi got off the bed, unfolded the screen in the room, and sat back on the bed.

Soon, Yuan Qu entered the room and stood outside the screen, bowing to her.

"Madam, this humble servant has been sent by our Old Lady and the Young Master to visit you. We hope you will take care of yourself and cherish your health."

"Please convey my thanks to your Old Lady and the Young Master."

These days, Ding Wenxi had deliberately stayed up at night, eaten less, and drunk less water, so her complexion was poor, her spirits were low, and her voice was hoarse. She looked every bit the part of someone overwhelmed with grief.

Yuan Qu said, "The Young Master has sent some household items for Madam. Please rest assured and stay in the courtyard residence. In the future, if you need anything, just send someone to the Marquis's mansion to find me."

"It is rare for the Young Master to be so kind, but I lack nothing. I only want to know where Yuxuan is." Ding Wenxi's voice became choked as she spoke.

Yuan Qu had worked with Yuxuan at Honghui Hall and had always been on good terms with her.

Yuxuan's body had not been found yet, but after disappearing for so long, she must have perished.

He could only lower his head and say softly, "Madam, please take care of yourself."

Ding Wenxi gave a bitter laugh. "She is my daughter. Everyone else can take care of themselves, but I cannot get over it."

Yuan Qu, hearing this, could only remain silent.

Ding Wenxi continued, "Please trouble you to convey a message to the Young Master. Yuxuan received much kindness from him while she was alive. As her mother, I am too embarrassed to trouble the Young Master any further. In a few days, I will leave the capital."

"Madam, you are leaving the capital?" Yuan Qu was slightly surprised and quickly advised, "Where can you go alone? Our Young Master is a man of his word. He will definitely keep his promise and take care of you for Yuxuan's sake."

"I do not doubt the Young Master, but my poor daughter... we don't even know where her body is. She is still a lonely ghost. I have heard that the masters at Wutai Mountain can light the Wheel of Reincarnation Lamp. I want to go and ask the great master to light a lamp and hold a memorial service for Yuxuan to help her reincarnate soon into a wealthy family."

As she spoke, Ding Wenxi covered her face and began to sob.

"It takes at least one or two months to travel from the capital to Wutai Mountain. Madam, you have just recovered from a serious illness. The journey is long and arduous. It is truly not advisable."

"This is the only thing I can do for Yuxuan in this lifetime." Although her voice was soft, her tone was firm.

At the moment, Zhao Xuanyou was locked in prison and unable to send messages. Yuan Qu, as a servant, had no way to intervene, so he could only try to persuade her.

"The weather is still cold. Madam, please wait until spring when it warms up before setting out?"
