"Every day I stay in the capital is torture for me." Ding Wenxi's voice became even more choked. "In the future, if Yuxuan's body is found, please ask the Young Master, for the sake of Yuxuan's past devoted service, to bury her properly."

"That goes without saying. The Young Master... will definitely find Yuxuan."

Yuan Qu knew better than anyone that Zhao Xuanyou could have left the Xingguo Duke's mansion unscathed that day. It was only because Cui Zaizhou had insulted Yuxuan that he had severely injured him.

Ding Wenxi got up from the bed and, separated by the screen, bowed to Yuan Qu. "On Yuxuan's behalf, I thank the Young Master for his great kindness. I have no use for the things sent by the Marquis's mansion. Please trouble you to take them back."

"I am just a servant. My master ordered me to deliver these things, so I can only deliver them, not take them back. Madam, please take care of yourself."

Yuan Qu took an envelope from his sleeve and placed it on the table with both hands, then silently retreated.

After Yuan Qu had left, Ding Wenxi picked up the envelope. Inside were 500 taels of silver, presumably the household expenses Yuan Qu had mentioned earlier.

Even in prison, Zhao Xuanyou had thought to take care of her. It was rare.

"Madam."

Ding Wenxi snapped out of her thoughts and saw Yangquan standing at the door. "Come in."

"What did the people from the Marquis's mansion say?" Yangquan closed the door and asked respectfully.

"They sent silver and tonics. They said it was the Young Master's intention."

Yangquan had specifically gone to inquire and learned that Zhao Xuanyou was in serious trouble this time. His subordinates in the Jin Yi Wei were desperately gathering evidence to help him clear his name. However, with Prime Minister Sun leading the joint investigation by the three courts, it would be difficult to resolve the matter easily.

Just as he was wondering what to say, Ding Wenxi spoke, "Yuan Qu came at just the right time. I have already told him that I want to go to Wutai Mountain to pray for blessings and summon Yuxuan's soul. This way, the Marquis's mansion has an explanation."

"Madam wants to leave the capital as soon as possible?"

Ding Wenxi nodded.

Previously, staying in the capital was to keep up the act and deceive everyone.

Now, the Xingguo Duke's mansion was not pursuing the arson incident, and Zhao Xuanyou was locked in prison, unable to protect himself.

There was no need for her to continue this charade.

Even if leaving was a bit rushed, no one would pay attention to such details.

Even if Zhao Xuanyou cared, by the time he got out of prison, it would be at least one or two months later. By then, she and Yuxuan would already be far away.

"It's for the best. It will prevent any unforeseen complications."

With the Seventh Prince protecting them, Yuxuan and her mother would naturally be able to leave safely.

"I have already packed everything I need to bring. We will set out the day after tomorrow."

"This subordinate will go prepare."

After Yangquan left the room, Ding Wenxi called Chen Da Niu over.

The act of Yuxuan's fake death had been a grand performance. Among the heartbroken people in the capital, besides Zhao Xuanyou, there was also Chen Da Niu.

Ding Wenxi had been pretending to cry in the room, but Chen Da Niu had been genuinely crying.

She got straight to the point. "Yuxuan's body is gone, and she is a lonely ghost. I plan to go to Wutai Mountain to light a Wheel of Reincarnation Lamp for her and hold a memorial service."

"Good. When do we leave?"

"Tomorrow."

Although Chen Da Niu was surprised, he blurted out, "Then I will go pack my things."

"Da Niu, you don't need to come with me."

"Then... then you're going alone?"

"I'm not going alone. I will bring the mansion's guards." Seeing Chen Da Niu's worried expression, Ding Wenxi softened her voice. "You stay in the capital and look after this mansion for me. They are outsiders, and I don't trust them."

"This..."

This reason was hard to refute, so Chen Da Niu could only nod.

"I don't know when I will return from this trip. You live comfortably in this mansion. If anything changes in the future, the deed to the house is in the drawer of that dressing table. Do as you see fit."

Yuxuan had told Ding Wenxi that during her most difficult times, only Chen Da Niu had taken care of her.

Ding Wenxi had considered selling this mansion to get more silver for Chen Da Niu.

But Zhao Xuanyou seemed to have feelings for Yuxuan, and selling the mansion right after his imprisonment would be heartless. It would be better to leave it for Da Niu to live in. Da Niu would not refuse, and this way, it would be a perfect solution.

Chen Da Niu waved his hands repeatedly. "I can help you guard the house, but there's no need to leave the deed to me."

"It's already there. Whether you want to live here or get married and have children in the future to liven up the place, Yuxuan would be happy for you."

chapters.title: A Thousand Sails
chapters.content:
Two days later, the sky was clear. The snow that had fallen the night before at Jiaoye Manor had melted under the winter sun, and droplets from the eaves pattered down like rain.

Knowing her mother would arrive today, Yuhan had specially asked the manor steward for two more charcoal braziers.

As she was adding charcoal, Wen Bo announced from outside, "They're here."

Yuhan quickly put down the tongs and hurried out.

Yangquan was still driving the carriage. Yuhan lifted the curtain and saw Ding Wenxi, whom she hadn't seen in days, inside.

"Mother!"

Yuhan was overjoyed.

She had done everything in her power to plan a fake death and escape, but the only person she couldn't stop worrying about was Ding Wenxi.

Now that mother and daughter were reunited, the huge weight in her heart finally settled.

But seeing her mother's familiar, gentle smile, like a long-lost sunlight on a gloomy winter day, her heart relaxed, and her nose tingled with emotion.

After all that planning, she had finally managed to leave the capital with her mother safely.

"Silly girl."

Ding Wenxi held her hand and stepped down from the carriage, then pulled her into an embrace.

"Miss Yuhan." To her surprise, Bingyun also jumped down from the carriage.

"Bingyun, are you alright?" Yuhan asked joyfully.

Bingyun cupped his fists in greeting to Yuhan. "I'm fine now. I'm sorry for worrying you, Miss."

"You were injured saving me."

Bingyun said, "It was my failure that put you in danger."

That night in the firewood shed, Bingyun had accidentally inhaled thick smoke and nearly lost consciousness. Fortunately, Wen Bo had rescued him from the fire in time, so he hadn't suffered any lasting damage.

After more than half a month of recovery, he was about 70-80% healed. He had volunteered to escort Yuhan and her mother south again.

Yangquan knew Yuhan had been feeling guilty about this, so he brought Bingyun along.

"They say it's colder when the snow melts than when it snows. Let's go inside to talk."

Yuhan supported Ding Wenxi into the house and brought a stool for her to sit by the charcoal brazier.

After she was seated, Yuhan immediately tucked a hand warmer into her hands.

Seeing her daughter so filial and obedient, Ding Wenxi's regret over forcing Yuhan to leave the capital because of her own identity lessened slightly.

She took Yuhan's hand and placed it on the hand warmer as well.

"You look well. It seems you've been happy here at the manor."

"Thanks to the books you sent, otherwise I'd be bored to death staying here every day."

Wen Bo helped carry the trunks Ding Wenxi had brought inside, then left, returning to his usual comfortable perch on the tree branch.

However, the snow on the branch had just melted, so he spread a straw raincoat on it.

"Where do we go next? Have you decided?" Ding Wenxi asked.

"Yesterday, knowing you were coming, I asked the steward to hire a boat for us. It's already docked at the canal wharf. If you're tired, we can rest here for a night before leaving. If not..."

"I'm not tired. Let's leave today."

Yuhan held Ding Wenxi's hand, looking at the dark circles under her eyes, and pouted unhappily. "Mother, you look much worse than when I left the capital. Let's rest for a night."

"I did that on purpose, not sleeping at night. I'll be fine in a few days."

"Just for the act?"

Ding Wenxi pursed her lips. "What else could I do? I'm fine. I just didn't sleep at night and slept during the day."

Seeing her mother's determined attitude, Yuhan nodded. Since they had decided to leave the capital, it was better to do so as soon as possible to avoid any unforeseen complications.

"Alright, then we'll leave for the wharf after lunch. Mother, what did you tell Big Cow when you left?"

Yuhan had kept her fake death a secret from Chen Da Niu, afraid he would blame himself.

"I told him I was going to Wutai Mountain to pray for your soul and asked him to look after the house for me."

"Big Cow has helped us so much. It's good to leave the house to him."

Ding Wenxi's heart stirred, and she patted the back of Yuhan's hand. "Before leaving the capital, the Prince sent Yuan Zhen to deliver 500 taels of silver, as well as some valuable medicines and tonics. I had Yangquan help me pawn them."

Zhao Xuanyou sent silver?

Was it to comfort her mother over the loss of her daughter?

She wondered what he was doing at this moment.

She had "died," and while he was accompanying the Feng family on their sightseeing in the capital, he probably wasn't very happy either.

Yuhan gently pinched her fingers, pushing Zhao Xuanyou out of her mind, and focused on Ding Wenxi.

"Mother, we have enough money. Why did you pawn the medicines? You could have kept them to nourish your body."

"It's inconvenient to carry those things on a long journey. It's better to exchange them for silver notes."

It made sense, so Yuhan nodded. "Don't worry, Mother. Wen Bo and I have already discussed it. Once we settle down, we'll find a way to make money. When I earn enough, I'll buy you the best medicines and tonics."

"Wen Bo... he..." Ding Wenxi glanced at Wen Bo, who was sitting on the tree branch, and asked softly, "Is he coming with us?"

"Yes, he's coming with us." Yuhan, worried that Yangquan outside might hear, lowered her voice. "We'll go to Yangzhou first. Wen Bo and I have already planned everything else."

"Alright."

Although Ding Wenxi didn't know Yuhan's plan, Yuhan was smarter and stronger than her. All she needed to do was follow Yuhan and try not to cause trouble.

The group ate lunch prepared by Wen Bo at Jiaoye Manor, then set off in the carriage.

The manor was more than twenty miles away from the canal wharf. By the time they arrived, it was already dark.

Fortunately, since they had chartered the boat, the boatman could set off at night.

The merchant ship had two levels. Since there were few of them, they all stayed on the upper deck.

However, for safety, Yangquan stayed on the lower deck to keep an eye on any unusual activity.

Yuhan hadn't seen Ding Wenxi in a long time and was very clingy. The mother and daughter shared a cabin near the bow of the ship. The cabin had an excellent view, with windows on both sides, and a small balcony right outside the door.

She stood on the balcony, greedily taking in the scenery under the moonlight; the boats coming and going on the canal, the dark mountains gradually receding on both sides, and the two clear waves created by the ship as it cut through the water.

Ding Wenxi sat in the cabin for a while. Seeing Yuhan standing against the wind, she took a coat and draped it over her shoulders.

"Mother, have you ever been on a boat before?"

Ding Wenxi nodded.

This surprised Yuhan.

"After the Empress Dowager entered the palace, she was always in favor. When the late emperor went south to Jiangnan, she was the only concubine he took with him. I naturally attended by her side."

"So you've been to Jiangnan before, Mother."

Ding Wenxi looked at the shimmering ripples on the canal under the moonlight, her thoughts drifting into memories.

"We traveled south on a dragon boat, visiting Yangzhou and Suzhou, and many beautiful places along the canal. We spent a full four months touring Jiangnan. It was during those four months that I met him."

Him?

Yuhan's heart stirred. She knew Ding Wenxi was referring to Cui Lingyuan, the Duke of Xingguo.

So that's how they met.

"Mother, when you were in the capital, did you ever think of going to see him?"

"I did," Ding Wenxi admitted frankly.

After a moment of hesitation, Yuhan still asked, "Do you... miss him?"

---

chapters.title: Returning the Token
chapters.content:
Hearing Yuhan's question, Ding Wenxi's gaze flickered.

"Actually, I've often thought of him over the years. Especially as you grew up day by day, I often wondered, if I hadn't taken you and hidden away, but left you with him, your life might have been better."

If Yuhan had grown up in the Duke of Xingguo's residence and met Zhao Xuanyou by chance in the capital, perhaps with Zhao Xuanyou's feelings for her, they might have become a perfect match.

"Of course not."

Cui Zaiting would think that Tao Shi and Cui Yi's good fortune was due to his upbringing in the academy, where his status as the young master of the Duke's residence kept others from daring to provoke him, and he didn't have to struggle under the Duke's legitimate wife.

But for a daughter, confined in the inner quarters, facing an unkind legitimate mother and a domineering legitimate sister, survival would be much harder. Everything from food, clothing, and daily necessities to marriage arrangements would be controlled by others.

As for Cui Lingyuan, Cui Zaiting's ability to study and pass the imperial examinations to expand the marquis's influence would naturally make him value Cui Zaiting more and prevent others from neglecting him.

"Regardless of the past or present, I think being with you, Mother, is the happiest."

In her heart, Ding Wenxi was the best mother.

Ding Wenxi never put on airs or scolded her like other parents. She was always gentle and kind to Yuhan. Even if Yuhan caused trouble, she didn't have to worry about being beaten.

She might not be a precious jewel, but she had been raised in Ding Wenxi's palms, never lacking food or clothing, nor had she suffered any grievances.

If it weren't for the hardships of her previous life, she would still be that wild girl growing up in the mountains.

Ding Wenxi pulled Yuhan into her arms, her eyes welling up slightly.

After so many twists and turns, mother and daughter had finally left the capital. From now on, they could live a peaceful life.

"Mother," Yuhan blinked and asked again, "What did you like about him before?"

"I won't tell you."

"Was it because he was exceptionally handsome in his youth? Or because he was a smooth talker who deceived you?"

Ding Wenxi patted Yuhan's shoulder and softly comforted her, "I know you don't like him and think he's a bad person. But regardless, it's because of him that I had you. I don't hate him."

Mother was a soft-hearted person. It didn't surprise Yuhan at all that she didn't hate Cui Lingyuan.

But what about her...

She only wanted to live well, to live for herself. Were these traits inherited from Cui Lingyuan's bloodline?

"Mother, do you still remember the painting of the hairpin you drew for me?" The winter night wind was cold, and Yuhan's voice carried a slight chill.

Ding Wenxi certainly remembered.

That day, Yuhan had asked for the betrothal token between her and Cui Lingyuan, so she had drawn that hairpin.

At the time, she had asked Yuhan if she intended to acknowledge her ancestry, but Yuhan had only said it was for precaution.

Hearing Yuhan mention the painting again, Ding Wenxi couldn't help but ask, "Where is that painting?"

"It was left there on New Year's Eve." Yuhan paused, then smiled at her, her eyes shimmering like the surrounding water. "I placed it on his desk."

"On his desk? Then he knows you are..."

"He should be able to guess." Yuhan's voice was light. "But by the time he figures it out, 'I' will already be dead."

Ding Wenxi hadn't expected Yuhan to have made such arrangements.

Surprised, she couldn't help but admire Yuhan's foresight.

No wonder the Duke of Xingguo's residence didn't report the fire to the authorities and even denied that two people had died the next day.

At first, he didn't know who the other person who died in the fire was. But when he discovered the painting of the hairpin in his study, he immediately guessed Yuhan's identity.

Fearful of exposing his old affair with Ding Wenxi, he had to cover it up.

"You even kept this from me."

"I didn't mean to keep it from you, Mother. Initially, I only wanted the painting in case the plan failed and I was caught in the residence. Revealing my identity might save my life."

So Yuhan had carried the painting with her.

That night, the plan went smoothly. After leaving the residence, Yuhan had asked Wen Bo to place the painting on Cui Lingyuan's desk.

With the residence map in hand and everyone busy with the fire, Wen Bo had moved freely.

"It's all my fault for giving you such a troublesome background."

"You're fine, and I'm fine too."

The Cui family wasn't entirely without merit. They had given her outstanding looks and a ruthlessness that came from deep within her bones.

Without that ruthlessness, she wouldn't have made it to this day.

Yuhan didn't speak anymore, just looked up at the moon in the sky.

The merchant ship moved swiftly on the canal, as if it might leave the moon behind.

Her gaze followed the moon, and unconsciously, she turned her head, making a circle in Ding Wenxi's arms.

Seeing Yuhan tilt her head against the railing, Ding Wenxi feared she might fall, so she quickly grabbed her.

Yuhan's gaze moved, and she suddenly jumped up, pointing at the top of the ship and shouting, "There's a thief eavesdropping!"

Ding Wenxi followed Yuhan's gaze and saw Wen Bo sitting alone on the roof of the ship.

"Little Wen, what are you doing up there?"

With both mother and daughter staring at him, Wen Bo was somewhat uncomfortable. He said dryly, "I wasn't eavesdropping."

Yuhan humphed, clearly not believing him.

He had to add, "I was already here before you came out."

But Yuhan didn't want to press the matter. Instead, she said, "The view must be better from the top of the ship, right?"

"It's pitch black. You can't see anything."

"I don't believe you. I want to go up and take a look." With that, Yuhan started climbing the railing.

Ding Wenxi had seen her grow up climbing trees with Chen Da Niu to get bird eggs, so she wasn't surprised by her actions. However, afraid she might fall onto the deck, she supported her from below.

Wen Bo had no choice but to go over and pull her up.

Watching Yuhan climb onto the roof of the ship and make triumphant gestures, Ding Wenxi's eyes softly warmed. She said, "Be careful," before going back into the cabin.

The ship's roof was built similarly to a regular roof, sloping. Yuhan used all fours to crawl to where Wen Bo had been sitting.

Since she had taken his spot, Wen Bo had to sit a little lower.

"Indeed, sitting higher gives a better view."

Wen Bo glanced at Yuhan, met her smile, and turned his face away, reiterating, "I wasn't eavesdropping just now."

During the day, there were many boats on the canal, but at night, there were few, mainly because pirates often appeared on the water.

As soon as they boarded the ship, the three of them had agreed that Bingyun would look after the sailors and boatmen, while Wen Bo and Yangquan would take turns keeping watch at night. If any suspicious boats approached, they would sound the alarm in time.

Tonight happened to be Wen Bo's shift. He had been sitting on the roof before Yuhan and Ding Wenxi came out.

"How much of our conversation did you hear?"

It was a good thing it was Wen Bo. If it had been Yangquan or Bingyun, it would have been troublesome. She would have to be more careful in the future.

Wen Bo turned his head to look at the dark mountains in the distance and didn't say a word.

He had heard everything. If he told her, she would be unhappy.

After a while, he hesitated and said, "So, the Duke of Xingguo is your..."

"Mmm."

Since Wen Bo was the one who placed the painting on Cui Lingyuan's desk, he had heard everything. There was nothing for Yuhan to deny.

"Don't go around spreading this. Right now, only he, my mother, and I know this secret. And you."

"I didn't want to know." Wen Bo glanced at Yuhan, sulking. "In the future, if you want to kill someone to silence them, you'll come to me first."

chapters.title: Blocking the Way
chapters.content:
The merchant ship sailed south with the current, never stopping day or night.

By the time the ship docked at the Yangzhou pier, it was already the eighth day of the second lunar month.

Having lived on the ship for more than half a month, accustomed to the swaying of the cabin, Yu Wan felt a little unsteady when her feet touched the ground. She walked back and forth along the shore to adjust.

"Mother, be careful."

"I'm fine."

Mother and daughter were not prone to seasickness, so the days spent sailing south were quite comfortable.

After leaving the dock, Bingyun hired a carriage to take them into Yangzhou city, heading straight for the largest restaurant in the city, Mingyue Tower.

There was a Qin Huai River in Yangzhou city, just like the one in Jinling, lined with wine shops and traversed by singing boats, commonly known as the "Little Qin Huai."

Mingyue Tower was built by the river, in a prime location, gathering the most talented dancers and singers in Yangzhou.

According to the boatman, besides dance performances, one could also watch acrobatics and magic tricks inside.

When they arrived at Mingyue Tower, the manager enthusiastically told them that for the past few nights, there had been dance competitions between Western Region dancers and Yangzhou dancers. Each night featured different dances, all of which were spectacular. They could pay in advance to reserve good seats.

If they preferred quiet, they could rent a decorated boat for a night tour on the Qin Huai River and even invite a singer to perform Jiangnan folk tunes on the boat.

Noticing they were female guests, the manager added, "If you don't like listening to songs, you can hire a musician to accompany you on the boat. We have instruments like the guqin, flute, and pipa. All our musicians at Mingyue Tower are young, handsome, and refined. They will surely satisfy the lady and the young miss."

Jiangnan truly lived up to its reputation as a land of romantic beauty. Even a first-time visitor like Yu Wan was impressed.

"We just got off the boat. Let's think about it after we settle in."

"Alright, if you have any needs, just let us know, and we can arrange it immediately." With that, he ordered a waiter to show them to their rooms.

Yu Wan, eager to see the scenery, naturally chose a room facing the river.

After entering the room and putting down their things, she couldn't wait to open the window and look outside.

The Qin Huai River during the day didn't seem particularly special, far from the dazzling descriptions in poetry, which left her somewhat disappointed.

However, after nightfall, the river was bustling with decorated boats, each hanging unique lanterns. The entire river was alive with light and shadow, and the melodious songs drifting from the boats captivated Yu Wan as she leaned out the window.

Truly, "The willows by the official road sway in the spring breeze, and the Qin Huai River stirs at dusk."

After resting at Mingyue Tower for two days, Yu Wan suggested going to another nearby restaurant, Zuixiang Tower, for a change of pace.

Bingyun and Yangquan had no objections, but Wen Sun, as he had done the previous two days, said he wanted to explore Yangzhou city by himself.

Yu Wan scolded him a couple of times before letting him go, taking Ding Wenxi, Bingyun, and Yangquan to find Zuixiang Tower.

Having eaten at Mingyue Tower for two consecutive days, a change of restaurant felt refreshing.

After finishing their meal, Yu Wan put down her chopsticks and smiled at Ding Wenxi, "Mother, you seem to be in good spirits. Let's go out and have some fun tonight."

"How do you want to have fun?"

"Mingyue Tower has a dance competition between Western Region dancers and Yangzhou dancers tonight. I've never seen Western Region dancing before and want to broaden my horizons."

Ding Wenxi thought seriously for a moment, then frowned, "Mingyue Tower is too big. The dance competition tonight will likely be packed with people. I don't want to join that crowd."

Bingyun, recalling the manager's words, also put down her chopsticks, "If the lady prefers quiet, we could rent a decorated boat for a river tour."

Yangquan nodded beside her, "And hire a singer to perform some tunes."

The women of Jiangnan spoke very gently, and who knew how melodious their singing would be.

However, as soon as she finished speaking, Yangquan realized her slip. Yu Wan might enjoy the crowd, but Ding Wenxi probably wasn't interested in singers.

"How about we go watch the dance competition tonight, and tomorrow night we rent a decorated boat to tour the Qin Huai River? What do you think?" Yu Wan suggested.

Ding Wenxi still shook her head, "Mingyue Tower is too noisy. You all go enjoy the crowd. I'll just take a walk by the river."

"You can't go out alone at night, Mother."

"Wen Sun doesn't like noise either. He can go with me." Ding Wenxi said, giving Yu Wan a meaningful look.

The mother and daughter exchanged glances before quickly composing themselves.

Yu Wan said, "It's still cold in early spring, Mother. Don't go for a walk by the river tonight. Tonight, you can rent a decorated boat, and we'll go for a night tour tomorrow."

"That works. Since we're here."

"Bingyun, Yangquan." Yu Wan was pleased, "They don't like crowds, so tonight, let's three of us go have some fun."

Bingyun and Yangquan were also visiting Yangzhou for the first time. Hearing that Yu Wan was taking them to watch the dance competition tonight, they were naturally looking forward to it.

Back at Mingyue Tower, Yu Wan and Ding Wenxi returned to their room to rest. By dinnertime, Wen Sun, who had been out strolling, appeared.

He walked up behind Yu Wan and whispered, "Everything is ready. But right now, Bingyun is still here, and I don't know where Yangquan is."

Yu Wan asked Bingyun, who vaguely said that Yangquan had probably gone shopping on the street.

Finally, after finishing dinner, Yangquan appeared.

Yu Wan subtly gave Wen Sun a look.

Back at Zheye Village, the two of them had planned to shake off Bingyun and Yangquan in Yangzhou. Staying at Mingyue Tower was just the first step, and now they had finally reached the second step.

After dinner, Wen Sun and Ding Wenxi followed the plan. They went out for a night tour on the Qin Huai River, while Yu Wan went to the first floor of Mingyue Tower to watch the dance competition.

The Western Region dancers were indeed different from the women of the Central Plains. Not only were they tall, but they also had full and alluring figures. Their dancing was as fluid and enchanting as a snake.

The Jiangnan dancers, on the other hand, were not as seductive but had a unique elegant and refined charm, which also drew cheers.

As Yu Wan watched, she poured wine for Bingyun and Yangquan; the wine had been prepared by Wen Sun in advance, laced with a colorless and odorless knockout drug.

Before the dance competition could conclude, Bingyun and Yangquan had already collapsed onto the table.

Yu Wan waited for a while, then asked a waiter to help carry them back to their room. She placed a letter she had written to Zhao Qi on the table.

After finishing all this, Yu Wan hurriedly left Mingyue Tower and rushed to the predetermined meeting place.

However, not long after leaving Mingyue Tower, a man wearing a fox mask blocked her path.

Yu Wan took two steps to the left, and the man followed her.

Yu Wan took two steps to the right, and the man followed her again.

It was clear that he was there to stop her.

Yu Wan immediately became tense.

Had Bingyun and Yangquan come after her?

No, Wen Sun had said that the drug was personally prepared by him and would definitely work. Moreover, if the two of them had come to catch her, they wouldn't be wearing masks.

The man's actions were clearly a taunt.

Yu Wan instinctively stepped back, but the man grabbed her hand.

In the bustling street, the man dared to touch her so boldly; he was incredibly audacious.

"Let go of me! My family is nearby. If you don't let go, I'll have you arrested!" Yu Wan shouted loudly. Sure enough, the passersby around them stopped to look.

But the man showed no fear. He still held her hand and said righteously, "Go ahead and shout! I was just wondering why there's no one around you."

The voice and tone were familiar to Yu Wan. He shouldn't be here, though.

She looked up at him in surprise.

The man was very pleased with her reaction. Under her gaze, he slowly removed his mask.

---

chapters.title: Sand Between the Fingers
chapters.content:
"Qi..." Yu Wan looked at Zhao Qi in shock, her fingers moving uncertainly before quickly hiding them in her sleeves to conceal her panic. "Young Master, how did you come to Yangzhou? You didn't desert the army, did you?"

Zhao Qi was dressed in a black martial arts outfit. After several months apart, he appeared slightly darker and taller than when he was in the capital.

Before, Yu Wan had been able to look at him eye to eye, but now she had to look up slightly.

"Of course I didn't desert the army." It had been so long since he last saw her, and instead of a smile, she asked if he had fled the camp, which made him feel somewhat disheartened. "My uncle sent someone to Jinling on business. I calculated that you would have arrived in Yangzhou by now, so I took the opportunity to request this task. I didn't expect to actually run into you."

"Thank you for your kindness in helping me leave the capital this time."

Zhao Qi heard the unfamiliarity in her tone and was displeased.

He couldn't find even a trace of joy on her face; instead, her delicate eyebrows were slightly furrowed, which made his heart sink. He blurted out, "You don't want to see me?"

She didn't want to, especially not tonight, at this critical moment.

Yu Wan realized her reaction had hurt him. Regaining her composure, she softly said, "How could that be? I was just startled a moment ago. I thought I had really encountered..."

"A rogue?"

"Mmm, I was afraid it was a rogue, or someone from the capital."

Listening to her explanation, Zhao Qi casually said, "Zhao Xuanyou has been arrested. Who else from the capital would chase you here?"

"He was arrested?" Yu Wan suddenly looked up at him, her eyes filled with shock.

Facing her clear eyes that seemed to reflect his own image, Zhao Qi suddenly felt a bit nervous.

He asked in surprise, "You didn't know?"

"I really didn't," Yu Wan shook her head repeatedly. "When did this happen? Why was he arrested?"

Zhao Xuanyou had been arrested for breaking into the Xingguo Duke's mansion to open a coffin and assault someone in his pursuit of Yu Wan's whereabouts.

Yu Wan would surely worry about Zhao Xuanyou if she knew, which was why Bingyun and Yangquan had kept it from her.

Zhao Qi felt like hitting himself hard.

They had both cleverly hidden the truth from Yu Wan, but he had let it slip.

After a moment's thought, Zhao Qi vaguely said, "It's nothing serious. He just made a mistake while handling a case, angered a court official, and was temporarily imprisoned."

"Just that?"

"He beat up a court official, leaving them seriously injured. The emperor will surely punish him."

Zhao Qi told the truth, so he spoke with confidence.

He wasn't lying to Yu Wan. The events were as he described, though he omitted the details of which case and whom he had beaten.

"Why are you alone on the street? Didn't Bingyun and Yangquan accompany you to protect you?"

Yu Wan was still absorbed in the shock of learning about Zhao Xuanyou's imprisonment.

Zhao Qi was wrong.

Zhao Xuanyou was indeed highly skilled in martial arts, but he was not a brute. On the contrary, he was meticulous and cautious in his actions. How could he have beaten a court official?

There must be more to the story.

He was actually arrested... For Yu Wan, this was actually beneficial, but she wasn't happy about it.

"You don't need to worry about him. The Marquis of Jingyuan has great military achievements. The emperor is just making a show of it; he will definitely release him in the end."

That was true. The emperor did trust Zhao Xuanyou greatly.

"I'm not worried about him," Yu Wan took a deep breath, quickly composing herself. "My mother went for a night tour on the Qin Huai River, and I asked them to follow her. Bingyun and Yangquan have been very kind to me. Your Highness must reward them."

"Understood."

"You promised. Don't go back on your word!"

Zhao Qi didn't know why she suddenly became so serious, but he nodded, "I will reward them. By the way, isn't there a highly skilled person with you? Where are they?"

"He is my friend. I can't order him around."

"Since when did you know someone so skilled?"

Yangquan should have informed him of everything that happened in the capital.

"I can know you, so why can't I know someone skilled in martial arts?" Yu Wan didn't want to say more about Wen Sun, for fear that Zhao Qi would recognize him. After teasing him, she asked, "Did you come from Jinling?"

Zhao Qi nodded.

The day before yesterday, he had received a message from Yangquan in Jinling and wanted to come immediately.

But this time, he was genuinely serious about gaining experience with his uncle and didn't want to delay official business, fearing it would make his uncle and Yu Wan look down on him. So he endured until today, finished his tasks, sent his subordinates ahead, and rode quickly to Yangzhou to see her.

"I have to leave soon."

Everyone else had already departed, and he would have to ride all night to catch up.

"Would you like to try some Jiangnan snacks?"

Seeing that she remembered he liked sweets, Zhao Qi's expression softened a bit. "Yes."

Especially with her.

Yu Wan reached out and grabbed his sleeve, pulling him forward.

For a moment, Zhao Qi felt as if he had returned to the days when they wandered the streets of the capital together.

But after a short while, Yu Wan let go of his sleeve and pointed to a restaurant, "The desserts at Zuixiang Tower are delicious. Let me take you to try them."

Inside Zuixiang Tower, they found a seat by the window on the second floor and soon ordered a large table full of sweets.

"I know what this is. It's Qingtuan."

Although Zhao Qi had never eaten in Yangzhou, as a prince, the imperial kitchen naturally had chefs who could make Jiangnan snacks.

"And this? You must have eaten it before." Yu Wan pointed to the honey-glazed lotus root.

Zhao Qi nodded.

"And this?"

Zhao Qi had actually eaten it before, but he shook his head.

"This is crab shell yellow," Yu Wan smiled. "It's very crispy."

Zhao Qi picked up his chopsticks and ate a piece of crab shell yellow, then a piece of honey-glazed lotus root.

"It's quite good. Better than my family chef's cooking."

Yu Wan knew he was just being polite and handed him a bowl of osmanthus sweet rice porridge. "This is also good. I have a bowl every day."

"The osmanthus fragrance here is different from... my family's. It's lighter."

"So my family's is better?"

"No," Zhao Qi lowered his head and took another spoonful. "I prefer the taste here."

Yu Wan remained silent for a long time.

Zhao Qi put down his spoon and saw her lost in thought, fearing she was still thinking about Zhao Xuanyou's imprisonment, which made him feel even worse.

How could he be so stupid? After finally seeing her, he had to mention Zhao Xuanyou in front of her.

No wonder she didn't want to pay attention to him.

"I should go."

Yu Wan heard and stood up with him, softly saying, "Your Highness, be careful on your night journey."

Zhao Qi was still dejected and only responded with an "mm," before heading out.

Yu Wan glanced at the fox mask he had left on the table, picked it up, and chased after him.

"Your Highness, your mask."

"Throw it away."

Hearing the anger in his voice, Yu Wan examined the mask and said, "Since Your Highness doesn't want it, I'll keep it. Looking closely, this mask resembles Your Highness a bit."

"Where does it resemble me?"

Yu Wan smiled and held the mask up to his face, comparing it. "It looks more like you when you're angry."

"Really?"

Yu Wan nodded, her smile as warm and bright as before.

Zhao Qi really enjoyed being with Yu Wan like this. Whether it was noisy or quiet around them, being with Yu Wan always brought a unique sense of tranquility.

"I should go."

After being away from the capital for several days, Yu Wan had been in high spirits. Now, watching Zhao Qi turn to leave, she finally felt a surge of emotion.

Yu Wan held the mask to her chest and softly said, "Take care, Your Highness. From now on, we might not be able to meet again. When I see this mask, I will remember your kindness to me and pray for your well-being."

The young man slightly furrowed his brows, instinctively feeling that Yu Wan's words were strange.

But tonight, for him, was a long-awaited reunion, and he was ultimately happy.

"Alright, I'm leaving."

With that, he hardened his heart and strode away, leaving with the guards waiting by the roadside.

Yu Wan watched his figure disappear into the night, bit her lip, and quickly ran towards the meeting place with Wen Sun.

A black awning boat was waiting under a newly sprouted willow tree.

Wen Sun, dressed as a boatman in a straw raincoat and conical hat, frowned when he saw Yu Wan. "Why are you so late?"

"I ran into a friend and was delayed for a while."

After Yu Wan boarded the boat and sat next to Ding Wenxi, Wen Sun rowed the boat away into the night.

Jiangnan's waterways were interconnected, and countless black awning boats navigated through them. No one would be able to trace her whereabouts again.

Zhao Xuanyou, Zhao Qi; none of them were her concern anymore.

chapters.title: A Pain That Cuts to the Bone
chapters.content:
When Zhao Xuanyou walked out of the prison of the Ministry of Justice, it was already the third day of the third lunar month.

After being trapped in prison for more than two months, when he saw daylight again, his eyes were still stung by the spring sunlight.

He did not raise his hand to shield his eyes; instead, he squinted and looked up toward the sunlight.

"Brother Xuanyou!" Ye Mo Xuan had received the news of his release and had been waiting here since early morning.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou emerge, he hurriedly had a servant bring a brazier and place it in front of him.

Afraid that Zhao Xuanyou might dislike such gestures, he explained with a smile, "Step over it to ward off bad luck."

Zhao Xuanyou indeed disliked these things, but he had no close brothers, and had little contact with his cousins. Since Ye Mo Xuan cared for him like a brother, he naturally wouldn’t refuse the kindness.

His dark eyes slightly lowered, he lifted his foot and stepped over the brazier.

"May good fortune follow you, Brother. From now on, everything will go smoothly."

"Thank you for taking care of Grandmother these days."

"For family, there’s no need to say such things!" Ye Mo Xuan was always gentle and humorous. He stepped forward and patted Zhao Xuanyou’s shoulder. "Hurry back to the residence. The old lady and the Marquis have been waiting for this day for a long time. They must be anxious by now."

Zhao Xuanyou followed Ye Mo Xuan into the carriage.

During the two months he was imprisoned, many things had happened in the capital.

After he gave Liu Quan the pearl burial objects taken from Cui Yi’s coffin, the emperor ordered the Brocade Guards to secretly investigate the matter.

Pan Xun and his men had kept watch outside the Xingguo Duke’s residence for over a month before finally catching the servants secretly moving items out.

He sent people to quietly follow them to a manor outside the city, which was registered under the name of the Ningguo Duke’s eldest son’s wife.

After waiting for the Xingguo Duke’s people to leave, Pan Xun entered to investigate. Although most of the boxes contained porcelain, five of them held precious pearls that Cui Lingyuan had meticulously collected over the years.

Connecting this to the previous tribute pearl case, it wasn’t hard to guess where these pearls, comparable to the imperial collection, had come from.

Tao Cheng was already dead, so it was impossible to get a confession from him.

But his family had been exiled to a remote and desolate land thousands of miles away. Since they were alive, they could be questioned.

Pan Xun made a decisive decision and sent a team to find Tao Cheng’s family.

On the surface, he maintained calm in the capital, waiting for news from those interrogating Tao Cheng’s family.

It turned out that Tao Cheng, knowing he couldn’t escape the death penalty, had taken all the blame because the Xingguo Duke’s residence had promised to take care of his family.

He didn’t fully trust his brother-in-law, so he had secretly left an account book for his son, detailing all the financial dealings with the Xingguo Duke’s residence over the years.

Apart from the silver obtained from illegally selling tribute pearls, because Cui Lingyuan loved pearls, a significant portion of the precious pearls obtained each year had to be offered to him.

After Tao’s family was exiled, the Xingguo Duke’s residence claimed that the officials were watching closely and that they needed to avoid suspicion for the first few years. They had never taken care of Tao’s family, who lived in extreme hardship in exile, losing two young children in succession. They had grown resentful toward the Cui family.

Now that the Brocade Guards had come to them, offering a chance to redeem themselves, they immediately revealed the location where Tao Cheng had hidden the account book.

With the account book in hand, the case became much simpler. Following the leads, many people were arrested, and both evidence and testimonies were presented to the emperor.

The emperor was naturally furious and ordered a thorough investigation.

The initial evidence had come from Cui Yi’s coffin. At that time, Cui Zai had repeatedly obstructed the opening of the coffin, so whether it was opening the coffin or the injuries sustained, Zhao Xuanyou had legitimate reasons.

The three judicial departments, which had been handling Zhao Xuanyou’s case, shifted their focus to investigating the Xingguo Duke’s residence.

Zhao Xuanyou was not surprised by these events, nor did he care much. In fact, he wasn’t even clear about what he did care about.

On the carriage, Ye Mo Xuan said something, but Zhao Xuanyou didn’t hear a single word. He just stared blankly out the window.

The shops were densely packed, pedestrians hurried along, street vendors called out their wares, and the capital’s streets were as bustling and noisy as ever, filled with traffic and people.

Everything seemed the same, yet it also seemed as if everything had changed.

"Brother, we’ve arrived at the Marquis’s residence. Grandmother and the Marquis are waiting for you at the gate."

Zhao Xuanyou followed Ye Mo Xuan out of the carriage and indeed saw the long-unseen Jingyuan Marquis supporting Old Lady Ye, standing at the gate waiting for him. Seeing their anxious and concerned expressions, his usually calm face finally showed some emotion.

"Grandmother, Father, it is Xuanyou’s fault for being unfilial." Zhao Xuanyou knelt before them, cupping his fists in apology.

"It’s good that you’re back. There’s no need for guilt," Old Lady Ye stepped forward and pulled him up. "Now that the corrupt officials have been caught and justice has been restored, you are not only blameless but have also made a great contribution."

In recent days, rumors had been swirling in the capital that the only son of the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence had been imprisoned, his future ruined, and that the noble reputation of this branch of the family could no longer be preserved.

Now that the Xingguo Duke’s residence was in trouble and Zhao Xuanyou was out of prison, Old Lady Ye naturally felt vindicated.

The Jingyuan Marquis was as tall as Zhao Xuanyou, but due to losing his beloved wife early and suffering from long-term illness, he was much thinner than Zhao Xuanyou.

Since returning to the capital, he had repeatedly entered the palace to seek an audience with the emperor. After confirming that the emperor intended to protect Zhao Xuanyou, he secretly contacted Pan Xun and had the Marquis’s guards assist Pan Xun in the investigation. Over the past two months, he had worked tirelessly, and his face showed signs of fatigue.

He stepped forward and patted Zhao Xuanyou’s shoulder, comforting him: "Indeed, it’s not your fault. There’s no need to apologize."

"The return of the heir is a joyous occasion. Don’t stand at the gate talking. Let’s go inside, wash off the dust, and then we can talk."

On the side, Concubine Wei, holding freshly cut willow branches, stepped forward. Old Lady Ye and the Jingyuan Marquis each took a branch and lightly brushed Zhao Xuanyou with them to ward off bad luck.

"Congratulations on your return, Brother!" Ye Mo Xuan shouted loudly. The many servants at the gate of the Marquis’s residence also joined in, welcoming Zhao Xuanyou back.

Since Zhao Xuanyou had been imprisoned on New Year’s Day, the Marquis’s residence had spent the New Year in a gloomy atmosphere. Only today did it finally have a touch of spring’s vibrancy.

However, being released from prison was not something to celebrate openly, so no firecrackers were set off. Instead, the family had a quiet welcome-home banquet.

The Jingyuan Marquis originally had many questions, but seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s low spirits, he didn’t say much. After the meal, he saw Ye Mo Xuan off and then let his son return to his room to rest.

The courtyard of Honghui Hall was as lush and green as ever, but it seemed even greener than usual.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at the gray walls covered with creeping figs and suddenly remembered a small thing.

He didn’t like planting flowers, so Yu Yuan had tried various ways to plant bamboo in the courtyard. Later, when she grew tired of bamboo, she had Zixuan bury many creeping figs at the corner of the wall.

Now that the weather was warming, the creeping figs had climbed up the gray walls and sprouted new leaves, as if a green screen had been spread across the wall.

If she had seen the creeping figs thriving like this, she would surely have boasted proudly.

Zhao Xuanyou forcibly suppressed the turmoil in his heart and stepped forward.

The maids, Yingsue and Qiuyue, who were under the corridor, saw him return and stood up to greet him.

In the past, whenever he returned from outside, Yu Yuan would sit here with Yingsue, watching the water in the stove while chatting and laughing.

She never wore makeup in Honghui Hall, and her clothes were casual. Her black hair was simply tied up with a single jade hairpin. When she saw him return, she wouldn’t immediately stand up to welcome him; she would just sit there and smile at him with a raised eyebrow.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yingsue and Qiuyue before him, and unconsciously reached for the broken hairpin that Cui Zaiting had given him.

It was at this moment that he finally had a tangible feeling about Yu Yuan’s death.

She was gone.

In Honghui Hall, he would never see her figure again. She had completely disappeared from his sight and his side.

---

chapters.title: Lingering in the Heart
chapters.content:
"Master, did... did this servant do something wrong?"

Under Zhao Xuanyou’s heavy gaze, Qiuyue was terrified, thinking she had made a mistake. Her face turned pale with nervousness.

Hearing her trembling voice, Zhao Xuanyou abruptly withdrew his gaze and turned to walk into the house.

Yingsue softly said to Qiuyue, "Move the stove to the back of the house."

Having worked in Honghui Hall for so long, Yingsue had often seen Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Yuan’s affectionate interactions. It wasn’t hard to guess what Zhao Xuanyou had been thinking about just now.

In the days immediately following Yu Yuan’s death, Yingsue had also shed many tears.

Two months had passed, and the emotions had seemingly faded. But now, seeing Zhao Xuanyou return, a wave of sorrow was stirred up again.

After sending Qiuyue away, Yingsue entered the room and presented the new clothes that had been prepared.

"Master, the old lady specifically instructed that the dirty clothes you’re wearing should be taken off and burned."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded, his gaze falling on Yingsue, and he paused again.

In the past, when he returned to the room, it was always Yu Yuan who brought the clothes to him.

Zhao Xuanyou inexplicably felt his heart beating heavily.

He forcibly suppressed the discomfort in his chest, took the clothes from Yingsue’s hands, and said in a low voice, "You may leave."

Yingsue silently retreated.

Zhao Xuanyou felt a heaviness in his head. He threw the clothes aside and went to fetch his nightclothes.

But when he reached the bed, he remembered that every time he changed into his nightclothes, he would always pull Yu Yuan over.

During the day, Yu Yuan would never agree, but he knew this and still pulled her, just to see her cute, exasperated expression when she was angry.

If she were here now, she would surely punch him a few times with her delicate fists.

Although her strength was considerable, in the end, she could never overpower him, and she would always end up being held by him and lying on the bed.

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly stood up, staring intently at the bed.

It was clearly the bed he was used to sleeping in, but now, all he could think of was the sight of Yu Yuan lying there.

She liked to sleep on the side near the wall, facing him.

Although the nightclothes were loose, her graceful figure still outlined the curves beneath them.

When they shared the bed, her breathing was long and steady.

She never moved much in her sleep; her arms and shoulders were neatly tucked under the covers, wrapping herself warmly and securely...

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly clenched his fists, trying hard to dispel the chaotic thoughts.

But the more he tried to remind himself that it was just an empty bed, the more vivid the fragmented memories of Yu Yuan became.

Even details he had never paid attention to before surfaced in his mind.

For example, the color of the nightclothes Yu Yuan had worn the last time they lay there together, the embroidery on them, and the expression in her eyes when she had been pulled out of the covers by him.

He wouldn’t be able to sleep.

Zhao Xuanyou forcibly suppressed his thoughts, threw the nightclothes aside, put on the new clothes Yingsue had brought, and turned toward the study.

But before entering the study, he seemed to see Yu Yuan occupying his desk, lying on it to read and practice calligraphy, as she often did.

He took a few steps forward, and through the window, seeing the Xiangfei bamboo in the courtyard, he seemed to see Yu Yuan, when she had first arrived at Honghui Hall, standing by this window to trim the bamboo branches to attract his attention.

Zhao Xuanyou had always been aware of his attachment to Yu Yuan.

But he had never realized that Yu Yuan occupied so much space in his life.

This was clearly his study, yet her presence was everywhere, inescapable, lingering in his heart.

Every little detail about her was connected, forming thread after thread, intertwining densely into a vast net that enveloped him.

Something in Zhao Xuanyou’s mind collapsed with a roar, destroying his reason and shattering the clarity of his mind.

He suddenly swept his hand across the desk, sending everything crashing to the floor.

But he still couldn’t breathe.

The vase Yu Yuan had used for the plum branches; smash.

The books Yu Yuan usually read; smash.

The bamboo curtain Yu Yuan had hung on the window; smash.

He wanted to destroy everything, to annihilate everything, to tear apart the net that trapped him.

By the time Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing rushed into the study, all they saw was the mess on the floor and Zhao Xuanyou with bloodshot eyes.

The two had never seen Zhao Xuanyou like this and were at a loss for what to do.

On this day when his name had been cleared, Zhao Xuanyou was so out of control, all because of Yu Yuan, whose body had been lost.

Looking at Zhao Xuanyou standing rigidly in the room, the two didn’t dare to speak, only lowering their heads and standing to the side.

In the deadly silence, the madness in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes finally began to cool bit by bit.

He realized that he couldn’t stay in Honghui Hall any longer.

Every moment spent here was torture for him.

Without a word, he quickly walked out of Honghui Hall.

"Master." Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing, fearing something might happen to him, immediately followed.

Outside the Marquis’s residence, standing on the bustling street, Zhao Xuanyou exhaled heavily, and his mind regained some clarity.

After a moment of hesitation, Yuan Zhen finally spoke.

"Yu Yuan is already gone. Please, Master, control your grief."

These words weren’t his place to say.

But neither the old lady nor the Marquis would understand the relationship between Master and Yu Yuan.

They wouldn’t think the death of a maidservant was significant, nor would they think Master would grieve for Yu Yuan.

Only he could say it.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t speak, only staring fiercely at him.

"Yu Yuan’s mother has already left the capital. She said she would go to Mount Wutai to ask a great master to pray for her soul and wish for a good rebirth in the next life." Yuan Zhen had also been grieving over Yu Yuan’s death. "The dead cannot be brought back to life. Master must continue living."

Zhao Xuanyou had just calmed down somewhat, but upon hearing this, the blood in his eyes surged again.

He grabbed Yuan Zhen by the collar and gritted his teeth. "You’ve been investigating around the Xingguo Duke’s residence for so long. Did you find no news about the body?"

After he was arrested, Pan Xun had led the Brocade Guards to closely monitor the Xingguo Duke’s residence, carefully inspecting the people and goods entering and leaving.

The Xingguo Duke’s residence had secretly moved things out, but they were only tribute pearls and porcelain; there was no body.

If they had the chance to dispose of the body, it must have been between New Year’s Eve night and the morning of New Year’s Day.

"We did ask every household, and we offered a heavy reward for information, but every household said they hadn’t seen the Xingguo Duke’s residence moving anything out."

There were two possibilities for not seeing anything.

One was that Cui Lingyuan had acted in secret, avoiding everyone’s notice.

The other was that Cui Lingyuan had never moved the body out at all.

Which was it?

That night, the firewood shed had caught fire, and the residence was in chaos. Initially, Cui Lingyuan didn’t know who had died in the fire, so he hadn’t sealed any information. Many people knew that two bodies had been carried out from the fire scene.

Even after confirming Cui Yi’s identity, he couldn’t have confirmed Yu Yuan’s identity.

If he had sent Yu Yuan’s body out of the Xingguo Duke’s residence that night, someone would have seen it.

Eliminating this possibility, the only remaining possibility was that Yu Yuan’s body was still inside the Xingguo Duke’s residence.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened abruptly. Without lingering any longer, he suddenly walked forward.

chapters.title: Grave Digging
chapters.content:
The case of the Duke of Xingguo’s embezzlement of tribute pearls had not yet been concluded. Cui Lingyuan and Cui Zaizhou had been taken into the custody of the Court of Judicial Review, while the rest of the family and servants were confined within the ducal mansion, under the supervision of officials from the same court.

When Zhao Xuanyou arrived at the Duke of Xingguo’s mansion, night had already fallen. He ordered Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing to wait outside, then, without the slightest hesitation, leaped over the wall.

Having spent years stationed in the military, he had only visited the ducal mansion two or three times after marrying Cui Yichu, so he was not very familiar with its layout. He could only rely on instinct as he made his way toward the secluded inner quarters.

Fortunately, the firewood shed had not yet been rebuilt after burning down, so it didn’t take much effort to find.

Frowning slightly at the sight of the shed reduced to ashes, Zhao Xuanyou thought the fire seemed unusually fierce.

Even if the shed had been piled high with dry firewood, there should have been water stored nearby. Once the flames rose, someone would have noticed and extinguished them immediately.

Recalling the exhumation at Qingyun Courtyard, he felt the burns on Cui Yichu’s body had been too severe. Her flesh had been completely charred, leaving only a set of scorched bones.

Zhao Xuanyou was no coroner, but years of military service had exposed him to all manner of corpses. He knew an ordinary fire wouldn’t reduce a person to such a state.

Gazing at the firewood shed before him, he was certain something was amiss with the blaze; it looked as if no one had even attempted to put it out.

His temples throbbed as he suppressed these doubts and stepped onto the shed’s platform, scanning the area.

Today, his only goal was to find Yumeng’s remains. There was no time for overthinking.

The ashes had already been cleared away by the mansion’s servants. Apart from a few half-burned pillars and collapsed bricks, there was nothing left.

Cui Lingyuan would not have left a body out in the open to attract attention. So where could it be?

The mansion’s rear garden had a pond. If someone wanted to dispose of a body without a trace, they could weigh it down with stones and sink it.

But the firewood shed was in a secluded location, far from the rear garden. To get there, one would have to pass through the servants’ quarters. If Cui Lingyuan had done that, someone would have seen.

Pan Xun had interrogated many people, and several had confessed to the existence of another body, though none knew its whereabouts. Clearly, they weren’t lying.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze darkened. If he were Cui Lingyuan, pressed for time and needing to cover his tracks, he would have disposed of the body nearby.

Nearby...

He surveyed his surroundings, carefully examining the area around the shed. When he reached the back, he caught sight of a well. His eyes sharpened, and he quickly approached it, only to find it filled with sand and soil.

His heart pounded violently.

The soil in the well looked similar in color to the surrounding earth, but after several spring rains, the grass around it had grown lush and green; yet not a single blade sprouted from the well.

He drew his sword and thrust it into the well. The blade struck stone with a metallic clang.

Using his sword, he began clearing away the filled earth.

Sure enough, beneath a thin layer of soil lay charred wood and blackened bricks. No wonder nothing grew there.

The well had not only been filled but filled after the firewood shed burned. What it concealed was obvious.

Zhao Xuanyou stood frozen, staring at the well.

After so much investigation, so much contemplation, the answer lay before him; yet he faltered.

Was Yumeng’s body buried beneath the ashes?

He couldn’t bear it. The delicate, alluring Yumeng, whose every glance carried a bewitching charm, now reduced to a pile of charred bones buried in a well.

His sword clattered to the ground. His towering, powerful frame trembled, and he slumped to the ground beside the well.

Under the pitch-black night, the moonlight seemed unnaturally pale.

He reached out and grabbed a handful of scorched earth. His mind kept flashing back to Yumeng’s face; her painted brows, her lively, beautiful eyes, the way her smile lit up like the spring sun whenever she saw him.

The early spring night wind was as biting as winter, slicing across his face like a blade.

Even now, he couldn’t fully accept her death.

Should he dig up this well?

If he unearthed her body and confirmed her death, would that bring closure?

Perhaps it was better to leave things as they were; never finding her body, forever clinging to the hope that she might still be alive.

These conflicting emotions tore at his heart.

In the dead of night, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly stood and stepped forward, bending over to dig at the scorched earth filling the well.

She had been ambushed, died in a place like this. No matter what state she was in, he had to take her back.

When Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing found him, they saw Zhao Xuanyou hunched over the well, digging like a mad dog.

“Master!”

The well was not only filled with earth and ashes but also bricks and tiles.

Zhao Xuanyou’s hands, already torn and bleeding from the sharp debris, were a bloody mess.

Seeing this, Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing rushed forward in alarm, trying to stop him.

“Get lost!” Zhao Xuanyou’s martial arts far surpassed theirs. Finding them in his way, he swung his fists without hesitation.

The two barely dodged, stumbling back.

“If Master wants to avenge Yumeng, just kill me. Don’t torture yourself!” Yuan Qing had been consumed by guilt since Yumeng’s disappearance, barely holding himself together.

He had never seen Zhao Xuanyou so out of control. Regret and grief surged within him, and he sobbed, “It’s all my fault! I saw Chen Da Niu being chased away but didn’t go after him. If I had, I would’ve known about Yumeng’s disappearance sooner, and she wouldn’t have died...”

Before he could finish, Zhao Xuanyou grabbed him by the collar.

Yuan Zhen was horrified. He knew Zhao Xuanyou’s emotions had been bottled up for too long. Right now, he was truly capable of killing.

Seeing that Yuan Qing made no attempt to resist, Yuan Zhen quickly stepped in, blocking Zhao Xuanyou’s fist with his own hands.

Though the pain was excruciating, it was better than Yuan Qing’s skull being crushed.

“Master, please calm down,” Yuan Zhen endured the pain and pleaded. “At the time, Chen Da Niu was driven away because the young mistress ordered the gatekeepers to do it. By the time Yuan Qing saw him, Chen Da Niu was already far gone.”

Yuan Qing had been heartbroken over Yumeng’s death. Yuan Zhen, upon hearing his mention of the gatekeepers driving someone away, had found it strange. After questioning Steward Song carefully, he learned it had been Feng Jirour’s order.

As a servant, there was nothing he could do about the young mistress’s commands. He had tried to reason with Yuan Qing several times, but the stubborn fool refused to listen.

A cold glint flickered in Zhao Xuanyou’s bloodshot eyes.

No wonder, when his grandmother had come to visit him in prison, she had sighed when mentioning the broken engagement.

Zhao Xuanyou’s imprisonment in the Ministry of Justice’s prison had dimmed his prospects. It was only natural that his maternal uncle and aunt would agree to return the betrothal gifts and call off the marriage. But Feng Jirour had agreed far too readily, even urging them to leave the capital as soon as possible. Now it made sense; she had a guilty conscience.

But he couldn’t blame anyone; not Yuan Qing, not Feng Jirour.

It was his own hesitation, his own mercy toward Cui Yichu, that had given her chance after chance to harm Yumeng.

If he had killed Cui Yichu decisively, none of this would have happened.

In the end, the blame lay with him.

The thorn buried deep in his heart suddenly turned into a dagger, carving into his flesh.

---

chapters.title: The Truth Is Her
chapters.content:
After a moment of silence, Zhao Xuanyou dragged his slightly trembling body back to the well.

Yumeng was still lying alone at the bottom. He had to bring her out.

Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing didn’t understand his obsession with the well, but his determination was unshakable. Since he refused their help, they had no choice but to search the area for tools.

Before long, one of them returned with an iron shovel.

“Master, let us dig. It’ll be faster.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s hands were caked with blood and dirt, a gruesome sight under the cold moonlight.

He said nothing, straightening up and reaching out for the shovel.

Yuan Zhen bowed his head and silently handed it over. But before Zhao Xuanyou could begin, they heard voices in the distance.

“Master.”

Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t truly mad. If he wanted to take Yumeng away, he couldn’t alert the guards from the Court of Judicial Review.

Without a word, he swiftly hid in the shadow of the courtyard wall.

The gate of the firewood shed creaked open.

An old servant woman cautiously poked her head in, then stepped inside. After glancing around, she whispered, “Come in quickly,” and two more servant women followed.

The three carried bamboo baskets, their expressions terrified.

“Hurry, burn them.”

They crouched down, taking out incense, candles, and joss paper from their baskets, and began burning the paper money toward the ruins of the firewood shed.

“Young Mistress, your servant knows you died unjustly, but I’ve never done anything to wrong you.”

“Young Mistress, take this paper money and move on. May you be reborn as a noble lady again.”

“Drink the Meng Po soup quickly and never come back to haunt us.”

Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing listened in shock. They never expected these women to be burning paper for Cui Yichu.

After the three servant women finished burning the paper, they slowly stood up.

“Burning the paper should be enough. You two should stop being so jumpy,” one of them said calmly.

The other two refused to back down. “It’s not that we’re being paranoid. On the day of the fire, we really saw the Young Mistress.”

“Oh, come on. The Young Mistress was burned to death. How could you have seen her outside the firewood shed? You must be seeing things.”

“We saw her clearly!”

“Yes! On New Year’s Eve, we were on night patrol. We saw the Young Mistress on the path from the side gate to the firewood shed. She didn’t speak to us. By the time we reached the firewood shed, it was already engulfed in flames.”

The skeptical servant woman asked, “So you’re saying she came from the direction of the firewood shed?”

“Yes. By then, the Young Mistress must’ve already been burned to death. Her spirit left her body, and we happened to see it.”

“They say ghosts don’t have shadows. You were carrying lanterns on patrol. Did you see her shadow?”

At this, the two servant women paused, then nodded. “Now that you mention it, she did have a shadow.”

“Yes, she had a shadow.”

The skeptical woman declared, “If she had a shadow, she wasn’t a ghost. If you ask me, you just saw a maid and mistook her for the Young Mistress.”

“The Young Mistress is the most beautiful woman in the capital. We’re not blind. How could we mistake a maid for her?”

“Exactly! The Young Mistress’s beauty is unmatched in the world. Even after her divorce from the Marquis’s heir, though her spirit was a bit dimmed, no maid could compare.”

“If that’s the case... the Young Mistress we saw that day seemed... seemed a bit fuller than usual.”

Before she could finish, a gust of wind rushed past, and a towering dark figure appeared before her. A hand clamped tightly around her throat.

The other two servant women were about to cry out when Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing struck them unconscious with chopping blows to the neck.

Zhao Xuanyou fixed the servant woman with a gaze darker than ever. “If you want to live, answer my questions. One at a time.”

The woman’s throat was constricted, unable to make a sound. She could only nod frantically, her eyes wide with terror.

Zhao Xuanyou loosened his grip, his eyes as dark as ink. “On New Year’s Eve, during the fire at the firewood shed, did you see Cui Yichu?”

His gaze was filled with murderous intent. Though freed, the servant woman was too intimidated to move.

“Y-Yes... No.”

“Yes or no?”

The woman’s face drained of color. Stammering, she said, “Not during the fire. It was... it was before we discovered the fire. Chen Mama and I saw the Young Mistress while on patrol.”

“Outside the firewood shed?”

“A little ways from it.”

“Did she speak to you?”

“N-No. We greeted her, but she just kept watching the fireworks in the sky. She didn’t acknowledge us. Ever since she returned from the Marquis’s mansion, she’s been in a foul mood, often beating and scolding the servants. We didn’t dare provoke her, so we left quickly.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s breathing hitched. He stared at the servant woman, enunciating each word carefully. “You said she looked fuller than usual?”

“Huh?” The woman hadn’t expected this question. She hesitated, then, after recalling the memory, nodded vigorously. “The Young Mistress had lost a lot of weight after her marriage. Even the finest clothes hung loosely on her. But that night, she was wearing a beautiful outfit, and her figure... her curves were very clear. Even though it was a cotton robe, you could see her chest, her waist. I even turned back to look at her again.”

Was it her?

Zhao Xuanyou had shared a bed with her for months. He knew her body intimately; her striking curves, her slender waist, her graceful, alluring bearing.

“Where you saw her. Was that area affected by the fire?”

“That spot is almost at the mansion’s exit. How could the fire have reached there? Even the area around the firewood shed wasn’t completely burned.”

The servant woman sighed. “If the water vats next to the firewood shed hadn’t been overturned, even the shed wouldn’t have burned so thoroughly.”

“There was a problem with the water vats?”

“When the night patrol discovered the fire, they immediately called for help to put it out. But the water vats nearby had all been knocked over. They had to fetch water from farther away, which wasted a lot of time.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression turned sharp.

He had never figured out why Cui Yichu set the fire. If Yumeng had already been captured and brought to the mansion, why set the fire? Moreover, that fire had reduced her to charcoal.

The facts recounted by the servant woman almost made him certain: the arsonist had not only trapped Cui Yichu in the firewood shed but had also sabotaged the water vats in advance, preventing the mansion’s people from extinguishing the fire and saving anyone.

Whoever did this wasn’t acting in self-defense; they had planned it meticulously.

“Take me to where you saw her.”

“Yes.” The servant woman nodded repeatedly, glancing at her unconscious companions before nervously leading Zhao Xuanyou out of the firewood shed’s courtyard.

After walking a long distance, she stopped. “It was here.”

“Which direction did she come from?”

“The direction we just came from.”

“Where did she go?”

“Ahead.”

“What’s ahead?” Zhao Xuanyou pressed.

The servant woman stammered, “It’s... it’s the laundry room. Further ahead is... the side gate.”

If you kept going straight, you’d exit the Duke of Xingguo’s mansion...

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze trembled.

At this moment, he finally understood everything that had happened on New Year’s Eve.

He had once thought that Cui Yichu’s death in the firewood shed was Yumeng’s retaliation. But the truth was far more shocking.

That night, it wasn’t Cui Yichu who had struck Yumeng; it was Yumeng who had taken the initiative, launching a secret and devastating counterattack against Cui Yichu.

chapters.title: Who Is She Hiding From?
chapters.content:
All the necessary questions had been asked. Zhao Xuanyou struck the old woman unconscious with a single palm.

Yuan Qing, still dazed from the earlier interrogation, suddenly came to his senses. His eyes lit up with joy as he looked at Zhao Xuanyou. "That old woman just now; does that mean Yu Ying... she's still alive?"

Yes.

Yu Ying was still alive.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t believe in supernatural forces. The night watchwoman couldn’t have encountered Cui Yichu’s ghost.

When the fire started in the firewood shed, Yu Ying had been hundreds of steps away. The side gate of the ducal mansion was right there; there was no way the fire could have reached her.

But...

Yuan Zhen looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, noticing the sudden dimming of his once-bright eyes, his expression turning cold.

As a household-born servant of the marquis’ mansion, Yuan Zhen had been favored by the Marquis of Jingyuan since childhood. He had trained in martial arts, swordsmanship, literature, and served as Zhao Xuanyou’s personal attendant. Clever and adaptable, he understood Zhao Xuanyou’s temperament better than anyone.

But he couldn’t fathom Zhao Xuanyou’s current demeanor.

He had publicly lost control when Yu Ying died. Now that he knew she might still be alive, why wasn’t there even a hint of joy on his face?

"That doesn’t make sense," Yuan Qing muttered. "If Yu Ying is still alive, why hasn’t she returned to the mansion? Even if she doesn’t care about us, wouldn’t she at least think of her own mother?"

While Yuan Qing was still confused, Yuan Zhen gradually came to a realization.

He finally understood why Zhao Xuanyou’s expression had grown even darker.

Only one person had died in the Xingguo Ducal Mansion; Cui Yichu. So whose was the other corpse?

Had Yu Ying left it behind?

Had she done so to make everyone believe she was dead?

But why?

Yuan Zhen glanced at Zhao Xuanyou with a hint of alarm. "Master, Yu Ying’s mother left the capital in the first month, saying she was going to Wutai Mountain to summon Yu Ying’s soul."

At the time, Yuan Zhen hadn’t thought much of it. But now, it seemed Yu Ying’s mother had left in an awful hurry.

The cold spring moonlight cast a pale glow on Zhao Xuanyou’s face, his gaze as deep as an abyss.

What Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing had said, he had already considered the moment he realized Yu Ying might be alive. For a brief instant, his mind went blank.

He wanted to ask why as well.

She had succeeded in her revenge. All she needed was to cover her tracks. Why go so far as to fake her death with a corpse?

Who was she hiding from?

And who was she running from?

An answer seemed to rise to the surface of his mind, but Zhao Xuanyou refused to dwell on it. He didn’t want to guess. He needed to find her and ask her himself.

Zhao Xuanyou pressed his thin lips together, his eyes cold and deep. Suddenly, he leapt forward and strode away.

There were no more useful clues left in the Xingguo Ducal Mansion.

"Does Master know where Yu Ying is?" Yuan Qing asked, bewildered.

Yuan Zhen had a rough idea of where Zhao Xuanyou was headed. He only said quietly, "Just follow. Less talking."

"Did I say something wrong again? Alright." Seeing the grim expressions on both Zhao Xuanyou and Yuan Zhen’s faces, Yuan Qing had no choice but to fall silent and hurry after them.

As expected, Zhao Xuanyou went to the separate courtyard. Now, only Chen Da Niu remained there.

After Yu Ying and her mother left, Chen Da Niu no longer needed so many helpers. He had dismissed the original servants and maids.

Hardworking as he was, he not only managed the entire courtyard but also set up a spirit tablet for Yu Ying in the room where she and her mother had once lived.

Noticing the lamp oil before the tablet was about to burn out, he quickly went to refill it.

As he turned around, he saw a tall figure standing at the doorway.

"You…" Chen Da Niu was about to ask who the person was when he caught sight of Yuan Qing and Yuan Zhen behind him. Instantly, he realized who stood before him. "Is that the Young Master?"

He had never had any direct dealings with Zhao Xuanyou, having only seen him from a distance once or twice.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t answer. His gaze was fixed straight on the spirit tablet behind Chen Da Niu.

"Do you live here alone now?" he asked.

"Yes." Chen Da Niu knew this house had been a gift from Zhao Xuanyou to Yu Ying. Now that Yu Ying was dead, it seemed as though Zhao Xuanyou had come to reclaim the property.

He recalled that before leaving, Ding Wenxi had deliberately left behind the deed, probably in anticipation of Zhao Xuanyou’s arrival.

He quickly went to the innermost layer of the dressing table in the inner room, retrieved the deed, and presented it to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the deed. In his dark, ink-like eyes, a flicker of emotion finally appeared. "Left for you?"

"No," Chen Da Niu said. Although Ding Wenxi had told him to live in this courtyard and raise a family there, as if she would never return, Chen Da Niu still felt he was merely looking after the place for her. "I’m just watching the house."

"She told you to watch it when she left?"

Chen Da Niu nodded. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s probing questions, he added, "After Yu Ying died, her mother locked herself in the room, crying every night. I was really afraid she wouldn’t come back after going to Wutai Mountain."

Zhao Xuanyou could see that the honest Chen Da Niu was completely in the dark. Otherwise, mother and daughter wouldn’t have left him behind.

A subtle shift passed through his eyes as he turned and left the courtyard.

From beginning to end, Chen Da Niu had been kept in the dark by Yu Ying. He had nothing useful to offer Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou had been imprisoned for two months. Yu Ying and her mother had left the capital at least a month and a half ago.

There were so many people in the capital. Even if he went door to door inquiring, no one would remember seeing someone like Yu Ying a month ago.

But there was one person in the capital who knew exactly what had happened that night.

Although Zhao Xuanyou had been imprisoned, he hadn’t been stripped of his title. Relying on his position as the Commander of the Brocade Guard, he entered the prison of the Court of Judicial Review even in the dead of night.

The Cui family, father and son, were serious offenders and were imprisoned deep within the prison.

The prison corridor was dim and deep. A jailer led the way with a torch, quickly arriving at Cui Lingyuan’s cell.

Cui Lingyuan had been imprisoned for over ten days. He wore a dark-colored robe, his hair still pinned with a jade hairpin. Though he was now a prisoner, his back remained ramrod straight.

Upon seeing Zhao Xuanyou, his expression remained indifferent, a hint of mockery in his eyes.

"I have a few questions," Zhao Xuanyou said bluntly.

Cui Lingyuan sat cross-legged on the wooden bed, listening to Zhao Xuanyou. Instead of responding, he closed his eyes as if meditating, showing no intention of engaging.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Cui Zaizhou, who was lying in the adjacent cell, and said in a deep voice, "If you answer my questions properly, I can arrange for a physician from the Brocade Guard to come and treat Cui Zaizhou."

Cui Zaizhou had been severely injured by Zhao Xuanyou. After being treated at home, his condition had improved slightly, but now that he was in prison, his injuries had taken a turn for the worse.

"Unnecessary!" Cui Lingyuan, who had been relatively composed, suddenly showed a flash of anger on his face. "We of the Cui family cannot accept your kindness."

Zhao Xuanyou said, "It was I who injured him, but you know very well why I did it."

Cui Lingyuan didn’t respond. He took a deep breath and regained his composure.
