Zhao Xuanyou looked at Cui Lingyuan, who sat with his eyes closed in the cell, his brows slightly furrowed.

Although the man had once been his father-in-law, they hadn’t interacted much, so Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t paid close attention to Cui Lingyuan’s appearance.

Even at forty, Cui Lingyuan still carried an air of noble elegance. He must have been a handsome man in his youth.

The dim candlelight in the prison corridor cast shadows on Cui Lingyuan’s face, accentuating his refined bone structure. Cui Yichu’s breathtaking beauty must have been inherited from him.

Zhao Xuanyou stared intently at Cui Lingyuan, and suddenly, his back tensed.

In fact, compared to Cui Yichu, Yu Ying bore a stronger resemblance to Cui Lingyuan.

---

chapters.title: A Fish in the Water
chapters.content:
"What is your relationship with Yu Ying?" Zhao Xuanyou blurted out.

Cui Lingyuan didn’t move a muscle. After a long moment, he slowly opened his mouth. "If you expect me to answer, either try torture or offer better conditions."

Cui Lingyuan was a serious offender detained by the Court of Judicial Review. Not only was Zhao Xuanyou currently suspended at home after his imprisonment, but even if he hadn’t been, as the Commander of the Brocade Guard, he had no authority to torture Cui Lingyuan.

Zhao Xuanyou had been inside for a while now. The only reaction from Cui Zaizhou in the adjacent cell was a few glances in his direction; he couldn’t even muster the strength to curse, clearly still severely injured.

Zhao Xuanyou shifted his gaze back to Cui Zaizhou, a mocking smile tugging at his lips. "If Cui Zaizhou continues to be imprisoned like this, he won’t last much longer. Could it be that you don’t care about your own son’s life or death?"

"How does it matter if I care? If the ducal mansion is gone, there’s no difference between him and me being alive or dead."

Cui Lingyuan’s answer was resolute. Zhao Xuanyou naturally understood his stance.

Through the iron bars, Cui Lingyuan’s gaze settled heavily on Zhao Xuanyou. "Help me escape, and I will tell you everything without reservation."

"You’re dreaming."

Zhao Xuanyou and the Cui family were already mortal enemies. To bring down the Xingguo Ducal Mansion, he had even collaborated with the irritating Pei Ta, only to fail at the last moment.

In the end, it was Yu Ying’s fire that not only burned down the mansion’s firewood shed and Cui Yichu but also engulfed the entire ducal mansion and all the Cui family members in flames.

"Then you needn’t waste your time here. I won’t say a word." Cui Lingyuan’s tone, surprisingly, lightened. "That day, you broke into the ducal mansion asking around and found nothing. Do you know why? Because I arranged everything myself. Even Zaizhou doesn’t know."

Zhao Xuanyou understood that Cui Lingyuan wasn’t bluffing.

Pan Xun had interrogated the mansion’s servants repeatedly, and not a single one knew there was a corpse buried in the well by the firewood shed. This proved Cui Lingyuan’s words were true.

The Cui family’s death sentence was already decided. Not only would verbal humiliation fail to make Cui Lingyuan talk, but even torture wouldn’t.

But Yu Ying had last been seen at the Xingguo Ducal Mansion, and the person who had erased her traces was Cui Lingyuan. If Cui Lingyuan refused to speak, Zhao Xuanyou had no way to track Yu Ying down.

If he couldn’t find Yu Ying, how could he ask her why she had run away?!

Zhao Xuanyou had never been at anyone’s mercy in his life, but now, his veins were nearly bursting with frustration.

He clenched his fists tightly, his voice low and heavy. "The tribute pearl case is already settled. The Xingguo Ducal Mansion will certainly face severe punishment. However, I do have a plan to save you."

"What plan?" Cui Lingyuan, who had been impassive all along, suddenly opened his eyes wide, staring fixedly at Zhao Xuanyou.

But Zhao Xuanyou wasn’t in a hurry to answer. Instead, he countered, "How many people broke into the Xingguo Ducal Mansion that night?"

Cui Lingyuan understood that without offering something, Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t easily reveal his hand.

"At least three."

"Did you kill anyone?"

Cui Lingyuan shook his head.

"Since you didn’t kill them, why did you bury the body?"

"You’ve dug deep and investigated thoroughly, haven’t you?"

Zhao Xuanyou gritted his teeth, cracking his knuckles. "Why did you cover up the fire in the first place? It shouldn’t have been just to hide the tribute pearls, right?"

Cui Lingyuan spoke slowly, "I’ve answered so many of your questions. Isn’t it your turn to answer mine? At this point, I don’t care about the fire at all. Only you can show me a way out. As I said, I will tell you everything without reservation."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes churned with dark clouds. He pointed to Cui Zaizhou beside him.

Cui Lingyuan was stunned.

"Sacrificing a pawn to save the chariot. Shouldn’t you be familiar with that? Didn’t you escape the same way last time?"

To Cui Lingyuan, Tao Cheng had indeed been a mere pawn, but Cui Zaizhou was his legitimate eldest son. How could he abandon him so easily?

"But even if... he takes the blame..."

"From the moment those tribute pearls were found, the Xingguo Ducal Mansion was doomed. However, a cunning old fox like you, if you survive, starting over won’t be difficult. I’ve shown you the way. Now it’s your turn to recount that night’s events in detail. If you lie, I won’t mind injuring another person."

Survival was indeed the most important. Cui Lingyuan listened to Zhao Xuanyou’s threat, his expression complex.

So intelligent, both literary and martial. If he had remained his son-in-law, how good would that have been?

Cui Lingyuan took a deep breath and said in a low voice, "That night, at least three people infiltrated the ducal mansion. They were not only familiar with the mansion’s layout but also highly skilled in martial arts. They were able to abduct Yichu from Qingyun Courtyard to the firewood shed, overturn all the water vats next to the shed, and escape the mansion unscathed after setting the fire. I pride myself on having many capable subordinates, but none are as well-trained as those people. I don’t know which power they belong to."

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart pounded wildly.

Neither abducting Cui Yichu nor overturning the water vats were things Yu Ying could have done alone.

This meant she had at least two accomplices; two accomplices with top-tier lightness skills and martial arts.

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly recalled the argument he had with the Crown Prince in front of the Imperial Study on New Year’s Day. At the time, the Crown Prince had accused him of setting the fire that killed Cui Yichu, and Zhao Xuanyou had retorted in kind.

The Eastern Palace had many experts, but the Crown Prince would never help Yu Ying burn Cui Yichu to death.

Apart from the Crown Prince and himself, there was only one person in the capital who had such skilled subordinates and was acquainted with Yu Ying; Zhao Qi.

Zhao Xuanyou abruptly stood up.

Cui Lingyuan narrowed his eyes. "Do you know who it is?"

Although Zhao Qi was young, with the Emperor’s and the Duke of Ningguo’s careful cultivation, he had many capable people under him, rivaling even the Eastern Palace.

If Yu Ying had asked him for help, he would certainly have agreed.

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent, his expression appearing calm, but his heart felt as if it were being fried in hot oil.

Of all his calculations, he had never expected Yu Ying to have been taken away by that brash youngster, Zhao Qi.

"You mentioned Yu Ying. Who is she? Is she the arsonist?" Cui Lingyuan truly didn’t know who Yu Ying was, but Zhao Xuanyou’s relentless pursuit clearly indicated her importance.

Cui Lingyuan recalled that during the separation ceremony, he had seen a maidservant by Zhao Xuanyou’s side in Honghui Hall. She was slightly younger than Yichu, not only resembling Yichu in appearance but also giving off an inexplicable sense of familiarity.

Was she the Yu Ying Zhao Xuanyou was looking for?

If that hairpin diagram was left by her... then she was his and Wenxi’s daughter...

"None of your concern." With that, Zhao Xuanyou quickly left the prison of the Court of Judicial Review.

Now that he knew who was behind it, the next steps would be much easier.

Although Zhao Xuanyou was currently suspended, he was still the Commander of the Brocade Guard. Pan Xun, having already transferred the tribute pearl case to the Court of Judicial Review, had some free time and was at Zhao Xuanyou’s beck and call.

Immediately, the Brocade Guard spread out like a fine net, placing informants and investigating Zhao Qi’s people left in the capital.

Soon, they got a lead: the two guards at the separate courtyard were Zhao Qi’s men.

After finding Bingyun and Yangquan, the rest became straightforward. The Brocade Guard followed the trail from the capital to Jiao Ye Village, and from Jiao Ye Village to Yangzhou.

Zhao Xuanyou rode through the night to Yangzhou, where he captured Bingyun and Yangquan at Mingyue Tower, but there was no sign of Yu Ying and her mother.

That had been over a month ago.

All leads ended there.

Zhao Xuanyou stood before Mingyue Tower, watching the countless black awning boats on the Qin Huai River, and suddenly understood why she had come here.

The waterways in the south were dense, and black awning boats were everywhere.

Once she boarded a boat, she was like a fish leaping into the water, leaving no trace behind.

She hadn’t intended to rely on Zhao Qi. She had only used his strength to take revenge, used his strength to leave the capital, and then shaken him off.

But he had no right to mock Zhao Qi. Back in the capital, when she had faked her death, she had already shaken him off as well.

In her heart, was he really not even as important as Zhao Qi?

The moment Zhao Xuanyou learned she was still alive, he realized that the extra corpse had been meant to deceive him.

He didn’t understand why she had to leave so desperately. He was unwilling to accept, unable to believe that she could be so heartless.

But the results of his relentless investigation only brought him greater disappointment.

To her, he had always been someone to humor, to play along with.

All the intimacy, the shared pillow and whispered words; it was only because he was the marquis’ heir, and she happened to be a maidservant in the marquis’ mansion.

He could no longer find her.

And she had never intended for him to find her.

The tender moments in Honghui Hall, she could discard without hesitation, without a trace of lingering affection.

Only he had been blinded by those moments, stubbornly clinging to the past.

In the late spring of Jiangnan, fine rain fell like silk, and the clouds drifted softly. Zhao Xuanyou closed his eyes, as if he had fallen into an ice cellar.

chapters.title: A Thousand Rivers and Mountains
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou stood by the Qin Huai River for a long time.

Pan Xun and the others stood with him from day into night. Seeing that he still had no intention of leaving, they had no choice but to step forward and ask, "Commander, do you need us to search every corner of Yangzhou City?"

What more was there to search...

Even if Bingyun and Yangquan couldn't match the Jin Yi Wei's ability to unravel the most tangled threads, they were far from incompetent.

After Yu Wan left, the two of them had stayed in Yangzhou City for over a month and found nothing. The Jin Yi Wei had also come up empty.

"Search."

Having come this far, how could Zhao Xuanyou give up?

"Take Yu Wan's portrait. Start from Mingyue Tower and question every household."

Yu Wan's faked death and escape had changed everything.

Zhao Xuanyou's emotions had been turned upside down as well.

He had gone from being someone who sought the truth and wanted to avenge her, to someone insignificant, discarded like a worn-out shoe.

During those days and nights when he was imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice's dungeon, watching the wax candles drip away, facing the thick stone walls alone, he would sometimes be overwhelmed by grief, and other times be consumed by rage, wishing to tear everything to pieces.

But Yu Wan was not dead. At this very moment, she was somewhere, laughing and smiling.

Given her nature, she would certainly find a cozy nest, arrange her life to be comfortable and at ease, and live happily with her mother, never thinking of him again.

Night had completely fallen.

Zhao Xuanyou stood by the Qin Huai River, watching the pleasure boats adorned with colorful lanterns, listening to the melodious, lingering songs of the singing girls, facing the splendid scenery of the south of the Yangtze River alone, yet his heart was a wasteland.

Pan Xun and his men turned Yangzhou City upside down for ten days.

Of course, some people had seen Yu Wan and her mother, but that was only when they were at Mingyue Tower. Apart from that, there was no other trace of them.

The Jin Yi Wei were the Emperor's personal guards, experts in gathering intelligence and solving cases, with eyes and ears everywhere. Relying on the Jin Yi Wei's powerful intelligence network, Zhao Xuanyou had traced from the capital to Yangzhou in just half a month.

But now, even this vast net could not catch Yu Wan.

Even if Zhao Xuanyou refused to give up, he had no way to continue the search.

He led his men back to the capital and was soon summoned into the palace by the Emperor.

In the imperial study, the Emperor's eyes were slightly downcast as he looked at Zhao Xuanyou standing before the imperial desk, and slowly exhaled.

"Have you had enough of this nonsense?"

Initially, when he appointed Zhao Xuanyou as the Commander of the Jin Yi Wei, it was because he appreciated his keen insight and measured approach, which could help him handle matters concerning the Empress and the Prince of Zhen Guo's residence.

Who would have thought that after the fire at the Prince of Xingguo's residence, Zhao Xuanyou would act as if he had lost his mind? First, he had opened a coffin and injured someone at the Prince's residence, then he had been imprisoned for two months and still wouldn't behave. As soon as he was released, he led Pan Xun and a large group of men around, chasing after a missing maid from his own residence.

Zhao Xuanyou knelt down and pleaded guilty: "This subject knows his crime and asks for Your Majesty's punishment."

The Emperor coldly snorted, "I heard you turned Yangzhou City upside down. What, still haven't found her?"

"No."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou's slightly darkened expression, the Emperor couldn't help but narrow his eyes.

The Jin Yi Wei were his personal guards, so naturally, everyone was his eyes and ears.

He knew who Zhao Xuanyou was looking for, and he also knew about the fire at the Prince of Xingguo's residence, in which Zhao Qi had also played a part.

Not to mention Zhao Xuanyou, even Zhao Qi, who still had a face of youthful innocence, had reached the age where he could be swayed by emotions.

Who knew what kind of breathtakingly beautiful face that Yu Wan had, to have reduced the two of them to this state.

"Rise."

If the Emperor had wanted to punish him, he would have stopped him when he led the Jin Yi Wei south.

Zhao Xuanyou remained kneeling on the ground.

The Emperor narrowed his eyes and said slowly, "You are a man of deep emotions, but you are not suited to remain in the Jin Yi Wei. In a few days, return to the Ming Jian Wei."

Even when he had taken action against the Prince of Xingguo's residence, Zhao Xuanyou had known that, regardless of whether he would be exonerated in the future, his position as Commander of the Jin Yi Wei would not last long.

The Jin Yi Wei were the Emperor's blade, and they had to strike wherever the Emperor pointed. How could they tolerate his willful actions?

"This subject obeys Your Majesty's decree and thanks Your Majesty for your great kindness."

This expression of gratitude was not mere formality; it came from the heart.

The Emperor had known that he had led the Jin Yi Wei south for personal reasons, yet he had neither stopped nor punished him, clearly intending to help him find the person he sought.

"You are quite sensible." The Emperor said with a smile, then sighed softly in his heart.

Here was someone who could have been his right-hand man, yet he was trapped by love, leaving the Emperor with no one to use.

As if he could see through the Emperor's thoughts, Zhao Xuanyou cupped his hands and said, "This subject has one more matter to report."

"Speak."

"Captain Pan Xun is thoughtful and steady in his actions, a rare talent with both literary and martial skills. Unlike this subject, he does not act impulsively. Your Majesty may consider entrusting him with greater responsibilities."

The Emperor's eyes flickered for a moment before he said slowly, "I see. You may withdraw."

During the month and a half that Zhao Xuanyou and his men had been in Jiangnan, the Ministry of Justice had concluded the case of the Prince of Xingguo's residence. The heir, Cui Zaizhou, had confessed to colluding with his maternal uncle, Tao Cheng, to embezzle tribute pearls. However, before the sentence could be carried out, he had fallen ill and died in prison. The Princess of Xingguo, Tao Shi, had taken her own life after his death.

Originally, the rest of the Cui family should have been exiled to the farthest reaches of the empire, but Ningguo Gong, seeing that his granddaughter, Shen Fen Yun, was with child and would certainly not survive the journey, had petitioned the Emperor for leniency as a respected elder of three reigns.

With such a highly respected figure as Ningguo Gong intervening, along with the subtle efforts of Prime Minister Sun and others, most of the court officials believed that the Cui family should be treated leniently.

After all, the first Prince of Xingguo had been the only scholar-official among the meritorious officials who had helped the Taizong Emperor conquer the world. His name was renowned in history for his wisdom and had always been highly respected by Confucian scholars.

After much consideration, the Emperor had ordered the Ministry of Justice to handle the case leniently. The title of the Prince of Xingguo was revoked, and the Cui family was demoted to commoner status.

In the Honghui Hall, Zhao Xuanyou's face showed no hint of joy upon hearing this news.

"Do you think the Emperor's punishment of them is too lenient?" Jingyuan Hou observed his dimmed gaze and asked.

The next day, Zhao Xuanyou would leave the capital for the Ming Jian Wei. That evening, Jingyuan Hou had specially come to Honghui Hall to drink with him, and the father and son had a heart-to-heart talk.

"The Emperor is indeed a benevolent ruler."

Zhao Xuanyou didn't care about the lives of the Cui family. He was only thinking of Yu Wan.

Although he wasn't sure if Yu Wan was Cui Lingyuan's daughter, she certainly hated the Prince of Xingguo's residence. Would she be happy or disappointed to hear this news?

Probably disappointed.

She would definitely say, "They got off too easily."

Zhao Xuanyou could almost imagine the expression on her face as she said that.

Jingyuan Hou watched Zhao Xuanyou's alternating expressions of pursed lips and furrowed brows and sighed softly. "Do you like that woman so much?"

Since returning to the Hou residence, Jingyuan Hou had learned about Yu Wan from Lady Ye's complaints and nagging.

Zhao Xuanyou had lost his mother at a young age, and his father had been plagued by injuries. At the age of ten, he had joined the army and quickly become the backbone of the Ming Jian Wei, supporting the Jingyuan Hou residence.

For this son, Jingyuan Hou had always felt guilty, and even now, after this trouble, he bore no resentment.

Zhao Xuanyou gathered his thoughts and looked at Jingyuan Hou.

"Father, I..."

Jingyuan Hou reached out and patted his shoulder. "I understand your feelings. I don't think you did anything wrong. Even if you want to marry her, I won't object."

Marry her?

Zhao Xuanyou was somewhat stunned.

"But," Jingyuan Hou changed the subject, "since she has decided to hide far away, it seems she has no feelings for you."

Zhao Xuanyou fell silent.

"Will you still look for her?" Jingyuan Hou asked.

"Of course."

Through a thousand rivers and mountains, he had to find her and get an answer from her.

---

chapters.title: Pearls
chapters.content:
Spring gave way to autumn, and the season gradually entered the Frost's Descent.

In the ship's cabin, Ding Wenxi was painting while Yu Wan was reading.

Since the day they had boarded the ship from Mingyue Tower, the mother and daughter had been living on the boat for over half a year.

Not long after leaving Yangzhou City, Wen Kuo had sold the previous black awning boat and replaced it with a larger one, partitioning the front and back into two small rooms.

Over the past six months, Wen Kuo had navigated the boat through the small towns of Jiangnan.

The best way to avoid being discovered was to leave no trace at all.

During this time, Yu Wan and Ding Wenxi rarely disembarked. They only went ashore when the boat was in the mountains or fields with no one around.

However, the cabin, though narrow, was not shabby.

On the table, a bamboo tube served as a vase, holding wild chrysanthemums picked that morning. The writing brushes, ink, paper, and inkstones were all fine quality purchased in Suzhou City.

When they had left, they had traveled light, taking only banknotes, the books Pei Ta had given, and the fox mask left by Zhao Qi.

"Mother, I don't understand this sentence. Director Pei's annotation only has one line, and I still don't get it after reading it."

"Let me see."

Although Ding Wenxi was not a talented scholar, she had some knowledge of music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. When Yu Wan encountered difficulties in her reading, Ding Wenxi could offer some guidance.

"Min ke shi you zhi, bu ke shi..."

As mother and daughter pondered over the Analects, Wen Kuo entered with a food box.

"I bought roast chicken."

Wen Kuo had a mysterious appearance and knew how to disguise himself. Over the past six months, he had been the one to go out for purchases and visit towns.

Seeing him return, Yu Wan's eyes curved into a smile as she set down her book to take the food box.

Ding Wenxi, skilled in household tasks, neatly arranged the brushes, ink, paper, and inkstones to the side and handed Wen Kuo a cup of tea.

Wen Kuo silently sat down to drink his tea while Yu Wan opened the food box and took out the roast chicken and dishes.

"What do you think of this place?"

"Not as scenic as Jiangnan," Wen Kuo said.

After drifting through Jiangnan for four months, they had been traveling eastward and were said to reach the river mouth in a few more days.

"If you like Jiangnan, we can go back to visit once we've settled down."

"I was just saying," Wen Kuo said after drinking his tea, and helped set the bowls and plates.

After months of drifting on the same boat, the three of them had long since become like family.

Ding Wenxi asked gently, "Yu Wan, you said this place is famous for its pearls. Did you see many pearl merchants in the marketplace?"

"Many. The streets are full of them. But they all sell small, irregularly shaped pearls. Most are like rice grains, not very pretty, and no one pays attention to them."

"Large, round pearls are all tribute items. Only the small, irregular ones make it to the common market. These beautiful and inexpensive things are exactly what my daughter and I want."

Yu Wan and Ding Wenxi had pondered their future livelihood for a long time.

Buying land and building a house would be good, but Yu Wan knew that Ding Wenxi enjoyed making jewelry. The hairpins, earrings, and necklaces she designed were all beautiful.

Since she had this interest, why not make a living from it?

But starting a jewelry business was not simple. They needed raw materials, craftsmen, and sales channels.

Yu Wan suddenly remembered what Pei Ta had said, that his father was a county magistrate in a small coastal city where pearls were abundant. So she had followed the waterways to this place to take a look.

"Not bad. Although we want to be in the jewelry business, if we buy expensive pearls, we'll inevitably have to deal with officials and nobles. Let's use these unwanted small pearls to make hairpins and necklaces. Thin profits, quick turnover."

"Mother is right."

Although Wen Kuo preferred Jiangnan, Qingsha Town was by the sea. The sea was vast and boundless, with a majestic momentum, offering a different kind of world.

"If you're so interested in Qingsha Town, why not go into town and take a look?"

"Okay."

They had been away from the capital for more than half a year. Qingsha Town was particularly remote, so it was unlikely anyone would recognize them.

After dinner, Ding Wenxi and Yu Wan changed their clothes and went into town with Wen Kuo.

Although Qingsha Town had suffered years of exploitation under the corrupt official Tao Cheng, in recent years, the local officials had changed, and the town had begun to recover.

The marketplace looked a bit run-down, but there were still many people coming and going.

After visiting several pearl shops, Ding Wenxi and Yu Wan were even more convinced of their previous idea.

Those pearls, although small and oddly shaped, still had a lustrous glow. With the right setting, they could be made into beautiful jewelry.

Once they had chosen a place to settle, the subsequent matters became much simpler.

It was still Wen Kuo who took the lead, spending sixty taels of silver to buy a house with a storefront on the west side of the town. The front could be used for business, and the back for living.

Compared to the capital's exorbitant land prices, this place was like a paradise on earth.

Soon, Wen Kuo spent more silver to have the local chief act as a guarantor for the three of them to register their household in the county yamen.

He claimed his surname was Ding, and he and Yu Wan posed as siblings, with Ding Wenxi naturally being their mother.

After obtaining the household registration and property deed, Yu Wan hired a few craftsmen to make a signboard, simply carved with the characters "Ding Ji Jewelry Shop."

She also hired someone to renovate the storefront, but nothing else was changed.

First, she needed to save money to purchase raw materials. Second, the jewelry they made was not intended to be sold in Qingsha Town.

After all, Qingsha Town was not prosperous. Most of its residents were fishermen and pearl divers, who neither had the spare money to buy jewelry nor, having seen so many pearls, would be interested in their products.

Yu Wan had come to Qingsha Town not only because it was remote and no one would recognize her, but also to buy cheap pearls. She planned to set up a workshop here to make pearl jewelry and then sell it in Jiangnan.

That was the plan, but whether it would succeed, she didn't know.

For now, they had a shop and raw materials, but the lack of craftsmen was troubling Yu Wan.

Ding Wenxi knew how to make jewelry, but she was getting older, her health was weaker than before, and even if she worked from morning till night, she alone couldn't produce much.

To expand the business, they naturally needed to recruit craftsmen.

Yu Wan asked the town's brokers to spread the word, but they only found one silversmith named Xu, who could make silver bracelets, hairpins, and earrings but had never worked with pearl jewelry.

After Ding Wenxi personally guided him, he managed to make a simple pearl hairpin, so the shop had its first jewelry craftsman.

But that was still not enough.

"Wen Kuo, you're strong. Why don't you learn jewelry-making from my mother?" After much thought, Yu Wan turned to Wen Kuo for help.

Wen Kuo retorted, "You're strong too. Why don't you learn? Once you do, you can inherit the family business."

"I can't do that kind of delicate work." Yu Wan was not making excuses. Although she was clever, she was naturally bad at fine handwork. Forget intricate carving; she couldn't even do embroidery. "Besides, I'm the manager here. I need to oversee everything."

"I'm the handyman here. I'm only responsible for odd jobs."

Wen Kuo had no other hobbies besides daydreaming. He either lay on a tree sunbathing or on a rooftop moon-gazing.

Listening to their bickering, Ding Wenxi couldn't help but smile, her face filled with affectionate amusement.

chapters.title: The Honest Official
chapters.content:
"Since our shop is going to make and sell jewelry ourselves, we naturally need our own craftsmen."

Ding Wenxi had learned her craft from the eunuchs and palace ladies of the Imperial Silver Workshop. In the palace, jewelry was made without regard to cost, aiming only for dazzling beauty to please the masters.

During the more than half a year they spent drifting on the river, she and Yuhuan had come up with many simple yet unique and beautiful designs. If they took these designs elsewhere to be made, others might copy them. So, they had to make them themselves before selling.

"Mother, if we can't find anyone to hire, why not take on some apprentices?"

Qingsha Town was remote and sparsely populated. It had been difficult enough to hire Master Xu; finding more people would be even harder.

Even if they spent a fortune to bring in craftsmen from elsewhere, since they weren’t locals and their families weren’t here, they wouldn’t stay long.

"Apprentices?"

"Yes. We have savings, so we’re not in a hurry to make money. Mother and Master Xu can make as much as they can, and slowly teach the apprentices. In a year or two, they should be skilled enough, and then Mother won’t have to work so hard."

"But in this town, people either fish or dive for pearls. Would anyone be willing to come to the shop to learn jewelry-making?"

"I’ve heard that local customs here don’t allow women on boats, so whether it’s pearl diving or fishing, it’s all men’s work. We can specifically recruit women."

In the common world, goldsmiths and silversmiths were all men, and their skills were passed down only to men, not women.

But in the palace, it was different. The Imperial Silver Workshop had many highly skilled palace ladies, and Ding Wenxi didn’t think women were any worse at making jewelry than men.

Listening to Yuhuan’s idea, Ding Wenxi naturally agreed.

"If women here have a hard time making a living, and we spread the word that we’re looking for female apprentices, offering food and teaching skills, there will definitely be people willing to come."

Yuhuan said, "For those who learn well and master the craft quickly, we can give them a reward. And if they stay here to work after learning, we’ll pay them the same as a skilled master."

Apprentices didn’t get paid; it was considered working in exchange for learning.

A craftsman’s wages were related to their skill and years of experience. Those who learned from them and stayed to work would be paid as skilled masters, which was a considerable incentive.

Ding Wenxi nodded in agreement. Seeing Wen Ji had been silent all along, she smiled and asked, "Xiao Wen, what do you think?"

"Huh? It’s good."

Wen Ji didn’t have any particular thoughts. Whatever Yuhuan thought was good, he thought was good too.

Even if he didn’t think it was good, Yuhuan would persuade him otherwise.

Having made up their minds, Yuhuan and Wen Ji went out together to find a broker.

"Yuhuan."

As soon as they stepped out of the shop, Wen Ji called out to her.

Sensing he had something to say, Yuhuan asked, "What is it?"

"You want to stay in Qingsha Town just because it produces pearls?"

"Yeah," feeling Wen Ji’s gaze on her, Yuhuan found it strange. They had been here for a while now, so why was he suddenly bringing this up? "Don’t you want to live here?"

Of course he did.

Originally, Wen Ji had loved the beautiful landscapes of Jiangnan. After coming to Qingsha Town, he had also grown fond of going to the seaside, often sitting there for half a day.

"Then why are you asking?"

Wen Ji glanced at Yuhuan. "You came here, is it really not because of someone else?"

Seeing him persist, Yuhuan said, "It’s because of the pearls, but not only because of the pearls. Qingsha Town is on the East China Sea, far from the capital. Living here, no one will recognize me and Mother. Plus, it’s close to Jiangnan, and with water routes, once our business takes off, it’ll be convenient to transport goods to Jiangnan."

She spoke from the heart, and Wen Ji listened in confusion.

"What did you think it was?" Yuhuan saw his strange expression and squinted as she leaned closer. "Spill it."

"I thought it was because of that Lord Pei."

Yuhuan was stunned. "Why would it be because of Lord Pei?"

Seeing Yuhuan’s bewildered look, Wen Ji said, "You really didn’t know that Lord Pei is the Prefect of Qingzhou?"

On the boat, Yuhuan had read Pei Tao’s books every day and discussed his annotations with Ding Wenxi. In Wen Ji’s mind, Yuhuan naturally held Pei Tao in high regard.

"Really?" Yuhuan was surprised. "How do you know?"

Qingsha Town was under the jurisdiction of Qingzhou. Yuhuan had only known that Pei Tao had been sent out to be a prefect, but she hadn’t known he had come to Qingzhou.

"This morning, when I went out, I heard people talking outside a teahouse. They all said he’s a good official, that Qingzhou has finally gotten a just and honest governor."

Pei Tao had left the capital half a year earlier than Yuhuan. By now, he had already been the prefect of Qingzhou for a year.

"I did learn about Qingsha Town’s pearls from Lord Pei, but I didn’t expect him to be the Prefect of Qingzhou."

Her father had been the magistrate of Qingsha Town and had been framed by Prefect Tao Cheng, which had led to his depression and death.

The emperor had sent Pei Tao to be the Prefect of Qingzhou, likely to have him eliminate corruption and bring renewal to the region.

After a moment of shock, a smile appeared on Yuhuan’s face.

"What are you happy about?" Wen Ji asked.

"Does it matter to you?" Yuhuan just smiled and walked ahead, not answering his question.

Wen Ji quickly caught up. "Are you going to see him?"

"No." Yuhuan frowned. "And even if I were, what does it have to do with you?"

"I’m just reminding you. Even though he’s the Prefect of Qingzhou now, it won’t be long before he returns to the capital to be an official there."

Wen Ji knew a little about court affairs. Someone like Pei Tao, who was highly favored by the emperor, would return to the capital after a few years in an external post to be given an important position.

"You’re overthinking it. I won’t go see him."

"Really?"

Yuhuan sighed. Seeing he didn’t believe her, she had to voice the thought in her mind: "We finally managed to leave the capital. Of course I won’t reconnect with people from the past. It’s not just about going to see him; now that I know he’s the Prefect of Qingzhou, I won’t even go to Qingzhou."

That made sense, but Wen Ji was still confused. "Then why were you smiling just now?"

Yuhuan justified confidently, "Lord Pei is a man of great talent and integrity. Under his governance, Qingzhou must be well-administered with harmonious people and thriving markets. It’ll be easy for us to do business without worrying about bullies or local tyrants oppressing us."

That did make sense.

Moreover, with him there, there wouldn’t be any bullies daring to oppress them in the first place.

Soon, Yuhuan found a broker and explained her plans.

The broker was surprised to hear they wanted to recruit women as artisan apprentices, but since he was paid to handle their affairs, he readily agreed and helped spread the word.

As Ding Wenxi had said, it was difficult for women in Qingsha Town to make a living. They couldn’t go out to sea to fish or dive for pearls. To earn money, they could only work as servants in wealthy households.

Now, with the jewelry shop offering apprenticeships, teaching skills for free, and providing meals, and with the possibility of staying on as workers after learning, it was like a pie falling from the sky.

Although many people doubted their skills, the offer of three meals a day alone was a significant benefit for poor families.

The broker quickly brought over a dozen women.

At this point, Master Xu, who had been hired for the shop, said he wouldn’t casually take on apprentices, especially not women.

Ding Wenxi’s skills had originally surpassed his, so if he wouldn’t teach, she could teach them herself, though she couldn’t take on too many.

She and Yuhuan carefully selected, and in the end, kept two young girls and one woman.

After much preparation, the workshop finally began to take shape.

---

chapters.title: Searching for Someone
chapters.content:
When Ding Wenxi made the first batch of hairpins, Yuhuan and Wen Ji cleared the counter and carefully displayed them.

As they had expected, the people of Qingsha Town were busy making a living and didn’t have much spare money to buy jewelry.

Not to mention buying, few people even came into the shop to inquire.

Yuhuan wasn’t panicked.

The reason they had decided to go into the jewelry business was that Jiangnan was prosperous. Even unknown small-town jewelry shops there had thriving businesses. These pieces of jewelry were originally intended for sale in Jiangnan.

Ding Wenxi understood her plan. While working with Master Xu to make jewelry, she also diligently taught the three apprentices. By the time the New Year passed, the three apprentices, though not yet skilled in fine work, could handle rough tasks.

With their help, the workshop’s output increased significantly, and soon they had accumulated a considerable stock of finished products.

With the experience from the first batch, Ding Wenxi soon recruited a second group of female apprentices. This time, even more people came, but she still only kept three.

Looking at the stock in the warehouse, Yuhuan selected two boxes of high-quality hairpins and, together with Wen Ji, took a boat to Jiangnan. They went from shop to shop to sell their jewelry.

Wen Ji wasn’t good with words, but he was skilled in disguise and helped Yuhuan change her appearance.

Everything is difficult at the beginning. At first, the two of them were turned away many times, barely able to say a few words before being thrown out.

But Yuhuan wasn’t the type to give up easily. If one shop didn’t work, she went to another. If one town didn’t want their goods, she went to the next.

Ding’s pearl hairpins were reasonably priced and had unique designs. After visiting many shops, they naturally found discerning shopkeepers willing to buy some to sell in their stores.

After wandering around Jiangnan for more than two months, they finally sold all the hairpins they had brought.

When they returned to Qingsha Town, Ding Wenxi immediately delivered good news: shops that had previously bought their hairpins had sent people to Qingsha Town to order more. They wanted not only hairpins but also earrings and bracelets.

As more and more people came to place orders, some shop owners suggested they change to a more impressive shop sign and stamp each piece of jewelry with their own mark.

Yuhuan thought it was a good idea. After discussing it with Ding Wenxi, they changed the sign above the door from "Ding’s Jewelry Shop" to "Yuyu Pavilion," which suited both the workshop’s trade and Yuhuan’s name.

Busy and bustling, another year passed. The business of Yuyu Pavilion gradually stabilized, with ten skilled artisans in the workshop and a steady output each month.

Their business partners all hoped they would expand the workshop and produce more goods, but Yuhuan refused.

A tall tree catches the wind. Yuyu Pavilion was already making a lot of money, enough for the three of them to live comfortably. If the business grew too large, it might invite trouble.

In the blink of an eye, it was the third spring since they had left the capital.

Yuhuan specially had the cook go to the market to buy pork, chives, wood ear mushrooms, bean sprouts, and cellophane noodles.

After checking the ingredients, Yuhuan climbed the wooden ladder to the roof and, as expected, saw Wen Ji sitting on the roof.

"Wen Ji, come here."

"What for?"

"I bought a lot of things. Today we’re having spring rolls."

Saying they were having spring rolls, but it was really for him to make them.

Seeing Wen Ji didn’t move, Yuhuan said, "What? Can’t I invite you, the young master, over?"

The shop’s business had always been managed by Yuhuan, while Wen Ji only looked after the home and guarded the shop. But outsiders only knew Wen Ji as the young master of Yuyu Pavilion and assumed he was the one in charge.

Wen Ji couldn’t argue with her and had to jump down from the roof, heading to the kitchen himself.

By the time Yuhuan came down from the ladder, he had already washed his hands, rolled up his sleeves, and started kneading the dough.

Although they had hired a cook, Yuhuan would occasionally have Wen Ji cook, saying it was to change the flavor.

While Wen Ji was making the wrappers, Ding Wenxi led a woman into the kitchen.

"Mother, Wen Ji is making fried spring rolls for us today." As soon as she spoke, Yuhuan noticed Ding Wenxi’s heavy expression and asked with concern, "What’s wrong?"

Ding Wenxi said, "A few days ago, didn’t I tell you that Qiahe hasn’t been to the workshop for two days?"

"Didn’t she say her elder brother is getting married, and her family is busy?"

Qiahe was one of the first female apprentices Ding Wenxi had taken in. She was clever and quick to learn anything.

Recently, she had said her elder brother was getting married, and there were many things to do at home, so she had been coming to the workshop less frequently.

She was the eldest daughter in her family, and her parents had originally sent her here to save on food expenses. They weren’t particularly good to her.

Knowing her difficult situation, Yuhuan hadn’t fired her but instead paid her daily wages for the days she worked.

"Yes, but previously she would at least come for half a day. This time, she hasn’t come for four days in a row. I was worried, so I had Lin Niangzi go to her house to check, but she wasn’t there."

This Lin Niangzi was from the same first batch of apprentices as Qiahe.

She was a widow who had managed to raise her two sons, who now worked on fishing boats. She had seized the opportunity to come to the workshop to learn a skill and had now become a reliable assistant to Ding Wenxi.

"Her mother said that three days ago, she went with her to Qingzhou City to buy things for her brother’s new room. But on the street, they got separated. She searched for half a day but couldn’t find her, so she assumed Qiahe had gone off exploring on her own. But after several days, she still hadn’t returned, and she thought Qiahe had come to Yuyu Pavilion."

"Why would Qiahe come to Yuyu Pavilion after getting lost in Qingzhou City?"

"Exactly. I told her not to talk nonsense. She took the girl out and lost her, didn’t search properly, and didn’t report it to the authorities. It’s really unforgivable."

Qiahe’s family had many children, and her parents couldn’t be bothered with her.

Now, with her elder brother getting married, the family was busy, and no one had time to look for her.

"Yuan’er, Qiahe is young. She’s been missing for so many days; I’m worried something has happened to her."

Qiahe was one of the first to learn the craft from Ding Wenxi. Apart from her troubles at home, she was usually obedient and clever, and Ding Wenxi had always liked her.

Seeing her disappear, she was naturally worried.

"Her family probably won’t do anything about it. Should we go to the county yamen to report it?" Lin Niangzi asked.

Yuhuan, however, shook her head. "She disappeared in Qingzhou City. Reporting it to the county yamen might not do any good. I’ll go to Qingzhou City to take a look."

After all, Qiahe was a young girl who worked in their workshop. Even if her family didn’t care, Yuhuan couldn’t ignore it.

A teenage girl missing for four full days; it was likely more bad than good.

In the worst case, they might have to look for her in the charity burial grounds.

"You and Ah Ji be careful." Ding Wenxi nodded.

Ever since they had started living as a family, Ding Wenxi had changed Wen Ji’s address from "Xiao Wen" to "Ah Ji."

Wen Ji liked this address. Whenever Ding Wenxi called him that, his indifferent eyes would soften a little.

"We know."

Wen Ji had been to Qingzhou City several times and was fairly familiar with the place, so there shouldn’t be any major issues.

Without time to change clothes or disguise herself, Yuhuan only took a veil to cover her face and, together with Wen Ji, rode a horse to Qingzhou City.

chapters.title: Investigating
chapters.content:
Qingsha Town was not far from Qingzhou Prefecture. An hour later, Yuhan and Wen Ji arrived at the city gate.

"How do you want to look for her?"

Yuhan frowned silently.

The worst-case scenario was that Qiahe had encountered a villain and was already dead.

Qiahe was at the age of a flower, with a delicate appearance. Either she had been kidnapped or sold.

She was probably still alive, but had been humiliated.

"Wen Ji, go to the charity morgue and ask if any bodies matching Qiahe's age have been sent there in the past few days, or if there have been any homicide cases. I'll go to Xiangyufang to ask about the human traffickers in Qingzhou City. Come to Xiangyufang after you're done."

The owner of Xiangyufang had business dealings with Shouyuxuan. Their business was large, selling jewelry, cosmetics, and silks. They had five storefronts on one street alone.

Thinking that the owner had extensive connections, and Yuhan was not familiar with the situation in Qingzhou City, she decided to visit and ask for help.

"Are we splitting up?" Wen Ji frowned slightly.

Seeing that he was worried about her, Yuhan said, "Splitting up will be faster. Xiangyufang is just around the corner, nothing will happen."

But Wen Ji insisted, "I'll take you there first, then go to the morgue."

He had promised Ding Wenxi to take good care of Yuhan, and he intended to keep his word.

"Alright."

Wen Ji accompanied Yuhan to the entrance of Xiangyufang. After watching her enter, he turned and hurried to the morgue.

Although Qingzhou Prefecture was not as prosperous as Jiangnan, it was the location of the prefectural government, making it much livelier than Qingsha Town. In Xiangyufang, besides women and girls picking out their favorite items, there were also young masters and scholars inquiring about prices.

After Yuhan introduced herself, the shopkeeper's wife came out with a smile. "Previously, it was always the young master who came to Qingzhou for business. This time, the young lady has finally come."

The shopkeeper's wife had met Yuhan once before when she visited Qingsha Town.

"You flatter me, I'm not much of a young lady."

Since she was visiting, Yuhan couldn't keep her veil on. She took it off and placed it aside. After exchanging pleasantries, the shopkeeper's wife smiled and asked if Shouyuxuan had new goods.

Yuhan got straight to the point and told her about Qiahe.

The shopkeeper's wife, being experienced, thought for a moment and said, "Miss Ding, I don't mean to think ill of others, but since Qiahe's family is in urgent need of money, it's likely that she wasn't kidnapped but was sold by her family to Qingzhou."

Yuhan, of course, understood this possibility.

Qiahe's family was greedy. Her elder brother was able to marry smoothly thanks to the wages Qiahe had saved at Shouyuxuan.

But she had three younger brothers, all of whom needed to marry, and her wages were not enough.

When she heard that Lin's family did not report Qiahe missing, Yuhan had already suspected this.

"Whether she was kidnapped or sold by her family, she would have passed through a human trafficker. My mother is very worried about her. No matter what, we need to find out her whereabouts."

"It's her fortune to have met you." After listening to Yuhan, the shopkeeper's wife told her about a few well-known human traffickers in the city. "I suggest you go to Wei Wu first. He has many connections and often looks for young and beautiful women to sell to Jiangnan. He pays well, and since her family is greedy, it's very likely they sold her through him."

Indeed, Shouyuxuan paid well. The amount that could tempt Qiahe's family must be substantial.

"Thank you for your guidance."

"I'll have someone invite Wei Wu over. I've done business with him before. Here, he should tell the truth."

Yuhan was delighted and thanked the shopkeeper's wife again.

The shopkeeper's wife sent an apprentice to find the man and had someone pour tea for Yuhan. She then went to attend to other customers.

Yuhan sat in the corner of the shop, slowly sipping her tea, feeling sorry for Qiahe.

If she was indeed sold by her family, and they had a contract, Yuhan wouldn't be able to take her away.

But since they knew each other, she had to at least find out if she was kidnapped.

As Yuhan was drinking her tea, a young man suddenly approached her. "Miss, is my master's clothing ready?"

"I'm not from the shop." Yuhan knew that sitting behind the counter had led to the misunderstanding and explained.

"I apologize for the disturbance."

The man quickly apologized and was about to ask someone else when the shopkeeper's wife came forward with a smile. "Pei Daren's clothing was sent to the prefectural office a quarter of an hour ago. It should be arriving soon."

"In that case, thank you for your trouble."

"It's our honor that Pei Daren chooses to have his clothes made at Xiangyufang. In the future, if there's anything, feel free to ask. If Pei Daren is too busy with official duties, I can send a tailor to his residence."

"My master doesn't like to trouble others. There's no need for such courtesy."

"It's not courtesy. Even other shops can send tailors to take measurements and make clothes at the customer's home."

"Alright, I'll inform my master." With that, the young man left.

After the man was far away, the shopkeeper's wife sighed. "Pei Daren is truly incorruptible. It's a blessing for us common people to have such a prefect in Qingzhou."

"Yes." Yuhan lightly agreed.

"Do you know? When the greedy official Tao was in charge of Qingzhou, life was miserable. Merchants earned some money, but it was all extorted by him. Alright, let's not talk about that," the shopkeeper's wife changed the subject and smiled again. "Miss Ding, have you met Pei Daren?"

"No."

"If you have the chance, you really should meet him."

"Why? Is Pei Daren very handsome?" Yuhan asked casually.

"Handsome? He's more like a celestial being. I've never seen anyone like him. Even if he does nothing and just stands there, people can't take their eyes off him."

When Pei Tao came to have his clothes made, all the embroidery girls in Xiangyufang came to see the commotion, causing quite a few laughs.

The shopkeeper's wife couldn't stop talking about Pei Tao. "I heard that he used to be in the capital and divorced his original wife. Now, many families in the city want to marry their daughters to him. Many matchmakers have visited, but Pei Daren has rejected them all. I wonder what kind of woman can catch his eye."

Yuhan was also curious.

Would he marry another clever and gentle noblewoman like Sun Qianran?

Probably. Even though he was exiled, there should still be many families in the capital who wanted to form a marriage alliance with him.

Seeing that Yuhan's expression was indifferent and she didn't respond, the shopkeeper's wife smiled. "At least, in the eyes of us ordinary people, that's the case. Miss Ding, you look in the mirror every day, so you must be used to it. Unlike us, who are easily surprised."

"Don't tease me. I'm just a country girl. How can I be compared to Pei Daren?"

The first time Yuhan saw Pei Tao, she was also surprised.

It wasn't even a face-to-face meeting. Before seeing Pei Tao, just hearing him speak made her feel that he was extraordinary.

Yuhan took a deep breath, not allowing her thoughts to be led astray by the shopkeeper's wife.

Qingzhou City was not small, and Pei Tao was an official. It was unlikely that he would be strolling the streets.

But she could encounter Pei Tao's subordinate at Xiangyufang. It wasn't impossible to meet Pei Tao on the street... Yuhan regretted not disguising herself before going out. After the shopkeeper's wife went to attend to other customers, she reached out and put her veil back on.

As she was daydreaming, Wen Ji returned.

---

chapters.title: Night Raid
chapters.content:
"How was the investigation at the morgue?" Yuhan asked with concern.

Wen Ji saw that she was still wearing her veil indoors and found it strange. He whispered, "I carefully checked all the bodies stored in the morgue. There was no Qiahe. I also asked around. There have been no homicide cases in the prefectural office these past few days."

Yuhan let out a slight sigh of relief. No matter what, it was good that she was alive.

"Do you need to look elsewhere?" Wen Ji asked.

"No need. Let's wait for the human trafficker to come here."

Wen Ji hummed in agreement and sat next to Yuhan. He glanced at her and asked, "Why are you still wearing your veil indoors?"

Knowing that he had been running around outside, Yuhan poured him a cup of tea and handed it to him.

"Do you know?" she whispered, "While waiting for you, Pei Tao's subordinate came to Xiangyufang to pick up his finished clothes."

"Did you see him?"

"No, only his subordinate."

"I saw him."

Wen Ji suddenly blurted out, surprising Yuhan. She turned to look at him. "Where did you meet him?"

"Outside the morgue. He was with many people, seemingly investigating a case."

"Did he see you?"

"He doesn't know me."

That was true. When Wen Ji was with the Crown Prince, he had seen Pei Tao a few times. As a dark guard, he usually wore a gray mask, so Pei Tao had never seen his real face.

"Young Master is here." The shopkeeper's wife saw that Wen Ji had also arrived and hurried over to greet him.

Wen Ji had been representing Yuhan and her mother for a long time and now knew how to exchange pleasantries with people.

Fearful that they might be bored, the shopkeeper's wife brought over a few plates of snacks.

As they were eating, they saw a shop assistant leading a man in his thirties into Xiangyufang.

The man cupped his hands in greeting as soon as he saw the shopkeeper's wife and smiled. "Last time, the few maids I sent over, are they still satisfactory?"

"Of course, the people you send are always reliable."

"Are you calling me here to add more people?"

"Not for now. I have two friends who want to ask about something. If you know anything, could you help?"

Hearing the shopkeeper's wife's words, the man's eyes rolled, and he flattered, "Since they are your friends, I will naturally help."

Yuhan immediately stepped forward and told the man about Qiahe.

Wei Wu, upon hearing Yuhan's words, was somewhat surprised. After a moment of hesitation, he said, "A few days ago, I did handle a maid from Qingsha Town. I have too many people, so I don't remember her name."

"Who sold her to you?" Yuhan pressed.

"It was her mother who brought her over. I'm not a kidnapper. If you don't believe me, go ask her mother."

Yuhan's heart sank.

If she had been kidnapped, she and Wen Ji could definitely rescue her. But if she was sold by her own mother, even if they involved the authorities, Yuhan would have no justification.

Wen Ji saw the disappointment in Yuhan's expression and spoke up. "Is she still with you? We want to buy her. Give us a price."

Wei Wu hadn't expected them to be so insistent about Qiahe. He didn't answer, looking at them with a guarded expression. "She's already been sold. If you have any questions, go ask her family. I'm busy."

"Sold to whom?" Yuhan saw his strange reaction and immediately pressed further.

Indeed, seeing their persistence, Wei Wu became impatient. "I said she's been sold. Who are you? If you suspect me, you can ask the authorities."

"Doing business should be about harmony and wealth," seeing that their conversation was about to break down, the shopkeeper's wife came over. "These two also have a good relationship with the girl named Qiahe. They just want to visit her in Qingzhou Prefecture. If it's convenient, they can pay her a visit."

Wei Wu's expression changed slightly, seemingly considering Xiangyufang's influence. He reluctantly said, "She's lucky. A wealthy man took a fancy to her and gave her family a lot of money. The buyer paid a lump sum and doesn't allow visits from relatives or friends. I do business with integrity, so I can't help you."

At this point, Wei Wu was unwilling to answer any more questions. He cupped his hands to the shopkeeper's wife and hastily left.

Yuhan glanced at Wen Ji, who understood. He lowered his head and also went out.

"Miss Ding, I also feel sorry for that girl. But with parents like hers, outsiders can't help her."

"I understand. Thank you for today's trouble. Since we rarely come to Qingzhou, I'll have my brother go out and buy some things. Can I wait for him here?"

"Of course. I'll have another pot of tea brought over."

Yuhan stayed at Xiangyufang for another half hour before Wen Ji returned. He nodded at Yuhan.

The two hadn't discussed anything beforehand, but after more than two years together, they had developed a good understanding.

With a glance from Yuhan, Wen Ji had gone out to follow Wei Wu and found out where he lived before returning.

Afterward, Yuhan bid farewell to the shopkeeper's wife, saying she wanted to return to Qingsha Town before dark.

Leaving Xiangyufang, Yuhan and Wen Ji went to a nearby restaurant and ordered a private room. They ate and drank tea, waiting until it was dark before leaving the restaurant.

"You don't need to go. I can handle it alone."

"No, we'll go together. That Wei guy is very cunning. This afternoon, his eyes were shifting. Qiahe is definitely not sold to some wealthy man."

Wen Ji could never refuse her. After thinking for a moment, he said, "When we get to his house, I'll go in first and take care of the people. Don't rush in."

"I know. I need to interrogate him, not cause a mess."

The two made their way in the dark to Wei Wu's residence. Although he was a human trafficker, his illicit earnings had allowed him to acquire a large mansion.

Fortunately, Wen Ji was the most skilled assassin in the world. He infiltrated the house and soon located Wei Wu's bedroom, successfully subduing him and his wife.

After Wen Ji brought Yuhan in, she saw Wei Wu tied to a chair, his eyes and mouth covered.

"In a moment, I will ask you a few questions. If you don't answer honestly, I will kill your entire family. Nod if you understand."

Yuhan glanced at Wen Ji. Usually quiet, he could deliver threats with precision.

Sure enough, after hearing his words, Wei Wu nodded repeatedly.

Wen Ji reached out and removed the cloth from his mouth, then looked at Yuhan.

"Where exactly did you sell Qiahe to?"

Hearing the name Qiahe, even with his eyes covered, Wei Wu knew who was in front of him.

He wore a miserable expression. "She's not related to you. Why do you have to find her?"

"Answer what I ask!" Wen Ji said, gripping his throat.

Wei Wu, with a sorrowful face, said, "I, I can't afford to offend you, but you can't afford to offend him either."

"Who is he?" Wen Ji asked.

Yuhan saw how afraid he was and didn't know who the person behind him was. After thinking for a moment, she said, "We don't want to cause trouble. As long as you hand over Qiahe, we will leave immediately. We won't ask about anything else."

There were indeed many unfortunate and evil people in the world. Yuhan couldn't save everyone, but she would try her best to save Qiahe, who was right in front of her.

Wei Wu muttered, "It's too late. She's already been handed over. Even the Heavenly King can't save her now."

Before Yuhan could finish speaking, a servant's voice suddenly came from outside the room. "Master, it's not good! The officials are here!"

chapters.title: Weakness
chapters.content:
Upon hearing the words "official authorities," Yu Wan instinctively thought of Pei Ta.

She looked up at Wen Jian, who understood her meaning. With a swift strike, he knocked Wei Wu unconscious.

After opening the door, Wen Jian moved like a shadow, swiftly knocking out the servants in the courtyard with a speed that left no time for reaction.

Yu Wan quickly ran into the courtyard, but heard many footsteps approaching.

"Go out the back."

Wen Jian led Yu Wan toward the back of the house. Just as they were about to reach the wall, he suddenly stopped and held Yu Wan back with his hand.

Yu Wan looked up and saw someone already sitting on the wall.

Her heart jolted. She had originally thought that the officials were just coming to question Wei Wu, but she hadn’t expected to be surrounded.

However, the other party’s clothing did not look like that of officials.

"Trying to escape?" The man immediately saw that Wen Jian had extraordinary skills and blew a whistle before pouncing at him.

Wen Jian quickly pushed Yu Wan to the side and started fighting with him.

Yu Wan, still in shock, glanced at the wall and ran straight toward it.

Wen Jian had excellent qinggong (lightness skill). If she could escape successfully, he would surely find a way to get away as well.

Although Wei Wu’s house was spacious, it was not the residence of a high-ranking official, so the walls were not very high.

Yu Wan struggled to climb to the top of the wall and was just about to jump over when Wen Jian suddenly shouted, "Be careful!"

She turned her head and saw that the man had reinforcements, who were heading straight for her.

She gritted her teeth and was about to jump down in one go, but then she saw people dressed as yajun (official guards) rushing over from outside the wall with shiny swords in their hands.

Seeing their gleaming blades, Yu Wan dared not jump.

After a moment of hesitation, she was grabbed by the arm and pulled down from the wall.

At this moment, Wen Jian was already surrounded by three people. Although he could barely hold his own, he was at a disadvantage.

He glanced at Yu Wan, and in that moment of distraction, the opponent lunged with a sword, actually cutting the human skin mask on his face.

"This Wei Wu has some tricks up his sleeve. He even has someone who can disguise themselves in his house!"

Yu Wan was startled by these words. When she looked at Wen Jian, his false face had already been cut off by the sword, revealing half of his face with a bright red birthmark.

The last time Yu Wan had seen Wen Jian’s real face was in the Hou Mansion’s dungeon. At that time, Yuan Qing had taken off his mask, and he had been too afraid to lift his head, only desperately groping on the ground for the mask.

Wen Jian stood frozen in place, instinctively covering his face.

The three men surrounding him would not let go of such a good opportunity and immediately aimed for his vital points.

Seeing Wen Jian knocked to the ground, Yu Wan was anxious. Taking advantage of the man holding her being off guard, she suddenly elbowed him in the chest, broke free, and rushed to Wen Jian’s side.

After all, they were official personnel. Seeing that Wen Jian had been defeated and Yu Wan was a woman who did not know martial arts, they did not continue to attack, only shouting, "Behave!"

Yu Wan ignored them. She only took off the veil from her own head and placed it on Wen Jian’s, covering his face.

That was the pain he did not want to reveal to the world. She had to protect it for him.

"It’s all my fault tonight," Yu Wan said softly.

It was she who had meddled in others' business and exposed their whereabouts. It was she who had thought that with Wen Jian’s martial arts, interrogating Wei Wu would be easy, which had brought them trouble.

"It’s not your fault. We were just unlucky."

It was just bad luck. They had only been in the Wei family for a short while when they encountered officials.

"Are you seriously injured?"

Wen Jian shook his head.

Yu Wan turned to look at those people.

"We are not part of the Wei family. Even if you are officials handling a case, you shouldn’t take it out on unrelated people like us."

The other party sneered, "If you weren’t guilty, why would you run when you see officials?"

"You aren’t even wearing official uniforms. Who knows who you are? You attacked and injured people. Why wouldn’t we run?"

Yu Wan’s words made sense, leaving the man unable to respond.

"What were you doing at Wei Wu’s house in the middle of the night?"

"Naturally, we wanted to buy some servants. Even if you are officials, you can’t arbitrarily arrest common citizens, right?" Seeing that the other party did not respond, Yu Wan continued, "Lord Pei is an upright official who loves the people like his own children. If he knew you arbitrarily injured civilians, he would severely punish you!"

After exchanging glances, another person said, "Come with us to the yamen, and you’ll know. If you are indeed good citizens, we will naturally let you go."

If the magistrate of Qingzhou was not Pei Ta, Yu Wan would not be afraid to go to the yamen.

But now... they could only take it one step at a time.

Yu Wan helped Wen Jian up and followed those people to the front courtyard. The entire Wei family had been brought out.

On this side, the officials from the yamen were counting the people. When they saw Yu Wan and Wen Jian, the captain asked, "Who are they?"

"They say they came to buy servants, but they have strong martial arts skills and can disguise themselves. We’ll take them to the yamen as well."

"Alright."

Perhaps because Yu Wan’s earlier words had been reasonable, the officers did not tie them up, only making them follow behind Wei Wu and his wife.

Just as they were about to reach the gate of the yamen, Wen Jian suddenly took action, restraining the nearby officer and seizing his throat.

"Don’t move, or I’ll kill him immediately."

As Wen Jian spoke, he gave Yu Wan a look. Yu Wan stood behind him, and the two of them, holding the officer hostage, slowly backed away. The people who had surrounded them earlier seemed to be truly intimidated and did not approach.

When they had retreated seven or eight zhang (a unit of length, approximately 3.3 meters) away, someone suddenly lunged at them, scattering a handful of powder.

Wen Jian knew it was poison and reached out to cover Yu Wan’s mouth and nose. However, since he was still holding a person, his movements were slowed.

Yu Wan only felt a strange smell enter her nose before she lost consciousness.

When she opened her eyes again, she was already in a soft bed.

She felt a headache and instinctively rubbed her temples. A stranger’s voice came from beside her.

"Miss, you’re awake?"

Someone helped her sit up.

Yu Wan looked at the unfamiliar little maid in front of her and had a bad feeling.

"Where am I?"

"This is the backyard of the Qingzhou yamen. I am Xique, sent by Lord Pei to take care of you."

Even though she had expected it, hearing the maid say this, Yu Wan’s mood was still complicated.

"How many days have I been unconscious?"

Xique grinned. "Not long, just two nights."

"What about the person who was with me? Where is he?"

"Miss, don’t worry. Your friend is fine. He was poisoned less severely than you and woke up this morning. He is currently staying in the room next door. I’ll go inform Lord Pei now. He will be very happy to know you’re awake."

"There’s nothing to be happy about." Although she and Wen Jian were both safe and sound, there really wasn’t anything to be happy about.

"You don’t know, Miss. This morning, Lord Pei brought you here and was very worried."

In the eyes of the servants, Pei Ta had always been refined, calm, and indifferent. This was the first time they had seen him so anxious.

Yu Wan gave a bitter smile but said nothing.

Xique fed her a few sips of water and then went out. However, before she could leave the room, she called out, "Lord."

---

chapters.title: Long Time No See
chapters.content:
"Miss is already awake. I was just about to inform Lord."

"Already awake?"

After three years apart, Pei Ta’s voice was still as clear as before.

Yu Wan’s heart was slightly uneasy. She subconsciously pulled up the blanket. When Pei Ta entered the room, she saw her hiding under the blanket, only her pair of eyes visible; beautiful and innocent, like a startled deer in the forest.

Seeing her pitiful appearance, Pei Ta’s slightly furrowed brows relaxed again.

"Miss Yu Wan, long time no see."

Yu Wan had just woken up. She was only wearing her sleeping clothes, and her hair was loose. She buried her head deeper into the blanket.

"Lord Pei, I trust you’ve been well."

Indeed, he had been well.

Three years had passed, and Pei Ta was still like a clear breeze and bright moon, elegant and refined. Standing there quietly, he made everything around him seem dim in comparison.

The moment their eyes met, Yu Wan quickly averted her gaze.

Seeing her covering herself with the blanket in embarrassment, Pei Ta said gently, "It’s good that you’re awake. Rest for now. If you need anything, have Xique call me."

"Last night at Wei Wu’s house, I…"

Seeing that Yu Wan was bringing up last night’s events, Pei Ta smiled warmly. "Rest first. We’ll talk when you’re feeling better."

With that, Pei Ta left the room.

Yu Wan on the bed let out a long sigh.

After hiding for three years, encountering an old acquaintance from the capital here was really troublesome.

Fortunately, it was Pei Ta.

"Miss, the medicine is ready." Xique entered with a bowl of herbal soup.

"Earlier, you said I was poisoned. What kind of poison was it?"

"I don’t know that." Xique replied cleverly, "Miss was poisoned by Lu Jie’s exclusive poison. But don’t worry, he said it’s not fatal. It just makes people weak and lose consciousness. Miss, rest assured and recover. After taking the antidote for a few more days, you’ll be fine."

After Xique said this, Yu Wan felt that her limbs were indeed weak.

"Who is Lu Jie?" She didn’t remember Pei Ta having such a person by his side.

"He is Lord’s guard. He usually follows Captain Li and others to handle cases."

It seemed that after three years, not only had Yu Wan changed, but so had Pei Ta.

Yu Wan drank the medicine in silence and felt much better. Then she asked, "Xique, I want to see my friend. Can you help me find a set of clothes?"

"Lord specifically ordered clothes and jewelry for Miss from Xiangyufang. I’ll get them right away."

Xique quickly brought out a clean and neat set of clothes. Seeing that Yu Wan’s movements were slow, she helped her change and combed her hair into a simple bun before supporting her as they walked out.

"Miss, your friend is staying in this room, but he doesn’t talk and won’t let us in."

"Xique, can you do me another favor?"

"Miss, just tell me."

"Please help me buy a mask. It doesn’t need to be pretty, just wearable."

"I’ll remember."

Xique knew that the man inside had half his face red, so when she heard Yu Wan’s request, she naturally agreed.

After Xique walked away, Yu Wan lightly knocked on the door and called out to the room, "It’s me. I’m coming in."

Without waiting for a response from inside, she pushed the door open and entered.

Wen Jian was sitting on the bed facing the wall, grumbling, "Are you alright?"

His human skin mask had been cut off last night, and now his real face was exposed. Naturally, he did not want anyone to see it.

Yu Wan replied, "I can’t use my strength. That Xique said I was poisoned by someone’s exclusive poison and need to take the antidote for a few more days to recover. How do you feel?"

When the poison was scattered, Wen Jian had been wearing the veil Yu Wan gave him. The thin gauze had blocked most of the powder, so he was not deeply poisoned.

"I’m already fine."

"Do you want some water?"

"No."

Yu Wan walked to the edge of the bed. Seeing that he refused to turn around, she sat down by the bed.

"Actually..."

"Don’t say anything."

Yu Wan did not speak but silently scooted closer to the bed.

Feeling her getting closer, Wen Jian moved back a bit.

"It was my fault last night. I shouldn’t have let you take the risk."

"It’s not your fault. It’s because I haven’t practiced martial arts much these past three years. Otherwise, we could have escaped."

"It’s no one’s fault. We were just unlucky last night."

Dealing with Wei Wu would have been easy for Wen Jian. Who could have expected that last night they would run into officials coming to arrest someone? It was truly unexpected that Pei Ta now had such formidable subordinates.

Wen Jian remained silent, only lowering his head further.

Yu Wan tugged at his arm. "Actually, even though you have a birthmark on your face, you’re not ugly."

"Stop talking." Wen Jian’s voice deepened.

"You’ve known me for so long. Is it appropriate for you not to let me see your face?" Seeing that Wen Jian still refused to speak, Yu Wan said, "You really aren’t ugly. It’s just a bit surprising the first time you see it. If you don’t believe me, ask my mother when we get back."

"Ask your mother? She won’t tell the truth either."

Ding Wenxi had never seen Wen Jian’s real face, but Wen Jian knew that if he asked her, she would definitely lie to comfort him.

"You’re afraid she’ll lie? Then when we get back, jump out and scare her. See what her reaction is."

"Too lazy to pay attention to you."

"Then you can turn around and scare me now."

"Get lost."

Wen Jian pushed her hand off his arm. He still refused to turn around, but Yu Wan could hear that his tone had relaxed a bit.

Yu Wan steeled her heart and grabbed his shoulder, leaning in to stare at his face.

Wen Jian had nowhere to hide or retreat. He could only let her examine his face while helplessly looking away.

"Had enough of a look?"

"Not yet."

Yu Wan said this, but knowing when to stop, she sat back down.

"So what if I looked? You really don’t look bad. Even if you walked down the street without a mask, you’d still look better than half the men out there."

"Shut up."

Yu Wan heard that Wen Jian’s tone had finally returned to normal. She slightly let out a breath of relief and changed the subject. "I saw Pei Ta earlier."

"Will he let us go?"

"After we explain the situation with Wei Wu’s family, he should let us go."

Wen Jian frowned. "I remember he has a good relationship with Zhao Xuanyou. Back then, the two of them worked together against the Crown Prince. Would he report our whereabouts to Zhao Xuanyou?"

It was the first time in three years that Yu Wan had heard someone mention Zhao Xuanyou’s name. She felt a sense of disorientation, as if it were a lifetime ago.

Zhao Xuanyou... She wondered if he was currently in the Hou Mansion, playing with his children.

Yu Wan collected her thoughts. "Their relationship isn’t good. In fact, they haven’t had any contact for a long time. So, Pei Ta won’t tell Zhao Xuanyou about our whereabouts."

"Then can we continue living here?"

"For the time being, there shouldn’t be any problems." Yu Wan pondered for a moment and sighed. "In a while, let’s see if anyone is willing to buy Shu Yu Xuan. We’ll take the money and find a new place to live."

Wen Jian heard this and turned to look at Yu Wan in astonishment.

"Really leaving Qingsha Town?"

"Don’t want to leave?" Yu Wan smiled.

Wen Jian really liked life in Qingsha Town. It was peaceful and stable. Doing nothing, just listening to the waves and feeling the sea breeze was better than countless things in the world.

However...

"There’s nothing I can’t bear to leave," Wen Jian said softly. "Wherever you go, I’ll go."

chapters.title: Unspoken
chapters.content:
After spending so much time together, Yu Yuan naturally understood Wen Ji’s feelings.

He was abandoned at birth and, having become a shadow guard, could not be seen in the light or by others.

"You can rest assured, the next home will be better than this one."

The Suiyu Pavilion business was going well. After a year, it had already recouped its costs, and in the second year, it roughly earned several hundred taels of silver. Selling the workshop and the shop would make the money on hand even more substantial.

Once a suitable place was found, they could buy a larger residence.

Ding Wenxi could plant flowers and tend grass, and Wen Ji could bask in the sun and daydream.

"Do you have no attachment to Qingsha Town at all?"

"Even if I do, it’s only because Mother and you are there. As long as we are all together, it doesn’t matter where we live."

Yu Yuan said it lightly, but when Wen Ji heard her group himself together with Ding Wenxi, his Adam’s apple rolled, and a strange emotion surged in his heart.

After his emotions settled a bit, Wen Ji hummed in agreement, "Have you thought about it? Once we leave Qingsha Town, we won’t be able to do the pearl jewelry business anymore."

"We’ll find another livelihood. Didn’t you once think about brewing wine? When we get to the next place, we can sell wine."

"Miss."

Before Wen Ji could respond, Magpie knocked on the door from outside.

"What is it?" Yu Yuan asked.

"The things you asked for have been bought."

Yu Yuan jumped off the couch and quickly opened the door. She took a white mask from Magpie’s hands. The mask only covered half the face and was only a temporary solution.

"Thank you."

"You’re welcome, Miss." Magpie said respectfully, "Just now, the steward of the master came to deliver a message. He said if Miss and the young master are feeling better, the master would like to invite you both to dinner."

"Please tell Master Pei that we are both fine now."

The sooner they clarified the matter with the Wei family, the sooner they could leave.

Since Pei Ta had sent someone to arrest Wei Wu, he must have discovered some unspeakable dealings, possibly related to Qiaihe.

With the authorities involved, they would certainly find Qiaihe faster than she could on her own.

Even if they couldn’t, Yu Yuan was already overwhelmed and had no other options.

"I understand. This servant will go and reply immediately. Right now, the master is still at the yamen handling official business. Please, Miss and young master, rest in the room for a while."

After Magpie left, Yu Yuan gave the mask to Wen Ji and returned to the previous room.

With nothing to do, she re-combed her hair into a neat bun.

By the time dusk fell, Magpie finally came to invite them to dinner.

It was the height of spring, and the scenery in the back courtyard of the yamen was pleasant. The trees lining the path on both sides had turned green, and everywhere the eye could see was lush with the vibrant greenery of spring.

Soon they arrived at the dining place. Pei Ta was already seated at the table, with the men who had gone to arrest Wei Wu the night before standing behind him.

"Miss Yu Yuan," upon seeing their arrival, Pei Ta stood up to greet them.

At this moment, he had changed into a stone-blue brocade robe, appearing tall and straight, refined and elegant, like a green bamboo standing before Yu Yuan.

"Master Pei." Yu Yuan lowered her head and bowed to him.

"Today, the yamen has been busy with many affairs, making you wait for a long time."

Yu Yuan said, "Qingzhou is blessed to have a magistrate like Master Pei."

Pei Ta's gaze flickered.

So she had known all along that he was the magistrate of Qingzhou, but simply didn’t want to see him.
