"This is not the yamen. Since you and I are friends, there’s no need to be so polite." Pei Ta led Yu Yuan and Wen Ji to their seats. "May I ask how to address this brother?"

Wen Ji cupped his hands towards Pei Ta, "Ding Ji."

Pei Ta didn’t know Yu Yuan’s mother’s name, so upon hearing this, he simply nodded. "That night, my subordinates were rude to you. Please forgive them."

The four men behind him all cupped their fists towards Yu Yuan, "We apologize for our mistake."

"That night, our timing and the situation were indeed inappropriate. It’s not their fault for misunderstanding. Since it was for official business, there’s really no need to apologize."

Seeing Yu Yuan’s courteous and measured words, one of them said bluntly, "Mainly, that young master’s martial arts were too good. We didn’t dare to take it lightly. In all our years traveling the jianghu, we’ve never seen such agility."

"He was just fortunate to have met a great master and learned from him." Yu Yuan glossed over it with a couple of words, then looked at Pei Ta. "Now that Master Pei has such capable subordinates, handling cases must be much smoother."

Noticing Yu Yuan’s curiosity, Pei Ta explained, "These four were originally jianghu people. I met them by chance on my way to take office in Qingzhou. Seeing their desire to serve the court, I kept them by my side."

So they were jianghu people. No wonder they used poison.

As they spoke, the dishes on the table were all served.

Yu Yuan looked at Pei Ta, then at the four men. "Since we’ve met through a fight, why don’t I toast you all with tea?"

The four men looked at Pei Ta. Only after Pei Ta nodded did they take their seats.

After Yu Yuan toasted them with tea, she turned to Pei Ta.

Pei Ta pursed his lips, said nothing, and lightly clinked his wine cup against her tea cup.

After three years apart, both of them had new circumstances. Many curiosities, many misunderstandings, many unspoken secrets were all in that cup, and all were understood without words.

After finishing the meal, Pei Ta ordered the dishes to be cleared and new tea to be served.

Judging the timing was right, Yu Yuan said at the right moment, "Master, the reason we went to Wei Wu’s house that night was to find someone."

Pei Ta’s eyebrows slightly furrowed, "To find Wei Wu?"

"No, to find someone’s whereabouts through him." Yu Yuan said, "In my jewelry shop in Qingsha Town, there was a helper named Qiaihe."

"You’ve been in Qingsha Town all this time?" Pei Ta looked at her with slight surprise, interrupting Yu Yuan.

Yu Yuan avoided his gaze and nodded, "Qingsha Town is famous for its pearls. Those small pearls that the palace doesn’t want are perfect for making jewelry."

"I went there some time ago and should have passed by your shop."

Qingsha Town was small, with only one east-west street. If Pei Ta had gone, he would indeed have passed by Suiyu Pavilion.

Yu Yuan continued, "Qiaihe didn’t come to the shop for several days in a row. When I sent someone to her house to ask, they said she got lost while visiting Qingzhou City. I found it strange that her family didn’t report her missing, so I came to Qingzhou with Ah Ji to investigate."

"You went to Wei Wu?"

"Yes. Wei Wu said he wasn’t a kidnapper, that Qiaihe’s family sold her to him."

Pei Ta listened thoughtfully, "Even though her family said she was missing, they never reported it. It’s likely they really sold her. How did you think to investigate Wei Wu?"

"I asked him where he sold Qiaihe, but he avoided my eyes and spoke vaguely."

"So you went to his house?"

"Yes. Ah Ji has good martial arts. I thought if we went to his house and scared him a bit, maybe he would reveal Qiaihe’s whereabouts." At this point, Yu Yuan’s smile was somewhat helpless. "Unfortunately, we ran into the authorities handling a case."

Unfortunately?

To meet again in Qingzhou, thousands of miles away, was actually quite a coincidence.

"How old is Miss Qiaihe? Is she married?"

"Qiaihe is fifteen this year. Although she is the eldest daughter in her family, she is not yet married."

Pei Ta slightly furrowed his brows, pondered for a moment, then looked up and said slowly, "Yu Yuan, it seems we are investigating the same case."

---

chapters.title: Unraveling the Threads
chapters.content:
Yu Yuan was surprised, "Does that mean the authorities have already found Qiaihe..."

Pei Ta shook his head.

One of Pei Ta’s subordinates spoke up, "Half a month ago, some idle men were fishing in the West River outside the city. They pulled up a burlap sack containing a woman’s corpse and several stones. It was clear someone had deliberately sunk the body. Master ordered us to search along the river to see if we could find more evidence. Unexpectedly, downstream in a backwater bay, we found several similar burlap sacks, all containing the same things."

"Were all the sacks containing women’s corpses?"

"Not only that, the sacks were of the same material, tied in the same way, and even contained a similar number of stones."

"It seems they were all done by the same person."

Pei Ta knew Yu Yuan was intelligent and nodded, "The coroner examined the bodies. Some had been dead for over half a year, others for two or three months, and the first one pulled up had been in the water for seven or eight days. According to the coroner, all the victims were like Qiaihe; around fourteen or fifteen years old and still virgins at the time of death."

Yu Yuan suddenly remembered Wei Wu’s words: "It’s too late. She’s already been sent over. Even the Heavenly King couldn’t save her now."

At the time, Yu Yuan thought he was referring to the powerful buyer behind him. Now it seemed there might be a double meaning: one, a threat that they had provoked someone they shouldn’t have; two, Qiaihe had already met her end, so no one could save her.

Yu Yuan felt a pang of sadness.

After more than two years together, such a lively and spirited young girl was gone. It was truly cruel.

After a moment, Yu Yuan asked, "So many bodies were found in the river. With so many people killed, didn’t anyone report it?"

"I had my suspicions before," Pei Ta sighed heavily, looking at Yu Yuan with a hint of helplessness. "But it wasn’t until you told me that Qiaihe was sold to Wei Wu by her family that I confirmed my earlier guess."

"That night, Ah Ji and I tied up Wei Wu and forced him to reveal Qiaihe’s whereabouts. He said even the Heavenly King couldn’t save her. I thought he was threatening me, but after hearing what you said, maybe it wasn’t just a threat. He probably knew what happened to those girls." After a pause, Yu Yuan suddenly realized, "Wei Wu was the one who selected the girls for that murderer. Those girls were all sold by their families, so when they disappeared or died, no one reported it."

"That’s right."

"How did Master Pei find Wei Wu?"

Pei Ta said, "The bodies pulled from the river were too decomposed to provide any evidence. They were stripped naked and stuffed into the sacks, leaving no physical clues. I had people post notices in the city, describing the approximate ages and times of death, asking families with missing girls to come and identify them. After ten days, no one came. I thought that the human traffickers must have many such girls, so I questioned all the traffickers in the city but found nothing."

"And then?" Yu Yuan was hearing about a case investigation for the first time and was somewhat curious. Before Pei Ta could answer, she asked, "Can you tell me about this?"

"Later, I interrogated several people separately and used some methods to finally get results. One person said that last year, Wei Wu approached him, asking if he had any fourteen or fifteen-year-old girls from poor, remote areas with clean backgrounds. He said there was a buyer willing to pay a high price. He sold two girls to Wei Wu but didn’t know where they ended up." Pei Ta paused, "When he saw the notices posted by the yamen, he thought of Wei Wu but was afraid of getting involved, so he didn’t dare speak up before."

"That Wei Wu is truly a beast." Hearing that he had harmed so many young girls, Yu Yuan also felt a surge of indignation.

"Now that we’ve caught Wei Wu, following the trail should lead us to solve the case soon."

Yu Yuan naturally trusted Pei Ta’s abilities.

"I just remembered something that might help you, Master."

"What is it?"

"Wei Wu said the person behind him is someone we can’t afford to offend. I don’t think he was just trying to scare me. You must be careful, Master."

Pei Ta nodded slightly, "It’s said that Wei Wu was willing to pay twenty taels of silver for a maid. With that kind of financial power, his backer must be of high status."

Twenty taels of silver?

No wonder Qiaihe’s parents looked down on the wages earned from working in the workshop.

Their daughter would eventually get married. Rather than letting her use her skills to earn money for her husband’s family, it was better to sell her for twenty taels to support her brothers.

Even though Yu Yuan felt sorry for Qiaihe, since Pei Ta was handling the case, she no longer needed to get involved.

"You can rest assured. Based on my deduction, Qiaihe should still be alive. I’ve ordered a strict interrogation of Wei Wu to find her as soon as possible."

"Qiaihe is really still alive?"

Pei Ta’s expression showed a trace of pain. After a moment of hesitation, he said softly, "The coroner said the women’s bones were intact, with no knife wounds or signs of poisoning. They must have been abused and tortured for a long time before dying."

"But you just said those bodies were still virgins?"

"Yes."

If they didn’t die from humiliation, could it be they were starved to death? Who knew what kind of demon was behind this case.

Yu Yuan clenched her fingers, barely maintaining her composure.

Pei Ta said solemnly, "Such a big case happened in Qingzhou, and I was completely unaware. It’s my negligence."

"There will always be good and evil people in the world. How can they all be eliminated?"

Listening to Yu Yuan’s words, Pei Ta’s deep eyes were filled with emotion as he slowly nodded.

"You still have residual poison in your system. It’s late. You should go back to your room and rest."

"I don’t have any more clues. Staying here would only delay your work, Master. Tomorrow morning, Ah Ji and I want to go home so my mother won’t worry."

Before Pei Ta could speak, the man beside him said, "Miss, don’t be in a hurry to leave. You still need to take medicine for three more days to eliminate the residual poison."

"Can’t you give me the antidote?"

The man stammered, "This... the poison and the antidote are my exclusive secret formulas. I really can’t share them. Please understand, Miss."

Pei Ta said, "Don’t worry. Tomorrow morning, I’ll send someone to inform your mother."

Yu Yuan’s body was indeed weak, and even speaking was a struggle to keep her spirits up.

At this point, it was clear they were unwilling to give up the antidote.

When they left the room, the moon was already high in the sky. Pei Ta’s four subordinates went to the jail to continue interrogating Wei Wu, while Pei Ta walked back with Yu Yuan and Wen Ji.

The cold moonlight stretched their shadows long.

Yu Yuan knew Pei Ta must have many questions for her. Although she felt helpless, she understood that what was meant to come would always come. Since they had met, there was no avoiding it. She glanced subtly at Wen Ji beside her.

Wen Ji understood and silently slowed his pace, putting some distance between himself and the other two.

chapters.title: Treasured in the Heart
chapters.content:
The way back wasn't far. Just as they were about to return to the small courtyard, Pei Ta halted his steps.

"Yuan, it's truly good to see you again."

The lantern at the courtyard gate was half-dim, softening Pei Ta's expression and voice.

Pei Ta had always treated her well; whether it was teaching her in the imperial palace, giving her calligraphy copies and the Four Books and Five Classics, or even obtaining the architectural drawings for her before leaving the capital.

Yuan had gained much from him but had never given anything in return.

Hearing his words, Yuan felt a mix of emotion and embarrassment. She only evaded, "Has Lord Pei heard about what happened in the capital?"

"Mm."

The scene of their parting in the capital felt like yesterday, yet everything was different now.

He had become the magistrate of Qingzhou, while she had become the owner of a jewelry shop in Qingsha Town.

Seeing the lively sparkle in Yuan's eyes, Pei Ta sighed softly, "You can do what I cannot."

"That's only because Lord Pei disdains to do such things. I have no other talents; I could only resort to such a desperate measure."

Yuan slightly lowered her gaze, turning her eyes away.

Pei Ta was an upright man; he must strongly disapprove of her arson for revenge.

In the past, Pei Ta had lectured her on many principles from the sages' books. She had studied them earnestly but clearly hadn't absorbed a single word.

"It is not a desperate measure," Pei Ta said solemnly.

"Ah?" Yuan widened her eyes in surprise, her heart stirring slightly. "How could it not be? Even I think it was a desperate measure."

If it weren't for the urgency of Ding Wenxi's secret forcing her to leave the capital, she wouldn't have used such a drastic method.

"Any strategy that can bring down the Xingguo Duke's mansion cannot be a desperate measure. How many officials in the entire court could achieve that?"

"The Xingguo Duke's mansion is in trouble?"

"You didn't know?"

"No."

After leaving the capital, the three of them had drifted on a boat for more than half a year before settling in Qingsha Town.

Having cut ties with the past, they naturally didn't inquire about the capital's affairs.

"It was just a fire in the firewood room. How could the Xingguo Duke's mansion get into trouble over that?"

At that time, she had asked Wen Qi to place the hairpin design drawn by her mother in Cui Lingyuan's study to make him wary.

Her mother was a runaway palace maid, and Cui Lingyuan would certainly not want anyone to know about his private affair with her. Even if Yuan set fire to the duke's mansion, he would definitely help cover it up.

Pei Ta looked at the confusion in Yuan's eyes, hesitated for a moment, then said slowly, "It is said that when the Brocade Guards investigated the Xingguo Duke's mansion, they found pearls as large as the tribute offerings in Cui Yichu's coffin. Following that lead, they uncovered the Xingguo Duke's mansion's crimes."

He didn't mention Zhao Xuanyou, only the Brocade Guards.

Yuan, of course, understood that the person who went to investigate the Xingguo Duke's mansion was Zhao Xuanyou, and the one who opened Cui Yichu's coffin was also Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Qi had said he was imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice's prison, which was likely related to this matter.

Yuan didn't continue asking about the Brocade Guards. She only asked, "Was Cui Lingyuan arrested?"

"Yes, but in the end, Cui Zaizhou took all the blame. Before the execution, he died in prison."

So Cui Zaizhou died in prison. Then Shen Fenyun must have become a widow.

But with her prestigious maiden family and a royal cousin, her life should not be too difficult.

"What about Cui Lingyuan?"

Yuan's concern for Cui Lingyuan surprised Pei Ta a little.

How many secrets did this graceful and intelligent woman hold?

"Embezzling tribute pearls is a serious crime. Even if Cui Zaizhou took the main blame, the others should still be exiled according to the law. However, the Duke of Ningguo couldn't bear to see his granddaughter suffer, so he joined many officials in petitioning the emperor for leniency. The emperor stripped Cui Lingyuan of his first-class duke title, confiscated the mansion, and demoted the Cui family to commoners."

Yuan pressed her lips together and said nothing.

Truly, like the saying goes, "A turtle lives a thousand years." Cui Zaizhou and Cui Yichu were both dead, yet Cui Lingyuan still lived.

"He actually escaped again."

Pei Ta said, "Without the duke title, he can no longer do evil in the future."

"Who knows."

Pei Ta had always thought that Yuan and Cui Yichu were mortal enemies. Now it seemed she despised Cui Lingyuan even more.

He understood that Yuan didn't want to talk about this, so he said, "In the past, when I was studying for the imperial examinations, I always thought about pleading for the people and punishing the wicked. But only after becoming an official did I realize that these eight words are not as simple as they are written in books. Being in the court, one must act according to the law, divine the emperor's intentions, and deal with colleagues. There are many times when one is helpless and not in control. The treacherous ministers have many cunning schemes and do not play by the rules. If one only follows conventions and sticks to old ways, it is impossible to compete with them."

"I only set fire to the firewood room. I dare not take credit for the rest."

Bringing down the Xingguo Duke's mansion was Zhao Xuanyou and the Brocade Guards' achievement.

"As the saying goes, pulling one hair moves the whole body. Without the cause you planted, there would be no result for the Brocade Guards. I also gained enlightenment from the young lady's pointers in the capital, gradually understanding the principles in the books."

"What principles?"

Yuan didn't feel that her actions followed any method or principle. She only knew to repay enmity with enmity.

Cui Yichu was her enemy in both lives. In her past life, he had killed her and taken her child. In this life, he had tried to kill her multiple times.

She hadn't waited for the fall of the Xingguo Duke's mansion. She had only taken revenge before leaving the capital.

When the great revenge was avenged, Yuan only felt a sense of relief.

As for the fall of the Xingguo Duke's mansion, it was completely beyond her expectations.

"Use and discard as the time demands; advance or retreat as I will."

"I don't understand." Yuan smiled casually, but there was still a hint of unease in her smile. She had something she wanted to ask but didn't know how to start. "Now that the tribute pearl case is solved, the Brocade Guards have made a great contribution, right?"

"Yes. The thousand-household commander Pan Xun, who was in charge of this case, was promoted by the emperor to be the commander of the Brocade Guards."

Then what about him? He should have been released long ago.

Seeing her deep in thought, Pei Ta easily guessed who she was hesitating about.

"The World Prince is no longer the commander of the Brocade Guards. He has returned to the northwest and remains the main commander of the Mingchan Guards."

These simple words brought Yuan a sense of relief.

It was good that he returned to the northwest.

In this life, Zhao Xuanyou stayed in the capital because she, as Cui Yichu, had asked him to. Now that Cui Yichu was dead and she had fled, he had returned to the Mingchan Guards. Finally, they were each safe and sound, with no further entanglements.

"In that case," Yuan gave Pei Ta a grateful smile.

Pei Ta didn't know what Yuan's attitude toward Zhao Xuanyou was.

In the past, when he saw them together, he could feel that Zhao Xuanyou doted on Yuan, and Yuan served him attentively and obediently.

Logically, if Yuan wanted to set fire to the Xingguo Duke's mansion, the first person she should ask for help would be Zhao Xuanyou. Yet Zhao Xuanyou knew nothing about it.

Did she not care about him at all?

After a moment of hesitation, Pei Ta still asked, "Don't you want to see him?"

"I don't avoid seeing anyone. I just want to draw a clear line with the past and live a peaceful life."

"So, it's me who is disturbing your peace."

Yuan smiled, "It's good that it's you, Lord Pei. You will keep my secret, won't you?"

"Then how should I address you now?"

"Ding Yuan."

Pei Ta's eyebrows twitched slightly as he glanced at Wen Qi not far away. "Then you two are..."

"He is my mother's adopted son, my younger brother."

Pei Ta nodded. "Everything about Miss Ding, I will treasure in my heart and not reveal a single bit."

---

chapters.title: The People on the Pirate Ship
chapters.content:
"Thank you, Lord Pei." Yuan gave Pei Ta a graceful bow.

"There's no need for such politeness between us." Before Yuan could speak again, Pei Ta said, "You still have residual poison in your body. Go back to your room and rest early. Once I finish this case, I will invite you to the best restaurant in Qingzhou for a meal to reminisce."

A thousand sails pass by a sunken ship. Of course, Yuan didn't want to reminisce.

Nevertheless, she had no reason to refuse at the moment, so she nodded in agreement.

After Pei Ta left, Wen Qi walked over to Yuan.

"Earlier, they said you have residual poison in your body. How do you feel?"

"Not uncomfortable, just weak."

Wen Qi said, "You were probably poisoned with something like Soft Bone Powder. I guess they deliberately didn't give you the antidote because they didn't want us to leave."

Yuan gave a bitter smile.

Perhaps that was the case. After all, Pei Ta knew she was capable of killing and arson. It was natural for him to be suspicious if she appeared at Wei Wu's house in the middle of the night without reason.

"Staying here is better than being locked up in jail."

"You're quite optimistic."

"We have nothing to do with this case anyway. No matter how they investigate, they won't find anything on us. Now that they are investigating Qiaihe, we can just ignore everything and enjoy a few days of comfort in the yamen."

"He said he's your friend, yet he deliberately didn't give you the antidote to keep you here. Do you still trust him?"

Trust or not...

Yuan pressed her lips together. "Actually, Lord Pei is also someone who has one foot on the pirate ship."

"Why?"

"Do you remember when you asked me why I was so familiar with the layout of the Xingguo Duke's mansion?"

"Because of him?"

"The architectural drawings in my hands were drawn by him."

Wen Qi recalled the thick stack of drawings in Yuan's carriage and silently cupped his hands toward Yuan in admiration.

"Now you know how capable I am, right?" Yuan accepted Wen Qi's admiration without modesty, smiling.

But as she was about to say something else, she yawned.

"Go to bed quickly. I'll keep watch tonight."

With Wen Qi by her side in the yamen, Yuan naturally had nothing to worry about. Yawning repeatedly, she went into the room.

She had thought she would stay in the yamen for two or three days. Once Pei Ta confirmed that they had nothing to do with Wei Wu, he would let them go.

But five days passed, and there was still no news of their release.

Feeling that she had recovered enough, Yuan asked Xique for news.

Xique only replied that Lord Pei had been busy with the case, leaving early and returning late, so she hadn't been able to meet him.

Yuan felt this was strange. Logically, Pei Ta wouldn't scheme against her, but staying in the yamen for too long still made her uneasy.

That evening, she and Wen Qi stood guard outside Pei Ta's courtyard, refusing to leave no matter who tried to persuade them.

Around the Zi hour (midnight), Pei Ta's figure finally appeared in the night.

"Lord Pei."

Hearing Yuan's voice, Pei Ta looked over in surprise and saw her approaching. "It's so late. Why are you standing here?"

"The poison in my body has been neutralized. I wanted to say goodbye to you, but you're never in the yamen."

Pei Ta nodded. "I've been busy with the case these past few days and forgot about this. Since you're fine, I'll arrange a carriage to send you back to Qingsha Town tomorrow."

"There's no need for such trouble. Wen Qi and I can ride back on our own."

"Yuan, I had originally thought I could solve the case by following Wei Wu's lead before your poison was neutralized, so your friend could return with you. Unfortunately, I broke my promise."

Catching Wei Wu should logically mean they were close to solving the case.

Yuan asked in confusion, "Didn't Wei Wu confess?"

"He didn't confess to anything."

Recalling the interrogation of Wei Wu earlier, Yuan said, "He seemed very afraid of the person behind him. It felt like, even though he's a greedy and cowardly man, he would rather die than betray the other party. He must know that the real mastermind is extremely vicious, and once he betrays them, they will harm his family."

"You guessed correctly. Wei Wu indeed refused to talk and, two nights ago, the jailers were negligent, and he killed himself by ramming his head against the wall in his cell."

"Wei Wu is dead?" Yuan understood why Pei Ta said the case couldn't be solved. Wei Wu was the one who had bought the young girls for the mastermind and was a crucial link.

Now that Wei Wu was dead, the trail had gone cold.

Pei Ta's expression was also heavy.

"These past few days, I've led people to search along both banks of the Xi River, but all we found were two more sacks besides the ones already retrieved."

"Didn't the people living along the Xi River ever see anyone throwing sacks into the river?"

"We've questioned them thoroughly several times. No one witnessed anything." After speaking, Pei Ta noticed Yuan's thoughtful expression and asked, "Do you have any ideas?"

The night breeze blew gently as Yuan stood in the wind, her dress billowing. She pondered Pei Ta's words deeply.

After a long while, she spoke, "The person who dumped the bodies put stones in the sacks. It seems he is cautious in his actions. He chose to dump the bodies in the Xi River, likely because he specifically picked nights when it was quiet. He has considerable power and probably sends others to do it, not doing it himself."

"You're right. If it weren't for those idle men going fishing in the river and accidentally retrieving a sack, no one would have known about such a horrifying case in Qingzhou."

"You previously posted a notice for people to identify the bodies. Knowing his actions have been exposed, he will probably lie low for now."

Everything Yuan said, Pei Ta had naturally considered as well.

With Wei Wu dead, the case had hit a dead end. It was impossible to investigate further.

But if he didn't investigate, how could he face those unnamed girls in the yamen?

"I've been thinking, why did he abduct these girls? Initially, I thought he wanted to violate them, but you said the bodies were all virgins. That doesn't make sense."

"That's correct. The coroner said the women were not injured and seemed to have been imprisoned for a long time. But I also can't figure out why he abducted them."

"Girls of fourteen or fifteen are as delicate and fresh as flowers. He specifically bought such girls, either for their youth and beauty or for their purity. If he abducted so many girls, it's impossible that he didn't violate or possess them, unless..."

"Unless what?"

Yuan's eyes flickered as she whispered, "Could it be that he wanted to possess them but couldn't... have them?"

Pei Ta frowned upon hearing this, then suddenly realized and stared intently at Yuan.

Yuan, uncomfortable under his gaze, looked away. "I was just thinking randomly. Maybe it's not correct."

"This matter is indeed suspicious. With no other leads, I'll try investigating this angle."

"Lord Pei, do you have a plan for the investigation?"

Pei Ta nodded. "If he is truly impotent, he must have sought medical treatment. Tomorrow morning, I'll send people to question all the major clinics. Since he has considerable power, he is definitely not an unknown figure. It should be easy to expose him."

Yuan thought for a moment, then suddenly shook her head. "Lord Pei, you can't ask like that."

chapters.title: Midnight Palpitations
chapters.content:
"Are you worried that the clinic might not tell the truth?"

Yu Wan nodded. "Though I don't know his background, Wei Wu was so afraid of interrogation that he took his own life in prison. It stands to reason that the physician who treated him wouldn't dare reveal his hidden illness."

"That does make sense."

Wei Wu was a heartless human trafficker who would stop at nothing for money, so cowardly and greedy that even he was scared into suicide. The physician would naturally be even less likely to speak up.

After a moment of thought, Pei Tao said in a deep voice, "Direct interrogation would indeed be difficult. It would be better to check the clinic's records of consultations and house calls. Given that man's status, even when seeking medical help, he would likely have the physician come to him."

"It would be best to look at the clinic's ledger of medicine sales." As soon as the words left her mouth, seeing Pei Tao's gaze fixed firmly on her, Yu Wan said somewhat embarrassedly, "Am I talking too much? Actually, I don't know anything about handling cases. I just say whatever comes to mind."

"How could that be?" Pei Tao chuckled. "You may have never handled a case before, but that doesn't mean you don't understand how to."

"Do you think what I said makes sense, then?"

"Of course it does. Medical records are easy to falsify, but the purchase and sale of medicinal herbs involve money. The accountant wouldn't dare omit or underreport them."

"True."

Gazing at Yu Wan under the dim yellow light, Pei Tao felt an inexplicable surge of emotion. "If only you were by my side..."

By his side?

Yu Wan looked at him in astonishment.

A rare look of panic suddenly appeared on Pei Tao's usually gentle face.

"Yu Wan, I... I didn't mean it that way. I mean, if, if you were a man, you could work in the yamen. Those long-unsolved cases would be no trouble for you."

"You flatter me, Lord Pei." Yu Wan lowered her head.

Perhaps because his earlier words had been somewhat impolite, Pei Tao turned aside, coughed a few times, and only spoke again when the atmosphere was less awkward. "Solving cases is my duty. It's already so late; I shouldn't keep you talking."

"It was I who talked too much."

"You weren't rambling. Every word you said was an eye-opener for me. Yu Wan, you are a remarkable woman."

When he first heard about the fire at Xingguo Duke's mansion on New Year's Eve, Pei Tao's first thought was of Yu Wan. After all, she had insisted on getting the architectural plans of the Xingguo Duke's mansion from him, clearly with some scheme in mind.

But then he thought it impossible. Yu Wan was just a weak woman. How could she have done such a thing?

Zhao Xuanyou seemed more likely.

It was he who set the fire at the Xingguo Duke's mansion, then entered the mansion under the pretext of investigating the fire, and naturally obtained evidence for the Tributary Pearl case, bringing down Cui Lingyuan.

Thinking of how Zhao Xuanyou had planned all this, when he heard that Yu Wan had gone missing, Pei Tao didn't believe she was dead.

After the Tributary Pearl case was closed, Zhao Xuanyou left the capital quickly. To this day, he remained unmarried, likely living a carefree life with Yu Wan in the borderlands.

But he never expected that Yu Wan had been living in Qingsha Town all along.

"Lord Pei, the residual poison in my body has already been resolved. I've been away from home for so many days; it's time to go back." Seeing that Pei Tao had been silent, lost in thought, Yu Wan finally had the chance to explain her purpose. "I came tonight to bid you farewell."

"You're leaving?"

Yu Wan said softly, "Since leaving the capital, I haven't been separated from my mother for this long."

"The day after you came to the yamen, I already sent someone to inform her of your safety."

Meeting Pei Tao's gaze, Yu Wan felt as if she had been seen through. Indeed, Pei Tao didn't want to let them leave.

"Do you still suspect that I have something to do with Wei Wu?"

"Of course not." When Pei Tao sent someone to Qingsha Town to report to Ding Wenxi, they also went to Qiahe's family to take a statement.

Qiahe's family had indeed sold her to Wei Wu for twenty taels of silver, claiming only that a wealthy family in Jiangnan wanted to buy a concubine for a marriage ritual, and nothing more.

"If you don't have any urgent matters to attend to, you might as well stay in the yamen for a few more days and help me think about this case. I'll have Lu Jie stay in the residence to serve you. If you think of anything, just have Lu Jie report it to me."

Yu Wan could see that he was truly stuck on this case, so he was grasping at straws by asking her.

In the past, she had owed him so many favors. Now that he had asked, it was hard for her to refuse.

"It's not that I'm in a hurry to leave; I'm just afraid I won't be of much help."

"Yu Wan, you mustn't underestimate yourself. You simply haven't had the chance to display your talents."

"Have you been reading books all this time since you left?"

Indeed.

The only things Yu Wan had taken from the capital were Pei Tao's books and calligraphy copies.

But saying this aloud seemed somewhat abrupt.

"I read them occasionally in my spare time. Usually, I'm busy with the shop." Yu Wan smiled and nodded. "Then Wenchu and I will respectfully comply and impose on you for a few more days."

"It's already very late. Let me escort you back to the courtyard."

Yu Wan hurriedly declined, "You've worked hard on the case, Lord Pei, and you still have to help tomorrow. There's no need to trouble yourself. Wenchu and I can walk back slowly."

"Very well."

Yu Wan bowed to him, then turned and walked toward Wenchu, who was not far away.

Wenchu observed her expression, then glanced at Pei Tao, and asked softly, "Can we go back tomorrow?"

"We'll have to stay here for a few more days."

Wenchu wasn't surprised to hear this.

She had stood there talking to Pei Tao for so long; clearly, she had taken everything he said to heart.

"What's the use of keeping you here if he's not even in the yamen during the day?"

"Lord Pei isn't keeping us here to see me. He wants me to help think about the case."

If anyone else heard that a prestigious prefect like Lord Pei wanted a common woman to help solve a case, they would find it absurd and laughable.

But not Wenchu.

If Yu Wan seriously thought about it, she might actually solve the case.

"It would be good if Qiahe were still alive. Then all your efforts wouldn't be in vain."

Compared to Yu Wan, Wenchu's personality was closer to Ding Wenxi's.

After two years together, this young master of his had developed feelings for everyone at the Jade Pavilion.

"Yes."

At first, Yu Wan had only come to Qingzhou to inquire. If her family had been sold, she would have let it go. But Wei Wu had been evasive and guilty, and with Wenchu's skills, they could have moved freely in Qingzhou. So they had raided Wei Wu's home at night.

Who would have thought that, by sheer bad luck, they would encounter the yamen officers arresting Wei Wu?

Or perhaps it wasn't bad luck, but good luck.

This thought flashed through Yu Wan's mind, and for a brief moment, she felt a strange lightness.

But after that fleeting moment, reason took over again.

Even if Pei Tao was different from others, she couldn't have any more entanglements with the past.

In a few more days, regardless of whether the case was solved, she had to take her mother and Wenchu and leave Qingzhou as soon as possible.

While Yu Wan's mind was in turmoil, Wenchu had been coldly watching her the whole time. But when he casually looked back, he made a new discovery.

"Your Lord Pei is still standing there watching you."

---

chapters.title: Fanciful Thoughts
chapters.content:
"You..." Yu Wan was at a loss for words for a moment. She paused, then glared at Wenchu skeptically. "Really?"

"Don't believe me? Look for yourself."

"I won't. And you're not allowed to look back either. Let's go."

Yu Wan buried her head and walked forward. After they had walked through the corridor and turned into the side veranda, she stopped and asked Wenchu, "Was he really watching us the whole time?"

"Not us. You." Wenchu said seriously.

Yu Wan's emotions were in disarray.

"He just wants me to help solve the case. Standing there, he probably wasn't watching me; just thinking about what we discussed earlier."

"Were you really talking about the case the whole time?"

Yu Wan nodded. "Wei Wu committed suicide in prison. Lord Pei has had people search the upper and lower reaches of the Xi River for days without finding anything, so that's why we talked for so long."

Wenchu thought for a moment. "If Wei Wu was driven to suicide, he must have known how ruthless that person was. There can't be many people in Qingzhou who would dare to do such a thing."

"Not necessarily someone from Qingzhou."

"If this case remains unsolved, will you have to stay in the yamen forever?" Wenchu asked.

"Of course not." Yu Wan said, "I'll help think about it for now. If there's still no progress in a few days, we'll definitely go back."

"You'd better keep your word."

With that, Wenchu walked ahead leisurely.

"Stop!" Yu Wan hurriedly called out to him. "What kind of attitude is that? When have I ever gone back on my word?"

Under Yu Wan's fierce glare, Wenchu helplessly scratched his head.

"I just want to go back soon."

Yu Wan's anger faded. She softened her voice. "Just three days. Three days, and we'll definitely go back."

"Fine."

"Actually, I agreed to help Lord Pei tonight because I did think of something. I'm just not sure yet."

Wenchu didn't think Yu Wan was boasting. He simply asked, "Do you want me to go investigate?"

"There are so many yamen officers here. Why would you need to take the risk? From now on, I won't let you do such things again."

Although several days had passed, every time she thought about what had happened that night at Wei Wu's house, Yu Wan felt a lingering fear.

If the prefect of Qingzhou hadn't been Pei Tao, then Yu Wan and Wenchu would already be in prison, with no one to turn to.

Her mother would be frantic with worry if she knew something had happened to them.

Yu Wan silently made up her mind: from now on, she would only take care of herself, her mother, and Wenchu. She would not meddle in others' affairs.

That was what she thought, but Wenchu interpreted it differently.

In the end, it was because he was too weak.

Although Wenchu was a secret guard, he wasn't naturally combative.

As a child, he had trained in qinggong because his master said he was suited for it; a path that could ensure his survival. Also, qinggong allowed him to avoid direct confrontation.

Even with qinggong, he hadn't pursued perfection.

As long as he was slightly better at it than the other secret guards in the Eastern Palace, that was enough.

Recalling the events of that night at Wei Wu's house, if one of the aggressive, all-rounder secret guards from the Eastern Palace had been with Yu Wan, they would have been unstoppable.

His master had once suggested that he also master projectile weapons in addition to qinggong, but he had only paid lip service and never practiced seriously.

If he had been proficient in both projectiles and qinggong, at the moment the ambush appeared on the wall, he could have thrown a projectile to drive them back and escaped with Yu Wan.

He needed to become stronger to protect those around him.

"Why aren't you talking?" After walking a while, seeing that Wenchu remained silent, Yu Wan couldn't help but ask, "If you really want to go back so soon, I'll go find Lord Pei tomorrow to tell him."

"I'm not in a hurry to go back." Wenchu suppressed his emotions and said quietly, "You two talked for so long earlier. I got sleepy waiting."

It was indeed very late. Yu Wan didn't say more. She returned to the small courtyard, tidied up a bit, and went to bed.

The next morning, Yu Wan woke up early and was about to find Wenchu to eat breakfast together, but Magpie said that Wenchu had gone out for a walk and told Yu Wan not to worry about him.

Yu Wan had felt something was off with him last night. She guessed that Wenchu didn't like being confined and probably didn't want to stay in the yamen for long.

He came and went without a trace, and Yu Wan didn't know where to look for him. After thinking for a moment, she decided to focus on the case first.

If she told Pei Tao all the clues she had thought of, she wouldn't need to stay in the yamen any longer.

"Miss Yu Wan, the prefect has ordered me to follow your instructions. I don't know what I should do."

"Which places does the Xi River pass through?"

Lu Jie replied, "Several counties. The upper and lower reaches are not under Qingzhou's jurisdiction."

As expected.

The body was found in the river within Qingzhou's territory, but the culprit might not have dumped it in Qingzhou, which was why Pei Tao's inquiries along both banks had yielded no witnesses.

"Could you find me a map? I want to carefully see which places the Xi River passes through, especially the upper reaches."

Pei Tao had governed Qingzhou for three years and had a good reputation. The culprit probably wouldn't dare commit the crime right under his nose; at most, they had Wei Wu purchase the girl in Qingzhou.

Since it was an open transaction with ample payment, there was no reason to alert the authorities.

"Very well." Although Lu Jie didn't believe that such a pretty young girl could solve a case, since Pei Tao had ordered it, he had to comply.

He immediately went to the yamen to fetch maps of Qingzhou and the surrounding prefectures.

Since the maps were quite large, the table could only hold one at a time. Yu Wan simply laid several maps in the shade of a tree in the courtyard, arranging them along the flow of the Xi River and piecing them together for a comprehensive view.

The culprit was cautious and secretive. There must be a reason they chose the Xi River to dump the body.

They certainly didn't live on the banks of the Xi River, but they wouldn't be too far away either.

Where could it be?

Pei Tao arrived at noon. The spring sun at midday was already quite strong, and the light was dazzling as it shone directly at him.

After entering the courtyard, he raised a hand to shield his eyes and squinted.

Lu Jie had been sitting by a stone table in the courtyard. Seeing Pei Tao, he quickly stood up and bowed but didn't speak, only pointing with his hand toward the side.

Pei Tao found this odd and followed the direction of Lu Jie's finger. He then saw someone kneeling under the shade of the tree.

Several maps were spread out haphazardly on the bluestone slabs of the courtyard. Yu Wan knelt beside the maps, tilting her head to examine them, occasionally moving on all fours to change her angle for a better look.

She was so absorbed that she didn't notice anyone had entered the courtyard.

"It should be here. No, this place is also possible." Yu Wan seemed to be talking to Lu Jie, but it sounded more like she was talking to herself. "Sigh, all these places are possible, and none are in Qingzhou. How can we find the real culprit?"

Pei Tao had always known she was delicate and beautiful, with an extremely charming appearance. But he had never harbored any fanciful thoughts about her looks.

The world had beautiful scenery, fine wine, and certainly no shortage of beautiful women. Why would he linger everywhere?

But now, seeing her rack her brains to solve the case; sometimes frowning, sometimes murmuring, sometimes sighing, sometimes smiling; a sudden, unfamiliar emotion surged within him.

chapters.title: Miscellaneous
chapters.content:
A hidden undercurrent seemed to sweep through him in an instant, plunging his mind into a blank void.

It was only when Yu Yuan called out to him several times as "Pei Da-ren" that Pei Tao snapped back to his senses, hastily offering her a smile. "I didn’t expect you to study maps."

"It was only after you gave me the Yingzao Fashi that I could understand these."

"You’ve read it all?"

"Mm."

Initially, to seek revenge, she had studied the architectural plans of Xingguo Duke’s mansion day and night, each diagram etched into her mind. Those rules and diagrams were not dull to her; instead, she found them fascinating, even reading the Yingzao Fashi multiple times.

When she heard Pei Tao mention that the killer had dumped the bodies in the Xi River, she had the idea to examine the maps. The killer must live along the Xi River; not too close, but certainly not far.

Pei Tao and his men had searched every inch of the Xi River within Qingzhou’s borders but found nothing, which meant the killer was not in Qingzhou. The bodies had simply drifted downstream from upstream.

"Just now, I heard you muttering to yourself. It seems you’ve gained some insight from these maps."

Yu Yuan replied, "It’s just a guess, perhaps not reliable. Did you go to the medical halls in the city today to investigate?"

"I checked the medical records and drug ledgers; nothing useful."

"As expected, he’s not in Qingzhou."

Seeing her certainty, Pei Tao asked, "Where do you think he is?"

"The true mastermind is likely in Ningzhou."

"Ningzhou?" Pei Tao pondered for a moment. "Why Ningzhou and not Muzhou?"

Tracing the Xi River upstream led to Muzhou, but after flowing six or seven li, the river abruptly turned west toward Ningzhou. That was why the people of Muzhou and Qingzhou called it the Xi River.

"Muzhou’s river is calm, with many villages along both banks, just like Qingzhou. But after the river turns west, both sides are mountains, sparsely populated. If someone wanted to dump bodies, they would certainly choose such a place."

After listening to Yu Yuan, Pei Tao’s gaze fixed deeply on the map.

Yu Yuan noticed his solemn expression and guessed he had thought of something.

Indeed, after a moment, Pei Tao pointed to a section of the river within Ningzhou’s borders and said in a low voice, "Six or seven li north from here, there’s a valley called Maple Leaf Valley. It’s covered in maple trees, red as crimson clouds; breathtaking. Many officials and nobles have villas there."

"Have you been there, Da-ren?"

"Last year, a classmate invited me to stay at his villa for two days." As he spoke, his expression grew heavier.

Yu Yuan studied his face. "Da-ren, have you thought of someone suspicious?"

Pei Tao hesitated for a moment before nodding.

When he had visited last year, he had indeed learned that a powerful figure lived in Maple Leaf Valley. That person had a reputation for ruthlessness and... matched the symptoms of the "buju" condition Yu Yuan had described. It was very possible he was the one they were looking for.

Finding a suspect should have been cause for celebration. But seeing Pei Tao’s difficulty, Yu Yuan asked, "Is he really that hard to deal with?"

"Not exactly. It’s just that he’s not within Qingzhou’s jurisdiction. As the magistrate of Qingzhou, I have no authority to arrest him there."

"So what do we do?"

The magistrate of Ningzhou was Pei Tao’s equal in rank. Naturally, he wouldn’t welcome Pei Tao meddling in his territory, let alone take orders from him. These bureaucratic matters were indeed troublesome.

"There’s still a way. I’ll write to the Ministry of Justice and request their intervention. Once their people arrive, I’ll find a way to lead the investigation toward Ningzhou."

With so many bodies found in the Xi River, it was already a major case; enough to warrant the Ministry of Justice’s involvement. But the current evidence wasn’t enough to tie it to Ningzhou.

Seeing Yu Yuan fretting with him, Pei Tao forced himself to set the matter aside. "Yu Yuan, you’ve really been a great help to me."

"Hardly. My earlier suggestion to check the medical halls was useless."

Pei Tao shook his head. "When the trail goes cold, the only way to keep investigating is to explore every possibility."

He had already searched all of Qingzhou. The killer was indeed not here.

Yu Yuan’s heart stirred.

Remembering that Wen Ji had said he wanted to go back yesterday, and then disappeared early this morning, probably still angry, she said, "Since you’re requesting the court to send investigators to Qingzhou, my staying at the yamen will only cause you trouble. Ji and I should leave soon."

She had brought up leaving several times before, and Pei Tao had no reason to keep her.

Now, he could only nod. "Alright, I’ll arrange for someone to take you tomorrow morning."

"No need. We can ride back on our own."

"Then I’ll prepare the horses for you."

"Thank you, Da-ren."

Watching Yu Yuan’s pleased expression, Pei Tao’s gaze darkened slightly.

"Earlier, I mentioned taking you to the best restaurant in Qingzhou. Since you’re leaving tomorrow, why not go tonight?"

Pei Tao had originally intended it as a welcome for her, but he understood that Yu Yuan was hiding her identity to prevent anyone from her past from discovering her whereabouts.

That night, his men had accidentally cornered Yu Yuan and Ding Ji, and the two had fought desperately to escape. It was the same now, probably.

Once she left, she would likely never return.

If before, Pei Tao had only wanted to keep her because of his suspicions about the case, now he wanted to keep Yu Yuan for an entirely different reason, that moment of distraction.

Pei Tao’s fingers curled inward.

"The chef at Yunyan Tower is as good as any in the capital. Their crab meat lion’s head is especially delicious."

"Won’t dinner interfere with your work, Da-ren?"

"There’s nothing left to investigate in Qingzhou city. After writing the letter to the Ministry of Justice today, I have no other tasks."

"Alright."

It was just one meal before leaving tomorrow. There was no harm in that.

Pei Tao smiled and bent down to pick up the maps scattered on the floor. Yu Yuan had spread them out everywhere and, feeling embarrassed, quickly reached to help.

Their hands brushed against each other unintentionally.

Yu Yuan startled and pulled her hand back, but Pei Tao acted as if nothing had happened, stacking the maps neatly.

"You rest well. See you tonight."

Yu Yuan said nothing, bowing her head slightly to him, but her heart was in turmoil.

She looked at her hand, then gently clenched her fist.

It was just a brief touch. Why did her hand feel so scorching?

Was it... because it was Pei Tao’s hand?

Wen Ji returned to the yamen when the sun was setting. As soon as he entered the courtyard, he saw Yu Yuan looking flustered.

"What happened?" Wen Ji asked.

Yu Yuan quickly composed herself. Turning to see Wen Ji’s sweaty face, she stood up and asked, "Where have you been?"

"Practicing by the river."

He still remembered the methods his master had used to train shadow guards in using hidden weapons. That morning, he had gone to the river to practice alone all day.

"Why did you suddenly go practice?"

"Nothing to do here anyway." Wen Ji muttered.

"Really? You’re not still mad at me?"

---

chapters.title: Night Banquet
chapters.content:
"Of course not."

Yu Yuan noticed the fatigue on his face and thought for a moment. "Want to hear some good news?"

Wen Ji raised an eyebrow and waited for her to continue.

"We can leave first thing tomorrow morning."

"Oh."

Seeing his indifferent expression, Yu Yuan couldn’t help but feel confused.

"Aren’t you happy?"

"I said it has nothing to do with leaving or not." Wen Ji scratched his head and walked past her into the house.

After all this time trying to coax him, he was still angry.

Yu Yuan was annoyed and grabbed him by the sleeve.

Wen Ji, caught by her, looked helpless. "I’m all sweaty. I want to take a shower."

"Pei Da-ren invited us to dinner tonight. I already accepted."

After Wen Ji gave a reluctant "Mm," Yu Yuan finally let go.

After talking with Wen Ji in the courtyard for a while, Yu Yuan’s thoughts finally cleared.

She returned to her room to rest briefly. When Xique came to call her, she got up, did a simple toilette, and left the yamen with Wen Ji.

A carriage was already waiting at the gate. When they boarded, Pei Tao was already inside.

Seeing them arrive, he smiled warmly and gestured for them to sit.

He was so handsome that even a casual smile felt like a sudden rain in the scorching heat of summer; cool and refreshing.

Because of what happened in the afternoon, Yu Yuan didn’t dare to face his smile directly and deliberately stayed behind Wen Ji.

Wen Ji had already noticed Pei Tao’s special attention toward Yu Yuan. Intending to sit near the door to give them space, he felt a nudge at his waist from Yu Yuan.

He managed to stay calm, turning to look at her silently before sitting next to Pei Tao, dryly addressing him as "Pei Da-ren."

Yu Yuan nodded to Pei Tao and took the seat by the carriage door.

Once she was settled, Pei Tao ordered the driver to head to Yunyan Tower.

Yunyan Tower was the best restaurant in Qingzhou. Though Yu Yuan had never been, Wen Ji had brought her and Ding Wenxi takeout from there during his business trips to Qingzhou, including the crab meat lion’s head Pei Tao had mentioned; it was indeed delicious.

But at this moment, Yu Yuan’s mind wasn’t on food.

In the carriage, Pei Tao occasionally exchanged a few words with Wen Ji.

Pei Tao was refined and articulate, naturally the kind of person others found hard to refuse.

Even though Wen Ji initially had no intention of talking much, he ended up engaging in conversation with him.

With the two of them talking, Yu Yuan’s silence didn’t seem out of place.

Soon, they arrived at Yunyan Tower. The manager, knowing Pei Tao was coming, personally greeted them at the entrance and led them to a private room on the third floor.

The room was quiet and undisturbed, and opening the window offered a view of Qingzhou’s night scenery.

Since the restaurant had been prepared in advance, the dishes were served quickly after they sat down.

"Yu Yuan, try the crab meat lion’s head."

Pei Tao stood up and served a spoonful into her bowl.

"Thank you, Da-ren." Yu Yuan said, glancing at Wen Ji. "This is Ji’s favorite dish."

Wen Ji had no idea what had happened in the yamen while he was out practicing all day to make Yu Yuan act so strangely.

He suddenly realized; maybe he shouldn’t be sitting at the same table with them.

But since Yu Yuan had already said that, he could only pick up his bowl and say, "It’s my favorite. I can eat a big bowl every time."

Pei Tao smiled and served Wen Ji a large spoonful.

The three ate in silence. Pei Tao occasionally commented on the dishes but didn’t serve Yu Yuan again or make a special effort to talk to her.

Just as Yu Yuan thought the meal would end smoothly, Wen Ji suddenly stood up.

"What’s wrong?" Yu Yuan asked.

"I need to step out for a moment."

Yu Yuan was surprised. "What for?"

Wen Ji’s expression shifted. Knowing she wouldn’t let it go, he steeled himself. "The restroom."

With that, he quickly left the room.

Only Pei Tao and Yu Yuan remained.

Yu Yuan bit her chopsticks, not daring to look at Pei Tao’s expression.

Even though their hands had only touched briefly that afternoon, it felt as if something earth-shattering had happened.

Pei Tao was always refined and courteous, with clear, steady eyes that made people comfortable around him.

But now, Yu Yuan felt his gaze on her was heavy. That piece of warm, smooth jade seemed to have turned into a scorching hot potato overnight, making her afraid to approach.

Yu Yuan silently prayed for Wen Ji to return quickly so they could go back to the yamen, sleep, and leave first thing in the morning.

"Would you like more tea?" Pei Tao asked.

"No need. I don’t drink much tea after dark."

Seeing her head lowered so deeply, Pei Tao felt a little helpless but knew she was uncomfortable. He simply said, "Alright."

He stood up and pushed open the window of the private room, letting in the cool night breeze.

"Is this better? Less stuffy?"

Yu Yuan bit her chopsticks and softly replied, "Mm." But her cheeks burned even hotter.

She couldn’t help but wonder if she was overthinking things. But Pei Tao’s words made it clear; he knew what she was thinking.

He... really...

"Compared to the capital, Qingzhou is still too small. At this hour, the capital should be lit up everywhere, glowing and dazzling." As he spoke, he turned back and smiled at her. "Since we’ve eaten enough, once Ding Gongzi returns, we can leave."

"Alright." Yu Yuan’s voice was soft, a strange feeling rising in her heart.

Her nose suddenly felt a little sore.

He knew she was struggling, so he had tactfully helped her avoid the awkwardness.

She had been scheming and calculating all along; this feeling was unfamiliar.

Pei Tao remained by the window, and Yu Yuan stayed at the table until Wen Ji’s footsteps were heard on the stairs, breaking the quiet atmosphere in the room.

"Ji, are you full?"

Of course he was. Wen Ji had been full for a while.

"Are we leaving?"

Yu Yuan nodded.

Wen Ji let out a long sigh of relief in his heart and immediately turned to leave. Yu Yuan and Pei Tao followed silently behind him.

The three stood for a moment at the restaurant’s entrance before the carriage arrived.

Wen Ji got in first, then turned to help Yu Yuan up.

As soon as she stepped inside, Pei Tao said from behind, "You two go back first. I’ll take a walk in the streets."

Wen Ji quickly glanced at Yu Yuan and, seeing her silent and withdrawn, said, "Then we’ll leave you to it, Da-ren."

The two entered the carriage. After hearing Pei Tao give the driver a few instructions, they set off toward the yamen.

After traveling a short distance, Wen Ji couldn’t resist lifting the carriage curtain to look back. Seeing Pei Tao indeed walking alone on the street, he looked at Yu Yuan suspiciously. "What did you two talk about earlier?"

Facing Wen Ji, all of Yu Yuan’s emotions vanished in an instant.

She sighed deeply. "So curious. Why did you go to the restroom?"

Wen Ji’s eyes flickered, unsure of what to say.

The reason he went to the restroom was... well, nature called.

But before he could say anything else, he saw the annoyance on Yu Yuan’s face suddenly turn into deep worry.

"Wen Ji... what should I do?"

chapters.title: Returning Home
chapters.content:
"You don’t want to leave?" Wen Kuo asked.

Yu Ying couldn’t answer whether she wanted to leave or not; her mind wasn’t on that at all.

She pulled open the carriage curtain, letting the wind rush in.

The spring night’s breeze carried a faint warmth, pleasant against her skin, but her heart ached.

She couldn’t bear the thought of Pei Ta traveling alone at night, but even if she got out of the carriage, what could she do?

It was just a fleeting, almost imperceptible feeling. All it would bring was endless trouble for Pei Ta; and for herself.

Wen Kuo watched her expression and said softly, "If you don’t want to leave, stay at the county office a few more days. I don’t mind."

"What good would staying a few more days do?"

She wasn’t speaking to Wen Kuo; she was speaking to herself.

Yu Ying took a deep breath, and her muddled thoughts finally cleared a little.

"Last time, you mentioned two bosses in Jiangnan who wanted to buy Shouyu Pavilion, right? When we get back, contact them. If the price is right, then it’s settled."

"Have you decided?"

"Mm."

Leaving was the cleanest way to cut through the mess.

As long as she left, she wouldn’t have to worry about Pei Ta anymore. As long as she left, she, her mother, and Wen Kuo could return to their quiet lives.

Seeing her resolve, Wen Kuo said no more.

When they returned to the government residence, the two of them went to rest. The next morning, they rode out of Qingzhou City.

They had been delayed in Qingzhou for nearly ten days. Thinking of Ding Wenxi, left alone in Qingsha Town, Yu Ying was eager to return, and they traveled swiftly.

"Yingying." Ding Wenxi, hearing they were back, rushed out immediately. She first pulled Yu Ying into her arms, then looked at Wen Kuo, frowning slightly. "A Kuo, why do you look thinner?"

"Do I?"

"Now that you’re back, I’ll have the cook make more dishes tonight to help you recover."

Seeing Yu Ying buried in her arms without a word, Ding Wenxi led them inside. Only after closing the door did she ask, "The people who came to report your safety before were from the government. What exactly happened in Qingzhou? How did you get involved with the officials?"

"It was a major case involving Qiao He. While Wen Kuo and I were investigating, we ran into government officials."

"And then?"

"They arrested us."

Ding Wenxi gasped. "Why arrest you? You two aren’t the ones who harmed Qiao He."

"Qiao He was sold to a human trafficker by her mother. I suspected something was off with the trafficker, so Wen Kuo and I went to his house to question him. That’s when the officials arrived and assumed we were accomplices."

"So the government released you after clearing things up?"

Yu Ying remained silent.

Wen Kuo, seeing this, spoke up. "The magistrate of Qingzhou, Pei Ta, is an old acquaintance of Yu Ying’s from the capital."

Ding Wenxi froze, then looked at Yu Ying in surprise.

She had never met Pei Ta, but his name was familiar to her.

Back when Yu Ying was in the capital, he had sent her paintings and books. Even after leaving the capital, Yu Ying had continued reading the books he gave her.

"He…"

"He said he wouldn’t reveal our whereabouts to anyone," Yu Ying said. "Mother, I’ve decided. Once Shouyu Pavilion is sold, we’ll leave this place."

"You’ve already made up your mind?"

Shouyu Pavilion had cost Ding Wenxi immense effort, from designing jewelry to crafting pieces to training apprentices. Every step had been her personal work.

Hearing that Yu Ying wanted to sell it, she naturally felt reluctant.

But Ding Wenxi also understood why Yu Ying had made this decision.

It was all because of her, this useless mother.

Perhaps one day, when she was gone, Yu Ying would finally be free to live in peace.

Yu Ying noticed Ding Wenxi’s thoughts and quickly took her hand. "Mother, we’ve lived by the sea for so long that both Wen Kuo and I are tired of it. Wen Kuo knows how to brew wine. Once we move to a place with clear waters and lush mountains, we’ll open a tavern."

"That’s right." After Yu Ying finished, Wen Kuo added, "It’s been too hard on you, always making jewelry. Next time, it’ll be my turn to support you both."

"I’ve always enjoyed making jewelry. It’s not hard at all." Ding Wenxi’s gaze fell on Wen Kuo, and she asked curiously, "Why do you always wear a mask?"

Wen Kuo’s half-face human skin mask, which he used to conceal his birthmark, had been torn the other night. Since then, he had been wearing a mask.

"I…"

"Wen Kuo has a birthmark on his face. It’s not pleasant to look at, so he usually disguises it. This time, while he was out, his disguise was accidentally ruined, so he’s wearing a mask for now."

Although they had been together for three years, Ding Wenxi had never seen Wen Kuo’s true appearance.

Wen Kuo looked at Yu Ying with gratitude.

Her words had explained the reason while also conveying his hardship.

"So that’s how it is. It’s good that you’re back." Ding Wenxi sighed. "It’s my fault. If I hadn’t urged you to look into Qiao He’s matter, none of this would have happened."

"If we could ignore Qiao He, then we wouldn’t be your daughter."

Yu Ying and Wen Kuo could manage, but Qiao He was Ding Wenxi’s personal apprentice. She couldn’t possibly ignore her.

"So is she in grave danger now?"

"Magistrate Pei said she’s not in immediate danger. The government is working hard to solve the case. I expect there will be news soon."

"Sigh. She’s a pitiful child. We’ve done our best, and that’s all we can do."

"So, Mother, you agree to sell Shouyu Pavilion?"

Ding Wenxi, despite her reluctance, understood that Yu Ying had made this decision for her sake.

She forced down her emotions and put on a smile. "Qingsha Town is so small. After three years, it’s indeed grown tiresome. Moving somewhere else would be good. I’d like to try A Kuo’s brewing skills too."

Wen Kuo said, "I’ll brew a jar for you to try today."

This chapter is not yet finished. Please click to the next page to continue reading the rest of the exciting content!

"There’s no need to rush. If we’re selling Shouyu Pavilion, you’ll have to run around for it."

"Two bosses from Jiangnan had previously expressed interest in buying Shouyu Pavilion. They’re reliable business partners. I’ll write to them today to ask. If the price is right, it won’t be a hassle."

"You two must be exhausted from the journey back. Go to your rooms to rest and tidy up. I’ll call you when dinner is ready."

Yu Ying nodded silently and stood up, heading to her own room.

Wen Kuo didn’t want to rest. He went back to his room, removed his mask, reattached the human skin mask, and then walked out.

The seaside was quiet and empty; perfect for practicing hidden weapons.

But before he could leave Shouyu Pavilion, Ding Wenxi called out to him.

"A Kuo, come here. I have something to ask you."

"What is it?" Wen Kuo followed Ding Wenxi to the side.

"What exactly happened to you two in Qingzhou City?"

"It’s just what Yu Ying said earlier. We ran into government officials, and Yu Ying was poisoned with Soft Bone Powder. She had to recover at the government office for a few days. Do you think she’s not in good spirits? Maybe the effects of the poison haven’t fully worn off yet."

Ding Wenxi shook her head. "I feel like she has something on her mind."

Wen Kuo fell silent.

"A Kuo, what exactly happened? Can you tell me?"

Wen Kuo looked troubled.

"Maybe you should ask Yu Ying directly. I can’t explain it well."

Wen Kuo did know that Yu Ying’s troubles were related to Pei Ta, but he wasn’t sure what exactly was bothering her.

Was she troubled by Pei Ta’s feelings for her? Or by the fact that she had to leave Pei Ta?

Wen Kuo couldn’t say for sure, and he didn’t want to.

In any case, Yu Ying’s decision was the best. Whatever she wanted was fine.

---

chapters.title: Speaking Face to Face
chapters.content:
Ding Wenxi knew that although Wen Kuo occasionally bickered with Yu Ying, it was all in good fun. When it came to serious matters, Wen Kuo always followed Yu Ying’s lead.

Seeing Wen Kuo’s evasiveness, Ding Wenxi said, "I’m just worried she encountered some trouble out there."

"She didn’t encounter any trouble. It’s just… it’s just…"

"Does it have something to do with that Magistrate Pei? What happened between them in Qingzhou City?"

Ding Wenxi had never met Pei Ta, but she knew he held a special place in Yu Ying’s heart. At the very least, Yu Ying had always treated the books he gave her like treasures.

"You should ask Yu Ying yourself. I don’t know anything." With that, Wen Kuo ran off like the wind.

Ding Wenxi sighed.

Yu Ying was good in every way, except she never shared her worries.

Back in the capital, whenever Ding Wenxi asked about the Marquis’s household, Yu Ying would change the subject.

She had asked, but Yu Ying never said a word. That was why she had tried asking Wen Kuo, only to find he was the same; no matter how she asked, he wouldn’t say.

After Yu Ying and Wen Kuo returned to Qingsha Town, life seemed to return to its usual calm on the surface.

Ding Wenxi continued to lead the artisans in making jewelry, sending batch after batch to Jiangnan. Yu Ying still managed the workshop’s affairs, and Wen Kuo still spent his days by the sea, leaving at dawn and returning at dusk, rarely seen.

But the letter sent to Jiangnan received a reply within half a month. The two bosses were both willing to buy Shouyu Pavilion, and their offers were reasonable.

However, Ding Wenxi asked Yu Ying to inquire with Xiangyu Workshop in Qingzhou City as well.

After all, the big bosses in Jiangnan didn’t lack artisans. What they wanted were the jewelry designs in Ding Wenxi’s hands. If they sold to them, sooner or later, the workshop in Qingsha Town would be shut down.

Most of the workers at Shouyu Pavilion had families and couldn’t leave Qingsha Town to make a living elsewhere.

Knowing Ding Wenxi’s attachment to the workshop, Yu Ying hesitated before sending Wen Kuo to Qingzhou City.

The manager of Xiangyu Workshop was indeed willing to take over Shouyu Pavilion, though the price offered was a bit lower.

Considering Ding Wenxi’s concerns, Yu Ying ultimately decided to sell Shouyu Pavilion to Xiangyu Workshop.

Qingsha Town wasn’t far from Qingzhou City, making management convenient. The land was cheap, and there was easy access to pearl procurement. She wouldn’t close the local workshop. In the future, the people of Shouyu Pavilion would still have a place.

To prevent complications, Yu Ying specifically instructed Wen Kuo to tell the manager not to spread the news. If word got out, the deal would be off. The manager naturally agreed.

By the time this matter was settled, more than a month had passed.

One day, Ding Wenxi was in the workshop guiding an apprentice in crafting silverware when she suddenly heard a commotion at the front of the shop.

A moment later, she saw Lin’s wife walking from the shop toward the backyard.

"What happened?" Ding Wenxi asked.

"Nothing much," Lin’s wife replied. "It’s just that a handsome young man came to the shop, and all the customers are gathered around to look at him."

"Is he here to buy jewelry?"

At Ding Wenxi’s question, Lin’s wife quickly lowered her voice. "He’s here to find our girl."

Ding Wenxi couldn’t help but frown. "How did he refer to Yingying?"

Lin’s wife, confused by the question, thought carefully for a moment before answering honestly, "He said he was looking for Miss Ding Ying."

"Don’t call Yingying yet. I’ll go take a look."

"Alright."

Ding Wenxi put down what she was holding and quickly walked toward the shop.

As soon as she entered, she saw a graceful young man of about twenty standing at the shop’s entrance. Tall and elegant, with refined bones and scholarly bearing, anyone passing by would inevitably take a second look.

Even though Ding Wenxi had never met him before, at first glance, she knew he must be the talented and elegant top scholar Yu Ying had often spoken of; Pei Ta.

For the prestigious Magistrate Pei to come to Shouyu Pavilion in plain clothes to find Yu Ying, Ding Wenxi finally understood the source of Yu Ying’s recent troubles.

"Are you here to find someone, young master?" Ding Wenxi asked.

Pei Ta turned at the sound of her voice and cupped his hands in greeting. "I am surnamed Pei. I am an old friend of Miss Ding Ying. I happened to pass through Qingsha Town and wanted to greet her."

Qingsha Town was isolated, with no villages in front and no shops behind. It stood alone by the East Sea. No one would pass through it on their way anywhere.

Ding Wenxi said, "So you’re Young Master Pei. I’ve long admired your reputation. Please, come have a cup of tea."

To the left of the shop was a partitioned room, usually used for receiving important guests.

After entering, Ding Wenxi first poured Pei Ta a cup of tea.

"My daughter Yingying has often said that Magistrate Pei frequently guided her in reading and writing, and she benefited greatly. As her mother, I must thank you on her behalf."

"Madam, there’s no need for such courtesy." Pei Ta stood up and accepted the tea with both hands. After taking a sip, he said, "Yingying is naturally intelligent. Her reading and writing skills are the result of her own hard work. I dare not take credit."

Ding Wenxi recalled how Yu Ying had once said that noble ladies in the capital had fought to marry him. Looking at Pei Ta’s appearance and manner, she understood a little. She decided to be direct. "Magistrate Pei, since you and Yingying are old acquaintances, you must know how difficult it was for her to leave the capital and make a living here in Qingsha Town."

"I do understand."

"Ever since Yingying was born, she has lived with me in the countryside. Though we lived simply, she grew up free and unconstrained, never suffering any grievances. It was because of my troubles that she sold all her property, even selling herself into servitude to become the concubine of the Marquis’s heir."

Some of what Ding Wenxi said, Pei Ta already knew; some was new to him.

He said nothing, merely waiting quietly for her to continue.

"I’m being forward in sharing so much family business, but I only hope that Magistrate Pei understands that Yingying became a concubine out of necessity. Even though she is no longer the naive and carefree girl she once was, she will never become anyone’s plaything."

"I have never thought of making Yingying my plaything." Pei Ta blurted out.

As soon as the words left his mouth, he couldn’t help but clench his fist.

These were words meant for Yu Ying, yet he had said them here instead.

He didn’t want to boast in front of Ding Wenxi. After taking a deep breath, he bowed respectfully to her.

"Madam, you must have some misunderstandings about me. I came here not to entangle Yingying or disrupt her life. I simply have some things I wish to say to her face to face."

"Your statuses are worlds apart. Some things simply don’t need to be said."

"Thank you for your advice, Madam, but how can we know if they need to be said unless we say them?"

Ding Wenxi hadn’t expected Pei Ta to be so stubborn. She immediately said, "Yingying told me you and your wife are deeply in love. She said you drank yourself into a stupor night after night, wasting away, for her sake. If you feel so deeply for another, then what is the point of coming to see Yingying, if not for amusement?"

Pei Ta’s gaze flickered. He hadn’t expected Yu Ying to have told her mother about those past events.

"If she wants to know, I will explain it myself. Madam, if you do not welcome me, I can wait for her outside the shop."

"You…"

Pei Ta stood up and left the tea room. The moment he pushed open the door, he saw Yu Ying standing in the shop, attending to customers.

chapters.title: The Sea Breeze is Damp
chapters.content:
At the moment she saw Pei Tao, Yu Ying’s eyes flickered with disbelief.

He had come?

He had actually come to Su Yu Xuan?

What did he want to do, or rather, what did he want to say?

Before she could ask, Pei Tao spoke first: "I came today because I have something to say to you."

Yu Ying glanced at Ding Wenxi, who had hurried out after her. There was a hint of anxiety in Ding’s eyes. Yu Ying didn’t know what they had talked about inside, but she could roughly guess it had something to do with her.

"Then... please come with me, Young Master."

Pei Tao was dressed in casual attire, so it was more appropriate to address him as Young Master.

"Alright."

"Yingying, don’t go," Ding Wenxi advised.

Earlier, Yu Ying had thought that if she never saw Pei Tao again, everything would fade away. But since he had come to her door, she had to clarify things. Otherwise, even her mother would worry.

Yu Ying said, "Mother, I’ll be right back."

Ding Wenxi had always been helpless with Yu Ying. Seeing her turn and walk away with Pei Tao, she could only sigh and turn to disperse the onlookers in the shop.

Qingsha Town only had two streets. Yu Ying and Pei Tao passed through the shops on the opposite side, walked through a low grove of windbreaking trees, and could see the distant sea.

Listening to the faint sound of waves, Yu Ying stopped and turned to face Pei Tao.

"Why has Young Master come to Qingsha Town today?"

"To find you."

Pei Tao answered directly.

"May I ask what brings you here?" Yu Ying had not yet figured out the subtle changes between her and Pei Tao, but she had already decided to leave this place, so there was no need to dwell on it.

Sensing that Yu Ying was no longer as uneasy as she had been that night at Yunyan Tower, Pei Tao’s gaze held a touch of desolation.

"The authorities have found Xia He. She and the other rescued women are being cared for by physicians arranged by the officials. Once they recover a bit and finish giving their statements, they will be sent back."

"The case is solved?" Yu Ying asked in surprise.

Pei Tao nodded.

"Who was the real culprit behind it all?"

Although Yu Ying had stopped looking into the matter, she and Wen Ji had spent considerable effort on it, so she was naturally concerned about the final outcome.

"The culprit, though not from Ning Prefecture, had a villa in Maple Leaf Valley. And..." Pei Tao paused, then lowered his voice, "Another thing is similar to your guess; he is a eunuch, though not impotent. So, those women, though tormented, were not deflowered."

"A eunuch?" Yu Ying was surprised. "Then he was..."

"The culprit is Hong Man, the eunuch in charge of the Market Shipping Office. Though his rank is not high, he oversees the imperial maritime and grain transport, so many people fawn over him, and he holds great power. In his villa in Maple Leaf Valley, he imprisoned more than twenty girls around Xia He’s age."

"And he...?"

Pei Tao’s expression was heavy. After a moment of silence, he said solemnly, "Somehow, he learned that using unbroken girls to cultivate yin pearls could restore his... manhood. So he had people buy girls around fourteen or fifteen to cultivate yin pearls. By the way, the pearls he used were also obtained from Qingsha Town."

Yu Ying had heard about cultivating yin pearls in town.

It was said that pearls were inserted into a girl’s body and left for forty-nine days before being taken out, ground into powder, and consumed for health benefits.

When she first heard about this, Yu Ying had nearly vomited, thinking it was just a bizarre and far-fetched rumor. She never expected someone to actually do it.

"So it was a eunuch. No wonder Wei Wu was so terrified."

Pei Tao nodded. "Besides Wei Wu, there were three other human traffickers helping him buy girls. They have all been captured."

"Since he is a eunuch, he must have come from the palace. I didn’t expect the case to be resolved so smoothly."

"It was a coincidence. When the officials from the Ministry of Justice and I traced the case to Ning Prefecture, we encountered people from the Jin Yi Wei conducting a secret investigation. Although Hong Man is only a fifth-rank official, the Market Shipping Office is a lucrative position. He embezzled a lot during his tenure, and the Jin Yi Wei had been investigating him. This time, they raided Hong Man’s villa, found the imprisoned girls, and also discovered the gold and silver he had hidden in Maple Leaf Valley. The Emperor was furious, so the case was handled very quickly."

When Yu Ying heard the words "Jin Yi Wei," her heart inexplicably skipped a beat.

"Who in the Jin Yi Wei was responsible for investigating this case?"

Pei Tao was slightly taken aback, then said softly, "It was their Deputy Commander, Pan Xun."

Yu Ying was not unfamiliar with the name Pan Xun.

Earlier, when Zhao Xuanyou first took over the Jin Yi Wei, he had praised Pan Xun’s abilities and promoted him to a thousand-household commander.

When Yu Ying met Zhao Qi in Yangzhou, Zhao Qi told her that it was Pan Xun who had followed the clues to uncover the Gongzhu case involving the Duke of Xingguo.

Although she had never met Pan Xun, she was certain he was Zhao Xuanyou’s man.

Pei Tao noticed the panic in Yu Ying’s expression and reassured her, "Pan Xun has been handling the case in Ning Prefecture and has never been to Qing Prefecture. Moreover, he has already escorted Hong Man back to the capital, leaving only a few people to assist the Ministry of Justice officials in collecting testimonies here."

"I see." Yu Ying let out a slight sigh of relief.

Pei Tao, though unaware that Pan Xun was a man personally promoted by Zhao Xuanyou, could easily guess the connection given that he was from the Jin Yi Wei.

"Don’t worry. I have already instructed Lu Jie and the others not to disclose your whereabouts to anyone."

He had already considered everything for her.
