Yu Ying didn’t know what to feel in her heart, but when she looked at Pei Tao, there was clearly more gratitude in her eyes.

"Thank you, Young Master, for informing me of this. On Xia He’s behalf, I thank you for saving her life."

Pei Tao met her gaze and said softly, "If it were only for this, I wouldn’t have needed to come to Qingsha Town in person."

Yu Ying, of course, understood the implication in his words.

Since she had decided to clarify things today, she didn’t want to beat around the bush.

"Then, did Young Master come to Qingsha Town for another reason?"

Pei Tao lightly responded with an "mm."

Yu Ying didn’t speak again. Instead, she turned and took a few more steps toward the sea.

The wind by the sea carried a damp, fishy smell. At first, it was unpleasant, but after a while, it became quite refreshing.

After a moment of silence, Pei Tao’s voice came through the howling wind.

"Yu Ying, do you still remember the time I got drunk at Taoran Inn?"

"I do. What about it?"

Of course, Yu Ying remembered.

That day, Pei Tao sat alone at Taoran Inn, drinking himself into a stupor. It was the first time Yu Ying had seen Pei Tao in such a despondent state.

Of course, that day was also very important to Yu Ying.

It was the first time she had the idea to set fire to kill Cui Yichu.

If not for that night, if not for meeting Pei Tao, if not for learning about the construction map from Pei Tao, Yu Ying might have sought revenge before leaving the capital, but it would not have been as satisfying as it was three years ago.

One fire, killing Cui Yichu, and also "killing" Yu Ying.

"That day, I felt as if my heart was dead, all my hopes were shattered. But looking back, I feel fortunate that heaven let me meet you."

---

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.content:
Yu Ying’s scattered thoughts gradually converged.

Ever since that day in the yamen studying the map, Pei Tao’s gaze toward her had subtly changed.

She had some idea why Pei Tao had come to Qingsha Town today.

She just hadn’t expected him to bring up that drunken night three years ago.

So she softly asked, "Why?"

"That day, I felt devastated, but in reality, the blow you suffered was no less than mine. Cui Yichu tried to harm you repeatedly, and like me, you wanted the Duke of Xingguo’s household to fall quickly. But while I drank and pitied myself, you comforted me and already thought of a countermeasure."

"It was only after hearing you mention the construction map that I came up with the idea."

"You didn’t just come up with it on the spot," Pei Tao said, looking at the faint smile on Yu Ying’s face. In her clear and tranquil eyes, a different emotion flickered. "From the moment I said that the Duke of Xingguo had escaped the Gongzhu case, you started thinking about how to make amends, how to seek revenge, and how to use the construction map from the fragments of my words."

"How could I be that clever?"

"You are that clever," Pei Tao said, his gaze slowly scanning her face. "You’re not just clever, you’re also resilient."

His praise was sincere, and as Yu Ying listened, she couldn’t help but smile.

"Stop praising me, Young Master, or I’ll start thinking I’m the cleverest person under heaven."

Pei Tao looked at the smug little expression on her face and, for a moment, was captivated by her soft and delicate features. After a while, he continued, "When I heard in Qing Prefecture that the Duke of Xingguo’s household had collapsed like a house of cards, I immediately thought of you. I knew the fire was related to the construction map, and it must have been related to you. I often wondered how you did it, but I couldn’t figure it out. I always hoped to see you again, to have you tell me what happened that night, how you planned it, and how you executed it."

"You... you mean after leaving the capital, you..."

"Yes," Pei Tao nodded solemnly at Yu Ying. "I mean, I’ve wanted to see you again for these three years."

With his heavenly renowned beauty, standing so close and saying such words, Yu Ying naturally found it hard to handle.

She didn’t dare meet his gaze, so she turned her face away, looking out at the distant sea.

"You just want to know the truth about the fire at the duke’s mansion," Yu Ying said, her words lacking conviction.

Pei Tao clearly meant more than that, but she could only feign ignorance.

"Earlier, I thought I just admired your intelligence. But when I saw you seriously studying the map in the courtyard that day, I realized I didn’t just admire your intelligence, and I didn’t just want to see you once. Yu Ying, I want to see you every day, all the time."

No one knew how he had tossed and turned these past three years, thinking about that night at Taoran Inn.

No one knew how he had repeatedly pondered every word she had said to him.

In the three years since being exiled from the capital, whenever he felt disheartened or dejected, he would think of Yu Ying from that night.

She had a blood feud with Cui Yichu, yet even when she learned that the Duke of Xingguo’s household had escaped unscathed, her eyes still sparkled.

Those lively eyes, Pei Tao could not forget, lingering in his thoughts.

So, after reuniting at the yamen and learning that she had not spent the past three years with Zhao Xuanyou in the northwest, his feelings had subtly changed.

"You..."

Yu Ying was not an inexperienced young girl.

In the past, when she was with Zhao Xuanyou, she had heard many blunt and unrestrained words from him.

But Pei Tao’s confession just now was the first of its kind she had ever heard.

He openly revealed his feelings, carefully presenting his heart to her.

Yu Ying’s emotions surged, and for a moment, tears welled in her eyes. But she bit her lip and forced the tears back.

She had to leave Qingsha Town. She had to stay away from everyone connected to the capital.

"Thank you for your kind words, Young Master."

Her words contained no rejection, yet every word was a rejection.

Pei Tao was an intelligent man and naturally understood.

His gaze suddenly sharpened as he looked down at Yu Ying. "Do you despise me?"

"How could I?" Yu Ying forced a smile. "In the capital, every young lady admires you, competing to marry you."

"I don’t care about others. I only ask you."

"I..." Pei Tao’s pressing question made Yu Ying feel cornered, so she tried her best to avoid his gaze.

"Just now, your mother told me not to entangle myself with you anymore."

Yu Ying was slightly taken aback and said through gritted teeth, "My mother was afraid you would come to ask me, so she answered for me in advance."

"So, what your mother said is what you think?"

Pei Tao’s eyes were as dark as ink, gazing deeply at Yu Ying.

Yu Ying hardened her heart and nodded.

Seeing her response, Pei Tao suddenly curved his lips into a smile. "Then do you, like the other girls, want to marry me?"

"I never said that." Yu Ying quickly denied.

"You did. Your mother’s words are your thoughts," Pei Tao’s eyes suddenly brightened, and his tone became lighter. "She said that there is a world of difference between our statuses, and that I was married before, so I might not be sincere toward you."

So her mother had actually said all that to Pei Tao...

She really had been worrying about her all along.

Yu Ying took a deep breath and countered, "Were her words wrong?"

"They’re not wrong, but those words show that you don’t dislike me. You just have many concerns and don’t dare accept me." Pei Tao spoke with his eyes fixed earnestly on Yu Ying.

She opened her mouth, not knowing how to respond.

She had heard that when scholars took the imperial examination, they had to answer the emperor’s questions. Now, Yu Ying finally understood why Pei Tao could be the number one scholar; it was not just because of his outstanding appearance.

"I have both. I don’t like you, and I have many concerns." Unable to refute him, Yu Ying could only deny it outright. "You have been very kind to me, Young Master. You gave me calligraphy and books. I respect you greatly, but I have no feelings of love for you."

"Really?"

"Of course. Moreover, you know that I set the fire at the Duke of Xingguo’s mansion. I am destined to live in hiding forever. How could I possibly have any connection with you?"

"I’ll marry Ding Ying." Pei Tao blurted out.

Marry her?

Yu Ying was stunned for a moment and shook her head. "Don’t joke, Young Master. What marriage?"

"You don’t believe me?"

Yu Ying steadied her mind and said solemnly, "This has nothing to do with belief. I am not a suitable match for you. I can never see the light of day, nor can I return to the capital. That’s all I have to say. Please, Young Master, do not come looking for me again in the future."

After saying this, Yu Ying turned and walked away.

"Yu Ying."

Pei Tao was naturally reluctant and wanted to follow her.

Hearing his footsteps, Yu Ying suddenly shouted, "Wen Ji!"

A dark shadow descended from the sky, placing itself between her and Pei Tao.

chapters.title: Touching the Reverse Scales
chapters.content:
"Pei Daren, please go back." Wen Ji shielded Yu Ying behind him, coldly looking at Pei Tao.

Pei Tao ignored Wen Ji's words, only looking at Yu Ying who had her back to him, his eyes filled with deep affection.

"I know you have many concerns. If you trust me, we can solve all of them. If you don’t want to return to the capital, we won’t."

The wind by the sea gradually grew stronger, blowing Yu Ying's apricot-colored spring dress until it fluttered, outlining her graceful and charming figure.

Her posture was indeed captivating, but she stubbornly refused to turn around, appearing utterly resolute in Pei Tao's eyes.

Wen Ji said, "Pei Daren, since Yu Ying has made her decision, nothing you say will change her mind."

"Ah Ji." Yu Ying stopped Wen Ji from saying more, only turning her head slightly, "Let's go."

Wen Ji understood, turning and pulling Yu Ying's arm, leading her away like a gust of wind, disappearing from Pei Tao's sight.

Even though Pei Tao was reluctant, he could no longer find any trace of Yu Ying.

After a moment, Wen Ji brought Yu Ying to a stop in a forest.

This place wasn't actually far from where they had been earlier. The sea was still visible, but a few thatched houses blocked the view.

Yu Ying looked around at the trees, noticing that many trunks had knife marks, and the ground was littered with leaves that looked neatly cut, as if sliced by a sharp blade.

"Do you usually come here when you go out?"

Wen Ji hadn't expected her to shift the conversation to him so quickly, so he could only respond with an "Mmm."

This place was densely wooded, suitable for practicing hidden weapons, and it wasn't far from the Jade House, so if something happened at the shop, he could still attend to it.

"Why are you suddenly so diligent in practicing?"

"I don’t want us... to be caught like that night again." This was a resolve Wen Ji had secretly made, but since Yu Ying asked, he answered truthfully.

"I was wondering, you’ve been going out early and coming back late these days, returning smelling of sweat."

"Stink?" Wen Ji turned his head and sniffed his own arm.

Seeing his action, Yu Ying couldn't help but laugh.

"Who said you stink?"

Wen Ji saw the smile return to Yu Ying's face and didn't mind her teasing. He just quietly watched her.

"Will Pei Daren back down?"

"He probably will."

Although Pei Tao was gentle and refined, Yu Ying understood that deep down, he was a very proud man.

Today, he had come to Qingsha Town and bared his heart to her, sharing the feelings he had held for the past three years. That was already the limit of what he could do.

Wen Ji watched as the smile in Yu Ying's eyes gradually faded.

He wanted to say something to make her feel better, but he couldn't think of anything.

Matters of love between men and women were something he simply didn't understand. How could he advise Yu Ying?

After some thought, Wen Ji supported Yu Ying's arm and led her to jump onto a high tree branch.

"Ah…" Yu Ying let out a soft cry, but when she looked into the distance at the sea, she immediately exclaimed in delight, "I never expected the sea to look so different from here."

"Sit down first."

At Wen Ji's reminder, Yu Ying finally held his hand and sat on the tree trunk, her other hand grabbing a branch.

"After living here for three years, I only now discovered such a beautiful view. It makes me a little reluctant to leave."

Wen Ji glanced at her, then looked at the distant sea: "Then don't leave?"

Yu Ying didn't make a sound, just quietly looked at the sea like him.

The waves rolled in one after another, endlessly and ceaselessly.

"How can we not leave?"

"Didn't he say he would find a way?"

Yu Ying gently shook her head.

From the moment she was reborn, she had already grown accustomed to solving her own problems.

Others might be smarter or stronger than her, but only the solutions she came up with herself were the most reliable.

"You don't trust him?"

"No."

In this matter, Wen Ji truly couldn't fathom Yu Ying's thoughts.

"Then do you like him or not?"

"Does it matter? We're leaving anyway."

Wen Ji's gaze flickered, but he didn't speak, just silently sat with Yu Ying.

After a long silence, Yu Ying nudged Wen Ji's arm.

"If you were me, what would you do?"

"Me?" Wen Ji pondered for a moment, "If I liked him a lot, I wouldn't leave."

"Not even if it meant death?"

Wen Ji hesitated for a moment, then nodded firmly.

Yu Ying watched his response, her expression brightening again.

"Little Wen, you're more infatuated than I am."

"Don't talk nonsense."

Wen Ji lowered his head deeply. What use was infatuation for someone like him? Who would like him?

Afraid that Yu Ying would tease him further, he countered, "You said you're not infatuated, does that mean you like him?"

Did she like him?

"I don't know." Yu Ying was indeed distracted by his question, digging her fingers into the tree bark. "Actually, when he said those things, I was very happy."

"What things?"

Wen Ji hadn't eavesdropped on Yu Ying and Pei Tao's conversation. He had only run over when he heard Yu Ying's call.

"Just..." If it were her mother asking, Yu Ying would certainly not say, but with Wen Ji, she had no reservations. No matter what she said or did, Wen Ji would just quietly accompany her. "He said that ever since he learned that the Hou Mansion fell because of me, he had been thinking of me constantly and wanted to see me again."

As expected, Wen Ji didn't judge, just lightly responded with an "Oh."

"He also said he was happy to know that I hadn't been with anyone else."

"That's it?"

Facing Wen Ji's calm expression, Yu Ying quickly blurted out, "He said he wants to marry me."

"Marry..." Wen Ji was finally moved, turning his head in surprise to look at Yu Ying. "Just now, when he was chasing you, it was to marry you?"

Yu Ying nodded.

"You refused him?"

Yu Ying nodded again.

Wen Ji frowned, not knowing what he was thinking. After a while, he looked at Yu Ying: "I see you're quite happy."

"Can't I be happy?" Yu Ying lowered her eyes, her cheeks puffing up. "It's the first time someone has said these things to me."

Moreover, that person was Pei Tao.

Looking at Yu Ying's snow-white cheeks, slightly flushed, Wen Ji thought for a moment: "Zhao Xuanyou never said that to you?"

Yu Ying hadn't expected Wen Ji to suddenly bring up Zhao Xuanyou.

"How would he say such things?"

"You were by his side for so long. He even repeatedly opposed the Crown Prince for your sake."

Yu Ying calmly said, "I was just his maid. He opposed the Crown Prince not because of me. Don't you remember why the Crown Prince sent you to capture me in the first place?"

That was true.

Wen Ji was very clear about the matters between the Crown Prince and Cui Yichu. As long as Zhao Xuanyou knew about this, if he had any integrity, he wouldn't submit to the Crown Prince.

However, Wen Ji still felt that Zhao Xuanyou had treated Yu Ying well, but seeing her expression, he didn't dare mention it again.

"Alright." Wen Ji said softly.

He had misspoken earlier, bringing up the wrong person, which upset Yu Ying. He scratched his cheek and added, "You like hearing what Pei Daren said, so does that mean you want to marry him?"

---

chapters.title: Defection
chapters.content:
The word "marry" was actually very distant for Yu Ying.

From the moment she sold herself into the Marquis's mansion, marriage had nothing to do with her.

As a servant, her marriage was a matter for her master to decide with a single word.

When she was sent to Zhao Xuanyou's bed by Cui Yichu and had a marital relationship with him, her life became tied to him alone. If she gained his favor, she could become a concubine or a secondary wife.

Even now, having left the capital and Zhao Xuanyou, although Yu Ying didn't intend to set up a chastity arch, she had prepared herself to never marry.

In the eyes of the world, a woman who had lost her virginity was indeed devalued, but Yu Ying didn't see herself that way. She wouldn't marry someone she looked down on just because she wasn't a virgin. It was difficult to find a balance, so marriage was out of the question.

Pei Tao knew she had been a concubine, and yet he still asked to marry her, which meant he didn't mind.

Yu Ying believed he didn't mind.

He didn't care about her past, didn't care about her need to hide, and was determined to marry her.

As Wen Ji had noticed, she was very happy... very happy.

But life wasn't just about being happy for a moment.

Pei Tao was a top scholar personally selected by His Majesty, enjoying imperial favor and smooth official career. Even if he had offended Prime Minister Sun, His Majesty had often protected him.

Previously, his father had been the county magistrate of Qingsha Town and died at the hands of Tao Cheng, who was then the prefect of Qingzhou. His Majesty had specially appointed Pei Tao to be the prefect of Qingzhou, which showed his deep intentions.

Under Pei Tao's governance, the people of Qingzhou lived in peace and prosperity. It was only a matter of time before he returned to the capital.

Refusing his proposal was good for Yu Ying, and even better for Pei Tao.

Wen Ji looked at Yu Ying's complicated expression and asked again, "If we didn't have to hide, would you marry him?"

"There are no so many ifs."

"Just answer me."

Wen Ji's persistent questioning left Yu Ying somewhat helpless.

Anyway, with Wen Ji, it didn't matter what she said.

"Marry him, of course I would. He's so handsome and a talented top scholar. Only a fool wouldn't marry him," Yu Ying said, her lips curling up again. "If I married him, I would definitely be the most glamorous woman in the capital."

"Really?"

"Of course. In the past, the noble ladies in the capital all competed to marry him, even the princesses were no exception."

Wen Ji had heard from the Crown Prince that the two princesses were extremely picky, looking down on everyone. He didn't know about them competing for Pei Tao.

"Actually, they weren't wrong. Pei Daren is truly a good man." Thinking of the times she had known Pei Tao in the past, Yu Ying's voice softened, her expression slightly moved. "Back in the imperial palace, he noticed that I wanted to study, so he let me attend classes with the Seventh Prince. When he found out I wanted to practice calligraphy, he gave me calligraphy models to copy and even indirectly had the Seventh Prince lend me the Four Books and Five Classics. I was just a maid, and apart from him, no one else would think I genuinely wanted to read and write."

Wen Ji, of course, knew that Yu Ying had always treasured those books, but he didn't know they were gifts from Pei Tao.

Looking at Yu Ying's animated expression, he suddenly felt a pang of discomfort.

No wonder Yu Ying never wanted to tell her mother about these things.

He wasn't clear on Ding Wenxi's exact identity, but Yu Ying had subtly hinted to him that Ding Wenxi's status was of great significance and was the reason Yu Ying had to leave the capital.

Having been together for three years, Wen Ji knew that their mother-daughter bond was deep. Yu Ying hid these things from Ding Wenxi because she was afraid that Ding Wenxi would be heartbroken to learn that Yu Ying had lost her chance at lifelong happiness because of her.

"Why the long face?" Yu Ying asked with a smile. "I should be happy that someone like Pei Daren likes me."

Wen Ji felt even worse.

"Yu Ying, you should marry him."

Yu Ying was slightly taken aback. "What did you say?"

"Didn't he say that no matter what your hardships are, he will find a way? You're so smart, you can help him think of solutions. I may not be of much use, but I will do my best to help. Yu Ying, since you like him, why must you leave?"

"Wen Ji, how can even you defect to his side?"

Yu Ying's tone was quite helpless.

She was willing to talk so much with Wen Ji because he never expressed his own opinions. No matter what she said, he would just comply.

But she hadn't expected Wen Ji to actually speak up for Pei Tao.

"I just think you shouldn't refuse him."

"If I don't refuse him, our whereabouts will eventually be exposed." Even though she was happy because of Pei Tao's confession, Yu Ying had never forgotten the reason they left the capital.

"I just think that way, you would be happier. Yu Ying, talk to him. What if he has a good solution?"

"I talked to him, and it made him even more unwilling to give up."

"Then I'll ask him for you?"

Yu Ying stared at him. "Since when have you been so enthusiastic?"

"Since when have I not cared about your affairs?"

Wen Ji retorted, but to Yu Ying, it felt different.

Marrying Pei Tao, becoming the prefect's wife, and being with him day and night did sound wonderful, but what she could hold onto now was only the peaceful life of their trio.

"Ying! Ah Ji!" Ding Wenxi looked up and waved at them.

Yu Ying responded with an "Ei," turning to Wen Ji, "How did my mother know we were here?"

"Earlier, she saw me going out early and coming back late, so she asked what I was doing. I told her I came here to daydream."

As he spoke, Wen Ji pulled Yu Ying, and they both jumped down from the tree.

"Mother, did something happen at the shop?"

"That Pei Daren has already left."

Yu Ying responded with an "Oh." Seeing the worry between Yu Ying's brows, Ding Wenxi sighed, "I know he's a remarkable and likable man, but I don't want you to follow in my footsteps. If I hadn't been pregnant under unclear circumstances back then, you wouldn't have suffered so much."

So Mother thought Pei Daren had intentions to toy with her, which was why she specially called him inside for a talk.

Seeing Wen Ji about to speak, Yu Ying fiercely glared at him.

Wen Ji had no choice but to shut his mouth and stand silently to the side.

Yu Ying linked arms with Ding Wenxi, leading her towards the Jade House. "I know, I've already made it clear to him. He won't come to the door again, will he?"

"Really? When he left, he..."

Yu Ying's heart twisted at Ding Wenxi's words.

"Did he say something to you when he left?"

"Not really."

Pei Tao hadn't said anything when he left, but his eyes seemed to reveal a stubborn unwillingness to give up. He probably wouldn't let it go easily.

In her view, Pei Tao was no different from Zhao Xuanyou. Men like them, high-ranking officials and nobles, always had to marry a noblewoman to manage the household.

Even if Yu Ying was clever and beautiful, able to gain their affection and temporary favor, in the long run, how could a concubine not suffer grievances?

When she was young, she had been blinded by love and hadn't considered these things. It was only when the Tao family came to the village to find her that she deeply felt the humiliation and powerlessness.

So she ran away. Although life in the village was poor and tiring, at least she didn't have to live in humiliation.

"Ying, let's leave this place of trouble as soon as possible."

chapters.title: Setting Sail Again
chapters.content:
"Alright."

Hearing Yu Wan agree so readily, Wen Kuo lowered his head even further.

Yu Wan smiled gently. "Mother, don’t worry. I’ve already had Ah Kuo go find a boat. Once it arrives at Qingsha Town, we can leave immediately."

"When will the deal with Xiangyu Workshop be settled?" Ding Wenxi asked.

"Yesterday, the mistress of the workshop already delivered the silver notes."

"Are we taking a boat again?"

"Qingsha Town’s official roads aren’t very wide. Taking a boat is still more convenient." After a pause, Yu Wan added, "Three years ago in Yangzhou, I promised to take you around Jiangnan properly, but the two of us just stayed hidden on the boat the whole time. This time, we must make up for it."

Ding Wenxi smiled and nodded. She didn’t care much for scenery; having her daughter by her side was enough.

"You’re right, Mother. It’s best not to delay leaving. Ah Kuo, hurry and arrange the boat. We’ll leave in a few days."

Wen Kuo gave a heavy nod.

Seeing his expression, Yu Wan understood what he was thinking.

How could she not know what he was worried about?

In truth, if Wen Kuo hadn’t arrived in time to take her away today, she might have already agreed to Pei Ta.

Mother was right; this place was no longer safe for them. And she couldn’t see Pei Ta again.

Leaving early was best for both of them.

"Mother, let’s go back to the shop. Ah Kuo still needs to practice."

Afraid that Ding Wenxi might notice something from Wen Kuo’s expression, Yu Wan stepped in front of him, blocking him from view, and took Ding Wenxi’s hand to walk back.

Ding Wenxi had indeed noticed Wen Kuo’s low spirits, but she assumed it was from practicing too hard. She advised, "Ah Kuo has been training so hard these days. His martial arts are already excellent. Why push himself so much?"

"I have to keep practicing, so I can protect you."

Ding Wenxi let go of Yu Wan’s hand and handed Wen Kuo a handkerchief. "Wipe your sweat."

Wen Kuo took the handkerchief, glanced at Yu Wan, and said nothing more.

"It’s been tough, hasn’t it? Today, the cook made chicken soup. I saved both drumsticks for him."

"Good."

Yu Wan and her mother laughed as they walked away. Wen Kuo stayed behind in the woods, continuing to practice his hidden weapons. By the time the sky darkened, he went to the blacksmith’s to pick up something before returning to the Yaoyu Pavilion. The shop had already closed by then.

"Back?" Yu Wan saw Wen Kuo and came out from the kitchen.

"Have you all eaten?"

"Mother invited Lin’s wife and a few others to have dinner at the shop today. We didn’t want to keep them waiting, so we ate first. I saved a drumstick for you."

The seamstresses at Yaoyu Pavilion had all been personally trained by Ding Wenxi, so their bond was special. Knowing they would be leaving soon, these days she had been finding excuses to keep them at the shop for meals and chats.

Wen Kuo didn’t mind, of course.

He followed Yu Wan into the kitchen and saw that the small table was already set with three dishes; Yu Wan had picked them out for him in advance.

Once Wen Kuo sat down, Yu Wan took a bowl from the stove and ladled out the chicken soup, placing the two promised drumsticks inside.

Wen Kuo looked at the table full of food but didn’t pick up his chopsticks immediately.

"I won’t try to persuade you anymore."

Seeing that Wen Kuo had seen through her intentions, Yu Wan’s eyes curved into a smile. "You may not talk much, but you’re actually quite good at persuading people."

"Really?"

Wen Kuo thought she was annoyed by his nagging and wanted him to be quiet. He hadn’t expected Yu Wan to say he was good at persuading.

"But I didn’t persuade you at all."

Yu Wan saw his dejected expression and smiled, raising her hand to show a tiny gap between two fingers. "Almost. Just a little more."

"So..."

Seeing Wen Kuo was about to speak, Yu Wan quickly cut him off. "You said yourself you wouldn’t persuade me anymore."

Wen Kuo opened his mouth but ultimately said nothing. He picked up his chopsticks and began eating the meal Yu Wan had saved for him.

The chicken soup had been simmered for half a day; the drumsticks were so tender they fell off the bone with a single bite.

Yu Wan sat beside him and noticed the bulging pouch at his waist. Curious, she asked, "What good stuff are you hiding in there?"

"Nothing much. I had the blacksmith make some hidden weapons for me."

Yu Wan knew Wen Kuo had been working so hard lately because of the incident at Wei Wu’s place where he had been captured. She was grateful to him.

"I’ve never seen hidden weapons like these before. Let me have a look."

Wen Kuo ate as he handed her the pouch.

Yu Wan poured all the hidden weapons onto the table. There were many strange shapes: small knives like willow leaves, iron balls the size of fingernails, cross-shaped spikes, and iron needles slightly thicker than embroidery needles.

Yu Wan’s eyes widened in surprise. She looked at Wen Kuo in astonishment. "You’re going to use all of these?"

Wen Kuo put down his bowl and chopsticks and shook his head. "Not all of them. I just want to try them out and see which ones feel better in my hand."

Yu Wan nodded as if she understood, carefully picking up one to examine.

"Where did you learn about so many kinds of hidden weapons?"

"In the past, I saw my master training others with them. Besides, this isn’t even that many."

The town’s blacksmith wasn’t specialized in making hidden weapons, so he could only craft these simple designs. More complex ones, like those with barbs or internal poison compartments, were beyond his skill.

"Use this one." Yu Wan picked up the small iron ball and shook it.

"Why?"

"Because this one looks the least like a weapon. If others don’t harm it, it won’t harm them either; just like you."

Wen Kuo was an undercover guard, but his personality was gentle, and he didn’t enjoy fighting or killing.

"Alright." Wen Kuo actually found the willow-leaf knife more comfortable, but since Yu Wan liked the iron ball, he would use the iron ball.

Yu Wan said nothing more, quietly playing with the hidden weapons on the table. After Wen Kuo finished eating and wiped his mouth, he said, "Actually, I already bought the boat a long time ago. It’s docked at the shipyard. If we want to leave, we can go tomorrow."

"When did you buy it?"

"As soon as you said you wanted to leave. I’ve also prepared everything we need."

Feeling Wen Kuo’s gaze on her, Yu Wan felt a little helpless.

Wen Kuo had said he wouldn’t persuade her anymore, but bringing up the boat now was clearly another way of persuading her.

Did she really have to leave?

Yu Wan asked herself again, but she forced herself not to think about Pei Ta.

"Mother also wants to leave soon. We’ve already taken the silver from Xiangyu Workshop. Staying here any longer would be taking advantage of them. Since the boat can leave tomorrow, let’s go tomorrow."

A tangled mess is best cut with a sharp knife.

Yu Wan dropped this line and went to find Ding Wenxi to tell her about leaving the next day.

The decision to leave Qingsha Town had been made a month ago. Ding Wenxi had already prepared everything, packing up the items in Yaoyu Pavilion and leaving a note for Lin’s wife. She and Yu Wan quickly packed their essentials that night.

The next morning, Yu Wan and Ding Wenxi changed their appearances and, along with Wen Kuo, carried their valuables out the back door of Yaoyu Pavilion, avoiding prying eyes as they hurried to the docks.

The new boat Wen Kuo had bought was much larger than the previous one, with two spacious cabins. They had even hired a boatman to help.

Seeing the owners board, the boatman raised the anchor and rowed the boat out of the shipyard.

Qingsha Town was near the sea, so the waterways were wide, making it easy to sail. But just as the boat had left the shore, a long, loud whinny from a horse on the shore made Yu Wan look up involuntarily.

---

chapters.title: Heartfelt Words
chapters.content:
She saw Pei Ta standing on the shore, riding his horse against the wind, his features as smooth as jade, his expression calm and serene.

How did he get here?

Yu Wan’s heartbeat unconsciously quickened, but it wasn’t from nervousness or fear.

The boat was sailing against the current but with the wind, and the moment their eyes met, the boat suddenly picked up speed.

Pei Ta on the shore frowned slightly but tightened his grip on the reins, urging his white horse forward along the riverbank. His usually calm and cold eyes now showed a hint of urgency.

"Wanwan, don’t stand outside in the wind," Ding Wenxi said, seeing that Yu Wan wasn’t entering the cabin. She stepped out and saw the shocking scene.

The boat moved with the wind, and Pei Ta on the shore spurred his horse to chase after it.

"How... how did he get here?"

Yu Wan glanced at Wen Kuo.

Wen Kuo shook his head.

He certainly wanted Yu Wan to be happy, but since she had decided not to see Pei Ta, how could he go against her wishes and inform him?

Yu Wan looked back at Pei Ta on the shore, biting her lip tightly.

She didn’t have time to think about how Pei Ta had learned of her whereabouts. All she knew was that he had come to chase after her.

Her eyes, bright and flowing like water, were filled with surprise, but an unexpected joy surged in her heart.

She looked at Pei Ta, who seemed to have descended from the heavens, and smiled brilliantly.

"Wen Kuo, help me."

Yu Wan called out softly. Wen Kuo already understood. In an instant, he smiled slightly, reached out, and swept Yu Wan into his arms. Amid Ding Wenxi’s exclamation, he carried Yu Wan like a bird skimming over the water’s surface and steadily set her down on the shore.

Seeing this, Pei Ta pulled hard on the reins, stopping his horse, then dismounted and quickly walked toward Yu Wan.

Yu Wan watched him getting closer and closer. Without thinking, she threw herself into his arms.

Pei Ta’s tense expression relaxed instantly. Holding Yu Wan in his arms, joy surged through his heart like a tidal wave.

He hadn’t been wrong.

Yu Wan thought the same as he did; she just had too many concerns, too many hardships.

He paid no mind to Wen Kuo beside them, only holding Yu Wan tightly in his arms.

Yu Wan’s heart was also pounding. Pei Ta’s embrace felt somewhat unfamiliar, yet it made her feel at ease.

After their emotions had settled somewhat, they loosened their hold a little.

Pei Ta looked down at Yu Wan and couldn’t help but laugh.

It turned out that before leaving this morning, Yu Wan had asked Wen Kuo to help her disguise herself. Not only had she darkened her face, but she had also stuck a mole on her cheek. From afar, the changes weren’t noticeable, but up close, she looked quite different.

Yu Wan met his amused gaze and, feeling a little embarrassed, stepped back from his embrace and scraped the mole off her face.

She didn’t like wearing human-skin masks. Wen Kuo had said that a face with a mole was easier to remember, so when others asked about her, people with moles would be the first to be ruled out. That’s why she had stuck on the mole.

"Is it very ugly?" Yu Wan asked softly.

She had carefully prepared this disguise to escape, yet he had seen through it.

Pei Ta saw her retreat and took a step forward. "Of course not," he said softly.

Even with this disguise, though it concealed her beauty, in his eyes, she still looked charming.

Yu Wan’s emotions had already calmed down. Thinking about how she had impulsively thrown herself into Pei Ta’s arms just now, she deeply regretted it.

But since she had already done it, she couldn’t go back to speaking harshly to Pei Ta as she had before.

"I..." Yu Wan stammered a few times, then decided not to talk about herself. Instead, she asked him, "How did you get here?"

Pei Ta’s eyes were filled with tender warmth. "When you chased me away yesterday, I already decided to come back today."

"But you’re the magistrate of Qingzhou City. How can you keep coming here?"

"That’s why I came so early. And because I came so early, I happened to catch you trying to leave secretly."

Yu Wan lowered her head, saying nothing.

She really didn’t know what to say.

She had made up her mind not to see him again, yet fate had brought them together once more.

The image of Pei Ta riding along the shore, chasing after the boat, lingered in her mind, temporarily robbing her of the ability to think rationally.

"I didn’t want to cause you trouble."

Seeing Yu Wan’s downcast eyes, Pei Ta sighed softly. "Yu Wan, I don’t want to cause you trouble either."

Yu Wan’s heart stirred, but she couldn’t freely express her emotions.

"I really... really can’t..."

Her mother was a palace maid who had escaped from the imperial palace, Wen Kuo was a secret guard who had escaped from the Eastern Palace, and she was a maidservant who had escaped from a marquis’s mansion.

None of them could afford to be discovered.

"Yu Wan," Pei Ta paused slightly, "I know. You never want to return to the capital, and you never want to see those people from the past again."

Yu Wan raised her eyebrows slightly, looking at him, waiting silently for him to continue.

"If you trust me, let me find a way, alright?"

Pei Ta’s voice was pleasant to hear, and he was so close. How could Yu Wan bring herself to refuse?

"How long will your solution take?"

Hearing her finally relent, Pei Ta smiled slightly. "A month. Is that alright?"

"Are you that certain?"

Pei Ta gave a soft "mm" in response. He reached out and took Yu Wan’s sleeve. "I’ve already received orders from the Ministry of Rites. I’ll be leaving Qingzhou soon. Once I return to the capital, they should be arranging a new position for me."

The Hong Man case had been handled brilliantly, and the Brocade Guards had played a significant role. Pei Ta had also made great contributions.

After the emperor read the case files, he thought that since Pei Ta had already been in Qingzhou for three years, he ordered the Ministry of Rites to summon him back to the capital.

"The emperor favors you. He’ll keep you in the capital."

"In the capital, there are those who want to keep me and those who want to send me far away. Yu Wan, I truly can’t guarantee everything, but I’ll do my best to go somewhere even farther than Qingzhou."

"But with your talent, isn’t staying in the capital the best way to make use of your abilities?"

Listening to Yu Wan’s concerns, Pei Ta’s gaze softened as it fell on her.

Today, she was dressed very plainly. Not only had she darkened her face, but she also wore no ornate hairpins or jade decorations. Yet to Pei Ta, Yu Wan had never been just about her beauty or stunning appearance.

She was so intelligent, thinking deeply and seeing far.

If she weren’t a woman, her scholarly achievements would not be inferior to his.

"Staying in the capital, with all its scheming and power struggles, would be a waste of my time. I’d rather be far from the capital, guarding one corner, and do some practical things for the people."

Yu Wan met his gaze and felt that his words came from the heart. She also smiled.

To her, as long as her family was by her side, anywhere would be fine.

Moreover, in the future, there would be one more person; Pei Ta.

Thirty li away from Qingzhou, in Ningzhou, two Brocade Guards who had stayed behind to handle the Hong Man case were taking statements from the imprisoned girls.

The girls rescued from Hong Man’s courtyard had suffered severe physical and mental trauma. So the magistrate had specially arranged a residence for them to recuperate. Only when their bodies and minds had recovered somewhat were they asked to recount their experiences, which the Brocade Guards recorded and had them sign.

So far, five or six women had finished giving their statements and been sent back.

And today, it was just Qiahe’s turn.

chapters.title: Waiting for You in Gusu
chapters.content:
Qiao He had not been in Ningzhou for long, so she had less to say than others.

The Brocade Guards quickly finished recording her testimony and presented it to her for her signature.

Qiao He signed as instructed, then looked up at the Brocade Guard in front of her and cautiously asked, "Officer, my family has already sold me. Could you... not send me back?"

"Hong Man has been arrested, and those indenture contracts are now void. You are not his servant, so naturally, you will be sent back home."

When her parents had tried to sell her before, Qiao He had begged and cried, but it had been to no avail.

She had no desire to return to that home; she would rather be bought by her master.

"Then when will you send me back?"

"There are still two women in Qingzhou whose testimonies haven't been recorded. We'll send you all back together once that's done."

"Yes." Qiao He slowly stood up.

Seeing her rise, the Brocade Guard quickly stopped her. "Wait."

Qiao He nervously said, "Officer, this commoner has already told you everything she knows."

"It's not about this case," the Brocade Guard explained, taking a portrait from the side. "Take a look. Have you seen this person before?"

Not long after the case at the Xingguo Duke's residence was closed three years ago, Zhao Xuanyou left the Brocade Guards and returned to the Mingchuan Guards. Meanwhile, Pan Xun, the captain he had promoted, was appointed as the Deputy Commander of the Brocade Guards.

Due to Pan Xun's competence and measured conduct, he quickly gained the emperor's favor and secured his position as Deputy Commander.

After that, Pan Xun distributed a portrait to his subordinates, ordering them to inquire about the whereabouts of the person in the portrait while handling cases in various places.

With orders from above, the subordinates naturally complied.

Even if they didn't know who the person in the portrait was or why they were searching for her, for the past three years, they had asked about her whenever they handled a case.

Qiao He looked up in confusion at the portrait.

The person in the painting was a young girl. She stood sideways by a low wall, wearing a delicate goose-yellow dress, holding a pair of scissors, trimming flowers and plants. But for some reason, she suddenly turned her head and smiled gently at the front, her eyebrows and eyes as beautiful as a painting, her figure graceful.

Seeing those familiar features, Qiao He was slightly startled.

The two Brocade Guards had only asked out of routine, but seeing Qiao He's reaction, they immediately became alert.

"Do you know her?"

The other party was from the Brocade Guards, and Qiao He was unsure why they were looking for her master.

Could her master be a fugitive?

Over the past three years as an apprentice at the Xiaoyu Pavilion, Qiao He had always been well taken care of by her master. She couldn't believe they were bad people.

While she was thinking about how to cover it up, the Brocade Guard suddenly slammed the table. "Speak quickly!"

Startled, Qiao He stammered, "I... I... think I've seen her."

"Where?"

"I can't remember."

Though the two Brocade Guards were not as skilled as Pan Xun, they had years of experience in handling cases and could easily tell that Qiao He was lying.

"Do you see that wall over there?"

Qiao He turned her head as the Brocade Guard indicated and saw the wall behind her, which was covered with strange and terrifying torture devices.

The Brocade Guard put on a stern front and coldly said, "If you don't confess honestly, those things on the wall will be used on you one by one until you remember."

Qiao He was so frightened by just the sight of them that her legs gave out, and she knelt down, repeatedly begging for mercy. "Officer, spare me! Please, spare me!"

"As long as you confess honestly, we can spare you. Now, where did you see the person in the portrait?"

"She... she is the eldest young lady of our Xiaoyu Pavilion."

Xiaoyu Pavilion?

The two Brocade Guards exchanged a glance. It seemed they would have to pay a visit to this eldest young lady of Xiaoyu Pavilion.

---

On the boat, Ding Wenxi ordered the boatmen to dock at the shore. Wen Mo saw her anxious expression and returned to the boat to inform her about Yu Wan's situation.

The grass was lush and green, and the spring scenery was beautiful. By the water, only Pei Ta and Yu Wan stood side by side.

Pei Ta, dressed in a green robe and a jade crown, was elegant and graceful. He looked at Yu Wan beside him and softly asked, "Where were you planning to go today?"

"I didn't have a specific destination in mind. Wherever the boat goes, I go."

"That is carefree. It makes one envious. Hearing that, I want to board the boat and travel with you."

"Then why don't you?" Yu Wan pursed her lips, a hidden sparkle in her eyes.

Pei Ta looked at her and smiled, but thinking about the road ahead, he said, "Have you already arranged everything for Xiaoyu Pavilion?"

Yu Wan hummed in agreement. "I sold it to the mistress of Xiangyu Workshop. The other things left in Qingsha Town were given to the artisans."

"So you still have to board the boat?"

Indeed.

The wind stirred their clothes. Yu Wan looked up at Pei Ta and softly said, "Yes."

"I will be going to the capital soon. If your whereabouts are uncertain, how will I find you?"

"You just said that there will be clarity in a month?"

Surrounded by the bright spring scenery, Yu Wan's thin spring dress revealed half of her collarbone, making her neck appear even more slender.

She stood by the water, her eyes shimmering, a beauty that even the clear river for ten miles could not compare to.

"Yes."

Pei Ta looked at her, but his heart was not at ease.

It would only take him ten days to ride from Qingzhou City to the capital. Once he entered the palace to see the emperor, the Ministry of Rites would be easy to handle.

Even though he now knew she had feelings for him, he was still uncertain about her decision to stay or leave.

Yu Wan was like a butterfly, gracefully flying into his arms, but she could also fly away at any moment.

"I will first take my mother and Ah Mo to travel around. In a month, I will go to Gusu for sightseeing. I think I will stay at Xiangyun Inn. If you have good news, come find me. If..."

The last time Wen Mo and Yu Wan went to Gusu City for business, they stayed at Xiangyun Inn. The inn was very elegant, with a spacious backyard and a beautiful Jiangnan garden. At that time, she had already decided to take her mother there again.

"Regardless, I will come find you."

Yu Wan lowered her gaze and softly said, "Okay."

Finally, she had given him an affirmative answer. Pei Ta was overjoyed, his eyes only on her gentle smile.

Yu Wan was indeed happy.

After so long of caution and restraint, she could finally act freely.

"I... I should go back to the boat. My mother must be worried."

"Should I go explain?"

"No need." Yu Wan tilted her head to look at him. "When you have definite news, Mother will naturally be happy for us."

She had said "us." Pei Ta nodded.

Their eyes were locked together. When Yu Wan felt her cheeks burning as if they were about to melt, she suddenly turned and walked toward the boat.

Seeing her leave, Pei Ta instinctively grabbed her wrist.

Yu Wan had just turned her head when she was suddenly pulled back into his arms.

The spring wind blew over the river, creating ripples on the water's surface.

"If you don't let go, my mother will really get angry."

Thinking that they would not see each other again for a month, even with his gentlemanly demeanor, Pei Ta could not bear to let go.

Yu Wan allowed him to hold her for a moment before pushing away the hand on her shoulder.

But she still held his palm.

Pei Ta's hand was not much wider than hers, but his fingers were longer.

Yu Wan squeezed his palm.

"Pei Ta, I will wait for you in Gusu."

---

chapters.title: The Best Fortune Stick
chapters.content:
"Wanwan, what on earth is going on!" As soon as Yu Wan returned to the boat, Ding Wenxi anxiously blocked her path. "How could you... Don't you know the principle of 'men and women should not touch each other'?"

Thinking of how Yu Wan had been held in Pei Ta's arms twice, Ding Wenxi was truly worried.

Yu Wan looked at Wen Mo, who slightly shook his head, indicating he had not said anything.

"Mother, don't worry."

"How can I not worry? We are about to leave, so why are you lingering with him?"

"We are leaving. Mo, tell the boatmen to continue."

Wen Mo glanced at Pei Ta on the shore, then looked uncertainly at Yu Wan. "Just leave like this?"

Yu Wan nodded, her eyes only on the man on the shore.

Seeing the clear smile in Yu Wan's eyes, Wen Mo couldn't understand her. Even though she and Pei Ta had exchanged feelings, why did she still want to leave?

But Yu Wan was the one in charge, so Wen Mo silently ordered the boatmen to weigh anchor and set off.

The boat slowly moved away from the shore. Pei Ta, on the shore, remounted his horse.

Yu Wan leaned on the railing, watching him. The branches of the willow trees swayed in the wind, intermittently blocking their line of sight.

Pei Ta, as before, rode his horse alongside the boat. Yu Wan watched him, her fingers tightly gripping the railing.

Even though these years had been difficult, with every step carefully planned, at this moment, with the spring breeze and clear skies, it was enough to make her heart rejoice.

"How long does he plan to follow us?" Wen Mo walked up to Yu Wan and muttered under his breath.

Yu Wan shot him a sidelong glance, and he obediently fell silent.

Soon, the river forked, and the boat entered the wider branch. Pei Ta could no longer follow and had to stand on the shore, watching Yu Wan's figure grow farther and farther away.

"Wanwan."

Hearing Ding Wenxi's angry voice, Yu Wan knew she had gone too far today.

Since Pei Ta was no longer in sight, Yu Wan turned around and, in a coaxing manner, took Ding Wenxi's hand.

"Mother, let me explain."

Ding Wenxi, with a stern face, said, "I really want to hear how you explain this."

Yu Wan took her hand and led her into the cabin. After helping her sit down, she stood beside her, massaging her shoulders.

"It's just..."

"Because he is handsome, you have a crush on him?"

"Isn't being handsome enough?" Yu Wan joked, but seeing that Ding Wenxi was not in the mood for jokes, she soon seriously said, "Mother, Pei Ta likes me, and I like him. That's all."

Hearing Yu Wan change to calling him "Pei Ta," which sounded so intimate, Ding Wenxi sighed. "But you finally managed to leave the capital. Why would you want to tie yourself to him? If you were willing to be a concubine, you could have stayed in the Marquis's mansion. Why go through all that trouble to leave the capital?"

At that time, the reason for leaving the capital was also because of her mother's identity.

But Yu Wan only dared to think this in her heart and did not dare to say it aloud.

Her mother was also concerned about her, which was why she was so upset.

"Who said Pei Ta wants me to be his concubine?"

"Then does he not even want you as a concubine? Does he just want to have a fleeting affair with you?"

Seeing Ding Wenxi's furious expression, Yu Wan patted her back to soothe her. "Don't overthink it. What fleeting affair? Pei Ta would never think that way! He said he wants to marry me."

As soon as these words were spoken, Yu Wan clearly felt Ding Wenxi's eyebrows twitch, and her expression changed several times in an instant.

This news was too sudden for her. She stared at Yu Wan for a moment.

"Did he tell you this today?"

That didn't make sense. Clearly, before their conversation, Yu Wan had already thrown herself into his arms.

"No, he told me yesterday when he came to Qingsha Town."

Ding Wenxi was silent for a long time, considering the pros and cons, and her anxious expression finally turned to joy.

She suddenly grabbed Yu Wan's hand and reproached her. "How could you not tell me about such a big matter?"

"We had already decided to leave Qingsha Town. Telling you wouldn't have changed anything."

"How could it be the same?" Ding Wenxi urgently said, "We have lived in Qingzhou for three years. Instead of being the boss of a jewelry shop, you could be the wife of a prefect!"

Yu Wan's past injury and illness, which had led her to become a maid in the Marquis's mansion, had always been a sore point for Ding Wenxi.

Her previously pure body had been given to Zhao Xuanyou. Now that she had left him, it would be difficult for her to remarry.

But Pei Ta had been married before, so he probably did not place as much importance on a woman's chastity as an unmarried man would.

His visit to Qingsha Town yesterday had shown his sincerity, and today he had ridden his horse to chase after their boat, which showed that he truly liked Yu Wan.

In Ding Wenxi's eyes, Yu Wan was naturally perfect and deserved to be cherished.

"Stop the boat. Tell Ah Mo to stop the boat immediately." Ding Wenxi said.

Seeing her mother's expression, Yu Wan couldn't help but smile. She sat down next to her and hugged her arm.

"Why stop? We agreed to take you to Jiangnan for a tour."

"Your marriage is more important. What is there to tour? Hurry and order the boat to stop."

"Mother," Yu Wan smiled, "Pei Ta will return to the capital in a few days. He has achieved great merit in this case, so he probably won't stay in Qingzhou any longer."

Hearing this, Ding Wenxi became worried again. "He is a top scholar. After years of training outside, the emperor will likely keep him in the capital. We can't return to the capital, so how do you and he plan to handle this?"

Seeing Ding Wenxi so anxious about her marriage, Yu Wan realized that if she didn't explain everything, her mother might keep overthinking.

"Pei Ta said he dislikes the scheming in the capital and would rather be a local official. He will try his best to arrange this when he goes to the capital."

If he succeeded, he would go to another place to be an official, and Yu Wan marrying him would indeed allow her to live a peaceful life.

But if he failed... Ding Wenxi looked at Yu Wan with concern.

Yu Wan smiled calmly. "In a month, I will wait for him in Gusu. If he keeps his promise and becomes a local official, I will follow him to his post. If he becomes a capital official again, then we are fated to be apart."

Ding Wenxi opened her mouth in surprise.

"Then isn't everything still uncertain?"

Yu Wan did not feel sad. "At least, I understand his intentions now."

Today, by the river, she had cast aside all her worries and acted freely. Even if she and Pei Ta couldn't be together in the future, she would not regret it.

Ding Wenxi looked at Yu Wan's bright and beautiful eyes, and her own expression softened.

"Wanwan, do you really like him that much?"

Yu Wan smiled and tilted her head to rest on Ding Wenxi's shoulder, jokingly saying, "Didn't you say it yourself? Pei Ta is handsome, and his voice is pleasant."

"Only that?"

Of course not only that.

"Pei Ta... apart from you, no, apart from you and Wen Mo, Pei Ta is the only one in this world who thinks I am clever and capable."

Ding Wenxi laughed. "Is that so?"

Yu Wan nodded very seriously.

Pei Ta always appreciated her, thought she was good, and thought she was amazing. When she was with him, Yu Wan truly felt clever and capable.

Looking at the light in Yu Wan's eyes, Ding Wenxi sighed softly.

She had heard that Hanshan Temple in Gusu was very spiritual. When they arrived in Gusu, she would definitely draw a fortune stick for them and pray for the best possible outcome.

chapters.title: Returning to the Old Land
chapters.content:
Pei Ta ceased his horse and returned to the government office, where the Lu brothers came forward to greet him.

"Another case?"

Lu Jie cupped his hands and replied, "The patrol officers just reported that two Brocade Guards have entered Qingzhou territory."

Pei Ta pondered briefly, thinking they might be here for the Hong Man case, and asked, "Have they brought back the girls sold to Ningzhou?"

"Yes, there is a girl with them, but they didn't hand her over to the government office. Instead, they took her directly to Qingsha Town."

"Qingsha Town?" That was not good.

In the Hong Man case, Qiao He from Qingsha Town had been sold to Ningzhou. Qiao He had worked at the Jade Pavilion.

Seeing Pei Ta's brows furrow instantly, Lu Cheng beside him asked, "Sir, is something amiss? Should we go and investigate immediately?"

As Pei Ta's subordinates, they knew he had been to Qingsha Town for two consecutive days.

Although they were unclear about the relationship between Pei Ta and Miss Ding Yuan, they assumed it was significant.

Pei Ta hesitated for a moment before saying softly, "No need to ask. Just pretend you know nothing. If you encounter them again, ask when they will bring back the other girls from Qingzhou."

He didn't quite understand why the Brocade Guards were still helping Zhao Xuanyou search for Yu Yuan, but since the Brocade Guards had already learned the truth from Qiao He, it wouldn't be difficult for them to discover that Yu Yuan had lived in Qingsha Town for three years.

Now that things had come to this, the fact that Yu Yuan was hiding in Qingsha Town could no longer be concealed.

If the Brocade Guards went to Qingsha Town first, and he sent someone to cover it up immediately afterward, it would seem too deliberate.

It was better to feign ignorance. After all, he genuinely didn't know Yu Yuan was in Qingsha Town.

Compared to this matter, another issue was more urgent.

"You two go to Wenshan Dock immediately."

"May I ask what Sir wants us to investigate?"

Pei Ta thought for a moment, recalling that besides the three of them, Yu Yuan's ship had also hired sailors. He then said, "This morning, Ding Yuan's family left by ship from Wenshan Dock. Their ship should have been docked there for some time. When you arrive at Wenshan Dock, remind them as necessary. If there are any records of ship transactions or movements, erase them all."

Zhao Xuanyou already knew Yu Yuan was alive. As long as Yu Yuan was far away from Qingsha Town, there would be no problem.

However, Yu Yuan had lived in Qingzhou for three years, and he was the magistrate of Qingzhou. This was an accident. If Zhao Xuanyou learned of this, he might not consider it an accident. Some arrangements still needed to be made.

"Miss Ding and her family have left?" Lu Jie asked in surprise.

But as soon as the words left his mouth, seeing that Pei Ta did not wish to say more, he quickly cupped his hands and said "Yes," then left swiftly.

Fortunately, Yu Yuan's family had left today, just in time to avoid the Brocade Guards.

When the Brocade Guards arrived in Qingsha Town and couldn't find Yu Yuan, they probably wouldn't be able to confirm immediately that she was the person Zhao Xuanyou was looking for. It would take a few days, which would give the Lu brothers enough time to go to the dock and handle the traces of Yu Yuan's departure by ship.

Pei Ta quickly entered the government office and ordered someone to invite the Deputy Governor and the Prefect of Qingzhou.

He was about to leave for the capital and would be transferred away from Qingzhou. There would be a vacancy for the magistrate of Qingzhou for two or three months. Before leaving, Pei Ta had to distribute and hand over all affairs clearly.

From the beginning when he came to Qingzhou, he knew he wouldn't stay long, but he had never treated the position of Qingzhou magistrate as a stepping stone. Instead, he always kept his duties in mind.

The Deputy Governor and the Prefect naturally understood that Pei Ta's trip to the capital this time meant he would not return. After offering their congratulations, they also accepted Pei Ta's distribution and handover of tasks one by one.

After handling these matters, Pei Ta began to take stock of his personal belongings in the government office, having Xique pack and seal them one by one, to be sent to him later when his transfer order arrived.

At dusk, the Lu brothers, Lu Cheng and Lu Jie, returned and reported that everything at the dock had been handled properly.

Pei Ta had a high reputation in Qingzhou, and the people at the dock naturally obeyed his orders.

After arranging all the matters in Qingzhou, Pei Ta did not inquire further about the Brocade Guards' search for the person. He took a few trusted followers and returned to the capital.

When he married Sun Qianran, Pei Ta had purchased a small residence in the south of the capital. However, the place was not spacious enough, and Sun Qianran had advised him to move to a larger mansion that was part of her dowry.

By the time they separated, Pei Ta had naturally returned all her dowry items. He had originally thought of living there again, but soon received a transfer order to Qingzhou.

He first went to the Ministry of Rites to register, then took his subordinates back to the small residence, where he simply tidied up the inside and outside.

After waiting at home for five days, someone from the palace arrived, saying the Emperor had summoned him.

Pei Ta changed his clothes and immediately followed the eunuch into the palace. He had originally thought they would talk in the imperial study as before, but the eunuch led him directly to the edge of the Phoenix Pond.

The Emperor had ordered a stage to be set up here, where they could enjoy songs and dances, or listen to operas.

Today, not only was the Emperor listening to the opera, but the Crown Prince and several other sons were also present to accompany him.

Since the Emperor's opera was only halfway through, the eunuch did not dare to approach and disturb, leading Pei Ta to wait aside.

Pei Ta originally looked straight ahead, waiting quietly, but he felt a gaze fall upon him.

He looked up and saw that it was Zhao Qi looking at him.

When he had given lectures to Zhao Qi at the imperial palace, they had gotten along quite well. Additionally, their relationship had grown closer after the trip to Heishui.

However, not long after returning to the capital, Zhao Qi had followed the Ningguo Duke's heir to the southeast, and Pei Ta had gone to Qingzhou. It had been three years since they last met.

The once sharp and youthful boy had grown up, sitting slightly taller than the Crown Prince beside him.

Pei Ta smiled at Zhao Qi, who nodded in greeting.

When the song on the stage finished, the eunuch finally stepped forward to announce Pei Ta.

"Bring him over."

Pei Ta followed the eunuch to the Emperor's presence. "Your subject Pei Ta greets Your Majesty. May Your Majesty live forever."

The Emperor's gaze lingered on Pei Ta for a moment before he smiled and said, "Today, I ordered a painter to capture the beautiful scenery of this Phoenix Pond. I remember your calligraphy is quite good, so you can inscribe it."

"Yes."

After Pei Ta responded, the eunuchs quickly brought over a table and laid out the painting the Emperor had mentioned.

The painting depicted the Emperor leading his sons as they enjoyed songs and dances by the Phoenix Pond.

Pei Ta picked up the brush and quickly finished the inscription, presenting it to the Emperor.

"Come and see how Pei Ta's inscription turned out."

Since the Crown Prince was present, it was natural for him to speak first.

Although he was displeased with Pei Ta over the Heishui County incident, he could see that the Emperor was in high spirits today and naturally would not say anything to dampen the mood. He simply praised Pei Ta's calligraphy.

The other three princes naturally did the same, but Zhao Qi stared at the calligraphy in silence.

The Emperor noticed his silence and asked, "Qi'er, what do you think?"

Startled by being called upon, Zhao Qi retrieved his thoughts and softly said, "Your son thinks similarly to the Crown Prince."

Pei Ta's calligraphy was indeed excellent.

Zhao Qi remembered that Yu Yuan had copied Pei Ta's handwriting. The letter she had left him three years ago was written in this very style.

---

chapters.title: Wish Fulfilled
chapters.content:
Ever since Yu Yuan disappeared, Zhao Qi had carried that letter with him, often taking it out to read.

So when he saw Pei Ta's inscription, he immediately thought of her again.

Yu Yuan...

Where on earth have you gone...

The Emperor noticed Zhao Qi's distraction again and thought he simply didn't enjoy the opera, hence his mind wandered.

He had always doted on Zhao Qi the most. After three years of training outside, Zhao Qi had grown taller and thinner. He had heard that his martial arts had greatly improved. It was rare for him to return to the capital, so the Emperor naturally wouldn't reprimand him for such a small matter.

Thus, he didn't order another opera but instead had musicians perform some refined and elegant music.

"The case of Hong Man has been almost concluded by the Brocade Guards. Although it happened in Ningzhou, it was you, the magistrate of Qingzhou, who uncovered it. You have made a great contribution."

Seeing the Emperor praising Pei Ta again, the Crown Prince had no choice but to follow suit. "Lord Pei has governed Qingzhou for three years. Apart from the Hong Man case, he has handled all other matters extremely well. I hear the local people even call him 'Pei Qingtian'!"

"Is that so?"

Pei Ta cupped his hands towards the Emperor. "The people of Qingzhou can live in peace and prosperity thanks to the Emperor's grace. As an official appointed by the court, it is my duty, and I dare not take credit."

These words were well-spoken, and the Emperor was naturally delighted.

"It is your achievement, and you deserve the credit. You have been in Qingzhou for three years; it's about time you moved to another place."

With these words, everyone present understood that Pei Ta would soon return to the capital.

Prince Ping spoke first. "Father Emperor, I recall there is a vacancy for an Assistant Minister in the Ministry of Justice. Lord Pei is highly educated, talented, upright, and hates evil. He would be very suitable for the Ministry of Justice."

The Crown Prince heard this and coldly scoffed.

Everyone could see that the Emperor favored Pei Ta, and it was clear that the Emperor intended to promote Pei Ta. Prince Ping had jumped at the chance to speak up.

Pei Ta was currently a fourth-rank prefect. An Assistant Minister in the Ministry of Justice was a third-rank official. After three years of service outside the capital and with the merit of solving the Hong Man case, it was reasonable for him to go to the Ministry of Justice.

The Crown Prince was seething inside, guessing that the Emperor would surely agree.

Once Pei Ta became the Assistant Minister of Justice, he would certainly owe Prince Ping a favor, making it easier for Prince Ping to act within the Ministry of Justice in the future.

The Emperor, hearing Prince Ping's words, indeed felt that the position of Assistant Minister of Justice was quite suitable for Pei Ta.

Pei Ta observed the Emperor's expression, and an image of Yu Yuan's beautiful face flashed through his mind. His gaze unconsciously tightened.

The Emperor did indeed intend to keep him in the capital. Success or failure depended on this moment.

Pei Ta cupped his hands towards Prince Ping. "Your Highness overpraises me. The capture of Hong Man was actually the Brocade Guards' achievement. He had been embezzling money for a long time, and the Brocade Guards had been watching him. Since the case happened in Ningzhou, and I was investigating other cases, I really dare not take credit from the Brocade Guards and the Ningzhou prefect."

Prince Ping had intended to do Pei Ta a favor, but he hadn't expected Pei Ta to suddenly become modest, leaving Prince Ping at a loss.

The Emperor, however, understood the implication in Pei Ta's words.

"You don't want to go to the Ministry of Justice?"

Seeing the Emperor's direct question, Pei Ta lowered his head. "I am merely a scholar who has read too many books and has a rigid mind. I fear I cannot handle the affairs of the Ministry of Justice. I beg Your Majesty to see clearly."

"What do you want then?"

Hearing the Emperor's question, Pei Ta didn't react much, but the Crown Prince coldly smiled in his heart. The Emperor truly did not hide his favoritism towards Pei Ta at all.

Pei Ta said, "I wish to stay in Qingzhou and continue to do some things for the people there."

The Emperor was in a good mood today and spoke kindly to him, clearly intending to promote him.

Pei Ta had already reached the highest position in Qingzhou. To be promoted further, he would have to be transferred elsewhere.

"It seems Lord Pei has his heart set on traveling the land and doesn't wish to stay in the capital," the Crown Prince said opportunely.

Among those present, he was the only one who didn't want Pei Ta to stay in the capital. Seeing that Prince Ping's suggestion had been rejected by Pei Ta, he felt a surge of joy.

"What position do you think is suitable for him?" the Emperor asked gravely.

"The Prince has lofty aspirations and is incorruptible. If he were to govern a region, he would certainly be a good parental official. I recall that the position of Provincial Inspector in Western Shu is currently vacant. Lord Pei could fill that vacancy."

The Provincial Inspector was a third-rank official, which was indeed a promotion.

However, Western Shu Province was thousands of miles away from the capital, a place where the Emperor's influence was distant. If Pei Ta went there, it would be at least three to five years before he returned to the capital.

If you can't eliminate someone you dislike, the next best thing is to send them as far away as possible.

The Crown Prince had his own calculations for expelling Pei Ta, but he didn't expect Pei Ta to be overjoyed upon hearing his words.

Western Shu was far from the capital. Once he and Yu Yuan went there, they might never see the people in the capital again.

As the Provincial Inspector of Western Shu, he would be able to ensure that Yu Yuan didn't suffer any grievances by his side.

Afraid that the Emperor might say something else, Pei Ta knelt before the Emperor and said solemnly, "I am willing to go to Western Shu and share Your Majesty's burdens."

The Emperor had intended to promote Pei Ta, but his original intention was to keep him in the capital.

He perceived the Crown Prince's underlying intent to eliminate potential rivals and had intended to settle the matter by appointing Pei Ta to the Ministry of Justice.

Unexpectedly, Pei Ta immediately knelt down to express his gratitude.

"You truly wish to go to Western Shu?"

"Yes. When I was studying, I was already captivated by the beautiful scenery of Western Shu as described by the Immortal Poet. If I can go to Western Shu to serve Your Majesty, it would be killing two birds with one stone."

Today's events were indeed somewhat unexpected for the Emperor.

He frowned in thought, "We will discuss this matter later. For now, let us enjoy the music and dance."

With the Emperor's words, neither the Crown Prince nor Pei Ta dared to speak further.

After listening to three songs, the Emperor finally showed signs of fatigue and ordered the procession to return to the palace.

"Your son bids farewell to Father Emperor."

Once the imperial carriage was far away, the Crown Prince glanced at Prince Ping with some satisfaction.

Over the past three years, the Emperor had increasingly relied on Prince Ping for state affairs, entrusting him with many tasks. He, the Crown Prince, had become somewhat of a figurehead.

Today, Prince Ping had been publicly embarrassed by Pei Ta, which truly pleased the Crown Prince. Consequently, his gaze towards Pei Ta also softened a bit.

"The position of Provincial Inspector in Western Shu is not bad. When the cabinet discusses this again, I will speak on your behalf."

"Your subject thanks His Highness, the Crown Prince, for his grace."

The Crown Prince nodded satisfactorily and left. Prince Ping, having been slighted by Pei Ta, felt uneasy and left without a word, taking his two brothers with him.

Only Zhao Qi remained standing in place.

"Lord Pei, it's been a long time."

"Your subject wishes the Prince good health."

Although Zhao Qi didn't care where Pei Ta was going, he found the earlier scene somewhat strange.

"Zhao Zun didn't have good intentions. Why did you go along with what he said?"

"I believe Your Highness misunderstood. I was not following the Crown Prince's words. What I said before the Emperor were my true feelings," Pei Ta understood Zhao Qi's good intentions and said warmly, "These three years away from the capital have been very relaxing for me. I truly do not wish to return to the capital."

"Do you not want to see those people named Sun?"

Pei Ta's eyebrows twitched slightly. He hadn't considered this, but if others thought so, it wouldn't be a bad thing.

"Some places, some people, are indeed better out of sight, out of mind."

Zhao Qi listened to his words and suddenly seemed lost in thought.

Out of sight, out of mind... Yu Yuan had hidden so far away. Who was it that she didn't want to see?

chapters.title: Each with Their Own Thoughts
chapters.content:
Pei Tao could tell there was a hidden meaning in his words.

However, he was unaware that Yu Ying had left the capital with Zhao Qi’s help back then, so he naturally couldn’t guess what Zhao Qi was thinking.

“Your Highness has been away for three years. Now that you’ve returned to the capital, do you, like me, feel a little out of place?”

“Not out of place. I was never familiar with it to begin with.”

Zhao Qi had grown up in the imperial palace, but his siblings were all cold and distant. The only people he cared about there were his father, the Emperor, and his maternal grandfather. Everyone else annoyed him just by looking at them.

But his father was not his father alone, and his maternal grandfather was not his grandfather alone.

To Zhao Qi, the most gentle thing in the capital was the sea of lights he had seen with Yu Ying that night when they climbed the city walls together.

Pei Tao listened to this and felt a slight pang of emotion.

After three years apart, Zhao Qi had grown taller, his skin a bit darker, and though his eyes still carried the noble pride of a prince, his brows now held a touch of stern resolve. He spoke with much more composure than before.

“Your Highness must be returning to the capital to be enfeoffed as a prince and establish your own estate. Allow me to congratulate you in advance.”

The Sixth Prince had already been enfeoffed and moved out of the palace last year. The Emperor had summoned Zhao Qi back, so this was indeed the intention.

But it was more than that.

In addition to being enfeoffed and granted an estate, the Emperor intended to select a princess consort for him.

These past few days, palace banquets had been held continuously, and noble ladies from the capital, around the same age as Zhao Qi, had been streaming into the palace like flowing water; clearly the Emperor’s arrangement.

Those women were all beautiful, each with their own charms, but they annoyed him just by looking at them.

Pei Tao saw Zhao Qi’s expression darken and wondered which of his words had touched a nerve.

Just as he was considering changing the subject, Zhao Qi suddenly asked, “Minister Pei, you are a married man. If you were to marry someone you dislike, how would that feel?”

Pei Tao had met Sun Qianran before their marriage, but it was practically a blind union.

After he passed the imperial examination as the top scholar, many high-ranking families in the capital had offered their daughters for him to choose from. It was his teacher from the academy who told him that Prime Minister Sun also intended to take him as a son-in-law.

The teacher said that Prime Minister Sun had once exerted great effort to help his father escape punishment, so he should repay the kindness.

Pei Tao naturally understood the reasoning behind his teacher’s words, so he went to propose marriage and wed Sun Qianran.

Though Sun Qianran was frail, she was gentle, kind, learned, and intelligent. Gradually, Pei Tao came to like her.

Even after he learned that Prime Minister Sun was not a righteous benefactor but a corrupt official in cahoots with Cui Lingyuan, he still did his best to maintain the facade of a good father-in-law and son-in-law relationship for Sun Qianran’s sake. After all, Sun Congdao was Sun Congdao, and Sun Qianran was Sun Qianran.

Unfortunately, it had all been his own wishful thinking.

“If you marry someone you dislike, you’ll find their face detestable, feel disgust at the sight of them, and every moment will feel like a fishbone stuck in your throat, like swallowing a knife that scrapes your insides.”

“So, Minister Pei, are you saying one must marry someone they like?”

“I believe so.” Seeing that Zhao Qi was deep in thought, and knowing that his own audience with the Emperor had gone well, Pei Tao said, “It’s rare to see Your Highness. If you’re also leaving the palace, why not join me for a drink at the Bright Moon Pavilion?”

“I am leaving the palace, but I won’t be going to the Bright Moon Pavilion.”

Zhao Qi had returned to the capital only three days earlier than Pei Tao. Because the Emperor missed him, he had been keeping the Emperor company until today, when the Emperor finally allowed him to leave the palace for some leisure.

He planned to first visit his maternal grandfather at the Ningguo Duke’s residence, then go see his cousin, Shen Hongyun.

Three years ago, the heir of the Xingguo Duke’s household had been imprisoned and died for embezzling tribute pearls. The entire Cui clan had been demoted to commoner status. Fortunately, his maternal grandfather had pleaded with court officials repeatedly, sparing the rest of the Cui family from exile.

After Cui Zaizhou’s death, Shen Hongyun had given birth to a posthumous child and was living with the child and the rest of the Cui family in a humble alley in the capital.

His uncle in the military often mentioned Shen Hongyun with deep regret, blaming himself for not finding her a good husband and letting her suffer such misfortune so soon after marriage.

Now that Zhao Qi had returned to the capital, he naturally wanted to go see her.

He had heard that Shen Hongyun, fearing her guilty status would implicate her maternal family, had refused any financial support from them. As a prince, Zhao Qi had no such concerns and would help however he could.

Family matters were not to be discussed with outsiders, so Zhao Qi didn’t elaborate to Pei Tao. Instead, he asked, “Has Minister Pei been in Qingzhou for these three years?”

“Yes. Like Your Highness, I’ve been by the sea. I heard that last year, Your Highness personally led troops to eliminate a group of pirates who had been harassing fishermen for years. Truly admirable.”

Zhao Qi’s gaze darkened slightly.

He had left the capital to train for Yu Ying’s sake. Unfortunately, she would never know about his achievements in the military.

Seeing Zhao Qi’s distraction, Pei Tao decided not to say more and simply walked out of the palace with him.

Just as they were about to exit the palace gates, Zhao Qi suddenly said, “Did you know that Zhao Xuanyou is returning to the capital?”

Pei Tao indeed did not.

Was Zhao Xuanyou’s return related to the Brocade Guards’ discovery in Qingsha Town?

It probably was. If he had truly let go of Yu Ying, why would the Brocade Guards still be secretly searching for her?

“I did not. Speaking of which, the Prince’s departure from the capital was quite sudden. I heard he had committed some offense.”
