Recalling that Zhao Xuanyou had lost control and beaten someone at the Xingguo Duke’s residence because of Yu Ying’s incident, Zhao Qi curled his lip.

What was so great about that? If he found out someone had harmed Yu Ying, he would do the same.

No, he would do far more, far more ruthlessly.

“A high-ranking official like the Commander of the Brocade Guards, acting so impulsively and publicly beating an unsentenced court official; such disregard for human life. The Emperor could not have allowed him to stay in the capital.”

“That’s true,” Pei Tao agreed faintly, though his heart was uneasy. Zhao Xuanyou was meticulous, and with the Brocade Guards’ assistance, it wouldn’t be easy to hide Yu Ying’s whereabouts from him.

After a moment’s thought, Pei Tao probed, “If His Majesty summons him back to the capital, it must be for another important task.”

A general could not leave his post without imperial orders. Doing so would be considered treason.

“Probably,” Zhao Qi replied. He had only overheard this in the imperial study and didn’t know the details. He exhaled heavily. “Do you still remember the days we spent together in Heishui County?”

“I do, of course. Heishui County was poor, but those days were carefree.”

“Indeed, carefree. Now you, I, and Zhao Xuanyou can still meet, but who knows when we’ll see Yu Ying again.”

Pei Tao was somewhat surprised by his words.

He remembered that Zhao Qi had been rather attached to Yu Ying back then, but Zhao Qi was usually indifferent to others, whether they were palace servants or even the Crown Prince and princesses.

He just hadn’t expected Zhao Qi to still be thinking of Yu Ying.

For some reason, hearing Zhao Qi mention Yu Ying in such a tone made Pei Tao feel a pang of discomfort.

He could only feign ignorance. “Does Your Highness know what exactly happened to Miss Yu Ying three years ago?”

“She disappeared. But she’s always been lucky; she’s probably still alive.”

Not only alive, but living well.

Zhao Qi still remembered the last time he saw her in Yangzhou, if only he hadn’t left then.

He had said this to spare Pei Tao, who had once cared for Yu Ying, from heartache. But to Pei Tao, it took on another meaning; he thought Zhao Qi was missing Yu Ying and wishing her well.

“Miss Yu Ying always turned misfortune into fortune in the past. This time should be no different.”

“Mm.”

Each lost in their own thoughts, they parted ways once they stepped out of the palace gates.

---

chapters.title: As Wished
chapters.content:
Upon returning to his residence, Pei Tao called for the Lu Cheng brothers.

Zhao Xuanyou’s return to the capital was too much of a coincidence. He didn’t know if it was the Emperor’s summons or Zhao Xuanyou’s own intention, but regardless, since he was still searching for Yu Ying, precautions were necessary.

“Lu Cheng, you will leave for Suzhou immediately.”

“May I ask what orders you have, my lord?”

“In twenty days, Miss Ding Ying will arrive at the Xiangyun Inn in Gusu City. Go there first, wait for her, and tell her…”

Lu Cheng saw Pei Tao hesitate, his gaze fixed on him, unsure what he was struggling with.

Pei Tao had not wanted to bring up Zhao Xuanyou in front of Yu Ying.

But since Zhao Xuanyou was still searching for her and had already discovered her past presence in Qingsha Town, she needed to be warned to take precautions.

If Yu Ying still harbored feelings for Zhao Xuanyou, that was beyond his control.

“Tell her that the Prince has been looking for her. He followed the lead from Qiahe all the way to Qingsha Town. I’ve already covered our tracks at the dock, so he won’t be able to find her there for now. You stay in Gusu and protect her until you hear from me.”

Lu Cheng didn’t know who the Prince was, but since Pei Tao had given the order, he accepted without question. He disguised himself and left the capital immediately.

For the next seven days, nothing happened.

Pei Tao spent most of his time at home waiting for news from the Ministry of Rites, occasionally going out to dine with old classmates.

On the eighth day, another message arrived from the palace: the Emperor had summoned Pei Tao to attend him in the imperial study.

Lately, the Emperor had taken a great interest in calligraphy and paintings. Many high-ranking officials had already been invited to the imperial study to appreciate them.

After listening to the old officials’ long-winded discussions, the Emperor wanted to hear the opinions of younger people. Last year’s imperial examinations had produced a good batch of new scholars, but compared to Pei Tao, they still fell short. Since Pei Tao was in the capital, the Emperor called for him.

Pei Tao waited outside the imperial study for a while before Prince Ping walked out.

“Your Highness,” Pei Tao greeted with a bow.

Though Prince Ping still held some resentment over Pei Tao’s refusal of the position of Assistant Minister of Justice, his expression remained courteous.

“The Emperor has just acquired three landscape paintings by Shi Zhi’ao and is admiring them. I suppose he wants to hear Minister Pei’s insights.”

Shi Zhi’ao was a famous painter from the previous dynasty, known for his elegant and refined style.

“Thank you for the guidance, Your Highness.”

Prince Ping gave a slight nod and left.

Pei Tao watched Prince Ping’s retreating figure.

In the three years he had been away from the capital, many changes had taken place.

The Emperor had grown to rely even more on Prince Ping, entrusting him with many important state affairs. Many officials in the court now held Prince Ping in high esteem.

On the other hand, the Crown Prince’s strongest supporter, the Zhen Guo Duke, had fallen off his horse during a military drill last year and was still recovering at home. People were whispering that the Emperor intended to transfer command of the Tiger Guards, one of the three major camps defending the capital, to someone else.

If the Crown Prince lost the Tiger Guards, it would be a significant blow to him.

If His Majesty had any intention of changing the heir, the world would surely fall into chaos. At that time, taking Yu Ying to the distant Shu region would allow them to avoid this trouble.

“Minister Pei, please enter,” the eunuch announced.

Hearing this, Pei Tao composed himself and entered the hall respectfully.

“This humble official, Pei Tao, kowtows to Your Majesty. May you live ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years.”

“Rise. Take a look at these three new paintings. Do you think they are genuine works by Shi Zhi’ao?”

Pei Tao’s family was not wealthy, and he had not studied antiques or paintings.

But since the Emperor had commanded it, he dared not refuse.

He examined the three paintings for a moment before cupping his hands. “In this humble official’s opinion, these three paintings are indeed by the same hand as the genuine Shi Zhi’ao work kept in the palace’s painting gallery.”

“These were sent by Zhao Xuanyou after his return to the capital. Genuine works by Shi Zhi’ao are rare. I only had one before, but he managed to find three at once.”

“Prince Zhao, even while on campaign, never forgets His Majesty’s great favor. He is truly devoted.”

Though speaking of Zhao Xuanyou, the Emperor kept his eyes on Pei Tao. “You’ve become much more cautious in your speech, never slipping up. You’d actually be quite suited to handling judicial matters.”

The position of Surveillance Commissioner was precisely one that oversaw judicial affairs in a province. The Emperor’s words…

Pei Tao’s heart stirred, but he didn’t dare speak recklessly, fearing he might ruin his chances. He simply lowered his head and listened to the Emperor’s instructions.

“That day at the theater, there were too many people. I couldn’t ask you then. Why did you accept the Crown Prince’s offer?”

“I have never spoken a false word to Your Majesty. In my three years in Qingzhou, I lived much more lightly than before and was able to do some practical things for the local people. Though Shu is farther away, I am truly willing to go.”

“Are you afraid of Sun Congdao causing you more trouble?”

“I am not concerned about Prime Minister Sun. Serving at Your Majesty’s side is what all court officials aspire to.”

“And you?” the Emperor asked, frowning.

Pei Tao bowed his head. “Three years ago, I realized I was nothing more than a pedantic scholar. I neither enjoy nor am capable of engaging in such political maneuvering. I beg Your Majesty to understand.”

In the Emperor’s eyes, Pei Tao was refined and scholarly, and though he liked him, he sometimes found him a bit too rigid.

“Alright, since you insist, you may go to Shu for two years. I will order the Ministry of Rites to arrange this in a few days.”

Pei Tao hadn’t expected the Emperor to agree so readily. He quickly knelt and expressed his gratitude.

“Thank you for Your Majesty’s great favor.”

Watching Pei Tao’s genuine smile, the Emperor felt a mix of helplessness and amusement.

He was still such a bookish fool; giving up the prestigious position of Assistant Minister of Justice to go to a remote and desolate place as a Surveillance Commissioner.

“There is a banquet at the Western Garden of the palace today. Since you’re already here, go and enjoy yourself.” The Emperor cleared his throat. “I recall that you and Qi’er get along quite well. Help me persuade him a little.”

“I…”

“Though this boy has trained for three years and greatly improved his martial skills and temper, unfortunately, the military is full of rough men. No one has taught him about matters between men and women. He’s seventeen and still a clueless boy. I’ve scolded him several times, but I don’t know if he’s truly dull or just pretending. Go and advise him for me. While you’re at it, help him consider the selection of a princess consort.”

Pei Tao was stunned.

The last time he had seen Zhao Qi in the palace, Zhao Qi had been troubled by the selection of a consort. He had given Zhao Qi a grand speech about choosing a wife. How was he supposed to change his tune now?

Still, he cupped his hands and said, “I obey Your Majesty’s decree.”

After leaving the imperial study, a young eunuch led Pei Tao toward the Western Garden.

Now that the Sixth Prince had been enfeoffed, only Zhao Qi remained in the Western Garden.

Thinking that his request to go to Shu had finally received the Emperor’s approval, Pei Tao’s steps were light.

No matter how much unsettling news he had received since returning to the capital, this one thing would surely bring a smile to Yu Ying’s face.

However, as soon as Pei Tao stepped into the Western Garden, he came face to face with the one person he least wanted to see.

chapters.title: A Narrow Path
chapters.content:
It was spring, but the Western Garden had a wide courtyard with no tall trees to block the sun, so the sunlight was blindingly bright.

Zhao Xuanyou wore the official robes of a military officer, the thick black brocade embroidered with a fierce tiger insignia. Tall and imposing, his handsome features exuded a stern and commanding presence as he strode quickly from the Western Garden.

Although Pei Tao had known Zhao Xuanyou would return to the capital, he hadn’t expected to run into him in the palace.

Compared to the distant and unreadable expression Pei Tao remembered, Zhao Xuanyou now looked cold and severe, his deep, tranquil eyes beneath his sword-like brows giving off an aura of untouchability.

As Pei Tao studied Zhao Xuanyou, Zhao Xuanyou also turned his gaze toward him.

The moment Pei Tao felt Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes on him, he understood: Zhao Xuanyou already knew about Yu Wan in Qingsha Town and suspected him, the Governor of Qingzhou.

After all, since that incident, Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Tao had become strangers, with Zhao Xuanyou ignoring him completely.

“Lord Zhao, it’s been a long time,” Pei Tao greeted him first with a slight bow.

Zhao Xuanyou frowned slightly but, unlike before, did not ignore him. He returned the bow.

“What a coincidence, Lord Pei is also entering the palace today.”

Pei Tao replied, “Indeed a coincidence. Just now in the Imperial Study, His Majesty mentioned that Lord Zhao has acquired three ancient paintings by the former dynasty’s master Ao. Each one is a rare treasure, truly remarkable.”

“There’s a lively banquet inside. I have other matters to attend to, so I won’t disturb Lord Pei’s enjoyment.”

“Take care, Prince.”

Pei Tao nodded slightly and was about to continue on his way.

But just as they passed each other, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly spoke.

“Have you seen Yu Wan?”

Ever since he learned that Zhao Xuanyou had returned to the capital, Pei Tao had anticipated they might meet and had privately considered how Zhao Xuanyou would act.

Given his usual behavior, Zhao Xuanyou would likely investigate secretly without making a sound. But it wasn’t out of the question for him to confront him directly.

He hadn’t expected that upon meeting today, Zhao Xuanyou would indeed question him outright.

“I have,” Pei Tao replied without changing his expression.

Zhao Xuanyou stopped in his tracks, his gaze fixed on Pei Tao’s face. “When?”

When he first heard from Pan Xun that Yu Wan’s trail had been found in Qingsha Town, his heart had first surged with joy, then filled with rage.

Qingsha Town was a place once governed by Pei Tao’s own father, and during the three years Yu Wan had been missing, Pei Tao had coincidentally been in Qingzhou.

Although he had questioned everyone in and out of the Jade Pavilion, they all claimed it was a family of three; a widow mother with a son and a daughter running a business. The daughter was unmarried, and their dealings were only with merchants, with no connection to any governor.

But Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t shake the feeling that there were no such coincidences in this world.

Perhaps Yu Wan had gone to Qingzhou because of Pei Tao. Or perhaps, over these three years, the two of them in Qingzhou had...

The thought alone made Zhao Xuanyou’s heart race with alarm.

His handsome brows tightened as he forcibly suppressed his chaotic thoughts, his deep gaze fixed on Pei Tao, searching for any clues in his eyes.

“Not long ago,” Pei Tao answered calmly, having prepared for this.

“How did you find her?”

“I didn’t know she was in Qingzhou. She came to find me.”

“Explain.”

“A young girl from her shop had gone missing. The family didn’t report it to the authorities, so she came to Qingzhou to search but found no leads. She had no choice but to seek me out.” Pei Tao’s long, arched brows lifted slightly. “Has Prince Zhao been searching for Miss Yu Wan all this time?”

“That is none of your concern.” Zhao Xuanyou didn’t hide his disdain for Pei Tao.

Pei Tao’s eyes flickered slightly in surprise, then he smiled faintly, just as calm as before. “Then I need not answer Prince Zhao’s questions. Farewell.”

As he watched Pei Tao walk toward the Western Garden, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly said, “Do you know she has already left Qingzhou?”

“None of my concern.”

Zhao Xuanyou was taken aback by his words, as if a wisp of cotton had lodged in his chest, making it hard to breathe in or out.

Pei Tao’s account matched what Pan Xun had found in Qingsha Town: Yu Wan had gone to Qingzhou City to investigate Jia He’s disappearance and had been delayed outside for nearly ten days before returning to Qingsha Town.

No matter what, today’s encounter with Pei Tao had yielded nothing.

After finally finding Yu Wan’s trail in Qingsha Town, she had slipped away like sand through his fingers.

Pei Tao followed the eunuch into the Western Garden. After walking a considerable distance, he glanced back and saw that Zhao Xuanyou had already disappeared.

He quickly replayed his conversation with Zhao Xuanyou in his mind. After confirming there were no flaws, his gaze relaxed slightly.

By the time he reached Zhao Qi, Pei Tao had already regained his composure.

“This official, Pei Tao, greets His Highness, the Seventh Prince.”

Today, Zhao Qi had been ordered by the Emperor to host a banquet in the Western Garden for the noble sons of the capital. But having spent three years in military training, he had little interest in feasting, drinking, or other frivolous pursuits. This banquet held no appeal for him either.

Especially since Zhao Xuanyou had just come by to annoy him. So when he saw Pei Tao, his mood finally improved a little.

“Lord Pei need not stand on ceremony. Sit and enjoy the music and dance.”

The nearby young eunuch understood and quickly brought a chair for Pei Tao to sit beside Zhao Qi.

Zhao Qi glanced at the dancers in the distance before turning back to Pei Tao.

“Did you run into Zhao Xuanyou on your way in?”

“I did.”

At the mention of Zhao Xuanyou, Zhao Qi’s anger flared.

Even though he, too, had been heartbroken over Yu Wan’s departure, Zhao Xuanyou had the nerve to come and provoke him.

Yu Wan had already left him. What right did Zhao Xuanyou have to question him as if he were the wronged party?

Pei Tao, however, slowly spoke up. “Just now, I learned from Lord Zhao that Miss Yu Wan is safe and sound. Your Highness can rest assured.”

He wasn’t aware of Zhao Qi’s feelings for Yu Wan. Thinking that Zhao Qi was still worried about her, he decided to take this opportunity to let him know she was alive.

It would ease Zhao Qi’s mind and prevent any contradictions in his own words.

“He told you about Yu Wan?” Zhao Qi asked in surprise.

From what Zhao Qi knew of Zhao Xuanyou, he should have been extremely secretive about Yu Wan’s affairs. Why would he voluntarily tell Pei Tao?

Pei Tao nodded.

“He said that for the past three years, Miss Yu Wan has been living in Qingsha Town.”

“Qingsha Town? That name sounds familiar.”

Pei Tao said, “The tribute pearl case of the Xingguo Duke’s mansion originated in Qingsha Town. It’s within Qingzhou’s borders. That’s why Prince Zhao asked me if I had ever encountered Miss Yu Wan.”

Zhao Qi suddenly stood up, pondering for a moment before muttering, “So she’s been hiding there all along.”

Hiding?

Pei Tao’s heart stirred at that word.

So Zhao Qi knew that Yu Wan was still alive?

Listening to this, he lowered his gaze and softly asked, “According to Prince Zhao, Miss Yu Wan has already left Qingsha Town.”

“Then where has she gone?” Zhao Qi grabbed his wrist urgently.

“Lord Zhao probably doesn’t know either.”

“So he’s been searching for Yu Wan all this time.” Zhao Qi’s expression turned strange. “And he actually found her.”

At the mention of this, Pei Tao’s expression also grew serious.

Zhao Xuanyou was a military officer and couldn’t leave his post without permission. In truth, once he returned to the army, Pei Tao could take Yu Wan to Xishu without worry.

But with the Jin Yi Wei assisting him, it was extremely troublesome.

---

chapters.title: A Gathering of Beauty
chapters.content:
Zhao Qi thought for a moment, then felt something was off.

“Hasn’t Zhao Xuanyou been stationed at the Mingjian Guard these past few years? Did he disregard the Emperor’s orders and leave his post without permission?”

“Probably not.”

Zhao Qi hurriedly pressed, “Then how did he find her?”

Over the past three years, he had also ordered Bingyun and Yangquan to continue searching for Yu Wan, but they had found nothing.

His martial skills might not match Zhao Xuanyou’s, but his subordinates were certainly not inferior.

“From what I know, the Jin Yi Wei have been helping Lord Zhao search for Yu Wan. This time, they found the clue about Yu Wan in Qingsha Town while investigating Hong Man’s case.”

“He even managed to get the Jin Yi Wei to work for him.” Zhao Qi scoffed.

The Jin Yi Wei were elite soldiers with a vast intelligence network, skilled in investigation. With their help, wasn’t Zhao Xuanyou bound to find Yu Wan before him?

Pei Tao observed Zhao Qi’s expression, and that earlier premonition resurfaced.

Zhao Qi seemed to care deeply about Yu Wan.

Uncertain of Zhao Qi’s stance, he decided to say less. He merely nodded in agreement and said nothing more.

“Your Highness.” A close attendant approached respectfully. “Her Majesty the Empress requests that Your Highness join her in the Imperial Garden for a conversation.”

“Scram.” Zhao Qi rolled his eyes. “I’m not going.”

He had invited the noble sons to a banquet in the Western Garden, while the Empress had invited noble ladies to the Imperial Garden for tea. Her request for him to go to the Imperial Garden was clearly a pretext; she wanted him to meet potential princess consorts.

Seeing Zhao Qi’s resistance, Pei Tao recalled the Emperor’s request in the Imperial Study and advised, “If Your Highness does not go, it may displease the elders. It would be better to make an appearance in the Imperial Garden to honor their intentions.”

Zhao Qi understood. The Empress’s flower-appreciation banquet was at the Emperor’s behest. If he didn’t go, he wouldn’t just be slighting the Empress; he’d be defying the Emperor’s will.

“Lord Pei, do you remember what you said that day?”

Pei Tao nodded.

Zhao Qi sighed. “I don’t want to marry someone I don’t love, but my father insists. What should I do?”

“Does Your Highness have someone in mind?”

Zhao Qi paused, then admitted honestly, “Yes.”

Pei Tao’s eyes narrowed slightly in surprise.

When he had interacted with Zhao Qi before, Zhao Qi had been a carefree youth. Not long after, he had gone to the military, surrounded by rough men. How could he have met someone he liked?

For some reason, Pei Tao thought of how anxious Zhao Qi had been when mentioning Yu Wan, and... his attitude toward Zhao Xuanyou.

In the past, although Zhao Qi often retorted to Zhao Xuanyou, he had deeply respected him.

But after today’s conversation, Pei Tao sensed a strong hostility from Zhao Qi toward Zhao Xuanyou.

Could his person of interest be... Yu Wan?

Pei Tao found it hard to believe, but the more he thought about it, the more plausible it seemed.

Testing the waters, he said, “Since Your Highness has someone in mind, why not inform His Majesty and ask for his blessing?”

“If only it were that simple.”

Setting aside the vast difference in their statuses, at the very least, Yu Wan would have to be present.

Recalling the words Yu Wan had said to him during their parting three years ago, Zhao Qi felt a dull ache in his heart.

He had been so foolish. How had he not realized those words were a farewell?

If he were given another chance, if she were to appear before him again, Zhao Qi would cause a scene if he had to, just to beg the Emperor for permission to marry her.

Zhao Qi clenched his fists tightly.

He absolutely could not let Zhao Xuanyou find Yu Wan before him.

He had to go see his father immediately.

“Your Highness?” Noticing Zhao Qi’s expression shift, Pei Tao asked tentatively.

Zhao Qi snapped back to reality and suddenly stood up. “You’re right, Lord Pei. I should go to the Imperial Garden. Otherwise, I’ll definitely displease my father and the Empress. You stay here and enjoy the performance a while longer.”

“No need. This official should also take his leave.” Pei Tao stood up as well.

The two left the Western Garden together. After Zhao Qi headed toward the Imperial Garden, Pei Tao made his way to the palace gates.

By now, the Imperial Garden was bustling with activity.

The Empress sat in the central Wisteria Pavilion, smiling as she conversed with the nearby concubines.

After the unexpected death of the Zhen Guo Duke last year, the Empress had changed her ways. Not only had she become more attentive to the Emperor, but she had also treated the harem concubines with kindness.

Because the Emperor was troubled by Zhao Qi’s marriage, she frequently invited noble ladies to the Imperial Garden to appreciate flowers and drink tea.

At the moment, the Imperial Garden was not only vibrant with blossoms and bathed in spring sunlight, but also filled with dazzling beauty; plump and slender figures adorned in splendid attire.

“Your Majesty, the Seventh Prince has arrived.”

“Bring him over at once.” The Empress said warmly.

Soon, the palace attendants brought Zhao Qi to the Empress. Although Zhao Qi despised this wicked woman, he had to maintain a facade.

If he didn’t show his face at the Imperial Garden, he would only face a scolding from the Emperor in the Imperial Study.

“This son greets Mother Empress.”

“We are all family. Qi’er, no need for formalities. Sit down.”

A palace attendant brought a chair over, and Zhao Qi, unable to leave immediately, had to sit.

After exchanging a few pleasantries with Zhao Qi, the Empress ordered the matron beside her to call over a few of the more outstanding noble ladies in the garden to the Wisteria Pavilion.

Zhao Qi kept his head turned away, thinking he just had to endure for a while. Suddenly, someone hugged his knee.

He frowned and looked down, only to see a chubby little child.

“Yi Yun, let go at once.” Zhuang Huaiyue, noticing the anger in Zhao Qi’s brows, quickly stepped forward to pull the child away.

This child was Zhuang Huaiyue’s firstborn son with the Crown Prince, named Zhao Yi Yun, just over two years old. He still couldn’t speak clearly.

But as the Crown Prince’s eldest son and the Emperor’s first grandson, he had been deeply cherished by the Empress since birth. He had been raised in the Kunning Palace, and even Zhuang Huaiyue herself came to the Kunning Palace daily to accompany her child.

However, Zhao Yi Yun tightly clung to Zhao Qi’s leg, mumbling “Daddy, Daddy.”

Zhao Qi sneered inwardly. He didn’t even recognize his own father. Was the child a fool?

Zhuang Huaiyue quickly crouched down and explained, “Yi Yun must miss his father. This is your Seventh Uncle. Say hello to Seventh Uncle.”

Zhao Yi Yun, though only two, could already say many words, albeit unclearly.

Hearing his mother’s instruction, he called out in a baby voice, “Seventh Uncle.”

Zhao Yi Yun’s face was as delicate as porcelain, his long lashes framing a pair of clear, innocent eyes. Though a boy, he looked as lovely as jade and snow.

“Yi Yun is such a good boy.” Zhao Qi awkwardly patted his head, then suddenly had an idea. He smiled and picked him up. “Do you only miss your father? Don’t you miss your Imperial Grandfather? Come, Seventh Uncle will take you to see Imperial Grandfather.”

“See Grandpa, see Grandpa.” Perhaps because Zhao Qi and the Crown Prince were brothers, Zhao Yi Yun showed no fear of Zhao Qi. Instead, he happily wrapped his arms around Zhao Qi’s neck.

“Mother Empress, I’ll take Yi Yun to play with His Majesty for a while and bring him back later.”

With that, Zhao Qi carried Zhao Yi Yun and hurried away.

Zhuang Huaiyue, however, was startled. The Crown Prince had told her before that he and Zhao Qi were on bad terms. If Zhao Qi suddenly took the child away...

Zhao Yi Yun was her lifeline. Through her son, she had brought her parents back to the capital and obtained the position of a noble consort. She couldn’t afford any mishaps.

She hastily turned to the Empress. “Your Majesty, the Seventh Prince may not have experience with children. This concubine wishes to go and check. If Yi Yun cries, I can tend to him.”

The Empress, of course, was also worried that Zhao Qi might harm her precious grandson. With a lift of her phoenix-like eyes, she said, “Go quickly.”

chapters.title: Attending to Personal Matters
chapters.content:
In the imperial study, the Emperor was discussing state affairs with two of his chancellor when he heard the eunuch announce that Zhao Qi had brought Zhao Yi Yun to see him. He was immediately taken aback.

Though one was his beloved youngest son and the other his favored eldest grandson, how had these two ended up together?

For now, he ordered Liu Quan to take them to a side chamber to have some refreshments, then continued discussing the remaining matters.

After finishing the government business, the Emperor walked to the side chamber. He saw a table laden with pastries and toys; Zhao Qi was savoring a bowl of sweet soup with great relish, while Zhao Yi Yun held a piece of cake, lying on the floor and eating with crumbs all over him.

"Pick Yi Yun up quickly, he might choke."

"Won't ch…" Zhao Qi had intended to say "won't choke to death," but remembering how others said the Emperor doted on his grandson, he swallowed the last word. "He won't choke. I'm watching him. Kids aren't that delicate."

"Grandpa! Grandpa!" Upon seeing the Emperor, Zhao Yi Yun rolled on the floor, scrambled to his feet, and toddled over, tugging at the Emperor's dragon robe in a coquettish manner.

The Emperor picked up Zhao Yi Yun and sat down beside Zhao Qi. Taking a handkerchief from Liu Quan, he wiped Yi Yun's mouth.

Three years ago, he had decided to depose the Crown Prince. But then, to his surprise, Consort Zhuanghuai gave birth to such an adorable grandson.

He was getting old and enjoyed spoiling his grandchildren. As he played with the child, his affection deepened, and he couldn't bear to see the poor boy, barely born, demoted to commoner status.

After much hesitation, he ordered Pan Xun to secretly tamper with the Mounted General's warhorse, causing the general to fall during a training exercise.

Though it was a regret that the Mounted General didn't die from the fall, the imperial physicians examined him twice and concluded he would never ride or lead troops again.

Severely injuring the Mounted General was a heavy blow to the Empress and the Crown Prince.

If they behaved themselves from now on, the Emperor could grant them a peaceful end.

"Why did you bring Yi Yun here?"

Zhao Qi replied, "This son originally wanted to enjoy the flowers in the Imperial Garden a while longer, but Yi Yun kept clinging to me and calling for Grandpa, so I had no choice but to bring him here first."

As he spoke, he picked up a rattle from the side and teased his nephew in the Emperor's arms.

Zhao Yi Yun seemed to like him, smiling as he reached out to grab it.

"You went to the Imperial Garden?" the Emperor asked.

"Of course. How could this son ignore Mother's kind arrangement?"

"Did you see any young ladies you fancy?"

Zhao Qi stuck out his tongue and grinned at the Emperor. "This son has been keeping Yi Yun company the whole time. I haven't had a chance to look around yet."

The Emperor let out a cold "Hmph."

"Father Emperor, this son has a request I hope you will grant."

"What request?"

The Emperor had been pressing Zhao Qi to marry, and Zhao Qi couldn't refuse, so he had to use delaying tactics.

"Mother summoned these beauties into the palace, and this son has seen them all since childhood. Whether I look or not, it's the same; they're not my ideal partner."

The Emperor was surprised. Every time he discussed marriage with Zhao Qi, the boy had been enthusiastic. But now, hearing him mention an "ideal partner" took the Emperor aback.

"You little rascal! Just pick a wife. What's all this about an ideal partner?"

"In the future, this son will be an idle prince. My princess consort won't have many duties. It's not like the Crown Prince, who needs to be so picky, right?"

The Emperor detected the subtext in his words and frowned slightly. "Did you see someone you like during your travels?"

"No," Zhao Qi denied immediately.

"If you do like someone, it doesn't matter if her background is humble, as long as her family is respectable and her character is good."

With Yu Wan's background and history, there was no way she would meet the Emperor's standards.

Zhao Qi had no intention of revealing everything to the Emperor now. He simply looked at him and said, "This son hasn't met the right person yet. But I don't want to marry someone I don't like, like Elder Brother the Crown Prince. Father Emperor, please agree to postpone the selection of my consort."

At the mention of the Crown Prince, the Emperor's expression darkened.

The Crown Prince's marriage was a sore point in his heart. If he had been more forceful in stopping it back then, perhaps things wouldn't have gone so wrong. One mistake led to another, and now it was beyond repair.

"Very well. Since you have your own ideas, I won't rush you for now."

"Then can this son still establish his own residence and leave the palace this year?" Zhao Qi looked at the Emperor pitifully. "Elder Brother Six is only a few months older than me, and he's already been enfeoffed as a prince. What about me?"

"Do you want to leave the palace that much?"

Zhao Qi forced a smile. "This son has been in the military for three years and is truly feeling stifled. I'd like to travel and also visit my own fief."

The Emperor had already selected Zhao Qi's fief, which was near the capital, in the Jiangbei region.

After a moment of deliberation, the Emperor nodded. "Your prince's residence should be almost ready."

Over the past three years, Zhao Qi had stayed obediently in the military. Not only had he stopped causing trouble as he used to, but his martial skills had also improved significantly, and he had even won several minor naval battles.

"Thank you, Father Emperor."

Zhao Qi was overjoyed and expressed his gratitude. Little Zhao Yi Yun, beside him, also chimed in with "Thank you, thank you."

Zhao Qi smiled and patted Zhao Yi Yun's head.

This kid, though only two years old, was far more likable than his father.

A prince had his own guards. Once he was in his own residence, with sufficient manpower and strong forces, he didn't believe he wouldn't be able to find Zhao Xuanyou.

Having settled his own business, Zhao Qi's eyes gleamed as he looked at the Emperor.

"Today, this son encountered Minister Pei and Minister Zhao. Minister Pei is still as handsome as ever, but Minister Zhao seemed a bit different."

After Zhao Xuanyou returned to the capital, the Emperor had also summoned him to the palace for an audience.

"After all those events, Xuanyou has become more steady."

"Has he? This son doesn't think so."

The Emperor narrowed his eyes, examining Zhao Qi.

Zhao Qi gave an awkward smile, avoiding the Emperor's gaze, and instead used the rattle to amuse Zhao Yi Yun.

"Qi'er, what exactly do you want to say?"

"This son heard a little about him and the Brocade Guards." Zhao Qi said slowly, "It's not a big deal."

"Speak."

Zhao Qi cleared his throat twice, pulled Zhao Yi Yun into his lap, and used the child as a shield between himself and the Emperor.

"He hasn't been the commander of the Brocade Guards for a long time, but this son heard that he's been having the Brocade Guards attend to his personal matters."

Zhao Qi was doing this for the first time in his life and felt a bit nervous.

As he spoke, he glanced at the Emperor's expression.

Seeing that the Emperor remained impassive, Zhao Qi hesitated internally.

But since he had already said half of it, he couldn't take it back. He had to steel himself and continue.

"The Brocade Guards are Your Majesty's personal guards, aren't they? It's not appropriate for them to attend to his personal matters." Zhao Qi felt uneasy and quickly added, "But he's always been careful in his actions. It must have been a momentary oversight. He didn't have any ill intentions."

The Emperor raised his eyes and gave Zhao Qi a measured look.

Zhao Qi quickly lowered his head to play with Zhao Yi Yun. "Big nephew, do you miss your mother? Uncle Seven will take you to see her."

"Mother! I want mother!"

What a good child.

Zhao Qi quickly picked up Zhao Yi Yun and, without waiting for the Emperor to say more, carried him away.

---

chapters.title: The Ideal in the Painting
chapters.content:
As the sun set, Yuan Zhen hurried into Honghui Hall.

The study was still simply and neatly arranged as before, except that the desk was scattered with brushes and rice paper.

Zhao Xuanyou stood in front of the desk, where an unrolled sheet of paper had only half a painting; a faintly outlined graceful figure.

Hearing Yuan Zhen's footsteps, Zhao Xuanyou frowned and said in a low voice, "Do you not understand the rules?"

Yuan Zhen abruptly stopped in his tracks, standing at the doorway, not daring to enter.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled over an unused sheet of rice paper and covered the painting before saying, "Come in."

"Minister Pan sent word. He will come to the Hou residence after the night curfew tonight." Yuan Zhen lowered his voice. "It should be about court matters. It sounds urgent."

Zhao Xuanyou's hand suddenly tightened around the brush, his sharp gaze shooting toward Yuan Zhen.

"Is there news of her again?"

"No, it's unrelated to Yu Wan. It should be about court matters. It sounds urgent."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded slightly, said no more, and rinsed the brush in the lotus-shaped brush washer a few times.

"Understood. You may leave."

"Yes."

Yuan Zhen silently retreated and closed the door behind him.

Zhao Xuanyou removed the sheet of rice paper covering the painting and began to paint again, slowly and carefully outlining the expression of the woman in the picture.

He was originally not skilled in painting.

But three years ago, when Pan Xun said he would take the portrait to search for Yu Wan in Yangzhou, the painters of the Brocade Guards had tried to capture her likeness, but none of their paintings had her spirit. So he picked up the brush himself, and since then, he couldn't stop.

He had painted every memory of Yu Wan.

Sometimes she stood by the window trimming flowers, sometimes she sat in the corridor laughing with others, sometimes she sat astride a horse, grinning triumphantly, and sometimes she occupied his desk, practicing calligraphy with a smug smile.

Of course, there was also her secret side.

Like the painting before him.

Yu Wan lay on the pillow, her dark hair scattered around her, her eyes misty as she gazed at him, half-drowsy, half...

He didn't understand why Yu Wan was so heartless toward him. Only by capturing her image on paper, framing it himself, and sealing it away could he barely dissipate the overwhelming longing.

The top two shelves of the bookcase were filled with brocade boxes, each containing rolls of his paintings, which he had brought back from the frontier.

Those brocade boxes were off-limits to anyone. A few days ago, when Autumn Moon was dusting the bookshelf, she accidentally moved one, and Zhao Xuanyou had flown into a rage. He reinstated the old rule of Honghui Hall: no one except Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing was allowed to enter his study.

After finishing the painting, he stared at it for a moment, then quickly covered it with another sheet of rice paper. He changed into clean clothes and went to Leshou Hall to have dinner with Grandmother Leaf.

"Grandmother."

After Zhao Xuanyou left the capital, the Pacification Marquis had stayed in the capital with the old madam for over a year. When the cold weather made his legs ache unbearably, he had taken his concubine to the south before the Winter Solstice.

But he had indeed helped Zhao Xuanyou persuade Old Madam Ye.

After returning to the capital this time, though Old Madam Ye still had the sorrow of not being able to hold a great-grandchild, she no longer said anything to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou accompanied the old madam for dinner and had some homemade apricot blossom wine.

When the time was about right, he returned to Honghui Hall.

The painting he had done in the afternoon was already half-dry. Zhao Xuanyou sat down and studied it for a while.

Yuan Zhen said from outside the door, "Master, Minister Pan has arrived."

"Have Yingsue prepare some food and wine to be sent to the warm pavilion."

"Yes."

Zhao Xuanyou covered the painting on the table again and stood up to leave.

Yuan Qing had just led Pan Xun in. Upon seeing Zhao Xuanyou, Pan Xun quickly cupped his hands in greeting.

"Worldly Son."

"No need for formalities. Let's sit and talk."

Zhao Xuanyou took Pan Xun to the warm pavilion. Yingsue and Yuan Zhen served the food and wine before silently withdrawing.

"Three years without seeing each other. I offer you a toast, Your Grace."

Over the past three years, they had exchanged letters in secret, but after Zhao Xuanyou stepped down as the commander of the Brocade Guards, they had not met in person.

"I am no longer the commander of the Brocade Guards. There's no need for such politeness."

"Without you, there would be no me today. I will never forget your kindness."

Back then, Pan Xun was just a minor centurion in the Northern Garrison of the Brocade Guards, with ambitions but no opportunity to realize them. It was Zhao Xuanyou who promoted him to a thousand-household commander and entrusted him with the case of the Xingguo Duke's residence, which earned him the Emperor's favor and made him the deputy commander of the Brocade Guards.

No one in the entire Brocade Guards had risen faster than him.

Moreover, Zhao Xuanyou's help to him didn't stop there.

Last year, when the Emperor ordered him to find a way to eliminate the Mounted General, it was Zhao Xuanyou who suggested tampering with the warhorse.

All these things, Pan Xun naturally remembered.

"Speak. What brings you here so late?"

At this, Pan Xun's gaze darkened.

"This afternoon, His Majesty summoned me to the imperial study and asked if I had found the person you were looking for."

"Did he scold you?"

"Not exactly, but he didn't seem happy either."

The Emperor had ascended the throne by stepping on several of his brothers, but after securing his rule, he had always practiced benevolent governance.

In Zhao Xuanyou's eyes, the current Emperor was generally a benevolent ruler, but beneath the surface, he was like a velvet glove covering an iron fist.

"He was warning you."

Pan Xun had thought the same, but he still found it strange.

"His Majesty must have known about this all along. He never said anything before. I don't know why he suddenly brought it up today."

Today...

A cold smile appeared on Zhao Xuanyou's lips.

Today at the West Garden gate, he had encountered Pei Ta. Pei Ta probably knew that the Brocade Guards were helping him search for someone, but given Pei Ta's status and character, it was impossible for him to go to the Emperor and gossip about the Brocade Guards' actions.

The only one who could cause trouble for him was Zhao Qi.

That little...

"You don't need to worry too much. His Majesty won't be angry for now. In the future, don't involve yourself in any of my affairs."

"And Miss Yu Wan?"

"My affairs are none of your concern. Don't even pass letters anymore."

Of course, he would continue searching for Yu Wan. Even without the Brocade Guards, he had other people.

She had been in hiding for three years, but finally, traces of her had appeared in Qingsha Town. This was the best opportunity to find her.

Zhao Qi must have understood this, which was why he was trying to trip him up at this moment, hoping to find her first.

"Understood."

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze shifted to Pan Xun. "Actually, this matter also serves as a reminder to you. The Brocade Guards are a sword His Majesty has forged for himself. This sword can only be wielded by him. You are now only half a step away from becoming the commander. Don't stray from the path."

Pan Xun seemed to ponder this and nodded. "I will never forget your guidance, Your Grace. It's getting late. I shouldn't stay too long. I'll take my leave now."

He had come secretly, so there was no need for Zhao Xuanyou to see him out. He cupped his hands again and left quickly.

Zhao Xuanyou picked up the wine cup on the table and took a sip.

The Brocade Guards were indeed a useful tool. Of course, he would use them again; when the time was right.

chapters.title: A Letter from Afar
chapters.content:
In Suzhou, April skies stretched high, grass grew long, swallows darted, and trees cast thick shade.

Yu Wan fanned herself with a newly bought beauty’s round fan, leaning by the window, watching the ripples on the Shantang River as small boats leisurely wove through the water.

These past few days, her mind had been restless.

, Because of the agreement she had made with Pei Tao.

It wasn’t that she disliked Pei Tao; it was just that after leaving the capital, the three of them had been living under assumed names, and reuniting with Pei Tao had truly been unexpected.

Yet, recalling the emotions she had felt when parting with him by the river that day, her heart had indeed been moved.

After leaving Qingzhou, they had taken a small detour through Jiangnan before arriving in Suzhou.

To be cautious, Yu Wan had not taken her mother to the previously agreed Xiangyun Inn. Instead, they stayed at another inn.

Every day, Wen Qi accompanied Ding Wenxi on outings, while Yu Wan, disliking disguises, stayed in her room.

As the day of her meeting with Pei Tao approached, Yu Wan ordered Wen Qi to go to Xiangyun Inn to look for him and see if Pei Tao had arrived.

The first day, nothing.

The second day, nothing.

On the third day, Wen Qi brought Lu Cheng back.

Not seeing Pei Tao, Yu Wan assumed their agreement couldn’t be fulfilled. A hint of disappointment flickered in her heart, but she forced a smile and turned to Lu Cheng. “Has Lord Pei decided to stay in the capital? Congratulations, then.”

Lu Cheng had received many instructions from Pei Tao before leaving. Knowing the relationship between Pei Tao and Yu Wan, he quickly replied, “No, my lord has already received the Emperor’s decree. He’s been promoted to the position of Surveillance Commissioner of the Western Shu Province. Now, he’s just waiting for the official transfer order from the Ministry of Rites before he can depart for Shu.”

Western Shu?

Surrounded by mountains on all sides, it was a distant place, but poetry often praised it as a fine land.

“So that’s how it is. I thought he wasn’t coming because…”

“Lord Pei also wanted to come to Suzhou to escort you, Miss. But something unexpected has come up, and he needs to stay in the capital to stabilize the situation. That’s why he sent me to deliver the news to you, so you wouldn’t worry.”

Yu Wan noticed the gravity in Lu Cheng’s expression and asked, “What happened?”

“The day you left Qingsha Town, the Brocade Guards went there.”

As expected, the Brocade Guards…

Yu Wan tightened her grip on the fan’s ribs and sighed. “Did Qiao He tell them?”

“Yes.” Lu Cheng quickly replied, “But don’t worry, Miss. When Lord Pei noticed the Brocade Guards’ movements, he had us go to the dock to cover things up. The records of your boat purchase and travel have all been erased. They only know you left Qingsha Town, but not how you left or where you went.”

“I see.”

Lu Cheng thought for a moment, then asked, “Where is that boat now?”

Yu Wan replied, “It’s docked at another shipyard. We came to Suzhou by carriage.”

Hearing this, Lu Cheng couldn’t help but admire the beautiful young woman before him.

She was so cautious in her actions that even if they hadn’t gone to the dock to erase traces, the Brocade Guards would have had a hard time finding her.

Originally, he had thought Lord Pei’s affection for her was due to her outstanding beauty, but now it seemed there was much more to it.

“What does Lord Pei think?” Seeing that Lu Cheng had fallen silent, Yu Wan asked.

Lu Cheng said, “The rest of the message was told to me by Lord Pei. I don’t understand what it means, but I can recite it word for word to you.”

“Please.”

“The Young Prince has returned to the capital. He knows you’ve been in Qingsha Town these past three years and will certainly suspect Lord Pei. So, Lord Pei needs to stay in the capital and lie low for now.”

Lu Cheng didn’t know who the Young Prince was, so he didn’t understand whom Lord Pei was so wary of.

But as soon as he finished speaking, he clearly saw Yu Wan’s brows tighten slightly.

Wen Qi, standing beside her, also looked at Yu Wan.

After a moment, Yu Wan’s expression returned to normal. She nodded. “Thank you for letting me know. I understand.”

“Lord Pei said he can’t come to Suzhou to escort you to Shu, so he sent me to take you there.”

Yu Wan pondered for a moment, then shook her head.

“You came to the capital with Pei Tao. If you’re seen with me, it’ll be easier to expose my whereabouts.”

“It won’t be that bad.”

Yu Wan didn’t respond.

Others might not know, but she was very clear.

That man was meticulous, with a mind as fine as dust. The slightest oversight would reveal a flaw in front of him.

He had already traced her to Qingsha Town. Without other leads, he would certainly keep a close eye on Pei Tao.

After thinking, Yu Wan looked up and asked, “Do you have any relatives in Suzhou? Or old friends in Jiangnan?”

Lu Cheng scratched his head. “I used to study martial arts at a martial arts school in the suburbs of Suzhou. Does that count as an old friend?”

“It does. Buy some gifts today and visit them. Stay there for a few days before returning to the capital.”

“Then, Miss… will you go to Shu?”

Yu Wan smiled. “When you return to the capital, tell Pei Tao that since he hasn’t broken his promise, I won’t either.”

Lu Cheng didn’t understand why Pei Tao and Yu Wan had to be so cautious, but after thinking, he could only nod.

“I understand. If anyone asks, I’ll just say I came to Suzhou to visit my master.”

“Don’t just say it. Really go visit.”

Zhao Xuanyou had the Brocade Guards helping him. It would be too easy for him to verify anything.

“Miss, don’t worry. I won’t cause you any trouble.” At this point, Lu Cheng took something out from his bosom. “Lord Pei asked me to bring this to you.”

Yu Wan saw that it was carefully wrapped. After taking it, she didn’t open it, only saying, “Thank you for your trouble.”

After Lu Cheng left, Wen Qi looked at Yu Wan.

“So, are we going to Shu?”

Yu Wan nodded, then after a moment’s thought, said, “They say the road to Shu is harder than climbing to the heavens. But I’ve just thought of something; we can go via Balin and take a boat all the way. That way, we won’t have to endure the hardships of crossing mountains and rivers.”

Wen Qi listened to her, looking at her with slight surprise.

“Lu Cheng just said Lord Pei is going to Shu, and you’ve already figured out how to get there?”

Yu Wan nodded.

“Did you guess he’d be appointed to Shu?”

Yu Wan let out a soft laugh. “How could anyone guess that?”

Wen Qi pressed, “Then how do you know taking a boat from Balin will avoid crossing mountains and rivers?”

Yu Wan raised her chin proudly and playfully tapped Wen Qi’s forehead. “Because I’m smart.”

Wen Qi listened to her self-satisfied words and just responded with an “Oh.”

“Just kidding. I read it in a book.” Yu Wan loved studying maps, and after reading so many, she naturally remembered the details.

She touched the package Lu Cheng had left behind. It felt like a book.

Opening it, she found it was indeed a book titled The Customs and Scenery of Western Shu.

In this world, only Pei Tao knew what she liked… But after being apart for so long, he wouldn’t just buy a book from the market, would he?

Yu Wan gently lifted a corner of the page and, sure enough, saw dense handwriting inside.

“What kind of book is this?” Wen Qi leaned over to look.

“No peeking!”

“What’s the big deal if I look?”

“It’s a book for me, not for you. If you want to read it, buy your own!”

Yu Wan hugged the book and hurried away.

---

chapters.title: Bringing Shame Upon Oneself
chapters.content:
“Congratulations to Your Highness on your move.”

Five days ago, the Emperor officially bestowed the title of Prince Rui upon Zhao Qi.

Last year, when the Sixth Prince was enfeoffed, the Emperor had already prepared a prince’s residence for Zhao Qi, who was far away in the southeast.

The Court Astronomer had determined today as an auspicious day for moving, so Zhao Qi moved into his prince’s residence today. The nobles of the capital all came to congratulate him on his new home.

Pei Tao had not yet completed the handover at the Ministry of Rites and was still in the capital. Today, he had to come to the prince’s residence to offer his congratulations.

“Lord Pei, no need for formalities. Be at ease today.”

Zhao Qi usually disliked social niceties, but today his attitude was quite good.

After all, the Emperor agreeing to first bestow the title and then discuss marriage was a great joy for him.

After becoming a prince, he no longer had to live in the imperial palace. He had more attendants and greater freedom of movement.

Thinking that he would soon be able to leave the capital to find Yu Wan, Zhao Qi was in high spirits. Even though he had to socialize all day, he had no complaints.

After presenting his gift, Pei Tao was led by a servant of the prince’s residence to the Zhaohu Tower, where the male guests were drinking tea and chatting.

Behind the main hall where Zhao Qi received guests was a clear stream diverted from the river outside the residence. On both sides of the pool, two pavilions had been built; one called Zhaohu Tower, the other Liuqing Pavilion.

Today, the male guests gathered in Zhaohu Tower, while the female guests were in Liuqing Pavilion.

“Her Highness, Princess Yining, has arrived.”

After the announcement, the elegantly dressed noblewomen and young ladies in Liuqing Pavilion all stood up and bowed to her.

Princess Yining, with her large belly, walked into the pavilion and said lightly, “No need for formalities,” then walked toward Princess Yian, the only one who hadn’t moved.

“Sister Yian, you usually don’t like going out, preferring to stay in the princess’s residence composing poetry. Why have you come out to join the fun today?”

Princess Yian fanned herself with a jade bone fan, glanced at Princess Yining’s belly, and humphed lightly. “My sister is seven months pregnant and still parading around socializing everywhere. Why can’t I come out?”

After returning to the capital from the Lichuan Imperial Palace, the Emperor, together with the Empress, quickly decided on the marriages of the two princesses.

Princess Yining was betrothed to Ye Moque, the son of the Anning Marquis. Princess Yian was betrothed to Xu Hongxuan, the youngest son of Chancellor Xu.

At first, both princesses were naturally dissatisfied with their marriages.

Although Ye Moque enjoyed leisure, he was not a dissolute man. After marriage, he was extremely attentive and considerate to Princess Yining. With his sweet-talking, he quickly won her heart. The two were inseparable and lived in harmony.

After more than a year of marriage, Princess Yining became pregnant. The Emperor was overjoyed and bestowed many rewards upon her.

Princess Yian’s situation was not as smooth.

The Chancellor’s family was known for its integrity, and Xu Hongxuan had been strictly educated by Chancellor Xu since childhood. He was upright and down-to-earth, but his personality was somewhat rigid. Naturally, this clashed with Princess Yian, who loved the limelight. After marriage, they often argued. Princess Yian simply drove Xu Hongxuan back to the Xu residence and lived alone in the princess’s residence.

Every month, she would host a literary gathering in the princess’s residence, inviting scholars and literati to compose poetry.

Rumors spread throughout the capital that Princess Yian kept male favorites in her residence, indulging in luxury and debauchery.

The Emperor severely reprimanded her several times, but she insisted she only loved poetry and had not done anything to disgrace the imperial family. The Emperor had no choice but to let her be.

“Now that my belly is big, I indeed don’t like moving around much. But the Prince Consort asked the imperial physician, who said that walking more is beneficial for childbirth. Even if I don’t go out to socialize, he makes me walk a few laps around the garden of the princess’s residence every day.”

Princess Yining now held unique favor with the Emperor, and her tone was naturally different from before, carrying a hint of smugness.

“That’s true. Especially for first-time mothers, if they are weak, they will suffer during childbirth.” The women around her chimed in, sharing their own childbirth experiences.

Princess Yian saw them surrounding Princess Yining like stars around the moon. She rolled her eyes, stood up, and walked away.

After a few steps, a subtle smile appeared in her eyes.

“Sister Qianran, you actually came out today.” Princess Yian put on a concerned and persuasive demeanor and sat down next to Sun Qianran. “I haven’t seen you much since you and Lord Pei separated.”

In Liuqing Pavilion, there were still those who were worse off than her.

No matter how much the Prince Consort disagreed with her, he wouldn’t dare to mention separation.

Sun Qianran withdrew her thoughts and explained indifferently, “Today, my father had official business, so I accompanied my younger brother to congratulate Prince Rui on his move.”

“Is that so?” Princess Yian smiled meaningfully. “I thought you came because Seventh Brother invited Lord Pei. By the way, Lord Pei has been back in the capital for almost a month. I even met him once in the palace. Have you not seen him yet?”

Sun Qianran knew Princess Yian was deliberately teasing her. She was intelligent and would never lose in a war of words.

But Princess Yian’s words had struck a sore spot.

Three years after their separation, she had not forgotten Pei Tao for a single day.

“Let Your Highness laugh at me.”

Seeing that she did not deny it, Princess Yian’s gaze flickered slightly. She suddenly became interested. “I happen to have a few words I want to say to Sixth Brother. If you have time, accompany me to Zhaohu Tower.”

As a princess and the elder sister of Prince Rui, she could naturally move freely within the prince’s residence.

Sun Qianran, hearing this, was overjoyed. “Thank you, Your Highness.”

Princess Yian had long been tired of seeing Princess Yining’s smug face. She immediately took Sun Qianran’s hand and walked toward Zhaohu Tower together.

The male guests in Zhaohu Tower, seeing the princesses arrive, all bowed respectfully.

Princess Yian looked around the room but did not see Pei Tao. She asked Prince Qing, Zhao Yue, “Where is Pei Tao?”

“He seems to be in the garden outside, with some people from the Hanlin Academy.”

Pei Tao had previously served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, so naturally, he got along better with these scholars and officials.

“Thank you.”

Princess Yian immediately pulled Sun Qianran toward the garden next to Zhaohu Tower.

As they reached the corridor, they saw Pei Tao standing with a few officials of similar age, chatting.

The spring sunlight filtered through the leaves, casting dappled shadows on him, making his fair skin and refined demeanor even more striking.

He stood among the flowers, talking leisurely with others, his posture graceful and his manner exceptionally at ease.

“Are you too cowardly to go over and say hello?” Princess Yian, with the intention of watching a show, saw Sun Qianran hesitate and was naturally displeased.

Sun Qianran took a deep breath and was about to muster the courage to go over when she suddenly saw Pei Tao take a few steps during the conversation, his sleeve brushing against a peony flower.

He turned to steady the peony branch, waiting until the flower stopped trembling before letting go.

But he did not turn back immediately. Instead, he stared at the peony for a moment, a faint, tender smile appearing in his eyes.

He raised his hand and gently touched a peony petal before resuming his conversation with the others.

Sun Qianran, watching this scene from the corridor, suddenly felt a wave of sadness. She turned and walked away.

Princess Yian saw her leave abruptly, her expected entertainment ruined. She hurried after her to the outside of Zhaohu Tower and grabbed her sleeve.

“You’ve come all this way. Why are you running?”

“There’s no need anymore.”

Pei Tao’s tenderness was already given to someone else. Going over to talk to him would only bring shame upon herself.

She just didn’t know who the woman was who had captured his heart.

Was his insistence on going to Shu also related to that woman?

chapters.title: Bashan and Shui of Shu
chapters.content:
"Yingying, the autumn equinox is almost here, shouldn't you go find Lord Pei?"

After parting ways with Lu Cheng in Gusu, Yu Ying, along with Ding Wenxi and Wen Shu, soon left Gusu as well.

They did not head to Western Shu but instead traveled south all the way to Lingnan, where they stayed for three full months.

The geographical records described Lingnan as a land beyond civilization, a place where the court exiled criminals.

But upon arriving in Suizhou City, Yu Ying found that although it was a place where various ethnic groups coexisted, its direct maritime routes to the Southern Ocean made trade flourish, rivaling even Jiangnan. It was far from a barren wasteland.

Lingnan was even farther from the capital, with many foreign ethnic groups and people from distant lands. No one paid any mind to outsiders like them.

If not for the agreement with Pei Ta to meet in Western Shu, Yu Ying would have loved to stay in Lingnan to do business. With the maritime routes connecting to foreign lands, she could certainly build something even greater than the Jingyu Pavilion.

Yu Ying ate lychees every day and had even developed a taste for the local dish of raw fish. She was living a life of great contentment.

Seeing her spending all day eating and drinking, Ding Wenxi couldn’t help but remind her of their plan to meet Pei Ta in Western Shu.

"From the capital to Western Shu, it would take at least three months. Even if everything goes smoothly, he’s probably still on the road."

"That’s his pace. We can go ahead first."

Yu Ying laughed, "It’s rare to be in Lingnan. Once we leave, we might never come back in this lifetime. We should enjoy it a bit longer."

Ding Wenxi couldn’t get used to the local food and didn’t share Yu Ying’s attachment to the place.

As a mother, she was more concerned about Yu Ying’s lifelong happiness.

"People say delays breed mishaps. Lord Pei has been promoted again after returning to the capital. What if he changes his mind?"

Seeing Ding Wenxi overthinking, Yu Ying didn’t know how to comfort her.

After all, whether Pei Ta would change his mind was not up to her.

Wen Shu suddenly spoke up, "He won’t."

He was usually a man of few words, and his sudden remark made Ding Wenxi and Yu Ying both laugh. Mother and daughter blurted out in unison, "How do you know?"

"Because I don’t think he would break his word."

He didn’t know Pei Ta, but he knew Yu Ying.

If Pei Ta had fallen for Yu Ying, how could he give her up?

Compared to Ding Wenxi’s worries and Wen Shu’s certainty, Yu Ying took a more relaxed view.

"If he changes his mind, then so be it. We’ll just consider it a trip to Western Shu. At worst, we’ll come back to Lingnan and settle down."

Ding Wenxi sighed helplessly, "Do you really like it here that much?"

"Mother, a few days ago, Wen Shu and I met a merchant ship returning from the Southern Ocean at the dock. The ship was loaded with many pearls, larger than those we saw in Qingsha Town, and their luster was different too."

Yu Ying spent her days dragging Wen Shu out to explore. After familiarizing themselves with Suizhou City, her favorite place to visit was the dock.

The dock was filled with merchant ships from distant seas, carrying all kinds of exotic goods that never failed to amaze Yu Ying.

"More beautiful?"

Yu Ying thought for a moment, "Not necessarily more beautiful, but each has its own merits. I think if you saw them, Mother, you could make unique jewelry suited to each pearl."

"Didn’t we agree that this time it’s your turn to treat me? I shouldn’t have to work hard making jewelry anymore."

"That’s true," Yu Ying tugged at Ding Wenxi’s sleeve and shook her arm. "Your daughter admits her mistake."

Wen Shu said, "The merchant ships from the Southern Ocean carry many goods. Even if we don’t make jewelry, we can do other things."

"Alright, alright. We’re going to Western Shu soon. Forget about the Southern Ocean merchant ships." Ding Wenxi took Yu Ying’s hand and earnestly advised, "I’m not joking with you. When the weather gets colder, heavy snow will block the mountains and freeze the rivers. It’ll be hard to enter Shu then. We can’t delay until next spring, can we?"

Mother’s words weren’t without reason.

After all, her health wasn’t what it used to be. Traveling in the bitter cold could indeed make her ill.

"Alright, then let’s set off a bit earlier."

Hearing this, Ding Wenxi was overjoyed.

They didn’t have much with them, so in two or three days, they packed up and bought a carriage to head for Baling.

Having traveled far and wide, the three of them didn’t find the journey particularly arduous.

A month later, they arrived in Baling. Yu Ying rented a boat to navigate the mountains into Shu. By the time they reached Anzhou, it was already past the Beginning of Winter.

To be cautious, Yu Ying and Ding Wenxi didn’t enter the city rashly. Instead, they stayed in a town on the outskirts, sending Wen Shu into the city first to gather information.

If Pei Ta had already arrived, they would send him a message.

If he hadn’t arrived yet, or if the position of the Surveillance Commissioner in Western Shu Province had been given to someone else, Wen Shu would return to discuss their next steps.

The weather in Shu was cold. Yu Ying went to the town to buy new cotton-padded clothes and quilts. Returning to the inn, she was just making the bed for Ding Wenxi when she heard a knock at the door.

"Who is it?" Yu Ying didn’t answer immediately, only cautiously asking.

"It’s me."

The voice outside was Wen Shu’s calm tone.

Could it be that there was still no news of Pei Ta?

Yu Ying’s heart sank, but she didn’t want to worry Ding Wenxi, so she casually walked over to open the door.

But when the door opened, it wasn’t just Wen Shu standing outside.

Pei Ta wore a dark green robe, a brocade belt at his waist, and a jade crown in his hair. His usually tranquil and detached eyes held a touch of eagerness.

And in that instant, a bright light flickered in Yu Ying’s eyes.

She opened her mouth, forgetting what she wanted to say, and just stood there at the doorway, staring at him.

She truly hadn’t expected Pei Ta to come here.

As she had thought earlier, even if Pei Ta had already arrived in Anzhou City, she would have proceeded cautiously, finding an opportunity to enter the city and settle down before meeting him.

For him to come out of the city to see her like this was indeed risky.

But... it also made her genuinely happy.

"Yu Ying." He called her name softly.

Ding Wenxi, although pleased that Pei Ta had arrived in Western Shu as promised, noticed the sparkling glances between the two. She recalled the scene of them embracing by the river last time.

They weren’t married yet, so she couldn’t allow them to be so intimate.

She stepped beside Yu Ying and called out, "Lord Pei."

With Ding Wenxi’s reminder, Pei Ta withdrew his gaze from Yu Ying and cupped his hands in greeting to Ding Wenxi.

"Madam."

Ding Wenxi subtly reached out and pulled Yu Ying’s hand, tugging her closer, and smiled at Pei Ta. "Lord Pei, when did you arrive in Anzhou?"

"About ten days ago."

"Coming from the capital, the journey should have been easier than ours from Lingnan."

The official roads from the capital were well-connected and smooth all the way to Baling.

"Yes, I rode a horse to Baling, then took a boat here."

Yu Ying pursed her lips. "We came by boat too."

As she spoke, her eyes remained fixed on Pei Ta, her smile as bright as the moon.

After a moment, she lowered her head slightly and coughed softly.

"Last time, Lu Cheng gave me that book. I’ve read it carefully."

Pei Ta looked at her childish demeanor and wished he could reach out and pinch her cheek.

But with Ding Wenxi and Wen Shu watching closely, he merely cleared his throat and said gently, "You must have had a hard journey. I’ve already found a residence in the city, and everything is prepared. You can move in today."

---

chapters.title: Even So
chapters.content:
He had only arrived in Anzhou ten days before them, yet he had already found a place for them?

Yu Ying looked at him in surprise. "Have you settled in already?"

Pei Ta’s eyebrows twitched slightly at her words. He said softly, "I’m staying at the official post house. The residence... I’ll find one later."

After a moment of hesitation, Yu Ying understood his meaning.

Did he mean to wait for her arrival before finding a place?

If he truly married her, that residence would be where they lived together, so it made sense to choose carefully.

Yu Ying’s cheeks flushed slightly. She turned her face away and said quietly, "Don’t just stand here talking. This inn room is small. Let’s go to the teahouse next door and sit for a while."

They had been apart for more than half a year. Many things had happened, and there was indeed much to talk about.

Pei Ta had originally intended to take them to the residence he found, but upon hearing Yu Ying’s suggestion, he nodded. "Shu is famous for its tea, which tastes a bit different. Let me treat you to tea."

Yu Ying followed him out of the inn. Wen Shu had intended to follow, but Ding Wenxi held him back.

"Let them talk alone for a while."

The teahouse was bustling with people, so Ding Wenxi wasn’t worried about them getting too intimate.

Pei Ta’s presence here showed he hadn’t changed his mind about their previous conversation. The two of them must have a lot to say, so letting them go to the teahouse for a while was fine.

Next to the inn was a Songfeng Teahouse, with a dozen or so tables arranged haphazardly, and no private rooms.

However, there weren’t many people drinking tea at the moment. Yu Ying and Pei Ta found a seat by the window, which was relatively quiet. After sitting down, they ordered a pot of tea and four plates of snacks.

Earlier, with Ding Wenxi and Wen Shu present, Pei Ta couldn’t stare at her freely. Although the teahouse was crowded, at least they were the only ones sitting close together.

Pei Ta’s heart was filled with the joy of reunion. He subtly moved closer to her and suddenly lowered his voice. "I missed you very much."

At the riverside that day, he had hastily confessed his feelings and then parted ways. In truth, Yu Ying had many doubts.

If it weren’t for her mother and Wen Shu witnessing that scene, Yu Ying would have almost thought it was a hallucination.

Her mother often nagged, worried that Pei Ta, after returning to the capital and receiving a better position, would change his mind.

Yu Ying often said it didn’t matter whether she married him or not, partly to reassure her mother, and partly to force herself to stay rational.

After so much travel, being able to sit in this teahouse with Pei Ta was no small feat.

Yu Ying lowered her gaze, but her lips still curved into a bright smile.

"So did I."

Her voice was soft, filled with joy.

Hearing her words, Pei Ta’s eyes flickered. He reached out and took her delicate, boneless hand in his, covering it with his wide sleeve.

Yu Ying’s heart pounded wildly. She let him hold her hand for a long while before asking, "Was everything in the capital going well?"

"Yes."

"Did... that person not want to keep you in the capital?"

After all, it wasn’t appropriate to casually mention "His Majesty" in public.

"He did have that intention. Fortunately, there was a vacancy in Western Shu Province, so I volunteered, and he approved."

Yu Ying said, "I think he likes you a lot and wants to promote you. Do you really not regret leaving the capital?"

"Do you want to hear the truth?"

"Mm."

"Apart from you, I indeed don’t want to stay in the capital. The capital is full of nobles and superiors; it’s restrictive everywhere. It’s not as free as being a Surveillance Commissioner in Western Shu."

Western Shu was surrounded by mountains on all sides, making travel inconvenient. However, it was far from a barren and desolate place. Instead, it was rich in resources with favorable weather.

"Moreover, I have you with me."

As he spoke, his palm continued to stroke Yu Ying’s hand, his eyes filled with tender smiles.

Yu Ying whispered, "Then do our previous words still count?"

"Of course. I’ve already thought it through. You can stay temporarily at the place I found. I’ve already asked a real estate agent to look for a residence in the city. He’s told me about several options. I thought we could decide after you’ve seen them. Once the residence is chosen, it will be easier to prepare for the other matters."

"Other matters?"

"The six etiquettes must be complete."

Yu Ying felt a little dazed.

When she had Wen Shu take her onto the boat that day, it had been an impulsive act.

Later, when he had confessed his feelings again and said he wanted to marry her, although she was happy, she had always felt as if she were floating in the air.

Now, sitting in Anzhou with her hand held by him, listening to him talk about choosing a residence and preparing the six etiquettes, Yu Ying suddenly felt: was she really going to marry him?

Before Yu Ying could respond, Pei Ta didn’t continue.

He silently watched Yu Ying, thinking she still had reservations, and tried his best to suppress his own disappointment.

After a long while, he softly said, "If you want to wait a little longer, it’s fine. I can wait for you."

"It’s not that." Yu Ying blurted out, then quickly added, "I’m not in a hurry either. It’s just..."

"Just what?"

"Just..." Yu Ying lowered her head, "It’s a bit hard to believe."

"Why is it hard to believe?"

Yu Ying didn’t look at Pei Ta, only staring at the green tea before her.

"I just can’t believe that you like me, and that you want to marry me."

"How could that be?" Pei Ta said, giving her hand a firm squeeze. "That doesn’t sound like something you’d say."

"Am I usually not modest enough?"

"Of course not, but you don’t underestimate yourself."

"Then I don’t underestimate myself." Yu Ying raised her chin, meeting Pei Ta’s gaze again. "Let me rephrase: I think you’re very good, and I can’t believe that someone as good as you is the one I’ve encountered."

As she spoke, her lively eyes filled with a soft smile, exuding tenderness.

Faced with such a smile, Pei Ta’s carefully calmed emotions were instantly thrown into disarray again.

If this weren’t a bustling teahouse, he would have pulled the person he had been yearning for day and night into his arms.

"It’s my good fortune to have met you."

It truly was good fortune.

During his month-long stay in the capital, he had learned that Zhao Xuanyou had always been concerned about her, and even Prince Rui Zhao Qi was very mindful of Yu Ying’s whereabouts.

If the one who had met Yu Ying first wasn’t him, but them, then whose hand would be holding Yu Ying’s now?

Yu Ying noticed the sudden depth in his gaze and looked at him inquiringly, half-jokingly and half-asking, "Have you changed your mind again?"

"How could I change my mind?"

Pei Ta suppressed his thoughts but when he looked at Yu Ying again, his feelings were different.

"What’s wrong?" Yu Ying asked, confused.

Pei Ta took a deep breath and finally spoke with difficulty.

"Lu Cheng must have told you that the Prince has also returned to the capital."

"You and him... met in the capital?"

Pei Ta nodded.

He was extremely reluctant to mention Zhao Xuanyou in front of Yu Ying, but his nature made it impossible for him to lie to her.

He could deceive others, but he didn’t want to deceive Yu Ying into marrying him.

"You must have also known that he has been sending the Brocade Guards everywhere to look for you."

"I know."

"He mentioned you to me. I could see that he has never let go of you and cares deeply for you."

"What do you want to say?"

Pei Ta tightened his grip on her hand, his gaze dark and profound. "Knowing all this, are you still willing to marry me?"

chapters.title: A Spring Rendezvous
chapters.content:
Yu Yuan’s gaze flickered, and the corners of her lips twitched slightly. "These two matters were originally unrelated."

Pei Tao hesitated for a moment, meeting her eyes before chuckling. "It’s my fault."

Of course, Yu Yuan wouldn’t blame Pei Tao.

Zhao Xuanyou was still searching for her. Regardless of his intentions, he clearly still held a grudge over her faked death and disappearance.

In an instant, memories of the past between her and Zhao Xuanyou flashed through Yu Yuan’s mind.

But it was only a fleeting moment before her emotions returned to normal.

"To me, the past in the Marquis’s mansion feels like a distant dream. I haven’t thought about it in a long time."

Her feud with Cui Yichu was a matter of her past life, and Zhao Xuanyou had been dragged into it by Cui Yichu.

The moment Cui Yichu died, everything had already ended.

After confirming her feelings for Zhao Xuanyou, Pei Tao secretly sighed in relief.

He took Yu Yuan’s hand and said solemnly, "From now on, every day here will be a new beginning."

"Mmm."

"Don’t you want to enter the city with me today?"

Yu Yuan pondered for a moment before voicing her concerns.

"You’ve been the magistrate of Qingzhou for three years, and I’ve been doing business in Qingsha Town. If he finds out, he’ll definitely be suspicious. I still can’t show my face in Anzhou City."

"Then..."

Seeing the tension in his brows, Yu Yuan said, "I’m only saying I should go out less, not that you can’t. Tell me where you’ve found to live. Tomorrow, I’ll take Mother and Ah Chi there myself."

"Then when can we..."

"How about we wait until spring? The weather is too cold now."

Even if the Brocade Guards had extraordinary abilities, they couldn’t stay in the remote land of Shu to monitor them forever.

Presumably, once they confirmed she wasn’t by Pei Tao’s side, it would be fine.

A hint of bitterness appeared in Pei Tao’s eyes.

"Does that mean I won’t be able to see you all winter if you’re hiding at home?"

Yu Yuan, of course, wanted to see him often too.

It’s just...

Seeing Yu Yuan’s troubled expression, Pei Tao exhaled deeply and then smiled. "We’ve been apart for more than half a year. Waiting until next spring isn’t a big deal. Preparing for the wedding will take time anyway."

At the mention of wedding preparations, Yu Yuan’s face turned red. "It’s not like we won’t see each other at all. If there’s something, you can send someone to tell Ah Chi. We can meet at a restaurant or teahouse and talk for a while."

"Is that okay? Your mother seems to be on guard against me."

"Mother is just worried about me."

Yu Yuan understood Ding Wenxi’s concerns. Given her past with Zhao Xuanyou, if she and Pei Tao were too close before marriage, she feared Pei Tao might look down on her.

"You can rest assured, I won’t…"

"I know."

Yu Yuan raised her eyebrows and smiled, reaching into his sleeve to hold his hand.

Thinking that they would have to be cautious from now on, Pei Tao cherished this moment of tenderness and was reluctant to leave the simple teahouse.

He let out a soft sigh.

Everything would be better by spring.

After a few months, Yu Yuan would be his wife, and they could be together day and night.

"I just thought about it. The residence you found; you should move in there. The three of us will go into the city and find our own place."

"Is it necessary to go that far?"

The man in question was Zhao Xuanyou, who could command the Brocade Guards. If they were to be cautious, they had to be thorough.

Pei Tao looked at Yu Yuan’s expression and knew her intentions.

"I understand. I’ll go back first. Once you’ve found a place to stay, remember to tell me."

Even though he was reluctant to leave, he couldn’t stay much longer.

He let go of her hand and stood up, leaving the teahouse.

Only after he had walked far away did Yu Yuan return to the inn.
