As soon as she entered, she saw Ding Wenxi and Wen Chi had already laid out the bedsheets and quilts.

"Yuan Yuan, aren’t we going into the city today?" Ding Wenxi asked.

Yu Yuan shook her head.

"Didn’t Magistrate Pei say he had already found a place for us?"

"I already told him we won’t be staying there. In a couple of days, Ah Chi will go into the city to look around, and we’ll find a suitable place ourselves."

"You don’t want to spend his money?"

Yu Yuan thought about what Pei Tao had said. After much hesitation, she decided to tell the truth.

After all, Mother and Wen Chi were always by her side. If the Brocade Guards were still searching for her, she would need their help to hide her tracks.

"It’s not about the money. He just told me that Zhao Xuanyou has been having the Brocade Guards look for me. When they were in the capital, Zhao Xuanyou even asked him about his time in Qingzhou. Although I haven’t had any contact with Pei Tao over these three years in Qingzhou, Zhao Xuanyou might not believe that."

A cold glint flashed in Wen Chi’s eyes when he heard this.

Ding Wenxi was also startled. After a moment of thought, she said worriedly, "Are you saying that the Prince might have the Brocade Guards come to Shu to investigate your whereabouts?"

"It’s possible."

"Then after running this far, do we still have to live in hiding?"

Yu Yuan comforted her, "The Brocade Guards are not his private army. They might help him investigate for a while, but they won’t stay here forever. Pei Tao and I have discussed it. We’ll avoid this winter, and once spring comes, we’ll get married. I’m afraid I won’t be able to go out often, so I’ll have to trouble Mother and Ah Chi to handle many things for me."

At the mention of marriage, Ding Wenxi finally showed a hint of joy.

"Family doesn’t mind trouble. Yuan Yuan, you’ve decided to get married in the spring?"

Yu Yuan nodded.

"The exact date still needs to be chosen by a fortune teller, but Pei Tao probably doesn’t want to wait too long."

"It’s better to do it early. Once you marry him, even if you go out less, it won’t matter."

"It’s already the Beginning of Winter. The Beginning of Spring isn’t far off. These days won’t be idle either. I’ve heard that brides are supposed to embroider their own dowry. I don’t know how to embroider."

"What’s there to fear? Your mother is here."

Yu Yuan was not skilled in needlework, but Ding Wenxi had nimble fingers. Not only could she make jewelry, but she was also adept at embroidery and sewing.

Ding Wenxi never expected to be able to prepare a dowry for Yu Yuan.

She immediately decided to make a headdress for Yu Yuan with her own hands.

With that in mind, she went to the adjacent room to draw a design with paper and brush.

Yu Yuan turned around and saw Wen Chi still standing in the room, a hint of worry in his eyes.

"What are you thinking about? Aren’t you happy for me?"

Wen Chi stepped forward and closed the door. Turning back to look at Yu Yuan, he said, "If the Brocade Guards are looking for you, we really need to be cautious."

"They’ve been searching for three years and haven’t found me, so it’ll be fine as long as we’re careful," Yu Yuan said, knowing he was worried about her. She smiled and reassured him.

"Mmm." Wen Chi secretly clenched his fingers.

He had some knowledge of the previous incident where the Crown Prince had tried to abduct Yu Yuan. He knew that Zhao Xuanyou was the kind of person who would never give up until he achieved his goal.

If Zhao Xuanyou found Yu Yuan, he would definitely find a way to take her away.

After all this time practicing lightness skills and hidden weapons, perhaps it was for this very day.

He didn’t say much more, only repeating Yu Yuan’s words: "It’ll be fine."

---

chapters.title: Another New Year's Eve
chapters.content:
Wen Chi’s voice was low, and Yu Yuan didn’t pay much attention at first. But when she turned to see his expression, she felt something was amiss.

"Don’t forget the trouble we encountered at Wei Wu’s place."

Wen Chi certainly remembered.

He had long since vowed never to let Yu Yuan and himself fall into such a predicament again.

"No matter what happens, we must take care of ourselves first, understand?"

Wen Chi knitted his brows tightly, refusing to speak. Yu Yuan, however, stared at him intently.

Unable to bear her gaze, Wen Chi finally said, "I understand."

Yu Yuan was afraid he didn’t truly mean it, so she added, "You’re fast on your feet. If something really happens, you run first. Then you can find a chance to save me later. If both of us fall, Mother won’t be able to save us."

Although she said this with a teasing tone, she wasn’t joking.

Wen Chi thought for a moment before finally nodding. "I understand."

Only after getting his word did Yu Yuan feel slightly at ease.

After all, she had seen Pei Tao today and had such a long conversation with him. She was still happy.

She then told Wen Chi her plan. Wen Chi would go into the city first to find a place to stay. It shouldn’t be on the same street as the place Pei Tao had found, but it shouldn’t be too far either.

Wen Chi was quite experienced with such tasks and quickly found a suitable residence, which he purchased directly.

He claimed to be a man who had returned from the Southern Ocean to search for relatives, only to find that they had already passed away. Since he owned property locally, his family was able to settle and obtain household registration.

However, they could no longer use the surname Ding. Ding Wenxi’s maternal family surname was Song, so Yu Yuan changed her name from Ding Yuan to Song Yu.

When they left Qingsha Town, Yu Yuan had only taken books and valuables with her. Now that she was getting married, everything had to be prepared from scratch.

Even if they couldn’t prepare dozens of dowry chests like wealthy families, they still needed jewelry, hair ornaments, silk fabrics, and tea cakes.

Wen Chi was in charge of purchasing household items like pots and pans, while Ding Wenxi personally made the headdress, jewelry, wedding dress, and quilt.

Seeing how busy the two of them were, even though Yu Yuan wasn’t skilled in needlework, she still helped Ding Wenxi as much as she could.

Pei Tao had just arrived in Shu and was unfamiliar with many matters in the government office, so the handover kept him busy.

The two of them could only meet four or five times a month. In the blink of an eye, New Year’s Eve had passed, and on the night of the Lantern Festival, Yu Yuan was sitting in front of her dressing table, combing her hair. Wen Chi knocked on her window.

"He’s here."

Yu Yuan was arranging her hair. "Ah," she said, "It’s not even dark yet. Why is he here so early?"

Wen Chi curled his lip and didn’t say anything.

Yu Yuan looked back at the mirror and stuck a flower-shaped ornament on her forehead. She swayed left and right in front of the mirror before changing the jade hairpin in her hair to a gold one.

On the night of the Lantern Festival, with the brilliant lanterns, wearing a jade hairpin seemed a bit too plain.

"Wen Chi, does this look good?" Yu Yuan stood up and walked to the window.

Wen Chi looked up at her carefully dressed appearance and said helplessly, "You’re going to wear a mask anyway. Does it matter if it looks good or not?"

"Well... he can still see me for a moment."

"It looks good."

Seeing Wen Chi’s lack of enthusiasm, Yu Yuan asked, "Do you want to go out tonight?"

"Do you want me to follow you?" Wen Chi asked strangely.

"Tonight, many young girls will be out for a night stroll. If you go out for a walk, you might meet your destined one."

Wen Chi didn’t respond and simply turned his face away.

Yu Yuan knew he didn’t like talking about this, so she reached out and patted his shoulder.

"I mean, you can go out for a while."

"Magistrate Pei is waiting for you. Hurry up and go out," Wen Chi said.

"I know."

Yu Yuan, afraid of keeping Pei Tao waiting, picked up the prepared fox mask from the table, draped a cloak over herself, and walked out.

Pei Tao, waiting outside, called out "Yuer" when he saw her, his gaze fixed firmly on her.

It was the dead of winter, and Yu Yuan wore a warm cloak made of precious Shu brocade, embroidered with hibiscus flowers. It matched her delicate and graceful demeanor perfectly. It was a gift Pei Tao had given her some days ago.

Seeing the flash of admiration in his eyes, Yu Yuan contentedly put on her mask.

She had spent so much time dressing up just for this moment.

Afraid she might catch a cold from the wind, Pei Tao reached out to put the hood on for her.

Yu Yuan asked, "Shall we go to the lantern market now?"

"We can walk slowly. By the time we get there, it should be dark."

Yu Yuan nodded and quietly took his hand.

On the Lantern Festival, young men and women were allowed to go out and enjoy themselves. With both of them wearing masks, no one would mind if they were a little more affectionate.

A slight smile also appeared on Pei Tao’s face. After putting on his mask, he walked side by side with her toward the lantern market.

Even though they were still some distance away from the lantern market, every household had hung up lanterns. Many people, like them, had come out early. The air was filled with the scent of perfume and the rustling of fine clothing, a dazzling and colorful scene.

"Have you eaten any glutinous rice balls today?" Yu Yuan asked.

"The new cook I hired has good skills. She’s from Jiangnan, so the food she makes should suit your taste."

Half a month ago, Pei Tao had chosen a residence and drawn a general layout of the courtyard to show Yu Yuan. She had liked it very much, so he bought it as their future home.

Hearing that Pei Tao had thought so carefully, Yu Yuan felt a sweet warmth in her heart.

"Last time you mentioned, was that door opened?"

Yu Yuan and Ding Wenxi were dependent on each other. Even after marriage, she didn’t want to be separated from her mother.

So Pei Tao had thought of giving Ding Wenxi the courtyard next to the street to live in. Inside, it would still be connected to the inner residence, but a new door would be opened from the outside, maintaining the appearance of separate households.

"The door frame was installed today. We just need to add furniture."

Pei Tao was eager to marry Yu Yuan, so he had given extra silver to the craftsmen to speed up the work.

Houses in Shu were far less expensive than in the capital, but the residence he had bought was not small. Adding furniture and servants would be quite costly.

Even though it was a bit presumptuous, Yu Yuan still asked, "Do you have enough money?"

Seeing Pei Tao’s slight surprise, Yu Yuan quickly said, "I mean, my dowry isn’t much. If there’s anything else needed for the house, I can buy it."

"Do you think I’m penniless?" Pei Tao listened to her cautious tone and couldn’t help but say in a low voice, "Yuer, don’t worry. I won’t let you live a hard life with me."

"I didn’t mean that," Yu Yuan muttered.

She actually did mean that.

After Pei Tao’s father was wronged and imprisoned, his family’s assets had been squandered because of the incident.

Although he was now a third-rank official in the imperial court, his salary wasn’t high. Without ancestral property and not being a corrupt official, how could he have much money on hand?

Pei Tao stopped in his tracks and seriously said to Yu Yuan, "We’re about to get married. There are some things I should have told you earlier."

"Do you still have any farmland?"

"No, but have you forgotten what I do?"

Yu Yuan narrowed her eyes and thought for a moment. "You’re a famous handsome man in the capital?"

But no matter how handsome he was, it wouldn’t bring in money.

Pei Tao couldn’t help but laugh when he heard this. "Think again."

"Are you... a zhuangyuan?"

"Now you’re getting it. That’s right."

But Yu Yuan was still confused.

Even if he was a zhuangyuan, the imperial court only granted official positions, not money.

Yu Yuan couldn’t figure it out, so she pretended to be annoyed. "Just tell me."

chapters.title: Behind the Mask
chapters.content:
Listening to Yu Wan’s voice, half playful and half pleased, Pei Tuo’s eyebrows twitched slightly.

“When I was studying at Luming Academy, a classmate of mine ran the largest bookshop in Jiangnan. His family business was thriving. That year, during the provincial examination, he failed while I ranked high. He believed I would become a jinshi in the future, so he discussed with me the idea of selling the essays and policy critiques I had written to his family’s bookshop.”

“So that’s how it was. But you sold them when you were still a juren candidate. Didn’t you lose out later when you became the top scholar?”

Pei Tuo smiled. “No wonder you used to be a boss; you think far ahead.”

“Don’t tease me. I just think you got the short end of the stick.”

“Actually, I didn’t. Back then, I was just a poor scholar, short on silver for the journey to the capital for the imperial examination. That money solved my urgent need and kept me from looking too destitute.”

“That’s true.”

Pei Tuo continued, “After I was fortunate enough to be chosen as the top scholar by His Majesty, many bookshops came to me. My classmate then offered me an exclusive deal; whatever profits my books made each year, they would give me half.”

“Your classmate does business quite fairly.”

Yu Wan, of course, understood why he was being so generous.

Pei Tuo was a promising top scholar. Though his classmate was wealthy, he was still a merchant. How could he dare to take advantage of the emperor’s favored man?

“Others see my official career as promising, so my books sell well. I earn several hundred taels of silver each year from them.”

It was also with the money from the bookshop that Pei Tuo had managed to buy a house in the capital, where land was as precious as gold.

“Yu’er, I may not compare to the dukes and noble families of the capital, but I will never let you suffer.”

Yu Wan could hear the implication in his words and couldn’t help but smile. “Of course. Actually, over these three years in Qingsha Town, I’ve earned quite a bit; enough for us to spend in Anzhou.”

Since Pei Tuo had already spoken of his finances, Yu Wan naturally had to mention her own.

However, the silver earned by the Jade Pavilion wasn’t just hers; her mother and Wen Shuo had shares too.

Pei Tuo said softly, “You just prepare your dowry at home. Leave the house to me; I’ll handle it, so you don’t have to worry. I’ve already consulted a fortune teller for an auspicious date. They all say the 25th of the second month is good. What do you think? Is it too soon?”

Hearing his rapid questions, Yu Wan, behind her mask, couldn’t help but purse her lips.

“I think it’s fine, but I still need to tell my mother before it’s settled.”

Her mother had always hoped she would marry soon; she would surely agree.

Yu Wan didn’t want to accept immediately; that would make her seem too eager.

“Good. When I take you back tonight, I’ll tell your mother myself.”

Yu Wan nodded. “Anyway, all the troublesome things are up to you. I’ll just wait peacefully for you to come and marry me.”

Listening to her soft voice, Pei Tuo could easily imagine the expression beneath her mask.

His heart trembled slightly, and suddenly, he leaned down and kissed her lightly through the mask.

---

A thousand miles away, in the capital, the city was adorned with lanterns and shimmering lights.

The emperor had grown increasingly fond of Zhao Yi Yun lately. To please his grandson, he had ordered the Imperial Household Department to set up a three-story lantern tower outside the palace gates.

Though one couldn’t climb the tower, each level was hung with colorful lanterns crafted by skilled artisans, dazzling in their variety and beauty.

Not only that, but the emperor had also invited the capital’s nobles to ascend the palace gate’s city wall to admire the spectacular lanterns together.

As the emperor held Zhao Yi Yun and played with him, Liu Quan stepped forward. “Your Majesty, the empress has arrived with someone.”

The emperor gave a slight nod. “Call Zhao Qi over.”

Liu Quan bowed and withdrew, quickly returning with Zhao Qi.

For some reason, Zhao Yi Yun was very fond of Zhao Qi. As soon as he saw him, he affectionately called out, “Uncle Qi,” and asked to be held.

Zhao Qi reached out and pinched his cheek, then cautiously glanced at the emperor.

“Father Emperor, do you want me to take Yi Yun to play?”

“He has a wet nurse. Why would he need you?” The emperor said irritably, then looked up and saw the empress leading a girl of about fifteen or sixteen toward them. He smiled. “Go greet your mother.”

Zhao Qi reluctantly turned and bowed to the empress. “This son greets Mother.”

“Thee need not stand on ceremony, Qi’er. Today is the Lantern Festival; just relax.”

“Empress, who is this young lady?” the emperor asked.

The empress pulled the girl forward and smiled. “In response to Your Majesty, this is Liang Xiaofeng, daughter of Liang Xuan, the newly appointed Assistant Minister of Justice.”

“This humble girl greets Your Majesty. May you live ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years.”

Liang Xiaofeng was a year younger than Zhao Qi. She had skin like snow and features as delicate as a painting; truly like a luminous pearl, with an exceptionally striking appearance.

But she was still young, and this was her first time meeting the emperor, so there was a trace of unease in her expression.

The emperor glanced at her and silently approved.

Previously, Zhao Qi had been picky about the noble ladies, likely wanting to marry an absolute beauty.

Seeing the emperor’s satisfaction, the empress said, “Xiaofeng, this is Prince Rui.”

“This humble girl greets Your Highness.”

Though she wasn’t born in the capital, her manners were impeccable.

The empress said, “Qi’er, why don’t you show Xiaofeng around?”

Liang Xiaofeng’s beauty was unmatched in the capital, or at least among the best. The empress assumed Zhao Qi would surely take a liking to her.

The emperor looked at Zhao Qi, who, upon seeing the empress bring a young lady over, understood the emperor’s intention in calling him. But facing the emperor’s gaze, he pretended to be oblivious and stood silently to the side.

“Zhao Qi.” The emperor, seeing that he was ignoring the empress’s suggestion, raised his voice.

Zhao Qi knew his father was angry. Reluctantly, he said, “This son obeys.”

He glanced at Liang Xiaofeng and lazily said, “Let’s go.”

Liang Xiaofeng had initially been confused as to why the empress had suddenly brought her to meet the emperor, but upon hearing that Prince Rui was to show her around, she understood the intention.

She bowed to the emperor and empress, then followed Zhao Qi away.

The city wall was crowded, and Zhao Qi walked quickly through the throng. Liang Xiaofeng had to hurry to keep up.

When they were finally a bit farther from the crowd, Zhao Qi stopped.

Liang Xiaofeng, a well-behaved young lady, was slightly out of breath from the brisk walk.

She nervously looked around at the sparse crowd and glanced at Zhao Qi.

Zhao Qi’s expression was unreadable.

He wasn’t blind; he could see that Liang Xiaofeng was an absolute beauty.

But he could also see that the emperor was very pleased with her, even arranging for them to meet on the Lantern Festival.

Clearly, this wasn’t a woman he could dismiss with a few words, as he had before.

He said coldly, “Is this your first time in the palace?”

“A few days ago, I came to the Kunning Palace with my mother, but this is my first time here.” She could tell Zhao Qi was in a bad mood and grew even more nervous. Looking around, she softly said, “The palace walls are built so high. Standing here, you can see the entire capital.”

Yes, the palace walls were even taller than the city walls. Standing here, one could indeed overlook the entire capital’s Lantern Festival lights.

Zhao Qi recalled the nights he had spent talking with Yu Wan on the city wall.

If only the person standing here with him now were Yu Wan, how wonderful that would be.

---

chapters.title: Why Not Cooperate?
chapters.content:
Palace attendants had placed many charcoal braziers along the city wall, so even with the cold night wind, it didn’t feel chilly standing there.

Liang Xiaofeng saw that Zhao Qi still wasn’t speaking and didn’t dare say more.

Having received the emperor and empress’s approval, she had been happy at first.

Zhao Qi was of noble status, close to her in age, and carried the bold, sharp aura of youth. Though she couldn’t say she was immediately smitten, she did feel a certain fondness for him.

But after standing here in silence for a moment, she realized Zhao Qi had no interest in her.

“This humble girl won’t disturb Your Highness any longer.”

“Don’t go.” Zhao Qi said.

His father had already been angered earlier. If he didn’t at least pretend to show her around for a while, it would only displease his father further.

Anyway, he had already been enfeoffed as a prince. It was better not to clash with his father now. Once the first month was over, he could immediately retreat to his fief to avoid him.

Liang Xiaofeng had no choice but to lower her head and say, “Yes.”

“Where… would you like to go?” Zhao Qi asked.

“This humble girl is new here. Everywhere seems wonderful.”

Zhao Qi exhaled deeply, glanced at the distant emperor and empress, and led Liang Xiaofeng forward.

After a few steps, they soon saw a tall, slender figure; it was Zhao Xuanyou.

On the Lantern Festival, with the entire city ablaze with lights, Zhao Xuanyou stood alone here. It was clear who he was thinking of.

Zhao Qi felt a rare sense of shared misery and called out, “Lord Zhao.”

Zhao Xuanyou turned around, saw Zhao Qi standing with a beautiful young girl, and cupped his hands in greeting.

“Your Highness.”

“This place is quiet. Lord Zhao, you’re quite at leisure.”

“Aren’t you the same, Your Highness?”

Zhao Qi looked at Liang Xiaofeng. “This is Zhao Xuanyou, Lord Zhao, the heir of the Jingyuan Marquis.”

“Greetings, Lord Zhao.” Liang Xiaofeng curtsied to Zhao Xuanyou and introduced herself. “My father is Liang Xuan, Assistant Minister of Justice.”

“Miss Liang.”

The Jingyuan Marquis’s household was highly respected. Zhao Xuanyou, when he was in the capital, was invited to the palace every year to admire the lanterns. This place was indeed quiet, with few people coming by.

The Lantern Festival was a rare day when young men and women could go out together. Zhao Xuanyou, alone and shadowed, looked at the dazzling streets and couldn’t help but feel a sense of things are the same, but the people are not.

Over the past three years, his mood had been poor, and because of Zhao Qi’s past actions, helping Yu Wan fake her death and escape, he had been unwilling to say much.

“I won’t disturb the two of you. I take my leave.”

Before Zhao Qi could speak, Zhao Xuanyou walked away.

“Wait.” Zhao Qi, seeing him leave, abandoned Liang Xiaofeng and chased after him.

Zhao Xuanyou stopped and glanced at him. “Today is the Lantern Festival. Your Highness should enjoy the holiday. There’s no need to seek unpleasantness.”

His tone was extremely blunt.

Zhao Qi knew that if it weren’t for the fact that they were on the palace gate’s city wall, Zhao Xuanyou might even have punched him.

But he had to stop him.

Ever since he learned in spring that Yu Wan had been hiding in Qingsha Town for the past three years, Zhao Qi had sent more people to Ice Cloud to investigate her whereabouts starting from Qingsha Town. But after all this time, they had found nothing.

He could only stop Zhao Xuanyou, hoping to find a clue from him.

“Tell me, where do you think she is now?” Zhao Qi said softly.

Zhao Xuanyou had been suppressing his anger for a long time. Hearing Zhao Qi bring this up, his long-repressed fury surged, and a hint of killing intent flashed in his eyes.

“I should be the one asking you that!”

Zhao Qi knew his words would provoke him, but that was his intention.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s expression change abruptly, his anger flaring, Zhao Qi understood; Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t found Yu Wan either.

He coughed twice, trying to make his tone sound lighter.

“Do you think she’s been happy these past three years in Qingsha Town?” Zhao Qi sighed heavily. “She must be. She’s that kind of person; no matter what, she’ll take good care of herself.”

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t respond.

But he knew Zhao Qi was telling the truth.

Yu Wan hadn’t been forced to leave the capital. She had planned her fake death and escape.

With her beloved mother by her side, money in hand, a skilled man protecting them, and a successful jewelry shop, she must have been living very comfortably.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s silence, Zhao Qi continued, “Actually, when she first came to me, I was very surprised. Out of nowhere, she suddenly wanted to do something so drastic, and then suddenly wanted to leave you. It was completely unexpected.”

At the time, Zhao Qi had been far away in the southeast. Zhao Xuanyou had never confronted him in person and didn’t know how he and Yu Wan had conspired.

Hearing Zhao Qi speak, his gaze flickered, and he looked at Zhao Qi intently.

“What did she tell you?”

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou had finally spoken, Zhao Qi’s thoughts returned to the city wall three years ago.

“She said Cui Yichu hated her deeply and had tried to kill her repeatedly. She asked me to leave two of my men in the capital to protect her when I left.”

Those two were Ice Cloud and Yangquan.

“She didn’t tell you she was leaving?”

“She did.” The night he had spent with Yu Wan replayed in Zhao Qi’s mind countless times. Every word she had said was crystal clear. “She said she wanted to use my people to deal with Cui Yichu. Once it was done, she would leave the capital with her mother. Her mother was used to living in the countryside and didn’t like staying in the capital. They wanted to find a quiet place to live.”

“Just that?”

Zhao Qi met Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze and understood what he wanted to ask.

“Of course, she mentioned you.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart suddenly tightened.

A storm brewed in his deep eyes. He suppressed the dull pain in his heart and stared straight at Zhao Qi.

“She said you would soon marry, that the marquis’s residence wasn’t her home, and that sooner or later, she would have no place there. It would be better to leave early rather than stay.”

Was it because he was going to marry?

Zhao Xuanyou clenched his fingers tightly.

When he had mentioned it to her before, she had seemed indifferent, even saying that Feng Jirou was a good match.

She had cared about Cui Yichu being alive, she had cared about him marrying. But why could she speak frankly to Zhao Qi and not to him?

In her heart, was he really not even as important as Zhao Qi?

“I’ve told you the truth. Now it’s your turn to tell me something.”

“What do you want to hear?” Zhao Xuanyou forcibly cut off his thoughts and regained his composure.

“You were the first to discover she was in Qingsha Town. You must have other leads. We both want to find her. Why not cooperate? We can set aside all our grievances until we find her.”

Zhao Xuanyou had no intention of cooperating with Zhao Qi.

He coldly said, “I wasn’t the first to know Yu Wan was in Qingsha Town. Pei Tuo was.”

“Pei Tuo?” Zhao Qi asked in shock.

Previously, when he had lamented Yu Wan’s disappearance, Pei Tuo had seemed to offer a few words of comfort.

“You didn’t know? The Qingsha Town where Yu Wan is… is in Qingzhou, where Pei Tuo served as prefect.”

“Has he been with Yu Wan these past three years?”

Zhao Xuanyou said nothing, his face cold.

He had sent people to monitor Pei Tuo in Shu for a while but hadn’t noticed anything unusual.

Zhao Qi racked his brain, recalling his encounters with Pei Tuo in the capital. The more he thought, the stranger it seemed. He muttered, “Could his insistence on going to Shu be related to Yu Wan?”

“What? Wasn’t going to Shu arranged by the Ministry of Personnel?”

Zhao Xuanyou had previously assumed that Pei Tuo had been sent to Shu because he was being sidelined by Premier Sun.

Zhao Qi’s gaze fell on the lonely figure of Liang Xiaofeng in the distance. “At first, Father Emperor was determined to make Pei Tuo Assistant Minister of Justice, but he repeatedly declined, begging Father Emperor to let him go to Shu as an official. I was there at the time, and I thought it was strange.”

Insisting on going to the remote land of Shu…

Zhao Xuanyou’s breath suddenly caught.

chapters.title: The Qin-Jin Alliance
chapters.content:
The city of Anzhou, though not as grand as the capital, was bustling with lively lantern markets thanks to the naturally optimistic and pleasure-loving people of Shu. The lantern market was as vibrant as the one in the capital.

Pei Tuo took Yu Wan to guess lantern riddles and play the game of pitching arrows into a vase. By the time he escorted her home, he was carrying three lanterns in his hands.

One was a carp lantern she had chosen herself, and the other two lotus lanterns were prizes Pei Tuo had won from guessing riddles.

Seeing that Yu Wan’s hands were full, Pei Tuo softly asked, “Do you really not need my help carrying them?”

“No.”

Yu Wan happily admired the lanterns in her hands.

Though she had lived two lifetimes, it was only today that she truly experienced what the Lantern Festival should be like.

Since the lanterns were won by Pei Tuo for her, she naturally wanted to carry them herself.

“I’ll hang this one by my window, and have Ah Jiang hang the other two on the trees in the courtyard.”

Since she refused to let go, Pei Tuo could only wrap his arm around her shoulders.

Watching her proud expression, he smiled and asked, “You like them that much?”

“Of course.”

“This year has been too busy, and I didn’t have time to prepare. Next Lantern Festival, I’ll make one for you myself.”

“You know how to make lanterns?” Yu Wan asked in surprise.

“I don’t, but I know how to make kites. Making lanterns shouldn’t be too difficult.”

If anyone else had said this, Yu Wan would have thought they were boasting, but coming from Pei Tuo, she believed him.

He was so clever; if he wanted to learn, he would certainly master it.

“You said it, and I’m holding you to it.”

“Mm, I’ll go find some books later and start studying in advance.”

Yu Wan had been wearing a fox mask all evening, so she didn’t need to hide her smile.

“You should first focus on our wedding.”

“As you command.”

As they spoke, the two had already arrived at Yu Wan’s doorstep.

Thinking that they would be married next month, Pei Tuo was no longer reluctant to part. Instead, he wished time would pass more quickly.

He raised his hand and knocked on the door. Soon, Wen Jiang came to answer.

Seeing the lanterns in Yu Wan’s hands, Wen Jiang asked, “Where do you want to hang them?”

Yu Wan handed him the two lotus lanterns. “Help me hang them on the tree.”

Wen Jiang responded with an “Oh,” and took the lotus lanterns.

“Is my mother asleep?”

“She’s in the house, the light’s still on.”

Yu Wan finally freed her hands to link arms with Pei Tuo. Softly, she said, “Let’s go inside and talk first.”

He had said himself that he needed to inform Ding Wenxi about the wedding date. Naturally, Yu Wan wouldn’t do it for him.

After entering the courtyard, Wen Jiang leapt onto the large tree and hung up the lotus lanterns.

In the winter, the branches were dry, but before the New Year, many small red lanterns had been hung as decorations. With the addition of the large lotus lanterns, the tree immediately looked more lively and vibrant.

Yu Wan, arm in arm with Pei Tuo, entered the main house and had him sit down. She then went to her boudoir to hang up the carp lantern before heading to Ding Wenxi’s room.

“Mother, why are you still making jewelry? It’s too hard on your eyes at night.”

“Other families’ daughters start preparing their dowry from birth. Since yours is so rushed, I naturally have to hurry and make some.”

“We can buy whatever is missing.”

“A dowry must be prepared by the maternal family. How can we buy everything from outside?”

“We won’t be separated in the future. Mother can slowly make them for me.”

Ding Wenxi set down her work and pulled Yu Wan to sit beside her. “Did you have fun today?”

Yu Wan nodded. Remembering that Pei Tuo was waiting in the main house, she said, “Mother, he’s here. He says he has something to tell you.”

After moving to Anzhou, Yu Wan’s family had kept a low profile, rarely going out. All their errands were run by Wen Jiang.

Whenever Yu Wan met Pei Tuo, she would carefully wear a veil and meet him at the restaurant. Naturally, Ding Wenxi had never met Pei Tuo before.

Seeing her daughter’s shy demeanor, Ding Wenxi could guess why Pei Tuo had come.

“I see. You go out and make him some tea first.”

Since this was a meeting with her future son-in-law, her casual attire was not formal enough. She naturally needed to change her clothes.

“Mm.”

Yu Wan nodded and left. She saw Pei Tuo sitting in the house and Wen Jiang standing at the door. Neither of them was speaking.

“Yu’er, has your mother gone to bed?”

“Not yet.” As she spoke, Yu Wan reached for the teapot.

Seeing her about to pour tea, Pei Tuo took the teapot from her hands and poured it himself.

“I see this house isn’t very big, but you’ve decorated it quite comfortably.”

“We had Ah Jiang find a small house on purpose. Since it’s just the three of us, a smaller place is easier to manage.”

Pei Tuo already knew that Wen Jiang was the Eastern Palace secret guard who had once kidnapped Yu Wan. Seeing how close he was to Yu Wan now, like family, he couldn’t help but marvel at the mysterious workings of fate.

The two sat and chatted idly for a while before Ding Wenxi, now properly dressed, emerged from the inner room.

Pei Tuo then composed himself, stood up, and respectfully bowed to her.

“Madam.”

Ding Wenxi smiled and nodded.

Yu Wan waited until her mother was seated before blushingly stepping behind her.

“My family’s fortunes have declined, but fortunately, the traditions of poetry and propriety remain. I am currently studying for the imperial examinations. I have long admired your daughter and now seek to marry her. I hope you will grant my request.”

Looking at the refined and elegant Pei Tuo before her, and thinking of Yu Wan’s future being secured, Ding Wenxi was naturally delighted. She agreed on the spot.

Originally, Pei Tuo had promised to marry Yu Wan with the six rites, but due to Zhao Xuanyou’s pursuit of Yu Wan, they had to keep things discreet and simplify the process.

Now, they exchanged tokens, and the matter was settled.

As it was late at night, Pei Tuo couldn’t stay long and rose to take his leave.

Yu Wan had intended to see him out, but Ding Wenxi held her back. Helpless, Yu Wan could only smile at Pei Tuo.

Wen Jiang, who had been standing at the door all this time, finally turned around and escorted Pei Tuo out of the courtyard.

However, as soon as Pei Tuo left the courtyard, Wen Jiang did not close the door. Instead, he followed him out.

Pei Tuo noticed that Wen Jiang had something to say, so he didn’t leave immediately. Instead, he quietly watched him.

“Lord Pei.” Wen Jiang hesitated for a moment before slowly speaking.

“Feel free to speak your mind.”

“I…” Wen Jiang kept his voice low. “I am nothing to Yu Wan. There are some things I shouldn’t say, but it’s better to lay everything out in the open.”

“Indeed.”

Although in Anzhou, Yu Wan had always relied on Wen Jiang to pass messages, every time Wen Jiang met Pei Tuo, he was concise and to the point, never wasting words.

In Pei Tuo’s eyes, Wen Jiang carried an air of mystery as well.

“Yu Wan… she likes you very much.” Wen Jiang paused before adding, “With her personality, if she didn’t like you very much, she wouldn’t marry you.”

“Then I am honored.”

“She is happy now, and I am happy for her. But you must never let her down, deceive her, or make her sad and cry.”

Yu Wan, though clever, was now completely taken with Pei Tuo and thought everything about him was perfect.

Ding Wenxi, though fond of nagging, was soft-hearted and couldn’t bring herself to say anything harsh.

As the only man in the household, even if Wen Jiang disliked speaking, he had to step forward and say something.

“I do not take my proposal lightly. If I break my word, Brother Wen, you are welcome to come and hold me accountable.”

Wen Jiang casually raised his hand, and Pei Tuo felt something whiz past his eyes before hitting the tree with a thud.

He turned his head and saw that the trunk of the large tree had been pierced through by something, leaving a small hole.

“Remember your words, or else, you’ll end up like this tree.”

---

chapters.title: Welcoming the Bride
chapters.content:
After the Lantern Festival, Yu Wan did not go out again. She stayed at home, content to prepare for her wedding.

By the twenty-fifth day of the second month, the weather was just beginning to warm, with thin clouds in the sky and a bright spring sun like a painted face.

Yu Wan had woken up before dawn, and Ding Wenxi personally combed and styled her hair.

“First comb from head to tail, second comb for white hair to the eyebrows, third comb for a house full of children and grandchildren…”

Listening to her mother’s auspicious words, Yu Wan pursed her lips as she looked at herself in the mirror, her eyes filled with tenderness.

Not only her phoenix crown, but even her wedding dress had been stitched and embroidered by Ding Wenxi herself.

Though the patterns on the hem were not as exquisite as those made by professional embroiderers, the tailoring was perfect, making Yu Wan’s figure appear tall and graceful, radiant and dignified.

After Yu Wan was fully dressed, she lifted her skirt and turned in front of the mirror. When she turned back to Ding Wenxi, she found tears in her mother’s eyes.

“Mother, don’t be sad. I’m not marrying far away. We’ll still live together, and we can see each other every day.”

“I’m not sad.”

Rather than saying she was reluctant to let her daughter go, Ding Wenxi was happier for her daughter.

Back then, when she had fallen from the cliff and was unconscious, Yu Wan had sold their family property to take her to the capital for treatment, and in the end, even sold herself into servitude at the Marquis’s mansion.

Now, Yu Wan had cured her illness and found a satisfactory husband. It was truly a case of suffering giving way to happiness.

“Wanwan, you have found a good home. I am happy for you.”

The groom had not yet arrived to welcome the bride, so she had to restrain her emotions.

The sound of drums and music grew louder from outside, and Wen Jiang knocked on the door from the outside.

“The wedding procession has arrived.”

Yu Wan had originally wanted to keep things simple, but Pei Tuo said that since they had skipped so many of the six rites, the wedding and the ceremony must not be neglected. They had to go through with the formalities.

“I’ll go out first.” Ding Wenxi said and left the room.

Wen Jiang pushed the door open and entered. Seeing Yu Wan in her bright red wedding dress, he was slightly taken aback.

“Do I look nice?” Yu Wan asked, her eyes full of joy.

“Yes.”

Wen Jiang walked forward, picked up the flower fan from the table, and handed it to her.

After Yu Wan used the fan to cover her face, he took her hand and led her outside.

“Watch the doorsill.”

In the main room, Ding Wenxi, dressed in her finest, sat in the place of honor. Pei Tuo stood in the middle of the room. His usual plain and simple clothes had been replaced with a bright red wedding robe, and his handsome features were filled with joy.

When Wen Jiang led Yu Wan out, Pei Tuo moved slightly to the side, took Yu Wan’s hand from Wen Jiang, and led her to bow and present tea to Ding Wenxi as a farewell.

Ding Wenxi was naturally pleased with this marriage, and at this moment, she was crying tears of joy.

After drinking the tea, Ding Wenxi gave the couple her heartfelt advice.

Earlier, Yu Wan had been comforting her mother, telling her not to be sad, but hearing these words, her own eyes gradually grew warm.

Pei Tuo, noticing Yu Wan’s sadness, secretly squeezed her fingers.

Feeling the warmth from his fingertips, Yu Wan’s heart settled slightly.

The bridesmaid beside them laughed, “The auspicious time has come. The bride should enter the sedan chair.”

Pei Tuo helped Yu Wan to her feet and led her outside. A crowd of neighbors had already gathered outside to watch the spectacle.

Lu Cheng, Lu Jie, and others who had accompanied Pei Tuo to welcome the bride were distributing candies and pastries to the crowd.

Amid the congratulations of the crowd, Pei Tuo helped Yu Wan into the sedan chair.

“Lift the sedan chair…”

At the bridesmaid’s command, the gongs, drums, and string instruments played in unison.

Pei Tuo mounted his horse, followed by Yu Wan’s sedan chair and the musical troupe. His subordinates and guards walked on either side of the procession to prevent anyone from bumping into it.

Wen Jiang followed alongside Yu Wan’s sedan chair with the bridesmaid.

A woman eating a pastry by the roadside curiously asked, “That groom is too handsome. He looks like an official.”

“I just asked his subordinates. He’s the new Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan Province, Lord Pei Tuo.”

“Lord Pei is impressive. He’s an imperial scholar personally selected by His Majesty.”

“How did he come to marry a bride from our street? That family rarely goes out, keeping to themselves. Who would have thought they’d produce an official’s wife?”

“I heard they returned from the Southern Ocean. Maybe they’re old acquaintances of Lord Pei.”

“The bride covered her face with a fan when she came out, but judging by her figure, she must be a great beauty.”

“Of course. Otherwise, how could Lord Pei have chosen her?”

The wedding procession took a different route back, symbolizing “not retracing one’s steps.” The entire way was filled with music and lively noise.

The onlookers on both sides, seeing the distinguished groom on horseback, also expressed their admiration.

Yu Wan sat upright in the sedan chair, listening to the noise outside, and let out a soft sigh.

She set the fan aside and took out a mutton-fat jade pendant from her body.

It was the betrothal gift Pei Tuo had given her, engraved with the words “White-Headed Together,” the characters bold and elegant, carved by a craftsman following his handwriting.

After today, she would be Pei Tuo’s lawfully wedded wife, Song Yu.

She trusted Pei Tuo’s sincerity. In the future, they would surely live in harmony as husband and wife, white-headed together.

Thinking of the wedding night ahead, Yu Wan couldn’t help but blush, gripping the jade pendant tighter.

“Ah Jiang, how much longer until we arrive?”

Wen Jiang, outside the sedan chair, replied, “After turning the corner ahead, we’ll be at the Pei residence. What’s wrong? Are you hungry?”

The day before, Ding Wenxi had specifically sent Wen Jiang to buy some pastries from the street, saying that the wedding day would be tiring. She had him carry them with him so that when Yu Wan got hungry, he could give her something to eat.

“I’m not hungry.”

“Then do you want some water?” Wen Jiang had also brought a water flask.

Hearing Wen Jiang’s concerned words, Yu Wan’s rapidly beating heart finally calmed down a bit.

“I’m fine. I just wanted to talk to someone.”

Just as the wedding procession was about to reach the Pei residence, the sedan chair suddenly jolted to a stop. Yu Wan, caught off guard, lurched to the side. She instinctively raised her hand to protect her head, but the jade pendant slipped from her grasp.

“Yu Wan, are you alright?” Wen Jiang immediately lifted the tassel curtain of the sedan chair, his voice filled with concern.

“I’m fine, I didn’t hit anything.” Yu Wan had thought the sedan bearers had slipped, but even the continuous drum and music had stopped. She felt something was amiss. “What happened?”

Seeing Wen Jiang staring fixedly ahead, Yu Wan grew even more anxious. She heard the bridesmaid muttering, “Today is supposed to be an auspicious day. Why is someone blocking the sedan chair in the street?”

Blocking a wedding procession was considered very inauspicious. Unless there was a deep grudge, people generally wouldn’t disrupt a wedding procession.

The bridesmaid stood on her tiptoes and looked ahead. She saw more than ten black-clad riders blocking the path of the wedding procession, completely obstructing the way.

The man leading them was dressed in a dark brocade robe, his posture straight and tall, his features cold and stern, staring at them intently.

Even from a distance, the bridesmaid could feel the killing intent radiating from him, cold enough to be terrifying.

“Who are those people? They look like they want to kill someone… What bad luck did I have to accept such a troublesome job?”

Hearing the bridesmaid’s mutterings, Yu Wan’s heart sank.

Before she could ask again, Wen Jiang slowly turned his head.

“Yu Wan, he’s here.”

chapters.title: Blocking the Bridal Sedan
chapters.content:
It was early spring, and the wind was not too cold.

Pei Tao silently watched Zhao Xuanyou, who stood in his way with a large contingent of men, their arrival fierce and clearly ill-intentioned.

Though the Lu brothers under Pei Tao’s command did not recognize Zhao Xuanyou, they saw that he had blocked the wedding procession and immediately drew their swords, leading the household guards to stand in front of Pei Tao’s horse.

“Who are you? How dare you block my lord’s path!”

Zhao Xuanyou did not answer. He merely lifted his chin and stared at Pei Tao.

Pei Tao could see that Zhao Xuanyou had traveled day and night, his boots still caked with mud. Yet, his deep, profound eyes were fixed intently on him, glowing with a crimson light.

Even so, Pei Tao showed no intention of retreat. He glanced at Lu Cheng, who understood and immediately ordered his men to seek reinforcements from the Anzhou prefect.

“Today is a joyous day for me, Pei. May I ask, Lord Zhao, why you are blocking the road?” Pei Tao’s tone was polite, but his words carried no hint of concession.

Yu Wan was already his wife. How could he allow Zhao Xuanyou to do as he pleased?

Though Zhao Xuanyou had brought many soldiers, this was Anzhou City. Even if Zhao had elite troops, Pei Tao’s status allowed him to summon enough official soldiers to counter them.

“I believe you already know why I am here,” Zhao Xuanyou said.

Pei Tao replied coolly, “Lord Zhao, as the commander of the Mingjuan Guard, appearing in Anzhou with so many troops may violate imperial decrees.”

“I have been assigned by the Ministry of War to inspect the troops. I am not derelict in my duty,” Zhao Xuanyou said.

“If you are here to inspect the troops, why block my path?”

Zhao Xuanyou shifted his gaze to the bridal sedan not far away, thinking of the person inside. A surge of complex emotions, anxiety, anger, resentment, and longing, suddenly welled up within him.

He forced himself to suppress his emotions and took a deep breath.

“An old friend is getting married. Can I not come to offer my congratulations?”

“Then I thank Lord Zhao for his congratulations. Now, please step aside.”

Zhao Xuanyou sneered, his expression dark. “Who said my old friend is you?”

He leaped off his horse, sword in hand, and strode forward.

“Stop him!” Pei Tao frowned and ordered.

At his command, his men immediately surrounded Zhao Xuanyou in layers.

Zhao Xuanyou’s dozens of cavalrymen also dismounted, drew their swords, and stood behind him.

The onlookers lining the streets, seeing both sides brandishing weapons, scattered in all directions.

Zhao Xuanyou lightly waved his hand, signaling his men to retreat.

He had come only for Yu Wan, not to massacre anyone. To deal with Pei Tao, he alone was enough.

He coldly looked at Pei Tao, dressed in his bright red wedding attire, and said grimly, “I said, I only want to say one word to her. Tell your men not to come and die.”

Pei Tao remained silent.

“What’s the matter? Don’t you dare let her see me? Afraid that if she sees me, old feelings will resurface, and she’ll obediently follow me away?”

“Zhao Xuanyou, she has no feelings for you. Let it go,” Pei Tao said indifferently.

From the moment Zhao Xuanyou saw the wedding procession, he had been struggling to control his emotions.

But hearing Pei Tao’s casual words, Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes turned icy, and his anger was fully ignited.

“What are you to speak of such things? How could you understand what is between her and me!”

As he spoke, he moved like a gust of wind, leaping forward toward the bridal sedan.

“Stop him!”

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was suddenly trying to abduct the bride, the Lu brothers immediately led the household guards to block him, drawing their blades. A chaotic fight ensued.

Inside the sedan, Yu Wan tightly clutched her wedding dress.

Wen Bo glanced at the fight not far away and whispered, “Although he is highly skilled in martial arts, Pei Tao’s men can hold him off for a while. I can take you away now while there’s chaos.”

“No.”

Yu Wan had heard every word Zhao Xuanyou said. She struggled to suppress her shock and anger, pondering the current situation.

He said he only wanted to say one word to her.

But how could he have gone to such lengths just to say a word of congratulations?

He must have some other reason to be so bold.

What had he done to be so confident? What could he say in one sentence to control her?

Ding Wenxi’s gentle face flashed in Yu Wan’s mind.

She was startled and immediately said to Wen Bo, “You must go back and find my mother. Take her and hide. If she’s not there, you hide by yourself.”

“What about you?”

“I won’t die. You go quickly.”

Zhao Xuanyou wanted her, not her life.

But Wen Bo knew Yu Wan did not want to return to the Hou residence.

Seeing Wen Bo still hesitating, Yu Wan urged, “Don’t forget what happened at Wei Wu’s place before. We absolutely cannot all be captured today.”

If Zhao Xuanyou captured all of them, it would be difficult for her to escape with all three of them.

“I just…”

Wen Bo simply could not bear to see Yu Wan’s happiness turn to dust so suddenly.

“Go now!”

Wen Bo clenched his fists tightly, reluctant but understanding that Yu Wan was right.

Zhao Xuanyou’s men had not yet made a move. Zhao Xuanyou alone had already defeated Pei Tao’s men.

Unless Wen Bo launched a surprise attack and killed Zhao Xuanyou in one strike.

But he was not confident in landing that strike, and Yu Wan… might not want Zhao Xuanyou dead.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou was about to reach the sedan, Wen Bo hardened his heart, flashed behind the sedan, and disappeared down the street like a gust of wind.

“Who dares to cause trouble in Anzhou City!”

The Anzhou prefect, having received word from Pei Tao’s men, arrived with a large contingent of officials. Though he did not know Zhao Xuanyou’s identity, seeing the many injured, he immediately shouted a warning, ordering Zhao Xuanyou to surrender his weapons.

Zhao Xuanyou had just defeated the Pei household guards blocking his way, but his sword had never left its sheath, and he had not taken any lives.

He coldly glanced at the Anzhou prefect.

“Zhao Xuanyou.”

The prefect had naturally heard of his reputation. The guards had reported the day before that Zhao Xuanyou, carrying orders from the Ministry of War, was inspecting troops in Xishu and passing through Anzhou.

He looked at Pei Tao, then at Zhao Xuanyou, unsure of what was happening. Finally, he looked uneasily at Pei Tao. “Lord, this…”

“He has injured people without cause. Arrest him.”

“Yes.”

After all, Pei Tao was the direct superior of the Anzhou prefect. He should listen to Pei Tao.

Moreover, Zhao Xuanyou had indeed injured people in the street and seemed intent on abducting someone’s bride. It was only right to arrest Zhao Xuanyou first.

At the prefect’s command, dozens of yamen runners formed a human wall, their sword points all aimed at Zhao Xuanyou.

“Do not move again, or we will not be polite.”

“There’s no need to panic. I only want to say a few words to the bride.”

The bridal sedan was only a few steps away.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes sharpened. He suddenly lifted his sword sheath and knocked over the yamen runners in front of him, then quickly walked to the bridal sedan.

Thinking of the woman inside, Zhao Xuanyou’s breathing became slightly obstructed, but without hesitation, he used his sword to lift the sedan curtain.

---

chapters.title: Return with Him
chapters.content:
The moment the sedan curtain was lifted, Yu Wan’s face came into view.

She was dressed in her wedding finery, her hands folded in her lap. The wide sleeves covered most of her hands, revealing only her slender fingertips.

The red wedding dress she wore was dazzling, the skirt embroidered with large blooms of twin lotuses, delicate and beautiful, symbolizing the unity of husband and wife.

Yet the beauty of the dress paled in comparison to her stunning appearance.

Naturally beautiful, and with Ding Wenxi’s skillful adornment, her eyebrows were like distant green mountains, the floral ornament at her brow vibrant, making her soft red lips and fair cheeks stand out even more.

Zhao Xuanyou, despite his murderous aura, was slightly taken aback at the sight of her.

He had once been the person most familiar with her, yet he had not known that she would be this breathtakingly beautiful in a wedding dress.

But this beauty was for someone else.

“Wanwan, I’ve come to take you away,” Zhao Xuanyou said coldly, his voice devoid of warmth.

“Is that all the Young Master has to say?” Yu Wan’s voice trembled slightly under the turmoil of her emotions.

Three years apart, and Zhao Xuanyou still had the same detached, handsome appearance, the same condescending tone. Only the stubble on his chin showed the weariness of his journey, leaving him no time for anything else.

“You don’t want to leave?”

“Young Master should see that I am about to be married. Why would a bride-to-be want to go with you?”

Yu Wan let out a helpless, soft laugh.

She was wearing a wedding dress, sitting in a bridal sedan. What gave him the idea that she wanted to go with him?

She had hands and feet. If she truly missed him, why hadn’t she gone to find him?

Seeing her response, Zhao Xuanyou’s hand twitched slightly.

After a long separation, there was not a trace of joy or smile in her eyes when she saw him; only surprise and guard.

For three years, he had repeatedly relived every moment they had spent together. The overwhelming longing had tormented him endlessly.

Yet in the end, she had put on a red wedding dress and joyfully thrown herself into another man’s arms.

His search, his attachment, his longing; all had turned into a joke in an instant.

Looking at the caution in Yu Wan’s eyes, Zhao Xuanyou forced down his emotions and said in a low voice, “Wanwan, don’t do something you’ll regret.”

He wanted to take her away and set everything right.

Yu Wan’s heart stirred. “Where is my mother?”

“She is safe.” His tone was calm, but the threat in his words made Yu Wan’s eyes turn cold.

As expected.

He had entered the city long ago, waiting for her bridal sedan to leave before making a move against her mother.

“Leave now, and you can see her sooner.”

“Yu’er, don’t be afraid.” Pei Tao rushed up from behind, seeing Zhao Xuanyou cornering Yu Wan in the sedan, his gaze sharp. “Zhao Xuanyou, this is not a place where you can do as you please.”

The commotion on the street had drawn the attention of the city guards, who rushed over with all their might.

These guards, fully armored, quickly surrounded Zhao Xuanyou, pointing their long spears at him.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou still refused to let go, Pei Tao angrily said, “If you truly admire her, you should let her decide her own affairs.”

“You dare speak to me of true feelings?” Zhao Xuanyou’s anger surged from his back to his head. The thought of Yu Wan marrying Pei Tao made him want to kill him on the spot. “Who do you think you are? You understand her so well? You’re just using a bit of past acquaintance to deceive her!”

As Zhao Xuanyou spoke, he suddenly rushed toward Pei Tao like a gust of wind and grabbed him by the collar.

Publicly and privately, his hatred for Pei Tao had been building for a long time.

But Pei Tao did not change color when grabbed by the collar. Instead, he coldly smiled at Zhao Xuanyou.

“At least, I understand her better than you do.”

Enraged, Zhao Xuanyou swung his fist at Pei Tao. Fortunately, Lu Cheng and the others reacted quickly, immediately raising their swords to block and taking the blow for Pei Tao.

The surrounding guards also rushed forward, forming a human wall in front of Pei Tao.

“Zhao Xuanyou!”

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou still trying to strike, Yu Wan stepped out of the sedan, her wide wedding dress billowing in the spring wind.

Hearing her voice, Zhao Xuanyou’s anger subsided slightly. He turned to look at her.

“I’ll go with you.” Yu Wan’s expression appeared calm.

From the moment Zhao Xuanyou had blocked the wedding procession, she knew it was over between her and Pei Tao.

Zhao Xuanyou’s obsession with her ran so deep that even if he hadn’t captured Ding Wenxi today, he would find another way to take her away.

Even if they drove him away today, he would return tomorrow, the day after.

“Yu’er, the archers will arrive soon. You don’t have to submit to his threats,” Pei Tao said, his gaze tightening as he tried to rush to Yu Wan’s side, only to be held back by his men.

Zhao Xuanyou’s dark face finally showed a hint of a smile.

He turned to look at Pei Tao and said coldly, “Surname Pei, she has chosen me. If you dare approach her again, I will show no mercy.”

At that moment, Yu Wan saw clearly the mockery in his eyes.

If she continued to hesitate, Pei Tao would certainly fight for her to the end, and more people would get hurt.

She looked at Lu Cheng beside Pei Tao. Lu Cheng understood and nodded slightly.

He knew Zhao Xuanyou’s martial arts were profound and mysterious. Any further action would surely injure Pei Tao. So, along with Lu Jie, he firmly held Pei Tao back, preventing him from moving forward.

“Stop hurting people. I want to leave quickly,” Yu Wan said, her voice trembling slightly in the wind as she reached out and grabbed Zhao Xuanyou’s sleeve.

He turned his head, his gaze faltering for a moment.

Yu Wan’s face was pale, her expression stiff. The beautiful features that once held a lively charm now seemed devoid of their usual spirit.

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart suddenly softened.

He had wanted to punish her severely, to force her to submit, to humiliate Pei Tao in public. But he did not want to see her like this.

He took a deep breath and reached out to her.

Yu Wan lowered her gaze and placed her hand in his palm.

Her hand was soft and warm. It felt like reclaiming a lost treasure, once touched, he would never let go.

“Yu’er, don’t go,” Pei Tao cried out.

No matter how arrogant Zhao Xuanyou was, he felt no fear.

Yu Wan liked him. She was willing to marry him.

There was still law in Xishu. Zhao Xuanyou did not have enough men to do as he pleased.

“You don’t have to fear him. I can find a way to counter any threat he makes.”

“Our marriage is over,” Yu Wan said softly. “Lord Pei, I have wronged you. I’m sorry.”

She could not bear to look into Pei Tao’s eyes and turned her head away.

Zhao Xuanyou, standing close by, could see the mist in her eyes.

Thinking of her current reluctance to leave Pei Tao, Zhao Xuanyou’s lips lost all color. He coldly looked at the city guards blocking his path to Yu Wan.

“Get out of the way.”

He wanted to take Yu Wan away quickly, to make her forget Pei Tao entirely.

The soldiers still pointed their spears at him but looked to Pei Tao for guidance. The archers had arrived and were ready to fire, awaiting his command.

Pei Tao was firmly held back by the Lu brothers. His handsome face was filled with pain and confusion.

His gaze remained fixed on Yu Wan, but Yu Wan allowed Zhao Xuanyou to lead her away without so much as a glance back.

Though she still wore the red wedding dress, she would not return home with him.

chapters.title: A Full Meal
chapters.content:
Because there was no order from Pei Ta, the soldiers dared not move.

The wall of people surrounding Zhao Xuanyou gradually parted under the prod of his long sword, creating a narrow path.

Under the tense gaze of the crowd, Zhao Xuanyou led Yu Wan by the hand forward until they reached his horse.

Yu Wan kept her eyes downcast, never glancing at anyone.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the blindingly red wedding dress on her and coldly asked, "Where is my cloak?"

"Yes." Yuan Zhen quickly handed over his cloak.

Zhao Xuanyou took the cloak and draped it over Yu Wan, then lifted her onto the horse.

As he reached around her to hold the reins, he felt a warm drop fall on the back of his hand.

It was just one of her tears, yet it pierced his hand like a knife.

Once they left this place, everything would be fine.

She did not belong to Anzhou, nor to Pei Ta.

Once she returned to his side, she would naturally forget everything.

Zhao Xuanyou closed his eyes briefly, hardening his heart as he urged the horse forward.

After leaving the city gates of Anzhou, Zhao Xuanyou rode east with Yu Wan, galloping for over two hours before finally reaching a ferry crossing.

Sichuan was surrounded by mountains on all sides, only the Yangtze River cut through the mountains like a sharp blade, surging forward.

A government boat was already docked at the crossing, with someone waiting there. Upon seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s arrival, they quickly stepped forward and cupped their hands in greeting, "General Zhao, the boat is ready and can depart at any time."

Zhao Xuanyou had not entered Shu privately; this trip was indeed an official mission from the Ministry of War. Those waiting here were also from the local military camp.

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was holding a woman in his arms, the man quickly averted his gaze and stepped aside.

"Thank you for your trouble." Zhao Xuanyou said indifferently.

"It is my honor to serve General Zhao."

Zhao Xuanyou said no more, waiting for Yu Wan to steady herself before leading her onto the boat. Yuan Zhen handed over a reward and followed them aboard.

"Where is my mother?"

After boarding, Zhao Xuanyou ordered the boatmen to set sail.

Once the boat left the shore, he looked around but did not see Ding Wenxi.

"She is fine."

"I want to see her."

Seeing the worry in her bright eyes, Zhao Xuanyou said in a deep voice, "I had Yuan Qing escort her ahead. She will be waiting for you at home."

"Home?" Yu Wan suddenly tensed, pressing further, "Where exactly have you taken her? My mother cannot return to the capital."

"Why can't she?"

"In any case, she cannot. Zhao Xuanyou, no matter what you want to threaten me with, do not take my mother to the capital."

Seeing her anxious expression, Zhao Xuanyou reached for her hand again. When their palms touched, he clearly felt her body tremble.

Zhao Xuanyou's heart tightened abruptly.

Even if their past affection had been nothing but a fleeting moment, she had always been accustomed to his touch. In fact, she used to snuggle into his arms even while sleeping.

Now, just holding her hand made her react as if pricked by a needle.

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze darkened, but he still held her hand firmly.

"Rest assured, the home I speak of is not in the capital."

He was not lying to her; Ding Wenxi was indeed not on this boat.

He had always been cautious in his actions. After capturing Ding Wenxi, he immediately had Yuan Qing take her away.

After all, this was Anzhou, and he had only brought a few dozen men. If he couldn't achieve a quick victory, he might not be able to outlast Pei Ta.

Given the deep bond between Yu Wan and Ding Wenxi, even if his attempt to snatch her away failed, Yu Wan would still end up following him in the end.

But things had gone quite smoothly.

She was still the same as before, judging the situation and not wasting effort on futile actions.

"The wind is strong on the boat; go rest in the cabin."

Yu Wan said nothing, pulling her hand from his grasp and turning to follow Yuan Zhen into the cabin.

As this was a government boat, the cabin was not only spacious but also comfortably furnished. The floor was covered with carpets, and the bedding on the couch was all fine Sichuan embroidery.

"Would you like to open the window for some air?" Over the past three years, too much had happened, and Yuan Zhen, looking at Yu Wan, didn't know what to say for a moment.

Yu Wan shook her head.

Seeing that Yuan Zhen was about to leave, she asked, "Where has he taken my mother?"

Yuan Zhen thought for a moment and did not explicitly answer, only softly saying, "To the place where the master has the final say."

The place where Zhao Xuanyou had the final say?

That should be Yuzhou City, where the Mingchuan Guard was stationed.

The Jingyuan Marquis's estate had been stationed in Yuzhou for generations, making him virtually the uncrowned king of Yuzhou.

If he took her mother to Yuzhou, without his word, no one would be able to take her away.

In the capital, although Zhao Xuanyou was also highly respected, he still had to consider the imperial family and powerful ministers, which constrained his actions.

In Yuzhou, even with Wen Kuo's help, it would be difficult to escape.

Yu Wan's mind was in turmoil. She took a deep breath and looked at Yuan Zhen gratefully, "Thank you."

"You're welcome." Yuan Zhen had previously been confused by Yu Wan. Clearly, the young master had been so good to her, yet she had gone to such lengths to escape from the capital.

But after seeing Yu Wan in Anzhou, Yuan Zhen understood.

Yu Wan was able to marry a third-rank inspector as his official wife, so naturally, she was unwilling to stay in the marquis's estate.

Seeing that Yu Wan's complexion was not good, Yuan Zhen knew she was in a bad mood and was about to quietly retreat when Zhao Xuanyou walked in.

"Prepare some food."

"Yes." Yuan Zhen respectfully withdrew.

Zhao Xuanyou closed the cabin door and turned to see Yu Wan looking at him with a guarded expression, his face darkened as he forced a slight smile.

The atmosphere in the cabin was indeed oppressive.

Zhao Xuanyou opened the window, and as the fresh air blew in, the oppression in his heart slightly dissipated.

He should have been fine once he found her.

But seeing her about to marry someone else with his own eyes, how could he possibly be fine?

He had many questions for her, but he didn't know where to start.

He turned and sat on the edge of the couch.

Yu Wan remained silent, only shifting further away.

"The boat is this small; where do you think you can hide?" Zhao Xuanyou glanced at her, his gaze dark and complex.

Yu Wan didn't know where she could hide either.

She just instinctively didn't want to be too close to him.

The two sat in silence, letting the river breeze blow in from the window, neither speaking.

"Master, the meal is ready."

"Come in."

As Yuan Zhen pushed open the door, the aroma of food wafted in.

Glancing at Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan's expressions, Yuan Zhen kept his head down, silently arranging the cups and dishes neatly before quickly retreating.

"You must be hungry after all this commotion."

Yu Wan was indeed hungry.

She had gotten up before dawn to dress and do her hair. Fearful of any mishaps during the wedding ceremony, she hadn't dared to eat much for breakfast or drink much water.

She turned her head and quietly looked at the table full of dishes.

The table was set with all the dishes she had loved to eat back in the marquis's estate: stir-fried bamboo shoots, steamed fish slices, shredded chicken with sauce, and sautéed pork. Clearly, they had been prepared especially for her.

But so what?

Her mother had been captured by him, and she was trapped here. She needed to eat her fill to have the strength to think of a way to escape. Only by eating well could she have the energy to run away.

Without waiting for Zhao Xuanyou to say more, Yu Wan picked up her chopsticks.

---

chapters.title: No Reluctance
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou sat down beside her but did not pick up his chopsticks, only watching her quietly.

Back in Honghui Hall, the two of them often sat like this in the side hall to eat.

Zhao Xuanyou had always enjoyed watching her eat.

She had been born with an extremely beautiful appearance. When idle, her hair was loosely coiled and hung over her shoulders, looking both charming and casual.

After so long, they were finally sitting at the same table again.

Zhao Xuanyou picked up his chopsticks and placed a piece of bamboo shoot into her bowl.

Yu Wan paused slightly in her eating, looking up at him.

"These are tasks servants should do. How can someone as noble as the young master serve others food?"

Zhao Xuanyou detected the sarcasm in her words but did not change his expression. He simply said gently, "I remember you used to like bamboo shoots, so I had them prepare these specially."

"I used to like them, but my tastes have changed. I can't eat a single bite now."

Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows twitched slightly, and a rare warmth appeared in his usually deep and profound eyes.

"At least you liked them before. It won't be hard to like them again in the future."

Yu Wan only stared at the bamboo shoot, saying nothing as she picked it out of her bowl and placed it on the table.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the bamboo shoot on the table and asked again, "If you don't want to eat it, that's fine. What else would you like? I can have them prepare something else."

"No need. I'm full."

Yu Wan put down her chopsticks and stood up, walking directly to the window; the farthest spot from him in the cabin.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at the glaring red wedding dress on Yu Wan and said softly, "There are clothes prepared in the cabinet. Change first."

Yu Wan countered, "Today is my wedding day. Why should I change?"

"You personally told Pei Ta that the wedding was off." Zhao Xuanyou reminded her indifferently.

Yes, she had said that.

But why had she said it? Didn't he understand?

When she left, Yu Wan hadn't dared to look at Pei Ta again. After saying those words, she had almost fled in a panic, not daring to meet Pei Ta's eyes.

No matter how hard Yu Wan tried to control herself, her eyes still welled up with tears.

At this moment, the boat was still some distance away from the Three Gorges of Badong, but the speed of the water had already increased. The government boat traveled downstream, and the mountains and houses on both sides receded like a galloping horse.

Yu Wan's spirit sharpened slightly. The river water always flowed eastward, never stopping for anyone or anything. But could people do the same?

She had been taken so far away by Zhao Xuanyou, yet her thoughts were still trapped in that sedan chair.

She didn't want to move forward; she only wanted to sit quietly in the sedan chair, waiting for Pei Ta to lead her out.

Pei Ta...

Yu Wan's hands tightly gripped the windowsill, struggling to restrain the sting in her eyes.

But she had to cut the Gordian knot.

Even if the soldiers had blocked the way, Zhao Xuanyou couldn't have taken her away. With his skills and temper, he would surely have injured Pei Ta.

Back then, Cui Zaizhou had been severely injured by Zhao Xuanyou in a fit of rage and eventually died in prison before the execution date.

She couldn't risk Pei Ta.

Seeing Yu Wan's tearful expression, Zhao Xuanyou's eyes darkened with dense clouds. After a moment of silence, he reached out to remove the phoenix crown from her head.

Sensing his movement, Yu Wan turned her head and held onto her phoenix crown, retreating slightly.

"I don't find it heavy."

"You don't look good in this outfit. In the future, I will prepare better phoenix crowns and beautiful dresses for you."

Zhao Xuanyou spoke with a calm expression.

Yu Wan, hearing these words, unconsciously glanced at him.

He was indeed very handsome, with a tall and refined figure. His usually deep and profound eyes showed a rare tenderness.

Three years apart had indeed changed him.

Not only had his gaze and tone changed, but the concubine position he had once promised her had also turned into phoenix crowns and beautiful dresses.

But Yu Wan had also changed.

"How can someone as lowly as this servant dare to aim so high as the young master?" She deliberately used her old form of address, intending to keep him at arm's length.

Such an attitude naturally caused Zhao Xuanyou's eyes to darken.

"Is it aiming high to be with me? Was it a suitable match to be with Pei Ta?"

"I am indeed not a suitable match for him, but we share a deep understanding..."

"Shut up!"

"I can choose not to speak, but Pei Ta and I have already exchanged marriage certificates. Even if you take me away today, I am already his wife."

When she left with him, Yu Wan had decided to play along, biding her time to rescue her mother.

Yu Wan was willing to go with him, but not to rekindle old feelings.

Some things had to be made clear; otherwise, he might think she would still be as compliant as before.

As the sky darkened a bit, the wind on the river grew stronger, and the blinding red wedding dress fluttered. Zhao Xuanyou's eyes were filled with coldness. "His wife is Song Yu, not you. I have no interest in Song Yu."

"Then who am I? Or am I just a maid in the marquis's estate, to be summoned and dismissed at your will?"

"If you like the identity of Ding Wan, then be Ding Wan."

Whether it was Ding Wan or Song Yu, she liked them.

But she no longer liked Zhao Xuanyou.

Seeing that she remained silent, Zhao Xuanyou added, "Whatever Pei Ta can give you, I can give you ten, a hundred times more."

"Is that so?" Yu Wan heard his words and, instead of getting angry, laughed. "I want Pei Ta. Will you give him to me?"

"You don't need to deliberately say things to provoke me."

"I am telling the truth. If I didn't truly like him, why would I marry him?" Yu Wan pleaded softly, "Zhao Xuanyou, let my mother go, and let me go as well. There are many noble ladies in the capital who admire you and want to marry you. Why not marry a girl who matches your status? The old madam would be very happy. She has always hoped for you to marry early and have children to continue the family line."

"Do you have true feelings?" Hearing Yu Wan's words, the jealousy and longing that Zhao Xuanyou had suppressed deep in his heart suddenly surged. He grabbed Yu Wan's wrist. "I ask you, when you were in the marquis's estate, how much of your heart did you truly give me?"

"Initially, I was drugged by Cui Yichu and sent to your bed. If you had known I was just a flower room maid, you wouldn't have touched me." His hand was like a shackle, and Yu Wan's wrist ached from his grip. She tried to push him away but couldn't budge him at all.

"I am asking about you." Zhao Xuanyou's gaze tightened, his handsome face as cold as frost. "When you left the marquis's estate, did you feel any reluctance?"

Over the past three years, he had thought countless times: why had she left him so decisively?

In her heart, had she ever felt even a little genuine affection for him?

On those sleepless nights, Zhao Xuanyou had thought that when he saw her again, the first thing he would ask was this.

Now that he had truly seen her, he couldn't bear to press her.

As long as she was willing to go back with him, he could pretend that the past had never happened, not mentioning it, not asking about it.

But she kept bringing up Pei Ta, looking as if she would be heartbroken without him, which Zhao Xuanyou simply could not tolerate.

He really wanted to know: when she had left him, had she felt the same way?

Pressed by him, Yu Wan's back was against the window, with no way to retreat. She could only meet his gaze and firmly say:

"I felt no reluctance."

chapters.title: A Doomed Fate, So What?
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou stared intently at Yu Wan, his eyes shifting between stormy and calm.

"Is there truly not the slightest bit of lingering affection?"

"Of course not."

Zhao Xuanyou grabbed her wrist and pulled her close to him.

"If you have no attachment at all, then why did you ask me to take you out of the city to ride horses that night?"

On the night before New Year's Eve, Yu Wan had begged him to take her out of the city to ride.

After she left, he had regretted that decision countless times.

"That day was because I wanted to ride horses." Yu Wan's rebuttal sounded weak. Knowing he wouldn't believe her, she could only say, "Does it matter whether there's affection or not? I've already moved on. Now, my heart belongs to someone else. Why must you dwell on the past?"

"You admit you once had feelings for me?"

"It was years ago. I don’t remember anymore."

"Then let me help you recall." Without waiting for her response, Zhao Xuanyou wrapped one arm around her waist and the other around her neck, pulling her into his embrace.

She seemed a little taller than before, and thinner.

He was so used to holding her that even the slightest change in her body was noticeable.

The wind on the river grew colder.

Caught off guard by his sudden embrace, Yu Wan desperately pushed against his shoulders, refusing to let his face come closer.

"Zhao Xuanyou, let go of me! How can you, the heir of a marquis, bully another man's wife like this?"

"You are my woman!" Zhao Xuanyou fixed his gaze on her, his eyes bloodshot. "Pei Ta knew you were my woman, yet he still laid hands on you. Do you think he’s a good man?"

"Even if he isn’t a good man, he would never treat me like you do!"

Zhao Xuanyou froze at her words, his grip loosening slightly.

"He..."

"You want to know how I felt when I left the marquis's mansion? I can tell you; I was happy, incredibly happy. Leaving the marquis's mansion meant I no longer had to be a slave or a servant. I no longer had to fear being punished for mistakes or fawn over my masters. You never truly loved the real me. I’m not gentle, I don’t smile often, and I certainly don’t enjoy blindly obeying others!"

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered a few times before he said hoarsely, "So to you, was there only suffering in the marquis's mansion?"

Looking at his expression, a bitter, helpless smile tugged at the corners of Yu Wan’s lips.

"You did pamper me. Because of me, there were no other concubines in the mansion. You treated me differently from the other maids. You held me as you slept, and when you were happy, you rewarded me with hairpins, rings, and dresses. But you know better than anyone that that’s all I was worth."

For the first time, a trace of panic appeared on Zhao Xuanyou’s usually calm and composed face.

"If you had been honest with me, if you had let me understand your feelings, you wouldn’t have had to fake your death. I would have helped you take revenge. I would have killed Cui Yichu for you! Why did you turn to Zhao Qi instead of confiding in me?"

Yu Wan lowered her gaze and let out a soft laugh.

"What was I supposed to say? That I wanted to be your legitimate wife? Zhao Xuanyou, if I had said that, you would only think I was overstepping. The Old Dowager made me drink so much contraceptive soup. Wasn’t that a constant reminder of my place?"
