"Wanwan, it was my fault for not considering you before. But now, my grandmother and father know my feelings for you. From now on, there will be no obstacles. I will marry you. There will be nothing between us. We can be together forever."

His tone was a gentleness she hadn’t heard in a long time, the kind he used when they were wrapped in each other’s arms in the tent.

Hearing his confession, a complex mix of emotions surged within her.

But Yu Wan still said, "But I don’t want to marry you."

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression shifted slightly.

"I don’t blame you for the past. In fact, I’m grateful to you. If it weren’t for you, I would have been tormented to death by Cui Yichu. It was also you who arranged for my mother to stay at the Taoran Inn to recover when she was in a coma."

She remembered everything he had done for her.

That was why, during her time in the marquis's mansion, she had served him and pleased him with all her heart.

"So what?" Zhao Xuanyou pressed, his voice low.

"You didn’t marry me before, and that wasn’t a betrayal. You only did what was expected of you. I had no right to blame you." Yu Wan bit her lip, her heart aching. "If it weren’t for Cui Yichu’s delusions and the twist of fate that led him to target me, you never would have noticed me. It was just a doomed fate that should never have happened. You should marry a noblewoman from a high-ranking family..."

"Are you and I a doomed fate, but you and Pei Ta are a perfect match?" Zhao Xuanyou gritted his teeth.

His urgent tone revealed his stubbornness.

Yu Wan felt helpless.

She had begged him for so long, yet he still refused to let go.

"Yes, he appeared at the right time. He knows my past, yet he doesn’t care about it. We love each other."

"A doomed fate, so what?"

Perhaps it was her firm belief in their "doomed fate," or her cold and distant attitude since their reunion, or perhaps it was jealousy toward Pei Ta. But as soon as she said "we love each other," Zhao Xuanyou’s long-suppressed emotions finally snapped. Like a wild beast out of control, he pushed her against the window and kissed her fiercely.

She was too stubborn. He wanted to show her that even if their fate was doomed, it was still a bond that would entangle them for life.

"Zhao Xuanyou!" Yu Wan, trapped against the window, could only twist her head to avoid him.

Feeling his warm lips on her cheek, anger and humiliation surged within her. Tears welled up in her eyes as she shouted desperately, "I hate you! I regret ever having feelings for you! You’re a beast! I never want to see you again! I will never forgive you!"

She cried so hard that her body trembled violently.

Zhao Xuanyou frowned, finally lifting his head.

Yu Wan’s face was pale, her phoenix crown had fallen to the ground during the struggle, and her once-perfect hairstyle was now a messy cascade over her shoulders.

Her usually bright eyes were now veiled with tears, the rims red and filled with panic and grievance.

The madness in Zhao Xuanyou’s mind finally began to fade.

"Wanwan."

His voice was hoarse as he called her name, lifting a stiff hand to try to wipe the tears from her cheeks.

Yu Wan suddenly pushed his hand away, her tear-filled eyes watching him warily.

"Don’t cry."

Zhao Xuanyou finally let go of her.

He hadn’t brought her here to treat her so roughly, to force himself on her.

He had already decided; he wanted to start over with her, to marry her, to grow old with her.

They had already taken the wrong path before; they couldn’t afford to make the same mistake again.

"It was my fault. I was an idiot. I shouldn’t have treated you like this."

Zhao Xuanyou muttered, staggering back a few steps.

---

chapters.title: The Happiest Time
chapters.content:
The river current grew faster.

Even though Zhao Xuanyou had let go, Yu Wan’s heart still pounded violently.

She remained leaning against the window, her eyes fixed on him.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s expression, if Yu Wan claimed her heart was untouched, that would be a lie.

As he said, a doomed fate was still a fate. From the moment Cui Yichu had sent her to his bed, their destinies had been intertwined.

Although Yu Wan had constantly reminded herself not to sink into his affection, she had wavered when he risked everything to rescue her from the prince’s hands.

Leaving the marquis's mansion had felt like waking from a long dream.

She had abandoned everything from her past, wanting to live a different life.

She pleaded with him again, "Zhao Xuanyou, you once wanted a noblewoman to manage your household and bear your children. It was just bad luck that you encountered Cui Yichu, which led to everything that happened. Now that Cui Yichu is dead and I’ve left, you should set things right by courting a virtuous woman, not coming to find me."

"To you, I am just..."

"A doomed fate?"

Zhao Xuanyou finished her sentence.

He didn’t approach her again, but his smile was tinged with a cold bitterness.

"Isn’t that the truth?" Yu Wan’s eyes welled up once more, her voice trembling slightly. "When we first met, wasn’t that exactly the kind of life you wanted? Back then, you were truly happy."

Though he had never said it, Yu Wan had felt his relaxation when she lay in his arms at night.

With the "wife" by his side, he was gentle, considerate, and gave her everything she asked for, without any guard.

"No." Zhao Xuanyou answered decisively.

The happiest moment of his life was when he confirmed she was still alive.

"What about you?" Zhao Xuanyou knew this wasn’t what Yu Wan wanted to hear, so he stopped, simply asking her, "When were you happiest?"

"Before you came to Anzhou." Yu Wan’s tone was equally resolute. "Every day, I was happy."

Perhaps it was because their earlier argument had drained him, but upon hearing Yu Wan’s answer, his expression looked eerily calm.

Too calm. He stood there like a statue, completely still.

After a long while, he finally said in a low voice, "Wanwan, your life is still long. What will happen in the future is unknown."

Though he was a military man, his literary talent was not inferior.

For a moment, Yu Wan found herself unable to retort.

However, glancing at the river outside, she let out a helpless laugh. "My mother is missing, and I’m trapped here by you. No matter what happens in the future, it certainly won’t be like this."

"Your mother is fine. She is not missing. As for the rest..." Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath and slowly said, "As for what happened earlier, it was my fault. I won’t force myself on you when you don’t want it."

He didn’t deny that he had trapped Yu Wan.

But for Yu Wan, his promise not to use force against her was the best outcome for now.

"You must be tired today. Rest early. We’ll disembark tomorrow."

With that, he pushed open the door and left.

Left alone in the cabin, Yu Wan turned her head toward the river, letting the cold wind from the water cool her burning cheeks before closing the window.

She tidied her hair, which had been messed up by Zhao Xuanyou’s forceful kiss, then bent down to pick up the phoenix crown that had fallen to the floor.

The crown had been personally crafted by Ding Wenxi, with intricate inlays. Even after falling to the ground, it remained unharmed.

If everything had gone as planned, it should have been Pei Ta who removed it from her head.

Yu Wan’s eyes welled up with tears.

She carefully placed the phoenix crown into a cabinet.

As expected, clean clothes had been prepared inside. Yu Wan set the crown down but didn’t take out the clothes.

Today was her wedding day with Pei Ta. No matter what, she didn’t want to take off this wedding dress.

---

Meanwhile, Anzhou City was in chaos.

News of the imperial inspector being publicly kidnapped had spread throughout the city. Despite the prefect’s efforts to disperse the onlookers, the street was still packed with people.

Idle men were animatedly describing the earlier scene; the bride’s heavenly beauty, the black-clad man’s unmatched martial arts, and how he had single-handedly defeated a group of soldiers, leaving them scattered on the ground.

Lu Cheng looked at the dazed Pei Ta and, steeling himself, stepped forward. "Sir, the carriage has arrived. Let’s return to the residence."

Pei Ta held a jade pendant in his hand, which he had picked up from the bridal sedan. The characters "White-Headed Together" were still clearly visible, but the person he was supposed to share a lifetime with had vanished.

"This is no place to talk. But Miss Song’s situation is not hopeless. Please return to the residence first, sir. I have something to report."

Hearing Lu Jie’s words, Pei Ta’s gaze shifted slightly, and he frowned. "What do you mean?"

"Please get in the carriage first, sir."

Pei Ta was about to board the carriage when another subordinate approached. "Young Master Wen has arrived."

Wen Kuo was still here?

This reminded Pei Ta that when Zhao Xuanyou had taken Yu Wan away, Wen Kuo had not appeared.

Given Wen Kuo’s friendship with Yu Wan, he should have intervened if he knew she didn’t want to leave.

"Bring him over."

Pei Ta took a deep breath.

Soon, Wen Kuo was brought before him. Pei Ta said, "Let’s talk in the carriage."

Wen Kuo followed Pei Ta into the carriage. Seeing Pei Ta in his bright red wedding attire, he felt even more distressed thinking about Yu Wan’s situation.

"Kuokuo, did Yu’er leave any instructions for you?"

"She said Zhao Xuanyou must have come prepared and told me to go home immediately to check."

Pei Ta’s expression darkened, his long fingers clenching into a fist.

"Did something happen to Madam?"

Wen Kuo nodded. "She was taken by Zhao Xuanyou."

"So he used Madam to coerce Yu’er." Pei Ta punched the carriage wall hard, his expression growing heavier. "It’s my fault. I should have arranged for someone to protect Madam."

Wen Kuo gave a slight nod.

Ding Wenxi was the most important person to Yu Wan. From what Yu Wan had said, she had even sold herself into servitude to raise money for Ding Wenxi’s treatment.

Zhao Xuanyou must have known about her filial piety and used this against her.

"Pei Ta, I will leave Anzhou. There are some things of Yu Wan’s that I’ve collected in my house. Could you help me look after them?"

"You’re going to rescue her?"

Wen Kuo nodded.

"Be patient. I’ve already sent people to investigate his whereabouts. We’ll act once we have information."

"Isn’t he taking Yu Wan back to the capital?"

"The capital is under the emperor’s watch. It’s not a place where he can act recklessly. I suspect he’ll return to Yu Prefecture. That’s his true stronghold."

"I understand. I’ll wait for your news."

Seeing that their conversation was nearly over, Lu Jie cupped his hands and said, "Sir, I have something to report."

"Speak."

"During the fight earlier, although I was no match for him, I managed to release poison powder. The poison is odorless and tasteless. He likely didn’t notice."

Lu Jie was skilled with poisons. Previously, when Wen Kuo and Yu Wan had been captured at Wei Wu’s home, it had been his poison.

"Are you sure he was poisoned?"

Wen Kuo had experienced Lu Jie’s poisons before and felt it was possible that Zhao Xuanyou had indeed been poisoned.

"If he was hit with Soft Bone Powder, as a military man, he would be anxious to find an antidote. Maybe we can use the antidote to exchange for Yu Wan."

chapters.title: Falling into the Water
chapters.content:
Yu Wan lay down fully clothed that night, unable to close her eyes.

In the three years since leaving the capital, she had always had her mother and Wen Tao by her side. This was the first time she felt so utterly alone.

Her mother was probably on another boat now, and Wen Tao was still in Anzhou.

Could he have guessed that Zhao Xuanyou would take her to Yuzhou?

Even if Yuan Qian was an old acquaintance of hers, he would never betray Zhao Xuanyou to help her send a message to Wen Tao.

Yu Wan lay in the cabin, suppressing her grievances with all her might, and finally fell asleep just before dawn.

"Miss? Miss?"

Yu Wan was in a deep sleep when Yuan Qian's voice woke her.

"What's the matter?"

Yuan Qian sighed in relief: "It's good that you're alright. The meal is ready. Would you like to eat?"

Yu Wan had stayed awake all night, missing breakfast, and now even the time for lunch had passed. Yuan Qian was worried about her, but didn’t dare to barge in, so he could only knock and ask.

"Alright."

"Right now, the boat has already reached Wushan. The scenery outside is wonderful. Would you like to eat on deck?"

When Yu Wan had come, she had traveled upstream, and passing through the Three Gorges of Badong, she hadn’t experienced the feeling of a light boat passing through countless mountains. She did want to go out and take a look.

She sat up, changing out of her red wedding dress into clothes from the wardrobe.

Perhaps Zhao Xuanyou had given special instructions, as the clothes in the wardrobe were of excellent quality, and the embroidery on the hem was Shu embroidery.

She picked out a plain light green skirt and paired it with a moon-white top before stepping out of the cabin.

The dining table was set in the middle of the front deck. Zhao Xuanyou was not there.

Not seeing him, Yu Wan breathed a sigh of relief and ate her meal in peace.

After she put down her chopsticks, she stood up and walked to the very front of the deck.

The weather was excellent today, and from the boat, she could see very far. Standing here, she could indeed feel the sensation of the great and small rapids being treacherous, and the green mountains on both sides rushing past like flying.

Although it was early spring, both banks were already lush and green.

As the boat passed, she could occasionally hear the cries of gibbons. To Yu Wan’s ears, these sounds were not terrifying or strange, but rather carried a unique charm.

When Zhao Xuanyou walked onto the deck, he saw her graceful figure leaning against the railing.

He signaled Yuan Qian to remain silent and simply gazed at her.

In the past, when they were at the Marquis's mansion, she had been a maidservant attending to him. As long as he was in the mansion, she would be by his side, and there were rarely opportunities to observe her from afar like this.

Now, after three years apart, so many barriers had formed between them. She had almost become someone else’s wife, and even observing her from a distance had become a luxury.

Recalling the scene of her in a red wedding dress, repeatedly calling out for Pei Ta, Zhao Xuanyou felt a dull ache in his heart.

After standing quietly for a while, he finally couldn’t resist walking up to her.

Yu Wan heard the footsteps and turned to see him. She wasn’t surprised, only silently shifted aside.

"How did you sleep last night?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

He knew she didn’t want to talk to him, but he still had to say something.

Yu Wan hummed in response, not adding anything else.

Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath and, like her, leaned against the railing, looking up at the towering, overlapping peaks. But all his thoughts were on Yu Wan.

"Your mother should have disembarked by now."

Knowing she didn’t want to acknowledge him, he deliberately brought up the topic she cared about most; her mother.

Sure enough, Yu Wan turned her head and fixed her gaze on him. "When you’re willing to let my mother go, then come talk to me."

Yesterday, she had cried so sadly, begging him, but he had remained resolute, refusing to let go. There was no need to soften her tone with him anymore.

Zhao Xuanyou absentmindedly admired the magnificent scenery of Wu Gorge, unmoved by her resistant attitude.

She had made it very clear; she had changed her heart.

What he needed to do now was slowly change her mind back.

He said softly, "Why should I let her go? You and your mother depend on each other. When you reach Yuzhou, where can she go?"

He made it sound as if he had a point.

Yu Wan tightly gripped the railing, once again lowering her head for her mother’s sake. "Zhao Xuanyou, don’t make my mother go to Yuzhou alone, okay? When we disembark, let her come with us, alright?"

"No."

Yu Wan scoffed and turned her face away again.

"Wanwan, I know there’s still someone with exceptional qinggong skills by your side. Yesterday, he didn’t appear by your mother’s side, nor by yours. Naturally, I have to take precautions. When we reach Yuzhou, you will see your mother."

"Are you Zhao Xuanyou? Are you afraid of one person?"

"When it comes to matters concerning you, I cannot help but be cautious."

Yu Wan only let out a cold laugh.

Seeing her anger, Zhao Xuanyou added, "Back in the capital, Yuan Qing was already acquainted with your mother. You know his character. With him escorting your mother, he will certainly take good care of her. Nothing will go wrong on the way."

"Do you know how heartbroken my mother will be not seeing me?"

"Yuan Qing will naturally tell her where you’re going to put her at ease."

Yu Wan stiffened, retorting, "Her daughter was kidnapped on her wedding day. How can she be at ease? Zhao Xuanyou, you consider yourself a filial person. When you say these things, don’t you feel any guilt?"

"This is only a temporary measure. When we reach Yuzhou, I will personally apologize to her."

"Who cares!"

With him here, Yu Wan no longer had any interest in appreciating the scenery of Wu Gorge. She turned to return to her cabin.

But the deck was windy, and Yu Wan’s sleeve had somehow gotten caught on the railing.

She turned and walked quickly, only to be abruptly held back.

Zhao Xuanyou saw her about to fall and reached out to catch her.

Feeling the man’s large hand on her waist, Yu Wan, in a moment of indignation, suddenly pushed him away.

"Don’t touch me!"

Yu Wan was not weak, but compared to Zhao Xuanyou, the difference was vast. In all their past confrontations, she had never gained the upper hand.

This push was, of course, like an egg striking a rock; she just wanted to vent her frustration.

Unexpectedly, Zhao Xuanyou’s body swayed, and he actually fell backward, tumbling from the bow of the ship into the water.

Yu Wan stood frozen in place.

Even when she heard the "splash" of him hitting the water, she still didn’t understand what had happened.

She just couldn’t fathom why Zhao Xuanyou, who had been right in front of her, had suddenly vanished from her sight.

"Master!" Yuan Qian cried out, "Master has fallen into the water! Quick, stop the ship and save him!"

Fallen into the water?

"Zhao... Zhao Xuanyou..."

Yu Wan finally came to her senses and rushed to the railing to look out.

But this was the turbulent Wu Gorge, where the river surged like dragons and snakes, roared like thunder, as if the Yao Pool had been poured out, or the Heavenly River had been overturned.

Even without anyone rowing, the boat would speed downstream as if flying.

In the brief moment she had been stunned, the boat had already drifted far from where Zhao Xuanyou had fallen.

"Zhao Xuanyou!" Yu Wan gripped the railing, shouting his name. But the only response was the rushing river and the distant cries of gibbons from the mountains.

Zhao Xuanyou had already disappeared without a trace.

---

chapters.title: Decisive Action
chapters.content:
"What happened? Where is the Young Master?"

The guards, who had been resting in the cabins, instantly rushed onto the deck.

Someone pointed at Yu Wan and shouted, "The Young Master was pushed into the water by that woman!"

These men Zhao Xuanyou had brought with him were veterans who had followed him into battle for many years. Though they weren’t sworn to die for him, their loyalty was no less than that of any sworn guard.

Because of this accusation, everyone around shot Yu Wan a sharp, hostile glance.

"He... just now..."

Everything had happened so quickly that Yu Wan hadn’t fully processed it yet.

Had he really been pushed in by her?

She had spent a considerable amount of time by Zhao Xuanyou’s side. Whether they were playfully fighting or standing off against each other, Zhao Xuanyou was not only strong but also extremely quick to react.

She had indeed pushed him with all her strength in a moment of anger, but that amount of force meant nothing to Zhao Xuanyou.

Facing the agitated guards, Yu Wan didn’t know how to explain what had just happened.

Seeing them surround Yu Wan with an accusatory stance, Yuan Qian immediately stepped in front of her. "Miss Ding is someone Master went through great trouble to bring back from Anzhou. If anything happens to her, the most important thing right now is to rescue Master."

The guards didn’t know Yu Wan’s background, but they had all seen how urgently Zhao Xuanyou had rushed to find her. Hearing Yuan Qian’s words, they finally calmed down.

"Hurry up and stop the ship to rescue him."

"Lower the dinghies. Anyone good at swimming, get in the water."

The guards cared most about Zhao Xuanyou’s safety and immediately sprang into action.

Yu Wan’s emotions settled slightly, and she looked at Yuan Qian gratefully. "Thank you."

Yuan Qian had, of course, seen Yu Wan push Zhao Xuanyou. For a moment, he didn’t know what to say.

"Just now, Master was acting a bit strange," Yu Wan thought for a moment and recounted what she had seen. "With his usual reactions, he would either sidestep or grab my hand in one move. How could he just stand there and let me push him in?"

Yuan Qian agreed with this.

It wasn’t just Yu Wan; even he wouldn’t have been able to push Master in.

Even if Master was willing to let Yu Wan hit him a few times, with his skills and reflexes, there was no way he would be pushed in by her.

"And also, his expression was a bit off. You know how he usually has a fierce look in his eyes, but just now, I felt his gaze was a little unfocused."

Unfocused?

Yuan Qian paused, recalling that last night when he had delivered water to the Young Master’s cabin, his eyes had also seemed a bit unfocused.

"Master has spent years in the northwest and isn’t used to being on a boat. Maybe he’s severely seasick, which is why..." Now was not the time to dwell on this. Yuan Qian sighed. "I need to go search the river. Miss, you should wait in the cabin for news."

By now, Zhao Xuanyou’s deputy had ordered the helmsman to dock the ship by the shore. The guards were searching the river in four dinghies, and someone had sent a signal into the sky. Downstream soldiers seeing this signal would also set up nets to intercept.

Yu Wan looked at the turbulent river, feeling that they wouldn’t find Zhao Xuanyou this way.

Recalling the description of Wu Gorge from the Records of Scenic Wonders, she said to Yuan Qian, "Go ask if there are any helmsmen or sailors on board from Badong County. They must be locals who grew up by the water."

The waters of Wu Gorge were far more turbulent than elsewhere.

Even large official ships could speed downstream as if flying. What chance did a single person have?

"Alright, I’ll go ask right away."

Seeing that Yu Wan was still concerned about Zhao Xuanyou’s safety, Yuan Qian quickly found a helmsman in his thirties.

"I’ve asked around. This man is a native of Badong County, raised by the river since childhood, and knows the waters well."

Yu Wan nodded and got straight to the point with the helmsman: "I’ve read in books that although the currents in Wu Gorge are rapid, eddy bays appear at regular intervals. How far ahead from here will we find an eddy bay?"

"There are three large eddy bays ahead from here: one at Chuanyun Cave, one at Woniu Mountain, and another below the Goddess Peak. But if someone is swept toward Goddess Peak..."

Goddess Peak was still some distance away. If the first two eddy bays didn’t allow for reaching shore, then by the time one reached Goddess Peak, there would be no chance of survival.

The helmsman only spoke the local dialect, but Yu Wan had lived in Anzhou for several months. As long as he spoke slowly, she could understand.

"Can someone who falls into the river survive?" Yuan Qian asked nervously. "I mean, someone who knows how to swim."

The helmsman answered bluntly: "Out of ten, one might survive. Knowing how to swim is useless in these waters, especially for outsiders who don’t know the currents are rapid and the riverbed is full of hidden reefs. The more you try to swim, the faster you exhaust your strength."

"Then what should one do to survive after falling in?" Yu Wan asked.

"Don’t try to swim to the shore. Float on the surface and keep drifting until you reach an eddy bay where the current slows. Then swim to shore."

She understood. "If you start swimming right away, the current is too strong to reach the shore. By the time you reach the eddy bay, you’d be too exhausted to make it."

"That’s right. But this is all just talk. Once you’re in, it’s up to fate. The river has many whirlpools and hidden reefs; you might not even make it to the eddy bay alive."

Zhao Xuanyou might know how to swim, but did he know that floating with the current was the only chance for survival?

Still, if drifting to an eddy bay was the only hope, then that was where they had to look.

"Shut your crow’s mouth!" Yuan Qian, annoyed by the helmsman’s blunt and inauspicious words, snapped. "Master is blessed by heaven. Nothing will happen to him."

The helmsman, scolded by Yuan Qian, lowered his head. But Yu Wan said, "Yuan Qian, go see if there are any dinghies available. We need to head to the nearest eddy bay immediately."

"You want to go look for him yourself?"

"You’re not thinking I’m trying to escape, are you?" After the incident of her faked death in the capital, Yuan Qian didn’t dare to let his guard down.

Although he was also anxious about Zhao Xuanyou falling into the water, in his heart, Zhao Xuanyou was capable of turning danger into safety.

If he carelessly let Yu Wan escape, he wouldn’t be able to answer to Master when he returned.

"My mother is still in your hands. What would happen to her if I ran? Besides, I don’t want him to die."

For both emotional and rational reasons, Yu Wan hoped Zhao Xuanyou would survive.

First, he had been pushed in by her. She resented him for taking her mother, but she didn’t wish death upon him.

Second, so many people had seen him being pushed into the river by her. He was the sole heir of the Jingyuan Marquis’s family. If he died here, the Marquis’s line would end, and his family and subordinates would never let her off.

Yu Wan’s words convinced Yuan Qian. He immediately said, "I’ll go find a boat right now."

At this moment, all the dinghies were being used by the guards, floating on the river.

Since Yu Wan was the one who had pushed Zhao Xuanyou into the water, the deputy was unwilling to spare a dinghy for her.

However, the deputy also understood that Yu Wan’s reasoning made sense. He immediately ordered a squad to head to the nearest Chuanyun Cave to investigate, while the remaining dinghies slowly searched downstream.

Yu Wan had no choice but to wait. Fortunately, it wasn’t long before a government ship that had seen the signal arrived to assist.

Although Yuan Qian held no military rank, he was a trusted aide of Zhao Xuanyou, so his words carried some weight. He managed to secure a dinghy.

The helmsman took charge of rowing, and Yuan Qian called upon a guard to accompany Yu Wan as they drifted downstream.

Chuanyun Cave had already been sent someone to check, so they immediately set off for the next eddy bay after Chuanyun Cave; Woniu Mountain.

chapters.title: Searching for Him
chapters.content:
The small skiff was light and swift, gliding faster than the official boats on the river.

Yu Wan sat in the skiff, gazing at the steep, axe-hewn cliffs on both banks, feeling the spray of water as the river crashed against the edge of the boat. She felt the peril of the Wu Gorge more deeply than ever.

The current was as swift as an arrow, smashing against the rocks on the shore and sending up countless droplets.

After a while of rapid drifting, the skiff finally slowed. The once turbulent river suddenly calmed, its surface as still as a mirror, reflecting the peaks on either side.

"There they are!" Yuan Zhe pointed to a skiff not far away.

Because the river was calm here, and there was a large reed bed along the shore, it was not easy to spot them.

"It's getting dark, let's hurry to the next place."

The helmsman began rowing, quickly leaving the eddy and re-entering the rapids. After about the time it takes for an incense stick to burn, they finally reached Woniu Mountain.

Here, the river widened, and the mountains gentled. From afar, it looked like a sleeping ox, hence the name Woniu Mountain.

Sure enough, the skiff could no longer drift here and had to rely on the helmsman to row.

There were no reed beds here, but there was a stretch of rocky shoals.

Everyone on the skiff looked around, and the guard who had followed them suddenly pointed to a spot and said, "There seems to be something hanging on that rock!"

Yu Wan looked over and saw a dark object hanging on a reef near the shore.

Remembering that Zhao Xuanyou was indeed wearing black clothes today, her heart suddenly jumped. She ordered the helmsman to row over immediately.

As the skiff got closer to the rock, Yu Wan looked at the person on the reef and almost stopped breathing.

Zhao Xuanyou was half-hanging on the rock, his hair bun long undone, his fine clothes tattered, his face as pale as paper.

Even more shocking was the faint red color on the reef beneath him.

Since she had known Zhao Xuanyou, she had never seen him in such a pitiful state.

He had always been cold and imposing, decisive in speech and action, invincible wherever he went.

"Master!" Yuan Zhe and the guard, seeing this, leapt onto the reef.

The helmsman muttered softly, "This is just bad luck, drifting and then hitting a rock."

"Row the boat over," Yu Wan ordered.

By the time the helmsman had rowed the skiff to the side of the reef, she heard the guard say, "Master's breathing is very weak."

That meant he was still alive.

The huge stone in Yu Wan's heart finally landed. When the skiff approached, she also jumped onto the reef.

"The water is too cold, let's pull Master up a bit," the guard said.

Yuan Zhe looked back at the skiff, frowning. "The skiff is too small. We need to take Master to the shore."

Since Zhao Xuanyou was in poor condition and urgently needed a doctor, Yuan Zhe immediately sent a signal for help.

Yu Wan looked at the blood on Zhao Xuanyou's lower body and reminded them, "His leg might be injured. Be careful not to touch it."

Only then did Yuan Zhe and the guard notice that Zhao Xuanyou's right leg was twisted in an unnatural position. They pulled open his clothes and saw a deep wound on his right leg, bone visible, still bleeding.

If they had arrived a moment later, Zhao Xuanyou would have died from blood loss right there.

"Sir, I have some liquor here." The helmsman quickly untied the gourd from his waist and threw it to Yuan Zhe.

Yuan Zhe and the guard, though not doctors, had some knowledge of external injuries from their years in the military.

Yuan Zhe immediately used the liquor to clean the wound, then tore his own clothes into strips to bandage it.

Meanwhile, the guard leapt from the reef and used his dagger to cut down several branches of consistent length.

After securing Zhao Xuanyou's right leg with the branches, the two of them carried him to the shore.

Yu Wan slowly jumped from the reef to the shore. Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was soaked, she crouched down and used a handkerchief to wipe his hair, then reminded them, "His clothes need to be taken off immediately, or he'll catch a cold."

"Yes."

Yuan Zhe helped her remove Zhao Xuanyou's wet clothes and put his own on him.

After all this was done, a team of reinforcements finally arrived.

They were soldiers stationed nearby who had seen Yuan Zhe's distress signal and come to investigate.

"Brother, what happened?"

"My master is Zhao Xuanyou, the heir of Jingyuan Hou's mansion. He was injured in an accident while patrolling the army on orders from the Ministry of War. He is now breathing weakly and urgently needs a doctor."

Since Zhao Xuanyou had not brought many people with him to Anzhou to find Yu Wan, and they were all elite, he naturally had not brought a military doctor.

Yuan Zhe presented his token, and after the other party confirmed his identity, they said, "So it's Master Zhao who is injured. However, this place is remote and lacks medical supplies. We need to take him to Badong County."

"He has a leg injury and cannot be moved easily. He needs to travel by carriage."

"Don't worry, we will arrange it properly."

Their camp was not far from here. Moments later, they returned with a carriage and helped carry Zhao Xuanyou into it.

They then ordered the helmsman to stay and wait for the people from the official boat, and escorted Zhao Xuanyou to Badong County.

As a high-ranking official of the court, the local magistrate naturally did not dare to neglect Zhao Xuanyou. He immediately arranged for Zhao Xuanyou to stay in the county yamen to recover and summoned the best doctors in the county to diagnose him.

After the doctors took turns examining him, they quickly reached a conclusion.

"Master Zhao must have hit a reef while drifting in the river, injuring his right leg. Fortunately, it was his leg and not his upper body. Bone injuries are difficult to heal, but with time, they will recover."

"That's right. The reason the heir is unconscious is not because of a head injury, but because the wound on his right leg is too large, causing excessive blood loss. With rest, he should wake up in a few days."

That was a relief. Yu Wan let out a slight sigh.

Suddenly, an elderly doctor with white hair said, "Master Zhao's pulse is weak. Besides excessive blood loss, there seems to be something else unusual."

Yuan Zhe asked urgently, "What's unusual?"

"It seems like he's been poisoned."

"Poisoned?" Yuan Zhe looked at Yu Wan subconsciously. "Then Master falling into the water was also because..."

Yu Wan also thought of what she had told Yuan Zhe earlier. Zhao Xuanyou had a scattered look in his eyes when he was on the deck. Could it be that he was already poisoned then?

"Doctor, do you have a way to detoxify him?"

"No need to worry. Master Zhao has not been poisoned with a lethal toxin. There should be no danger to his life. I have taken some blood samples and will examine them further at the clinic."

"Thank you, Doctor."

"It is my honor to treat Master Zhao. There's no need to be polite."

After the doctors wrote the prescriptions, Yuan Zhe ordered someone to prepare the medicine.

Yu Wan returned to the inner room, untied the temporary bandage from the riverside, dried the wound, and reapplied the medicinal powder.

Yuan Zhe watched her careful actions and couldn't help but say, "When Master wakes up and knows that it was you who applied the medicine, he will be very happy."

Would he be happy?

After all, it was she who had pushed him down.

Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou, who lay on the bed with his eyes closed, and sighed. No matter what, she hoped he would wake up soon.

After she finished rebandaging the wound with white cloth, she turned to Yuan Zhe. "Do you think when did he get poisoned?"

"Naturally, it was yesterday."

Yesterday?

Yu Wan was slightly startled.

Pei Ta's subordinate, Lu Jie, was skilled in using poison. Could it be that Zhao Xuanyou was poisoned while fighting someone in the street?

---

chapters.title: Lingering Spring Rain
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou was unconscious for three days, and the spring rain lingered for three days.

Badong's climate was humid. Even though Yu Wan stayed indoors all day, she always felt her clothes were damp.

At this moment, she was sitting by the bed applying medicine to Zhao Xuanyou.

The doctor had reset the bone in his right leg two days ago, but the wound from the reef was too deep and had been soaked in river water for a while. It needed to be cleaned twice a day and reapply medicinal powder.

As the medicinal powder touched the wound, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly let out a muffled groan.

For the past two days, whether it was applying medicine or feeding him water, he had shown no reaction. But now, his facial expression twitched slightly, looking very painful.

Had he woken up?

"Zhao Xuanyou?" Yu Wan called softly.

Perhaps because of the pain, his forehead was covered in cold sweat, but his eyes remained closed.

"You endure it a little. I'll try to be quick."

Yu Wan quickly applied the medicine and skillfully tied the bandage.

When she looked up, the man on the bed had half-opened his eyes and was quietly staring at her.

"You're awake?"

Zhao Xuanyou was pale and had no strength to speak. He couldn't even fully open his eyes.

"Your leg hit a reef. The injury is severe. The doctor said it will take at least half a year to recover. But other than that, it's just minor scrapes."

Seeing his lips were slightly chapped, Yu Wan thought to get up and bring him water.

But as soon as she moved, she felt her sleeve being pulled.

Yu Wan turned back and met his weak gaze, feeling a mix of helplessness and pity.

He had always been cold and hard-hearted. In all the time she had known him, this was the first time she had seen him look so childlike.

She had no choice but to soften her tone. "I'm getting you water."

After he let go of her hand, Yu Wan called Yuan Zhe in and told him that Zhao Xuanyou had woken up.

"Really?" Yuan Zhe was overjoyed. "Thank heavens, he woke up in just three days! This is great news. I'll go get the doctor right away."

With that, Yuan Zhe hurried off.

Yu Wan went to the table and poured a cup of warm water, then fed it to him.

After Zhao Xuanyou regained consciousness, feeding him water was much easier than before. She didn't have to pry open his mouth or worry about water spilling from the corner of his lips onto the pillow.

By the time he finished the cup of water, Yuan Zhe had already arrived with the doctor in tow.

The doctor examined his wound and took his pulse before prescribing a new medicine, instructing him to take it on time every day.

When Yu Wan came back in the evening to change his dressing, Zhao Xuanyou's spirits had improved a lot. He had even asked Yuan Zhe to help him sit up on the bed.

Seeing him showing off, Yu Wan couldn't help but say, "Your leg wound is too deep. The doctor said you shouldn't move now."

"Then should I lie back down?" Zhao Xuanyou's face was still pale, his voice weak, but his tone carried a hint of teasing.

"You've already sat up, so don't move around."

Yu Wan said helplessly, sitting back down by the bed. She lifted the blanket and began to undo the bandage.

The wound was too deep and had not yet scabbed over, so every grain of medicinal powder sprinkled on it caused excruciating pain.

But Zhao Xuanyou didn't make a sound.

It was only after Yu Wan finished bandaging the wound that she noticed the cold sweat on his forehead.

Zhao Xuanyou quietly watched Yu Wan.

At this moment, she was not on guard or distant. Her expression was somewhat soft, and her gaze, as it fell on him, carried a tenderness he had only seen in the past.

"Wanwan, you sitting here reminds me of the days in Honghui Hall."

Yu Wan did not speak. She raised her hand with a handkerchief to wipe his sweat, but before the handkerchief could touch his forehead, it was blocked by his hand.

"Do you dislike this servant's clumsy hands?"

Hearing her deliberately refer to herself as a "servant," Zhao Xuanyou's eyes flickered. In a hoarse voice, he said, "You are no longer a servant of the Hou's mansion. You don't have to do these things anymore."

Yu Wan's eyes showed a hint of surprise, not understanding what he meant.

"Will you let me go?"

Zhao Xuanyou let out a light laugh, clearly not meaning that.

He did enjoy her care, but she had said before that her days in the Hou's mansion were not happy.

"I came to find you, not to make you return as a maid."

Yu Wan was not surprised by this answer, but she was momentarily speechless.

The room was very quiet, with only the sound of rain outside.

She put away her handkerchief and was about to get up to leave when Zhao Xuanyou suddenly asked, "How long was I unconscious?"

"Today is the third day."

"Where is this place?"

"This is the rear residence of the Badong County Yamen. The magistrate has vacated a courtyard for you to recover."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou frowning in silence, Yu Wan could roughly guess what he was thinking.

Badong was not far from Anzhou. He was worried that Pei Ta would chase him here.

So she said, "Don't think about leaving. The doctor said the wound on your leg is too deep. It will take at least ten days or half a month to heal. It's not advisable to move, let alone travel by carriage. No matter what, we have to wait at least a month."

Zhao Xuanyou curved the corner of his lips slightly.

She understood him well. In any case, this was a good thing.

"You know you were poisoned, right?" After a moment of silence, Yu Wan still brought up the topic of the poison.

Zhao Xuanyou responded with an "mm."

"If you knew, why didn't you say anything?"

"What good would it do to say it? Anyway, it's not fatal."

Yu Wan had experienced Lu Jie's "Soft Bone Powder." Although it wasn't life-threatening, it made her bones ache and weaken, which was quite uncomfortable.

"The doctors here don't know how to detoxify you."

"We'll handle it when we return to Yuzhou."

With just a few words, he made his attitude clear.

He would not go back to Pei Ta for the antidote.

Seeing Yu Wan looking down in silence, Zhao Xuanyou said indifferently, "Fighting with others naturally comes with risks. It has nothing to do with you."

"Then my pushing you into the water also has nothing to do with you?" Yu Wan countered.

Zhao Xuanyou raised his chin. Seeing a hint of guilt in Yu Wan's eyes, he said softly, "If you had known I was poisoned, would you not have pushed me down?"

Yu Wan turned her head to look at the rain curtain outside the window.

"I just wanted you to let me go. I didn't want you to die."

"Do you want to leave that much?"

"Would you be willing if I had captured the Old Taijun and used her to coerce you into doing things for me?"

Outside the window, the rain grew heavier, and the raindrops pounded the leaves, making a rustling sound.

Through the window lattice, Yu Wan could see the tree shadows swaying in the wind.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her back and could hear the grievance in her tone.

"You should rest. Call me if you need anything."

She simply got up.

Rather than saying things that would lead nowhere, it was better to go outside for some air.

"Wanwan."

Before she could round the screen, Zhao Xuanyou called out to her.

Yu Wan turned back.

"I have a question in my heart. Answer me truthfully."

"I may not answer."

"No, you must answer." Zhao Xuanyou stared at her intently, asking the question that had been buried in his heart. "You left the capital for three years. If the person who found you now was not Pei Ta, but me, would you have married me?"

Married...

Yu Wan was slightly distracted. She said indifferently, "There's no point in talking about something that didn't happen. Your Highness should focus on recovering."

With that, Yu Wan walked straight out.

There was a point, of course there was.

If she had just flatly denied it, he probably would have let her go.

But her evasive answer had opened a small gap in the thick, dark clouds, allowing a ray of spring sunlight to shine through, illuminating a glimmer of light.

Even if there was only a glimmer of possibility, he would strive for it to the end.

chapters.title: Sneaking In During the Rain
chapters.content:
Yu Ying walked to the corridor and pulled over a chair to sit down.

The rain had lightened a bit now. No longer could one see large raindrops; instead, the courtyard seemed shrouded in a misty veil.

Zhao Xuanyou had been unconscious for three days. Yu Ying and Yuan Zhe had taken turns caring for him by his side. Now that he had finally awakened, it was a relief.

"Miss." Yuan Zhe, having decocted the medicine, entered from outside holding an umbrella. Seeing Yu Ying sitting blankly in the corridor, he said, "If you're tired, you should rest. I'll keep watch over the young master."

"Alright." Yu Ying did not refuse.

The first two days of caring for him while he was unconscious had not been troublesome. Now that he was awake, if she continued to attend to him closely, she would inevitably have to speak with him.

Yu Ying did not want to speak with him.

Just now, they had seemed to say little, but she still felt a strange suffocation.

Lost in thought, something suddenly struck the ground beside her embroidered shoes.

Had it fallen from a tree?

Yu Ying stared at the object on the ground and saw it was a pink flower bud.

She paid it no mind, but then a second flower bud dropped right in front of her.

A sudden chill ran through her. She gripped the chair with both hands, then took a deep breath, forcing her expression to return to normal.

She glanced left and right, confirming that Yuan Zhe was still inside taking care of Zhao Xuanyou, before slowly standing up and walking to the edge of the corridor, pretending to look around casually.

As she lifted her head, she saw a person squatting on the nearest large tree to the house. That person was wearing the tanuki mask she had bought during the Lantern Festival.

A surge of wild joy welled up in Yu Ying’s heart. She did her best to suppress the expression on her face and slowly walked sideways.

After Zhao Xuanyou moved into this courtyard, Yuan Zhe had dismissed all the original maids. Only he and Yu Ying entered and exited the house.

The deputy general had arranged guards at various points around the county office, and they would patrol the small courtyard once a day.

At this moment, there should be no one else in the courtyard.

Yu Ying looked back once more, then quickly jumped down from the corridor and ran to the side room next to the courtyard wall.

As soon as she entered the room, she felt a gust of wind behind her.

"Wen Sun!" Yu Ying turned around and, seeing Wen Sun removing his mask, her nose suddenly felt a sting. "When did you arrive?"

She didn’t forget to go forward and close the door of the side room.

"Yesterday."

"Then why did you only appear now?"

Wen Sun said helplessly, "You're either in the house or with that young servant. How could I appear?"

"So you've been hiding in the mansion all this time without being discovered?"

"This endless rain has actually been helpful to me."

Seeing Wen Sun’s clothes and hair were soaked through, Yu Ying couldn’t help but say, "But you can’t keep getting drenched in the rain."

Seeing Wen Sun, Yu Ying naturally thought of Pei Ta, who had been left in Anzhou.

After a moment of hesitation, she finally asked, "How is he?"

"He’s quite heartbroken. He’s been thinking about how to rescue you."

Wen Sun saw that his words had already made Yu Ying’s eyes red, so he quickly changed the subject: "Do you know where Mother is being held? I’ve circled the county office several times but couldn’t find where she’s imprisoned."

Having pretended to be mother and son for three years, Wen Sun calling her "Mother" came quite naturally.

At the mention of Ding Wenxi, Yu Ying pushed down her tangled emotions, her eyes dimming as she softly said, "Mother didn’t travel with me. Zhao Xuanyou had someone send her to Yuzhou first."

"Already sent to Yuzhou? That’s a bit troublesome."

After Zhao Xuanyou fell into the water, Pei Ta’s side had also received the news.

Knowing that they were currently in Badong County recovering from injuries, Wen Sun had rushed over overnight.

Thinking that Zhao Xuanyou was seriously injured, the number of people guarding Yu Ying and her mother would certainly be reduced. Perhaps he could rescue them.

He hadn’t expected Ding Wenxi to have already been sent to Yuzhou first.

"Yuzhou is under the jurisdiction of the Marquis of Jingyuan. There, Zhao Xuanyou’s word carries more weight than the emperor’s. Without his say-so, it will be very difficult to rescue my mother."

Wen Sun hesitated for a moment before slowly saying, "There is still one way."

"You mean the fact that he’s been poisoned?"

"You know?"

Yu Ying nodded slightly.

Seeing the faint dimness in Yu Ying’s eyes, Wen Sun didn’t understand, so he asked, "What happened?"

"That day, I didn’t know he had been poisoned with Lu Jie’s Soft Bone Powder, so I pushed him off the boat."

Upon hearing this, Wen Sun suddenly understood why Yu Ying had been taking such good care of Zhao Xuanyou.

"What do you plan to do?"

"I don’t know."

Wen Sun was not unfamiliar with these four words.

He had been by Yu Ying’s side for a long time. When she said "I don’t know," it usually wasn’t that she truly didn’t know, but rather that she already knew and didn’t know how to say it.

Looking at Yu Ying’s distressed and aggrieved expression, Wen Sun, though still maintaining his usual expressionless face, had a noticeably softer tone.

"What do you want me to do?"

These simple words made Yu Ying’s eyes light up instantly.

Apart from her mother, Wen Sun was the person who treated her the best in this world.

"Can... can you help Zhao Xuanyou get the antidote?"

"Do you really want to cure his poison?" Wen Sun didn’t quite understand. "Since he can’t cure the poison himself, wouldn’t it be better for us to use the antidote to exchange for Mother’s freedom?"

"It’s not good."

Wen Sun pursed his lips and didn’t speak.

"He’s not the kind of person who can be threatened. Even if I said that, he wouldn’t agree to release Mother." Yu Ying sighed. "This time he fell into the river and was seriously injured. With the poison on top of that, I’m afraid it will be very hard for him to recover. He is a martial general after all. If he ends up disabled... Wen Sun, please help me."

"I didn’t say I wouldn’t help you."

Although Wen Sun had doubts about Yu Ying’s decision, since it was her wish, he would naturally comply.

"Yu Ying, will we still return to Anzhou?"

"We can’t go back."

From the moment Zhao Xuanyou took her away, her and Pei Ta’s relationship had already ended.

When she decided to marry Pei Ta, she had thought she could live a peaceful life in the remote land of Shu.

Since Zhao Xuanyou knew her whereabouts, even if he hadn’t taken her mother away, with his stubbornness, he was bound to entangle her to the end.

"You don’t want to marry Lord Pei anymore?" Wen Sun asked curiously.

"How can I have the face to marry him after running off with another man in my wedding dress?"

Was that so?

Wen Sun felt that if Yu Ying could escape successfully, Pei Ta would definitely still want to marry her.

But since Yu Ying said so, there must be her reasons.

"Then will you marry Zhao Xuanyou in the future?"

"I’m only staying by his side as a temporary measure for now. Let’s first go to Yuzhou to meet up with Mother, and then we’ll figure out what to do next."

"Alright."

Wen Sun had always trusted Yu Ying’s words without doubt.

Whether it was Zhao Xuanyou or Pei Ta, if Yu Ying liked them, then they were good. If Yu Ying didn’t like them anymore, then they were irrelevant.

After thinking for a moment, Wen Sun asked again, "When I go back to get the antidote, do I need to hide it from Lord Pei?"

Wen Sun had grown close to Pei Ta solely because Yu Ying liked Pei Ta.

Now that Yu Ying was not going to marry Pei Ta, in Wen Sun’s eyes, Pei Ta was naturally someone to be wary of as well.

"You... first find a way to get the antidote. Once you have it..."

Wen Sun waited quietly for Yu Ying to continue.

"Say goodbye to him for me."

---

chapters.title: No Heart to Love the Beautiful Night
chapters.content:
"How should I say it?" Wen Sun hesitated. "That you will never return to Anzhou?"

"Just say..."

The jade pendant that served as their betrothal token had already been dropped in the bridal sedan that day. Yu Ying had already spoken the words of breaking off the engagement.

But those simple words were indeed cruel to Pei Ta.

In terms of both emotion and reason, she owed him a proper apology.

"You wait for me here for a moment."

Yu Ying finished speaking, pushed open the door, and walked into the rain.

She quickly entered the main house and, through the screen, saw Yuan Zhe massaging Zhao Xuanyou’s legs by the couch.

Taking advantage of his busyness, Yu Ying entered the adjacent study, took paper, ground ink, and picked up a brush.

After putting down the brush, she thought for a moment, then took out another sheet of paper and began copying poems from the poetry collection beside her.

While she was copying, Yuan Zhe came over with a plate of pastries.

"What is this?" Yu Ying, without changing her expression, put down the brush and looked over curiously. "It smells so good."

"It’s just been sent from the kitchen; shadow beef, a local specialty here. It’s still hot. Miss, try some."

"Thank you." Yu Ying took the plate and tried a thin slice. It was indeed crispy, fragrant, and spicy; very delicious. "You try some too."

"There’s more outside. I’ll go attend to the young master. I won’t disturb Miss’s calligraphy practice."

Back when Yu Ying was in Honghui Hall, she practiced calligraphy every day, so Yuan Zhe naturally didn’t find it strange.

After Yuan Zhe left, Yu Ying copied two more poems before quietly taking the previously written letter and leaving the room.

Returning to the side room, Wen Sun was still waiting inside.

Yu Ying handed the letter to him.

"Is this a letter for Lord Pei?" Wen Sun took the letter and looked up at Yu Ying. "Then I don’t need to say anything else?"

Although nearly a year had passed, the scene of Pei Ta riding a horse to the riverbank to search for her seemed like it was just yesterday.

That was also a spring day. Yu Ying didn’t know what had come over her then, but she had boarded the boat without any hesitation.

She had waited for his news in Suzhou, then brought her mother and Wen Sun to Shu to find him, and they had become engaged. Though they hadn’t spent much time together, everything had been too beautiful.

Sure enough, beautiful things only appeared in dreams.

Now that the dream was over, everything should end.

Yu Ying took a deep breath and steeled herself. "You don’t need to say anything. He will understand."

"Then I’ll leave first." Wen Sun carefully put away the letter and looked at Yu Ying.

Yu Ying nodded and instructed, "Be careful. If... you can’t get the antidote, come back and discuss it with me first."

"I know. You take care of yourself too."

"That’s natural." No matter how many worries she had, in front of her mother and Wen Sun, she always seemed without a care. "You wait here. I’ll go out and keep watch for you."

Yu Ying pushed open the door and walked out of the side room. After confirming there was no one around, she turned back and nodded at Wen Sun.

Wen Sun understood and quickly left the side room. His figure soon disappeared into the rain.

The spring rain obscured the view and muffled sounds. With Wen Sun’s skills, he naturally came and went without a trace.

After leaving the county office, Wen Sun immediately headed to the dock, boarded a ship to Shu, and arrived in Anzhou two days later.

When the servants of the Pei mansion saw it was him, following Pei Ta’s earlier instructions, one sent someone inside to announce his arrival while the other directly led Wen Sun to Pei Ta’s study.

As soon as Wen Sun entered the study, Pei Ta, dressed in a light blue robe, stood up from behind his desk, his eyes filled with urgency.

"Have you seen Yu’er?"

"I found her."

"She... didn’t come back with you?"

Wen Sun shook his head and briefly told Pei Ta what he had learned in Badong County.

"After Zhao Xuanyou fell into the river, he was seriously injured. His leg was broken, and he had deep cuts from the reefs. He couldn’t even sit in a carriage. They will stay in Badong for a while."

Pei Ta’s eyes flickered, as if realizing something. "Yu’er is staying there to take care of him?"

"Yu Ying didn’t know he had been poisoned with Soft Bone Powder, so that’s why she pushed him off the boat into the river. So she..." Wen Sun looked at Pei Ta’s expression, paused, and then said, "She wants to ask you, Lord Pei, to give me the antidote for Soft Bone Powder to cure Zhao Xuanyou."

"And what about her?" Pei Ta could give Zhao Xuanyou the antidote, but he only cared about Yu Ying. "After curing Zhao Xuanyou, will she come back?"

"Before Zhao Xuanyou’s accident, he had already sent Mother to Yuzhou. Yu Ying and I will still go to Yuzhou."

"And after that?"

Wen Sun thought for a moment and realized he couldn’t give Pei Ta any answer, so he took out Yu Ying’s letter from his waist and handed it to him.

Pei Ta took the folded letter. Though he hadn’t read a single word, a foreboding sense of unease filled his heart.

He took a deep breath and opened the letter. Before he could read it carefully, his eyes fell on the last sentence.

"...This life holds no fate, I wish you to find another good match."

Pei Ta clutched the letter, his lips moving as if he wanted to say something. Suddenly, he staggered back a few steps and bumped into the bookshelf beside him.

Several books fell to the ground with a clatter. One copy of Yutai Xinyong landed open in front of him, right on the page with "From this point on, no heart to love the beautiful night."

"Lord Pei."

Hearing the noise, the young servant outside hurried in to check. Seeing the fallen books, he quickly went to pick them up.

"I’m fine." Pei Ta said softly.

Outside the window, a light rain began to drizzle. Wen Sun turned his head and, from where he stood, could see two banana trees.

The banana leaves, saturated with rain, were an especially vibrant green.

Pei Ta also looked up and saw the banana trees outside the window. A pale smile appeared on his lips. "After she read Li Qingzhao’s poem, she said the study must have banana trees planted outside so that when she was tired from reading, she could lift her eyes and see that touch of green."

"Did she plant them?"

Pei Ta lightly hummed in agreement, then murmured, "Who planted the banana trees in front of the window? Their shade fills the courtyard. Leaf by leaf, heart by heart, unfurling with lingering affection."

The poem was too sad.

He shouldn’t have planted those banana trees.

Wen Sun wasn’t well-versed in poetry, but he could hear the sorrow in Pei Ta’s voice.

Even though he was eager to get the antidote and return to Yu Ying, he didn’t urge Pei Ta, instead standing silently by his side.

After a long while, he finally heard Pei Ta say, "Go call Lu Jie over."

Soon, Lu Jie arrived in a hurry. Pei Ta said, "Give the antidote for Soft Bone Powder to Mr. Song."

Lu Jie was stunned for a moment, then immediately beamed with joy. "So that Zhao fellow is willing to exchange the antidote for a person?"

But as soon as the words left his mouth, he noticed that Pei Ta’s face showed no joy. He glanced at Wen Sun beside him, who was also expressionless.

The atmosphere in the room was heavy, not like there was good news.

He silently took out a white porcelain bottle from his embrace and waited for Wen Sun to take it before instructing, "Take one spoonful each day. You can eat it directly or mix it with water. Just finish this bottle and it’ll be fine."

"Thank you."

Wen Sun secured the antidote and was about to turn and leave when he suddenly thought of something.

After a moment of hesitation, he still asked, "Does Lord Pei have any words you’d like me to pass on to her?"

"Tell her..." Pei Ta’s voice paused for a long time before he sighed softly, "There’s no need to feel guilty."

chapters.title: Promise
chapters.content:
When Wen Sun returned to the Badong County Yamen, Yu Ying was sitting under the veranda reading a book.

Zhao Xuanyou had told her not to attend to him, so she was content to stay idle, letting Yuan Qian serve him while she spent her days reading and writing.

Hearing the rustling in the trees, Yu Ying suddenly looked up and indeed saw the familiar mask.

She dared not make a sound and quickly walked toward the side room.

Wen Sun followed her into the side room and handed her the white porcelain bottle containing the antidote.

"Lu Jie said to take one spoonful a day. Once the bottle is finished, there will be no more trouble."

Yu Ying held the porcelain bottle, pursed her lips, and looked up at Wen Sun.

Wen Sun understood and whispered, "He said you don’t need to feel guilty."

Don’t need to feel guilty?

Hearing those four words, Yu Ying’s heart jolted. In the end, he was still thinking of her.

"I see." Yu Ying’s voice was low. She paused, then looked up at Wen Sun with gratitude. "You’ve been running around so much. It must have been tiring."

Wen Sun frowned at her words. "Why are you saying this to me?"

They had never been so formal with each other before.

Yu Ying smiled slightly. "Wait for me here. I’ll go inside and deliver the medicine."

"Mm."

Yu Ying turned around, took several deep breaths to steady herself, then took the porcelain bottle into the main house.

Since the day he had impulsively sat up and torn his wound, he had been lying obediently on the bed for the past few days.

Hearing Yu Ying’s footsteps, he turned to look at her, his eyebrows twitching slightly as he gave her a faint smile.

After he woke up, though Yu Ying still lived in the small courtyard, she hadn’t exchanged more than a few words with him each day.

Yu Ying said, "There really is something."

"Go on."

Aside from leaving him, he would agree to anything.

Yu Ying stepped forward and took out the white porcelain bottle, placing it by his pillow.

"This is the antidote for the Soft Bone Powder. Take one spoonful each day. Once the bottle is finished, you’ll be fine."

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly propped himself up halfway.

"You went to find him?"

Seeing him staring at her intently, Yu Ying remained silent.

After a moment of silent eye contact, the tension in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes gradually dissipated.

Yu Ying had been in the county yamen all this time. How could she have gone to find Pei Ta?

"You got injured because I pushed you into the water. Finding the antidote for you is my way of making amends."

"How did you get the medicine?"

"I have my ways."

"That person by your side?"

"That’s none of your concern."

Zhao Xuanyou listened to her words, his gaze dark and unfathomable, lost in thought.

Yu Ying had said all she needed to say. She nodded at him, then turned to leave.

Zhao Xuanyou on the bed suddenly grabbed her hand.

Yu Ying turned back, her eyes fixed on him. "Zhao Xuanyou, you said you wouldn’t touch me!"

He let go of her hand but still held onto her sleeve.

The spring weather was warming, and Yu Ying’s spring dress was thin. Since it was a garment Zhao Xuanyou had specially prepared for her, the fabric was fine, with intricate embroidery. Even the hibiscus flowers on the cuffs were vivid and charming.

"You look very beautiful in this dress," Zhao Xuanyou said softly.

Yu Ying lifted her hand, pulling her sleeve from his fingers, and said indifferently, "Is that what you wanted to say?"

"No," Zhao Xuanyou paused slightly, looking at the displeasure in her eyes. He examined her more seriously. "Yingying, I’m very happy you found the antidote for me."

Yu Ying still kept a straight face.

"I’ll return the favor. How about that?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s body was still weak, so his voice was soft.

But this light voice in Yu Ying’s ears was like a clap of thunder.

Her heart trembled with surprise, joy, and mostly disbelief.

Could it be that he was going to let her go?

No, he had gone to great lengths to find her. How could he possibly let her go?

In that brief moment, the flicker of joy in Yu Ying’s heart vanished like smoke.

She didn’t speak, silently waiting for him to continue.

"Yingying, as long as you promise not to marry Pei Ta again and have nothing to do with him, once we reach Yuzhou, I won’t restrain you."

"Really?" Yu Ying’s eyes held some doubt.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze remained fixed on her face, not missing any of her reactions.

Regardless, Yu Ying’s current reaction greatly relieved his mood.

He hummed in agreement, his expression still cool as usual.

"Then you promise not to marry Pei Ta?"

When Yu Ying had sent Wen Sun to get the antidote, she had already let go of her connection with Pei Ta.

"Even if I promise to have nothing to do with him, it doesn’t mean I’ll have any ties with you."

"I know. So you agree?"

"Who knows if you’re lying to me? Whether I agree or not depends on seeing my mother."

Zhao Xuanyou smiled slightly. "Then I’ll take it as your agreement. Rest assured, I keep my word. From this moment on, I won’t have anyone follow you. You’re free to come and go, and your friend doesn’t need to hide in the shadows."

"You say it so easily. You’ve taken my mother, and you talk to me about freedom to come and go?"

"Yingying, once you reach Yuzhou, you’ll understand everything."

"There’s no need to wait until Yuzhou. I understand everything already. It would be best if you do too."

With that, Yu Ying quickly walked out.

Her mind was in turmoil.

Logically, she should be happy that Zhao Xuanyou had agreed to let her go once they reached Yuzhou.

But deep down, there was a lingering unease.

He seemed very certain that she would change her mind once they reached Yuzhou.

What was in Yuzhou?!

Yu Ying shook her head hard, dispelling the chaotic thoughts.

She couldn’t let Zhao Xuanyou lead her by the nose. In Yuzhou, aside from her mother, there was nothing that could attract her.

Wen Sun, who was in the side room, saw her return and stood up to ask, "Did you give him the antidote?"

"Yes."

"Is there anything else you need me to do?"

"Nothing else." Yu Ying reached out and pulled Wen Sun’s sleeve, leading him outside.

Wen Sun asked in surprise, "What are you doing?"

"Zhao Xuanyou promised to let me go once we reach Yuzhou. We don’t need to think of any other plans. We just need to wait until we get to Yuzhou, see my mother, and leave together."

"He said that? Can we trust him?"

Yu Ying lowered her gaze. "It should be trustworthy."

As the two of them just walked out of the side room, Yuan Qian came forward and, looking at Wen Sun’s unfamiliar face, asked curiously, "Is this young lady’s sworn brother?"

"He’s my sworn younger brother," Yu Ying corrected.

Wen Sun had been abandoned by his parents and didn’t know his exact birth date.

It wasn’t clear whether he was older or younger than Yu Ying.

When they had settled in Qingsha County, Yu Ying had insisted he become her younger brother to take advantage of him.

Wen Sun had gone along with it.

"Young master." Yuan Qian quickly greeted Wen Sun and said, "I’ll go prepare a room for you right away." With that, he hurried off.

"I’m staying here too?"

"Of course. Without you and Mother around, I’m all alone and bored to death." Yu Ying sighed.

When they were around, Yu Ying could vent her temper and frustrations directly at them. In front of others, she had to endure.

Yu Ying shook Wen Sun’s sleeve.

"Let’s go to the roof for a while."

---

chapters.title: Wu Mountain Rain
chapters.content:
"Be careful."

Spring rains had been falling for days, and the green tiles on the roof were a bit slippery.

Yu Ying hadn’t thought much of it at first, but as soon as she stepped on them, she found them a little slippery.

Seeing this, Wen Sun simply took her with him in a leap to the ridge of the roof.

At this moment, sitting on the roof ridge with Wen Sun, it felt as if they had returned to the days in Qingsha Town.

"Wen Sun, do you blame me?" Yu Ying suddenly asked, looking at the lush garden.

Wen Sun was confused by her words. "Blame you for what?"

"Blame me for acting on impulse. If I hadn’t impulsively boarded the ship last year, Mother wouldn’t be alone in Yuzhou now, and you wouldn’t have to run around doing things for me."

Wen Sun had never felt that doing things for Yu Ying was a bother.

After thinking for a moment, he said, "It was a bit impulsive, but you didn’t do anything wrong. Back then, so many noble ladies in the capital were infatuated with him. Whoever he asked to marry, they would have been willing."

"Yeah, that’s why I wanted to be reckless once. In the end, it was just a pipe dream."

It wasn’t raining today, but the sky was thick with clouds, and it looked like it would rain again soon.

"It wasn’t a pipe dream," Wen Sun said softly, turning his head to look at Yu Ying.

Her cheeks were like fine snow, her eyebrows and eyes were exquisite, and her eyes seemed filled with the spring rain, shimmering brightly.

Her beauty alone was enough to captivate a nation, let alone her clever mind.

There might be no shortage of beauties in the world, but there was only one Yu Ying.

It was no wonder Zhao Xuanyou and Pei Ta were fond of her.

Yu Ying smiled bitterly. "You don’t need to comfort me. I understand very well that someone of my status doesn’t have the right to talk about love."

The world was just that cruel.

"If you weren’t a maidservant, but a young lady from a noble family, you and Zhao Xuanyou would have been a very well-matched pair."

Yu Ying was slightly taken aback and looked at Wen Sun.

She was a little surprised that Wen Sun had mentioned Zhao Xuanyou instead of Pei Ta.

"Why bring him up?"

"I just think that if that were the case, you wouldn’t have left the capital at all."

"There are no so many 'if's. Even if I were a noble lady, I might not have met him. And even if I had, he might not have taken a fancy to me."

There had been too many twists and turns to get to this point. Perhaps it was truly a doomed fate.

If it were anything else, Wen Sun could have helped, but with matters of the heart, he truly couldn’t.

"Want some candy?" Wen Sun took out an oiled paper package from his bosom.

"Is it hawthorn candy?"

"Mm, from Guixiang Tower."

When Yu Ying had first arrived in Anzhou, she couldn’t get used to the local food, but she had liked the hawthorn candy from Guixiang Tower. Every time Wen Sun went out, he would bring her a pack.

When Wen Sun had left Anzhou with the antidote, he had specially gone to Guixiang Tower to buy some to bring with him.

Seeing Yu Ying focus on eating the candy, Wen Sun suddenly said, "Actually, going to Yuzhou is a good thing."

"Why do you say that?"

"When we left the capital, didn’t you say you wanted to take me traveling the world? We’ve gone from north to south, to the East Sea, to Lingnan, and now we’ve entered Shu. Soon we’ll be going to the northwest. Isn’t this perfect?"

"You do have a point when you put it that way."

"Besides, before we always had to sneak away. This time, with Young Master Zhao taking us, we’ll have good food and drink all the way. It’s not bad. Anyway, you won’t have to send me on errands anymore."

"Don’t want to run errands for me?" Yu Ying pretended to be angry.

Wen Sun had no choice but to agree repeatedly and beg for mercy.

Inside the main house, Zhao Xuanyou was drinking his medicine. His hearing was excellent, and he suddenly frowned and asked, "Is someone coming?"

Yuan Qian was stunned for a moment, then came to his senses. "It’s not an assassin. It’s Miss Ying and her sworn brother on the roof. I suppose they haven’t seen each other for a long time and wanted a quiet place."

Talking on the roof?

That was quite a romantic notion.

There were indeed many things he hadn’t done with Yu Ying yet. He would save them for another day.

Zhao Xuanyou took the medicine bowl from Yuan Qian’s hands and drank it all in one go.

After Wen Sun arrived in Badong, Zhao Xuanyou kept his promise and did not restrict Yu Ying’s movements.

Yu Ying and Wen Sun often went out during the day, strolling freely around the county seat. Whenever they saw interesting and fun jewelry, they would buy it. They rarely crossed paths with Zhao Xuanyou.

A month later, the wound on Zhao Xuanyou’s leg finally healed completely. Though pressing on it still caused some pain, at least it no longer bled.

Having been delayed in Badong for so long, Zhao Xuanyou had long since lost his patience and insisted on leaving as soon as possible.

It seemed that Zhao Xuanyou had fallen into the water from the previous official boat, so this time they switched to another ship, which was even more luxurious than the last.

Zhao Xuanyou got out of the carriage and was helped onto a wooden wheelchair by Yuan Qian.

Yu Ying saw that the wheelchair was quite exquisitely made and couldn’t help but take a look. When she inadvertently met Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, she quickly averted her eyes.

After Yuan Qian pushed Zhao Xuanyou onto the ship, Yu Ying led Wen Sun aboard.

Zhao Xuanyou said, "Don’t go into the cabin yet. A little further ahead is the Goddess Peak. Among the Twelve Peaks of Wu Mountain, the Goddess Peak is the most solitary. Since we’re here, we should naturally take in the view."

These words were naturally for Yuan Qian, but also for Yu Ying.

When Yu Ying had entered Shu by boat before, it was winter. The sky was overcast, and when she passed this place, the Goddess Peak was hidden in the clouds and mist, unseen.

This time, leaving Shu, she likely wouldn’t return in this lifetime, so she couldn’t miss it.

She and Wen Sun didn’t enter the cabin either and stood at the bow of the ship.

Soon, the sailors weighed anchor, and the official ship sailed downstream, moving smoothly without obstruction.

After about half an hour, the river suddenly narrowed at the Kuimen, and the waves crashed heavily against the hull, splashing up large sheets of water mist.

After a rapid stretch, the current finally slowed, and the ship began to drift slowly.

"Goddess Peak is here." Someone shouted.

Yu Ying followed the voice and looked up, indeed seeing a peak standing in the clouds and mist ahead.

The morning mist had not yet dispersed, and the mountain mist was like gauze, winding around the mountain waist.

The rugged outline appeared and disappeared in the mist, resembling a woman looking back at the river, with the floating mist as her swaying sleeves.

Yu Ying had only intended to casually enjoy the scenery, but looking at the peak before her, she was suddenly deeply moved and stared at it in a daze.

Zhao Xuanyou turned his wheelchair and slowly approached Yu Ying.

"Legend has it that she is the daughter of the Queen Mother of the West. Because she fell in love with the mortal world, she was exiled here and turned into a peak."

Yu Ying didn’t speak, only gazing at the mist-shrouded peak. The river was turbulent, and the ship swayed slightly. Her fingertips unconsciously tightened around the railing.

"Do you believe in legends?" Yu Ying asked.

Zhao Xuanyou shifted his gaze from the Goddess Peak to Yu Ying and gave a low laugh. "I believe that human hearts are more stubborn than rocks."

Sensing his implication, Yu Ying remained silent.

The river wind swept by, dispersing a wisp of mist, and the outline of the Goddess Peak became clearer.

The ship slowly passed beneath the peak. The water roared, and the waves surged like snow. On both banks, the gibbons’ cries were mournful, their echoes reverberating through the valleys, like the Goddess’s soft sobs.

"I’ve also read in books that if a woman from Shu has someone in her heart, she will make a wish to the Goddess Peak, praying for mutual love. If the man breaks her heart, the mist on the peak will turn into tears of rain, soaking the entire Wu Mountain."

"Would you make a wish to the Goddess Peak?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Yu Ying looked down at the river. In the deep whirlpools, who knew how many unfulfilled vows had sunk.

"There are so many people making wishes. How could the Goddess hear them all clearly?"

Watching the mist grow thicker, Yu Ying said to Wen Sun, "Let’s go back to the cabin." With that, she left.

Zhao Xuanyou sat alone at the bow, looking up at the Goddess Peak gradually disappearing into the mist, a smile appearing in his eyes.

He had known all along that she was the same as him.

chapters.title: Yuzhou City
chapters.content:
Two days later, they finally disembarked from the official boat and set off toward Yuzhou by land.

As Yu Wan and Wen Qi mounted their horses, Yuan Zeng directed the guards to carry Zhao Xuanyou onto a carriage.

The scene was quite the opposite of their previous travels.

Sensing the mockery in Yu Wan’s eyes, Zhao Xuanyou felt a pang of frustration and ordered his men to set off immediately.

Three days later, the muddy tributary of the Jing River appeared beside the official road, and the tea stalls by the roadside had a few grains of sand scattered in their drinks.

After another ten days of travel, the lush alfalfa fields suddenly gave way to more and more camel thorns, gradually spreading from sparse clumps into a gray-green ocean.

Once, a horse’s hoof startled a few desert sparrows, which flapped past her face, and she clearly saw the rust-colored feathers unique to desert birds.

Yu Wan greedily took in the unfamiliar scenery, feeling her small world expand once more.

When they stayed overnight at a posthouse, Yu Wan couldn’t help but linger outside.

The moon in the desert was round and red, illuminating one sand dune after another like frozen waves. The night was somewhat eerie, yet exceptionally beautiful.

Zhao Xuanyou told her that beyond this desert lay Yuzhou.

When the sky the next day was tinged with the colors of dusk, they finally arrived at the outskirts of Yuzhou City.

Ahead of them, a camel caravan was entering the city in the twilight. Among them, a white camel carried a foreign beauty, her face veiled with a golden silk mask, her features indistinct, but her figure alone revealed her to be a stunning beauty.

Yu Wan had no interest in beauties; she only looked at the stacks of goods on the other camels and asked curiously, “What are they transporting?”

“Persian carpets,” Yuan Zeng said proudly. “Don’t let Yuzhou’s distance from the Central Plains fool you; this place may be remote, but it’s far from desolate. Foreign merchants from the Western Regions all come here to trade.”

“I see.”

Wen Qi, listening beside her, also seemed to gain some insight.

“These camels are just like the coral ships we saw in Lingnan; they both transport exotic treasures, except one travels by water and the other by land.”

Yu Wan nodded.

Zhao Xuanyou was the general stationed in Yuzhou, and with his arrival, the soldiers at the city gates dared not slack off, immediately clearing the way for the rest of them.

As they passed the camel caravan, Yu Wan couldn’t resist taking another look.

There was also a Marquis of Jingyuan’s residence in Yuzhou City, located right in the center.

Yu Wan stepped down from the carriage and saw the guards lifting Zhao Xuanyou into a wheelchair. She walked over, took the wheelchair from the guard’s hands, and pushed Zhao Xuanyou toward the residence.

“Where is my mother?”

“No need to rush. You’ve traveled a long way; rest a bit first.”

Zhao Xuanyou replied lightly.

The wheelchair came to an abrupt stop. Zhao Xuanyou reacted quickly, grabbing the armrest to keep from falling.

Yu Wan restrained her anger. “Then you must at least tell me where my mother is so I can go meet her.”

He had coerced her all the way from Shu to here for her mother’s sake, and now he had the nerve to say there was no need to rush.

How could she not be anxious?
