Perhaps guessing her thoughts, Zhao Xuanyou said, “No need to meet her. She’s also at the marquis’s residence. Change your clothes and go see her.”

“Has my mother been staying at the marquis’s residence all this time?”

Yu Wan had assumed he would have hidden her mother somewhere secret after kidnapping her.

“I wouldn’t mistreat her; she’s your mother. Rest assured, during her stay here, the servants have treated her as an honored guest.”

“She’s your prisoner in Yuzhou. How can you call that an honored guest?”

“Your mother was free to go out as she pleased, just not allowed to leave Yuzhou.”

Yu Wan scoffed. “Being trapped in Yuzhou is indeed better than being trapped in the marquis’s residence, but it’s still imprisonment. My mother doesn’t care about wealth or status; she only cares about me.”

If her mother had cared about wealth or status, she wouldn’t have left Cui Lingyuan to live alone in the village.

“I see. If you don’t want to rest, I’ll have Yuan Zeng take you to her now.”

“Resting isn’t necessary, but I can change clothes first.”

Yu Wan pushed Zhao Xuanyou a little farther until they reached a fork in the path, where Zhao Xuanyou waved his hand, signaling Yuan Zeng to take the wheelchair.

“Liu Mama, take the young lady to Madame Ding.”

At Zhao Xuanyou’s words, an amiable old woman stepped forward, bowed to Yu Wan, and said, “Madame Ding has been missing you greatly. Please follow me.”

Thinking of her mother, Yu Wan’s heart stirred. She instinctively turned to look at Zhao Xuanyou, wanting to thank him.

But then she thought better of it; her mother had been taken by him, not invited as a guest. What was there to thank? She just glared at him.

Zhao Xuanyou took her glare in stride.

“Yu Wan, I’ve already had the kitchen prepare dinner. Go visit your mother first, then come eat. We can talk later.”

He had made a promise to Yu Wan: as long as she severed all ties with Pei Ta and came with him to Yuzhou, he would set her family free.

Now that he brought it up, it seemed he intended to keep his word.

Hearing this, Yu Wan’s expression softened slightly. She nodded at him, then followed Liu Mama with Wen Qi.

The marquis’s residence in Yuzhou was simply and rustically decorated, but its layout was far more spacious, with each courtyard built wide and open.

Yu Wan and Wen Qi walked along the residence’s covered corridors for a long time before finally reaching Ding Wenxi’s quarters.

“Young lady, young master, please come in. Madame Ding knew you were arriving today and has been waiting inside.”

Liu Mama pushed open the courtyard gate as she spoke.

Yu Wan hummed in acknowledgment and quickly stepped inside.

Before she even saw her mother, she heard a familiar voice call out, “Yu Wan.”

Yu Wan looked in the direction of the voice and saw Ding Wenxi standing under a crabapple tree in the courtyard, dressed in a sky-blue silk gown, her hair loosely pinned with a jade hairpin.

“Mother?”

Not only was Yu Wan stunned, but Wen Qi was also taken aback.

“It’s only been less than two months since we parted. Have you two already forgotten me? Why are you just standing there?” Ding Wenxi sighed in exasperation, walking forward from under the tree. She took each of their arms and led them to the stone table beneath the tree to sit. “You look well.”

“Mother, you look too beautiful in this outfit,” Yu Wan said honestly.

Back in the village, when Ding Wenxi dressed like a village woman, that was one thing, but later in Qingsha Town, for the sake of convenience at work, she usually wore rough, narrow-sleeved clothes.

Seeing the surprise in Yu Wan and Wen Qi’s eyes, Ding Wenxi said helplessly, “These clothes were prepared by the residence’s servants. I had no choice but to wear them.”

Recalling what Zhao Xuanyou had said earlier, it seemed he hadn’t lied.

Her mother had not suffered during her time in Yuzhou.

“I and Ah Qi traveled all this way to rescue you, and yet you’ve been living comfortably here, forgetting all about us.”

“Ungrateful girl, every day here has been like sitting on pins and needles. I’ve been longing to see you and Ah Qi. How could I forget about you?” Though she had a premonition upon seeing Yu Wan in Yuzhou, Ding Wenxi still asked, “What happened between you and Lord Pei?”

---

chapters.title: Jade Hairpin and Jade Pendant
chapters.content:
“I’ve already broken off the engagement.” Yu Wan tried to keep her expression light.

In front of Ding Wenxi, she was used to sharing only good news, not wanting to worry her.

Ding Wenxi sighed.

She also understood that Zhao Xuanyou had brought her to Yuzhou for Yu Wan’s sake.

He had gone to such lengths. How could he possibly allow Yu Wan to marry Pei Ta?

“It’s still my fault for dragging you into this.”

“How could it be? Once he sets his mind to something, he’ll see it through no matter what. Even without you, he would have found another way.”

Yu Wan had missed her chance with someone like Pei Ta, and Ding Wenxi truly felt sorry for her.

But she could see that Yu Wan was trying to comfort her. The die was cast, and she didn’t want to nag further and upset Yu Wan.

“Yu Wan, will we have to live in Yuzhou from now on?”

“Not necessarily. Wen Qi said that since none of us have been to the northwest before, we might as well travel around while we’re here.”

“Will the Marquis let you leave?” Ding Wenxi was skeptical.

Yu Wan’s gaze flickered, but she told the truth to prevent her mother from overthinking. “He said that as long as I don’t marry Pei Ta, he’ll let me go.”

“Then what are his plans for you? Does he still want you to return to the marquis’s residence as a concubine?”

Back in the capital, Zhao Xuanyou had already said he wanted to make Yu Wan a concubine. Now that he had found her, he must want to pick up where they left off.

But Ding Wenxi didn’t want Yu Wan to live a life of humiliation in the marquis’s residence.

“I’ve already talked it over with him. Once we reach Yuzhou, we’ll have nothing to do with each other.”

Seeing Yu Wan’s expression, Ding Wenxi didn’t press further. Instead, she took out two items from her sleeve; a jade hairpin and a jade pendant.

“I had nothing to do, so I bought a few pounds of mutton-fat jade from a Hu merchant. Unfortunately, I don’t know how to carve jade, so I wasted a lot of material before making these two things. Do you like them?”

The jade hairpin for Yu Wan was pure white and lustrous, with an oily sheen. The top was carved into a magnolia flower, simple and elegant.

The jade pendant for Wen Qi was engraved with the characters “平安” (peace and safety).

Wen Qi held the pendant and said softly, “I like it very much.”

“Mother, you actually made a jade hairpin? You’re amazing!” Yu Wan said, then took the silver hairpin from her hair and replaced it with the jade one, securing her bun. “If you opened a jade jewelry shop here, you’d probably make a lot of money.”

Ding Wenxi’s eyes flickered as she thought. “Jade here is much cheaper than in the Central Plains. If carved into bracelets or hairpins, they could sell for five or six times the price in the capital or Jiangnan. There’s definitely business to be done.”

“Have you dealt with Hu merchants before?”

“Only bought a few pieces of jade. Actually, Yuzhou may be remote, but it’s a good place. The local customs are influenced by the Hu people, so it’s much more relaxed than the Central Plains. The women here are bold and spirited; they can ride horses, do business, and manage their own households.”

“You think this place is good?”

“You’ve always said Lingnan is good for business, but Yuzhou has great potential too,” Ding Wenxi said with a helpless smile. “It’s a shame we sold Yu She Xuan. Otherwise, with the connections we built with the big merchant firms in Jiangnan, we wouldn’t have to worry about selling jade hairpins or bracelets.”

“Actually…”

Zhao Xuanyou had been insisting that Yu Wan reclaim her identity as Ding Wan and had even ordered his subordinates to address her as Miss Ding.

As long as she regained her identity as Ding Wan, even without Yu She Xuan, rebuilding connections with the Jiangnan merchant firms wouldn’t be difficult.

Seeing Yu Wan hesitate, Ding Wenxi pressed, “Actually what?”

“If you want to do business, once our lives settle down, we can look for another way to make a living.”

“Mmm.”

Ding Wenxi took Yu Wan’s hand, about to say more, when a cheerful voice came from outside.

“Yu Wan! Yu Wan!”

Though she hadn’t heard it in a long time, Yu Wan immediately recognized who it was.

She turned her head and, as expected, saw Yuan Qing running into the courtyard with a joyful expression.

“Yu Wan, it’s wonderful!” Yuan Qing rushed up to her, examining her carefully. “You’re alive. It’s really wonderful!”

Although Zhao Xuanyou had determined three years ago that Yu Wan had faked her death to escape, he hadn’t been entirely certain.

Now, seeing her with his own eyes, the feeling was different.

“You seem taller than before,” Yu Wan said. “And more handsome.”

Three years had passed since they last met, and Yuan Qing had shed his youthful immaturity, though his eyes remained clear.

Yuan Qing rubbed his head. “I’m not good-looking at all. Don’t tease me. Anyway, I’ll never be as tall as the Marquis.”

“How is Yingxue?” Yu Wan asked.

“She’s fine. Anyway, the Marquis hasn’t been in the capital these past few years, so she’s been living leisurely at Honghui Hall.”

Yu Wan couldn’t help but smile. “That makes sense. Has Yingxue married yet?”

Back at Honghui Hall, Yingxue had often mentioned her family arranging a marriage for her. Three years had passed. Surely she wasn’t already a mother by now?

“No. I don’t know the details, but the Marquis has already sent someone to the capital to bring her here. You can ask her yourself when she arrives.”

Zhao Xuanyou had sent someone to bring Yingxue?

Yu Wan was slightly startled.

He didn’t need a maidservant by his side, so why go to the trouble of bringing Yingxue all this way? Naturally, it was because of her close friendship with Yingxue.

He claimed he would give her freedom in Yuzhou, but his heart clearly had other intentions.

Yuan Qing, seeing Yu Wan’s silence, didn’t know what he had said wrong, so he fell quiet. His gaze then landed on Wen Qi beside her.

Wen Qi had altered his appearance today, so his face looked somewhat unfamiliar.

Yuan Qing narrowed his eyes, studying him, then suddenly exclaimed, “It really is you!”

Seeing Wen Qi lower his gaze, Yu Wan gave him a subtle signal, then turned to Yuan Qing. “He’s my adopted brother. What’s the matter?”

“He’s your adopted brother? Isn’t he that person from the Eastern Palace?”

Wen Qi was slender and light-bodied, naturally suited for qinggong. Since Yuan Qing was also a martial artist, when he had escorted Wen Qi back to the capital before, though they hadn’t spoken much, he had some impression of his build.

Earlier, when Zhao Xuanyou was investigating Yu Wan’s whereabouts, they had learned that a martial arts expert was by her side, but even Bingyun and the others didn’t know his background.

They never expected him to be the Eastern Palace’s shadow guard who had abducted Yu Wan.

Realizing that Yuan Qing had seen through Wen Qi’s identity, Yu Wan decided there was no need to hide it anymore. “It’s him. We became friends in the capital, and later, after leaving the capital, we became siblings. His identity is special; apart from the Marquis, you can’t tell anyone else, or the Eastern Palace won’t spare him.”

“I see. Understood.”

Yuan Qing was Zhao Xuanyou’s close attendant and was utterly loyal to him.

Even if Yu Wan told him not to tell Zhao Xuanyou, he would definitely report it to him. There was nothing more she could do.

“Miss Yu,” Yuan Zeng also entered the courtyard. Seeing so many people under the crabapple tree, he laughed. “Quite lively here.”

“Is something the matter?” Yu Wan asked.

“The dining hall has prepared dinner. The Marquis sent me to invite you to eat.”

chapters.title: Begging You
chapters.content:
Yuan Can finished speaking, and fearing Yu Wan would refuse, quickly added, "His Lordship said he already promised you."

"I know."

Yu Wan stood up to leave, but Ding Wenxi stopped her.

She anxiously admonished, "The Heir has held a high position for a long time. Don't confront him directly."

"I know, Mother. Don't worry, I'll be careful."

Yu Wan adjusted her sleeves slightly and followed Yuan Can out.

After passing through two corridors, Yuan Can led Yu Wan to Mingguang Hall.

This Mingguang Hall was located in the center of the mansion, connecting the front courtyard and the rear residence, similar to the Honghui Hall of the Marquis's mansion in the capital. It was also where Zhao Xuanyou usually lived.

As they entered the courtyard gate, a spring breeze happened to blow, and the two tall trees in the courtyard rustled pleasantly.

Yu Wan couldn't help but pause, looking up. The tree trunks were gnarled and twisted like a dragon's claws, yet the leaves were tender and green, fresh and vibrant.

"This is a poplar tree. It was planted by the first generation of the Marquis's family when they were stationed in Yu Province."

"That must be over a hundred years old."

"Yeah, but for a poplar, that's still young. Poplars are born to live a thousand years, stand a thousand years after death. They are long-lived." Seeing Yu Wan's interest in the poplar tree, Yuan Can added, "Thirty miles out of Yu Province, there's a poplar forest. That's where it's truly magnificent. Some other day…"

Yuan Can had intended to say that some other day, Zhao Xuanyou would take Yu Wan to see the poplar forest. But as soon as the first two words left his mouth, he realized his slip.

Zhao Xuanyou was still confined to a wheelchair, unable to stand, let alone take Yu Wan out of the city for a stroll.

He gave a dry laugh and took back his words, "Miss, you should go inside first. His Lordship might be waiting."

By now, it was getting late. The veranda was lit with candles, their flickering light casting a warm glow on Zhao Xuanyou in his wheelchair.

"Let's eat first, before the food gets cold."

After Yu Wan was seated, Zhao Xuanyou handed her a pair of chopsticks.

Yu Wan had been upset, but seeing his demeanor and his condition in the wheelchair, she felt a pang of pity and accepted the chopsticks.

The candlelight flickered in the veranda, illuminating the table full of exquisite dishes.

Yu Wan glanced at the dishes, her gaze pausing slightly.

The dishes on the table were clearly divided, on the left were northwestern specialties like roasted lamb, sesame cakes, and stir-fried noodles with meat slices; on the right were Jiangnan dishes such as Longjing shrimp, sweet and sour lotus root slices, water shield soup, and even a plate of osmanthus cakes.

It was thoughtfully prepared.

Having traveled all the way from Shu, she hadn't had many peaceful meals. Now, with the aroma wafting through the veranda and the feast before her, Yu Wan felt her stomach growl with hunger.

She picked up a piece of osmanthus cake; soft, sweet, and glutinous, no different from what she had in Jiangnan.

"Does the Marquis's mansion also employ Jiangnan chefs?"

Zhao Xuanyou casually replied, "I don’t particularly like these dishes, so naturally, there weren’t any before. But knowing you would come, I specially had someone find one."

Yu Wan ate a slice of roasted lamb and, remembering the Jiangnan begonia tree in Ding Wenxi's courtyard, looked up and asked, "That begonia tree wasn’t planted because of me, was it?"

"That was planted by my father." Zhao Xuanyou nodded. "My mother was from Jiangnan. After they married, my father thought they would live here, so he had that begonia tree planted."

"An orange tree grows in Huainan as an orange, but in Huaibei, it becomes a trifoliate orange. How can that begonia tree grow so well?"

"The soil in that courtyard was all transported from Jiangnan, and it’s watered daily, so it grows well."

"The Marquis went to great lengths for his wife. But..."

Seeing Yu Wan’s shift in tone, Zhao Xuanyou roughly guessed her meaning. "You want to say that he also took Concubine Wei, so he wasn’t truly devoted?"

"Isn’t that the case? True love should be unique."

Zhao Xuanyou listened to her words, nodding thoughtfully. "That makes sense. But there were indeed reasons for it."

Yu Wan ignored him and focused on eating.

After trying all the main dishes, she served herself a bowl of water shield soup. The tender, smooth texture melted on her tongue. For a moment, she felt as if she were back in her childhood, her mother by the stove making soup, the steam rising as she called her over to taste it.

Yu Wan lowered her eyes and swallowed gently.

"How is the taste?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"Very good."

Since the water shield soup was placed far from Zhao Xuanyou, and he was confined to his wheelchair, Yu Wan served him a bowl as well.

Zhao Xuanyou’s lips curved slightly, and he picked up his spoon to eat.

He originally didn’t like vegetable dishes, and though he had tried water shield soup before, today’s flavor was different.

After finishing the meal, Zhao Xuanyou had the dishes cleared and desserts brought out. He also poured Yu Wan a cup of wine.

"This is grape wine from the Western Regions. Try some."

Yu Wan did not take the wine. She looked up at Zhao Xuanyou and got straight to the point. "You said you invited me to dinner, and now that we’ve eaten, it’s time to talk about the real matter."

"The real matter?" Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow.

At his reaction, Yu Wan’s heart twisted. "Could it be that you’re going back on your word?"

"Regret what? I will keep my promises to you. If you want to leave, I won’t stop you. I’ve said it before; I only have one condition."

Yu Wan calmly replied, "You wanted me to leave Pei Tao. I’ve done that."

"It’s not just that, Wanwan. I want you to never have any entanglement with Pei Tao again."

Yu Wan took a deep breath. "I said I could do that."

Zhao Xuanyou’s knuckles lightly tapped the table, the sound soft but resonant in her heart.

"Besides that," he slowly said, "whatever you want to do, I will support."

Yu Wan was silent for a long time before suddenly smiling. "Really?"

He smiled too, but the light in his eyes was fixed intently on Yu Wan. "Of course."

"You know I want to take my mother and Ah Bi away."

"That’s true." Zhao Xuanyou did not deny it.

"Then why did you hire a Jiangnan chef in the Marquis’s mansion? You just said yourself that you don’t like Jiangnan cuisine!"

"The chef was indeed hired for you."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou trying to evade, Yu Wan decided to be blunt. "You knew I wanted to leave, yet you still hired a chef for me?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered, and he did not respond immediately.

Yu Wan thought he was feeling guilty, and a surge of anger rose within her.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you said you wouldn’t lie to me anymore! But you used my mother to coerce me, bringing me all the way to Yu Province, saying that once I came, you wouldn’t detain me. But in your heart, you never intended to let me go."

"I do want to keep you, but I’m not going back on my word."

"Ridiculous! Just admit it; you never intended to let me go. If you truly wanted to let me go, why hire a Jiangnan chef and bring Yingxue all the way from the capital?"

Zhao Xuanyou listened to her accusations, stiffening for a moment before slowly looking up at her.

Yu Wan’s eyelashes trembled, and her eyes unconsciously reddened. "I really shouldn’t have believed you. You used every means to deceive me into staying in Yu Province. Everything you said was a lie. What is this?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened with a deep, pained expression, as if a blunt knife were cutting into his heart.

Before Yu Wan’s tears could fall, he softly said:

"Begging you."

---

chapters.title: Beauty in Delicate Softness
chapters.content:
The candlelight in the veranda burned quietly. Yu Wan listened to Zhao Xuanyou’s words and was so angered by those four words that she laughed.

"Your Lordship is truly skilled at twisting the truth!"

"Isn’t it the truth?"

"Stop pretending to be foolish!" Yu Wan’s voice was not loud, but the sharpness returned to her previously reddened eyes. "Clearly, it was you who captured my mother and made me follow you to Yu Province. How dare you say you’re the one begging me? If that’s not twisting the truth, what is?"

After a pause, Yu Wan continued, "In Anzhou and Badong, how many times did I beg you? And now you say you’re the one begging me? If you never intended to let me leave, why bother making a false promise?"

"That’s two different matters." Zhao Xuanyou frowned. "Back then, you were about to marry Pei Tao. If I hadn’t taken some measures, how could I have stopped your wedding?"

Yu Wan’s beautiful eyes widened in anger at his words. "So you admit you used underhanded tactics against my mother?"

A hint of embarrassment flashed in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes.

Though he was not a man of upright virtue, he had always conducted himself with some principles, at least he had never bullied the weak or oppressed women and children.

This time, the only reason he had sent someone to capture Yu Wan’s mother was because the situation had been urgent.

She had already put on her wedding dress to marry Pei Tao. He had no choice but to take drastic measures to take her away first.

"If I hadn’t used those tactics, I would have had to watch you marry Pei Tao with my own eyes!"

"I can overlook what happened with my mother for now. My marriage to Pei Tao has already been canceled. What more do you want?"

"I want you to stay by my side." Zhao Xuanyou admitted frankly.

"Then have someone tie me up."

Seeing the resistance in Yu Wan’s eyes, Zhao Xuanyou softened his voice. "Wanwan, this time I won’t use methods you dislike."

He turned his wheelchair toward Yu Wan and reached out to pull her.

But Yu Wan dodged his hand, looking at him with guarded suspicion.

"Speak if you have something to say."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at the thin anger on Yu Wan’s face and said stiffly, "I won’t tie you up, nor will I force you to marry me. I just want you to stay in Yu Province a little longer. After you left the capital, you’ve been doing business in Qingsha Town. Actually, Yu Province is also a great place for business. I heard from Yuan Qing that your mother has made many jade carvings. Apart from mutton-fat jade, there are many rare gems and treasures from Tianzhu and Hu merchants at prices much lower than in the Central Plains. Using these to make jewelry would be far better than the inferior pearls you used before."

He had even investigated what kind of business the Jade Pavilion did?

Thinking that her mother had bought many jade materials outside, it was probably also Zhao Xuanyou’s arrangement for Yuan Qing to cater to her interests and take her mother shopping.

"Wanwan, in my current state, it will take at least half a year to recover enough to stand. How could I possibly force you?"

Perhaps because he mentioned his injury, Zhao Xuanyou felt Yu Wan’s attitude soften slightly. After a pause, he added, "Don’t make a decision in a hurry. Tomorrow, I’ll take you around Yu Province city."

"Didn’t you just say you have limited mobility? How can you go out for a stroll?" Yu Wan retorted. "If I want to go out, I don’t need to trouble Your Lordship."

Though she still refused him, it was clear she had some intention of staying in Yu Province to look around.

"You don’t know Yu Province, nor do you know those Tianzhu merchants. If you wander around alone, you might run into swindlers."

"I’ve been a merchant for years. I can tell if someone is a swindler."

"But you’ve never seen those gems before. Wouldn’t it be better to have a familiar person to guide you?"

Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou’s self-satisfied expression, her delicate eyebrows furrowing. "Have you thought all this through already?"

Meeting her gaze, Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened. His Adam’s apple rolled, and he said in a low voice, "You should know that when I make a move in chess, I’ve already thought ten steps ahead."

"From the day you knew I was in Anzhou, had you already planned everything in Yu Province?"

Zhao Xuanyou did not answer, tacitly admitting it.

"So now that you’ve taken so many steps, what step are you thinking of next?"

Though her words carried a hint of accusation, Zhao Xuanyou paid no mind, his gaze lingering on her beautiful face.

"Do you really want to hear?"

Hearing his tone, Yu Wan knew what he was about to say was definitely not what she wanted to hear.

She turned her face away coldly. "Forget it. It’s probably just more of your schemes."

Zhao Xuanyou, however, smiled.

Before he could speak, Yuan Can rushed in from outside.

"What’s the matter?" Zhao Xuanyou asked calmly.

Yuan Can said, "Prince Rui has arrived."

Yu Wan, being far from the capital, did not know about Zhao Qi’s enfeoffment, but she could easily guess which prince had come all the way to Yu Province.

"Prince Qi?" She looked at Zhao Xuanyou’s indifferent expression. "Did you know he was coming?"

"I didn’t know he would come, but of course, I’m not surprised."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes revealed a faint hint of hatred.

If it weren’t for Zhao Qi’s interference in helping Yu Wan escape the capital, Zhao Xuanyou wouldn’t have had to search for four years to find her.

His resentment for Zhao Qi was even greater than for Pei Tao.

The day Yuan Xi received the news from Zhao Qi, Zhao Xuanyou immediately set off for Shu to take Yu Wan away.

Zhao Qi might not have realized it at the time, but he was no fool. Two months was enough time for him to come to his senses.

This young man was able to chase all the way to Yu Province, which showed the depth of his feelings for Yu Wan.

However, this also played into Zhao Xuanyou’s calculations.

His arrival in Yu Province at this time was, in a way, doing Zhao Xuanyou a favor.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yu Wan and, as expected, saw a shadow cross her eyes. She clearly did not want to see Zhao Qi.

Without showing his intentions, he reached out and grabbed Yu Wan’s wrist, pulling her into his embrace.

Yu Wan was deep in thought about how to face Zhao Qi when, suddenly, she found herself sitting on Zhao Xuanyou’s lap.

The candlelight flickered, casting their shadows on the wall, suddenly merging into one.

"What are you doing?" Yu Wan angrily demanded. "Are you going back on your word again?"

She truly hadn’t expected Zhao Xuanyou to suddenly hold her.

Just a moment ago, they had been discussing serious matters.

"Wanwan, I’m helping you." Zhao Xuanyou said hoarsely.

Through the thin spring robe, her slender waist was almost too small to encircle.

The familiar scene stirred something in him, and the years of cultivated composure and restraint began to crumble.

A beauty so delicate and soft. How could he resist when she was the one he loved?

Fortunately, as soon as Yu Wan sat on his lap, the not-yet-fully-healed wound sent a slight tearing pain through him, helping him maintain some clarity.

"You’re twisting the truth again."

Yu Wan tried to struggle free from his embrace, but his arms held her tightly.

Zhao Xuanyou knew she was furious, so he said, "Do you know why Prince Rui has come?"

Yu Wan fell silent.

"Most of the royal princes are enfeoffed after marriage."

"So Prince Qi has married?"

"The Emperor picked through all the noble ladies in the capital for him, but he didn’t take a fancy to any of them. Though he has been granted the title of Prince Rui, there is still no mistress in the Prince Rui’s mansion."

This...

Yu Wan silently tightened her grip.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled the person in his arms closer.

"Wanwan, if you want him to let go of his obsession, listen to me."

chapters.title: A Long Journey
chapters.content:
Yu Ying indeed did not want to have any further entanglement with Zhao Qi.

She held no lingering feelings for Zhao Qi, and since he was of noble blood, the only thing she could do for him was to stay far away from him.

Now that she had called off her engagement with Pei Tao, if Zhao Qi found out that she did not want to be with Zhao Xuanyou, he would likely not let the matter rest.

Yu Ying lowered her gaze, clearly agreeing with Zhao Xuanyou’s words.

Taking advantage of the situation, he pressed further, "Put your hand on my shoulder."

Yu Ying glared at him fiercely, then clenched her fist and pounded his shoulder once.

"Is it still necessary at this point?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered as he caught a glimpse of the spring scenery revealed at her collar, and felt the softness of her chest pressed against his. His voice hoarse, he said, "I was just joking with you."

If they grew any closer, he might regret his promise.

"Master, His Highness, Prince Rui, has arrived."

As soon as Yuan Zao’s voice fell outside, someone quickly pushed open the door and entered the pavilion.

But the moment he saw Yu Ying, the joy in his eyes instantly turned to icy stiffness.

Yu Ying hastily stood up from Zhao Xuanyou’s embrace and curtsied to Zhao Qi.

It had been four years since she last saw Zhao Qi.

The once-youthful lad had grown much taller. His features were refined and gentle, his eyes still sharp and youthful. Though his complexion was not as fair as before, he now carried the vigorous and heroic aura of a man hardened by the battlefield.

Recalling the naive boy she had parted with in Yangzhou, Yu Ying felt a pang of emotion and lowered her head, addressing him, "Your Highness."

"I had an accident some days ago and injured my right leg. I am unable to stand and greet Your Highness properly. I hope Your Highness will forgive me." Zhao Xuanyou, seated in his wheelchair, cupped his hands toward Zhao Qi. "May I ask if Your Highness has come to Yuzhou for official business or a private visit?"

But Zhao Xuanyou’s words meant nothing to Zhao Qi. His eyes were fixed solely on Yu Ying.

He had a thousand words to say to her, but the moment he saw her sitting in Zhao Xuanyou’s lap, all his words stuck in his throat, unspeakable.

It was as if he had been transported back to the time in Heishui County when he had seen the two of them kissing passionately by the lake.

Did she still have feelings for Zhao Xuanyou?

Yu Ying could clearly sense Zhao Qi’s obsessive unwillingness to let go, but there was nothing she could do.

The more she did, the more Zhao Qi would misunderstand.

"Your Highness, please have a seat." Yu Ying pulled out a chair for Zhao Qi, but he just stood there, staring at her without moving.

Yu Ying had no choice but to say, "There is grape wine in the residence. Would Your Highness like to try some?"

"Yingying." Zhao Xuanyou reached out and pulled her back onto his lap, pressing her shoulder down to make her sit. "Soon you will be the mistress of the Marquis’s residence. You shouldn’t be doing these things yourself."

Mistress of the Marquis’s residence?!

Yu Ying secretly glared at him but said nothing, obediently nodding.

"Yuan Zao, pour wine for His Highness."

"Yes."

Yuan Zao was also aware of the awkward atmosphere in the pavilion. He quickly fetched a cup and poured wine for Zhao Qi before swiftly retreating.

Seeing that Zhao Qi was still standing there, Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze darkened.

"Your Highness must be tired from the journey and not in the mood to talk. I will have my servants take you to rest. We can discuss matters tomorrow."

This was clearly a hint for him to leave.

Zhao Qi’s emotions finally calmed somewhat. He looked at Yu Ying, only to see her avoiding his gaze. He had no choice but to sit in the chair she had pulled out earlier.

"I have no official business. I just wanted to visit Yuzhou since I’ve never been here before."

"I see." Zhao Xuanyou subtly held Yu Ying’s hand and glanced at Zhao Qi. "Your Highness honors us with your presence. Normally, I would host a banquet to welcome you, but as I am still recovering from my injuries, I am unable to do so. I hope Your Highness will understand."

"It’s fine."

After enduring a moment, Zhao Qi finally asked, "You... are you two getting married?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

"But Yu Ying is your maidservant. If you marry her, would the Old Madam and the Marquis agree?"

"Yingying will be my lawfully wedded wife. The affairs of the Marquis’s residence are none of Your Highness’s concern. There are many foreign taverns in Yuzhou run by Hu women. At this hour, they are still quite lively. Since Your Highness has come to experience the local customs of Yuzhou, you must not miss the Hu women’s taverns. As I am not mobile, I will have my servants take you there to find some amusement."

Zhao Qi lowered his eyes and said, "I am tired from the journey. Not today."

"I suppose the Marquis’s residence is spacious enough. Your Highness need not stay at the post station. I will have my servants prepare a courtyard for you. Please wait here for a moment."

Under normal circumstances, Zhao Xuanyou would never allow Zhao Qi to stay in his own Marquis’s residence and be an eyesore.

But now, he couldn’t be happier if Zhao Qi stayed as long as possible, until Yu Ying agreed to marry him.

After speaking, Zhao Xuanyou called Yuan Zao back in and ordered him to have the kitchen prepare another table of food and wine.

"Since my accident, my strength has not been what it used to be. I am already sleepy at this hour. Please excuse me for not keeping you company." With that, Zhao Xuanyou turned his gaze to Yu Ying, his voice softening. "Yingying, let’s go back to our room."

Back to their room?

Even though Yu Ying was furious at Zhao Xuanyou’s words, since he had said them, she naturally couldn’t refute. She could only go along with him and say, "Indeed, it is time to rest."

Hearing this, Zhao Qi’s clear eyes showed a hint of painful struggle.

Yu Ying’s beautiful brows lifted slightly as she pretended not to notice. She smiled at him briefly before quickly turning away, walking behind Zhao Xuanyou and pushing his wheelchair out.

Once inside Zhao Xuanyou’s bedroom, Yu Ying let out a long sigh of relief.

She truly hadn’t expected Zhao Qi to chase her all the way to Yuzhou, nor had she expected him to still not let go of her.

If it weren’t for Zhao Xuanyou standing in her way, she truly didn’t know how to face Zhao Qi.

She could harden her heart to break off her engagement with Pei Tao, and she could coldly reject Zhao Xuanyou, but she couldn’t bring herself to be harsh with Zhao Qi.

All along, Zhao Qi had treated her extremely well.

He was still young at heart, and if he heard her cold words, he might not be able to bear it.

It would be better to use Zhao Xuanyou as a shield to make Zhao Qi give up on her completely.

"What are you thinking about? Weren’t you going to rest?"

The bedroom was brightly lit with tall candles, and a faint sweet fragrance lingered in the air.

Yu Ying looked at Zhao Xuanyou in surprise. "Don’t you dislike incense?"

"I do indeed dislike the scent of these spices bought from Tianzhu merchants."

Yu Ying had wanted to ask why he had incense in the room if he disliked it, but before the words could leave her mouth, she remembered the Jiangnan chef he had mentioned earlier.

The incense was also prepared for her.

Yu Ying let go of the wheelchair and took a step back. "Even if we are putting on a show for His Highness, I haven’t married you yet. I can’t share a room with you."

"Who said I wanted you to sleep here?" Zhao Xuanyou retorted, though in truth, his heart ached a little.

Yu Ying and he had once been the closest of people. Even during her menstrual days, she would still want him to hold her while she slept.

Now, they had become distant.

The Tianzhu merchant had said this incense was a love potion; even the heartless would be moved by its scent.

Yet she remained unmoved, her heart as hard as stone.

Yu Ying couldn’t guess his thoughts and simply said, "I’ll go back now."

"Yingying, wait." Zhao Xuanyou spoke again.

---

chapters.title: The Mistress’s Allowance
chapters.content:
Yu Ying turned her head and frowned. "What else is there?"

Zhao Xuanyou said gently, "Tomorrow morning, I’ll take you to the city. I have people who understand Persian and Tianzhu languages. It will be convenient for doing business."

He had indeed thought of everything.

Considering Zhao Qi’s arrival, Yu Ying finally nodded in agreement.

It was getting late, so Yu Ying went straight out. As she passed the main house, she glanced at the pavilion. Zhao Qi had already left.

With her and Zhao Xuanyou gone, how could Zhao Qi have the mind to taste the grape wine?

Yu Ying had never felt anything for Zhao Qi. No matter what, she would end up letting him down.

A servant was waiting outside. Seeing Yu Ying come out, he quickly lit a lantern to escort her back to the Tangli Courtyard.

At this moment, the Tangli Courtyard was brightly lit, and even the crabapple tree was adorned with several small lanterns that swayed gently in the wind, exuding a delicate elegance.

Ding Wenxi and Wen Bo had already finished dinner and were chatting over dessert.

Seeing Yu Ying return, Ding Wenxi asked with concern, "How did your talk with the Heir go?"

Yu Ying rephrased her agreement with Zhao Xuanyou.

"He was injured because of me. It wouldn’t be right for me to leave in a hurry. I’ll take my leave after he recovers a bit more."

"That’s fine. You make your own decisions."

Ding Wenxi understood Zhao Xuanyou’s intention in bringing her here. Given how deeply he felt for Yu Ying, it would be difficult for her to leave.

But Yu Ying was strong-willed. Once she made up her mind, Ding Wenxi couldn’t stop her and could only follow her wishes.

Yu Ying took her hand and said softly, "After all, we’ve traveled a long way to Yuzhou. It’s rare to experience the local customs here. He’s a local powerhouse, and with him protecting us, we don’t have to hide our actions. Tomorrow morning, he’s taking me out to the streets."

Ding Wenxi said, "I have some leftover fabric. I plan to make a jade bracelet for you. I’ve already been to Yuzhou City several times, so I won’t go."

Yu Ying knew her mother enjoyed making jewelry and didn’t insist. She then looked at Wen Bo.

No need to ask; Wen Bo would go with her.

As it was getting late, Ding Wenxi went into the house to rest.

Wen Bo looked at Yu Ying, and she beckoned him with a flick of her finger. Wen Bo followed her to the crabapple tree in the courtyard.

It was mid-spring, the peak season for crabapple blossoms. Even at night, the tree was stunningly beautiful, and a gentle breeze carried its fragrance throughout the courtyard.

"Have you changed your mind again?" Wen Bo asked.

Earlier, Yu Ying had been resolute with him about leaving as soon as they reached Yuzhou.

Ding Wenxi could ask Yu Ying anything, and she could answer without batting an eye. But when Wen Bo asked like this, Yu Ying always felt a little guilty.

"The situation has changed."

Wen Bo looked up and suddenly said, "Do you want to marry Zhao Xuanyou now?"

"You’re jumping to conclusions! No." Yu Ying was taken aback by his words and quickly explained, "Prince Rui has come to Yuzhou."

"Prince Rui?" Wen Bo didn’t know about Zhao Qi being granted a principality.

"It’s the Seventh Prince. He’s now the Prince Rui."

Wen Bo had known about Zhao Qi’s feelings for Yu Ying before. Hearing that Zhao Qi had also chased her to Yuzhou, he wasn’t surprised.

But he was thinking of something else.

"Has Bingyun come?"

Earlier, Wen Bo and Bingyun had accompanied Yu Ying on her night raid of Xingguo Duke’s residence. They had gone through a harrowing experience together, and since Bingyun was also skilled in qinggong, they had chatted a few times and gotten along quite well.

"How would I know?"

Yu Ying felt a mix of helplessness and amusement.

Wen Bo never commented on her actions, which made her feel more at ease.

"Prince Rui probably won’t leave Yuzhou for a while. If Bingyun and Yangquan are here, we’ll definitely see them." She added a reminder, "Don’t let it slip to Mother about Prince Rui and me."

Wen Bo nodded.

"By the way, why are you wearing a mask again?" Yu Ying asked.

Tonight, Wen Bo was wearing the raccoon cat mask that Yu Ying had bought for him.

He raised a hand to touch the mask on the side with the birthmark and said indifferently, "Wearing a human skin mask for too long makes my face ache. A regular mask is more comfortable."

In the past, when he was a dark guard, Wen Bo had always worn a mask.

After leaving the capital, to blend in as an ordinary person, wearing a mask all the time would be too conspicuous, so he had to use a human skin mask.

"I’ve heard that the ointments from Persian merchants are very good. Tomorrow, I’ll buy you a jar from the market."

"Mm."

After giving all her instructions, it was late, so Yu Ying returned to her room to rest.

After days of hard travel, Yu Ying was truly exhausted and quickly fell into a deep sleep. When she woke up the next day, the sky was already bright.

Yu Ying lay in bed with her eyes open for a long while before reluctantly getting up.

After she changed her clothes and stepped out, she saw Ding Wenxi and Wen Bo both standing on the veranda, seemingly watching something.

"Mother, why are you standing there?"

Ding Wenxi turned to look at her with a strange expression but didn’t say anything.

Yu Ying walked over, yawning, but when she saw more than a dozen people kneeling in the courtyard, she was startled, and all her sleepiness vanished.

"What... what are you doing?"

The leading maidservant respectfully replied, "Miss, we have come to the Tangli Courtyard to serve you at the Heir’s command."

Yu Ying wasn’t surprised that Zhao Xuanyou would arrange servants for her, but this was too many.

"Are all of you here to work in the Tangli Courtyard?"

"Yes."

"Please report back to the Heir that we don’t need so many people here. Three or four will be enough."

The Tangli Courtyard already had one maidservant and one matron serving Ding Wenxi. Adding more people would make the courtyard too noisy.

The maidservant replied, "The Heir specifically ordered that you will soon be the Heir’s wife, and all arrangements should be made accordingly."

Yu Ying was, of course, familiar with the rules of the Marquis’s residence.

The Heir’s wife would have two senior maids, four second-class maids, six third-class maids for odd jobs, and four matrons at her service.

Adding these up, the number matched the people kneeling in the courtyard.

But at this moment, Yu Ying didn’t care about the servants at all.

She could feel Ding Wenxi and Wen Bo both looking at her because of the words "Heir’s wife."

Ding Wenxi looked at Yu Ying, wanting to say something but hesitating.

Even though Wen Bo was wearing a mask, Yu Ying could guess what his expression would be beneath it.

Last night, she had told Wen Bo so much, and now, all of a sudden, the title of "Heir’s wife" had appeared. Wen Bo must be wanting to tease her.

"Yingying," Ding Wenxi finally couldn’t hold back. She pulled Yu Ying aside and whispered, "How long has it been since you broke off your engagement with Director Pei? It’s too heartless to marry the Heir so soon."

"Mother, you misunderstood. I am not..."

Yu Ying was thinking about how to explain when Ding Wenxi continued, "Even if your old feelings have reignited, you should still take things step by step."

Take things step by step... Zhao Xuanyou was the one who wanted to take things step by step!

Yu Ying finally realized Zhao Xuanyou’s intentions and felt a surge of anger. She left the courtyard and headed straight for the Mingguang Hall.

chapters.title: The Scent of Gunpowder
chapters.content:
Inside the Bright Light Hall, Zhao Xuanyou was currently seated at a desk handling military affairs.

Though his patrol of the army was a task assigned by the Ministry of War, he remained the commander of the Mingxi Guard. Even with a deputy commander stationed in the army, there were still many military matters that the deputy could not resolve, piling up for him.

"Zhao Xuanyou." Yu Ying stormed into the Bright Light Hall, her face flushed with anger. The moment she saw him, she said, "What nonsense have you been telling the people at the residence? Who is your worldly wife?"

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her furious expression, and instead, the corners of his mouth lifted.

She had left him for four years, and now she had finally returned to his side. Even if she was angry with him, it was far better than before.

"I did this to deal with Rui Wang. I specifically had Yuan Qing instruct them to say that."

"Is it really to deal with Rui Wang, or to deal with me?" Yu Ying recalled the scene from last night when he had held her in his arms. How could she believe him now?

Zhao Xuanyou spoke slowly and calmly, his eyes not the least bit flustered.

"Both."

His straightforward admission left Yu Ying at a loss for words.

She huffed, her expression turning fiercer. "From now on, do not take the opportunity to touch me again, or I will not stay in Yuzhou."

"Understood." Zhao Xuanyou agreed readily, smiling as he looked at her. Then, he changed the subject, "Have you had breakfast yet?"

"No, I'm going back to eat with my mother."

"It's boring to eat at the residence. Let me take you to try some authentic local breakfast in Yuzhou city. I'll invite your mother as well."

"My mother is busy making jade bracelets and doesn't want to go out."

"Then just us?"

Yu Ying did indeed want to go out and look around. "Alright, I'll go back to my room and call A Tang to come with us."

At the mention of "A Tang," Zhao Xuanyou could not help but frown.

This man had accompanied Yu Ying for four years, and now he even lived in the same courtyard as her. It was far too intimate.

Even if they were sworn siblings, they were not related by blood. It was not appropriate to be so casual.

"That A Tang is the former Eastern Palace secret guard who captured you?"

As expected, Yuan Qing had told him everything.

"You already know, so why ask?"

"I'll arrange another place for him to live. As the wife of the worldly heir, it's not proper for you to live in the same courtyard as him."

"He is my brother."

Zhao Xuanyou said, "The marquis' residence is large enough. I will arrange a place for him closer to you."

Wen Tang practiced martial arts every day, so having his own courtyard would indeed be more convenient.

Yu Ying, hearing this, did not insist. After thinking for a moment, she added, "My mother and I are used to taking care of ourselves. We don't need so many servants in the courtyard."

"You are the wife of the worldly heir. The number of servants to keep is naturally up to you."

Hearing him address her so naturally, Yu Ying found it grating.

"In front of the prince, you can say that. There's no need to mention it in front of me."

With that, Yu Ying returned to the Tangli Courtyard. She had her mother select half of the servants to keep and sent the rest away. She also told Wen Tang about the arrangement for separate courtyards.

Yu Ying and Ding Wenxi were both women, and it was indeed inconvenient for them to live in the same courtyard as Wen Tang. Wen Tang naturally agreed without hesitation.

Yu Ying then returned to her room to freshen up a bit before leading Wen Tang back to the Bright Light Hall.

Yuan Qing was already waiting at the courtyard gate, pushing Zhao Xuanyou's wheelchair.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the masked Wen Tang but did not say much. He only said to Yu Ying, "There are three major restaurants in Yuzhou city that are quite good. The owner of Zuixian Tower is from the capital, so their food is probably more to your taste. Let's go to Zuixian Tower today."

"As you wish."

Hearing Yu Ying refer to herself as a "guest," Zhao Xuanyou naturally understood that she was trying to distance herself from him. He did not mind and ordered Yuan Qing to push him forward.

Yu Ying and Wen Tang followed behind his wheelchair.

They had not walked far when they encountered Zhao Qi coming their way.

Zhao Qi's gaze naturally fell on Yu Ying first.

Since their eyes had met, Yu Ying curtsied to him. Then, she saw that the person standing behind him was indeed Bingyun.

She turned to Wen Tang, and sure enough, Wen Tang also turned his head to look at her.

"Prince." Zhao Xuanyou greeted indifferently.

Since Yu Ying had turned her face away, Zhao Qi had to withdraw his gaze. When he turned to Zhao Xuanyou, his expression darkened a few shades. "Isn't the worldly heir seriously injured and unfit to travel? Why is he going out today?"

"I promised Ying to take her to Zuixian Tower for some local breakfast. Naturally, I cannot go back on my word."

Zhao Xuanyou called her "Ying" repeatedly, more intimately than before.

"I have just arrived and haven't tried the local breakfast either."

The moment Zhao Xuanyou saw Zhao Qi, he guessed that Zhao Qi would follow them. So he said, "In that case, would the prince be willing to grace us with your presence at Zuixian Tower?"

"Let's go."

Zhao Qi, with his noble status, should have walked at the very front.

But he deliberately lagged behind a few steps, walking alongside Yu Ying and Wen Tang.

"Ying, when did you arrive in Yuzhou?"

Seeing Zhao Qi approaching Yu Ying as if no one else was present, Zhao Xuanyou, who was in the wheelchair ahead, was naturally displeased. He coldly reminded, "Prince, Ying's full name is Ding Ying."

"I know, I just forgot for a moment."

Zhao Qi had sent Bingyun and Yangquan to Qingsha Town to investigate and indeed knew the name Ding Ying.

"Then... can I call you Ying as well?" Zhao Qi asked.

Hearing Zhao Qi's words, Zhao Xuanyou could not help but sneer.

"Ying is my betrothed wife. It would be inappropriate for the prince to address her so."

Zhao Qi retorted without hesitation, "Since she is not yet married, you are nothing to her. Besides, Ying herself hasn't said anything."

The name "Ying" was too intimate, and Yu Ying naturally did not want Zhao Qi to address her that way.

But she heard the tension between Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Qi and feared they would argue further over this. So she said, "The prince and I are old friends. Just call me Yu Ying as before."

"Alright." Since Yu Ying had spoken, Zhao Qi, though reluctant, did not say anything more. "Yu Ying, you still haven't said when you arrived in Yuzhou."

"I arrived in Yuzhou yesterday, just like the prince."

So they both arrived yesterday.

He was too stupid not to have realized earlier that Yu Ying and Pei Ta were both in Shu.

If he had thought of it sooner, he might have found Yu Ying before Zhao Xuanyou and not lost the initiative.

Soon, they exited the marquis' residence. Yuan Qing continued to push Zhao Xuanyou's wheelchair in front.

"The Zuixian Tower is very close to the marquis' residence. Just walk down this main street in front of the gate and turn a corner, and we'll be there." Feeling the atmosphere was a bit strange, Yuan Qing said dryly.

Unfortunately, no one responded to him. He had no choice but to silently push Zhao Xuanyou forward.

Zhao Xuanyou was annoyed by Zhao Qi sticking close to Yu Ying. Suddenly, he noticed a small pebble on the ground out of the corner of his eye.

He lightly coughed, but Yuan Qing did not catch on at all.

Helpless, Zhao Xuanyou turned the wheel himself, and the wheelchair rolled directly over the small pebble, causing it to jolt.

This time, Yuan Qing reacted quickly, steadying the wheelchair and preventing Zhao Xuanyou from falling.

"Master, are you alright?"

"Clumsy." Zhao Xuanyou said coldly, "Ying, you push me."

---

chapters.title: The Glass Cup
chapters.content:
Yu Ying knew Zhao Xuanyou was using the same old trick, but under the current circumstances, there indeed was no better solution.

"Alright." Yu Ying softly agreed, walking over to Yuan Qing to take the wheelchair and push Zhao Xuanyou forward.

Zhao Xuanyou's wheelchair was exquisitely crafted. Although it was sturdy, it was not heavy, and pushing it was effortless.

With Zhao Qi no longer speaking, Yu Ying breathed a sigh of relief and began to carefully observe her surroundings.

Yuzhou city was far less grand than the capital, and the marketplace was noticeably more dilapidated. However, there were still many people in the marketplace.

Zhao Xuanyou, though seated in the wheelchair and unable to see her, said at the right moment, "Now that the weather is warming up, more oases are appearing in the desert. Many caravans crossing the desert have arrived, as well as many merchants from the Central Plains. That's why the city is so crowded. When autumn comes and the weather cools, Yuzhou will become desolate."

So that was why.

"Was the caravan we met at the city gate that day also crossing the desert?"

"Mm, camels are the ships of the desert. Even if they encounter sandstorms, they can still remain safe. If you're interested, I can take you to ride a camel another day."

"Can you ride?"

"I can watch you ride."

As the two of them chatted casually, Zhao Qi's expression grew darker.

However, Zuixian Tower was indeed very close to the marquis' residence, and they arrived at the restaurant in no time.

The moment the manager saw Zhao Xuanyou, he was about to arrange for them to go to a private room on the second floor. But since Zhao Xuanyou was in a wheelchair, he arranged for them to sit by the window on the first floor.

To prevent disturbances, he also had a waiter remove the nearby tables and set up a screen for some privacy.

Zhao Qi, being the most noble, naturally sat in the middle. Yu Ying and Zhao Xuanyou sat opposite each other.

Wen Tang did not want to sit at the same table as them, so he went to sit alone at a nearby table.

Yu Ying noticed this and looked up at Bingyun with a smile. "A Tang guessed last night that you would come. He was very happy. Since it's rare for you to come to Yuzhou, you should sit down and try the local breakfast."

Wen Tang was now Yu Ying's sworn brother, so he was different from before.

But Bingyun was Zhao Qi's attendant and did not dare to act on his own. He could only look at Zhao Qi.

"Go." Zhao Qi said in a bad mood.

Bingyun hesitated but, since his master had agreed, he obediently went to sit at Wen Tang's table.

Zhao Qi did not necessarily need Bingyun to attend to him.

It was just that seeing Yu Ying being so gentle even to Bingyun made him feel a bit stifled.

Zhao Xuanyou noticed this and ordered Yuan Qing not to wait on him but to go sit and eat at the side.

Soon, the waiter brought out the dishes. First, each person received a freshly baked sesame cake. Then, each was given a bowl of spicy pepper soup, followed by beef noodle soup. Zhao Xuanyou and Yuan Qing had wide noodles, while the others had extremely thin hand-pulled noodles.

In the center of the table was a large plate of hand-grabbed mutton, a large plate of sesame paste stuffed pancakes, and a plate of gourd chicken.

Yu Ying, unlike Zhao Xuanyou, could not eat meat so early in the morning. After trying a few bites of the sesame cake, she ladled two spoonfuls of the spicy pepper soup. Finding it not to her taste, she focused on eating her noodles.

Although the chefs at the marquis' residence in the capital included some from the northwest, the noodle soup here did taste fresher.

"Prince, would you like to try the stuffed pancakes?"

"No need." Zhao Qi lowered his head, picking at his noodles.

This reaction pleased Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou simply ignored Zhao Qi and occasionally picked up food for Yu Ying.

"I haven't even finished the beef in my noodles. Don't add mutton. I can't finish it all."

"You don't like the spicy pepper soup?"

"It's a bit too strong."

Zhao Xuanyou smiled. "When I first came here, I couldn't get used to it either. But over time, I found that no other soup could compare to the spicy pepper soup."

The atmosphere at their table was strange, but at the table next to them, Wen Tang, Bingyun, and Yuan Qing were eating lively.

Yuan Qing was talkative and, since Wen Tang and Bingyun were new to the place, he explained the preparation of each dish to them in detail.

Bingyun had a gentle personality and got along well with Yuan Qing.

Wen Tang usually did not like to talk to anyone except Yu Ying, but since he had some history with Bingyun, he was not as reserved today and occasionally joined in the conversation.

Yu Ying lowered her head, eating her noodles while listening to the lively conversation at the other table. She regretted not sitting over there.

Finally, the meal was over. Zhao Xuanyou said, "After eating, I want to take Ying to visit the Hu Merchant Market. Would the prince like to join us?"

"No need. I'll just look around by myself."

Zhao Qi could see that with Zhao Xuanyou blocking the way, he would not have a chance to talk to Yu Ying. Staying here would be useless.

After saying this, he threw down his chopsticks and stood up.

Bingyun, seeing this, also stood up.

"It's rare to meet friends. You don't need to follow me today."

With that, Zhao Qi led his other attendants away.

Bingyun hesitated, but Yu Ying spoke up, "Since the prince has said so, you should stay and explore with us."

In Yu Ying's eyes, Bingyun was her savior, so he was different from others.

"Yes." Bingyun nodded and sat back down.

Zhao Xuanyou slightly furrowed his brows but ultimately said nothing. When everyone had finished eating, he led them toward the Hu People's Market.

The so-called Hu People's Market was actually two adjacent streets.

The imperial court had specifically designated these two streets to allow foreign merchants to purchase or lease shops to do business.

Since Zhao Qi had already left, Yu Ying handed the task of pushing the wheelchair back to Yuan Qing. She walked with Wen Tang and Bingyun.

"This time, Yangquan didn't come with the prince?"

Bingyun replied, "Yangquan went to handle other matters last year."

Yu Ying was slightly stunned before asking, "Over the past few years, has the prince always had you looking for me?"

"Yes." Bingyun answered, and then, fearing Yu Ying might misunderstand, he quickly added, "I quite enjoyed this task. You once said that you are not afraid to go to unfamiliar places, and wherever you go, you can see different scenery. Over the past few years, I've traveled to many places. It's been like touring mountains and rivers, broadening my horizons."

Before Yu Ying could respond, Yuan Qing, who was some distance away, chimed in, "Yeah, I love following Master on business trips the most. Staying in the capital is too boring."

Zhao Xuanyou lightly coughed, and Yuan Qing stuck out his tongue, falling silent.

Wen Tang asked, "Have you been to Qingsha Town as well?"

"Mm." Bingyun nodded. "I didn't expect you to live there for three years. I took a look around, and it's indeed a very peaceful place."

"A Tang really likes it there. Whenever he has time, he goes to the beach to space out."

"I go to practice martial arts." Wen Tang corrected.

Yu Ying chatted and laughed with the two of them, feeling quite at ease.

"Up ahead is the Hu People's Market." Zhao Xuanyou said.

Yu Ying's attention was quickly drawn to the bustling noise ahead. When they entered the street, she looked at the goods on both sides, her eyes darting from one item to another, taking in the novel sights.

Finally, Zhao Xuanyou found an opportunity to speak.

"Ying, that shop over there is a Tianzhu spice shop. The incense I burned in my room last night was bought there."

"These are all Persian carpets. The patterns are intricate and very exquisite."

"And those are glass cups from Da Shi. Do you like them?"

Yu Ying nodded. "They're beautiful."

The Hu merchants on both sides, with their high noses and deep-set eyes, had short knives with gemstone inlays at their waists. They were shouting and selling in broken official language.

The air was filled with the mixed scents of cumin, musk, and leather, hot and bold.

Suddenly, Yu Ying felt as if she had entered another world.

chapters.title: The Hu Market
chapters.content:
After walking a bit further, they arrived at a jewelry shop. Yu Wan’s attention was immediately drawn to the dazzling gemstones, and she couldn’t resist stepping inside for a closer look.

"May I help you, miss?" A woman wearing a golden veil emerged from the inner room, speaking fluent Mandarin.

The veil covered the lower half of her face, leaving only a pair of deep, ink-black eyes visible; eyes that seemed to possess a mesmerizing, soul-capturing power.

Looking at the golden silk veil, Yu Wan suddenly recalled the person riding a white camel at the city gate yesterday; it was the same woman before her now.

"I’m just browsing," Yu Wan said.

The counter displayed gemstones of various colors, glowing brilliantly, ruby red, peacock blue, amber yellow, each with its own unique charm, none inferior to the others.

The woman smiled and nodded at Yu Wan, saying nothing more as she quietly accompanied her.

"Is this a ruby?" Yu Wan suddenly asked.

"Yes. But this one isn’t good. I have another that would suit you better."

As she spoke, the woman took out a brocade box from the drawer beneath the counter. Opening it revealed a ruby the size of a pigeon’s egg.

Yu Wan stared at the ruby, unable to look away. It was so large yet remarkably pure, without a single impurity. Through the gem, she could even see the woman’s eyes clearly.

"Don’t you have an old saying? ‘Flowers for a beauty.’ A peerless beauty like you naturally deserves the finest gem."

As she said this, she wasn’t looking at Yu Wan but at Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Wan disliked this feeling. Coolly, she said, "No need."

With that, she left the jewelry shop.

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow and followed her out. The Indian woman holding the ruby remained deep in thought.

After leaving the jewelry shop, Yu Wan continued forward and entered a jade shop.

"Top-quality Hetian jade! Would the young lady like to take a look?" A Hu merchant with a white headscarf beckoned to Yu Wan, holding several jade pieces in his palm that looked as smooth as congealed fat.

Yu Wan took one from his hand, lightly tracing its surface with her fingertip before turning it toward the sunlight to examine its luster. "This piece has too much green speckling."

The merchant immediately realized she was knowledgeable and quickly said, "I have other pieces here. How about this jade bracelet, miss?"

She took the bracelet and inspected it. This one was quite good; the material was pure, without impurities, and had excellent luster.

"How much for this bracelet?"

"Twenty taels."

Seeing Yu Wan’s silence, the merchant hurriedly added, "At this price, you can only find it in Yu Prefecture. In the Central Plains, it would cost at least fifty taels."

That was true.

But since she was in Yu Prefecture, why would she pay Central Plains prices?

"Ten taels, plus those few pieces you were holding earlier."

Her mother had recently taken a liking to jade, and though those pieces had some green speckling, their luster was still good. Taking them back would give her mother something to practice with.

The Hu merchant quickly waved his hands. "Impossible!"

Yu Wan smiled faintly. "The weather is warm now, and Hu merchants are arriving one after another. If you don’t sell it for ten taels today, you won’t even get ten taels later."

Yesterday, she had seen camel caravans at the city gate, and today, they were already setting up shops to sell gemstones. Recalling what Zhao Xuanyou had said that morning, Yu Wan understood that in spring, Hu merchants would gradually make their way to Yu Prefecture. By summer, most of their goods would be sold, and by autumn, they would leave.

Today, there might only be two jade shops, but tomorrow, there could be three or four.

Seeing the merchant’s silence, Yu Wan said, "Then forget it."

"Wait, I’ll sell them all to you for ten taels." The merchant knew she was right and reluctantly wrapped up the pieces for her.

Yu Wan directly put the jade bracelet on her wrist.

Her fair, delicate skin complemented the lustrous bracelet perfectly.

Zhao Xuanyou stared for a moment, his gaze deepening.

Yu Wan always said he didn’t understand her, but now it seemed he truly didn’t know her well enough.

He had seen her in Honghui Hall; lowering her head, obedient and gentle, serving him with tenderness. He had seen her on the bed; soft and helpless, her eyes hazy with desire. But he had never seen this side of her…

Like a fish in water, effortlessly skillful.

As they spoke, Yu Wan had already moved ahead to the shop of a Persian merchant, which sold carpets.

This time, she didn’t buy the carpet she liked but instead asked the merchant about bulk purchase prices.

Zhao Xuanyou sat in his wheelchair, silently watching Yu Wan’s every word and action.

After leaving the shop, Wen Gua asked, "If we open another shop, are we not doing a jewelry store anymore?"

Earlier, Yu Wan hadn’t asked about bulk purchases at the gemstone or jade shops, but she had at the carpet shop.

"Opening a jewelry store is familiar territory, but right now, we only have my mother who can make them. To train a group of artisans like before would take another two or three years to get on track. These Persian carpets are so magnificent; they’d surely be favored by nobles and wealthy merchants in Jiangnan. It might be better to start with the carpet business first to support the jewelry store."

Wen Gua nodded thoughtfully. "The major trading firms we’ve worked with before can sell any kind of goods. If our products are good, they’ll definitely take them."

Since they had restored the identities of Ding Wan and Ding Gua, the firms they had previously collaborated with would naturally trust them.

Ice Cloud, listening to Wen Gua’s articulate reasoning, laughed. "It’s been years since I’ve seen you, and now you’ve become quite the business expert."

"I had no choice," Yu Wan said. Both she and Ding Wenxi couldn’t show their faces, so Wen Gua had been forced into the role of the young master. "I just follow Yu Wan’s lead."

After finishing their tour of the street, they went to a nearby restaurant for lunch before continuing their stroll.

By the time they had visited all the shops in the Hu market, it was already evening.

Upon returning to the Marquis’s residence, Ice Cloud went to report to Zhao Qi, Wen Gua delivered Yu Wan’s purchases to the Tangli Courtyard, and Yu Wan accompanied Zhao Xuanyou to Mingguang Hall.

After entering, Yuan Qing and Yuan Zhi silently withdrew.

Yu Wan poured herself a cup of water first, moistening her throat before pouring one for Zhao Xuanyou as well.

He took the cup but didn’t drink, only staring at her quietly. "Wanwan, I never knew you were so skilled in business."

Yu Wan smiled. "Now you admit you don’t understand me."

"I do admit it. But I’ll have plenty of opportunities to learn, won’t I?"

Yu Wan didn’t respond.

"You came with me to Mingguang Hall. Do you have something to say?"

"You have piles of documents on your desk, clearly with many military affairs left unresolved. Since I’ve promised not to leave, you don’t need to follow me around every day."

Zhao Xuanyou gave a faint smile. "Who said I was just following you around?"

If he hadn’t gone to the Hu market today, how would he have seen this other side of her?

At the thought, Zhao Xuanyou sighed.

"I followed you out not to spy on you, but simply to be closer to you."

---

chapters.title: Blocking Her Path
chapters.content:
"Actually, that’s not what I meant." Yu Wan reached out and lightly touched the pile of documents on the desk, then said softly, "I only went to the market to make purchases. You have so much work to handle; there’s no need for you to come with me."

So she was considering him.

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in acknowledgment. As the commander of the Mingchan Guard, he had already been away for over three months; he truly couldn’t always be by her side.

After a moment’s thought, he admonished, "When you go out in the future, besides Wen Gua, take a few more people with you."

As soon as the words left his mouth, he added, "Not that I doubt your safety. Yu Prefecture may seem peaceful now, but seven or eight years ago, it was engulfed in war. Now that I’ve suffered serious injuries, the news has likely spread. There may be people stirring in the shadows."

Yu Wan wasn’t very familiar with frontier warfare.

But she knew that Zhao Xuanyou had achieved great military merits when he joined the army over a decade ago.

Presumably, such merits came from battle.

"Yu Prefecture has only been at peace for seven or eight years?" Looking at the bustling Hu market today, Yu Wan found it hard to imagine.

"Mm."

"Are the ones stirring trouble in Yu Prefecture the Persians and Indians?"

Zhao Xuanyou shook his head. "Persia and India are far from here. They only seek profit, not Yu Prefecture itself. I’m talking about the Wuhuan."

Yu Wan knew the geography of the Central Plains by heart but had never studied the lands beyond.

"Where is Wuhuan?"

"The Wuhuan are northwest of Yu Prefecture. They are nomadic, and in winter, the desert isolates them, so they dare not act recklessly. But in spring, when the grass is lush, they start stirring. Eight years ago, the Wuhuan chieftain died by my sword, which is why they’ve been behaving for these years."

After speaking, Zhao Xuanyou noticed a faint smile tugging at Yu Wan’s lips.

"What are you smiling about?"

"You never used to tell me these things."

Zhao Xuanyou was taken aback.

He suddenly recalled some past events.

When Yu Wan had accompanied him to the Lichuan Imperial Palace, she had diligently attended lessons with Zhao Qi every day, and she had been exceptionally studious with her books.

In hindsight, there had been signs all along. Pei Ta had noticed them, but he hadn’t; allowing Pei Ta to exploit the opportunity.

"If you like hearing about it, I’ll tell you more in the future."

"It’s just talk. My mother wants to reopen the jewelry store, and I need to help her get it running." When they had left Qingsha Town, Yu Wan and Wen Gua hadn’t felt much sorrow, but Ding Wenxi had been different.

Xiaoyu Xuan had been her life’s work. The jewelry sold there was all her own designs, and the workers had been personally trained by her one by one.

Though Ding Wenxi had never said it, Yu Wan knew how hard it was for her to let go.

"Have you chosen a location for the store?"

"This morning, we passed two places with shops for rent. The locations were decent, but we’ll look around a few more days before deciding."

She was thorough.

"Once you’re done with your mother’s matters, come help me."

Yu Wan looked at him suspiciously. "Help you with what?"

Zhao Xuanyou tilted his chin toward the pile of documents on the desk. "You pushed me into the river, and I suffered serious injuries. Now I don’t even have the strength to hold a brush. You should at least help me handle these military affairs."

"I don’t understand military affairs."

"You don’t, but I can teach you."

Yu Wan glanced at him, realizing this was his response to their earlier conversation.

She only said quietly, "Let’s talk about it later. I might not even manage the business properly. How could I help with something like this? It’s late. You should rest early."

"Mm, it’s not urgent."

After leaving Mingguang Hall, Yu Wan let out a quiet sigh.

Compared to the coercion she had faced in Anzhou, Zhao Xuanyou now seemed to have regained his usual noble and self-assured demeanor.

But compared to the red-eyed, coercive Zhao Xuanyou, interacting with this version of him made her even more tense.

What was she afraid of...? Afraid of falling for him?

Yu Wan clenched her fingers, biting her lip as she walked forward.

Just as she was nearing Tangli Courtyard, a figure suddenly appeared from the corner of the corridor.

It was Zhao Qi.

He was still wearing the same purple brocade robe from that morning, with a gold-embroidered pouch at his waist and a golden crown on his head.

Even in the darkness of night, his noble bearing was impossible to miss.

This was the only path from Mingguang Hall to Tangli Courtyard. He was waiting here, clearly lying in wait.

Seeing that he had no attendants with him, Yu Wan instinctively took a step back and curtsied. "Your Highness."

After speaking, she tried to walk past him, but he stretched out his arm to block her.

Yu Wan looked up at him, but before she could ask, Zhao Qi said, "How much longer do you intend to avoid me?"

"I don’t understand what Your Highness means."

"You do!" Zhao Qi’s gaze locked onto Yu Wan, his tone carrying an unquestionable firmness.

This was a tone he had rarely used with her before.

Feeling the pressure in his eyes, Yu Wan sensed something was wrong but had no immediate countermeasure.

Perhaps some things couldn’t be avoided by running.

Yu Wan sighed inwardly. "If Your Highness has any orders, please speak freely."

---

Inside Mingguang Hall, Zhao Xuanyou had not retired for the night. Instead, he turned his wheelchair back to the desk.

He didn’t handle any official business but simply sorted the documents on the desk into two piles.

One pile contained confidential documents related to the northwestern defense, while the other consisted of personnel matters, weaponry, provisions, and military horses.

Earlier, when he mentioned having Yu Wan help with military affairs, she had shown some interest.

He would first handle the urgent matters himself, then leave the rest for when he could teach Yu Wan.

Yuan Zhi hurried in, assuming Zhao Xuanyou was personally organizing the desk. "Master, let the servants handle this."

"Mind your own business." Zhao Xuanyou ignored him, continuing to sort through the documents.

Yuan Zhi didn’t take the reprimand to heart, after all, he had come in for a reason.

"Master, someone just reported that Prince Rui has gone toward Tangli Courtyard."

Zhao Qi had come for Yu Wan. With Pei Ta’s past actions as a cautionary tale, Zhao Xuanyou naturally had to be more vigilant.

Though he hadn’t gone so far as to have Zhao Qi monitored, he had left people near Zhao Qi’s courtyard to keep an eye on his movements.

Hearing Yuan Zhi’s words, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression darkened instantly, and he tightly clenched the documents in his hand.

Seeing his master’s cold demeanor, Yuan Zhi felt a hint of helplessness.

If his master’s legs were fine, he would have rushed out the door by now.

"Should I go to Tangli Courtyard? If Prince Rui is blocking Miss Wan’s path, I can find a way to help her."

"No need."

Zhao Xuanyou returned to sorting the documents.

He could somewhat understand Zhao Qi’s feelings. After traveling thousands of miles to Yu Prefecture, only to have Yu Wan refuse to even speak to him, Zhao Qi must feel unwilling to accept it and wanted answers.

If he wanted to stop her, then let him. After all, Yu Wan had no romantic feelings for Zhao Qi. It would be best if that boy gave up his hopes soon.

Yuan Zhi stood silently to the side, watching Zhao Xuanyou’s calm expression as he continued organizing the documents.

He couldn’t quite understand Zhao Xuanyou’s attitude. Normally, shouldn’t his master have sent him to stop this immediately?

But since Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t given the order, Yuan Zhi didn’t dare act on his own. He simply stood by in silence.

Unexpectedly, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly set down the documents in his hand and turned his wheelchair around the desk.

Yuan Zhi had assumed he was heading to the bedroom to rest, but instead, Zhao Xuanyou moved straight toward the door, his wheelchair rolling faster and faster.

chapters.title: Corridor Conflict
chapters.content:
Zhao Qi had not seen Yu Ying since their parting in Yangzhou four years ago.

He often recalled the scene of that night, his tumultuous emotions suppressed and surging in his heart, hoping only to see Yu Ying again and confess his feelings.

But Zhao Xuanyou had always stood in his way, preventing him from getting close to her.

Only now did he finally have a chance to be alone with Yu Ying.

Zhao Qi was no longer the naive boy he had been four years ago. Facing his burning gaze, Yu Ying instinctively took a step to the side, putting some distance between them.

"Ying, I know; you were forced to come to Yuzhou by Zhao Xuanyou. Your mother was captured by him, so you were compelled to reconcile with him, right?"

Yu Ying was slightly taken aback and looked at Zhao Qi. "You knew about what happened in Anzhou?"

"Yes, I sent someone to investigate, though I was a bit late."

Zhao Qi had not expected Yu Ying to marry Pei Tao, but since their engagement had already been called off, and now Yu Ying was in Zhao Xuanyou’s grasp, Pei Tao no longer mattered.

"With me here, you don’t need to fear Zhao Xuanyou. I won’t let him harm you or your mother."

Yu Ying shook her head. "I am not afraid of him."

"I am now the Prince of Rui, with my own fiefdom. I will take you and your mother there. No one will harm you there."

"Your Highness, my mother and I wish to stay in Yuzhou."

Zhao Qi’s expression grew darker at her words, but he still forced himself to remain calm, lowering his voice. "Do you remember what you said to me on the city tower in the capital? You said you wanted to leave Zhao Xuanyou, that you needed my help. Ying, I remember every word you said. When you need help, I will always be there. And that hasn’t changed."

"Your Highness’s kindness to me, I also remember. It was true when I said I wanted to leave Zhao Xuanyou, and it is also true now that I wish to stay in Yuzhou."

Zhao Qi stared intently at Yu Ying, the redness in his eyes unmistakable.

He stepped forward and grabbed her wrist. "I know Zhao Xuanyou forced you to come to Yuzhou. I am now the Prince of Rui. With me here, you don’t need to fear him. Stop pretending to be strong. I won’t let you suffer."

"I am not suffering." Yu Ying said firmly. "The truth is, I want to stay here."

She was not lying. Compared to Zhao Qi’s prince’s residence, she truly preferred to stay in Yuzhou.

Zhao Qi looked at her resolute expression, his heart aching, yet he was powerless to change her mind. He could only try to persuade her helplessly. "Do you want to say that your feelings for Zhao Xuanyou run deep? But three years ago, you were determined to leave him, and three years later, you still wanted to marry Pei Tao! Did you think of him even when you were marrying Pei Tao?"

"No."

"Then that’s it! Ying, come with me. I will protect you and treat you well for the rest of my life."

Yu Ying forcefully pulled her wrist from his grip and shook her head decisively. "I do not have romantic feelings for Your Highness."

Zhao Qi’s gaze tightened abruptly, and he punched the corridor pillar heavily.

"Why can Pei Tao, but not me?"

He stared fixedly at Yu Ying, his expression as heavy and oppressive as thick, dark clouds.

Yu Ying turned her face away, avoiding his eyes.

"Your Highness has also fallen for someone before. You should understand that some things cannot be forced."

"So you can have feelings for Pei Tao, for Zhao Xuanyou, but not for me?"

Yu Ying heard the sorrow in his voice and felt a pang of guilt.

He was no longer just the young prince he had been before; he was now a prince second only to the emperor.

The fact that he could speak to her in such a tone made her realize that this was not the time for her to soften her heart. She had to make her words clearer.

"Three years ago, I left Zhao Xuanyou not because I had no feelings for him, but because I had no choice but to leave the capital.
