Besides, he was about to marry, and there was no place for me by his side. I decided to marry Pei Tao because of a stroke of fate, but our destiny was too shallow. Coming to Yuzhou, I was indeed forced by Zhao Xuanyou at first, but now I truly wish to stay. He didn’t understand me before, and I had many misunderstandings about him. I don’t know how far we can go in the future, but we’ll see as we go."

These were her true feelings, ones she had not even shared with her mother or Wen Biao.

Zhao Qi stared fixedly at Yu Ying.

Compared to when they were on the city tower, Yu Ying had also changed. The coy and innocent demeanor was gone, replaced by a faint detachment and refined elegance in her brows. No matter how he looked at her, she was a rare beauty.

During the days she had been missing, Zhao Qi had tossed and turned in sleepless nights, dreaming of her in vivid, tender dreams.

He had thought of her for too long. Even though she spoke so resolutely, he was not willing to give up.

"You’re just used to being by Zhao Xuanyou’s side. Once you’ve been with me for a while, you’ll get used to it too."

"It’s not the same with Zhao Xuanyou."

"There’s no difference!"

Zhao Qi’s eyes were stormy. He grabbed Yu Ying’s wrist again and pulled her forward.

If he could just take her away, that would be enough.

All he lacked was the chance to be with her.

She didn’t like Zhao Xuanyou that much. If he just had the chance to be with her, she would eventually fall for him.

Yu Ying was startled and tried to pull Zhao Qi’s hand away, pushing him back.

A cold wind suddenly swept through the flower-lined stone path.

In her peripheral vision, Yu Ying saw a dark shadow. The next moment, she felt a tall figure block her, followed by the sound of flesh striking flesh. Zhao Qi released her wrist at that moment.

Over the past few years, Zhao Qi had trained in the military, and his martial arts had improved greatly compared to before. Even though Zhao Xuanyou was still recovering from serious injuries, he managed to block Zhao Xuanyou’s palm strike.

However, Zhao Xuanyou’s profound internal strength still sent Zhao Qi stumbling back several steps.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled Yu Ying behind him, his voice cold and furious. "Ying is my betrothed. If you dare to lay a hand on her again, it won’t be just this one strike."

The man’s words were domineering, but Yu Ying was puzzled as to how he had suddenly stood up.

She looked down and noticed that his right leg was trembling violently.

He. Had actually forced himself to stand up?

Yu Ying’s heart jolted, and she stepped out from behind him, clinging to his right arm like a dependent bird.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered, realizing she was supporting him, silently helping to take the weight off his right leg.

The frost on his face actually softened slightly.

"Hah," Zhao Qi’s face twisted into a cold smile. "I want to take her away. What can you do about it?"

Zhao Xuanyou coldly replied, "She doesn’t want to go with you. Moreover, this is Yuzhou. Without my permission, you won’t be able to take away even a mosquito."

"You! Do you think Yuzhou is some lawless land?"

"Precisely because Yuzhou is not a lawless land that I dare to say this. The imperial court has already decreed that princes are not allowed to leave their fiefdoms without permission, let alone collude with military officers. Now, Your Highness has not only left your fiefdom but has also come to this important military stronghold in the northwest. As the defending general, I must report this to the court. If Your Highness does not wish to be questioned by His Majesty and the Crown Prince, you should leave Yuzhou by tomorrow morning."

---

chapters.title: "Goodbye"
chapters.content:
"Your Highness!" The prince’s guards rushed over.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou strike Zhao Qi, they glared at Zhao Xuanyou with hostility.

However, Yuan Zhen quickly arrived with the Hou residence guards.

The once-quiet corridor suddenly became tense.

Yu Ying truly had not expected Zhao Qi to suddenly try to forcefully take her away. After all, during their previous interactions, Zhao Qi had never taken advantage of his status as a prince.

She also had not expected Zhao Xuanyou to strike Zhao Qi. After all, Zhao Qi was the Prince of Rui, and Zhao Xuanyou, as a subject, would be committing an act of insubordination by laying hands on him.

But both things had happened.

Since the conflict had started because of her, Yu Ying felt she should say something.

But both men had their pride, and at this moment, no matter which side she took, it would be a great humiliation to the other.

She could only lower her gaze and do her best to support Zhao Xuanyou.

"Your Highness came to Yuzhou without the court’s permission. If this spreads, it will not be favorable for you."

Zhao Qi didn’t really care about Zhao Xuanyou’s threats. He only looked at Yu Ying. From beginning to end, she had not once looked at him.

Should he be angry?

Ever since he had known Yu Ying, she had been by Zhao Xuanyou’s side.

After all these years of twists and turns, she had simply returned to Zhao Xuanyou’s side.

Perhaps it really was time for him to leave.

"Goodbye," he said to Yu Ying.

Yu Ying’s heart stirred.

These were the last three words Zhao Qi had said to her when they parted in Yangzhou.

He was saying goodbye to her.

Seeing that Zhao Qi was not stubbornly persistent, Yu Ying felt genuine happiness for him from the bottom of her heart.

Zhao Qi was the emperor’s most beloved son, and now he was the Prince of Rui. In the future, he would certainly have a good princess consort, and his prospects would be limitless.

Yu Ying would remember his kindness to her and wish him well.

She did not say more, bending slightly to give Zhao Qi a respectful bow.

Zhao Qi looked at her, weakly curving the corner of his mouth, then turned and left dejectedly. Yin Ping, Bingyun, and the others followed him.

After they had walked far away, the man beside her let out a soft hiss.

"Sit down quickly!" Yu Ying suddenly snapped back to reality and helped Zhao Xuanyou sit down on the edge of the corridor.

The physician had instructed that Zhao Xuanyou’s bone fracture had already healed, and the external wounds had also closed, but the injuries to his leg were too deep. He would need at least another four or five months of rest before he could attempt to stand.

Today, not only had he stood up, but he had also used qinggong to leap over and fight someone. Clearly, his leg could no longer bear the strain, and it began to spasm violently.

Large beads of cold sweat formed on Zhao Xuanyou’s forehead, and his face also looked somewhat ferocious due to the pain.

"Yuan Zhen, go call the physician," Yu Ying ordered.

"No need." Zhao Xuanyou forced himself to endure, clenching his fists tightly. "You may leave."

The bones had healed, and the wounds had closed. Even if the physician came, there was nothing he could do.

What he needed was rest. Today’s reckless action had worsened his injury, and he would have to rest for another month.

"Yes." Yuan Zhen had no choice but to lead the guards away.

The corridor, which had been crowded with people moments ago, was now left with just the two of them.

Yu Ying sat beside Zhao Xuanyou, wanting to wipe the sweat from his brow, but she saw him turn his face away.

His expression was rigid and cold, clearly struggling to suppress the pain.

She knew he was being stubborn and did not want her to see him like this.

"I won’t look then." Yu Ying said softly, turning her face away and sitting quietly beside him.

The night wind gently blew through the corridor, and the surroundings returned to silence.

After a long while, Yu Ying felt the person beside her move. He had stretched out his arm and pulled her into his embrace.

"Are you not in pain anymore?" Yu Ying asked.

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression was still somewhat stiff, but he answered a different question, lowering his voice. "Ying, I heard everything."

"Heard what?"

"The things you said to Zhao Qi." As if afraid Yu Ying would still refuse to admit it, Zhao Xuanyou added, "Not everything, but from the part where you said you truly wanted to stay in Yuzhou."

Yu Ying was momentarily speechless.

Though he hadn’t heard everything, he had heard almost all of it.

Seeing her reaction, he continued, "I heard you say, 'Zhao Xuanyou is different.'"

Hearing the pride in his voice, Yu Ying pushed away the arm he had draped over her shoulder and muttered, "You stood there eavesdropping for so long?"

"How else would I know your true feelings if I didn’t stand there?"

"Those may not have been my true feelings."

Zhao Xuanyou did not try to hold her again but moved a little closer. "If you truly didn’t want to stay in Yuzhou, you would have gone with Zhao Qi just now."

"Would you have let me go if I wanted to?"

At these words, Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered, dark and unclear. After a long moment, he said quietly, "If I were certain that you had no feelings for me at all, I would have made the same choice as Zhao Qi. But you and I both know that you do have feelings for me, so naturally, I cannot let you go."

Yu Ying lowered her gaze, no longer refuting his words.

Seeing that she had finally tacitly acknowledged it, Zhao Xuanyou’s heart, which had been suspended for so long, finally settled back a little. The tension on his face, caused by the pain in his leg, finally gave way to a smile.

"You finally admit that you have feelings for me."

Since Yu Ying had known him, he had almost never spoken in such a lighthearted tone.

"When you left the capital back then, besides my upcoming marriage, what other reasons were there? Was it related to your mother?"

Since Yu Ying had admitted her feelings for him, he naturally wanted to press his advantage and eliminate all her concerns.

When they left Anzhou, she had said she couldn’t take her mother back to the capital. Zhao Xuanyou had taken note of that.

"Yes." Yu Ying did not deny it.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded but did not pursue the matter further. He simply said, "Yuzhou is thousands of miles away from the capital. Your mother lives here, and no one will be able to harm her."

In Yuzhou, he had the confidence to say that.

Yu Ying remained silent.

"You don’t believe I can do that?"

"How could that be?"

"Ying, can you tell me, what exactly is your hang-up? Why? You could easily agree to Pei Tao’s proposal, yet you keep avoiding me?"

Yu Ying met Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, feeling a pang of sorrow in her heart.

She could sense the affection and persistence in his eyes, but she found herself at a loss for words.

Her connection with Zhao Xuanyou was certainly much deeper than with Pei Tao. But precisely because she and Pei Tao had no past, it was easier to be with him.

Zhao Xuanyou did not know that she carried memories from her past life.

But Yu Ying did. That had been a life she had truly lived. In that brief lifetime, she had carried his child for ten months and given birth.

She couldn’t help but recall how, in her past life, Zhao Xuanyou had lived a happy and beautiful life with Cui Yichu, completely unaware of her existence.

She understood it wasn’t Zhao Xuanyou’s fault, but she couldn’t help the knot in her heart when facing him.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her, lost in thought, and couldn’t help but move closer to her.

When his lips touched her cheek, she turned her face away, avoiding his kiss.

The intensity in his eyes faded slightly, and he slowly sat up straight, asking again, "If you don’t say it, how can I explain? Do you want us to keep going like this?"

"You can’t explain it. It’s not your fault."

That was the Zhao Xuanyou of her past life. Moreover, even in that past life, he had been deceived by Cui Yichu.

Zhao Xuanyou heard her words and actually curved his lips into a smile. "If it’s not my fault, then just say it outright."

Facing his persistent gaze, Yu Ying’s eyelashes trembled.

Even though lifetimes had passed, he was still Zhao Xuanyou, wasn’t he?

Perhaps she really could tell him.

chapters.title: A Weight Lifted
chapters.content:
The wind stirred the treetops, and the night was as cool as water.

Yu Ying’s eyes shimmered as she silently gazed at Zhao Xuanyou.

After a long silence, she finally lifted her delicate chin and spoke slowly, “Do you still remember Cui Yichu’s plan from back then?”

Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t thought of that name in a long time.

He was slightly taken aback, unsure how this related to Cui Yichu, but since Yu Ying asked, he carefully recalled.

“She lost her chastity before marriage and wanted to use you to deceive everyone.”

“It wasn’t just that.”

Zhao Xuanyou pondered for a moment, then remembered more.

“Back then, she had secretly conceived the Crown Prince’s child but was expelled from the palace by the Empress. With no choice, she used a harsh medicine to abort the child, damaging her foundation so she could never bear children again. She didn’t just want you to consummate the marriage for her; she also wanted you to father a child for her, to help her deceive everyone.”

Thinking of what had happened in her past life, Yu Ying felt a suffocating heaviness in her chest and sighed softly.

“Her original plan was this: during the half month you were in the capital, I would take her place and sleep with you. If all went well, after you left, I would be diagnosed with a pulse of pregnancy. She would arrange for me to leave the residence and then announce to the world that she was with child. By the time you returned to the capital next year, she would be holding my child and claiming it as hers.”

At this, Yu Ying’s voice grew choked.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t know how Yu Ying could be so familiar with Cui Yichu’s detailed plan, but he had never seen her show sadness in front of him. Seeing her like this now, he lowered his head and leaned closer.

“You’re in the Marquis’s residence, so you’re reminded of Cui Yichu’s sordid schemes, and that’s why you don’t want to stay here?”

Yu Ying shook her head.

The secrets of her two lives were not something she wanted to reveal to anyone.

After carefully choosing her words, Yu Ying said, “I just want to ask you one question.”

“Go ahead.”

“If Cui Yichu’s plan had succeeded, and she had obtained my child, and then gotten rid of me, erasing all traces, and when you returned to the capital, would you have lived happily with her as husband and wife until old age?”

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow, finding it somewhat unbelievable.

Seeing the solemn look in Yu Ying’s eyes, he suppressed his doubts and thought again.

“If I found out she had borne me a child, I would indeed be overjoyed and would rush back to the capital as soon as possible to be with her and the child.”

As expected.

Cui Yichu’s plan had been flawless.

In her past life, she must have lived a smooth and pleasant life, enjoying Zhao Xuanyou’s affection and the filial piety of Yu Ying’s child.

A wave of sorrow rose in Yu Ying’s heart.

Thinking of how Cui Yichu had obtained everything in her past life by stepping on her bones, she felt that the fire she had set in this life was still too lenient a revenge.

“But…”

Hearing these two words from Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Ying’s dim gaze lifted slightly.

“Do you think I can’t tell the difference between you and her?”

“You only met me at night, and in half a month, you never even saw my face.”

Zhao Xuanyou reached out and took her shoulder, lowering his voice. “Do you look down on me?”

“What else could it be?”

“Do you remember when you asked me to dismiss Zhou Mama?”

Yu Ying certainly remembered.

Getting rid of Zhou Mama had been the first step in her revenge plan.

And because this step had gone smoothly, everything afterward had become easier.

“At that time, although I didn’t know that someone else had taken her place at night, I could sense that the personalities of the person in the day and the person at night were completely different. Back then, I thought it was because the Duke’s residence had strict control over the young lady, and Zhou Mama was a confidante of the Duchess, so Cui Yichu had to suppress her true nature in front of her.”

“So you didn’t ask any questions and just dealt with Zhou Mama?”

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement. Seeing the tears welling in Yu Ying’s eyes, he reached out and gently pressed the corner of her eye.

“But I’m talking about something else. I didn’t ask you to deal with Zhou Mama, nor did I ask you to stay in the capital. Every night, I drank the sedative tea Cui Yichu gave me and slept deeply. Until you left the capital, until I was silenced, I never exchanged a single word with you.”

“Even if I returned to the capital a year later, even if I never saw you again, as long as Cui Yichu truly approached me, I would know she wasn’t the same person as you.”

Yu Ying felt like he was trying to comfort her.

“How could that be? Although my figure is different from hers, she could just say that her body changed after childbirth and gloss over it.”

“That excuse might work on others, but not on me. Yingying, don’t forget that I am a martial artist. A person’s weight can change, but their bones cannot.”

Yu Ying was slightly stunned and looked at him fixedly.

Zhao Xuanyou continued, “I have practiced martial arts for many years and have also trained soldiers for many years. I am extremely familiar with people’s figures and bone structures. For example, your guard, Wen Qiao, after seeing him once, I could tell that his bones were delicate and his build was extremely light, making him a rare talent for practicing lightness skills.”

“What you mean is…”

Zhao Xuanyou placed his hand over Yu Ying’s, gently tracing the bones of her fingers, and lowered his voice. “Even if I couldn’t see your face clearly, during those nights you accompanied me, I had already memorized your figure in my heart.”

Yu Ying was dazed for a moment before gradually coming to her senses.

“So, even if you returned to the capital a year later, and Cui Yichu thought everything was foolproof as she went to serve you, as soon as you touched her, you would know she was different from the person before.”

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t know she was talking about her past life; he simply listed the evidence he knew. “That night when the side room of Liu Fang Pavilion caught fire, the moment I held you, I knew you were the one who had lain in my arms at night.”

So that was why…

No wonder he had directly carried her to Honghui Hall in front of everyone.

This thought struck her, and a flicker of joy rose in Yu Ying’s heart.

That’s right; the man before her was meticulous. Even if Cui Yichu’s plan had gone smoothly, he might still have noticed something amiss.

In her past life, after her death, Cui Yichu might not have had such an easy time.

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze deepened as he watched the dull light in Yu Ying’s eyes suddenly regain its brilliance.

In the dark, thick night, her eyes shone like stars, captivating him.

Zhao Xuanyou had never thought that a woman’s every smile and frown could stir his emotions so deeply.

After all, he was a man of both literary and martial prowess, capable of deciding the fate of the nation.

On the battlefield, no matter what kind of enemy he faced, he could charge forward unstoppably, as if invincible.

In the imperial court, when it came to scheming against the civil officials, he was just as formidable, navigating the Emperor’s presence with ease.

Yet, he found himself emotionally affected by Yu Ying’s every move.

When she cried, his heart ached as if twisted by a knife.

When she smiled, he felt elated and bright.

The feared heir of the Jingyuan Marquis, in front of her, was just a man experiencing his first stirrings of love.

“Yingying, have you untangled the knot in your heart?”

Having confided the old matters hidden in her heart to him, the demon that had haunted her for so long finally saw a glimmer of light. At this moment, Yu Ying truly felt a weight lifted.

“Zhao Xuanyou, thank you.”

Her clear eyes were filled with tender warmth; this was the first time since their reunion that she had shown him such an expression.

“You know what kind of thanks I want.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s breathing grew heavy. He pressed his hand against her shoulder, pushing her back against the corridor pillar.

---

chapters.title: Ardent
chapters.content:
Yu Ying’s head was already pressed against the pillar, with no room to retreat.

She couldn’t help but grow tense, the corners of her lips slightly lifting in a sweet, honeyed tone. “I can be your advisor and help you handle military affairs.”

“That’s acceptable.” Zhao Xuanyou’s Adam’s apple bobbed as his gaze remained fixed on her, his voice slightly hoarse. “But it’s not enough.”

Although her face still held a smile, her eyes and breathing were somewhat flustered, and her slender fingers unconsciously covered her collar.

Zhao Xuanyou was in high spirits.

Even though they had been separated for four years, Yingying still remembered his habits from when they were together before.

However, back then, their first meeting had been in bed, and everything had happened too quickly, too hastily. Now that they had a second chance, Zhao Xuanyou hoped, as she wished, to take things slowly.

He didn’t reach out his hand; instead, he lowered his head and kissed her lips.

Yu Ying’s gaze stiffened for a moment, and she even forgot to breathe.

The warmth on her lips felt both unfamiliar and strangely familiar.

She had intended to push him away, but sensing the restraint and awkwardness in his kiss, she inexplicably softened. The hand covering her collar climbed to his shoulder, and she quietly closed her eyes.

Sensing her change, Zhao Xuanyou’s heart swelled with joy, and he naturally pulled her into his arms.

Since he was sitting sideways, the movement tugged at his leg injury.

When the pain came, he didn’t even furrow his brow, completely absorbed in her warmth and softness.

They hadn’t kissed in a long time, and at first, it was a little awkward, but soon it grew passionate and lingering, until Ding Wenxi interrupted them.

“Yingying?”

Hearing her mother’s voice, Yu Ying abruptly pushed Zhao Xuanyou away, her face flushed as she stood up. Seeing Ding Wenxi and Wen Qiao coming out to look for her in the distance, she was at a loss for words.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t pull her back.

Tonight, as far as he was concerned, was already deeply satisfying.

Not only had he driven away Zhao Qi, but Yu Ying had also acknowledged her feelings for him, and they had even shared physical intimacy.

“Yingying, help me bring the wheelchair over.”

Earlier, to stop Zhao Qi from taking Yu Ying away, Zhao Xuanyou had used lightness skills to leap over, leaving his wheelchair far behind.

“Alright.”

Wen Qiao turned his head and spotted the wheelchair on the corridor. Before Yu Ying could move, he had already pushed it over and helped her support Zhao Xuanyou into the wheelchair.

Yu Ying softly asked, “Do you want me to push you back?”

“No need, I’ll go back first.”

The Marquis’s residence was flat, and Zhao Xuanyou had become quite skilled with his wheelchair by now. He didn’t need anyone to push him to return.

However, after he had gone a short distance, Yuan Ai appeared from the side and began pushing him back.

“It’s late, let’s go back to the room.” Yu Ying said quietly.

Wen Qiao didn’t react much and silently followed beside her.

Ding Wenxi’s gaze was clearly somewhat complicated. Yu Ying stepped forward and linked arms with her, stifling a yawn. “Mother, I’m so tired after walking all day.”

“Then go back to your room and sleep early.” Ding Wenxi had no way to deal with her daughter. Seeing her lips red and glossy, still damp, she wiped her mouth with a handkerchief and then led her toward the Tangli Courtyard.

“Mmm.” Yu Ying obediently replied, leaning against Ding Wenxi. “Mother, today on the street I saw two rental shop locations that were both quite good. Tomorrow, let’s go take another look together. If they’re suitable, we can buy them.”

“You looked at shops today?”

Yu Ying smiled. “Yes, from the Marquis’s residence all the way to the Hu People’s Market, I checked everything carefully. I even bought a jade bracelet.”

As she spoke, Yu Ying lifted her sleeve, revealing the bracelet on her wrist for Ding Wenxi to see.

Looking at the bracelet, which was as delicate and smooth as her skin, Ding Wenxi nodded. “The quality is very good. I thought you only bought the jade material.”

“I bought the bracelet; the jade material was a gift from the Hu merchant. Mother, have you seen celestial stones from Tianzhu before?”

“I have. They’re very beautiful.”

“The stones are easier to use for jewelry than pearls.”

Celestial stones could be cut into shapes, and their colors were varied, making them more versatile.

“Yes, I’ve thought about that before, but I didn’t know how long we would stay in Yuzhou. Now…”

Having witnessed Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying’s intimacy firsthand, Ding Wenxi naturally understood that they would be staying in Yuzhou for the long term.

Yu Ying’s feelings were her own decision, so Ding Wenxi could indeed consider opening a shop.

The next morning, Zhao Qi indeed left with his guards, and Yu Ying did not go to see him off.

Zhao Qi had already bid her farewell the night before, so there was no need to meet again.

She only prepared a food box filled with pastries and had Wen Qiao deliver it to Bingyun, who should understand.

After Zhao Qi left, Yu Ying devoted herself to preparing the jewelry shop for her mother.

The shop was located halfway between the Marquis’s residence and the Hu People’s Market. Apart from the convenient location, it was also because the layout was the same as the old Ju Yu Xuan in Qingsha Town; a two-story building in the front with a small courtyard in the back.

The old Ju Yu Xuan, including its signboard and shop, had already been sold to someone else. Now that she was returning to the old business, she naturally needed a new signboard.

After much consideration, Ding Wenxi settled on the name “Linglong Workshop.”

However, this time, she didn’t have the energy to personally train apprentices, so she hired two experienced jade carving masters instead.

Yu Ying purchased a large amount of jade material from the Hu People’s Market and had the two masters create pieces in the styles preferred by the Jiangnan merchants. Once the first batch of jade hairpins and bracelets was completed, Wen Qiao took the goods to Jiangnan.

After Linglong Workshop began to take shape, Yu Ying also found herself with free time and started helping Zhao Xuanyou in his study.

Since that night when they had kissed in the corridor, both of them had pretended as if nothing had happened.

For Yu Ying, that kiss had come too suddenly, and she was completely unprepared to start anew with Zhao Xuanyou.

For Zhao Xuanyou, his leg injury was not yet healed, and acting rashly would be undignified. It would be better to recover first and then prove his prowess in front of her.

Under the current circumstances, having Yu Ying by his side at all times was already the best situation.

Seeing Yu Ying’s interest in military affairs, he forced himself to focus and seriously explained military matters to her.

As time progressed toward the Grain in Ear season, a thousand miles away, the summer lotuses bloomed in abundance on Taiye Pool.

The Emperor, seeing this, held a Clear Lotus Banquet by the pool.

After three rounds of drinks, the Crown Prince, watching the Emperor playing with Zhao Yi Yun, smiled and said, “Today is a family banquet, but we’re missing my seventh brother. If only he were in the capital too.”

Zhao Qi had been away from the capital for more than half a year, and the Emperor indeed missed him. He sighed, “He’s at an age where he can’t sit still. He’s comfortable in his fief and doesn’t want to return to the capital.”

Beside him, the Prince of Ping said, “Seventh Brother still has the restless heart of a youth. Once he’s married, he’ll settle down.”

The Crown Prince didn’t speak but gave Prince Qing, Zhao Yu, a meaningful look.

Zhao Yu said, “I think Seventh Brother has no intention of getting married at all. Father and Mother have spent so much effort on his marriage, and he doesn’t even appreciate it. And I’ve heard something else…”

He drew out his words, and even the Emperor was drawn in by the suspense.

The Crown Prince deliberately put on a stern face. “Then why don’t you speak?”

“Father, your son is not tattling. I heard that Seventh Brother recently left his fief without permission and went to Yuzhou. It seems… it was for a woman.”

Prince Ping frowned slightly upon hearing him shift the topic to Zhao Xuanyou. “He probably went to Yuzhou to renew old ties with Xuanyou.”

“What old ties?” Zhao Yu laughed. “I heard he took a fancy to Xuanyou’s unwed wife. Xuanyou probably hates him for it.”

“Nonsense!” The Emperor’s brows furrowed, and he suddenly slammed the table.

chapters.title: PhotNight White
chapters.content:
In the thick of summer, the courtyard was lush with greenery. A grape trellis had been set up outside the study window, its vines sprawling like a brocade canopy.

Yu Ying sat by the window, helping Zhao Xuanyou review and approve official documents.

She wore a thin, light pink summer dress, her dark hair pinned up with a jade hairpin made by Ding Wenxi. The jade earrings matched the hairpin, creating a fresh and elegant look.

After assisting in the study for two months, Yu Ying had become familiar with Zhao Xuanyou’s duties as the commander of the Mingjuan Guard.

Apart from training and inspecting the Mingjuan Guard and overseeing the military defense of Yu Prefecture, Zhao Xuanyou also managed military supplies, supervised border trade, collected tariffs, and recorded the movements of people at the passes.

However, since he was recovering from his injuries at the Marquis’s residence, the daily roll calls and city wall patrols were handled by Deputy Commander Shen Jiao. Zhao Xuanyou only needed to review military reports daily and periodically submit the military situation around Yu Prefecture to the Ministry of War.

With no current battles, aside from occasional disputes at the Hu market, everything else proceeded routinely.

Yu Ying had grown so accustomed to the work that she could handle most tasks without consulting Zhao Xuanyou. He would only give a final review before having Yuan Zhi and Yuan Qing send the documents out.

His leg injury had taken over three months to heal, and though the sharp pain in his right leg had subsided, it remained weak and numb, preventing him from standing.

After finishing the military reports, Yu Ying looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, who was reading a letter with a deep, contemplative gaze.

“Is it a letter from the capital?”

“Mmm.”

“Has something happened?”

Zhao Xuanyou folded the letter, narrowed his eyes in thought, and said, “It’s not exactly an emergency, but there is something.”

He was always measured in his actions. If it were a confidential military report, he wouldn’t have told Yu Ying.

But since he was being cryptic, she knew it wasn’t a military matter.

“What is it then?”

Zhao Xuanyou placed the letter on the table, propped his chin on his hand, and looked straight at Yu Ying, a hint of a smile in his eyes. “His Majesty has arranged a marriage for Prince Rui. The wedding is set for September.”

Yu Ying wasn’t surprised by the news. Prince Rui was already eighteen, and most princes married at sixteen or seventeen. He was on the later side.

“Which family’s daughter did His Majesty choose for the prince?”

“Liang Xiaofeng, the daughter of Liang Xuan, the Assistant Minister of War.”

“That’s a beautiful name,” Yu Ying said sincerely. But noticing Zhao Xuanyou’s expression, she asked in confusion, “Why do you frown at the prince’s marriage?”

Zhao Xuanyou’s expression shifted slightly. “Prince Rui had been keeping His Majesty in good spirits, and His Majesty had agreed not to rush him into marriage. This time, the marriage was arranged for a reason.”

Hearing the gravity in Zhao Xuanyou’s tone, Yu Ying realized something. “Does it have to do with us?”

Zhao Xuanyou was pleased with her use of “us.” He smiled briefly, then hesitated before speaking. “Someone told His Majesty that Prince Rui came to Yu Prefecture not for sightseeing but to take my betrothed. His Majesty was furious and summoned Prince Rui back to the capital, ordering him to marry in the capital before taking his princess to his fief.”

Yu Ying immediately saw the problem.

“It’s true that Prince Rui’s visit to Yu Prefecture couldn’t be kept secret, but how did what happened that night spread so far?”

After all, the only people present that night were Zhao Xuanyou’s trusted aides and Zhao Qi’s guards. Who would have reported the conflict between Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Qi back to the capital?

“Either someone close to him has been planted as a spy, or there’s a mole in the Marquis’s residence.”

Zhao Qi’s affairs were none of his concern, but he absolutely could not tolerate a spy in his own ranks.

Yu Ying looked at his serious expression and softly said, “I don’t know if Yuan Zhi still remembers the guards he took to the corridor that night. If there’s a list, it wouldn’t be hard to investigate.”

Zhao Xuanyou had always known she was intelligent, and in a moment, she had figured it out.

“I just recalled the guards from that night. If the spy is indeed in the Marquis’s residence, there are two or three people who might be suspicious.” As he spoke, Zhao Xuanyou looked up and smiled. “It’s not a big deal. Oh, aren’t you going out today?”

“Yes, the Hu merchant you introduced said he had new Dayuan horses. I made plans with Ah Qiang to go pick one.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s mount was a famous black Dayuan horse that had been with him through countless battles, brave and invincible.

Yu Ying also wanted a Dayuan horse, but she had never found a suitable one. Yesterday, the merchant had sent word to Linglong Pavilion that several good horses would arrive today, so she had arranged with Wen Qiang to go take a look.

“Do you want me to go with you?”

“No need. You’ve taught me how to pick a horse, and I remember. If I find one I like, I’ll bring it back to show you.”

Zhao Xuanyou gave a slight nod. “Yuan Qing also has a good eye for horses. Have him go with you.”

He needed to focus on investigating the spy in the residence. This matter was urgent; the longer it dragged on, the more secrets would leak.

Yu Ying nodded and left the study. Yingxue immediately approached her.

She had arrived in Yu Prefecture a month ago and had been staying close to Yu Ying ever since.

“Miss, Young Master Wen is already waiting for you in the front courtyard.”

So Wen Qiang had arrived. Yu Ying quickened her steps toward the front courtyard.

Wen Qiang was waiting idly, not in the mood for tea. When he saw Yu Ying, he walked up and said directly, “Let’s go.”

Yu Ying and her group then headed toward the Hu market. The horse market was near the city gate, filled with the scent of hay, leather, and the unique smell of horses; not pleasant.

However, the Dayuan horses were impressively tall and truly magnificent.

At first glance, the horses’ coats shimmered like clouds and mist; snow-white, date-red, jet-black, and even the rare silver-maned blue roan.

The Hu merchant, with his curly beard, approached and greeted in broken official speech: “The new horses are all here. Miss, feel free to choose.”

Yu Ying didn’t say much. She walked forward and began examining the horses one by one.

When she saw the first date-red horse, Yuan Qing quietly said, “Its hind hooves are too narrow. It’ll go lame on long journeys.”

Yu Ying nodded and looked at the second horse, a black one. The horse saw her and lightly pranced, letting out a loud neigh.

Before Yuan Qing could speak, Yu Ying said, “This horse has a beautiful waistline, but its fetlocks are too thick, aren’t they?”

Yuan Qing couldn’t help but bow slightly to her in admiration.

Zhao Xuanyou had previously told Yu Ying the standards for selecting war horses: first, the eyes; bright and clear like hanging bells, with a calm inner light; second, the hooves; hard as iron and of moderate width, the foundation of a fine steed.

“I’m just guessing,” she said with a laugh.

Selecting a horse was a profound skill, and what Zhao Xuanyou had taught her was only the basics.

As they joked, Yu Ying’s gaze fell on the edge of the enclosure. A snow-white steed stood alone in the corner, its entire body like freshly fallen snow, except for its four black hooves, as if it were stepping on ink clouds.

Looking at its coat, her eyes flickered. “Baiye the Night-Shining White?”

That was a highly prized breed among horse connoisseurs, said to be priceless.

Even the Hu merchant praised, “Miss has a good eye. That one is a true descendant of the Heavenly Horse.”

“How much?”

“For someone from the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, I’ll give you a discount; one thousand taels.”

To be honest, as soon as Yu Ying saw Baiye the Night-Shining White, she had set her heart on it.

But she wasn’t Zhao Xuanyou; she didn’t need a horse for battle, charging across the battlefield.

She usually just rode for leisure, and spending a thousand taels on a horse seemed extravagant.

But she did truly like that horse.

As Yu Ying hesitated, Wen Qiang said, “Horses like this are usually wild and hard to tame. Try it out first.”

The Hu merchant, seeing the situation, also stepped forward. “There’s no room to run here. Miss, go outside the city to test-ride it. Once you’ve ridden a true divine steed, you’ll understand why people are willing to pay a thousand gold for a horse.”

Yu Ying had only ridden gentle horses before and wasn’t sure if she could handle this one.

Baiye the Night-Shining White stood quietly, its black eyes fixed on Yu Ying as if it understood her.

“Then I’ll try it.”

Yuan Qing, hearing that Yu Ying wanted to test the horse, advised, “First go and lead the horse, pet its head and mane. If it lets you touch it, it’ll probably let you ride it.”

“I know.”

The Hu merchant led Baiye the Night-Shining White over. As Yu Ying raised her hand, the horse unexpectedly lowered its head on its own.

“Good horse!” Yu Ying joyfully took the reins from the Hu merchant and led the horse toward the city gates herself.

Summer had arrived, and the shallow grassland in front of the city gate from spring had grown into a lush meadow over a foot tall.

A cool breeze blew from the grasslands, rustling Yu Ying’s sleeves and bringing a refreshing sensation.

“Giddyup…” Yu Ying mounted the horse, lightly pressing the stirrups. Baiye the Night-Shining White understood and began to trot with her.

After making a small circle in front of the city gate, Yu Ying rode back to the group.

“Looks steady,” Wen Qiang asked.

“It does.” Just now, on the horse’s back, Yu Ying could clearly feel Baiye’s intelligence. It watched the road and slowed its steps slightly when turning to prevent her from feeling unsteady.

“Boss, lower the price a bit more, and I’ll buy it.”

“One thousand taels is already cheap. In the Central Plains, people would pay a thousand gold for it! Miss, if you don’t believe me, ride faster, and you’ll see how amazing it is.”

Yu Ying gently stroked the horse’s mane and whispered, “Let’s go one more round. This time, let’s go faster.”

Baiye the Night-Shining White snorted, as if understanding her words, and carried her off into the distance, clearly faster than before, yet still graceful and steady.

Wen Qiang watched Yu Ying riding happily but felt something was off.

He walked over to Yuan Qing and quietly asked, “I don’t know much about Dayuan horses. Are they all this gentle?”

“Dayuan horses are much more spirited than Central Plains horses.”

Wen Qiang’s heart stirred. “Then this horse is a bit too gentle.”

Yuan Qing, hearing this, indeed felt that a famous steed like Baiye the Night-Shining White should be extremely difficult to tame.

Seeing Yuan Qing’s expression, Wen Qiang didn’t wait for him to speak. He shouted toward Yu Ying in the distance, “Yu Ying, ride back quickly!”

Yu Ying, though she hadn’t heard him clearly, still pulled the reins to stop the horse, then turned it around toward the city gate.

Wen Qiang had just let out a sigh of relief when suddenly, a long, clear whistle cut through the air!

The whistle was crisp, but it seemed to drift from very far away.

Baiye the Night-Shining White’s muscles instantly tensed. Its previously calm black eyes suddenly turned fierce!

It reared up with a loud neigh. Before Yu Ying could react, it suddenly changed direction and bolted like an arrow from a bow!

“Yu Ying!”

Wen Qiang’s face changed dramatically. He leaped up, pushing his qinggong to the limit, and rushed toward the horse like a green shadow, trying to jump onto its back.

But Baiye the Night-Shining White seemed to anticipate this. It suddenly made a sharp turn in another direction, causing Wen Qiang to miss and fall empty-handed.

Yu Ying tightly gripped the reins. She tried to stop the horse, but Baiye the Night-Shining White completely ignored her, running faster and faster!

She couldn’t jump off the horse and risk her life, so she could only lean down and hug its neck tightly, her fingertips turning white from the effort.

As Baiye the Night-Shining White ran farther and farther away, Wen Qiang clenched the iron beads in his hand but couldn’t throw them. If the horse was injured, Yu Ying would be too.

“I’ll go after her.”

Yuan Qing mounted a horse and led the guards in pursuit, galloping in the direction Baiye the Night-Shining White had taken.

Wen Qiang forced himself to calm down. Before the whistle, Baiye the Night-Shining White had been obeying Yu Ying.

The whistle was a command for the horse. Someone had used the horse to lure Yu Ying. What did they want with her?

Could it be directed at Zhao Xuanyou?

At this thought, Wen Qiang hurried toward the city gate.

Yuan Qing had already left a guard behind to detain the Hu merchant before leaving.

Wen Qiang knew this matter was connected to the Hu merchant. He grabbed the man by the collar.

“Speak! Where did you take Yu Ying?”

“Since I’ve captured her, why would I tell you where she is?” The Hu merchant’s eyes showed no fear; instead, his face was filled with a smug smile at the success of his scheme.

Wen Qiang knew he wouldn’t get any answers this way. He only said to the guard, “Immediately report Yu Ying’s disappearance to the Young Master.”

“Yes.”

But the guard had only taken a few steps when a group of horsemen rode out from the city. The leader’s robes fluttered in the wind, his face dark. It was Zhao Xuanyou!

“Young Master, Miss Yu Ying was taken away by the Hu merchant’s horse!” the guard reported urgently.

Wen Qiang brought the Hu merchant before Zhao Xuanyou.

He was somewhat surprised. Zhao Xuanyou’s leg injury hadn’t healed. How could he ride a horse?

But in the next moment, he saw that Zhao Xuanyou’s right leg was tied to the stirrup with a rope to prevent him from falling.

At the sight of Zhao Xuanyou, the Hu merchant’s face twisted with rage. He cursed, “Zhao Xuanyou! Eight years ago, you killed my son at Gray Wolf Lake! Today is finally the day you pay with your life!”

“To take revenge, you’ve hidden in Yu Prefecture for long enough,” Zhao Xuanyou said coldly.

This Hu merchant had been doing business in Yu Prefecture for several years. Zhao Xuanyou had purchased hundreds of military horses from him and had never noticed anything amiss.

“As your people say, a gentleman’s revenge is a dish best served cold.”

“Kidnapping a young girl. What kind of gentleman does that?” Thinking of how this man dared to target Yu Ying, Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes filled with a chilling intent. With a swing of his long sword, the Hu merchant’s head fell to the ground.

Wen Qiang was somewhat shocked. “Isn’t it too soon to kill him? Does Young Master know who’s behind this?”

“More or less. What exactly happened?”

A short while ago, a beggar had delivered a letter to the Marquis’s residence, demanding that Zhao Xuanyou bring the military deployment maps of the Northwest to Gray Wolf Lake in exchange for Yu Ying.

Eight years ago, Zhao Xuanyou had killed the leader of the Wuhuan at Gray Wolf Lake. It seemed this group had come to avenge that old grievance.

Wen Qiang recounted what had happened after Yu Ying chose Baiye the Night-Shining White, then added, “Yuan Qing took men to pursue on horseback. But I don’t think they’ll catch up.”

In the past, Crown Prince Zhao Zun had ridden a Heavenly Horse even better than Baiye the Night-Shining White.

But Zhao Zun, accustomed to luxury, rode only for pleasure, so Wen Qiang hadn’t thought much of the Heavenly Horse’s capabilities.

But after seeing how Baiye the Night-Shining White had carried Yu Ying away with lightning speed, Wen Qiang realized that on the vast, boundless grasslands, nothing could outrun it.

“Young Master, I’ll go with you to Gray Wolf Lake.”

“Good.”

Although the enemy had specified that Zhao Xuanyou must go alone, Wen Qiang’s qinggong was superb, and he had ways to conceal himself from detection.

Zhao Xuanyou then said to Yuan Zhi, “The Wuhuan want Yu Prefecture. After I leave, have Deputy Commander Shen immediately close the city gates and prohibit anyone from entering or leaving. Thoroughly investigate every person in the Hu market and root out the spies remaining in Yu Prefecture. Take a team of good men and go to Gray Wolf Lake by another route. Wait five li away for my signal.”

“Yes.”

Once everything was arranged, Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Qiang rode off toward the depths of the grasslands.

chapters.title: Divine Steed
chapters.content:
Meanwhile, Yuan Qing and the guards galloped in the direction Baiye the Night-Shining White had taken.

Yu Ying tightly gripped the reins, her heart pounding. She tried to pull back, but the horse ignored her completely, running faster and faster.

She couldn’t jump off; it would be suicide. So she leaned down, clinging to the horse’s neck, her fingers white from the strain.

Baiye the Night-Shining White ran like the wind, its hooves barely touching the ground. The grasslands stretched endlessly, and the horse showed no sign of tiring.

Yu Ying’s mind raced. Who would do this? And why?

The whistle had been the signal. Someone had trained Baiye to respond to it. But who?

The Hu merchant? But he had seemed genuine. Unless...

Unless he had been part of the plot all along.

The thought sent a chill down her spine.

She had to stay calm. Panic wouldn’t help.

She took a deep breath, trying to steady her racing heart. The horse was fast, but it wasn’t invincible. There had to be a way to stop it.

She remembered Zhao Xuanyou’s lessons. A good rider didn’t just control the horse; they worked with it.

But Baiye wasn’t listening.

She tried pulling the reins again, harder this time. The horse only tossed its head, as if annoyed by her resistance.

Then, an idea struck her.

She shifted her weight slightly, leaning to one side. The horse adjusted its balance instinctively.

It was still responding to her, even if it was fighting her control.

She did it again, more deliberately this time. The horse hesitated, its stride faltering for just a moment.

Encouraged, she tried a third time, putting all her strength into the movement.

Baiye the Night-Shining White slowed, its ears twitching as if confused by the mixed signals.

Yu Ying didn’t let up. She kept leaning, kept pulling, her voice steady despite her fear. “Whoa. Easy, girl. Easy.”

The horse’s pace slackened further. It was working.

Then, without warning, Baiye reared up, its front legs pawing at the air.

Yu Ying barely kept her seat, her arms locked around the horse’s neck.

For a heart-stopping moment, she thought she would fall. But then the horse settled back onto all fours, its breath coming in great, heaving gusts.

Yu Ying didn’t waste a second. She yanked the reins hard, her voice sharp. “Stop!”

Baiye the Night-Shining White resisted, but it was tiring. Its wild energy was fading.

Finally, after what felt like an eternity, the horse slowed to a trot, then a walk, then, blessedly, to a stop.

Yu Ying slumped forward, her forehead pressing against the horse’s sweaty neck. She was shaking, her body drained of strength.

But she was alive. And she was free.

She lifted her head, scanning the horizon. The city was nowhere in sight. She had no idea how far she’d been taken.

But she knew one thing: she couldn’t stay here.

She took a deep breath, steeling herself. She had to get back.

She gathered the reins again, her voice firmer this time. “Let’s go home.”

Baiye the Night-Shining White flicked its ears, as if considering her words.

Yu Ying held her breath.

Then, to her relief, the horse turned, its hooves thudding against the earth as it began to trot back the way they’d come.

The return journey was slower, but steady. Yu Ying kept a tight grip on the reins, her eyes scanning the horizon for any sign of pursuit; or rescue.

She didn’t know how long she’d been riding when she finally spotted a familiar landmark; a cluster of rocks that looked like a crouching tiger. She remembered passing it on the way out.

Her spirits lifted. She was on the right path.

As the sun began to dip below the horizon, casting long shadows across the grasslands, Yu Ying finally saw the city walls in the distance.

Tears pricked at her eyes. She was going to make it.

But her relief was short-lived.

A group of riders appeared on the horizon, moving toward her at a rapid pace.

Yu Ying’s heart leaped into her throat. Were they friends or foes?

She pulled Baiye to a stop, her mind racing. She couldn’t outrun them if they meant her harm. But she couldn’t just sit here and wait, either.

She made a quick decision. She would ride toward them, but be ready to flee at the first sign of trouble.

She urged Baiye forward, her eyes never leaving the approaching riders.

As they drew closer, she recognized the lead rider’s dark, flowing robes.

Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Ying’s breath caught. He was here. He had come for her.

But then she noticed something else. His right leg was bound to the stirrup, his face set in a grim line.

He was still injured. He shouldn’t be riding.

But there was no time to dwell on it. The riders were almost upon her.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes locked onto hers, and in that moment, Yu Ying felt a wave of emotion so strong it nearly knocked her from the saddle.

She had been so scared. So alone.

But now he was here.

The riders surrounded her, but Yu Ying only had eyes for Zhao Xuanyou.

“Yu Ying,” he said, his voice rough with emotion. “Are you hurt?”

She shook her head, her throat too tight to speak.

He reached out, his hand cupping her face. His touch was warm, grounding. “You’re safe now.”

Yu Ying leaned into his touch, her eyes closing briefly. When she opened them again, she saw the concern in his gaze, the tension in his jaw.

She wanted to tell him she was fine. That she had been so scared, but she had handled it.

But all that came out was a whisper. “I’m okay.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s thumb brushed her cheek, his voice low. “Let’s go home.”

Yu Ying nodded, her grip on the reins loosening slightly.

But then Baiye the Night-Shining White suddenly tossed its head, its ears flattening against its skull.

A warning.

Yu Ying’s blood ran cold.

She turned, following the horse’s gaze.

On the horizon, a cloud of dust was rising. More riders. And they were coming fast.

Zhao Xuanyou’s hand dropped from her face, his expression turning icy. “Wuhuan.”

Yu Ying’s heart pounded. They weren’t safe yet.

Zhao Xuanyou’s voice was sharp, cutting through the tension. “Wen Qiang, take Yu Ying back to the city. Now.”

Wen Qiang didn’t hesitate. He rode up beside Yu Ying, his hand reaching for Baiye’s reins. “Miss, come with me.”

Yu Ying wanted to protest. She didn’t want to leave Zhao Xuanyou. But she knew he was right. She would only be a liability in a fight.

She nodded, her voice steady despite the fear coiling in her stomach. “Be careful.”

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze was fierce, determined. “I will.”

Then, with a final look at Yu Ying, he turned his horse, riding out to meet the approaching riders with his guards at his back.

Yu Ying watched him go, her heart in her throat.

Wen Qiang urged Baiye forward, and Yu Ying had no choice but to follow.

As they rode, she couldn’t shake the image of Zhao Xuanyou, injured and outnumbered, riding toward danger.

She had to trust him. She had to believe he would come back to her.

But the fear lingered, a cold knot in her stomach.

Because she knew, more than anything, that she couldn’t lose him.

chapters.title: The Hiding Place
chapters.content:
The wind howled as Yu Wan crouched low on the horse's back.

Riding a wild horse was like courting death; she could only cling tightly to it to ensure she wasn’t thrown off.

Zhao Xuan’s steed, Zhaoyebai, carried Yu Wan across the grasslands, and the deeper they went, the denser the grass became.

Yu Wan could sense that although the horse was running fast, it was shockingly steady. A sudden realization struck her; Zhaoyebai wasn’t running wild, nor did it want to throw her off. Instead, it was taking her somewhere.

She cautiously loosened one hand from the reins, and sure enough, the horse remained steady.

She couldn’t panic. The enemy only wanted to use Zhaoyebai to kidnap her, not kill her.

Zhao Xuan and Wen Shi would definitely come looking for her. In the vast grasslands, she needed to leave them some markers.

Yu Wan gritted her teeth, gripping the reins tightly with one hand while reaching for her hair with the other.

She pulled out the sheep-fat jade magnolia hairpin, her fingertips trembling slightly. It was a gift from her mother when she first arrived in Yu Province, and she had worn it ever since. But now…

She steeling her heart, she threw the hairpin away.

After Zhaoyebai had run a bit further, Yu Wan removed one of her earrings.

One by one, her jewelry was discarded; the jade bracelet by a shallow stream, the necklace into the tall grass, the handkerchief from her sleeve caught on a low tree.

Gradually, she had no more ornaments left to throw.

Yu Wan gritted her teeth again. Rip! She tore a strip of thin fabric from her sleeve and threw it behind her.

She didn’t know if Zhao Xuan would be able to find these things.

But if she didn’t leave them, in the vast grasslands, they would have no way to track her.

Zhaoyebai seemed to notice her actions. Suddenly, it reared its head and neighed loudly, speeding up even more. Yu Wan clung desperately to its neck, feeling the tension in its muscles.

As the sky gradually darkened, the lush green grasslands turned pitch black, as if they could swallow everything at any moment.

It was then that Zhaoyebai began to slow down.

Soon, it carried Yu Wan around a small valley, and she suddenly noticed a flicker of firelight in the distance.

Yu Wan’s heart pounded violently.

Zhao Xuan had told her that the Wuhuan were nomadic people who followed the grass for generations. Those who could hide deep in the grasslands must be them.

They had captured her to threaten Zhao Xuan.

Zhaoyebai brought Yu Wan to a bonfire.

Yu Wan’s entire body tensed. By the firelight, she saw more than a dozen gray-brown tents scattered around the valley.

Was this a Wuhuan tribe?

As she zoned out, Yu Wan heard a chatter of women’s voices. Only then did she notice a woman in Indian attire affectionately patting Zhaoyebai’s face and talking to it, seemingly praising it.

“You?” Upon seeing the woman’s face clearly, Yu Wan exclaimed in surprise.

The woman in the red sari looked up, her gaze alluring.

It was the same Indian beauty she had encountered at the city gate and the Hu people’s market before.

“Aren’t you Indian? Why did you capture me?”

“I do indeed have no grudge against you, but someone else has a blood feud with Zhao Xuan.”

“Get down!”

Before Yu Wan could react, someone roughly yanked her off the horse with brute force.

Yu Wan looked around. The bonfire roared, illuminating the fierce faces of the Wuhuan warriors.

Perhaps sensing the softness of Yu Wan’s wrist, the man who pulled her looked at her with a lecherous gaze.

However, after staring at her for a moment, he tied her hands with a rope.

Yu Wan suppressed the panic in her heart and looked around by the firelight. She noticed that the outskirts of these tents were hidden with caltrops and tripwires; clearly a carefully arranged hiding place.

“Tiya, has the person been captured?” A cold voice came from the central tent.

The Indian woman named Tiya patted Zhaoyebai’s neck, letting it go graze nearby, then smiled and walked forward.

“Prince, do you still doubt me? My horse is the smartest in the world.”

The tent flap lifted, and a young man stepped out.

He looked to be around the same age as Zhao Xuan, draped in a Wuhuan royal wolf-fur cloak. His features were sinister, with an old scar on his left cheek.

He ignored Tiya and strode straight to Yu Wan, sizing her up from head to toe.

“Zhao Xuan’s woman doesn’t look like much.”

Yu Wan felt uncomfortable under his gaze. After a moment, she defended herself, “I’m just his maid, not his woman.”

“Don’t be modest. The prince has spies in the Marquis’s residence. Everyone there knows you’re his betrothed.”

Yu Wan’s heart sank.

There were indeed spies in the Marquis’s residence, but unfortunately, Zhao Xuan hadn’t had time to uncover them before this incident.

“So what if I am? The Young Marquis is severely injured. Even if I’m captured, he can’t come save me. Your plan won’t work.”

The Wuhuan prince burst into laughter, then suddenly grabbed her chin. “If he doesn’t come, that’s fine too. If he doesn’t come, you can keep me company for a while. When I’m tired of you, I’ll throw you back to him so he can slowly savor the aftermath.”

Noticing the torn sleeves on Yu Wan, his eyes narrowed, and he reached out to pull at her clothes.

He was incredibly strong, and with one tug, he tore open half of her garment, exposing her fair shoulder.

“Ooh!” The surrounding Wuhuan men, seeing this, immediately let out excited shouts.

Facing these beast-like men, Yu Wan’s heart pounded with fear.

“Prince,” Tiya suddenly grabbed his hand, “What’s so special about this woman compared to me? How can you be interested in her?”

“She’s Zhao Xuan’s woman, of course I’m interested.”

“Hmph,” Tiya pretended to be angry, “Then what am I?”

“You are, of course, my beloved.”

“Easy to say.” Tiya gave a coy laugh, then added, “This woman still has some use. I’ll take charge of her for now. If Zhao Xuan really doesn’t care about her, then the prince can deal with her as he pleases.”

“Fine.”

He had waited eight years for this revenge, for the murder of his father. Of course, he wouldn’t risk everything for a small matter now.

Tiya turned around, grabbed Yu Wan’s shoulder, and pushed her into a nearby tent.

This tent was scented, and the floor was covered with Persian carpets; clearly Tiya’s living quarters.

Once the tent flap was lowered, Yu Wan whispered, “Thank you.”

Tiya sat on the bed, looking down at her with a superior air. “It was my plan to capture you. Why are you thanking me?”

“If it weren’t for you just now, I would have been… Anyway, thank you.”

“Don’t thank me too soon.”

Yu Wan, of course, understood that Tiya was an enemy.

But Tiya wasn’t a Wuhuan; she had no grudge against Zhao Xuan. Perhaps she was a breakthrough point.

She cautiously glanced at Tiya, putting on a frightened look. “Who are those people outside? Why did they capture me?”

“You really don’t understand?” Tiya asked.

Yu Wan shook her head.

Tiya smiled. “The most handsome man just now is named Asuhan. He’s the youngest son of the Wuhuan king. Eight years ago, he escaped from Zhao Xuan’s sword. All these years, he’s been plotting his revenge. Do you remember when you came to my shop that day?”

“Was Asuhan there that day?”

“Of course not. These years, I’ve been gathering intelligence for him in Yu Province. That day, as soon as I saw Zhao Xuan’s attitude toward you, I knew my chance had come.”

---

chapters.title: The Lame Lover
chapters.content:
“That day?”

Yu Wan recalled the first time she had visited the Hu people’s market. She remembered that Zhao Xuan had not entered Tiya’s shop but had stood at the door watching.

“The moment I saw the way he looked at you, I knew how much he valued you.” Tiya’s Mandarin was better than that of any other foreigner Yu Wan had encountered in Yu Province.

If one ignored her exotic face, it would be hard to believe she was from India.

“Is that so?” Yu Wan gave a faint smile. “He’s a womanizer. He treats all women the same. You’ve misjudged this time. You’ve captured someone useless. Your Wuhuan lover won’t spare you.”

“If he were truly a womanizer, how could I not have gotten close to him?”

Yu Wan, upon hearing this, unconsciously retorted, “You tried to seduce him?”

“Why are you so nervous?”

Realizing she had been momentarily distracted, Yu Wan lightly coughed and regained her composure. “Many women have tried to seduce Zhao Xuan. Though he’s a womanizer, he’s also picky. You’re not his type.”

“He’s a cripple now. I’m not picky either.”

“Truly not picky?” Yu Wan looked around, her gaze falling back on Tiya. “I’ve heard that in India, the caste system is strict; the whiter the skin, the nobler the person. A beauty like you must come from a good background. Your tent is so different from the others around here. You don’t belong here at all.”

Tiya, of course, came from a good background.

Unfortunately, her father had lost a power struggle, and she had become a plaything for his enemies.

It was because of that unbearable memory that, even though she didn’t like Yu Wan, she had still stopped Asuhan when he tried to assault her.

Noticing the fleeting pain in Tiya’s eyes, Yu Wan thought for a moment and advised, “Why don’t you stay in Yu Province and live a peaceful life? You can find a man if you want, or not if you don’t. Why stay in a place like this?”

“Will you give Zhao Xuan to me?”

If it were before, Yu Wan would certainly have said yes.

But for some reason, even though she knew she was just talking nonsense with Tiya, she didn’t want to casually agree.

“He’s a cripple. He’s not worthy of you. As long as you let me go, I’ll help you find someone better than him.”

Tiya let out a cold humph, looking indifferent.

Her eyes were dark and large, as still as a deep pool.

“No need. And don’t waste your breath trying to persuade me to let you go. Years ago, it was Asuhan who killed my enemy with his own hands. Now it’s my turn to help him take revenge.” As she spoke, Tiya sat in front of the mirror and began applying makeup, making her face even more alluring.

She changed into a purple sari, then walked toward the tent exit. Before leaving, she turned back to Yu Wan, “No one dares enter my tent. If you’re not honest and try to run out, and those men catch you, I won’t be able to help you.”

With that, she walked out.

Outside was the vast grassland. Even if Yu Wan could escape the tent, she couldn’t escape the grassland.

Moreover, her hands were still tied, and she couldn’t even ride a horse.

She wondered if Zhao Xuan and Wen Shi had found the jewelry she had dropped.

Lost in thought, Yu Wan’s stomach let out a loud gurgle.

After being carried by Zhaoyebai all day, she hadn’t eaten or drunk anything and was already parched.

On the table in the tent, there was a wine flask and a plate of apples. Yu Wan, paying no mind to her bound hands, walked to the table, bent down, and bit the mouth of the flask. She managed to tilt it with her mouth, and a stream of sweet grape wine flowed into her mouth.

Though half of it spilled, she still drank the other half.

After drinking the wine, Yu Wan set her sights on the plate of apples. Unable to grab them, she opened her mouth and bit directly into one.

However, the grape wine, though it tasted sweet and sour, was quite strong.

Yu Wan had a low tolerance for alcohol. After just a few bites of the apple, she became dizzy and fell asleep.

When Tiya entered the tent the next day, she saw Yu Wan lying on the Persian carpet, fast asleep. Then she noticed the wine flask lying on its side on the table, and several half-eaten apples scattered on the ground.

Without hesitation, she walked forward and gave Yu Wan a few light kicks.

Yu Wan opened her bleary eyes, saw Tiya, and slowly sat up.

“You’re quite the prisoner, enjoying yourself.”

“That’s only because the young lady is kind. That’s why I can stay here.” Yu Wan understood the principle of survival of the fittest. In this place, aside from Tiya, no one would reason with her. Of course, she had to speak humbly. “I was so thirsty yesterday, and my hands were tied like this. I had no choice but to waste your grape wine and apples.”

Seeing her being so sensible, Tiya didn’t say anything. Soon, she brought her a bowl of water and threw a piece of flatbread.

“Ration it. This is all there is for today.”

Time passed extremely slowly in the tent. Tiya sat at the table, weaving strange knots with colored ropes, not speaking to Yu Wan.

As it neared dusk, there was a sudden commotion outside the tent.

The Wuhuan people chattered in their language, and Tiya’s expression changed, her gaze becoming serious.

She threw down the rope in her hands, draped her sari over her shoulders, and walked out.

Although Yu Wan couldn’t understand what the people outside were saying, she could clearly sense their tense emotions.

Was it Zhao Xuan?

It had to be him. Only Zhao Xuan could make them so vigilant.

Yu Wan’s mind was in turmoil.

She knew Zhao Xuan was capable, but this was a trap Asuhan had spent eight years carefully designing for him. Could he really avoid it?

Yu Wan stood up and quickly walked to the tent entrance. She saw the Wuhuan tribe members gathering outside their tents; there were over a hundred of them.

Asuhan was speaking in their language; Tiya stood beside him, listening silently.

After Asuhan finished speaking to his people, Tiya began to argue with him about something.

She reached out to pull Asuhan, but he pushed her away with one hand, sending her crashing to the ground.

Not long after, Asuhan led a group of people on horseback and left. The remaining group began to dismantle the tents, as if preparing to break camp.

Tiya got up from the ground, dusted off her sari, and turned toward her tent. She saw Yu Wan poking her head out of the tent, looking around.

“Thinking of escaping?”

Yu Wan retreated back into the tent. Tiya entered but didn’t speak, only lowering her head to pack her things.

Yu Wan tentatively asked, “Are you leaving this place?”

Tiya didn’t answer her.

Yu Wan wasn’t discouraged and continued, “What happened just now? Why did Asuhan push you? I thought he liked you a lot. I didn’t expect him to be so harsh with you.”

Hearing the provocation in Yu Wan’s words, Tiya said with a sinking face, “You have the time to worry about me; you should worry about yourself instead.”

“I don’t even know what’s going on now, so how can I worry?”

“Your lame lover has come to find you.”

So it really was Zhao Xuan?

With his intelligence, he must have known it was a trap, yet he still came.

Yu Wan felt a mix of joy and worry. She forced down the anxiety in her eyes and asked again, “If he’s fallen into the trap, why did you and Asuhan argue?”

“We should have left immediately since Zhao Xuan is doomed, but he insists on meeting Zhao Xuan one last time.”

As soon as Tiya finished speaking, a few tragic screams suddenly came from outside.

chapters.title: You Wish
chapters.content:
Tiya frowned slightly, but then more screams came.

Although she didn’t know what was happening outside, it was clear that only the Wuhuan people could produce so many screams.

Yu Yuan knew that her rescuers had arrived, and a surge of wild joy filled her heart.

Just as she was about to shout to let the people outside know she was here, she saw Tiya pull out a dagger inlaid with rubies from beside her.

"You, don’t be impulsive. We don’t even know what’s happening out there. Let’s see first."

Tiya said no more. She grabbed Yu Yuan’s arm, pressed the dagger to her neck, and forced her to walk outside.

Feeling the sharp edge of the blade against her neck, Yu Yuan didn’t dare to breathe. Her breath almost stopped.

Outside the tent, the night had completely fallen.

The Wuhuan people hadn’t lit any campfires tonight, but the full moon in the sky was exceptionally bright, casting an amber glow over the mountain hollow.

Earlier, the Wuhuan people, busy packing up camp, were now sprawled on the ground, screaming in agony.

A few survivors waved their knives and shouted, but they had no idea who they were shouting at.

Tiya had assumed it was Zhao Xuanyou’s men attacking, but after looking around, she saw no enemies; only the fallen Wuhuan warriors.

Yu Yuan’s eyes welled up with tears, but she knew exactly who had come.

"If you don’t want her to die, stop right now!" Tiya had no choice but to shout into the void.

Yet the remaining Wuhuan in the hollow continued to fall one by one.

Tiya was clearly flustered. She suddenly pressed the dagger to Yu Yuan’s face.

"If you don’t stop, I’ll slash her face first!"

The moment she finished speaking, Tiya distinctly felt a strong gust of wind rush toward her.

When she blinked and refocused, a person wearing a civet cat mask stood before her.

Though she couldn’t see their face, their figure was slender, much thinner than Zhao Xuanyou’s.

Tiya exclaimed in surprise, "You’re not Zhao Xuanyou."

Wen Ji, of course, didn’t answer her. He only looked at Yu Yuan to check her condition.

After seeing Tiya’s grip on the dagger and its direction, he raised his hand and shot out an iron bead.

"Ah…" Tiya’s wrist acupuncture point was struck hard. The dagger clattered to the ground, and she collapsed with it.

Wen Ji pulled Yu Yuan behind him and raised his hand to launch another hidden weapon, but Yu Yuan stopped him.

"Don’t kill her."

"But she just tried to slash your face." Ever since the time Wen Ji and Yu Yuan were both captured by Pei Ta’s men, he had decided never to show mercy in a fight.

Tonight, against these Wuhuan people, every strike he made was aimed to kill.

"She helped me before. Just leave her here to fend for herself."

Wen Ji hummed in acknowledgment and put the iron bead away.

His earlier strike had been heavy. Tiya felt as if her wrist was about to shatter. Her beautiful face instantly lost all color.

She gritted her teeth against the pain and looked at Yu Yuan. "So this is the man you wanted me to help you find?"

Seeing that Tiya still had the energy to joke even in this state, Yu Yuan said, "You wish!"

She turned to Wen Ji and asked urgently, "Where is he?"

Wen Ji, of course, knew who Yu Yuan was asking about. He took out the jade hairpin Yu Yuan had thrown earlier from his sleeve and quietly explained everything.

"I followed the Prince all the way here tracking you. Asuohan is skilled in martial arts and has many men. A direct confrontation would have been unfavorable for you. So the Prince went to Grey Wolf Lake alone, and I waited until Asuohan took his men there before coming to rescue you."

The things she had thrown away had indeed come in handy, allowing them to track her here.

But now, Yu Yuan’s heart was gripped by Wen Ji’s words.

"He… went alone? Asuohan took so many men with him earlier. He’s still injured. How can he handle so many people by himself?"

Wen Ji naturally understood that Zhao Xuanyou had deliberately used himself as bait to lure away most of the Wuhuan forces, allowing him to rescue Yu Yuan smoothly.

He only cared about Yu Yuan and had no objections to this plan.

Seeing how anxious Yu Yuan was, Wen Ji said, "Then I’ll go help him now."

"We’ll go together. Their horses are over there." Yu Yuan was about to take Wen Ji to find the horses, but he stopped her. "I’ll go help. You should ride a horse back on your own."

Guessing Yu Yuan’s concerns, Wen Ji added, "Yuan Qu is leading people to meet the Prince five miles away from Grey Wolf Lake. You go back first. I know what I’m doing."

Yu Yuan heard the determination in Wen Ji’s voice. Knowing she couldn’t fight, she realized going would only be a hindrance. She finally nodded.

The two had only taken a few steps forward when Tiya, behind them, said, "If you two want to live, get on a horse right now and ride east without looking back. Don’t stop for even a moment."

Yu Yuan detected something in Tiya’s tone and paused, turning back to look at her. "What do you mean?"

Tiya’s face was covered in cold sweat from the pain in her wrist. She answered evasively, "Look at the moon in the sky."

Tonight’s moon was large and round, as if unusually close to the earth. Staring at it always gave one an eerie feeling.

"Just now, you spared my life, so now I return the favor. A once-in-a-century sandstorm is coming from the Western Regions. Grey Wolf Lake has no shelter. No matter how many men Zhao Xuanyou takes there, it won’t help. He’s doomed. If you leave now, you might still make it."

As Tiya spoke, she raised her hand and whistled.

Soon, the sound of hooves approached. The horse Zhaoyebai leapt out of the darkness and came straight to Tiya.

Tiya endured the pain in her right hand and tried to mount the horse with her left, but she couldn’t muster the strength.

Wen Ji gave her a push, and Tiya settled onto the horse. She turned back to look at him.

"You really are a good man."

With that, she gave a soft whistle. Zhaoyebai carried her away quickly.

"Yu Yuan, is what she said about the sandstorm true?"

"There’s no reason for her to lie to me." Earlier, Tiya had argued with Asuohan, likely trying to persuade him to leave quickly. Unfortunately, Asuohan was determined to kill Zhao Xuanyou with his own hands and didn’t listen to her advice.

Tiya riding away eastward without looking back also proved her words were true.

"Then I’ll immediately send the Prince a signal to retreat." Before parting, Zhao Xuanyou had given Wen Ji the signal flares used by the army.

He promptly fired a green flare into the sky to warn Zhao Xuanyou at Grey Wolf Lake, then went to the Wuhuan’s stable to fetch a horse.

"The Prince should understand the signal means there’s a trap. You ride my horse east first. I’ll go to Grey Wolf Lake to check. If the Prince is unharmed, we’ll come after you immediately."

"You take care of yourself too."

"I know."

Yu Yuan’s heart was in turmoil, but she still got on the horse as instructed.

Once out of the hollow, Wen Ji parted ways with Yu Yuan and rode alone toward Grey Wolf Lake to the west.

But Yu Yuan did not leave.

They had come to rescue her. At a time like this, she truly couldn’t bring herself to abandon them and flee alone.

---

chapters.title: The Sandstorm
chapters.content:
The night wind began to howl. Yu Yuan felt sand in the air, making each breath difficult.

Tiya hadn’t lied; the sandstorm was coming.

This sandstorm was the trap Asuohan had meticulously prepared for Zhao Xuanyou.

Grey Wolf Lake was surrounded by flat land. Once the all-consuming sandstorm arrived, Zhao Xuanyou would have no chance of survival.

Not just Zhao Xuanyou.

It might already be too late for her to leave.

There had to be a way to survive! Yu Yuan forced herself to calm down. She turned back to look at the chaotic campsite, dismounted, and ran back to Tiya’s tent.

She took a veil from Tiya’s cabinet and wrapped it around her face to block the wind and sand. After gathering some supplies from the camp, she remounted her horse and rode in the direction Wen Ji had gone.

Even with the veil over her head, fine grains of sand still stung her hands like needles.

By the moonlight, she saw a massive gray-yellow wall slowly approaching her on the horizon.

This was the great sandstorm Tiya had spoken of; the wall of death that devoured everything.

"Hya!"

Yu Yuan dug her heels into the horse’s sides. The steed neighed and charged toward Grey Wolf Lake.

The sand in the wind grew thicker, and visibility worsened.

Yu Yuan took a whistle from her bosom; another item she had found in Tiya’s tent.

She blew it hard. The whistle’s sound was piercing.

By now, Asuohan and his men should have already left Grey Wolf Lake. If Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Ji were still there, they should be able to hear her whistle.

Yu Yuan rode and blew the whistle, anxiously scanning her surroundings.

Through the swirling dust, she suddenly spotted a black steed coming against the wind.

The man on the horse wore a black robe that flapped in the wind. His face was as pale as paper, but a smile lingered at the corner of his lips.

"Zhao Xuanyou!"

Yu Yuan shouted, but the howling wind swallowed her voice. She could only urge her horse toward him.

As she got closer, she saw that his right leg was tied to the stirrup with hemp rope, so that was how he was riding.

Yu Yuan’s eyes stung.

The man across from her was speaking, but Yu Yuan couldn’t hear what he was saying.

The sandstorm was almost upon them. This was no time for reunions. Yu Yuan blew the whistle again, then beckoned to him, signaling him to follow.

Visibility grew worse by the moment.

Every so often, Yu Yuan would blow the whistle a few times, leading Zhao Xuanyou all the way back to the hollow’s camp.

The sandstorm hadn’t fully arrived yet, so the hollow still provided some shelter from the wind.

Yu Yuan dismounted first and used a dagger to cut the rope binding Zhao Xuanyou’s leg.

He had been traveling through the grasslands for two days, and the rope had already cut into his flesh, stained red with blood.

Tears welled in Yu Yuan’s eyes, but Zhao Xuanyou remained calm.

He dismounted, supporting himself on his left leg.

Yu Yuan hurried over to help him, but Zhao Xuanyou didn’t let her. Instead, he pulled her into his arms.

"Have you suffered these past two days?"

"Not at all. They didn’t harm me."

Yu Yuan had so much to say to him, but she only managed those two short sentences.

The sandstorm was approaching. There was too much to do.

Yu Yuan grabbed his hand and whispered into his ear, "The sandstorm is almost here. Just hiding in this hollow won’t be enough. We need to prepare quickly."

Zhao Xuanyou had never experienced a sandstorm before, but seeing the slowly approaching wall, he could imagine its terror.

He turned and patted the horse’s back. "Go find your own way to survive."

The black horse neighed and galloped out of the hollow.

Yu Yuan helped Zhao Xuanyou to the back of Tiya’s tent. There happened to be a sunken area, not a cave, but large enough to hold both of them.

"You stay here and don’t move. I’ll get some things."

"I’ll help you."

Zhao Xuanyou tried to stand, but Yu Yuan stopped him with her hand.

"No more moving. If you end up disabled, I won’t pay you any mind in the future."

Her words were a threat, but her expression was only filled with concern.

Zhao Xuanyou’s right leg truly couldn’t take any more strain.

"Stay put. I have the strength."

Yu Yuan ran off, quickly moving things from Tiya’s tent to their shelter. She first laid down a Persian rug, then took the grape wine and fruits Tiya had stored.

The Wuhuan people had been packing up camp before Wen Ji’s ambush, so many supplies were already packed. This made things easier for Yu Yuan, who simply moved several large bundles over.

"Yu Yuan, the sandstorm is almost here. Come back quickly."
