As the gray-yellow wall drew nearer, urgency flashed in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes. He called out to Yu Yuan.

Even though he had faced many life-and-death traps before, this moment with Yu Yuan was the one he least wanted to die in.

"There’s still the most important step!"

Yu Yuan dragged over a tent pole the Wuhuan people had dismantled, setting it up like a beam in the sunken area.

Seeing how much effort it took her, Zhao Xuanyou forced himself to stand and helped her press the pole into the ground.

"One pole isn’t sturdy enough."

Yu Yuan panted heavily but, without hesitation, dragged over another tent pole.

Once Zhao Xuanyou had secured both poles, Yu Yuan laid two layers of tent fabric over them, then weighed down the edges with burlap sacks she had transported.

After finishing, Yu Yuan had no strength left. She collapsed into Zhao Xuanyou’s arms.

"Yu Yuan, drink some water."

Yu Yuan weakly hummed in response, letting him feed her. After gulping down a large mouthful, she stopped him.

"We don’t know how many days we’ll be stuck here. We should ration the water. It’s a shame I’m not strong enough. If I could have carried all their water over, we’d have more to spare."

"This is enough for us. Don’t risk going out again."

Outside, the wind howled fiercely. Sand and gravel pelted the tent fabric like countless claws scratching.

Zhao Xuanyou looked around and felt an unexpected sense of peace.

This place couldn’t be called a tent, nor was it a cave, but Yu Yuan had arranged it well. The ground was covered with Persian rugs and Wuhuan felt mats. Besides dry rations and water, there was grape wine and fruit.

He never would have imagined that in such a crude place, the word "home" would rise in his heart.

This was a refuge Yu Yuan had built with her own hands, and it was also a cozy nest.

Yu Yuan nestled in Zhao Xuanyou’s arms, completely drained.

She recalled the times she had lain in his arms like this before, but the past was nothing like the present.

"Did you meet Wen Ji?" Yu Yuan asked.

Zhao Xuanyou said quietly, "No. I saw the retreat signal he sent, but I didn’t see you. I didn’t want to leave."

Yu Yuan’s heart felt as if it had been pricked by something, but she didn’t know what to say. She only asked, "Zhao Xuanyou, does your leg hurt?"

"It’s fine."

Watching the blood from his right leg drip onto the Persian rug, Yu Yuan forced herself to sit up again.

"Don’t be stubborn. Tell me what you need, and I’ll get it for you." Zhao Xuanyou reached out to press her shoulder, wanting her to rest.

Yu Yuan huffed lightly, "I’ll stop the bleeding first. Once that’s done, I won’t fuss over you anymore."

chapters.title: I'm Here
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou met her clear eyes and was momentarily dazed.

Seeing that he didn’t speak, Yu Wan moved his hand aside, crawled over, and retrieved the things they needed.

The depression was not small, but neither was it large; enough for them to lie down or sit, but not enough for them to stand up.

Yu Wan took the supplies and sat in front of Zhao Xuanyou, carefully pulling open his pants. She gasped sharply at the sight.

The wounds where the ropes had cut into his flesh were horrific, the surrounding skin bruised purple.

"This will hurt. Bear with it."

"It's fine."

Yu Wan knew he had an extremely high pain tolerance. She smiled at him, then carefully poured mare’s milk wine over his wounds, softly saying, "This mare’s milk wine probably isn’t as effective as strong liquor, but it’s better than grape wine. For now, we’ll have to make do."

After cleaning the wound, Yu Wan began sprinkling medicinal powder.

It was a wound medicine made by the Wuhuan people, much cruder and more potent than the medicines of the Central Plains.

Zhao Xuanyou suddenly jerked his head back, his Adam’s apple rolling, but he didn’t make a sound.

Yu Wan took a dagger, cut a piece of her inner garment, and bandaged his wound before finally relaxing, collapsing back into the crook of his arm.

Knowing she was exhausted, Zhao Xuanyou propped himself up slightly and rummaged through the supplies beside them, finding some Wuhuan dried rations.

"Eat something."

He stuffed a hard, stone-like piece into her mouth.

Yu Wan frowned but still chewed and swallowed it. Though Tiya hadn’t starved her, she hadn’t given her enough to eat either. She was already starving.

"What is this?"

"Milk curds," Zhao Xuanyou said, feeding himself a piece as well before tearing off a piece of dried meat and feeding it to Yu Wan. "Wuhuan food may not taste good, but it’s filling and easy to preserve. Perfect for us right now."

Yu Wan chewed the dried meat, her cheeks aching from the effort.

"Earlier, you always told me how good pepper soup was, but I could never get used to it. Right now, a bowl of pepper soup would be perfect."

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her pouting, aggrieved expression and gently pulled her into his arms. "When we return to Yuzhou, I’ll take you to Zui Xiang Lou for pepper soup first."

"Mmm, when we return to Yuzhou, besides pepper soup, I also want a big serving of mutton soup dumplings."

Listening to her talk about what she would do when they returned to Yuzhou, Zhao Xuanyou’s heart stirred.

The sandstorm was upon them. Though they were temporarily sheltered here, their lives hung by a thread.

If they truly made it back to Yuzhou alive...

"Yuan Yuan," the light in the tent was dim, but Zhao Xuanyou reached out, cupping her face to bring her closer.

His palm was scorching, his gaze even more intense.

Some words, if not said now, might never have the chance to be spoken.

"What’s wrong?" Sensing the fire in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes, Yu Wan slightly lowered her head.

"When we return to Yuzhou..."

Outside, the sandstorm raged, the howling of the wind and sand growing wilder.

Even with the protection of the mountain depression and the slanted tent that wouldn’t easily blow over, the tent fabric groaned under the strain, tearing sounds echoing ominously.

Suddenly, a corner of the tent was blown open by the gale, and yellow sand began pouring in through the gap. Though it wasn’t fast, it was relentless.

Yu Wan was startled.

If this continued, they would be buried alive.

They had to do something!

Instinctively, she lunged toward the sand leak, adding her weight to press down the tent fabric, barely managing to block the influx of sand.

Zhao Xuanyou naturally saw the urgency of the situation. Though his leg injury made movement difficult, his strength far surpassed Yu Wan’s.

He immediately shifted to the other side of the tent, using his body to press down the fabric.

Together, under the shelter of the two main poles and the mountain’s slope, they propped up a triangular space, like a desert fox’s den, forming a barrier against the wind and sand.

Sand particles still seeped through, but visibly less and less.

"This sandstorm is terrifying. It feels like the grassland outside has been completely swallowed."

Yu Wan muttered, suddenly thinking of something.

She pulled out the dagger Tiya had left at her waist, stabbed it into the ground, and began digging with all her strength.

"Yuan Yuan, what are you doing?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

"The sandstorm will bury this place. It’s too cramped here now. We need to dig it bigger while there’s still some airflow, or before the sandstorm stops, we’ll both suffocate here."

Zhao Xuanyou immediately understood. Using the short knife he carried, he joined Yu Wan in digging the depression deeper, pushing the soil out through the gaps at the edge of the tent.

Yu Wan had already expended too much energy earlier, but fortunately, Zhao Xuanyou still had strength left. Soon, they had deepened the depression by a fold; it was now clearly a small cave.

"This should be enough, right?"

Yu Wan looked at the short knife, now worn beyond recognition, knowing Zhao Xuanyou’s strength was also nearing its limit. She nodded at him.

As the saying goes, do your best and leave the rest to fate. They had done everything they could; the rest was up to heaven.

Feeling the sandstorm outside crashing down like huge waves, Zhao Xuanyou pushed all the supplies to Yu Wan’s side, pressing the tent fabric down for her.

Before Yu Wan could react, he had already pulled her into his arms, using his body to shield her from the most violent sand intrusion.

Outside, the sand raged like the end of the world, as if the heavens and earth were in chaos.

Curled up in Zhao Xuanyou’s arms, Yu Wan could still hear his steady, powerful heartbeat.

In this second life, she was the most cowardly, afraid of death.

She wanted to live differently, to live longer, to make up for the brief life she had lost before.

But for some reason, at this life-and-death moment, she felt strangely at peace.

This was fine too.

If this life ended like this, it seemed there was nothing to regret.

After an unknown amount of time, the wind outside gradually weakened.

Yu Wan’s eyes flickered, a spark of vitality returning.

"Did you feel that?" came Zhao Xuanyou’s hoarse voice from above.

Yu Wan looked up and saw the pile of sand that had poured in beside him. It was both heartbreaking and a little amusing.

"I feel the wind is weaker. Have we survived the worst?"

"Mmm, probably."

That was great.

She was alive. Zhao Xuanyou was alive too.

"Since the wind is weaker, we don’t have to keep pressing down the tent fabric. We can go lie down."

Yu Wan happily scrambled out of his arms and redistributed some of the supplies from the other side to weigh down this part of the tent fabric.

Zhao Xuanyou, however, did not move.

The tent was too dark for Yu Wan to see his expression.

But as she reached up and touched his chin, she felt it was burning hot.

"You have a fever!" Yu Wan gasped, quickly pulling him toward the Persian rug.

After he lay down, Yu Wan realized his entire body was scorching.

"Yuan Yuan, I want to drink some water..." Zhao Xuanyou said hoarsely.

"Okay, I’ll get water right away." Yu Wan hastily found the waterskin that had rolled to the side, carefully lifting his neck to feed him.

Zhao Xuanyou slightly opened his eyes, his blurred gaze falling on her face.

The tent was small and dim; he couldn’t see her face clearly, only her bright, star-like eyes.

"Yuan Yuan." He called softly.

Yu Wan, hearing the weakness in his voice, felt a sting in her nose and tears welled up.

"I’m here."

---

chapters.title: Whispers in the Sand Tent
chapters.content:
He reached for her, trying to touch her face, but after groping for a moment, he still couldn’t find it.

The mist in Yu Wan’s eyes grew thicker.

She should have noticed his discomfort earlier. From the moment he followed her to the mountain hollow, he had already been a little off.

Not as sharp as usual, his reactions seemed slower.

He had just been forcing himself to stay alert, not wanting to distract her.

Yu Wan took his hand, feeling the scorching heat of his palm. The heat made the touch on her hand even more pronounced.

"Do you want to drink some grape wine? After drinking, have a good sleep. Maybe you’ll feel better tomorrow."

"I don’t want to sleep," Zhao Xuanyou stubbornly said.

After drinking water, Zhao Xuanyou’s voice was no longer as hoarse as before.

It was rare to have this time alone with her; he didn’t want to waste it by sleeping.

"Then drink more water. I just checked, we still have plenty of water, enough for several days." After he drank half a pot, Yu Wan tore off a piece of dried meat to feed him.

Fearful he might choke, she tore it into finer pieces.

Zhao Xuanyou lay quietly for a while, feeling a little better. He exhaled deeply.

"Yuan Yuan, if we still have enough water, help me rinse the wound again."

Earlier, when she had washed his wound with mare’s milk wine, it had felt uncomfortable.

Zhao Xuanyou had some medical knowledge and knew his fever was due to the rope burns.

Though they needed to conserve water, if the wound wasn’t treated properly, it would become a burden for Yu Wan.

"We have enough."

Yu Wan undid the bandage and rinsed the wound again with water. Then she picked up the Wuhuan medicinal powder, hesitating as she asked, "Should I sprinkle this?"

She didn’t quite trust the Wuhuan remedies.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded. "It works."

Yu Wan sprinkled the powder on the wound, feeling his body twitch a couple of times. His expression stiffened, and she softly said, "Actually, you don’t have to endure the pain silently. I won’t laugh at you."

"I never intended to cry out."

He had joined the army in his early teens. Back then, everyone looked down on him as a mere child.

To establish his authority, he naturally couldn’t cry or scream when he got cut or stabbed by swords. Over time, even when he felt excruciating pain, he had grown used to not shouting, enduring it until it passed.

Though he bled, he didn’t shed tears. But this time, with her by his side, his mood wasn’t heavy, and he truly didn’t feel the pain.

Listening to Yu Wan cutting the fabric, and thinking about how she had torn off pieces of her sleeve to leave a trail for him, he said, "You’ve torn so much of your clothes. How much do you have left?"

Yu Wan heard the implication in his words and felt a mix of anger and helplessness.

"At a time like this, you still have the mood for that?"

"I always have the mood for that with you."

Yu Wan had only heard Zhao Xuanyou make such suggestive remarks before. Back in Qingsha Town, when a hooligan tried to flirt with her, he hadn’t even finished his sentence before Wen Tao beat him up in the street.

Of course, she despised others for talking nonsense, but when Zhao Xuanyou did it... he said it so naturally that it didn’t sound vulgar to her. It was as if they were an old married couple.

"Too lazy to pay attention to you." Yu Wan said indifferently, giving his shoulder a very perfunctory pat.

Zhao Xuanyou stubbornly said, "Hit me harder. I’m not that weak."

"Shut up."

Yu Wan stuffed a piece of milk curd into his mouth to silence him, then took a small sip of water herself.

She had told Zhao Xuanyou they had plenty of water, but she was being very frugal with her own consumption.

The wind and sand outside seemed to have lessened, but who knew how long it would take to completely pass.

Moreover, once the sandstorm ended, the original grassland might have turned into a desert. To get out, they would still need water and dried rations. It was always wise to conserve.

"Besides your right leg, is there anywhere else that doesn’t feel well?" Yu Wan asked again.

"Nothing else feels wrong." Hearing her worried tone, Zhao Xuanyou pulled her close, hugging her tightly to show her his strength.

Knowing he was forcing himself, Yu Wan didn’t expose him. She just went along with his words. "Then you better get well soon."

"Rest assured, when I’m better, I’ll make sure to..." His lips twitched slightly as he lowered his voice.

"Zhao Xuanyou!"

Yu Wan cursed him fiercely and tried to pull away from his arms.

Zhao Xuanyou quickly pulled her back, softly coaxing, "If you don’t like it, I won’t say it. I’m a patient now, weak. You can settle the score with me after I recover."

"You should close your eyes and rest for a while." Yu Wan also knew he wasn’t in good condition and wasn’t truly angry.

"I’ve closed my eyes."

The night was much colder than the day. Yu Wan pulled over another piece of sheep’s wool felt to cover them both.

"Yuan Yuan." Zhao Xuanyou called again.

Yu Wan turned over to face away from him, deliberately ignoring him, wanting him to fall asleep quickly.

But he also turned onto his side, wrapping his arms around her from behind.

Yu Wan couldn’t help but say, "Your leg is still injured!"

"It’s just a minor scratch. It’s nothing." Before Yu Wan could say anything else, Zhao Xuanyou softly asked, "Do you still remember the last time we lay together?"

The last time... lay together...

Yu Wan’s eyelashes trembled.

"It should be the night before New Year’s Eve."

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement, adding, "It was the night before New Year’s Eve, four years ago."

At that time, he was still the commander of the Brocade Guards. Not only was he busy with official duties, but his family was also busy preparing for the New Year and his wedding. He barely had time to exchange a few words with Yu Wan each day.

He remembered that night when he returned to Honghui Hall, it was already very late. But Yu Wan wanted him to take her horseback riding outside the city.

Her beautiful eyes looked pitiful and full of anticipation.

He had almost agreed, but then thought that there would be plenty of time in the future, so it could wait.

That night, he had still held Yu Wan as she slept, but he didn’t know it would be their last night together.

Not waiting for Yu Wan’s response, Zhao Xuanyou felt a pang of hurt. He smiled helplessly, his voice hoarse as he said, "Yuan Yuan, there’s something I want to say now."

Yu Wan quickly replied, "Say it."

He pulled the person in his arms even closer, his hoarse voice finishing the words he hadn’t been able to say before.

"When I forced you to leave Anzhou, I didn’t feel good about it. I decided I would never force you to do anything again. So I wanted to give you time, to slowly wait for you to change your mind. But when the sandstorm hit, I regretted it. I don’t know how much longer I can live. If I keep waiting, what if I don’t make it before you come around? Like four years ago, I wanted to wait until after the New Year to take you to trample snow and admire plum blossoms, but you left me before that New Year. Yuan Yuan, we’ve already wasted four years. Don’t push me away anymore. When we return to Yuzhou alive, marry me, okay?"

Yu Wan, still facing away from him, didn’t speak.

Zhao Xuanyou’s brows furrowed slightly, a stab of pain in his heart.

She was still hesitating!

Still had reservations!

She still hadn’t let go of the person in Anzhou!

Zhao Xuanyou had been invincible on the battlefield, and of course, he didn’t want to retreat in front of her either.

He turned Yu Wan’s shoulder, flipping her over.

In the darkness, Yu Wan didn’t dodge his gaze. She just looked up at him, her beautiful eyes vivid and clear, like a pool of spring water from an empty mountain.

Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but reach out, cupping her face and brushing aside the loose strands of hair that had fallen over her face.

"Yuan Yuan, we…"

Before he could finish, Yu Wan suddenly spoke, cutting him off.

"Okay."

chapters.title: Fulfilling Each Other
chapters.content:
The wind and sand outside the tent still raged, howling through the dark night.

Inside the tent, however, it suddenly fell silent.

After a long while, Zhao Xuanyou finally spoke: "Will you marry me?"

He still cupped her face, and though neither could see the other's expression clearly in the darkness, Yu Wan detected the subtle change in his tone.

He asked cautiously, as if he didn’t quite believe her answer.

"Yes, I’ve agreed," Yu Wan replied softly.

The moment her words fell, Zhao Xuanyou rolled over with her, pinning her beneath him.

"You wouldn’t just be saying that out of pity for me, would you?"

He was feverish, his body burning hot, and though he pressed against her, Yu Wan found it strangely comforting in this moment.

But he was too close; his hot breath tickled her ears and chin.

"Your Highness the Heir, what’s there to pity? If anything, I’m the pitiful one."

Hearing her slightly aggrieved yet tender words, Zhao Xuanyou felt a little more at ease, but doubt still lingered.

"Say it again."

"Say what?"

"That you’ll marry me."

At this moment, they were so close they could clearly see each other’s eyes.

Yu Wan lifted her gaze. Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes were like a deep, tranquil spring, profound and serene, yet brimming with hidden affection.

He stared at her intently, waiting for a definitive answer.

"I’ve already said it twice. Why must I say it again?"

"Just one more time."

He was being so shameless. Yu Wan, pinned beneath him and unable to move, had no choice but to comply. She said once more, "I will marry you."

This time, she spoke clearly and completely. Zhao Xuanyou was pleased, but it still wasn’t enough.

"Say it again. Say you’ll marry me, and it’s not just because I’m injured and you’re trying to comfort me."

"Zhao Xuanyou, are you ever going to stop?" Yu Wan couldn’t help but complain, even though she knew he was still recovering from serious injuries.

"Annoying to death. I’ve changed my mind, I don’t want to, "

Before she could finish, Zhao Xuanyou suddenly covered her mouth with his hand and lowered his voice. "Not that line."

Perhaps sensing the irritation in her eyes, he softened his tone. "Just one last time."

Yu Wan let out a silent sigh in her heart.

She had never imagined Zhao Xuanyou would have a moment like this, so afraid of losing what he had.

He was the esteemed heir, the formidable commander of the Mingchuan Guard, usually cold and noble, a man of few words who never wavered once he spoke.

Who would have thought he’d obsessively repeat the same question over and over because of a single sentence?

Yu Wan couldn’t quite describe her own feelings. Her heart raced, just like when she had been reborn and found herself consciously held in his arms; panicked, flustered, yet filled with a faint joy.

"Zhao Xuanyou, I want to marry you because I like you."

"You like me?" Zhao Xuanyou’s Adam’s apple bobbed, but he wasn’t asking Yu Wan; he was murmuring to himself. "You like me."

He narrowed his eyes, looking at Yu Wan in his arms. She was still the same soft, fragrant beauty as before, but this time, it wasn’t just sharing a bed with different dreams. Their hearts were truly connected.

He nodded slightly, then whispered again, "You like me."

Just as Yu Wan was about to say he wasn’t keeping his word, he suddenly lowered his head and captured her lips.

This time, it wasn’t the restrained and awkward kiss from the corridor before. This was bold and possessive, easily claiming her lips.

He didn’t seem feverish at all, only holding her tighter and tighter.

Yu Wan felt as if she could barely breathe. She squirmed in his arms in protest.

But the man’s breathing was heavy, with no intention of stopping. Instead, he wrapped an arm around her slender waist, invading her space as recklessly as he had in the past.

After a few muffled sounds, Yu Wan pushed against his shoulder.

Normally, her strength was no match for his, but he was still weak from his injuries and fever. With all her might, she managed to push him away slightly.

Feeling the heat radiating from him, she whispered, "At least wait until you’re better."

"Wanwan."

Zhao Xuanyou listened to her soft, sweet voice, as if he had returned to the days when they had whispered to each other in intimacy.

No, it was even better than before.

Back then, he had only considered Yu Wan his concubine, and she had seen him as a temporary shelter from the storm.

Now, they understood each other’s hearts and had promised themselves to each other for life.

He lowered his head and kissed her brow, then her cheek. When he tried to kiss elsewhere, Yu Wan swung a light fist at him.

"Ah."

Zhao Xuanyou’s Adam’s apple moved again. In the end, he restrained the urge to devour her completely; not that he had much choice. In his current state, not only would it worsen his injuries, but he might also... fail halfway.

After four years apart, he really didn’t want that to happen.

Eventually, he released Yu Wan and rolled back onto the Persian rug.

"Wanwan, you finally said it. You like me."

Yu Wan, resting her head on his arm, couldn’t help but say, "Did you really need to hear it so many times?"

"Of course." Zhao Xuanyou was still basking in the afterglow of their intimacy, his voice hoarse as he said, "You have no idea how long I’ve waited to hear those words."

Yu Wan listened, but her mind wandered to the past. She suddenly asked, "How long?"

"From the moment you left."

Yu Wan let out a soft laugh. "That wasn’t very long."

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze flickered. He caught the implication in her words and reached out to lightly tap her nose. "And you?"

Yu Wan met his gaze without flinching, her eyes clear and bright. "It was before you."

Zhao Xuanyou was slightly taken aback.

"Is that strange?" Yu Wan pushed his hand away and said concisely, "If I had told you I liked you, that I had feelings for you before leaving the Marquis’s mansion, what would you have done?"

"I..." Zhao Xuanyou’s emotions surged, and for a moment, he was at a loss for words.

Yu Wan continued, "You would have reminded me to know my place, that you’d give me what I was entitled to, but I couldn’t take what wasn’t mine."

He was the powerful commander of the Brocade Guard, wielding great authority, basking in the emperor’s favor, at the peak of his glory.

And she was just a lowly concubine in the Marquis’s mansion. Though beautiful and charming, she could only serve with her looks, never expecting permanence.

No one knew what Yu Wan had thought before leaving the capital.

Leaving Zhao Xuanyou had been a difficult decision.

But these thoughts and struggles, Yu Wan had never shared with anyone, not even her mother, despite her repeated inquiries.

After all, she was of low status. Being able to live peacefully with her mother was already a luxury. How could she dare to dream of having Zhao Xuanyou all to herself?

"Wanwan, I understand now." Zhao Xuanyou suddenly felt a great weight lift.

He had always resented her for leaving, always been angry at her heartlessness.

But it was only now that he realized, if she hadn’t left, he never would have truly had her.

It was her ruthlessness back then that had made this possible.

She no longer had to endure hardship, and he no longer had to suffer loneliness.

They whispered to each other, their intimacy lasting long into the night.

---

chapters.title: Dredging Up the Past
chapters.content:
Yu Wan said she had been the first to fall for him.

Zhao Xuanyou pondered for a moment before a smile of joy spread across his face.

But after a while, he murmured, "Not necessarily. You might not have been the first."

Yu Wan let out a soft humph, clearly not buying it.

"Don’t believe me?"

Of course she didn’t. She pressed her lips together and bluntly exposed his reasoning. "What you call ‘falling for me’ is just lust at first sight."

In the darkness, her eyes still sparkled.

"So what if it was lust at first sight? Isn’t that a kind of feeling?"

Ever since Zhao Xuanyou had argued with her about fate and doomed love, Yu Wan knew that though the man usually spoke little, he had a silver tongue and could easily lead her astray.

Seeing Yu Wan left speechless, Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow. "Well? Does that mean I fell for you first?"

If he counted lust as part of it, then it could be traced back to the very first night they met.

"Too lazy to argue with you. You win."

Hearing the dissatisfaction in Yu Wan’s voice, Zhao Xuanyou, his voice rough, said, "How can you say I won? You’re the one who changed your heart."

He sounded so sour. Yu Wan retorted, "You’ve been married and engaged. What about you?"

"I have been married and engaged, but I’ve only ever had feelings for you. What about you?"

"Didn’t you like Cui Yichu?" Yu Wan asked quickly.

Zhao Xuanyou might have a silver tongue, but so did she.

"I liked Cui Yichu..."

Did he?

When he had married Cui Yichu, Zhao Xuanyou had indeed held great expectations for her.

Cui Yichu was his equal in status, the most beautiful woman in the capital, and renowned for her talent. Marrying such a wife should have led to a harmonious life, like a perfect match made in heaven.

But the moment he lifted her bridal veil and saw Cui Yichu’s ashen, lifeless expression, his hopes had been dashed.

"You think I had feelings for her because of you, not her." Zhao Xuanyou pulled her waist closer, certain as he said, "And you? That time... was it really love?"

"Do you really want to hear?"

Hearing Yu Wan’s soft counterquestion, Zhao Xuanyou felt a surge of frustration, like a toothless tiger; prey was taunting him, but he couldn’t reach out with his claws or bite.

"I don’t want to hear," he said fiercely. "Irrelevant people. Let’s not bring them up."

Fierce as he was, there was a hint of bluster in his voice.

Yu Wan nestled quietly in his arms, her gaze shifting like water, and for a moment, she said nothing.

Outside, the sandstorm raged, the grains like blades, pelting the tent fabric with a constant rustling.

Seeing Yu Wan’s silence, Zhao Xuanyou regretted bringing up the past.

After a moment of quiet, he tightly wrapped both arms around her waist and said softly, "Do you know what I was thinking when we passed the Goddess Peak on the boat?"

"What could you have been thinking? You don’t even believe in the legend of Goddess Peak. You couldn’t have been praying to the Goddess of Wu Mountain, could you?"

"A light boat has passed ten thousand mountains."

Yu Wan curved her lips slightly. Of course she understood his meaning.

"I know."

Zhao Xuanyou had truly been worried that his earlier words might shake Yu Wan’s resolve. Only upon hearing those three words did he finally feel at ease. "Then it’s settled. We’ll get married as soon as we return to Yu Prefecture."

His voice was extremely low, carrying a hint of pleading.

Feeling his warm breath, Yu Wan blinked and said, "No."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered, a sudden panic rising within him.

He was usually dignified, composed, and unreadable, but now Yu Wan’s light words had thrown his emotions into turmoil.

Yu Wan saw the fluster in his eyes and felt a slight sense of triumph.

But considering he was still feverish, she retained a shred of conscience and didn’t continue to torment him.

"Getting married isn’t that simple. Even though I’ve agreed, you still need to formally propose to my mother. And what about the Old Dowager and the Marquis? Don’t you need to inform them? What if they disapprove of this marriage?"

Zhao Xuanyou went from despair to relief in an instant. Realizing Yu Wan was just teasing him, he pulled her beneath him and kissed her a few more times.

Only when Yu Wan was breathless did he ease up slightly, soothing his earlier embarrassment.

"There’s nothing to inform them of. They all know my feelings for you."

"Do you want me to marry you in secret in Yu Prefecture?"

"Of course not. But you’re not entirely wrong," Zhao Xuanyou pondered for a moment before making a decision. He cupped her face and solemnly declared, "The three letters and six etiquettes, a proper wedding; none of that can be skipped. Once we return to Yu Prefecture, I’ll write to my grandmother and father immediately to inform them of this."

Yu Wan reached up to touch the tent fabric above them, which had been shielding them from the sandstorm. Earlier, she had been grateful she had layered two sheets, but now she regretted not adding three or four more.

Suddenly, she said, "Do you think we’ll make it back to Yu Prefecture alive?"

"We won’t die."

He had gone through so much trouble to find Yu Wan, and after so many hardships, they had finally pledged themselves to each other. How could he die here?

Yu Wan reached out and touched his forehead; still burning hot.

Her fingers moved down to his excessively dry lips. She quickly sat up and fed him water from a waterskin.

Only after he finished drinking did she say, "Since you don’t want to die, drink some water and get some proper rest."

Zhao Xuanyou sighed, "Wanwan, I’m not being stubborn. I really can’t sleep."

Normally, if someone had a fever and felt unwell, they would take medicine and rest to feel better.

But today, after he and Yu Wan had settled their marriage, even though his body felt heavy and sluggish, he couldn’t bring himself to feel the slightest bit sleepy.

Seeing Yu Wan’s figure crouched by the storage area, rummaging through something, Zhao Xuanyou said, "Don’t bother. I’ve had water, that’s enough."

"There are a lot of things in Tiya’s tent. Maybe there’s something useful."

Unfortunately, they couldn’t light a candle inside the tent, so Yu Wan had to search in the dark.

After a long while, she finally found Tiya’s jar of ointment. As she opened the lid, a strong fragrance wafted out.

Zanzibar was rich in spices, and this scent was much stronger than those from the Central Plains. The pungent aroma made Yu Wan wrinkle her nose.

But Zhao Xuanyou was feverish, and his vision and sense of smell weren’t sharp, so he let Yu Wan apply the ointment to his lips.

"Just that eager to kiss me?" Zhao Xuanyou teased.

Sure enough... he always had that kind of mindset.

Yu Wan rolled her eyes and put the ointment jar aside, playing along. "Yes, I really want to..."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s smug expression, Yu Wan suddenly pounced and bit his neck.

Zhao Xuanyou had trained in martial arts for years, and his body was as solid as a fortress, except for his neck, which was his weak point.

Her bite made him hiss in pain.

Yu Wan, seeing she had hurt him, turned away in satisfaction and continued rummaging through the box.

Her clothes were either torn to make markers or used as bandages for Zhao Xuanyou, leaving them tattered. Earlier, she had specifically taken one of Tiya’s dresses, and now she decided to put it on.

Zhao Xuanyou rubbed the shallow teeth marks on his neck and coldly huffed, "You bite so hard. Are you part dog?"

"I’m part wolf."

Noticing Yu Wan changing clothes beside him, a hint of ambiguity flickered in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes, and a wild thought crossed his mind.

"Not bad, liking to bite. Try biting somewhere else."

Yu Wan had just put on her sleeve and, without thinking, blurted out, "Bite where?"

chapters.title: Seeing the Light of Day Again
chapters.content:
The sandstorm raged for three full days.

The hastily erected tent trembled violently in the gale but somehow remained standing.

Still, countless grains of sand had seeped through the cracks, piling up on the Persian carpet beneath Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou. She had to repeatedly dig away the sand around her to keep from being slowly buried.

Zhao Xuanyou’s condition fluctuated; more often unconscious than awake, his fever stubbornly refusing to break.

Seeing him burning up and drifting in and out of consciousness, Yu Wan feared that night might have been his last burst of vitality before death.

Anxious, she saved all the water for him, drinking only mare’s milk wine and grape wine herself.

Her tolerance for alcohol was poor, so she dared not drink much, fearing she might pass out and leave them both to be buried alive by the shifting sand. She only took a sip when the thirst became unbearable.

On the third day, as Yu Wan counted on her fingers, the howling wind finally ceased.

She tried to lift the tent fabric to check outside, only to find that a thick layer of sand had indeed buried the tent. The slightest movement caused sand to pour inside.

Pulling the tent open in one go seemed impossible.

If only Zhao Xuanyou were uninjured and healthy.

With his strength…

As Yu Wan fretted, a deep voice came from behind her: “The wind has stopped?”

“Mm, the sandstorm is over, but it seems we’re buried under sand. If we can’t lift the tent in one go, the sand will pour in and bury half of us.”

“Help me up.”

Yu Wan crawled to his right side and helped him sit up.

His arm no longer felt as scorching as before.

“Your fever broke?” she asked joyfully.

Zhao Xuanyou was still weak, but his mind was indeed much clearer.

Yet in front of Yu Wan, he refused to show vulnerability, forcing himself to stay alert.

Yu Wan, however, was thinking quickly.

With Zhao Xuanyou’s help, lifting the sand-covered tent together wouldn’t be difficult…

She picked up the wool felt that had been covering them and held it over their heads. Even if the sand cascaded down, it wouldn’t fill their mouths and noses.

“Wait, I’ll help you stand, and then we’ll lift the tent together.”

“Alright.” It was daytime outside, so even buried under sand, they could see clearly.

Zhao Xuanyou looked around their makeshift “home” of the past three days and asked gently, “Should we bring some water and rations?”

“Yes, outside is nothing but sand. We don’t know how long it’ll take to get out, so we should bring supplies.”

Yu Wan filled the empty waterskins with mare’s milk wine and also took a bag of dried meat, hanging them all on herself before steadying Zhao Xuanyou’s right arm.

Together, they gathered their strength and stood up, pushing the tent fabric open.

The sand piled on the tent was too thick; even with both their strength, they couldn’t fully lift it, only managing to expose their heads.

Fortunately, before the sandstorm hit, they had deepened the small depression they were in. The sand had piled up but hadn’t buried them completely; only up to their knees.

“At least we weren’t buried alive.” Yu Wan sighed in relief, tossing aside the wool felt and taking deep breaths of fresh air.

The once-lush grassland had turned into a desert.

Outside, the sky was clear, and the sand was scorching under the sun.

Yu Wan struggled to climb out of the sand first, then pulled Zhao Xuanyou out like uprooting a radish.

“It’s too hot.”

Yu Wan quickly retrieved the wool felt, spreading it on the sand to sit on.

The sandstorm had blown from the northwest to the southeast. If they kept heading northeast, they should be out soon.

But while Yu Wan could walk, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t with his leg injury.

Yu Wan silently fed him a few sips of mare’s milk wine, deep in thought about what to do. Then Zhao Xuanyou frowned and said, “Someone’s coming.”

At his words, Yu Wan also seemed to hear hoofbeats.

Could it be reinforcements?

As she was about to look, Zhao Xuanyou pressed her shoulder down, pulling her to lie flat on the sand.

“What’s wrong?”

The moment she asked, she understood his intention.

With his disappearance, the guards of Yu Prefecture would surely spare no effort to rescue him. But it wasn’t just the Mingli Guards who would search for him; Asuhun might be looking too.

Without knowing if the newcomers were friend or foe, hiding was the safest choice.

The two lay quietly on the back slope of the sand dune, hearing the hoofbeats draw near, then fade, as if circling the desert.

They really were searching for someone!

“I’ll take a look.”

Yu Wan slowly crawled up the sand dune a little. Soon, she spotted a group of riders.

They were too far away for her to see their faces clearly, but among them was a woman in bright, eye-catching clothes; clearly Tiya.

Why was she here?

Had she brought Asuhun’s forces?

Yu Wan was confused, but then she noticed the masked man riding beside Tiya.

Wen Shan?

How was he with Tiya?

Though filled with questions, seeing Wen Shan put Yu Wan at ease.

She turned back to Zhao Xuanyou. “It’s Wen Shan. We’re saved!”

With that, Yu Wan took out her whistle and blew with all her might.

The piercing sound carried far, and the group immediately turned toward them.

Seeing they had noticed, Yu Wan stood up and waved from the sand dune.

Wen Shan spurred his horse forward, galloping over in an instant.

“Yu Wan!” He grabbed her hand, his voice heavier than she had ever heard. “You… you’re really still here.”

Yu Wan smiled at him. “I’m fine, perfectly fine!”

Then she carefully examined him.

“Are you alright?”

That day, Wen Shan had left only moments before her. He had promised to find Zhao Xuanyou, and over these three days, Yu Wan had been worried about him too.

Now, seeing him safe and sound, she finally relaxed.

The other six or seven horses soon arrived.

At the front was Tiya, riding Photnight White, followed by Yuan Zhen, Yuan Qing, and other Hou Mansion guards.

“Young Master!” Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing scrambled over the sand dune. The moment they saw Zhao Xuanyou lying there, their eyes reddened, and they rushed forward.

“Don’t wail. I’m not dead yet.”

In front of others, Zhao Xuanyou remained the unshaken commander of the Mingli Guards.

Thinking of his injuries, Yu Wan quickly stepped forward. “The young master’s right leg was badly lacerated by a hemp rope that day. For the past three days, I’ve only been able to apply some inferior Uwan medicine. If you’ve brought proper medicine, please reapply it for him.”

This time, Yuan Zhen had naturally anticipated Zhao Xuanyou might be injured and had brought a medical kit. He immediately removed the crude bandage from Zhao Xuanyou’s leg and reapplied the medicine.

Wen Shan paid no attention to Zhao Xuanyou, only asking Yu Wan, “Where have you been hiding these past few days? I was so afraid you…”

Yu Wan pursed her lips, about to speak, when she caught sight of Tiya out of the corner of her eye.

“I’ve been here the whole time. But you. How did you end up with her?”

---

chapters.title: Exposing Each Other’s Secrets
chapters.content:
“That day, I was originally going to Grey Wolf Lake to find the young master. But halfway there, the sandstorm grew worse, and I started worrying about you, so I decided to turn back and look for you.” Wen Shan briefly recounted what had happened that day.

No wonder he hadn’t been with Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Wan said, “I was also heading to Grey Wolf Lake at the time. How come we didn’t run into each other?”

Wen Shan lowered his head, recalling the scene from that day, still feeling a lingering fear.

“The sandstorm was too fierce. I hadn’t gone far when I lost my sense of direction and couldn’t find my way back to the mountain hollow. My horse was spooked and ran wildly with me on its back.”

“And then you met Tiya?”

Wen Shan hesitated for a moment before nodding, though it seemed the situation wasn’t that simple.

Yu Wan was about to ask more when Tiya rode her horse closer.

Looking at Yu Wan’s purple Indian attire, Tiya smiled and said, “I didn’t expect the young lady to look so beautiful in Indian clothes.”

“It’s because your clothes are beautiful to begin with.”

Yu Wan hadn’t expected to meet her again so soon.

Hearing Tiya’s familiar tone, she felt a little uncomfortable.

But from Wen Shan’s fragmented words, Yu Wan guessed that his ability to return here was likely thanks to Tiya, so she didn’t treat Tiya as an enemy.

“When we return to Yu Prefecture, I’ll definitely prepare a new set of clothes to return to you.”

“It looks better on you than it ever did on me. No need to trouble yourself.”

Tiya spoke sincerely. After doing business in Yu Prefecture for several years, Yu Wan was the most beautiful person she had ever seen.

Before Yu Wan could respond, Zhao Xuanyou called out from behind, “Wan.”

She turned to see Yuan Zhen helping Zhao Xuanyou onto a horse.

Since Zhao Xuanyou’s leg was injured, he couldn’t tie it to the stirrup again, or the new injury would worsen the old one. So someone needed to ride with him; and naturally, that someone was Yu Wan.

Yu Wan knew they should return to Yu Prefecture as soon as possible. She turned back to Tiya. “Will you return to Yu Prefecture with us?”

“I’ve already been spared by you and the young master. How could I go to Yu Prefecture and cause trouble for you two?”

That was true.

This time, Yu Wan’s abduction had been largely thanks to Tiya and her horse, Photnight White.

“Farewell.” Tiya directed this to Wen Shan.

Wen Shan nodded at her, then watched as Tiya rode away. When he turned back, he saw Yu Wan staring intently at him and asked, “Aren’t you leaving?”

“Of course I am.”

Yu Wan averted her gaze and walked over to Zhao Xuanyou, who pulled her onto the horse.

They had ridden together before, but back then, Zhao Xuanyou had been the one controlling the horse. Now, it was the opposite.

Once Yu Wan had a firm grip on the reins, Zhao Xuanyou wrapped his arms around her waist from behind, even resting his head on her shoulder.

He was tall and broad, so leaning on her like this was a little awkward.

“Your men are still here. Aren’t you afraid they’ll laugh at you?”

“Laugh at what? They should be envying me instead.”

Yu Wan knew his face was growing thicker by the day, so she didn’t bother arguing. With a sudden kick to the stirrup, she urged the horse forward, carrying him with her.

The Uwan camp had been deep in the grasslands, and it took their group more than two hours to reach the gates of Yu Prefecture.

It was then that Yu Wan understood why the city had been built here; several miles to the north, there was a mountain that blocked the wind and sand from the west.

The guards, seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s safe return, immediately opened the gates to welcome them.

Back at the Hou Mansion, Yu Wan first called for a physician to examine Zhao Xuanyou.

The hemp rope had caused a flesh wound, but it wasn’t serious. The physician said that with medicine and rest, the fever would break in a couple of days.

While the servants were preparing the medicine, Yuan Qing entered to announce that Shen Jiao, the deputy commander of the Mingli Guards, had come to report on the progress of rooting out spies within the city over the past four days.

This was a matter of great importance, so Zhao Xuanyou ordered Yuan Qing to bring Shen Jiao into the study.

“Wan, you should go back to the Tangli Courtyard to rest. Tonight, I’ll have a banquet prepared in Mingguang Hall. I hope your family will grace us with your presence.”

Thinking of his promise to propose marriage upon his return, Yu Wan softly replied, “Mm,” then added, “Remember to take your medicine,” before leaving with Wen Shan for the Tangli Courtyard.

Before they even entered the courtyard, Ding Wenxi rushed out from the house. Upon confirming Yu Wan was unharmed, she pulled her into a tight embrace.

Seeing Ding Wenxi’s bloodshot eyes, Yu Wan could imagine how worried and sleepless her mother had been these past few days.

Though her own nose stung with emotion, she forced a smile to comfort her. “Don’t worry, Mother. I’m fine. Not a scratch on me.”

Ding Wenxi sighed, then looked at Wen Shan, patting his shoulder. “When you two didn’t return, I kept thinking that if anything happened to you, I wouldn’t want to live either.”

“Mother, don’t talk nonsense. All three of us will live long and happy lives.” Yu Wan linked arms with Ding Wenxi and teased, “Let me tell you a secret, Ah Shan. This time, he didn’t just run into a sandstorm. He also had a stroke of romantic luck!”

At her words, Wen Shan, standing beside her, stiffened slightly.

If not for his mask, his expression would have been priceless.

“Romantic luck?” Ding Wenxi was indeed hooked by those three words. She looked at Wen Shan in surprise. “Which girl?”

“She’s making it up.” Wen Shan said lightly and quickly, his voice sounding unnatural.

Yu Wan didn’t say more, just let out a soft “Hmph.”

Wen Shan, seeing the mischievous smile on Yu Wan’s face, feared she might say more and quickly turned to Ding Wenxi. “Yu Wan spent the last few days with the young master; just the two of them.”

At this, Ding Wenxi naturally turned to Yu Wan.

“You and the young master were alone together this whole time?”

Yu Wan hadn’t expected Wen Shan to counterattack. She explained, “The sandstorm scattered everyone. I was running around when I bumped into him. His leg was injured, and he’s been running a fever ever since.”

“Is the young master’s injury serious?”

“It’s past the worst. The fever is gradually breaking.”

Ding Wenxi wanted to ask Yu Wan about her plans, but seeing that she had just returned, she decided to wait until she had rested properly.

“There are snacks and sweet soup on the table. Go inside and have some. I’ll go to the kitchen to check on dinner.”

“Mother, you don’t need to handle these things yourself.”

“If it weren’t for the fact that you two just came back from the brink of death, I wouldn’t bother with you at all.” Wen Shan loved practicing martial arts, and Yu Wan was always holed up in Zhao Xuanyou’s study. The business of Linglong Pavilion was all managed by Ding Wenxi alone.

She had always loved gold, silver, and jade, so she didn’t mind overseeing Linglong Pavilion.

“Yes, yes, yes.”

Once Ding Wenxi had gone to the kitchen, Yu Wan and Wen Shan entered the house one after the other.

Yu Wan took a sip of tea and picked up a piece of mung bean cake, but instead of eating it, she fixed Wen Shan with a dark look.

Wen Shan took a piece of mixed fruit cake but hadn’t eaten it yet when he met her gaze.

“What?”

Yu Wan gave a cold laugh. “You know exactly what.”

“I don’t.”

“You spent the last three days with Tiya?”

At Yu Wan’s pressing question, Wen Shan helplessly let out an “Mm.”

He actually wasn’t going to answer honestly.

Yu Wan put down the mung bean cake and suddenly reached for Wen Shan’s mask.

chapters.title: The Proposal
chapters.content:
But no matter how fast she moved, she couldn’t outpace Wen Ji’s reaction.

Wen Ji grabbed her hand, spun around, and took several steps back, putting distance between them.

Although Yu Yuan hadn’t removed his mask, she had just been close enough to see that Wen Ji’s ears were bright red.

“Why are your ears red?” Yu Yuan asked with a smile.

“I’m just angry at you,” Wen Ji, cornered by Yu Yuan’s persistence, knew she wouldn’t let it go, so he had to say, “There’s nothing between me and Tiya. We just happened to meet.”

“If that’s really the case, why did she say goodbye to you alone?”

“That day, her hand was broken by my hidden weapon. It was in bad shape, but she asked me to help her. In exchange, she knew of a sheltered cave nearby and took me there. I treated her hand, and we stayed there together for two days.”

Yu Yuan listened to Wen Ji’s words, pondering, then asked, “Did she also lead you all back today?”

“After the sandstorm, the original grassland was completely covered by sand. I couldn’t tell the direction at all. Her horse, Zhaoyebai, is very smart and could lead us back to the original place. On the way, we met Yuan Qing and the others, so we came back together.”

“You really don’t have any feelings for her…” Yu Yuan narrowed her eyes.

“She doesn’t even know what I look like. What could happen? Nothing did, and we won’t see each other again in the future.”

Hearing Wen Ji say this, Yu Yuan understood that he was telling the truth.

Tiya wasn’t just from a different world; she was also Asuhan’s lover. Asuhan had orchestrated such a grand scheme, and Zhao Xuanyou would never let it go easily. Who knew what would happen next?

Even if Tiya wasn’t an enemy, she would never be a friend.

Yu Yuan had originally wanted to tease Wen Ji, but at this point, she gave up.

“No more questions?” Wen Ji glanced at Yu Yuan’s expression and calmly asked, “Can I eat the cakes now?”

Yu Yuan secretly sighed.

No matter what, Wen Ji deserved a woman who truly liked him.

After a moment’s thought, she followed Wen Ji’s lead: “Tiya isn’t a simple woman. It’s for the best if there’s nothing between you. In the future, you’ll definitely find…”

“I’m eating.” Wen Ji interrupted her, clearly not wanting to talk about it anymore.

“Mmm, try the mung bean cake. It’s still warm.”

The two ate a little before each returning to their rooms to bathe and change.

After washing thoroughly from head to toe, Yu Yuan felt like she had come back to life.

In an unprecedented move, Yu Yuan even applied fragrant ointment to her body.

But as she applied it, she felt a flicker of confusion.

She usually couldn’t be bothered to put on makeup, so why was she applying ointment now?

Was it for Zhao Xuanyou?

Yu Yuan’s face suddenly burned. She thought to herself that it wasn’t necessary, but after finishing her body, she also applied hair oil to her hair.

By the time she was dressed and walked out, Ding Wenxi caught a whiff of her fragrance.

“Don’t you usually dislike applying ointment?”

Yu Yuan replied, “Your daughter was trapped for so long. If I don’t smell nice, Mother might not let me get close.”

Ding Wenxi pursed her lips. “Just now, Yingxue said that tonight, both I and Ah Ji are to dine at Mingguang Hall. Do you know what the Young Master has planned?”

“I do.” Yu Yuan smiled slightly, linking arms with Ding Wenxi and leaning against her shoulder.

Seeing the bright smile on Yu Yuan’s face, Ding Wenxi could more or less guess.

“Yuan Yuan, have you thought it through?” In Ding Wenxi’s eyes, both Pei Ta and Zhao Xuanyou were excellent matches.

Whoever Yu Yuan liked, Ding Wenxi wouldn’t find strange.

But after this kidnapping ordeal, Ding Wenxi felt that being with Zhao Xuanyou might be much more dangerous.

“I have.”

Ding Wenxi held her hand, patting the back of it, and whispered, “Then you must promise me that such things will never happen again.”

Yu Yuan blinked. “Then Mother shouldn’t be telling me this. She should tell Zhao Xuanyou. If he can’t do it, then you shouldn’t agree.”

Hearing Yu Yuan naturally call out Zhao Xuanyou’s name, Ding Wenxi’s brows and eyes softened imperceptibly.

What she feared most was that Yu Yuan, intimidated by Zhao Xuanyou’s power, would be forced into marriage. Now that she confirmed Yu Yuan truly wanted to marry him, she was at ease.

Yu Yuan sat in the room, telling Ding Wenxi about what happened when the sandstorm hit. She spoke vividly, but Ding Wenxi listened with alarm.

Unknowingly, night fell. It was time for dinner, but Yingxue came in to say that the Young Master had left the residence on business and wouldn’t be able to join them for dinner. However, he had sent a food box for Yu Yuan.

Yu Yuan assumed he was busy dealing with the spies and didn’t pay much mind.

She was only worried that his fever hadn’t subsided, and going out again might worsen his condition.

Noticing Ding Wenxi’s disappointment in Zhao Xuanyou’s broken promise, Yu Yuan quickly said, “This time I was kidnapped by the Wuhuan prince because he has eyes in the city. If we don’t root out this spy, who knows what other troubles may arise. It’s safer to catch them all in one go.”

Ding Wenxi chided, “He hasn’t even come to propose yet, and you’re already explaining for him like family.”

“I’m just stating the facts, not explaining for him. Fortunately, Mother has prepared dinner for me and Ah Ji. Let’s go to the courtyard to eat. We can even watch the stars while we eat.”

The dishes had already been prepared, and soon a table was set under the begonia tree.

Yu Yuan invited Yingxue to sit with them and opened the food box Zhao Xuanyou had sent. Inside was a large bowl of Sichuan pepper soup, with the words “Zui Xiang Lou” inscribed on the rim of the bowl.

He had remembered what she said when she was trapped.

The other three, seeing Yu Yuan’s lips curl at the sight of the Sichuan pepper soup, tactfully refrained from trying it.

Yu Yuan drank a bowl by herself and found the taste excellent. She even wondered why she had thought it was bad before.

After dinner, the four sat in the courtyard chatting for a while before each retiring to their rooms.

After the harrowing few days, whether they had been trapped in the desert or had stayed in Yuzhou, everyone was exhausted and soon fell asleep.

The next morning, Yu Yuan was still fast asleep when Yingxue shook her awake.

“Yingxue,” Yu Yuan, half-asleep and rubbing her eyes, refused to sit up, “What’s wrong?”

“The Young Master is here.”

“Here? He came to Tangli Courtyard?” Yu Yuan was still groggy.

Unlike Yu Yuan’s tired appearance, Yingxue was beaming. She wiped Yu Yuan’s face with a handkerchief and pulled her up. “Madam is already in the main house. Hurry up, Miss.”

By the time she sat in front of the dressing mirror, Yu Yuan was finally more awake.

After changing clothes, she left the bedroom. As she entered the main house, she was immediately struck by the atmosphere inside.

Ding Wenxi sat in the center of the room, looking solemnly at Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou wore a deep blue brocade robe. Although seated in a wheelchair, his posture was straight, exuding an extraordinary presence.

Behind him stood eight guards, each holding a red lacquered gift box filled with pearls, jade, silk, and various gemstones.

At the door, Yuan Ze and Yuan Qing held a pair of live geese, their wings tied with red silk in an elegant knot.

---

chapters.title: Laying Down the Ground Rules
chapters.content:
Hearing Yu Yuan’s footsteps, Zhao Xuanyou turned his head to look, his cold, imposing eyes softening slightly.

Yu Yuan had come out in a hurry, wearing a floor-length apricot-colored begonia-patterned ruqun, with a powder-purple soft smoke-gauze short top. Her hair, pinned up with a jade hairpin, seemed a bit simple compared to her magnificent attire.

Meeting Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, Yu Yuan smiled at him, then quickly walked to stand behind Ding Wenxi.

Seeing Yu Yuan arrive, Wen Ji stepped aside to make room for her.

Zhao Xuanyou cupped his fists in greeting to Ding Wenxi.

“Madam has been in Yuzhou for a long time, yet I have not come to pay my respects until now. I hope Madam can forgive me.”

Though his expression remained characteristically cold, his tone was respectful and humble.

“Young Master is too polite. I am but a commoner’s wife, unworthy of such a grand gesture from the Young Master,” Ding Wenxi said, looking at Zhao Xuanyou in his wheelchair, understanding his purpose. She asked gently, “May I ask, Young Master, what brings you here so early today?”

This was the first time Ding Wenxi had formally met Zhao Xuanyou face to face.

Facing her prospective son-in-law, Ding Wenxi’s feelings were somewhat complicated.

First, she had been forcibly brought to Yuzhou by Zhao Xuanyou’s men. Although Yuan Qing had been courteous throughout the journey, she knew Zhao Xuanyou had intended to capture her to pressure Yu Yuan.

Second, Zhao Xuanyou was the heir of a marquisate, with a better family background and wealth than Pei Ta. However, he was a military general.

Yuzhou might be peaceful now, but warfare could break out at any time. If Yu Yuan married him, her life might not be stable.

Even if he could protect Yu Yuan, the battlefield was unpredictable. What if he got injured...

But no matter what Ding Wenxi thought, it was useless. Now that Yu Yuan had changed her mind about him, she wouldn’t refuse Zhao Xuanyou even if Ding Wenxi did.

Zhao Xuanyou took a jade ruyi scepter from one of his guards. The jade was lustrous and fine, with the characters “Eternal Unity” engraved at the top.

Zhao Xuanyou presented the jade ruyi to Ding Wenxi with both hands, his gaze burning like stars as he solemnly declared, “I have come today with these geese to ask for Ding Yuan’s hand in marriage.”

However, Ding Wenxi did not reach for the jade ruyi.

Yu Yuan glanced at her mother, not understanding her intentions.

Could it be that her mother wanted to refuse his proposal?

Faced with this unexpected turn, Zhao Xuanyou remained composed, maintaining his respectful demeanor. “If Madam agrees to betroth Ding Yuan to me, I will do everything in my power to ensure she lives a life of happiness and security. I can also promise you here and now that I will never take a concubine.”

At these words, not only Ding Wenxi but also the guards behind Zhao Xuanyou were taken aback.

They all knew that Yu Yuan had once been a concubine in the marquisate and were aware of the Young Master’s feelings for her.

It was already unprecedented for the Young Master to marry a former maid, and now he was even vowing never to take a concubine...

In noble families, having multiple wives and concubines was common. Moreover, with the marquisate’s lineage being so sparse, it was a good time to have more children. Having more women in the household would be beneficial.

But they only dared to grumble in their hearts. The Young Master’s decisions were such that even the Old Madam and the Marquis might not be able to oppose them.

“If Madam does not believe me, I can swear on my life to the heavens.”

“There’s no need.” Ding Wenxi had not originally intended to bring this up. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s sincerity, she also spoke bluntly. “Yuan Yuan was once your maid. Although she now has a new identity, everyone in the marquisate in the capital knows her. You still have elders in the marquisate. You must ensure that they all accept Yuan Yuan as your wife. She cannot follow you to Yuzhou in an ambiguous position.”

“Madam, rest assured. My grandmother and father have long been aware of my feelings for Yuan Yuan and understand that I will marry no one but her. Yesterday, after returning to Yuzhou, I sent a messenger on a fast horse to inform them of my intention to propose.”

Ding Wenxi nodded. “Then we will wait for a reply from the elders of the marquisate before discussing the marriage.”

“Very well.” Zhao Xuanyou readily agreed, then asked, “If Madam has any other concerns, please let me know.”

Ding Wenxi indeed had other concerns. She looked at Zhao Xuanyou, then at the guards behind him.

Zhao Xuanyou understood and waved for them to retreat to the courtyard.

Once only Ding Wenxi’s family and Zhao Xuanyou remained in the room, Ding Wenxi slowly began to speak.

“I know that you and Yuan Yuan have already exchanged your feelings. But she is young and inexperienced, so as her mother, I must lay down some ground rules.”

Zhao Xuanyou respectfully replied, “Please go ahead, Madam.”

“When Yuan Yuan was in the marquisate, because she was a concubine, she was made to take contraceptive medicine. Although she is healthy, no one can say for sure what long-term effects such medicine might have on her body.”

Before Yu Yuan had gone to Anzhou, Ding Wenxi had specifically asked a physician.

After examining her pulse, the physician had said that Yu Yuan’s pulse was normal, but contraceptive medicine was inherently harmful to women. Whether it would affect fertility could only be known after marriage.

“Just now, the Young Master said that after marrying Yuan Yuan, you would not take any concubines. Naturally, I am happy to hear this, but what if Yuan Yuan cannot bear children in the future?”

Zhao Xuanyou was slightly taken aback.

He had indeed not considered this aspect. His gaze flickered as he looked at Yu Yuan with a hint of heartache, then said in a deep voice, “It was because of me that Yuan Yuan took the contraceptive medicine in the first place. If there are any consequences, it is only right that I bear them. Madam, rest assured, no matter what happens, I will never take a concubine.”

“Even if it means the marquisate’s lineage comes to an end?”

“I still have three uncles in the capital, and they have many children and grandchildren. If Yuan Yuan and I truly cannot have children, I will choose a suitable heir from among my nephews to adopt. They are all of my grandfather’s bloodline, so the marquisate’s lineage will not end.”

“Good. I trust the Young Master’s word is as good as gold.” Hearing Zhao Xuanyou’s candid response, Ding Wenxi had no further doubts.

Previously, her impression of Zhao Xuanyou had come only from Yu Yuan’s fragmented words, and she had known little of his character.

After today’s conversation, she viewed Zhao Xuanyou in a new light.

Though he was born into a marquisate and held a noble status, he was nothing like the idle, pleasure-seeking young masters of the capital’s aristocratic families.

Although he was a military general, he spoke with refined manners, his conduct measured, clearly a man of depth and vision.

Such a man was certainly capable of protecting Yu Yuan for a lifetime.

“Then, Madam, are you willing to betroth Yuan Yuan to me?” Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Ding Wenxi’s gaze now held genuine admiration. Hearing his words, she nodded. “Once we receive a reply from the elders of the marquisate, you and Yuan Yuan can set the wedding date.”

“Thank you, Madam.”

As soon as Zhao Xuanyou finished speaking, Yu Yuan, who had been quietly standing beside Ding Wenxi, suddenly spoke up, “Wait.”

At this, the other three people in the room turned to look at her.

“Mother, I have something I want to say to him.”

Ding Wenxi looked at her in surprise. “You’ve... changed your mind again?”

“Wait until I’ve spoken with him, then you’ll know.” With that, Yu Yuan pushed Zhao Xuanyou’s wheelchair toward the inner room, leaving Ding Wenxi and Wen Ji staring at each other in bewilderment.

chapters.title: Two Secrets
chapters.content:
As soon as they entered the inner room, Yu Wan closed the door behind her.

Zhao Xuanyou turned his head to glance at her, frowning slightly, unsure what she intended to do.

Yu Wan sat down at the table, poured herself a cup of water, and after drinking it, tried to pull a chair over to sit beside Zhao Xuanyou. But he grabbed her wrist and pulled her onto his lap.

"Wanwan, you'd better say something I want to hear."

Looking at his tightly knit brows, Yu Wan curled her lips slightly and pressed her hand against his forehead.

"I bet it's something you don't want to hear."

"Then don't say it." Zhao Xuanyou coldly huffed, "Today I'm in a good mood, I only want to hear good news."

"But what my mother said just now made a lot of sense."

"Are you worried about the contraceptive medicine? Wanwan, I told you…"

Yu Wan's gaze flickered, a hint of a smile appearing in her eyes.

"My mother said something very reasonable just now: it's better to lay all the cards on the table. We're getting married soon. If I hide something from you now and you find out later, it might only add to our troubles if you can't accept it."

"What exactly do you want to say?"

Yu Wan's eyes dimmed slightly. After a moment of silence, she softly said, "My parentage."

Her voice was very low, but those four simple words made Zhao Xuanyou's heart skip a beat.

"You mean your father?"

Yu Wan nodded.

Zhao Xuanyou studied her expression, lifted his chin, and asked softly, "Do I know him?"

Talking to him was indeed effortless.

Yu Wan nodded again.

To be honest, Zhao Xuanyou had been curious about Yu Wan's parentage, but he truly hadn't expected that he would know her biological father.

After a moment of silent eye contact, Zhao Xuanyou thought for a while and then said, "You keep saying we should lay all the cards on the table, yet you're hesitating. Could it be that your father has a feud with our Jingyuan Marquis Estate?"

Yu Wan pursed her lips and nodded, then raised her hand to point at her own face.

At this point, there was no need to hide it anymore. It was better to reveal everything at once.

"Looking at this face, who can you think of?"

Cui Yichu?!

Zhao Xuanyou had even considered that Yu Wan might be of imperial blood.

After all, he could see that Ding Wenxi was a great beauty, with elegant manners, and it was possible that she had been favored by the emperor by a stroke of luck.

But Yu Wan was actually Cui Lingyuan's daughter!

The feud between Zhao Xuanyou and the Cui family was not shallow.

In fact, personally, his hatred for the Cui family was even greater than for Asuhan.

"You... you are really Cui Lingyuan's daughter?"

"That's what my mother said." Yu Wan said, placing her hand on Zhao Xuanyou's shoulder, "What do you think? Now that you know I'm Cui Lingyuan's daughter, do you still want to marry me?"

"Marry, of course I will marry you."

Zhao Xuanyou naturally wouldn't change his mind because of this.

It was just ironic that, in the end, Cui Lingyuan turned out to be his father-in-law.

"Wanwan, when did you find out he was your father?"

"Remember how you used to wonder how I could read? Actually, I was also very curious about my mother, so after she woke up, I asked her about it."

Yu Wan was telling the truth. But after Zhao Xuanyou heard it, a greater confusion arose in his heart.

"Then the reason your mother couldn't stay in the capital was because of Cui Lingyuan?"

Yu Wan had long known that Zhao Xuanyou was as sharp as a needle, so she wasn't surprised that he could quickly connect one thing to another.

"Let me finish talking about my parentage first, and then I'll talk about my mother's matter."

Zhao Xuanyou's eyes narrowed slightly as he gently pinched her chin.

"How many secrets are you hiding?"

"Not many secrets, just this one. The other one is my mother's secret." Yu Wan shook his shoulder, "Do you really not mind that I'm Cui Lingyuan's daughter?"

Of course he didn't mind.

At this moment, Zhao Xuanyou was more curious about Yu Wan's parentage.

"You knew that the Xingguo Duke's Estate was your home, yet you went to set fire to it?"

"It was just a firewood shed, it can't be called arson." Because of Cui Yichu, Yu Wan only had hatred for the Xingguo Duke's Estate, "Besides, the Xingguo Duke's Estate is Cui Yichu's home, not mine."

From the time Yu Wan was born until she grew up, she had never seen Cui Lingyuan, nor had she ever been to the Xingguo Duke's Estate. How could that be her home?

That made sense, but Zhao Xuanyou asked, "Have you never thought about acknowledging your ancestry?"

"Given my situation, talking about acknowledging my ancestry is a bit ridiculous. Originally, whether to acknowledge or not wasn't up to me." After finishing, Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou with a smile, "Later, I heard about what you did to the Xingguo Duke's Estate. I was very happy. Thank you."

Toppling the Xingguo Duke's Estate and getting rid of Cui Yichu were both Yu Wan's obsessions in her second life.

In her previous life, the reason Cui Yichu could do whatever he wanted to Yu Wan was because of the power of the Xingguo Duke's Estate.

Zhao Xuanyou not only severely injured Cui Zaizhou but also successfully gathered enough evidence for the Jin Yi Wei to bring down the Xingguo Duke, which thoroughly avenged Yu Wan.

Yu Wan was sitting on his lap, and with every breath, he could smell the faint fragrance from her body.

Zhao Xuanyou's eyes darkened as he lowered his voice, "This is not the attitude to thank someone."

Yu Wan leaned forward and kissed his cheek.

"Not enough."

"Then I'll owe you."

Outside, Ding Wenxi and Wen Tao were still sitting there. Zhao Xuanyou had just left a good impression on his future mother-in-law, so naturally, he wouldn't cause a scene with Yu Wan here.

Because of this, Yu Wan suddenly thought of the people in the capital.

"What about the other people in the Cui family? How are they doing now?"

Zhao Xuanyou hadn't deliberately inquired about the Cui family's news, but when he returned to the capital, he heard the gossip from Ye Moqing.

"They can't compare to the glorious days of the past, but they're not homeless."

"Is it because of the Ningguo Duke's Estate?"

Shen Tongyun was the legitimate eldest granddaughter of the Ningguo Duke. Before her marriage, she was deeply loved. After Cui Zaizhou confessed and died in prison, her natal family must have been heartbroken and would secretly support them.

Zhao Xuanyou lightly hummed in agreement, "The Ningguo Duke's Estate went through a lot of trouble to give them a small house to live in. This was originally because the emperor couldn't bear it, and I think the Seventh Prince also pleaded for them. So, they turned a blind eye. Shen Tongyun gave birth to a son for Cui Zaizhou, and now she lives in that small house with more than a dozen members of the Cui family."

"Miss Tongyun is actually a very good person. It's a pity she met Cui Zaizhou."

The Cui family's embezzlement of tribute pearls and public funds would be exposed sooner or later.

From the beginning, her marriage was inauspicious.

Zhao Xuanyou had no particular friendship with Shen Tongyun, so he naturally had no feelings about it.

He continued, "Do you remember Cui Zaiting?"

"Cui Yichu's second brother?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded, "Now Cui Zaiting is the one supporting the Cui family. He has good literary talent and found a job as a teacher. He also sells some calligraphy and paintings to supplement the family's income."

Cui Zaiting... He was one of the few good people in the Cui family.

After hearing so much from Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Wan suddenly became curious, "What about Cui Lingyuan? How is he doing now?"

---

chapters.title: Wedding for Good Luck
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou said, "After the family was confiscated, Cui Lingyuan went to the Yunshan Temple in the suburbs of the capital to become a monk."

"Became a monk?" Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou in surprise. She didn't believe that Cui Lingyuan would sincerely retreat into Buddhist life. She said helplessly, "He was the main culprit behind the embezzlement of the tribute pearls, but it's the other members of the Cui family who are suffering in the capital while he hides in the temple, living a carefree life. What kind of place is Yunshan Temple to actually accept him?"

"The abbot of Yunshan Temple has known him for many years. I imagine his days in the temple are quite comfortable."

Zhao Xuanyou's feelings towards Cui Lingyuan were complicated.

The feud was deep, but on the other hand, although Cui Lingyuan was dishonest, he was extremely cunning and could be considered a hero in his own right.

Moreover, now that he knew Cui Lingyuan was Yu Wan's biological father, the situation became even more complicated.

"Does Cui Lingyuan know that you are his daughter?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Yu Wan sighed, "When I left the capital, I thought I wouldn't go back, so I left something for him. He should be able to guess."

Zhao Xuanyou also remembered the scene when he went to see Cui Lingyuan after Yu Wan left the capital.

At that time, Cui Lingyuan in prison had a moment of distraction when he heard the name "Yu Wan."

He must have realized then that the maid Yu Wan from the Marquis Estate was his daughter.

Thinking that Yu Wan didn't want to acknowledge Cui Lingyuan as her father, Zhao Xuanyou pondered for a moment and said gently, "If Cui Lingyuan hears the name Ding Wan, will he think of you?"

"Ding is my mother's surname. If we get married and he finds out, he should be able to guess that Ding Wan is me." Hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this, Yu Wan asked, "Aren't we going to live in Yuzhou?"

"You will naturally be in Yuzhou when I am there, but you are the mistress of the Marquis Estate. Sooner or later, you will have to return to the capital. Besides, won't you have to pay respects to your grandmother and father?"

An ugly daughter-in-law will eventually have to meet her parents-in-law. Yu Wan would have to go to the capital sooner or later.

"Are you saying that Cui Lingyuan will come to pester me?"

Zhao Xuanyou said softly, "A man like him, if you were just a maid in the Marquis Estate, he would probably leave you alone for the rest of your life. But once you become my wife, you will have value to him. However, you don't need to worry. As long as you don't want to see him, I won't let him harass you."

Yu Wan looked at the handsome and composed man in front of her, and a smile unconsciously rose to her lips.

Hearing that he had already considered everything, Yu Wan's eyes curved, and she suddenly kissed his cheek.

The kiss came too quickly and was somewhat sudden.

However, Zhao Xuanyou reacted extremely fast. He wrapped his arm around her waist and kissed her back heavily, but his target was not her cheek, but her lips.

"That's enough." Yu Wan refused to let him enjoy it any longer and pushed him away, "We've said all the unpleasant things. Let's go out."

They had been hiding in the room talking for so long that her mother outside must be worried to death.

Sure enough, as soon as they came out of the inner room, Ding Wenxi immediately looked over anxiously.

Zhao Xuanyou took the jade ruyi from the guard's hand and still presented it to Ding Wenxi with both hands.

This time, Ding Wenxi naturally accepted it.

"The things in the courtyard are not betrothal gifts, just for Madame and Wanwan to use," Zhao Xuanyou still said modestly, "When the letter from the Marquis Estate arrives, I will immediately report to Madame."

"Then I will wait for the good news."

"Worldly Son, you still have many matters to attend to. Hurry back to Mingguang Hall."

Hearing Yu Wan's eviction order, Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow.

However, since Asuhan dared to target Yu Wan this time, he would not let it go just like that.

With a leg injury, he couldn't personally lead troops out of the city to pursue them. He had to deploy people to do it, so there were indeed many things to do.

"Madame, I will take my leave first. If there's anything, just send someone to Mingguang Hall to deliver a message."

After speaking, Zhao Xuanyou led the guards out. Seeing Yuan Qian and Yuan Qing struggling with the wild goose in their hands, Yu Wan asked with a smile, "What about the wild goose?"

"We'll keep it for now."

After Zhao Xuanyou left Tangli Courtyard, Ding Wenxi quickly pulled Yu Wan to her side, "You looked so tense earlier. What happened?"

Since only Ding Wenxi and Wen Tao were left in the room, Yu Wan did not hide anything.

"He and the Cui family have a deep feud after all. I still told him about my connection with the Cui family."

"It was indeed something that should be said."

Since Zhao Xuanyou's attitude after coming out of the room clearly showed that he didn't mind, Ding Wenxi did not ask further.

After thinking for a moment, Yu Wan added, "I haven't told him about Mother's matter yet, but he also knows that Mother can't go to the capital. It's fine as long as you live peacefully in Yuzhou in the future."

If he didn't mind her matter, he naturally wouldn't mind Ding Wenxi's matter either.

"I understand. It seems the Worldly Son is eager to get married. I need to prepare your dowry as soon as possible."

"He said he will prepare it."

"Worldly Son will prepare your dowry?" Ding Wenxi asked in surprise.

"I will also oversee it. Mother doesn't need to work so hard."

Ding Wenxi frowned and thought for a moment, "I will still prepare your wedding dress and phoenix crown. I won't interfere with the rest."

"Thank you for your hard work, Mother."

"What hard work? It's my own daughter getting married."

Ding Wenxi still had to rush to the shop to pick some good gemstones to make a phoenix crown for Yu Wan. After giving a few instructions, she left.

Wen Tao, who had been silent all along, came forward and asked, "After you get married, will you go back to the capital with the Worldly Son?"

"I will definitely go back once. You and Mother can wait for me in Yuzhou. He is the guardian of Yuzhou and won't stay in the capital for long. He'll be back in Yuzhou in a month or two."

Like Ding Wenxi, Wen Tao could never return to the capital.

With Old Lady Ye being advanced in age, Zhao Xuanyou should bring her back to the capital to pay respects this year.

Hearing Yu Wan say this, Wen Tao could only nod.

The letter from the Marquis Estate arrived at Mingguang Hall half a month later.

Yu Wan was helping Zhao Xuanyou write official documents when Yuan Qing handed over a letter.

"Master, a letter from the capital, written by the Marquis."

"Father returned to the capital?" Zhao Xuanyou was somewhat surprised and took the letter, quickly tearing open the envelope.

Yuan Qing said, "This subordinate doesn't know the details."

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou's eyes gradually become serious, he silently retreated.

Yu Wan was slightly stunned and put down the brush. After Zhao Xuanyou finished reading the letter, she asked, "What happened in the capital?"

"Father says that Grandmother is not feeling well, so he rushed back to the Marquis Estate to attend to her. He hopes that we can return to the capital to get married as soon as possible to bring good luck to Grandmother."

As Zhao Xuanyou spoke, he handed the letter to Yu Wan.

Yu Wan quickly scanned it and was also startled.

"Is Old Lady Ye's condition that serious?"
