"Visit we will, but you must save the best items for us."

"That goes without saying."

The Marchioness of Anning watched as Yu Ying chatted amically with the other ladies. Casually, Yu Ying mentioned her family's shop, both promoting her business and subtly refuting the rumors.

It was true that she had been a maid when her family was in decline, but her family had indeed been in the merchant business.

When the Marchioness of Anning first heard that Zhao Xuanyou was going to marry a merchant's daughter, she had felt that the girl's status was too low to be a suitable match for him. However, since Old Madam Ye did not object, she, as a relative, could not say much.

Later, when rumors spread that the merchant's daughter identity was false and that Yu Ying was actually a concubine's maid, she had felt that Zhao Xuanyou was being reckless.

When Old Madam Ye had asked her to take Yu Ying to the Prince's mansion the day before, she had been reluctant. But since Old Madam Ye was the aunt of the Anning Marquis, she had ultimately agreed.

After a brief conversation with Yu Ying in the carriage, she had realized that Yu Ying was well-spoken, elegant, and not at all the vulgar and coarse person the rumors had made her out to be, except for her appearance.

Seeing Yu Ying handle herself with ease at the Prince's mansion, the Marchioness of Anning couldn't help but sigh in admiration. Zhao Xuanyou indeed had good taste.

While they were talking in the flower hall, a palace attendant entered and announced, "The Prince and Princess Consort are about to perform the wedding ceremony."

Everyone hurried to the front hall.

Since there were many male guests, Yu Ying did not push her way to the front. She simply stood on her tiptoes to catch a glimpse.

The wedding ceremony at the Prince's mansion was presided over by the Ministry of Rites, and the proceedings were grand and intricate.

After standing on her tiptoes for a while, Yu Ying's toes began to ache.

She quietly stepped back and rubbed her neck.

As she turned her head, she unexpectedly came face to face with someone she never thought she would see.

chapters.title: No Turning Back
chapters.content:
It had been months since they last met, and Pei Tao looked much thinner than before.

His features had always been refined and flawless, but now, with his gauntness, his eyes and brows appeared sharper.

To others, Pei Tao was usually gentle and scholarly, but Yu Wan knew that beneath that exterior, he had a sharp edge.

Like now, the way he looked at her was filled with that sharpness.

"Lord Pei."

Yu Wan truly had not expected to see him here.

Seeing him so thin, she felt a pang of sadness and guilt.

"Do you not want to see me with that expression?"

Yu Wan remained silent.

If it were just an old acquaintance she didn’t wish to see, she would have pretended to be pleased.

But he was Pei Tao. She couldn’t bring herself to give such a perfunctory response.

"Lord Pei, I’m sorry."

These words were something she should have said to him when she left Anzhou.

But back then, she was with Zhao Xuanyou in Badong, recovering from his injuries, and could only send a letter through Wen Gao.

Pei Tao had replied with four words: No need to feel guilty.

Of course, Yu Wan still felt guilty.

Especially now, standing before him, that guilt was even harder to suppress.

A bitter smile flickered across Pei Tao’s refined features.

He knew he shouldn’t have come to see her. He wasn’t here to listen to her apologies.

She was already Zhao Xuanyou’s wife. The best thing he could do for her was to stay out of her life.

Yet, when he had spotted her from afar in the crowd, he couldn’t stop himself from approaching.

He had thought that when she saw him, she might feel a sense of longing, or perhaps some grievance. At the very least, he expected to see some pain in her eyes.

But reality had disappointed him.

Yu Wan was indeed surprised by his appearance, but she remained calm.

Just from meeting her gaze, those eyes filled with guilt, Pei Tao knew she was living well now.

In the half year since she had left Anzhou, Pei Tao had tossed and turned in bed, assuming she must be suffering too. But the truth was, she had already let go when she wrote that letter to break off their engagement.

Pei Tao took a deep breath, forcing down the emotions in his eyes until his expression returned to normal. Then, with a light chuckle, he said, "It’s been so long. There’s no need to dwell on it. I just came over to greet an old friend."

An old friend?

Even as he said it, Yu Wan knew they could never be just old friends.

Her long lashes trembled slightly, but she didn’t know how to respond.

How could she possibly remain friends with Pei Tao?

Not for Zhao Xuanyou’s sake, nor for Pei Tao’s.

"Lord Pei, take care."

Yu Wan curtsied deeply, then turned to find the Lady of Anning Marquis.

She didn’t have the heart to say farewell forever, but Pei Tao was clever enough to understand her meaning.

Though her expression remained calm, her heart was filled with melancholy.

Leaving Anzhou had been out of necessity, but marrying Zhao Xuanyou had been her own choice.

Back when she had been with Pei Tao, her words and actions had been sincere. But some things were simply beyond her control; twists of fate.

Moreover, Yu Wan did not regret marrying Zhao Xuanyou.

After everything she had been through, she was certain of her feelings for him. To her, Zhao Xuanyou had always been different.

It was a little heartless, but it was the truth.

"Did you see the Princess Consort when you went forward? There are too many people, I only caught a glimpse from afar," the Lady of Anning Marquis asked softly.

"I did see her in the palace the other day when we admired the flowers together. The Princess Consort is so beautiful. How could I compare to her?" Yu Wan replied, though her mind was heavy with thoughts.

As she forced herself to engage in conversation with the ladies around her, her peripheral vision caught Sun Qianran sitting in the corner of the flower hall.

Sun Qianran met her gaze with a half-smile.

When had she arrived?

Yu Wan’s heart skipped a beat.

Given Sun Qianran’s obsession with Pei Tao, she must have known he had returned to the capital. And since Pei Tao was on good terms with Zhao Qi, she would have known he would attend the banquet at the Prince’s residence.

Someone so fixated on Pei Tao… she must have seen Yu Wan speaking with him just now.

Yu Wan averted her gaze, only to meet the concerned look of the Lady of Anning Marquis. "Do you have a feud with that woman?"

"We knew each other back when I was still a maidservant."

Back then, their interactions had been decent, but because of Pei Tao, Sun Qianran probably saw her as a mortal enemy.

"No wonder she’s been staring at you since we walked in."

Yu Wan sighed helplessly.

As long as Sun Qianran didn’t cause trouble, she could think whatever she wanted.

"Come, come, let’s go to the bridal chamber and join the fun," Lady Yin said, noticing their hushed conversation. She linked arms with them, eager to see her good friend, the Lady of Complete Blessings, presiding over the bridal customs.

Yu Wan, uncomfortable under Sun Qianran’s gaze, was more than happy to follow them toward the bridal chamber.

At that moment, inside the bridal chamber, Zhao Qi and Liang Miaofeng sat side by side in front of the bridal canopy, surrounded by royal relatives. Prince Ping was busy with court affairs and had not attended, while Princess Yi’an and Yi’ning had their own reasons for staying away. Only Prince Qing and Prince Jing had brought the other relatives to gather around.

Since Yu Wan and her group had arrived late, they missed the Lady of Complete Blessings’ poetry recital and the scattering of the bridal bed. Zhao Qi and Liang Miaofeng were just about to drink the nuptial wine from their joined cups.

Zhao Qi spotted Yu Wan and froze, his cup suspended in midair.

Memories flooded his mind.

At the Lichuan Summer Palace, Yu Wan had accompanied him in his studies and martial arts practice. She had wiped the sweat from his brow when he was drenched, and when he craved sweets, she had made him sweet soups and pastries.

Back then, he hadn’t been sure what he felt for Yu Wan. He only knew she was the best maidservant in the world, and he was happy to have her serve him forever.

But then, on the city tower under the glow of lanterns, Yu Wan had personally told him she did not love Zhao Xuanyou. That news had filled him with such joy he felt he might fly.

Yet, while she had meticulously planned her fake death to escape the capital, she had also left him behind in Yangzhou.

She may have wanted to leave Zhao Xuanyou, but she had never intended to stay with him.

Later, when he heard she was to marry Pei Tao, only for Zhao Xuanyou to ruin the engagement, he thought perhaps he had another chance. But in the few days they spent together in Yu Prefecture, that sliver of hope had been shattered.

"Your Highness."

Liang Miaofeng called to him softly.

Zhao Qi snapped out of his thoughts and looked at the woman before him.

She was dressed in an elaborate, multi-layered wedding gown, one hand holding a painted fan to her face, the other holding a wine cup.

Her fingers were actually quite beautiful, long and fair, but from holding the cup for too long, they trembled slightly.

Zhao Qi’s gaze lingered for a moment.

If the one he couldn’t have today were Yu Wan, what would she do?

With her personality, she probably wouldn’t feel the pain of unrequited love.

She was the kind of person who never looked back.

Zhao Qi took a deep breath, then looked at Liang Miaofeng again. He gave a soft "mm" and, together with her, raised the nuptial cup to his lips and drank it all in one go.

---

chapters.title: A Harmonious Marriage
chapters.content:
After the wedding ceremony, Zhao Qi stood up and cupped his hands in greeting to the relatives who came to offer their congratulations, then led them to the front hall for the banquet.

Once the male guests had all left, Yu Wan finally followed the Lady of Anning Marquis and the others to the dining area for the women.

After lunch, the maids led them back to the flower hall for tea.

The Lady of Anning Marquis and Lady Yin, along with a few others, were old friends who had known each other for years. They sat together, chatting endlessly. Yu Wan sat beside them, listening quietly, occasionally interjecting a few words without having to exert herself in social pleasantries.

As the sun began to set, the female guests gradually started to take their leave.

The Lady of Anning Marquis, still heartbroken over Yao Yao’s condition, did not wish to stay long at the Prince’s residence. She took Yu Wan with her to bid farewell to the hosts.

At this moment, Zhao Qi was surrounded by Prince Jing, Prince Qing, and other imperial relatives, being plied with wine. He was drenched in the scent of alcohol, his eyes slightly red.

As the Lady of Anning Marquis spoke, Zhao Qi’s gaze remained fixed on Yu Wan.

Yu Wan met his gaze calmly. After the Lady of Anning Marquis finished speaking, she curtsied to him and offered her congratulations.

"Thank you, ladies," Zhao Qi said softly, then ordered his attendants to escort them out.

Once Yu Wan and the Lady of Anning Marquis had left, Prince Qing and the others once again surrounded Zhao Qi with wine cups, determined to get the groom drunk.

"Thank you for supporting me today, Lady Anning," Yu Wan said as soon as they were in the carriage.

The Lady of Anning Marquis smiled. "Even if you had attended the banquet alone, anyone who spoke to you would realize your character is nothing like the rumors suggest."

"Still, I should thank you." Changing the subject, Yu Wan asked about the Princess’s residence. "These past few days, both the Marquis and I have been in the palace, so we haven’t been able to visit the Princess and the Prince Consort. How is the young Lady County doing?"

At the mention of her pitiful granddaughter, the Lady of Anning Marquis’s eyes reddened.

"I visit the Princess’s residence every day when I have the time. After taking the imperial physician’s antidote, Yao Yao is no longer as foolish as before. She can speak a little and recognize the Princess and the Prince Consort, but her reactions are still very slow."

"That’s good news if she’s improving. With time, she’ll surely get better and better."

The Lady of Anning Marquis gave a bitter laugh. "The imperial physician said that while the poison is slowly being purged, Yao Yao was poisoned for too long, and her mind may already be damaged. Even if the poison is completely removed, she won’t recover fully."

"How... how unfortunate for the Lady County."

"Isn’t it? Now that Yao Yao is improving, the Princess’s spirits have lifted considerably. That’s why the imperial physician didn’t dare say this in front of the Princess; he only told Mo Han. That child was raised by my own hands, and I’ve never seen him cry so much."

It was all the Empress’s doing. It was a shame she had failed in her rebellion and died, leaving nothing but endless pain for others.

As they spoke, the carriage arrived at the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence. Yu Wan saw the Lady of Anning Marquis off, then returned to the residence to pay her respects to Lady Ye before heading back to her own courtyard, Tangli Yuan.

She lazily reclined on a daybed, sipping sweet soup, her mind drifting to Zhao Qi’s wedding, then to Yao Yao’s condition at the Princess’s residence, and finally to Pei Tao.

Pei Tao’s return to the capital must have been by imperial decree.

Had Sun Qianran done something to make it happen?

Not necessarily.

With the fall of the Jiang clan and Zhao Zun, their influence in both the imperial court and the harem had been purged by the Emperor. Though the two Prime Ministers remained standing, many positions in the court had opened up.

Perhaps the Emperor himself had ordered Pei Tao’s return.

Yu Wan thought this was the most likely explanation. If Sun Qianran truly had the ability to bring Pei Tao back to the capital, she would have done it long ago, rather than waiting until now.

Normally, Pei Tao’s return to office in the capital would have eased some of Yu Wan’s guilt.

But seeing how thin he looked today, she knew that Zhao Xuanyou taking her away had dealt a heavy blow to Pei Tao; one he still hadn’t recovered from.

But what could she do?

Go and comfort him, tell him to forget her, or urge him to find another suitable young lady? None of those things were her place to do.

If she were to speak to Pei Tao again, it would only complicate matters further.

He must have understood her intentions from their meeting today.

Yu Wan took a deep breath, then exhaled heavily, forcing all thoughts of Pei Tao out of her mind.

The Prince of Rui’s residence remained lively until late into the night.

After the last guest had left, an attendant respectfully reminded, "Your Highness, it’s time to enter the bridal chamber."

The bridal chamber?

Zhao Qi had drunk a lot today, and his mind was already blank. Hearing the eunuch’s words, he looked somewhat dazed.

Seeing that he didn’t respond, the eunuchs on either side stepped forward to support him.

The autumn equinox had passed, and the night wind carried a chill.

As the eunuchs helped Zhao Qi outside, the cold wind blew away some of his drunkenness, restoring a bit of his clarity.

"Your Highness, do you wish to go to the bridal chamber?" The eunuch was his confidant and naturally understood Zhao Qi’s feelings about this marriage. Seeing that he had sobered up a little, he quietly asked for his preference.

Zhao Qi thought of the bridal chamber, and of Liang Miaofeng, her face partially hidden behind the bridal fan.

Two days ago, the Emperor had summoned him to the palace. He had praised Liang Miaofeng as an excellent young lady and instructed Zhao Qi to treat his wife well after marriage, to accompany her for life, and to support each other until old age.

The Emperor had said that in his life, he had been with many women, each with her own charms, but in the end, he had been betrayed by the one closest to him.

Zhao Qi respected his father above all else. Seeing how the Emperor had aged overnight, his heart ached.

Both for his father’s decline and for his own disappointment.

Zhao Qi wanted Yu Wan, but Yu Wan had never felt the same for him.

He had knelt before the Emperor and promised not to disappoint his expectations.

"Go to the bridal chamber," Zhao Qi said softly.

The eunuch, seeing his decision, dared not say more. He supported Zhao Qi as they walked toward the bridal chamber.

In the courtyard, besides the Prince’s residence servants, there were also the maids and servants who had accompanied Liang Miaofeng as part of her dowry.

Seeing Zhao Qi, reeking of alcohol, enter the courtyard, they all bowed and stepped aside.

Zhao Qi walked to the corridor, then waved his hand to dismiss the eunuchs. Alone, he pushed open the door and entered.

After stepping around the embroidered golden screen at the entrance, Zhao Qi saw his new bride sitting upright at the edge of the bed.

She was still wearing her heavy bridal attire, and the hand that had been holding the fan trembled slightly, just as it had when they drank the nuptial wine.

Zhao Qi felt a pang of pity. He quickly stepped forward, took the fan from her hand, and set it aside.

The room was silent. Liang Miaofeng placed her hands in her lap, waiting for Zhao Qi to speak.

After a moment of nervousness, she gathered her courage and looked up at him.

Zhao Qi said nothing. He just stood by the bed, looking down at her.

Liang Miaofeng’s nose suddenly felt a sting.

She thought of Princess Yi’an’s words: She was not the Princess Consort Zhao Qi wanted.

"What’s wrong?" Zhao Qi finally spoke.

"I..."

Zhao Qi’s lips twitched slightly, but he didn’t say anything more. Instead, he reached out and removed the heavy phoenix crown from her head.

"Your Highness, we..."

"Go to sleep early."

With that, Zhao Qi removed his outer robe and lay down on the bed.

chapters.title: Longing for a While
chapters.content:
After Yu Wan left the palace, Zhao Xuanyou began to miss the days they spent together in the Western Garden.

Even with Zhao Yi Yun tagging along, being able to have breakfast and dinner with Yu Wan every day, and whispering to each other after intimacy at night was no different from living in the Marquis's mansion.

Now, only Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Ji remained in the Western Garden, sitting in silence, which was truly depressing.

Fortunately, it had been nearly two months since he entered the palace. Jiang's spies in the palace had all been removed, and the case had been transferred to the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review. Zhao Xuanyou then bid farewell to the Emperor.

After all, he was not the commander of the Brocade Guard; staying in the palace was not proper.

After this incident, although the Emperor relied on Zhao Xuanyou even more, the previous urgent matters that required Zhao Xuanyou to lead the Brocade Guard were no longer necessary.

Moreover, the Emperor knew that Zhao Xuanyou had just married and had been busy in the palace for more than two months. Even a man of iron needed rest.

"Xuanyou, you have worked hard these days. You may leave the palace and return home today."

"Serving Your Majesty is my duty. I dare not claim credit."

The Emperor did not say more.

Zhao Xuanyou was already the minister he valued and trusted the most. He would not be stingy with what was due to Zhao Xuanyou; there was no need to say it here.

After waiting for the Emperor's nod, Zhao Xuanyou bowed and retreated.

Leaving the Qianqing Palace, Zhao Xuanyou let out a sigh. Thinking of returning to the mansion, his mood improved greatly.

After taking only a few steps forward, he saw a eunuch leading a young man in official attire quickly approaching the Qianqing Palace.

Coincidentally, it was the person Zhao Xuanyou least wanted to see; Pei Ta.

Pei Ta had received a secret edict to return to the capital twenty days ago. On the second day after returning to the capital, he attended Zhao Qi's wedding and saw Yu Wan, the one he had been longing for.

Unfortunately, for Pei Ta, the meeting was not as good as the memory.

When he hadn't seen her, he could still deceive himself that Yu Wan had no choice. But the moment he saw Yu Wan, he understood that no matter what her feelings were when she left, she had truly married Zhao Xuanyou from the bottom of her heart.

Pei Ta looked up and saw Zhao Xuanyou's tall and noble figure, with profound eyes, staring coldly at him.

They had unexpectedly met in the palace.

"Lord Zhao."

Zhao Xuanyou was a favorite of the Emperor. The eunuch leading Pei Ta, seeing the situation, quickly bowed to him.

Since the eunuch greeted Zhao Xuanyou, Pei Ta had to slow his pace and looked up at Zhao Xuanyou without evasion.

However, Zhao Xuanyou did not stop. He responded with a mere "mm" to the eunuch and quickly walked forward.

The eunuch, who worked in the Qianqing Palace, had interacted with Zhao Xuanyou several times before but had never seen him so cold.

Looking back to see Pei Ta's expression, it was dark and unclear.

Did these two have a feud?

The eunuch suppressed the doubt in his heart and continued leading Pei Ta towards the Qianqing Palace.

Zhao Xuanyou's mood turned extremely sour due to the unexpected encounter with Pei Ta in the palace. It only improved slightly when he thought of Yu Wan waiting for him at the Marquis's mansion.

While waiting for the Marquis's mansion carriage, a carriage bearing the Xiang family's insignia slowly stopped in front of the palace gate.

The curtain was lifted, and Sun Qianran alighted from the carriage, carrying a food box.

The palace's daily food supply for officials was not as luxurious as that of the harem. Although the Prime Minister's ration was much better than that of other officials, Prime Minister Sun was picky. Every day, his family would send food boxes to the palace.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at her, having no intention of greeting her.

From their first meeting at the Lichuan Summer Palace, he had disliked this couple. Although their marriage had long been estranged, Zhao Xuanyou's dislike for these two had only grown stronger.

After Sun Qianran handed the food box to the guard at the gate and gave a red envelope, she turned around and saw the Marquis of Jingyuan's carriage approaching from afar. An idea struck her, and she walked over to Zhao Xuanyou's side.

Zhao Xuanyou's expression was as cold as a snow-capped mountain frozen for millennia, with no intention of acknowledging her.

"Lord Marquis must have already known that Pei Ta has returned to the capital," Sun Qianran said, completely unaffected by Zhao Xuanyou's coldness, and even smiled gently. "After all, the Marchioness and Pei Ta have a deep friendship. They were even at the point of discussing marriage."

Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows suddenly furrowed.

"What does that have to do with you?"

"Of course, it has nothing to do with me. However, on the day of Prince Rui's wedding, when I went to the Prince's mansion as a guest, I happened to see the Marchioness talking to Pei Ta in a corner. It seems that after not seeing each other for a long time, they couldn't help but catch up on old times upon meeting."

Zhao Xuanyou was highly intelligent. Upon hearing this, he naturally understood Sun Qianran's intention to sow discord.

However, his mind still couldn't help but waver.

Had Yu Wan met Pei Ta at the Prince's mansion? What would they talk about?

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou did not retort coldly as before, Sun Qianran knew her words had taken effect and decided to continue.

"The Marchioness must like refined and scholarly men, right? Back at the Lichuan Summer Palace, she practiced calligraphy and read books every day. Whenever she didn't understand something, she would ask Pei Ta. At that time, Pei Ta would praise her for being intelligent and insightful."

At this point, Sun Qianran couldn't help but sigh.

"Please don't laugh at me, Lord Marquis. Back then, when I saw Pei Ta guiding the Marchioness, I even felt a little jealous. But I thought to myself that the Marchioness was, after all, Lord Marquis's maid, and she would definitely know her place. I didn't expect that after the Marchioness regained her freedom, she would continue to live in Qingzhou. It seems they have some fate."

Zhao Xuanyou had been thinking about Yu Wan meeting Pei Ta. Upon hearing Sun Qianran's long speech, he coldly said, "Yu Wan is exceptionally beautiful and intelligent, so naturally, she has many admirers. I just didn't expect Pei Ta to have set his sights on her so early. Truly despicable and shameless."

The Marquis's mansion carriage slowly stopped in front of the palace gate. Yuan Zhan jumped down from the carriage and respectfully approached Zhao Xuanyou.

"If anyone speaks ill of Yu Wan in front of others again, hmph, just try it."

With that, Zhao Xuanyou boarded the carriage and left without a backward glance.

Yuan Zhan glanced at Zhao Xuanyou's terrifyingly dark expression and didn't dare to speak a word during the entire journey.

Upon returning to the Marquis's mansion, Zhao Xuanyou grabbed the gatekeeper.

"Is the Lady at the mansion?"

"Yes."

Zhao Xuanyou let go of the gatekeeper and strode towards the Tangli Courtyard.

After being treated with the best trauma medicine in the palace, Zhao Xuanyou's right leg still couldn't engage in combat, but walking was no longer a problem.

Yuan Zhan followed behind him, his heart pounding. With the Lord's current demeanor, was he going to confront the Lady? What could he do? He couldn't even warn the Lady in advance.

All he saw was Zhao Xuanyou striding quickly to the Tangli Courtyard and suddenly pushing open the courtyard gate.

The autumn sun was pleasant today. Yu Wan had Pan Xia move a bamboo cooling chair to the corridor.

She was eating grapes while flipping through the military books on Zhao Xuanyou's bookshelf.

After assisting Zhao Xuanyou with so many military affairs in Yuzhou, reading military books was no longer as difficult as deciphering heaven's will.

"Lord has returned," Ran Dong, who was sitting in the courtyard picking swallow nest hair, quickly stood up.

Yu Wan also looked towards Zhao Xuanyou, her beautiful eyes blinking as she smiled at him, the corners of her lips curling up.

---

chapters.title: The Vinegar Jar Tips Over
chapters.content:
As it was close to noon and the temperature was still warm, Yu Wan was basking in the sun, so she was dressed lightly. She wore a simple oriole-yellow long skirt with chrysanthemum patterns on the hem, perfect for the autumn scenery. A piece of sheer silk covered her chest, revealing her fair and delicate collarbone when she looked up.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou return, Yu Wan put down the military book and lightly jumped down from the bamboo cooling chair, running into the courtyard to greet him.

Having not seen him for several days, Yu Wan was naturally overjoyed to see him suddenly return.

Seeing him standing at the door without speaking, Yu Wan grabbed his sleeve and asked, "Is the task in the palace done? Or, did you just come back to see me?"

Facing Yu Wan's delighted expression, the anger Zhao Xuanyou had been accumulating since leaving the Qianqing Palace suddenly dissipated.

"The task is done."

After speaking, Zhao Xuanyou reached out and horizontally lifted Yu Wan into his arms, striding towards the house.

Yu Wan had been overjoyed by his return, but suddenly found her feet leaving the ground as he picked her up.

With so many maids in the courtyard, Yu Wan felt a moment of shyness and could only bury her head in his shoulder.

Zhao Xuanyou carried her all the way into the house and set her down on the edge of the couch.

She had thought he would act quickly, but instead, he sat beside her, staring deeply at her, his profound eyes seemingly holding a grudge.

Yu Wan didn't understand and just smiled at him.

"Why this expression?" She reached out to hold his chin, leaning closer to him. "Have you grown accustomed to living in the palace and now find my Tangli Courtyard not spacious or luxurious enough?"

Zhao Xuanyou remained silent.

Having not seen him for many days, Yu Wan truly missed him and didn't dwell on his minor mood.

After all, Zhao Xuanyou had been extremely busy in the palace, working tirelessly for two months. He must be exhausted.

Having finally returned home, there was no reason to pester him with questions.

Yu Wan thought for a moment, then leaned in to give him a light, brief kiss.

His thin lips were as soft and warm as expected.

Assuming he was finally done with his tasks and exhausted, she tilted her head and smiled at him. "I'll have the maids prepare a meal first. After eating, you can rest for a while, and then we can go greet Grandmother and Father."

As soon as she finished speaking, Yu Wan's waist was suddenly gripped by Zhao Xuanyou, and she was pushed onto the couch by him.

Desire surged, disrupting the rhythm.

Outside, the autumn wind blew gently, and the leaves of the crabapple tree in the courtyard rustled.

After a few autumn winds, the slightly yellowed leaves would begin to fall.

Pan Xia stood under the corridor, listening to the sounds from the room, her face reddening as if it would drip blood.

"Autumn Moon Sister, should we still go to the kitchen to order the meal?" Pan Xia turned her head and asked softly.

Pan Xia and Ran Dong were maids brought into the Marquis's mansion by Yu Wan from outside. They were still young and had not been in the mansion for long, so many things required them to seek advice from Chun Xing and Autumn Moon, who worked in the Honghui Hall.

Although Autumn Moon was a bit farther away, she could guess what the master and mistress were doing in the room.

"The kitchen has only prepared the Lady's meal. Since it's not urgent now, Ran Dong, go to the kitchen and have them prepare a few dishes that the Lord likes."

"Yes." Ran Dong responded and left.

Autumn Moon then instructed Chun Xing and Pan Xia to stand in the corridor to wait and listen for orders, while she herself went to the Leshou Hall to report that the Lord had returned and that they would go to pay respects to the Old Lady later.

After this well-organized arrangement, by the time Yu Wan came out after cleaning up, the maids had already set the table with dishes and wine.

There were steamed fish, eight-treasure tofu, and stir-fried pork with lilies that Yu Wan loved, as well as stir-fried lamb and eight-treasure duck that Zhao Xuanyou liked. Additionally, there were several light seasonal vegetables and a mountain delicacy chicken soup.

Normally, upon Zhao Xuanyou's return, Yu Wan would enthusiastically arrange things for him. However, today he had returned in a manner unlike his recent gentle demeanor, being particularly fierce in their intimate moments.

He seemed somewhat like the way he was before they had grown close; greedily taking what he wanted without a word.

Zhao Xuanyou served Yu Wan a bowl of her favorite chicken soup and placed it in front of her.

Seeing Yu Wan's eyebrows slightly furrow, he asked, "Did I hurt you?"

It didn't hurt, but his earlier reckless actions had completely ignored her words, which made Yu Wan feel a bit uncomfortable.

"I was going to ask you that," Yu Wan said, not drinking the chicken soup he had served. Instead, she looked up at him. "Earlier, when you returned, you had a black face, as if someone owed you money. Then, you entered the room without saying a word. I already told you, I didn't want it from behind today..."

Her words came to an abrupt halt.

There were still two maids standing around, both unmarried. Yu Wan didn't want to speak too explicitly.

"Yu Wan, let's eat first so the food doesn't get cold."

Zhao Xuanyou gave a dry cough.

Seeing the master and mistress talking about such things, Chun Xing quickly exchanged a glance with Pan Xia, and the two silently retreated.

Once only the couple remained in the room, Zhao Xuanyou pulled up a chair and sat next to Yu Wan. He wrapped an arm around her waist and whispered coaxingly, "Yu Wan, I didn't hear you earlier."

"Really didn't hear, or pretended not to hear?" Yu Wan was not so easily fooled.

Zhao Xuanyou had indeed heard, but he hadn't taken it to heart at the time.

He had been thinking about Sun Qianran's provocation and the fact that when he couldn't find Yu Wan before, she had been with Pei Ta.

At the palace gate, he had put on a tough front with Sun Qianran, saying that many people admired Yu Wan and Pei Ta was just one of them.

But Zhao Xuanyou knew in his heart that Pei Ta was different from the others.

Zhao Qi also liked Yu Wan, but he could feel no jealousy towards Zhao Qi because he knew Yu Wan had never liked Zhao Qi.

"So simple a question requires so much thought?"

Zhao Xuanyou snapped out of his reverie and hardened his head. "Pretended not to hear."

"Hmph." Yu Wan gave a cold laugh and turned her face to look at him askance.

She knew this was his favorite way, and she wasn't unwilling to comply.

However, every time he did this, he would charge in recklessly, exerting all his strength on her. After such exertion, she felt as if her bones were falling apart.

Yu Wan wanted to wait until evening for such activities. After all, she could just curl up in his arms afterward and sleep, and by the next morning, she would be mostly rested.

But he had to cause a commotion at noon, leaving her without even the strength to hold chopsticks. All she wanted to do was lie on the couch and not move.

"I've been away for so long. Forgive me this once. It won't happen again."

Seeing him lower his head to beg for forgiveness, Yu Wan had no intention of endlessly blaming him. After all, she had enjoyed it too.

"I said evening. Now I don't even have the strength to hold a bowl of soup."

Her soft words and aggrieved tone made it difficult for Zhao Xuanyou to resist. He regretted his actions even more.

He knew Sun Qianran was trying to sow discord between them, but he had still fallen for it. He had returned with a dark face, and upon hearing Yu Wan speak, he had deliberately ignored her, wanting to see her weak and begging for mercy.

He picked up the chicken soup and scooped a spoonful to her lips.

"You don't have the strength to eat. Let me feed you."

A hint of mockery appeared in Yu Wan's eyes as she lightly opened her mouth, allowing him to feed her.

After finishing half a bowl of chicken soup, Zhao Xuanyou served her food and added rice to her bowl, taking care of Yu Wan's meal properly before picking up his own chopsticks.

"You should eat quickly too. The stir-fried lamb will be gamey if it gets cold," Yu Wan said softly again.

"I'm not that particular."

Zhao Xuanyou had returned at mealtime and, after spending much of his energy with Yu Wan, was already quite hungry.

He picked up his bowl and poured an entire plate of stir-fried lamb onto his rice, devouring it all in a whirlwind.

Yu Wan found it amusing. Where in the capital were there nobles who ate like him?

Seeing that he had eaten most of his meal, Yu Wan took a napkin to wipe his mouth.

Glancing at her gentle demeanor, Zhao Xuanyou hesitated for a moment before finally speaking the words that had been weighing on his mind.

"I encountered Pei Ta in the palace today."

chapters.title: The Stinking Man
chapters.content:
Was it because of Pei Tao?

Meeting Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze, Yu Wan felt a mix of helplessness and annoyance.

So, earlier when he had been like a wild beast, it was because he had run into Pei Tao?

Yu Wan withdrew her handkerchief and casually placed it on the table, letting out an "oh."

Zhao Xuanyou stared at her intently, hoping she would mention having seen Pei Tao at the Prince Rui’s residence and tell him that she had never spoken to Pei Tao at all.

But Yu Wan didn’t continue.

"You’re not surprised?" Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but add another sentence.

Yu Wan looked at him with a smile that wasn’t quite a smile.

It wasn’t strange that he would be jealous, but he was clearly testing her.

What was he trying to do?

"Indeed, I’m not surprised. After all, Pei Tao and I often exchange letters to share updates. When he returned to the capital, I even hosted a welcome banquet for him."

Exchange letters?

Zhao Xuanyou’s mind buzzed. Facing Yu Wan’s angry gaze, even a fool would realize she was upset.

"Wanwan, don’t say such things in anger."

"You want to hear the truth? Fine. I still have lingering feelings for Pei Tao. I’ve always…"

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flickered. He pulled Yu Wan into his arms and covered her mouth, preventing her from saying more.

Seeing that he wouldn’t let go, Yu Wan opened her mouth and bit him hard.

She was truly angry. The bite was so fierce that even with Zhao Xuanyou’s calloused hands, deep teeth marks were left.

Zhao Xuanyou endured the pain, deeply regretting his loose tongue.

But a sour voice in his heart kept asking, why hadn’t she mentioned running into Pei Tao at Prince Rui’s residence?

He didn’t dare to ask further. All he could do was softly say, "I was wrong. Don’t be angry."

Zhao Xuanyou loosened his grip on her mouth.

Only then did Yu Wan release her bite, angrily saying, "The moment I mention his name, you fly into a rage. Why do you keep asking me about it then? Shouldn’t I be the one who’s angry?"

Zhao Xuanyou, remembering the lesson from just now, didn’t dare to speak again.

"You insist on hearing me talk about him all the time. Only then would you be satisfied, only then would you be happy." By the end, Yu Wan’s voice grew more aggrieved. "If I still liked him, I wouldn’t have agreed to marry you in the first place."

"I know, I know," Zhao Xuanyou hurriedly pulled Yu Wan into his arms. "Today I was momentarily possessed. I said the wrong thing. Wanwan, don’t be angry."

Yu Wan pushed away his arms and struggled out of his embrace, standing up beside him.

Zhao Xuanyou also stood up and crowded next to her, leaning down to kiss her.

"Get away."

Yu Wan slapped him away with one hand and took another step back.

"Since you’ve eaten your fill, don’t stay here. Go quickly and pay your respects to the old madam and father."

Thinking of how this man had been so fierce and ruthless with her on the couch just because he had seen Pei Tao, Yu Wan was extremely annoyed.

Just seeing Pei Tao once made him so angry. At the end of the day, he still didn’t trust her.

"You come with me."

"Go by yourself." Yu Wan didn’t want to see him right now.

Zhao Xuanyou had no choice but to resort to shamelessness.

"Grandmother and father hope that the whole family can be together and harmonious. If we go together, they’ll be happy."

Yu Wan knew he was deliberately using their elders to pressure her, but she also knew he was telling the truth.

She swung her fist at his chest and cursed, "You stinking man! I shouldn’t have married you!"

Zhao Xuanyou’s brows twitched. With a thick skin, he said, "I smell pretty good right now."

The incense burner in the room was already emitting a sweet fragrance, and Zhao Xuanyou’s usual clothes were scented with cold incense by the maids at Yu Wan’s request. Indeed, he smelled very good.

Seeing that Yu Wan didn’t say any more angry words, Zhao Xuanyou breathed a sigh of relief and took her hand to walk out.

The couple first went to Leshou Hall to pay their respects to the old matriarch, then went to see the old Marquis.

Zhao Xuanyou had been entrusted with a critical mission to enter the palace and take charge, which was not something the old Marquis was happy about. However, the Empress and the Crown Prince had already fallen, and although the Emperor’s body was injured, his life was not in danger. The court had not fallen into chaos.

"Someone in the court has submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of Prince Ping as the Crown Prince. What do you think?" After dismissing the surrounding servants, the old Marquis asked.

"Currently, Concubine Li is in charge of the harem, and Prince Ping, along with two prime ministers, are managing the front court. They have all the advantages. Requesting to establish him as the Crown Prince is just a way to curry favor with him early on."

"Whether it’s an advantage or not depends entirely on the Emperor’s health."

The old Marquis spoke bluntly. Not only Zhao Xuanyou, but Yu Wan also understood.

If the Emperor’s body couldn’t hold on for a few more years, then to ensure a smooth transition of power and the empire, the Emperor would pass the throne to the older Prince Ping.

If the Emperor still had a long life ahead, and the other three princes had all matured, the Emperor would certainly choose the best candidate from among them, and that candidate might not be Prince Ping.

"Father, rest assured. I will act cautiously and won’t easily take sides."

Zhao Xuanyou knew his father was reminding him not to get too close to Prince Ping, so he immediately reassured the old Marquis.

"The situation in the court is always changing rapidly. Until the very last moment, no one knows who the winner will be. For a family like ours, there’s no need to take sides early. Preserving ourselves by staying wise and cautious is the best strategy. You must both be careful when you’re out. Remember, more words lead to more mistakes."

Others were vying to submit memorials to stop the establishment of Prince Ping as the Crown Prince for the sake of power and profit.

The Jingyuan Marquis’s family already had a hereditary title that would never be revoked. They didn’t need to be so aggressive. As long as they didn’t make mistakes, they could maintain their generational honor.

"We understand, Father."

Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou responded.

The old Marquis nodded slightly and let them leave first.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t have to go to the palace for duty, so he suddenly found himself with free time. He had originally wanted to take Yu Wan to stay at the plum garden outside the city for a few days, but Yu Wan was still angry and said she had to busy herself with the opening of Linglong Fang.

Yu Wan was leaving early and returning late, busy with her business, leaving Zhao Xuanyou idle at home.

But at the root of it all, it was because he had fallen for Sun Qianran’s provocation, returned home, and upset Yu Wan. He had to bear the consequences himself.

A few days later, the Marquis’s residence received an invitation to the 60th birthday celebration of Premier Xu.

Premier Xu was not as infamous as Premier Sun. He was highly respected, with students all over the court. For his birthday, Zhao Xuanyou naturally had to go and offer his congratulations.

Since Yu Wan was busy with the shop and couldn’t spare the time, he had to go alone with the invitation card.

Autumn was deepening, and the weather was getting colder day by day.

Zhao Xuanyou rode his horse to the front of the Premier’s residence, handed his cloak to the doorman, and walked into the residence.

As he was a favorite of the Emperor, the servants of the Premier’s residence were naturally very enthusiastic, pointing out the various arrangements of the residence as they led him through.

After passing through a corridor filled with calligraphy and paintings, the servant respectfully said, "These calligraphy and paintings were all created by court officials and Premier Xu’s students for his 60th birthday. Each one is a masterpiece."

Zhao Xuanyou was in no hurry to go to the front to exchange greetings with others. He stopped and began to appreciate these calligraphy and paintings.

There were various forms of the character for longevity (寿), paintings of the South Pole Immortal holding a peach of longevity, and some congratulatory poems.

As Zhao Xuanyou looked, he stopped in front of a handwritten copy of The Memorial Before the Expedition (Out of the Army Table).

The calligraphy was extremely well done, with strong and slender strokes, and a lively style.

But Zhao Xuanyou stood here not because the calligraphy was good. He just felt that the horizontal, vertical, hook, and flick strokes of the writer seemed somewhat similar to Yu Wan’s handwriting.

He subconsciously lowered his head to look at the signature.

chapters.title: Strong Medicine to Cure Him
chapters.content:
At the end of the handwritten copy, there was a line of small characters: "Written by Pei Miaozhi in the summer of the Jia-Shen year at the Chenmu Study."

Pei Tao, styled Miaozhi.

Was this Pei Tao’s handwriting?

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart beat violently, almost leaping out of his chest.

"Do you like this piece of calligraphy, Lord Zhao?" The young servant leading the way saw Zhao Xuanyou standing still in front of The Memorial Before the Expedition and enthusiastically approached. "This is the handwriting of Lord Pei Tao. Although he is skilled in both calligraphy and painting, he rarely allows his works to circulate. It is because of our Premier’s high prestige that he sent this copy of The Memorial Before the Expedition as a birthday gift."

Although Pei Tao was famous for his talent, Zhao Xuanyou had never seen his calligraphy or paintings before.

The two served in the same court, one as a civil official and the other as a military general, with no official business between them. When they met by chance at the Lichuan Summer Palace, Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t paid attention to Pei Tao’s handwriting.

He hadn’t expected Yu Wan’s handwriting to be somewhat similar to his brushstrokes.

Since when had this been the case?

Had she been practicing his calligraphy since she started learning to write?

"Lord Zhao, shall we go and offer our congratulations to the Premier first, then come back to appreciate the calligraphy and paintings at leisure?"

"Is Pei Tao here?"

The servant thought he had developed an appreciation for Pei Tao after seeing The Memorial Before the Expedition, so he eagerly said, "Lord Pei sent someone to the Premier’s residence a few days ago to deliver the gift in advance. He said he had received an imperial decree to go out of town on official business and is not in the capital."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded a few times and followed the servant forward. After forcing himself to walk a few steps, he suddenly felt a bit lightheaded. He made an excuse and turned around, hastily leaving the Premier’s residence.

His heart was filled with mixed emotions.

He knew that Yu Wan was not the type to drag things out. After marrying him, she would wholeheartedly be his wife and have nothing to do with Pei Tao.

That day, after being provoked by Sun Qianran, he couldn’t help but reveal his emotions when he returned home. Yu Wan’s angry and aggrieved reaction proved that she had long let go of Pei Tao.

But one of Sun Qianran’s words had always been like a thorn firmly embedded in Zhao Xuanyou’s heart. It didn’t hurt, but he couldn’t pull it out no matter what.

Sun Qianran said, "Madame Hou must really like refined scholars like Pei Tao, right?"

No matter how much Zhao Xuanyou despised Pei Tao, he had to admit that Pei Tao was elegant and talented, with unparalleled admiration and scholarship. He was a paragon of virtue and fame in the capital.

Of course, Zhao Xuanyou didn’t think he was inferior to Pei Tao.

It was just that he was a military general, accustomed to taking lives and deciding fates. In the eyes of others, he was ultimately a ruthless man, lacking Pei Tao’s refined and scholarly charm.

Yu Wan’s connection with him had always been circumstantial.

Initially, it was Cui Yichu who had drugged her and forced her into his bed.

Yu Wan had lost her virginity to him, and to survive, she had to tie herself tightly to him, this big tree.

He had developed feelings for her over time due to her warmth, but at that time, she could have chosen to leave him, especially after meeting Pei Tao and deciding to marry him.

If he hadn’t captured Ding Wenxi to blackmail her, she would already be Pei Tao’s wife.

Zhao Xuanyou had originally disdained such a baseless assumption, but because of today’s calligraphy, his heart had been provoked again by Sun Qianran’s words.

At the Lichuan Summer Palace, Yu Wan had no feelings for Pei Tao. Even so, she had practiced his calligraphy, presumably because she genuinely appreciated it.

Zhao Xuanyou really wanted to know: if Yu Wan had been born into the Xingguo Duke’s family, without a seriously ill mother, without any threats, between him and Pei Tao, whom would she choose?

A ruthless military general with blood on his hands, or a refined and elegant scholar...

This was originally a trivial matter, but suddenly it had become an obsession.

Zhao Xuanyou wandered aimlessly through the streets until someone blocked his path, bringing him slightly back to his senses.

"Brother-in-law, what’s wrong with you?"

It was Wen Bo.

The address "brother-in-law" made Zhao Xuanyou a little more clear-headed. He looked up at Wen Bo. "Where’s Wanwan?"

"She’s at the shop."

These days, everyone had been busy with the opening of Linglong Fang. Yu Wan had said she would treat everyone to food, and since Wen Bo was quick on his feet, she had sent him out to buy some.

"Just her alone?" Zhao Xuanyou frowned.

"Yuan Qing and a few guards from the residence are there. I’m about to go back too. It should be fine. Are you... not feeling well?"

Just now, Wen Bo had been carrying a greaseproof paper package on the street when he saw Zhao Xuanyou in a daze, almost getting hit by a speeding carriage without noticing. That was why he had come over to ask.

"I’m fine."

"Brother-in-law, I bought a lot of snacks. If you want, you can come with me to Linglong Fang to take a look. Later, we can take Yu Wan home directly."

Wen Bo felt that Zhao Xuanyou was acting strangely and thought it wasn’t good to let him wander the streets alone, so he invited him to come along.

"Alright."

Zhao Xuanyou was feeling very troubled.

In the past, at times like this, he would go to Ye Mo Han, pour out his heart, and get drunk until he passed out.

But now, with such a big incident at the Princess’s residence, Ye Mo Han was exhausted both mentally and physically. His own troubles were not worth mentioning.

Zhao Xuanyou followed Wen Bo forward. Before long, they arrived in front of a shop right on the street.

The shop’s signboard was already hung above the door, though the red silk cloth covering it had not yet been removed.

The characters on the signboard were written by Zhao Xuanyou at Yu Wan’s request. At the time, she had praised him so much that he had been quite pleased with himself.

Now, thinking about it, she had praised his signboard, but her own handwriting was practiced from Pei Tao’s. What was this about?

"Husband?"

Yu Wan was in the shop testing the first batch of rouge made by the Chen Da Niu couple. Looking up and seeing Wen Bo and Zhao Xuanyou entering one after the other, she looked at him joyfully.

"Aren’t you supposed to be at the Premier’s residence offering birthday congratulations?"

"I did. I just didn’t feel like staying there."

After all, they were husband and wife. Yu Wan could tell from his expression that something was wrong. Without saying much, she had someone lead Zhao Xuanyou to the back courtyard to rest, saying she still had things to finish and would join him later.

Back in the shop, Yu Wan continued inspecting the rouge and glanced at Wen Bo.

After distributing the snacks to everyone, Wen Bo sat down next to Yu Wan.

"How did you end up with him?" Yu Wan asked.

"I saw him on the street. He was so distracted that he almost got hit by a carriage and didn’t even react. I was afraid he might get into an accident, so I brought him here." Wen Bo finished and then whispered, "Did you two have a fight?"

Yu Wan shook her head.

Ever since they had been trapped in the desert and confirmed their feelings for each other, they had never had a fight.

But Yu Wan knew something was wrong with him lately.

He often hesitated when speaking and frequently stole glances at her when at home.

What’s more, during their intimate moments, he would repeatedly urge her at critical moments to say that she cared about him the most and only him.

Once or twice would have been fine, but every time was like this. Even if Yu Wan was dense, she could sense there was a problem.

At the root of it all was what happened after he mentioned running into Pei Tao in the palace that day.

Yu Wan had originally thought that after his jealous outburst and subsequent apologies, the matter was over. But it seemed Zhao Xuanyou had never really let it go.

A heartache required a heart’s medicine. No, Zhao Xuanyou’s illness required strong medicine to cure.

With that thought, Yu Wan picked up the teapot and walked straight up to Zhao Xuanyou.

chapters.title: Making Things Worse
chapters.content:
"Why are you at the shop at this hour? The Prime Minister's residence hasn't even started the banquet yet."

Yu Wan had poured the tea, and when she saw him reach for it, she lifted her hand and drank it herself.

Zhao Xuanyou knew his sudden appearance was a bit abrupt. He understood that his true feelings were too embarrassing to voice, so he vaguely said, "I just came to offer birthday congratulations to the Prime Minister. As long as the courtesy is shown, there's no need to say much to others."

Fearful that Yu Wan wouldn't believe him, he added, "I was thinking of going to the Princess's residence to see Ye Mo Yuan, but I met Ah Bo on the way, so I came here first."

Yu Wan responded with an "Oh," and slowly sipped her tea.

Zhao Xuanyou picked up the teapot, about to pour himself some tea, when Yu Wan suddenly spoke, "I thought you had run into Pei Tao at the Prime Minister's residence."

"He didn't go," Zhao Xuanyou blurted out, immediately realizing his mistake.

If he had said he didn't know, it would have been fine, but saying "he didn't go" made it seem like he cared too much.

Yu Wan naturally picked up on this.

She let out a soft scoff in her heart, looking at the man sitting beside her, and smiled brightly as she asked, "Husband, is there nothing you want to tell me?"

"Tell you what?" Zhao Xuanyou feigned casualness in his reply. Fearful of her further questioning, he added, "Once you're done with your work, let's go home together."

Yu Wan had originally intended to have an open and honest conversation with him again, but seeing him play dumb, she didn't want to indulge him or humor him any longer.

After all, the anxious one wasn't her. If he wanted to keep things bottled up, so be it. Let him hold it in until he couldn't anymore.

"I have plenty of things to do at the shop, and I've already made plans with Da Niu and Xiu Fang to have dinner at Mingyue Tower tonight. I won't be back until dark."

"You're always leaving early and coming back late. You should at least make time to talk to Grandmother."

Zhao Xuanyou, at a loss for words, could only bring up Old Lady Ye.

"You're right. Tomorrow I'll go to Leshou Hall to have breakfast with Grandmother."

With that, Yu Wan stood up and went into the shop.

Zhao Xuanyou sat alone in the courtyard for a while, a belly full of grievances with nowhere to vent.

"Brother-in-law, it's lunchtime at the shop. Do you want to join us?"

By noon, Wen Bo walked up to him and asked.

Zhao Xuanyou looked up and saw Yu Wan sitting lively at the dining table with the others from the shop, feeling even more stifled.

"Let's go out to eat? My treat."

Wen Bo usually didn't stay too far from Yu Wan, but after spending so much time with Zhao Xuanyou in the palace, though they couldn't be considered close friends, their relationship had improved significantly.

He could see that Zhao Xuanyou was in a bad mood today. After some thought, he still nodded.

After informing Yu Wan at the dining table, Wen Bo followed Zhao Xuanyou out.

The two walked in silence, casually finding a restaurant. After sitting down, before the food arrived, Zhao Xuanyou drank several cups by himself.

Once the dishes were served, Wen Bo ate for a while. Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou still hadn't touched his chopsticks, he hesitated before speaking, "Are you angry with Yu Wan because Director Pei returned to the capital?"

"I'm not angry with her."

Zhao Xuanyou indeed wasn't angry with Yu Wan, and it wasn't because Pei Tao had returned to the capital that he was upset.

At the root of it all, he felt that he didn't hold enough weight in Yu Wan's heart.

Wen Bo didn't know what to say.

After all, Zhao Xuanyou's petty thoughts were something even Yu Wan could only guess at, let alone Wen Bo.

Thinking it was related to Pei Tao, Wen Bo said, "Back when Yu Wan was doing business in Qingsha Town, she really didn't have any prior contact with Director Pei. Usually, I was the one running around outside, and Yu Wan rarely even left the house, let alone had any dealings with Director Pei. It was only when the Brocade Guards came to handle a case that we met Director Pei."

"Mmm."

Yu Wan had already told Zhao Xuanyou about these things long ago.

Sensing Wen Bo's intention to comfort him, Zhao Xuanyou bitterly smiled, "It's unrelated."

Unrelated?

Wen Bo responded with an "Oh," racking his brain for a while before admitting to himself that he was powerless to console Zhao Xuanyou. He picked up his chopsticks again.

Once Wen Bo had eaten most of his meal, Zhao Xuanyou remembered that Yu Wan would often sit on the roof with Wen Bo to talk. He asked, "When you were in Qingsha Town, did she ever mention me?"

"No."

Wen Bo answered without hesitation, catching Zhao Xuanyou off guard.

Seeing his choked expression, Wen Bo realized he had added fuel to the fire and quickly added, "She never mentioned Director Pei either."

This did little to comfort Zhao Xuanyou.

He didn't want to be on the same level as Pei Tao.

In Yu Wan's heart, he should be unique, more important than anyone else at any time.

"Back then, Yu Wan did reject Director Pei." Wen Bo carefully watched Zhao Xuanyou, thinking this should comfort him.

Sure enough, Zhao Xuanyou's eyes flickered, "That surnamed Pei was pestering her relentlessly?"

Yu Wan hadn't hidden her past with Pei Tao from Zhao Xuanyou, but she hadn't gone into detail about it either. Zhao Xuanyou found this new information interesting.

Could it be considered pestering?

"Not really pestering, because the next day..." Wen Bo clearly saw Zhao Xuanyou's face darken further. Realizing he was making things worse, he quickly stood up, "Brother-in-law, I should go back to the shop to help."

He wanted to help Yu Wan convince Zhao Xuanyou, but he truly didn't have the ability. It was better to just keep quiet.

Wen Bo slipped out the window, and Zhao Xuanyou, unable to stop him, sat alone in the restaurant drinking his sorrows away. He forcefully dispersed his thoughts before returning to the Marquis's residence. By the time Yu Wan returned home in the evening, he had already returned to normal.

Seeing that Yu Wan looked a bit fatigued, Zhao Xuanyou pulled her into his embrace, removing her hairpin and loosening her hairstyle.

Yu Wan allowed him to help her remove her makeup and change clothes. Once the couple sat down by the bed, she finally spoke, "Is there nothing you want to ask me?"

Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows twitched, "Are you tired?"

Seeing him play dumb again, a hint of grievance instantly appeared in Yu Wan's eyes.

This man clearly had a thorn in his heart, yet he refused to say anything.

He wanted her to coax him, wanted her to guess.

"I'm tired." Yu Wan said, raising her hand to push Zhao Xuanyou off the bed, "I want to sleep alone these days. You move back to Honghui Hall."

Zhao Xuanyou hadn't expected Yu Wan to say this and quickly clung to her side again.

"If you won't go to Honghui Hall, then I will move there."

Zhao Xuanyou could hear the seriousness in Yu Wan's tone. Meeting her clear gaze, he felt momentarily at a loss.

Yu Wan widened her eyes, "Zhao Xuanyou, I'm asking you one last time. What exactly happened when you returned from the palace that day? Why are you hiding it from me?"

He wasn't unaware of Yu Wan's past with Pei Tao. If it were really as simple as meeting Pei Tao in the palace, how could he have been acting so strangely these past few days?

Zhao Xuanyou's eyebrows knitted tightly. The events of that day were truly difficult for him to put into words.

"So you've been hiding a secret in your heart, not considering me your pillow partner."

"It's not that." Seeing Yu Wan's harsh words escalate, Zhao Xuanyou could tell that continuing to hide the truth would only make things worse. "That day, when I was in the palace and encountered Pei Tao, we really didn't say anything to each other."

Yu Wan remained silent, waiting for him to continue.

"But when I left the palace, I ran into Sun Qianran. She said she saw you and Pei Tao reminiscing at Prince Rui's residence."

Yu Wan's expression showed a hint of surprise as she looked at him in astonishment.

She had originally thought Zhao Xuanyou was being jealous and planned to have a good talk with him tonight. Who would have thought it was due to someone else's instigation?

---

chapters.title: Hoist with One's Own Petard
chapters.content:
"So you believed her and thought I was having an affair?"

"No!" Zhao Xuanyou quickly denied, "I never thought that!"

Yu Wan turned her face away at these words.

"She said that Pei Tao had admired you since the time at the Lichuan Summer Palace. I remembered how you used to study with Pei Tao back then. If you hadn't been a maid in the Marquis's residence, perhaps you would have liked Pei Tao first." At this point, Zhao Xuanyou bitterly smiled, "Today, I saw Pei Tao's handwritten letter at the Prime Minister's residence and only then realized that you have been copying his calligraphy all along."

"Stop talking."

Yu Wan felt a tightness in her chest.

It didn't surprise her at all that Sun Qianran would sow discord between her and Zhao Xuanyou.

There were plenty of people in the capital who gossiped about her, a mere concubine. Sun Qianran was just one of them.

What she cared about was always Zhao Xuanyou's attitude.

If he was jealous because she met Pei Tao, Yu Wan could console and coax him. If he minded that she copied Pei Tao's calligraphy, she could explain it to him.

But he had been influenced by an outsider's instigation, which truly angered Yu Wan.

There were so many people outside talking about her. If he listened to Sun Qianran today and made a fuss, what about tomorrow when he heard from someone else?

The more Yu Wan thought about it, the more upset she became.

She stood up, intending to leave, but Zhao Xuanyou reached out and grabbed her arm, "Wanwan, where are you going?"

"I want to be alone. I'm sleeping in Honghui Hall tonight."

Zhao Xuanyou's expression froze for a moment. He could hear the chill in Yu Wan's tone.

He knew he had touched a sore spot with Yu Wan, and saying more might only make her angrier. So he chose to back down.

"You stay here. I'll go to Honghui Hall."

Yu Wan pulled her hand back and sat down by the bed again. Before Zhao Xuanyou could say anything else, she coldly stated, "Goodbye, don't let the door hit you on the way out."

Zhao Xuanyou said in a deep voice, "You should rest early."

After leaving the Tangli Courtyard, Zhao Xuanyou walked swiftly, his mind still echoing with Yu Wan's dismissive words.

As he approached the entrance of Honghui Hall, Zhao Xuanyou's frustration grew heavier, pressing down on him until he could barely breathe. He punched the nearby tree trunk heavily. The already yellowing leaves were almost all shaken off by the impact, falling with a rustling sound.

Yuan Zhen hadn't seen him this angry in a long time. He shrank his head to the side, not daring to make a sound.

Zhao Xuanyou stood quietly under the tree, thinking about today's argument with Yu Wan.

Yu Wan wasn't angry because he was jealous; she was angry because he had been influenced by an outsider's instigation.

However, Sun Qianran's original intention was to make Zhao Xuanyou think that Yu Wan and Pei Tao had rekindled their old feelings. Instead, Zhao Xuanyou had worried that he wasn't Yu Wan's first choice because of her words.

The situations were different, but it was indeed caused by an outsider's instigation. Zhao Xuanyou was willing to take the blame for this.

Ever since the two of them had safely escaped the sandstorm, their days had been quite pleasant.

Even if he was exhausted from his daily duties, no matter how tired he was, at night he could always count on Yu Wan's gentle words by his side.

Perhaps he had been living too comfortably, giving rise to these useless petty thoughts.

The autumn night was chilly, but tonight was clear.

The moon was bright, and the stars were sparse, bathed in clear light.

Yu Wan had driven him back to Honghui Hall, which had an element of pouting, but she was genuinely angry.

Zhao Xuanyou blew on his cold hands for a long time. The frustration in his chest finally began to dissipate, and he felt a dull pain in the back of his hand from punching the tree.

He turned around and quickly returned to the Tangli Courtyard.

Inside the room, Pan Xia brought water for Yu Wan to soak her feet.

Yu Wan closed her eyes to rest while soaking her feet. She heard Qiuyue outside call out, "Marquis."

She couldn't help but frown and look over.

Zhao Xuanyou stood outside the threshold, meeting Yu Wan's aggrieved gaze. Thick-skinned, he said, "Wanwan, I'm still staying in Tangli Courtyard tonight."

"You're not leaving, so I will."

"If I move to Honghui Hall, won't Grandmother and Father know that we've had a fight? Then they'll definitely worry and come ask questions."

Zhao Xuanyou brought up the elders of the residence, which happened to strike a chord with Yu Wan.

Old Lady Ye and the old Marquis treated her, their new daughter-in-law, extremely well. If this marital discord were to alarm them, it would indeed be disrespectful.

Seeing Yu Wan soften, Zhao Xuanyou added, "I'll sleep on the beauty couch over there. If you're still angry, just don't talk to me."

The maids in the room and under the corridor watched as the Marquis acted humbly in front of his wife, all of them as if watching a play, but none dared to laugh out loud.

"You can sleep wherever you want." Yu Wan said with a straight face.

This was her way of agreeing to let him stay in Tangli Courtyard.

Zhao Xuanyou let out a sigh of relief and asked Qiuyue to help him prepare the beauty couch by the window.

After washing her feet, Yu Wan changed into her nightclothes and was about to go to sleep. As she walked past the screen, she couldn't help but glance at Zhao Xuanyou's side, and she couldn't help but curl her lips.

The beauty couch was not only narrow for Zhao Xuanyou but also too short. He lay on the couch with his calves hanging off the edge, looking both ridiculous and pitiful.

Serves him right, Yu Wan thought to herself.

Who told him to listen to others' instigations and then act on petty thoughts? He deserved a good punishment.

Seeing such a tall man cramped up in that small space, half of Yu Wan's frustration melted away.

After that, Yu Wan continued to leave early and return late to the shop, and in the evenings, she still refused to speak to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou had no choice but to make conversation out of thin air, repeatedly failing but continuing to try.

It wasn't until the sixth day, after Yu Wan had finished breakfast, that she finally looked up at him.

"Come with me to the shop today."

"Alright." Zhao Xuanyou didn't know what Yu Wan wanted him to do, but as long as she was willing to talk to him, he would do anything.

Yu Wan stood up and walked to the corridor. Chun Xing took a cloak and fastened it for her.

As the saying goes, a spell of autumn rain brings a spell of cold. Yu Wan took a deep breath and immediately felt a chill at the tip of her nose.

Zhao Xuanyou followed from behind, trying to take Yu Wan's hand, but she coldly slapped it away.

He knew Yu Wan had softened her attitude and went to tug at her cloak.

Yu Wan turned her head and glared at him. He pressed his lips into a smile, seemingly a bit smug, but the next moment, he obediently let go.

Wen Bo was waiting for Yu Wan outside the courtyard. Seeing the couple walking towards him one after the other, he suddenly remembered when they used to live in Qingsha Town. A neighbor had a large, impressive black dog that, because Yu Wan liked to feed it meat bones, had taken a liking to her.

That dog would bare its teeth at others but wag its tail around Yu Wan, running back and forth, hoping for her attention.

It was somewhat similar to the current scene.

Seeing the couple getting closer, Wen Bo lowered his head and puffed out his cheeks, afraid he might laugh out loud.

Yu Wan, seeing his strange expression, glanced at him and walked straight ahead.

The three of them took a carriage to Linglong Fang. After exchanging a few pleasantries with Xiu Fang, Yu Wan led Zhao Xuanyou upstairs.

There was a tastefully decorated tea room on the second floor, used specifically for receiving distinguished guests.

Yu Wan sat in the main seat at the tea table, pouring tea while gesturing with her chin towards Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou turned around suspiciously and saw Wen Bo open a small door in the corner, only then realizing there was a small partition there.

"Go in."

Before Zhao Xuanyou could ask, Yu Wan gave the order.

He could only suppress his doubts and obediently enter the partition.

As the door closed, Wen Bo pulled the adjacent decorative screen over to cover the door.

Xiu Fang came up with some fruit and said, "Wanwan, the Young Master Pei you mentioned has arrived."

chapters.title: A Clear View from the Sidelines
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou, hiding in the partition, was taken aback by these words.

Had Yu Ying deliberately brought him to Linglong Fang to meet Pei Ta?

Why did she want him to hide here?

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t quite understand Yu Ying’s arrangement. He took a deep breath and forcibly suppressed his emotions.

"Invite him upstairs for tea."

"Alright."

Listening to Yu Ying’s words, Xiu Fang quickly led Pei Ta to the second floor.

Pei Ta stood at the door, his gaze on Yu Ying, but he didn’t speak.

He wore a deep indigo brocade robe, which made him appear even more refined and handsome, his beauty surpassing bamboo.

His appearance alone was enough to attract everyone’s attention.

After Xiu Fang brought him in, she returned downstairs to attend to her duties.

Yu Ying stood up and spoke first, "Lord Pei, please take a seat."

Pei Ta looked deeply at Yu Ying, then sat down at the tea table as instructed.

When they had met at Prince Rui’s residence, although Pei Ta and Yu Ying hadn’t exchanged many words, he already understood her current intentions and stance.

He hadn’t let go of his feelings for Yu Ying, but he had his pride and wouldn’t entangle her any longer.

"I’ve already given the things you left in Anzhou to Big Brother Da Niu."

Back then, Yu Ying had been forcibly taken away from Anzhou by Zhao Xuanyou, leaving some belongings behind.

When Pei Ta returned to the capital, he collected these items and brought them back with him.

Before leaving the capital, he had sent a servant to Linglong Fang to find Chen Da Niu, asking him to deliver the items to Yu Ying.

Unexpectedly, as soon as he returned to the capital, his servant reported that Chen Da Niu had already visited and asked him to come to Linglong Fang, as Yu Ying wanted to thank him in person.

Unable to fathom Yu Ying’s intentions, he hesitated but ultimately came as promised.

"Thank you, Lord Pei."

Looking at Yu Ying sitting across from him, Pei Ta’s emotions were in turmoil.

At a time like this, he should have said some polite words, but for some reason, he didn’t want to say a single word.

Yu Ying poured tea for him. After setting down the teapot, seeing that he had no intention of drinking, she didn’t urge him.

"Those books left in Anzhou were ones I brought from the capital. They followed me from the capital to Qingzhou, then to Suizhou, and finally to Anzhou. I’m truly grateful you helped return them to the capital."

Those books had always been Yu Ying’s treasured possessions.

As their family of three wandered from place to place, aside from money and valuables, only those books had stayed with them.

Yu Ying picked up her tea cup. "The last time we met at the prince’s residence, I actually had a lot I wanted to say to you. But the encounter was too sudden, and the prince’s residence wasn’t the place for such a conversation. That’s why I invited you here today. Lord Pei, I offer you this tea in place of wine, to thank you for all your care at the Lichuan Imperial Palace."

After their encounter at the prince’s residence, Yu Ying knew her reaction had been too cold.

Their parting had been too hasty, and the letter she had left for Pei Ta contained only a few words. For the sake of both emotion and reason, the entanglement between them deserved a proper explanation.

"Lichuan Imperial Palace? That was too long ago."

Pei Ta shifted his gaze away from Yu Ying, staring quietly at the purple clay teapot on the table.

Hearing her bring up the past, the only words that came to his mind were "the times have changed, but the people have not."

At this time last year, he had just arrived in Shu to take up his post, searching everywhere for a suitable residence, dreaming of a sweet future with his beloved. In all his imaginings, the beautiful woman before him had always been present.

Now, she sat across from him, her hair piled high, her long dress embroidered, still as beautiful as ever, but she had already drawn a clear line between them.

"I was truly lucky to have met you and Miss Sun there." Recalling the past, Yu Ying’s lips curved slightly. "Back then, I was so bold. Watching you teach Prince Rui, I even thought of studying alongside him. Everyone else thought it was a joke, but you and Miss Sun were the only ones who encouraged me."

Pei Ta’s heart ached. Looking at Yu Ying, who was so close, he said faintly, "If it’s about Lichuan Imperial Palace, there’s no need to thank me. Everything I did back then was to get closer to the Marquis."

"But you really did help me."

Studying was not an easy task. Yu Ying could teach herself to recognize characters, but the Four Books and Five Classics couldn’t be understood just by knowing the words.

Even the most talented person needed a teacher to guide them.

If not for his and Sun Qianran’s repeated praise of her intelligence, if not for his permission to let her attend his lectures, if not for the many simple and clear annotations he wrote for her, Yu Ying would never have been able to tackle those profound and abstruse books.

Seeing Pei Ta lower his gaze in silence, Yu Ying drank the cup of tea in one go, then poured a second cup.

"This cup is on behalf of Zhao Xuanyou. What he did in Anzhou was indeed wrong."

At that time, Zhao Xuanyou had already arrived in Anzhou early, but instead of finding Yu Ying directly, he had bided his time, waiting until her wedding day to block the bridal sedan on the street, all to publicly humiliate Pei Ta.

Pei Ta, hearing Yu Ying’s words, thought of something else.

He finally picked up the tea cup on the table. The cold tea entered his heart, slightly calming his emotions.

Yu Ying had invited him today to express her gratitude and apologize. After today, they might never have such a conversation again.

Pei Ta suddenly raised his gaze.

"Speaking of the Marquis, I have a question I’d like to ask you."

"Please go ahead."

"If... when we met in Qingzhou, I had told you that Zhao Xuanyou had never married because of you, would you still have agreed to me?"

Back in Qingzhou, Pei Ta had asked Yu Ying if she wanted to know about Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Ying had said she didn’t, and he had let out a long sigh of relief.

He couldn’t bring himself to deceive Yu Ying, but since she said she didn’t want to hear, he could turn a blind eye and avoid the topic.

"I don’t know." Yu Ying sighed deeply. "But I probably would have been very confused."

In her past life, Yu Ying had died at the hands of a vicious mistress and lost her own son. In this life, she had been reborn and would rather not marry than live under someone else’s control.

She hadn’t left Zhao Xuanyou because there was no affection between them.

If she had known earlier that Zhao Xuanyou had called off his marriage because of her, she wasn’t sure what she would have done, but she definitely wouldn’t have been unmoved.

Pei Ta looked at Yu Ying and smiled slightly. "Back then, I also had my own motives. So, we’re even now. There’s no need to talk about who owes whom."

With that, Pei Ta stood up, cupped his hands toward Yu Ying, and walked straight downstairs.

"Ah Ji, see Lord Pei out."

Wen Ji nodded and followed Pei Ta downstairs. When they reached the shop’s entrance, Pei Ta stopped and turned to look at Wen Ji.

"Does Lord Wen have any more instructions?" Wen Ji asked.

"You’ve always understood Yu Ying’s feelings, haven’t you?"

The street was bustling, but Pei Ta’s voice was as clear and cool as water.

Wen Ji could more or less guess his intention.

Pei Ta probably felt that Yu Ying had never truly liked him.

Wen Ji didn’t think so, but he couldn’t speak for Yu Ying on this matter.

After a moment of silence, Wen Ji shook his head. "It was only after the Marquis fell into the river that I realized her feelings for him were different."

When Zhao Xuanyou had fallen into the river while departing by boat, he had been unconscious for several days after being rescued.

During that time, he couldn’t give orders, and his trusted followers naturally prioritized his safety over monitoring Yu Ying.

If Yu Ying had asked to leave, Wen Ji would have done everything in his power to take her away.

But Yu Ying hadn’t said she wanted to leave.

At that time, she might not have realized it herself, but as an observer, Wen Ji saw clearly; she couldn’t bear to leave Zhao Xuanyou.

---

chapters.title: Finally Speaking from the Heart
chapters.content:
Hearing no more sounds from the room, Zhao Xuanyou pushed open the partition door and stepped out. Pulling aside the screen, he saw Yu Ying sitting alone at the tea table.

"Yingying, are we alright?"

He walked to Yu Ying’s side and reached out to rub her head.

"What do you think?"

Occasional disagreements between husband and wife were normal; they wouldn’t fall apart over trivial matters.

Zhao Xuanyou curved his lips slightly, looking at Yu Ying’s thoughtful expression. Knowing she was thinking about Pei Ta, he gently advised, "Since he said everything is settled, you don’t need to feel guilty from now on."

"Mmm, I’ve been thinking I should give him a proper explanation in person."

Yu Ying’s arrangement today was more for Pei Ta’s sake than for Zhao Xuanyou.

Everything in Anzhou had been too chaotic and rushed; she owed Pei Ta an explanation.

Now that she was married into the Marquis’s household, private interactions with Pei Ta were inappropriate. Since Zhao Xuanyou had suspicions, she might as well let him be present.

She had said everything she wanted to say to Pei Ta. Now, it was time to focus on Zhao Xuanyou.

"Lord Pei allowed me to attend his lectures and gave me those books. At Lichuan Imperial Palace, I only felt gratitude toward him."

As Yu Ying spoke, her beautiful eyes were as clear and serene as a starry night.

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in acknowledgment, looking somewhat guilty.
