Back then, Yu Ying had enjoyed practicing calligraphy and studying, but although he often held her hand to teach her how to use the brush, his intentions had been more playful and affectionate than serious about her scholarly pursuits.

"Later, when we met again in Qingzhou, he confessed his feelings to me and said he was willing to marry me. I was surprised and touched... No one had ever said such sweet words to me before. I thought that if I missed him, perhaps no one else would ever say such things to me."

"So I agreed, and when I left Qingzhou, I was truly overjoyed."

She had never discussed her feelings about Pei Ta with Zhao Xuanyou in detail, fearing he might overthink.

Now, reflecting on it, she decided it was better to be clear and honest to prevent him from overthinking.

"It was my fault. These are things I should have told you first."

"Whether said earlier or later, perhaps it was all fated. It took that moment to understand. When you took me away from Anzhou, I truly thought you were the most hateful person in the world. But when you disappeared beneath the river’s surface, a part of me disappeared with you. I couldn’t bear the thought of you dying."

When Zhao Xuanyou was unconscious, Wen Ji could have taken her away.

If it had been someone else trying to force her, she would have left without hesitation, even resorting to killing them.

But not Zhao Xuanyou.

It was only then that Yu Ying realized how much Zhao Xuanyou meant to her.

"I’ve told you everything I can think of. Even if you still believe others over me, I doubt swearing oaths would help."

Zhao Xuanyou never believed Yu Ying would be entangled with Pei Ta.

His recent troubles were merely triggered by Sun Qianran’s words, stirring up unnecessary doubts. Seeing the fatigue in Yu Ying’s eyes, he said softly, "You don’t need to explain the past. I didn’t believe her provocation. It’s just that I’m too greedy; I want you to like me no matter what."

Like him no matter what?

Watching this usually composed and strategic man speaking such tender words in front of her, Yu Ying felt a mix of helplessness and sweetness.

He had been affected by Sun Qianran’s provocation because, deep down, he felt she didn’t care enough for him.

Back then, he had done everything to marry her, and now he worried that she had only agreed to the marriage because she was forced, not because she loved him enough.

But Yu Ying hadn’t expected Zhao Xuanyou to be so anxious and insecure over this.

"Had I known this would happen, you should have been nicer to me back then," she huffed, biting her lip as she looked at him, and angrily said, "All you knew was to order me around, always talking about marrying your cousin, and even accepting handkerchiefs from others..."

Hearing Yu Ying bring up old grievances, Zhao Xuanyou simply pulled her closer into his embrace, lowering his head to gently rub his chin against her cheek.

"Back then, I was always thinking about the Marquis’s prestige and reputation, thinking I couldn’t indulge in your warmth. But love isn’t something that can be controlled by reason. Marrying my cousin was the compromise I came up with at the time."

Yu Ying, of course, knew that his "compromise" had taken her into consideration.

It was just that in her past life, the mistress had been too vicious, and Yu Ying hadn’t dared to take the risk.

She didn’t blame Zhao Xuanyou.

If their positions were reversed, and she was the daughter of a marquis while Zhao Xuanyou was a servant or groom in the household, she might not have dared to take that step either.

It was often the case that one only realized the value of something when it was gone.

This applied to Zhao Xuanyou, and to her as well.

It had been no easy feat for them to reach this point.

He had poured his heart out, and Yu Ying naturally wouldn’t let him down. She decided to tell him all her feelings.

She looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, reaching out to gently trace his browbone.

"When I was a maid, I didn’t dare say how much I liked you, nor did I allow myself to feel that way. I admired you, but I also revered you, not daring to harbor any improper feelings, fearing that one wrong step would ruin everything. But after all the twists and turns, I’m very clear that my feelings for you are different. Zhao Xuanyou, I’m very fortunate that you were willing to marry me. If we have a daughter in the future, I hope she can marry a man like you; someone with both ambition and unwavering devotion."

Yu Ying often said Zhao Xuanyou was calm and composed, but on reflection, she had been even more stingy with words of affection due to her past life experiences.

Even after they were married, she had never spoken so candidly.

Hearing her say this now, a different kind of emotion surged in Zhao Xuanyou’s heart.

She liked him, only him.

He lowered his head and kissed her, his movements gentle and lingering.

After a long while, he finally released her.

"To be honest, my literary talent isn’t bad either. If you encounter any difficulties in your studies in the future, feel free to ask me."

"Alright." Yu Ying’s eyes sparkled as she suddenly said, "Back then, watching you instruct Prince Rui in martial arts, I was envious. It’s a shame I can’t start learning martial arts midway through life."

She had only seen Zhao Xuanyou fight a few times. Each time, with a sword in hand, he was sharp and invincible, leaving a deep impression on her.

If she had such skills, she could just take action against anyone she disliked, and most of the world’s troubles would be solved with a single strike.

"You want to learn martial arts?" Zhao Xuanyou showed a hint of surprise.

Yu Ying looked up, her clear eyes flashing as she waved her fists at him. "You don’t believe me?"

Watching Yu Ying’s fierce posture, Zhao Xuanyou took her fists in his large hands.

"I do believe you. With your wild temper and strength, you’re a great candidate for martial arts."

"I think so too." Yu Ying said, nestling into his chest.

"Shall I teach you?"

"Isn’t it too late to start now?"

"It’s a bit late to become as skilled as me, but learning some self-defense techniques isn’t difficult."

"Really?"

If he said so, Yu Ying was genuinely excited.

"As long as you’re willing, we can start today."

"Then it’s settled!"

Seeing the brightness in Yu Ying’s eyes, Zhao Xuanyou’s emotions surged even more.

Hearing her bare her heart to him brought a satisfaction deeper than any physical intimacy.

He had initially been attracted to her beauty, and she had her own considerations in love. They had both hesitated and doubted.

But through all the changes and twists of fate, they had ended up understanding each other and pledging their lives to one another.

chapters.title: A Dying Request
chapters.content:
Linglong Fang opened smoothly half a month later. The several noble ladies who had met Yu Wan at the prince's mansion all sent people to support the business, purchasing many high-priced items.

The shop was located in a prime spot with excellent foot traffic.

Xiu Fang was capable and hardworking, managing both the jewelry and cosmetics shops with great competence. Yu Wan thus stopped going to the shop and went with Zhao Xuanyou to the plum garden outside the city to live a quiet life.

The early plums were in full bloom there, and the scenery was becoming increasingly beautiful.

While their days were peaceful, the imperial court was in turmoil.

After the joint trial by the Three Courts, the deposed empress and the deposed crown prince were convicted of treason. The officials who had sided with them were also implicated, leaving many vacancies in the court. Many took advantage of this opportunity to rise rapidly, and Pei Tao was one of them, transferring from the position of Inspector of the Sichuan Province to the position of Assistant Minister of Revenue.

Zhao Xuanyou, who had made great contributions in this case, did not receive an official position as others had speculated. Instead, he was granted the honorary title of General of the Cavalry, a second-rank official.

Although the title of Grand General sounded impressive, it was merely an honorary title with no real responsibilities. Apart from attending grand court sessions, there was little for him to do on a daily basis.

Zhao Xuanyou did not mind. Together with Yu Wan, he built a small dock by the stream behind the plum garden and had a new plaque made for the garden, naming it Plum Blossom Cove. They spent their days boating, admiring the plum blossoms, and he taught Yu Wan some martial arts, living a life of great contentment.

It was only when Pan Xun sent someone to deliver a message that the couple returned to the capital from the outskirts.

"I'll go in with you." As the carriage arrived outside the imperial prison, Zhao Xuanyou said to Yu Wan.

Jiang Shi and Zhao Zun had been sentenced to death. Although not everyone in the Eastern Palace had to die, Zhuang Huaiyue, as the crown prince's concubine, could not escape punishment.

With the execution date approaching, Zhuang Huaiyue knew of the close relationship between the Brocade Guards and Zhao Xuanyou. She asked them to pass a message to Yu Wan, saying she wanted to see her.

When they were both maids, Yu Wan and Zhuang Huaiyue had barely spoken, let alone had any friendship.

Zhuang Huaiyue wanted to see her, probably because she had learned that Yu Wan had taken care of Zhao Yi Yun in the palace.

After much hesitation, Yu Wan decided to visit her in prison.

Zhao Xuanyou did not want her to have any connection with the Eastern Palace, but since Yu Wan insisted on going and it was not a big deal, he accompanied her to the imperial prison.

Most of the prisoners here were royal family members and high-ranking officials, so it was not as dark and damp as ordinary prison cells. Although the lighting was poor, it did not feel stifling.

Especially after the deposed empress and the deposed crown prince's faction were imprisoned, the other prisoners were moved elsewhere, leaving most of the cells empty.

Zhao Xuanyou accompanied Yu Wan inside, a faint, ambiguous smile on his face.

"Why are you smiling?" Yu Wan asked.

"Returning to an old haunt," he replied.

Yu Wan had been feeling a bit nervous, but upon hearing this, she couldn't help but laugh softly. "Were you locked up here last time?"

Zhao Xuanyou responded with an "mm."

"Who told you to hit people randomly?"

As the couple joked, the Brocade Guard leading the way took them to the deepest part of the corridor.

Jiang Shi and Zhao Zun were both held in the deepest part. Jiang Shi seemed to be lying on a wooden bed and did not get up even when she heard the noise, instead turning over to face the wall.

Zhao Zun, however, looked over at the sound of their footsteps. Upon seeing them, his eyes sharpened momentarily.

The once arrogant crown prince, now a prisoner, locked eyes with them briefly before quickly turning his face away, sitting with his back to them.

Zhao Xuanyou casually withdrew his gaze. He had no interest in kicking a man when he was down.

"Lord Hou, Lady Hou, Zhuang is in this cell."

Zhuang Huaiyue, formerly the crown prince's concubine, now shared a cell across from the deposed crown princess, Jiang Ru Shuo.

Upon seeing Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan, Zhuang Huaiyue suddenly stood up from the grass-woven cushion in the corner, quickly walking to the cell door.

She had once been a great beauty, but after nearly two months in prison, she had become extremely thin, and her once pitifully charming eyes were now worn and haggard.

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had indeed come to the imperial prison, Zhuang Huaiyue felt a lump in her throat, and tears welled up in her eyes.

"Brother Xuanyou, thank you. You always send charcoal in the snow."

After the Zhuang family fell from grace, she was taken into the Ministry of Rites to serve as an official servant. It was Zhao Xuanyou who had taken her into the Hou mansion. Although he had banished her from Honghui Hall, he had not truly punished her, allowing her to accompany the old lady in copying sutras and reciting Buddhist scriptures, living a leisurely life.

Zhao Xuanyou indifferently replied, "Minister Zhuang helped my father when he was an official. There's no need for thanks."

Zhuang Huaiyue turned to Yu Wan, "Lady Hou, thank you for saving Yi Yun's life."

"You're welcome. I was just following orders. I truly envy you for having such a well-behaved child." Yu Wan pushed a bundle she had brought through the wooden bars of the cell. "The weather is getting colder. I brought you a few new padded jackets."

Zhuang Huaiyue took the bundle and bitterly smiled, "Yi Yun is indeed well-behaved. It's a pity he was born to a mother with such little fortune."

Yu Wan consoled her, "His Majesty dotes on Yi Yun greatly. Consort Feng seems to be a gentle and kind person. In the future, Yi Yun will live in the palace, and his days will surely be peaceful and stable."

After Yi Yun was born, Zhuang Huaiyue had pinned all her hopes on her son, even neglecting Zhao Zun.

Although her death was near, Zhao Yi Yun had not been implicated by his grandmother and father. He had been adopted by the Fourth Prince to preserve his status as an imperial grandson, which made her waiting for death less desperate.

"Lady Hou," Zhuang Huaiyue looked around, confirming that the jailers and Brocade Guards were not nearby. She suddenly moved closer to Yu Wan, reaching through the cell door to grab Yu Wan's hand, and whispered, "I left some things for Yi Yun with Ziyan. After thinking it over, I believe it's best to entrust them to you."

"Me?" Yu Wan was surprised.

Zhuang Huaiyue glanced at Zhao Zun in the distance and Zhao Xuanyou beside her, then continued in a low voice to Yu Wan, "Although they are for Yi Yun, after you take them, how you use them is entirely up to you."

This was a dying request, and Zhuang Huaiyue's voice trembled slightly as she spoke.

After a moment of silence, she took half a step back and bowed to Yu Wan, "This cell is so stifling. Lady Hou, if you pity me, please have the jailer send some storybooks over."

She changed the subject so quickly that Yu Wan nodded, following her words, "Then I will send someone to bring them another day, along with some more quilts."

"Thank you, Lady Hou."

Yu Wan understood that Zhuang Huaiyue had asked her to come only to personally deliver this message.

After saying what needed to be said, Yu Wan, arm in arm with Zhao Xuanyou, left the cell.

Zhao Xuanyou had excellent hearing and had caught most of Zhuang Huaiyue's whisper to Yu Wan. "Just listen to what she said. Don't get involved."

He did not want Yu Wan to have any connection with the Eastern Palace.

Yu Wan, however, remained silent.

Seeing this, Zhao Xuanyou knew she had already made up her mind and could only helplessly say, "As you wish."

"I'll think about it some more."

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow but said no more.

He knew her temperament well. In the end, curiosity would always win out.

Besides, he wasn't afraid of her causing any trouble. If anything happened, he would be there to handle it.

The couple returned to the Hou mansion and, after changing clothes at the Tangli Courtyard, went to the Leshou Hall to pay their respects to Old Lady Ye. They happened to find the mansion's physician taking Old Lady Ye's pulse.

Seeing the couple return, Old Lady Ye was naturally delighted. After greeting them, she pulled Yu Wan to sit beside her and said to the physician, "It's rare to have you here. Examine Wanwan to see if she needs any treatment."

Yu Wan knew that Old Lady Ye was eager for a grandson. She obediently rolled up her sleeve, revealing her fair arm.

Beside her, Pan Xia placed a silk handkerchief on her wrist.

---

chapters.title: Bloodline Fusion
chapters.content:
Yu Wan's menstrual cycle had not arrived this month. Since there was no doctor at Plum Blossom Cove and she hadn't felt any discomfort, she hadn't mentioned it to Zhao Xuanyou.

Now that she was about to have her pulse taken, she felt a bit uneasy.

Zhao Xuanyou remembered that Yu Wan had once taken a contraceptive decoction and was worried that the physician might say something inappropriate in front of his grandmother and Yu Wan. He, too, felt a bit anxious.

The physician took her pulse for a moment through the silk handkerchief, and his eyes flickered.

"Physician Yang, is something wrong?" Yu Wan could see that the physician had noticed something and asked uneasily.

Old Lady Ye, unaware of the couple's concerns, looked at the physician with hopeful eyes and asked urgently, "Is Wanwan with child?"

"Don't rush, Grandmother." Zhao Xuanyou, seeing Old Lady Ye's high expectations, feared that she might later blame Yu Wan if disappointed. He gently advised, "Wanwan hasn't been eating well these past few days. Maybe it's because of that."

He wasn't lying. Yu Wan usually had a good appetite, and he had noticed that she had been eating less at Plum Blossom Cove than usual, sometimes just one steamed bun for breakfast.

He thought she simply didn't like the chef's cooking there and hadn't considered other possibilities.

"Early pregnancy often causes poor appetite," Old Lady Ye, desperate for a great-grandchild, ignored Zhao Xuanyou and pressed the physician, "Is she pregnant?"

The physician said, "Based on the pulse alone, I cannot be certain. If we remove the silk handkerchief, perhaps we can see more clearly."

Yu Wan, hearing this, removed the silk handkerchief from her wrist herself.

The physician re-examined her pulse and, after a moment, stood up, cupped his hands, and smiled. "It is indeed a pregnancy pulse. Congratulations, Old Lady, Lord Hou, Lady Hou."

Old Lady Ye was overjoyed. "Heavens bless me, I finally have a great-grandchild! Mama Xing, quickly prepare a large red envelope for Physician Yang."

Pregnant?

Yu Wan instinctively placed her hand on her belly, feeling a surge of joy. She looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, only to see that his face showed no reaction.

"Stinky boy, you're going to be a father, and you're just standing there like an idiot!" Old Lady Ye gave Zhao Xuanyou a hard pat. "Hurry up and coax your wife."

Zhao Xuanyou had been in a daze and muttered, "I'm going to be a father?"

He looked down at Yu Wan, who was sitting there with her fair hands crossed over her stomach, looking up at him with a smile.

When he had heard Ding Wenxi mention that the contraceptive medicine was extremely harmful to women's bodies, Zhao Xuanyou had already prepared himself for the possibility of having no children with Yu Wan.

He was born this way; always preparing for the worst-case scenario so that he could handle any eventuality with composure.

Seeing Old Lady Ye's joy, the physician added, "Lady Hou's pregnancy pulse is less than a month old. The pulse is still not very clear. I am about 70% certain. We can be completely sure in another half month."

"Alright, then we'll wait another half month," Old Lady Ye, hearing this, was not anxious. She knew that early pregnancy was unstable, and one had to be careful. It was not good to get too excited too soon. "Wanwan, I usually don't restrict you, but from now on, I can't let you run around outside anymore."

"Yes."

Yu Wan obediently agreed and glanced at Zhao Xuanyou.

The physician said it would take another half month to be completely sure, but Yu Wan instinctively felt that she was pregnant.

Her menstrual cycle had always been very regular.

Now that she was pregnant, she would be extremely careful without Old Lady Ye's reminder.

At Plum Blossom Cove, she had been practicing martial arts with Zhao Xuanyou every day. Fortunately, she hadn't harmed the baby in her womb.

"Do I need to take medicine to secure the pregnancy?" Old Lady Ye asked.

"Medicine is three parts poison. It's better not to take pregnancy-securing medicine when there are no symptoms," Physician Yang, who had been treating the Hou family for many years, said frankly. "Lady Hou is in good health. She just needs to take better care of herself daily. I'll write a list of foods to avoid, and the kitchen can stay away from them."

The Hou family was a noble family with the finest food and clothing. Yu Wan, as the Lady Hou, already had a rich diet and did not need any special tonics.

"Thank you, Physician." Zhao Xuanyou said, cupping his hands in gratitude to the physician.

He restrained the surging emotions within him and walked over to Yu Wan, kneeling down beside her and placing his hand on her belly.

Yu Wan's waist was still as soft and slender as ever, with no visible changes.

But thinking that a little life, a fusion of their bloodlines, was growing inside her, Zhao Xuanyou felt a deep sense of emotion.

Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou, his eyes filled with tenderness, and felt her heart race.

In her past life, her child had always been a source of heartache. After marriage, she had secretly hoped to conceive soon. But now that the pregnancy was confirmed, it still came as a surprise.

She and Zhao Xuanyou shared the same feelings; joy mixed with a little nervousness and panic.

No matter what, in this life, with Zhao Xuanyou by her side, she felt that there was nothing to fear.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou kneeling in front of Yu Wan in such an affectionate manner, Old Lady Ye's smile deepened. She did not disturb the couple and ordered the maids to inform the Old Lord and prepare the kitchen once the physician had written the dietary restrictions for the pregnancy.

Before long, the Old Lord and Concubine Wei arrived, surrounding Yu Wan with their care and concern.

Due to this joyous news, Old Lady Ye had Mama Xing set up a banquet in Leshou Hall, and the family had a lively meal together.

After the meal, Zhao Xuanyou took Yu Wan back to the Tangli Courtyard.

As soon as they left the courtyard of Leshou Hall, away from the elders of the mansion, Zhao Xuanyou no longer needed to suppress his joy. He directly lifted Yu Wan into his arms.

Yu Wan let out a soft exclamation, wrapping her arms around his neck. "I can walk by myself," she said softly.

Zhao Xuanyou solemnly replied, "Didn't Grandmother just say that from now on, you are the most important person in the Hou mansion? I must take good care of you. How can I let you walk by yourself?"

Seeing his expression, Yu Wan couldn't help but laugh. "Who wants you to carry me? It's not like you've never carried me before. If you want to take care of me, you should do something you've never done before."

"Like what?"

"Like cooking for me tonight."

"What do you want to eat?"

Yu Wan tilted her head in thought. "Roast duck."

"Alright."

Seeing how quickly he agreed, Yu Wan's eyes sparkled with amusement. "You agreed so quickly. Are you planning to buy one from outside to fool me?"

"How dare I fool you, the noble Lady Hou?" he replied.

"Do you know how to make it?" she asked.

"I'll have the chef teach me." Zhao Xuanyou was confident in his intelligence. Although he had never cooked before, he believed he could handle it.

Yu Wan pressed her lips together. "Then I'll look forward to it."

They were so close that Yu Wan could see her own reflection in Zhao Xuanyou's eyes.

She looked at him and suddenly asked, "Are you happy?"

"Of course," Zhao Xuanyou replied without hesitation, his gaze slightly surprised. "Why would you worry about that?"

Yu Wan nestled in his arms without speaking.

At this moment, the two most precious treasures in Zhao Xuanyou's arms were the people he cherished most in his life. Thinking this, even his usually cold and stern demeanor couldn't help but curve into a smile.

Zhao Xuanyou lowered his head and kissed Yu Wan, then carried her steadily forward.

chapters.title: Rouge Plum Pavilion
chapters.content:
Half a month later, the imperial physician examined Yu Wan again and confirmed her pregnancy. The Marquis's residence was filled with joy.

Yu Wan valued the child in her womb more than anyone else. Without her grandmother's reminder, she obediently stayed home to nurture the baby.

However, the plan to return to Yuzhou had to be postponed.

Originally, the couple had planned to stay in the capital for two or three months before returning. Unexpectedly, the events of the deposed empress and the deposed crown prince's rebellion occurred. Zhao Xuanyou requested an imperial decree to stay in the capital to celebrate the New Year before returning to the military.

Now that Yu Wan was pregnant, she needed ten months to carry the child, not to mention at least one or two years in the capital to raise the child after birth.

The capital had the best doctors and medicines in the world, so staying in the capital was best for the child.

Calculating this, Yu Wan realized she would not see her mother for at least two or three years. Although her days in the capital were harmonious and happy, thinking of her mother far away made her nose tingle with emotion. She picked up her pen and wrote a letter to Ding Wenxi, describing recent events.

Zhao Xuanyou knew her concerns and became even more attentive, finding joy in the trivial matters of the boudoir.

Since Yu Wan was staying indoors, she couldn't fulfill Zhuang Huaiyue's request to find Ziyan. So she sent Wen Bo to run the errand.

Ziyan indeed had a sandalwood box sent by Zhuang Huaiyue, containing a dozen or so books. However, they were all collections of literature available on the market.

Yu Wan couldn't figure out what was so important about these books.

Zhao Xuanyou flipped through them for a while but couldn't find anything special, so he had Yuan Xi store them in the warehouse.

As winter progressed, heavy snow fell, and the cold north wind howled, withering the plants. However, the noble families in the capital hosted many banquets.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan received numerous invitations at home, all of which they politely declined. It wasn't until the imperial physician said that Yu Wan's pregnancy was three months along and she should go out for some activity that Yu Wan, by the summons of Consort Li, went to Yuzhao Garden to appreciate the plum blossoms.

Yuzhao Garden was a royal garden in the suburbs of the capital, covering a vast area. The front mountain and the back courtyard were planted with flowers and trees for all seasons, ensuring a beautiful scene every season.

Now was the season when the winter plum blossoms were in full bloom. Consort Li, along with the concubines of the harem, went to Yuzhao Garden to appreciate the flowers and also invited the ladies from the noble families of the capital.

Zhao Xuanyou escorted Yu Wan to the entrance of Yuzhao Garden, then went to find a place to ride his horse. He would wait until the flower appreciation gathering ended to pick up Yu Wan.

As it was a gathering of ladies, it was not appropriate for him to follow. However, since Yu Wan was with child and could not bring maids due to her status, he was still worried. So he had Wen Bo secretly enter Yuzhao Garden to keep an eye on Yu Wan from a distance.

A palace maid led Yu Wan along the way, warmly saying, "Her Highness Consort Li arrived at Yuzhao Garden just a stick of incense ago. She is at the Rouge Plum Pavilion now."

Yu Wan found the name intriguing. When she arrived, she saw the mountain covered with blooming red plum blossoms, brilliant like the evening glow, and understood why the place was so named.

Here, only red plum blossoms were planted, which was different from the scenery of her own Plum Blossom Valley, each having its own merits.

Yu Wan didn't have time to appreciate the scenery fully and followed the palace maid into the hall to pay her respects.

Compared to the biting cold wind outside, the hall was warm like spring.

"Your humble servant greets Her Highness Consort Li."

"Ah, it's the Marchioness of Jingyuan. It's been a long time. I heard you've been staying home to nurture your pregnancy," Consort Li maintained her usual dignified manner and spoke kindly. "It's rare for you to come out, so don't stand for too long. Be seated."

The eunuch quickly brought an embroidered stool over.

Yu Wan thanked her and then sat down as instructed.

Consort Li was in high spirits and was very enthusiastic about organizing the banquet.

Today's plum appreciation gathering had invited many ladies. After Yu Wan arrived, more people came one after another. Even Princess Yi'an and Princess Yi'ning made an appearance.

After Princess Yi'an spread rumors about Yu Wan in the capital, Zhao Xuanyou had used the same tactic against her, ordering people to spread the news of Princess Yi'an's scandalous affairs.

Such exciting news about the princess quickly spread, and Princess Yi'an's bi-monthly elegant gatherings were canceled. The male favorites kept in the princess's residence were also quietly driven away.

As for Princess Yi'ning, she had been staying at home with Ye Moqian to take care of her daughter after the incident.

Seeing the two princesses, Yu Wan was somewhat surprised.

Whether intentionally or not, she had formed a rivalry with both princesses.

She was thinking about whether to go outside to appreciate the plum blossoms to avoid them when she noticed Princess Yi'ning looking at her.

The last time they met, Yu Wan had blocked Princess Yi'ning's hairpin.

Since their eyes had met, Yu Wan nodded at Princess Yi'ning in greeting.

Princess Yi'ning looked at her and then averted her gaze.

Her eyes no longer held the hatred from that day of rage but instead showed fatigue.

Upon closer inspection, Yu Wan noticed that her waist was slightly rounder than before.

Was Princess Yi'ning also pregnant?

"Marchioness."

Yu Wan turned her head and saw that the young lady standing beside her was actually Princess Consort Liang Miaofeng.

"Princess Consort." Yu Wan quickly stood up to return the greeting.

After becoming the princess consort, Liang Miaofeng's attire was much more luxurious than before. She wore a sea-tang red makeup flower satin dress, with a long gauze skirt trailing on the ground. The golden thread-embroidered patterns rippled like a lake as she moved.

Her appearance was even more beautiful than before, but there was a hint of worry between her eyebrows.

"I want to go out and appreciate the flowers. Would the Marchioness like to join me?"

"Alright." Yu Wan agreed happily.

She didn't want to stay in the hall anyway, and it was even better to go with Liang Miaofeng.

After all, she had already torn her face with Princess Yi'an. If Princess Yi'an came out to find trouble with her, as a subject's wife, she couldn't afford to offend a princess.

But Liang Miaofeng was the Princess Consort of Rui, with a status equivalent to Princess Yi'an. Princess Yi'an would have to show some restraint.

Knowing that Yu Wan was pregnant, Liang Miaofeng took the initiative to hold her hand and walk towards the exit of the hall.

A few days ago, the capital had just experienced snowfall. The palace servants of Yuzhao Garden had long since cleared the snow and thin ice from the stone steps. Because Consort Li was visiting to appreciate the flowers today, they had also used charcoal stoves to dry the small paths around the palace, so walking on them was not slippery.

Seeing that Liang Miaofeng carefully held her hand, Yu Wan expressed her gratitude: "Princess Consort, there's no need to worry. My body is not much different from before I was pregnant."

"No morning sickness? When my sister-in-law was pregnant, her morning sickness was terrible. She vomited everything she ate."

"I had a poor appetite a few days ago, but I didn't vomit much. I just ate less." After a pause, Yu Wan asked, "Earlier, I noticed that Her Highness Yi'ning's figure is rounder than before. Could it be..."

"Her Royal Highness is five months pregnant," Liang Miaofeng sighed softly. "Calculating the time, she was already pregnant before the incident with Yao Yao, but she didn't pay attention to her own body at that time. She only found out she was pregnant after the morning sickness started."

As they spoke, the two women, holding hands, walked towards the plum forest, weaving through the sea of red clouds.

After walking a bit farther from the palace, there were no guards along the path. Yu Wan felt a hint of unease and turned her head slightly, catching a glimpse of Wen Bo's face appearing among the plum trees.

With him nearby, she could relax and walk around.

When Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou lived in Plum Blossom Valley, she had learned a lot about plum blossoms from the gardener who took care of them. Now, just like when she was in the Imperial Garden, she began to appreciate the plum blossoms with Liang Miaofeng.

Before long, the two of them reached a pavilion halfway up the mountain to rest.

Liang Miaofeng looked at the mountain full of red plum blossoms and then at Yu Wan, feeling a sense of emotion rising in her heart. "Listening to the Marchioness speak really makes me feel how fast time flies. No wonder..."

---

chapters.title: Crisis in the Plum Forest
chapters.content:
Her voice stopped abruptly.

Yu Wan looked at Liang Miaofeng in surprise.

Liang Miaofeng lowered her head slightly, with a hint of apology, looking embarrassed as if she had accidentally revealed her thoughts: "Marchioness, I..."

Seeing that she wanted to speak but hesitated, Yu Wan sensed that she had no ill intentions, so she asked, "Has the Princess Consort been well lately?"

"Everything is fine." Liang Miaofeng lowered her gaze, her expression quite dim.

"If the Princess Consort has any difficulties, feel free to speak up."

Today was a rare sunny day in winter. Standing in the pavilion, although there was a cold wind blowing, the gentle sunlight enveloping them made it not feel cold.

Seeing that Liang Miaofeng remained silent, Yu Wan asked, "Did you have a dispute with the Prince?"

The mountainside was quiet, with only the sound of the wind passing through the plum forest.

"We haven't quarreled," Liang Miaofeng said softly. "The Prince treats me quite well."

Although she said this, Yu Wan could hear the disappointment in her tone.

"Then why does the Princess Consort look so worried?"

"The Prince... he doesn't like me."

Yu Wan was even more surprised.

She and Liang Miaofeng were not close friends, so it was unlikely that the other party would suddenly share such private matters with her.

After a moment of thought, Yu Wan asked directly, "Princess Consort, are you telling me this because you've heard some rumors?"

Liang Miaofeng became even more uneasy.

She had indeed paid special attention to Yu Wan because of Princess Yi'an's instigation, but she didn't intend to cause trouble for Yu Wan.

"Marchioness, I don't know how to explain this to you."

"Then take your time."

After all, she was Zhao Qi's wife and seemed like a gentle person. Yu Wan was not angry and just wanted to clarify.

"Previously, I met Princess Yi'an, and she said that the Prince..." Fearful of Yu Wan's misunderstanding, she repeatedly waved her hands. "I didn't believe Princess Yi'an's words."

So it was Princess Yi'an.

Nothing good could come from her mouth.

Yu Wan remained silent, waiting quietly for Liang Miaofeng to continue.

"I came to find the Marchioness because I want to ask for your advice. I really don't know how to get along with the Prince." Liang Miaofeng sighed, her eyes reddening. "No matter what I do, the Prince is always indifferent."

"Get along?" Yu Wan felt a mix of amusement and helplessness.

Liang Miaofeng was actually asking her how to get along with Zhao Qi?

How could she teach that?

"I met the Prince when I was still a maid in the Marquis's residence. Usually, I just followed orders. When the Prince was studying or practicing martial arts, I would attend to him by the side."

"When the Prince practiced martial arts every day, I was also by his side, but he rarely spoke to me and often told me to go back to my room."

Looking at Liang Miaofeng's disheartened expression, Yu Wan had an idea: "Princess Consort, do you live with the Prince?"

Yu Wan's question was somewhat indirect. Liang Miaofeng was stunned for a moment before realizing what she meant. She lowered her head in embarrassment: "We haven't consummated our marriage."

Yu Wan had already guessed this before asking. Thinking of Liang Miaofeng's current embarrassment, she didn't stare at her. Instead, she leaned against the pavilion's railing, gazing at the sea of red plum blossoms.

"Do you sleep in separate rooms?" Yu Wan asked.

Having already said the hardest part, Liang Miaofeng had no burden in speaking further.

"The Prince mostly rests in the study," Liang Miaofeng said, cautiously looking at Yu Wan. "Marchioness, I'm telling you all this, and I really don't mean to cause trouble for you. It's just that... I don't know what to do. I don't dare to tell my mother about these things for fear of worrying her, and I can't discuss such matters with my sister, Miaotong."

Liang Miaofeng herself had only been taught about marital affairs by her mother half a month before her marriage. Her younger sister, Liang Miaotong, was still completely clueless about these matters.

"But I don't know how to help you." Yu Wan said truthfully.

How could she advise Zhao Qi on this matter?

"I just want to know, based on your understanding of the Prince, is he a very stubborn person when it comes to feelings? Is it useless no matter how hard I try?"

Zhao Qi had done many things for Yu Wan, and even chased her to Yuzhou four years after her disappearance. He could be considered a persistent person.

However, when Zhao Qi left Yuzhou, he seemed heartbroken, which probably meant he understood that there was no possibility between them.

He had not consummated his marriage with Liang Miaofeng for so long. Was it because he hadn't let go of his feelings?

It was possible, but Yu Wan felt it was unlikely.

She carefully recalled every word Liang Miaofeng had said, and suddenly had an idea. "You said the Prince mostly rests in the study. What about the minority of the time? Besides the wedding night, has he ever rested in your room?"

"He has... twice," Liang Miaofeng thought for a moment and said softly. "Both times were when he returned from the palace late at night, and he would escort me back to my room. I invited him to stay."

"Sounds like the Prince treats you quite well."

"The Prince is not as unpredictable as people say. Although he always keeps me at a distance, he won't let me lose face in front of others or servants."

Yu Wan thought for a moment and smiled. "If I may, Princess Consort, you could be a bit bolder."

"How to be bolder?"

"You and the Prince have already slept in the same bed. Why wait for him to consummate the marriage? Can't you do it yourself?"

"Me?" Liang Miaofeng's fair face quickly turned red. "How can I consummate the marriage?"

"Before your marriage, Lady Liang should have taught you, right?"

"But if I go..." Liang Miaofeng's face turned redder as she spoke, almost as if it would drip blood. "Won't the Prince think I'm too promiscuous?"

"You are husband and wife. It is only natural for you to consummate the marriage. What promiscuous or not?"

Yu Wan had heard before that Zhao Qi had been stationed with the army for external training. When he got married, the prince's residence was also very quiet, with no concubines or even bedchamber maids.

He might not be very knowledgeable about such matters.

Yu Wan didn't know if Zhao Qi still had feelings for her, but since he was willing to escort Liang Miaofeng back to her room and occasionally shared the same bed, even if there were no intimate actions, it showed that he didn't reject Liang Miaofeng.

Perhaps if Liang Miaofeng was bolder, the marital deadlock could be broken.

"But I'm afraid the Prince will dislike me."

"A forced melon is indeed not sweet. I'm just suggesting. What to do and when to do it is still up to the Princess Consort to decide."

Liang Miaofeng felt a mix of hope and melancholy.

She really didn't expect to encounter such a problem. In any case, after talking with Yu Wan, she felt much better.

"Sister! Sister!"

A clear voice came from outside the pavilion. Yu Wan turned her head and saw Liang Miaotong and a few girls of similar age coming down the mountain.

After exchanging greetings, the group walked down the mountain together, with Liang Miaofeng and Yu Wan leading the way, and the young girls following behind.

Not long after, a eunuch carrying a large vase walked up the mountain.

"Princess Consort."

"No need for formalities."

Since the stone path was not wide, Liang Miaofeng and Yu Wan stood side by side. Logically, the eunuch should step off the stone path to let them pass.

Liang Miaofeng, being kind-hearted and not wanting to put on airs as a princess consort, thought about the snow covering the ground off the path. She took a step forward to make way.

"Thank you, Princess Consort."

The eunuch, holding the large vase, gratefully bowed to Liang Miaofeng.

For some reason, his hand slipped, and the vase began to fall. He quickly tried to catch it, but somehow, his entire body suddenly lunged towards Yu

chapters.title: Targeting Her Child
chapters.content:
In the instant the eunuch lunged at her, Yu Wan sensed a flicker of malice in his eyes.

He had come to crash into her on purpose! No, he wasn’t just trying to hit her. He meant to harm her!

In that split second, Yu Wan instinctively clutched her stomach and abruptly sidestepped.

"Madame Hou, be careful!" Liang Miaotong behind her instinctively reached out to steady her.

Seeing that he had missed, the eunuch abruptly stopped in his tracks and turned to grab Yu Wan instead.

He had a powerful grip, seemingly trained in martial arts, and yanked Yu Wan’s wrist, intending to fling her down the mountain.

"Help! Someone, help!" Liang Miaofeng snapped out of her daze and shouted loudly.

The other noble ladies, terrified by the scene, screamed and fled backward, assuming there was an assassin.

Yu Wan, relying on her own strength, twisted her hand to break his grip.

Liang Miaotong also clung tightly to Yu Wan, preventing the eunuch from pulling her away.

By now, Yu Wan understood his intention; he didn’t want to kill her but to create an "accidental fall from the cliff" to harm the child in her womb.

She would never let him succeed!

But the man was a trained fighter. Even if Yu Wan and Liang Miaotong gave it their all, they were no match for him.

Just then, a sudden projectile whistled through the air, striking the eunuch’s shoulder and wrist with two sharp thuds, the pain forcing him to instinctively let go.

Yu Wan’s taut nerves finally relaxed. She turned her head and saw a familiar figure sprinting toward her. In moments, he was by her side.

Wen Shu propped up Yu Wan’s shoulder, pulling her back as he hurled another iron pellet at the eunuch.

"Yu Wan, are you alright?" Wen Shu asked in a low voice.

"I’m fine."

"I came too late…"

Before Wen Shu could finish, a cry of alarm came from Liang Miaofeng beside them.

It turned out that the moment Yu Wan escaped, the eunuch, though wounded by Wen Shu’s projectiles, refused to give up. He grabbed Liang Miaotong and tumbled down the mountainside with her.

"Tong’er! Tong’er!"

Liang Miaofeng shouted in panic, but the terrain was treacherous, and the eunuch, dragging Liang Miaotong, quickly vanished from sight.

"You must go check on her!" Remembering how Liang Miaotong had risked everything to help her in that critical moment, Yu Wan grew anxious.

Wen Shu did not move.

He had snuck in to protect Yu Wan. The guards hadn’t arrived yet, and there might still be more attackers targeting her. He couldn’t leave.

"The guards will be here soon. You must go down the mountain to save Miss Miaotong. If she’s unharmed, leave immediately."

With anyone else, Yu Wan would prioritize her own safety. But Liang Miaotong had been pulled into this because she tried to save her.

How could Yu Wan rest easy not knowing if she was alive or dead?

Moreover, Wen Shu wasn’t supposed to be here.

If the guards saw him, it would cause trouble. Entering the Jade Mirror Garden without permission was a capital offense, even if it wasn’t the imperial palace.

"Take care of yourself." With that, Wen Shu dashed off in the direction where Liang Miaotong had fallen.

Yu Wan stepped through the snow back onto the stone steps and took Liang Miaofeng’s hand.

"Madame Hou," Liang Miaofeng looked at Yu Wan helplessly, "what on earth… what is going on?"

"Someone wants to harm my child," Yu Wan said quietly. "The masked man is my friend. He’s gone to save Miss Miaotong. When the guards arrive, don’t mention that he was here."

"Can’t we speak of him?" Liang Miaofeng’s face drained of color.

She was deeply worried about her sister’s safety. Though she tried to suppress her emotions, tears still streamed down her face.

"Princess Consort, where is the assassin?"

Finally, the guards of the Jade Mirror Garden arrived, surrounding them immediately.

"The assassin took my sister and rolled down the mountain. You must go check on her!"

"Understood."

The guards split into two groups; one to search for Liang Miaotong down the mountain, the other to escort the two women back to the main hall.

After the brief panic subsided, Yu Wan’s mind finally calmed.

Carefully recalling who had come to the Jade Mirror Garden to admire the plum blossoms today, she had a good idea who might be behind this attack.

The most suspicious was Princess Yi’an, who had clashed with her openly before.

Previously, at the Qianqing Palace, Zhao Xuanyou had humiliated Princess Yi’an in front of everyone. Afterward, Yi’an spread rumors about her, only for Zhao Xuanyou to counter by exposing her scandalous affairs in the Princess’s residence.

She must hate Yu Wan to the bone.

But Princess Yi’ning was also a possibility.

As an enraged mother, she had once blamed Crown Prince Zhao Yi for the death of her daughter, the deposed empress. That resentment could easily extend to Yu Wan, who protected Zhao Yi.

Both princesses had the means to arrange people in the Jade Mirror Garden.

Before long, Yu Wan and Liang Miaofeng returned to the main hall.

Consort Li had already heard about the assassination attempt from the palace attendants and exclaimed, "How could there be an assassin in the Jade Mirror Garden? What are the Feathered Forest Guards doing!"

"Consort, my sister’s life is in danger! Please send more people to find her!" Tears streamed down Liang Miaofeng’s face as she thought of her sister’s plight.

"Quick, help Princess Consort Rui sit down! Rest assured, I will send people to find Miss Miaotong!"

While Consort Li comforted Liang Miaofeng, Yu Wan’s gaze swept across the hall.

First, she met Princess Yi’ning’s eyes.

Yi’ning’s expression was somewhat blank. Seeing Yu Wan looking at her, she did not look away but seemed confused.

She didn’t understand why an assassin would appear in the Jade Mirror Garden, let alone why they would target Liang Miaotong, an innocent young girl.

It wasn’t her.

Yu Wan shifted her gaze to Princess Yi’an.

Compared to Yi’ning, Yi’an’s eyes were far more complex. She stared deeply at Yu Wan, her expression a mix of surprise at Yu Wan’s unharmed appearance and lingering resentment.

When their eyes met, Yi’an instinctively averted her gaze for a moment before lifting her chin to look back at Yu Wan, feigning boldness.

Yes, she was a princess. Even if she had tried to harm Yu Wan, what could anyone do?

Not to mention the deed hadn’t been uncovered yet. Even if it were, Consort Li would likely cover it up to avoid scandal.

After confirming it was Princess Yi’an, Yu Wan calmly withdrew her gaze.

Yi’an had insulted her, and she could tolerate that. She could even endure the rumors Yi’an spread about her.

But Yi’an had tried to harm her child. That she could never tolerate!

Even if Consort Li did not seek justice for her, Yu Wan would find her own way to repay the favor!

"Wan, are you alright?" After consoling Liang Miaofeng, Consort Li turned to Yu Wan with concern. "You’re with child now; you mustn’t be frightened."

"In response to Your Highness, this subject is unharmed."

"That’s good. Still, we mustn’t be careless." Consort Li was especially kind to Yu Wan because she had learned from Prince Ping that Zhao Xuanyou held her in high regard.

If Yu Wan were to lose the child here, it would be a disaster.

"I didn’t bring an imperial physician today. Here’s what we’ll do: I’ll send someone to take you back to your residence immediately, and have a doctor discreetly examine whether you need medicine to secure the pregnancy."

"Thank you for your concern, Your Highness. Miss Miaotong of the Liang family was harmed because of me. I’d like to wait until she’s found before returning."

Consort Li’s eyes flickered in surprise. "You mean the assassin was targeting you?"

---

chapters.title: Sweeping It Under the Rug
chapters.content:
"The assassin was indeed targeting this subject." Yu Wan adjusted her sleeves and lowered her gaze respectfully. "Just now, as Princess Consort Rui and I were walking down from the halfway point, we encountered a eunuch carrying a flower vase. He pretended to slip and deliberately threw the vase at me, trying to push me down the mountain. Fortunately, Miss Miaotong helped me steady myself. However, Miss Miaotong was caught up in it and was dragged down the cliff by the eunuch."

"A eunuch carrying a flower vase?" Consort Li frowned, her expression shifting.

She currently managed the rear palace but lacked the phoenix seal, so she took extra care in handling palace affairs and hosting banquets.

Today, she had rarely ventured out of the palace to the Jade Mirror Garden to admire the plum blossoms, only to have an assassination attempt occur.

If it had been an outsider, that would be one thing. But a eunuch?!

"Yes." Yu Wan continued, "Besides this subject, Princess Consort Rui, and Miss Miaotong, several other noble ladies also witnessed it."

The young girls who had been scared into running away earlier were still shaken. They nodded along with Yu Wan’s words.

As Consort Li knitted her brows in silence, Princess Yi’an slowly spoke up: "Could it be remnants of the deposed empress? Earlier, the Marquis of Jingyuan led the Brocade Guards to arrest the deposed empress and crown prince’s followers in the palace, claiming they had all been caught. But it’s very possible there are still stragglers in the Jade Mirror Garden, taking this opportunity to retaliate against the Marquis of Jingyuan’s wife!"

As soon as she finished, the concubines and ladies in the hall began to murmur among themselves.

"It really could be the deposed empress’s remnants."

"No wonder they targeted the Marquis of Jingyuan’s wife!"

"Exactly! If they can’t harm the Marquis of Jingyuan, they’ll go after his wife."

"It’s a brilliant move; revenge on the Marquis and embarrassment for Consort Li, all in one stroke."

Consort Li looked at Yu Wan, then at Princess Yi’an, her mind already made up.

Though she was a former dancer with little formal education or talent, she had survived the deposed empress’s oppression, which spoke to her cunning.

The deposed empress’s remnants might indeed still lurk in the palace and Jade Mirror Garden. But if they sought revenge, they would target her first, not push Yu Wan.

This act didn’t seem like an assassination; it was more like a deliberate attempt to cause a miscarriage.

Such a petty, low-level tactic was beneath the deposed empress’s followers.

As her thoughts raced, Consort Li’s gaze toward Princess Yi’an sharpened.

Princess Yi’an was also seething inside.

The original plan was for the eunuch to carry a flower vase past Yu Wan, pretend to slip, and drag her down the mountain.

The Jade Mirror Garden was covered in snow. Even if Yu Wan tumbled down, she wouldn’t die, but she would likely miscarry; a fitting lesson for her.

Afterward, if anyone investigated, it would just be an accident.

Who knew Yu Wan would return unharmed to the Rouge Plum Pavilion, while it was Princess Consort Rui’s sister who had been dragged down the mountain?

Had they targeted the wrong person?

What incompetence.

They couldn’t even handle such a simple task, and now she had to clean up the mess.

Fortunately, she wasn’t afraid of Consort Li pursuing the matter thoroughly.

Consort Li was eager to demonstrate her ability to manage the rear palace to the emperor. She would surely downplay the incident to avoid the plum-viewing banquet being marred by an assassination attempt.

Meeting Consort Li’s gaze, Princess Yi’an knew she had read her intentions.

Consort Li cursed the girl in her mind for causing trouble at her banquet.

Still, Yi’an had correctly judged her intentions.

She truly did not want the matter to escalate.

Consort Li lifted her chin and said calmly, "It may not necessarily be an assassin, nor necessarily the deposed empress’s remnants. Everyone, refrain from wild speculation."

"Yes."

Since she had spoken, no one in the hall dared to continue discussing, and they all fell silent.

Consort Li gave a satisfied smile, then turned to Yu Wan and Liang Miaofeng. "This was sudden, and you must be shaken. Rest assured, I will have the Feathered Forest Guards investigate today’s incident thoroughly."

Yu Wan understood that Consort Li wanted her to drop the matter. She had never expected Consort Li to seek justice for her, so she simply responded with a respectful bow.

"But…" Liang Miaofeng frowned.

In her view, the assassin had harmed her sister, Miaotong. For Consort Li, who was in charge of the rear palace, to dismiss the presence of a villain in the Jade Mirror Garden so lightly was unfair.

Before Liang Miaofeng could finish, a palace maid entered and reported, "Consort Li, Miss Miaotong has been found."

"How is Tong’er?"

Liang Miaofeng anxiously stood up and grabbed the maid who had rushed in with the news.

The maid, still held by her, reported to Consort Li, "The mountain is covered in thick snow. Miss Miaotong is alive, but her leg is broken."

Her leg was broken?

Liang Miaofeng wasn’t too heartbroken. When her sister had been dragged away by the assassin, she had already braced for the worst.

As long as she was alive, it was fine!

A broken leg could heal with time. What mattered was that she was alive.

"Where is she?"

"She’s been carried to the side hall. The lady-in-waiting was just examining her wounds."

"And the assassin?"

"When the guards found Miss Miaotong, she was alone. No one else was seen."

Had the eunuch escaped?

Probably not. He had been hit by several of Wen Shu’s projectiles; he couldn’t have gotten away unscathed.

"I’m going to see Tong’er." Liang Miaofeng was only concerned about her sister’s safety and hurried toward the side hall without another thought.

Yu Wan also stood up. "Your Highness, this subject would also like to go see her."

"I’ll go with you."

Earlier, Liang Miaofeng had only said "but," yet Consort Li had already sensed the underlying issue.

After all, she was Princess Consort Rui. If she wasn’t satisfied, it might lead to complications.

Yu Wan followed Consort Li to the side hall.

As soon as they entered, they saw a lady-in-waiting binding Liang Miaotong’s leg to a wooden splint.

Since Consort Li hadn’t brought an imperial physician today, she was fortunate to have a lady-in-waiting with some medical knowledge to provide emergency care.

After Consort Li offered a few words of concern, she gave a light cough, and the palace attendants in the room all withdrew, leaving only the four of them.

"Since Miaotong is safe, let’s treat today’s incident as an accident."

As expected, Consort Li had come to the side hall not to check on Liang Miaotong’s injuries but to silence the three of them.

"An accident?"

Liang Miaofeng was naturally unwilling to let the culprit who had harmed her sister go unpunished.

Consort Li said indifferently, "Miaotong is still an unmarried girl. If word spreads that she was taken by an assassin, it would damage her reputation."

"But the assassin was a eunuch."

"Who knows if he was really a eunuch when no one caught him?" After a pause, Consort Li turned to Yu Wan. "Madame Hou, what do you think?"

Consort Li and Yu Wan both knew who was truly behind today’s events, though their suspicions differed. But Yu Wan knew that investigating further would lead to the same dead end.

"This subject believes Your Highness speaks wisely."

"Sister, let’s listen to Her Highness." The weak Liang Miaotong on the bed also spoke up.

A woman’s reputation was indeed important. Liang Miaofeng eventually nodded in agreement.

Consort Li gave a satisfied nod. "Rest assured, I won’t let you suffer for this. Later, you can take my carriage back to the capital."

"Thank you, Your Highness."

After Consort Li left the side hall, Yu Wan approached the bed and said solemnly, "Miss Miaotong, thank you for your help today. I will never forget this life-saving kindness."

chapters.title: Irreplaceable
chapters.content:
"Madame Hou need not feel guilty. The palace maid just checked my leg injury and said it’s not serious. I’ll be fine in a month or two."

It was a stroke of luck in misfortune. Winter’s bitter cold had frozen the ground, and the mountains were blanketed in snow. Liang Miaotong had been wearing a padded jacket and a rabbit-fur cloak, which had softened the fall.

Seeing Liang Miaotong comforting her instead, Yu Wan said, "From now on, if the Princess Consort or you need anything, just ask. I will do my best to help."

"Tong’er is right. The assassin is to blame, not Madame Hou. I never expected Her Grace the Noble Consort to drop the matter."

"The Noble Consort knows who the real culprit is, which is why she said not to investigate."

Liang Miaofeng’s eyes widened, a chill running down her spine.

"Does Her Grace know? And Madame Hou too?"

Yu Wan nodded slightly and whispered, "Today, I implicated the Princess Consort and you. I owe you my life, and I will repay this debt in the future."

"It’s not your fault," Liang Miaofeng sighed. But recalling how her sister had been on the brink of death today, she couldn’t help but feel a lingering fear. "Father and Mother always told me to be cautious in the palace. I used to dismiss their warnings, thinking they were being overly cautious. But today, I truly understood what they meant."

Though Zhao Qi and she had their differences, the inner quarters of Prince Rui’s residence were peaceful, with no other women vying against her. She had no idea how treacherous the palace could be.

After chatting for a while in the side hall, a palace maid came to report that the carriage was ready, and the eunuchs would soon arrive to carry Liang Miaotong.

Since Zhao Xuanyou had promised to pick her up, and with Wen Kun and the assassin still unaccounted for, Yu Wan was worried. She didn’t want to travel with Noble Consort Li, so she stood up to go to the main hall to inform her.

After she left, Liang Miaofeng helped her sister sit up and accidentally felt something hard under her cloak.

"What is this?" Liang Miaofeng asked.

"Nothing," Liang Miaotong replied vaguely.

Liang Miaofeng, concerned only for her sister’s well-being, didn’t think much of it. She waited for the eunuchs to bring in the stretcher and helped her sister onto it.

Yu Wan returned to the main hall just in time to hear Noble Consort Li telling everyone that the incident with the assassin was a false alarm. The eunuch carrying the vase was not an assassin; he had accidentally pushed Liang Miaotong down the mountain while falling. He had already been dealt with according to palace rules.

If this had happened in the imperial palace, it wouldn’t have been so easily dismissed. But in the Jade Illumination Garden, with Noble Consort Li’s word, no one dared to object.

Relieved that the matter was settled, Noble Consort Li let out a small sigh. Hearing Yu Wan say she would wait for the Hou residence’s carriage to pick her up, she smiled and asked, "Is it Marquis Jingyuan who is coming to pick you up?"

"Yes. The Marquis happens to be meeting friends outside the city today, so he can take me back to the capital with him."

Hearing that Zhao Xuanyou was coming to the Jade Illumination Garden to pick up Yu Wan, Princess Yi’an’s expression suddenly changed.

Originally, the plan to harm Yu Wan was supposed to look like an accident. But Yu Wan had come out unscathed.

She wasn’t afraid of the Emperor finding out, nor was she afraid of being held accountable. But remembering how Zhao Xuanyou had fiercely confronted her on Yu Wan’s behalf in front of the Qianqing Palace, she couldn’t help but feel a twinge of fear at the thought of facing him.

She clenched her fists, suppressing the unease in her heart, and stood up to follow Noble Consort Li and the Liang sisters back to the capital.

After Noble Consort Li left, the atmosphere in the Rouge Plum Pavilion relaxed somewhat.

Some acquainted ladies approached to express their concern for Yu Wan. Following Noble Consort Li’s instructions, Yu Wan only said that she had been frightened at the time and mistakenly thought the eunuch had intentionally bumped into her.

After chatting with the ladies for a while, Yu Wan found herself alone. She had some pastries and then noticed Princess Yi’ning standing alone by the window, admiring the plum blossoms. After a moment’s thought, she decided to go over and greet her.

"Are you alright?"

"I’m fine for now, thank you for your concern, Princess."

Since the incident at the Qianqing Palace, the two of them hadn’t seen each other.

Yu Wan took the initiative to break the ice, and Princess Yi’ning was indeed moved.

After a moment of hesitation, she whispered, "Last time, I was actually grateful that you stopped me. If I had really killed Yi Yun, the Emperor would never have forgiven me, and I would have been haunted by guilt forever."

Though the two princesses of the imperial family seemed equally arrogant and domineering on the surface, their true natures were different.

Princess Yi’ning was indeed willful, but she was not cruel and had never done anything truly wicked.

At the Qianqing Palace, she had received too much shocking news, and her spirit had nearly collapsed. In a fit of extreme anger, she had wanted to kill Zhao Yi Yun, but that had been a momentary impulse.

After calming down, she too had felt a lingering fear.

"I heard from the Marquis that Yao Yao’s condition has improved somewhat."

"She is out of danger now. She can recognize me and her father, but most of the time, she’s still... dull and slow." Mentioning her daughter, Yi’ning’s eyes instantly darkened.

"Back then at the Qianqing Palace, the imperial physicians said her chances were slim. But Yao Yao pulled through, which shows the poison wasn’t as deadly as feared. With time and care, she will surely get better."

"I hope she recovers soon."

"The imperial physicians in the Imperial Hospital are highly skilled, but as the saying goes, ‘There’s always someone better.’ There are many talented doctors among the common folk. Don’t give up on Yao Yao’s illness. Keep seeking medical help; perhaps one day, the right treatment will be found."

Princess Yi’ning looked at Yu Wan with a hint of surprise in her eyes.

"I didn’t expect you to say that," she lowered her head, gently rubbing her swollen belly, and bitterly smiled. "This child was conceived before Yao Yao’s accident, but I didn’t realize it at the time. After learning of the pregnancy, it was as if all the relatives who were grieving over Yao Yao were suddenly saved. Even my mother and mother-in-law stopped worrying about Yao Yao’s illness, saying this child is Heaven’s way of making amends to me."

"How can such a thing make amends?" Yu Wan sighed softly.

Even if she had another child, Yao Yao’s illness wouldn’t disappear. She would still need to continue seeking treatment.

"Yes, Yao Yao is Yao Yao. Even if I have other children, no one can replace her." In a short moment, Princess Yi’ning’s impression of Yu Wan changed greatly.

"Princess, Madame Hou, the Prince Consort and the Marquis have arrived at the gate of the Jade Illumination Garden," an eunuch respectfully announced.

As expected, when Yu Wan saw that Princess Yi’ning hadn’t left with Noble Consort Li earlier, she guessed that Ye Moqing was also out of the city today and might even be with Zhao Xuanyou.

"Let’s go." Princess Yi’ning took the initiative to link arms with Yu Wan and walked out of the Rouge Plum Pavilion.

Since both of them were pregnant, Noble Consort Li had instructed the eunuchs to carry them out in palanquins before leaving. Soon, they arrived at the main gate.

The carriages of the Princess’s residence and the Marquis’s residence were parked one after another at the entrance.

Before Yu Wan could step out of the palanquin, she saw Zhao Xuanyou striding toward her. His heavy dark cloak fluttered in the wind, and the sword at his waist swayed slightly.

"Wanwan."

Seeing the concern in his usually stern eyes, Yu Wan knew he was already aware of what had happened.

Before Yu Wan could step down from the palanquin, he reached out and lifted her into his arms.

"I’m fine."

Feeling the cold aura around him, Yu Wan gently placed her hand on his shoulder and said softly, "I’m fine, and the child is fine too."

Zhao Xuanyou responded with a low "mm," his face darkening terribly.

Yu Wan could see the coldness in his expression, but knowing this was not the place to talk, she didn’t say more and simply rested her head on his shoulder.

As long as he was by her side, he was her strongest support, and she feared no ambushes.

---

chapters.title: Did She See Too?
chapters.content:
"Big brother, your sister-in-law had a scare today. Take her back and have a doctor examine her immediately."

Knowing that Zhao Xuanyou would send Yu Wan to the Jade Illumination Garden today, Ye Moqing had arranged to meet Zhao Xuanyou at a nearby estate for tea and conversation.

When Yuan Zhe had reported the trouble at the Jade Illumination Garden earlier, he hadn’t hidden anything from Ye Moqing. At that moment, Ye Moqing had seen the killing intent in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes.

He followed Zhao Xuanyou straight to the Jade Illumination Garden. Hearing from the guards at the gate that there was no assassin, and that it was only a young lady from the Liang Minister’s residence who had fallen and been injured while others were unharmed, Zhao Xuanyou’s expression improved slightly.

Ye Moqing knew the matter wasn’t that simple, but since Noble Consort Li had decided to cover it up, that would be the final outcome.

Zhao Xuanyou only responded with a low "mm."

His gaze toward Yu Wan was still gentle, but his expression was dark, with a chest full of suppressed anger.

At this moment, not saying much was already an exercise in extreme restraint.

Princess Yi’ning stepped out of the palanquin and said to Yu Wan, "I have a hot spring estate in the outskirts of the capital. When we have time, let’s go and stay there together."

"Thank you, Princess." After speaking, Yu Wan gently nudged Zhao Xuanyou. "Husband, let’s go home."

Zhao Xuanyou carried Yu Wan into the carriage. Before the carriage could move forward, he asked anxiously, "Are you feeling unwell anywhere?"

"I’m fine. Liang Miaotong helped me, and Ah Kun was there too." After finishing, Yu Wan asked, "Did you see Ah Kun?"

"Yes, he brought back a half-dead eunuch, saying he was the one who tried to harm you."

Confirming that Wen Kun was safe, Yu Wan felt at ease.

She looked up at Zhao Xuanyou, her eyes also revealing a trace of hatred. "It was Princess Yi’an."

Zhao Xuanyou was not surprised.

He had already ordered people to interrogate the half-dead eunuch, but that side had not yet yielded results. However, it wasn’t hard to figure out who had a grudge against the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence. Princess Yi’an was the likely culprit.

Past verbal disputes were one thing, but she had actually dared to target Yu Wan and the child. If Zhao Xuanyou could tolerate this, how could he be a worthy husband and father?

"I know."

He only said four words, and Yu Wan didn’t press further.

Yu Wan nestled in Zhao Xuanyou’s arms and soon fell asleep. When she opened her eyes again, Zhao Xuanyou was already carrying her out of the carriage.

"I can walk myself." Seeing that he refused, Yu Wan smiled. "The residence’s physician said I shouldn’t just lie down all the time. I need to move around more, or I won’t have the strength for childbirth later."

Seeing her eyes curved in a smile, as beautiful and charming as ever, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but soften.

When the two returned to the Tangli Courtyard, Autumn Moon immediately invited the residence’s physician over.

She was carrying a child, so the most important thing now was to take care of herself and the baby. As for other matters, Zhao Xuanyou would handle them.

After the physician took her pulse, he confirmed that both Yu Wan and the child were unharmed.

No sooner had the physician left than Yuan Zhe entered, saying that Prince Ping had invited Zhao Xuanyou to his residence for a talk.

"His Highness probably wants us to endure this in silence."

Zhao Xuanyou neither agreed nor disagreed. He reached out and tucked a strand of hair behind Yu Wan’s ear.

"You eat something, take a nap, and when you wake up, I’ll be back."

Yu Wan nodded.

She poured a cup of tea for Zhao Xuanyou. After he drank it, he left without even changing his clothes.

"Has Ah Kun returned?" Yu Wan asked.

"I’ve been in the courtyard all along and haven’t seen Young Master Ah Kun. I’ll go ask Yuan Qing." Autumn Moon helped Yu Wan remove her cloak and went out to deliver the message. Soon, Yuan Qing arrived with Wen Kun.

Yu Wan saw that Wen Kun’s expression was somewhat strange. With a glance, she signaled Autumn Moon and Yuan Qing to leave.

"You look like something’s wrong. What happened?"

Wen Kun sat down beside Yu Wan and answered evasively, "Are you alright?"

"I’m fine. I wasn’t scared."

"I was careless today," Wen Kun said, filled with regret. "I shouldn’t have been so far from you."

Recalling the scene in the plum forest, Yu Wan also felt a lingering fear.

"It was indeed urgent at the time. If it weren’t for Miss Miaotong’s help, I might have really been pulled down. I’m fine, but Miaotong was injured. I should prepare a generous gift and visit her later." After saying this, Yu Wan looked up at Wen Kun. "What happened after you went down the mountain? How did you bring that eunuch back?"

"When I went to save you, my mask was caught on a plum tree branch and fell off. The eunuch saw my face, so I brought him back first."

So that was it.

After thinking for a moment, Yu Wan asked again, "Did Miss Miaotong see your face?"

Wen Kun let out a barely audible "mm."

There were many servants in the Marquis’s residence, and loose lips were inevitable. When Wen Kun was in the residence, he rarely wore a mask, usually using the same human skin mask to disguise himself.

"Did you reveal your identity to her when you saved her?"

"I said I was your guard."

"Then there’s no problem. When I visit the Liang residence next time, I’ll explain it to her."

Since Noble Consort Li had suppressed the matter, the palace wouldn’t send anyone to question Liang Miaotong.

However, trespassing in the Jade Illumination Garden was a capital offense. If Liang Miaotong told her parents, it might cause unnecessary trouble.

After thinking for a moment, Yu Wan said, "I’ll go to the Liang residence tomorrow."

Wen Kun remained silent.

Yu Wan guessed that he was upset because someone had seen his face. In truth, she had always had an idea in mind but had refrained from bringing it up out of consideration for Wen Kun’s feelings.

Since the topic had come up now, she might as well bring it up.

"Ah Kun?"

"Hmm?"

"The imperial physicians in the palace are highly skilled. Previously, even the young lady from the Princess’s residence who was poisoned and nearly beyond saving was revived by them. Would you like me to ask your brother-in-law to arrange for an imperial physician to take a look at you?"

"Look at what?" Wen Kun asked instinctively. Only after the words left his mouth did he realize what she meant. He stared at Yu Wan. "Do you find me ugly now?"

Yu Wan shot him an annoyed glance. "Do you think that’s what I meant?"

Wen Kun muttered, "I’ve gotten used to being ugly."

"Then you don’t want to see an imperial physician?"

"No." Wen Kun turned his face away. "Besides, who am I? Can I just see an imperial physician whenever I want?"

"You’re my brother. If you want treatment, the imperial physician will help you."

"No."

This answer didn’t surprise Yu Wan. If Wen Kun wasn’t willing, there was nothing she could do.

Yu Wan had hoped he would try to treat his birthmark, but since he was so stubborn, she couldn’t force him.

"Suit yourself."

After Wen Kun left, Yu Wan sat at the table, thinking about the day’s events. After finishing her swallow’s nest soup, she lay down on the couch to sleep, as Zhao Xuanyou had instructed before leaving.

She slept very deeply.

When she opened her eyes, the Tangli Courtyard was still quiet.

"Madame is awake."

The night watch maid, Pan Xia, approached the couch and helped Yu Wan sit up.

"What time is it?"

"It’s already the Hai hour (around 9-11 PM)."

Already the Hai hour?

Hadn’t he said that when she woke up, she would see him?

"Has the Marquis returned?" Yu Wan asked.

Pan Xia poured a cup of warm water and handed it to Yu Wan, respectfully replying, "The Marquis returned half an hour ago. Seeing that Madame was asleep, he told us not to disturb you."

"Where is he now?"

"The Marquis and Young Master Ah Kun have both left the residence," Pan Xia added, "Yuan Qing also told us not to say anything, but I’m only telling Madame."

So late at night, what were Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Kun doing outside?

chapters.title: The Stolen Kiss
chapters.content:
When Liang Miaofeng returned to Prince Rui’s residence, she saw the lights on inside and hesitated for a moment.

"Is the Prince here?"

The maid replied, "Yes."

Liang Miaofeng entered the room and saw Zhao Qi sitting under the lamp reading a book. She approached and called out, "Your Highness."

Zhao Qi looked up, closed the book, and seeing the fatigue in her eyes, asked, "The servants said your sister had an accident? How is she?"

"She fell off the mountain while admiring the plum blossoms at Yuzhao Garden. I took her home, so I returned late."

Zhao Qi frowned. "Is she badly injured?"

"Her shin hit a tree trunk and broke, but her life is not in danger. She just needs to rest for two or three months."

"His Majesty gave me some palace medicines the other day. Tomorrow, send someone to take some to the Liang residence."

"Thank you, Your Highness."

Seeing that Liang Miaofeng was in low spirits, Zhao Qi stood up and said, "You should go to bed early."

As Zhao Qi passed by her, Liang Miaofeng suddenly reached out and grabbed his sleeve.

"Is there something else?" Zhao Qi turned his head to look at her.

Liang Miaofeng recalled Yu Wan’s encouragement that day, feeling somewhat hesitant.

She didn’t have the courage to take the initiative to ask Zhao Qi to consummate their marriage, but at least she could ask him to stay the night here.

"Your Highness, can you stay here tonight?"

Previously, the two times Zhao Qi had stayed overnight were his own initiative; Liang Miaofeng had never asked.

Sensing Zhao Qi’s hesitation, Liang Miaofeng immediately regretted it.

Yu Wan said to take the initiative, but that was because she was the kind of girl everyone liked. Both Zhao Qi and Zhao Xuanyou admired her, so she could say whatever she wanted.

But what about herself?

Zhao Qi didn’t like her. The two times he had stayed here were just to give her some face. He felt...

"Alright."

Just as Liang Miaofeng was in deep distress, Zhao Qi unexpectedly agreed.

Seeing Liang Miaofeng staring at him blankly, Zhao Qi looked at her silently for a moment, then turned his face away and sat back at the table to read.

Liang Miaofeng was overjoyed. She ordered the maids to prepare hot water for a bath and personally brought Zhao Qi a quilt, placing a small hand warmer in his bed.

When Zhao Qi went to bathe, she didn’t dare to attend to him. She removed her hairpins and sat blankly in front of the dressing mirror.

Only when the maid said Zhao Qi had already gone to bed did she wash up, change into her nightclothes, and go to him.

Zhao Qi had already closed his eyes. Liang Miaofeng climbed onto the bed from the foot and lay down on the other pillow.

The maid silently lowered the bed curtains and blew out the warm yellow candlelight.

They had shared a bed several times before, and that was all.

Each slept on their own pillow, under their own quilt.

"Your Highness." Perhaps because today had gone smoothly, Liang Miaofeng gathered her courage and spoke again.

"Hmm?"

"Actually, Tong'er’s fall from the mountain today was not an accident."

In the darkness, Liang Miaofeng secretly inched a little closer to Zhao Qi, clutching the quilt.

"Not an accident? What do you mean?"

"Today, when we were walking down the mountain with the Marchioness of Jingyuan, a eunuch carrying a flower vase came towards us. When he reached the Marchioness, he dropped the vase and it flew towards her. After she dodged, he actually reached out to try to pull her down the mountain..."

"Did something happen to her?" Zhao Qi interrupted, suddenly turning to look at her.

"Your Highness, rest assured. The Marchioness is safe. During the struggle, Tong'er fell down the mountain."

Zhao Qi felt slightly relieved upon hearing this, but soon realized something was off.

Why would Liang Miaofeng tell him to rest assured? That tone...

"How did you end up walking with her?"

"Sister Yi’an once told me that Your Highness and the Marchioness had some connection. Out of curiosity, I struck up a conversation with her. Unexpectedly, we got along quite well and admired the flowers together." Since she had already said this much, Liang Miaofeng decided to come clean.

She had wanted to know Zhao Qi’s feelings for Yu Wan.

But hearing the urgency in Zhao Qi’s voice just now, she understood; Zhao Qi still hadn’t let go of Yu Wan.

Even though Liang Miaofeng had prepared herself for this, she couldn’t help but shed tears upon confirming that her husband’s heart belonged to another woman.

"Yi’an? She came to you to talk about Yu Wan?" Zhao Qi knew nothing good would come from Yi’an’s involvement and was about to curse, but then he heard soft sobbing. "You... what’s wrong?"

"I’m fine."

Hearing the tears in her voice, Zhao Qi felt a headache coming on, as well as a touch of panic.

"Don’t listen to Yi’an’s nonsense. The Marchioness and I... there’s nothing between us. She doesn’t even like me."

"And what about you, Your Highness?"

"I..." Zhao Qi choked for a moment, recalling all the memories with Yu Wan, feeling a dull ache in his heart. "I’ve said it already. She doesn’t like me. What else can I do?"

These words were naturally painful for Liang Miaofeng to hear.

She quietly wiped her tears with the corner of the quilt, trying her best not to cry anymore.

She didn’t want to cling or force anything. Continuing this conversation would only humiliate herself.

However, the quilt covering her face was suddenly lifted.

In the darkness, she met Zhao Qi’s dark eyes.

"You’ve been crying?"

Liang Miaofeng was extremely beautiful, and at this moment, with tears in her eyes, there was a soft and moving charm about her.
