Zhao Xuanyou had rested for several more days, but after returning to the capital, a lot of official business had piled up, and he resumed his days of leaving early and returning late.

Yu Wan, under the guidance of the Old Madame, took on the responsibilities of the Madame of the Marquis Estate. She had to account for the harvests from the fields and shops, arrange the items needed for the New Year celebrations at the Marquis Estate, and prepare New Year gifts for the various relatives and friends.

Fortunately, she was a new bride and pregnant, so although the Old Madame was teaching her, she also had her father-in-law and Concubine Wei help manage the account room affairs, with Wen Tao assisting from the side. Yu Wan also took this opportunity to put her four personal maids to use.

Even so, Yu Wan had no more opportunities to go out.

No matter how others helped, as the mistress of the Marquis Estate, she had to be informed about all matters to have a clear understanding and handle things with ease.

Although it was hard work, the New Year at the Jingyuan Marquis Estate was very lively.

The Old Madame was in good health, Zhao Xuanyou was an official of the second rank, and the Marquis Estate had three generations living together in harmony. Next year, there would even be four generations under one roof, which was something to look forward to.

The whole family accompanied the Old Madame in staying up late on New Year's Eve. After the old year passed and the new year began, the couple set off firecrackers at the entrance of the Marquis Estate before heading to the Tangli Courtyard.

At this moment, the capital was filled with a joyful and festive atmosphere, and the sound of firecrackers could be heard from far and near.

Yu Wan, holding Zhao Xuanyou's hand as they walked forward, suddenly felt a bit distracted.

As she was lost in thought, her feet suddenly left the ground as Zhao Xuanyou picked her up horizontally.

"It's snowing," Zhao Xuanyou said softly.

There was a light dusting of snow on the ground, and he was worried about Yu Wan slipping, so he decided to carry her back.

Yu Wan held onto his shoulder with one hand and opened the other, and soon a cold snowflake drifted into her palm.

It was small, but its shape was still beautiful.

"What are you thinking about?" he asked.

Yu Wan smiled slightly and kissed him on the chin.

"Some old memories."

That New Year's Eve, Zhao Xuanyou had stayed at the Marquis Estate to celebrate the New Year with his grandmother, while she, along with Wen Tao, Bingyun, and Yangquan, had quietly sneaked into the Xingguo Duke Estate, beginning an adventure.

chapters.title: A Myriad of Lights
chapters.content:
Just as he was about to say something to Yuxuan, he saw her yawn.

Zhao Xuanyou knew she had been exhausted during the last month of the year. Tonight, she had insisted on staying up with her grandmother to welcome the New Year and set off firecrackers with him, which had pushed her to the limit.

He carried Yuxuan back to the Tangli Courtyard, tucked her in, and lay down beside her.

On the first day of the New Year, Yuxuan slept in late, while Zhao Xuanyou went to the palace early to pay his respects.

Yuxuan went to Leshou Hall to wish her grandmother a Happy New Year, then sent a servant to Yunshui Nunnery to donate a large sum for incense offerings. Just as she was having lunch, Zhao Xuanyou returned.

He sat beside Yuxuan, let her feed him a mouthful of fish soup, and then said, "When I left the palace, His Majesty specifically instructed me to bring you to the palace to enjoy the lanterns on the Lantern Festival."

Yuxuan asked in surprise, "His Majesty?"

"Yes, it's for Zhao Yi Yun. I suppose he mentioned it to His Majesty before, which is why there was this decree. The palace's festival celebrations are lively, with all kinds of exquisite lanterns that can't be seen among the common people. I think you'll be interested. As for other concerns, with me by your side, nothing will happen."

With him accompanying her, Yuxuan had nothing to worry about.

Moreover, Princess Yi'an, who had repeatedly caused trouble before, had been suffering from nightmares and had not recovered. Consort Li had sent her to a Taoist temple for cultivation to calm her mind, and no one knew when she would return to the capital.

Yuxuan still did not go out during the New Year, only hosting relatives twice at the Marquis's residence, and inviting Chen Da Niu and Xiu Fang over once.

On the day of the Lantern Festival, Zhao Xuanyou took Yuxuan to the palace before dark.

As the saying goes, "Once bitten, twice shy." When Yuxuan passed through the grand palace halls again, her state of mind was very calm.

After paying their respects to the Emperor and Consort Li at the Qianqing Palace, a eunuch quickly led them to the place to view the lanterns.

In front of the palace gate tower, performers from the Southern Office were presenting a dance, which was captivating.

In Zhao Xuanyou's view, these songs and dances were no different from previous years, but it was the first time Yuxuan had seen them, and she watched intently.

Zhao Xuanyou accompanied her for a long time until the songs and dances ended, then they walked towards the gate tower.

At this time, many people were already standing on the city wall, including the imperial concubines, royal family members, court officials, and their wives.

The Emperor and Consort Li were still in the Qianqing Palace, and Prince Ping was hosting the event here, surrounded by a crowd like the moon among stars.

Zhao Xuanyou was afraid that someone might bump into Yuxuan and the child, so he did not go near Prince Ping. Instead, he took Yuxuan to the edge of the crowd.

Both sides of the city wall were hung with lanterns contributed by skilled craftsmen from various places, each one showcasing their life's work, truly a dazzling and spectacular sight.

However, the couple had not admired the lanterns for long when an inner attendant came over and said that Prince Ping wanted to speak with Zhao Xuanyou.

"Go ahead, I'll wait for you here."

The city tower was heavily guarded with a guard every five steps, so it was unlikely that anyone would dare to cause trouble here.

"I'll be right back."

Zhao Xuanyou followed the inner attendant away, and Yuxuan leaned against the city wall, looking out at the palace.

The lanterns outside the palace were naturally not as exquisite as those inside, but they were livelier, with the entire city filled with fish and dragon lanterns, and intersecting lights.

Thinking that among the myriad of lights, there was one that belonged to her and Zhao Xuanyou, she couldn't help but feel warm in her heart.

This year, after admiring the palace lanterns, by next year's Lantern Festival, she would have given birth to the child for several months, and she could go with Zhao Xuanyou to the streets to see the lanterns among the crowd, which would be even more interesting.

"Marquisess."

A crisp voice came from behind her. Yuxuan recognized it and turned around to see Feng Zhao Yi holding Zhao Yi Yun's hand behind her.

Yuxuan quickly curtsied, "This concubine greets Feng Zhao Yi and His Highness the Royal Grandson."

"No need for such formalities, you are with child, be careful." Feng Zhao Yi said, placing Zhao Yi Yun's small hand in Yuxuan's, "This child has been missing you for a long time. Tonight, I'll leave him in your care."

"Yes."

Seeing Yuxuan agree, Feng Zhao Yi went to join the other concubines.

Yuxuan could not squat down, so she could only lower her head to look at him.

It had been a long time since she had seen Zhao Yi Yun, and he seemed to have grown a bit taller. With Feng Zhao Yi's careful care, his complexion was much better than before, and his eyes were not as timid as when he lived in the Western Garden.

"Do you like watching lanterns, Yi Yun?"

Zhao Yi Yun nodded vigorously, "Does the Marquisess like watching lanterns?"

"I do too."

"Which one do you like the most?"

The most favorite?

Yuxuan thought carefully about the lanterns she had seen just now, then softly said, "I like the glass lantern in the front. What about you?"

Zhao Yi Yun pulled Yuxuan towards the front.

Seeing him leading her in the opposite direction of the crowd, Yuxuan was afraid that Zhao Xuanyou would not be able to find her when he returned. She told a guard nearby to inform Zhao Xuanyou of her whereabouts.

"Yi Yun, have you been here on the city tower to see these lanterns before?"

"Mmm, I came a few days ago."

Zhao Yi Yun led Yuxuan through the winding colorful lanterns, walking a long distance before stopping in front of a running horse lantern.

As the wind blew, the running horse lantern spun rapidly. Yuxuan stared at the scenes flashing on the lantern and couldn't help but feel a pang of sadness.

The lantern depicted the story of Shenxiang splitting the mountain to save his mother. Zhao Yi Yun must be missing his own mother.

But Yuxuan knew that in the last month of the year, the Emperor had already bestowed poisoned wine upon those imprisoned in the heavenly prison, not allowing them to live past the New Year.

"Yi Yun, do you know what story this is?"

"Yes, Zhao Yi Mother told me."

Yuxuan didn't know what to say for a moment.

Suddenly, Zhao Yi Yun looked up and tugged at Yuxuan's hand, "Marquisess, are my father and mother still alive?"

He didn't know yet?

Before Yuxuan could figure out what to say, Zhao Yi Yun whispered, "I heard the eunuchs talking in secret, but when I asked Zhao Yi Mother, she wouldn't tell me."

Yuxuan didn't want to lie to him, but the truth was too heavy and cruel for a child his age. How could she tell him honestly?

While she was pondering her words, Yuxuan suddenly felt that something was not quite right.

She looked around and saw Pei Ta and Zhao Qi standing not far away, both looking in her and Zhao Yi Yun's direction.

Yuxuan had thought she might encounter Pei Ta and Zhao Qi in the palace, but she hadn't expected them to be walking together.

She felt no particular emotion, but at this moment, Zhao Xuanyou was not by her side. When he came over and saw this scene, with his personality, he would inevitably tease her.

Since they had all met, Yuxuan couldn't pretend not to see them.

"Prince Rui, Minister Pei."

Yuxuan curtsied.

Zhao Yi Yun did not recognize Pei Ta. He looked at Zhao Qi and called out, "Uncle Qi."

"You need not be so polite, Marquisess." Zhao Qi felt a bit surprised at this moment.

Tonight, there was a family banquet in the palace. After the banquet, he and Liang Miaofeng came to the city tower to view the lanterns. Unintentionally, they had also seen Zhao Xuanyou and Yuxuan appreciating the songs and dances below the city tower.

After ascending the tower, Liang Miaofeng was pulled away by the other three princess consorts to chat, and he didn't want to go near Prince Ping, so he wandered to a less crowded area. He met Pei Ta and they walked together.

But they hadn't walked far before they encountered Yuxuan.

It was truly a coincidence.

chapters.title: Try and You'll Know
chapters.content:
"Uncle Qi."

Sensing the movement behind him, Zhao Yi Yun turned around and ran a few steps to Zhao Qi's side.

Since he was a child, he had always been fond of Zhao Qi. Last time in the Qianqing Palace, all the other uncles and aunts wanted to send him to the temple, but only Uncle Qi had spoken up for him.

Zhao Qi withdrew his gaze and rubbed Zhao Yi Yun's little head.

The deposed empress was the culprit who caused his mother's death, and Zhao Zun had always been at odds with him. By rights, he should stay away from Zhao Yi Yun. However, this child liked to be close to him, and unconsciously, he had also come to care for Zhao Yi Yun as his nephew.

"How did you end up here? Where is Feng Zhao Yi?"

"She is over there admiring the lanterns. She let me play with the Marquisess."

"I see."

Zhao Qi said, looking at Yuxuan.

The last time he saw her was in the Qianqing Palace. At that time, Yuxuan was holding Zhao Yi Yun and secretly gesturing to him, asking him to remind the Emperor that Zhao Yi Yun could be adopted by the Fourth Brother.

At that time, she was ordered to take care of Zhao Yi Yun, and her attire was simple and plain, with few hair ornaments.

Tonight, she had come to the palace to view the lanterns, so naturally, she was dressed more elaborately.

Looking at Yuxuan, Zhao Qi was reminded of many past events.

He had once hoped to stand on the palace city tower with Yuxuan, overlooking the magnificent streets of the capital. Now that he was truly standing here, everything was different.

Both Yuxuan and himself had changed.

The night grew darker, but the fireworks in the sky became even more dazzling.

Yuxuan saw Zhao Yi Yun looking up at the fireworks in the sky and softly asked, "Do you want to walk forward and continue looking at the lanterns, or do you want to go back to find Zhao Yi Mother?"

Zhao Yi Yun lowered his head, not knowing what he was thinking.

Pei Ta, who had been silent all along, spoke up, "This year, the Governor of Weizhou presented a 'Wansui Ao Mountain' lantern. I heard it is placed on the city tower of Yuhua Gate. It should be worth seeing."

The Ao Mountain lantern was made by stacking thousands of small lanterns together, resembling the Penglai Fairy Mountain. It was complex and time-consuming to make, truly a rare sight.

Listening to his words, Yuxuan recalled the events of last year's Lantern Festival.

At that time, she and Pei Ta had already set their wedding date and had expectations for the future. He had told her that he would make a lantern for her with his own hands by next year's Lantern Festival.

So much had happened in the past year, catching both Pei Ta and Yuxuan off guard.

When they had reunited before, Yuxuan had still been able to handle it with composure.

But at this moment, seeing him and being reminded of their past promise by the scene, Yuxuan felt a slight tension in her heart and was indeed a little sad.

"Thank you, Minister Pei. Yuhua Gate is a bit far. I don't know if Yi Yun and I can walk that far. Let's just go with the flow and see where we end up."

A complex emotion quietly surfaced in Yuxuan's heart.

From the initial warmth and friendliness when they first met, to the subtle feelings that arose upon reuniting, and then their meeting again in Anzhou, where they agreed to marry, only to end up on separate paths in the end; many things were beyond their personal control.

Yuxuan had already made her decision, but being reminded of the past still gave rise to a sense of guilt.

"Let's just walk and see. That's fine too."

Pei Ta's tone was gently warm, a familiarity long lost.

During their two meetings in the capital, Yuxuan could hear the disappointment and sadness in his voice.

But at this moment, he had somewhat regained the calm and scholarly demeanor he had when they first met at the Lichuan Travel Palace.

"Do you want to go see it?"

Zhao Xuanyou's voice came from the side.

Yuxuan turned her head, and the emotions that had been weighing on her heart quietly faded away.

"The lanterns in the palace all seem quite extraordinary to me. Any one of them looks good. Yi Yun, do you want to go see it?"

"Yes," Zhao Yi Yun said softly.

He had never seen a Wansui Ao Mountain lantern before. Earlier, he had thought Yuxuan didn't want to go, so he hadn't said anything.

Now that Zhao Xuanyou suggested going, he gathered his courage and told the truth.

"Then let's slowly walk over there."

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement, nodded slightly at Zhao Qi and Pei Ta, and took Yuxuan and Zhao Yi Yun forward.

Zhao Qi had not spoken the whole time. After the three of them walked away, he patted Pei Ta on the shoulder and said with a light smile, "Let's go somewhere else."

Pei Ta averted his gaze, nodded, and followed Zhao Qi in the opposite direction.

Yuxuan turned her head to look at Zhao Xuanyou and teased, "Aren't you angry?"

In the past, in such situations, Zhao Xuanyou would always be jealous and treat Pei Ta with great disdain.

But today, he seemed quite calm.

Zhao Xuanyou lightly hmphed, "Do you really think I'm such a petty person?"

Yuxuan smiled, "I'm just putting myself in your shoes."

"Oh?" Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow, looking at Yuxuan with interest. "So, you're the one who gets jealous?"

"You can try and find out."

Zhao Xuanyou grabbed Yuxuan's other hand and secretly pinched her palm.

Try what? He wasn't stupid.

Fireworks bloomed one after another in the night sky. The two stopped talking and looked up to admire them for a while before continuing forward.

"Marquisess, are you tired?" Zhao Yi Yun asked softly. "Actually, I don't need to see the Ao Mountain lantern."

"Are you tired, Yi Yun?" Yuxuan asked gently.

Zhao Yi Yun shook his head. He was worried about Yuxuan.

"When the Lan and Yun Madames from the Eastern Palace were pregnant, my mother told me not to pester them to play anymore, and not to bump into them. I have to be careful."

Huaiyue had truly raised her child well.

But Huaiyue and the Lan and Yun Madames Zhao Yi Yun mentioned were all already deceased.

"I'm not tired. However, if you are tired, you can ask the Marquis to carry you."

Yuxuan was in good physical condition, and the palace roads were clean and not slippery, so walking to Yuhua Gate would not be difficult for her.

Zhao Yi Yun looked at Zhao Xuanyou carefully upon hearing this.

Compared to Yuxuan's gentle smile, he had always been afraid of Zhao Xuanyou.

During the month they spent together in the Western Garden, Zhao Yi Yun was well aware that the only time the cold and icy eyes of the Marquis of Jingyuan showed any tenderness was when he looked at the Marquisess.

Sure enough, as soon as Yuxuan finished speaking, the Marquis of Jingyuan reached out and picked him up.

Zhao Yi Yun didn't say anything, just held onto him tightly.

Before the Emperor and his father were in trouble, everyone in the palace liked to hold him. But after that, apart from Zhao Xuanyou and Yuxuan, no one else had held him.

Feng Zhao Yi was in poor health and would be out of breath after walking a short distance.

And the Emperor, when summoning him, would only talk to him from afar, no longer lifting him onto his lap to play as he had before.

If those two were like this, it went without saying for the others in the palace.

Yuxuan's gaze flickered unintentionally, and she caught sight of the tears in Zhao Yi Yun's eyes.

She sighed in her heart and took out a handkerchief to wipe his tears.

Zhao Yi Yun sniffled and said, "Marquis, you don't have to carry me. I can walk by myself."

"He has the strength, don't worry." Yuxuan said with a smile to comfort him.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at her, the corners of his mouth twitching, "Indeed, he has plenty of strength. Carrying one more person like you wouldn't be a problem."

Zhao Yi Yun was stunned for a moment, then asked curiously, "Can the Marquis carry two people?"

Realizing what Zhao Xuanyou was about to do, Yuxuan immediately tried to dodge to the side.

Zhao Xuanyou, still carrying Zhao Yi Yun, pursued her relentlessly. With his long legs, he quickly caught up to Yuxuan, pulled her into his arms, and then lifted her up as well.

"Put me down quickly."

Yuxuan wasn't doubting his strength, but even though there were fewer people admiring the lanterns here, there were still many guards on the city tower. If they saw Zhao Xuanyou carrying two people, it wouldn't look good.

"The Marquis really is strong." Zhao Yi Yun sincerely admired.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at Yuxuan's rare panic and felt even more pleased with himself. He carried both of them and continued walking forward.

But they hadn't walked far when they saw someone standing ahead, smiling at them.

chapters.title: Eternal Longevity
chapters.content:
"Your Majesty."

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan turned toward the voice and saw the Emperor standing not far away, supported by Eunuch Liu.

After the case of the deposed empress and crown prince's poisoning and treason was resolved, the original staff of Qianqing Palace were released, and Eunuch Liu was reinstated as the chief eunuch, attending to the Emperor once more.

In the presence of the Emperor, they dared not continue their play. Zhao Xuanyou immediately set Yu Wan and Zhao Yi Yun down, and the three of them bowed to the Emperor.

Zhao Yi Yun glanced timidly at the Emperor and softly called out, "Royal Grandfather."

"No need for formalities, rise." The Emperor looked at the three of them, a smile appearing on his face for the first time in a long while. "Have you come here for some peace and quiet as well?"

It turned out the Emperor had not gone to the main palace gate with Consort Li to see the lanterns, but had come alone to view the Wan Sui Ao Shan lantern here.

Zhao Xuanyou respectfully replied, "This subject heard that the Wan Sui Ao Shan lantern is grand in scale, majestic in momentum, and carries the meaning of eternal longevity. I came specifically to pay my respects."

The Emperor smiled, gazing at the magnificent Wan Sui Ao Shan lantern, his eyes filled with deep meaning.

After he was poisoned, although the imperial physicians discovered it in time, the poison was potent. Even a small amount on Yao Yao's forehead had caused great harm to the body, and he had not yet recovered.

The imperial physicians did not dare to speak of it, but he knew he would never recover to his former state. Tasting the words "eternal longevity," he felt a mix of emotions.

What eternal longevity? It was uncertain if he could even live another five years.

After a moment of silence, the Emperor reached out and gently patted Zhao Yi Yun's head, then called Zhao Xuanyou to accompany him toward the city wall.

Guessing that the Emperor and his minister had words to exchange, Yu Wan took Zhao Yi Yun's hand and walked in the opposite direction.

"Yi Yun, that walking lantern depicts the Legend of the White Snake. You told me that story before."

Before Zhao Yi Yun could answer, Yu Wan noticed his downcast expression and asked, "What's wrong?"

Zhao Yi Yun shook his head, refusing to speak.

Yu Wan guessed it was because of the Emperor.

To Zhao Yi Yun, the Emperor had ordered the arrest of his grandmother and parents, and was no longer as affectionate as before. In his heart, he likely harbored some resentment toward the Emperor.

He was still too young to understand that the current situation was already a great show of favor from the Emperor.

Yu Wan wanted to comfort him, but the Emperor was nearby, and the surroundings were filled with the Emperor's eyes and ears. She couldn't say much.

Moreover, even if she did, Zhao Yi Yun might not understand. She had to give up.

To Yu Wan's surprise, Zhao Yi Yun quickly put away his sorrowful emotions and tugged at her hand. "Madame Hou, I heard Consort Zhao say that you and Lord Hou will be leaving the capital?"

"Yes, Lord Hou is a military general appointed by His Majesty to guard the border. He cannot stay in the capital for long."

"Are you leaving too?"

Yu Wan nodded. "I am Lord Hou's wife. Naturally, I will be with him."

Zhao Yi Yun seemed to understand but didn't quite, falling silent for a moment before asking, "Then when can I see you again?"

"We will return to the capital every one or two years for the New Year. If we come back next year, we can watch the lanterns together during the Lantern Festival."

"Mmm."

The two of them watched the lanterns together for a long time before Zhao Xuanyou finally returned.

"Where is His Majesty?" Yu Wan asked softly.

"The night wind is too strong. His Majesty has already returned to the palace."

Zhao Xuanyou picked up Zhao Yi Yun with one hand and held Yu Wan's hand with the other, returning to the main gate of the imperial palace. By this time, it was getting late, and the officials had already started leaving the palace. Most of the people had dispersed, but Prince Ping and Consort Li were still there.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou carrying Zhao Yi Yun, Prince Ping, who rarely showed affection, teased Zhao Yi Yun.

After Yu Wan returned Zhao Yi Yun to Consort Feng, she turned back and saw Prince Ping still talking to Zhao Xuanyou. She stood alone, watching the lanterns.

Rui Wang's wife, Liang Miaofeng, saw her standing alone and came over to chat.

Yu Wan glanced at her and saw that her complexion was good. She smiled and said, "Wangfei, your face is as gentle as the spring wind. It seems you have been doing very well these days."

Liang Miaofeng heard the teasing in Yu Wan's words but was not annoyed. Instead, she laughed. "Indeed, there are no worries. It's also thanks to Madame Hou's auspicious words last time."

Compared to the lukewarm relationship she had with Zhao Qi when they first got married, their relationship had improved significantly.

"Zhao Qi spends every meal with me when he is at the residence and stays overnight in my courtyard. We have more and more to talk about."

"I told you, His Highness was already smitten. He just couldn't bring himself to admit it. If you just crook your finger at him, he can't resist."

Yu Wan was very happy for Liang Miaofeng. Liang Miaofeng's heart raced.

She knew Yu Wan misunderstood. She and Zhao Qi had not yet consummated their marriage. But she had already told Yu Wan about it once, and Yu Wan had given her advice. There was no need to repeat the same thing in front of Yu Wan.

Moreover, the problem was different now.

In the past, she didn't understand Zhao Qi and couldn't figure out the crux of their issues.

Now... she wanted to solve the problem herself.

After chatting for a while, Zhao Xuanyou finally extricated himself from Prince Ping. The couple bade farewell to Liang Miaofeng and left the palace.

Once they were in the Hou residence's carriage, Yu Wan asked, "Will Prince Ping be unhappy that you and Zhao Yi Yun are getting too close?"

"He doesn't care much about Zhao Yi Yun now."

After Liu Quan returned to Qianqing Palace, the Emperor was once again surrounded by his own confidants. Seeing that his three younger brothers had begun to assist in governing the country, Prince Ping naturally felt some panic.

"He explained to me about urging me to return to Yuzhou, saying that if I was willing, he could find another reason to keep me in the capital until after you give birth."

"Should we stay?"

Yu Wan was determined to stay by Zhao Xuanyou's side.

"He said that, but His Majesty probably wants me to return to Yuzhou."

Yu Wan was slightly startled, recalling that the Emperor had called Zhao Xuanyou aside earlier to discuss this.

"It's better to return early."

Although she was pregnant and traveling hundreds of miles posed some risks, she did want to return to Yuzhou as soon as possible.

Missing her mother was one reason, but more importantly, the situation in the court might be unstable. Only by returning to Yuzhou, with Zhao Xuanyou's troops by their side, could their family live in peace.

In case of any changes in the court, they could advance or retreat as needed.

Yu Wan did not say these words to Zhao Xuanyou, but she knew he thought the same.

With just a glance, Zhao Xuanyou curved his lips and pulled her into his arms.

"His Majesty has bestowed a medical woman. With her taking care of you on the way back to Yuzhou, we can be more at ease."

In the common folk, most physicians were men, and the same was true for the Imperial Physicians' Office.

However, to facilitate the daily care of the empresses and concubines, the Imperial Physicians' Office specifically selected some clever palace maids to study gynecological medicine.

The Emperor bestowing a medical woman to the Hou residence was indeed a great honor.

Thinking of the earlier encounter with the Emperor, Yu Wan said, "Perhaps we have benefited from Yi Yun's presence."

Zhao Xuanyou lightly hummed in agreement and said no more.

As the Hou residence's carriage rolled away, Liang Miaofeng was still standing on the palace city tower, blowing in the cold wind.

The number of people on the city wall was decreasing, but she didn't know where Zhao Qi had gone.

She sighed softly, feeling a sense of loss.

Earlier, she had boasted in front of Yu Wan that everything was going well, but in the short time since then, she seemed to have been forgotten by Zhao Qi once again...

---

chapters.title: The One in My Heart
chapters.content:
"Has Prince Rui not arrived yet?" Princess Ping, who was in charge of entertaining the ladies today, saw Liang Miaofeng standing alone and asked with a smile, "Shall I send someone to inquire?"

"Thank you, Sister-in-law."

Liang Miaofeng didn't want to trouble others, but since it was so late, she needed to know if Zhao Qi had returned to the prince's residence first.

The palace was filled with palace maids and eunuchs, and every movement was noticed. Princess Ping had asked, and the eunuch quickly returned with a message, saying that Zhao Qi had found a quiet place to drink with Pei Ta.

So he had forgotten about her.

Liang Miaofeng steeled herself and thanked Princess Ping, deciding to return to the prince's residence first.

Princess Ping noticed her low spirits and advised, "The seventh prince used to receive a lot of guidance from Minister Pei in his studies, and they have worked together on official business. It's been a long time since they've seen each other, so they are probably drinking and catching up. Sister-in-law, don't take it to heart."

Although Prince Ping and Zhao Qi's brotherly relationship was not great, Liang Miaofeng was gentle and kind, and she spoke and acted in a way that pleased others, never gossiping about others. Princess Ping got along well with her.

"Thank you for your concern, Sister-in-law."

Liang Miaofeng bade farewell to Prince Ping and his wife, then returned to the prince's residence alone in her carriage.

Her mind was in turmoil. After entering the room, she hastily wiped her face and changed into her sleeping clothes, intending to go to bed. Then she heard a maid say that Zhao Qi had returned.

"Prince." She forced herself to perk up and step forward, but after saying these two words, she silently retreated to the side.

Zhao Qi's eyebrow twitched slightly, noticing her unusual mood. He recalled that they had entered the palace together but had not watched the lanterns together. He opened his mouth to explain, "Tonight, I met Minister Pei, and we talked about many old times. I lost track of time and forgot. By the time I returned to the city tower, you had already left."

This explanation was within Liang Miaofeng's expectations. Their marital relationship was fragile, and it wasn't just today. Often, he would leave her with a perfunctory excuse and then turn away.

Liang Miaofeng, out of her admiration for Zhao Qi and his noble status as a prince, never dared to show her grievances.

Even tonight, she didn't say much, only forcing a smile, "I see. It's late. Prince, you should go and rest."

This was her way of dismissing him.

In the past, whenever he came to see Liang Miaofeng, she would always invite him to stay overnight. Tonight's reaction clearly showed she was unhappy.

Zhao Qi looked at her as she lowered her eyes and remained silent, wanting to say something but swallowing his words. He turned and walked out of the room toward his study.

But as he walked out of the courtyard, he paused and looked back at the house.

The lights inside were already out. The maidservant waiting under the eaves looked at him nervously.

Zhao Qi didn't speak, waving his hand at the maid.

"Prince." The maid lowered her head and walked forward.

"When did the Princess return?"

"About the time it takes for an incense stick to burn after the Prince returned."

So she had waited on the city wall for that long.

Zhao Qi had indeed had a great time chatting with Pei Ta tonight, but he hadn't considered Liang Miaofeng at all.

Qing Dai, the maidservant who had served Liang Miaofeng for a long time, knew her mistress's thoughts well. Seeing that Zhao Qi seemed about to leave, she hurriedly said, "Tonight is the Lantern Festival, a joyous occasion. This servant takes the liberty to invite the Prince to rest here."

It was presumptuous for a servant to say such things to her master, and Zhao Qi frowned slightly upon hearing it.

Liang Miaofeng clearly did not want him to stay, and he had just come out of the room. If he went back, wouldn't he face her cold gaze again?

Zhao Qi walked forward but then turned back, entering the room directly.

After that time Liang Miaofeng had kissed him, although they had both pretended it never happened, their interactions had become much more harmonious. Zhao Qi often stayed overnight, and even without lights in the room, he easily found his way to the bed.

But standing by the bed, Zhao Qi hesitated.

He had already explained what he could. He didn't know what else to say.

"Qing Dai, I'm fine. You may leave."

The voice was trembling, seemingly laced with tears. Zhao Qi felt something was amiss. He abruptly lifted the curtain and sat on the edge of the bed, pulling the person hiding under the covers up.

Liang Miaofeng was surprised at first, but then she saw Zhao Qi's face clearly.

"Prince?"

Zhao Qi didn't speak, reaching out to touch her cheek. Indeed, it was wet with tears.

Liang Miaofeng was surprised that Zhao Qi had returned. Her heart was filled with mixed emotions. She lowered her head and used the corner of the blanket to secretly wipe away her tears.

"I'm not feeling well. Prince, please rest in the study tonight."

"I did indeed chat too much with Minister Pei tonight. I didn't mean to leave you waiting there. It was my fault. I should have sent someone to inform you."

"I understand."

Zhao Qi earnestly explained, but Liang Miaofeng's indifferent response frustrated him. "If you're angry, just let it out. Why hide in the blankets and cry?"

Liang Miaofeng looked up at Zhao Qi, meeting his cold eyes, and was at a loss for words.

She was angry, but could she express it freely?

In the darkness, their gazes collided silently. Zhao Qi said, "Don't always stay silent like this."

"Usually at the residence, I speak three sentences before the Prince answers one. I wonder if the Prince is the same with Madame Jingyuan?"

Liang Miaofeng said softly.

She knew Zhao Qi was dissatisfied with her reaction.

To Zhao Qi, he had already lowered himself to coax her, so she should accept his good intentions and maintain their mutually respectful demeanor.

Under normal circumstances, Liang Miaofeng would do so, but tonight, after seeing Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou, watching Zhao Xuanyou's attentive care for Yu Wan, she couldn't help but wonder how Zhao Qi had treated Yu Wan in the past.

Liang Miaofeng's words were like a basin of ice water poured over Zhao Qi.

He furrowed his brows fiercely, like a wild beast whose tail had been stepped on.

"Why bring her up?"

Liang Miaofeng met his gaze without flinching, staring straight at him.

"If tonight the person accompanying the Prince to the palace to see the lanterns was Madame Hou, would the Prince have left her alone on the city tower and gone to a quiet place to drink with friends without a word?"

Zhao Qi did not answer. He couldn't answer, and his eyes suddenly became flustered.

After being rejected by Yu Wan in Yuzhou, he had indeed tried to let go of his feelings for her and remove her from his heart.

After getting married, he was even more determined to break free from his emotional demon and live a good life with Liang Miaofeng.

He had always thought he was doing well. Every time he saw Yu Wan, his emotions were calmer.

But Liang Miaofeng's question left him speechless.

In the past, he had longed to bring Yu Wan to the imperial city wall to see the lanterns. If tonight the person accompanying him to the palace to see the lanterns was Yu Wan, he wouldn't have left her alone because he met a friend.

"Miaofeng, I..." Zhao Qi still wanted to explain, subconsciously reaching for her hand, but his tone was somewhat stiff.

"Prince, there's no need to say anything." Liang Miaofeng pushed his hand away.

She turned her face away, moving farther apart. The sharp gaze she had when confronting Zhao Qi quickly dimmed.

So he still didn't care for her.

Even if he stayed overnight, even if he explained, even if their relationship had improved a lot, it was just a marital facade that needed to be maintained because of the Emperor's bestowed marriage.

He had never considered her as the one in his heart.

chapters.title: Spring Arrives
chapters.content:
After returning from the palace lantern festival, Yu Wan resumed her secluded life, never stepping outside.

By the time the case at the Central Army Governor's residence was concluded, it was already the second day of the third lunar month.

Spring was warming, flowers were in full bloom, and the ice and snow on the official roads had long since melted; it was the perfect time to return to Yu Province.

After discussing with the old Marquis, Zhao Xuanyou quickly made the necessary preparations.

Yu Wan was pregnant and couldn’t travel hastily. As a military officer, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t accompany her at a leisurely pace to Yu Province. They had no choice but to split into two groups.

Zhao Xuanyou would take the guards and ride ahead to Yu Province first. The old Marquis, Concubine Wei, and Wen Bo would accompany Yu Wan at a slower pace. Though they would depart on the same day, Yu Wan’s group would arrive in Yu Province a month later than Zhao Xuanyou.

With the old Marquis and Wen Bo by her side, Zhao Xuanyou felt somewhat at ease.

But to be extra cautious, he found a maidservant skilled in martial arts for Yu Wan. After all, men and women were different, and in many situations, a maidservant could attend to her more conveniently.

With this arrangement, plus the presence of the residence’s physicians and medical attendants, Zhao Xuanyou finally felt reassured.

Zhao Xuanyou handled all the departure arrangements, so Yu Wan didn’t have to worry about a thing. Thinking of her imminent departure from the capital, she sent invitations to Princess Yinning and Wangfei Liang Miaofeng of the Rui Prince’s residence to come to the Marquis’s estate to enjoy the flowers.

Princess Yinning arrived with her daughter, but from the Rui Prince’s residence, it was Liang Miaotong who came holding the invitation.

After inquiring, Liang Miaotong explained that her mother had been unwell lately, and her elder sister had returned to the Liang residence to attend to her. That was why the invitation had been delivered from the prince’s residence to the Liang residence.

Lady Liang, thinking that Miaotong had been recovering from her injuries and hadn’t gone out for a long time, allowed her to visit the Marquis’s estate. It would serve both as an apology to Yu Wan and as an outing to enjoy the flowers and relax.

Yu Wan listened with some confusion. Liang Miaofeng was the esteemed Wangfei of the Rui Prince. Even if Lady Liang was unwell, there were still sons, daughters-in-law, and daughters at home. Why would the Wangfei need to return to her maiden home to attend to her?

Since Princess Yinning was Liang Miaofeng’s elder cousin, Yu Wan didn’t press further and simply invited them to drink tea and enjoy the flowers.

Liang Miaotong had met Princess Yinning a few times in the palace. Since Liang Miaotong was lively and clever, Princess Yinning naturally got along well with her.

After the three of them had sat and chatted for a while, Yao Yao, feeling restless in the unfamiliar environment, started fussing and demanding to go home to find her father. Princess Yinning had no choice but to take her leave.

Only Yu Wan and Liang Miaotong remained in the garden.

“Madam Hou, may I stay and play a little longer with you?” Liang Miaotong saw that Princess Yinning had left and worried that staying might inconvenience Yu Wan. But since she rarely got to go out, she truly didn’t want to return home so early. She asked Yu Wan somewhat embarrassedly.

Yu Wan smiled. “Ever since I became pregnant, I’ve been so bored staying in the Marquis’s residence. If you’re willing to stay and keep me company, I’d be overjoyed.”

After a moment’s thought, Yu Wan asked, “Do you know how to play Go?”

During her secluded days of pregnancy, Zhao Xuanyou, fearing she might be bored, had taught her how to play.

He was an expert at the game, so it was only natural that Yu Wan lost to him every time. But she noticed that he always won by just one or two pieces; clearly, he controlled the entire game, even calculating how much she would lose by. Realizing this made playing with him rather uninteresting.

“I do, but I’m not very good.”

“You don’t need to be modest. I’ve only just learned, so I’ll need you to be patient with me.”

With that, Yu Wan had Chun Xing fetch a Go board and set it up under a flowering tree. She played two games with Liang Miaotong.

As it turned out, their skills were quite evenly matched; both were mediocre, which made for an engaging back-and-forth with wins and losses on both sides.

“Is Lady Liang’s illness serious? I’ll have someone fetch a ginseng root for her to help her recover.”

“Madam Hou, there’s no need to be so polite. We have more than enough tonics at home.” Liang Miaotong glanced at Yu Wan and sighed. “Actually, my mother isn’t sick. My sister had a falling out with the Prince and wanted to stay at home for a while. My mother was afraid people would gossip about my sister, so she pretended to be ill.”

In a society that valued filial piety, if a mother was ill, even a married daughter returning home to care for her would not be criticized.

Yu Wan was slightly surprised.

During the Lantern Festival, Liang Miaofeng had been in high spirits and told Yu Wan that everything was going well.

Liang Miaotong waited for Yu Wan to place her piece, then pondered where to place her own white stone while stealing a glance at Yu Wan.

But her glance had another reason.

The Liang sisters had always been close. When Liang Miaofeng had been upset at her maiden home, crying, Liang Miaotong recalled Princess Yi’an’s earlier attempt to sow discord. She vaguely suspected that Zhao Qi might still have unresolved feelings for Yu Wan.

Given how affectionate the Marquis of Jingyuan and his wife were, it was clear without asking that Yu Wan was not involved.

But she was also worried for her sister.

She placed her piece haphazardly and asked softly, “Madam Hou, do you think the Prince is the kind of person who clings to the past?”

Yu Wan paused for a moment, understanding what Liang Miaotong was asking.

She gently shook her head, then, after some thought, shared her honest opinion.

“If it’s truly the Prince and Wangfei having a quarrel, that might actually be a good thing.”

“Why?”

“If they argue and have disagreements, it means they still engage with each other and have expectations. If there were truly no feelings left, it would be like still water; completely calm.”

“Is that so?” Liang Miaotong seemed to half-understand. “Do you and the Marquis also argue?”

“We don’t anymore, but in the past, when we fought, it was like a great battle; life and death.”

“Really?” Liang Miaotong’s eyes widened.

Too bad Yu Wan wasn’t her real sister; otherwise, she would have loved to pester her for stories about before they got married.

Yu Wan met her curious gaze and said gently, “When you have someone you like and are discussing marriage, you’ll understand.”

“Madam Hou, don’t tease me,” Liang Miaotong’s face suddenly turned red.

“This reaction… could it be that you already have someone in mind?”

“How could that be?”

Liang Miaotong answered too quickly. Yu Wan recalled her earlier suspicions about Liang Miaotong and Wen Bo and felt a little disappointed.

It seemed she had been mistaken.

“At every palace banquet, the noblewomen of high-ranking families can’t stop praising you. There must be many matchmakers visiting your home.”

Liang Miaotong was a very likable young lady, with a father who was a second-rank official and a sister who was a Wangfei. With such beauty and family background, even noble and aristocratic families would admire her.

“There are, but…”

“You don’t fancy them?”

After all, she was an unmarried girl, and discussing her own marriage in public was somewhat embarrassing. Liang Miaotong hesitated for a moment before softly saying, “My parents think it’s better to find a scholar.”

Yu Wan pondered for a moment and understood the Liang couple’s considerations.

The Liang family had only recently moved to the capital from another region. They were a family of scholars, and their financial resources were far less substantial than those of the long-established families in the capital.

Liang Miaofeng’s marriage to the Prince was an unexpected honor bestowed by the Emperor. The family itself had no intention of climbing the social ladder through marriage. Their first choice was to marry their daughters to dignified scholars.

“Do you feel the same way?”

“I…” Liang Miaotong said in distress, “Well, I don’t want to suddenly marry a stranger like my sister did.”

---

chapters.title: Sending Her Home
chapters.content:
Yu Wan had gone through so many trials with Zhao Xuanyou to reach this point, so she understood Liang Miaotong’s feelings.

Marriage had always been a matter of parental arrangement and matchmaker’s words; blind marriages where everything depended on luck.

Zhao Qi was an excellent man, but whether Miaofeng’s marriage to him was a good one was still uncertain.

Seeing her sister unhappy even after marrying into the prince’s residence naturally made Liang Miaotong overthink.

Yu Wan gently rubbed her belly, thinking that if she was carrying a girl, she would definitely find her a well-known family in the future. She would also ensure that the girl herself agreed to the marriage before allowing it, so she wouldn’t have to enter a blind marriage.

“Yu Wan.” A voice came from behind her; Wen Bo.

Yu Wan turned her head and waved at him.

Seeing that Yu Wan was sitting next to Liang Miaotong, Wen Bo hesitated for a moment before approaching.

While staying long-term in the capital at the Marquis’s residence, to prevent the servants from growing suspicious, he always used the same human-skin mask.

Naturally, Liang Miaotong had never seen this face before.

“Miaotong, this is my younger brother, Ding Bo.”

“Young Master Ding.”

Liang Miaotong stood up and greeted him.

“Bo, this is the daughter of Minister Liang.”

Wen Bo silently returned the greeting, then turned to look directly at Yu Wan. Knowing that Yu Wan had deliberately called him over to talk, he said in a low voice, “The carriages and luggage are all ready. When you have time, check if there’s anything you’ve forgotten.”

“Alright.”

Seeing that Wen Bo was ill at ease, Yu Wan let him leave.

After Wen Bo had walked away, Liang Miaotong seemed thoughtful. She smiled and asked, “Madam Hou, when are you leaving for Yu Province?”

“The Marquis has almost finished handing over his duties. We’ll leave the day after tomorrow.”

“So soon?”

Yu Wan didn’t mention that Zhao Xuanyou had to leave, and she had to go with him; she couldn’t wait even a day. She just smiled and said, “The weather is perfect now. If we wait any longer, it might get too hot.”

“That’s true.” Liang Miaotong suddenly thought of something. “Yu Province is to the west, so you’ll be leaving through the West City Gate the day after tomorrow, right?”

Yu Wan nodded.

“I’ll come to see you off.”

“There’s no need for such courtesy.”

Liang Miaotong curved her lips into a smile. “Madam Hou, don’t refuse. Otherwise, my mother won’t let me out of the house. It’s settled then.”

Yu Wan smiled in agreement.

The two played Go in the garden for a while before Madam Xing came to deliver a message: the Old Dowager had heard that Liang Miaotong was a guest at the estate and invited them to dine at Leshou Hall.

The Old Dowager had no granddaughters, so seeing a clever and lively girl like Liang Miaotong naturally made her happy. She ordered the servants to prepare a place for Liang Miaotong to take a nap at Leshou Hall and kept her at the estate for half a day longer.

Liang Miaotong, who had been cooped up at home, was delighted to linger at the Marquis’s estate until nightfall without her mother or sister around to restrain her.

Because they had discussed Wangfei Liang returning to her maiden home to attend to her “ill” mother, the Old Dowager had many tonics taken from the storage and gave them to Liang Miaotong to take home.

Liang Miaotong hadn’t planned to stay so long and had only brought one maidservant and a coachman.

Yu Wan was worried about her safety on the road at night and asked Wen Bo to escort her home.

When Wen Bo refused to move, Yu Wan said, “It’s already so late. She’s a young girl with only two servants who don’t know martial arts. What if they encounter some villains?”

“This is the capital.”

“There’s no shortage of lawsuits in the Jingzhao Prefecture.” Yu Wan wasn’t trying to tease him. She genuinely didn’t feel at ease letting Liang Miaotong return home alone at night.

She was a guest at the Marquis’s estate, so they had to ensure she was safely escorted home.

Of course, the Marquis’s estate had many guards, so it wasn’t necessary to specifically send Wen Bo. But… it was killing two birds with one stone.

Wen Bo didn’t say any more. He jumped onto the carriage and sat next to the coachman.

Watching the Liang family’s carriage disappear into the distance, Yu Wan turned around and bumped into Zhao Xuanyou’s chest.

He had returned to the estate long ago but had quietly eaten dinner at Tangli Courtyard because Yu Wan was still entertaining guests.

“You and Miss Miaotong really hit it off.”

He had originally thought that with only two guests, Yu Wan wouldn’t be occupied for long. Who knew Liang Miaotong would stay until nightfall?

Yu Wan thought for a moment. “I do get along better with Miaotong than with the Rui Wangfei.”

Compared to her calm and quiet elder sister, Liang Miaotong was lively and suited Yu Wan’s active nature better.

“Did you deliberately send Wen Bo to see her off?”

“Half and half. I feel like there’s something between them, but Wen Bo doesn’t want to talk about it, so I didn’t ask.” Yu Wan, holding Zhao Xuanyou’s hand, walked toward the estate. “If there’s truly nothing between them, they won’t talk much on the way. It won’t do any harm.”

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her and chuckled softly.

Yu Wan was intelligent and always acted naturally, without leaving a trace.

Given Wen Bo’s personality, if Liang Miaotong had no interest in him, he certainly wouldn’t let her be troubled.

Soon, the day of departure arrived.

Early in the morning, the old Marquis took them to bid farewell to the Old Dowager. The Old Dowager, of course, tearfully saw them off.

However, the Old Dowager was advanced in years and had lived comfortably in the capital for so long. She didn’t want to endure the hardships of travel to Yu Province. She only instructed Yu Wan to take care on the road and to rest locally if she felt unwell, rather than forcing herself to continue.

Yu Wan naturally agreed to all of this.

After saying goodbye to the Old Dowager, the group set off toward the city gate.

At the city gate, Liang Miaotong had indeed come to see them off, even bringing some pastries she had made herself.

Ye Moquan also came with several close friends of Zhao Xuanyou to bid farewell.

“Next year when we meet again, the two of you will be a family of three. Let’s go to the hot spring villa then.”

“Alright.” Zhao Xuanyou readily agreed.

As they spoke, someone said, “When I came over earlier, I ran into Director Pei Tuo. I thought he was also coming to see you off.”

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow but said nothing.

After the pleasantries, he cupped his hands in farewell to everyone and led the Marquis’s estate carriages out of the city gate.

But for Yu Wan, this was not a true farewell.

When they reached the pavilion ten li outside the city, Zhao Xuanyou would part ways with her.

“Wanwan.”

Before the carriage had even come to a complete stop, Zhao Xuanyou’s voice came from outside.

Understanding that the time to part had come, Yu Wan felt truly disheartened.

She tightly clutched the red bean cake in her hand, refusing to get out of the carriage or even lift the curtain; afraid she might not be able to resist begging Zhao Xuanyou to stay by her side.

She wasn’t usually sentimental, but ever since becoming pregnant, her emotions had been unstable, and she often found herself on the verge of tears.

“I’ll take care of myself. You don’t need to worry.” She held back her tears, trying to make her voice sound calm. “Be careful on your journey.”

Zhao Xuanyou, of course, didn’t want to leave Yu Wan either. But as a military officer, he had his duties and couldn’t accompany her on the slow journey.

“Mmm, I’ll wait for you in Yu Province.”

With that, he rode away.

Only when the sound of hooves had faded into the distance did Yu Wan finally lift the curtain to watch him go.

The spring sun shone warmly, and the breeze was gentle and soft.

Zhao Xuanyou rode away with the wind, his dark robe billowing.

His figure had long been imprinted in Yu Wan’s heart, but at this moment, she still couldn’t bear to look away, wishing she could follow him.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.content:
The winter in Yuzhou was bitterly cold, but the summer was even more oppressive and stifling than the capital.

Zhao Xuanyou wore a thin summer robe, sitting in the study absentmindedly flipping through a book, while an ice basin beside him slowly emitted a cool breeze.

He wasn’t usually this meticulous, but for Yu Wan and the child’s sake, he had ordered an ice cellar to be built in the Hou residence before the New Year, storing a large amount of ice blocks.

Yuan Zi, standing at the door, saw him lift his head. Without waiting for Zhao Xuanyou to ask, knowing what he wanted to know, he shook his head before Zhao could speak.

Zhao Xuanyou raised his eyebrows helplessly, picked up the book again, but couldn’t focus on a single word.

The day before, his father had sent someone ahead to report that they would arrive in Yuzhou today, telling Zhao Xuanyou not to go out to meet them and just wait at the Hou residence.

Zhao Xuanyou had ordered all the rooms to be cleaned, the kitchen had been busy since yesterday, and the ice basin had been placed today.

Everything was ready except for the final piece.

"Master!" Yuan Qing’s loud shout came from the courtyard.

Before Yuan Qing could say more, Zhao Xuanyou threw down the book in his hand and quickly walked out of the room toward the outside.

Like a gust of wind, he swept out of the Tangli Courtyard. Yuan Qing scratched his head and called out behind him, "The mistress’s carriage has arrived at the residence gate."

The sun hung high in the sky, and the tall trees on both sides of the path were wilting under the heat. Zhao Xuanyou faced the incoming heatwave, rushing all the way to the residence gate, his eyes fixed ahead, his eagerness to see that face growing more urgent.

Finally, at the residence gate, he saw the figure he had been longing for day and night.

Yu Wan wore a loose summer dress, her jet-black hair, like brocade, loosely tied in a falling horse bun. Her beautiful features showed a hint of fatigue, but her waist was noticeably thicker than when they had parted.

Before Zhao Xuanyou could call out to her, she seemed to sense something and turned her head to look his way.

The moment she saw him, a sudden gleam of joy rose in her beautiful eyes, and her face, which had been tired from days of travel, instantly brightened.

"Zhao Xuanyou."

She called his name and ran toward him.

Zhao Xuanyou quickly rushed to her side, wanting to hold her tightly but fearing it might hurt the child. He could only wrap his arm around her shoulders to steady her.

But Yu Wan paid no heed, her hands entwining around his waist like vines. Due to her large belly, she leaned sideways against his shoulder.

Feeling the familiar broad shoulders, the fatigue from the long journey dissipated with the hot wind.

"Tired?"

Yu Wan nuzzled against him greedily in his arms, then straightened up and softly said, "I’m not tired. It’s Father and Auntie who took care of me all the way and must be exhausted."

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t speak, his gaze lingering on her face for a moment before he took her hand and walked forward.

When the husband and wife reunited in an embrace, Old Marquis Zhao, Wen Sun, and Madame Wei had also entered the residence. Since they were all family, no one found it inappropriate.

"Father, Auntie, Ah Sun, thank you for taking care of Yu Wan all the way."

Zhao Xuanyou’s greeting was solemn. The Old Marquis, seeing this, quickly said, "Yu Wan is the Hou residence’s daughter-in-law. It’s only natural for us to take care of her. We’re all family; there’s no need for thanks."

"Father, the residence has prepared a meal. Let’s go eat first."

The couple hadn’t seen each other for a long time and had much to say, but they couldn’t ignore their family and just return to their courtyard.

Zhao Xuanyou led everyone to the flower hall, where the meal was already set. After everyone was seated, Zhao Xuanyou asked Yuan Qing, "Where is Mother-in-law?"

Yuan Qing quickly replied, "Master, someone has already been sent to invite her. She should arrive soon." After Zhao Xuanyou returned to Yuzhou, Ding Wenxi thought it inappropriate to live under the same roof as her son-in-law without Yu Wan present, so she had moved to the shop to live.

Hearing this, the Old Marquis asked, "Did you also invite my relative by marriage today?"

"Yes."

"Then I’ll go back to my room to change clothes first."

Yu Wan wanted to say it wasn’t necessary, but she understood that her father-in-law was showing respect to her maternal family, so she didn’t say anything.

The Old Marquis and Madame Wei left the table to change clothes. Zhao Xuanyou ordered someone to bring Yu Wan a bowl of chicken soup to drink first, then sat down with Wen Sun to talk about their journey.

As they were speaking, Ding Wenxi entered from outside. The moment she saw Yu Wan, her eyes filled with tears.

"Mother."

Having been away from Yuzhou for more than half a year, the moment she saw her mother, Yu Wan’s tears fell unexpectedly. She stood up and ran over.

Zhao Xuanyou, fearing she might fall, quickly followed behind her.

Ding Wenxi held Yu Wan in her arms, gently touching her belly, her eyes reddening. But seeing Yu Wan crying freely, and thinking it was a family banquet, she softly comforted her and, together with Zhao Xuanyou, helped Yu Wan sit back down.

"Is this the relative by marriage?" The Old Marquis, now in a more formal set of clothes, stepped into the flower hall.

Seeing Yu Wan in tears, it wasn’t hard to guess Ding Wenxi’s identity.

Zhao Xuanyou had already explained to Ding Wenxi earlier that this time, the Old Marquis and Madame Wei had escorted Yu Wan to Yuzhou. Ding Wenxi stood up to greet the Old Marquis and bowed.

"Old Marquis."

The Old Marquis was smiling as he returned the greeting, but when he saw Ding Wenxi’s appearance clearly, his eyes were filled with astonishment.

"Yu Wan is your daughter?!"

Ding Wenxi wasn’t surprised by the Old Marquis’s reaction. Years ago, when she had followed the Empress Dowager to Jiangnan, she had come into contact with the Old Marquis.

She had long known that he was Zhao Xuanyou’s father, but although they knew each other, they weren’t close, so she hadn’t specifically mentioned it to Zhao Xuanyou.

"Father, do you know my mother?" Yu Wan, hearing this, wiped her tears and asked curiously.

Zhao Xuanyou, on the other hand, had already informed the Old Marquis that Yu Wan’s mother had previously worked in the palace and had a special status, and would be staying in Yuzhou in the future.

The Old Marquis didn’t mind Yu Wan’s background, nor did he care about the relative by marriage.

He just never expected that Yu Wan’s mother would be someone he knew.

After a brief moment of surprise, the Old Marquis knew this wasn’t the place to reminisce. He smiled at Yu Wan and said, "We had a brief encounter in the past. I never expected to have such a connection as in-laws through our children."

"Let’s eat first." Zhao Xuanyou, seeing the situation, invited everyone to take their seats.

The family sat together, lively and intimate. By the time they finished eating, half an hour had passed.

Ding Wenxi originally wanted Yu Wan to return to her room to rest, but Yu Wan had a belly full of questions and refused to let go of her.

Zhao Xuanyou knew she hadn’t seen her mother for too long, so he gave up his seat and went to Wen Sun’s courtyard to chat with him.

Ding Wenxi supported Yu Wan as they entered the Tangli Courtyard. As soon as they sat down, Yu Wan eagerly asked, "Mother, what exactly is going on between you and General Shen? He said he wants to propose to you. Do you like him, or is it just his one-sided wish? Mother, why didn’t you tell me before that you knew Father-in-law?"

At this moment, Ding Wenxi was more concerned about Yu Wan’s condition. Seeing Yu Wan ask a series of questions, she said helplessly, "With so many questions, where do I even start?"

Yu Wan lightly huffed, "One by one. Start with General Shen."

---

chapters.title: Overcoming the Difficulties
chapters.content:
"Don’t rush to ask me about that first. Let’s talk about you," Ding Wenxi didn’t answer Yu Wan’s question but instead asked, "You’ve been traveling all this way with a big belly. Are you feeling uncomfortable anywhere?"

Before Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou got married, Ding Wenxi had been worried that the contraceptive medicine Yu Wan had taken might affect her fertility. Now, seeing Yu Wan’s belly, she finally felt at ease.

"Mother, rest assured. The child and I are both doing very well." Yu Wan knew her mother was worried about her and softly said, "On the way back from the capital, the imperial physicians and medical women checked my pulse every day. They said my body is healthy and the fetus is stable."

"Where did you find the medical woman?"

"After the lantern festival in the palace, the Emperor bestowed her upon me."

Ding Wenxi knew that many medical women in the palace had remarkable medical skills, but because they were palace maids, they couldn’t become imperial physicians.

"How many months along are you now?"

"Seven months."

Ding Wenxi nodded, then took an object from her sleeve and handed it to Yu Wan.

Yu Wan took a look and saw it was a white jade peace knot.

"After I found out you were pregnant, I personally polished this peace knot. It symbolizes peace and safety for you and the child."

"Thank you, Mother." Yu Wan held the peace knot in her hand. The jade was lustrous and smooth, and the shape was plump and full.

Yu Wan naturally loved it and hung the peace knot together with her sachet.

After putting away the peace knot, Yu Wan looked up at Ding Wenxi. "Mother has asked daughter so many questions. It’s time for you to talk about yourself. What’s going on between you and General Shen?"

At the mention of Shen Jiao, Ding Wenxi’s eyes clearly showed difficulty.

Yu Wan waited for a while but didn’t get an answer, so she began to have her own guesses.

If her mother was uninterested in him, she would have directly answered.

The reason she couldn’t answer was probably because she had feelings but felt embarrassed to tell Yu Wan.

Thinking of this, Yu Wan also understood why Shen Jiao had written a letter to the capital.

If he hadn’t said anything, Ding Wenxi probably would never have been able to bring it up to Yu Wan.

After all, she was Zhao Xuanyou’s mother-in-law, and Shen Jiao was Zhao Xuanyou’s subordinate.

"If Mother is fond of General Shen, just accept his proposal. There’s no need to worry about me." When Yu Wan first heard this news, she was indeed shocked and even felt a bit of aversion from the bottom of her heart.

After the initial shock, Yu Wan gradually accepted the matter.

Her mother had lived a very difficult life. When she first fell in love, she liked a man like Cui Lingyuan, who was unfaithful. She was half-coaxed and half-deceived into living in a villa, lost her virginity, and became pregnant.

Later, she realized that Cui Lingyuan wouldn’t stay with her forever. After leaving the villa, she raised Yu Wan alone.

Now that she was no longer young, if she could find someone who truly cared for her, it would indeed be a joyous and congratulatory matter.

"Wanwan, I..." Ding Wenxi, hearing Yu Wan’s words, looked even more embarrassed.

She hesitated for a long time before softly saying, "It’s not that I don’t want to explain to you. It’s just that I’m confused myself. After he confessed his feelings, I haven’t seen him for a while."

"Did Mother reject him?"

Ding Wenxi nodded.

"Does Mother not like him, or are there other concerns?"

"Wanwan, since you’re asking me, let’s just drop this matter."

Yu Wan was slightly taken aback but didn’t continue to persuade.

On the way back from the capital to Yuzhou, Yu Wan had repeatedly thought about her mother’s marriage. If her mother and Shen Jiao were mutually in love, she would be happy that her mother had found someone to entrust her life to.

But from her mother’s words, it seemed she and Shen Jiao hadn’t reached the point of discussing marriage, and they hadn’t even confessed their feelings to each other.

In that case, there was no need to rush into persuasion. It was enough for her mother to know her attitude.

"If Mother has someone she loves, I will only be happy for you."

Ding Wenxi, hearing this, naturally felt warmed and looked at Yu Wan with a smile.

After a moment of hesitation, she held Yu Wan’s hand and said earnestly, "What I care about most right now is you and my grandchild. I don’t care about anything else. Giving birth is not an easy thing. As your mother, I must be by your side to help you through this difficult time."

"In any case, your daughter, grandson, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law all hope that you will be happy. Whatever Mother wants to do, whoever Mother wants to be with, we will all support you."

After leaving Cui Lingyuan, Ding Wenxi had locked away her heart, devoting all her love to Yu Wan.

After Shen Jiao expressed his feelings, her first reaction was indeed fear of embarrassing Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan, so she immediately rejected Shen Jiao and stopped seeing him.

Hearing this, perhaps after Yu Wan gave birth safely, she could seriously consider the matter.

For now, she truly couldn’t focus on anything else.

"Oh right, why didn’t Mother mention before that she knew Father-in-law?"

Ding Wenxi smiled gently. "When the late Emperor took the Empress Dowager to Jiangnan, many nobles and officials followed. Cui Lingyuan was there, and so was Zhao Xuanyou’s father. Like Zhao Xuanyou, he was strong in martial arts, brave and resourceful. So when the late Emperor and Empress Dowager traveled incognito, he would follow and guard them. I followed the Empress Dowager and encountered him several times."

"Did you never talk?"

"We did, but we weren’t close. I thought he might have forgotten about a palace maid he met long ago, so I never mentioned it to you or Zhao Xuanyou."

Yu Wan laughed. "Mother is so beautiful. Anyone who has seen you would never forget."

It wasn’t that Yu Wan was blindly praising her; she genuinely thought Ding Wenxi was beautiful.

However, her mother always said that the Empress Dowager’s beauty was unparalleled in the harem. She wondered what kind of beauty the Empress Dowager was.

"You child, always saying things that make people embarrassed," Ding Wenxi, reminded of past events, thought of something else. "The Old Marquis probably met Zhao Xuanyou’s mother in Jiangnan."

"Did Mother also see Mother-in-law?"

"No," Ding Wenxi shook her head. "I only heard about how the Jingyuan Hou’s heir saved a young lady from bandits. I remember you said Zhao Xuanyou’s mother was from Jiangnan. Maybe she was the young lady he saved."

Yu Wan only knew that the Old Marquis had deep feelings for his wife. She didn’t expect there to be such a story behind their meeting.

"What a past," Yu Wan couldn’t help but sigh. "Even Zhao Xuanyou probably doesn’t know."

Zhao Xuanyou had told Yu Wan that after his mother passed away, the Old Marquis became silent and reserved. Although he cared about Zhao Xuanyou’s studies and martial arts, the father and son weren’t particularly close.

"It’s just my guess. The Old Marquis’s wife has been gone for so many years. Bringing up these things might make the Old Marquis and Zhao Xuanyou sad."

"I understand."

"You rest well," after talking for so long, Ding Wenxi stood up. "Now that you’re back, I’ll move back to the Hou residence. We can talk anytime."

Childbirth was always a dangerous ordeal for women. With Yu Wan already seven months pregnant, Ding Wenxi needed to be by her side at all times.

"Mother should also go rest. We can talk again later."

After Ding Wenxi left, Yu Wan remembered Zhao Xuanyou’s reluctant gaze earlier and ordered Peng Xia to inform Zhao Xuanyou.

After traveling day and night for so long, she was truly exhausted. She changed into her sleeping clothes and wanted to lie down to wait for Zhao Xuanyou.

But before she could lie down, she heard footsteps behind her.

Her body was heavy and slow to move. Before she could turn her head, the person behind her stretched out his arms and wrapped them around her.

In the next moment, her nose was filled with the man’s long-missed warm breath.

chapters.title: The Embroidered Canopy
chapters.content:
From the moment Yu Wan entered the residence, Zhao Xuanyou had been restraining himself.

He restrained himself during meals, he restrained himself while she and her daughter shared private conversations. After enduring all this, Zhao Xuanyou almost savagely captured her lips, his arms pulling her closer than usual.

Yu Wan was kissed into a daze, feeling his fingers weave through her hair. Her already loose bun cascaded down like a waterfall.

She tilted her head to look at him, so close, and her heartbeat instantly lost its rhythm.

After a moment, Zhao Xuanyou released her, his deep eyes fixing on her before he pulled her to sit at the edge of the couch.

"Are you exhausted?"

"A little." In his presence, Yu Wan didn’t need to pretend.

She pulled him down to lie with her, as they used to, resting her head on his arm, her lips curving slightly. "Did you miss me?"

"What do you think?"

Yu Wan’s smile deepened. "Do you miss me, or do you miss the child?"

Knowing she was teasing him, Zhao Xuanyou didn’t take the bait. "Is there a difference?"

Whether it was her or the child, both were the apple of Zhao Xuanyou’s eye.

Yu Wan was about to speak when she felt the baby move inside her. She grabbed Zhao Xuanyou’s large hand and placed it on her belly.

"Did you feel that?" Yu Wan asked softly.

Zhao Xuanyou’s brows twitched, looking at Yu Wan in surprise. "The baby is moving?"

Yu Wan had mentioned the baby’s movements to Zhao Xuanyou when they were in the capital. But back then, the baby was still small, and by the time she called Zhao Xuanyou over, the baby had already settled down.

Now, the baby was seven months along, and its movements were more frequent; little hands and feet poking and kicking here and there.

This was the first time Zhao Xuanyou had felt the baby move, and a strange sensation welled up in his heart.

When he learned Yu Wan was pregnant, he was of course overjoyed. But it wasn’t until this moment, feeling the little one moving inside her, that he truly grasped the reality of becoming a father.

While he was still in a daze, Yu Wan, leaning on his arm, had fallen asleep.

When she opened her eyes again, Zhao Xuanyou’s hand was still resting on her belly.

"Still not done feeling?" Seeing his focused expression, Yu Wan let out a soft sigh.

Zhao Xuanyou withdrew his gaze, noticing the thin layer of sweat on her forehead. He picked up the handkerchief from the pillow and wiped it for her. "Are you hot? Should I add more ice?"

The ice stored in the marquis's residence was all reserved for Yu Wan, but they didn’t dare use too much. Only one ice basin was placed by the couch.

"It’s not hot in the room. It’s just that you’re holding me too tightly; I feel like I’m sleeping next to a furnace."

Hearing her playful complaint, Zhao Xuanyou withdrew his arm and shifted away slightly.

"Is this better?"

"You didn’t let me push you away." Yu Wan couldn’t help but pout.

Hot as it was, she still enjoyed sleeping next to the furnace.

Zhao Xuanyou got up, fetched a round fan from the side, then pulled Yu Wan back into his arms. With his other hand, he gently fanned her.

Looking at his slightly aggrieved expression, Yu Wan felt a pang of pity for him. She stopped resting on his arm and instead sat up against the soft pillow.

Though she sympathized, she didn’t let up with her words. "A great general like you, unwilling to serve?"

Zhao Xuanyou sighed. "Ever since you became pregnant, not only can I not touch you, but now I can’t even hold you properly."

Perhaps due to her excellent diet, Yu Wan’s belly was particularly large. Lying flat was uncomfortable for her; she could only sleep on her side with a soft pillow for support.

With such a big belly, it was also inconvenient to embrace Zhao Xuanyou. Indeed, the couple could no longer be as intimate as they once were under the embroidered canopy.

Seeing his pitiful look, Yu Wan thought for a moment. "Actually, it’s not impossible."

"Hmm?" Zhao Xuanyou looked up at her, his gaze suddenly turning suggestive. "You mean that?"

Early in her pregnancy, the residence physician had cautioned Zhao Xuanyou that during the first three months, they absolutely must not engage in marital relations. The physician hadn’t mentioned what to do afterward, and Zhao Xuanyou hadn’t asked.

After all, pregnancy was no trivial matter. Even if he yearned for Yu Wan, he wouldn’t act recklessly.

Moreover, he could see how much Yu Wan valued this pregnancy. He hadn’t brought it up because he didn’t want her to be disappointed in him, thinking he only cared about his own pleasure and not her or the child’s safety.

But now it was Yu Wan who had brought it up...

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened. "Wanwan?"

"What ‘that’? I don’t understand."

"What ‘that’? I don’t understand." Before reaching Yuzhou, the medical attendant had told Yu Wan that it was actually safe to be intimate at this stage. Now, seeing Zhao Xuanyou’s burning gaze, she felt a flicker of fear.

After all, he was usually a bit fierce, and now that he had abstained for so long, what if he couldn’t control himself...

"I was just joking. Forget it."

Yu Wan gave him a coaxing smile and reached out to push his head away.

But Zhao Xuanyou remembered the softening in her tone earlier. He didn’t dare pin her down as he used to, but instead leaned in from the side to kiss her.

Feeling his caution and care, Yu Wan gradually relaxed and let go of her worries.

"Be gentle."

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement, his movements growing even more tender.

The maids outside were well aware of the couple’s affection and paid no mind to the sounds from within. They silently stood guard at the door, preparing water.

It was only when Yu Wan called them in much later that they efficiently attended to her, helping her clean up, change clothes, and replace the bedding.

Zhao Xuanyou didn’t need the maids to attend to him. He washed up on his own, changed his clothes, and walked to the edge of the couch.

Meeting Yu Wan’s lazy, soft gaze, Zhao Xuanyou cleared his throat and asked with concern, "Are you uncomfortable anywhere?"

After the maids tactfully retreated, Yu Wan deliberately shot him a fierce look. "Now you ask? Why didn’t you stop when I told you to earlier?"

Zhao Xuanyou felt a bit embarrassed but hardened his scalp. "I was already being very gentle."

How could such matters be stopped the moment someone said so?

Moreover, if he had stopped, it would have taken even longer afterward.

"Really, nowhere is uncomfortable?"

"No." Seeing that he was genuinely worried, Yu Wan dropped the fierce look in her eyes and smiled at him.

Only then did Zhao Xuanyou relax. He lowered his head and kissed her brow, then carried her from the edge of the couch to the soft couch by the window.

Yu Wan was always quick to feel hungry, and after such exertion, she was both hungry and thirsty. She drank the swallow’s nest soup that Pan Xia brought over in one gulp, then had a bowl of rose dew.

While the couple was eating and chatting, Yuan Qing came to say that the old marquis had asked Zhao Xuanyou to come speak with him.

After Zhao Xuanyou left, Yu Wan called Yingxue to her side.

Previously, Yu Wan had thought she would only be in the capital for a month or two before returning, so she hadn’t brought Yingxue with her. Who knew that things in the capital would drag on, and with her pregnancy, she ended up staying for more than half a year.

"Does the mistress have any orders?" Yingxue asked.

"There is indeed something I need to discuss with you," Yu Wan said, pulling Yingxue to sit beside her. Though they were now mistress and servant, Yu Wan had never forgotten the bond they once shared.

Yingxue was the first friend she had made after her rebirth. During her most difficult times, Yingxue, like Chen Da Niu, had helped her a great deal.

Now that Yu Wan had the means to repay them, she would spare no effort.

---

chapters.title: First Stirrings of Love
chapters.content:
Yingxue’s gaze flickered, and her expression grew solemn as she silently looked at Yu Wan.

Seeing her grow tense, Yu Wan spoke gently, "Before we left the capital, your mother came to see me. She said she had found a marriage prospect for you in the capital; a silk merchant with a wealthy and kind family. She said you knew them."

"I do know them. A long time ago, when their business wasn’t doing well, they were our neighbors."

"Did your mother mention this to you?"

Yingxue nodded.

Their family were hereditary servants of the marquis’s household, and over generations, they had managed to live comfortably.

Moreover, as the head maid in the heir’s courtyard, Yingxue had influence with the masters, so merchant families were eager to form a marriage alliance with her. Many had come to propose to Yingxue’s family.

Yu Wan observed Yingxue’s attitude and saw that she wasn’t enthusiastic about this marriage.

Yingxue’s eyes were still tense. "Did my mother ask the mistress to send me back to the capital? Did the mistress agree?"

"I didn’t refuse."

Yingxue’s family was in the capital, and Yu Wan had never intended to keep her in Yuzhou permanently.

However, due to a conversation with Liang Miaotong before leaving the capital, where she learned of Liang’s anxiety over her own marriage, Yu Wan had kept an open mind about Yingxue’s situation and hadn’t given a definitive answer.

"I told your mother that I’m pregnant and need someone by my side. I might not be able to leave you for a year or two."

With the mistress saying this, Yingxue’s mother couldn’t object.

Of course, this wasn’t the whole truth, but it did give Yingxue some room.

If Yingxue liked this marriage prospect, Yu Wan would arrange for her to return to the capital as soon as possible and prepare a generous dowry for her wedding.

If Yingxue had other thoughts, Yu Wan also wanted to know what she planned to do.

"Tell me the truth. What do you think?"
