"I..." Yingxue lowered her head, hesitating for a long time without speaking.

Yu Wan slowly ate a piece of cake, and seeing that she still wasn’t speaking, said, "Have you taken a liking to someone?"

"No."

Yingxue answered quickly, but her cheeks flushed crimson at the same time.

"What’s there to be embarrassed about with me? Who is it?" Recalling that Yingxue had worked in the marquis’s residence in the capital for so many years without ever developing feelings for anyone, but now she had been in Yuzhou for over a year...

Yu Wan pondered for a moment, then realized. She looked up and smiled. "So who is it?"

Yingxue still didn’t say a word.

"Afraid I’ll laugh at you? Or do you think it’s impossible with him?"

Yingxue lowered her head in silence for a while before looking up at Yu Wan. "I..."

"Just too embarrassed to say?"

Yingxue nodded slightly.

As Liang Miaotong had said, marriages were always arranged by parents and matchmakers. For a maid like Yingxue, besides her parents, the master’s family could also arrange her marriage; either as a concubine or to a servant or a young male servant.

Yingxue had never thought she would have a say in her own marriage.

Even with her friendship with Yu Wan, she had never dared to hope that Yu Wan would help her with this.

For a maid, being able to serve in the Marquis of Jingyuan’s household was already extremely fortunate.

"Someone you met in this marquis’s residence?"

Yuan Can and Yuan Qing were old acquaintances. If Yingxue had developed feelings, she would have done so long ago. It definitely wasn’t them.

"Yes."

The few personal guards around Zhao Xuanyou were tall and imposing, but they hadn’t stayed in Yuzhou during this return to the capital.

As for the guards and servants left in the residence here, Yu Wan couldn’t think of anyone who might catch Yingxue’s attention.

"One of Ming Mei’s guards?"

"No," after saying so much to Yu Wan, Yingxue finally let go of the burden in her heart. "It’s one of the Marquis’s guards who was brought over from the capital."

A guard brought to Yuzhou?

Yu Wan looked at her in surprise, then quickly remembered the Eastern Palace secret guard that Wen Jian had asked Zhao Xuanyou to help rescue.

At that time, to avoid detection in the capital, the man was immediately sent to Yuzhou.

But Yu Wan couldn’t recall his name at the moment.

"Does the mistress know about this?" Yingxue saw the confusion in Yu Wan’s eyes and thought she didn’t know of the man’s existence.

"I do know. He’s a friend of Ah Jian’s, though I haven’t met him yet."

"I only know he’s Young Master Ah Jian’s friend." Yingxue let out a soft sigh, a faint, unknowing smile tugging at her lips. "He’s always so mysterious. I know his surname is Lin, but I don’t even know his given name."

Hearing this, Yu Wan suddenly remembered his name; Lin Zheng.

But since his identity was special, and it was unclear how Zhao Xuanyou would arrange things for him in the future, she didn’t mention his name.

"How did you meet him?"

Yingxue replied, "During the New Year, Madam Ding hosted a New Year’s Eve dinner at the marquis’s residence, and he was there."

Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Wan, and Wen Jian had stayed in the capital for the New Year. Ding Wenxi had gathered all the people left in Yuzhou for a New Year’s Eve meal.

Lin Zheng was Wen Jian’s friend, so Ding Wenxi hadn’t forgotten him.

During the banquet, Yingxue mentioned how bored she was with nothing to do in the residence all day. Ding Wenxi then said she would go to the Western Regions to purchase a batch of jade after the New Year and asked Yingxue to accompany her.

When Ding Wenxi mentioned that the trip might be dangerous and that she should bring more guards, Lin Zheng volunteered, saying his martial arts were decent and that he wanted to go along to protect them.

"He really is extremely skilled. On our merchant trip, we encountered bandits, and he took down more than a dozen by himself."

According to Wen Jian, Lin Zheng’s lightness skills and hidden weapons weren’t as good as his, but in all other martial arts, he was better than Wen Jian. He had been highly regarded in the Eastern Palace and was presumably capable of taking on ten opponents at once.

His willingness to volunteer to protect Madam Ding on her trip to the Western Regions showed that he was a person who knew how to repay kindness.

"So it was during this trip that you developed feelings?" Yu Wan asked with a smile. "Have you exchanged feelings with him?"

Yingxue shook her head.

Yu Wan understood. Yingxue wasn’t sure of Lin Zheng’s feelings, so she couldn’t give Yu Wan a clear answer.

"I understand. I’ll have Ah Jian ask him about this for you."

Yingxue’s eyes lit up, realizing that Yu Wan intended to help. Her face turned even redder.

"Whatever the mistress decides is fine."

Overwhelmed with shyness, she blurted this out and then fled, her face still red.

Yu Wan watched her retreat, her heart filled with the first stirrings of love, and suddenly felt a pang of envy.

She and Zhao Xuanyou had first met in bed. They had been together as if they were already husband and wife before they even truly knew each other. Though they had been through all kinds of trials, they had never experienced this stage of tentatively exploring each other’s feelings.

She wondered what it would feel like to have a slow-burning romance with Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Wan sat by the window, lost in thought, when Pan Xia entered and said, "Mistress, Auntie Qianqin has arrived."

"Please bring her in at once."

Qianqin was an imperial physician bestowed by the emperor. She was gentle and highly skilled in medicine. She had taken great care of Yu Wan throughout the journey, and Yu Wan respected her deeply.

"Mistress." Qianqin greeted respectfully.

"No need for formalities, Auntie. Please, take a seat." After Qianqin was seated, Yu Wan spoke softly. "Auntie, you’ve worked hard accompanying me on this journey. You don’t need to come over for the next few days. Rest well in the residence to avoid any discomfort from the change in environment."

Qianqin said, "Is the mistress feeling unwell? Just now, the Marquis sent Yuan Qing to ask me to come to the Tangli Courtyard to see you."

So it was Zhao Xuanyou.

He must have been worried that their earlier intimacy might have affected the baby and had specifically called Qianqin over.

Considerate as it was, it made Yu Wan feel a little embarrassed.

"I’m not uncomfortable." Yu Wan wasn’t about to admit the real reason. After a moment’s thought, she said, "It’s just that the baby has been moving a lot lately."

"I’m not uncomfortable." Yu Wan wasn’t about to admit the real reason. After getting up from the couch, she didn’t feel any discomfort. After a moment’s thought, she said, "As I’ve mentioned before, the baby has been moving a lot lately; almost constantly."

chapters.title: Double Joy
chapters.content:
"Is it moving more than before?"

On the way back to Yuzhou, Yuhan had mentioned this to Qianqin. At that time, the palace physician had diagnosed Yuhan and said she was fine. Since Yuhan showed no other discomfort, Qianqin didn't think much of it.

Hearing Yuhan bring it up again, Qianqin thought for a moment and asked Yuhan to lift her blouse.

As soon as her belly was exposed, Qianqin saw the little one inside indeed moving nonstop.

She watched quietly for a while before asking respectfully, "Madam, may I touch carefully?"

Yuhan had not been worried initially, but upon hearing this, the smile on her face faded, and she silently nodded.

Qianqin crouched down and gently ran her hands over Yuhan's belly, her expression unreadable.

Yuhan's heart sank further, regretting her playful antics with Zhao Xuanyou.

But upon reflection, the baby had been moving a lot these past few days, not just after she and Zhao Xuanyou had been intimate.

She suppressed her anxiety as best she could. Just then, Zhao Xuanyou stepped in from outside. Seeing the scene, his expression turned serious.

Yuhan saw him return and signaled him not to speak, but the worry on her face betrayed her feelings.

Zhao Xuanyou silently walked to Yuhan's side and took her hand, feeling her fingertips trembling slightly. He gave her hand a reassuring squeeze.

No matter what happened, he would be by her side.

Qianqin furrowed her brows and touched for a long while before helping Yuhan pull her clothes back down.

Before she could speak, Yuhan couldn't hold back and asked, "Aunt, what's wrong?"

"Please don't worry, Madam. Your pregnancy is stable, and there's nothing wrong."

Yuhan finally let out a sigh of relief. Zhao Xuanyou put his arm around her shoulders and looked at Qianqin.

Qianqin realized the couple had misunderstood and quickly said, "I just had a guess after hearing Madam's words, so I wanted to touch your belly."

At this point, Qianqin's tone paused slightly: "The reason Madam's belly is moving so much is because you're carrying twins."

Twins?

Yuhan was stunned. After a moment of daze, she instinctively turned to Zhao Xuanyou.

"Is this... good news?" Zhao Xuanyou said uncertainly.

It should be, right?

With twins in her belly, the family would have two children; this should be a double blessing.

Yuhan wasn't nervous about pregnancy.

After all, in her past life, she had given birth to a son for Zhao Xuanyou. This life was familiar territory.

But she truly hadn't expected it to be different from her past life; she was carrying twins.

Qianqin said, "Congratulations, Lord Zhao, Congratulations, Lady Zhao."

Hearing Qianqin's congratulations, Yuhan finally relaxed: "Aunt, is there anything I need to be careful about?"

"There's nothing special Madam needs to be careful about. Just continue as before." After thinking for a moment, Qianqin added, "If possible, find a midwife who has delivered twins before. Experience is always better than inexperience."

Carrying twins wasn't much different from carrying a single child during pregnancy, but giving birth to two was indeed more arduous than one. With an experienced midwife, it would be much more reassuring.

"Thank you for the reminder, Aunt. Is there anything else?"

"I can't think of anything else. If Lord Zhao is still worried, consult the palace physician again."

"Thank you for your trouble."

After seeing Qianqin off, Zhao Xuanyou immediately called the steward over, ordering him to find a midwife in Yuzhou City who had delivered twins before. He also had Yuan Qian invite the palace physician over.

The palace physician couldn't distinguish between a single or twin pregnancy from the pulse alone, but since Yuhan's pulse was fine, it naturally reassured Zhao Xuanyou.

By dinner time, the news of Yuhan's twins had spread throughout the Marquis's mansion. Ding Wenxi and the Old Marquis came to the Tangli Courtyard to express their concern.

Everyone had thought the Marquis's mansion would add one baby, but to their delight, it turned out to be two.

Zhao Xuanyou saw them growing more and more joyful and feared they would disturb Yuhan's rest endlessly. So he announced a family banquet for the next day at noon and sent them out of the Tangli Courtyard. When he turned back, he saw Yuhan pulling Wen Bin aside to whisper.

He could only helplessly return to the room, wash up, and bring Yuhan clean nightclothes. Then he sat by the bed, absently flipping through a book.

After waiting for a long while, Yuhan finally returned to the room.

"There are too many people in the family. Everyone wants to talk to you," Zhao Xuanyou said with a touch of jealousy, "I wanted to talk to you for a while, but I had to wait."

"I had something to ask Ah Bin," Yuhan said with a smile, sitting beside him and letting him help her change into her nightclothes.

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow but said nothing.

What could be more important than her and the two children in her belly?

"Do you remember Lin Jin, the one we rescued from the heavenly prison?" she asked.

"No, I don't."

Hearing him pretend not to remember, Yuhan didn't mind at all. She tilted her head and kissed his face. Seeing the smile return to his brows, she continued, "Yingxue and Lin Jin went on a business trip to the Western Regions with my mother. After they returned, she developed feelings for him. She doesn't know his feelings yet, so I asked Ah Bin to help find out."

"First you're arranging things for Wen Bin, then for Yingxue. You, don't worry too much."

"Where does it say I'm worrying? I'm just going with the flow."

Forced love was not sweet. Yuhan had not interfered with Wen Bin's feelings, nor could she control Yingxue's heart. She was just helping where she could.

Seeing her relaxed expression, Zhao Xuanyou lowered his head and kissed her forehead.

He disliked meddling in others' affairs the most, but since Yuhan liked to, he let her be.

She had married him, and he should let her live a peaceful and happy life, free to do as she pleased.

He wanted to cherish her in the palm of his hand, to protect her, not to restrict her.

Of course, from now on, he would have to protect not only Yuhan but also the two little ones growing bigger day by day in her belly.

"Zhao Xuanyou, they kicked me again," Yuhan said coquettishly.

Zhao Xuanyou rubbed her belly and pretended to be fierce: "Let them be bold for now. Once they're born safely, I'll deal with them properly."

Though he said that, Zhao Xuanyou felt his heart soften as he felt the movement in Yuhan's belly.

Going from one baby to two was indeed a pleasant surprise for Zhao Xuanyou and Yuhan, but their daily lives didn't change much on the surface.

Yuhan continued to eat and drink as usual and walked around the mansion as usual. However, as the due date approached, her belly grew larger, and her body became heavier.

Zhao Xuanyou noticed some stretch marks appearing on the lower part of Yuhan's belly. He didn't tell Yuhan but instead collected some precious spices and medicinal herbs and asked Qianqin to prepare a fragrant ointment according to a palace secret recipe. He had the maids secretly apply it to Yuhan after her bath.

He didn't think these few marks would detract from Yuhan's beauty, but if they could be quietly dealt with, it would be better.

When Ding Wenxi learned of this, she appreciated Zhao Xuanyou even more.

Zhao Xuanyou was an impeccable son-in-law, but since Yuhan had been Zhao Xuanyou's maid in the past, Ding Wenxi had been worried that Zhao Xuanyou might treat Yuhan the same way he treated a concubine.

Witnessing Zhao Xuanyou's thoughtful gestures in such minor details was enough to prove that he genuinely cared for Yuhan.

She also grew closer to the in-laws of the Marquis's mansion.

As Yuhan's due date approached, Ding Wenxi and Concubine Wei prepared the delivery room in the Marquis's mansion. Zhao Xuanyou successfully found two midwives who had delivered twins before. Combined with the two midwives he had previously found, there were four midwives on standby in the Marquis's mansion.

Yuhan felt he was making too much of a fuss but admitted she was indeed a bit nervous about giving birth to twins.

On the day before the summer solstice, Yuhan felt a pain in her lower abdomen every now and then. As the pain became more frequent, she quickly called Qianqin over.

Upon inquiry, it turned out to be the signs of labor.

---

chapters.title: A Turn for the Better
chapters.content:
Immediately, the maids took Yuhan to the delivery room. Qianqin directed the maids to boil water and prepare for the birth, and had the kitchen prepare soup.

Zhao Xuanyou had been accompanying her by the bed, but soon Ding Wenxi and Concubine Wei arrived and drove him out.

He, of course, refused.

Yuhan's abdomen was in occasional cramps, but she could still endure it.

"There are too many people in the room. You wait outside."

At this moment, besides Yuhan's personal maids, there were Ding Wenxi, Concubine Wei, Qianqin, and four midwives in the room. Indeed, it was too crowded.

Since Yuhan had spoken, Zhao Xuanyou had to leave.

"I'll wait outside the whole time. Call me if anything happens."

Zhao Xuanyou paid no mind to the others' gazes in the room, lowering his head to kiss Yuhan's forehead.

Concubine Wei, seeing this, expressed her concern for Yuhan before taking two midwives out to wait outside and assist.

Ding Wenxi sat by the bed, holding Yuhan's hand. Though she smiled to comfort her, her heart was in her throat.

When she had given birth to Yuhan, it had taken a day and a night. Thinking of Yuhan having to deliver twins, she couldn't help but worry.

She silently prayed to the gods, asking them to bless Yuhan with a quick labor and less pain.

After more than an hour of such tension, Yuhan saw blood and her water broke. The contractions became more frequent.

After the midwife examined her, she said she could already feel the baby's head. Everyone became tense, and the midwife immediately had Yuhan try to push.

Outside, Zhao Xuanyou heard Yuhan's loud cries of pain and felt a rush of blood to his head. He stepped forward to barge in.

The Old Marquis stopped him, telling him to wait patiently for news here.

After all, there were experienced midwives, a medical woman, and Yuhan's mother inside. There were enough people, and he wouldn't be of any help if he went in. Instead, he would only cause more chaos.

The palace physician on standby, seeing this, also came out to comfort him, saying that Yuhan was healthy and not usually delicate. She often walked around, so she would definitely have a safe delivery.

Zhao Xuanyou's mind was in turmoil. He was also worried that his rash actions might distract Yuhan and sap her strength. He forced himself to wait outside.

After half an hour of anxious waiting, a clear baby's cry finally came from the room.

Had she given birth?

The baby inside was still crying, but Yuhan's cries continued as well.

Zhao Xuanyou could no longer wait. He rushed into the room. The room was filled with a strong smell of blood. Ding Wenxi, Qianqin, and the midwives were all gathered around the bed.

The other two midwives were on the side, holding a newborn baby wrapped in swaddling clothes.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou barge in, they quickly bowed: "Lord Zhao."

"How is Madam?"

"Congratulations, Lord Zhao. Madam has successfully given birth to a young master." With that, the midwife brought the child to Zhao Xuanyou to see.

The newborn was wrinkled, with a red face.

For some reason, the baby stopped crying. The midwife was a bit worried, but then she saw the baby's eyes open a slit.

This was rare, as newborns rarely opened their eyes.

However, with Yuhan still crying out in pain beside them, neither Zhao Xuanyou nor the midwife paid much attention.

One was born, and there was still another in Yuhan's belly.

Zhao Xuanyou was extremely worried. His eyes were fixed solely on Yuhan.

He was tall, and even though he wasn't crowded around the bed, he could see Yuhan's pained face.

He wanted to rush to her side to accompany her but was afraid of causing more trouble.

The midwife also advised: "Lord Zhao, it's better to wait outside. The young master was born so smoothly; the other one should be quick as well."

"This is smooth?" After hearing Yuhan's cries for so long, Zhao Xuanyou truly couldn't believe the midwife's words.

"Of course it's smooth. It hasn't even been an hour yet."

Zhao Xuanyou felt slightly reassured and exited again.

Learning that Yuhan had smoothly given birth to a baby boy, the Old Marquis waiting outside was overjoyed and also advised Zhao Xuanyou to be at ease.

The midwife who had delivered several sets of twins said that after the first birth, the second would come quickly.

But Zhao Xuanyou waited outside in agony for a long time with no further news from the room, only Yuhan's cries.

"What's going on?" Zhao Xuanyou grabbed Pan Xia, who had come out to fetch water.

Pan Xia lowered her head: "This servant heard Aunt Qianqin say that the baby's position is not right. It might take some more time."

"The first one was fine, wasn't it?" Wen Bin, hearing this, couldn't stay calm either. "How could the second one be in the wrong position?"

"This servant doesn't understand, but Aunt Qianqin is trying her best to adjust the baby's position for Madam. It should be fine."

By now, it was already evening.

The sky was covered with thick clouds tonight. Neither the moon nor the stars were visible, as if a storm was approaching.

It felt as if a hand in the darkness had tightly grabbed Zhao Xuanyou's heart, rendering him immobile.

"Understood. Go back in and do your work." The Old Marquis rescued Pan Xia and patted Zhao Xuanyou's shoulder. "Since the medical woman is handling it, it should be fine."

The atmosphere, which had just lightened due to the birth of the first child, instantly turned heavy again.

Yuhan continued to cry out in the room, and the crowd outside became increasingly silent.

As the time approached the Zi hour (midnight), just when Zhao Xuanyou was about to go mad, another baby's cry finally came from the room.

However, this cry was noticeably weaker than the first child's. If they hadn't been paying full attention to the sounds in the room, they wouldn't have heard it at all.

Zhao Xuanyou, with a heart full of anxiety, rushed in again.

This time, only Qianqin and Ding Wenxi were by the bed. Seeing him arrive, Qianqin stood up to make room.

Yuhan was sprawled on the bed. After experiencing the tearing pain of childbirth, waves of afterpains still coursed through her body.

But she knew she had made it through.

"Yuan."

Looking at Yuhan's weak appearance, Zhao Xuanyou's heart twisted even more.

He took Yuhan's hand from Ding Wenxi, his own palm trembling slightly.

He had never experienced fear in his life, but just now, while waiting outside, he had suddenly been overwhelmed by immense worry and terror.

If someone wanted to harm Yuhan, he wasn't afraid. He would face any challenge head-on; even the Emperor himself wouldn't be spared.

But if Yuhan couldn't give birth safely, he couldn't save her.

In the past hour, he could have lost Yuhan at any moment.

"Have you seen the children?" Yuhan was extremely weak, but she could see that Zhao Xuanyou was even more nervous than her. She even managed to smile at him.

"I've seen our eldest. He's red and chubby, very cute. The midwife has already taken him to the wet nurse," seeing Yuhan trying to comfort him, Zhao Xuanyou quickly perked up and smiled at her. "You rest for a while. Once you've regained your strength, I'll have them bring the children over."

"Okay."

Yuhan didn't have an ounce of strength left and didn't dare to force herself.

Pan Xia brought over some chicken congee. Zhao Xuanyou had intended to feed Yuhan himself, but then he noticed Qianqin looking at him, seemingly having something to say.

Zhao Xuanyou discreetly handed the congee to Ding Wenxi and followed Qianqin behind the screen.

chapters.title: Let Me Explain
chapters.content:
Qianqin saw Zhao Xuanyou approaching and didn’t beat around the bush. She took the swaddled infant from the midwife, whose face was grave.

Zhao Xuanyou took one look and knew what Qianqin wanted to say.

The child in front of him clearly looked much smaller than his brother. What was worse, his complexion had a faint purplish tint.

Zhao Xuanyou took the swaddled baby from her hands and immediately felt how light he was.

Even though Zhao Xuanyou had never seen other newborns before, he had seen countless wounded and dead on the battlefield. He knew all too well what a purplish skin tone meant.

Suddenly, Zhao Xuanyou felt a wave of dizziness and lightheadedness.

Yet, even so, when he glanced at Yu Wan sitting on the couch drinking soup, he forced himself to remain calm. After returning the baby to the midwife, he signaled Qianqin to follow him outside.

"Lord Hou, the girl’s condition is not good," Qianqin reported truthfully.

Girl?

Was that tiny bundle just now the daughter he had longed for?

But how could she be...

"Why is there such a big difference between the two children?"

"With twins, one is always stronger and the other weaker. When two children share the same womb, the stronger one inevitably crowds the other."

But the difference between the two children in Lady Hou’s womb was too great. Fortunately, Lady Hou had gone into labor today. The little girl already had a purplish tint; if she had been crowded for a few more days, she might have been stillborn.

"Lord Hou need not worry too much. The girl can still cry, which is good news. If we take good care of her and she reaches full term, there should be no major issues. I will also discuss with the court physician to see if there’s anything else we can do besides having a wet nurse feed her."

Zhao Xuanyou had hoped for a long and happy life for his family of four, but he never expected his little daughter to struggle even to reach full term.

Qianqin knew Zhao Xuanyou doted on his wife and daughter and would find this hard to accept.

However, since she had been ordered by the Emperor to attend to Yu Wan, she had to tell them the truth.

"Instruct the midwife and wet nurse not to reveal this to Wanwan," Zhao Xuanyou quickly regained his composure and made a decision. "When Wanwan wants to see the children, just bring the older one."

Yu Wan was weak and needed to recover some strength first.

"Yes."

Qianqin respectfully acknowledged and went to discuss the care of the frail little girl with the court physician.

"Xuanyou, how is Wanwan? Nothing happened to her, right?"

Old Marquis Zhao and Wen Ji had been waiting in the courtyard. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou speaking with Qianqin in the corridor with a grave expression, they asked with concern.

Facing their concerned gazes, Zhao Xuanyou said, "Yu Wan has successfully given birth to twins, a boy and a girl."

"That’s good, that’s good," the old marquis said, beaming with joy.

Wen Ji, however, noticed Zhao Xuanyou’s furrowed brows. "Brother-in-law?"

Knowing she was worried about Yu Wan’s safety, Zhao Xuanyou cleared his throat a few times, waiting for his emotions to settle before saying softly, "Just now, Aunt Qianqin said the girl is naturally frail. You know about this now, but do not mention it in front of Wanwan. I will tell her myself."

With that, he turned and went back inside.

In a short while, the midwife and maids had cleaned up the room.

Yu Wan, having drunk the chicken soup, lay on the couch with her eyes closed, resting.

When Zhao Xuanyou entered, Ding Wenxi stood up to make room for him.

Yu Wan had given birth safely, so there was nothing for her to worry about. She should let the young couple have some private time. Besides, she had been so focused on Yu Wan earlier that she hadn’t even had a chance to see the two newborn grandchildren. She needed to go check on them.

Zhao Xuanyou knew Ding Wenxi had been with Yu Wan for so long and must be exhausted. He gave her a deep, respectful bow.

After everyone else had left the room, he sat down by the couch.

There was still a faint smell of blood in the room. Yu Wan lay motionless, as if all the energy had been drained from her, her face etched with exhaustion.

Zhao Xuanyou thought of her earlier cries of pain and knew how much she had suffered.

He couldn’t help but reach out and touch Yu Wan’s damp hair, soaked with sweat.

Feeling his touch, Yu Wan lifted her eyelids and smiled at him.

"Still hungry?"

"Not hungry, just want some water."

Seeing that she could still speak clearly, Zhao Xuanyou knew her body wasn’t too severely weakened. His heart, which had felt like it was sinking, revived a little.

No matter what, both children were alive, and Yu Wan was fine. He needed to cheer up.

Seeing there was still a bowl of chicken soup on the table, Zhao Xuanyou picked it up and fed her half a bowl.

After drinking the soup, Yu Wan asked, "Where are the children?"

"They’ve been taken to the wet nurses. Mother and Concubine Wei are there watching over them. Don’t worry."

"I’m their mother, and I haven’t even seen my own children yet."

"It’s so late, you’re tired, and the servants are exhausted too. You can see them tomorrow."

Yu Wan had gone through hours of labor, and it was now late at night. She had no strength left, and the servants had been busy for a long time.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this, she could only nod.

"Before, we always guessed whether it would be a son or a daughter. I never expected that Heaven would favor us so much as to give us both a son and a daughter at once."

Looking at the smile in Yu Wan’s eyes, Zhao Xuanyou’s mind was filled with the pitiful image of his daughter.

He took a deep breath and agreed, "Yes, from now on we will have both son and daughter. Wanwan, I’ll carry you back to our room. Don’t sleep here."

The delivery room was filled with the smell of blood, and it had always been the plan to move Yu Wan back to the Tangli Courtyard to rest after giving birth.

Of course, most importantly, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t bear to say any more.

Zhao Xuanyou put a windproof hood on Yu Wan and wrapped her in a clean thin blanket before picking her up.

It was the height of summer, so there was no need to worry about catching a cold, but it was better to be safe.

As they left the room, Wen Ji was still in the courtyard.

Everyone in the Marquis’s residence was concerned about Yu Wan and the children, but Wen Ji only cared about Yu Wan.

Yu Wan smiled, "Don’t worry, I can talk and eat. I’m fine."

The delivery room was right next to the Tangli Courtyard. Zhao Xuanyou took only a few steps before carrying Yu Wan back to their familiar bedroom.

"Ah…"

When Yu Wan was placed on the couch, she felt a tug in her lower body and let out a soft cry of pain.

Zhao Xuanyou’s heart ached terribly. He tucked the thin blanket around her.

"Go to sleep early. Tomorrow morning, I’ll have the wet nurse bring the children in for you to see."

Yu Wan was indeed very tired. Holding Zhao Xuanyou’s arm, she quickly fell asleep.

Zhao Xuanyou sat silently by the couch, waiting until she was in a deep sleep before carefully getting up and leaving.

As soon as he stepped out, he saw Wen Ji still waiting there. Zhao Xuanyou asked him to go inside and keep Yu Wan company.

If Yu Wan woke up, Wen Ji could keep her company and talk to her.

Zhao Xuanyou himself quickly walked towards the Xifeng Courtyard, where the two children and the wet nurses were staying.

Although it was late at night, the room was brightly lit. The old marquis, Ding Wenxi, Concubine Wei, Qianqin, and the court physician were all gathered there.

Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath and stepped inside.

---

chapters.title: New Life
chapters.content:
"Xuanyou."

By now, everyone in the Marquis’s residence knew about the second child’s condition. They were gathered around the court physician and Qianqin discussing the matter. When Zhao Xuanyou arrived, the old marquis also looked grave. He stepped aside, signaling Zhao Xuanyou to stand next to him.

Zhao Xuanyou approached and, upon seeing his daughter’s pitiful state, his heart immediately clenched.

Because it was summer, the wet nurse had already removed the swaddling and placed the girl on the bed, covered with a thin gauze blanket.

This was something Ding Wenxi had sewn in advance for the two children.

The girl, already weak from birth, looked even more pitiful curled up in sleep.

"The court physician and Aunt Qianqin have examined her carefully. Although the child is weak, she can cry, eat, and sleep. As long as we take good care of her, there won’t be any problems."

"Have they been fed?" Zhao Xuanyou asked.

Qianqin replied, "Yes, they’ve been fed. The young master has been taken to the next room to sleep."

Though the young master had eaten more, the young lady had only taken a few sips before she was full.

Little as it was, as long as she could eat and sleep, she could gradually grow stronger.

The court physician also said, "Lord Hou, rest assured. I will research some medicinal meals for the wet nurse to strengthen her body with tonics, so the young lady can slowly build up her health."

Just now, Qianqin had carefully checked the milk of several wet nurses and selected two with richer milk to specifically take care of the young lady.

"Thank you for your trouble."

Zhao Xuanyou’s mood lightened slightly.

No matter the cost or effort, as long as there was a way to save her, it was fine.

Ding Wenxi stood beside them for a while before silently turning to the adjacent room.

Since the child was already asleep, the wet nurse stood up and gave her a respectful bow without speaking.

Ding Wenxi didn’t mind. She waved her hand, signaling the wet nurse to rest for a while, and sat at the head of the bed, looking at her little grandson.

Newborns were all wrinkled, but Ding Wenxi thought his features resembled Yu Wan’s when she was born, and her heart softened even more.

She reached out to touch the child’s tiny hand, but unexpectedly, the child opened his eyes a slit the next moment.

"Good child, did I wake you?" Ding Wenxi gently patted his body, trying to coax him back to sleep, but the child still kept that eye slit open.

Newborns either ate or slept, but this child was different; he actually kept his eyes open.

"Is it because you can’t see your father and mother that you won’t sleep?" Ding Wenxi picked him up and said softly, "Your mother just gave birth to you and your sister. She’s exhausted and needs to rest for the night. Your father is currently with your sister. She wasn’t strong enough in the womb, so your father needs to take care of her first. As the older brother, you should give way to your sister. Tonight, let your maternal grandmother stay with you. Tomorrow morning, we’ll take you to see your father and mother."

She rambled on, but the child still didn’t close his eyes.

Ding Wenxi had been with Yu Wan during her labor, and Yu Wan had been gripping her wrist the whole time, which was still red.

After holding him for a while, her arms ached, so she laid the child back down and lay beside him.

"Do you know? You look exactly like your mother when she was little. She grew up to be a great beauty, so you will definitely be a handsome man. I wonder how many girls will like you in the future. But, it’s too early to tell you all this. Right now, you only know how to eat and sleep. You can’t understand these things yet."

The little baby beside her let out a burp.

If he were truly a newborn, he naturally wouldn’t understand. But he had lived through a full lifetime before.

Just moments after his last breath, he heard the voice of his father, who had passed away ten years ago.

He had exerted great effort to open his eyes and finally saw the person in front of him.

It was his father, but much younger than in his memories.

His father had only glanced at him before handing him to someone else. He tried to call out to his father but found he couldn’t make a sound.

It was then that he realized he had somehow become a newborn baby.

Before he could figure out more, he was carried into a quiet room.

Only the wet nurse was there with him, and he couldn’t understand anything.

His small body tired easily, and after thinking for a while, he dozed off.

When he felt someone touch him, he opened his eyes and saw Ding Wenxi. He never expected her to be his maternal grandmother.

Maternal grandmother...

This word was very foreign to him.

In his past life, he had a father, a grandfather, and a great-grandmother, but no maternal grandmother.

When he was young, his father said his mother had died in childbirth. It wasn’t until he had established his own family that his father told him his mother had been murdered by villains after giving birth to him.

This life was truly different.

Not only did he have a father and grandfather, but also a mother and maternal grandmother.

Wait... his grandmother said he had a sister...

How did a sister come into the picture?

Moreover, according to his grandmother, his sister was his twin, and while he was strong, his sister was very frail. That was why his father couldn’t come see him tonight; he had to stay with his sister.

Zhao Mianze, oh Zhao Mianze, you couldn’t have taken up so much space in your mother’s womb that you squeezed your sister, could you?

What a mess this was.

Well, there was nothing he could do now. His father and mother would surely find a way to save his sister. He might as well obediently wait for his grandmother to take him to see them tomorrow morning.

He didn’t even know if this mother was the same one from his past life.

He yawned. Keeping his eyes open for so long had exhausted his newborn body.

No matter what the situation was in this life, his father was still the same father. Things would turn out fine.

As Zhao Mianze fell into a peaceful sleep, Yu Wan in the Tangli Courtyard lay awake, unable to sleep.

Wen Ji heard the movement inside and went to the couch. "Yu Wan?"

"Ah Ji?"

Seeing that Yu Wan was indeed awake, Wen Ji hung up the bed curtains and went to the table to fetch some water.

As Yu Wan drank, Wen Ji said, "The maids outside have been cooking porridge. If you’re hungry, I’ll get you a bowl."

"Okay."

Yu Wan hadn’t eaten a single grain of rice all day, only a little soup, and she had indeed been woken up by hunger.

Wen Ji quickly went out and came back with a bowl of chicken porridge.

It had been simmered for a long time, and the chicken had melted into the rice grains.

Yu Wan ate a mouthful of the porridge and felt some strength return to her body.

Noticing that it was so late and Wen Ji was still by her side, she suddenly felt suspicious.

"Is my husband still with the children?"

Wen Ji nodded.

Yu Wan slightly furrowed her brows, staring at Wen Ji. "Did something happen?"

Given Wen Ji’s nature, he wouldn’t hide anything from Yu Wan. However, since Zhao Xuanyou had instructed him to let Yu Wan know personally, it was better for their family matters to be handled by themselves.

"It’s not really an incident, just a small issue."

"The children have an issue?"

"Don’t worry, both are fine." Seeing her anxiety, Wen Ji hurried to reassure her. "I think Qianqin mentioned something to my brother-in-law, but I didn’t catch it all. Wait for him to come back, and you can ask him."

Yu Wan considered Wen Ji’s tone and believed him that it wasn’t a big deal.

But when it came to her children, how could she possibly feel at ease?

chapters.title: Tell Me the Truth
chapters.content:
Wen Sun saw her restless expression and, after a moment's thought, pulled up a chair and sat down, deciding to chat with her.

"Are you still in pain?"

Yu Ying had been in labor for several hours, and Wen Sun had been waiting outside the whole time.

As a shadow guard, he had endured countless inhuman training and hardships that others had never experienced.

In his heart, Yu Ying was even tougher than him. If she could cry out in such agony, childbirth must be an incredibly painful experience.

"Much better now."

Actually, she was still in pain. Right after giving birth, her lower body had been numb, so she hadn’t felt much. But after resting for so long, the pain from the tearing became more noticeable, though still bearable.

Wen Sun said, "The midwife said you had a smooth delivery. I can't imagine how unbearable it must be for those who don’t."

Hearing Wen Sun’s words, Yu Ying smiled. "Your wife will be comforted to know you think that way."

"Don’t tease me." Seeing that Yu Ying had the energy to joke, Wen Sun was relieved to see she had recovered a lot.

Since Yu Ying didn’t seem sleepy, Wen Sun said, "Last time you asked me to speak to Lin Zheng. I’ve already mentioned it to him."

The matter concerned Yingxue’s future, and sure enough, Yu Ying’s attention was drawn.

"What did he say? Does he like Yingxue?"

"He... said he doesn’t know."

Doesn’t know?

Yu Ying felt a little helpless. Liking was liking, not liking was not liking. How could there be a "doesn’t know"?

If he liked her, she would arrange their marriage. If he didn’t, she could at least give Yingxue a clear answer.

"How can he give such an ambiguous answer?"

Wen Sun said, "I actually understand how he feels."

"Did you also say 'I don’t know' when a girl told you she liked you?"

Seeing Yu Ying bring the topic back to himself, Wen Sun couldn’t help but blush.

"No girl has ever said she liked me. I just meant that Lin Zheng is like me; we were both trained as shadow guards from a young age. We only knew how to follow orders and never thought about how to live after leaving our master, let alone marriage and children."

Lin Zheng had been rescued from the heavenly prison by Zhao Xuanyou. He was alone, with nothing to his name.

His current state was probably similar to Wen Sun’s back then; he had no idea how to live an ordinary life.

"I remember you had some money when you left the Eastern Palace. Since Lin Zheng is highly regarded by the Crown Prince, he should have saved more, right?"

"He had a small house in the capital and some savings, but they were probably all confiscated by the Brocade Guards."

That made sense.

In a case of treason, those who deserved death were executed, and all their property was confiscated.

"Money isn’t the issue. If he and Yingxue truly love each other, I’ll prepare a sufficient dowry for Yingxue."

As for Lin Zheng himself, he was highly skilled in martial arts and had been well-regarded in the Eastern Palace. Zhao Xuanyou should be able to find him a good position to support his family.

But this matter required Zhao Xuanyou’s approval. Yu Ying couldn’t make promises recklessly.

Yu Ying asked, "After talking to him, do you think he likes Yingxue?"

"They seem to get along well. As for whether it’s love, I’ll ask him more clearly another day."

This answer finally satisfied Yu Ying.

"Are you still chatting?" Zhao Xuanyou lifted the curtain and entered from outside. Seeing them talking, he smiled slightly.

"How are the children?"

"The wet nurse fed them, and they’ve both fallen asleep."

Their daughter had been underweight in the womb, but fortunately, she could eat and sleep, so she would slowly grow stronger. Zhao Xuanyou felt much better.

Seeing him return, Wen Sun exchanged greetings and then tactfully left.

Zhao Xuanyou walked to Yu Ying’s side. Seeing her still awake in the middle of the night, he couldn’t help but say, "You were in pain all day. Aren’t you tired?"

In front of Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Ying didn’t want to pretend or act strong. She honestly said, "I am tired, but my body aches, and my throat is uncomfortable. It’s hard to sleep."

"Have you eaten anything?"

"Yes, I have. What about you?"

Zhao Xuanyou had eaten dinner, but after working late into the night, he was actually hungry again.

Seeing that Yu Ying wasn’t sleepy, Zhao Xuanyou ordered the kitchen to prepare a large bowl of chicken noodle soup. Yu Ying originally didn’t want to eat, but seeing him eat with relish, she let him feed her a few bites.

After the couple had filled their stomachs, Zhao Xuanyou changed clothes and prepared for bed.

"Tell me the truth. Why did you stay at Xifeng Courtyard for so long?"

Yu Ying was still awake so late not only because of the pain but mainly because she was worried about the children.

During the intense labor, she hadn’t been able to think about much. But now that she had calmed down, her thoughts were much clearer.

After their son was born, the midwife had cleaned him up and brought him to her to offer congratulations.

But when their daughter was born, the midwife and Qianqin had taken the child aside, seemingly whispering to each other.

And then Zhao Xuanyou had stayed at Xifeng Courtyard for so long...

There was Grandmother, Concubine Wei, wet nurses, and medical women there. What could have kept him there for so long?

"Is it that our daughter..." Yu Ying couldn’t bring herself to finish the sentence.

Zhao Xuanyou knew she was clever. Seeing that she had already noticed something was amiss, he didn’t hide it anymore.

"Our son was strong and healthy in your womb, but our daughter was a bit frail. Earlier, we were afraid you’d worry, so we didn’t bring her over for you to see."

"How frail is she?"

As soon as Yu Ying asked, tears welled up in her eyes.

Zhao Xuanyou gently pressed her tear duct and comforted her, "Qianqin and the府医 have confirmed that our daughter can eat and sleep. Although she’s a bit weaker coming out of the womb, she’ll slowly grow stronger."

"This is such a big matter. Why didn’t you tell me earlier?"

Earlier, when he saw their daughter’s little face was purple, how could Zhao Xuanyou have brought her to Yu Ying?

Now that he was sure their daughter was out of danger, he dared to tell Yu Ying.

"It was only hidden for a while. Tomorrow morning, I’ll have them bring the children over for you to see."

Tonight, the Marquis’s residence welcomed two new lives, which should have been a great joy. Unfortunately, their daughter’s frailty had cast a shadow over the happiness.

Fortunately, everything was safe.

Yu Ying didn’t speak for a long time. Zhao Xuanyou knew she wouldn’t be able to sleep tonight.

"Shall we think of names for the children?"

Even when Yu Ying had just conceived, the family had started brainstorming names; both for boys and girls.

When they learned that Yu Ying was carrying twins, they started over, considering names for two boys, two girls, or one of each. Even Old Lady Ye, who was staying in the capital, had sent a letter to Yuzhou with the names she had come up with.

"You’ve already decided, haven’t you?" Yu Ying said.

Zhao Xuanyou had already come up with several names, but the old Marquis and Ding Wenxi had also suggested some. With Old Lady Ye’s additions, there were more than twenty names in total.

The family was so enthusiastic about this matter, and Yu Ying’s literary talent couldn’t compare, so she hadn’t bothered to think about it.

"There are so many names, and no one can convince the others. You’re their mother. You choose."

---

chapters.title: Mianze
chapters.content:
Yu Ying had seen all the names the elders had come up with, and she knew the ones Zhao Xuanyou had suggested.

Originally, she had been indecisive. After all, each name carried deep meaning and represented the family’s wishes for the two children.

But after learning about their daughter’s frailty, Yu Ying suddenly had an idea.

"I remember Grandmother came up with a pair of names with very good meanings."

"Which pair?"

"Mianze and Ruiyan."

Zhao Xuanyou silently repeated the names Zhao Mianze and Zhao Ruiyan a few times and grew to like them.

"They sound pleasant, and the meanings are excellent."

When Old Lady Ye had chosen these two names, she had hoped for the Marquis’s descendants to have lasting fortune and longevity, which aligned with Yu Ying’s current wishes.

"Yes. Grandmother has lived a peaceful and prosperous life, full of health and longevity. I hope our children can share some of her good fortune."

Zhao Xuanyou knew she was still worried about their daughter. He gently stroked her hair and softly said, "They will."

The couple embraced and talked for a while before Yu Ying finally felt sleepy and fell into a deep sleep.

Originally, Zhao Xuanyou had told the wet nurse to bring the children over the next morning, but since Yu Ying was sleeping so deeply, he instructed them to take good care of the children at Xifeng Courtyard.

By noon, Yu Ying woke up, and Yingxue brought lunch.

Compared to the chicken congee she had after giving birth yesterday, today’s lunch was much more sumptuous, with steamed fish, eight-treasure tofu, stir-fried green melon, and of course, a bowl of chicken soup.

Yu Ying hadn’t eaten much the night before, so she had essentially gone a day and a night without food.

As she was eating, Ding Wenxi arrived.

Last night, after Yu Ying had given birth, she had been extremely weak. Zhao Xuanyou had carried her back to Tangli Courtyard shortly after, so mother and daughter hadn’t had a chance to talk.

Seeing that Yu Ying had a good appetite, Ding Wenxi didn’t need to ask to know that she was already out of danger.

Since Yu Ying didn’t need to breastfeed the children herself, she could recover gradually by eating and resting on time during her confinement.

After a brief exchange of greetings, Yu Ying said, "Mother, the Marquis and I have already chosen names for the children."

"Oh?"

"The eldest is Zhao Mianze, and the second is Zhao Ruiyan."

"Mianze, Ruiyan; such beautiful names with wonderful meanings."

Although Ding Wenxi’s suggested names hadn’t been chosen, hearing that Yu Ying had selected these two names, she understood the hopes she and Zhao Xuanyou had for the children and naturally thought they were good choices.

"Did Xuanyou tell you about Ruiyan?"

"I already know."

Seeing that Yu Ying’s emotions were relatively stable, Ding Wenxi felt slightly relieved and softly said, "Last night, I stayed at Xi Feng Hall for a long time. I saw both children. Mianze looks very healthy and sleeps soundly. Ruiyan is small and thin, but she can eat, and she slept peacefully last night. She’ll grow stronger gradually."

Hearing this, Yu Ying’s thoughts returned to the children.

She had only caught a brief glimpse of Mianze yesterday and hadn’t seen her little Ruiyan yet.

As she looked up, she saw Yingxue leading two wet nurses into the room.

Yu Ying reached out to take the swaddled baby from one of them. As soon as she saw the chubby baby inside, she knew it was her son, Zhao Mianze.

In her past life, the son she had given birth to had been taken away by Madame Zhou before she even got a chance to see him. She didn’t know if that son had been as sturdy as Mianze.

Seeing the tears in her eyes, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but worry.

She had cried just seeing their son. What would happen when she saw their frail daughter?

"Yingying." He sat down next to Yu Ying and wiped away her tears.

Yu Ying sniffled, suppressing the memories of her past life. She lowered her head, kissed her son, then handed the swaddled baby to Zhao Xuanyou and reached out to take her daughter.

At the first sight of her daughter, Yu Ying’s breath caught in her throat.

Her daughter was noticeably smaller than her son, looking wrinkled. Before Yu Ying even realized it, the tears she had been holding back surged forward.

Zhao Xuanyou gave the wet nurse a look, and the wet nurse quickly stepped forward. "Madam need not worry too much. Miss is weaker than Young Master, but among the children I’ve cared for, she’s not the smallest. If she can survive outside, she’ll certainly thrive in such a wealthy family."

The wet nurse wasn’t just offering empty comfort.

The little girl looked particularly pitiful because her brother was so robust. The comparison between the two made the difference more obvious.

When she had just been born yesterday, her complexion had been a bit purple, which wasn’t good. But after a night of care, her little face already looked much healthier.

"There’s something else I’d like to report to Madam."

Since Yu Ying was staring at her daughter without speaking, Zhao Xuanyou asked, "What is it?"

"Young Master... doesn’t like drinking milk."

"What?" Zhao Xuanyou asked in surprise, and Yu Ying also looked up.

The wet nurse had originally wanted to tell Yu Ying, but since Yu Ying had been distracted, and it was a bit awkward to discuss such matters in front of Zhao Xuanyou, she hesitated. But now that she had started, she had to continue. "We several wet nurses tried to feed Young Master, but he wouldn’t drink. Finally, one wet nurse thought of expressing the milk and feeding him with a spoon, and he drank a little."

"Did he eat enough?"

"He can drink three spoonfuls at a time. For a newborn, that’s quite a lot."

"Did you ask Grandma Qianqin? What did she say?"

"Grandma Qianqin said that as long as he can eat, it’s fine. Maybe the child doesn’t know how to suckle."

Hearing this, Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying felt a little relieved.

Yu Ying turned her head, her eyes still fixed on her daughter.

Ding Wenxi saw this and, along with the wet nurses and maids, left the room, allowing the family of four to have some quiet time together.

Zhao Xuanyou held his son and sat next to Yu Ying.

He looked at Yu Ying, then at the daughter in her arms.

He had seen their daughter right after she was born last night. At that time, his heart had almost been shattered.

Now, as he looked at his daughter, his emotions had already calmed. He simply sat beside Yu Ying, softly comforting her.

Zhao Mianze lay in his swaddle, tilting his head to look at his young father, his feelings somewhat complicated.

His father had passed away ten years ago. He never thought he would see his father again, especially not so young and handsome.

His father looked at his sister, then glanced down at him and suddenly sighed.

Zhao Mianze understood. His sister had been born frail, and his parents must be very worried. And just now, the wet nurse had "reported" that he wouldn’t drink milk, which must have also worried his father.

He wasn’t trying to cause trouble for his parents on purpose. It was just that... as a grown man, he simply couldn’t accept the idea of drinking milk.

If it were his mother’s, that would be fine, but it was from a wet nurse.

Anyway, he could drink from a spoon. After some time, his parents would understand that he wouldn’t starve.

This morning, when he learned that his parents had named him Zhao Mianze, he was almost certain that in this life, he was still himself. But what about his mother...

In his past life, Zhao Mianze had never seen his birth mother. But in this life, he had a father, a mother, and a sister.

What was going on?

In his past life, his father had rarely spoken to him about his mother. In his old age, when he occasionally mentioned her, he would say he knew nothing about her.

But Zhao Mianze thought, if his father had truly known nothing about his mother, how could he have raised him alone?

Fortunately, he was still just a newborn baby. He had plenty of time to figure everything out.

Since heaven had given him a different life, he would definitely cherish and protect his hard-won family, ensuring that his father and mother could grow old together.

chapters.title: Confinement Period
chapters.content:
"You just gave birth, and Aunt Qianqin reminded you to rest more," Zhao Xuanyou said, worried that Yu Yuan’s arms would ache from holding the child for so long. He wanted to take his daughter from her, but Yu Yuan refused to let go.

"You hold Mianze properly. I’ll hold Ruiyan. She’s so light, how could holding her tire me?"

Seeing how insistent Yu Yuan was, Zhao Xuanyou had no choice but to let her be.

But after waiting a while, Yu Yuan still showed no intention of putting the child down. He had to persuade her again, "Let the wet nurse take her back to sleep for a while. You can hold her again at dinner."

Before Yu Yuan could respond, Zhao Xuanyou called the wet nurse in. After handing over their son, he waited a moment, and finally, Yu Yuan released her grip.

Once the wet nurse had taken both children away, Yu Yuan leaned against Zhao Xuanyou, feeling so aggrieved she wanted to cry.

She couldn’t understand it; Zhao Xuanyou was so strong and healthy, and she wasn’t weak either. So why was their daughter so frail?

Looking at her daughter’s tiny arms and legs, Yu Yuan couldn’t help but want to cry.

"Earlier, I heard my father say that when I was born, I was just as small as Ruiyan," Zhao Xuanyou said.

"Really?" Yu Yuan looked at him, confused.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded, his expression darkening slightly as he recalled his past, though his tone remained calm. "My mother suffered a lot during her ten months of pregnancy. When I was born, I weighed only five jin. My grandmother even worried I wouldn’t survive. But look at me now; I’m fine."

Seeing that Zhao Xuanyou was bringing up his own painful past to comfort her, Yu Yuan grabbed his arm and shook it, then tilted her head to kiss him.

Zhao Xuanyou smiled faintly. "Our daughter must take after me. She’ll definitely grow up just as strong."

"I just can’t help feeling sad whenever I look at her. I didn’t mean to bring up your painful memories."

His mother had passed away so many years ago, yet her absence remained a scar in Zhao Xuanyou’s heart.

Perhaps it no longer hurt, but the scar would always be there.

Mentioning his late mother made Yu Yuan suddenly think of something. "A few days ago, I heard my mother say that your father and mother met in Jiangnan. Did you know that?"

"I do. The Feng family is a scholarly clan in Jiangnan. Does my mother-in-law know my mother?"

So his father had never mentioned it to him.

"Not that she met your mother, but she’s heard about your parents’ story," Yu Yuan said softly. "I told you before; my mother met Cui Lingyuan when she accompanied the late emperor and empress on their tour of Jiangnan. At that time, many noble youths from the capital followed the imperial procession, and your father was among them."

"My mother shouldn’t have had any contact with the imperial carriage, though."

"From what I heard, your mother was saved by your father when she encountered bandits, and that’s when they fell in love at first sight."

"I see."

The Jingyuan Marquis’s residence was a high-ranking noble family in the capital. Historically, their marriages were arranged among the well-connected aristocratic families in the capital. For example, Zhao Xuanyou’s grandfather had married a lady from the Ye family of the Anning Marquis’s residence. Zhao Xuanyou had always wondered. Though his maternal grandfather held a high official position, how had his father ended up proposing to a daughter from a scholarly family?

Now it turned out his parents had met by chance in Jiangnan and fallen in love at first sight.

Given his father’s character, once he had set his mind on someone, he would naturally bring her into the family.

Thinking of this, Zhao Xuanyou sighed. "But who knows if that encounter was a blessing or a curse. My grandmother once told me that after my mother married into the marquis’s residence, she was often criticized by my grandmother for not conceiving. The more my father protected her, the more distressed she felt."

"Did your father always protect your mother? What about Concubine Wei?"

"Concubine Wei was my mother’s maid. Back then, my mother had been unable to conceive for years. My grandmother was anxious, and my mother was even more so," Zhao Xuanyou explained.

Yu Yuan had heard before that the marquis and his wife had a deep affection for each other. Learning from Ding Wenxi that his parents had fallen in love in Jiangnan, she had guessed that the marquis must be as devoted as Zhao Xuanyou.

Now, hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this, she became even more confused.

If the marquis had been so devoted to his wife, why had he elevated Concubine Wei?

Seeing her expression, Zhao Xuanyou explained, "Concubine Wei was my mother’s personal maid. After my mother had been married for several years without conceiving, my grandmother grew anxious, and my mother was even more so. So she herself elevated her own maid to the status of concubine. My father opposed it at the time and never shared a bed with Concubine Wei."

"Ah, I see."

No wonder Concubine Wei had never borne any children.

Zhao Xuanyou continued, "In the end, my mother conceived me. But that pregnancy was extremely difficult for her. After giving birth to me, her health deteriorated. Even though my father used the finest tonics to nourish her, she only lived a few more years. After my mother passed away, Concubine Wei devoted herself to helping my grandmother raise me. My grandmother noticed her feelings for my father and sent her to Yuzhou."

"Ah, I see."

In Yu Yuan’s memory, Concubine Wei was a chaste and gentle woman who got along well with both the masters and servants of the marquis’s residence. She hadn’t realized that Concubine Wei’s path had been so difficult.

It was no wonder Zhao Xuanyou always cherished the memory of his late mother but remained kind to Concubine Wei.

After a moment of silence, Yu Yuan said, "When we first decided to return to Yuzhou, your father was too embarrassed to come with us. Now that you two are finally together, you don’t have to always stay by my side and the children’s. You can spend time with your father, drink with him, talk with him."

Their father-son bond was deep, but because they hadn’t spent much time together, there was some estrangement between them. Feelings like the story of how his parents met in Jiangnan were things his father should have told him personally.

Zhao Xuanyou held Yu Yuan and gently rubbed her hair before pressing a kiss to her forehead.

The days of her confinement were peaceful and sweet.

Though Zhao Mianze refused to nurse and had to be fed with a spoon by the wet nurse every day, he ate and slept well, his body strong. As for Zhao Ruiyan, though she had been born weak, as Aunt Qianqin had said, she could eat and sleep well and was very well-behaved.

Apart from the short time she spent nursing, Ruiyan spent the rest of her time sleeping. Day by day, she grew fairer and plumper.

Neither child cried or fussed, and the wet nurses all said they had never cared for such well-behaved children.

Seeing the children thriving, Yu Yuan finally felt at ease and shifted some of her attention back to herself.

Since she didn’t need to nurse the children herself, the physician had given her stir-fried barley sprouts to dry up her milk.

After ten months of pregnancy, even though she hadn’t overeaten, her figure had still softened and rounded. Even after giving birth, she couldn’t fit into her old clothes.

Yu Yuan wanted to quickly regain her former figure, so during her confinement, she ate lightly.

Though she stayed indoors, she made sure to move around slowly in the mornings and evenings when it was cool.

By the time the children were a month old, Yu Yuan’s waist was only an inch larger than before her pregnancy.

When she proudly showed this off to Zhao Xuanyou, he stared for a moment before clearing his throat awkwardly.

---

chapters.title: Bathing
chapters.content:
In his eyes, though Yu Yuan’s waist wasn’t as slender as before, her chest had become even more striking.

He couldn’t look away.

"I’m talking to you," Yu Yuan said.

Zhao Xuanyou sighed helplessly. "Don’t rush to fit into your old clothes. It’s better to wear looser ones."

The full-month banquet for Mianze and Ruiyan would have many guests. He didn’t want others staring at Yu Yuan.

Yu Yuan didn’t catch the subtext. Stubbornly, she said, "I can fit into my old clothes."

"Suit yourself." Zhao Xuanyou gave in.

Yu Yuan tried on two more outfits before finally choosing one for the banquet.

Returning to the window, she saw Zhao Xuanyou sitting absentmindedly, lost in thought.

"It’s getting dark. I’ll have Yingxue bring the children over."

"Not tonight." Zhao Xuanyou exhaled heavily and pulled Yu Yuan into his arms. "Even though we have two more people in the family, you can’t just focus on them and ignore me."

Since both children were so well-behaved, they rarely cried at night.

After resting for about ten days, Yu Yuan had the wet nurses take turns bringing the children to the Tangli Courtyard. At night, the children slept between the couple.

At first, Zhao Xuanyou had enjoyed this warm family scene. But now, if he wanted to hold Yu Yuan close, it was difficult.

During her confinement, it had been fine, but now that it was over, and Yu Yuan still wanted to sleep with the children, how were they supposed to be intimate?

At this point, Yu Yuan couldn’t help but understand Zhao Xuanyou’s intentions.

Before she could speak, Zhao Xuanyou’s "magic claws" reached out.

Even through her clothes, the softness was intoxicating.

Yu Yuan was a little annoyed, but then she thought about how, ever since she became pregnant, Zhao Xuanyou had lived like a monk.

After returning to Yuzhou from the capital, they had only been intimate once.

After that, out of concern for the twins, Zhao Xuanyou had been on his best behavior every night, not daring to touch her at all.

Seeing his pitiful state, Yu Yuan softened her voice. "Then let them stay in Xifeng Courtyard tonight. We can have them back tomorrow."

Zhao Xuanyou knew his wife was being kind. The corners of his lips twitched, but his smile was bittersweet.

He had subtly asked Aunt Qianqin for advice. Having served many noblewomen in the palace, Aunt Qianqin naturally understood his meaning.

Considering how much Zhao Xuanyou cherished Yu Yuan, she said that it should be fine after the confinement period, but resting an extra month would be even better.

After some thought, Zhao Xuanyou said, "Tonight, let Mianze and Ruiyan sleep with the wet nurse."

Even with children, they should have time for themselves as a couple.

His hands didn’t stop moving. Yu Yuan bit her lip. "I agreed, but don’t go too far tonight."

Zhao Xuanyou sighed deeply. "Don’t worry, I won’t. I just want to help you bathe."

During her month of confinement, Yu Yuan had followed tradition and not bathed, only letting the maids help her wipe down.

Now that her confinement was over and they had guests to entertain, Yu Yuan had ordered the maids to prepare water so she could bathe properly that night.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou’s words, Yu Yuan smiled and teased, "A mighty Marquis of Jingyuan. Now you’re all talk and no action?"

"I was being considerate, thinking you should rest another month. Don’t mistake my good intentions."

Yu Yuan just gave him a coy smile and lightly poked his chin.

That night, Zhao Xuanyou served Yu Yuan in the bath, carefully washing her. After drying her off and carrying her back to the bed, he proudly said, "Didn’t I keep my word?"

Keep his word? Apart from that place, he had taken advantage of her everywhere else.

Zhao Xuanyou lay down beside her. Yu Yuan and the two children had safely passed the most dangerous first month after birth. With her in his arms, he could finally breathe a sigh of relief.

The full-month banquet for the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence was lively.

Local relatives and friends in Yuzhou all came to offer their congratulations. Close friends from the capital also sent gifts. Especially when Old Lady Ye heard that Yu Yuan had safely given birth to twins, she sent over all her most precious treasures; all for Yu Yuan.

As for the two great-grandchildren, Old Lady Ye gave them a box, saying it was for the whole family to open together.

The evening after the banquet, Yu Yuan had a Persian rug laid out under the begonia tree, with a bamboo mat on top, and brought the whole family out to enjoy the cool air.

Yu Yuan placed her son on the bamboo mat and sat against the tree, holding her daughter.

Zhao Xuanyou opened the box his grandmother had sent. When he saw what was inside, he laughed.

It turned out the box contained his childhood toys.

Though they had been stored for over a decade, Old Lady Ye had them refurbished and cleaned, so they looked just as they had before.

Yu Yuan glanced at them. The nine-linked rings and Lu Ban locks were too advanced for the little ones, so she picked up a cloth tiger and placed it next to Zhao Mianze, then took a rattle and shook it to amuse her daughter.

Both children were the apples of her eye.

But her son had been born strong, while her daughter, though improving day by day, still seemed small and fragile compared to her brother.

Yu Yuan couldn’t help but pay more attention to her daughter.

Zhao Mianze, seeing his mother focusing on his sister with the rattle, felt a little sour.

He understood; his mother wasn’t being partial. It was just that his sister had been born weaker.

Moreover, as the older brother, he should be the one taking care of his sister.

As he brooded, Zhao Mianze suddenly felt lighter.

His father had taken his sister from his mother’s arms, and his mother had picked him up.

"You’ve grown so well, Mianze."

Yu Yuan held her son in front of her, weighing him in her arms, and kissed his forehead.

His mother smelled so good.

Zhao Mianze sniffed and tried his best to open his eyes wide to look at her.

During her confinement, his eyelids had been heavy, and he could only open his eyes a little. Even though he saw his mother every day, he hadn’t been able to see her clearly.

Now, with his mother holding him in front of her, he finally saw her face clearly.

She was delicate and beautiful, with fair, soft skin and a radiant glow.

Zhao Mianze took one look at her and confirmed that this woman was indeed his mother from his past life. Her brows and eyes were too much like his own from before.

Previously, he had always doubted, afraid that he was a reincarnated soul in another’s body, fearing that in this life, his father had married someone else and lived a fulfilling life. But it turned out his father had married his very own mother, who had passed away early in his past life.

His nose twitched, and with a loud "Wah!" he burst into tears.

"Oh, why is Mianze crying?" Ding Wenxi happened to enter the Tangli Courtyard and saw the family of four sitting under the begonia tree to enjoy the cool air. She hadn’t wanted to disturb them, but when Zhao Mianze started crying, she couldn’t help but approach in concern. "Mianze is usually so sensible. He rarely cries."

"Maybe I didn’t hold him properly." Yu Yuan looked at her wailing son, feeling a pang of guilt.

During her confinement, Zhao Xuanyou had constantly reminded her not to overexert herself, so she had rarely held the children. And when she did, it was mostly Ruiyan.

It seemed she would have to hold her son more often in the future, or he might not feel close to her.

chapters.title: Clashing Destinies
chapters.content:
As soon as Ding Wenxi entered the courtyard, the maidservants immediately brought over chairs.

Zhao Xuanyou, fearing that his mother-in-law might sit idle, ordered someone to invite Wen Qi, the Old Marquis, and Madame Wei to join them in enjoying the cool evening.

Yuzhou was close to the Western Regions, so in summer, the fruits there were even fresher and more abundant than in the capital.

The whole family took turns holding the two children and playing with them. Amidst the laughter, they also gave the children pet names: "Chun" for Zhao Mianze and "Ning" for Zhao Ruiyan, both names carrying their hopes for the children.

Unfortunately, despite their high hopes, after her confinement period, their daughter caught colds one after another.

Both children were raised the same way, eating, sleeping, and going out together. Chun was perfectly fine, but Ning fell ill repeatedly.

Yu Wan knew her daughter was weak from birth and did not blame the wet nurse or the maids. While carefully tending to her daughter, she no longer dared to take Ning outside.

Neither husband nor wife spoke of it, but a heavy weight pressed on both their hearts.

Their daughter couldn't stay indoors forever, could she?

If summer was already so difficult, what would happen when autumn arrived and the weather turned cold?

The marquis's household cautiously reached the hundredth day of the two children. Yu Wan had no mood to host a grand celebration, so they simply gathered as a family for a meal.

After dinner, Yu Wan placed the two children on the couch and carefully tucked them in.

Ning had already fallen asleep, but Zhao Mianze was still wide-eyed, staring at Yu Wan.

Seeing her son's well-behaved appearance, Yu Wan couldn't help but reach out and pinch his cheek.

"Mother sent a letter today."

Zhao Xuanyou changed into his nightclothes and walked to the side of the couch, his expression somewhat unclear.

Sensing the strangeness in Zhao Xuanyou's tone, Yu Wan immediately looked up with concern: "Is she disappointed?"

Originally, they had persuaded the Marquis to come to Yuzhou with them, hoping to give Zhao Xuanyou more time to bond with his father. But the Old Dowager was advanced in years and accustomed to living in the capital, so naturally, she wouldn't leave with them.

Both Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had promised the Old Dowager that they would bring Chun and Ning back to the capital to see their great-grandmother at the end of the year. But with Ning's frail health, it was impossible to take her back to the capital.

Last month, Zhao Xuanyou had already sent a letter to his grandmother, mentioning Ning's congenital weakness and informing her that this year, only he and the Old Marquis would return to the capital for the New Year.

Yu Wan knew how much the Old Dowager Leaf longed to see her two great-grandchildren, but she couldn't bear to be separated from the children. Since Ning couldn't travel, naturally Chun would have to stay as well.

"Grandmother knows about Ning's frail health and understands our difficulties. Even if we didn't say anything, she wouldn't let Ning take the risk."

"Then what is it?"

Zhao Xuanyou sat down beside Yu Wan and sighed, "After learning about Ning's congenital weakness, Grandmother was also very worried. She personally went to Bailin Temple to pray for the safety of both children and also drew lots there."

"Was it an upper or lower lot?" Yu Wan asked anxiously.

Bailin Temple had a very prosperous incense business, and the masters in the temple were not charlatans but enlightened monks.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou speak so seriously, Yu Wan was extremely nervous.

"Both children drew upper lots."

"Amitabha, thank the Buddha for his blessings."

Seeing Yu Wan's relief, Zhao Xuanyou's expression became even stranger.

Yu Wan pushed him with her hand and looked at him in confusion: "If they are upper lots, why do you have such an expression? Stop keeping me in suspense. Are you trying to worry me to death?"

Zhao Xuanyou wasn't trying to keep her in suspense; he just didn't know how to say it.

"The lot texts for both children are of the highest quality, but the master in the temple said that when these two lots are placed together, they clash."

"Clash?" Yu Wan paused for a moment before realizing, "You mean Chun and Ning's destinies clash?"

At this point, Yu Wan also understood Zhao Xuanyou's hesitation.

If the lot texts said that her two darlings' destinies clashed, didn't that mean Ning's illnesses were because Chun was harming her?

"This... is nonsense, right?"

Although she said so, Yu Wan didn't sound confident.

If it were monks from somewhere else, Yu Wan could dismiss them as heretics, but Bailin Temple was different.

"Grandmother didn't believe it at first either, so she also invited a Taoist from Fulong Observatory to divine for both children. The divination..."

The Old Dowager Leaf had believed in Buddhism for more than a decade, but for the sake of her two great-grandchildren, she had broken her usual practice and entered a Taoist temple, only to receive the same result.

"Also the same?"

Sensing Yu Wan's concern, Zhao Xuanyou took her hand, "The Taoist also said that both children have good destinies. Our Chun is even a 'heaven-sent star.' You don't need to worry too much."

"But they are siblings, destined to be family. If they harm each other..."

Yu Wan looked at her sleeping daughter, remembering how she had been burning with fever last month, unable to even drink milk, and couldn't help but feel her nose tingle.

On the side, Zhao Mianze, listening to his parents' conversation, panicked.

His parents might not have realized the implications of the phrase "heaven-sent star," but Zhao Mianze understood all too well.

He didn't belong here at all.

At this moment, Zhao Mianze finally confirmed that he wasn't possessing a body but had appeared out of thin air in his mother's womb, taking his sister's place and squeezing her until she was thin and small, congenital deficiency.

Sister, I'm sorry, truly sorry.

Unfortunately, he was now just a little baby who could only lie there, unable to make amends to his sister.

After a moment of silence, Yu Wan asked: "Can we ask them to perform a ritual to resolve the clash for the two children?"

"They did mention a method, but it's not a ritual."

"What should we do?" Yu Wan looked at Zhao Xuanyou expectantly.

Zhao Xuanyou lowered his eyes and said softly, "Adopt one of the children out, and the clashing destinies can be broken."

What?

Adopt a child out?

Upon hearing this, Yu Wan didn't get angry but laughed instead.

At this moment, the son beside Yu Wan hummed a few times. Yu Wan turned her head and saw her son looking restless, so she quickly picked him up.

"Chun, don't be afraid. Mother will take good care of you and your sister. You will both grow up well in the Marquis's mansion. No one will be adopted out."

This was said not only for the two children to hear but also for Zhao Xuanyou and herself.

Both children were her flesh and blood; she would never give them up for adoption.

And Zhao Xuanyou, how could he bear to part with them?

In the letter, the grandmother mentioned that she had already discussed it with the Anning Marquis's family. They could adopt Ning into the Ye family. This way, the child would still be connected to the Marquis's family by name and could still be raised in the Marquis's mansion.

Yu Wan's words just now also expressed his own feelings.

He gently patted his restless son and, together with Yu Wan, softly coaxed, "Chun, don't be afraid. Father will protect you."

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan decided to pretend that this matter never happened. However, the Old Dowager had already anticipated that the couple would not be willing to part with their children. She had written to the Old Marquis and Ding Wenxi about the lot texts and divination results she obtained from Bailin Temple and Fulong Observatory.

The next morning, as soon as the couple got up, Zhao Xuanyou was called away by the Old Marquis.

Yu Wan had just sat up when Yingxue said that Ding Wenxi also wanted to see her.

Yu Wan was feeling anxious and didn't go over, choosing instead to stay by the children's side on the couch.

As she was lost in thought, she heard footsteps behind her.

---

chapters.title: Adoption
chapters.content:
Yu Wan looked up and met Wen Qi's worried gaze.

For some reason, thinking about her mother and father-in-law inquiring about the children's destinies, Yu Wan felt a sense of heaviness in her heart.

But if it was Wen Qi asking, she felt no burden at all.

Her gaze was steady, neither evasive nor forced a smile. She pursed her lips slightly, gesturing for Wen Qi to sit down.

"Did Chun and Ning sleep with you last night?"

"They were both very well-behaved at night. Not to mention one night, even if I had to take care of them every night, it wouldn't be tiring." After a pause, Yu Wan looked at Wen Qi, "Did you hear about it?"

Wen Qi nodded.

"Do you believe in these things?" Yu Wan asked.

Wen Qi naturally didn't believe in ghosts, and based on his understanding of Yu Wan, she probably didn't either.

But Wen Qi could see that in the past few days, when Ning was ill, Yu Wan had been exhausted, both physically and mentally, for her sake.

When it came to herself, she might not believe in such superstitions, but when it came to Ning, she might not dare to take the risk.

"I don't believe in it."

"Then why are you here to persuade me on Mother's behalf?"

In the eyes of the elders, Ning would eventually get married. Even if she was adopted into another family, it wouldn't matter much, as she could still be raised in the Marquis's mansion.

But Yu Wan simply didn't agree.
