Hearing this, Wen Qi realized that Yu Wan had misunderstood his intentions. After waiting for her to change Chun and Ning's diapers, he softly said, "Actually, you could adopt Ning to me."

Yu Wan looked at Wen Qi in surprise.

"Is this Mother's idea or yours?"

"This morning, Mother told me about Chun and Ning's clashing destinies. I had an idea in my mind. It's my own thought; I haven't discussed it with Mother yet. I just came to ask for your opinion first."

Yu Wan looked at her son and daughter sleeping side by side on the couch and sighed softly.

"I know you mean well, but your brother-in-law and I will never send our children away."

"How could I send the child away when I and Mother will always be by your side?"

Yu Wan turned to look at Wen Qi, giving him a grateful smile: "We are a family. No matter where the children live, we will never let them belong to someone else."

"How could they belong to someone else? Mother's surname is Ding, my surname is Ding, your surname is Ding. If Ning also takes the surname Ding, wouldn't she still be part of the family? Back when we entered Shu, you even allowed us to follow your maternal grandmother's surname, Song. No matter what, Ning taking the surname Ding won't make her any less a part of the family."

Yu Wan was momentarily stunned by Wen Qi's words.

Surname Ding?

Yes, she and Wen Qi were now called Yu Wan and Ding Qi, respectively. They both took their mother's surname. Their mother was also Ning's relative, so taking the surname Ding would still make her part of the family.

"Ding Ruiyan, that sounds very nice."

Ding Ruiyan...

Yu Wan silently repeated the name in her heart a few times and indeed found it pleasant.

"But in the future, you will eventually get married."

"Even if I get married in the future, I won't leave you and Mother," Wen Qi said firmly.

Moreover, adopting Ning under his name didn't mean he would actually take Ning away to care for her himself.

Ning would still be the precious daughter of the Jingyuan Marquis's family, growing up under the doting love of her parents.

"You think about it. If you feel it's appropriate, discuss it with your brother-in-law."

Wen Qi could see that Yu Wan was already considering it and didn't urge her to make a decision.

Adopting a daughter was no small matter. It required not only the consent of the couple but also the approval of the Old Dowager and the Old Marquis.

"I understand. Don't mention this to Mother for now."

Wen Qi nodded. After a moment of thought, he smiled at Yu Wan and said, "Apart from Ning's matter, Mother has something else to worry about."

"What is it?"

Wen Qi coughed twice, "During Chun and Ning's hundred-day banquet, General Shen also came to offer his congratulations."

Yu Wan hadn't thought about Shen Jiao for a long time.

After returning to Yuzhou, since Ding Wenxi learned that Yu Wan was pregnant with twins, she rarely went out, staying in the Marquis's mansion to take care of Yu Wan and personally preparing small clothes and quilts for the two children.

Zhao Xuanyou had mentioned to Yu Wan once that he had spoken privately with Shen Jiao.

Shen Jiao said he genuinely wanted to marry Ding Wenxi and hoped that Zhao Xuanyou could help plead his case.

Since Ding Wenxi had rejected him, the two had not spoken again.

Originally, when he wrote to the capital, it wasn't because he and Ding Wenxi had agreed on the marriage. He just felt that Ding Wenxi wasn't indifferent to him but refused to agree due to the face of her son-in-law and daughter.

He thought that if Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan didn't mind, then Ding Wenxi's knot would be untied.

Zhao Xuanyou had expressed his own attitude to him but also told him that Ding Wenxi truly didn't want to see him. If she ever changed her mind, she would let him know.

By the time Yu Wan gave birth to Chun and Ning, the entire Marquis's household was focused on the two children, and Ding Wenxi spent all her days in Xifeng Courtyard, with no time to think about Shen Jiao's affairs.

"Mother saw him during the hundred-day banquet?"

"Not that Mother wanted to see him, but he blocked Mother in the courtyard."

"He barged into the inner quarters?" Yu Wan asked in surprise.

Previously, Zhao Xuanyou had said many good things on behalf of General Shen. If he had truly trespassed into the inner quarters of the Marquis's mansion to harass Mother, then she would certainly not agree to this marriage.

"No. Yesterday, the wet nurse took Chun to the front courtyard to show him to the guests. Mother saw that the wet nurse had forgotten Chun's hat and was afraid that Chun would also catch a cold, so she went to the front courtyard to deliver the hat."

Although it was Ning who had been ill, Ding Wenxi was equally careful with Chun, taking great care of him.

Yu Wan breathed a sigh of relief. So they met in the front courtyard.

She looked at Wen Qi and said helplessly, "You saw Mother being accosted and didn't go up to help?"

"How could I appear when Mother was talking to someone?"

Wen Qi had noticed Shen Jiao walking towards Ding Wenxi and had quietly followed, afraid that Shen Jiao might be disrespectful to Mother.

But Shen Jiao didn't do anything to Mother, and Mother didn't turn and leave immediately either. Instead, she stood there and talked to Shen Jiao for a while.

Yu Wan wasn't surprised.

From the very beginning, when she discussed this matter with Mother, she had determined that Mother didn't dislike Shen Jiao. As for whether there were any feelings, Mother said there weren't, but Yu Wan wasn't sure.

"Anyway, Mother will make her own decisions about her matters. We should just pretend we don't know anything."

Wen Qi nodded. Before he could say anything else, Zhao Xuanyou came into the room, walking around the screen.

"Ah Qi, you're here."

"Brother-in-law." Wen Qi was already very familiar with Zhao Xuanyou and even greeted him with a smile.

Zhao Xuanyou walked to the side of the couch and looked at the two little ones sleeping on it before turning around.

"Speaking of which, I have something to discuss with you."

"What is it?"

"Your friend, Lin Zheng. Has he decided where he wants to go?"

Lin Zheng was an imperial guard of the Eastern Palace. Originally, Zhao Xuanyou had saved him from the heavenly prison for Yu Wan's sake. Although he had been sent to Yuzhou, Zhao Xuanyou's forces were already full of elite soldiers, and he wasn't familiar with Lin Zheng, so there was no need to incorporate him into the Mingmi Guard.

chapters.title: Not Distant
chapters.content:
"There's no problem with him staying in Yu Prefecture, but I can't keep him in the Mingzuan Guard for now."

With Lin Geng's skills, he would naturally be unwilling to be just a low-ranking soldier in the Mingzuan Guard.

But Zhao Xuanyou didn't know him well, so there was no trust to speak of.

At this point, Zhao Xuanyou slightly furrowed his brows. "Has he ever said anything to you?"

"Not really."

Although Wen Gao often spent time with Lin Geng, their conversations mostly revolved around old stories from their days as secret guards in the Eastern Palace, reminiscing about how the once-second-only-to-the-prince Eastern Palace Crown Prince had now been reduced to ashes.

As for the future, Wen Gao had only mentioned Yingxue; other matters were beyond his interference and arrangement.

Back then, he had asked Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan to rescue Lin Geng from the heavenly prison, which had already fulfilled the bond of their childhood friendship.

Wen Gao felt a little embarrassed as he said to Zhao Xuanyou, "Brother-in-law, you've stumped me. Actually, I don't know if he wants to stay in Yu Prefecture; that's just my assumption."

In Wen Gao's view, if Lin Geng wanted to leave, he would have done so when they returned to Yu Prefecture last year.

But in the end, it was still just Wen Gao's own thought.

Zhao Xuanyou knew Wen Gao was mistaken and added, "The Mingzuan Guard is a troop passed down through generations by the Jingyuan Marquis's family. I can't recklessly place him there. If he wants to seek a position in Yu Prefecture, I can arrange it."

Yu Wan saw that both of them were worried about the other misunderstanding them, so she smiled and said, "I have a good idea. Would you like to hear it?"

How could Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Gao refuse when she had spoken?

"Previously, when my mother went to the Western Regions to purchase jade, Lin Geng once volunteered. The Western Regions have many small countries, and there are plenty of bandits who rob merchants. Linglong Fang had previously lost a batch of goods. If Lin Geng is willing, we can entrust the future merchant trips to the Western Regions to him."

Lin Geng was a former Eastern Palace secret guard who had quietly escaped from the heavenly prison. Whether he joined the Mingzuan Guard or worked for the government, his skills would surely attract attention and possibly invite trouble.

The fact that he hadn't left Yu Prefecture might also be due to his concern about being recognized elsewhere.

Going to the Western Regions would be different. In the eyes of the Hu people, all Central Plains people looked similar. Who would pay attention to him?

Zhao Xuanyou nodded slightly. "That's a good idea. If he is willing to stay in Yu Prefecture, he can work at Linglong Fang for a few years. If a suitable position comes up later, I'll arrange it."

Wen Gao thought that going to the Western Regions for trade was an excellent idea. He had read the Western Regions' records of customs and scenery collected by Yu Wan and was quite interested in the exotic customs of Tianzhu and Persia.

When Lin Geng went on his merchant trips to the Western Regions, Wen Gao even wanted to go along.

Wen Gao had come today to discuss the adoption matter with Yu Wan. He could see that Yu Wan was already moved and needed to discuss it with Zhao Xuanyou. After sitting for a while in the Tangli Courtyard, he left.

Zhao Xuanyou sat down next to Yu Wan. Following her gaze, he saw that Ah Chun had already woken up and was looking at them with wide eyes.

He picked up the rattle beside him and shook it a couple of times. The crisp dong dong dong sound made Ah Chun wave his little arms as if trying to grab it.

The father and son played happily, and Yu Wan smiled along, then took the rattle and softly said, "Ah Ning is still asleep. Don't wake her."

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement and put his arm around Yu Wan's shoulder. "I've already talked to Father about the adoption..."

Before he could finish, Yu Wan covered his mouth with her hand.

"Let me speak first."

Zhao Xuanyou raised an eyebrow, signaling his agreement.

He could see that Yu Wan's eyes were as calm as a deep pool, with a touch of charming grace added to the worry and hesitation from the day before. It was clear that she had made up her mind.

He stared into Yu Wan's eyes, waiting for her answer.

"Let's have Ah Ning adopted by Ah Gao."

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze froze for a moment before he came back to his senses and asked, "Did he come to talk about this just now?"

"Mmm," Yu Wan's voice was soft, with a hint of reluctance and pity. "If Ah Ning is adopted by her, she'll take the Ding surname in the future, and it won't feel distant from us."

Last night, the couple had discussed and agreed on this, but Yu Wan had barely slept.

Zhao Xuanyou indeed didn't believe in ghosts or gods, but Yu Wan was different.

She was a person who had lived a previous life. If there were no ghosts or gods in the world, how could she have been reborn?

She hadn't seen ghosts or gods with her own eyes, but she believed that many things simply couldn't be explained.

Both the master of White Horse Temple and the Taoist priest of Fulong Observatory said that the two children's fates clashed. If they weren't adopted out, wouldn't Ah Ning be tormented by illness for the rest of her life?

Yu Wan couldn't gamble with her daughter's life.

After getting up, she wanted to persuade Zhao Xuanyou. She was waiting for Zhao Xuanyou to return from his father's place and tell her that he had changed his mind. Coincidentally, Wen Gao had come over.

"You think it's okay?" Zhao Xuanyou hadn't spoken for a long time, so Yu Wan had to ask.

Yu Wan changing her mind so quickly did surprise Zhao Xuanyou a bit.

But after thinking carefully, he felt the same as Yu Wan.

Although no matter where Ah Ning was adopted, she would still be by their side, adopting her to Wen Gao didn't feel distant at all.

First, because he shared the Ding surname with Yu Wan, and second, because of his deep friendship with Yu Wan. Not to mention Yu Wan, even Zhao Xuanyou was sure that he would never betray Yu Wan.

"Ding Ruiyan?"

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this name, Yu Wan's heart moved, and a smile immediately appeared in her eyes as she nodded firmly.

"Ah Ning looks too pitiful when she's sick. Let's try this method first. If her health really improves in the future, I'm willing to have her adopted out for her sake. If there's still no improvement..." Yu Wan sighed, "If it's Wen Gao, we can always adopt Ah Ning back into our own family without any issue."

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

"I understand."

After the couple had decided, they informed the old Marquis and Ding Wenxi the same day.

For the old Marquis, whether the adoption was to the Anning Marquis's family or to Wen Gao didn't make much difference. Ah Ning wasn't really being sent to another family, so there was no need to insist on the title of the Marquis's granddaughter. After all, raised in the Marquis's residence, who wouldn't know she was Zhao Xuanyou's daughter when it came time to discuss her marriage?

For Ding Wenxi, it was an extra layer of delight. With Ah Ning taking her surname, she felt much closer to her.

Perhaps the two children really did have clashing destinies.

After autumn, the weather grew colder day by day. After Ah Ning changed from Zhao Ruiyan to Ding Ruiyan, she didn't fall ill even once.

By the time the cold December arrived, the old Marquis and Zhao Xuanyou prepared their New Year goods to return to the capital to spend the New Year with the old madam.

This was supposed to be the first New Year for their family of four, but Yu Wan understood better that her grandmother was advanced in years, and the number of New Years she could spend with her was decreasing year by year. Zhao Xuanyou should return to fulfill his filial piety.

Yu Wan busied herself with arranging a lively Laba Festival for the family in Yu Prefecture.

The next morning, Zhao Xuanyou kissed his sleeping son and daughter and left with Yu Wan.

It was the middle of winter, and he originally didn't want Yu Wan to see him off.

But the journey to the capital was long, and a round trip would take at least two months before he could return. Naturally, he couldn't bear to waste a single moment.

Yu Wan rode her horse with Zhao Xuanyou out of Yu Prefecture until they reached the pavilion ten miles away to finally part.

"Take care of yourself and the children."

"You must be careful in the capital as well."

Zhao Xuanyou touched her cheek, feeling the chill from the cold wind, and urged Yu Wan to return to the residence quickly.

But she refused and insisted that he mount his horse first.

Zhao Xuanyou knew her stubbornness and had no choice but to comply, mounting his horse and leaving first.

Yu Wan watched his retreating figure with unwavering eyes, her heart filled with melancholy, both for the separation and for the situation in the capital.

The emperor had still not established a new crown prince, and the capital was filled with undercurrents. Yu Wan only hoped that he would not get involved and would return quickly for a family reunion.

---

chapters.title: Warmth
chapters.content:
The New Year in Yu Prefecture was quite lively.

Yu Wan had her mother and Ah Gao by her side, as well as her growing son and daughter. With Wei Concubine, Yingxue, and Lin Geng, the Marquis's residence was filled with a harmonious atmosphere.

When Ah Chun first tried to sit up by himself, Yu Wan instinctively wanted to tell someone beside her, only to realize that Zhao Xuanyou wasn't there.

She had always thought she didn't need anyone to live, but unknowingly, she had grown accustomed to having him by her side.

For a moment, she felt a sense of loss and wrote him a sappy letter.

Fortunately, the New Year brought renewal and continuous joy.

During the Lantern Festival, Wen Gao urged Lin Geng to go out and see the lanterns. Yu Wan also took Yingxue from another direction. Amid the intersecting lights, Yingxue mustered her courage and confessed her feelings to Lin Geng. This time, Lin Geng didn't hesitate but responded decisively, even proposing marriage on the spot.

Yu Wan quickly wrote a second letter to Zhao Xuanyou, asking him to negotiate with Yingxue's parents and prepare a decent betrothal gift to send to Yingxue's family.

To Yu Wan, Yingxue was a friend who had helped her in her time of need, like a close sister.

Yingxue's family was in the capital, so the Marquis's residence was her maternal home in Yu Prefecture.

Ding Wenxi also knew of the deep friendship between Yu Wan and Yingxue, so she recognized Yingxue as her daughter and personally prepared her dowry.

Lin Geng didn't disappoint Yingxue either. He was skilled in martial arts and strategy. After two trips to the Western Regions for trade, both the goods and the companions returned safely. Other merchants in Yu Prefecture, who had suffered greatly from bandits beyond the pass, flocked to Linglong Fang to ask Lin Geng to help them transport their goods.

Yu Wan immediately had an idea and helped Lin Geng set up an escort agency.

Of course, it wasn't for free. In the future, whenever Lin Geng went to the Western Regions, he would have to help Linglong Fang purchase goods. As for how much silver he earned beyond that, it would depend on his own abilities.

While busy with the wedding preparations for Yingxue and Lin Geng, Ding Wenxi finally had a realization.

Her life had been full of setbacks, and she had missed out on many things. Now that Yu Wan had grown up, started a family, and become a mother, she could start thinking about her own life.

Yu Wan and Wen Gao noticed that their mother had started talking to General Shen again but deliberately pretended not to know.

Their mother carried a heavy burden in her heart and, unlike Yingxue, didn't want others' help. Hastily exposing the matter might only scare her.

Although life was peaceful, Yu Wan only hoped that Zhao Xuanyou would return soon.

Soon, March arrived. Spring in Yu Prefecture came later than in the Central Plains, and the branches that had been barren all winter had just begun to sprout new green leaves.

On this day, Ding Wenxi brought over a few newly made spring clothes for Ah Chun and Ah Ning. Yu Wan held them up to the children to compare.

Just as she was marveling at how fast the children were growing, Pan Xia rushed in to say that the Marquis had returned.

Yu Wan was stunned, but after coming back to her senses, she put down the clothes and hurried out.

She had only just run out of the Tangli Courtyard when she saw Zhao Xuanyou's tall figure appear before her.

Amid the surprise, Yu Wan couldn't help but feel a pang of sadness.

Clearly, she had been living well without him, but she still missed him.

Zhao Xuanyou saw Yu Wan coming out to greet him. In a flash, he appeared in front of her and grabbed her shoulders.

He had rushed back day and night from the capital and hadn't even rested at the post station last night, enduring a night of cold wind, which made him feel chilled to the bone.

"Miss me?"

There was a slight note of pride in his tone.

Yu Wan felt the coldness in his clothes and felt a pang of heartache. Hearing him tease her, she didn't engage in their usual banter but honestly said, "I missed you terribly."

There were still many people around, and Zhao Xuanyou had originally intended to restrain himself. But upon hearing this, the hand he had placed on Yu Wan's shoulder suddenly lifted her up.

The bright spring light shone on the two of them. Yu Wan's eyes sparkled, and her entire body softened.

"Let's go back and see the children first."

Afraid that Zhao Xuanyou would carry her all the way back, Yu Wan whispered, "Mother is also there."

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in agreement and carried her all the way to the entrance of the Tangli Courtyard before setting her down, then took her hand and walked inside.

As they passed the large crabapple tree, Zhao Xuanyou looked up and said, "The crabapple flowers in the capital have all bloomed. Ours here have only just sprouted new leaves."

"It's a good thing there was nothing to delay you in the capital, so you could return in time for us to enjoy the flowers together."

Zhao Xuanyou's gaze flickered slightly, but he didn't say anything.

Yu Wan noticed this and couldn't help but feel a little nervous, wondering what changes had occurred in the imperial court.

"It's Ah Chun's father who has returned."

Ding Wenxi heard the commotion in the courtyard and came out carrying Zhao Mianze.

Zhao Mianze was stronger than other babies of the same age. At just over six months old, he could already sit up by himself. Hearing that his father had returned, he turned his head to look at him, intending to greet his father but only managing to babble.

He couldn't help but feel a sense of sorrow in his heart. Being unable to walk or talk, being a baby was too boring.

"Ah Chun can already sit up." Zhao Mianze was quite heavy, but Ding Wenxi loved to hold him. Afraid that her hands would get tired, Yu Wan took Zhao Mianze and handed him to Zhao Xuanyou.

During the three months in the capital, Zhao Xuanyou had constantly missed his wife and children. Now, holding Zhao Mianze, he couldn't resist giving him a few kisses.

After Ding Wenxi exchanged a few pleasantries with her son-in-law, she left the Tangli Courtyard.

Zhao Xuanyou took Yu Wan and Zhao Mianze into the inner room and picked up Ah Ning, who was playing on the couch.

Ah Ning hadn't been sick all winter. Although she was much smaller than her brother, she had become much rounder.

At six months old, the baby hadn't grown any teeth yet, and drool would flow out whenever she smiled. She wore a new apricot-colored dress embroidered with rabbit patterns, and the soft hat on her head also had long rabbit ears. It was enough to melt Zhao Xuanyou's heart.

Zhao Xuanyou sat on the edge of the couch with the soft Ah Ning in his arms and picked up the cloth tiger beside him to play with her.

Ah Ning loved this cloth tiger the most. As soon as she saw it, she laughed.

Father and daughter played happily, while Yu Wan sat beside them with Zhao Mianze in her arms, looking somewhat helpless.

After playing with his daughter for a while, Zhao Xuanyou looked up at Yu Wan and couldn't help but smile. "What's with that expression?"

Yu Wan hesitated for a moment before sighing softly. "I don't know how to put it. This child, Ah Chun..."

"What's wrong?"

"You see how happily Ah Ning is laughing. But Ah Chun isn't like that. He couldn't even nurse as a baby and had to be fed with a spoon by the wet nurse. Now that he's older and can sit up, he doesn't react no matter how we tease him with toys. I don't know if he..."

Zhao Mianze had been sitting beside them, lost in thought. Hearing Yu Wan's words, his mind buzzed. Was his mother taking him for a fool?

He simply didn't like the childish language the wet nurses used to coax him, and of course, he had no interest in rattles or cloth tigers.

He hadn't expected his mother to think he was a fool.

Just as he was feeling helpless, he felt his father's inquisitive gaze on him.

Had he already started worrying his parents before he could even repay their kindness?

Zhao Mianze made up his mind and, looking at the cloth tiger his father offered, reluctantly waved his little fist to push the cloth tiger aside.

"Quite strong," Zhao Xuanyou turned to Yu Wan and smiled. "He just doesn't want to play."

chapters.title: The Illegitimate Son
chapters.content:
Yu Wan was surprised and looked at her son.

Zhao Mianze had been well-fed and was now plump, with round eyes just like Yu Wan’s.

Since his mother suspected he might be a fool, he didn’t dare stay still any longer. He quickly imitated his little sister’s cute mannerisms and blinked at his mother a few times.

Seeing her son’s adorable expression, Yu Wan’s heart, which had been suspended for so long, finally settled.

“It’s good that you’re not. I’ve been worried for a long time.”

Zhao Xuanyou pinched his son’s chubby cheek and ordered the maid to take the child away.

Yu Wan noticed the deepening look in his eyes and knew that something significant must have happened in the capital. After waiting for Ran Dong to close the door, she smiled faintly. “What happened?”

“It’s not exactly a problem, but there are indeed a few things. One big, one small. Which do you want to hear first?”

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou being so mysterious, Yu Wan felt slightly at ease.

If he still had the mind to tease her, it probably wasn’t a catastrophic event.

“The small one.”

“Cui Zaiting followed me to Yuzhou.”

“Did he run into trouble in the capital?” Yu Wan asked.

“I didn’t ask, and he didn’t say,” Zhao Xuanyou answered honestly. “I had Yuan Xi settle him elsewhere first. What do you plan to do?”

He had brought Cui Zaiting to Yuzhou because he knew Cui Zaiting had helped Yu Wan before.

But he wasn’t sure if Yu Wan intended to treat Cui Zaiting as family, so he hadn’t brought him directly back to the Marquis’s residence.

Yu Wan certainly hadn’t considered immediately acknowledging him as her brother.

It wasn’t that she bore any ill will toward Cui Zaiting, but she was afraid that if she and the Cui family acknowledged each other, it might upset her mother.

Her mother had once said that she had often thought: if she had returned Yu Wan to Cui Lingyuan back then, Yu Wan would have grown up in luxury in the Duke’s mansion, which would have been better than living as a peasant girl with her.

In any case, if Cui Zaiting needed help, she would do her best.

“Shouldn’t we talk about the big matter now?”

The playful glint in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes faded. He glanced at the warm spring light outside the window and said slowly, “His Majesty has ordered me to bring Zhao Yi Yun here.”

If Yu Wan had only been slightly surprised to hear that Cui Zaiting had come to Yuzhou, she was now completely stunned.

This was indeed a big matter.

“Is Yi Yun already in Yuzhou?”

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

“Does Cui Zaiting know?”

“Only my father and I know. No one else who came with us is aware.”

To avoid drawing attention, Zhao Xuanyou had deliberately ordered people to gather many items from the Marquis’s mansion’s storeroom, saying they were to be brought back to Yuzhou. They filled four carriages, and Zhao Yi Yun was hidden in one of them, rarely stepping out during the day.

Even though Cui Zaiting had traveled with them, he had never once come face to face with Zhao Yi Yun.

The two personal guards responsible for Zhao Yi Yun’s care had been ordered to conceal his whereabouts but did not know his true identity.

“Did something happen to Consort Feng?”

Consort Feng was a very gentle woman, but she had suffered greatly after losing her child in her early years, which had ruined her health.

“Consort Feng is fine. It’s His Majesty’s health that isn’t good.”

“Then…”

“For now, there’s no immediate problem, but you also understand that once His Majesty is gone, Consort Feng won’t be able to protect Zhao Yi Yun.”

“So His Majesty wants to have Yi Yun adopted by us?”

Zhao Xuanyou shook his head and said solemnly, “By now, the palace should have already announced Yi Yun’s death.”

“Death? Then what about Yi Yun?”

“His Majesty hopes that he will live under an assumed name from now on and live peacefully as a commoner in Yuzhou.”

Yu Wan had taken care of Zhao Yi Yun for over a month and had a good relationship with the child. Although his father wasn’t a good man, she knew the child had a kind heart.

“Then what should we do? His Majesty entrusted him to us, so he must hope that we will take care of him personally.”

“Yes.”

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

He and Zhao Zun were enemies, and he didn’t want to have anything to do with Zhao Yi Yun. However, the child did have some of the Zhao family’s blood, so he was somewhat related to the Marquis’s residence.

Moreover, Yu Wan liked the child, so when the Emperor summoned him, he agreed without hesitation.

“I’ve been thinking. It’s best to raise him in the Marquis’s residence, but it would be too conspicuous if we raise him under our own names.”

If they couldn’t raise him under their names, then…

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan’s eyes met, and they both understood what the other was thinking.

“No.” Yu Wan shook her head. “A Chi hasn’t married yet. First, there’s an extra daughter, and now a son?”

Zhao Xuanyou naturally understood this reasoning.

“Then, should we ask A Chi for his opinion?”

Ask?

With Wen Chi’s temper, as soon as Zhao Xuanyou opened his mouth, he would definitely agree without hesitation.

“Actually, it would just be registered under his name, but we would still raise him.” Zhao Xuanyou truly couldn’t think of a better candidate.

The Emperor had entrusted Zhao Yi Yun to him, so he naturally had to keep Zhao Yi Yun under his watch.

Adopting Zhao Yi Yun as his own son would draw too much attention, but treating him as a relative’s child was the most suitable.

Unfortunately, he had no brothers or sisters, so the only option was his brother-in-law, Wen Chi.

“Wanwan, don’t worry. When A Chi finds someone he likes in the future, I will explain everything to them. It won’t affect A Chi’s marriage.”

“You’ll go explain?”

“Don’t believe me?”

“I do,” Yu Wan sighed. She naturally knew that although Zhao Xuanyou usually didn’t talk much, he was actually very persuasive and could easily convince others. “But we can’t keep taking advantage of A Chi like this.”

“Then what do you think is appropriate? I’ll listen to you, but he must have a reasonable excuse to stay in the Marquis’s residence.”

Although the Emperor said he wanted Zhao Yi Yun to live an ordinary life, Zhao Xuanyou understood that Zhao Yi Yun was the Emperor’s beloved grandson. The Emperor had made many arrangements to protect him and would certainly be secretly observing the situation in Yuzhou.

Yu Wan hesitated for a moment before an idea came to her.

But Zhao Xuanyou could see that there was a deeper meaning in her gaze.

“If it’s not a good idea, don’t say it.”

Their tacit understanding had reached the point where a single glance or small gesture was enough for them to understand each other. Yu Wan knew he had guessed it, and she couldn’t help but smile.

“Why isn’t it a good idea?”

“Everyone knows I’m infatuated with you. After all these years of searching for you and refusing to marry, suddenly having such a big son would surely raise suspicions.”

Yu Wan looked at his displeased expression and gently rubbed his eyebrow with her hand.

“In the capital, rumors say you couldn’t forget Cui Yichu, which is why you chose me because I look like her. After Cui Yichu’s death, you were stationed in Yuzhou for years. It wouldn’t be strange if you had a lover in Yuzhou and had an illegitimate child. Yi Yun’s age fits.”

Yu Wan’s eyes were captivating, and Zhao Xuanyou was slightly dazzled by her soft words, but he knew she was digging a hole for him.

“Explain clearly. What do you mean it wouldn’t be strange if I had an illegitimate child?”

“I’m not saying you did. I’m talking about the gossip of others. Anyway, Yi Yun has to be raised in the Marquis’s residence, so it’s most appropriate for him to be your son. His Majesty would also be more satisfied with this arrangement.”

This was indeed a good point.

The Emperor had entrusted Zhao Yi Yun to him, hoping he would take care of Zhao Yi Yun for life. Only if Zhao Yi Yun was under his name would the Emperor be at ease.

---

chapters.title: A Big Family
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou took a deep breath.

After much thought, he realized there was indeed no better solution.

“Where is Yi Yun now?”

“I brought him into the Marquis’s residence. He’s currently settled in the Lancui Pavilion.”

“I’ll go see him.”

Yu Wan stood up, and Zhao Xuanyou reached out to hold her hand. “He’s tired from the journey. There’s no need to rush.”

“It’s precisely because he’s traveled so far that I need to go see him.”

Zhao Yi Yun was so young and had already experienced so many hardships; first losing his parents, and now his imperial grandfather. Suddenly arriving in this unfamiliar place, he must be very scared.

Yu Wan ordered Pan Xia to prepare some snacks before pulling Zhao Xuanyou along to the Lancui Pavilion.

The Lancui Pavilion was in a secluded location, close to the Marquis’s residence’s side gate. Zhao Yi Yun had entered the residence quietly through this gate.

At the entrance of the courtyard stood several of Zhao Xuanyou’s trusted guards. Seeing them approach, they quickly bowed in greeting.

Yu Wan ordered the maids to stay outside, and only she and Zhao Xuanyou entered the courtyard.

Zhao Yi Yun was sitting in the courtyard, resting his head on his hand, looking somewhat lost. Hearing the sound of the courtyard gate opening behind him, he instinctively looked back.

It had been over a year since they last met. Zhao Yi Yun had grown taller and thinner. The baby fat on his once-chubby face had disappeared, revealing a hint of his young boyish features.

“Marquis’s wife.”

Zhao Yi Yun’s eyes instantly brightened.

Yu Wan had always had a good relationship with the child. Thinking that the Emperor had sent him to her and Zhao Xuanyou, and that they would now live together as family, she felt the mysterious workings of fate.

“You must be exhausted from traveling all the way from the capital to Yuzhou.”

Zhao Yi Yun, however, shook his head.

Seeing how sensible he was, Yu Wan sat down beside him and softly asked, “Do you know that from now on, you’ll be living here with the Marquis and me?”

“Can I live with you?” Zhao Yi Yun asked, slightly surprised.

“Of course. His Majesty entrusted you to us, so naturally you’ll live with us.”

“But…”

Seeing the disbelief in Zhao Yi Yun’s eyes, Yu Wan realized that Zhao Xuanyou had brought him here in secret and hadn’t had a chance to sit down and talk with him. So she said, “Don’t you want to live with us?”

“Of course not.” Zhao Yi Yun lowered his head. After a moment of silence, he looked up and said, “When I left the palace, my imperial grandfather said that from now on, I should live as a commoner, quietly and peacefully. If I live in the Marquis’s residence, I’ll bring trouble to you.”

Back in the Qianqing Palace, Zhao Yi Yun had witnessed the cruel words spoken by his uncles and aunts. Though he was young, he knew many people didn’t want him alive.

After his imperial grandfather was poisoned, his health had never been good, which was why he had been sent away with the Marquis of Jingyuan.

“As long as you’re willing to live with us, we’re not afraid of trouble.”

“Really?”

Facing Zhao Yi Yun’s cautious gaze, Yu Wan couldn’t help but feel a pang of sympathy and nodded firmly at him.

After a moment’s thought, she added, “However, from now on, you can no longer be called Zhao Yi Yun.”

“Then what should I be called?”

“I’ve already discussed it with the Marquis. From now on, you’ll be his son, a legitimate young master of the Marquis’s residence.”

Zhao Yi Yun instinctively looked at Zhao Xuanyou.

Compared to Yu Wan’s kindness, he was actually a little afraid of Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou did not disappoint him and, like Yu Wan, gave him an affirmative answer.

“However, from now on, you can’t be called Yi Yun anymore. You must forget everything that happened in the capital and start a new life in Yuzhou.”

“Then what should I be called?”

“How about…” Zhao Xuanyou mentally compared the names Mianze and Ruiyan before quickly making a decision. “Do you like the name Cheng’an?”

“Cheng’an.” Yu Wan softly repeated the name. Fearful that Zhao Yi Yun might not understand its meaning, she explained, “It means ‘heaven’s blessing and peace.’ It’s a good name.”

Zhao Yi Yun liked his original name, which his imperial grandfather had personally given him at birth.

But when he left the palace, his imperial grandfather had repeatedly urged him to live peacefully. So, the name Cheng’an did carry his grandfather’s hopes for his future.

“Marquis, I like this name.”

Zhao Xuanyou, hearing this, ruffled his hair and then taught him a cover story, such as that his mother was a maid in the Marquis’s residence and that he had grown up with her in the countryside.

Yuzhou was far from the capital and completely under Zhao Xuanyou’s control. The Marquis’s residence here was even more like an iron fortress than the one in the capital.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan only informed the steward about Zhao Yi Yun’s status as an illegitimate son, stating that they had no intention of entering him into the family registry and would not take him back to the capital to acknowledge his ancestors.

Additionally, they specifically mentioned that having an illegitimate son was not a glorious thing, so they ordered the servants not to spread the news. The people in the residence just needed to know that a new young master had been added.

In Yuzhou, there weren’t many people who dared to gossip about Zhao Xuanyou, so the news of an additional illegitimate son in the residence did not cause much of a stir in the city.

The Marquis’s residence now had three children, so Yu Wan set about rearranging their living quarters.

The Xifeng Courtyard was already spacious. She had it reorganized and divided into three smaller courtyards, one for Zhao Yi Yun, one for Zhao Mianze, and one for Ding Ruiyan.

Although A’ning was a girl, she was still a baby, and it would be livelier for her to live near her two brothers.

When she was older, Yu Wan would naturally prepare a separate boudoir for her.

Zhao Yi Yun was gentle by nature and enjoyed playing with his younger siblings. When A’ning was sleeping, he would stay with A’chun, and when A’chun was sleeping, he would go play with A’ning.

Seeing that he was happy in the Marquis’s residence, Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan were also relieved.

After settling Zhao Yi Yun, Yu Wan told her mother about Cui Zaiting coming to Yuzhou.

Ding Wenxi naturally had some resistance toward the Cui family, but upon hearing that Cui Zaiting was kind-hearted and had once warned Yu Wan when someone was plotting against Ding Wenxi, she understood his character.

Seeing that her mother had let go of her grudge, Yu Wan invited Cui Zaiting to the Marquis’s residence for a meal.

During the meal, Yu Wan asked about his reason for coming to Yuzhou and learned that the Duke of Ning, out of love for his granddaughter, had arranged for Shen Fengyun and her son to be settled in a villa in Jiangnan.

As for Cui Zaiting, after years of hardship, he had long since seen the true nature of the rest of the Cui family and no longer wanted to stay in the capital. So he decided to come to Yuzhou to seek a living.

He told Yu Wan not to worry or go out of her way to arrange anything for him.

He was well-educated and had once passed the imperial examinations. In Yuzhou, there were few scholars, and even fewer with good education. He had already secured a teaching position at the largest academy in the city.

Yu Wan wasn’t surprised by this decision, as it suited his scholarly spirit. She only told him to visit the Marquis’s residence more often in the future.

Not long after, Lin Cheng returned from the Western Regions with a trade caravan. This time, he had helped seven merchants in the city purchase goods and made several hundred taels of silver in one trip. Finally, he could hold his head high and marry Yingxue.

He was an Eastern Palace secret guard and was very familiar with Zhao Yi Yun. If they didn’t inform him in advance, he might accidentally let something slip if he encountered Zhao Yi Yun.

Thus, Yu Wan arranged for him to come to the residence for a talk.

chapters.title: The Secret in the Books
chapters.content:
The moment Lin Geng saw Zhao Yi Yun, he froze.

The Eastern Palace had fallen long ago, and he never expected to see his young master again in Yuzhou, thousands of miles away.

Yu Ying noticed his reaction and told him about the Emperor entrusting Zhao Yi Yun to the care of the Marquis's residence.

Lin Geng immediately said, "Madam, I was originally a secret guard of the Eastern Palace. From now on, I will naturally protect the young master by his side."

"You have Xing Xue now, and also the escort agency. It wouldn't be convenient for you to serve as a guard again. Rest assured, since he will be the young master of the Marquis's residence from now on, the Marquis and I will protect him fully."

"If the Marquis and Madam have any tasks for me, please just ask."

Upon hearing this, Yu Ying suddenly remembered something.

When she visited Zhuang Huaiyue in the heavenly prison, Zhuang Huaiyue had instructed her to retrieve some things for Zhao Yi Yun from Ziyan. When she brought them back, she found it was a box of books and placed it in the Marquis's storage.

When Zhao Xuanyou took Yi Yun away from the capital, thinking that the box of books was a memento from Zhuang Huaiyue for Zhao Yi Yun, he brought them all to Yuzhou.

A few days ago, when the couple discussed this matter, they still felt that there must be something hidden in that box of books.

Wen Tao had been away from the Eastern Palace for several years, and even after reading those books, he couldn't find any clues.

As for Lin Geng... he was not like Wen Tao, who only served as a guard by the Crown Prince's side. He also managed many secret guards under him.

If there was indeed a secret hidden in the books left by Zhuang Huaiyue, Lin Geng should know about it.

"Pan Xia, take the young master to the courtyard to play for a while."

"Yes."

Pan Xia stepped forward, took Yi Yun's hand, and led him out, closing the door behind them.

Yu Ying solemnly said, "I met Zhuang Liangdi for the last time in the heavenly prison. She entrusted me with a box of books, saying they were for Yi Yun. Those books seemed to be ordinary ones that could be bought from any bookshop. I really couldn't understand why she would leave such a box of common books for Yi Yun."

Seeing Lin Geng's confused expression, Wen Tao also said, "I have carefully examined those books and found nothing hidden within them. But if they were just books, Zhuang Liangdi wouldn't have gone through so much trouble to give them to you, sister."

"Books?" Lin Geng's eyes seemed to show a hint of understanding. After a moment of silence, he said, "In the Eastern Palace, there was someone skilled in using a special ink to write on paper. If Zhuang Liangdi entrusted them to you before her death, I guess the books contain secrets written with that ink, meant to be passed on to the imperial grandson."

So that was it. Yu Ying hurriedly asked, "How can we reveal the true words? Do you know how to make the ink?"

"I don't know how to make the ink, but to see the words clearly, we don't need the ink. We just need to soak the books in oil," Lin Geng said. During his service, he had received secret orders written with such ink.

"I see, thank you."

Lin Geng saw the situation and cupped his hands to Yu Ying, then respectfully retreated and left. When he reached the door, he saw the wet nurse holding A Ning under the sea tang tree, and Zhao Yi Yun picking a flower to tease A Ning. The flower swayed, and A Ning laughed aloud.

It was truly a great fortune for the young master to be able to live in the Marquis's residence for the rest of his life.

Although Yu Ying did not let him see the secret hidden in the books, Lin Geng could roughly guess what it was.

Handing those books to the Marquis's Madam was probably not only Zhuang Liangdi's intention but also the Crown Prince's.

Now that everything had settled, he didn't know what the Marquis and Madam would do... but it was not something he should ponder over now.

Lin Geng withdrew his gaze and quickly left the Tangli Courtyard.

After learning how to uncover the secret in the books, Yu Ying had Wen Tao bring a jar of oil from the kitchen. The two of them tried soaking a book in the oil. Only when all the pages were saturated did they take it out.

After letting it dry slightly, they opened it again, but it was still the same old story, with no changes.

Wen Tao thought for a moment: "Maybe only one or two of these books contain the secret."

After all, if Zhuang Huaiyue had given Yu Ying only one book, it would have been too obvious, and people would have suspected that the book contained a secret and examined it carefully.

By hiding the book with the secret among more than a dozen books, even if someone wanted to investigate, it would be difficult to crack the secret.

Yu Ying found Wen Tao's reasoning sound.

With this experience, they no longer soaked the entire book in oil. Instead, they laid out all the books and poured a spoonful of oil on the first page of each.

After waiting for about the time it takes for an incense stick to burn, the text on one of the books indeed changed.

Yu Ying and Wen Tao leaned in for a closer look. After seeing the few words on it, both of them were shocked.

Wen Tao steadied his mind and soaked the entire book in the jar.

"Marquis," came the voice of Ran Dong paying respects outside the room.

Hearing that Zhao Xuanyou had returned, Yu Ying's unease instantly dissipated. She stood up and went to the door to open it.

Zhao Xuanyou met her gaze, slightly narrowed his eyes, and gently poked her cheek with his finger. "What's wrong?"

Yu Ying smiled at him but didn't speak. She pulled him inside.

Passing the gilded landscape screen in the room, Zhao Xuanyou first saw the books spread out on the floor, then saw Wen Tao taking a book out of the oil jar.

He glanced at Yu Ying and asked in a deep voice, "Are those the books from Huaiyue?"

"Yes. Earlier, Lin Geng came by and mentioned that in the Eastern Palace, there was a method of using special ink to write secrets on paper. Sister and I tried it with those books, and indeed, one of them contained a secret."

The deposed Empress Jiang had ordered the Duke of Zhen Guo to privately cast weapons, which was first discovered by Zhao Xuanyou. After reporting to the Emperor, the Emperor had ordered the Jin Yi Wei to secretly investigate the matter, but they had not been able to find anything even until the fall of the deposed Empress and the deposed Crown Prince.

Zhao Xuanyou had an idea of what secret might be hidden in that book.

The three of them sat at the table, none of them speaking.

After the hidden text in the book was fully revealed, Zhao Xuanyou used chopsticks to separate the pages and quickly flipped through them.

As expected, the book not only detailed the location where the privately cast weapons were hidden but also listed the chess pieces that the Empress and the Crown Prince had painstakingly planted in the court over the years.

After the Empress's poisoning plot was exposed, most of their forces in the capital were eliminated by Zhao Xuanyou. However, there were still many generals in various military camps who remained loyal to them, hidden very deeply. Some were openly close to Prince Ping, and others were even high-ranking generals under the Duke of Ningguo.

But what pleased Zhao Xuanyou was that although the Empress had planted people in the Yuzhou government, the Ming Chao Guard was clean.

Yu Ying said, "No wonder the Jin Yi Wei couldn't find where those weapons were hidden after investigating for several years. It turns out they were hidden separately by these people."

Wen Tao looked at Yu Ying and then at Zhao Xuanyou. "What should we do with this book?"

Zhao Xuanyou felt a moment of helplessness.

If they had discovered the secret in the book before Zhao Yi Yun was brought to Yuzhou, he would have certainly submitted it to the Emperor in a secret memorial.

But now that Zhao Yi Yun had become his son, everything was different.

"Let's put it away for now," Yu Ying said thoughtfully, her eyes flashing slightly.

Zhao Xuanyou saw the expression on her face and nodded. "Mm, let's pretend nothing happened today."

These people had been absolutely loyal to Jiang and Zhao Zun in the past. Now that they were both dead, and it was widely known that Zhao Yi Yun was already "dead" and the Eastern Palace line was broken, there was no need for them to continue opposing the court. They wouldn't cause any more trouble.

There was no need to destroy the book. After all, Zhao Yi Yun was alive and well in the Jingyuan Marquis's residence. Who knew what variables might arise in the future?

---

chapters.title: Clinging to Mother
chapters.content:
With only the three of them in the room, they settled the matter without needing to say much more. They all understood what to do in the future.

Zhao Xuanyou took the book and left. Yu Ying and Wen Tao went to the courtyard to accompany the children.

The weather was getting hotter day by day. Even under the thick shade of the sea tang tree, the children soon broke out in a sweat.

Yu Ying took the children back inside, where those who drank milk did so, and those who ate sweet soup did the same.

After the meal, the children were all tired and wanted to sleep.

Yu Ying placed A Chun and A Ning side by side at the innermost part of the bed, had the eldest Zhao Yi Yun sleep on the outside, and sat at the edge of the bed to fan them.

At this time of year, they hadn't started using ice basins yet, and the breeze from the fan was just right.

"Madam, you should lie down and rest for a while. Let this slave girl fan you," Ran Dong said respectfully.

"It's fine," Yu Ying thought for a moment, then added, "Have the kitchen steam two plates of rice cakes for the children."

Zhao Yi Yun liked to eat osmanthus rice cakes, and Zhao Mian, along with Ding Ruiyan, were close to weaning age and had started learning to eat other foods. Besides congee, they also ate soft rice cakes.

"Yes."

After Ran Dong left, Yu Ying continued fanning the three children.

Zhao Yi Yun and A Ning soon fell asleep, but Zhao Mian kept his eyes open, looking at her.

Yu Ying reached out and poked her son's little arm, softly saying, "Brother and sister are both asleep. A Chun should sleep too."

But instead of closing his eyes, her son reached out to grab Yu Ying's finger, his round, bright eyes looking at her pitifully.

"Trying to be coy with Mother again."

Yu Ying had no choice but to pick up her son.

Zhao Mian lay contentedly in Yu Ying's arms, finally satisfied.

Looking at her son's smiling face, Yu Ying's heart melted.

When they were first born, both A Chun and A Ning had wrinkled little faces, and it was impossible to tell who they resembled.

Now that they were almost a year old, their features had developed, and it was clear that A Chun took after Yu Ying, with delicate and small features. Ding Wenxi said he looked exactly like Yu Ying when she was little.

Yu Ying looked at her son and could imagine what she had looked like in the past.

Seeing that her son was still holding her finger, Yu Ying couldn't help but laugh. "How is A Chun even more clingy than his sister?"

A Ning was obedient and quiet but not fussy. She was close to everyone in the family, and whoever held her, she wouldn't cry or make a fuss. She was also close to the two wet nurses.

A Chun was different. He particularly disliked being held by the wet nurses and maids. He would fuss as soon as they touched him and would rather sit and play by himself than let them hold him.

Originally, they thought he just didn't like being held by others, but when it came to Yu Ying, he turned into a clingy child. As long as Yu Ying was around, he would desperately reach out to grab her and insist on her holding him.

Zhao Xuanyou had some complaints about this. With his son clinging to his mother all day, he feared he would never amount to anything.

If it weren't for the fact that he was still a baby who couldn't speak properly, Zhao Xuanyou would have already subjected him to family discipline.

Yu Ying also felt that her son was too fond of being coy with her, but her feelings were different from Zhao Xuanyou's.

A Ning had been frail since birth. Even after being adopted by Wen Tao and not falling ill again, her health was still weaker than A Chun's.

Therefore, Yu Ying devoted most of her energy to her daughter, holding her much more often than her son.

Although her son could only call her "Mother," Yu Ying felt that this little guy thought she cared more for his sister, hence his clinginess.

"A Chun, be good. Mother doesn't only care for your sister and not you. It's just that your sister used to be sick often, so I paid more attention to her," Yu Ying softly coaxed. "Mother loves A Ning, and also loves you just the same."

Of course, Zhao Mian was deliberately being coy to get Yu Ying to hold him, but he wasn't trying to compete with his sister for favor. He just really wanted to be close to his mother.

In his past life, he had no memory of having a mother from the moment he could remember. He had the love of his great-grandmother, grandfather, and father. As the heir of the Marquis's residence, he wanted for nothing, and he didn't feel like he was missing anything.

It wasn't until he was reborn as a baby that he realized how happy it was to have a mother by his side.

Zhao Mian just wanted to stay by his mother's side.

Especially after hearing his father say that if he was still this clingy when he grew up, he would definitely be punished with family discipline. He immediately decided to continue clinging.

While he was still young, every moment he could cling was precious. In the future, if he tried to cling, he would definitely get a beating.

Just as he was enjoying being in his mother's arms, his father's voice suddenly came.

Zhao Xuanyou saw Yu Ying holding their son at the edge of the bed and frowned. "Is he being coy and making you hold him again?"

"Maybe it's because of the heat. He can't sleep," Yu Ying said with a smile.

Zhao Xuanyou stepped forward to take Zhao Mian from her.

Yu Ying anticipated his move and, holding Zhao Mian, dodged to the side.

When Zhao Xuanyou's eyes met his son's, he felt a hint of cunning in his son's clear, bright eyes.

Without further ado, he took Zhao Mian from Yu Ying's arms.

"You be careful, don't hurt A Chun," Yu Ying couldn't help but say.

"Let him sleep by himself," Zhao Xuanyou glanced at his son and, seeing him tightly closing his eyes, raised an eyebrow and placed him back on the bed. "He's getting heavier. There's no need to hold him all the time."

"That's why we should hold him more now. When he grows up, we won't be able to hold him at all."

Zhao Xuanyou knew Yu Ying doted on the children but didn't want to spoil them. He was also concerned that Yu Ying's arms would ache from holding them too long.

He took Yu Ying's wrist and massaged it for her.

Yu Ying laughed. "I'm strong. I'm not that delicate."

After the husband and wife exchanged jokes, Yu Ying asked, "Did you put the things away properly?"

Thinking of the book containing the secrets of the Eastern Palace, Zhao Xuanyou heavily responded, "Mm."

"Has there been any news from the court recently?"

After the children were born, Yu Ying's heart was completely devoted to them. She rarely had time for leisure activities like reading and playing chess, let alone paying attention to the court's situation.

Their family was far from the capital. As long as there was no war on the border, no matter how turbulent the court was, it had nothing to do with them.

But with the sudden appearance of Zhao Yi Yun and that book in the Marquis's residence, Yuzhou and the capital were connected in a secret way.

"The Emperor intends to send several princes to their respective fiefs outside the capital."

"Including Prince Ping?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

"But isn't the Emperor's health much worse than before?"

Logically, at this time, they should quickly establish a crown prince to stabilize the situation when the Emperor passed away.

"If the Emperor wanted to establish Prince Ping, he would have done so long ago. Why wait until now?"

In the past, when Zhao Zun was the Crown Prince, Prince Ping acted cautiously and had a good reputation among the court officials.

After Zhao Zun's downfall, Prince Ping helped manage the court affairs, and many previously unnoticed problems became apparent. He had ambitions but lacked the ability, and he had no tolerance for others. Even neutral officials like Minister Xu and Minister Sun, who had already sided with him, had complaints about him. Needless to say, the Emperor, who was concerned about the country's stability.

"In the past, it was easy for us to stay out of trouble, but with Yi Yun now with us, he carries the royal bloodline. It will be difficult for him not to get involved."

"You're right. Yi Yun is the Emperor's eldest grandson. Although Zhao Zun has been deposed, his name has not been removed from the imperial genealogy. As the eldest son of the fourth prince, if the Emperor suddenly passes away without an heir, Yi Yun would be qualified to compete for the throne."

Zhao Yi Yun was already over five years old. Having experienced great upheavals at a young age, he was much more precocious than his peers.

He was clearly aware of his identity as an imperial grandson and remembered the deceased Zhao Zun and Zhuang Huaiyue. When he grew up, would he truly remain indifferent?

"When the time comes, we'll deal with it. I don't think that child is heartless."

Yu Ying smiled at Zhao Xuanyou. He rarely praised Zhao Yi Yun, but in reality, he also approved of the child.

Anyway, Zhao Yi Yun had already called her "Mother." Yu Ying would raise him the same way as Zhao Mian. If he didn't go astray, Zhao Xuanyou and she would certainly keep their promise to protect him.

If he harbored any ill intentions, no one could help him.

Lying on the bed pretending to sleep, Zhao Mian was shocked by his parents' words.

Zhao Yi Yun?

That illegitimate child who clings to his mother and sister every day is Zhao Yi Yun?

chapters.title: Zhao Mianze's Memories
chapters.content:
Zhao Mianze eavesdropped on his parents' conversations every day and had already known that the older brother who suddenly appeared in their home was not a child from his father’s concubine, but someone his parents had reluctantly adopted out of necessity.

What he never expected was that the child was Zhao Yi Yun.

In his previous life, when Zhao Mianze was ten years old, his father had taken him to Yuzhou.

Around that time, the current emperor had passed away. Several princes and two chancellor officials searched the imperial palace but couldn’t find the emperor’s will for succession. After a brief dispute among the court officials, the elder Prince Ping, Zhao Huan, ascended the throne.

After taking the throne, Emperor Ping suppressed his three younger brothers to consolidate his power. First, he fabricated charges against Prince Jing, Zhao Lin, confiscated his prince’s mansion, and demoted his entire family to commoners. Three months later, Zhao Lin fell seriously ill and died.

Following this, Emperor Ping drastically reduced the powers of Prince Qing Zhao Yu and Prince Rui Zhao Qi as imperial princes.

While dealing with his brothers, Emperor Ping also retaliated against the officials who had opposed his ascension, including Chancellor Xu who had remained neutral.

A change of dynasty on the throne naturally caused tremors in the court.

However, Emperor Ping acted too hastily and brutally, making it easy for others to turn against him.

Sure enough, half a year later, Prince Qing and Prince Rui, unwilling to wait for their doom, rebelled one after another.

They had justification for their actions. The emperor’s close attendant, Liu Quan, claimed that the late emperor had left a will for the succession, but it had been opened and destroyed by Prince Ping and Chancellor Sun before anyone else could see it.

Liu Quan didn’t know which prince the late emperor had intended to pass the throne to, but it was certainly not Prince Ping.

If the will had named Prince Ping, why would he have destroyed it?

Liu Quan took the opportunity while Prince Ping had not yet fully controlled the situation to leave the palace and go into hiding until the two princes rose up.

Unfortunately, Prince Qing and Prince Rui fought separately and were unable to resist the court. Soon, Prince Qing was defeated, while Prince Rui, with the support of the Ningguo Duke’s mansion, continued to hold out.

A thousand miles away in Yuzhou, all was calm. Zhao Mianze studied diligently, practiced martial arts, listened to his grandfather and father discuss military strategies, and heard them talk about the treacherous political situation in the capital.

Matters like the imperial will and the struggle for succession were too distant for Zhao Mianze. All he cared about was riding his horse outside the city after finishing his studies.

His mount was a fine steed carefully selected by his father. On the grasslands, it galloped like the wind, making him feel as if he were flying.

It was also while riding outside the city that Zhao Mianze met a young man. The other’s horse was also excellent. After a race, they developed mutual admiration and began racing together every day.

Although they often chatted, they never exchanged names.

But half a year later, the young man never appeared again.

Not long after, another rebellion broke out. The rebel was a general stationed in the southwest, but he supported not Prince Rui, but the deposed crown prince’s grandson, Zhao Yi Yun.

At the same time, Chancellor Xu, who had been forced to retire by Zhao Huan, also led a group of his disciples to support Zhao Yi Yun.

As it turned out, when the late emperor passed away, Chancellor Xu had also been summoned to the palace by imperial decree. However, the Jin Yi Guard had intercepted him and secretly handed Zhao Yi Yun over to him.

While Chancellor Xu was leaving the palace to arrange for Zhao Yi Yun, the late emperor suddenly passed away. Only Consort Li, Prince Ping, and Chancellor Sun were by his side, leading to the destruction of the will.

Chancellor Xu believed they not only destroyed the will but also suspected them of regicide.

With the support of the literati scholars, Zhao Yi Yun’s momentum grew rapidly. After more than a year of fierce battles among the three factions, Prince Rui suddenly formed an alliance with Zhao Yi Yun, willing to support his ascension to the throne.

Zhao Mianze heard from his father that Prince Rui was not someone greedy for power. He had rebelled not only because Zhao Huan had relentlessly pressured him to seek a way out, but also to avenge the late emperor.

After the alliance, morale soared, and they won several battles in a row.

Chancellor Sun, who had originally supported Zhao Huan, suddenly defected, claiming that Consort Li and Zhao Huan had indeed poisoned the late emperor, destroyed the secret decree, and even presented evidence.

With both human and physical evidence, Zhao Huan was a traitor whom anyone could execute.

The Mingchui Guard also took action at this time, joining Zhao Yi Yun in marching into the capital.

Zhao Mianze wanted to go to the battlefield with his father, but his father said he wasn’t ready and shouldn’t be impatient. He had no choice but to stay obediently by his grandfather’s side.

After Zhao Huan’s death, Prince Rui returned to his fiefdom. Zhao Yi Yun smoothly ascended the throne. Zhao Mianze’s grandfather took him to the capital to congratulate the new emperor and attend the coronation ceremony.

It was then that Zhao Mianze discovered that the new emperor was the young man with whom he had raced horses outside Yuzhou City.

Upon seeing Zhao Mianze, Zhao Yi Yun was also delighted and kept him by his side, entrusting him with important tasks. But that was all in his previous life.

Now, hearing his parents talk about Zhao Yi Yun, Zhao Mianze felt a sense of unease.

How did Zhao Yi Yun end up in his home? And would he still be able to become emperor...

Zhao Mianze reached up to scratch his face. Well, he couldn’t be bothered with these trivial matters.

Although in his previous life, he and Zhao Yi Yun had been close, with a lifetime of harmonious relations between monarch and subject, he had finally gained parents and a sister in this life. He just wanted to stay with them and live happily. He couldn’t be bothered with things like brotherhood.

If he caused trouble for his parents, Zhao Mianze wouldn’t show any mercy.

"This child, he never sleeps properly." Yu Wan was discussing matters in the capital with Zhao Xuanyou when she glanced at Zhao Mianze, who was tossing and turning, and wanted to pick him up to soothe him to sleep.

Zhao Xuanyou pulled her back into his arms.

"He’s had little sleep since birth. Don’t hinder his growth. Let him be."

Zhao Mianze gathered his thoughts and sighed.

Ah, he missed another chance to be held by his mother.

"Wanwan." Zhao Xuanyou shifted his gaze from his son and suddenly lowered his head to nuzzle close to Yu Wan, his nose gently touching her forehead.

The touch was sudden. Yu Wan instinctively tried to retreat, but he caught her in one swift motion.

"The children are all sleeping here. Wait until they’re asleep, then we’ll carry them back to the room."

As soon as Yu Wan said this, Zhao Mianze’s heart jolted.

What did his parents want to do?

They weren’t planning to... here, were they?

Although he was a reincarnated soul, he didn’t want to witness his parents’ intimate moments.

Zhao Xuanyou let out a soft hum and kissed her lightly.

"I can’t wait. Now."

"Don’t be silly."

All three children were lying on the couch. Especially Zhao Yi Yun, who was already so big. If they made any noise, they would definitely wake him up.

Zhao Xuanyou looked at her flushed and shy appearance, his eyes gentle but with a hint of teasing. "What are you thinking? What do you think I want to do?"

"Who cares what you think? Let go!"

Zhao Xuanyou indeed let go of the couch, but then pulled Yu Wan up.

"Wanwan, it’s a clear night. Let’s go riding outside the city."

This took Yu Wan by surprise.

"Riding? Now?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s voice was low in her ear, "Mmm, let’s go now. Just the two of us."

They had known each other for a long time, and their marriage was not recent.

But thinking back, it seemed they were always busy with something, and many things they wanted to do were delayed again and again.

Like riding out to the grasslands at night to look at the stars.

Zhao Xuanyou knew their hearts were connected and that they could walk through the rest of their lives together. He also knew they had all the time in the world, but some things didn’t need to wait, and couldn’t wait.

Under his steady gaze, a blush rose on Yu Wan’s cheeks, and her heart warmed and surged.

"Okay."

Tomorrow would be another day, but none could compare to today.

---

chapters.title: Good Things Happen
chapters.content:
"Sister, is it true that we’re leaving the capital tomorrow?"

The sun was shining brightly in the capital, but the Prince Rui’s mansion was filled with a chilly atmosphere, completely unaffected by the summer heat.

Liang Miaotong wore a thin, cool soft smoke gauze hibiscus summer dress. Her figure was much fuller than last year, but her brows still held the innocence of a young girl.

"Prince Rui’s departure to his fiefdom is the emperor’s decree. Prince Ping, Prince Jing, and Prince Qing have already left the capital. The Prince Rui’s mansion can’t delay any longer." Even though Liang Miaofeng and Zhao Qi didn’t get along, she was still his princess consort and naturally had to follow him.

Seeing her sister frowning in silence, Liang Miaofeng sighed softly in her heart.

Over the past year, matchmakers had frequently visited the Liang residence to propose marriages for Liang Miaotong. Their parents had also found suitable candidates, but Liang Miaotong refused to agree no matter what.

Last month, she had a dispute with their parents at home. Feeling distressed, Liang Miaofeng took her to stay at the prince’s mansion for a while.

"Can’t you stay in the capital, sister?"

"That won’t do." After two years as a princess consort, Liang Miaofeng, no matter how naive, understood the treacherous nature of the imperial family.

If Zhao Qi went to his fiefdom and she stayed in the capital, others would only think she had ulterior motives.

As long as the emperor didn’t designate a crown prince, the imperial family would have no peaceful days.

Every time Liang Miaofeng entered the palace, she could sense the probing in others’ words. She was tired. Going to the fiefdom might allow her to live a quieter life.

"You still don’t want to go home?"

"I don’t want to go back. If I do, our parents will force me to marry again. I don’t want to marry someone I don’t like."

Liang Miaofeng heard the implication in her sister’s words and couldn’t help but ask, "You’ve been refusing to marry. Tell me honestly, who have you taken a fancy to?"

"I haven’t taken a fancy to anyone." Liang Miaotong answered firmly. Perhaps afraid her sister would ask more, she added, "I just don’t want to marry someone I don’t like, and I don’t want someone to marry me when they don’t like me at all. Sister, seeing how hard your life is, my heart aches for you. I don’t want my future to be the same."

"You’re talking about yourself. Don’t drag me and the prince into this."

"Sister, stop deceiving our parents and yourself. The prince doesn’t treat you well at all."

"You’re talking nonsense! Go back to your room and pack. I’ll arrange a carriage to send..." Liang Miaofeng’s gaze flicked to the window, and her voice stopped abruptly.

Zhao Qi had intended to come and inform her about their departure tomorrow, but he didn’t expect to hear the sisters’ argument as he approached the door.

Liang Miaotong realized she had misspoken and stepped back, bowing. "Greetings to Prince Rui."

Zhao Qi looked at Liang Miaofeng. Seeing her silent, she only bowed to him. Under his handsome brows, his eyes held a hint of depth.

"Rise."

Zhao Qi stepped into the room and sat beside Liang Miaofeng.

Liang Miaotong observed their expressions and stepped forward to plead guilty. "Prince Rui, just now I spoke recklessly. Please punish me, but don’t take it out on my sister."

Zhao Qi’s face showed no emotion.

He was already in his early twenties, but his brows and eyes were still as clean and clear as they were in his youth.

"You’re just sisters talking among yourselves. What’s there to plead guilty for?" Zhao Qi’s voice was cold, as if considering for a moment before he looked up at Liang Miaotong. "Marriage is a lifelong matter and indeed shouldn’t be decided hastily."

His words did express Liang Miaotong’s feelings, but Liang Miaotong knew that this prince brother-in-law might not be talking about her.

Could he be saying that his marriage to her sister was hasty?

Liang Miaotong looked at her sister in surprise, but saw that her sister’s face was as calm as water, showing no reaction.

She sighed softly in her heart. It seemed their marital relationship was worse than she had imagined.

When she was still unmarried, she and her sister had been the closest. But now, each sister had her own concerns. Although their affection remained, they could no longer talk about everything as they once did.

Liang Miaotong lowered her head, unsure of what to say.

"Tong’er, go back to your room and pack. I’ll arrange a carriage to send you home."

Liang Miaotong looked at her sister, her eyes filling with tears.

"I know."

Unexpectedly, Zhao Qi said, "If you don’t want to go home, you can come with us to Qizhou for a short stay. When you’ve had enough fun, I’ll send someone to take you back to the capital."

Liang Miaotong looked up in surprise. She hadn’t expected Zhao Qi to speak up.

"As for your parents, I’ll go explain to them."

For a moment, Liang Miaotong’s feelings were complicated. Her sister had a hard life in the prince’s mansion, so she naturally had complaints about Zhao Qi, her brother-in-law. But she hadn’t expected Zhao Qi to offer to help her.

Liang Miaotong looked at her sister, who, although silent, nodded slightly at her.

"Thank you, Prince Rui. Thank you, sister." She had never been good at hiding her feelings. In an instant, her expression brightened. "I’ll go back to my room and pack now."

After bowing, Liang Miaotong, like a little bird, happily skipped out.

Seeing her sister so happy, Liang Miaofeng’s mood also lightened a bit. She hoped her sister could get what she wanted and live a smooth and happy life.

But as Liang Miaofeng stared at her sister’s retreating figure, Zhao Qi kept watching her.

After a long time, Liang Miaofeng withdrew her gaze and turned to meet Zhao Qi’s eyes.

She didn’t look at him. Instead, she picked up the teapot to pour him tea.

Zhao Qi didn’t drink the tea. Watching her lowered, beautiful brows and eyes, he slowly spoke, "You won’t blame me for meddling, will you?"

After the Lantern Festival last year, the two had quarreled. Liang Miaofeng had returned to her maiden home to "nurse her illness" for two months. In the end, it was Zhao Qi who came to take her back.

After returning to the prince’s mansion, the two tacitly agreed not to mention that matter and continued their lukewarm life.

"How could I? Tong’er is so happy. I should thank you, Prince Rui." She spoke sincerely, but after saying this, she quickly changed the subject. "All the items and servants have been checked and prepared. Prince Rui, rest assured. We can set off early tomorrow morning."

Her expression was gentle, and her manners were perfect, but Zhao Qi could sense her distance.

Zhao Qi remembered that after she had mustered the courage to steal a kiss from him, her eyes had hidden a bright light in the darkness, exceptionally charming and affectionate.

Over the past year, Zhao Qi had often savored that feeling.

"Does Tong’er have someone she likes?"

"She won’t admit it, but she probably does. However, with her temper, hiding it like this, it must be someone our parents wouldn’t approve of."

Although her sister refused to say anything, Liang Miaofeng knew her family’s temperaments well enough to guess most of it.

"When we get to Qizhou, ask her. If there’s anything I can do to help, don’t hesitate to speak up."

Liang Miaofeng hummed in agreement. Suddenly, she looked up at Zhao Qi, her usually gentle eyes sharpening slightly.

"Prince Rui, do you care so much about Tong’er because you feel a kinship as fellow victims of circumstance?"

Zhao Qi’s brows twitched slightly as he looked at Liang Miaofeng in surprise.

She was right. Seeing Liang Miaotong’s resistance to her parents’ orders, he had indeed thought of his own past efforts to avoid marriage, which was why he offered to let Liang Miaotong go with them to the fiefdom.

But his surprise now wasn’t from the panic of having his intentions exposed, but from the realization of how well she understood him.

Even though she kept her distance, she had always kept him in her heart.

Did she still like him?

Was her coldness toward him just because of heartbreak and pride?

For Zhao Qi, wasn’t this another kind of empathy?

Zhao Qi had lived for twenty years. Apart from his feelings for Yu Wan, he had never been in love with anyone else.

His understanding of women’s feelings was indeed shallow. He hadn’t expected that Liang Miaofeng wasn’t truly indifferent to him, but was held back by pride and grievance, not daring to get close.

Zhao Qi suppressed the tumult in his heart, let out an "mm" sound, and pretended to be calm. "Yeah."

Seeing Liang Miaofeng indeed couldn’t hide her melancholy and lowered her eyes, Zhao Qi’s heart could no longer contain his emotions. He reached out and pulled her into his arms.

"Prince Rui, you..."

Through the thin summer dress, Liang Miaofeng could feel his warm and solid chest.

She felt both surprised and wronged.

What was he doing?

Did he think she was pitiful?

Sensing Zhao Qi’s arms tightening around her, Liang Miaofeng’s eyes welled up with tears.

"Let go of me."

Zhao Qi still didn’t loosen his grip. "Feng’er, let’s not be angry with each other anymore."

Liang Miaofeng felt even more wronged. He didn’t even like her. How could he say she was being stubborn?

"You admitted you wanted to avoid this marriage. How is that me being stubborn? The emperor bestowed this marriage, and no one could refuse. In the future, we’ll just keep up appearances and continue as we have been."

"I admitted I didn’t want to marry you back then, but you should ask how I feel now."

Now?

Liang Miaofeng bit her lip, her eyes red as she looked up at him.

Their family, though insignificant compared to the imperial family, was still an official family. Her parents doted on her, and she had grown up with siblings in harmony, like a precious jewel, never having suffered any grievances.

It was only after marrying Zhao Qi that she had tasted all kinds of bitterness.

"Who cares how you feel?"

Zhao Qi finally realized that her words were expressing her grievances. Without another word, he lowered his head to kiss her.

Liang Miaofeng instinctively turned her face away to dodge, so the kiss landed on her ear.

Her earlobe instantly burned from the touch.

But that wasn’t all. His thin lips then brushed against her soft cheek before firmly landing on her lips.

Liang Miaofeng was caught off guard, and her mind seemed to go blank.

She and Zhao Qi had kissed before, but this time felt completely different.

Her waist was firmly held by Zhao Qi. She could feel the warmth of his palm and the softness of his thin lips.

She nestled in his arms, motionless, letting him kiss her freely.

After a long while, he finally loosened his grip slightly.

"Feng’er, we’re fine now, aren’t we?"

Liang Miaofeng lowered her eyes, panting softly. After a moment, she said, "Who said we’re fine? The things you did in the past were too hurtful. I haven’t forgiven you yet."

"Take your time. You’ll forgive me eventually." Zhao Qi lowered his head and kissed her forehead again. "But, we’ve been married for so long. Shouldn’t we finally consummate the marriage?"

"Consummate?"

Liang Miaofeng was stunned for a moment. Before she could react, Zhao Qi had already picked her up.

The maids outside had been thinking about whether to bring more tea after hearing their masters talk for so long. Before they could speak, they heard the sounds from inside the room.

The two maids were initially surprised. They pressed their ears to the door and listened carefully. Then, they understood.

Before Princess Consort was married, the madam had already instructed them about such matters.

It was true that Prince Rui and Princess Consort had shared a bed many times, but they had never truly consummated their marriage.

Given the sounds inside...

"Go prepare water. The masters will need it later."

chapters.title: Another Spring
chapters.content:
Five years passed in the blink of an eye.

It was March again, and Yuzhou was still caught between warmth and cold.

"Mother, the peach blossoms outside my window have bloomed. I picked one for you."
