Yumeng was deep in thought by the window, composing a poem, when Zhao Yi Yun entered holding a peach blossom branch.

He was already ten years old, exuding the vibrant energy of a young boy.

His appearance closely resembled Huaiyue; fair and handsome, with serene features.

Yumeng took the peach blossom from his hands with a smile, turned to fetch a vase from the nearby antique shelf, and personally arranged the branch inside.

"Mother, haven't you finished your homework yet?"

When Zhao Yi Yun turned six, Zhao Xuanyou and Yumeng had arranged for his education. After searching for teachers in Yuzhou City, they decided to invite Cui Zaiting to the residence to teach.

Cui Zaiting had studied under a great Confucian scholar and ranked among the top three in the imperial examinations. If not for the downfall of the Xingguo Duke’s mansion, he would have certainly achieved top honors in the national examinations.

Moreover, he excelled in calligraphy and painting, making him the most suitable teacher.

Yumeng had previously studied on her own, barely grasping the basics. Now, with such an excellent teacher at home; and her own brother at that, with no need to avoid suspicion; she naturally did not want to miss the opportunity. She attended classes with Zhao Yi Yun every day.

Of course, she had to complete the same assignments as Zhao Yi Yun.

Cui Zaiting was gentle and meticulous, but when it came to teaching, he was strict and treated both Zhao Yi Yun and Yumeng equally.

Yumeng was fairly familiar with the Four Books and Five Classics and usually did well in her assignments, but poetry was another matter; she often messed up the tonal patterns.

Previously, she had asked Ding Wenxi to help write a poem, but Cui Zaiting saw through it immediately. He had said that poor writing was fine, but deception was not.

Today, after the morning lesson, Cui Zaiting assigned them homework: to write two quatrains on the theme of spring.

Yumeng sat by the window, racking her brains, and had only managed half a poem.

"Have you finished already?" she asked.

Zhao Yi Yun hummed in agreement, glanced at the desk, and smiled. "Mother hasn't finished yet?"

Yumeng sighed, not bothering to pretend otherwise. "I simply don’t have the talent for poetry."

"But Mother has other talents."

Hearing this, Yumeng’s heart softened. Zhao Yi Yun was always so considerate in speech and action; raising him had not been in vain.

Not only was he obedient and sensible in front of her and Zhao Xuanyou, but he was also very harmonious with his younger siblings.

Thinking of her own son, Yumeng couldn’t help but feel a headache coming on. Her daughter, Ding Ruiyan, had started speaking in full sentences before she was two, and Zhao Mianze had been able to call for his father and mother around the same time. But while her daughter had quickly progressed to full sentences, Zhao Mianze had only just started speaking in complete sentences at nearly four years old.

Not only that, but he was extremely clingy to Yumeng, almost always following her around, constantly asking to be held.

Zhao Xuanyou had long wanted to discipline him with the family rules, but Yumeng had stopped him.

She wasn’t trying to spoil the child; she was afraid Zhao Mianze might truly be simple-minded.

But Zhao Mianze was not simple-minded at all. Though he had spoken late, his words and actions were remarkably mature, with a hint of sharpness.

Though he didn’t dare act recklessly in front of Zhao Xuanyou and Yumeng, he had no shortage of ways to exasperate others.

"Mother..." Ding Ruiyan burst in from outside, her voice trembling with tears, and threw herself at Yumeng, looking wronged.

"Who bullied Aning?" Yumeng asked gently.

Ding Ruiyan puffed out her cheeks, fuming. "I was picking flowers for Mother in the garden, and Second Brother came over and threw my flowers away!"

That little brat.

Yumeng was about to comfort her daughter when she saw Zhao Mianze enter, also holding a few peach blossom branches.

"Mother, do you like these flowers?"

All three children knew Yumeng loved flowers, and each day they would pick flowers from the courtyard to give her.

To preserve their kind intentions, Yumeng had stopped having the maids cut flowers, leaving the vases in the room empty each day, waiting for the three of them to bring flowers.

"Achen, Aning said you bullied her and threw away her flowers."

Zhao Mianze said, "There were two big bugs on that flower branch. That’s why I threw it away, Mother, really!"

Yumeng believed him. After all, this child usually doted on his little sister.

"Then why didn’t you explain to your sister?"

"She ran away too fast. I didn’t have time to say anything."

Yumeng looked at his leisurely demeanor. She had almost calmed down, but now she was annoyed again.

Just as she was about to scold him, Zhao Yi Yun took a handkerchief and wiped the tears from Aning’s face, softly saying, "Second Brother didn’t mean to bully anyone. He was afraid the bugs on the flower branch would bite Aning."

Aning still pouted in silence.

Zhao Yi Yun continued, "Let’s go back to the garden and pick new ones. We’ll use the biggest vase for Aning’s flowers."

"Mhm." Aning finally broke into a smile, grabbing Zhao Yi Yun’s hand and swaying it.

Zhao Yi Yun turned to Yumeng. "Mother, I’ll take Aning to the garden."

"Go ahead, but don’t run too fast. Be careful not to fall."

Watching Zhao Yi Yun lead Aning to the garden, Yumeng turned her head and saw Zhao Mianze leaning over the desk, looking at her half-finished poem.

"Achen wants to learn characters?"

Learn characters?

He just wanted to appreciate his mother’s poetry, but... how should he put it? It wasn’t very good.

Zhao Mianze took the opportunity to snuggle into Yumeng’s arms. "Mother, when will you teach me to read?"

"I can’t be your teacher. When you’re a little older, you’ll study with your elder brother. Your maternal uncle has great scholarship; he’ll teach you both."

Yumeng and Cui Zaiting had not formally acknowledged their relationship, but the way they addressed each other in the residence had changed.

Cui Zaiting was the children’s maternal uncle, and Wen Hao was their second maternal uncle.

Zhao Mianze still remembered everything from his past life. Why would he need to study with his maternal uncle again?

But in this small, delicate body, he could skip the literary studies, but martial arts lessons were non-negotiable; he couldn’t miss a single one.

"Mother, teach me my name first." Zhao Mianze coaxed.

In front of others, he put on the demeanor of a mature adult, but in front of Yumeng, he was even more of a spoiled child than Aning.

Yumeng looked at him, rooting around like a little pig at her side, and felt both amused and exasperated.

Since she couldn’t finish her poem anyway, she placed her son on her lap, picked up her brush, and wrote the three characters "Zhao Mianze," teaching him each one.

Mother and son were happily learning the characters when Zhao Xuanyou, dressed in military attire, quickly entered from outside.

"Something happened?"

At this hour, Zhao Xuanyou should have been drilling troops at the Mingju Guard. The fact that he had returned home in military attire meant something big had occurred.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at the maids in the room. They all understood and were about to take Zhao Mianze away, but he stubbornly clung to Yumeng.

Zhao Mianze had a plan.

In his past life, the emperor had passed away when he was ten. In this life, he had been born five years later, so the time was now.

He would rather take a beating than leave. He wanted to stay and listen for any changes, perhaps even help his parents come up with ideas.

"You may leave." Yumeng spoke, still holding Zhao Mianze. The maids respectfully withdrew.

Normally, if Zhao Xuanyou saw Zhao Mianze clinging to Yumeng like this, he would immediately pull him away. But today, he had no time for that.

He picked up Yumeng’s teacup and drank it in one gulp, then said in a deep voice, "A urgent summons came from the palace. His Majesty is critically ill and orders us to immediately go to the capital to attend to him."

---

chapters.title: The Storm Approaches
chapters.content:
"His Majesty..."

Years ago, after the emperor was deposed, Consort Jiang had poisoned him. Although the imperial physicians had discovered and treated it in time, the emperor’s body had still suffered greatly, significantly shortening his lifespan.

Yumeng had not interacted much with the emperor, but from his affection for Zhao Yi Yun, she could tell he was a man of deep emotions.

Apart from her sadness, Yumeng was also confused.

Although Zhao Xuanyou was of the imperial clan, he was not a close relative of the royal family. The emperor had sons and daughters. Why summon Zhao Xuanyou to the palace to attend to him?

A thought suddenly occurred to her.

"You just said 'us'?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s gaze darkened. "The imperial edict indeed orders you and me to take the three children back to the capital to attend to His Majesty."

"This decree is too strange."

Zhao Yi Yun was not even registered in the family genealogy. In the capital, there were only rumors that Zhao Xuanyou had a child from a concubine.

It would be one thing to summon their family of four, but to include Zhao Yi Yun as well? The emperor would obviously not issue such a decree.

Zhao Mianze, sitting on his mother’s lap, blinked as he thought.

Having lived five years in this life, Zhao Mianze had noticed many things. Apart from the earth-shattering changes in his own family, many external matters had also changed accordingly. However, people and events unrelated to the marquis’s mansion remained unchanged.

So, the emperor would definitely pass away this year, and Zhao Yi Yun would become emperor.

"Do we really have to take the children back to the capital?"

"If we, as a family, do not return to the capital, it would be defying the imperial decree."

So they had to go.

"I can’t understand why His Majesty would do this. Could it be that he misses his grandson?"

"That’s possible. However, although the decree is genuine, it may not be His Majesty’s intention."

Yumeng was surprised. "You mean someone is forging the imperial decree?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded, his gaze growing even darker. "The news of Yi Yun being here must have leaked. The other party wants to eliminate us all in one fell swoop."

The people who had taken Zhao Yi Yun out of the palace were all the emperor’s close attendants, absolutely loyal to him.

As the emperor’s condition worsened, these people would inevitably seek their own way out. If they pledged allegiance to the new emperor, they could secure their own wealth and status.

With their lives at stake, Liu Quan, Pan Xun, and others in the Qianqing Palace and the Brocade Guard were all possible suspects.

The news of Zhao Yi Yun being in Yuzhou was likely an offering to the new master.

"It’s likely the work of Consort Li."

With the four princes all in their fiefs, if the emperor was truly on his deathbed, then the one in charge in the palace would be the highest-ranking Consort Li.

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes darkened. "His Majesty’s condition must be very bad."

This sudden illness must have come on very quickly, catching His Majesty off guard.

If Consort Li could use the imperial seal to issue a decree, it meant the emperor was currently unable to give orders.

"If that’s the case, by the time we return to the capital, His Majesty might..." Yumeng did not finish her sentence. She looked at Zhao Xuanyou. "Do we really have to go back?"

"If we return, Yi Yun might still have a chance to survive."

From the moment the emperor had entrusted Zhao Yi Yun to the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion, their fates had been tied together.

If his identity had remained hidden, it would have been fine. But now that it was exposed, the marquis’s mansion had no way out.

Once Prince Ping ascended the throne, he would not spare Zhao Yi Yun, nor the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion.

"Mengmeng, don’t be afraid. I’ve been prepared for this."

A hint of a smile appeared on Zhao Xuanyou’s usually stern face.

Adopting Zhao Yi Yun had not been his original intention, but since he had come to his family, he had to plan ahead and be prepared for anything.

Not just for Zhao Yi Yun, but for the people he cherished most.

Zhao Mianze lowered his head, pretending to play with the brush, while eavesdropping on his parents’ conversation. Their decision did not surprise him at all.

Compared to his parents’ worries about the future, he was quite at ease.

Although there were many variables in this life, Zhao Yi Yun was destined to be the ultimate winner. This was not just confidence in his parents, but also his understanding that, for the vast majority of people, Zhao Yi Yun was the better choice.

Prince Ping had all the advantages and naturally did not need to win over his three younger brothers. Once he ascended the throne, the situation of these three brothers would be dire.

There were officials in the court who supported Prince Ping, and there were also those who followed the other three princes, but the majority were neutral.

If Prince Ping and Consort Li truly usurped the throne by forging a decree, Zhao Yi Yun could rightfully gain their support.

Thinking about what would happen in the future, Zhao Mianze felt a hint of excitement.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at his son, who was scribbling randomly, assuming he wasn’t paying attention to their conversation. He continued, "Pack up quickly. We’ll set off tomorrow."

To reassure Yumeng, Zhao Xuanyou explained, "His Majesty has not been completely unprepared these past few years. The commanders of the three major camps in the capital region are all loyal to him and have no connection to Prince Ping. The capital won’t descend into chaos."

"Then how dare Consort Li and Prince Ping act this way?"

"They don’t have the ability to rebel with an army, but with the imperial seal in their hands, they may have forged an edict of abdication. They’re waiting for the three princes and other imperial relatives to arrive in the capital before revealing it."

Prince Ping wanted not only the throne but also to eliminate his three brothers and nephews in one go to ensure absolute security.

"Are you really afraid?"

Zhao Xuanyou had joined the army in his early teens. He had come this far by being decisive and swift. Knowing where Zhao Yi Yun and the marquis’s mansion’s future lay, he would charge forward without hesitation.

But now he had a weakness. No matter how ruthless he was, he couldn’t ignore it.

Yumeng rubbed Zhao Mianze’s head, her gaze flickering. "I’m just worried about the children’s safety. As long as they’re safe, I’m not afraid of anything."

After a pause, Yumeng said, "No one in the capital has seen Yi Yun. We don’t have to take him with us."

"If we all leave, he may not be safe in Yuzhou."

No matter how powerful the Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion was in Yuzhou City, the city was not impenetrable. Once they left, Prince Ping might send assassins.

"How much have you prepared in advance? Zhao Xuanyou, what else are you hiding from me?"

"Everything I’ve told you is what I just thought of," Zhao Xuanyou said, pressing his lips together. He had indeed only learned of the emperor’s critical condition a quarter of an hour ago, and many of his thoughts had formed on the way back. Of course, there were also many things he had started planning after Zhao Yi Yun arrived in Yuzhou. "Yi Yun will travel with us, but he’ll exchange clothes with his book boy. We’ll play it by ear when we get to the capital."

Yumeng said nothing.

The bright spring light filtered through the gauze curtains, casting a soft glow over the study. But Yumeng’s heart was in turmoil.

Through fire and water, she could accompany Zhao Xuanyou anywhere, but taking the children to the capital. How could she, as a mother, not be afraid?

After a long silence, Yumeng looked into Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes and softly asked, "If it comes to the worst... I mean, if Prince Ping resorts to force, can you protect the children?"

"Yes."

He had always been far-sighted and rarely made mistakes. The only miscalculation in his life was encountering Yumeng.

With his firm answer, Yumeng felt reassured.

"Exchanging identities with the book boy is a good idea, but the children need skilled people to protect them secretly."

If there were secret guards, that would indeed be reassuring...

"I’ll go talk to Lin Geng."

The Jingyuan Marquis’s mansion had a tradition of martial arts, and the head of the household was highly skilled. They didn’t need secret guards. Lin Geng had been an elite secret guard of the Eastern Palace, and Zhao Yi Yun was his former master, so he was trustworthy.

"Lin Geng is indeed reliable. However, on our way back to the capital, I think we should make a detour to Yingzhou."

Zhao Xuanyou was slightly taken aback, then understood. "Ah Hao is in Yingzhou?"

chapters.title: The Moon in the Sky
chapters.content:
At the mention of Wen Ji, Yu Wan’s beautiful eyes lit up with a smile.

"I just received a letter from him two days ago. He said they’ve already returned to Yingzhou."

"He certainly lives a carefree life."

Five years ago, Zhao Xuanyou received a letter from the Prince Rui’s mansion. When he opened it, there was another envelope inside; this one addressed to Wen Ji.

After reading the letter, Wen Ji didn’t say much, but he seemed deeply troubled.

Yu Wan sat with him on the rooftop, and after their conversation, he left Yuzhou.

Over these five years, Wen Ji had returned a few times, but Zhao Xuanyou never asked what he had been doing.

Now that Yu Wan mentioned Yingzhou, the Prince Rui’s fief, it was clear what Wen Ji had been occupied with these past few years.

"With Ah Ji there, everything will be even more secure."

After discussing with his wife, Zhao Xuanyou went to see the old Marquis.

The old Marquis understood that once Zhao Yi Yun’s identity was exposed, the Jingyuan Marquis’s household would have no way out. They had no intention of rebellion; everything was just for self-preservation.

Having decided to return to the capital with their family, they set off from Yuzhou the next noon.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had only brought Zhao Mianze and Ding Ruiyan back to the capital for New Year’s the previous year.

Zhao Mianze still carried his usual air of indifference toward all things, while Ding Ruiyan, upon learning he could return to the capital to see his great-grandmother, was overjoyed and chattered nonstop the entire way.

Only Zhao Yi Yun seemed a little down.

He was worried about his uncles in the capital, who were eyeing the throne like tigers, and also about the Emperor’s failing health.

Over the years, he had studied and learned proper etiquette, and now he understood the Emperor’s care for him more deeply than when he was a child.

Yu Wan knew the Emperor’s days were numbered but offered no empty comfort. No matter what happened, their family would stand by him.

They traveled east for ten days before Zhao Xuanyou asked the old Marquis to rest with the three children at a post station for two days. Meanwhile, he and Yu Wan rode south for a day and arrived in Yingzhou by nightfall.

They found an inn to stay in, and the next morning, following the directions in Wen Ji’s letter, they quickly reached a mountain valley.

A winding stream flowed out from the valley, and on the lush grass by the creek stood two familiar figures.

Liang Miaotong stood on the bank, her face lit with a bright smile. After saying something, she kicked up the water, sending a high spray into the air.

Wen Ji, dressed in a green robe, stood in the stream. He made no effort to avoid the incoming splash, letting the water soak his clothes.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan, seeing the two playing so freely in the water, instinctively reined in their horses. A silent understanding passed between them; they shouldn’t have come to Yingzhou; they shouldn’t disturb this peaceful, secluded paradise.

But Wen Ji had already heard the hoofbeats. He looked up and spotted Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan.

Since they had been seen, there was no reason to avoid them. The couple urged their horses forward.

"Marquis’s wife." Liang Miaotong rushed forward in a few steps, took Yu Wan’s hand, and said joyfully, "It’s been years since we last met. You still look as beautiful as a celestial being, Madame."

Yu Wan couldn’t help but laugh at these words. "Miaotong, your silver tongue has only grown sharper over the years."

Liang Miaotong giggled, then greeted Zhao Xuanyou before pulling Yu Wan over to see the fish they had just caught.

"Brother-in-law." Wen Ji stepped forward and cupped his hands in greeting to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at his brother-in-law, amused. "No wonder you’re never home for more than a few days a year. Turns out you’ve been living the life of an immortal here."

Wen Ji’s face flushed slightly. In a low voice, he said, "These past few years, I’ve traveled many places with Miaotong. We only returned here last month."

He now wore a small, silver mask that just covered the birthmark on half his face, leaving his delicate brows and eyes uncovered.

To Zhao Xuanyou, Wen Ji’s true appearance felt somewhat unfamiliar.

After studying him for a moment, Zhao Xuanyou patted his shoulder and said gently, "Life is short. To share such a bond with someone and wander the world together. What could be more wonderful?"

Even Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t help but feel a pang of envy.

He and Yu Wan had never been so free and unrestrained.

"I never expected things to go this far with Miaotong."

When Wen Ji first received Liang Miaotong’s letter, he hadn’t wanted to go.

Their statuses were worlds apart; she was the beloved daughter of a high-ranking official, while he was an abandoned child with a disfigured face, trained as a shadow guard, doomed to live in the shadows. How could they ever be a match?

But Yu Wan had urged him to go to Yingzhou.

They had known each other for a long time. The fact that Liang Miaotong had left the capital to avoid marriage and even written to him from the Prince Rui’s mansion showed that this was no impulsive decision; she had made up her mind.

If Wen Ji didn’t respond, how great a blow would that be to her?

Regardless of their future, Wen Ji owed it to her to give a face-to-face answer.

With that resolve, he went to Yingzhou, only to find Liang Miaotong in the prince’s mansion, her spirits low and her usual brightness gone.

He hadn’t realized how much she cared for him.

To Wen Ji, she was like the radiant moon in the sky; he didn’t want to drag her down into the dust.

But she had left her parents behind, choosing to stay in Yingzhou. Rumors must have spread among the noble families of the capital, and Wen Ji couldn’t bear the thought of her facing it all alone.

Since she refused to be confined to the inner quarters, he accompanied her on her travels across the world.

One could never have both the fish and the bear’s paw. He couldn’t give her a marriage envied by all, but at least he could fulfill one of her wishes.

One day, when she looked back on this time, it wouldn’t be all regret.

"Brother-in-law, you and my sister suddenly coming here. Is there an urgent matter?" Wen Ji wasn’t used to discussing such romantic matters with Zhao Xuanyou. Realizing the two of them had ridden all this way, there must be trouble.

Zhao Xuanyou hesitated for a moment before speaking. "There is indeed something."

Bringing Wen Ji into the capital was a risk, but Zhao Xuanyou believed the odds were in their favor.

If they succeeded, Wen Ji would have the merit of supporting the new emperor, making him a suitable match for Liang Miaotong.

As he spoke, his gaze flicked toward Yu Wan.

Yu Wan happened to look up at that moment. Their eyes met, and the couple exchanged a knowing smile.

"Madame, are you here to take Ah Ji away?" Liang Miaotong asked. "I know it was wrong of me to keep him here, but we haven’t… we’ve only been traveling together."

"I know. We came for another reason," Yu Wan said softly. "How much do you know about what’s happening in the capital?"

"A few days ago, my sister sent word that His Majesty is gravely ill. She and the Prince are going to the capital to attend to him. Are you and the Marquis also going to the capital for this reason?"

"Yes." Since Liang Miaotong and Wen Ji were clearly devoted to each other, Yu Wan considered her family. She spoke frankly: "There may be upheaval in the capital. This time, we’re bringing the children with us, and having Ah Ji with us will make me feel much more at ease."

At this, Yu Wan looked at Liang Miaotong with concern. "The Prince and Princess are not in Yingzhou. If I take Ah Ji away, you’ll be left alone here. Should I send you back to the prince’s mansion today?"

This secluded valley was remote and quiet; it might not be safe for a young woman like Liang Miaotong to stay here alone.

Liang Miaotong was startled by Yu Wan’s words.

When her sister had sent word a few days ago, she hadn’t thought much of it. But now, hearing Yu Wan say there might be upheaval in the capital, she suddenly realized: the Emperor was gravely ill, yet no crown prince had been named. Her brother-in-law and sister were going to the capital not just to attend to the Emperor, but would inevitably be drawn into the struggle for the throne.

Naive as she was, she understood that a change in the throne often came with bloodshed.

Her entire family was in the capital. Would they be in danger?

At this thought, Liang Miaotong tightly gripped Yu Wan’s hand. "Madame, I want to go back to the capital with you."

---

chapters.title: The Worst-Case Plan
chapters.content:
"You haven’t been home in years. It’s good to go back for a visit."

Yu Wan hadn’t asked Zhao Xuanyou about his arrangements in detail, but since he dared to bring the three children into the capital, she assumed no major chaos would erupt.

Thinking of Liang Miaotong and Wen Ji’s relationship, Yu Wan added, "If you’re worried about Minister Liang and Madame Liang’s displeasure, I’ll go with you to the Liang residence."

Liang Miaotong and Wen Ji had traveled together for years, their hearts long connected.

By all rights, the man’s family should formally explain the situation to the woman’s family.

"Madame, I…" Liang Miaotong’s cheeks flushed, but before she could speak, her gaze caught Zhao Xuanyou and Wen Ji approaching, and she quickly lowered her eyes.

Yu Wan said, "Miaotong has been away from home for years. She wants to return to the capital. Since it’s still early, let’s set off soon."

If they left now, they could reach the post station where the old Marquis and the others were staying by nightfall.

Without delay, the four of them set off immediately.

Their group included the elderly and children, so they didn’t ride at full speed. They had previously worried that Prince Ping might send assassins after them, but the journey had been smooth so far.

Twenty days later, they arrived in the capital. Zhao Xuanyou was summoned to the palace, the old Marquis took the three children back to the Marquis’s mansion, and Yu Wan, along with Wen Ji, escorted Liang Miaotong to the Liang residence.

Liang Miaotong hadn’t fled home in secret; she had followed Princess Rui to the fief. In the capital, this hadn’t caused a major scandal, but it was still a great blow to Minister Liang and his wife.

Fortunately, Liang Miaofeng had returned to the capital earlier and visited her parents, explaining Liang Miaotong’s experiences over the past few years. So when Yu Wan and Wen Ji met Minister Liang and Madame Liang, they weren’t taken by surprise.

Yu Wan first mentioned that Liang Miaotong had accumulated many sketches during her travels. Seeing the thick stack of drawings, Minister Liang and Madame Liang realized their daughter had indeed been traveling and not eloping. Their hearts were filled with complex emotions.

Liang Miaotong was their precious youngest daughter. Being the baby of the family, she had always been more spoiled and free-spirited than her siblings. Yet, after years of travel, she remained as innocent and lively as ever, which showed how well Wen Ji had protected her.

A man and a woman traveling together without crossing the boundaries of propriety also spoke to Wen Ji’s character.

Though Wen Ji wasn’t the kind of son-in-law Minister Liang and Madame Liang had originally envisioned, they found him acceptable.

Seeing their tacit approval, Yu Wan pulled Madame Liang aside and said that the Marquis’s household was willing to formalize the marriage as soon as possible. However, given the Emperor’s current poor health, it wouldn’t be appropriate to arrange a wedding now. They could discuss it later, and she would ensure Liang Miaotong wasn’t wronged.

Madame Liang was intelligent and understood Yu Wan’s implication.

The Emperor’s health was failing fast. The palace would soon be in turmoil. Compared to her youngest daughter’s marriage, she was more concerned about Prince Rui and Princess Rui.

With the position of crown prince still vacant, even if Prince Rui had no intention of seizing the throne, others would see him as a threat. One wrong move could lead to the downfall of the entire family.

Seeing the worry in Madame Liang’s eyes, Yu Wan bluntly stated that since their families were soon to be related by marriage, if the Liang family encountered any trouble in the future, the Jingyuan Marquis’s household would do their best to help.

To others, this might sound presumptuous.

The Liang family was connected to Prince Rui by marriage, so naturally, Prince Rui would handle any issues. But Madame Liang knew that the Jingyuan Marquis held high rank and power. No matter who ascended the throne, his position would remain unshaken. Hearing Yu Wan’s words did ease her mind considerably.

With matters settled, Yu Wan and Wen Ji returned to the Marquis’s mansion. When they arrived at Leshou Hall, Old Madame Ye had one hand around Zhao Mianze and the other around Ding Ruiyan, basking in familial joy.

After exchanging greetings, Yu Wan went to see Zhao Yi Yun and instructed Wen Ji and Lin Jing to stay by his side at all times.

As night fell, Zhao Xuanyou finally returned home.

"Where are Ah Chun and Ah Ning?" he asked, seeing Yu Wan sitting alone at the table.

Hearing his tone, Yu Wan felt slightly reassured. She stood up, took his hand, and led him into the inner room.

"They’re at Leshou Hall."

Their family had lived in Yuzhou for years, and whenever they returned to the capital for New Year’s, Ah Chun and Ah Ning would stay at Leshou Hall.

Old Madame Ye was advanced in years, and having the two children spend more time with her was a way to show filial piety.

Zhao Xuanyou hummed in acknowledgment, then turned and pressed a kiss to Yu Wan’s forehead before sitting down with her on the chaise.

"How is His Majesty’s health…?"

"Very poor," Zhao Xuanyou said, his expression darkening. "I heard he can only stay awake for two or three hours a day. He can’t speak or move."

"Is the palace now under the control of Consort Li and Prince Ping?"

"In the first few days after His Majesty fell ill, Consort Li was indeed in charge. The imperial decree summoning us to the palace was probably issued then. Later, His Majesty was lucid for half a day and ordered Liu Quan to summon Chancellor Xu and Chancellor Sun to the palace to manage state affairs. The imperial seal was also given to Chancellor Xu. After the four princes arrived in the capital, they took turns attending to His Majesty in the Qianqing Palace."

Taking turns attending to the Emperor?

With the position of crown prince still vacant, everyone had a chance. Naturally, they would all be vying for power.

Yu Wan’s eyes flickered as she looked at Zhao Xuanyou. "Do Consort Li and Prince Ping know that Yi Yun is with us?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded.

He and Prince Ping had some acquaintance. Naturally, Prince Ping had kept him for a talk today.

"Right now, the palace is no longer under Consort Li’s control, and he can’t be bothered with Yi Yun anymore."

Zhao Yi Yun was the son of the deposed crown prince and had been declared dead. To Prince Ping, the greater threat was clearly his three younger brothers.

"So, he still wants to win you over."

"Once His Majesty passes, he will act immediately."

During their private conversation in the palace, Zhao Xuanyou had even detected a hint of dissatisfaction in Prince Ping’s words toward his birth mother, Consort Li.

If Consort Li had been ruthless and clever enough, she should have ensured the Emperor’s "passing" before the two chancellors entered the palace, then issued a secret decree for Prince Ping to ascend the throne. The other three princes were far away in their fiefs and would have been powerless to stop it.

But in Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes, that wasn’t the case. If Consort Li truly had such intelligence and means, the Emperor wouldn’t have allowed her to manage the inner palace.

"Why is Prince Ping in such a hurry? As the eldest son, if there’s no imperial decree naming an heir, he would naturally inherit the throne."

Zhao Xuanyou smiled faintly, lowering his voice. "There’s a rumor in the palace that His Majesty wrote an imperial decree naming his successor long ago. No one knows where it’s hidden or to whom it was entrusted."

"Though it’s just a rumor, I believe it."

The Emperor had been in poor health ever since the poisoning. Knowing his days were numbered, he must have made arrangements.

Everyone knew Prince Ping wasn’t the Emperor’s preferred successor. Among the others, Prince Qing Zhao Yu was frivolous and fond of women, which the Emperor disliked. Prince Jing Zhao Lin and Prince Rui Zhao Qi were the more likely candidates.

Yu Wan sighed. "All we can do is wait and see."

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had no intention of rebelling; they only sought to protect themselves.

Prince Ping knew Zhao Yi Yun’s identity, so they absolutely couldn’t allow him to ascend the throne. If the imperial decree named Prince Jing or Prince Rui, that would be fine.

But Prince Ping wouldn’t sit idly by. Chaos in the capital was inevitable. In the midst of such turmoil, how should the Marquis’s household proceed?

Seeing Yu Wan lost in thought, her cheeks puffed with worry, Zhao Xuanyou couldn’t resist leaning in for a kiss.

"With me here, I won’t let our family suffer."

After a month of travel, the couple had been busy caring for the elderly and the young, and it had been a long time since they had a moment alone.

Yu Wan cupped Zhao Xuanyou’s face and stared directly into his eyes.

"What?"

Yu Wan’s expression remained blank as she let out a light humph. "I want to see what kind of schemes you’re hiding in that heart of yours."

Zhao Xuanyou pressed his lips together and said nothing. "You said it yourself; we’ll wait and see. I’ve just made the worst-case preparations, that’s all."

chapters.title: Coincidence
chapters.content:
The Emperor’s condition showed no improvement. Each day, he would only awaken for a couple of hours, able to move nothing but his eyes; let alone speak.

Fortunately, his condition had not worsened. The four princes and two princesses took turns attending to him in pairs, none willing to let anyone else be alone with the Emperor.

Beneath the palace’s calm surface, undercurrents surged. This very tranquility was the harbinger of an impending storm.

With Zhao Xuanyou by her side, Yu Ying’s mood remained light. Apart from tending to her grandmother at the Marquis’s residence, she occasionally ventured out to visit friends.

One morning, she took a carriage to Yunshui Nunnery to offer incense for her family’s safety.

Years ago, the nuns of Yunshui Nunnery had taken in Ding Wenxi when he was gravely ill. Yu Ying had never forgotten their kindness and sent the Marquis’s steward to the nunnery every year to contribute to its upkeep.

The nuns recognized Yu Ying immediately. Upon her arrival, they quickly led her to the main hall to offer incense.

After kneeling and praying before the Buddha with folded hands, Yu Ying rose to greet the abbess. As they exchanged pleasantries, her gaze flickered to a familiar figure seated on a meditation cushion in the corner.

The woman had already noticed Yu Ying. Seeing her look over, she stood up from the cushion.

“Madame Hou.”

Yu Ying studied Sun Qianran, whom she had not seen in years, her eyes narrowing slightly. Since the other had greeted her, she naturally returned the courtesy.

“Miss Sun.”

Sun Qianran, observing Yu Ying’s elegant attire and flawless makeup, smiled faintly. “It’s been so long since we last met, yet Madame Hou remains as beautiful as ever.”

“Miss Sun flatters me. You look well yourself.”

Indeed, though Sun Qianran’s clothes were plain and her hair unadorned, her complexion was far better than Yu Ying remembered.

“So the two benefactors know each other,” the abbess murmured a Buddhist invocation before joining their conversation.

As it turned out, Sun Qianran had been a patron of Yunshui Nunnery for years. After hearing from the abbess that many young girls in the city went hungry and still had to work, she had donated silver to renovate the kitchen and have hundreds of vegetarian buns steamed daily.

The abbess added that Sun Qianran, fearing the girls might take the buns home to their families instead of eating them, had stipulated that the buns could only be eaten on the nunnery’s premises, though they could eat as many as they wanted.

After speaking with some of the girls, the abbess learned they lacked any means to support themselves. Since Sun Qianran was already inclined to charity, she hired two embroidery mistresses to teach the girls needlework at the nunnery every day.

Sun Qianran thought learning a trade was a good idea, but she believed literacy was even more important. Even if they went out to work, knowing how to read and write would make it harder for others to take advantage of them.

Since then, Sun Qianran had come to Yunshui Nunnery every few days to teach the girls to read. That morning, she had just finished a lesson when the abbess invited her to join the nuns in reciting scriptures.

Yu Ying was slightly surprised by this. The last time they had met, Sun Qianran had been consumed by heartache, her thoughts entirely occupied by Pei Ta.

Noticing their acquaintance, the abbess invited them to the tea room to sit for a while before excusing herself to oversee the recitation.

Once she left, the tea room fell silent.

Yu Ying lifted her teacup and took a sip. The tea, roasted by the nuns themselves, had a faint bitterness that lingered pleasantly on the palate.

Sun Qianran smiled. “When I first came to Yunshui Nunnery, I had no idea Madame Hou was also a patron here. Later, when the abbess mentioned you, I never expected our connection to run so deep.”

Most noble families in the capital made offerings at Baima Temple or Yunshan Temple. Yunshui Nunnery, being a convent, was located in a poor, noisy neighborhood with dilapidated surroundings.

“I used to come here to burn incense and pray when I was still a maidservant,” Yu Ying said. “Now that my circumstances have improved, I naturally continue to contribute. But Miss Sun…” A flicker of sharpness entered her gaze. “You don’t strike me as the type to visit a place like this.”

Sun Qianran caught the implication in Yu Ying’s words and replied coolly, “Madame Hou must remember how frail I used to be. A single trip outside the city would leave me bedridden for days. It was by chance that I passed by Yunshui Nunnery and spoke with the abbess, which is how I came to be here.”

“Miss Sun is of noble birth. Contributing money to the nunnery is one thing, but personally teaching those girls to read and write is another.”

Yu Ying raised an eyebrow, her gaze piercing.

Sun Qianran was one of the most intelligent women Yu Ying had ever met. But she also knew that beneath her refined exterior, Sun Qianran had a calculating, pragmatic streak; likely inherited from her father, Minister Sun. She approached everything with cold logic, weighing only gains and losses.

Skilled in scheming, yet indifferent to sentiment.

Pei Ta had seen this clearly, which was why he had resolutely cut ties with her.

They could never be of one mind. The so-called harmony and mutual understanding she had spoken of was nothing but a pretense to deceive him.

Sun Qianran was taken aback for a moment. She stared at Yu Ying in silence before sighing in resignation. “It was indeed a coincidence that I first came here. But seeing the eternal lamp you had offered before the Buddha statue was an even greater coincidence.”

“You offer prayers here, and so do I. If you returned to the capital, I suppose you would, at the abbess’s invitation, ensure those ragged little girls had enough to eat and learned a trade. And I would personally teach them to read and write. Teaching them to fish, so to speak; I would do it better than you, no matter what.”

Normally, Sun Qianran spoke in measured, careful tones, leaving much unsaid. It was rare for her to speak so candidly.

Yu Ying’s sharp gaze softened slightly. “Do you do all this… still for him?”

Pei Ta had been in the capital these past few years, and Yu Ying had not heard any news of his marriage. In Sun Qianran’s heart, there must still be some hope.

“At first, yes. But not anymore.” Sun Qianran met Yu Ying’s eyes steadily. “The abbess here may not be famous, but she is wise and deeply versed in Buddhist teachings. Those dirty little girls are lively and adorable. Teaching them to read brings me joy. I come here every day because I want to, not to outdo you, nor to make Pei Ta change his mind.”

This time, it was Yu Ying’s turn to be surprised.

But Sun Qianran’s gaze was sincere enough to convince her.

Moreover, given their respective positions, Sun Qianran had no reason to lie to her.

No wonder Yu Ying had felt she was a different person the first time she saw her that day.

“In that case, congratulations.”

Breaking free from inner demons and living life with peace of mind was worthy of celebration.

Sun Qianran smiled. Noticing that only the two of them remained in the tea room, her eyes flickered, and she spoke softly, “They say when the wind fills the tower, the storm is coming. Lord Hou and Madame Hou’s return to the capital now suggests you have come prepared.”

Yu Ying had not expected such a sudden shift in conversation. Suspicion arose. “Did you come here today specifically to wait for me?”

“How would I have known you’d come out today?” Sun Qianran laughed. “Perhaps it’s fate. Heaven must have intended to lend me a hand.”

That was true; Yu Ying’s visit to Yunshui Nunnery had been a last-minute decision.

“I know little of court politics. If Miss Sun is delivering a message on behalf of your father, please have Minister Sun speak directly with my husband.”

“At a time like this, Lord Hou wouldn’t deign to acknowledge my father,” Sun Qianran sighed. “I know all about the things my father has done. If the one he supports doesn’t end up on the throne, he won’t be able to escape unscathed.”

“I truly don’t understand what you’re talking about.”

“If you don’t, then let it be,” Sun Qianran lowered her voice further. “But if you do, I have more to say.”

---

chapters.title: The Whereabouts of the Imperial Decree
chapters.content:
Yu Ying pondered for a moment but neither rose to leave nor responded.

Sun Qianran, after all, had lived in the capital for years and enjoyed her father’s trust. She knew many of Minister Sun’s secrets.

Prince Ping knew the whereabouts of Zhao Yi Yun. What about Minister Sun?

If Minister Sun knew where Zhao Yi Yun was, the Marquis’s household would need to respond.

She glanced at Sun Qianran, waiting for her to continue.

“My father is a man of ambition, as Madame Hou must have heard. He is now taking a great risk by supporting Prince Ping.”

“Do you think Prince Ping has little chance of winning?” Yu Ying suddenly asked.

Sun Qianran let out a soft laugh, clearly not optimistic about Prince Ping’s prospects. She quickly continued, “I couldn’t persuade my father, but he is still my own flesh and blood. If something happens to him, I will inevitably be implicated.”

Yu Ying understood her meaning.

The struggle for the throne was a matter of life and death. Everyone knew Minister Sun had sided with Prince Ping. If Prince Ping failed, the new emperor would certainly not spare Minister Sun’s entire clan.

Yu Ying still did not engage, merely responding coolly, “Minister Sun holds great power and influence, and his strategies are flawless. Miss Sun need not worry.”

Sun Qianran neither agreed nor disagreed. After a moment of silence, she said softly, “The political situation changes in an instant. Today, my father may be powerful, but tomorrow, he could be a prisoner.”

Her reasoning was simple.

In the struggle for power, either the east wind would prevail over the west, or the west over the east.

She wished her father, like Minister Xu, had chosen not to take sides. But her father was too eager to rise above all others. He had been suppressed by Minister Xu all his life and was willing to gamble everything on this one chance.

Her father had obtained everything he wanted in life except this one thing, so he was willing to risk it all. But she was different.

She had too many regrets in life. Just as she had begun to recover and start a new life, she did not want to gamble.

The Marquis of Jingyuan had not taken sides, so whoever ascended the throne would not move against his family.

“You were born into privilege, the jewel of the Minister’s household. Unless Minister Sun falls from power, no one can help you.”

This was precisely why she had firmly sided with her father and broken ties with Pei Ta.

“But I am just an insignificant woman. If Lord Hou is willing to lend a hand, could he save my life?”

“Why should we help you?” Yu Ying countered.

“Of course, I wouldn’t ask for help without offering something in return,” Sun Qianran’s eyes gleamed as she looked up at Yu Ying. “I want to make a deal with Lord Hou and you.”

A deal?

Yu Ying had not expected her to be so direct. She had not played any verbal games today.

“What do you have to offer?”

Sun Qianran lowered her voice even further. “I know who has the Emperor’s decree of enthronement.”

At the mention of the decree, Yu Ying’s body jolted slightly, and she stared at Sun Qianran in surprise.

After a moment’s thought, she did not believe her.

“Setting aside whether this decree even exists, even if it does, if Prince Ping and Minister Sun had obtained it, they would either produce it immediately or destroy it. Why would they let the news out?”

“My father and Prince Ping naturally want to find it,” Sun Qianran’s eyes flashed with a hint of mockery. “It’s just that they don’t know where it is.”

“They don’t know, but you do?”

“When the deposed Empress and Crown Prince failed, my father had me enter the palace to attend to Zhao Yi Yun. At that time, Zhao Yi Yun was living in the Qianqing Palace, and so was I, coming and going daily.”

Yu Ying remembered this.

At the time, the Emperor had been poisoned, and Pan Xun had even specifically summoned her and Zhao Xuanyou from Yu Prefecture, hoping she could enter the palace to secure this opportunity.

“And?”

“My father went to great lengths to plant his people in the Qianqing Palace, intending to make full preparations. Later, when the Emperor’s health improved, he recalled Eunuch Liu to his side. The people my father and Minister Xu had planted around the Emperor were all expelled by Eunuch Liu.”

“But you still have eyes and ears in the palace.”

Sun Qianran smiled and nodded.

“So, are you interested?”

Yu Ying found the question odd. “Why would Lord Hou and I be interested in the decree? You should approach Prince Jing, Prince Qing, or Prince Rui, not me.”

“They don’t know what kind of person I am. Why would they believe I’d betray my father to save myself?”

“Do you think I understand you?” Yu Ying’s eyes sparkled with amusement. “Miss Sun’s words truly flatter me.”

Sun Qianran smiled openly.

Apart from her father and Pei Ta, Yu Ying was indeed the only one who understood her nature.

“I don’t think Prince Ping will win. Even if he obtains the decree, it won’t change anything.” Sun Qianran lowered her gaze and continued, “But today, meeting you at Yunshui Nunnery must be the work of the Buddha, intending to save my life. I have no other requests. I only want to trade this information for my life.”

Her body was frail, and she relied on a life of luxury to sustain herself. Unable to flee far in times of turmoil, even if she foresaw Prince Ping’s failure, she could not leave the capital to escape disaster.

“I have no need to make a deal with you,” Yu Ying initially refused, then paused before changing her tone. “But people are naturally curious. If you tell me, then in the future, if there’s an opportunity to help you, I will do my best.”

After this long conversation, Yu Ying finally understood her situation.

Because Minister Sun had sided with Prince Ping, a rift had formed between father and daughter. Sun Qianran did not know Zhao Yi Yun’s whereabouts, and Minister Sun was unaware of the information his daughter possessed.

Yu Ying had no intention of making a deal with her, but knowing the whereabouts of the decree could only be beneficial, not harmful.

She did not want Sun Qianran to discern her true intentions, so she spoke vaguely.

Sun Qianran could speak if she wished, but Yu Ying would not press her.

“The Emperor entrusted the decree of enthronement to Minister Xu. If he were to suddenly pass away, Minister Xu would read the decree aloud. However, I don’t know where Minister Xu has hidden it.”

Yu Ying suddenly realized.

Sun Qianran only knew that the decree was with Minister Xu. This information alone was not enough to make a deal with anyone.

She suspected that Sun Qianran had only brought it up today to curry favor with her.

“In that case, my earlier words still stand. I will do my best.”

Yu Ying maintained her calm demeanor, bid farewell to Sun Qianran, and left.

It was only upon returning to the Marquis’s residence that she realized her heart was racing.

Zhao Xuanyou had always told her not to worry about such matters, and she had never dwelled on them. Today, she had unexpectedly learned such significant news, and it left her deeply unsettled.

Since Zhao Xuanyou had not yet returned home, Yu Ying called for Wen Ge and told him everything that had happened that day.

“Where do you think Minister Xu would hide the decree?”

Wen Ge thought for a moment. “Once the Emperor passes, the palace will fall under the control of the noble concubine. Therefore, the decree cannot be in the palace.”

“In Minister Xu’s residence?”

“Many royal relatives and nobles in the capital have built secret chambers. Minister Xu has been in office for over twenty years, so his residence must have one as well.” At this point, Wen Ge had a sudden inspiration. “Lin Leng, while in the Eastern Palace, was ordered to investigate the secrets and weaknesses of the important ministers to help the Empress and Crown Prince maintain control. He should know Minister Xu well. Why not ask him?”

Wen Ge was skilled in qinggong and had a gentle temperament. Zhao Zun had always kept him by his side as a guard, and he had never been sent out on missions.

Lin Leng, however, was different. As the head of the secret guards, he had handled many confidential matters for Zhao Zun and possessed a great deal of classified information.

Now that Yu Ying knew of the decree’s existence, she could not pretend otherwise.

In a moment, she made up her mind and ordered a maid to summon Lin Leng.

chapters.title: A Bold Gamble
chapters.content:
When Lin Jing arrived, he brought Zhao Yi Yun and the young servant along with him.

He was tasked with protecting Zhao Yi Yun’s safety, so wherever he went, he had to follow, and even when coming to the Tangli Courtyard, he didn’t feel at ease leaving Zhao Yi Yun alone there.

Once the maid closed the door, Zhao Yi Yun quickly ran to Yu Wan and threw himself into her arms.

"Mother."

Since returning to the capital, mother and son had not been this intimate.

After returning to the capital, Yu Wan had been pretending to be indifferent to the child from the outer chamber, not allowing him to come to the Tangli Courtyard to pay his respects.

Old Master Ye pretended to be angry and didn’t let the illegitimate great-grandson live in the Leshou Hall, only occasionally sending some food over.

This was both to confirm the status of the outer chamber child and to reduce contact between others and Zhao Yi Yun.

"Have you been bored staying in the courtyard all this time?"

"No." Although he said so, Zhao Yi Yun’s eyes betrayed him. Facing Yu Wan’s clear gaze, he could only smile guiltily.

In Yuzhou, although his daily lessons were packed, he could ride out of the city and go to the Hu people’s market with his younger siblings. It was incredibly free.

In the capital, he could only read books by himself every day, practice martial arts with Wen Ji and Lin Jing, and it was even difficult to play with his sister for a while.

"Mother, when are we going back to Yuzhou?"

"Miss Yuzhou?"

This time, Zhao Yi Yun didn’t pretend to be strong and honestly nodded.

Yu Wan also wanted to take the children back to Yuzhou peacefully, but their family had already been drawn into the struggle for the throne.

Going against the current, one must advance or retreat.

If they didn’t fight for it, they would have to beg the one in power for mercy, hoping they would show compassion and spare their lives.

"Do you still remember what happened when you were little?"

Zhao Yi Yun was slightly stunned and silently lowered his gaze.

When they left the capital, he was already five years old.

He didn’t know many details about the fall of the Eastern Palace, but he was very clear that his biological father had been the Crown Prince of the Eastern Palace, and the person on the dragon throne was his own grandfather.

"Mother, I’ve forgotten what happened before."

Yu Wan patted his shoulder and softly said, "Has returning to the capital made you sad?"

"A little."

After hesitating for a long time, Zhao Yi Yun softly replied.

He liked his parents, Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan, very much, but the parents in his memories were also very good. Especially his mother, who was beautiful and gentle, always had endless stories to tell him.

Yu Wan held him in her arms and comforted him for a while before having Ran Dong take him and the young servant to the side hall for snacks.

She slightly composed herself and told Lin Jing about the situation she had learned from Sun Qianran.

Lin Jing pondered for a moment and said in a low voice, "Prime Minister Xu has the merit of following the current emperor since the beginning. However long His Majesty has been on the throne, Prime Minister Xu has held the prime minister’s seal for that long. If His Majesty has any last wishes, the decree to establish the heir is most likely in Prime Minister Xu’s hands."

At this point, Lin Jing looked up at Yu Wan. "Madam, do you want me to go to the Prime Minister’s residence to search for the decree?"

"I do have that intention." Yu Wan decided to be straightforward. "Yi Yun’s identity has already been exposed. For now, only Prince Ping knows, but we can’t be sure he won’t tell others. Others will inevitably be wary of Yi Yun’s identity. To protect him and the Marquis’s residence, we must take the initiative."

The decree to establish the heir would certainly not name Prince Ping, but it would also absolutely not name Zhao Yi Yun, who had been exiled from the capital long ago.

Lin Jing’s eyes trembled violently.

The fall of the Eastern Palace had been six years ago. Could there be a turning point now?

His heart was suddenly filled with turbulent waves.

He had been much more diligent as a dark guard than Wen Ji, and his loyalty to Zhao Jun had been much stronger.

Hearing Yu Wan’s idea, he immediately cupped his hands. "This subordinate is willing to go to the Prime Minister’s residence immediately to investigate and will definitely retrieve the decree."

Yu Wan nodded and thoughtfully said, "Something so important, Prime Minister Xu will definitely hide it in a secret room or a hidden compartment. If you go blindly searching, it will be like looking for a needle in a haystack."

"Then..."

"You two will sneak into the Ministry of Works tonight and see if you can find the architectural plans of the Prime Minister’s residence."

Lin Jing still didn’t know what Yu Wan wanted the architectural plans for, but Wen Ji’s eyes lit up.

Many years ago, he had seen Yu Wan carefully studying the architectural plans of the Xingguo Duke’s residence and finding the best route in and out.

Although confused, Lin Jing did not question Yu Wan’s decision.

"This subordinate will prepare immediately. However, regarding the young master... I will arrange for others to protect him. You two can focus solely on the decree. No matter how late it is, come find me once you have the architectural plans."

"Yes." Wen Ji and Lin Jing responded together, and the two quickly opened the door and left.

But as soon as they opened the door, Zhao Mianze outside bumped into them.

Wen Ji, afraid he would fall, squatted down to catch him. "Eavesdropping here!"

Zhao Mianze was not panicked at all.

He had indeed been eavesdropping, but his mother would certainly not blame him.

He laughed and said, "Uncle, don’t mind me," then struggled free from the embrace and went into the house.

Wen Ji naturally didn’t care and went with Lin Jing to discuss the matter of sneaking into the Ministry of Works.

"Ah Chun, what were you doing hiding by the door?"

Zhao Mianze said, "I came to see Mother. Aunt Ran Dong wouldn’t let me in, so of course I had to listen to see what secrets Mother and Uncle had."

"Then what did you hear?" Yu Wan asked with a smile.

Zhao Mianze pretended to be disappointed and shook his head.

"Big Brother is here too."

Yu Wan took Zhao Mianze’s hand and walked towards the side hall. Zhao Yi Yun, seeing his younger brother, hurriedly asked, "Where is Ah Ning?"

Zhao Mianze’s small body housed an old soul. He found both Zhao Yi Yun and Ah Ning immature, so he rarely played with them. Instead, Zhao Yi Yun and Ah Ning were closer.

Thus, he was not surprised by Zhao Yi Yun’s reaction and lazily sat at the table, picking up a piece of osmanthus cake.

"She’s still at Leshou Hall playing the nine-linked rings with Grandmother."

Zhao Mianze did everything with an air of nonchalance. Although Old Master Ye doted on him, over time, he still found his great-granddaughter cuter and kept her close every day.

This gave Zhao Mianze the perfect excuse to slip away to Yu Wan’s side.

Zhao Yi Yun responded with an "Oh" and served Zhao Mianze a bowl of snow pear soup before sitting quietly beside him.

Yu Wan, seeing this, ordered Ran Dong to go to Leshou Hall and bring Ah Ning over to play for a while.

It was rare for the children to be together, and soon the side hall was filled with laughter.

However, the sky outside suddenly darkened, and thick black clouds rolled in. Before long, it started to rain.

Yu Wan was busy preparing dinner when Zhao Xuanyou arrived home, stepping through the rain.

The couple had dinner with the children, and because the rain was getting heavier, they arranged for the children to sleep in the Tangli Courtyard that night.

After the children had all gone to bed, the two finally lay down on the couch.

As they embraced to sleep, Yu Wan told Zhao Xuanyou about the day’s events.

"Ah Ji and Lin Jing don’t know if they’ve managed to get into the Prime Minister’s residence yet."

Sensing Yu Wan’s worry, Zhao Xuanyou comforted her, "They are both well-trained dark guards. A little rain is nothing. In fact, such weather makes it less likely for them to be discovered when sneaking into the Ministry of Works."

"Am I being too trusting of Sun Qianran? Could this be a trap set for me?"

Yu Wan had acted decisively, but her heart was still anxious.

After all, she had no experience with court struggles and was afraid that one careless move could plunge her entire family into an abyss of endless suffering.

---

chapters.title: Rainy Night
chapters.content:
Zhao Mianze had drunk an extra bowl of preserved plum soup at night and, after sleeping for a while, got up to use the restroom.

The rain had been falling continuously outside, and the banana leaves in the courtyard were being washed by the rain, making a rustling sound that dispelled much of his drowsiness.

On his way back, he suddenly heard low voices coming from his parents’ room.

Zhao Mianze hesitated for a moment before tiptoeing towards that direction.

It wasn’t that he wanted to pry into his parents’ private affairs, but this return to the capital was a matter of great importance.

Having eavesdropped on his mother and uncle’s conversation during the day, he wanted to hear his father’s plans as well. In case something went wrong, he could find a way to remind his parents.

Fortunately, tonight all the children were sleeping in the Tangli Courtyard. Yu Wan was worried that they might not sleep well if there was thunder in the middle of the night, so she deliberately left the door open.

Zhao Mianze quietly crouched behind the screen and could hear their conversation.

He heard Zhao Xuanyou say, "In the entire capital, the person His Majesty trusts the most is probably Prime Minister Xu. If there really is a decree, it is most likely with him."

Prime Minister Xu held a high position and great power, being the leader of all officials. It would be most convincing for him to announce the imperial decree, and even the princes would not dare to object.

"It’s good to have Ah Ji and Lin Jing go look for it," Zhao Xuanyou said softly.

If they couldn’t find it, it wouldn’t be a big problem, but if they did...

Zhao Mianze also agreed with his father’s words.

After all, in his previous life, the emperor had entrusted Zhao Yi Yun to Prime Minister Xu, which showed how much the emperor trusted Prime Minister Xu.

Many things had changed in this life, but it made sense for the decree to be with Prime Minister Xu.

Hearing Zhao Xuanyou say this, Yu Wan felt a little more at ease. After thinking for a moment, she asked, "During dinner, you seemed distracted. What were you thinking about?"

Zhao Xuanyou knew he couldn’t hide any change in expression from her. He slowly said, "Two commanders of the Five City Military Commission have been bribed by Prince Ping."

The Five City Military Commission didn’t have many troops, but they were responsible for maintaining order in the capital.

Previously, Zhao Xuanyou had said that no major chaos could arise in the capital.

The Three Major Camps in the capital were under the command of His Majesty’s trusted generals, and Prince Ping couldn’t mobilize them. The palace had the Jin Yi Wei keeping watch, so there shouldn’t be any major problems. However, they hadn’t considered the Five City Military Commission.

"What good would it do for Prince Ping to control the Five City Military Commission?" Yu Wan asked. "Does he want to harm the common people?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, Yu Wan realized something and was suddenly alarmed. "The families of all the civil and military officials live in the capital. The people of the Five City Military Commission can’t attack the capital or defeat the regular army, but they can go to each official’s residence to seize their families. That would be the most effective."

The Five City Military Commission was in charge of the capital’s security. They knew every street and alley, and which officials lived where, and how many family members each had.

As long as they controlled the families of the officials, it was like holding hostages.

Not to mention others, even if Yu Wan and the children were captured, Zhao Xuanyou would have to yield.

"What should we do?" Yu Wan was usually calm in the face of other matters, but when it came to the children, she couldn’t help but feel anxious.

Zhao Xuanyou advised, "If we didn’t know about this, we might have been caught off guard. Since we know, I will take precautions."

The Five City Military Commission didn’t have many people after all. If His Majesty were to suddenly pass away, Prince Ping would need to control the families of so many high-ranking officials in the capital in a short time. Even if a hundred people were assigned to the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, as long as they prepared in advance, it wouldn’t be much of a threat.

"How is His Majesty’s condition?" Yu Wan asked softly. "How much longer can he hold on?"

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyes flashed, and he didn’t speak. Suddenly, he got up from the couch.

Yu Wan was about to ask when she caught sight of Zhao Xuanyou lifting Zhao Mianze from behind the screen.

"Ah Chun, what were you doing hiding behind the screen?"

Zhao Mianze had originally thought that, being young and light-footed, his parents would be too busy talking to notice him. Who knew he would still be caught by his father.

Seeing that he was about to be lifted to the couch by his father, Zhao Mianze looked at Yu Wan pitifully. "Mother, the rain outside is too loud. I was a little scared, so I came over."

The rain outside was indeed very loud, but Zhao Xuanyou didn’t believe he was scared.

This kid had a look of being impervious to persuasion and was more composed than Zhao Yi Yun, who was five years older. How could he be afraid of the rain?

Yu Wan, however, took her son from Zhao Xuanyou’s hands.

"Mother, I want to sleep with you both."

Zhao Mianze, emboldened, grabbed Yu Wan’s arm and acted coy.

Before Zhao Xuanyou could speak, Yu Wan agreed.

Noticing Zhao Xuanyou’s dissatisfaction with her indulgence of their son, she had Zhao Mianze sleep on the innermost side, with her in the middle.

Zhao Xuanyou had no choice but to let her have her way.

The rain fell all night and only stopped the next morning.

After breakfast, Zhao Xuanyou left the house, and Yu Wan took the children to Leshou Hall to pay their respects to Old Master Ye.

When they returned to the Tangli Courtyard, Wen Ji and Lin Jing were already standing on the veranda.

After exchanging a glance with Wen Ji, Yu Wan knew they had obtained the architectural plans of the Prime Minister’s residence. She silently entered the house and waited until the maids had served tea before dismissing the attendants.

"The architectural plans of the Prime Minister’s residence are all here." After a pause, Wen Ji added, "We also took the architectural plans of Prince Ping’s residence."

"Very good. It’s better to be prepared."

However, there was no need to risk going to Prince Ping’s residence for now.

The Prime Minister’s residence was very large. After looking at the general layout, Yu Wan selected a few important places to examine.

The study was the most likely place to have secret rooms and hidden compartments, so it was naturally the place that needed to be thoroughly searched.

In addition, the main courtyard where Madam Xu lived, the library, and the warehouse also needed to be investigated.

Wen Ji circled the few places Yu Wan had pointed out on the general layout and quickly worked out an entry and exit route with Lin Jing. They could sneak into the Prime Minister’s residence that very night.

After they left, Yu Wan studied the general layout alone for a while, feeling that she had missed something.

She traced several routes on the map with her hand and suddenly discovered a problem.

The Lanfang Pavilion on the west side of the Prime Minister’s residence didn’t seem to have a clear purpose, and its location was quite remote. If entering from the main gate of the residence, there was only one path leading to it.

But the Lanfang Pavilion was actually very close to Prime Minister Xu’s study. If a back door was opened from the study, or a secret passage was built, it wouldn’t take much effort.

At this thought, Yu Wan’s heart began to race.

She quickly had Ran Dong invite Wen Ji over and told him her idea.

Wen Ji naturally agreed with her and decided to go with Lin Jing that night to investigate the Lanfang Pavilion directly.

As soon as it got dark, it started raining again outside.

With no children around to laugh and play, the only sound in the Tangli Courtyard was the rain.

Originally, Yu Wan had thought to talk to Zhao Xuanyou to ease her mind when he returned home, but Yuan Qing came to report that Zhao Xuanyou had urgent business outside the capital and wouldn’t return until the next day.

Outside the window, the rain beat against the banana leaves. Yu Wan had no romantic thoughts.

"Mother."

A clear child’s voice interrupted her tangled thoughts. Yu Wan turned her head and saw Zhao Mianze handing an oil-paper umbrella to Chun Xing with a smile.

"Ah Chun, why are you here? Have you had dinner?"

"I already ate with Grandmother and Ah Ning." Zhao Mianze entered the house and stuck close to Yu Wan. "I want to sleep with you tonight."

He had heard at Leshou Hall that his grandfather had told his great-grandmother that his father wouldn’t be home tonight. Thinking about his parents’ plans, he was a little worried, so he ran over by himself.

His mother wasn’t as experienced with court intrigues as his father. When she was uncertain, maybe he could help.

Yu Wan had no idea about her son’s thoughts. Seeing him acting coy, her heart naturally softened, and she quickly ordered the maids to bring hot water to soak their feet and drive away the cold.

Mother and son talked for a long time before Zhao Mianze went to sleep.

Yu Wan, however, couldn’t sleep at all.

She lit a candle and sat by the window. After sitting for more than an hour, her mind finally calmed down a bit, and she dozed off with her head resting on her hand.

At 5:30 AM, she suddenly awoke and opened her eyes to see Wen Ji standing beside her.

chapters.title: Facing the Storm
chapters.content:
"Ah Ji."

At the sight of Wen Ji returning safely, Yu Ying finally felt the taut string in her mind loosen greatly.

Without a single unnecessary word, Wen Ji directly said, "I found the item."

Yu Ying's heart pounded wildly, wanting to say something but feeling as if a fishbone was stuck in her throat. She simply reached out to Wen Ji.

Outside, the rain was heavy, and Wen Ji was drenched from head to toe.

He took out a bright yellow scroll from his bosom and handed it to Yu Ying without hesitation.

Yu Ying took the scroll but did not open it immediately.

"Was it found in the Lanfang Pavilion?"

"It seemed like a storage place for miscellaneous items, but Lin Jing found the entrance to a secret passage in the Lanfang Pavilion. After entering, we discovered it led to the study, but there were no hidden compartments there. Lin Jing guessed there might be more to the passage, so we went back, tapping the walls, and finally found where the imperial edict was kept."

Although Lin Jing's lightness skills were not as good as Wen Ji's, he was indeed more knowledgeable and quite skilled in mechanisms. Tonight's successful retrieval of the edict was largely his doing.

But Yu Ying had no time to be happy. She tightly clutched the edict and looked up at Wen Ji, "Did you open it and look?"

Wen Ji didn't understand Yu Ying's intention in asking this, but he truthfully replied, "Lin Jing and I both looked at it."

Yu Ying, hearing this, felt a surge of complex emotions. She realized she had asked a redundant question.

Lin Jing and Wen Ji had infiltrated the Prime Minister's residence at night precisely to retrieve the edict. Naturally, they would have opened it to confirm it was what they were looking for.

"It's good that you confirmed it."

After saying this, Yu Ying let out a long sigh. She lifted the lid of the incense burner in the room and threw the edict inside.

Fearful that the edict might not burn completely, she threw in two more fire starters.

Wen Ji looked at the burning edict in the incense burner in astonishment. "You're not going to look at it?"

Yu Ying curved her lips into a smile.

Wen Ji was the person she trusted most in this world. In terms of trust alone, he even surpassed Zhao Xuanyou.

Yu Ying only wanted to obtain the edict; she did not want to know who the emperor truly intended to pass the throne to.

"I don't want to look, and I don't want Zhao Xuanyou to see it either."

Wen Ji paused for a moment before quickly understanding Yu Ying's meaning. He watched as the edict burned to ashes in the incense burner and softly said, "This is for the best."

Yu Ying's eyes were slightly red, and her fingers trembled gently.

Originally, she and Zhao Xuanyou had agreed to retrieve the edict and then discuss their next steps. Burning it was her own idea.

Wen Ji didn't say much, but his words struck a chord with Yu Ying.

No matter what, he always stood by her side, supporting her.

"I will remind Lin Jing to act as if nothing happened."

"Mm," reassured by Wen Ji's words, Yu Ying quickly calmed down and softly said, "You must be tired tonight. Go back to your room and warm up."

"I'm fine," Wen Ji said, then quietly left the Tangli Courtyard.

Yu Ying sat by the window for a while, then got up and checked the incense burner, confirming that the edict had turned to ashes before returning to the bed.

She adjusted the blanket for Zhao Mianze, who was fast asleep, and then lay down herself.

In the darkness, Zhao Mianze opened his eyes.

Tonight, he had originally stayed in the Tangli Courtyard because he was worried about his mother. Unexpectedly, he witnessed the scene of his mother burning the edict.

From his mother's and uncle's conversation, it seemed they had burned the edict without his father's knowledge.

Zhao Mianze listened to his mother's even breathing, pursed his lips, and smiled. He had underestimated his mother.

Both his grandfather and father were loyal to the country and would never commit treason. If they had obtained the edict and knew who the emperor truly intended to pass the throne to, they would certainly hesitate.

By burning the edict, his mother ensured that no one had a way out. Neither the Marquis's residence nor Prime Minister Xu had any options.

Without the edict of succession, no matter which royal prince or grandson was nominated to the throne, it would not be considered treason.

This was a brilliant move.

A faint smile that didn't belong to his age appeared on Zhao Mianze's youthful face. But after a moment, he rested his head on his mother's shoulder and quickly fell asleep.

By dawn, the weather finally cleared.

Early in the morning, Zhao Mianze went to the garden and picked a few branches of newly bloomed crape myrtle, placing them in a porcelain vase with clear water on the table.

The refreshing summer sunlight streamed into the room, with water droplets still hanging on the petals and leaves, exuding a vibrant vitality.

Mother and son had their breakfast as usual in the veranda, and as usual, they went to the Leshou Hall to pay their respects to the old lady, as if nothing had happened.

A peaceful day passed. When Yu Ying went to bed at night, Zhao Xuanyou had not yet returned. It wasn't until she got up in the middle of the night to relieve herself that she saw a candlelight flickering on the screen.

It turned out to be Zhao Xuanyou's silhouette cast on the screen by the candlelight. She could clearly see him sitting upright in a chair.

There seemed to be other people in the room, whispering reports to Zhao Xuanyou. After a while, Zhao Xuanyou gave some instructions and dismissed them.

The shadow on the screen suddenly moved, and Yu Ying looked up to see Zhao Xuanyou walking around the inner room screen towards her.

"Did I wake you?"

Yu Ying was wearing a newly made mint-green Hangzhou silk nightgown, her long hair hanging down, looking as fresh and delicate as a newly sprouted willow.

Zhao Xuanyou stared for a moment, then quickly stepped forward and pulled her into his arms.

"You weren't home, and the space beside my pillow was empty. Of course, I couldn't sleep."

After having children, Yu Ying rarely showed her girly side, but with just this one sentence, Zhao Xuanyou was stirred with desire.

As they embraced and fell onto the bed, getting intimate, Yu Ying softly said, "Husband, I burned the edict."

Zhao Xuanyou's hand, which had been inside her nightgown, paused at her words. He looked at Yu Ying in astonishment.

He had supported Yu Ying in retrieving the edict.

After all, with the edict in his hands, the initiative would be in his control.

But as for how to use the edict, he hadn't figured that out yet. He would have to know first who the emperor intended to pass the throne to.

"You really burned it?"

"Mm, the ashes are still in the incense burner." Yu Ying said in a muffled voice.

She looked like a child who had done something wrong, twisting Zhao Xuanyou's clothes with her fingers, gazing at him pitifully, her eyes and brows full of tenderness.

Although Zhao Xuanyou was surprised, he quickly understood Yu Ying's intention.

By not letting him see the edict, she didn't want him to bear any psychological burden.

Zhao Xuanyou kissed her puffed cheek, his eyes growing darker.

In the embroidered canopy, fragrant and dense, she was more beautiful than the flowers.

He had always wanted to shield her from the wind and rain, not letting her suffer the slightest harm. But she was willing to stand side by side with him, facing the storm together.

"Yingying, with me, you don't need to go out of your way to consider these things. Don't you trust me?"

He didn't want her to worry about his stance or considerations. He would always stand by her side.

Sometimes, he even envied the trust Yu Ying had in Wen Ji.

"It's not that I'm going out of my way or that I don't trust you. I just don't want to know, and since we are husband and wife, you don't need to know either. This way, it's fair."

Of course, she trusted Zhao Xuanyou. She just didn't want to put him in a difficult position.

Zhao Xuanyou understood her good intentions and smiled slightly, pulling her even closer.

With the edict burned, he didn't need to consider any possibilities.

He didn't need to feel any guilt towards the emperor either. After all, he truly had never seen the edict.

As time approached the Grain in Ear season, the weather grew hotter day by day, and the atmosphere in and around the capital became oppressively stifling.

Just when everyone was struggling to breathe, the palace tolls rang the funeral bell.

---

chapters.title: Defying Heaven
chapters.content:
The tolling of the funeral bell in the palace carried many implications.

It confirmed the emperor's passing, announced it to the world, and also signified that someone in the palace had taken control of the situation, ensuring stability without chaos.

Since the emperor had not established a crown prince, and there was no empress or queen in the harem, the palace naturally respected Consort Li and Prince Ping as the highest authorities, with Prince Ping being the eldest among the imperial sons.

Thus, the palace was now under the control of Consort Li and Prince Ping.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying had long known about the emperor's failing health. Upon hearing of his passing, they were both shocked and grieved.
