But this was not the time for reminiscence. With the funeral bell tolling, all officials in the capital had to enter the palace immediately to mourn.

Zhao Xuanyou removed his official hat, changed into mourning clothes, and turned to look at Yu Ying, his heart filled with emotions.

After taking a deep breath, Zhao Xuanyou pulled her into his arms.

"Don't worry. Stay at home and don't receive any visitors. I've already made all the arrangements."

"You take care in the palace as well."

Zhao Xuanyou responded with an "mm" and kissed her forehead before quickly walking out.

As soon as he left, Yu Ying ordered the servants to remove all the festive decorations in the residence and hang up white banners and lanterns.

After everything was arranged, she had Ran Dong bring Zhao Yi Yun over.

When Zhao Yi Yun entered, there was a hint of unease in his eyes. Seeing Yu Ying in mourning clothes, his expression became even more anxious.

"Mother, what happened in the residence?"

Yu Ying pulled him to sit beside her and sighed softly.

No matter how reluctant she was, she had to tell the truth: "His Majesty has passed away."

Zhao Yi Yun's lips moved slightly, but no words came out. His eyes quickly reddened, and his expression turned sorrowful.

Yu Ying silently took out the mourning clothes and helped him put them on.

"Before Father and Mother returned to the capital, did you already suspect this?"

Zhao Yi Yun, though young, was far more mature than his peers. Over the years, he had been diligent in both his studies and martial arts.

He had originally been exiled to Yuzhou by the imperial family. This sudden return to the capital with his parents had filled him with questions.

At this point, Yu Ying saw no reason to hide the truth from him.

"We were ordered to bring you back to the capital by the palace."

"By the palace? Did Royal Grandfather want to see me?"

The emperor had once doted on this grandson so much; it was natural to assume he would want to see him before passing.

But now, Yu Ying had to tell him it wasn't out of familial affection.

"Consort Li and Prince Ping discovered your whereabouts and issued a false edict to have us bring you back to the capital."

"So I..."

Zhao Yi Yun started to speak but stopped mid-sentence.

He vividly remembered the events in the Hall of Mental Cultivation. His third uncle, Prince Ping, had been very cold to him and insisted on sending him to a monastery.

Now that Royal Grandfather had passed away, and his third uncle knew his whereabouts, and his parents had brought him back to the capital, he dared not think about what might happen next.

He closed his eyes briefly and looked up at Yu Ying.

"I've been very happy in Yuzhou these past five years. Mother, no matter what happens, I won't blame you."

"What are you thinking?" Yu Ying, hearing this, realized he had misunderstood. She quickly pulled him into her arms, feeling both heartache and amusement. "We didn't bring you back to the capital to hand you over."

Zhao Yi Yun asked in surprise, "If Father and Mother didn't want to hand me over to Third Uncle, why not leave me in Yuzhou?"

"That was considered, but your identity has already been exposed. Hiding in Yuzhou won't work forever. Your father and I don't want you to spend your life hiding and running."

"Does that mean our whole family will live in the capital from now on?"

Yu Ying smiled gently, "Hopefully."

"But can my identity allow me to stay in the capital long-term?"

"You are the legitimate eldest grandson of the late emperor. Staying in the capital is only natural. Who can compare to you?"

Although Prince Ping was the eldest son, Zhao Yi Yun, as a grandson, held the advantage of being legitimate, which was not insignificant in the succession.

"Mother," Zhao Yi Yun's eyebrows twitched, and his youthful face grew increasingly solemn.

He didn't quite understand Yu Ying's meaning, or rather, he found it hard to believe.

The title of the legitimate eldest grandson of the imperial family had long seemed distant to him. Now, hearing those words again, he was truly shocked.

After a long silence, he asked, "Can I still be called Zhao Yi Yun in the future?"

Yu Ying's eyes shimmered as she patted his shoulder reassuringly and softly said, "Man proposes, God disposes. Whether we succeed or not, I can't make any promises right now. But I will try my best, and your father will too. No matter what, we will protect you."

Hearing Yu Ying's words, Zhao Yi Yun's wildly beating heart gradually settled back into his chest.

After a moment of hesitation, Zhao Yi Yun said, "No matter what, Father and Mother will always be my family."

Yu Ying was slightly taken aback and looked at the young boy in front of her with renewed respect. With just a few words, he had understood the current situation and considered the future.

She and Zhao Xuanyou hadn't thought that far ahead. To protect themselves, they could only keep moving forward.

At this moment, in front of the palace gates, officials were arriving one after another. The crowd of courtiers was in mourning, and the sound of weeping filled the air.

Zhao Xuanyou walked through the crowd to the main gate, only to find the palace gates tightly closed, with heavy guards. Several Feathered Forest Guards stood at the gate with swords, not allowing the officials to enter.

He stood for a while, and soon both Prime Ministers arrived.

After some conversation, they learned that Prince Ping and Princess Yinning had stayed in the palace overnight to attend to the emperor in his final moments.

"Why aren't the other three princes here?" an official asked.

Normally, upon the emperor's passing, Princes Jing, Qing, and Rui should have been the first to arrive at the palace to mourn.

Prime Minister Xu also found it strange and used his authority as the leader of the officials to reprimand the commander of the Feathered Forest Guards. Prime Minister Sun, however, remained silent, maintaining a calm demeanor.

Zhao Xuanyou was not surprised.

Before the funeral bell announced the emperor's passing, Consort Li and Prince Ping had already taken action. At this moment, the three princes were likely confined to their residences.

After a long standoff, the palace gates finally opened. Chen Lin, the deputy director of the Hall of Mental Cultivation, came out and announced that by the order of Consort Li, the two Prime Ministers, the six department ministers, and several other high-ranking officials were invited into the palace to discuss the succession of the new emperor.

Prime Minister Xu frowned upon hearing this. Prime Minister Sun, however, feigned ignorance and said that since the late emperor had not established a crown prince, it should be Consort Li who convenes a grand court session for the officials to nominate the new emperor.

"In response to the Prime Ministers, last night, as His Majesty was on his deathbed, in the presence of Consort Li, Consort Xin, Prince Ping, and Princess Yinning, he left behind a will for the succession. Consort Li invites all the officials to enter the palace first, to read the will together and confirm the new emperor."

Although Chen Lin did not say who the new emperor was in the will, with only Prince Ping present in the palace, it was self-evident who the will named.

The officials were all astute individuals who had risen through the imperial examinations. They exchanged glances, understanding the implication.

"In that case, Prime Minister Xu, let us enter the palace immediately to verify the authenticity of the edict," Prime Minister Sun said leisurely.

Prime Minister Xu glanced at him, his expression extremely unpleasant.

However, having served for decades and having once participated in the struggle for the crown prince with the late emperor, he had experienced all kinds of storms. Naturally, he was not intimidated by the current situation and showed no fear.

Zhao Xuanyou, as the distinguished General, was naturally among those named by Chen Lin. Without a word, he followed Prime Minister Xu into the palace.

The master of ceremonies stepped forward and instructed the officials left outside the palace gate to line up according to their ranks and mourn.

Meanwhile, the palace gates closed tightly again after the group of high-ranking officials entered.

chapters.title: Mourning the Emperor
chapters.content:
Chen Lin led more than a dozen high-ranking officials directly to the Hall of Supreme Harmony. At this moment, the emperor’s coffin was placed in the center of the palace.

Most of the officials who came here were veteran ministers. The moment they saw the coffin, a few of them fainted from grief.

The emperor may not have matched the sage rulers of history in both literary and military achievements, but he was indeed a benevolent ruler. Whether it was his treatment of concubines, children, officials, or common people, he always governed with benevolence.

Zhao Xuanyou gazed at the coffin, his heart heavy.

He endured his sorrow and lifted his eyes to survey his surroundings.

Consort Li’s eyes were red and swollen, seemingly from excessive grief. Supported by two palace maids, she stood in the center of the hall, with seven or eight other concubines behind her, weeping with covered faces.

Prince Ping and his sister, Princess Yining, stood beside the coffin, their expressions also filled with sorrow. However, there was no sign of Eunuch Liu Quan in the hall.

Liu Quan had been extremely loyal to the late emperor. It was likely that he had already been detained by Consort Li and Prince Ping.

After the high-ranking officials one by one paid their respects before the coffin, Consort Li, suppressing her grief, recounted the scene from last night when the emperor left behind the decree to establish the heir.

It was customary for the emperor to summon several high-ranking officials as witnesses when issuing a final decree. However, the emperor’s illness had struck so suddenly last night that there was no time to summon the two prime ministers and the six ministers. Only Consort Li, Prince Ping, and a few concubines were present. When Consort Li inquired about the succession, the emperor, in a moment of clarity before death, personally declared that Prince Ping should inherit the throne. He ordered Princess Yining to record the decree, and after witnessing the affixing of the imperial seal, the emperor passed away.

"Eunuch Chen, show the late emperor’s final decree to the officials," Consort Li said, lowering her head to wipe her tears, overwhelmed with sorrow.

Chen Lin held the decree and walked to the front of the officials.

It was true that a dying person might experience a moment of clarity, so it was not unusual for the emperor to leave a verbal decree regarding the succession before his death.

This decree was transcribed by Princess Yining according to the emperor’s verbal order, so it was in Princess Yining’s handwriting, and the seal affixed was also genuine.

Moreover, the emperor currently had no legitimate eldest son, so it was reasonable and proper to establish the eldest son, Prince Ping, as the heir.

Thus, led by Prime Minister Sun, the high-ranking officials all confirmed that the decree was valid and stated that the most urgent task was to hold the enthronement ceremony as soon as possible.

Thinking that after so many years as a powerless prince he was finally about to become the Son of Heaven, Prince Ping’s eyes, which had been filled with grief, flickered with a trace of excitement.

He was about to speak when Xu Xiang, who had been silent all along, suddenly spoke up.

"Did His Majesty truly leave a verbal decree last night?"

Hearing Xu Xiang’s words, Consort Li and Prince Ping’s eyes both narrowed sharply, but they quickly regained their composure. They had already arranged everything, so even if Xu Xiang had some trump card, they were not afraid.

"Last night, it was I and Princess Yining who attended to His Majesty in his illness. When Father Emperor left the verbal decree, Mother Consort and the other concubines happened to be visiting the Hall of Supreme Harmony, so besides my sister and I, they all heard it as well."

These words seemed flawless, but in reality, they were full of loopholes.

After the emperor fell ill, the four princes and two princesses took turns attending to him. In the harem, only Consort Li, the highest-ranking, was allowed to visit daily.

Last night, when the emperor passed away, Prince Ping and Consort Li "coincidentally" were both in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, while the others present were low-ranking concubines. By reason, Consort Li would never have allowed them near the emperor unless she intended for them to serve as witnesses.

Zhao Xuanyou glanced at Princess Yining and saw that her eyes were filled with anxiety, yet she remained silent.

She did not seem to be Prince Ping’s accomplice, but rather someone coerced by him.

At this moment, Consort Li’s face showed no trace of sadness. Instead, it darkened as she angrily reprimanded, "Prime Minister Xu, do you mean to suggest that the decree is false?"

"Three months ago, His Majesty summoned me and another official to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, where he personally wrote a decree to establish the heir. The person designated was not Prince Ping, so I can confirm that this final decree is problematic."

Zhao Xuanyou’s eyebrows twitched slightly.

So, when the emperor left his final decree, besides Xu Xiang, there was another person present.

He was not surprised.

For the House of Jingyuan, the greatest threat was Prince Ping, who knew Zhao Yi’s identity. As long as Prince Ping failed, everything else could be resolved.

Prince Ping spoke slowly, "If that is the case, then please, Prime Minister Xu, present the handwritten decree left by Father Emperor so that everyone else can judge its authenticity."

As soon as he finished speaking, Consort Li said, "Prime Minister Xu is a senior and respected official. The decree he presents is likely genuine. However, as Prime Minister Xu himself said, that was three months ago. During the time His Majesty was gravely ill, the princes all attended to him at his bedside. Some were deeply filial, while others were perfunctory. His Majesty saw it all, so it is only natural that his intentions changed."

They had long heard that the emperor had left a decree to establish the heir, though they did not know to whom it was given. It must have been to a high-ranking official. For this reason, the mother and son had long prepared a countermeasure.

They did not deny the authenticity of the other decree, making their own seem reasonable.

With two decrees and two princes vying for the throne, Prince Ping, being the elder, naturally had the advantage.

Yet, for some reason, Zhao Xuanyou, observing the expressions of Prince Ping and his mother, felt that their schemes went beyond this.

Thinking of the three princes who had yet to enter the palace, Zhao Xuanyou had some speculations.

Prime Minister Sun had already sided with Prince Ping. At this moment, he also said in a deep voice, "Prime Minister Xu is highly respected. Her Highness the Consort and His Highness the Prince naturally trust him. However, words alone are not enough. Now that His Majesty has passed, the decree should be presented first to confirm its authenticity before discussing other matters."

Listening to their words, which seemed to place them on the same side, Zhao Xuanyou keenly perceived a subtle difference.

Prince Ping and his mother believed that Xu Xiang had the decree, but Prime Minister Sun’s tone suggested he knew Xu Xiang could not produce it.

This was not surprising.

Sun Tanran had once abandoned Pei Tao for her father. At this life-and-death juncture, even if she only wanted to save her own life, she could not completely disregard her father’s safety.

Xu Xiang, experienced and composed, showed no fear. He calmly said, "When the other three princes enter the palace, I will announce the decree."

All the civil and military officials had arrived at the palace gates to pay their respects, yet the three princes were still nowhere to be seen. This clearly indicated that Prince Ping had made a move.

Xu Xiang’s words struck directly at Prince Ping’s weakness.

Unexpectedly, Prince Ping’s expression did not change in the slightest. He said indifferently, "I wonder what my three brothers are doing. It’s been so long, and they still haven’t entered the palace."

Minister of Personnel Ho Min, a disciple of Xu Xiang, had been listening for a while. He understood that his mentor’s decree was definitely not naming Prince Ping as the heir. Hearing Prince Ping’s casual words, he could not help but say, "The princes’ residences are so close to the imperial palace. The civil and military officials have been here for so long, yet the three princes have not appeared. Were they ever summoned to enter the palace?"

"What do you mean by that, Minister Ho?" Consort Li coldly snorted. "The palace has already tolled the funeral bell. The entire city knows of His Majesty’s passing. How could they three not know?" She then ordered in a deep voice, "Eunuch Chen, send someone to the princes’ residences to urge them. If they still do not enter the palace, have the Brocade Guards arrest them for defying the imperial decree."

"Yes," Chen Lin responded respectfully.

While waiting for the three princes to enter the palace, the people remaining in the Hall of Supreme Harmony continued to kneel before the coffin, mourning.

Zhao Xuanyou was pondering the current situation when he noticed Xu Xiang making a gesture toward him.

chapters.title: To the Victor Go the Spoils
chapters.content:
Zhao Xuanyou subtly withdrew his gaze. After a long while, when he looked back, he saw that Xu Xiang had already left the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

He understood that Xu Xiang had something to say to him. Just as he was about to rise and go find him, an inner attendant approached and said that Prince Ping had something to discuss with him.

Zhao Xuanyou slightly raised an eyebrow. With both sides trying to win him over, he could only wait and see how things developed.

He followed the inner attendant to a side hall, where Prince Ping was sitting and drinking tea.

"Have some tea to moisten your throat."

After entering the palace early in the morning to mourn, and going through such a long ordeal, Zhao Xuanyou’s throat was indeed parched. He did not decline and drank two cups of tea as suggested.

Prince Ping looked at Zhao Xuanyou and said softly, "Over the years, you have been in Yu Prefecture, so we have indeed grown distant. But we have known each other since we were children, Xuanyou. You should stand by my side."

"Your Highness is the emperor’s eldest son and has the decree to establish the heir," Zhao Xuanyou knew the other party wanted to hear him pledge his loyalty. At this moment, Prince Ping held the advantage in the palace. Saying a few words of submission would not be difficult for Zhao Xuanyou, but given their long-standing acquaintance, he still spoke a few words from his heart. "As long as it is legitimate, the civil and military officials will naturally support it."

All the officials had arrived at the palace gates, yet the three princes were missing. How could Zhao Xuanyou believe that this was not the doing of Consort Li and Prince Ping?

Prince Ping was not wrong to want to be emperor, but he had used the wrong methods. No one could help him.

These last two sentences both expressed Zhao Xuanyou’s stance and served as a warning to Prince Ping to stop and turn back from the brink.

Prince Ping naturally understood Zhao Xuanyou’s meaning. He withdrew the smile from his face, and his eyes grew cold. "You have heard it. Prime Minister Xu has another decree in his possession. His is handwritten by Father Emperor, while mine was transcribed by my royal sister. Naturally, others will believe his more."

"If that is truly the case, then the civil and military officials must be gathered to discuss it together. It is not something I can interfere with."

At this point, Prince Ping understood Zhao Xuanyou’s meaning. There was no need to maintain a friendly demeanor. He coldly said, "Zhao Xuanyou, how many times has this prince helped you in the past? Now that I need your assistance, you act as if you owe me nothing."

Zhao Xuanyou was not intimidated by him and remained composed. "Your Highness has indeed helped me many times. As the saying goes, ‘one good turn deserves another.’ I will certainly repay the debts I owe."

He would repay favors in kind. It was not as if he would risk his life and the House of Jingyuan just because of a few small favors.

Not to mention that Prince Ping had threatened him with Zhao Yi’s identity, even without that, Zhao Xuanyou would never risk the House of Jingyuan to follow Prince Ping in rebellion.

Prince Ping gave a sinister smile but said nothing. He waved his hand, dismissing Zhao Xuanyou.

He was only one step away from the throne. If anyone else dared to defy him at this moment, he would have them arrested. For example, that unwise Liu Quan.

But Zhao Xuanyou was different.

He was highly skilled in martial arts. The few guards in the side hall could not restrain him. Who knew, he might even turn against Prince Ping.

In any case, Prince Ping was confident of victory. Once he ascended the throne, there would be plenty of opportunities to deal with Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou left the side hall and returned to the coffin. Xu Xiang had already knelt back down.

Xu Xiang also wanted to confirm Zhao Xuanyou’s stance. However, the area was filled with Prince Ping’s people. Earlier, Xu Xiang had excused himself to go out for a moment, but there had always been inner attendants guarding him, making it impossible to speak with any familiar officials.

Seeing Zhao Xuanyou being called away by Prince Ping, Xu Xiang was anxious.

However, seeing Zhao Xuanyou return with Prince Ping looking gloomy behind him, Xu Xiang felt slightly reassured.

Not long after, Princess Yining, overwhelmed by grief, was supported away by palace attendants to rest. Soon after she left, a mournful voice suddenly rang out from outside the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

"Father Emperor!"

Everyone turned their heads and saw Prince Qing Zhao Yu, his eyes red, running into the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

His grief was understandable, but strangely, the distances from the Prince Qing’s, Prince Jing’s, and Prince Rui’s residences to the imperial palace were all similar. There was no reason for Prince Qing to appear while Princes Jing and Rui were still missing.

As Prince Qing was mourning, Chen Lin approached Consort Li and reported, his face showing a trace of grief.

"Consort Li, upon hearing of His Majesty’s passing, Prince Jing was so overwhelmed with grief that he took his own life with a sword to follow His Majesty."

"What?! How could this be?" Consort Li exclaimed in shock, as if she was too stunned to speak.

Her shock was feigned, but the shock of the others present was genuine.

No matter how grieved one was, how could a prince in his twenties with a wife and children take his own life to follow the late emperor?

Prince Qing also froze in place upon hearing this news.

Xu Xiang, who had been restraining himself, finally could not hold back. He stood up and pointed at Prince Ping, denouncing him, "Did Prince Jing fall victim to your poisonous hand?"

Prince Ping, instead of getting angry at being accused so directly, smiled coldly, a sinister expression on his face.

With Xu Xiang’s years of political cunning, it was unlikely that he would fly into a rage over this news. At most, he would be as stunned as everyone else in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

The only possibility was that the late emperor’s decree to establish the heir named the fifth prince.

It seemed he had been right to send someone to kill the fifth prince first.

"Preposterous!" Consort Li, hearing Xu Xiang’s accusation, immediately stopped her mourning and angrily reprimanded, "Xu Mian, how can you slander us so? Prince Ping entered the palace to attend to His Majesty before his passing and never left the Hall of Supreme Harmony. If you accuse him of harming others, you must present evidence."

Prime Minister Sun chimed in, "Instead of arguing about this, Prime Minister Xu, why don’t you present the decree to establish the heir? Once the new emperor is confirmed, all matters can be left to the new emperor to decide. We need not engage in this verbal dispute."

"Hmph," Xu Xiang did not respond to him. Instead, he turned to Prince Qing, "Your Highness, after hearing the funeral bell toll in the palace today, why did you not enter the palace immediately?"

Prince Qing was still in shock over his fifth brother’s suicide. Hearing Xu Xiang’s words, he came back to his senses slightly and instinctively looked at Prince Ping.

Prince Ping did not even glance at him, clearly not taking him seriously.

Prince Qing was an incompetent and idle noble, but he understood the concept of mutual dependence. Less than a day after Father Emperor’s passing, with his body not yet cold, Prince Ping had already killed a brother. Once Prince Ping ascended the throne, how long could he and Zhao Qi expect to live?

"After hearing the funeral bell toll in the palace, I intended to enter immediately. However, my residence was surrounded by the soldiers of the Five City Patrol. They said there was an imperial decree ordering me to stay in my residence. It was not until half an hour ago that someone from the palace came, and I was able to leave my residence."

Prince Qing’s words made everything clear to those present.

Prince Ping had long since ordered the Five City Patrol to surround the three princes’ residences. Therefore, the deceased Prince Jing could not possibly have taken his own life out of grief.

"Prince Ping, you have ruthlessly killed your own brothers and forged a decree to seize the throne. In the end, it will all be in vain," Xu Xiang declared.

"Hmph, what forged decree? I only know that to the victor belong the spoils. As long as I ascend the throne, the traitors will naturally be you," Prince Ping firmly believed that history was written by the victors and would not listen to Xu Xiang’s words.

It was not surprising that Xu Xiang opposed him, but even the usually incompetent Prince Qing dared to stand against him. This truly surprised Prince Ping.

He had allowed Prince Qing to enter the palace, originally intending to first intimidate his most incompetent brother. Who would have thought that even Prince Qing would defy him? It seemed he had been too lenient, allowing them to become so bold.

"Seize Zhao Yu and Xu Mian!"

Before the guards in the Hall of Supreme Harmony could move, shadows flickered within the hall. In the next moment, Prince Qing and Xu Xiang

chapters.title: Divide and Conquer
chapters.content:
"Zhao Xuanyou! How dare you!" Prince Ping looked at the three people standing outside the Qianqing Palace, and his pupils suddenly twitched. "Guards! Seize all three of them!"

Before Prime Minister Xu could steady himself, he furiously rebuked, "Zhao Huan, you have forged the imperial decree to usurp the throne and slaughtered your brothers. Your conspiracy will never succeed!"

"Seize them at once!" Prince Ping's face darkened upon hearing Prime Minister Xu's shout.

As the guards of the Qianqing Palace approached with their swords drawn, Zhao Xuanyou showed no fear. He took a few steps back with Prince Qing and Prime Minister Xu.

Prince Qing couldn't help but feel his legs weaken at the sight.

He nervously looked at Zhao Xuanyou and whispered, "You should be able to defeat these people, right?"

Zhao Xuanyou didn't respond. Just then, Pan Xun, leading more than a dozen Brocade Guards, rushed forward and drew their swords to confront the guards.

When the late emperor was seriously ill, Prime Minister Xu, to prevent Concubine Li from doing as she pleased in the palace, proposed under the pretext of strengthening the guards that the Brocade Guards enter the palace to assist the Feathered Forest Guards in patrolling. Thus, Pan Xun and his men had been stationed in the palace for some days.

Before entering the palace, Zhao Xuanyou had sent a message to Pan Xun.

Pan Xun was someone Zhao Xuanyou had personally promoted, and their relationship was deep. Although Zhao Xuanyou had not explicitly told Pan Xun about Zhao Yi Yun's matter, Pan Xun was naturally willing to stand on his side when he spoke up.

Moreover, Prince Ping had forged the imperial decree to usurp the throne and harmed his brothers, committing a heinous crime that no subject could tolerate.

As the two sides confronted each other, Prime Minister Xu continued to shout at the palace guards, "Zhao Huan has forged the imperial decree to usurp the throne and intends to rebel. If you follow him in resistance, you will be executed without pardon!"

Many Feathered Forest Guards showed doubt upon hearing this.

Seeing this, Prince Qing couldn't help but join in, shouting, "Prince Ping is a traitor! Following him will only lead to your death!"

After the late emperor's passing, the harem was led by Concubine Li. Prince Ping presented the imperial decree for establishing the heir, and the Feathered Forest Guards naturally followed his orders.

Now, hearing what Prime Minister Xu and Prince Qing said, the guards hesitated.

After all, they were all loyal to the late emperor and had not been bribed by Prince Ping. No one wanted to be a traitor.

Prime Minister Xu had high prestige. Seeing him confront Prince Ping like this, several court officials who had previously remained silent in the Qianqing Palace stepped forward to support him, saying that Prince Ping's decree was suspicious. Although they were immediately gagged and seized by the eunuchs beside them, the situation had clearly changed.

Seeing that the palace guards had not immediately taken action, Zhao Xuanyou gave Pan Xun a signal. The Brocade Guards immediately took Prime Minister Xu and Prince Qing away to hide.

"With the imperial decree for establishing the heir in my possession, Zhao Yu, Xu Ming, and Zhao Xuanyou are the real traitors. Kill them immediately!" Prince Ping had not expected Prime Minister Xu to stir the hearts of the people with just a few words without even presenting the decree, and his heart was filled with murderous intent.

After the emperor's passing last night, the commander of the Feathered Forest Guards had decided to swear allegiance to Prince Ping. He arrived promptly and ordered his subordinates to chase Zhao Xuanyou and his group.

Fortunately, the Brocade Guards left in the palace were all top experts. Soon, they retreated to the Duixiu Mountain in the Imperial Garden.

This was the highest point in the Imperial Garden, with only two narrow paths leading up, making it easy to defend and hard to attack.

Pan Xun divided his men into two groups, each guarding one of the paths. The Feathered Forest Guards could only surround the mountain and shoot arrows randomly upwards.

Duixiu Mountain was lush with flowers and trees, and there were several artificial rockeries. Zhao Xuanyou took Prime Minister Xu and Prince Qing to hide in a cave within one of the rockeries to avoid the stray arrows.

"Do you have any other plans?" Prince Qing, who had previously been emboldened by the pain of losing his father and brother in the Qianqing Palace, now felt a wave of fear as he listened to the whistling arrows outside. He said with a bitter face, "We can hide here for a while, but not forever. We'll all be caught soon."

Pan Xun saw that neither Prime Minister Xu nor Zhao Xuanyou wanted to pay attention to Prince Qing. He advised, "Your Highness, please be patient. I have prepared some water and dry rations. There won't be any problems for a while."

"You prepared this earlier?" Prince Qing asked in surprise.

"Prepared today."

Prince Qing, having made a fool of himself, looked at Prime Minister Xu again. "Did Father really leave an imperial decree for establishing the heir? Wasn't it for Third Brother? Why didn't you bring it out earlier? Why wait until Third Brother caused such a big commotion?"

"The decree is of course real, and it was not for Prince Ping."

Prime Minister Xu sighed deeply. How he wished the late emperor had established the heir earlier to ensure a smooth transition of power.

However, the treasonous plot by the deposed empress, Jiang, and the deposed crown prince, Zhao Zun, years ago had greatly intensified the late emperor's suspicions.

He no longer trusted his pillow partner, nor his own flesh and blood. He felt that everyone around him wanted to harm him.

Not long after his condition improved, the late emperor sent all his sons to their fiefs, not keeping a single one in the capital.

Over the years, the emperor's health had been poor, and the court officials repeatedly petitioned for the establishment of the heir, but the emperor ignored them all.

It wasn't until three months ago, when the late emperor sensed his end was near, that he hastily left a decree. However, he still instructed Prime Minister Xu that the decree must not be read until after the emperor's passing.

He was still worried that announcing it early would lead the heir to harm him to ascend the throne sooner.

"Who did Father want to pass the throne to?" Prince Qing asked urgently.

He knew he was not a strong candidate, and his father would not pass the throne to him. But now that his third brother had rebelled and his fifth brother was dead, only he and Zhao Qi remained. Suddenly, the possibility of him becoming emperor had greatly increased.

Prime Minister Xu did not look at him; he only looked at Zhao Xuanyou.

"The person His Majesty wanted to pass the throne to was Prince Jing. But it seems that Prince Jing has already fallen victim to Prince Ping's schemes. I'm afraid he is in great danger."

Zhao Xuanyou said, "Regardless, Prince Ping's rebellion is a fact. Once the chaos in the palace is settled, we will gather the civil and military officials to elect a new emperor."

Prince Qing's heart beat even more violently. Since his father was not passing the throne to Zhao Qi, the decree for establishing the heir was now useless. When the court elected a new emperor, it would naturally follow the order of the imperial sons, which would be his turn.

Truly, just when he thought all was lost, a new path appeared.

A huge opportunity had fallen into his lap...

Prince Qing immediately echoed, "That's right. The top priority is to quell Zhao Huan's rebellion. Do you have any strategies?"

Strategies? Zhao Xuanyou certainly had some.

Prince Ping had currently won over the Feathered Forest Guards and the Five City Cavalry, controlling the imperial palace. But these forces were far from enough to control the entire capital.

From the beginning, Prince Ping had confined the three princes in their residences and allowed high-ranking officials into the palace. He wanted the civil and military officials to quickly confirm the authenticity of his decree and smoothly become emperor.

In addition, Prince Ping had concentrated his elite forces to attack Prince Jing.

These two moves were well-played, but there was a fatal weakness: he could not delay. Once the decree was not recognized, his conspiracy would be exposed.

"We need to rescue Princess Yineng and have her reveal the truth in front of the civil and military officials," Zhao Xuanyou said.

Princess Yineng was the key witness to Prince Ping's forged decree. As long as she confirmed that she was coerced by Prince Ping, all his lies would crumble.

He could easily guess why Princess Yineng had written a fake decree and given false testimony for Prince Ping. Prince Ping must have captured her mother and forced her to obey.

Prime Minister Xu nodded in agreement and then said to Zhao Xuanyou, "There is a secret decree written by the late emperor hidden above the beam in my study. It states that if the heir is not Prince Jing, the commanders of the three major camps in the capital region must follow orders to enter the capital and quell the rebellion immediately."

No wonder Prime Minister Xu had the confidence to confront Prince Ping directly. It turned out the late emperor had left him a backup plan.

Zhao Xuanyou nodded and ordered Pan Xun to immediately find Princess Yineng, while he himself would leave the palace to retrieve the secret decree mentioned by Prime Minister Xu.

However, as Zhao Xuanyou left the palace, a group of people was also dispatched from the palace. They joined forces with the Five City Cavalry outside the palace and went to the residences of Prince Qing, the Prime Minister, and the Marquis of Jingyuan to capture their families.

---

chapters.title: Addressing the Rear
chapters.content:
"Madam, people from the palace have arrived."

Yu Wan was in the room accompanying her daughter in painting when Qiuyue rushed in from outside, looking somewhat flustered.

"How many people have come?" Yu Wan had already mentally prepared herself and asked without looking up.

After Zhao Xuanyou left the residence, he ordered Yuan Zhen and Yuan Qing to close the gates tightly, not to open them for anyone.

Qiuyue, seeing Yu Wan's calm expression, also calmed down slightly. "A eunuch delivering an imperial decree and more than a dozen guards have come. The cavalry has also sent a team, probably about a hundred people. The main and side gates of the marquis's residence are now surrounded by them."

"You take all the maids in the courtyard to Leshou Hall. Old Madam has prepared melon seeds and tea. Today, everyone is excused from their duties. They can eat, drink, or even play dice and cards, but gambling is not allowed."

Yu Wan had already thought of a plan. The servants would surely be in a panic, so gathering all the maids and servants in Leshou Hall to make some noise would prevent their hearts from being in turmoil.

As for the servants and pages in the front courtyard, Zhao Xuanyou had long since sent most of them to the Mist Garden outside the city, replacing them with his trusted guards. These guards were now protecting the main and side gates of the marquis's residence.

After all the maids and servants had gone to Leshou Hall, Yu Wan called her three children over. Together, they packed some food and toys and headed towards Honghui Hall.

After confirming that there was no one around, Yu Wan led the three children into the dungeon.

This was the only secret room in the marquis's residence and the most hidden.

A few days ago, Zhao Xuanyou had ordered people to arrange it. Thick soft mats were laid out, and two noble consorts' couches were placed inside. With the candles lit, it didn't feel dark or terrifying.

As they entered the dungeon, both Yu Wan and Wen Ji recalled some past events. The last time they were together in a dungeon, it was truly a time of crisis and tension.

At that time, they were desperately trying to save themselves, and neither of them could have imagined that they would reach this day.

However, this was not the time for nostalgia. After exchanging a smile, their expressions became solemn.

"What a secret place this is in our residence!"

Little A'ning, oblivious to the changing political landscape in the capital and unaware of the soldiers surrounding the residence, found the dungeon novel and fun.

Like a happy sparrow, she ran around inside and outside, then had an idea. She dragged the soft mat from the outside into the cell and arranged the toys she had brought one by one on the mat.

Zhao Mian, on the other hand, understood that they were experiencing a change in imperial power and remained completely calm.

He could see the slight anxiety in his mother's eyes, but at his age, it would be unnatural to speak up and comfort her. He simply followed A'ning into the cell to play.

"Mother, how long do we have to hide here?" Zhao Yi Yun stood beside Yu Wan and asked worriedly.

Yu Wan rubbed his head and softly said, "Not too long. Your father said the capital will be in chaos for at most two days."

After the emperor fell ill, his suspicions grew, and imperial power became even more centralized. Prince Ping was able to win over the Five City Cavalry, but that was all. These forces were far from enough to control the entire capital.

At this moment, the soldiers surrounding the marquis's residence suggested that Zhao Xuanyou had already confronted Prince Ping in the palace. Prince Ping wanted to capture their family to control Zhao Xuanyou.

"I and your uncle cannot stay here with you forever. You are the eldest brother; you must take care of your younger siblings."

"Mm." Zhao Yi Yun nodded understandingly, then asked, "Are you going to find Father?"

"I won't leave the residence either. The servants are in a panic right now, and I need to go out to calm them down." Zhao Yi Yun was already sensible, so Yu Wan did not hide the truth from him and explained her plan.

The guards at the gate were all elite, and Yu Wan believed they could not be breached by force. However, there were still many maids and servants in the residence.

If Yu Wan hid with the children, these servants would surely panic, and chaos could lead to unforeseen events. Yu Wan needed to appear and reassure everyone.

Zhao Yi Yun understood and grabbed Yu Wan's hand. "Mother, you must be careful."

"Just take care of yourselves." Yu Wan said, then entered the cell to kiss her son and daughter before leaving with Wen Ji.

She left Lin Geng to look after the three children and went to Leshou Hall with Wen Ji.

However, halfway there, Yu Wan suddenly stopped, as if she had thought of something.

"Ah Ji, go to the Liang residence."

"Go to the Liang residence?"

"The palace must have already broken ties. Compared to our family, the three princes pose a greater threat to Prince Ping. He will definitely take action against them. Their residences must also be surrounded. The Liang residence might be affected. Go and check on them."

The guards at the princes' residences were more numerous than at the marquis's residence. Especially Prince Rui, Zhao Qi, had formidable subordinates like Bingyun by his side. It was unlikely they would have any problems in a short time.

Liang Chengxiang must have entered the palace as soon as the funeral bell rang. At this moment, only the women and a few guards were left at home, which might be dangerous.

Wen Ji understood Yu Wan's meaning, but Lin Geng was watching the children, and Zhao Xuanyou was not at the residence...

"The marquis's residence is well-prepared. Those hundred people cannot break in. Go to the Liang residence quickly."

Wife and children were Zhao Xuanyou's weaknesses.

In addition to arranging enough people, he had also managed to bring four heavy crossbows into the capital. At this moment, there were two crossbowmen at the main gate and two at the side gate of the marquis's residence.

Heavy crossbows were strictly controlled weapons by the court. Although the Ming Ji Guard had them, they could not be used privately.

These few heavy crossbows were privately made by the deposed empress, Jiang, for her treasonous plot years ago.

Zhao Xuanyou had sent people to find where she hid the weapons. They had not touched the other swords, only disassembled the heavy crossbows and transported them into the capital separately before reassembling them in the marquis's residence.

Yu Wan had not gone to the gate to inquire, but she assumed that those who had forced their way in had already been killed.

After thinking for a moment, Yu Wan added, "If the Liang residence is safe for now, don't let them stay there. Take them to the Mist Garden to stay for a few days. The supplies there are still complete."

The jewelry and cosmetics shops in the capital were doing well. Two years ago, Chen Da Niu and his wife had purchased a residence and moved out with their children.

The Mist Garden had been empty, with only a few servants maintaining it daily.

In these turbulent times, it would be more appropriate for the Liang family to move to the Mist Garden to avoid trouble. Wen Ji did not hesitate any longer and left the residence to go to the Liang family.

Yu Wan entered Leshou Hall. The courtyard already had seven or eight octagonal tables set up. The maids and servants were all sitting together, but each one looked uneasy, with no mind to eat, drink, or play.

As soon as they saw Yu Wan enter, everyone's eyes turned to her.

Could it be that the soldiers surrounding the residence were here to search the house and punish them?

Yu Wan looked around and smiled. "It's rare for you to have a day off. Why are you all looking so gloomy?"

The maids tried to force a smile, but none could manage it.

Yu Wan became serious. "I suppose you all know that the late emperor has passed away. Now, someone has forged the imperial decree to usurp the throne. The people surrounding the marquis's residence are all rebel soldiers."

"Rebel soldiers?"

"The matters of the court will be handled by the civil and military officials. It will be settled in a few days. There's no need to panic. If anything happens, the marquis and I will take responsibility."

As soon as she finished speaking, Old Madam Ye, leaning on her cane, walked out of the house.

She was advanced in years, and although she had no serious illnesses, she had aged considerably and was not as strong as before.

"The Marquis of Jingyuan has been loyal for generations. No matter how chaotic it is outside, the chaos will not reach inside the marquis's residence."

With the two mistresses of the residence coming forward, the servants finally felt a bit more at ease.

Yu Wan supported Old Madam Ye back into the house. Old Madam Ye asked with concern, "Where are Ah Chun and Ah Ning?"

"They are in the dungeon."

"That place is dark and dirty. It's a hardship for them."

"Grandmother, rest assured. They find it novel and are playing happily inside."

Yu Wan was confident that no one could break into the marquis's residence. But to be safe against any unforeseen circumstances, if someone did break in, they certainly wouldn't be able to catch the children.

"The kitchen staff also cannot rest today. Remember to reward them generously once this is over."

"Grandmother, rest assured. I've already had Pan Xia reward them once."

Not only the kitchen staff but also the guards in the front courtyard deserved rewards. However, that was a matter for later.

Old Madam Ye nodded in satisfaction. Her gaze wandered for a moment before she sighed, "I hope the chaos in the capital will be settled as soon as possible."

The news of Prince Ping forging the imperial decree to usurp the throne had already quietly spread throughout the capital. Prince Ping, with nothing to lose, had the cavalry arrest the families of the more than a dozen officials who had entered the palace. At this moment, the capital was indeed in chaos.

But that was beyond Yu Wan's control. She took a deep breath to calm herself and sipped some hot tea.

chapters.title: Quelling the Rebellion
chapters.content:
In the Qianqing Palace, Prince Ping glared furiously at the guard before him.

"How could you fail to take down a marquis' mansion with so many men?"

The guard hung his head. "The Jingyuan Marquis' mansion was well-prepared. They even had heavy crossbows guarding the gate. We lost more than twenty men before we could even get close."

Heavy crossbows at the marquis' mansion?

Prince Ping clenched his fists, momentarily too angry to speak.

He had always considered his three younger brothers as his greatest threats, but he had overlooked Zhao Xuanyou.

From the moment the late emperor entrusted Yi Yun to Zhao Xuanyou, Zhao Xuanyou must have begun his preparations.

Before he could think further, a eunuch rushed in, his face panicked. "Your Highness, something bad has happened..."

The eunuch had caught Prince Ping at a bad moment. Hearing the inauspicious words, Prince Ping immediately kicked him. "Speak properly."

"Your Highness," the eunuch endured the pain in his chest and knelt up, "Princess Yinning has been taken away by the Brocade Guards."

"Taken away?" Prince Ping was stunned. He grabbed the eunuch's collar and lifted him up. "Didn't I order you to send more people to watch her?"

After a pause, Prince Ping suddenly remembered something. "What about her mother?"

The eunuch, nearly suffocated by his grip, managed to say, "She was taken away too."

Princess Yinning was the most crucial piece in his path to usurp the throne. She had written a false imperial decree for him and testified that the late emperor had passed the throne to him on his deathbed. But now that this piece was taken, it would surely become a sharp dagger aimed at him.

The commander of the Feathered Forest Guard hurried into the Qianqing Palace, his face grave. "Your Highness, the guards at the Shenwu Gate have rebelled. They opened the palace gates, and the Brocade Guards have taken Prince Qing, Princess Yinning, and Chancellor Xu out of the palace. They..."

"What do they want to do?"

"They want to slander Your Highness in front of the civil and military officials."

In fact, the guards at the Shenwu Gate had opened the gates after hearing Princess Yinning accuse Prince Ping of forging the imperial decree to usurp the throne, and then followed them out.

After all, there were so many guards in the palace. Many were loyal to the court and did not want to become rebels for no reason.

"Send people to the palace gate immediately! Kill them before Princess Yinning and Xu Ming speak! Especially Yinning, she must die!"

Prince Ping forced himself to calm down and quickly made a decision.

The only person who could prove he had forged the decree was Yinning. As long as Yinning was dead, he still had room to argue with the false decree.

Looking at his anxious subordinates in the Qianqing Palace, Prince Ping spoke with authority. "Everyone, do not panic. Prince Jing is already dead. The decree in Xu Ming's hands is now worthless. As long as Yinning keeps silent, the one who ascends the throne will still be me."

His words made sense. The originally disheartened subordinates regained their spirits and immediately arranged for the assassination of Yinning.

However, Prince Ping still underestimated the situation.

Zhao Xuanyou took the secret letter from the Chancellor's residence and immediately went to the three major camps around the capital to summon them. He galloped through the three camps and finally finished before nightfall.

After the three commanders learned of Prince Jing's death and Prince Ping's rebellion, they carefully verified the secret decree and immediately led their troops to the capital to suppress the rebellion.

The three major camps were responsible for defending the capital's safety and were not far from the city. They marched through the night and arrived at the capital before the city gates opened the next morning.

The defending general saw the dust flying outside the city and was momentarily flustered. He did not dare to open the city gates on time. Seeing this, Zhao Xuanyou rode alone to the city gate.

The three major camps had come to quell the rebellion, not to attack the city. They couldn't force their way in, so they had to wait outside the city for Zhao Xuanyou to negotiate.

At this moment, Chancellor Xu arrived with Prince Qing and Princess Yinning, and together with Zhao Xuanyou, they persuaded the defending general to open the city gates.

Chancellor Xu, knowing that the three major camps would come, deliberately had the Brocade Guards spread the word in the palace that he and Princess Yinning were going to the palace gate to accuse Prince Ping to the civil and military officials. In reality, under the protection of the Brocade Guards, they hid in the city, waiting for Zhao Xuanyou to lead the army back to the capital to meet them.

The capital had fallen into chaos because the Military Police Office had been arresting officials and their families everywhere since the day before. Many thugs took advantage of the chaos to loot, kill, and set fires, causing widespread disorder.

Many noble families suffered losses, and both the nobles and commoners had encountered difficulties.

Zhao Xuanyou commanded the soldiers from the three major camps to split up and rush to the various alleys of the capital to restore order.

The soldiers of the Military Police Office had rarely left the capital. They were good at catching thieves and investigating cases but were far inferior to the mighty army of the three major camps in actual combat.

However, Zhao Xuanyou did not order his soldiers to treat the Military Police Office as rebels to be eliminated. Instead, he shouted slogans, pointing out Prince Ping's rebellion and promising amnesty to those who immediately surrendered their weapons.

The ordinary soldiers of the Military Police Office had no idea why they were arresting the families of the officials. They only knew they were following orders. Now, hearing that they had participated in a rebellion, they were immediately frightened.

Rebellion was not just a matter of losing one's head; it was a crime punishable by the extermination of nine generations.

Thus, without much effort, most of the soldiers surrendered. The remaining few who resisted stubbornly were shown no mercy and were all killed.

By nightfall, Zhao Xuanyou had completely controlled the chaos in the city. He divided half of his troops to maintain order in the capital, while he led the main force to surround the imperial palace.

He did not order an attack on the imperial palace. After all, their purpose was to quell the rebellion, not to create chaos.

Moreover, apart from Consort Li and Prince Ping, there were thousands of eunuchs, palace maids, and guards in the imperial palace who were mostly innocent people coerced by Prince Ping. They could not all be killed indiscriminately.

Chancellor Xu greatly approved of this approach. It could both protect the palace buildings and reduce casualties. By surrounding but not attacking, the people inside the palace could not hold out for long.

The news of Prince Ping's rebellion spread throughout the palace, and now the palace was in a state of panic.

The palace's daily supply of fruits, meats, and vegetables were all fresh goods transported from outside the city. The inner court did not have much food stored, and with so many people in the palace, they could not last long. At most, they could hold out for ten days.

Zhao Xuanyou ordered the soldiers to shout surrender slogans outside the palace walls every day, neither attacking nor investigating.

After two days of chaos, both the nobles and commoners in the capital were still in shock and needed to stabilize their morale.

He and Chancellor Xu gathered the officials in the city, found a place as a temporary government office, and summoned the city's officials to sort out the matter of Prince Ping's usurpation.

On the night of the late emperor's passing, Prince Ping and Princess Yinning were attending to the emperor in the Qianqing Palace.

After confirming the emperor's death, Prince Ping immediately sealed off the news. On one hand, he falsely claimed the emperor's command to have the Military Police Office surround the three princes' mansions. On the other hand, he threatened Princess Yinning's mother's life, forcing Princess Yinning to write a false decree of abdication and then affix the imperial seal.

After doing all this, the next morning, the palace tolls rang for the emperor's death.

The guards of the three princes' mansions were originally enough to resist the Military Police Office. However, Prince Ping had planted an accomplice in Prince Jing's mansion, who struck down Prince Jing.

Apart from the rebellious Prince Ping, the late emperor had two remaining sons, Prince Qing and Prince Rui... But the most urgent task was still to capture Prince Ping, quell the rebellion, and the new emperor could be discussed later.

Chancellor Xu and Zhao Xuanyou divided their forces. Zhao Xuanyou was responsible for eliminating Prince Ping's remaining followers in the capital, rectifying the Military Police Office and the Capital Guards. Chancellor Xu led the officials to restore the operations of the various government departments.

On the seventh day, as the capital gradually restored order, news finally came from the imperial palace. Hundreds of guards and palace servants had rebelled against Prince Ping and opened the palace

---

chapters.title: The New Emperor
chapters.content:
When Zhao Xuanyou led his troops into the Qianqing Palace, the hall was empty.

But with a slight lift of his eyes, he saw a person sitting on the dragon throne in the center; it was Prince Ping.

He was wearing a bright yellow dragon robe, but his spirit seemed drained. Although still alive, his appearance was withered, and compared to a dead man, he only had a breath left.

When the palace was first besieged, he was furious and violent, hating Xu Ming, Zhao Xuanyou, and Pan Xun for opposing him. He couldn’t understand why, despite having all the advantages, he still lost.

Of course, he hated the late emperor even more.

Clearly, he was the eldest son. Clearly, he had managed court affairs for so long. Why didn’t the late emperor pass the throne to him? It was because the late emperor had underestimated him, which was why the officials did not recognize him!

At first, the people around him were still offering advice and strategies. But as the siege of the palace continued day by day, these people turned against him one by one.

Chancellor Sun first advised him to surrender, but after being rejected, he cursed Prince Ping as useless.

The guards, eunuchs, and palace maids around him hid one by one, trying to escape the palace to find a way to survive. Even his most doting and supportive mother blamed him for being too greedy, saying it would have been better to remain a prince.

At this point, he didn’t even have the strength to be angry.

Hearing the movement in the hall, Prince Ping moved his eyelids. Against the light, he couldn’t see the newcomer’s face clearly, but recognizing the tall and straight figure, he guessed who it was.

"Zhao Xuanyou, you’ve come."

Prince Ping’s voice carried endless sarcasm.

And even more self-mockery.

As he himself had said, to the victor belong the spoils. He had lost, and there was no one to blame.

"You once said that you would repay the favors you received from me in kind. Do those words still count?"

Zhao Xuanyou replied, "They do."

Prince Ping had indeed helped him a lot. He couldn’t assist in the rebellion, but he would repay the debts he could.

"My mother is kind-hearted by nature. Everything she did was forced by me. You must spare her life."

"I will do my best."

Hearing these words, Prince Ping on the dragon throne let out a light laugh, then suddenly roared, "Not counting those small favors from before, this time, I have finally helped you a great deal! Is this favor not enough to save my mother?"

Prince Ping was the only one who knew where Zhao Yi Yun was.

He wasn’t a fool. If it weren’t for Zhao Yi Yun, with Zhao Xuanyou’s cautious nature, he wouldn’t have been so actively involved in quelling the rebellion.

He had killed Prince Jing to pave his own way. Now that he had failed, it naturally paved the way for Zhao Yi Yun.

Zhao Xuanyou, of course, understood Prince Ping’s implication.

He glanced at the long sword beside the dragon throne, knowing Prince Ping’s intention. Considering their past acquaintance, he finally relented.

"I promise you, Your Highness, I will ensure Consort Li’s safety."

Hearing his guarantee, Prince Ping let out a long sigh.

His mother was intelligent and clever, but at heart, she was a kind person. Of course, she hoped he could become emperor, but she had always disapproved of his forging the decree to usurp the throne. She really shouldn’t have been implicated by him.

Perhaps he truly shouldn’t have usurped the throne. In the short half month, he felt as if it had been ten years, so exhausting.

He took one last look at Zhao Xuanyou, who seemed like a heavenly soldier descending, his heart filled with mockery.

He had lost, but his brothers couldn’t win either.

That was fine too.

Prince Ping’s hand caressed the intricate patterns on the dragon throne, gazing lovingly at the majestic five-clawed golden dragon. A moment later, he suddenly swung the long sword and committed suicide.

"Xuanyou! Why didn’t you stop him?!"

When Chancellor Xu led the officials to the Qianqing Palace, they saw Prince Ping dead on the dragon throne.

Blood sprayed from Prince Ping’s neck, splattering his dragon robe and the throne, a gruesome sight.

Chancellor Xu was a little angry. With Zhao Xuanyou’s skills, he could definitely have stopped Prince Ping from killing himself.

Zhao Xuanyou did not deny it and calmly said, "Prince Ping was, after all, the late emperor’s eldest son. If the late emperor were still alive, he would have left him some dignity."

That was true.

In the past, the late emperor had also given Emperor Jiang and Zhao Zun enough face.

"Forget it. Have the body of the rebellious prince buried in a coffin."

During the days the palace was besieged, the common people in the capital had already regained their former peace. With Prince Ping’s death, the palace was soon cleaned up.

Prince Ping’s body was buried, Consort Li was imprisoned in the Cold Palace, and the officials who had followed Prince Ping in his rebellion were all imprisoned.

Chancellor Sun also proclaimed his innocence, claiming he was forced by Prince Ping. But Chancellor Xu didn’t bother arguing with him and just locked him up, saying he would be dealt with after the new emperor ascended the throne.

The affairs of the rear palace were temporarily managed by Princess Yinning’s mother, while the front court was jointly managed by Prince Qing, Prince Rui, and Chancellor Xu.

The interrupted funeral affairs had to continue, and the country could not be without a ruler for a day. The most pressing issue now was the choice of the new emperor.

Chancellor Xu took the initiative to convene a grand court session, where the two princes and the civil and military officials discussed this matter together.

The late emperor had left Chancellor Xu only one decree of succession, but according to Chancellor Xu, this official decree had disappeared.

However, Chancellor Xu had another command from the emperor to the three major camps around the capital. Although it was a military order, it mentioned the succession to Prince Jing.

In addition, when writing the decree of succession, apart from Chancellor Xu, the Minister of Personnel was also present as a witness. Therefore, the civil and military officials could be sure that Chancellor Xu had not lied about the succession.

Thinking about it, the emperor had made sufficient preparations to ensure a smooth succession.

Even if the decree was stolen, there was another secret order to mobilize the troops.

But no one expected Prince Ping to cut off the retreat by directly killing Prince Jing, rendering the decree of succession useless.

According to the rules of the ancestors, in such a situation, the eldest legitimate son should be established. The late emperor had no legitimate sons left, so between the two remaining princes, Prince Qing should ascend the throne.

Prince Qing was not a particularly wicked person, but his usual behavior was somewhat erratic. The officials naturally had different opinions, feeling that since Prince Qing was only a few months older than Prince Rui, and their ages were similar, if they were to support Prince Qing, they might as well support Prince Rui.

Prince Rui, Zhao Qi, had the Ningguo Duke’s mansion as his backing, and there were many who supported him.

However, there were also many officials who upheld the rituals and laws, believing that no matter how close in age Prince Qing and Prince Rui were, Prince Qing was still the elder and should ascend the throne.

When the two factions of officials were arguing fiercely, someone suddenly proposed that the late Fourth Prince had a son, Zhao Yi Yun, who, as the late emperor’s eldest legitimate grandson, also had the qualifications to ascend the throne.

The person who said this was naturally not Zhao Xuanyou, but one of the people on the list left by the Eastern Palace.

Zhao Xuanyou then timely presented the late emperor’s handwritten order to him, explaining that someone in the capital was a threat to Zhao Yi Yun, so he had falsely spread the news of Zhao Yi Yun’s death and entrusted him to Zhao Xuanyou for upbringing.

This order was given by the late emperor to Zhao Xuanyou out of concern that Zhao Yi Yun’s identity would be exposed and bring disaster to the Jingyuan Marquis’ mansion. Now, it had become ironclad proof of Zhao Yi Yun’s identity.

The remnants of the Eastern Palace had been almost entirely purged, and few remained in the court. Originally, no one would have thought that a royal grandson could surpass Prince Qing and Prince Rui. But Zhao Yi Yun was Zhao Xuanyou’s adopted son, meaning the Jingyuan Marquis’ mansion fully supported Zhao Yi Yun. The two arguing factions suddenly became three.

Zhao Yi Yun was registered under the Fourth Prince, and his status as the eldest royal grandson was undeniable. They could argue their case as well.

In this chaotic situation, Chancellor Xu’s attitude became particularly crucial.

After much deliberation, he did not immediately express his stance but proposed to see Zhao Yi

chapters.title: Hesitation and Conviction
chapters.content:
Xu Xiang had his own considerations.

On the day the late emperor issued his final decree, he had discussed his sons with Xu Xiang.

Prince Ping had a narrow mind, lacking the tolerance to accommodate others, and his schemes were insufficient.

Prince Qing was frivolous in nature, and whether in scholarship or martial arts, he was the worst among the sons.

Prince Rui was the late emperor’s most beloved youngest son, intelligent and upright, but having lost his mother at a young age, he acted impulsively and often let emotions cloud his judgment, making him unsuitable to be emperor.

In comparison, Prince Jing had the right temperament, character, and ability, making him a suitable guardian of a peaceful and prosperous era.

By the rules of propriety, Prince Qing Zhao Yu was ranked before Prince Rui and the imperial grandson. However, Prince Qing was the one the late emperor least wanted to succeed him.

Seeing that some court officials had come forward to support Zhao Yi Yun, even though Zhao Xuanyou remained silent, Xu Xiang could easily guess that this was Zhao Xuanyou’s doing.

Out of trust in the old marquis and Zhao Xuanyou, Xu Xiang decided to meet the boy first before making a decision.

Xu Xiang was highly respected, with disciples all over the court. As one of the top meritorious officials in suppressing the rebellion alongside Zhao Xuanyou, once he spoke, the others also agreed to meet Zhao Yi Yun.

The earlier three groups had been able to argue endlessly, each citing classics and holding their own opinions, precisely because Xu Xiang had not yet taken a stance.

Prince Qing instinctively wanted to refute.

His only competitor had originally been Zhao Qi. Now, out of nowhere, Zhao Yi Yun had appeared, reducing his chances of becoming emperor, wasn’t that so?

But the court officials said Zhao Yi Yun was one of the candidates for the new emperor. Whether he succeeded or not, he should still attend this court session. Each cited classics and precedents, and Prince Qing couldn’t find a reason to object. He could only watch helplessly as the eunuch hurried away.

In the Jingyuan Marquis’s residence, Yu Ying was not surprised to see the decree-bearing eunuch.

In fact, ever since Wen Shuo and Lin Jian had gone to the prime minister’s residence to steal the secret decree, they had been working toward this moment.

Zhao Yi Yun had been a young master of the marquis’s residence for a long time, and there were no imperial grandson’s robes in the house. Yu Ying selected a grand set of clothes for him. After he was fully dressed, she patted his shoulder.

“Mother, will you accompany me into the palace?”

Without a summons, Yu Ying couldn’t enter the palace.

“I’ll send you to the palace gates with your younger brother and sister. Your father is in the Golden Throne Hall. With him there, you don’t need to be afraid.”

Zhao Yi Yun stiffly nodded.

It had been nearly six years since he left the imperial palace. He hadn’t expected to return one day.

“Big brother is going to the imperial palace?” A Ning, listening to their conversation, hopped over and tugged at Zhao Yi Yun’s sleeve.

“Yes, we’ll wait for good news from big brother at the palace gates.”

Good news?

A Ning tilted her head, not understanding what good news could come from the palace. But she usually liked her big brother the most. Seeing his solemn expression, she said without asking why, “We will definitely wait for good news.”

Her voice was soft and childish. Yu Ying and Zhao Yi Yun, hearing her comforting words, felt their heavy expressions relax a little.

“Let’s go. Don’t keep the officials in the palace waiting too long.”

Yu Ying held Zhao Yi Yun’s hand with one hand and A Ning’s with the other. She turned her head and saw Zhao Mianze. He still had his usual carefree look. Seeing Yu Ying looking at him, he obediently followed behind her.

Before long, the carriage stopped in front of the palace gates.

Yu Ying had Zhao Mianze take A Ning to wait in the carriage while she took Zhao Yi Yun, following the eunuch toward the palace gates.

Just as they were about to be stopped by the guards, Pan Xun led a few brocade-clad imperial guards out of the palace.

Seeing Pan Xun, Yu Ying knew it must be Zhao Xuanyou’s arrangement. She felt at ease handing Yi Yun over to Pan Xun.

Yi Yun was now a contender for the throne. Who knew if someone might try to attack him on the short journey from the palace gates to the Golden Throne Hall.

She stood at the palace gates until she could no longer see their figures before returning to the carriage.

Seeing Yu Ying deep in thought, A Ning tugged at her arm. “Mother, why does big brother have to enter the palace?”

Zhao Yi Yun’s identity had already been made public. Whether he became emperor or not, his status as an imperial grandson would be restored.

Yu Ying said, “Big brother was originally from the palace. Today is like him returning home.”

“Then why can’t we go in? Isn’t that our home too?” In A Ning’s mind, big brother was family, so big brother’s home was naturally her home too.

Yu Ying rubbed A Ning’s little head and smiled. “If we wait for good news from big brother, he will invite A Ning to play in the palace in the future.”

A Ning became more and more confused, frowning as she pondered her mother’s words.

She really couldn’t understand. Big brother was her brother, so why did she need an invitation to enter the palace?

Zhao Mianze saw that Yu Ying was very anxious. Although he wanted to continue pretending to be naive, he couldn’t bear to see Yu Ying so worried that it might affect her health. So he said, “Mother, don’t worry. Big brother will definitely receive good news.”

His tone was not as innocent as A Ning’s but was instead very firm.

Yu Ying, hearing his maturity beyond his years, suddenly smiled.

Her son had grown a bit, and his appearance was becoming more and more like hers. But he was still so young, yet his words and actions were exactly like Zhao Xuanyou’s style.

Although she thought her son was just parroted her words to comfort her, she inexplicably felt at ease, as if Zhao Xuanyou were by her side.

“There should be good news.”

If Zhao Yi Yun was summoned to the palace, Zhao Xuanyou must have already secured his qualification to inherit the throne.

Yu Ying didn’t know Prince Qing well, but she had heard from Zhao Xuanyou that he had a poor reputation and was the late emperor’s least favorite son.

The Prince Rui she knew was inherently kind, but his temperament was indeed a bit extreme.

Yi Yun was intelligent and quick to learn, whether in scholarship or martial arts. Having suffered in his early years, his temperament was steady, gentle but not weak.

Having raised Zhao Yi Yun for so many years, Yu Ying had never seen him lose his composure. He was always at ease and responded with grace.

He should be able to gain the recognition of the court officials.

Yu Ying let out a soft sigh and silently hoped in her heart.

While she was waiting anxiously in the carriage for news, Zhao Yi Yun was following Pan Xun toward the Golden Throne Hall.

Pan Xun was full of curiosity about this young imperial grandson and kept glancing at him.

When their gazes inadvertently met, Zhao Yi Yun neither fawned nor acted arrogantly but nodded slightly with composure.

Pan Xun quickly withdrew his gaze, a smile appearing at the corner of his lips.

Zhao Xuanyou had shown him great favor, and the two of them indeed got along well. If Zhao Xuanyou wanted to support the imperial grandson, he would naturally follow suit.

But he was still uncertain in his heart. Could a young man who had just returned from the border really convince the court officials?

Soon, he escorted Zhao Yi Yun to the Golden Throne Hall.

As soon as Zhao Yi Yun stepped into the hall, the gazes of all the civil and military officials fell on him.

This place was extremely familiar to him, and such attention was not unfamiliar either. In his childhood, he had indeed been the center of attention, the focus of all eyes.

But this feeling was indeed long lost. Many vague memories surged like a tide.

He remembered the scene of his grandmother and father being arrested, his dear mother whom he never got to bid farewell to, and the scene of being forced to leave the palace by his uncles and aunts.

Zhao Yi Yun’s heart beat extremely fast, and his eyes showed a trace of pain.

Should he really return to the imperial palace?

Would his fate be even more tragic than his father’s?

In his hesitation, he saw Zhao Xuanyou standing at the front of the officials, and his heart suddenly calmed. His gaze became firm as he walked forward.

---

chapters.title: The Dust Settles
chapters.content:
"Sixth Imperial Uncle, Seventh Imperial Uncle." Zhao Yi Yun cupped his hands in greeting to Prince Qing and Prince Rui.

The young man had inherited his birth mother’s elegant and refined appearance, as smooth as jade and as beautiful as bamboo. But his eyes, tempered by the winds and frosts of the desert and grasslands, held a sharpness that his peers lacked.

"Yi Yun has grown so much."

The last time Prince Qing and Prince Rui had seen Zhao Yi Yun, he was still a young child. Now, seeing him so sharp and capable, they truly felt that a few days apart made a world of difference.

After greeting the two imperial uncles, Zhao Yi Yun, under Zhao Xuanyou’s guidance, paid his respects to Prime Minister Xu and the other senior officials.

Xu Xiang asked Zhao Yi Yun about his experiences over the past few years, and Zhao Yi Yun responded with ease.

Prince Qing kept staring at Xu Xiang’s expression from the side. Seeing his appreciation for Zhao Yi Yun, Prince Qing’s mind buzzed as if it were about to explode.

He might enjoy eating, drinking, and playing around, but he was not stupid.

The late emperor had maintained a balance, with Prime Minister Xu and Prime Minister Sun standing on equal footing. Now that Prime Minister Sun was in prison, the officials who had previously aligned themselves with him were in a panic, looking for a way out.

Because of Prime Minister Sun, these people had been very close to Prince Ping and had offended many other princes.

If Prince Qing or Prince Rui ascended the throne, they would certainly not let these people off.

Zhao Yi Yun was different. He was an imperial grandson who had returned from outside, and none of them knew him. His foster father, Zhao Xuanyou, although a great meritorious official in suppressing the rebellion, had previously had a good relationship with Prince Ping and had not made enemies with them. As long as they behaved themselves, they could continue to serve in the court.

Thus, more and more court officials began to support Zhao Yi Yun.

Xu Xiang, however, remained cautious. In this situation, he did not immediately express his stance but instead turned to Prince Qing and Prince Rui, asking for their opinions.

Prince Qing was naturally furious, his face turning pale as he glared at the officials who supported Zhao Yi Yun. He loudly declared, “I am the late emperor’s eldest son. Whether by ancestral rules or Confucian etiquette, it should be me who inherits the throne. How can it be the turn of Zhao Yi Yun, this brash child?!”

His words were reasonable, but he was neither the man the late emperor wanted nor the one recognized by the court officials.

Seeing that the officials remained silent, Prince Qing turned to Prince Rui in a huff. “Aren’t you going to say something? Are we brothers just going to be outmaneuvered like this?”

Everything that happened today was indeed unexpected for Zhao Qi.

He didn’t have much desire for the throne.

When his father was alive, he had repeatedly been told to settle his temperament, but he had repeatedly defied his father in matters of marriage. Even in the first two years after marrying Miaofeng, things had been bumpy, truly disappointing his father.

The reason he stood up against Prince Qing was that this sixth brother of his was even more unreliable than he was.

His father’s body was not yet cold, and he was still immersed in grief, yet his third brother had plotted treason, his fifth brother had been assassinated, and his sixth brother was making a scene with the court officials over the throne.

Looking at his nephew, whom he hadn’t seen in a long time, Zhao Qi was shocked that his father had entrusted his nephew to Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying.

In his father’s heart, Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Ying were more trustworthy than his own sons, weren’t they?

Recalling his father’s past protection and affection for Zhao Yi Yun, Zhao Qi couldn’t help but sigh. If his father could see Zhao Yi Yun today, he would surely be very pleased.

Zhao Qi withdrew his thoughts and said solemnly, “Yi Yun is indeed the most suitable candidate.”

“Zhao Qi, have you gone mad?” Prince Qing felt a pain in his chest, as if he could spit out a mouthful of old blood.

He said what he said, but he knew Zhao Qi hadn’t gone mad.

He was a few months older than Zhao Qi, and Zhao Qi had no reason to compete with him.

Now that Zhao Qi had taken the lead in supporting Zhao Yi Yun, Zhao Yi Yun would surely reciprocate and remember his kindness in the future.

Clearly, he was the eldest son, clearly he had the most reason, but instead, he was being played like a clown by these people.

Thinking this, Prince Qing felt even more pain in his chest.

Due to Zhao Qi’s statement, even the officials like the Duke of Ningguo, who had originally supported Prince Qing, fell silent.

Xu Xiang saw that the time was right. His gaze swept over the officials. “A country cannot be without a ruler for a day. Since this is the will of the people, I am willing to support the imperial grandson in inheriting the throne.”

“The officials are willing to support the imperial grandson in inheriting the throne.”
