Watching the officials in the Golden Throne Hall kneel and pay their respects to him, Zhao Yi Yun was stunned for a moment. Then, under the guidance of the eunuchs, he sat on the dragon throne.

He was not unfamiliar with the dragon throne.

In his childhood, his imperial grandfather often held him on his lap to play, but he never expected that after so many twists and turns, he would end up sitting on the dragon throne.

Zhao Yi Yun looked at the sea of officials kneeling on the ground, listening to the earth-shaking chants of “Long live the emperor,” and tightly gripped the dragon heads on the armrests.

He was the Son of Heaven.

Thinking of the past, his eyes were no longer confused.

The eunuchs respectfully led Zhao Yi Yun to the inner hall to change into the dragon robe. Zhao Qi looked at the pained Prince Qing beside him and softly comforted him, “No matter what, think about Fifth Brother. Originally, it should have been him who inherited the throne, but now he has followed Father.”

Prince Qing initially thought Zhao Qi was sarcastically mocking him as he had when they were children. But upon careful consideration, on that day in the Qianqing Palace, he had almost been killed by the deranged Prince Ping.

If he couldn’t become emperor, being able to live peacefully as a prince was indeed much better than dying.

Thinking this, Prince Qing felt much better.

With the new emperor ascending the throne, the first matters to address were the late emperor’s funeral, Prince Ping’s treason case, and the coronation ceremony.

Although Zhao Yi Yun was young, with the help of the senior officials, each matter was handled in an orderly manner.

When all matters were settled, the eunuch announced the end of the court session. Pan Xun, standing by his side, led him toward the inner hall.

With only two or three people around, Zhao Yi Yun finally let out a long sigh.

“Where is my father?” After calming down a bit, he looked at Pan Xun beside him.

Pan Xun respectfully replied, “In response to Your Majesty, the marquis has been ordered to handle Prince Ping’s treason case. At this moment, he has already gone to the Ministry of Justice with the Minister of Justice.”

Zhao Yi Yun was stunned.

Every word reminded Zhao Yi Yun that his status had changed, and he was no longer considered part of the marquis’s family.

But he couldn’t be bothered with that. He said again, “My mother and younger brother and sister have been waiting at the palace gates. Send someone to invite them into the palace immediately.”

“This official obeys the decree.”

Zhao Yi Yun had just entered the palace today and had no trusted aides around him. Pan Xun didn’t dare to leave his side, so he ordered a eunuch to go and find Yu Ying and her three children.

Before long, the eunuch brought them into the Qianqing Palace.

Seeing Yu Ying about to kneel with Zhao Mianze and A Ning to pay their respects, Zhao Yi Yun quickly said, “Mother, you don’t need to perform the rites.”

Fearful that Yu Ying might not listen, he quickly stepped forward to support her and ordered the surrounding eunuchs to withdraw, including Pan Xun.

A Ning looked around at everything and curiously asked, “Big brother, will you live here from now on?”

“Mmm, probably yes.”

“Then won’t I be able to see you every day?” A Ning puffed out her cheeks in dissatisfaction.

Zhao Mianze had long expected Zhao Yi Yun to become emperor. He leisurely picked up a dessert from the table, stuffed one into A Ning’s hand, and comforted her, “Big brother is the emperor. As long as he wants to see us, he can see us anytime.”

A Ning gave a vague “Oh” and obediently ate the cake.

Yu Ying saw Zhao Yi Yun’s frowning, hesitant expression and, thinking of A Ning’s words, consoled him, “Yes, you can see your younger brother and sister whenever you want.”

Zhao Yi Yun was silent for a while, then carefully looked at Yu Ying. “Mother, can you hug me?”

chapters.title: Moving House
chapters.content:
Speaking of which, it had been a long time since Yu Wan had held Zhao Yi Yun in her arms.

Her younger brothers and sister were always clinging to their mother, so as the elder brother, he naturally couldn’t compete with them for attention.

Yu Wan was taken aback for a moment, then felt a pang of heartache and pulled Zhao Yi Yun into her embrace.

Zhao Yi Yun, holding onto Yu Wan’s shoulders, whispered, "Mother, I don’t want to be separated from you all."

This...

Yu Wan thought for a moment and comforted him, "Today, we’ll stay in the palace and keep you company. After dinner, we’ll return to the Hou residence."

Zhao Yi Yun lowered his gaze and remained silent.

"Since we’re all in the capital, and the Hou residence isn’t far from the palace, as long as you summon us, we’ll come immediately," Yu Wan said softly. "When your younger brother starts his studies, we can have him be your study companion and stay in the palace with you all the time."

"Me?" Zhao Mianze opened his mouth in surprise.

What did this have to do with him?

In his past life, he had a good relationship with Zhao Yi Yun, but he didn’t want to be a study companion. He just wanted to stay at the Hou residence with his father, mother, and sister.

Moreover, he didn’t need to study seriously in this life. He only needed to focus on martial arts to strengthen his body.

Seeing Zhao Mianze’s strong reaction, Yu Wan frowned and glared at him. He sighed, said "Fine," and helplessly picked up a pastry to eat.

Zhao Yi Yun said softly, "They say the emperor is the Son of Heaven and can do whatever he wants. If I want you all to stay in the palace, why can’t it be done?"

"The Son of Heaven is indeed supreme. But because he stands so high, every official and commoner watches his every move. So even the Son of Heaven must act in accordance with rites and laws. Everything must be done properly and with justification."

Proper and with justification...

Zhao Yi Yun pondered these four words repeatedly in his mind.

Seeing him lowering his head, Yu Wan thought he was still upset about this matter and added, "Don’t worry. When you see your father, there will surely be a way."

There was no empress dowager in the palace, and the former manager of the Six Palaces, Li Guifei, had also been imprisoned.

Since the late emperor had entrusted Zhao Yi Yun to the Jingyuan Hou residence, it was reasonable for her and Zhao Xuanyou to take care of him until he grew up. This matter should be negotiable.

"Tonight, your younger brother will stay in the palace to keep you company. Your sister and I will leave after dinner."

Zhao Mianze was a hundred times unwilling, but fine, staying for one night was no big deal.

Seeing Zhao Yi Yun’s expression relax a little, Yu Wan admonished, "When it’s just our family together, you can address us as you used to. But if there are outsiders present, your words and actions must befit an emperor."

Perhaps it wasn’t so much like an emperor, but Zhao Yi Yun was now the true emperor.

Zhao Yi Yun’s just relaxed brows furrowed again. This meant he could no longer call Yu Wan "Mother."

Yu Wan knew he wouldn’t be able to adjust immediately. She rubbed his head and whispered, "Although it may be inconvenient, there are many more advantages. From now on, you won’t have to live in hiding. You are the ruler of the world, and you can address the regrets in your heart one by one. With you, our whole family will benefit."

Zhao Yi Yun was slightly taken aback, thinking of many things. His eyes lit up, and he nodded solemnly to Yu Wan.

"I’ve never been to the inner hall of the Qianqing Palace before. Take us around for a look."

"Alright."

Zhao Yi Yun had often entered and exited the Qianqing Palace as a child and was very familiar with both the inside and outside of the palace. He led his family around to visit, chatting as they went, as if they had returned to the pleasant times in Yuzhou.

By dinnertime, the inner attendants announced that Zhao Xuanyou had arrived at the palace gate. Zhao Yi Yun immediately ordered someone to invite him in.

Just yesterday, the whole family had been having dinner at the Hou residence. Today, they were in the Qianqing Palace.

As they tasted the imperial cuisine, Zhao Xuanyou also brought good news.

He and Prime Minister Xu had already discussed it. Since the late emperor had left a decree entrusting Zhao Yi Yun to the Hou residence for upbringing, until Zhao Yi Yun grew up, he and Yu Wan could stay in the palace to take care of him.

"Then where will we live?" Yu Wan asked.

"Still at Beiyuan."

Beiyuan had been empty ever since the late emperor’s sons had grown up. It would be most appropriate for their family to move there.

Zhao Yi Yun’s gaze flickered, but he said nothing.

After dinner, Zhao Xuanyou and Pan Xun rearranged the staff in the Qianqing Palace.

Liu Quan had refused to give false testimony for Prince Ping after the late emperor’s passing and was arrested and severely tortured by Prince Ping. He had suffered serious injuries. Having been loyal to the late emperor all his life, Zhao Yi Yun granted him a mansion and allowed him to enjoy his old age in peace in the capital.

Chen Lin, the deputy director of the Qianqing Palace, had sided with Prince Ping and naturally could not stay. He was immediately expelled from the palace.

Pan Xun had stayed in the palace for a period of time and recommended a few trustworthy young eunuchs to work in the Qianqing Palace.

Yu Wan also ordered her four senior maids to be summoned into the palace, asking Qiuyue and Ran Dong to temporarily stay in the Qianqing Palace to take care of Zhao Yi Yun’s daily needs. With Lin Jing also serving as a guard in front of the emperor, things were now well taken care of.

By nightfall, after waiting for Zhao Yi Yun and Zhao Mianze to fall asleep in the Qianqing Palace, Yu Wan, together with Zhao Xuanyou, took their daughter to Beiyuan.

The moon was bright, and the stars were sparse. Zhao Xuanyou carried the sleepy A Ning in one arm and held Yu Wan’s hand with the other.

"Yi Yun is very anxious. Tomorrow, find an excuse to have a good talk with him."

Zhao Xuanyou responded with an "Mmm," then glanced at Yu Wan. "And you?"

Yu Wan was taken aback.

Previously, as the Hou’s wife, she only needed to manage the Jingyuan Hou residence well. From now on, with their family living in the palace, everyone’s attention would be on her. Zhao Yi Yun couldn’t do as he pleased, and neither could she.

Yu Wan didn’t answer Zhao Xuanyou’s question but instead asked with a smile, "And you?"

Previously, he only needed to manage the Mingchuan Guard and the affairs of Yuzhou. Now, with Zhao Yi Yun still young, the affairs of the court couldn’t be entirely left to Prime Minister Xu. After eliminating their common enemy, the court needed new balances and checks.

Ascending the throne was just the first step. Countless obstacles and difficulties awaited them in the future.

"What am I afraid of?"

The night was as dark as ink, and the moonlight was like a white silk ribbon.

Zhao Xuanyou met Yu Wan’s gaze, then suddenly leaned down and kissed her lips.

Yu Wan was surprised and tried to push him away, but she was afraid of disturbing A Ning in his arms and didn’t dare use much force.

Normally, at the Hou residence, he did as he pleased, and the servants were used to it. Yu Wan didn’t mind.

But today was different.

Although Pe Xia and Chun Xing were used to it, there were several palace maids and eunuchs following them... and there were also patrolling guards passing by nearby... Yu Wan’s face turned completely red.

After moving into the imperial palace, Yu Wan and Zhao Xuanyou were indeed very busy.

Due to the investigation into Prince Ping’s treasonous rebellion, many officials in the court were implicated. They needed to dismiss and investigate these people and find replacements for the vacancies.

Prime Minister Xu was indeed upright, but it was inevitable that he had personal motives. He recommended only his own disciples, and Zhao Xuanyou naturally couldn’t allow the court to become a one-man show under Prime Minister Xu.

However, as a military general, Zhao Xuanyou was not as familiar with civil officials as Prime Minister Xu. After much consideration, he spared many officials who had been associated with Prince Ping and Premier Sun. Although these people had sided with Prince Ping, their connections were not deep, and they had a good reputation after years in office. Keeping them could be seen as an act of benevolence by the new emperor, which would help soothe public sentiment and also serve as a check on Prime Minister Xu’s power.

As for court affairs, Zhao Yi Yun followed Prime Minister Xu and Zhao Xuanyou’s arrangements, but three days after his enthronement, he issued his first decree, ordering all the late emperor’s concubines to be moved to a separate courtyard outside the capital.

The palace was crowded, and with so many mistresses around, there was bound to be idle gossip.

Removing them would not only make it easier to manage the imperial palace but also allow the Hou family to live in peace and quiet.

However, this left the rear palace without a mistress, so Yu Wan had to take charge and manage the palace affairs.

Amid her busy and dizzying schedule, Yu Wan thought of someone.

chapters.title: A New Day
chapters.content:
Princess Yining was Yu Wan’s good friend and Zhao Yi Yun’s own aunt. If she were willing to step forward and manage the palace affairs, the entire palace, top to bottom, would surely accept her.

However, after inquiring, Yu Wan learned that Princess Yining had been frightened by the incident where Prince Ping had coerced her into issuing a false decree. She was still emotionally unstable, and Ye Mo Wan and her children had been staying with her at the Hot Spring Villa to keep her company.

Upon further reflection, Princess Yining’s eldest daughter had become dull-witted after being poisoned by the deposed Empress Jiang, who was Zhao Yi Yun’s own grandmother. Even if Princess Yining did not resent Zhao Yi Yun, it was impossible for her to have no lingering bitterness.

It wouldn’t be good for her or for Zhao Yi Yun.

Yu Wan abandoned this idea and sent many tonics to Princess Yining’s Hot Spring Villa. She then racked her brain and thought of Sun Qianran.

They had had disagreements before, but ultimately, there was no deep enmity between them. Sun Qianran had never done anything harmful to Yu Wan, and she had previously taken care of Zhao Yi Yun in the palace, so Zhao Yi Yun was not unfamiliar with her.

With Sun Qianran’s intelligence and capability, she was more than capable of handling the complex palace affairs.

After proposing this candidate, Zhao Xuanyou also agreed.

Sun Premier was still in prison. Given the many crimes he had committed in the past, it was unlikely he would survive. Keeping Sun Qianran in the palace as a female official might invite criticism, but it would also reassure the court officials who were not part of Prime Minister Xu’s faction.

After discussing it with Zhao Xuanyou, Yu Wan invited Sun Qianran into the palace.

After all the late emperor’s concubines were moved out of the palace, the vast imperial palace became much quieter.

Yu Wan and Sun Qianran sat in a cool pavilion in the imperial garden. Everything around them was fresh and bright under the warm sunlight.

Today, Yu Wan wore a light jade-colored gauze dress. At first glance, it seemed unremarkable, but the fabric was actually precious ice silk. The cuffs and hem were embroidered with dark patterns of butterflies and begonia flowers in gold thread, exuding an elegant yet noble charm.

"Miss Sun, have some tea."

In contrast, Sun Qianran wore a plain and simple dress. Although her attire was modest, her complexion was good.

"Thank you, Madam Hou, for keeping your promise."

The palace servants were all waiting outside the pavilion, allowing the two women to speak freely.

Having survived the disaster, she felt only gratitude toward Yu Wan.

Yu Wan asked, "Where are you staying now?"

Sun Qianran had long anticipated the downfall of Prince Ping and her father. She had made preparations early on.

After Sun Premier was imprisoned, only two of her brothers, who had connections with Prince Ping, were arrested. The rest of the family was not charged, but after the Ministry of Justice confiscated the Premier’s residence, they were left homeless.

"I had previously asked the abbot of Yunshui Nunnery to help me purchase a small courtyard nearby. It only has three rooms, but it’s enough for my mother, Xiang Xu, and me."

She had been a patron of Yunshui Nunnery for many years and had a deep friendship with the abbot.

She had given the abbot a generous sum of incense money in advance, and the abbot had purchased a house in the nunnery’s name, which was not registered with the Ministry of Justice.

Living next to Yunshui Nunnery, she and her mother and daughter could look out for each other with the nuns.

"Is Xiang Xu still with you?"

Xiang Xu was Sun Qianran’s senior maid. In the past, at the Lichuan Summer Palace, she had gotten along well with Yu Wan.

"Yes, apart from my mother, only Xiang Xu has been with me all along." Sun Qianran sighed softly, lost in memories for a long moment. Then she looked up at Yu Wan. "I’ve been rambling on about myself. It’s truly rude. May I ask, Madam Hou, why have you summoned me to the palace today?"

Although Yu Wan was still the Madam of the Hou residence, the situation was different now. She was the foster mother of the new emperor, and in the future, who knew what her position would be? For now, she was in charge of the rear palace.

Sun Qianran didn’t know what Yu Wan was planning, but based on her understanding of Yu Wan, it wouldn’t be anything bad.

"You know that I come from a humble background and am completely unfamiliar with palace affairs and rules. His Majesty’s coronation ceremony is approaching, and there are many tasks in the palace that need to be handled. With so many things to manage, I’m really overwhelmed. I’d like to ask for your help."

"Me?"

In Sun Qianran’s mind, she and Yu Wan were neither enemies nor friends.

With the Premier’s residence confiscated and herself left with no one to rely on, Yu Wan had unexpectedly asked her to help in the palace.

"Are you willing?"

Sun Qianran was slightly taken aback and looked up to meet Yu Wan’s gaze.

Even after raising three children, Yu Wan’s expression still showed no signs of fatigue or distress. Her beautiful eyes were as lively and bright as when they first met.

Sun Qianran gently pinched her fingers, feeling a surge of emotions.

When she first met Yu Wan, Sun Qianran had been kind to her, but it was out of a desire to win over Zhao Xuanyou.

After spending a long time together in Lichuan, she realized that Yu Wan was intelligent and talented, and she also envied Yu Wan’s good health.

Watching Yu Wan work hard to study and practice calligraphy, Sun Qianran felt a faint bitterness.

Later, when she learned that Pei Ta was devoted to Yu Wan, her jealousy grew even stronger, and she finally lost her composure in front of Yu Wan.

After her impulsive outburst, she realized that her fate with Pei Ta was over, and it wasn’t Yu Wan’s fault. Her emotions gradually calmed down, and in the end, before her family’s downfall, she went to Yu Wan to make a deal.

She had watched Yu Wan rise step by step from a maid in the Hou residence to her current position, just as Yu Wan had watched her fall from her previous status to where she was now.

She didn’t need to ask Yu Wan if she had ulterior motives, and Yu Wan didn’t need to pry into her past.

Although they weren’t friends, there were many things that were hard to say to those around them, yet the other seemed to understand.

"If Madam Hou trusts me, I am willing."

"Very well."

Yu Wan believed she could manage the palace affairs properly. After discussing it with Zhao Yi Yun, Zhao Yi Yun indeed remembered Sun Qianran and immediately appointed her as a female official in the palace.

Freed from the tedious palace affairs, Yu Wan focused on accompanying Zhao Yi Yun in the Qianqing Palace to review memorials.

Back in Yuzhou, she and Zhao Yi Yun had attended lectures together with Scholar Cui Zaiting, and in their studies, they were like classmates.

In the Qianqing Palace, Yu Wan and Zhao Yi Yun sat at a desk reviewing memorials, while Zhao Mianze and A Ning drew pictures beside them. Even in the magnificent palace, they felt as relaxed and happy as they had in Yuzhou.

Zhao Yi Yun had ascended the throne hastily and was still young. Every day, the memorials were first annotated by Prime Minister Xu and the six ministry officials before being sent to the Qianqing Palace.

Zhao Xuanyou had many things to attend to, so it was Yu Wan who accompanied Zhao Yi Yun to read the memorials every day.

Although it was called reviewing, Zhao Yi Yun was more focused on understanding the workings of the court. The two of them would analyze the issues reported in the memorials, discuss their own solutions, and then compare them with the annotations made by the officials.

Most of the time, the officials’ annotations were indeed better than theirs. But over time, they were also able to identify shortcomings in the officials’ annotations.

When they were unsure, they would ask Zhao Xuanyou and then send the memorials back for further discussion.

"Mother, look at this memorial." One day, after reading a memorial, Zhao Yi Yun thoughtfully handed it to Yu Wan.

Yu Wan recognized the familiar, forceful handwriting and her expression faltered slightly.

"This is a memorial from Minister Pei of the Ministry of Works. He says that there are many vacancies in various departments. Rather than appointing unsuitable old officials just to fill the positions, it would be better to hold an additional special imperial examination to select new talent and bring fresh blood into the court."

Pei Ta was the Assistant Minister of Works. During Prince Ping’s rebellion, he had been away from the capital, supervising river construction. By the time he returned to the capital, the chaos in the city had already been resolved.

"Mother, do you think it’s inappropriate?"

Seeing that Yu Wan remained silent, Zhao Yi Yun asked in confusion.

Although his time as emperor was still short, Zhao Yi Yun understood that most of the officials were Prime Minister Xu’s disciples, and the rest were deeply entrenched in their own factions. Their support for him was based on the situation, not genuine loyalty.

If they could hold an additional special examination, the newly selected talents would naturally be loyal to him and could be used by him.

But he didn’t know why his mother seemed troubled.

chapters.title: Childishness
chapters.content:
"Sounds reasonable." Yu Wan withdrew her thoughts and took the memorial to read it carefully. The more she read, the more she agreed with Pei Ta's suggestion.

The imperial examination was held every three years. If no special examination was added, the next examination would be in a year and a half. By then, the vacant positions would have been filled.

"However, there is one thing that needs careful consideration. If Prime Minister Xu is in charge of the examination again, the selected talents will become his disciples."

Zhao Yi Yun frowned slightly. After a moment of thought, he still found it difficult. "Father is probably not suitable. It's hard for scholars to be convinced if a military general presides over the imperial examination."

Yu Wan did have a candidate in mind, but...

After a moment of hesitation, she slowly said, "Lord Pei would be very suitable."

Pei Ta was not one of Prime Minister Xu's faction. He was a top scholar, learned and wise, renowned throughout the land. It would be most appropriate for him to preside over this special examination.

Zhao Yi Yun had a good impression of Pei Ta, but since he had only recently become emperor, he was not very familiar with the court officials.

Yu Wan's suggestion took him by surprise. Logically, she had never met Pei Ta and should not trust him so much.

"Pei Ta is not one of Prime Minister Xu's people, right?"

"He is trustworthy." Yu Wan said with certainty.

Zhao Yi Yun noticed Yu Wan's thoughtful expression and glanced at the handwriting on the memorial. Suddenly, he realized something.

Pei Ta's handwriting was very similar to his mother's. No, perhaps it should be said that his mother's handwriting was very similar to Pei Ta's. Pei Ta's handwriting was even better.

"Mother, do you know Pei Ta?" Zhao Yi Yun asked tentatively.

Yu Wan nodded.

"Then let Lord Pei preside over the special examination."

Among the civil officials, there was finally a capable minister who was not part of Prime Minister Xu's faction. Zhao Yi Yun was genuinely happy.

However, before he could say more, Yu Wan added, "If your father asks, just say it was about this memorial."

Did his mother mean not to mention that she recommended Pei Ta?

Zhao Yi Yun did not yet understand matters of love between men and women. Hearing Yu Wan's words and recalling the similarity between her and Pei Ta's handwriting, he vaguely sensed something and nodded in response, "I understand."

Yu Wan did not think Zhao Xuanyou would be jealous. It was just that it was better to avoid unnecessary complications.

A month later, Zhao Yi Yun's coronation ceremony was finally ready. Ding Wenxi, Cui Zaiting, Yingxue, and others who had stayed in Yuzhou all returned to the capital.

On that day, Zhao Yi Yun rode in the imperial carriage from the main gate of the palace to the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan shared a carriage and followed closely behind.

This was originally against the rules, but Zhao Yi Yun had insisted, and in the end, Prime Minister Xu and the others relented.

The common people lined both sides of the street, vying to catch a glimpse of the emperor.

Zhao Yi Yun's experiences were too legendary and were the favorite stories of the storytellers.

After the complex ceremonies at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Zhao Yi Yun was already exhausted. However, there was still a state banquet in the palace, so he had to force himself to keep going.

Yu Wan had already noticed his fatigue. Halfway through the banquet, she claimed to be tired and took Zhao Yi Yun back to the bedchamber.

As soon as they left the Golden Throne Hall, Zhao Yi Yun got into the sedan chair and immediately fell asleep, yawning repeatedly.

Yu Wan followed the sedan chair for a while before someone approached from the front.

Upon seeing Zhao Yi Yun, the person immediately bowed.

"He's asleep. There's no need for formalities, Prince." Yu Wan did not have the heart to wake Zhao Yi Yun.

"Thank you, Your Majesty." Zhao Qi completed the courtesies and stood aside to let Zhao Yi Yun's sedan chair pass.

However, as they passed by, Zhao Qi suddenly spoke, "Madam Hou, could you stay a moment?"

Yu Wan was slightly surprised and ordered the eunuch to take Zhao Yi Yun back to the palace first.

"Greetings, Prince." She lowered her eyes and curtsied to Zhao Qi. "There were too many people at the banquet just now. I didn't notice that you had left."

Since the people around were all trusted servants, Zhao Qi spoke bluntly, "I have always been like this. I cannot stay for more than the time it takes to drink a cup of tea at any palace banquet, big or small."

It was precisely because of this rebellious character that the late emperor had deemed him unsuitable to bear the responsibility of the emperor.

Since returning to the capital, Yu Wan had seen Zhao Qi from a distance a few times, but they had not spoken.

After several years, Zhao Qi was dressed in a brocade robe, appearing more dignified and impressive than before.

"Prince and Princess Wang have been blessed with a son. I haven't had the chance to congratulate you in person."

Two years ago, Liang Miaofeng had given birth to a son. The Hou family had prepared a very generous gift, but because of the distance, they had not attended the hundred-day banquet.

"Also, thank you, Prince, for speaking highly of Ah Ji on my behalf to Minister Liang."

"It was a small matter. Madam Hou need not remember it."

Since Zhao Yi Yun had acknowledged Yu Wan as his mother, Wen Ji was naturally the emperor's maternal uncle. With this relationship, there would be no obstacles to Wen Ji's marriage with Liang Miaotong. Zhao Qi would not claim credit for this.

"There is one thing I want to ask Madam Hou."

Seeing Zhao Qi's gaze deepen, Yu Wan glanced at the maid, who understandingly stepped back a bit.

"Prince, please feel free to speak."

Zhao Qi took a deep breath and said in a low voice, "I have a doubt in my mind. When the Third Brother rebelled, the residences of Prince Jing, Prince Qing, and Prince Rui were all surrounded. Logically, both the Sixth Brother and I were his enemies, but he did not act against us. He only killed the Fifth Brother. The Third Brother could not have obtained the imperial edict, so I guess someone obtained the imperial edict and told its contents to the Third Brother."

The Prince of Ping had falsified the imperial edict to usurp the throne. Prince Jing had died unjustly. Zhao Yi Yun had been enthroned by the ministers. These events had happened too quickly. At the time, Zhao Qi had not been able to think carefully. Only after calming down did he notice some clues.

Today, when he met Prince Qing, he casually asked and learned that on the day of the rebellion, Prince Qing's residence, like Prince Rui's, had only been surrounded and no assassins had broken in. This indicated that Prince Ping had only wanted to kill Prince Jing.

Why?

Could it be that Prince Ping knew that the late emperor wanted to pass the throne to Prince Jing?

Only Prime Minister Xu and another court official knew about the imperial edict. During Prince Ping's rebellion, they had resisted fiercely and never surrendered. It was absolutely impossible for them to have leaked the information to Prince Ping.

Prime Minister Xu had said that the imperial edict was stolen. Had Prince Ping stolen the imperial edict? That was unlikely. If Prince Ping had obtained the imperial edict and killed Prince Jing, he would not have needed to stage the charade of falsifying the edict. He could have simply waited to ascend the throne according to the order of seniority.

There were no clues pointing to the thief of the imperial edict. However, in this struggle for the throne, the only beneficiary was Zhao Yi Yun. Therefore, the person who stole the imperial edict and revealed its contents to Prince Ping could only be...

Yu Wan's gaze flickered slightly, but her expression did not waver in the least.

"Why does the Prince ask me?"

"Was it Zhao Xuanyou?" Zhao Qi asked directly.

Yu Wan was equally direct in her response, "The imperial edict you mentioned, he has not even seen it."

"Have you seen it?" Zhao Qi countered.

The night wind was slightly chilly. Yu Wan gathered her sleeves and folded her hands. She met Zhao Qi's gaze and lifted her eyes but did not speak.

She had not ordered Wen Ji and Lin Jing to do this.

But Lin Jing was the leader of the Eastern Palace secret guards. He had long been involved in the former empress and Zhao Zhen's plots for the throne. After seeing the edict, he naturally knew what to do.

All he needed to do was leak the news that the late emperor intended to pass the throne to Prince Jing to Prince Ping, and Prince Ping would take action.

Zhao Qi already understood her meaning. He quietly observed the woman in front of him.

Compared to her previous delicate and lively appearance, Yu Wan's demeanor was now more gentle and dignified. She wore a precious brocade dress with a jade belt around her waist and her hair styled in an elaborate high bun, which made her figure appear even more graceful and tall.

In the night wind, her sheer cloak flowed like water, dancing lightly.

"If the Prince has no other instructions, I will take my leave."

Yu Wan curtsied to him and walked towards Zhao Yi Yun's sedan chair in the distance.

"Wait."

After taking a couple of steps, Zhao Qi spoke again from behind.

Yu Wan stopped and turned back to look at Zhao Qi, silently waiting for him to finish speaking.

"If, and I say if, the person written on the edict was me, would you still have done this?"

As soon as the words were spoken, Yu Wan felt as if she saw the young man who had made a promise to her on the city tower years ago.

Zhao Yi Yun had already been stably enthroned. His doubts were clearly not out of hostility but a desire for an answer.

This kind of thought was indeed somewhat childish, but it moved Yu Wan.

"No."

Since Zhao Xuanyou had brought her back, her attitude towards Zhao Qi had always been distant.

But at this moment, it was a long-lost gentle certainty.

Zhao Qi wanted to say something but did not know what to say. He simply nodded at her.

Yu Wan looked at the bewilderment in his eyes and wanted to tell him that it was the truth, but more words would be unnecessary.

She curtsied again and turned to leave.

The night wind grew colder. Zhao Qi's emotions were exceptionally complex, and his fingers tightened.

Even though Yu Wan had answered without hesitation, he could not tell if she was telling the truth or not.

What she said might be the truth, or it might be a lie to make him happy.

In the end, he had never really known the true Yu Wan. So, in the past, did he like Yu Wan, or did he like the Yu Wan he had imagined?

The stars tonight were not those of last night. For whom does the wind and dew stand in the middle of the night?

It didn't matter.

chapters.title: End of Main Text
chapters.content:
After the enthronement ceremony, Zhao Yi Yun officially became the emperor recognized by heaven, earth, and ancestors. Following tradition, he rewarded meritorious officials and bestowed favors upon many.

Prime Minister Xu, as the leader of all officials, had already reached the highest rank and was additionally granted the title of Grand Preceptor, placing him above all other officials and honoring him as the Duke of the State. Pei Ta, who had been entrusted with important tasks, was promoted from Assistant Minister of Works to Minister of Rites. Other officials who had contributed to suppressing the Prince’s rebellion were also rewarded according to their merits.

Lin Cheng, who had followed Zhao Yi Yun from Yuzhou to the capital, became the commander of the Feathered Forest Guard. Wen Jian, being Zhao Yi Yun’s nominal uncle by marriage and thus a relative by marriage, was granted the title of Marquis of Ping’an. However, this was a nominal title, unlike the Marquis of Jingyuan, who commanded an army.

Wen Jian had never been interested in officialdom; everything he did was to help Yuwán. Such a generous reward and honor were the best for him. He remained a free spirit, a carefree man beyond worldly concerns, living a life of ease and comfort.

Cui Zaiting had taught Zhao Yi Yun in Yuzhou for several years. As both his real uncle and teacher, he could have been directly appointed to an official position. However, being a scholar at heart, he insisted on participating in the special imperial examination to earn his own reputation before taking office. Yuwán initially wanted to persuade him to be more flexible, but Zhao Xuanyou said that officials highly valued academic degrees. Those who passed the imperial examination could hold their heads high anywhere, while non-degree holders would be looked down upon when seeking promotions. Yuwán gave up on persuading him, confident that with his talent, he would pass with flying colors.

The court officials had no objections to these rewards, but a great controversy arose when it came to rewarding Zhao Xuanyou and Yuwán.

By convention, the emperor’s adoptive parents should be honored as the Duke and Duchess of En, with a mansion built to the specifications of a prince’s residence. They would also be granted the privileges of not bowing to the emperor and wearing swords and shoes in the imperial court, demonstrating both the emperor’s filial piety and their status as subjects.

But Zhao Yi Yun did not want this. He wanted Zhao Xuanyou, Yuwán, Zhao Mianze, and Aning to live with him in the palace forever.

He remembered Yuwán once saying that an emperor’s actions must be proper and justified. If Zhao Xuanyou became the Duke of En, then the four of them would have to live in the Duke of En’s mansion. Staying in the palace long-term would be improper and unjustified.

In the Golden Hall, Zhao Yi Yun shocked everyone by proposing to honor Zhao Xuanyou as the Grand Emperor and Yuwán as the Grand Empress Dowager.

The officials were naturally stunned and knelt to beg him to retract the order.

The rituals and laws were strict. If Zhao Xuanyou became the Grand Emperor and Yuwán the Grand Empress Dowager, it would confuse the bloodline and completely shake the legitimacy of the royal family.

But Zhao Yi Yun was not acting on a whim; he had prepared thoroughly.

He summoned the Minister of the Imperial Clan and presented the imperial genealogy.

The genealogy recorded the lineage, generations, legitimacy, names, birth and death dates, marriages, and titles of all royal clan members. It was the sole proof of royal identity.

Although there were distinctions between close and distant relatives within the royal clan, as long as one’s name was recorded in the genealogy, they were considered part of the royal family. Zhao Xuanyou’s name had long been recorded in the genealogy, so honoring him as the Grand Emperor would not confuse the royal bloodline.

Since the rituals and laws allowed it, the eloquent court officials could not find a reason to object.

Moreover, Zhao Yi Yun’s attitude was firm.

Though his appearance was youthful, his tone brooked no argument, already possessing the dignity of an emperor.

Without proper titles, every act of filial piety toward Zhao Xuanyou and Yuwán might seem unreasonable and require further discussion in the court.

Overnight, Yuwán went from a marchioness to the Grand Empress Dowager, a result she had never anticipated.

Not only that, Zhao Mianze was elevated to the rank of a prince due to his connection, while Aning, nominally Wen Jian’s daughter, was first granted the title of a county princess.

Two unexpected individuals were also honored.

One was Yao Yao, the daughter of Princess Yining. After Yao Yao was deposed, she was poisoned by Jiang’s wife. Ye Moqian and Princess Yining had persistently sought medical treatment for her for a long time. Although Yao Yao was not mentally impaired, her reactions were slow. Zhao Yi Yun granted her the title of a noble lady, ensuring she would be honored and cared for all her life.

The other was Zhao Yi Yun’s biological mother, Zhuang Huaiyue. He had always believed that his mother had died unjustly, having never harmed anyone. He insisted on posthumously honoring her as Empress Gongxian and ordered the construction of a grand mausoleum for her proper burial.

Zhao Xuanyou and Yuwán, of course, supported him.

By posthumously honoring his mother, it proved that he had not misjudged this child. He was kind and filial, not a heartless person.

They subtly felt that when Zhao Yi Yun grew older, he would surely rehabilitate his biological father, Zhao Zun.

When that day came, they would not say anything.

If Zhao Yi Yun were heartless toward his biological parents, how could he be affectionate toward his adoptive parents?

After the rewards were bestowed, Yuwán and Zhao Xuanyou moved with their children from the North Park to the Kunning Palace, which was closer to the Qianqing Palace. Living together as a family was no different from their days in Yuzhou.

Winter arrived in the capital in the blink of an eye. Scholars from various regions successively arrived in the capital to participate in the special imperial examination.

Over the past few months, Zhao Xuanyou and Yuwán had been busy and fulfilled.

The palace had appointed a suitable chief eunuch, and various vacancies had been filled.

Since Sun Qianran did not want to stay in the palace for long, Yuwán, grateful for her hard work during this period, sent her out of the palace and bestowed a residence upon her.

She and Zhao Xuanyou devoted themselves to taking care of Zhao Yi Yun, helping him share the burden of complex government affairs.

It was not that they wanted to usurp power, but Zhao Yi Yun was at the age where he should be studying and practicing martial arts. If he had to review all the memorials every day after court, he would have no time left for his studies and training.

Moreover, he was still growing, and could not be overworked.

Every day after court, besides attending classes and practicing martial arts, Yuwán would let him play with his siblings for an hour, leaving them to decide what to play.

The titles of Grand Emperor and Grand Empress Dowager came in handy here. Before Zhao Yi Yun took personal charge of government affairs, handling court matters was proper and justified, and no one could criticize them.

If they were the Duke and Duchess of En, they would likely have been accused of plotting to usurp the throne long ago.

This year’s snow arrived slightly later than usual but with great force. After a night of heavy snow, the entire palace was blanketed in white.

Calculating the time Zhao Yi Yun would finish his lessons, Yuwán ordered the imperial kitchen to prepare a warming chicken soup and personally delivered it to the Qianqing Palace.

The palace was warm as spring inside, and after staying for a long time, she wanted to go out for a walk.

As soon as she stepped outside, a cold gust of wind hit her face, making her cheeks feel icy. However, the sight of the sparkling snow was truly pleasing to the eye.

The palace servants had already cleared the snow and thin ice from the pathways. Yuwán, carrying the food box, soon arrived at the Qianqing Palace.

A half-finished snowman stood beside the palace steps, likely a masterpiece left by Aning earlier that morning.

Zhao Mianze preferred to be alone, so Aning often clung to Zhao Yi Yun, frequently waiting for him at the Qianqing Palace after court.

As Yuwán ascended the steps, a young eunuch respectfully approached and informed her that the emperor was inside the palace discussing state affairs with court officials.

Fearful of disturbing the meeting, Yuwán handed the food box to the young eunuch and turned to leave. After taking a few steps, she heard a voice call out, “Mother.”

She turned back with a smile and indeed saw Zhao Yi Yun, dressed in imperial robes, walking out of the palace, followed by an old acquaintance she had not seen in a long time.

“This official, Pei Ta, pays respects to Her Majesty the Grand Empress Dowager.”

After a brief exchange of glances, Pei Ta bowed in greeting.

Compared to before, Pei Ta had not changed much. His skin was still as fair as jade, and he stood tall and straight like a bamboo, though his eyes seemed even more tranquil.

“Lord Pei, no need for formalities,” Yuwán said softly.

As her gaze shifted, she caught sight of the sachet hanging from Pei Ta’s waist.

The embroidery on the sachet was not exquisite; it looked more like the work of a beginner rather than a skilled seamstress.

“Mother.” Zhao Yi Yun stepped forward to take the food box from Yuwán’s hands and then passed it to a nearby eunuch. “The weather is so cold; you could have ordered a palace maid to deliver the food. There was no need to come yourself.”

“I’ve been indoors for too long and wanted to take a walk.”

Pei Ta stood silently to the side, listening to their exchange. When Zhao Yi Yun remembered him and turned back, he said, “This official takes his leave.”

Zhao Yi Yun nodded, and after Pei Ta had left, Yuwán asked, “Were you just discussing the results of the special imperial examination with Lord Pei?”

“No,” Zhao Yi Yun replied. “Lord Pei mentioned that in previous years, the imperial examinations were held in spring or summer. This year’s special examination is temporary, and many scholars from the south are unaware of the harsh winter in the north. Today, he came to request a decree to prepare winter clothes for the poor scholars from the south.”

After the news of the additional special imperial examination spread across the land, scholars from various regions flocked to the capital to seize this opportunity. Many had not anticipated the severity of the northern winter.

Pei Ta had studied in Jiangnan before and was well aware of the difference between the winters in the south and the north.

He also knew that many poor scholars had borrowed money for their journey to the capital and could not even afford an inn, instead staying in temples. Winter clothes and blankets were expensive and a significant cost.

Last night’s heavy snow would be difficult for some to endure.

“That is indeed a good suggestion. Did you approve it?”

Zhao Yi Yun nodded.

Yuwán looked into the distance at Pei Ta.

Against the backdrop of the white snow, he walked alone, perfectly blending with the pure and ethereal scenery.

“Mother, why do you and Lord Pei not seem like old friends? I thought you would exchange pleasantries.”

Just now, both of them had looked very calm, with no intention of reminiscing.

If Zhao Yi Yun did not know that their handwriting was similar, he would have thought they were meeting for the first time.

Yuwán curved the corners of her lips but did not speak.

Exchange pleasantries?

It had been many years since they last met, and she indeed had many questions for Pei Ta. If they were old friends, they should sit down and have a good chat.

During their years in Yuzhou, Pei Ta had volunteered to work in the Ministry of Works but did not stay long in the capital. Instead, he traveled around supervising the construction of river works and border defense projects.

She was curious about the mountains and rivers he had seen, the vast oceans, curious about the sachet at his waist and whose handiwork it was, whether he was about to get married.

A man as good as him should not be alone.

But Yuwán did not have the right to ask out of curiosity. After all, they were more than just old friends.

“Mother, did I say something wrong?” Seeing Yuwán staring blankly at the snow, Zhao Yi Yun looked at her as if he had done something wrong.

Yuwán snapped out of her thoughts and smiled. “How could that be? I just thought of an idea and got lost in thought.”

“What good idea? Tell me quickly, Mother.”

“I plan to rent an inn where all the poor scholars from out of town taking this special examination can stay until the second month of next year.”

This special examination was to select talents, balance the old officials in the court, and consolidate Zhao Yi Yun’s throne.

The court had prepared for several months, but for those far from the capital, it was very sudden.

People had come from afar without hesitation to take the exam, and Yuwán wanted to reciprocate their sincerity. Since it was the first time the exam was held in the dead of winter, they should not let them suffer.

“That’s a good idea, but there’s no need for Father and Mother to spend the money. I can have the Ministry of Rites handle it.”

Yuwán, however, shook her head with a smile.

The positions of Grand Emperor and Grand Empress Dowager were hard-won by Zhao Yi Yun and a group of ministers. Although it was justifiable by rituals and laws, many court officials were dissatisfied.

By taking the initiative to arrange accommodation for these scholars from afar, they could not only demonstrate imperial grace but also win people’s hearts.

These future officials, having received their help, would not speak ill of them.

Coincidentally, Chen Da Niu and his wife had made a lot of money from their cosmetics shop over the past few years. Last month, they had purchased an inn in the capital, which was perfect for taking care of their business and helping them make a good impression.

“Don’t worry, Father and I have enough money. Let us do this to earn a good reputation.”

“Alright.” Zhao Yi Yun came back to his senses.

In the court, the generals all followed Zhao Xuanyou’s lead, but the civil officials were different.

If Father and Mother took the initiative to help the poor scholars spend the winter in the capital, it would be a good story and a gesture of goodwill toward the scholars.

“Mother, Brother.”

In the distance, Aning let go of Zhao Xuanyou’s hand and ran happily toward Yuwán and Zhao Yi Yun.

After the heavy snow, the nannies, fearing Aning would catch a cold, had dressed her very warmly. Her hat and clothes were trimmed with fur, making her look like a delicate little white rabbit as she ran.

“Be careful, the ground is still wet.”

Yuwán said with a smile. Zhao Yi Yun stepped forward to take Aning’s hand.

Aning’s appearance bore traces of Zhao Xuanyou and Yuwán, but she resembled Ding Wenxi more, with a delicate bone structure and picturesque features.

Officially a county princess, the palace servants all knew that Aning was a truly precious little princess.

As soon as she saw Zhao Yi Yun, Aning smiled and asked, “Did Big Brother see the snowman I made?”

Her smile was bright, and her face was fair and tender, making her look like a little fairy sculpted from snow.

Zhao Yi Yun touched her furry hat and gently said, “I saw it. After I finish my training, let’s decorate the snowman together.”

After saying this, Zhao Yi Yun looked at Zhao Xuanyou and called out, “Father.”

It was time for Zhao Yi Yun’s martial arts training. Although two skilled guards had been arranged as his teachers, in reality, Zhao Xuanyou personally taught him. This was a tradition passed down through generations in the Jingyuan Marquis’s family.

Zhao Mianze glanced at the snowman by the steps and tugged at Yuwán’s sleeve, muttering, “Mother, come make a snowman with me.”

Making snowmen was childish, but it was acceptable for Mother to play along.

This boy was naturally very clingy to Yuwán. Zhao Xuanyou shot him a glare, startling Zhao Mianze into shrinking behind Yuwán.

Yuwán used to worry that Zhao Mianze would be spoiled and unable to handle things, but over time, she realized that although he was clingy, he was not foolish or weak, so she did not mind.

She pushed Zhao Xuanyou’s arm. “You and Yi Yun go train first. I’ll make snowmen with the two little ones.”

Zhao Xuanyou responded with an “mm” and gently pinched Yuwán’s nose. “Work hard and make four more.”

Aning, confused, asked, “Father, why make four more?”

“Two big snowmen and three small ones. Think about why.”

Zhao Yi Yun and Zhao Mianze, of course, knew why. Aning tilted her head and thought for a moment before realizing, “Oh, we’re making snowmen of our whole family!”

She blinked her big eyes and had a new idea. She grabbed Zhao Xuanyou’s sleeve and coaxed, “Father, can I make your snowman?”

Aning had her own little plan. Second Brother liked Mother the most and would definitely make a snowman of Mother. She had to take over making Father’s snowman.

As for Big Brother... he was the emperor, the most generous, and wouldn’t compete with them.

“Of course, Aning can make it.” Zhao Xuanyou looked at his daughter, his heart melting.

“Yay!” Aning hopped and skipped to play in the snow. In her excitement, she fell onto the snow-covered ground.

The nearby nanny was terrified, fearing that the master would blame her for not taking good care of Aning.

Zhao Yi Yun wanted to help her up, but Yuwán stopped him. “Let her play.”

Sure enough, Aning got up by herself, brushed the snow off her knees, and proudly smiled at Yuwán.

The ground was snowy, and Aning was dressed warmly, so she wouldn’t get hurt.

Although she had been extremely pampered since birth, she was not a spoiled child. Yuwán even planned to have Zhao Xuanyou teach her martial arts.

“You two go train. Come back later to admire our snowmen.”

Yuwán had it all planned out. The whole family would play in the snow together, and in the evening, they would have a hot pot in the Kunning Palace.

Snowy days were perfect for enjoying a hearty hot pot.

Zhao Xuanyou took Zhao Yi Yun toward the training grounds. After walking a short distance, he could not help but stop and look back.

The two children were squatting on the ground, and Yuwán was shoveling snow with a wooden shovel.

Even though she was working, her movements were swift and decisive.

Before meeting Yuwán, he had been like a sharp blade tempered by the northwest wind and frost, cold and distant.

At that time, he thought that marrying a beautiful and virtuous wife and living a stable life in the marquis’s mansion would be the best life.

He had never imagined that he would fall so deeply in love with Yuwán, searching the world for her after she left, refusing to marry anyone else.

He had never imagined everything that followed: life and death trials, having children, and the whole family ascending to the imperial city.

In the distance, Yuwán, tired from shoveling snow, stopped to rest. Looking up, she saw Zhao Xuanyou and Zhao Yi Yun standing far away, watching them.

Yuwán’s eyes sparkled as she waved to them. “How about skipping training today?”

“Father?” Zhao Yi Yun was naturally tempted. He looked cautiously at Zhao Xuanyou and, seeing him nod, happily ran toward his siblings.

The young emperor, who maintained his imperial demeanor in front of officials, regained his lively spirit in front of his family.

Zhao Xuanyou also quickened his pace and tightly held Yuwán’s hand.

“What are you doing? Are you going to shovel snow?” Yuwán held the wooden shovel protectively with her other hand and raised an eyebrow at him with a smile. “I haven’t had enough fun yet.”

Zhao Xuanyou did not speak. He gently rubbed her hand, unwilling to let go.

From the capital to Yuzhou, and then from Yuzhou to this majestic imperial city, she had always been by his side.

Because of her, the spring flowers, autumn moon, summer sun, and winter snow were all worth looking forward to.

Zhao Xuanyou held Yuwán’s hand tightly, and she let him. Snow began to fall again from the sky, and the three children played and laughed, catching snowflakes with their faces turned up against the wind, fearless and bright.

chapters.title: Extra – Wen Jian 1
chapters.content:
Winter was supposed to be a time of deep snow and desolation, yet the countless red plum trees in Yuzhao Garden were in full, vibrant bloom.

Liang Miaotong walked along the mountain path with three other noble girls of similar age, surrounded by plum blossoms as radiant as clouds. The young ladies were all delighted.

"Tong’er, let’s go to the streets together on Lantern Festival night."

"Then it’s settled, we’ll go together."

In previous years, Liang Miaotong had always gone out with her elder sister, Liang Miaofeng. But now that her sister had become a princess consort, even if she didn’t enter the palace to see the lanterns, she would still be with her husband, Prince Rui. So when someone invited her to go see the lanterns, she was naturally pleased.

"It’s a deal!"

A gust of wind carried the scent of plum blossoms as the girls chattered and walked forward.

Suddenly, someone said, "Isn’t that Princess Rui up ahead?"

Liang Miaotong looked in the direction of the voice and saw Liang Miaofeng and Yu Wan walking hand in hand toward them.

She happily waved at them, then led her friends forward to exchange greetings before walking down the mountain together.

"I’ve never met the Lady of Jingyuan Marquis before," someone whispered.

"She’s really beautiful. I heard others say the Marquis is very devoted to her. No wonder."

"If he weren’t deeply in love, how could the Marquis have married a merchant’s daughter?"

Liang Miaotong liked Lady Jingyuan very much. Although her friends weren’t speaking ill of her, talking about her behind her back still made her unhappy. She took a few steps forward, distancing herself from them.

Not long after, a eunuch carrying a vase walked up the mountain. Liang Miaotong glanced at him, then turned her gaze back to the blooming red plum blossoms.

She saw a plum blossom blown from the branch by the wind and caught it in her palm.

Lost in thought, she suddenly heard a crisp sound. Looking up, she saw that the vase had shattered.

Before she could react, she saw the eunuch reach out to grab Yu Wan.

Yu Wan resisted, but seemed to be overpowered. Liang Miaotong immediately stepped forward and grabbed the eunuch’s arm.

In the standoff, a sharp weapon whistled through the air, followed by the eunuch’s agonized scream.

Liang Miaotong was just feeling relieved when her shoulder was suddenly grabbed. Before she could react, she was pulled and thrown down the mountain.

The world spun as her leg crashed heavily into a plum tree.

Liang Miaotong was born with a dull sense of pain and didn’t feel much agony, but she knew she had fallen hard because she could no longer feel that leg.

She tried to sit up to check her injury, but she was so dizzy that she struggled for a moment before collapsing back onto the ground.

Lying in the snow, she looked up at the plum blossoms on the branches, wondering where the eunuch had fallen. If he hadn’t fallen, would he come to finish her off next?

Dying here wouldn’t be so bad.

Liang Miaotong closed her eyes. When she opened them again, she saw a figure appear before her and froze.

The man was dressed in a tight-fitting outfit, and his face had no features; or rather, he was wearing a mask.

"Who are you?" she asked.

He didn’t speak but crouched down to examine her leg. He pressed a few of her acupuncture points.

Liang Miaotong suddenly felt her mind clear a little. Before she could ask another question, he said, "Your leg is broken. Don’t move."

His voice was soft and gentle, his words brief, but he didn’t sound cold.

"Are you a palace guard?"

He shook his head and helped her sit up by supporting her shoulders.

Seeing her leg in such a state, yet pale and silent, he found it strange.

The wind in the plum forest was exceptionally cold.

As she tumbled down the cliff, her cloak had been caught on a branch. He turned back, retrieved the cloak, and returned to drape it over her.

"Your injuries are serious. I’ve stopped the bleeding, so there’s no danger to your life. Soon, guards and palace servants will come to rescue you."

Liang Miaotong listened and felt he was about to leave.

Looking at the white mask, she suddenly reached out and removed it.

The first thing she saw was half of a refined and elegant face.

His appearance couldn’t be called handsome, but his eyes were exceptionally clear, as if they had never been tainted by the mundane world.

But in the next moment, Liang Miaotong saw the birthmark on the other side of his cheek.

So he wore the mask because of this birthmark...

Although she didn’t know his background, Liang Miaotong understood that he meant no harm; he had come to save her.

"I didn’t mean to..." A strong sense of guilt surged within her. Like a child who had done something wrong, she lowered her head, clutching the mask tightly as if wanting to apologize, but felt that nothing she said could make up for her mistake.

He moved his fingers, as if to take the mask back, but seeing her holding it to her chest, he said nothing more. Instead, he stood up and went to drag the half-dead eunuch over.

Liang Miaotong, seeing this, finally spoke again, "You’re leaving?"

He nodded.

"Who are you, really?" Liang Miaotong pressed.

"I am a guard of the Marquis’s residence. Don’t tell the palace people you’ve seen me."

With that, he carried the eunuch and disappeared into the plum forest in a flash.

He had come quickly and left even faster.

If Liang Miaotong hadn’t been holding his mask, she would have worried that all of this was a hallucination after her fall.

She didn’t feel much pain, but her head was still spinning, and her body was weak. Leaning against the plum tree, she waited quietly for a while before finally hearing the sounds of guards searching for her.

Remembering his warning, Liang Miaotong hid the mask in her cloak.

The guards soon found her and carried her back to the Yan Zhi Mei Pavilion.

Her sister and Lady Jingyuan were very worried about her. Only when they saw that her life was not in danger did they feel slightly relieved.

When Consort Li said they would not investigate the matter further, and seeing that her sister and Lady Jingyuan had no objections, Liang Miaotong also said nothing, only hiding the mask more carefully.

After Consort Li left, Lady Jingyuan expressed her gratitude for Liang Miaotong’s help and solemnly thanked her.

Liang Miaotong really wanted to ask Lady Jingyuan about the name of the masked man.

But the Yan Zhi Mei Pavilion was full of palace people. If she rashly asked such questions, she feared it might bring trouble to him and Lady Jingyuan.

Moreover, as an unmarried young lady, it would be improper for her to pursue the name of a guard. She didn’t know how Lady Jingyuan would view her.

Liang Miaotong returned home with a heavy heart. When her parents learned of her leg injury, they were heartbroken. She consoled them while feeling a pang of melancholy at the thought of being bedridden for months.

Fortunately, her sister sent someone to buy many storybooks from the street to help pass the time.

Her parents had originally forbidden her from reading such books, but given her serious injury, they made an exception.

Reading the stories of scholars and beauties in the books, Liang Miaotong felt an inexplicable restlessness.

Her life was supposed to be like that of other noble ladies in the capital: married off by her parents’ arrangement to a husband she had never met.

Everyone said her sister was fortunate, but Liang Miaotong knew her sister had worries.

Her sister didn’t speak of them, only to avoid worrying her family.

The stories of love at first sight and mutual affection in the books had not happened to her sister, nor would they happen to her.

In her moment of dejection, Liang Miaotong remembered the mask she had brought back from Yuzhao Garden.

Every Lantern Festival, she would buy exquisitely unique masks at the festival. Compared to the masks in her collection, this one was only a half-finished product; the craftsman hadn’t even had time to decorate it.

Yet now, looking at it, it seemed special.

Pure and clean, untouched by dust, just like his gaze.

Liang Miaotong suddenly decided to hang this mask with her other beautiful masks.

---

chapters.title: Extra – Wen Jian 2
chapters.content:
A broken bone required a hundred days to heal. Even though Liang Miaotong had a dull sense of pain, she still had to lie in bed obediently to recover.

After the New Year came the Lantern Festival. Although she could walk with a crutch now, she certainly couldn’t go out to see the lanterns in this state.

Seeing her gloomy mood, Lord Liang and Lady Liang had someone buy more than a dozen different lanterns from the street and hang them in the courtyard.

She was happy, of course, but there was still a hint of regret in her heart.

After the maid had helped her to bed, she waited until the maid left, then got up by herself, dressed, and slowly took a mask from the wall with the help of her crutch. She then slowly made her way to the courtyard.

The lanterns in the courtyard were still lit. Liang Miaotong put on the white mask and lightly touched the lanterns.

If her leg hadn’t been injured, she would be wearing a mask and carrying a lantern, playing in the streets right now.

Suddenly, the man from Yuzhao Garden appeared in her mind.

Was he at the lantern festival now? Would he meet some girl?

Probably not. Lady Jingyuan had said he was a guard, so he probably had duties on Lantern Festival night.

She shouldn’t be thinking about these things...

As she pondered, she suddenly heard a slight rustling sound.

She looked in the direction of the noise and caught a glimpse of a figure sitting in the tree. She was startled.

Before she could scream for help, the figure jumped down from the tree.

"It’s you?" Liang Miaotong said in surprise, but she didn’t notice the flicker of joy in her heart. "How did you get into my courtyard? You’re trespassing!"

"I came... to get my mask back," Wen Jian said.

After returning from Yuzhao Garden, Yu Wan had tested him several times.

Yu Wan knew him too well. With his qinggong skills, it was impossible for him to easily lose his mask.

He wasn’t deliberately deceiving Yu Wan; he himself didn’t understand why he had allowed Liang Miaotong to take his mask.

Unable to explain, he chose not to.

Wen Jian had come to the Liang residence several times. Each time, he intended to take back the mask and sever this distraction, but he always ended up lingering outside her courtyard.

Tonight, he dared to appear because he saw her wearing his mask.

He wanted to know if she, like him, had developed a distraction.

Liang Miaotong’s ears turned bright red when he mentioned the mask.

She had intended to take it off and return it to him, but if she did that now, he would surely see her flushed face, which would be too embarrassing.

She quickly came up with an excuse: "This is a mask I bought myself. It’s not yours."

Wen Jian responded with an "Oh" and said nothing more.

The cold wind made the lanterns in the courtyard sway. Perhaps because the mask concealed her expression, Liang Miaotong felt bolder.

"Your birthmark is gone?"

"I used a disguise."

No wonder he looked a little different from that day. Hearing that he could disguise himself, Liang Miaotong’s curiosity about him grew.

"Lady Jingyuan said you’re a guard at the Marquis’s residence?"

"Mmm." Even if he wasn’t a guard at the Marquis’s residence, his status was still worlds apart from hers. There was no need to tell the truth.

"You don’t have to be on duty tonight?"

"No."

She cleared her throat and softly asked, "It’s Lantern Festival tonight. Why don’t you go to the festival?"

Zhao Xuanyou and Yu Wan had gone to the palace to see the lanterns. Before leaving, they had driven him out, telling him to go to the festival himself.

Wen Jian had wandered the streets for a long time before ending up at the Liang residence.

He certainly wasn’t going to say that. Instead, he mimicked her earlier response and asked, "Do you want to go to the lantern festival?"

"Yes," Liang Miaotong blurted out, her face filled with regret. "But my leg just healed, and I still don’t have the strength to walk."

The festival was crowded; with her crutch, she would be easily bumped into.

"If you really want to go out, I can carry you."

Thinking of his ability to appear and disappear without a trace, Liang Miaotong immediately perked up. "Yes! You can fly. Take me flying out!"

"Can I carry you instead?"

He was worried about offending her, as she was a noble lady.

"Mmm, that’s fine."

After all, in Yuzhao Garden, he had already held her hand and supported her shoulders. If they were already crossing the line of propriety between men and women, then tonight wouldn’t make much difference.

Moreover, tonight was Lantern Festival, a day when men and women strolled together.

"It’s cold outside. Do you want to wear more clothes?"

"There’s a cloak on the beauty’s couch by the window. Could you help me get it?" As she watched him go into the room, Liang Miaotong couldn’t help but remind him, "Don’t wake the maid."

As soon as the words left her mouth, she realized they were unnecessary.

With his qinggong skills, there would be no problem.

Wen Jian draped the cloak over her, then turned and crouched in front of her.

Liang Miaotong’s cheeks turned red. She steeled herself and climbed onto his back.

He steadied her, then suddenly stood up and quickly carried her out of the Liang residence.

There was no curfew in the capital tonight, and the streets were still lively.

Even on a night like Lantern Festival, Wen Jian couldn’t carry a young lady through the streets openly.

Liang Miaotong was wearing a mask, but she was still a noble lady. If she were recognized by an acquaintance, it would damage her reputation.

So Wen Jian took Liang Miaotong through the streets and alleys until they reached the Luo Yue Tower.

Luo Yue Tower was located in the center of the lantern market and had three stories. Sitting on the roof of Luo Yue Tower, one could overlook the entire lantern market.

Wen Jian carefully helped Liang Miaotong sit down. "The snow just melted, and the roof is slippery. Don’t move around."

Liang Miaotong was bold, but not reckless. Sitting on the ridge, she grabbed the hem of Wen Jian’s clothes.

The roof was bitterly cold. Liang Miaotong wrapped herself tightly in the cloak and quietly watched the bustling lantern market below.

The lanterns here were not as grand or ingenious as those in the palace, but the market was teeming with people, each face beaming with smiles. This was a lively, human warmth that couldn’t be seen in the palace.

Liang Miaotong naturally preferred the lively folk lantern festival.

It was her first time sitting in such a place, and her eyes were filled with curiosity and joy.

Wen Jian turned his head, his gaze falling on her as he silently accompanied her.

No need for many words. He had no grand expectations. Being able to sit here with her and enjoy the lanterns was enough.

As the hour approached midnight, Wen Jian took Liang Miaotong back to the Liang residence.

The night’s experience was too magical. Liang Miaotong wanted to thank him, but before she could, he disappeared in a flash.

At first, she didn’t understand. Gradually, she realized.

The gap between their statuses was too vast. Spending Lantern Festival together to watch the lanterns was already a luxury. Taking another step forward would be overstepping the boundaries.

Her parents often discussed her marriage prospects, mentioning either noble young masters from the capital or promising young talents; people she had never met, who would be her future destination.

She couldn’t indulge in this.

Not long after the Lantern Festival, her sister, Liang Miaofeng, returned to her maiden home from the Prince’s residence.

She seemed to have been wronged in the Prince’s residence and cried in her mother’s arms for a long time.

Liang Miaotong didn’t ask her why she was crying.

Prince Rui, her brother-in-law, didn’t like her sister. Every day spent in the Prince’s residence must have been difficult for her sister.

And what about her?

In the future, if she married someone who didn’t like her, what kind of life would she have?

She didn’t know what she should do, or rather, she didn’t know what she could do. But she often thought of their first meeting in Yuzhao Garden and the night she held onto his clothes while sitting on the roof, watching the lanterns.

When she heard that the Jingyuan Marquis’s family would soon return to Yuzhou, she couldn’t help but go to the Marquis’s residence.

Lady Jingyuan treated her very kindly and played a game of Go with her in the garden.

He appeared.

His appearance had changed again, but Liang Miaotong still recognized him at a glance.

Lady Jingyuan said his name was Ding Jian, and he was her younger brother.

Liang Miaotong was surprised, but a glimmer of hope arose in her heart. This way, their statuses weren’t so mismatched, right?

But he acted very cold, as if he didn’t recognize her at all.

She wanted to find an opportunity to ask him, so she continued to linger at the Marquis’s residence.

Fortunately, the Old Madame and Lady Jingyuan treated her very kindly. Not only did they not find her troublesome, but they also invited her to stay for dinner. When it got dark, they even had him escort her home.

After leaving the Marquis’s residence, Liang Miaotong looked at him, but he turned his head away and busied himself with saddling the horse.

Liang Miaotong frowned slightly and silently got into the carriage.

chapters.title: Extra – Wen Jian 3
chapters.content:
On the way back from the Marquis's residence to the Liang residence, Liang Miaotong and Wen Jian did not exchange a single word.

When they arrived at the gate of the Liang residence, her mother, seeing that she had returned home so late, came out personally to scold her for being thoughtless and lingering at the Marquis's residence for so long.

As Liang Miaotong was pulled into the residence, she couldn't help but look back, but Wen Jian still did not turn around and rode away straight.

Of course, she was heartbroken.

The events of the Lantern Festival night were nothing but a fleeting moment, a dream that was now time to wake from.

But she still couldn't let go.

On the day the Marquis of Jingyuan and his wife left the capital, she dressed up and went to the city gate to see them off.

Wen Jian was naturally there as well.

He stayed with the guards the entire time, and Liang Miaotong had no chance to speak with him at all.

The Marchioness seemed to notice her worries and asked a few questions, but she herself retreated.

After seeing off the Marchioness, Liang Miaotong returned home dejected.

Her sister had stayed at her parents' home for two months before her brother-in-law, Prince Rui, came to take her back.

Her parents could see that there were problems between the couple, but since Prince Rui was of noble status, no one dared to ask too much.

After her sister returned to the prince's residence, her parents continued to look for a marriage match for her. After much thought, she went to the Prince Rui's residence to seek her sister's protection.

However, not long after, the emperor issued a decree ordering all princes to return to their fiefs.

Once her sister left the capital, she would have to return home and let her parents arrange her marriage. In her frustration, she quarreled with her sister, and her words struck her sister's pain points, only to be caught by Prince Rui.

Knowing she had caused trouble, Liang Miaotong was at a loss, but unexpectedly, the situation took a turn for the better.

Prince Rui allowed her to follow them to Yingzhou for a while and would explain the situation to her parents.

After arriving in Yingzhou, Liang Miaotong finally opened her heart to her sister and told her about her feelings for Wen Jian.

Her sister did not blame her for being reckless and even guessed why Wen Jian had stopped acknowledging her after the Lantern Festival.

The Marchioness came from a merchant family, and there had always been gossip about her in the capital.

To be fair, the Marchioness's family background did not match that of the Marquis of Jingyuan. It was the Marquis who was deeply in love with her and insisted on marrying her.

Moreover, compared to the Marchioness, whose beauty could topple cities, Wen Jian's appearance was marred, making Liang Miaotong feel even more inferior.

It wasn't that Wen Jian was heartless towards Liang Miaotong, but that he didn't dare to approach her.

Encouraged by her sister, Liang Miaotong wrote a letter to Yuzhou. She did not reveal her feelings in the letter but wrote about her recent experiences in Yingzhou, treating him as a long-lost friend.

The courier from Prince Rui's residence traveled day and night, and the letter was delivered to Yuzhou in a few days.

When the gatekeeper saw that someone from the prince's residence had arrived, he reported the matter to Zhao Xuanyou.

Zhao Xuanyou had long known about Wen Jian and Liang Miaotong's affair. Upon seeing the words "To Jian, Personal" written on the envelope, he immediately gave the letter to Wen Jian.

By the time Yu Wan heard about this, it was already dark.

After the Marquis's residence had two little ones, everyone's attention was focused on the siblings. As a mother, Yu Wan's heart was completely devoted to the two children.

When they left the capital, she had intended to help Wen Jian, but due to giving birth and Ah Ning's illness, she had neglected to do so.

She hurried to Wen Jian's small courtyard and, as expected, found him sitting alone on the roof.

Yu Wan did not call him down but ordered someone to bring a ladder and climbed onto the roof herself.

"Be careful," Wen Jian reminded her.

After giving birth, Yu Wan had been taking good care of herself, but her physical strength was still not as good as before. Moreover, it had been a long time since she had climbed a roof, and she indeed felt a bit unsteady stepping on the green tiles.

She decided to crawl on all fours towards the ridge, sitting down next to Wen Jian.

It had been a long time since they had talked like this.

"Did Tong'er write to you?" Yu Wan asked directly.

"Mmm."

This time, Wen Jian did not deny his connection with Liang Miaotong.

Yu Wan asked again, "Did you two secretly meet in the capital before?"

"Just once."

"If you had told me earlier, I would have helped you propose marriage in the capital."

"Yu Wan," Wen Jian lowered his gaze, "I am not worthy of her."

Yu Wan understood.

It wasn't just their family backgrounds; Wen Jian's appearance was also an issue.

"As long as you like her, there must be a way."

"It's not like that. I don't want to deceive her and her family. They should know what kind of person I am."

"How is it deception? Tong'er knew what you looked like the first time she saw you."

Wen Jian remained silent.

Yu Wan pinched her fingers. Although she came from a humble background, she was naturally beautiful and indeed could not empathize with Wen Jian's feelings.

After thinking for a moment, she softly said, "What did Tong'er say in her letter? Is she doing well in the capital?"

"She's not in the capital. She followed Prince Rui and the Princess to their fief."

Yu Wan was surprised.

To avoid the marriage arrangements made by Lord Liang and Lady Liang, she had fled to Zhao Qi's fief?

Liang Miaotong's feelings for Wen Jian were much more determined than Yu Wan had thought.

"Did she only write about that?"

"She wrote about the customs and scenery she had seen in Yingzhou. The Prince and Princess doted on her, allowing her to go out often, which was much more free than when she was in the capital."

"Ah Jian, I know you don't like me interfering in this matter, but there are some things I really want to tell you."

Wen Jian raised his eyes and met Yu Wan's gaze.

Having known each other for many years, they had long developed a tacit understanding.

It wasn't that he didn't allow Yu Wan to interfere in his affairs, but he knew that Yu Wan, in order to help him, would spare no effort, and would inevitably involve Zhao Xuanyou, and he didn't want to cause trouble for them.

"You speak."

"Tong'er left her parents to go to Yingzhou, which is her way of showing her attitude towards you."

Wen Jian's expression darkened slightly, with a hint of reluctance.

In his heart, he always felt that he was not worthy of Liang Miaotong.

Yu Wan's gaze flickered slightly. She didn't ask him any more questions but instead asked, "Do you think I am worthy of Zhao Xuanyou?"

"Of course," Wen Jian said without hesitation.

Yu Wan smiled, "Do you think, in the eyes of the noble families in the capital, I am worthy of Zhao Xuanyou?"

Wen Jian's thin lips moved slightly, but he said nothing.

"Do you think Zhao Xuanyou would despise me for my humble background?"

"Of course not."

"That's the point. He chose me, and I chose him. We don't care what others think. Since Tong'er has chosen you, and you have chosen her, why care about what others think? She has already seen your appearance and doesn't mind at all."
